\section*{Rights and Use}

\noindent$\bullet$ Source text base in this edition comes from public-domain materials.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Brenton Septuagint 1851 English, LXX2012 English, TSK, and R. H. Charles's\par
\noindent 1917 *Book of Enoch* are treated here as public-domain sources.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ UKJV distributed here as public-domain text; credit line included here as\par
\noindent requested and gladly given: `I love Jesus (UKJV)`.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Editor's original material in this project is released under `CC-BY 4.0`,\par
\noindent except where a separate notice applies.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Current build system still carries provisional OpenBible fallback data in a\par
\noindent few places. That layer is `CC-BY`, not public domain, and should be removed\par
\noindent for a strict all-public-domain release.\par

\section*{Editorial Perspective}

\noindent$\bullet$ This edition confesses Holy Scripture as God's inerrant word and the\par
\noindent word-for-word inspired revelation given in the original writings.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This project gives deliberate weight to Septuagintal and other early textual\par
\noindent witnesses because complete Greek biblical codices such as Vaticanus and\par
\noindent Sinaiticus are centuries earlier than complete medieval Masoretic codices\par
\noindent such as Leningrad.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This project also gives serious attention to Hebrew textual plurality before\par
\noindent medieval standardization, especially in light of Dead Sea Scroll evidence.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This edition argues that many New Testament quotations align more closely\par
\noindent with Septuagintal or other non-Masoretic forms than with the later medieval\par
\noindent Masoretic tradition.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This edition also treats some later Jewish textual standardization and\par
\noindent revision as theologically significant for Christian readers, especially where\par
\noindent christological, angelological, or supernatural themes appear reduced or\par
\noindent redirected in later forms of the text.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This rationale includes passages such as Genesis 6 and other texts where\par
\noindent older readings help illuminate biblical supernatural themes and later New\par
\noindent Testament usage.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ This is an editorial rationale page, not an attempt to settle every point of\par
\noindent modern text-critical debate inside one preface.\par

\section*{Research Notes}

\noindent$\bullet$ Earliest complete Greek biblical codices preserving broad Septuagintal text:\par
\noindent 4th-5th century AD.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Oldest complete medieval Masoretic codex commonly used in printed editions:\par
\noindent Leningrad Codex, AD 1008.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Earlier Greek Septuagint fragments and codices place major LXX witness\par
\noindent history more than a millennium earlier than the standard complete Masoretic\par
\noindent codex base used in modern printed Hebrew Bibles.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Dead Sea Scrolls show earlier Hebrew textual diversity long before medieval\par
\noindent Masoretic stabilization.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Jude 14-15 explicitly cites Enochic prophecy.\par
\noindent$\bullet$ Many New Testament quotations are widely recognized as being closer to the\par
\noindent Septuagint than to the later Masoretic wording.\par

\section*{Number Meanings}

\noindent 1: Unity, God’s Sovereignty\par
\noindent Represents the oneness of God (Deuteronomy 6:4, "The Lord our God is one"). Symbolizes primacy and the beginning.\par
\noindent 2: Union, Division, or Witness\par
\noindent Signifies partnership or confirmation by two witnesses (Ecclesiastes 4:9; Matthew 18:16). Can also indicate contrast or division.\par
\noindent 3: Divine Completeness, Trinity\par
\noindent Reflects the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) and divine perfection (Matthew 28:19; John 21:14, Jesus’ third appearance post-resurrection).\par
\noindent 4: Creation, Universality\par
\noindent Associated with the created world (four corners of the earth, four seasons; Revelation 7:1). Represents God’s creative works.\par
\noindent 5: Grace, God’s Goodness\par
\noindent Linked to God’s favor and grace (five offerings in Leviticus; Genesis 43:34, five portions for Benjamin). Often tied to human weakness met by divine strength.\par
\noindent 6: Humanity, Imperfection\par
\noindent Represents human effort or falling short of divine perfection (created on the sixth day, Genesis 1:26-31; 666 as the number of the beast, Revelation 13:18).\par
\noindent 7: Perfection, Completion\par
\noindent Denotes spiritual perfection and God’s completed work (seven days of creation, Genesis 2:2; seven seals in Revelation). Highly significant in Scripture.\par
\noindent 8: New Beginnings\par
\noindent Symbolizes renewal or a new order (eight people saved on Noah’s ark, Genesis 7:13; circumcision on the eighth day, Leviticus 12:3). Represents resurrection and "born again".\par
\noindent 9: Divine Completeness, Finality\par
\noindent Symbolizes divine completeness or finality (nine fruits of the Holy Spirit, Galatians 5:22-23; nine people with leprosy in Scripture).\par
\noindent 10: Divine Order, Completeness of Order\par
\noindent Represents a complete system or human responsibility (Ten Commandments, Exodus 20; ten plagues, Exodus 7-12).\par
\noindent 11: Disorder, Chaos, Judgment\par
\noindent Symbolizes disorder or judgment (eleven dukes of Edom; eleven officials offended by truth).\par
\noindent 12: God’s Government, Authority\par
\noindent Indicates divine authority or organization (twelve tribes of Israel, Genesis 49:28; twelve apostles, Matthew 10:1-2). Denotes the Creator's foundation or perfect authority\par
\noindent 13: Rebellion, Lawlessness\par
\noindent Symbolic of rebellion (Nimrod as generation 13 in Ham's line; thirteen things that defile a person).\par
\noindent 14: Double Spiritual Perfection\par
\noindent Multiplies the perfection of 7 (fourteen days for Passover; lineage from Abraham to Jesus in sets of 14).\par
\noindent 15: Rest After Deliverance\par
\noindent Symbolizes rest following deliverance (Feast of Unleavened Bread on Nisan 15). Key references: Genesis 15:12-16 (Abraham's vision), Exodus 12:40-42 (Exodus from Egypt).\par
\noindent 16: Love and Loving\par
\noindent Represents the duality of true love (16 qualities of God's love in 1 Corinthians 13:4-8). Key references: Genesis 46:18 (Jacob's migration), 1 Corinthians 13:4-8.\par
\noindent 17: Overcoming the Enemy, Victory\par
\noindent Represents complete victory (ten + seven; Day of Atonement themes).\par
\noindent 18: Bondage\par
\noindent Symbolizes physical or spiritual bondage (Israelites oppressed for 18 years). Key references: Judges 3:14, Luke 13:11-12 (woman healed after 18 years).\par
\noindent 19: God's Perfect Order in Judgment\par
\noindent Symbolizes perfect order concerning judgment (10 + 9). Key references: Joshua 19:38 (Naphtali's cities), Psalm 19 (heavens declare God's glory).\par
\noindent 20: Perfect Waiting\par
\noindent Symbolizes complete waiting (twice ten; age for Levite service).\par
\noindent 21: Great Wickedness, Rebellion, and Sin\par
\noindent Represents an outgrowth of sin and rebellion (21 sins in 2 Timothy 3:1-5). Key references: 2 Timothy 3:1-5, Revelation 21:21 (New Jerusalem).\par
\noindent 22: Light\par
\noindent Symbolizes light and revelation (22 Hebrew letters). Key references: Psalms 119:105, John 12:46.\par
\noindent 23: Divine Protection and Guidance\par
\noindent Symbolizes protection, blessing, and judgment (Psalm 23). Key references: Psalm 23, 1 Corinthians 10:8 (23,000 fell).\par
\noindent 24: Priesthood\par
\noindent Symbolizes the priesthood and worship (24 courses of priests). Key references: 1 Chronicles 23-24, Revelation 4:4 (24 elders).\par
\noindent 25: Grace Upon Grace\par
\noindent Symbolizes multiplied grace (25 cubits in Ezekiel's temple). Key references: John 1:16-17, Ezekiel 40:13.\par
\noindent 26: Eternal God (YHWH)\par
\noindent Symbolizes God's eternal nature (Gematria of YHWH=26). Key references: Genesis 1:26 (creation in God's image), Exodus (Moses as 26th generation).\par
\noindent 30: Dedication to a Task\par
\noindent Represents dedication or maturity (Jesus' ministry at 30; price of betrayal).\par
\noindent 33: God's Promises\par
\noindent Connected to divine promises (Jesus' age at death; 33 times "three" in Revelation).\par
\noindent 40: Testing, Trial, Preparation\par
\noindent Associated with periods of testing or probation (40 days of rain in Noah’s flood, Genesis 7:12; Jesus’ 40 days in the wilderness, Matthew 4:2).\par
\noindent 50: Holy Spirit, Pentecost, Deliverance\par
\noindent Linked to the outpouring of God's Spirit (Pentecost, 50 days after Passover; Jubilee every 50 years;).\par
\noindent 60: Threshold of Later Life, Pride\par
\noindent Represents entering life's final phase (threescore years; influences like pride in parables;).\par
\noindent 70: Completeness, Restoration\par
\noindent Represents fullness or a significant period (70 years of exile, Jeremiah 25:11; 70 disciples sent out, Luke 10:1).\par
\noindent 666: Perfection of Imperfection, Beast\par
\noindent Symbolizes ultimate human imperfection and Satan's system (mark of the Beast, Revelation 13:18)\par

\section*{Genesis Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Moses\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Received as Mosaic in Jewish and Christian tradition; the Pentateuch is treated as Moses' writing, with only final inspired editorial updating where needed.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Jesus appealed to Moses in John 5:46-47; see also Mark 12:26 and Luke 24:27,44.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 1446-1406 BC during Israel's wilderness period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology yields the shorter primeval and patriarchal timeline; from creation to Jacob's family entering Egypt it is markedly shorter than the LXX, especially in Genesis 5 and 11.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} LXX chronology is longer than the MT in the antediluvian and postdiluvian genealogies, chiefly because several patriarchal begetting ages are 100 years higher.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} From creation through Joseph's death; written for covenant Israel as foundational history of origins, sin, nations, and the patriarchal line.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To give the true beginning of the world, man, sin, nations, and the covenant line, and to trace the promised seed through the fathers.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} creation; fall; flood; Babel; Abrahamic covenant; promised seed; election; providence; covenant land\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Primeval history 1-11; Patriarchal history 12-36; Joseph and the descent to Egypt 37-50.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Genesis g (4Q7) and other early Qumran Genesis fragments Hasmonean period ca. 100-1 BC | Subst. 4QpaleoGenesis-Exodus (4Q12), an extensive though fragmentary Hebrew witness covering large stretches of Genesis and Exodus Hasmonean period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Alexandrinus, Volume 1 (Genesis-2 Chronicles) 5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Chronographical treatment of Genesis traditions by Demetrius the Chronographer (late 3rd century BC)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Genesis survives in both MT and LXX forms; the LXX genealogical numbers in chapters 5 and 11 are often longer. Early Jewish and Christian chronographers frequently reflect awareness of the longer Greek chronology.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Because Christ and the apostles treat Moses as author, this edition receives Genesis as Mosaic in authorship and originally inerrant in wording; later textual divergence in transmission does not overturn the inspiration of the autographs.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Genesis 1}
\markright{GENESIS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But the earth was unsightly and unfurnished, and darkness was over the deep, and the Spirit of God moved over the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And God said, Let there be light, and there was light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And God saw the light that it was good, and God divided between the light and the darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night, and there was evening and there was morning, the first day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it be a division between water and water, and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And God made the firmament, and God divided between the water which was under the firmament and the water which was above the firmament. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And God called the firmament Heaven, and God saw that it was good, and there was evening and there was morning, the second day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God said, Let the water which is under the heaven be collected into one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so. And the water which was under the heaven was collected into its places, and the dry land appeared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And God called the dry land Earth, and the gatherings of the waters he called Seas, and God saw that it was good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God said, Let the earth bring forth the herb of grass bearing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree bearing fruit whose seed is in it, according to its kind on the earth, and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the earth brought forth the herb of grass bearing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree bearing fruit whose seed is in it, according to its kind on the earth, and God saw that it was good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there was evening and there was morning, the third day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth, to divide between day and night, and let them be for signs and for seasons and for days and for years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And let them be for light in the firmament of the heaven, so as to shine upon the earth, and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And God made the two great lights, the greater light for regulating the day and the lesser light for regulating the night, the stars also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And God placed them in the firmament of the heaven, so as to shine upon the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and to regulate day and night, and to divide between the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And there was evening and there was morning, the fourth day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And God said, Let the waters bring forth reptiles having life, and winged creatures flying above the earth in the firmament of heaven, and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And God made great whales, and every living reptile, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every creature that flies with wings according to its kind, and God saw that they were good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And God blessed them saying, Increase and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let the creatures that fly be multiplied on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And there was evening and there was morning, the fifth day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature according to its kind, quadrupeds and reptiles and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and cattle according to their kind, and all the reptiles of the earth according to their kind, and God saw that they were good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And God said, Let us make man according to our image and likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the flying creatures of heaven, and over the cattle and all the earth, and over all the reptiles that creep on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And God made man, according to the image of God he made him, male and female he made them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And God blessed them, saying, Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the seas and flying creatures of heaven, and all the cattle and all the earth, and all the reptiles that creep on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And God said, Behold I have given to you every seed-bearing herb sowing seed which is upon all the earth, and every tree which has in itself the fruit of seed that is sown, to you it shall be for food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And to all the wild beasts of the earth, and to all the flying creatures of heaven, and to every reptile creeping on the earth, which has in itself the breath of life, even every green plant for food; and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And God saw all the things that he had made, and, behold, they were very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name of God: Elohim (אֱלֹהִים) — God; mighty one(s) Common English renderings: God. The most common opening name for God in Scripture; grammatically plural in form but regularly used with singular verbs for the one true God. Heb. vocab: Elohim (אֱלֹהִים) = God; gods. Common English renderings: God; gods; divine beings. Morphologically plural but often takes singular verbs for the God of Israel. Heb. vocab: erets (אֶרֶץ) = earth; land. Common English renderings: earth; land; country. May denote the whole earth or a specific territory depending on context. Heb. vocab: shamayim (שָׁמַיִם) = heavens; sky. Common English renderings: heaven; heavens; sky. A plural form commonly used for the sky and heavenly realm. Heb. vocab: bara (בָּרָא) = to create. Common English renderings: create. In the Hebrew Bible God is the usual subject of this verb. Gk. vocab: theos (θεός) = God; god. Common English renderings: God; god. In context this lemma may denote the true God or a false god. Gk. vocab: ouranos (οὐρανός) = heaven; sky. Common English renderings: heaven; heavens. The plural heavens often underlies English singular heaven. Gk. vocab: gē (γῆ) = earth; land. Common English renderings: earth; land. Can mean the whole earth or a particular land. \textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: ruach (רוּחַ) = spirit; wind; breath. Common English renderings: spirit; wind. A major term for spirit, breath, or wind, with meaning determined by context. Heb. vocab: mayim (מַיִם) = water. Common English renderings: water; waters. Plural form often functioning as a mass noun. Heb. vocab: choshekh (חֹשֶׁךְ) = darkness. Common English renderings: darkness. Frequently paired with light in literal and metaphorical contrast. Heb. vocab: panim (פָּנִים) = face; presence. Common English renderings: face; presence. Plural form often used for personal presence or surface. Gk. vocab: pneuma (πνεῦμα) = spirit; wind; breath. Common English renderings: Spirit; spirit; wind. Meaning is determined by context: divine Spirit, human spirit, wind, or breath. Gk. vocab: hydōr (ὕδωρ) = water. Common English renderings: water. A common creation term that also carries symbolic force in Scripture. Gk. vocab: skotos (σκότος) = darkness. Common English renderings: darkness. A major biblical image for darkness, ignorance, evil, and judgment. Gk. vocab: prosōpon (πρόσωπον) = face; presence. Common English renderings: face; presence. Can mean face, appearance, or presence. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: or (אוֹר) = light. Common English renderings: light. A major theological image for life, revelation, and salvation. Heb. vocab: amar (אָמַר) = to say. Common English renderings: say. The most common verb of speech in biblical Hebrew. Gk. vocab: phōs (φῶς) = light. Common English renderings: light. A major biblical image for creation, truth, holiness, and revelation. \textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: tov (טוֹב) = good. Common English renderings: good. Broad term for moral, functional, and aesthetic goodness. Heb. vocab: ra’ah (רָאָה) = to see. Common English renderings: see. Can imply perception, provision, or concern. Heb. vocab: badal (בָּדַל) = to divide; separate. Common English renderings: divide; separate. Creation and holiness term of distinction. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: yom (יוֹם) = day. Common English renderings: day. Can mean daylight, a full day, or an era depending on context. Heb. vocab: laylah (לַיְלָה) = night. Common English renderings: night. The regular counterpart to day in the creation account and beyond. Heb. vocab: qara (קָרָא) = to call; proclaim; read. Common English renderings: call; proclaim; read. Very broad term for naming, summoning, and proclamation. Heb. vocab: echad (אַחַד) = one. Common English renderings: one. Can denote singularity, unity, or firstness in sequence. Gk. vocab: hēmera (ἡμέρα) = day. Common English renderings: day. Can refer to a day, daylight, or a defined time period. Gk. vocab: nyx (νύξ) = night. Common English renderings: night. Used literally and sometimes figuratively for darkness. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: tavekh (תָּוֶךְ) = midst; middle. Common English renderings: midst. Frequent relational term for being among or within. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: asah (עָשָׂה) = to do; make. Common English renderings: do; make. One of the most common verbs, used widely for God’s actions and human deeds. Heb. vocab: tachat (תַּחַת) = under; instead of. Common English renderings: under; instead of. Spatial and substitutionary term. Heb. vocab: ken (כֵּן) = so; thus; right; yes. Common English renderings: so; thus; yes. Its sound matches the English name Ken; the resemblance is coincidental, while the Hebrew word means so, thus, right, or yes. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: maqom (מָקוֹם) = place. Common English renderings: place. Common term for location, sometimes reverentially for God’s place. Heb. vocab: qavah (קָוָה) = to wait; hope. Common English renderings: wait; hope. Elsewhere a major hope term though this first use is from a different sense/etymology in some analyses. Heb. vocab: el (אֶל) = to; toward. Common English renderings: to; unto. Direction marker preposition. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: yam (יָם) = sea. Common English renderings: sea. Also used for large bodies of water such as the Mediterranean. Gk. vocab: thalassa (θάλασσα) = sea. Common English renderings: sea. A major creation and exodus term. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: ets (עֵץ) = tree; wood. Common English renderings: tree; wood. Context can emphasize living tree or timber/wood. Heb. vocab: peri (פְּרִי) = fruit. Common English renderings: fruit. Used for produce, offspring, and metaphorical results. Heb. vocab: zera (זֶרַע) = seed; offspring. Common English renderings: seed; offspring. A key covenant term for descendants and promise. Heb. vocab: min (מִן) = from. Common English renderings: from; of. Preposition of source, separation, or partitive relation. Gk. vocab: sperma (σπέρμα) = seed; offspring. Common English renderings: seed; offspring. Can mean seed for sowing or descendants. Gk. vocab: karpos (καρπός) = fruit; produce; result. Common English renderings: fruit. Used literally of produce and figuratively of outcomes. Gk. vocab: dendron (δένδρον) = tree. Common English renderings: tree. A common natural term with symbolic uses. Gk. vocab: chortos (χόρτος) = grass; herbage. Common English renderings: grass. Used of grass, fodder, or green growth. Gk. vocab: xylon (ξύλον) = wood; tree; timber. Common English renderings: tree; wood. Can mean wood, timber, tree, or wooden instrument. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: mo’ed (מוֹעֵד) = appointed time; meeting. Common English renderings: feast; appointed time; congregation. Used for festivals and tent of meeting. Heb. vocab: ot (אוֹת) = sign; mark. Common English renderings: sign; token. Used for miraculous signs, covenant tokens, and symbolic markers. Heb. vocab: le (לְ) = to; for; belonging to. Common English renderings: to; for. Very common preposition/prefix with broad functions. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: kokhav (כּוֹכָב) = star. Common English renderings: star. Used literally and symbolically for multitude or rulers. Heb. vocab: memshalah (מֶמְשָׁלָה) = dominion; rule. Common English renderings: dominion; rule. Used for governmental authority and dominion. Heb. vocab: qatan (קָטָן) = small; little; young. Common English renderings: small; little; least. Used of size, age, and status. Heb. vocab: gadol (גָּדוֹל) = great; large. Common English renderings: great; large. Common term for greatness, size, and rank. Heb. vocab: shenayim (שְׁנַיִם) = two. Common English renderings: two. Basic numeral, important in witness and pair contexts. Gk. vocab: astēr (ἀστήρ) = star. Common English renderings: star. A celestial term with narrative and symbolic significance. Gk. vocab: hēlios (ἥλιος) = sun. Common English renderings: sun. A creation term that also appears in poetic and apocalyptic contexts. Gk. vocab: selēnē (σελήνη) = moon. Common English renderings: moon. The standard Greek term for moon. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: natan (נָתַן) = to give. Common English renderings: give. Broad verb for giving, setting, appointing, and handing over. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: mashal (מָשַׁל) = to rule; speak proverb. Common English renderings: rule. A different noun form gives proverb; the verb here is dominion. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: chai (חַי) = living; alive. Common English renderings: living; alive. Appears in many forms for life and living beings. Heb. vocab: nephesh (נֶפֶשׁ) = soul; life; living being. Common English renderings: soul; life. Often denotes the living self or life rather than an abstract immaterial soul. Heb. vocab: nephesh chayyah (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה) = living creature. Common English renderings: living creature; living soul. Compound phrase used for animals and humanity as living beings. Heb. vocab: of (עוֹף) = bird; flying creature. Common English renderings: fowl; bird. General term for flying creatures. Gk. vocab: zōē (ζωή) = life. Common English renderings: life. Used for life broadly, including eternal life in later biblical theology. Gk. vocab: psychē (ψυχή) = soul; life; self. Common English renderings: soul; life. Can mean life, living being, or the inner self. Gk. vocab: peteinon (πετεινόν) = bird. Common English renderings: fowl; bird. A common Greek Bible term for birds or flying creatures. \textsuperscript{21} Heb. vocab: kol (כֹּל) = all; every; whole. Common English renderings: all; every. One of the most frequent quantifying words. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: barakh (בָּרַךְ) = to bless. Common English renderings: bless. A central verb in creation, covenant, and worship. Heb. vocab: ravah (רָבָה) = to become many; increase. Common English renderings: multiply; increase. Key creation and covenant multiplication term. Heb. vocab: parah (פָּרָה) = to be fruitful. Common English renderings: be fruitful. Closely paired with multiplication in blessing formulas. Heb. vocab: male (מָלֵא) = to fill; be full. Common English renderings: fill; full. Used literally and figuratively for fullness. Gk. vocab: eulogeō (εὐλογέω) = to bless; speak well of. Common English renderings: bless. A foundational blessing verb represented by its lexical form. \textsuperscript{24} Gk. vocab: zōion (ζῷον) = living creature; animal. Common English renderings: beast; living creature. A broad term for living creature, especially in Revelation and the Greek Old Testament. Gk. vocab: thērion (θηρίον) = wild beast; beast. Common English renderings: beast. Usually denotes a wild animal or beast. \textsuperscript{26} Heb. vocab: adam (אָדָם) = man; humankind; Adam. Common English renderings: man; mankind; Adam. Used both as a personal name and as a collective for humanity. Heb. vocab: dag (דָּג) = fish. Common English renderings: fish. Basic aquatic creature term. Heb. vocab: ke (כְּ) = as; like. Common English renderings: as; like. Comparative preposition/prefix. Gk. vocab: anthrōpos (ἄνθρωπος) = human being; person. Common English renderings: man; person. Often refers to humanity generally rather than specifically to a male. Gk. vocab: ichthys (ἰχθύς) = fish. Common English renderings: fish. The ordinary Greek term for fish. Gk. vocab: ptēnon (πτηνόν) = bird; winged creature. Common English renderings: fowl; bird. A general term for winged creatures. Gk. vocab: eikōn (εἰκών) = image; likeness. Common English renderings: image. An important term for image, representation, or likeness. \textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: zakhar (male) (זָכַר) = male. Common English renderings: male. Adjectival/noun use meaning male sex. Heb. vocab: neqevah (נְקֵבָה) = female. Common English renderings: female. Counterpart to male in creation language.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} that, ; the light from the darkness Heb. between the light and between the darkness \textsuperscript{5} and; And the evening and the morning were Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was \textsuperscript{6} Let there, ;, ;, ; firmament Heb. expansion \textsuperscript{11} Let the; grass Heb. tender grass fruit \textsuperscript{14} Let there;, ;, ;, lights Or, rather, luminaries or light-bearers; being a different world from that rendered light, in the day from the night between the day and between the night and let \textsuperscript{16} to rule Heb. for the rule, etc.; , ; he made the stars also Or, with the stars also \textsuperscript{20} Let the waters, ; moving or, creeping, life Heb. a living soul; fowl that may fly Heb. let fowl fly, This marginal reading is more conformable to the original, and reconciles this passage with . The word fowl, from the Saxon fleon, to fly, exactly corresponds to the original, which denotes every thing that flies, whether bird or insect. open firmament Heb. face of the firmament \textsuperscript{24} Let, ;, ; Cattle, denotes domestic animals living on vegetables; - Beasts of the earth, wild animals; especially such as live on flesh; and - Creeping things, reptiles; or all the different genera of serpents, worms, and such animals as have no feet. \textsuperscript{26} Let us; man In Hebrew, Adam; probably so called either from the red earth of which he was formed, or from the blush or flesh-tint of the human countenance. The name is intended to designate the species. in our; have dominion \textsuperscript{29} I have; bearing Heb. seeding to you \textsuperscript{30} life Heb. a living soul\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 2}
\markright{GENESIS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the heavens and the earth were finished, and the whole world of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And God finished on the sixth day his works which he made, and he ceased on the seventh day from all his works which he made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because in it he ceased from all his works which God began to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} This [is] the book of the generation of heaven and earth, when they were made, in the day in which the Lord God made the heaven and the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and every herb of the field before it was on the earth, and all the grass of the field before it sprang up, for God had not rained on the earth, and there was not a man to cultivate it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But there rose a fountain out of the earth, and watered the whole face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And God formed the man [of] dust of the earth, and breathed upon his face the breath of life, and the man became a living soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And God planted a garden eastward in Edem, and placed there the man whom he had formed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God made to spring up also out of the earth every tree beautiful to the eye and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of learning the knowledge of good and evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And a river proceeds out of Edem to water the garden, thence it divides itself into four heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The name of the one, Phisom, this it is which encircles the whole land of Evilat, where there is gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the gold of that land is good, there also is carbuncle and emerald. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the name of the second river is Geon, this it is which encircles the whole land of Ethiopia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the third river is Tigris, this is that which flows forth over against the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord God took the man whom he had formed, and placed him in the garden of Delight, to cultivate and keep it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord God gave a charge to Adam, saying, Of every tree which is in the garden you may freely eat, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil—of it you⌃ shall not eat, but in whatever day you⌃ eat of it, you⌃ shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord God said, [It is] not good that the man should be alone, let us make for him a help suitable to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And God formed yet farther out of the earth all the wild beasts of the field, and all the birds of the sky, and he brought them to Adam, to see what he would call them, and whatever Adam called any living creature, that was the name of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Adam gave names to all the cattle and to all the birds of the sky, and to all the wild beasts of the field, but for Adam there was not found a help like to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And God brought a trance upon Adam, and he slept, and he took one of his ribs, and filled up the flesh instead thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And God formed the rib which he took from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Adam said, This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and shall cleave to his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: tsava (צָבָא) = army; host. Common English renderings: host; army. Used of heavenly hosts and earthly armies. \textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: shavat (שָׁבַת) = to cease; rest. Common English renderings: rest; cease. Verb behind Sabbath observance. Heb. vocab: sheva (שֶׁבַע) = seven. Common English renderings: seven. A key number associated with completion and oath language. Gk. vocab: ergon (ἔργον) = work; deed. Common English renderings: work; deed. A broad term for work, act, or deed. \textsuperscript{4} Name of God: Yahweh (יהוה) — The LORD; He is; the Self-Existent One Common English renderings: LORD. The covenant name of God, often represented in English Bibles as LORD in small capitals. Name of God: Yahweh Elohim (יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים) — LORD God Common English renderings: LORD God. Combines the covenant name with the general divine title, stressing both God’s majesty and personal covenant relation. Heb. vocab: YHWH (יהוה) = the covenant name of God. Common English renderings: LORD; Jehovah. The divine name, traditionally read as Adonai in Jewish reading practice. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: adamah (אֲדָמָה) = ground; soil; land. Common English renderings: ground; earth; land. Often thematically linked to אדם, humanity from the ground. Heb. vocab: avad (עָבַד) = to serve; work. Common English renderings: serve; work. Used for labor, service, and worship. Heb. vocab: sadeh (שָׂדֶה) = field. Common English renderings: field. Agricultural, pastoral, and burial term. Gk. vocab: agros (ἀγρός) = field. Common English renderings: field. A standard agricultural and parabolic term. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: yatsar (יָצַר) = to form; fashion. Common English renderings: form; fashion. Used of potter imagery and God’s shaping work. Heb. vocab: afar (עָפָר) = dust. Common English renderings: dust. Connected with mortality, humiliation, and creation. Gk. vocab: pnoē (πνοή) = breath; blowing. Common English renderings: breath. A term for breath or blowing, distinct from but related to πνεῦμα. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: nata (נָטַע) = to plant. Common English renderings: plant. Used literally for planting and figuratively for establishment. Heb. vocab: qedem (קֶדֶם) = east; antiquity. Common English renderings: east; ancient time. Spatial and temporal term for east or ancient past. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: daat (דַּעַת) = knowledge. Common English renderings: knowledge. Often relational and moral rather than merely informational. Heb. vocab: ra (רַע) = evil; bad. Common English renderings: evil; bad. Can denote moral evil or disaster/harm depending on context. Heb. vocab: chayyim (חַיִּים) = life. Common English renderings: life. Plural form commonly used for life as a state or gift. Heb. vocab: mar’ah (מַרְאָה) = appearance; vision. Common English renderings: vision; appearance. Can denote visible appearance or visionary sight. Gk. vocab: gnōsis (γνῶσις) = knowledge. Common English renderings: knowledge. A general term for knowledge, morally shaped by context. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: rosh (רֹאשׁ) = head; chief. Common English renderings: head; chief; beginning. Used for body part, leader, summit, or starting point. Gk. vocab: potamos (ποταμός) = river; stream. Common English renderings: river. The standard term for river or stream. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: zahav (זָהָב) = gold. Common English renderings: gold. Important for wealth, tabernacle, and idolatry polemics. Heb. vocab: shem (שֵׁם) = name. Common English renderings: name. In Hebrew thought a name often carries identity, reputation, and authority. Gk. vocab: onoma (ὄνομα) = name. Common English renderings: name. Names often carry significance of identity, character, or calling. Gk. vocab: chrysos (χρυσός) = gold. Common English renderings: gold. A standard term for gold, literal and symbolic. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: even (אָבֶן) = stone. Common English renderings: stone. Used literally and in memorial, temple, and messianic imagery. Gk. vocab: lithos (λίθος) = stone. Common English renderings: stone. The ordinary term for stone, often with building or memorial associations. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: shamar (שָׁמַר) = to keep; guard; observe. Common English renderings: keep; observe; guard. Important for covenant obedience and priestly guarding. Heb. vocab: natsar (נָצַר) = to keep; preserve. Common English renderings: keep; preserve. Often overlaps with guarding, preserving, or keeping watch. Heb. vocab: laqach (לָקַח) = to take. Common English renderings: take. Can imply receiving, seizing, marrying, or taking away. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: tsavah (צָוָה) = to command. Common English renderings: command. A key verb for divine instruction and covenant obligation. Heb. vocab: akhal (אָכַל) = to eat. Common English renderings: eat. Common verb in creation, law, fellowship, and judgment. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: mavet (מָוֶת) = death. Common English renderings: death. A central theological term in covenant sanction and mortality. Heb. vocab: mut (מוּת) = to die. Common English renderings: die. Core mortality verb, also in death-penalty formulas. Gk. vocab: thanatos (θάνατος) = death. Common English renderings: death. Used literally and theologically throughout Scripture. \textsuperscript{19} Name meaning: Adam (Adam) — Man; of the red earth First human formed from the ground; his name is literally what he was made from. Heb. vocab: shem (שֵׁם) = name. Common English renderings: name. Signifies identity, reputation, and authority. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: matsa (מָצָא) = to find. Common English renderings: find. Used for discovery, encounter, and divine favor. \textsuperscript{21} Heb. vocab: basar (בָּשָׂר) = flesh. Common English renderings: flesh; body. Used for literal flesh, kinship, and human frailty. Heb. vocab: sagar (סָגַר) = to shut. Common English renderings: shut; close. Opposite of opening; common in judgment and protection scenes. Gk. vocab: sarx (σάρξ) = flesh. Common English renderings: flesh. A major biblical term for flesh, bodily existence, and in Paul often fallen humanity. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: ishshah (אִשָּׁה) = woman; wife. Common English renderings: woman; wife. Context determines whether ‘woman’ or ‘wife’ is intended. Heb. vocab: banah (בָּנָה) = to build. Common English renderings: build. Used for building structures, dynasties, and households. Gk. vocab: gynē (γυνή) = woman; wife. Common English renderings: woman; wife. Context determines whether woman or wife is intended. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: ish (אִישׁ) = man; האיש. Common English renderings: man; husband. Can mean man in contrast to woman or husband in family setting. Heb. vocab: etsem (עֶצֶם) = bone; essence; selfsame. Common English renderings: bone; body; selfsame. Can refer literally to bone or emphatically to the selfsame day. Gk. vocab: anēr (ἀνήρ) = man; husband. Common English renderings: man; husband. Often specifically an adult male, sometimes a husband. Gk. vocab: ostoun (ὀστοῦν) = bone. Common English renderings: bone. The ordinary term for bone. \textsuperscript{24} Heb. vocab: av (אָב) = father. Common English renderings: father. Basic kinship term with broad theological and ancestral importance. Heb. vocab: em (אֵם) = mother. Common English renderings: mother. Basic family term, also used metaphorically for sources and origins. Gk. vocab: patēr (πατήρ) = father. Common English renderings: father. Used both of human fathers and of God. Gk. vocab: mētēr (μήτηρ) = mother. Common English renderings: mother. A common kinship term, literal in most occurrences.\par}

Ish \textsuperscript{24} leave; cleave; and they shall be one flesh The LXX, Vulgate, Syriac, Arabic, and Samaritan read, "they two; " as is also read in several of the Parallel Passages.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 3}
\markright{GENESIS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the two were naked, both Adam and his wife, and were not ashamed. Now the serpent was the most crafty of all the brutes on the earth, which the Lord God made, and the serpent said to the woman, Therefore has God said, Eat not of every tree of the garden? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the woman said to the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God said, You⌃ shall not eat of it, neither shall you⌃ touch it, lest you⌃ die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the serpent said to the woman, You⌃ shall not surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For God knew that in whatever day you⌃ should eat of it your eyes would be opened, and you⌃ would be as gods, knowing good and evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes to look upon and beautiful to contemplate, and having taken of its fruit she ate, and she gave to her husband also with her, and they ate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the eyes of both were opened, and they perceived that they were naked, and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons to go round them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the afternoon; and both Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God in the midst of the trees of the garden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord God called Adam and said to him, Adam, where are you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said to him, I heard your voice as you walked in the garden, and I feared because I was naked and I hid myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God said to him, Who told you that you were naked, unless you have eaten of the tree concerning which I charged you of it alone not to eat? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Adam said, The woman whom you gave to be with me—she gave me of the tree and I ate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord God said to the woman, Why have you done this? And the woman said, The serpent deceived me and I ate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord God said to the serpent, Because you have done this you are cursed above all cattle and all the brutes of the earth, on your breast and belly you shall go, and you shall eat earth all the days of your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I will put enmity between you and the woman and between your seed and her seed, he shall watch against your head, and you shall watch against his heel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And to the woman he said, I will greatly multiply your pains and your groanings; in pain you shall bring forth children, and your submission shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And to Adam he said, Because you have listened to the voice of your wife, and eaten of the tree concerning which I charged you of it only not to eat—of that you have eaten, cursed [is] the ground in your labors, in pain shall you eat of it all the days of your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to you, and you shall eat the herb of the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} In the sweat of your face shall you eat your bread until you return to the earth out of which you were taken, for earth you are and to earth you shall return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Adam called the name of his wife Life, because she was the mother of all living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And God said, Behold, Adam is become as one of us, to know good and evil, and now lest at any time he stretch forth his hand, and take of the tree of life and eat, and [so] he shall live forever— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So the Lord God sent him forth out of the garden of Delight to cultivate the ground out of which he was taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he cast out Adam and caused him to dwell over against the garden of Delight, and stationed the cherubs and the fiery sword that turns about to keep the way of the tree of life.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: nachash (נָחָשׁ) = serpent. Common English renderings: serpent. Important in Eden narrative and symbolic uses. Gk. vocab: ophis (ὄφις) = serpent. Common English renderings: serpent. The ordinary Greek term for serpent. \textsuperscript{5} Gk. vocab: ophthalmos (ὀφθαλμός) = eye. Common English renderings: eye. A major bodily term, literal and figurative. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: ayin (עַיִן) = eye; spring. Common English renderings: eye; fountain. Can mean eye literally or spring/source by metaphor. Gk. vocab: epithymia (ἐπιθυμία) = desire; craving; lust. Common English renderings: lust; desire. Can be neutral in Greek usage, but often negative in biblical moral contexts. \textsuperscript{7} Gk. vocab: phyllon (φύλλον) = leaf. Common English renderings: leaf. A standard botanical term. Gk. vocab: sykē (συκῆ) = fig tree. Common English renderings: fig tree. The fig tree is a recurring biblical image. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: shama (שָׁמַע) = to hear; obey. Common English renderings: hear; listen; obey. In covenant contexts hearing implies responsive obedience. Heb. vocab: qol (קוֹל) = voice; sound. Common English renderings: voice; sound. Used for speech, thunder, crying, and proclamation. Heb. vocab: halakh (הָלַךְ) = to walk; go. Common English renderings: walk; go. Used for literal movement and metaphorical conduct. Heb. vocab: im (עִם) = with. Common English renderings: with. Associative preposition of accompaniment. Gk. vocab: anemos (ἄνεμος) = wind. Common English renderings: wind. A natural term that also appears in vivid imagery. Gk. vocab: phōnē (φωνή) = voice; sound. Common English renderings: voice. A common biblical term for voice, sound, or utterance. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: yare (יָרֵא) = to fear; revere. Common English renderings: fear; reverence. When directed toward God often means reverent awe. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: arar (אָרַר) = to curse. Common English renderings: curse. Common verb for bringing covenantal or judicial curse. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: aqev (עָקֵב) = heel; עקב. Common English renderings: heel. Appears in the Jacob narrative by wordplay and in key texts. Gk. vocab: pous (πούς) = foot. Common English renderings: foot. Literal foot and figurative subjection both occur. Gk. vocab: kephalē (κεφαλή) = head. Common English renderings: head. Literal head and figurative leadership both occur. \textsuperscript{16} Gk. vocab: teknon (τέκνον) = child. Common English renderings: child. A general term for child, often emphasizing relationship. Gk. vocab: lypē (λύπη) = sorrow; grief. Common English renderings: sorrow. A term for grief, pain, or sorrow. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: ba’avur (בַּעֲבוּר) = for the sake of; because of. Common English renderings: for; because. Motivational/causal expression. \textsuperscript{19} Heb. vocab: lechem (לֶחֶם) = bread; food. Common English renderings: bread; food. Basic term for bread and sometimes food generally. Heb. vocab: shuv (שׁוּב) = to return; turn back. Common English renderings: return; turn. Core term for repentance, restoration, and physical return. Gk. vocab: artos (ἄρτος) = bread; loaf. Common English renderings: bread. Usually bread specifically, though sometimes food more generally. \textsuperscript{20} Name meaning: Eve (Chavah) — Living; life-giver Mother of all living; the name given after the promise of redemption. Heb. vocab: chayah (חָיָה) = to live. Common English renderings: live. Verb for life, revival, and sustaining. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: olam (עוֹלָם) = long duration; eternity. Common English renderings: ever; everlasting; world. Carries the sense of indefinite duration, ancient or future. Heb. vocab: yad (יָד) = hand. Common English renderings: hand. One of the most frequent body-part metaphors for power and agency. Heb. vocab: pen (פֶּן) = lest. Common English renderings: lest. Negative purpose particle. Gk. vocab: cheir (χείρ) = hand. Common English renderings: hand. Used literally and metaphorically for power or agency. \textsuperscript{24} Heb. vocab: derekh (דֶּרֶךְ) = way; path. Common English renderings: way; path; journey. Literal and metaphorical term for conduct and pilgrimage. Heb. vocab: keruv (כְּרוּב) = cherub. Common English renderings: cherub. Heavenly throne-associated being. Heb. vocab: shakhan (שָׁכַן) = to dwell. Common English renderings: dwell. Related to divine dwelling and the later Shekinah concept. Heb. vocab: cherev (חֶרֶב) = sword. Common English renderings: sword. A frequent war and judgment symbol. Gk. vocab: hodos (ὁδός) = way; road; path. Common English renderings: way; road. Can be literal or metaphorical for conduct or course of life.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 4}
\markright{GENESIS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and brought forth Cain and said, I have gained a man through God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And she again bore his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it was so after some time that Cain brought of the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Abel also brought of the first born of his sheep and of his fatlings, and God looked upon Abel and his gifts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} but Cain and his sacrifices he regarded not, and Cain was exceedingly sorrowful and his countenance fell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord God said to Cain, Why are you become very sorrowful and why is your countenance fallen? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Have you not sinned if you have brought it rightly, but not rightly divided it? be still, to you shall be his submission, and you shall rule over him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go out into the plain; and it came to pass that when they were in the plain Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord God said to Cain, Where is Abel your brother? and he said, I know not, am I my brother's keeper? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said, What have you done? the voice of your brother's blood cries to me out of the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now you [are] cursed from the earth which has opened her mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When you till the earth, then it shall not continue to give its strength to you: you shall be groaning and trembling on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Cain said to the Lord God, My crime [is] too great for me to be forgiven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} If you cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from your presence, and I shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth, then it will be that any one that finds me shall kill me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord God said to him, Not so, any one that slays Cain shall suffer sevenfold vengeance; and the Lord God set a mark upon Cain that no one that found him might kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So Cain went forth from the presence of God and lived in the land of Nod over against Edem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Cain knew his wife, and having conceived she bore Enoch; and he built a city; and he named the city after the name of his son, Enoch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And to Enoch was born Gaidad; and Gaidad begot Maleleel; and Maleleel begot Mathusala; and Mathusala begot Lamech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Lamech took to himself two wives; the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the second Sella. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Ada bore Jobel; he was the father of those that dwell in tents, feeding cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the name of his brother was Jubal; he it was who invented the lute and harp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Sella also bore Thobel; he was a smith, a manufacturer both of brass and iron; and the sister of Thobel was Noema. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Lamech said to his wives, Ada and Sella, Hear my voice, you⌃ wives of Lamech, consider my words, because I have slain a man to my sorrow and a youth to my grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Because vengeance has been exacted seven times on Cain's behalf, on Lamech's [it shall be] seventy times seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Seth, saying, For God has raised up to me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain killed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Seth had a son, and he called his name Enos: he hoped to call on the name of the Lord God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: Cain (Qayin) — Acquired; spear Eve said, “I have acquired a man with the help of the LORD,” but he became the first murderer. Heb. vocab: harah (הָרָה) = to conceive. Common English renderings: conceive. A key fertility and birth term. \textsuperscript{2} Name meaning: Abel (Hevel) — Breath; vanity; futility His life was short and vanished like a breath; the first martyr. Heb. vocab: tson (צֹאן) = flock; small livestock. Common English renderings: flock; sheep. Often includes sheep and goats collectively. Heb. vocab: yasaf (יָסַף) = to add; continue. Common English renderings: add; increase; again. Common auxiliary-like verb meaning continue or do again. Gk. vocab: adelphos (ἀδελφός) = brother. Common English renderings: brother. Literal sibling language often extends to fellow members of a people or community. Gk. vocab: probaton (πρόβατον) = sheep. Common English renderings: sheep. A common pastoral term used literally and figuratively. Gk. vocab: poimēn (ποιμήν) = shepherd. Common English renderings: shepherd. Used of literal shepherds and figuratively of leaders. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: minchah (מִנְחָה) = gift; grain offering; tribute. Common English renderings: offering; meat offering; present. May refer to tribute gift or cultic offering. Gk. vocab: chronos (χρόνος) = time; duration. Common English renderings: time. Usually denotes the passage or duration of time. \textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: bekhor (בְּכוֹר) = firstborn. Common English renderings: firstborn. A major inheritance and theological term. Gk. vocab: dōron (δῶρον) = gift; offering. Common English renderings: gift; offering. Can mean a present or a sacred offering. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: chatta’t (חַטָּאת) = sin; sin offering. Common English renderings: sin; sin offering. Can refer to moral failure or the offering for it. Gk. vocab: hamartia (ἁμαρτία) = sin; offense. Common English renderings: sin. The standard biblical term for sin and culpable wrongdoing. Gk. vocab: thyra (θύρα) = door. Common English renderings: door. A literal door or figurative point of access. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: qum (קוּם) = to arise; stand. Common English renderings: arise; rise up. Major verb for action, resurrection imagery, and establishment. Gk. vocab: phonos (φόνος) = murder. Common English renderings: murder. A term for homicide or murder. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: dam (דָּם) = blood. Common English renderings: blood. Associated with life, violence, atonement, and covenant. Heb. vocab: tsa’aq (צָעַק) = to cry out. Common English renderings: cry out. Often used for cries for justice or distress. Gk. vocab: haima (αἷμα) = blood. Common English renderings: blood. Important for life, sacrifice, covenant, and guilt. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: peh (פֶּה) = mouth. Common English renderings: mouth. Literal and figurative for speech or opening. Heb. vocab: patach (פָּתַח) = to open. Common English renderings: open. Used literally and metaphorically for womb, mouth, ears, heaven. Gk. vocab: stoma (στόμα) = mouth. Common English renderings: mouth. Literal mouth and figurative speech are both common. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: avon (עָוֹן) = iniquity; guilt. Common English renderings: iniquity; guilt. Often includes both the act and its culpability. Heb. vocab: nasa (נָשָׂא) = to lift; carry; bear. Common English renderings: lift up; bear; carry. Its sound closely resembles the English name NASA; this is an ironic English sound-alike only, not an etymological connection. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: yashav (יָשַׁב) = to sit; dwell. Common English renderings: sit; dwell; inhabit. Used for enthronement, settlement, and habitation. \textsuperscript{17} Name meaning: Enoch (Chanok) — Dedicated; trained; initiated Walked so closely with God he was taken without dying. Heb. vocab: ben (בֵּן) = son. Common English renderings: son; child. Can refer literally to a son or more broadly to a descendant or member. Heb. vocab: ir (עִיר) = city. Common English renderings: city. Basic urban term with major narrative and prophetic importance. Gk. vocab: huios (υἱός) = son. Common English renderings: son. Used literally and in theological or covenantal senses. Gk. vocab: polis (πόλις) = city. Common English renderings: city. The common Greek word for city. \textsuperscript{18} Name meaning: Lamech (Lamech) — Powerful; overthrower; possibly poor or despairing Father of Noah; spoke of relief from the curse, though his line also produced violence. Heb. vocab: yalad (יַלַד) = to bear; beget. Common English renderings: bear; bring forth; beget. Standard birth verb for mothers and fathers in genealogies. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: ohel (אֹהֶל) = tent. Common English renderings: tent; tabernacle. Common dwelling term; also used for sacred tent. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: nechoshet (נְחֹשֶׁת) = bronze; copper. Common English renderings: brass; bronze. Metal term often rendered ‘brass’ in older English. Heb. vocab: barzel (בַּרְזֶל) = iron. Common English renderings: iron. Associated with strength, tools, and harsh oppression. \textsuperscript{25} Name meaning: Seth (Seth) — Appointed; compensation; placed God appointed another seed instead of Abel; the chosen line continues through him. \textsuperscript{26} Name meaning: Enosh (Enosh) — Man; mortal; frail In his days men began to call upon the name of the LORD; highlights human weakness. Heb. vocab: enosh (אֱנוֹשׁ) = man; mortal. Common English renderings: man; mortal. Stresses humanness and frailty.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} knew Cain That is, gotten or acquired. I have \textsuperscript{2} Abel Heb. Hebel And Abel, ; a keeper Heb. a feeder; , tiller \textsuperscript{3} am 129, bc 3875 in process of time Heb. at the end of days, Either at the end of the year, or of the week, i.e., on the Sabbath.; the fruit \textsuperscript{4} the firstlings; flock Heb. sheep, or, goats fat had; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} If thou doest well; be accepted or, have the excellency; sin; unto thee or, subject unto thee, *marg. \textsuperscript{10} What; blood Heb. bloods crieth \textsuperscript{13} My punishment is greater than I can bear. or, Mine iniquity is greater than that it may be forgiven. \textsuperscript{14} driven; from thy; fugitive; that \textsuperscript{15} Therefore; sevenfold;, ; set a mark etc. Or, rather, "gave a sign or token to Cain, that those who found him should not kill him." \textsuperscript{16} went; Nod So called from nad, "a vagabond, " which Cain is termed in . \textsuperscript{17} Enoch, and he; the name \textsuperscript{18} am cir, 194, bc cir, 3810 Lamech \textsuperscript{20} the; father The inventor or teacher, . dwell \textsuperscript{21} am cir, 500, bc cir, 3504 father the harp \textsuperscript{23} hear; I have slain a man to my wounding or, I would slay a man in my wound, etc. to my hurt or, in my hurt \textsuperscript{25} am 130, bc 3874 and called; Seth Heb. Sheth; i. e. appointed, or put God \textsuperscript{26} am 235, bc 3769 To him Enos Heb. Enosh, to call upon the name of the Lord. or, call themselves by the name of the Lord.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 5}
\markright{GENESIS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This [is] the genealogy of men in the day in which God made Adam; in the image of God he made him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} male and female he made them, and blessed them; and he called his name Adam, in the day in which he made them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Adam lived two hundred and thirty years, and begot [a son] after his [own] form, and after his [own] image, and he called his name Seth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the days of Adam, which he lived after his begetting Seth, were seven hundred years; and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now Seth lived two hundred and five years, and begot Enos. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Seth lived after his begetting Enos, seven hundred and seven years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Enos lived one hundred and ninety years, and begot Cainan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Enos lived after his begetting Cainan, seven hundred and fifteen years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Cainan lived one hundred and seventy years, and he begot Maleleel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Cainan lived after his begetting Maleleel, seven hundred and forty years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Maleleel lived one hundred and sixty and five years, and he begot Jared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Maleleel lived after his begetting Jared, seven hundred and thirty years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And all the days of Maleleel were eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jared lived one hundred and sixty and two years, and begot Enoch: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and Jared lived after his begetting Enoch, eight hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty and two years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Enoch lived one hundred and sixty and five years, and became the father of Mathusala. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Enoch was well-pleasing to God after his begetting Mathusala, two hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty and five years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Enoch was well-pleasing to God, and was not found, because God translated him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Mathusala lived one hundred and sixty and seven years, and begot Lamech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Mathusala lived after his begetting Lamech eight hundred and two years, and begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And all the days of Mathusala which he lived, were nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Lamech lived one hundred and eighty and eight years, and begot a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he called his name Noe, saying, This one will cause us to cease from our works, and from the toils of our hands, and from the earth, which the Lord God has cursed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Lamech lived after his begetting Noe, five hundred and sixty and five years, and begot sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and fifty-three years, and he died.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: sefer (סֵפֶר) = book; scroll; document. Common English renderings: book; bill; scroll. Written record term of lasting importance. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: shanah (שָׁנָה) = year. Common English renderings: year. Basic time term, also used verbally for repetition in another stem. Heb. vocab: me’ah (מֵאָה) = hundred. Common English renderings: hundred. Common counting term in narrative and law. Gk. vocab: etos (ἔτος) = year. Common English renderings: year. A basic chronological term. \textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: bat (בַּת) = daughter. Common English renderings: daughter. Used literally and figuratively for peoples, cities, and nations. Heb. vocab: achar (אַחַר) = after; behind. Common English renderings: after. Temporal and spatial after-ness term. \textsuperscript{9} Name meaning: Kenan (Kenan) — Possession; smith; spear Continues the line; name echoes the acquired theme of the pre-flood world. \textsuperscript{12} Name meaning: Mahalalel (Mahalalel) — Praise of God; the shining one of God His very name is a shout of praise in a darkening world. \textsuperscript{15} Name meaning: Jared (Yered) — Descent; he shall come down Traditional interpretation points to descent or coming judgment. \textsuperscript{21} Name meaning: Methuselah (Methushelach) — When he dies, it shall be sent; man of the dart His death coincided with the Flood; his name is often taken as a prophecy of judgment. \textsuperscript{29} Name meaning: Noah (Noach) — Rest; comfort; relief The ark brought rest from judgment. Heb. vocab: ma’aseh (מַעֲשֶׂה) = deed; work. Common English renderings: work; deed. Used for human labor and divine acts. Heb. vocab: nacham (נָחַם) = to comfort; relent. Common English renderings: comfort; repent. Semantic range includes consolation and relenting. Heb. vocab: nechamah (נֶחָמָה) = comfort. Common English renderings: comfort. Related to consolation and relief.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} book The original word rendered "book, " signifies a register, account, history, or any kind of writing., ; in the likeness \textsuperscript{3} am 130, bc 3874 hundred The chronology differs in the Hebrew Text, the Samaritan, the LXX, and Josephus. The LXX adds 100 years to each of the patriarchs Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, and Enoch, before the birth of their sons; while they take 20 from the age of Methuselah, and add 6 to that of Lamech Thus the space from the creation to the deluge is made 2, 242 years, according to the Vatican copy, but 2, 262 by the Alexandrine; and the sum total by Josephus is 2, 265, by the Samaritan 1, 307, and the Hebrew Text, 1, 656. The sum total from the Deluge to the 70th year of Terah, according to these authorities, is, Heb. 292; Sam. 942; Sept.
