\subsection*{Genesis 6}
\markright{GENESIS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Noe was five hundred years old, and he begot three sons, Sem, Cham, and Japheth. And it came to pass when men began to be numerous upon the earth, and daughters were born to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that the sons of God having seen the daughters of men that they were beautiful, took to themselves wives of all whom they chose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord God said, My Spirit shall certainly not remain among these men for ever, because they are flesh, but their days shall be one hundred and twenty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now the giants were upon the earth in those days; and after that when the sons of God were wont to go in to the daughters of men, they bore [children] to them, those were the giants of old, the men of renown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord God, having seen that the wicked actions of men were multiplied upon the earth, and that every one in his heart was intently brooding over evil continually, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} then God laid it to heart that he had made man upon the earth, and he pondered [it] deeply. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And God said, I will blot out man whom I have made from the face of the earth, even man with cattle, and reptiles with flying creatures of the sky, for I am grieved that I have made them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But Noe found grace before the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And these [are] the generations of Noe. Noe was a just man; being perfect in his generation, Noe was well-pleasing to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Noe begot three sons, Sem, Cham, Japheth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the earth was corrupted before God, and the earth was filled with iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupted; because all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord God said to Noe, A period of all men is come before me; because the earth has been filled with iniquity by them, and, behold, I destroy them and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Make therefore for yourself an ark of square timber; you shall make the ark in compartments, and you shall pitch it within and without with pitch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And thus shall you make the ark; three hundred cubits the length of the ark, and fifty cubits the breadth, and thirty cubits the height of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall narrow the ark in making it, and in a cubit above you shall finish it, and the door of the ark you shall make on the side; with lower, second, and third stories you shall make it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And behold I bring a flood of water upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life under heaven, and whatever things are upon the earth shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall enter into the ark, and your sons and your wife, and your sons' wives with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And of all cattle and of all reptiles and of all wild beasts, even of all flesh, you shall bring by pairs of all, into the ark, that you may feed them with yourself: male and female they shall be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Of all winged birds after their kind, and of all cattle after their kind, and of all reptiles creeping upon the earth after their kind, pairs of all shall come in to you, male and female to be fed with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you shall take to yourself of all kinds of food which you⌃ eat, and you shall gather them to yourself, and it shall be for you and them to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Noe did all things whatever the Lord God commanded him, so did he.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: lev (לֵב) = heart. Common English renderings: heart. The heart in Hebrew anthropology is the center of thought, will, and desire. Heb. vocab: levav (לֵבָב) = heart. Common English renderings: heart. Poetic/full form of לב. Heb. vocab: machashavah (מַחֲשָׁבָה) = thought; plan. Common English renderings: thought; device; plan. Can denote thought, design, or intention. Gk. vocab: kardia (καρδία) = heart. Common English renderings: heart. In biblical usage the heart is the center of thought, desire, and will. Gk. vocab: dianoia (διάνοια) = mind; thought; understanding. Common English renderings: mind; understanding. Denotes thinking, understanding, or disposition. Gk. vocab: ponēria (πονηρία) = wickedness; evil. Common English renderings: wickedness. A substantive term for moral evil. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: chen (חֵן) = favor; grace. Common English renderings: grace; favor. A major term for favor graciously shown. Gk. vocab: charis (χάρις) = grace; favor. Common English renderings: grace; favor. Often denotes favor freely shown, though it can also mean thanks or graciousness. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: tsaddiq (צַדִּיק) = righteous. Common English renderings: righteous; just. Describes one who conforms to God’s standard. Heb. vocab: tamim (תָּמִים) = blameless; whole; without blemish. Common English renderings: perfect; blameless; without blemish. Used ethically of persons and physically of acceptable sacrifices. Heb. vocab: dor (דּוֹר) = generation. Common English renderings: generation. Important for genealogies, history, and covenant continuity. Gk. vocab: teleios (τέλειος) = perfect; mature; complete. Common English renderings: perfect. Can mean complete, mature, or blameless. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: shalosh (שָׁלוֹשׁ) = three. Common English renderings: three. Common numeral with symbolic and narrative significance. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: chamas (חָמָס) = violence; wrongdoing; injustice. Common English renderings: violence; wrong. Its sound closely resembles the modern name Hamas; the resemblance is striking in English, while the Hebrew word itself literally denotes violence or wrongdoing. Heb. vocab: lifnei (לִפְנֵי) = before; in the presence of. Common English renderings: before. Literally ‘to the face of’; common prepositional form. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: shachat (שָׁחַת) = to ruin; destroy; corrupt. Common English renderings: destroy; corrupt. Can refer to corruption or physical destruction. \textsuperscript{13} Gk. vocab: plērēs (πλήρης) = full. Common English renderings: full. A common adjective for fullness or completeness. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: kaphar (כָּפַר) = to cover; make atonement. Common English renderings: make atonement; purge. Cultic term underlying atonement language. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: berith (בְּרִית) = covenant. Common English renderings: covenant. One of the most important biblical terms for covenant relationship and obligation. Heb. vocab: bo (בּוֹא) = to come; enter. Common English renderings: come; go in. A highly frequent motion verb. Gk. vocab: diathēkē (διαθήκη) = covenant; testament. Common English renderings: covenant; testament. A major biblical covenant term. \textsuperscript{21} Gk. vocab: brōsis (βρῶσις) = eating; consumption; food. Common English renderings: meat; rust; eating. Can refer to food or to consumption, as context requires.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 7}
\markright{GENESIS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord God said to Noe, Enter you and all your family into the ark, for you have I seen righteous before me in this generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And of the clean cattle take in to you sevens, male and female, and of the unclean cattle pairs male and female. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And of clean flying creatures of the sky sevens, male and female, and of all unclean flying creatures pairs, male and female, to maintain seed on all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For yet seven days [having passed] I bring rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every offspring which I have made from the face of all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Noe [did] all things whatever the Lord God commanded him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Noe was six hundred years old when the flood of water was upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And then went in Noe and his sons and his wife, and his sons' wives with him into the ark, because of the water of the flood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And of clean flying creatures and of unclean flying creatures, and of clean cattle and of unclean cattle, and of all things that creep upon the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} pairs went in to Noe into the ark, male and female, as God commanded Noe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass after the seven days that the water of the flood came upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In the six hundredth year of the life of Noe, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on this day all the fountains of the abyss were broken up, and the flood-gates of heaven were opened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} On that very day entered Noe, Sem, Cham, Japheth, the sons of Noe, and the wife of Noe, and the three wives of his sons with him into the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the wild beasts after their kind, and all cattle after their kind, and every reptile moving itself on the earth after its kind, and every flying bird after its kind, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} went in to Noe into the ark, pairs, male and female of all flesh in which is the breath of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they that entered went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded Noe, and the Lord God shut the ark outside of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the flood was upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and the water abounded greatly and bore up the ark, and it was lifted on high from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the water prevailed and abounded exceedingly upon the earth, and the ark was borne upon the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the water prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains which were under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Fifteen cubits upwards was the water raised, and it covered all the high mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And there died all flesh that moved upon the earth, of flying creatures and cattle, and of wild beasts, and every reptile moving upon the earth, and every man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And all things which have the breath of life, and whatever was on the dry land, died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And [God] blotted out every offspring which was upon the face of the earth, both man and beast, and reptiles, and birds of the sky, and they were blotted out from the earth, and Noe was left alone, and those with him in the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the water was raised over the earth one hundred and fifty days.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: bayit (בַּיִת) = house; household. Common English renderings: house; household. Can mean physical house, family line, or temple. Gk. vocab: oikos (οἶκος) = house; household. Common English renderings: house; household. Can denote a building, household, or family line. \textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: tame (טָמֵא) = unclean. Common English renderings: unclean. Cultic impurity term with broad practical consequences. Heb. vocab: tahor (טָהוֹר) = clean; pure. Common English renderings: clean; pure. Cultic and moral purity term. Gk. vocab: katharos (καθαρός) = clean; pure. Common English renderings: clean; pure. Ceremonially and morally important in biblical usage. Gk. vocab: akathartos (ἀκάθαρτος) = unclean; impure. Common English renderings: unclean. The opposite of clean, used in ceremonial and moral contexts. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: chodesh (חֹדֶשׁ) = new moon; month. Common English renderings: month; new moon. The calendrical term tied to lunar cycles. Gk. vocab: pēgē (πηγή) = spring; fountain. Common English renderings: spring; fountain. A source of water; often figurative for source or origin. \textsuperscript{12} Gk. vocab: brochē (βροχή) = rain. Common English renderings: rain. Used of rainfall and divine provision or judgment. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: gavar (גָּבַר) = to prevail; be mighty. Common English renderings: prevail; be mighty. Conveys growing strength or dominance.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} every clean, ; sevens Heb. seven, seven not \textsuperscript{4} For, ; forty days, and every, destroy Heb. blot out \textsuperscript{10} after seven days or, on the seventh day, waters \textsuperscript{11} second month The first month was Tisri, which answers to the latter end of September and first half of October; the second was Marchesvan, which answers to part of October and part of November. all, ; windows or, flood-gates \textsuperscript{19} and all the high hills At the present day every mountain where search has been made, conspire in one uniform, universal proof that they all had the sea spread over their highest summits; shells, skeletons of fish, etc., having been found there. \textsuperscript{22} breath of life Heb. breath of the spirit of life \textsuperscript{23} every living substance The most incontestable evidence has been afforded of the universality of this fact. The moose deer, a native of America, has been found buried in Ireland; elephants, native of Asia and Africa, in the midst of England; crocodiles, natives of the Nile, in the heart of Germany; and shell fish, never known in any but the American seas, with the entire skeletons of whales, in the most inland counties of England.; and Noah \textsuperscript{24} compare with of this chapter, The breaking up of the fountains of the great deep, and the raining forty days and nights, had raised the waters fifteen cubits, or twenty-two feet and a half, above the highest mountain; after which forty days, it appears to have continued at this height one hundred and fifty days more.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 8}
\markright{GENESIS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And God remembered Noe, and all the wild beasts, and all the cattle, and all the birds, and all the reptiles that creep, as many as were with him in the ark, and God brought a wind upon the earth, and the water stayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the fountains of the deep were closed up, and the flood-gates of heaven, and the rain from heaven was withheld. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the water subsided, and went off the earth, and after one hundred and fifty days the water was diminished, and the ark rested in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the water continued to decrease until the tenth month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the heads of the mountains were seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass after forty days Noe opened the window of the ark which he had made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he sent forth a raven; and it went forth and returned not until the water was dried from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he sent a dove after it to see if the water had ceased from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the dove not having found rest for her feet, returned to him into the ark, because the water was on all the face of the earth, and he stretched out his hand and took her, and brought her to himself into the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove from the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the dove returned to him in the evening, and had a leaf of olive, a sprig in her mouth; and Noe knew that the water had ceased from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove, and she did not return to him again any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year of the life of Noe, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water subsided from off the earth, and Noe opened the covering of the ark which he had made, and he saw that the water had subsided from the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And in the second month the earth was dried, on the twenty-seventh day of the month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord God spoke to Noe, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Come out from the ark, you and your wife and your sons, and your sons' wives with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And all the wild beasts as many as are with you, and all flesh both of birds and beasts, and every reptile moving upon the earth, bring forth with you: and increase you⌃ and multiply upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Noe came forth, and his wife and his sons, and his sons' wives with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And all the wild beasts and all the cattle and every bird, and every reptile creeping upon the earth after their kind, came forth out of the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Noe built an altar to the Lord, and took of all clean beasts, and of all clean birds, and offered a whole burnt offering upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord God smelled a smell of sweetness, and the Lord God having considered, said, I will not any more curse the earth, because of the works of men, because the imagination of man is intently bent upon evil things from his youth, I will not therefore any more strike all living flesh as I have done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} All the days of the earth, seed and harvest, cold and heat, summer and spring, shall not cease by day or night.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: zakhar (זָכַר) = to remember. Common English renderings: remember. When God remembers, it often signals covenant action. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: chaser (חָסֵר) = to lack. Common English renderings: lack; want. Can denote deficiency or diminution. \textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: nuach (נוּחַ) = to rest; settle. Common English renderings: rest. Basis of Noah’s name in wordplay and rest theology. Gk. vocab: oros (ὄρος) = mountain; hill. Common English renderings: mountain. A common geographical term with symbolic importance. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: yonah (יוֹנָה) = dove. Common English renderings: dove; pigeon. Common in narrative symbolism and sacrificial law. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: yachal (יָחַל) = to wait; hope. Common English renderings: hope; wait. Patient expectation term in lament and trust. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: rishon (רִאשׁוֹן) = first; former. Common English renderings: first; former. Can mean first in sequence or former in time. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: dibber (דִּבֶּר) = to speak. Common English renderings: speak. Often more formal or deliberate than אמר. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: yatsa (יָצָא) = to go out. Common English renderings: go out; come out. Important in exodus, warfare, and daily movement. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: mizbeach (מִזְבֵּחַ) = altar. Common English renderings: altar. Place of sacrifice and memorial worship. Heb. vocab: olah (עֹלָה) = burnt offering. Common English renderings: burnt offering. Offering wholly consumed on the altar. Gk. vocab: thysiastērion (θυσιαστήριον) = altar. Common English renderings: altar. The standard term for altar in sacrificial contexts.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} God remembered; , ;, ; the cattle; a wind \textsuperscript{3} continually Heb. in going and returning hundred \textsuperscript{4} the ark seventh month That is, of the year, not of the deluge. Ararat is generally understood to be Armenia, as it is rendered elsewhere, in which there is a great chain of mountains, like the Alps or the Pyrenees, upon the highest part of which, called by some, "The Finger Mountain, " the ark is supposed to have rested. \textsuperscript{5} decreased continually Heb. were in going and decreasing, the tenth. \textsuperscript{7} a raven; went forth to and fro Heb. in going forth and returning \textsuperscript{9} found; and she; pulled her Heb. caused her to come \textsuperscript{14} From this, it appears, that Noah was in the ark a complete solar year, or 365 days; for he entered it on the 17th day of the 2nd month, in the 600th year of his life, and continued in it till the 27th day of the 2nd month, in the 601st year of his life, as we see above. \textsuperscript{21} smelled, ; sweet savour Heb. savour of rest curse, for or, though the imagination; neither; as I \textsuperscript{22} While the earth remaineth Heb. as yet all the days of the earth, seedtime Most of the European nations divide the year into four distinct parts, called quarters or seasons; but there are six divisions in the text, which obtained in Palestine among the Hebrews, and exist among the Arabs to the present day. According to this gracious promise, the heavenly bodies have preserved their courses, the seasons their successions, and the earth its increase for the use of man.; day\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 9}
\markright{GENESIS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And God blessed Noe and his sons, and said to them, Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and have dominion over it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the dread and the fear of you shall be upon all the wild beasts of the earth, on all the birds of the sky, and on all things moving upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea, I have placed them under your power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And every reptile which is living shall be to you for meat, I have given all things to you as the green herbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But flesh with blood of life you⌃ shall not eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For your blood of your lives will I require at the hand of all wild beasts, and I will require the life of man at the hand of [his] brother man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He that sheds man's blood, instead of that blood shall his own be shed, for in the image of God I made man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But do you⌃ increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and have dominion over it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And God spoke to Noe, and to his sons with him, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And behold I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and with every living creature with you, of birds and of beasts, and with all the wild beasts of the earth, as many as are with you, of all that come out of the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will establish my covenant with you and all flesh shall not any more die by the water of the flood, and there shall no more be a flood of water to destroy all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord God said to Noe, This [is] the sign of the covenant which I set between me and you, and between every living creature which is with you for perpetual generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of covenant between me and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it shall be when I gather clouds upon the earth, that my bow shall be seen in the cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you, and between every living soul in all flesh, and there shall no longer be water for a deluge, so as to blot out all flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And my bow shall be in the cloud, and I will look to remember the everlasting covenant between me and the earth, and between [every] living soul in all flesh, which is upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And God said to Noe, This [is] the sign of the covenant, which I have made between me and all flesh, which is upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now the sons of Noe which came out of the ark, were Sem, Cham, Japheth. And Cham was father of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} These three are the sons of Noe, of these were men scattered over all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Noe began to be a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he drank of the wine, and was drunk, and was naked in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Cham the father of Chanaan saw the nakedness of his father, and he went out and told his two brothers without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Sem and Japheth having taken a garment, put it on both their backs and went backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their face [was] backward, and they saw not the nakedness of their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Noe recovered from the wine, and knew all that his younger son had done to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he said, Cursed be the servant Chanaan, a slave shall he be to his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he said, Blessed [be] the Lord God of Sem, and Chanaan shall be his bond-servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} May God make room for Japheth, and let him dwell in the habitations of Sem, and let Chanaan be his servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Noe lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And all the days of Noe were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Gk. vocab: phobos (φόβος) = fear; terror; reverence. Common English renderings: fear. Can denote terror, fear, or reverent awe. \textsuperscript{12} Gk. vocab: aiōn (αἰών) = age; world. Common English renderings: world; age. Can denote an age, a long duration, or the world-order depending on context. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: qeshet (קֶשֶׁת) = bow. Common English renderings: bow. Weapon term and also the rainbow sign in context. \textsuperscript{16} Gk. vocab: aiōnios (αἰώνιος) = eternal; age-lasting. Common English renderings: eternal; everlasting. Often describes what belongs to the age to come or endures forever. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: Kena’an (כְּנַעַן) = Canaan. Common English renderings: Canaan. Land and people central to patriarchal promise. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: kerem (כֶּרֶם) = vineyard. Common English renderings: vineyard. Significant in blessing, judgment, and prophetic imagery. Gk. vocab: ampelos (ἄμπελος) = vine. Common English renderings: vine. A common agricultural term with rich symbolic use. \textsuperscript{21} Heb. vocab: shatah (שָׁתָה) = to drink. Common English renderings: drink. Used literally and metaphorically of imbibing wrath or wisdom. Heb. vocab: galah (גָּלָה) = to uncover; go into exile. Common English renderings: reveal; uncover; carry away. In later texts often central to exile language. Heb. vocab: yayin (יַיִן) = wine. Common English renderings: wine. Common beverage term with festal and moral associations. Heb. vocab: yatsa (יָצַע) = to spread out. Common English renderings: spread. Used literally for stretching or spreading. Gk. vocab: oinos (οἶνος) = wine. Common English renderings: wine. The ordinary term for wine. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: ketef (כֶּתֶף) = shoulder. Common English renderings: shoulder. Used literally and for bearing burdens. Gk. vocab: himation (ἱμάτιον) = garment; cloak. Common English renderings: garment; raiment. A common outer garment term. \textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: doulos (δοῦλος) = slave; servant. Common English renderings: servant; bondman. Often stronger than English servant, denoting servitude or bondage.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{11} And I; neither shall all \textsuperscript{18} Shem; Ham, Canaan Heb. Chenaan \textsuperscript{25} Cursed, ; a servant The devoted nations, which God destroyed before Israel, were descended from Canaan, and so were the Phoenicians and Carthaginians, who were at length subjugated with dreadful destruction by the Greeks and Romans. The Africans, who have been bought and sold like beasts, were also his posterity. \textsuperscript{26} Blessed; the Lord; Shem his servant or, servant to them \textsuperscript{27} enlarge or, persuade Japheth denotes enlargement, and how wonderfully have his boundaries been enlarged; for not only Europe, but Asia Minor, part of Armenia, Iberia, the whole of the vast regions of Asia north of Taurus, and probably America, fell to the share of his posterity. he shall dwell These words may mean either that God or that Japheth shall dwell in the tents of Shem. In either sense the prophecy has been literally fulfilled. dwell\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 10}
\markright{GENESIS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now these [are] the generations of the sons of Noe, Sem, Cham, Japheth; and sons were born to them after the flood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The sons of Japheth, Gamer, and Magog, and Madoi, and Jovan, and Elisa, and Thobel, and Mosoch, and Thiras. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the sons of Gamer, Aschanaz, and Riphath, and Thorgama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the sons of Jovan, Elisa, and Tharseis, Cetians, Rhodians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} From these were the islands of the Gentiles divided in their land, each according to his tongue, in their tribes and in their nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the sons of Cham, Chus, and Mesrain, Phud, and Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Chus, Saba, and Evila, and Sabatha, and Rhegma, and Sabathaca. And the sons of Rhegma, Saba, and Dadan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Chus begot Nebrod: he began to be a giant upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He was a giant hunter before the Lord God; therefore they say, As Nebrod the giant hunter before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, and Orech, and Archad, and Chalanne, in the land of Senaar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Out of that land came Assur, and built Ninevi, and the city Rhooboth, and Chalach, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and Dase between Ninevi and Chalach: this is the great city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Mesrain begot the Ludiim, and the Nephthalim, and the Enemetiim, and the Labiim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and the Patrosoniim, and the Chasmoniim (whence came forth Phylistiim) and the Gaphthoriim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Chanaan begot Sidon his firstborn, and the Chettite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and the Evite, and the Arukite, and the Asennite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the Aradian, and the Samarean, and the Amathite; and after this the tribes of the Chananites were dispersed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the boundaries of the Chananites were from Sidon till one comes to Gerara and Gaza, till one comes to Sodom and Gomorrha, Adama and Seboim, as far as Dasa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} There [were] the sons of Cham in their tribes according to their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And to Sem himself also were children born, the father of all the sons of Heber, the brother of Japheth the elder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Sons of Sem, Elam, and Assur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram, and Cainan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And sons of Aram, Uz, and Ul, and Gater, and Mosoch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Arphaxad begot Cainan, and Cainan begot Sala. And Sala begot Heber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And to Heber were born two sons, the name of the one, Phaleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother Jektan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Jektan begot Elmodad, and Saleth, and Sarmoth, and Jarach, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and Odorrha, and Aibel, and Decla, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Eval, and Abimael, and Saba, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and Uphir, and Evila, and Jobab, all these were the sons of Jektan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And their dwelling was from Masse, till one comes to Saphera, a mountain of the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} These were the sons of Sem in their tribes, according to their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} These are the tribes of the sons of Noe, according to their generations, according to their nations: of them were the islands of the Gentiles scattered over the earth after the flood.\par

May refer neutrally to nations or pejoratively to Gentiles in context. Heb. vocab: mishpachah (מִשְׁפָּחָה) = family; clan. Common English renderings: family; kindred. Gk. vocab: glōssa (γλῶσσα) = tongue; language. Common English renderings: tongue; language. Gk. vocab: basileia (βασιλεία) = kingdom; reign. Common English renderings: kingdom. Can denote a realm or the active reign of a king. \textsuperscript{21} Gk. vocab: presbyteros (πρεσβύτερος) = elder; older man. Common English renderings: elder. Can refer to age or recognized senior status.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 11}
\markright{GENESIS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the earth was one lip, and there was one language to all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass as they moved from the east, they found a plain in the land of Senaar, and they lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And a man said to his neighbor, Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire. And the brick was to them for stone, and their mortar was bitumen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they said, Come, let us build to ourselves a city and tower, whose top shall be to heaven, and let us make to ourselves a name, before we are scattered abroad upon the face of all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the sons of men built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord said, Behold, [there is] one race, and one lip of all, and they have begun to do this, and now nothing shall fail from them of all that they may have undertaken to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Come, and having gone down let us there confound their tongue, that they may not understand each the voice of his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord scattered them thence over the face of all the earth, and they left off building the city and the tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} On this account its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confounded the languages of all the earth, and thence the Lord scattered them upon the face of all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And these [are] the generations of Sem: and Sem was one hundred years old when he begot Arphaxad, the second year after the flood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Sem lived, after he had begotten Arphaxad, five hundred years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Arphaxad lived one hundred and thirty-five years, and begot Cainan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Arphaxad lived after he had begotten Cainan, four hundred years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. And Cainan lived one hundred and thirty years and begot Sala; and Canaan lived after he had begotten Sala, three hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Sala lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Heber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Sala lived after he had begotten Heber, three hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Heber lived one hundred and thirty-four years, and begot Phaleg. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Heber lived after he had begotten Phaleg two hundred and seventy years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Phaleg lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Ragau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Phaleg lived after he had begotten Ragau, two hundred and nine years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Ragau lived one hundred thirty and two years, and begot Seruch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Raau lived after he had begotten Seruch, two hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Seruch lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot Nachor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Seruch lived after he had begotten Nachor, two hundred years, and begot sons and daughters, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Nachor lived one hundred and seventy-nine years, and begot Tharrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Nachor lived after he had begotten Tharrha, one hundred and twenty-five years, and begot sons and daughters, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Tharrha lived seventy years, and begot Abram, and Nachor, and Arrhan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And these [are] the generations of Tharrha. Tharrha begot Abram and Nachor, and Arrhan; and Arrhan begot Lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Arrhan died in the presence of Tharrha his father, in the land in which he was born, in the country of the Chaldees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Abram and Nachor took to themselves wives, the name of the wife of Abram was Sara, and the name of the wife of Nachor, Malcha, daughter of Arrhan, and he was the father of Malcha, the father of Jescha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Sara was barren, and did not bear children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Tharrha took Abram his son, and Lot the son Arrhan, the son of his son, and Sara his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son, and led them forth out of the land of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Chanaan, and they came as far as Charrhan, and he lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And all the days of Tharrha in the land of Charrhan were two hundred and five years, and Tharrha died in Charrhan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: davar (דָּבָר) = word; matter; thing. Common English renderings: word; thing. A broad and important term for word, matter, event, or affair. Gk. vocab: cheilos (χείλος) = lip. Common English renderings: lip. Often used in speech and worship contexts. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: yarad (יָרַד) = to go down; descend. Common English renderings: go down. Often geographical or metaphorical descent. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: am (עַם) = people. Common English renderings: people. Often the covenant people, but also other peoples. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: chadal (חָדַל) = to cease; desist. Common English renderings: cease; leave off. Stopping or refraining term.\par}

It was of a pyramidical form, consisting of eight square towers, gradually decreasing in breadth, with a winding ascent on the outside, so very broad as to allow horses and carriages to pass each other, and even to turn. This magnificent structure is so completely destroyed that its very site is doubtful; and when supposed to be discovered, in all cases exhibiting a heap of rubbish., ; Isa. 13:1-14:32; Jer. 50:1-51:64; the face \textsuperscript{11} am 2158, bc 1846 Shem begat sons \textsuperscript{16} am 1757, bc 2247 Eber; Peleg, Phalec \textsuperscript{29} Sarai, Milcah, Iscah is called the daughter-in-law of Terah ( ), as being Abram's wife; yet Abram afterwards said, "she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother" ( ). Probably Haran was the eldest son of Terah, and Abram his youngest by another wife; and thus Sarai was the daughter, or grand-daughter of Terah, Abram's father, but not of his mother. \textsuperscript{31} am 2078, bc 1926 took, they went; Ur was probably the place called Ouri, in Mesopotamia, two days' journey from Nisibis, in the way to the river Tigris.; the land, bc cir, 1923, am cir, 2081 Haran, ; Charran\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 12}
\markright{GENESIS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Abram, Go forth out of your land and out of your kindred, and out of the house of your father, and come into the land which I will show you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you and magnify your name, and you shall be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will bless those that bless you, and curse those that curse you, and in you shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Abram went as the Lord spoke to him, and Lot departed with him, and Abram was seventy-five years old, when he went out of Charrhan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Abram took Sara his wife, and Lot the son of his brother, and all their possessions, as many as they had got, and every soul which they had got in Charrhan, and they went forth to go into the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abram traversed the land lengthwise as far as the place Sychem, to the high oak, and the Chananites then inhabited the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord appeared to Abram, and said to him, I will give this land to your seed. And Abram built an altar there to the Lord who appeared to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he departed thence to the mountain eastward of Baethel, and there he pitched his tent in Baethel near the sea, and Aggai toward the east, and there he built an altar to the Lord, and called on the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abram departed and went and encamped in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, because the famine prevailed in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass when Abram drew near to enter into Egypt, Abram said to Sara his wife, I know that you are a fair woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} It shall come to pass then that when the Egyptians shall see you, they shall say, This is his wife, and they shall kill me, but they shall save you alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Say, therefore, I am his sister, that it may be well with me on account of you, and my soul shall live because of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it came to pass when Abram entered into Egypt—the Egyptians having seen his wife that she was very beautiful— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} that the princes of Pharao saw her, and praised her to Pharao and brought her into the house of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they treated Abram well on her account, and he had sheep, and calves, and asses, and menservants, and women-servants, and mules, and camels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And God afflicted Pharao with great and severe afflictions, and his house, because of Sara, Abram's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Pharao having called Abram, said, What is this you have done to me, that you did not tell me that she was your wife? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore did you say, She is my sister? and I took her for a wife to myself; and now, behold, your wife is before you, take her and go quickly away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Pharao gave charge to men concerning Abram, to join in sending him forward, and his wife, and all that he had.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: berakhah (בְּרָכָה) = blessing. Common English renderings: blessing. Can denote bestowed favor or the spoken blessing itself. \textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: kataraomai (καταράομαι) = to curse. Common English renderings: curse. A verb of invoking or placing a curse. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: yam (יָם) = west; sea. Common English renderings: sea; west. By orientation from the land of Israel, sea can imply west. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: negev (נֶגֶב) = south; dry land. Common English renderings: south. Geographical southland region and direction. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: Mitsrayim (מִצְרַיִם) = Egypt. Common English renderings: Egypt. Major place of bondage, refuge, and redemption. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: sar (שַׂר) = prince; ruler; official. Common English renderings: prince; captain. Administrative and military title. Heb. vocab: halal (הָלַל) = to praise. Common English renderings: praise. Root behind hallelujah in later usage. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: baqar (בָּקָר) = cattle; herd. Common English renderings: cattle; oxen; herd. Can denote herd animals broadly or cattle specifically. Gk. vocab: bous (βοῦς) = ox; cow. Common English renderings: ox. Used for ox, cow, or cattle. Gk. vocab: onos (ὄνος) = donkey; ass. Common English renderings: ass; donkey. A common domestic-animal term. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: nega (נֶגַע) = affliction; plague; mark. Common English renderings: plague; sore. Wide range from disease to struck affliction.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} the souls, *marg. in and into; Canaan So called from Canaan the son of Ham, lies between the Mediterranean sea on the west, the wilderness of Paran, Idumea, and Egypt on the south, the mountains of Arabia on the east, and the mountains of Lebanon and Phoenicia on the north. Its length, from Dan to Beersheba, is about 200 miles, and its breadth, from the Mediterranean sea to its eastern borders, about 90. \textsuperscript{6} passed Sichem, ; Shechem, Sychar, Sychem plain The word rendered "plain" should be rendered "oak, " or according to Celsius, the "turpentine-tree." \subsection*{Genesis 13}
\markright{GENESIS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Abram was very rich in cattle, and silver, and gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he went [to the place] whence he came, into the wilderness as far as Baethel, as far as the place where his tent was before, between Baethel and Aggai, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} to the place of the altar, which he built there at first, and Abram there called on the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Lot who went out with Abram had sheep, and oxen, and tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the land was not large enough for them to live together, because their possessions were great; and the land was not large enough for them to live together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there was a strife between the herdmen of Abram's cattle, and the herdmen of Lot's cattle, and the Chananites and the Pherezites then inhabited the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abram said to Lot, Let there not be a strife between me and you, and between my herdmen and your herdmen, for we are brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Behold! is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me; if you [go] to the left, I will go to the right, and if you go to the right, I will go to the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Lot having lifted up his eyes, observed all the country round about Jordan, that it was all watered, before God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrha, as the garden of the Lord, and as the land of Egypt, until you come to Zogora. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Lot chose for himself all the country round Jordan, and Lot went from the east, and they were separated each from his brother. And Abram lived in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Lot lived in a city of the neighbouring people, and pitched his tent in Sodom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But the men of Sodom were evil, and exceedingly sinful before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And God said to Abram after Lot was separated from him, Look up with your eyes, and behold from the place where you now are northward and southward, and eastward and seaward; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} for all the land which you see, I will give it to you and to your seed for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And I will make your seed like the dust of the earth; if any one is able to number the dust of the earth, then shall your seed be numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Arise and traverse the land, both in the length of it and in the breadth; for to you will I give it, and to your seed for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Abram having removed his tent, came and lived by the oak of Mambre, which was in Chebrom, and he there built an altar to the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: alah (עָלָה) = to go up; ascend. Common English renderings: go up; ascend; offer. Used for movement uphill, pilgrimage, and offerings. \textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: kesef (כֶּסֶף) = silver; money. Common English renderings: silver; money. Common monetary and metal term. Gk. vocab: argyrion (ἀργύριον) = silver; money. Common English renderings: silver; money. Often refers to silver as wealth or payment. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: yakhol (יָכֹל) = to be able. Common English renderings: be able; can. Common modal verb for ability or capacity. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: riv (רִיב) = to contend; dispute. Common English renderings: strive; contend. Used in legal controversy and covenant lawsuit imagery. Gk. vocab: eris (ἔρις) = strife; contention. Common English renderings: strife. Common in vice lists and conflict descriptions. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: yamin (יָמִין) = right hand; south. Common English renderings: right hand; right. Often a symbol of strength, favor, or direction. Heb. vocab: semol (שְׂמֹאל) = left. Common English renderings: left. Directional counterpart to right. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: tsafon (צָפוֹן) = north. Common English renderings: north. Directional and symbolic term.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2086, bc 1918 the south The south of Canaan; as in leaving Egypt, it is said he "came from the south, " ( ), and the southern part of the promised land lay north-east of Egypt. \textsuperscript{3} from, Bethel and Hai i.e., The place which was afterwards called Bethel by Jacob, and so called when Moses wrote; for its first name was Luz ( ). \textsuperscript{7} a strife; Canaanite, ; dwelled i.e., They were there when Abram and Lot came to pitch their tents in the land. \textsuperscript{8} Let; brethren Heb. men brethren \textsuperscript{9} Is not, if thou wilt \textsuperscript{10} and beheld; the plain; the garden; Zoar, ; Instead of "Zoar, " which was situated at the extremity of the plain of Jordan, the Syriac reads "Zoan, " which was situated in the south of Egypt, and in a well-watered country. \textsuperscript{18} plain Heb. plains Mamre, Hebron, ; altar\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 14}
\markright{GENESIS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the reign of Amarphal king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, that Chodollogomor king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} made war with Balla king of Sodom, and with Barsa king of Gomorrha, and with Sennaar, king of Adama, and with Symobor king of Seboim and the king of Balac, this is Segor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} All these met with one consent at the salt valley; this is [now] the sea of salt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Twelve years they served Chodollogomor, and the thirteenth year they revolted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in the fourteenth year came Chodollogomor, and the kings with him, and cut to pieces the giants in Astaroth, and Carnain, and strong nations with them, and the Ommaeans in the city Save. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Chorrhaeans in the mountains of Seir, to the turpentine tree of Pharan, which is in the desert. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And having turned back they came to the well of judgment; this is Cades, and they cut in pieces all the princes of Amalec, and the Amorites dwelling in Asasonthamar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king of Sodom went out, and the king of Gomorrha, and king of Adama, and king of Seboim, and king of Balac, this is Segor, and they set themselves in array against them for war in the salt valley, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} against Chodollogomor king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations, and Amarphal king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, the four kings against the five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now the salt valley [consists of] slime-pits. And the king of Sodom fled and the king of Gomorrha, and they fell in there: and they that were left fled to the mountain country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they took all the cavalry of Sodom and Gomorrha, and all their provisions, and departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they took also Lot the son of Abram's brother, and his baggage, and departed, for he lived in Sodom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And one of them that had been rescued came and told Abram the Hebrew; and he lived by the oak of Mamre the Amorite the brother of Eschol, and the brother of Aunan, who were confederates with Abram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abram having heard that Lot his nephew had been taken captive, numbered his own home-born [servants] three hundred and eighteen, and pursued after them to Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he came upon them by night, he and his servants, and he struck them and pursued them as far as Choba, which is on the left of Damascus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he recovered all the cavalry of Sodom, and he recovered Lot his nephew, and all his possessions, and the women and the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after he returned from the slaughter of Chodollogomor, and the kings with him, to the valley of Saby; this was the plain of the kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Melchisedec king of Salem brought forth loaves and wine, and he was the priest of the most high God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he blessed Abram, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, who made heaven and earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and blessed be the most high God who delivered your enemies into your power. And Abram gave him the tithe of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king of Sodom said to Abram, Give me the men, and take the horses to yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I will stretch out my hand to the Lord the most high God, who made the heaven and the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} [that] I will not take from all your goods from a string to a shoe-latchet, lest you should say, I have made Abram rich. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Except what things the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men that went with me, Eschol, Aunan, Mambre, these shall take a portion.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: melekh (מֶלֶךְ) = king. Common English renderings: king. Central political and messianic term. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: melach (מֶלַח) = salt. Common English renderings: salt. Associated with preservation, covenant, and barrenness. Gk. vocab: halas (ἅλας) = salt. Common English renderings: salt. A common substance with covenantal and symbolic associations. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: nafal (נָפַל) = to fall. Common English renderings: fall. Used literally, militarily, and spiritually. \textsuperscript{18} Name of God: El (אֵל) — God; mighty one; strong one Common English renderings: God. A basic Semitic word for God, often appearing alone or in compound divine names and titles. Name of God: El Elyon (אֵל עֶלְיוֹן) — God Most High Common English renderings: most high God; God most high. Title emphasizing God’s absolute supremacy over heaven, earth, kings, and nations. Heb. vocab: kohen (כֹּהֵן) = priest. Common English renderings: priest. A central cultic office term. Gk. vocab: hiereus (ἱερεύς) = priest. Common English renderings: priest. The usual Greek term for priest. \textsuperscript{24} Heb. vocab: na’ar (נַעַר) = youth; servant. Common English renderings: lad; young man; servant. Flexible term ranging from child to servant or attendant.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 15}
\markright{GENESIS 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after these things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram, I shield you, your reward shall be very great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Abram said, Master [and] Lord, what will you give me? whereas I am departing without a child, but the son of Masek my home-born female slave, this Eliezer of Damascus [is my heir.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abram said, [I am grieved] since you have given me no seed, but my home-born [servant] shall succeed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And immediately there was a voice of the Lord to him, saying, This shall not be your heir; but he that shall come out of you shall be your heir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he brought him out and said to him, Look up now to heaven, and count the stars, if you shall be able to number them fully, and he said, Thus shall your seed be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abram believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said to him, I am God that brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans, so as to give you this land to inherit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said, Master [and] Lord, how shall I know that I shall inherit it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to him, Take for me an heifer in her third year, and a she-goat in her third year, and a ram in his third year, and a dove and a pigeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So he took to him all these, and divided them in the midst, and set them opposite to each other, but the birds he did not divide. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And birds came down upon the bodies, [even] upon the divided parts of them, and Abram sat down by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And about sunset a trance fell upon Abram, and behold! a great gloomy terror falls upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it was said to Abram, You shall surely know that your seed shall be a sojourner in a land not their own, and they shall enslave them, and afflict them, and humble them four hundred years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the nation whoever they shall serve I will judge; and after this, they shall come forth hither with much property. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But you shall depart to your fathers in peace, nourished in a good old age. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And in the fourth generation they shall return hither, for the sins of the Amorites are not yet filled up, even until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when the sun was about to set, there was a flame, and behold a smoking furnace and lamps of fire, which passed between these divided pieces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} In that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, To your seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The Kenites, and the Kenezites, and the Kedmoneans, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the Chettites, and the Pherezites, and the Raphaim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and the Amorites, and the Chananites, and the Evites, and the Gergesites, and the Jebusites.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name of God: Magen (מָגֵן) — Shield Common English renderings: shield. God identifies Himself as Abram’s shield, defender, and reward. Heb. vocab: magen (מָגֵן) = shield. Common English renderings: shield. A central military and theological protection image. Gk. vocab: logos (λόγος) = word; speech; matter. Common English renderings: word; saying; matter. A broad term for word, message, report, or matter. Gk. vocab: misthos (μισθός) = wages; reward. Common English renderings: reward; hire. Can refer to wages, recompense, or reward. \textsuperscript{2} Name of God: Adonai (אֲדֹנָי) — Lord; Master Common English renderings: Lord. A reverent title for God’s lordship, sovereignty, and authority. Name of God: Adonai Yahweh (אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה) — Lord GOD Common English renderings: Lord GOD. A solemn compounded form often rendered Lord GOD, especially in prophetic and covenant contexts. Heb. vocab: Adonai (אֲדֹנָי) = Lord; Master. Common English renderings: Lord. Reverential title for God, often substituting for YHWH in reading. \textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: yarash (יָרַשׁ) = to inherit; dispossess. Common English renderings: inherit; possess. Used for receiving land and driving out occupants. \textsuperscript{4} Gk. vocab: splanchnon (σπλάγχνον) = inward parts; affections. Common English renderings: bowels; inward parts. In biblical idiom the inward parts can represent deep feeling. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: nabat (נָבַט) = to look. Common English renderings: look. Often emphasizes attentive looking. Heb. vocab: safar (סָפַר) = to count; recount. Common English renderings: count; tell. Used for numbering and narrating. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: tsedaqah (צְדָקָה) = righteousness; righteous act. Common English renderings: righteousness. Often overlaps with צדק but can emphasize righteous conduct or status. Heb. vocab: aman (אָמַן) = to confirm; support; believe. Common English renderings: believe; trust; establish. Verb behind ‘amen’ and terms for faith/faithfulness. Heb. vocab: chashav (חָשַׁב) = to think; reckon; plan. Common English renderings: think; devise; account. Used for accounting, weaving skill, and planning. Heb. vocab: tsedeq (צֶדֶק) = righteousness; justice. Common English renderings: righteousness. A foundational righteousness term closely related to right order and justice. Gk. vocab: dikaiosynē (δικαιοσύνη) = righteousness; justice. Common English renderings: righteousness. A central biblical term for uprightness, justice, and right standing. Gk. vocab: pisteuō (πιστεύω) = to believe; trust. Common English renderings: believe. A central faith verb represented by its lexical form. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: ayil (אַיִל) = ram. Common English renderings: ram. Common in sacrifice and symbolic strength imagery. Heb. vocab: ez (עֵז) = goat. Common English renderings: goat. Often appears in sacrificial and pastoral contexts. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: shemesh (שֶׁמֶשׁ) = sun. Common English renderings: sun. Often associated with timekeeping and occasionally polemic against idolatry. Heb. vocab: eimah (אֵימָה) = terror. Common English renderings: terror; dread. Intense fear or horror. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: ger (גֵּר) = sojourner; resident alien. Common English renderings: stranger; sojourner. Protected outsider under Israelite law. Gk. vocab: douleia (δουλεία) = slavery; bondage. Common English renderings: bondage. The abstract noun for slavery or servitude. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: shalom (שָׁלוֹם) = peace; wholeness; well-being. Common English renderings: peace. A rich biblical term for peace, completeness, welfare, and harmony. Gk. vocab: eirēnē (εἰρήνη) = peace. Common English renderings: peace. A key biblical term for peace, wholeness, and well-being. Gk. vocab: gēras (γῆρας) = old age. Common English renderings: old age. A term for old age or advanced years. \textsuperscript{16} Gk. vocab: anomia (ἀνομία) = lawlessness; iniquity. Common English renderings: iniquity. A strong term for violation of law and moral order. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: esh (אֵשׁ) = fire. Common English renderings: fire. Used for literal fire, divine presence, judgment, and sacrifice. Gk. vocab: lampas (λαμπάς) = torch; lamp. Common English renderings: lamp; torch. A light source, often in night scenes or theophany.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 16}
\markright{GENESIS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Sara the wife of Abram bore him no children; and she had an Egyptian maid, whose name was Agar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Sara said to Abram, Behold, the Lord has restrained me from bearing, go therefore in to my maid, that I may get children for myself through her. And Abram listened to the voice of Sara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So Sara the wife of Abram having taken Agar the Egyptian her handmaid, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Chanaan, gave her to Abram her husband as a wife to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he went in to Agar, and she conceived, and saw that she was with child, and her mistress was dishonored before her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Sara said to Abram, I am injured by you; I gave my handmaid into your bosom, and when I saw that she was with child, I was dishonored before her. The Lord judge between me and you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abram said to Sara, Behold your handmaid is in your hands, use her as it may seem good to you. And Sara afflicted her, and she fled from her face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And an angel of the Lord found her by the fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Sur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Agar, Sara's maid, whence come you, and wither go you? and she said, I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the angel of the Lord said to her, I will surely multiply your seed, and it shall not be numbered for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Behold you are with child, and shall bear a son, and shall call his name Ismael, for the Lord has listened to your humiliation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He shall be a wild man, his hands against all, and the hands of all against him, and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And she called the name of the Lord God who spoke to her, You are God who sees me; for she said, For I have openly seen him that appeared to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore she called the well, The well of him whom I have openly seen; behold it is between Cades and Barad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Agar bore a son to Abram; and Abram called the name of his son which Agar bore to him, Ismael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Abram was eighty-six years old, when Agar bore Ismael to Abram.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: atsar (עָצַר) = to restrain; shut up. Common English renderings: restrain; withhold. Used for God withholding rain or womb-opening. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: shafat (שָׁפַט) = to judge; govern. Common English renderings: judge. Can refer to ruling, vindicating, or condemning. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: mal’akh (מַלְאָךְ) = messenger; angel. Common English renderings: angel; messenger. Used for human messengers and heavenly beings. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: rov (רֹב) = multitude; abundance. Common English renderings: multitude; abundance. Used for quantity, multitude, and greatness. \textsuperscript{11} Name meaning: Ishmael (Yishmael) — God hears God heard Hagar’s affliction in the wilderness. Gk. vocab: tapeinōsis (ταπείνωσις) = humiliation; low estate. Common English renderings: low estate; humiliation. Can denote humble condition, affliction, or abasement. \textsuperscript{13} Name of God: El Roi (אֵל רֳאִי) — God who sees me; God of seeing Common English renderings: God sees me. Hagar’s name for God after He saw her affliction in the wilderness.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2092, bc 1912 bare, ; Egyptian, name, Agar \textsuperscript{2} the Lord, ; obtain children Heb. be builded, ; hearkened \textsuperscript{3} am 2093, bc 1911 had gave, his \textsuperscript{6} Abram; in; as it pleaseth thee Heb. that which is good in thine eyes, dealt hardly with her. Heb. afflicted her. fled \textsuperscript{7} found the fountain; Shur The desert of Shur being between the south of Canaan, where Hebron was situated, and Egypt, it is likely that Hagar was returning to her own country. \textsuperscript{8} Sarai's maid; whence; I flee \textsuperscript{11} shalt; , Ishmael i.e. God shall hear because; hath \textsuperscript{12} be a; wild The word rendered "wild" also denotes the "wild ass; " the description of which animal in, affords the very best representation of the wandering, lawless, freebooting life of the Bedouin and other Arabs, the descendants of Ishmael. his hand he shall \textsuperscript{14} Beer-lahri-roi, That is, The well of him that liveth and seeth me., Kadesh\par}
