\subsection*{Genesis 17}
\markright{GENESIS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abram was ninety-nine years old, and the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, I am your God, be well-pleasing before me, and be blameless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abram fell upon his face, and God spoke to him, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I, behold! my covenant [is] with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And your name shall no more be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraam, for I have made you a father of many nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will increase you very exceedingly, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come out of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I will establish my covenant between you and your seed after you, to their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be your God, and [the God] of your seed after you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I will give to you and to your seed after you the land wherein you sojourn, even all the land of Chanaan for an everlasting possession, and I will be to them a God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God said to Abraam, You also shall fully keep my covenant, you and your seed after you for their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And this [is] the covenant which you shall fully keep between me and you, and between your seed after you for their generations; every male of you shall be circumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you⌃ shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between me and you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the child of eight days [old] shall be circumcised by you, every male throughout your generations, and [the servant] born in the house and he that is bought with money, of every son of a stranger, who is not of your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He that is born in your house, and he that is bought with money shall be surely circumcised, and my covenant shall be on your flesh for an everlasting covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the uncircumcised male, who shall not be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from its family, for he has broken my covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And God said to Abraam, Sara your wife—her name shall not be called Sara, Sarrha shall be her name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And I will bless her, and give you a son of her, and I will bless him, and he shall become nations, and kings of nations shall be of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abraam fell upon his face, and laughed; and spoke in his heart, saying, Shall there be a child to one who is one hundred years old, and shall Sarrha who is ninety years old, bear? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Abraam said to God, Let this Ismael live before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And God said to Abraam, Yes, behold, Sarrha your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac; and I will establish my covenant with him, for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to him and to his seed after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And concerning Ismael, behold, I have heard you, and, behold, I have blessed him, and will increase him and multiply him exceedingly; twelve nations shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarrha shall bear to you at this time, in the next year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he left off speaking with him, and God went up from Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Abraam took Ismael his son, and all his home-born [servants], and all those bought with money, and every male of the men in the house of Abraam, and he circumcised their foreskins in the time of that day, according as God spoke to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Abraam was ninety-nine years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Ismael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And at the period of that day, Abraam was circumcised, and Ismael his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and all the men of his house, both those born in the house, and those bought with money of foreign nations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name of God: El Shaddai (אֵל שַׁדַּי) — God Almighty Common English renderings: Almighty God; God Almighty. A patriarchal divine title emphasizing God’s overwhelming power and sufficiency. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: tsachaq (צָחַק) = to laugh. Common English renderings: laugh. Used for joy, disbelief, and mockery. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: nasi (נָשִׂיא) = leader; prince. Common English renderings: prince; ruler. Used for tribal leaders and prominent chiefs. \textsuperscript{23} Gk. vocab: oikia (οἰκία) = house; household. Common English renderings: house. Closely related to οἶκος, often emphasizing the dwelling.\par}

By this Abraham did not express his unbelief or weakness of faith, but his joy at the prospect of the fulfilment of so glorious a promise; and to this our Lord evidently alludes, . \textsuperscript{20} I have blessed twelve and I \textsuperscript{25} Not only the Jews, but the Arabs, who are the descendants of Ishmael, retain the rite of circumcision to this day; and the latter perform it, as the other Mahometanus also do, at the age of thirteen.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 18}
\markright{GENESIS 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And God appeared to him by the oak of Mambre, as he sat by the door of his tent at noon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold! three men stood before him; and having seen them he ran to meet them from the door of his tent, and did obeisance to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said, Lord, if indeed I have found grace in your sight, pass not by your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let water now be brought, and let them wash your feet, and do you⌃ refresh [yourselves] under the tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I will bring bread, and you⌃ shall eat, and after this you⌃ shall depart on your journey, on account of which [refreshment] you⌃ have turned aside to your servant. And he said, So do, as you have said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abraam hasted to the tent to Sarrha, and said to her, Hasten, and knead three measures of fine flour, and make cakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Abraam ran to the kine, and took a young calf, tender and good, and gave it to his servant, and he hasted to dress it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he took butter and milk, and the calf which he had dressed; and he set them before them, and they did eat, and he stood by them under the tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to him, Where is Sarrha your wife? And he answered and said, Behold! in the tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said, I will return and come to you according to this period seasonably, and Sarrha your wife shall have a son; and Sarrha heard at the door of the tent, being behind him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Abraam and Sarrha were old, advanced in days, and the custom of women ceased with Sarrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Sarrha laughed in herself, saying, The thing has not as yet happened to me, even until now, and my lord is old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord said to Abraam, Why is it that Sarrha has laughed in herself, saying, Shall I then indeed bear? but I am grown old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Shall anything be impossible with the Lord? At this time I will return to you seasonably, and Sarrha shall have a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But Sarrha denied, saying, I did not laugh, for she was afraid. And he said to her, Nay, but you did laugh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the men having risen up from thence looked towards Sodom and Gomorrha. And Abraam went with them, attending them on their journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraam my servant what things I intend to do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But Abraam shall become a great and populous nation, and in him shall all the nations of the earth be blest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For I know that he will order his sons, and his house after him, and they will keep the ways of the Lord, to do justice and judgment, that the Lord may bring upon Abraam all things whatever he has spoken to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord said, The cry of Sodom and Gomorrha has been increased towards me, and their sins are very great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I will therefore go down and see, if they completely correspond with the cry which comes to me, and if not, that I may know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the men having departed thence, came to Sodom; and Abraam was still standing before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Abraam drew near and said, Wouldest you destroy the righteous with the wicked, and shall the righteous be as the wicked? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Should there be fifty righteous in the city, will you destroy them? will you not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they be in it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} By no means shall you do as this thing [is] so as to destroy the righteous with the wicked, so the righteous shall be as the wicked: by no means. You that judge the whole earth, shall you not do right? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Lord said, If there should be in Sodom fifty righteous in the city, I will spare the whole city, and the whole place for their sakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Abraam answered and said, Now I have begun to speak to my Lord, and I am earth and ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if the fifty righteous should be diminished to forty-five, will you destroy the whole city because of the five [lacking]? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I should find there forty-five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he continued to speak to him still, and said, But if there should be found there forty? And he said, I will not destroy it for the forty's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he said, Will there be anything [against me], Lord, if I shall speak? but if there be found there thirty? And he said, I will not destroy it for the thirty's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said, Since I am able to speak to the Lord, what if there should be found there twenty? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I should find there twenty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he said, Will there be anything [against me], Lord, if I speak yet once? but if there should be found there ten? And he said, I will not destroy it for the ten's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the Lord departed, when he left off speaking to Abraam, and Abraam returned to his place.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: hishtachavah (הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה) = to bow down; worship. Common English renderings: worship; bow down. A physical act of prostration often expressing worship. Heb. vocab: yatsav (יָצַב) = to stand firm; station oneself. Common English renderings: stand; set. Often for positioning oneself or something. Gk. vocab: proskyneō (προσκυνέω) = to worship; bow down. Common English renderings: worship. The standard biblical verb for bowing down or worshiping. \textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: kyrios (κύριος) = lord; master. Common English renderings: Lord; lord; master. This lemma can denote a human master or the divine title, depending on context. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: sa’ad (סָעַד) = to support; sustain. Common English renderings: stay; sustain. Often of sustaining with food or divine support. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: par (פַּר) = bull. Common English renderings: bullock; bull. Frequent in sacrificial legislation. Gk. vocab: moschos (μόσχος) = calf. Common English renderings: calf. A common sacrificial and pastoral term. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: chalav (חָלָב) = milk. Common English renderings: milk. A staple food and symbol of abundance. Heb. vocab: amad (עָמַד) = to stand. Common English renderings: stand. Standing implies readiness, endurance, or appearance before God. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: orach (אֹרַח) = path; way. Common English renderings: path. Often poetic synonym for דרך. Heb. vocab: zaqen (זָקֵן) = old; elder. Common English renderings: old; elder. Can denote age or community leadership. \textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: kairos (καιρός) = appointed time; season. Common English renderings: time; season. Often signifies a fitting, appointed, or decisive time. Gk. vocab: rhēma (ῥῆμα) = word; saying; utterance. Common English renderings: word; saying. Often denotes a spoken word or specific utterance. \textsuperscript{19} Heb. vocab: mishpat (מִשְׁפָּט) = judgment; justice; ordinance. Common English renderings: judgment; justice. A central legal and ethical term for judgment, justice, and due order. \textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: kaved (כָּבֵד) = heavy; weighty; honored. Common English renderings: heavy; grievous; weighty. Its sound resembles the English word caved; this is a sound coincidence only, while the Hebrew root conveys heaviness, severity, or honor depending on context. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: panah (פָּנָה) = to turn. Common English renderings: turn. Literal and figurative turning term. \textsuperscript{25} Heb. vocab: shofet (שֹׁפֵט) = judge. Common English renderings: judge. Both judicial official and, in context, God as judge. Gk. vocab: krisis (κρίσις) = judgment; decision. Common English renderings: judgment. Can denote judicial process, decision, or judgment. \textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: anah (עָנָה) = to answer; respond. Common English renderings: answer. One of several roots spelled this way; this one means respond. \textsuperscript{32} Heb. vocab: eser (עֶשֶׂר) = ten. Common English renderings: ten. Basic numeral, also associated with completeness and commandments.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} appeared, ; Mamre, and he sat In these verses we have a delightful picture of genuine and primitive hospitality. A venerable father sits at the tent door, not only to enjoy the current of refreshing air, but that if he saw any weary and exhausted travellers, he might invite them to rest and refresh themselves during the heat of the day, and the same custom still continues in the east. It was not the custom, nor was there any necessity, for strangers to knock at the door, or to speak first, but to stand till they were invited. \textsuperscript{2} And he; three; he ran bowed \textsuperscript{4} wash your feet In those ancient times, shoes such as ours, were not in use; and the foot was protected only with sandals or soles, fastened round the foot with straps. It was, therefore, not only necessary from motives of cleanliness, but also a very great refreshment, in so hot a country, to get the feet washed at the end of a day's journey; and this is the first thing that Abraham proposes., ; tree Rest in the shade was the second requisite for the refreshment of a weary traveller. \textsuperscript{5} And I; bread This was the third requisite, and is introduced in its proper order; as eating immediately after exertion or fatigue is very unwholesome. comfort Heb. stay; are ye come Heb. ye have passed \textsuperscript{6} Make ready quickly Heb. hasten three \textsuperscript{8} he took; stood; and they \textsuperscript{19} For I; command;, ; that the \textsuperscript{21} I will go down This is spoken figuratively; and as the Jewish writers speak, according to the language of men. So eyes, ears, hands, and other members of the body are attributed to God, for effecting those things which men cannot accomplish without these members.; see; I will know \textsuperscript{22} the men, stood The two, whom we suppose to have been created angels, departed at this time; and accordingly two entered Sodom at evening: while the one, called Jehovah throughout the chapter, continued with Abraham, who "stood yet before the Lord." - Scott. \textsuperscript{25} be far that the; Shall;, ; Judge\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 19}
\markright{GENESIS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the two angels came to Sodom at evening. And Lot sat by the gate of Sodom, and Lot having seen them, rose up to meet them, and he worshipped with his face to the ground, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold! [my] lords, turn aside to the house of your servant, and rest from your journey, and wash your feet, and having risen early in the morning you⌃ shall depart on your journey. And they said, Nay, but we will lodge in the street. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he constrained them, and they turned aside to him, and they entered into his house, and he made a feast for them, and baked unleavened cakes for them, and they did eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But before they went to sleep, the men of the city, the Sodomites, compassed the house, both young and old, all the people together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they called out Lot, and said to him, Where are the men that went in to you this night? bring them out to us that we may be with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Lot went out to them to the porch, and he shut the door after him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and said to them, By no means, brethren, do not act villanously. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But I have two daughters, who have not known a man. I will bring them out to you, and do you⌃ use them as it may please you, only do not injury to these men, to avoid which they came under the shelter of my roof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they said to him, Stand back there, you came in to sojourn, was it also to judge? Now then we would harm you more than them. And they pressed hard on the man, even Lot, and they drew near to break the door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the men stretched forth their hands and drew Lot in to them into the house, and shut the door of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they struck the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, and they were wearied with seeking the door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the men said to Lot, Have you here sons-in-law, or sons or daughters, or if you have any other friend in the city, bring them out of this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For we are going to destroy this place; for their cry has been raised up before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law who had married his daughters, and said, Rise up, and depart out of this place, for the Lord is about to destroy the city; but he seemed to be speaking absurdly before his sons-in-law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But when it was morning, the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise and take your wife, and your two daughters whom you have, and go forth; lest you also be destroyed with the iniquities of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they were troubled, and the angels laid hold on his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, in that the Lord spared him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass when they brought them out, that they said, Save your own life by all means; look not round to that which is behind, nor stay in all the country round about, escape to the mountain, lest perhaps you be overtaken together with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Lot said to them, I pray, Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} since your servant has found mercy before you, and you have magnified your righteousness, in what you do towards me that my soul may live, —but I shall not be able to escape to the mountain, lest perhaps the calamity overtake me and I die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Behold this city is near for me to escape there, which is a small one, and there shall I be preserved, is it not little? and my soul shall live because of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said to him, Behold, I have had respect to you also about this thing, that I should not overthrow the city about which you have spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Hasten therefore to escape there, for I shall not be able to do anything until you are come there; therefore he called the name of that city, Segor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The sun was risen upon the earth, when Lot entered into Segor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Lord rained on Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he overthrew these cities, and all the country round about, and all that lived in the cities, and the plants springing out of the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And his wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Abraam rose up early to go to the place, where he had stood before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he looked towards Sodom and Gomorrha, and towards the surrounding country, and saw, and behold a flame went up from the earth, as the smoke of a furnace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it came to pass that when God destroyed all the cities of the region round about, God remembered Abraam, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew those cities in which Lot lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Lot went up out of Segor, and lived in the mountain, he and his two daughters with him, for he feared to dwell in Segor; and he lived in a cave, he and his two daughters with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the elder said to the younger, Our father is old, and there is no one on the earth who shall come in to us, as it is fit in all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Come and let us make our father drink wine, and let us sleep with him, and let us raise up seed from our father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} So they made their father drink wine in that night, and the elder went in and lay with her father that night, and he knew not when he slept and when he rose up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And it came to pass on the morrow, that the elder said to the younger, Behold, I slept yesternight with our father, let us make him drink wine in this night also, and do you go in and sleep with him, and let us raise up seed of our father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} So they made their father drink wine in that night also, and the younger went in and slept with her father, and he knew not when he slept, nor when he arose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the two daughters of Lot conceived by their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the elder bore a son and called his name Moab, saying, [He is] of my father. This is the father of the Moabites to this present day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the younger also bore a son, and called his name Amman, saying, The son of my family. This is the father of the Ammanites to this present day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: sha’ar (שַׁעַר) = gate. Common English renderings: gate. Important for city life, judgment, and public authority. \textsuperscript{8} Gk. vocab: skia (σκιά) = shadow. Common English renderings: shadow. Used literally and figuratively for shelter or transience. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: yaga (יָגַע) = to toil; grow weary. Common English renderings: labor; weary. Used for fatigue and fruitless struggle. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: avad (אָבַד) = to perish; destroy. Common English renderings: perish; destroy. A key judgment and loss term. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: chazaq (חָזַק) = to be strong; strengthen. Common English renderings: be strong; strengthen. Used for courage, force, and hardened resolve. \textsuperscript{19} Heb. vocab: chesed (חֶסֶד) = steadfast love; covenant mercy; lovingkindness. Common English renderings: mercy; lovingkindness. A major covenant term for loyal love, mercy, and faithful kindness. Gk. vocab: eleos (ἔλεος) = mercy; compassion. Common English renderings: mercy. Frequently used of divine mercy and covenant compassion. Gk. vocab: sōzō (σῴζω) = to save; rescue. Common English renderings: save. A central salvation verb represented by its lexical form. \textsuperscript{24} Gk. vocab: pyr (πῦρ) = fire. Common English renderings: fire. Used literally and often symbolically for judgment or purification.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And there came two angels. Or, rather, "the two angels came, " referring to those mentioned in the preceding chapter, and there called "men." It seems (from ), that these two angels were sent to Sodom, while the third, who was the Lord or Jehovah, remained with Abraham., rose; bowed \textsuperscript{2} turn wash Nay Instead of lo, nay, some manuscripts have lo, to him. "And they said unto him, for we lodge in the street; " where, nevertheless, the negation is understood. Knowing the disposition of the inhabitants, and appearing in the character of mere travellers, they preferred the open street to any house; but not yet willing to make themselves known, as Lot pressed them vehemently, and as they knew him to be a righteous man, they consented to take shelter under his hospitable roof. \textsuperscript{6} Lot door Two words are here used for door. The first pethach, which is the door-way, at which Lot went out; the latter, deleth, the leaf of the door, which he shut after him when out. \textsuperscript{11} with blindness The word sanverim, rendered "blindness, " and which occurs only here, and in, is supposed to denote dazzlings, deceptions, or confusions of sight from excessive light; being derived by Schultens, who is followed by Parkhurst, from the Arabic sana, to pour forth, diffuse, and nor, light. Dr. Geddes, to the same purpose, thinks it is compounded of the Arabic sana, which signifies a flash, and or, light. The Targums, in both places where it occurs, render it by eruptions, or flashes of light, or as Mercer, in Robertson, explains the Chaldee word, irradiations.; that they \textsuperscript{15} hastened; are here Heb. are found iniquity or, punishment \textsuperscript{21} I; thee Heb. thy face that \textsuperscript{22} for; called; Zoar i.e. little \textsuperscript{24} the Lord; brimstone The word rendered "brimstone, " (q.d. brennestone, or brinnestone, id est burning-stone), is always rendered by the LXX "sulphur, " and seems to denote a meteorous inflammable matter. \textsuperscript{26} looked This unhappy woman, says the Rev. T. Scott, "looked back, " contrary to God's express command, perhaps with a hope of returning, which latter supposition is favoured by our Lord's words, "Let him not return back. Remember Lot's wife." She was, therefore, instantaneously struck dead and petrified, and thus remained to after ages a visible monument of the Divine displeasure.; and \textsuperscript{37} am 2108, bc 1896 Moab This name is generally interpreted of the father; from mo, of, and av, a father. Moabites \textsuperscript{38} Benammi i.e., Son of my people, from ben, a son, and ammi, my people. children\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 20}
\markright{GENESIS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abraam removed thence to the southern country, and lived between Cades and Sur, and sojourned in Gerara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Abraam said concerning Sarrha his wife, She is my sister, for he feared to say, She is my wife, lest at any time the men of the city should kill him for her sake. So Abimelech king of Gerara sent and took Sarrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And God came to Abimelech by night in sleep, and said, Behold, you die for the woman, whom you have taken, whereas she has lived with a husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But Abimelech had not touched her, and he said, Lord, will you destroy an ignorantly [sinning] and just nation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Said he not to me, She is my sister, and said she not to me, He is my brother? with a pure heart and in the righteousness of my hands have I done this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And God said to him in sleep, Yes, I knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I spared you, so that you should not sin against me, therefore I suffered you not to touch her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But now return the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and shall pray for you, and you shall live; but if you restore her not, know that you shall die and all your. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and he spoke all these words in their ears, and all the men feared exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abimelech called Abraam and said to him, What is this that you have done to us? Have we sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me a deed, which no one ought to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abimelech said to Abraam, What have you seen in [me] that you have done this? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Abraam said, Why I said, Surely there is not the worship of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For truly she is my sister by my father, but not by my mother, and she became my wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass when God brought me forth out of the house of my father, that I said to her, This righteousness you shall perform to me, in every place into which we may enter, say of me, He is my brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abimelech took a thousand pieces of silver, and sheep, and calves, and servants, and maidservants, and gave them to Abraam, and he returned him Sarrha his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Abimelech said to Abraam, Behold, my land is before you, dwell wherever it may please you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And to Sarrha he said, Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver, those shall be to you for the price of your countenance, and to all the women with you, and speak the truth in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abraam prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his women servants, and they bore children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Because the Lord had fast closed from without every womb in the house of Abimelech, because of Sarrha Abraam's wife.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: chalam (חָלַם) = to dream. Common English renderings: dream. Used for revelatory and ordinary dreams. Heb. vocab: chalom (חֲלוֹם) = dream. Common English renderings: dream. Noun form for dreams, often revelatory in Genesis. \textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: tom (תֹּם) = integrity; completeness. Common English renderings: integrity; perfection. Often paired with moral blamelessness. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: chata (חָטָא) = to sin; miss the mark. Common English renderings: sin. Basic verb of sin and guilt. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: navi (נָבִיא) = prophet. Common English renderings: prophet. One called to speak God’s message. Heb. vocab: palal (פָּלַל) = to pray; intercede. Common English renderings: pray. Verb behind prayer, often intercessory. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: ozen (אֹזֶן) = ear. Common English renderings: ear. Hearing organ and metaphor for obedience. Gk. vocab: ous (οὖς) = ear. Common English renderings: ear. A term for hearing, obedience, and attention. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: yirah (יִרְאָה) = fear; reverence. Common English renderings: fear; reverence. Often expresses the fear of the LORD as covenantal devotion. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: elef (אֶלֶף) = thousand; clan unit. Common English renderings: thousand. Can mean literal thousand or a social unit depending on context. Heb. vocab: hokhiach (הוֹכִיחַ) = to reprove; decide; correct. Common English renderings: reprove; rebuke. Legal and wisdom term for correction or deciding. Heb. vocab: tsaraf (צָרַף) = to refine; smelt. Common English renderings: refine; try. Used for metals and metaphorically for tested words or people. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: rapha (רָפָא) = to heal. Common English renderings: heal. Used physically, spiritually, and nationally. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: rechem (רֶחֶם) = womb. Common English renderings: womb. Source imagery behind compassion terms.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am cir, 2107, bc cir, 1897 from, Kadesh, ; Gerar was a city of Arabia Petrea, under a king of the Philistines, 25 miles from Eleutheropolis beyond Daroma, in the south of Judah. From, it appears to have been situated in the angle where the south and west sides of Canaan met, and to have been not far from Gaza. Jerome, in his Hebrew Traditions on Genesis, says, from Gerar to Jerusalem was three days' journey. There was a wood near Gerar, spoken of by Theodoret; and a brook ( ), on which was a monastery, noticed by Sozomen. \textsuperscript{3} a dream, ; a dead; a man's wife Heb. married to an husband \textsuperscript{5} in the integrity or, simplicity, or sincerity; and innocency \textsuperscript{7} a prophet The word navi, rendered a prophet, not only signifies one who foretell future events, but also an intercessor, instructor. See note on; see note on; and see note on . The title was also given to men eminent for eloquence and literary abilities. Hence Aaron, because he was the spokesman of Moses to the Egyptian king, is called a prophet., ; pray;, ; surely, ; all \textsuperscript{9} What hast; a great; ought \textsuperscript{12} And yet; she is the Ebn Batrik, in his annals, among other ancient traditions, has preserved the following: "Terah first married Yona, by whom he had Abraham; afterwards he married Tehevita, by whom he had Sarah." \textsuperscript{15} my land, where it pleaseth thee Heb. as is good in thine eyes \textsuperscript{16} thy; thousand What these pieces were is not certain; but it is probable they were shekels, as it is so understood by the Targum; and the LXX render it didrachma, by which the Hebrew shekel is rendered in . behold Or, "behold IT (the 1, 000 shekels) is to thee, " etc. a covering thus\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 21}
\markright{GENESIS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord visited Sarrha, as he said, and the Lord did to Sarrha, as he spoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And she conceived and bore to Abraam a son in old age, at the set time according as the Lord spoke to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abraam called the name of his son that was born to him, whom Sarrha bore to him, Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Abraam circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, as God commanded him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Abraam was one hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Sarrha said, The Lord has made laughter for me, for whoever shall hear shall rejoice with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And she said, Who shall say to Abraam that Sarrha suckles a child? for I have born a child in my old age. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraam made a great feast the day that his son Isaac was weaned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Sarrha having seen the son of Agar the Egyptian who was born to Abraam, sporting with Isaac her son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} then she said to Abraam, Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the word appeared very hard before Abraam concerning his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But God said to Abraam, Let it not be hard before you concerning the child, and concerning the bondwoman; in all things whatever Sarrha shall say to you, hear her voice, for in Isaac shall your seed be called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And moreover I will make the son of this bondwoman a great nation, because he is your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abraam rose up in the morning and took loaves and a skin of water, and gave [them] to Agar, and he put the child on her shoulder, and sent her away, and she having departed wandered in the wilderness near the well of the oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the water failed out of the skin, and she cast the child under a fir tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And she departed and sat down opposite him at a distance, as it were a bow-shot, for she said, Surely I can’t see the death of my child: and she sat opposite him, and the child cried aloud and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And God heard the voice of the child from the place where he was, and an angel of God called Agar out of heaven, and said to her, What is it, Agar? fear not, for God has heard the voice of the child from the place where he is. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Rise up, and take the child, and hold him in your hand, for I will make him a great nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of springing water; and she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the child drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And God was with the child, and he grew and lived in the wilderness, and became an archer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he lived in the wilderness, and his mother took him a wife out of Pharan of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it came to pass at that time that Abimelech spoke, and Ochozath his friend, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, to Abraam, saying, God is with you in all things, whatever you may do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now therefore swear to me by God that you will not injure me, nor my seed, nor my name, but according to the righteousness which I have performed with you you shall deal with me, and with the land in which you have sojourned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Abraam said, I will swear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Abraam reproved Abimelech because of the wells of water, which the servants of Abimelech took away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Abimelech said to him, I know not who has done this thing to you, neither did you tell it me, neither heard I it but only today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Abraam took sheep and calves, and gave them to Abimelech, and both made a covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Abraam set seven ewe-lambs by themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Abimelech said to Abraam, What are these seven ewe-lambs which you have set alone? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Abraam said, You shall receive the seven ewe-lambs of me, that they may be for me as a witness, that I dug this well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Therefore he named the name of that place, The Well of the Oath, for there they both swore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they made a covenant at the well of the oath. And there rose up Abimelech, Ochozath his friend, and Phichol the commander-in-chief of his army, and they returned to the land of the Phylistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Abraam planted a field at the well of the oath, and called there on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Abraam sojourned in the land of the Phylistines many days.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: paqad (פָּקַד) = to attend; appoint; visit. Common English renderings: visit; appoint; number. Context determines whether for blessing, judgment, or administration. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: yeled (יַלֶד) = child; boy. Common English renderings: child; lad. General term for a child or youth. \textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: planaō (πλανάω) = to lead astray; wander. Common English renderings: err. A common biblical verb of wandering or deception. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: tsame (צָמֵא) = to thirst. Common English renderings: thirst. Expresses physical thirst and spiritual longing. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: bakhah (בָּכָה) = to weep. Common English renderings: weep; cry. Common verb of grief and intense feeling. Heb. vocab: chets (חֵץ) = arrow. Common English renderings: arrow. Projectile term also used metaphorically. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: shava (שָׁבַע) = to swear. Common English renderings: swear. Related by wordplay to the number seven in some contexts. \textsuperscript{25} Heb. vocab: gazal (גָּזַל) = to rob; plunder. Common English renderings: rob; spoil. Can refer to theft, seizure, or violent taking. \textsuperscript{30} Heb. vocab: ed (עֵד) = witness. Common English renderings: witness. Legal and covenantal term for one who bears testimony. Gk. vocab: martyrion (μαρτύριον) = testimony; witness. Common English renderings: testimony. Closely related to μαρτυρία, often referring to the thing testified. \textsuperscript{33} Name of God: El Olam (אֵל עוֹלָם) — Everlasting God Common English renderings: everlasting God. Highlights God’s eternal nature and enduring covenant faithfulness.\par}

Alluding to the seven ewe lambs. The verb rendered "to swear" is derived from the word translated seven. \textsuperscript{33} grove or, tree; The original word eshel, has been variously translated a grove, a plantation, an orchard, a cultivated field, and an oak; but it may denote a kind of tamarisk, as it is rendered by Gesenius, the same with the Arabic athl . Beersheba; called, on the name Dr. Shuckford justly contends, that the expression rendered, "he called on the name, " signifies "he invoked in the name." everlasting\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 22}
\markright{GENESIS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after these things that God tempted Abraam, and said to him, Abraam, Abraam; and he said, Behold! I [am here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said, Take your son, the beloved one, whom you have loved—Isaac, and go into the high land, and offer him there for a whole burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abraam rose up in the morning and saddled his ass, and he took with him two servants, and Isaac his son, and having split wood for a whole burnt offering, he arose and departed, and came to the place of which God spoke to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} on the third day; and Abraam having lifted up his eyes, saw the place afar off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Abraam said to his servants, Sit you⌃ here with the ass, and I and the lad will proceed thus far, and having worshipped we will return to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abraam took the wood of the whole burnt offering, and laid it on Isaac his son, and he took into his hands both the fire and the knife, and the two went together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Isaac said to Abraam his father, Father. And he said, What is it, son? And he said, Behold the fire and the wood, where is the sheep for a whole burnt offering? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abraam said, God will provide himself a sheep for a whole burnt offering, [my] son. And both having gone together, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} came to the place which God spoke of to him; and there Abraam built the altar, and laid the wood on it, and having bound the feet of Isaac his son together, he laid him on the altar upon the wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abraam stretched forth his hand to take the knife to kill his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And an angel of the Lord called him out of heaven, and said, Abraam, Abraam. And he said, Behold, I [am here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, Lay not your hand upon the child, neither do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, and for my sake you have not spared your beloved son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Abraam lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold! a ram caught by his horns in a plant of Sabec; and Abraam went and took the ram, and offered him up for a whole burnt offering in the place of Isaac his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abraam called the name of that place, The Lord has seen; that they might say today, In the mount the Lord was seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And an angel of the Lord called Abraam the second time out of heaven, saying, I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, because you have done this thing, and on my account have not spared your beloved son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand which is by the shore of the sea, and your seed shall inherit the cities of their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And in your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because you have listened to my voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Abraam returned to his servants, and they arose and went together to the well of the oath; and Abraam lived at the well of the oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass after these things, that it was reported to Abraam, saying, Behold, Melcha herself too has born sons to Nachor your brother, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Uz the firstborn, and Baux his brother, and Camuel the father of the Syrians, and Chazad, and {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Azav and Phaldes, and Jeldaph, and Bathuel, and Bathuel begot Rebecca; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} these are eight sons, which Melcha bore to Nachor the brother of Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And his concubine whose name was Rheuma, she also bore Tabec, and Taam, and Tochos, and Mocha.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: nasah (נָסָה) = to test; try. Common English renderings: tempt; prove; test. Used of divine testing and human tempting. \textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: ahav (אָהַב) = to love. Common English renderings: love. A central verb for divine and human love. Gk. vocab: agapaō (ἀγαπάω) = to love. Common English renderings: love. A foundational verb for love, represented by its lexical form. \textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: neanias (νεανίας) = young man. Common English renderings: young man. Denotes a younger male. \textsuperscript{6} Gk. vocab: machaira (μάχαιρα) = sword; knife. Common English renderings: sword. A blade term used literally and figuratively. \textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: seh (שֶׂה) = small livestock animal. Common English renderings: lamb; kid. Generic term often clarified by context as sheep or goat. Gk. vocab: amnos (ἀμνός) = lamb. Common English renderings: lamb. A sacrificial lamb term of major theological importance. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: yare (יָרֵא) = to fear; revere. Common English renderings: fear; reverence. A covenantally important verb for fear, awe, and reverent obedience. \textsuperscript{14} Name of God: Yahweh Yireh (יְהוָה יִרְאֶה) — The LORD will provide; The LORD will see Common English renderings: The LORD will provide. Abraham’s memorial name after God provided the ram in Isaac’s place. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: chol (חוֹל) = sand. Common English renderings: sand. Image for innumerable descendants. \textsuperscript{18} Gk. vocab: hypakoē (ὑπακοή) = obedience. Common English renderings: obedience. A noun for hearing under, hence obedience.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2132, bc 1872, Jos, Ant God; tempt Or prove, or try, as tempt, from tento, originally signified. Behold, here I am Heb. Behold me \textsuperscript{7} My father; Here am I Heb. Behold me, but, lamb or, kid \textsuperscript{14} called, ; Jehovahjireh i.e. The Lord will see, or provide, ; In; it shall be seen "In the mount of the Lord it shall be provided." The meaning is, that God, in the greatest difficulties, when all human assistance is vain, will make a suitable provision for the deliverance of those who trust in Him. \textsuperscript{17} in blessing, ; I will multiply, ; shore Heb. lip, thy seed; Josh. 1:1-10:43 \textsuperscript{20} am 2142, bc 1862 told Milcah, Nahor \textsuperscript{21} Huz, Uz Buz Kemuel might have given name to the Kamilites, a people of Syria, mentioned by Strabo, to the west of the Euphrates. Aram Syrians; *title\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 23}
\markright{GENESIS 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the life of Sarrha was one hundred and twenty-seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Sarrha died in the city of Arboc, which is in the valley, this is Chebron in the land of Chanaan; and Abraam came to lament for Sarrha and to mourn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abraam stood up from before his dead; and Abraam spoke to the sons of Chet, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I am a sojourner and a stranger among you, give me therefore possession of a burying-place among you, and I will bury my dead away from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sons of Chet answered to Abraam, saying, Not so, Sir, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} but hear us; you are in the midst of us a king from God; bury your dead in our choice sepulchres, for not one of us will by any means withhold his sepulchre from you, so that you should not bury your dead there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Abraam rose up and did obeisance to the people of the land, to the sons of Chet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abraam spoke to them, saying, If you⌃ have it in your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me, and speak for me to Ephron the son Saar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let him give me the double cave which he has, which is in a part of his field, let him give it me for the money it is worth for possession of a burying-place among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now Ephron was sitting in the midst of the children of Chet, and Ephron the Chettite answered Abraam and spoke in the hearing of the sons of Chet, and of all who entered the city, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Attend to me, my lord, and hear me, I give to you the field and the cave which is in it; I have given it you before all my country men; bury your dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Abraam did obeisance before the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said in the ears of Ephron before the people of the land, Since you are on my side, hear me; take the price of the field from me, and I will bury my dead there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But Ephron answered Abraam, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Nay, my lord, I have heard indeed, the land [is worth] four hundred silver didrachmas, but what can this be between me and you? nay, do you bury your dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Abraam listened to Ephron, and Abraam rendered to Ephron the money, which he mentioned in the ears of the sons of Chet, four hundred didrachmas of silver approved with merchants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the field of Ephron, which was in Double Cave, which is opposite Mambre, the field and the cave, which was in it, and every tree which was in the field, and whatever is in its borders round about, were made sure in its borders round about, were made sure {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} to Abraam for a possession, before the sons of Chet, and all that entered into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} After this Abraam buried Sarrha his wife in the Double Cave of the field, which is opposite Mambre, this is Chebron in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So the field and the cave which was in it were made sure to Abraam for possession of a burying place, by the sons of Chet.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: saviv (סָבִיב) = around; surrounding. Common English renderings: round about. Preposition/adverb for surrounding space.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2144, bc 1860 Sarah It is worthy of remark, that Sarah is the only woman whose age, death, and burial are distinctly noted in the Sacred writings. an \textsuperscript{2} Kirjatharba; came For the convenience of feeding his numerous flocks, Abraham had several places of temporary residence; and it is likely, that while he sojourned at Beer-sheba, as we find he did from of the preceding chapter, Sarah died at Hebron, which was 24 miles distant. mourn \textsuperscript{6} my lord, ; a mighty prince Heb. a prince of God; prince \textsuperscript{9} much money Heb. full money \textsuperscript{10} dwelt Or, sitting (as the word frequently denotes) among the children of Heth, at the gate of the city, where all public business was transacted. Ephron, though a chief man, might have been personally unknown to Abraham; but now he answers for himself, making a free tender of the field and cave to Abraham, in the presence of all the people, which amounted to a legal conveyance to the Patriarch. audience Heb. ears all that, ; his \textsuperscript{15} is worth Though the words "is worth" are not in the Text, yet they are clearly implied, to adapt the Hebrew to the English idiom. A shekel, according to the general opinion, was equal in value to about 2s. 6d. of our money, but according to Dr. Prideaux, 3s. English. In those early times, money was given in weight; for it is said ( ) that "Abraham weighed, " wayishkal, the silver; and hence, we find that it was a certain weight which afterwards passed as a current coin; for the word shekel is not only used to denote a piece of silver, but also to weigh. shekels\par}
