\subsection*{Genesis 24}
\markright{GENESIS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abraam was old, advanced in days, and the Lord blessed Abraam in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Abraam said to his servant the elder of his house, who had rule over all his possessions, Put your hand under my thigh, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and I will adjure you by the Lord the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that you take not a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Chananites, with whom I dwell, in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But you shall go instead to my country, where I was born, and to my tribe, and you shall take from thence a wife for my son Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the servant said to him, Shall I carry back your son to the land whence you came forth, if haply the woman should not be willing to return with me to this land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abraam said to him, Take heed to yourself that you carry not my son back there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, who took me out of my father's house, and out of the land whence I sprang, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, I will give this land to you and to your seed, he shall send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife to my son from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if the woman should not be willing to come with you into this land, you shall be clear from my oath, only carry not my son there again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraam, and swore to him concerning this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the servant took ten camels of his master's camels, and [he took] of all the goods of his master with him, and he arose and went into Mesopotamia to the city of Nachor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he rested his camels without the city by the well of water towards evening, when damsels go forth to draw water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, O Lord God of my master Abraam, prosper my way before me to day, and deal mercifully with my master Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Behold! I stand by the well of water, and the daughters of them that inhabit the city come forth to draw water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it shall be, the virgin to whoever I shall say, Incline your water-pot, that I may drink, and she shall say, Drink you, and I will give your camels drink, until they shall have done drinking—even this one you have prepared for your servant Isaac, and hereby shall I know that you have dealt mercifully with my master Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass before he had done speaking in his mind, that behold, Rebecca the daughter of Bathuel, the son of Melcha, the wife of Nachor, and [the same] the brother of Abraam, came forth, having a water-pot on her shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the virgin was very beautiful in appearance, she was a virgin, a man had not known her; and she went down to the well, and filled her water-pot, and came up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the servant ran up to meet her, and said, Give me a little water to drink out of your pitcher; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and she said, Drink, Sir; and she hasted, and let down the pitcher upon her arm, and gave him to drink, till he ceased drinking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And she said, I will also draw water for your camels, till they shall all have drunk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And she hasted, and emptied the water-pot into the trough, and ran to the well to draw again, and drew water for all the camels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the man took great notice of her, and remained silent to know whether the Lord had made his way prosperous or not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it came to pass when all the camels ceased drinking, that the man took golden ear-rings, each of a drachm weight, and he [put] two bracelets on her hands, their weight was ten pieces of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he asked her, and said, Whose daughter are you? Tell me if there is room for us to lodge with your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And she said to him, I am the daughter of Bathuel the son of Melcha, whom she bore to Nachor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And she said to him, We have both straw and much provender, and a place for resting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the man being well pleased, worshipped the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and said, Blessed be the Lord the God of my master Abraam, who has not suffered his righteousness to fail, nor his truth from my master, and the Lord has brought me prosperously to the house of the brother of my lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the damsel ran and reported to the house of her mother according to these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Rebecca had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran out to meet the man, to the well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it came to pass when he saw the ear-rings and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rebecca his sister, saying, Thus the man spoke to me, that he went to the man, as he stood by the camels at the well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said to him, Come in hither, you blessed of the Lord, why stand you without, whereas I have prepared the house and a place for the camels? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the man entered into the house, and unloaded the camels, and gave the camels straw and provender, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men that were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he set before them loaves to eat; but he said, I will not eat, until I have told my errand. And he said, Speak on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he said, I am a servant of Abraam; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} and the Lord has blessed my master greatly, and he is exalted, and he has given him sheep, and calves, and silver, and gold, servants and servant-maids, camels, and asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Sarrha my master's wife bore one son to my master after he had grown old; and he gave him whatever he had. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And my master caused me to swear, saying, You shall not take a wife to my son of the daughters of the Chananites, among whom I sojourn in their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} But you shall go to the house of my father, and to my tribe, and you shall take thence a wife for my son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And I said to my master, Haply the woman will not go with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And he said to me, The Lord God to whom I have been acceptable in his presence, himself shall send out his angel with you, and shall prosper your journey, and you shall take a wife for my son of my tribe, and of the house of my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Then shall you be clear from my curse, for whenever you shall have come to my tribe, and they shall not give her to you, then shall you be clear from my oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And having come this day to the well, I said, Lord God of my master Abraam, if you prosper my journey on which I am now going, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} behold, I stand by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city come forth to draw water, and it shall be [that] the damsel to whom I shall say, Give me a little water to drink out of your pitcher, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} and she shall say to me, Both drink you, and I will draw water for your camels, this [shall be] the wife whom the Lord has prepared for his own servant Isaac; and hereby shall I know that you have wrought mercy with my master Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And it came to pass before I had done speaking in my mind, straightway Rebecca came forth, having her pitcher on her shoulders; and she went down to the well, and drew water; and I said to her, Give me to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And she hasted and let down her pitcher on her arm from her head, and said, Drink you, and I will give your camels drink; and I drank, and she gave the camels drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter are you? tell me; and she said, I am daughter of Bathuel the son of Nachor, whom Melcha bore to him; and I put on her the ear-rings, and the bracelets on her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And being well-pleased I worshipped the Lord, and I blessed the Lord the God of my master Abraam, who has prospered me in a true way, so that I should take the daughter of my master's brother for his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} If then you⌃ [will] deal mercifully and justly with my lord, [tell me], and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And Laban and Bathuel answered and said, This matter has come forth from the Lord, we shall not be able to answer you bad or good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Behold, Rebecca is before you, take her and go away, and let her be wife to the son of your master, as the Lord has said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And it came to pass when the servant of Abraam heard these words, he bowed himself to the Lord down to the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And the servant having brought forth jewels of silver and gold and raiment, gave them to Rebecca, and gave gifts to her brother, and to her mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And both he and the men with him ate and drank and went to sleep. And he arose in the morning and said, Send me away, that I may go to my master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And her brethren and her mother said, Let the virgin remain with us about ten days, and after that she shall depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} But he said to them, Hinder me not, for the Lord has prospered my journey for me; send me away, that I may depart to my master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And they said, Let us call the damsel, and enquire at her mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} And they called Rebecca, and said to her, Will you go with this man? and she said, I will go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} So they sent forth Rebecca their sister, and her goods, and the servant of Abraam, and his attendants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} And they blessed Rebecca, and said to her, You are our sister; become you thousands of myriads, and let your seed possess the cities of their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And Rebecca rose up and her maidens, and they mounted the camels and went with the man; and the servant having taken up Rebecca, departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And Isaac went through the wilderness to the well of the vision, and he lived in the land toward the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} And Isaac went forth into the plain toward evening to meditate; and having lifted up his eyes, he saw camels coming. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} And Rebecca lifted up her eyes, and saw Isaac; and she alighted briskly from the camel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} and said to the servant, Who is that man that walks in the plain to meet us? And the servant said, This is my master; and she took her veil and covered herself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} And the servant told Isaac all that he had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} And Isaac went into the house of his mother, and took Rebecca, and she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted for Sarrha his mother.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: yarekh (יָרֵךְ) = thigh. Common English renderings: thigh. Body term appearing in oath and battle imagery. \textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: shevuah (שְׁבוּעָה) = oath. Common English renderings: oath. Derived from the verb to swear. \textsuperscript{22} Gk. vocab: drachmē (δραχμή) = drachma. Common English renderings: piece of silver. A coin or weight term. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: yesh (יֵשׁ) = there is; there exists. Common English renderings: there is. Its sound is close to the English word yes, though the Hebrew particle actually expresses existence rather than agreement. \textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: emet (אֱמֶת) = truth; faithfulness. Common English renderings: truth. A covenantally rich term for reliability and truth. Gk. vocab: alētheia (ἀλήθεια) = truth. Common English renderings: truth. Can denote truthfulness, reliability, or what is true. \textsuperscript{41} Heb. vocab: alah (אָלָה) = oath-curse; imprecation; curse. Common English renderings: curse; oath. Its sound closely resembles the English rendering Allah; this is only a phonetic resemblance in English, while the Hebrew term refers to an oath-curse or imprecation. \textsuperscript{60} Heb. vocab: sane (שָׂנֵא) = to hate. Common English renderings: hate. Can indicate enmity, rejection, or lesser preference in context.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} was old, ; well stricken in age Heb. gone into days blessed \textsuperscript{4} to my kindred, ; There does not appear in all this concern the least taint of worldly policy, or any of those motives which usually govern men in the settlement of their children. No mention is made of riches, or honours, or natural accomplishments, but merely of what related to God. - Fuller. \textsuperscript{7} Lord; took which spake, ; angel \textsuperscript{10} for or, and all the, Mesopotamia; city \textsuperscript{11} kneel; women go out to draw water Heb. women which draw water go forth \textsuperscript{14} And let; she that; thereby \textsuperscript{16} fair to look upon Heb. good of countenance, known \textsuperscript{21} wondering at;, ; to wit i.e. "to know, " or "to learn" the Lord \textsuperscript{22} took; earring or, jewel for the forehead; From the word being in the singular number, it is not likely to have been an ear-ring, or a "jewel for the forehead, " but "a jewel for the nose, a nose-ring, " which is in use throughout Arabia and Persia, particularly among young women. It is very properly translated επιρρινον, "an ornament for the nose, " by Symmachus; and Sir John Chardin informs us, that "it is a custom in almost all the East, for the women to wear rings in their noses, in the left nostril, which is bored low down in the middle. These rings are of gold, and have commonly two pearls and one ruby between, placed in the ring. I never saw a girl or young woman in Arabia or in all Persia, who did not wear a ring after this manner in her nostril." of half bracelets The word rendered "bracelet, " from a root which signifies "to join or couple together, " may imply whatever may clasp round the arms and legs; for rings and ornaments are worn round both by females in India and Persia. The small part of the leg, and the whole arm, from the shoulder to the wrist, are generally decorated in this way. As these were given to Rebekah for "her hands, " it sufficiently distinguishes them from similar ornaments for the ankles. \textsuperscript{27} Blessed, ; of his; the Lord;, of my \textsuperscript{28} of, her mother's Some have conjectured from this, that her father Bethuel was dead; and the person called Bethuel ( ), was a younger brother. This is possible; but as Dr. A. Clarke remarks, the mother's house might be mentioned were even the father alive; for in Asiatic countries, the women have apartments entirely separate from those of the men, in which their little children and grown-up daughters reside with them. This was probably the case here; though, from the whole narrative, it is very probable that Bethuel was dead, as the whole business appears to be conducted by Rebekah's brothers. \textsuperscript{32} he ungirded i.e. Laban ungirded straw Straw, by the eastern mode of threshing, was cut or shattered, and reduced to a kind of chaff. With this, sometimes mixed with a little barley, the eastern people still feed their labouring beasts, as they anciently did. wash \textsuperscript{37} And my, ; Canaanites The Canaanites were infected with gross idolatry; and consequently, not proper persons with whom to form so intimate a connection; especially as Jehovah had shown Abraham that they were filling up the measure of their iniquity, and were doomed to destruction. \textsuperscript{38} But, my father's i.e., Where the family of Haran his brother had settled; and where he himself had remained some time with his father Terah. Nahor did not dwell at Ur of the Chaldees, but at Haran in Mesopotamia. The true worship of God seems to have been in some measure preserved in this family, though afterwards corrupted. \textsuperscript{39} Peradventure We may see, says Calmet, by this and other passages of Scripture ( ), what the sentiments of the ancients were relative to an oath. They believed that they were bound precisely by what was spoken, and had no liberty to interpret the intentions of those by whom the oath was made. \textsuperscript{44} Both; the woman;, appointed Those events, which appear to us the effect of choice, contrivance, or chance, are matters of appointment with God; and the persuasion of this does not prevent, but rather encourage, the use of all proper means; at the same time that it confines us to proper means, and delivers the mind from useless anxiety about consequences. \textsuperscript{49} now if; deal kindly and truly Heb. do mercy and truth; that I \textsuperscript{50} Laban These seem both to be brothers, of whom Laban was the eldest and chief. The opinion of Josephus appears to be very correct, that Bethuel, the father, had been dead some time., The thing; we \textsuperscript{53} jewels Heb. vessels, The original word denotes vessels, utensils, instruments, furniture, or dress; and these presented by Abraham's servant might have been of various kinds., brother No mention is made of her father. precious This term, rendered "precious things, " as may be seen in the parallel texts, is used to express exquisite fruits or delicacies, and precious plants or flowers, but here it may mean gifts in general, though rather of an inferior kind to those mentioned above. \textsuperscript{55} a few days or, a full year, or ten months \textsuperscript{60} they, ; be thou the mother Or, "be thou for thousands of myriads; " a large family being always considered, in ancient times, as a proof of the peculiar blessing and favour of God. thousands thy seed \textsuperscript{63} to meditate or, to pray, They who acknowledge God in all their ways, will find him present to direct their paths, and make their way prosperous; and when the prayer of faith meets with an immediate answer, the glory ought as speedily to be rendered to God in solemn praise and thanksgiving. \textsuperscript{67} his mother; Sarah's tent Sarah, being dead, her tent, which, according to the custom of the east, was distinct from that of Abraham, became now appropriated to the use of Rebekah. and took; comforted\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 25}
\markright{GENESIS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abraam again took a wife, whose name was Chettura. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And she bore to him Zombran, and Jezan, and Madal, and Madiam, and Jesboc, and Soie. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jezan begot Saba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were the Assurians and the Latusians, and Laomim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the sons of Madiam [were] Gephar and Aphir, and Enoch, and Abeida, and Eldaga; all these were sons of Chettura. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But Abraam gave all his possessions to Isaac his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But to the sons of his concubines Abraam gave gifts, and he sent them away from his son Isaac, while he was yet living, to the east into the country of the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And these [were] the years of the days of the life of Abraam as many as he lived, one hundred and seventy-five years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abraam failing died in a good old age, an old man and full of days, and was added to his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Isaac and Ismael his sons buried him in the double cave, in the field of Ephron the son of Saar the Chettite, which is over against Mambre: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [even] the field and the cave which Abraam bought of the sons of Chet; there they buried Abraam and Sarrha his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass after Abraam was dead, that God blessed Isaac his son, and Isaac lived by the well of the vision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And these [are] the generations of Ismael the son of Abraam, whom Agar the Egyptian the handmaid of Sarrha bore to Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these [are] the names of the sons of Ismael, according to the names of their generations. The firstborn of Ismael, Nabaioth, and Kedar, and Nabdeel, and Massam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and Masma, and Duma, and Masse, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and Choddan, and Thaeman, and Jetur, and Naphes, and Kedma. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} These [are] the sons of Ismael, and these are their names in their tents and in their dwellings, twelve princes according to their nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these [are] the years of the life of Ismael, one hundred and thirty-seven years; and he failed and died, and was added to his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he lived from Evilat to Sur, which is opposite Egypt, until one comes to the Assyrians; he lived in the presence of all his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And these [are] the generations of Isaac the son of Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Abraam begot Isaac. And Isaac was forty years old when he took as wife Rebecca, daughter of Bathuel the Syrian, out of Syrian Mesopotamia, sister of Laban the Syrian. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Isaac prayed the Lord concerning Rebecca his wife, because she was barren; and the Lord heard him, and his wife Rebecca conceived in her womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the babes leaped within her; and she said, If it will be so with me, why is this to me? And she went to enquire of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord said to her, There are two nations in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your belly, and one people shall excel the other, and the elder shall serve the younger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the days were fulfilled that she should be delivered, and she had twins in her womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the first came out red, hairy all over like a skin; and she called his name Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And after this came forth his brother, and his hand took hold of the heel of Esau; and she called his name Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when Rebecca bore them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the lads grew, and Esau was a man skilled in hunting, dwelling in the country, and Jacob a simple man, dwelling in a house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Isaac loved Esau, because his venison was his food, but Rebecca loved Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Jacob cooked pottage, and Esau came from the plain, fainting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Esau said to Jacob, Let me taste of that red pottage, because I am fainting; therefore his name was called Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Jacob said to Esau, Sell me this day your birthright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Esau said, Behold, I am going to die, and for what good does this birthright [belong] to me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Jacob said to him, Swear to me this day; and he swore to him; and Esau sold his birthright to Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Jacob gave bread to Esau, and pottage of lentiles; and he ate and drank, and he arose and departed; so Esau slighted his birthright.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: chatser (חָצֵר) = court; enclosure; village. Common English renderings: court; village. Can refer to encampment, village, or courtyard. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: darash (דָּרַשׁ) = to seek; inquire. Common English renderings: seek; inquire. Frequently used of consulting the LORD. \textsuperscript{23} Gk. vocab: koilia (κοιλία) = belly; womb. Common English renderings: belly; womb. Context determines whether belly or womb is intended. \textsuperscript{25} Name meaning: Esau (Esav) — Hairy; red Born hairy and red; sold his birthright for red stew. \textsuperscript{26} Name meaning: Jacob (Yaaqov) — Supplanter; heel-grabber Grabbed Esau’s heel at birth; later supplanted him and became Israel.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} am cir, 2152, bc cir, 1852 she bare; Zimri Midian, ;, ; Judg. 6:1-8:35 Shuah \textsuperscript{3} am cir, 2180, bc cir, 1824 Sheba; Dedan; Asshurim \textsuperscript{4} am cir, 2200, bc cir, 1804 Ephah \textsuperscript{5} am cir, 2175, bc cir, 1829, ; Isaac typified the Son of God, "whom HE hath appointed Heir of all things." \textsuperscript{6} concubines, ; gifts; sent east country Arabia Deserta, which was eastward of Beer-sheba, where Abraham dwelt. \textsuperscript{13} the names Nebajoth From Nebajoth sprang the Nabatheans, who inhabited Arabia Petraea; from Kedar, the Cedreans, who dwelt near the Nabatheans; and from Jetur, the Itureans, who inhabited a small tract of country east of Jordan, which afterwards belonged to Manasseh.; Kedar \textsuperscript{15} Hadar or, Hadad, More than 300 manuscripts and printed editions read Hadad, as in . Tema; Naphish These are evidently the same people mentioned in, who, with the Itureans, assisted the Hagarenes against the Israelites, but were overcome by the two tribes of Reuben and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. \textsuperscript{16} castles The word tiroth, rendered "castles, " is supposed by some to denote here "towers, " fortified rocks, or mountain-tops, and fastnesses of various kinds in woods and hilly countries; but it rather means, "shepherds' cots, " surrounded by sufficient enclosures to prevent the cattle from straying, as the cognate Syriac word teyaro, and Arabic tawar, signify "a sheep-fold." twelve \textsuperscript{17} am 2231, bc 1773 these are gathered \textsuperscript{18} Havilah, as thou toward; died Heb. fell; in the \textsuperscript{20} am 2148, bc 1856 when he, the Syrian \textsuperscript{21} am 2167, bc 1837 entreated; because, ; and the; and Rebekah \textsuperscript{23} Two nations, two manner, ; the elder \textsuperscript{25} Esau The word Esau has been generally considered to imply made, formed, or perfected; or perfect, robust, etc. But it appears to be a dialectical variation of the Arabic atha, to be covered with hair; whence athai, hairy, as no doubt the word Esau imports, in allusion to the circumstance of his being covered with red hair or down at his birth. \textsuperscript{26} And after took Jacob Isaac was \textsuperscript{27} a cunning, a plain man, ; dwelling \textsuperscript{28} he did eat of his venison Heb. venison was in his mouth, Rebekah \textsuperscript{30} with that same red pottage Heb. with that red, with that red pottage, This, we are informed ( ), was of lentiles, a sort of pulse. Edom i.e. red \textsuperscript{32} at the point to die Heb. going to die and what, ; birthright\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 26}
\markright{GENESIS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine, which was in the time of Abraam; and Isaac went to Abimelech the king of the Phylistines to Gerara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord appeared to him and said, Go not down to Egypt, but dwell in the land, which I shall tell you of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And sojourn in this land; and I will be with you, and bless you, for I will give to you and to your seed all this land; and I will establish my oath which I swore to your father Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven; and I will give to your seed all this land, and all the nations of the earth shall be blest in your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Because Abraam your father listened to my voice, and kept my injunctions, and my commandments, and my ordinances, and my statutes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Isaac lived in Gerara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the men of the place questioned him concerning Rebecca his wife, and he said, She is my sister, for he feared to say, She is my wife, lest at any time the men of the place should kill him because of Rebecca, because she was fair. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he remained there a long time, and Abimelech the king of Gerara leaned to look through the window, and saw Isaac sporting with Rebecca his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abimelech called Isaac, and said to him, Is she then your wife? why have you said, She is my sister? And Isaac said to him, [I did so], for I said, Lest at any time I die on her account. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abimelech said to him, Why have you done this to us? one of my kindred within a little had lain with your wife, and you would have brought [a sin of] ignorance upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Abimelech charged all his people, saying Every man that touches this man and his wife shall be liable to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Isaac sowed in that land, and he found in that year barley one hundred-fold, and the Lord blessed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the man was exalted, and advancing he increased, till he became very great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he had cattle of sheep, and cattle of oxen, and many tilled lands, and the Phylistines envied him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And all the wells which the servants of his father had dug in the time of his father, the Phylistines stopped them, and filled them with earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Abimelech said to Isaac, Depart from us, for you are become much mightier than we. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Isaac departed thence, and rested in the valley of Gerara, and lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Isaac dug again the wells of water, which the servants of his father Abraam had dug, and the Phylistines had stopped them, after the death of his father Abraam; and he gave them names, according to the names by which his father named them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the servants of Isaac dug in the valley of Gerara, and they found there a well of living water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the shepherds of Gerara strove with the shepherds of Isaac, saying that the water was theirs; and they called the name of the well, Injury, for they injured him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And having departed thence he dug another well, and they strove also for that; and he named the name of it, Enmity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he departed thence and dug another well; and they did not strive about that; and he named the name of it, Room, saying, Because now the Lord has made room for us, and has increased us upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he went up thence to the well of the oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Lord appeared to him in that night, and said, I am the God of Abraam your father; fear not, for I am with you, and I will bless you, and multiply your seed for the sake of Abraam your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he built there an altar, and called on the name of the Lord, and there he pitched his tent, and there the servants of Isaac dug a well in the valley of Gerara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Abimelech came to him from Gerara, and so did Ochozath his friend, and Phichol the commander-in-chief of his army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Isaac said to them, Therefore have you⌃ come to me? whereas you⌃ hated me, and sent me away from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they said, We have surely seen that the Lord was with you, and we said, Let there be an oath between us and you, and we will make a covenant with you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} that you shall do no wrong by us, as we have not abhorred you, and according as we have treated you well, and have sent you forth peaceably; and now you are blessed of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he made a feast for them, and they ate and drank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they arose in the morning, and swore each to his neighbor; and Isaac sent them forth, and they departed from him in safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And it came to pass in that day, that the servants of Isaac came and told him of the well which they had dug; and they said, We have not found water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he called it, Oath: therefore he called the name of that city, the Well of Oath, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Esau was forty years old; and he took as wife Judith the daughter of Beoch the Chettite, and Basemath, daughter of Helon the Chettite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they were provoking to Isaac and Rebecca.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: mitsvah (מִצְוָה) = commandment. Common English renderings: commandment. Refers to specific commanded obligations. Gk. vocab: entolē (ἐντολή) = commandment. Common English renderings: commandment. Used for commandments or authoritative injunctions. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: zara (זָרַע) = to sow. Common English renderings: sow. Basic agricultural verb, also linked with offspring imagery. \textsuperscript{24} Name of God: Elohe Avraham (אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם) — God of Abraham Common English renderings: God of Abraham. A covenant formula identifying God by His faithful relationship to the patriarchs.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2200, bc 1804 the first And Isaac Abimelech \textsuperscript{3} Sojourn, ; I will be, ; unto thee, oath \textsuperscript{7} She is my sister, ; fair \textsuperscript{12} sowed The author of the "History of the Piratical States of Barbary" observes (p. 44), that the Moors of that country are divided into tribes like the Arabians, and like them dwell in tents, formed into itinerant villages; that "these wanderers farm lands of the inhabitants of the towns, sow and cultivate them, paying their rent with the produce, such as fruits, corn, wax, etc. They are very skilful in choosing the most advantageous soils for every season, and very careful to avoid the Turkish troops, the violence of the one little suiting the simplicity of the other." It is natural to suppose, that Isaac possessed the like sagacity, when he sowed in the land of Gerar, and received that year an hundred-fold. received Heb. found an hundredfold; blessed \textsuperscript{13} And the man waxed great Dr. Adam Clarke remarks, that there is a strange and observable occurrence of the same term in the original, which is literally, "And the man was GREAT, and he went, going on, and was GREAT, until that he was exceeding GREAT." How simple is this language, and yet how forcible! waxed great; went forward Heb. went going \textsuperscript{14} had possession; servants or, husbandry envied \textsuperscript{15} his father's had stopped In those countries, a well of water was a great acquisition; and hence, this mode of injuring new settlers, or revenging themselves on their enemies, is still resorted to among the inhabitants. \textsuperscript{16} Go Dr. A. Clarke observes, that this is the first instance on record of what was termed among the Greeks, ostracism, i.e., the banishment of person from the state, of whose power, influence, or riches, the people were jealous. mightier \textsuperscript{18} in the days Houbigant contends, that instead of bimey, "in the days, " we should read, avdey, "servants; " agreeably to the Samaritan, Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate: "And Isaac digged again the wells of water which the servants of Abraham his father had digged." and he \textsuperscript{20} did strive Esek i.e. Contention \textsuperscript{22} digged The wells in Arabia are generally dug in the rock. Their mouths are about six feet in diameter, and they are from nineteen to twenty feet in depth. But Niebuhr informs us, that many wells are from 160 to 170 feet deep. Rehoboth i.e. Room the Lord, be fruitful \textsuperscript{26} Abimelech, Phichol, as well as Abimelech, "father king, " seems to have been a name of office or dignity among the Philistines; for it is not probable that they were the same as are mentioned in the days of Abraham (, ). \textsuperscript{28} We saw certainly Heb. Seeing we saw was with; , ; Let there \textsuperscript{29} That thou wilt Heb. If thou shalt, etc not, the blessed \textsuperscript{33} Shebah i.e. an oath therefore Beersheba i.e. the well of the oath; This may have been the same city which was called Beer-sheba a hundred years before this, in the time of Abraham; but as the well, from which it had its name originally, was closed up by the Philistines, the name of the place might have been abolished with the well; when, therefore, Isaac re-opened it, he restored the ancient name of the place. \textsuperscript{34} am 2208, bc 1796 And Esau, the daughter; Bashemath \textsuperscript{35} Which, grief of mind Heb. bitterness of spirit\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 27}
\markright{GENESIS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after Isaac was old, that his eyes were dimmed so that he could not see; and he called Esau, his elder son, and said to him, My son; and he said, Behold, I [am here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said, Behold, I am grown old, and know not the day of my death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now then take the weapons, both your quiver and your bow, and go into the plain, and get me venison, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and make me meats, as I like them, and bring them to me that I may eat, that my soul may bless you, before I die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Rebecca heard Isaac speaking to Esau his son; and Esau went to the plain to procure venison for his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Rebecca said to Jacob her younger son, Behold, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Bring me venison, and prepare me meats, that I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now then, my son, listen to me, as I command you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And go to the cattle and take for me thence two kids, tender and good, and I will make them meats for your father, as he likes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall bring them in to your father, and he shall eat, that your father may bless you before he dies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jacob said to his mother Rebecca, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I a smooth man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Peradventure my father may feel me, and I shall be before him as one ill-intentioned, and I shall bring upon me a curse, and not a blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And his mother said to him, On me be your curse, son; only listen to my voice, and go and bring [them] me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So he went and took and brought them to his mother; and his mother made meats, as his father liked [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Rebecca having taken the fine raiment of her elder son Esau which was with her in the house, put it on Jacob her younger son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And she put on his arms the skins of the kids, and on the bare parts of his neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And she gave the meats, and the loaves which she had prepared, into the hands of Jacob her son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he brought [them] to his father, and said, Father; and he said, Behold I [am here]; who are you, son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Jacob said to his father, I, Esau your firstborn, have done as you told me; rise, sit, and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Isaac said to his son, What is this which you have quickly found? And he said, That which the Lord your God presented before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Isaac said to Jacob, Draw near to me, and I will feel you, son, if you are my son Esau or not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Jacob drew near to his father Isaac, and he felt him, and said, The voice [is] Jacob's voice, but the hands [are] the hands of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he knew him not, for his hands were as the hands of his brother Esau, hairy; and he blessed him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and he said, Are you my son Esau? and he said, I [am]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he said, Bring hither, and I will eat of your venison, son, that my soul may bless you; and he brought [it] near to him, and he ate, and he brought him wine, and he drank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Isaac his father said to him, Draw near to me, and kiss me, son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he drew near and kissed him, and smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him, and said, Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of an abundant field, which the Lord has blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And may God give you of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of corn and wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And let nations serve you, and princes bow down to you, and be you lord of your brother, and the sons of your father shall do you reverence; accursed is he that curses you, and blessed is he that blesses you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it came to pass after Isaac had ceased blessing his son Jacob, it even came to pass, just when Jacob had gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he also had made meats and brought them to his father; and he said to his father, Let my father arise and eat of his son's venison, that your soul may bless me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Isaac his father said to him, Who are you? And he said, I am your firstborn son Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Isaac was amazed with very great amazement, and said, Who then is it that has procured venison for me and brought it to me? and I have eaten of all before you came, and I have blessed him, and he shall be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out with a great and very bitter cry, and said, Bless, I pray you, me also, father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he said to him, Your brother has come with subtlety, and taken your blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he said, Rightly was his name called Jacob, for behold! this second time has he supplanted me; he has both taken my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing; and Esau said to his father, Have you not left a blessing for me, father? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Isaac answered and said to Esau, If I have made him your lord, and have made all his brethren his servants, and have strengthened him with corn and wine, what then shall I do for you, son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Esau said to his father, Have you [only] one blessing, father? Bless, I pray you, me also, father. And Isaac being troubled, Esau cried aloud and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Isaac his father answered and said to him, Behold, your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And you shall live by your sword, and shall serve your brother; and there shall be [a time] when you shall break and loosen his yoke from off your neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Esau was angry with Jacob because of the blessing, with which his father blessed him; and Esau said in his mind, Let the days of my father's mourning draw near, that I may kill my brother Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the words of Esau her elder son were reported to Rebecca, and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, Behold, Esau your brother threatens you to kill you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Now then, my son, hear my voice, and rise and depart quickly into Mesopotamia to Laban my brother into Charran. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And dwell with him certain days, until your brother's anger {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} and rage depart from you, and he forget what you have done to him; and I will send and fetch you thence, lest at any time I should be bereaved of you both in one day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Rebecca said to Isaac, I am weary of my life, because of the daughters of the sons of Chet; if Jacob shall take a wife of the daughters of this land, therefore should I live?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: nafshi (נַפְשִׁי) = my soul; my life. Common English renderings: my soul; my life. Represents נפש in a common suffixed form in devotional contexts. \textsuperscript{9} Gk. vocab: tragos (τράγος) = goat. Common English renderings: goat. A standard term for goat, often in sacrificial contexts. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: qelalah (קְלָלָה) = curse. Common English renderings: curse. Noun form for spoken or enacted curse. Gk. vocab: eulogia (εὐλογία) = blessing; praise. Common English renderings: blessing. A word of blessing or the blessing conferred. Gk. vocab: katara (κατάρα) = curse. Common English renderings: curse. The opposite of blessing in covenant and judgment language. Gk. vocab: pseudos (ψεῦδος) = lie; falsehood. Common English renderings: lie. A noun for falsehood and deceit. \textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: tsavvar (צַוָּאר) = neck. Common English renderings: neck. Image for obstinacy, ornamentation, or embrace. \textsuperscript{28} Gk. vocab: sitos (σῖτος) = grain; wheat. Common English renderings: corn; wheat. Often denotes grain in general or wheat specifically. \textsuperscript{35} Gk. vocab: dolos (δόλος) = deceit; guile. Common English renderings: guile; deceit. A term for deceit, trickery, or treachery. \textsuperscript{40} Heb. vocab: paraq (פָּרַק) = to break off; tear away. Common English renderings: break off. Used for removing burdens or ornaments. \textsuperscript{44} Gk. vocab: orgē (ὀργή) = wrath; anger. Common English renderings: wrath. Frequently used of settled anger and divine wrath.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2244, bc 1760 dim; eldest son \textsuperscript{3} I, take me Heb. hunt \textsuperscript{4} that I may eat The blessing, says Dr. A. Clarke, which Isaac was to confer on his son, was a species of divine right, and must be communicated with appropriate ceremonies. As eating and drinking were used among the Asiatics on almost all religious occasions, and especially in making and confirming covenants, it is reasonable to suppose, that something of this kind was essentially necessary on this occasion; and that Isaac could not convey the right, till he had eaten of the meat provided for the purpose by him who was to receive the blessing. that my \textsuperscript{9} two; savoury Matammim, from taam, to taste or relish. How dressed is uncertain, but its name declares it nature. \textsuperscript{12} feel; a deceiver; and I shall \textsuperscript{15} goodly raiment Heb. desirable; The Septuagint translates it "a goodly robe, " which was a long garment that great men used to wear (; ). The priest afterwards in the law had "holy garments" to minister in ( ). Whether the first-born before the law had such to minister in is not certain: for, had they been common garments, why did not Esau himself or his wives keep them? But being, in likelihood, holy robes, received from their ancestors, the mother of the family kept them in sweet chests, from moths and the like; whereupon it is said ( ), "Isaac smelled the smell of his garments." \textsuperscript{16} skins Travellers inform us, that the Eastern goats have long, fine, and beautiful hair, of the most delicate silky softness; indeed the animals generally in those hot countries are not covered with so thick a coat of hair as they are in more northerly regions; so that Isaac might easily be deceived, when his eyes were dim, and his feeling no less impaired than his sight. \textsuperscript{20} Because; to me Heb. before me \textsuperscript{22} The voice How wonderful, says Mr. Scott, is that difference which there is betwixt the faces and the voices of the several individuals of the human species! Scarcely any two of the innumerable millions are exactly alike in either, and yet the difference cannot be defined or described! The power, wisdom, and kindness of our Creator should be admired and adored in this remarkable circumstance; for they are very visible. This description of Jacob is not unaptly accommodated to the character of a hypocrite. His voice, his language, is that of a Christian; his hands, or conduct, that of an ungodly man, but the judgment will proceed from God, the Judge of all, at the last day, as in the present case, not by the voice, but by the hands. \textsuperscript{27} blessed the smell of a field A field where aromatic plants, flowers, fruits, and spices grew in abundance, with which these garments (see note on ) of Esau might probably have been perfumed by being laid up with them., ; which \textsuperscript{28} of the dew, ; the fatness, ; plenty \textsuperscript{29} Let people, ; be lord, ; *title; cursed \textsuperscript{33} trembled very exceedingly Heb. trembled with a great trembling greatly, ; taken Heb. hunted thou camest yea \textsuperscript{36} Jacob i.e. a supplanter, ; he took \textsuperscript{37} I have; with sustained or, supported \textsuperscript{39} Behold; the fatness or, of the fatness; It is here foretold, says Bp. Newton, that as to temporal advantages, the two brothers should be much alike. (See note on .) \subsection*{Genesis 28}
\markright{GENESIS 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Isaac having called for Jacob, blessed him, and charged him, saying, You shall not take a wife of the daughters of the Chananites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Rise and depart quickly into Mesopotamia, to the house of Bathuel the father of your mother, and take to yourself thence a wife of the daughters of Laban your mother's brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And may my God bless you, and increase you, and multiply you, and you shall become gatherings of nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And may he give you the blessing of my father Abraam, even to you and to your seed after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which God gave to Abraam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So Isaac sent away Jacob, and he went into Mesopotamia to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebecca the mother of Jacob and Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esau saw that Isaac blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Mesopotamia of Syria as he blessed him, to take to himself a wife thence, and [that] he charged him, saying, You shall not take a wife of the daughters of the Chananites; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and [that] Jacob listened to his father and his mother, and went to Mesopotamia of Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Esau also having seen that the daughters of Chanaan were evil before his father Isaac, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Esau went to Ismael, and took Maeleth the daughter of Ismael, the son of Abraam, the sister of Nabeoth, a wife in addition to his [other] wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Jacob went forth from the well of the oath, and departed into Charrhan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And came to a certain place and slept there, for the sun had gone down; and he took [one] of the stones of the place, and put it at his head, and lay down to sleep in that place, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and dreamed, and behold a ladder fixed on the earth, whose top reached to heaven, and the angels of God ascended and descended on it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord stood upon it, and said, I am the God of your father Abraam, and the God of Isaac; fear not, the land on which you lie, to you will I give it, and to your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And your seed shall be as the sand of the earth; and it shall spread abroad to the sea, and the south, and the north, and to the east; and in you and in your seed shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And behold I am with you to preserve you continually in all the way wherein you shall go; and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not desert you, until I have done all that I have said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and said, The Lord is in this place, and I knew it not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he was afraid, and said, How fearful is this place! this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jacob rose up in the morning, and took the stone he [had] laid there by his head, and he set it up [as] a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he called the name of that place, the House of God; and the name of the city before was Ulam-luz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If the Lord God will be with me, and guard me throughout on this journey, on which I am going, and give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and bring me back in safety to the house of my father, then shall the Lord be for a God to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, shall be to me a house of God; and of all whatever you shall give me, I will tithe a tenth for you.\par

A gathered community term, especially covenantal. \textsuperscript{13} Name of God: Elohe Yitzchak (אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק) — God of Isaac Common English renderings: God of Isaac. Continues the covenant identification of God with the patriarchal line. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: parats (פָּרַץ) = to break through; burst out. Common English renderings: break forth. Gk. vocab: elaion (ἔλαιον) = olive oil. Common English renderings: oil. Usually olive oil in ordinary or sacred use. \textsuperscript{20} Gk. vocab: euchē (εὐχή) = vow; prayer. Common English renderings: vow; prayer. Can mean vow or prayer according to context.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} God, ; and make, ; a multitude Heb. an assembly \textsuperscript{4} the blessing, ; wherein thou art a stranger Heb. of thy sojournings, which \textsuperscript{5} sent away Jacob Whoever observes Jacob's life, after he had surreptitiously obtained his father's blessing, will perceive that he enjoyed very little worldly felicity. His brother purposed to murder him, to avoid which he was forced to flee from his father's house; his uncle Laban deceived him, as he had deceived his father, and treated him with great rigour; after a servitude of 21 years, he was obliged to leave him in a clandestine manner, not without danger of being brought back, or murdered by his enraged brother; no sooner were these fears over, than he experienced the baseness of his son Reuben, in defiling his bed; he had next to bewail the treachery and cruelty of Simeon and Levi toward the Shechemites; then he had to feel the loss of his beloved wife; he was next imposed upon by his own sons, and had to lament the supposed untimely end of Joseph; and to complete all, he was forced by famine to go into Egypt, and there died, in a strange land. So just, wonderful, and instructive are all the ways of Providence! \subsection*{Genesis 29}
\markright{GENESIS 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob started and went to the land of the east to Laban, the son of Bathuel the Syrian, and the brother of Rebecca, mother of Jacob and Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he looks, and behold! a well in the plain; and there were there three flocks of sheep resting at it, for out of that well they watered the flocks, but there was a great stone at the mouth of the well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And there were all the flocks gathered, and they used to roll away the stone from the mouth of the well, and water the flocks, and set the stone again in its place on the mouth of the well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jacob said to them, Brethren, whence are you⌃? and they said, We are of Charrhan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to them, Know you⌃ Laban, the son of Nachor? and they said, We do know [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to them, Is he well? And they said, He is well. And behold Rachel his daughter came with the sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jacob said, it is yet high day, it is not yet time that the flocks be gathered together; water you⌃ the flocks, and depart and feed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said, We shall not be able, until all the shepherds be gathered together, and they shall roll away the stone from the mouth of the well, then we will water the flocks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} While he was yet speaking to them, behold, Rachel the daughter of Laban came with her father's sheep, for she fed the sheep of her father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother, that Jacob came and rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jacob kissed Rachel, and cried with a loud voice and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he told Rachel that he was the near relative of her father, and the son of Rebecca; and she ran and reported to her father according to these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass when Laban heard the name of Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him, and brought him into his house; and he told Laban all these sayings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Laban said to him, You are of my bones and of my flesh; and he was with him a full month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Laban said to Jacob, Surely you shall not serve me for nothing, because you are my brother; tell me what your reward is to be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now Laban had two daughters, the name of the elder was Lea, and the name of the younger, Rachel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the eyes of Lea were weak. But Rachel was beautiful in appearance, and exceedingly fair in countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jacob loved Rachel, and said, I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Laban said to him, [It is] better that I should give her to you, than that I should give her to another man; dwell with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jacob served for Rachel seven years, and they were before him as a few days, by reason of his loving her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Jacob said to Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a marriage-feast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it was even, and he took his daughter Lea, and brought her in to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Laban gave to his daughter Lea, Zelpha his handmaid, as a handmaid for her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it was morning, and behold it was Lea; and Jacob said to Laban, What is this that you have done to me? did I not serve you for Rachel? and therefore have you deceived me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Laban answered, It is not done thus in our country, to give the younger before the elder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Fulfil then her sevens, and I will give to you her also in return for your labor, which you labor with me, yet seven other years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her sevens; and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Laban gave to his daughter his handmaid Balla, for a handmaid to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he went in to Rachel; and he loved Rachel more than Lea; and he served him seven other years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And when the Lord God saw that Lea was hated, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Lea conceived and bore a son to Jacob; and she called his name, Ruben; saying, Because the Lord has looked on my humiliation, and has given me a son, now then my husband will love me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And she conceived again, and bore a second son to Jacob; and she said, Because the Lord has heard that I am hated, he has given to me this one also; and she called his name, Simeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And she conceived yet again, and bore a son, and said, In the present time my husband will be with me, for I have born him three sons; therefore she called his name, Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And having conceived yet again, she bore a son, and said, Now yet again this time will I give thanks to the Lord; therefore she called his name, Juda; and ceased bearing.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: avodah (עֲבֹדָה) = service; work; worship. Common English renderings: service; work. Can denote labor or cultic service. \textsuperscript{32} Name meaning: Reuben (Reuven) — Behold a son Leah’s first son; hoped it would win Jacob’s love. \textsuperscript{33} Name meaning: Simeon (Shimon) — Heard The LORD heard that Leah was hated. \textsuperscript{34} Name meaning: Levi (Levi) — Joined; attached Leah hoped her husband would be joined to her; tribe of priests. Heb. vocab: Levi (לֵוִי) = Levi; Levite. Common English renderings: Levi; Levite. Tribal name later associated with priestly service. \textsuperscript{35} Name meaning: Judah (Yehudah) — Praise Royal tribe and ancestor of Messiah. Heb. vocab: Yehudah (יְהוּדָה) = Judah. Common English renderings: Judah. Tribal name central to kingship and messianic expectation. Heb. vocab: yadah (יָדָה) = to praise; give thanks; confess. Common English renderings: praise; thank; confess. Depending on stem, can denote thanksgiving or confession.\par}
