\subsection*{Genesis 30}
\markright{GENESIS 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Rachel having perceived that she bore Jacob no children, was jealous of her sister; and said to Jacob, Give me children; and if not, I shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jacob was angry with Rachel, and said to her, Am I in the place of God, who has deprived you of the fruit of the womb? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Rachel said to Jacob, Behold my handmaid Balla, go in to her, and she shall bear upon my knees, and I also shall have children by her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And she gave him Balla her maid, for a wife to him; and Jacob went in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Balla, Rachel's maid, conceived, and bore Jacob a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Rachel said, God has given judgment for me, and listened to my voice, and has given me a son; therefore she called his name, Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Balla, Rachel's maid, conceived yet again, and bore a second son to Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Rachel said, God has helped me, and I contended with my sister and prevailed; and she called his name, Nephthalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Lea saw that she ceased from bearing, and she took Zelpha her maid, and gave her to Jacob for a wife; and he went in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Zelpha the maid of Lea conceived, and bore Jacob a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Lea said, [It is] happily: and she called his name, Gad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Zelpha the maid of Lea conceived yet again, and bore Jacob a second son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Lea said, I am blessed, for the women will pronounce me blessed; and she called his name, Aser. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Ruben went in the day of barley harvest, and found apples of mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Lea; and Rachel said to Lea her sister, Give me of your son's mandrakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Lea said, [Is it] not enough for you that you have taken my husband, will you also take my son's mandrakes? And Rachel said, Not so: let him lie with you tonight for your son's mandrakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jacob came in out of the field at even; and Lea went forth to meet him, and said, You shall come in to me this day, for I have hired you for my son's mandrakes; and he lay with her that night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And God listened to Lea, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Lea said, God has given me my reward, because I gave my maid to my husband; and she called his name Issachar, which is, Reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Lea conceived again, and bore Jacob a sixth son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Lea said, God has given me a good gift in this time; my husband will choose me, for I have born him six sons: and she called his name, Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And after this she bore a daughter; and she called her name, Dina. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and he opened her womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And she conceived, and bore Jacob a son; and Rachel said, God has taken away my reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And she called his name Joseph, saying, Let God add to me another son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass when Rachel had born Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Restore my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, that I may depart, for you know the service wherewith I have served you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Laban said to him, If I have found grace in your sight, I would augur [well], for the Lord has blessed me at your coming in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Appoint me your wages, and I will give [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Jacob said, You know in what things I have served you, and how many cattle of your are with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For it was little you had before my time, and it is increased to a multitude, and the Lord God has blessed you since my coming; now then, when shall I set up also my own house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Laban said to him, What shall I give you? and Jacob said to him, You shall not give me anything; if you will do this thing for me, I will again tend your flocks and keep them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Let all your sheep pass by today, and separate thence every grey sheep among the rams, and every one that is speckled and spotted among the goats—[this] shall be my reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And my righteousness shall answer for me on the morrow, for it is my reward before you: whatever shall not be spotted and speckled among the goats, and grey among the rams, shall be stolen with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Laban said to him, Let it be according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he separated in that day the spotted and speckled he-goats, and all the spotted and speckled she-goats, and all that was grey among the rams, and every one that was white among them, and he gave them into the hand of his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he set a distance of a three days' journey between them and Jacob. And Jacob tended the cattle of Laban that were left behind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Jacob took to himself green rods of storax tree and walnut and plane tree; and Jacob peeled in them white stripes; and as he drew off the green, the white stripe which he had made appeared alternate on the rods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he laid the rods which he had peeled, in the hollows of the watering-troughs, that whenever the cattle should come to drink, as they should have come to drink before the rods, the cattle might conceive at the rods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} So the cattle conceived at the rods, and the cattle brought forth [young] speckled, and streaked and spotted with ash-colored [spots]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Jacob separated the lambs, and set before the sheep a speckled ram, and every variegated one among the lambs, and he separated flocks for himself alone, and did not mingle them with the sheep of Laban. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And it came to pass in the time wherein the cattle became pregnant, conceiving in the belly, Jacob put the rods before the cattle in the troughs, that they might conceive by the rods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} But he did not put them in [indiscriminately] whenever the cattle happened to bring forth, but the unmarked ones were Laban's, and the marked ones were Jacob's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the man became very rich, and he had many cattle, and oxen, and servants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: qana (קָנָא) = to be jealous; zealous. Common English renderings: jealous; zealous. Can express sinful envy or righteous zeal. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: chevel (חֶבֶל) = cord; region; sorrow. Common English renderings: line; lot; sorrow. A varied term for measuring line, territory, or pain. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: cherpah (חֶרְפָּה) = reproach; disgrace. Common English renderings: reproach; shame. Often a social disgrace removed by divine intervention. \textsuperscript{24} Name meaning: Joseph (Yosef) — He adds; may He add God added to his blessings despite betrayal; savior of his family. \textsuperscript{30} Heb. vocab: me’at (מְעַט) = little; few. Common English renderings: little; few. A term of smallness or insufficiency. \textsuperscript{32} Heb. vocab: keves (כֶּבֶשׂ) = lamb. Common English renderings: lamb. Important sacrificial animal term. \textsuperscript{37} Gk. vocab: rhabdos (ῥάβδος) = rod; staff. Common English renderings: rod; staff. Used literally of staff or rod and figuratively of authority. \textsuperscript{40} Heb. vocab: paras (פָּרַשׂ) = to spread; separate. Common English renderings: spread; divide. Literal and cultic separation term.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when Rachel envied Envy and jealousy are most tormenting passions to the breast which harbours them, vexatious to all around, and introductory to much impatience and ungodliness. "Who is able to stand before envy?"; or else I die \textsuperscript{3} Behold, she shall; have children by her Heb. be built up by her, *marg. \textsuperscript{6} am 2256, bc 1748 God; Dan that is, Judging \textsuperscript{8} great wrestlings Heb. wrestlings of God, ; *marg. and she, ; Naphtali that is, My wrestling; Nephthalim \textsuperscript{9} am 2256, bc 1748 left, gave her \textsuperscript{11} she, ; Gad that is, A troop, or company \textsuperscript{13} am 2257, bc 1747 Happy am I Heb. In my happiness, will call.; and she, ; Asher that is, Happy \textsuperscript{14} am 2256, bc 1748 mandrakes The mandrake may be the Hebrew dudaim . It is so rendered by all the ancient versions, and is a species of melon, of an agreeable odour. Hasselquist, speaking of Nazareth in Galilee, says, "What I found most remarkable at this village was the great number of mandrakes which grew in a vale below it. I had not the pleasure of seeing this plant in blossom, the fruit now (May 5th, O. S.) hanging ripe on the stem, which lay withered on the ground. From the season in which this mandrake blossoms and ripens fruit, one might form a conjecture that it was Rachel's dudaim . These were brought her in the wheat harvest, which in Galilee is in the month of May, about this time, and the mandrake was now in fruit." The Abbee Mariti describes it as growing "low like a lettuce, to which its leaves have a great resemblance, except that they have a dark green colour. The flowers are purple, and the root is for the most part forked. The fruit, when ripe in the beginning of May, is of the size and colour of a small apple, exceedingly ruddy, and of a most agreeable odour. Our guide thought us fools for suspecting it to be unwholesome." \subsection*{Genesis 31}
\markright{GENESIS 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob heard the words of the sons of Laban, saying, Jacob has taken all that was our father's, and of our father's property has he gotten all this glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jacob saw the countenance of Laban, and behold it was not toward him as before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord said to Jacob, Return to the land of your father, and to your family, and I will be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jacob sent and called Lea and Rachel to the plain where the flocks were. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to them, I see the face of your father, that it is not toward me as before, but the God of my father was with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ too know that with all my might I have served your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But your father deceived me, and changed my wages for the ten lambs, yet God gave him not [power] to hurt me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If he should say thus, The speckled shall be your reward, then all the cattle would bear speckled; and if he should say, The white shall be your reward, then would all the cattle bear white. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So God has taken away all the cattle of your father, and given them to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass when the cattle conceived and were with young, that I saw with my eyes in sleep, and behold the he-goats and the rams leaping on the sheep and the she-goats, speckled and variegated and spotted with ash-colored spots. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the angel of God said to me in a dream, Jacob; and I said, What is it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, Look up with your eyes, and behold the he-goats and the rams leaping on the sheep and the she-goats, speckled and variegated and spotted with ash-colored spots; for I have seen all things that Laban does to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I am God that appeared to you in the place of God where you anointed a pillar to me, and vowed to me there a vow; now then arise and depart out of this land, depart into the land of your nativity, and I will be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Rachel and Lea answered and said to him, Have we yet a part or inheritance in the house of our father? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Are we not considered strangers by him? for he has sold us, and quite devoured our money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} All the wealth and the glory which God has taken from our father, it shall be our's and our children's; now then do whatever God has said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jacob arose and took his wives and his children up on the camels; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and he took away all his possessions and all his store, which he had gotten in Mesopotamia, and all that belonged to him, to depart to Isaac his father in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Laban went to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole her father's images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jacob hid [the matter from] Laban the Syrian, so as not to tell him that he ran away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he departed himself and all that belonged to him, and passed over the river, and went into the mountain Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But it was told Laban the Syrian on the third day, that Jacob was fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And having taken his brethren with him, he pursued after him seven days' journey, and overtook him on Mount Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And God came to Laban the Syrian in sleep by night, and said to him, Take heed to yourself that you speak not at any time to Jacob evil things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Laban overtook Jacob; and Jacob pitched his tent in the mountain; and Laban stationed his brothers in the mount Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Laban said to Jacob, What have you done? therefore did you run away secretly, and pillage me, and lead away my daughters as captives taken with the sword? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Whereas if you had told me, I would have sent you away with mirth, and with songs, and timbrels, and harp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And I was not counted worthy to embrace my children and my daughters; now then you have wrought foolishly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And now my hand has power to hurt you; but the God of your father spoke to me yesterday, saying, Take heed to yourself that you speak not evil words to Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Now then go on your way, for you have earnestly desired to depart to the house of your father; therefore have you stolen my gods? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid; for I said, Lest at any time you should take away your daughters from me, and all my possessions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jacob said, With whoever you shall find your gods, he shall not live in the presence of our brethren; take notice of what I have of your property, and take it; and he observed nothing with him, but Jacob knew not that his wife Rachel had stolen them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Laban went in and searched in the house of Lea, and found [them] not; and he went out of the house of Lea, and searched in the house of Jacob, and in the house of the two maidservants, and found them not; and he went also into the house of Rachel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Rachel took the idols, and cast them among the camel's packs, and sat upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And she said to her father, Be not indignant, Sir; I can’t rise up before you, for it is with me according to the manner of women. Laban searched in all the house, and found not the images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Jacob was angry, and strove with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my injustice, and what my sin, that you have pursued after me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and that you have searched all the furniture of my house? what have you found of all the furniture of your house? set it here between your relations and my relations, and let them decide between us two. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} These twenty years have I been with you; your sheep, and your she-goats have not failed in bearing; I devoured not the rams of your cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} That which was taken of beasts I brought not to you; I made good of myself the thefts of the day, and the thefts of the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} I was parched with heat by day, and [chilled] with frost by night, and my sleep departed from my eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} These twenty years have I been in your house; I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years among your sheep, and you did falsely rate my wages for ten lambs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Unless I had the God of my father Abraam, and the fear of Isaac, now you would have sent me away empty; God saw my humiliation, and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you yesterday. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And Laban answered and said to Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the cattle are my cattle, and all things which you see are mine, and [the property] of my daughters; what shall I do to them today, or their children which they bore? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Now then come, let me make a covenant, both I and you, and it shall be for a witness between me and you; and he said to him, Behold, there is no one with us; behold, God is witness between me and you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And Jacob having taken a stone, set it up for a pillar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Jacob said to his brethren, Gather stones; and they gathered stones and made a heap, and ate there upon the heap; and Laban said to him, This heap witnesses between me and you today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And Laban called it, the Heap of Testimony; and Jacob called it, the Witness Heap. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and the pillar, which I have set between me and you; this heap witnesses, and this pillar witnesses; therefore its name was called, the Heap witnesses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And the vision of which he said—Let God look to it between me and you, because we are about to depart from each other, — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} If you shall humble my daughters, if you should take wives in addition to my daughters, see, there is no one with us looking on. God [is] witness between me and you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And Laban said to Jacob, Behold, this heap, and this pillar are a witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} For if I should not cross over to you, neither should you cross over to me, for mischief beyond this heap and this pillar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} The God of Abraam and the God of Nachor judge between us; and Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And he offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his brethren, and they ate and drank, and slept in the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And Laban rose up in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; and Laban having turned back, departed to his place.\par

Noun and verb forms are common in worship and celebration. \textsuperscript{29} Gk. vocab: dynamis (δύναμις) = power; might; force. Common English renderings: power; might. Carries the idea of revolt against rightful authority. \textsuperscript{42} Heb. vocab: pachad (פַּחַד) = fear; dread. Common English renderings: fear; dread. Strong fear term, sometimes a divine epithet in Jacob’s speech. \textsuperscript{54} Heb. vocab: zevach (זֶבַח) = sacrifice; slaughter offering. Common English renderings: sacrifice. Often a fellowship-type slaughter offering. Gk. vocab: thysia (θυσία) = sacrifice. Common English renderings: sacrifice. A key sacrificial term, literal and theological.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Jacob; glory "Glory" is here used for "wealth, " riches, or property; since those who possess riches, generally make them the subject of glory. The original word cavod, signifies both "glory" and "weight." \textsuperscript{2} countenance; it was as before Heb. as yesterday and the day before; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} ten times The Hebrew, âsereth monim, is literally, as Aquila renders, "ten numbers; " and Symmachus, "ten times in number; " which probably implies an indefinite number. (See note on .); God \textsuperscript{10} a dream, ; rams or, he-goats ringstreaked grisled The original word, beroodim, from barad, "hail" means marked with white spots like hail; to which our word grisled, from the old French gresle, now grκle, hail, perfectly agrees; hence greslκ, spotted with white on a dark ground. \textsuperscript{11} the angel, Here am I \textsuperscript{12} Lift up I have seen \textsuperscript{19} images Heb. teraphim, ; These might have been images devoted to superstitious or idolatrous purposes, as they are termed gods by Laban, in . The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan render it, tzalmanaya, "images; " the LXX and Theodoret, ειδολον, "idols; " Aquilla, μορφωματα, "figures; " and the Persian, asterlabha, "astrolabes." \textsuperscript{20} unawares to Laban Heb. the heart of Laban (See note on ). \textsuperscript{24} the Syrian; dream, ; , Take heed; either good or bad Heb. from good to bad \textsuperscript{27} Wherefore, ; steal away from me Heb. hast stolen me, *marg. that I with mirth; tabret \textsuperscript{29} the power; the God, ; , yesternight Take \textsuperscript{32} whomsoever This was rash, and might have produced fatal effects; but Jacob was partial to Rachel, and did not suspect her; and he was indignant at being accused of a crime which he deeply abhorred. Scott., before, ; For Jacob \textsuperscript{34} had taken, furniture The word, car, rendered "furniture, " properly denotes "a large round pannier, " placed one on each side of a camel, for a person, especially women, to ride in. It is a hamper, like a cradle, having a back, head, and sides, like a great chair. Moryson describes them as "two long chairs like cradles, covered with red cloth, to hang on the two sides of the camel." Hanway calls them kedgavays, which "are a kind of covered chairs, which the Persians hang over their camels in the manner of panniers, and are big enough for one person to sit in." Thevenot, who calls then counes, says that they lay over them a cover, which keeps then both from the rain and sun; and Maillet describes them as covered cages, hanging on each side of a camel. The late Editor of Calmet has furnished a correct delineation of these cars, as seen on one side of a camel, copied from Dalton's Prints of Egyptian Figures. searched Heb. felt \textsuperscript{35} my lord; rise up; custom \textsuperscript{39} torn of; I bare or stolen \textsuperscript{44} let us, ; a witness, ; God can put a bridle into the mouth of wicked man to restrain their malice; and then, though they have no love for his people, they will pretend to it, and try to make a merit of necessity. Scott. \textsuperscript{46} brethren, Gather, ; an heap The word gal, rendered "heap, " properly signifies a round heap or circle; probably like the Druidical remains in this country, which have been traced in India, Persia, Western Asia, Greece, and Northern Europe. These usually consist of irregular circles of large stones, with a principal one in the midst; the former probably being used for seats, and the latter for an altar; corresponding to the stone set up as a pillar by Jacob, and the heap of stones collected by his brethren. They appear to have been used, as Gilgal undoubtedly was (; ., . ) as temples, and as places for holding councils, and assembling the people. For a satisfactory elucidation of this subject, consult the Fragments to Calmet, Nos. 156, 735, 736. \textsuperscript{47} Jegarsahadutha i.e. the heap of witness, Chald Galeed i.e., the heap of witness. \subsection*{Genesis 32}
\markright{GENESIS 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob departed for his journey; and having looked up, he saw the host of God encamped; and the angels of God met him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jacob said, when he saw them, This is the Camp of God; and he called the name of that place, Encampments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother to the land of Seir, to the country of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he charged them, saying, Thus shall you⌃ say to my lord Esau: Thus says your servant Jacob; I have sojourned with Laban and tarried until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And there were born to me oxen, and asses, and sheep, and menservants and women-servants; and I sent to tell my lord Esau, that your servant might find grace in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to your brother Esau, and behold! he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jacob was greatly terrified, and was perplexed; and he divided the people that was with him, and the cows, and the camels, and the sheep, into two camps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Jacob said, If Esau should come to one camp, and strike it, the other camp shall be in safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jacob said, God of my father Abraam, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, you [are] he that said to me, Depart quickly to the land of your birth, and I will do you good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let there be to me a sufficiency of all the justice and all the truth which you have wrought with your servant; for with this my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I am become two camps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I am afraid of him, lest haply he should come and strike me, and the mother upon the children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But you said, I will do you good, and will make your seed as the sand of the sea, which shall not be numbered for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he slept there that night, and took of the gifts which he carried [with him], and sent out to Esau his brother, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats, two hundred sheep, twenty rams, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} milch camels, and their foals, thirty, forty kine, ten bulls, twenty asses, and ten colts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he gave them to his servants [each] drove apart; and he said to his servants, Go on before me, and put a space between drove and drove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he charged the first, saying, If Esau my brother meet you, and he ask you, saying, Whose are you? and whither would you go, and whose are these possessions advancing before you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You shall say, Your servant Jacob's; he has sent gifts to my lord Esau, and behold! he is behind us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he charged the first and the second and the third, and all that went before him after these flocks, saying, Thus shall you⌃ speak to Esau when you⌃ find him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and you⌃ shall say, Behold your servant Jacob comes after us. For he said, I will propitiate his countenance with the gifts going before his presence, and afterwards I will behold his face, for perhaps he will accept me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So the presents went on before him, but he himself lodged that night in the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he rose up in that night, and took his two wives and his two servant-maids, and his eleven children, and crossed over the ford of Jaboch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he took them, and passed over the torrent, and brought over all his possessions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he saw that he prevailed not against him; and he touched the broad part of his thigh, and the broad part of Jacob's thigh was benumbed in his wrestling with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he said to him, Let me go, for the day has dawned; but he said, I will not let you go, except you bless me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he said to him, What is your name? and he answered, Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he said to him, Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name; for you have prevailed with God, and shall be mighty with men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Jacob asked and said, Tell me your name; and he said, Therefore do you ask after my name? and he blessed him there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Jacob called the name of that place, the Face of God; for, [said he, ]I have seen God face to face, and my life was preserved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the sun rose upon him, when he passed the Face of God; and he halted upon his thigh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Therefore the children of Israel will by no means eat of the sinew which was benumbed, which is on the broad part of the thigh, until this day, because [the angel] touched the broad part of the thigh of Jacob—[even] the sinew which was benumbed.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{28} Name meaning: Israel (Yisrael) — God contends; strives with God Wrestled with God and prevailed; name of the covenant nation. Heb. vocab: Yisra’el (יִשְׂרָאֵל) = Israel. Common English renderings: Israel. Name of Jacob and of the covenant nation.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} God's; the name;, ; Mahanaim i.e. two hosts, or camps; Mahanaim was situated between Gilead and the river Jabbok, near the present Djezan. \textsuperscript{3} sent; land The land, or mountains, of Seir was situated south and east of the Dead Sea; forming a continuation of the eastern Syrian chain of mountains, beginning with Antilibanus, and extending from thence to the eastern gulf of the Red Sea. Seir, ; country Heb. field Edom \textsuperscript{9} Jacob; O God, ; the Lord \textsuperscript{10} not worthy of the least of all Heb. less than all; mercies; truth; my staff; two bands \textsuperscript{11} Deliver;, ; the mother; with Heb. upon \textsuperscript{13} which to his hand Or, "under his hand" or power; i.e., what Providence had put in his power or possession. a present \textsuperscript{14} This was a princely present. The "thirty milch camels" were particularly valuable; for among the Arabs they constitute a principal part of their riches; being every way so serviceable, that the providence of God appears peculiarly kind and wise in providing such animals for those countries, where no other animal could be of equal service. The she-camel gives milk continually, not ceasing even when with young; the milk of which, when mixed with three parts of water, affords the most pleasant and wholesome beverage. \textsuperscript{20} I will appease; , peradventure; of me Heb. my face \textsuperscript{22} his two wives, ; the ford Jabbok Or, "the ford of Jabbok, " a stream which takes its rise in the mountains of Gilead, and falls into the Jordan to the south of the lake of Gennesareth. It is now called the Zerka. \textsuperscript{23} sent them Heb. caused to pass \textsuperscript{24} wrestled; man, ; breaking of the day Heb. ascending of the morning \textsuperscript{26} Let me go; I will not; thou bless \textsuperscript{28} Thy name, ; Israel i.e. a prince of God as a prince Or, according to the LXX, Vulgate, Houbigant, Dathe, and Rosenmuller, "because thou hast power with God, thou shalt also prevail with men." There is a beautiful antithesis between the two terms, with ΰμδιν, Elohim, God, the Almighty, with ΰπωΡιν, anashim, weak, feeble men, as the word imports; seeing thou hast had power with the Almighty, surely thou shalt prevail over perishing mortals. power; with men \textsuperscript{30} Jacob Peniel; Peniel i.e. the face of God, Peniel, or Penuel, was evidently situated near the ford of Jabbok, on the north of that stream, about forty miles from Jerusalem. I have\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 33}
\markright{GENESIS 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and saw, and behold! Esau his brother coming, and four hundred men with him; and Jacob divided the children to Lea and to Rachel, and the two handmaidens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he put the two handmaidens and their children with the first, and Lea and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But he advanced himself before them, and did reverence to the ground seven times, until he drew near to his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Esau ran on to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him; and they both wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Esau looked up and saw the women and the children, and said, What are these to you? And he said, The children with which God has mercifully blessed your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the maidservants and their children drew near and did reverence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Lea and her children drew near and did reverence; and after this drew near Rachel and Joseph, and did reverence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said, What are these things to you, all these companies that I have met? And he said, That your servant might find grace in your sight, my lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Esau said, I have much, my brother; keep your own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Jacob said, If I have found grace in your sight, receive the gifts through my hands; therefore have I seen your face, as if any one should see the face of God, and you shall be well-pleased with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Receive my blessings, which I have brought you, because God has had mercy on me, and I have all things; and he constrained him, and he took [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, Let us depart, and proceed right onward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to him, My lord knows, that the children are very tender, and the flocks and the herds with me are with young; if then I shall drive them hard one day, all the cattle will die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let my lord go on before his servant, and I shall have strength on the road according to the ease of the journey before me, and according to the strength of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Esau said, I will leave with you some of the people who are with me. And he said, Why so? it is enough that I have found favor before you, [my] lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Esau returned on that day on his journey to Seir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jacob departs to his tents; and he made for himself there habitations, and for his cattle he made booths; therefore he called the name of that place, Booths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jacob came to Salem, a city of Secima, which is in the land of Chanaan, when he departed out of Mesopotamia of Syria, and took up a position in front of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he bought the portion of the field, where he pitched his tent, of Emmor the father of Sychem, for one hundred lambs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he set up there an altar, and called on the God of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: chanan (חָנַן) = to be gracious; show favor. Common English renderings: be gracious; show favor. Used of divine grace and human favor.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{8} What meanest thou by all this drove Heb. What is all this band to thee, to find \textsuperscript{9} have enough; my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself Heb. be that to thee that is thine \textsuperscript{10} if now, ; receive To accept a present from an inferior was a customary pledge of friendship; but returning it implied disaffection. It was on this ground that Jacob was so urgent with Esau to receive his present. I have seen \textsuperscript{11} my blessing; and because; enough Heb. all things; urged him \textsuperscript{14} according as etc. Heb. according to the foot of the work, etc.; and according to the foot of the children. be able; unto Seir \textsuperscript{15} leave Heb. set, or place, What needeth it? Heb. Wherefore is this? find grace \textsuperscript{17} Succoth; not, Succoth i.e. Booths, Succoth was on the east of Jordan, between the brook Jabbok and that river, about 40 miles from Jerusalem, and consequently near Penuel; where a city was afterwards built, which Joshua assigned to the tribe of Gad. Jerome says, that Succoth was in the district of Scythopolis; and the Jews inform us, that the name of Darala was sometime after applied to it. \textsuperscript{18} Shalem The word Shalem in the Samaritan Shalom, should probably be rendered "in peace, " or "in safety; " as it is translated by the Chaldee, Arabic, Coverdale, and Matthewes.; a city of Shechem Or, rather, "the city Shechem, " which was situated in a narrow valley, abounding with springs, between Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, having the former on the north, and the latter on the south; 10 miles from Shiloh, and 34 from Jerusalem. It became the capital of Samaria, after the ruin of the city of that name.; Sychar, Sychem, Padan-aram \textsuperscript{19} bought; Hamor; Emmor pieces of money or, lambs \textsuperscript{20} altar, Elelohe-Israel i.e. God, the God of Israel\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 34}
\markright{GENESIS 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Dina, the daughter of Lea, whom she bore to Jacob, went forth to observe the daughters of the inhabitants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Sychem the son of Emmor the Evite, the ruler of the land, saw her, and took her and lay with her, and humbled her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he was attached to the soul of Dina the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and he spoke kindly to the damsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Sychem spoke to Emmor his father, saying, Take for me this damsel to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jacob heard that the son of Emmor had defiled Dina his daughter (now his sons were with his cattle in the plain). And Jacob was silent until they came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Emmor the father of Sychem went forth to Jacob, to speak to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Jacob came from the plain; and when they heard, the men were deeply pained, and it was very grievous to them, because [the man] wrought folly in Israel, having lain with the daughter of Jacob, and so it must not be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Emmor spoke to them, saying, Sychem my son has chosen in his heart your daughter; give her therefore to him for a wife, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and intermarry with us. Give us your daughters, and take our daughters for your sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And dwell in the midst of us; and, behold, the land is spacious before you, dwell in it, and trade, and get possessions in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Sychem said to her father and to her brothers, I would find grace before you, and we will give whatever you⌃ shall name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Multiply [your demand of] dowry very much, and I will give accordingly as you⌃ shall say to me, only you⌃ shall give me this damsel for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the sons of Jacob answered to Sychem and Emmor his father craftily, and spoke to them, because they had defiled Dina their sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Symeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, said to them, We shall not be able to do this thing, to give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised, for it is a reproach to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Only on these terms will we conform to you, and dwell among you, if you⌃ also will be as we are, in that every male of you be circumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And we will give our daughters to you, and we will take of your daughters for wives to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will be as one race. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But if you⌃ will not listen to us to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the words pleased Emmor, and Sychem the son of Emmor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the young man delayed not to do this thing, for he was much attached to Jacob's daughter, and he was the most honorable of all in his father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Emmor and Sychem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke to the men of their city, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} These men are peaceful, let them dwell with us upon the land, and let them trade in it, and behold the land is extensive before them; we will take their daughters to us for wives, and we will give them our daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Only on these terms will the men conform to us to dwell with us so as to be one people, if every male of us be circumcised, as they also are circumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And shall not their cattle and their herds, and their possessions, be ours? only in this let us conform to them, and they will dwell with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And all that went in at the gate of their city listened to Emmor and Sychem his son, and they were circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin every male. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain, the two sons of Jacob, Symeon and Levi, Dina's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city securely, and killed every male. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they killed Emmor and Sychem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dina out of the house of Sychem, and went forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But the sons of Jacob came upon the wounded, and ravaged the city wherein they had defiled Dina their sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses they took, and all things whatever were in the city, and whatever were in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they took captive all the persons of them, and all their store, and their wives, and plundered both whatever things there were in the city, and whatever things there were in the houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Jacob said to Symeon and Levi, You⌃ have made me hateful so that I should be evil to all the inhabitants of the land, both among the Chananites and the Pherezites, and I am few in number; they will gather themselves against me and cut me in pieces, and I shall be utterly destroyed, and my house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they said, Nay, but shall they treat our sister as an harlot?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{19} Heb. vocab: chafets (חָפֵץ) = to delight in; desire. Common English renderings: delight; desire. Used of pleasure, will, and divine delight. \textsuperscript{25} Heb. vocab: betach (בֶּטַח) = security; safely. Common English renderings: safely; secure. Expresses confidence or safety.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2272, bc 1732 Dinah, the daughter \textsuperscript{2} Shechem, saw her; took her defiled her Heb. humbled her \textsuperscript{3} soul; kindly unto the damsel Heb. to the heart of the damsel; *marg. \textsuperscript{12} Ask me On the practice of purchasing wives, Deut. Lam. Roque says, "Properly speaking, a young man who would marry must purchase his wife; and fathers among the Arabs are never so happy as when they have many daughters. They form part of the riches of the house. Accordingly, when a young man would treat with a person whose daughter he is inclined to marry, he says to him, 'Will you give me your daughter for fifty sheep, for six camels, or for a dozen cows?' according to the rank of her family, and the circumstances of him who desires to marry her." dowry \textsuperscript{24} hearkened In thus falling into this measure, the Shechemites must either have had great affection for their chief and his son, or have been under the influence of the most passive obedience. The petty princes of Asia have always been absolute and despotic; their subjects paying them the most prompt and blind obedience. The following instance will sufficiently illustrate and confirm this statement: Abu Thaher, chief of the Carmathians, about the year 930, with only 500 horse, went to lay siege to Bagdad. The khalif's general marched out to seize him; but before the attack, sent an officer to summon him to surrender. "How many men has the khalif's general?" said Abu Thaher; "30, 000, " replied the officer. "Among them all, " says the Carmathian chief, "has he got three like mine?" Then ordering his followers to approach, he commanded one to stab himself, another to throw himself from a precipice, and a third to plunge into the Tigris. All three instantly obeyed, and perished! Then turning to the officer, he said, "He who has such troops need not value the number of his enemies!" went out, every male \textsuperscript{30} Ye have; , to stink; and I being; and I shall\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 35}
\markright{GENESIS 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And God said to Jacob, Arise, go up to the place, Baethel, and dwell there; and make there an altar to the God that appeared to you, when you fled from the face of Esau your brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jacob said to his house, and to all that were with him, Remove the strange gods that are with you from the midst of you, and purify yourselves, and change your clothes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And let us rise and go up to Baethel, and let us there make an altar to God who listened to me in the day of calamity, who was with me, and preserved me throughout in the journey, by which I went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they gave to Jacob the strange gods, which were in their hands, and the ear-rings which were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the turpentine tree which is in Secima, and destroyed them to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So Israel departed from Secima, and the fear of God was upon the cities round about them, and they did not pursue after the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Jacob came to Luza, which is in the land of Chanaan, which is Baethel, he and all the people that were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he built there an altar, and called the name of the place Baethel; for there God appeared to him, when he fled from the face of his brother Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Deborrha, Rebecca's nurse, died, and was buried below Baethel under the oak; and Jacob called its name, The Oak of Mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God appeared to Jacob once more in Luza, when he came out of Mesopotamia of Syria, and God blessed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And God said to him, Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name; and he called his name Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God said to him, I am your God; increase and multiply; for nations and gatherings of nations shall be of you, and kings shall come out of your loins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the land which I gave to Abraam and Isaac, I have given it to you; and it shall come to pass that I will give this land also to your seed after you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And God went up from him from the place where he spoke with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God spoke with him, [even] a pillar of stone; and offered a libation upon it, and poured oil upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jacob called the name of the place in which God spoke with him, Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [[And Jacob removed from Baethel, and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Gader,]] and it came to pass when he drew near to Chabratha, to enter into Ephratha, Rachel travailed; and in her travail she was in hard labor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass in her hard labor, that the midwife said to her, Be of good courage, for you shall also have this son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass in her giving up the ghost (for she was dying), that she called his name, The son of my pain; but his father called his name Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} So Rachel died, and was buried in the way of the course of Ephratha, this is Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jacob set up a pillar on her tomb; this is the pillar on the tomb of Rachel, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass when Israel lived in that land, that Ruben went and lay with Balla, the concubine of his father Jacob; and Israel heard, and the thing appeared grievous before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the sons of Jacob were twelve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The sons of Lea, the firstborn of Jacob; Ruben, Symeon, Levi, Judas, Issachar, Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the sons of Rachel; Joseph and Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the sons of Balla, the handmaid of Rachel; Dan and Nephthalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the sons of Zelpha, the handmaid of Lea; Gad and Aser. These [are] the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Jacob came to Isaac his father to Mambre, to a city of the plain; this is Chebron in the land of Chanaan, where Abraam and Isaac sojourned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the days of Isaac which he lived were one hundred and eighty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Isaac gave up the ghost and died, and was laid to his family, old and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 36}
\markright{GENESIS 36}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the generations of Esau; this is Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Esau took to himself wives of the daughters of the Chananites; Ada, the daughter of Aelom the Chettite; and Olibema, daughter of Ana the son of Sebegon, the Evite; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and Basemath, daughter of Ismael, sister of Nabaioth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Ada bore to him Eliphas; and Basemath bore Raguel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Olibema bore Jeus, and Jeglom, and Core; these [are] the sons of Esau, which were born to him in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and all his possessions, and all his cattle, and all that he had got, and all things whatever he had acquired in the land of Chanaan; and Esau went forth from the land of Chanaan, from the face of his brother Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For their substance was too great for them to dwell together; and the land of their sojourning could not bear them, because of the abundance of their possessions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Esau lived in mount Seir; Esau, he is Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And these [are] the generations of Esau, the father of Edom in the mount Seir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And these [are] the names of the sons of Esau. Eliphas, the son of Ada, the wife of Esau; and Raguel, the son of Basemath, wife of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the sons of Eliphas were Thaeman, Omar, Sophar, Gothom, and Kenez. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Thamna was a concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau; and she bore Amalec to Eliphas. These [are] the sons of Ada, the wife of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these [are] the sons of Raguel; Nachoth, Zare, Some, and Moze. These were the sons of Basemath, wife of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And these [are] the sons of Olibema, the daughter of Ana, the son of Sebegon, the wife of Esau; and she bore to Esau, Jeus, and Jeglom, and Core. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} These [are] the chiefs of the son of Esau, [even] the sons of Eliphas, the firstborn of Esau; chief Thaeman, chief Omar, chief Sophar, chief Kenez, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} chief Core, chief Gothom, chief Amalec. These [are] the chiefs of Eliphas, in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Ada. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these [are] the sons of Raguel, the son of Esau; chief Nachoth, chief Zare, chief Some, chief Moze. These [are] the chiefs of Raguel, in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, wife of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And these [are] the sons of Olibema, wife of Esau; chief Jeus, chief Jeglom, chief Core. These [are] the chiefs of Olibema, daughter of Ana, wife of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} These [are] the sons of Esau, and these are the chiefs; these are the sons of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And these [are] the sons of Seir, the Chorrhite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, Sobal, Sebegon, Ana, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and Deson, and Asar, and Rison. These [are] the chiefs of the Chorrhite, the son of Seir, in the land of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the sons of Lotan [were] Chorrhi and Haeman; and the sister of Lotan, Thamna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And these [are] the sons of Sobal; Golam, and Manachath, and Gaebel, and Sophar, and Omar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And these [are] the sons of Sebegon; Aie, and Ana; this is the Ana who found Jamin in the wilderness, when he tended the beasts of his father Sebegon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And these [are] the sons of Ana; Deson—and Olibema [was] daughter of Ana. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And these [are] the sons of Deson; Amada, and Asban, and Ithran, and Charrhan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And these [are] the sons of Asar; Balaam, and Zucam, and Jucam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And these [are] the sons of Rison; Hos, and Aran. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And these [are] the chiefs of Chorri; chief Lotan, chief Sobal, chief Sebegon, chief Ana, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} chief Deson, chief Asar, chief Rison. These [are] the chiefs of Chorri, in their principalities in the land of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} these [are] the kings which reigned in Edom, before a king reigned in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Balac, son of Beor, reigned in Edom; and the name of his city [was] Dennaba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Balac died; and Jobab, son of Zara, from Bosorrha reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Jobab died; and Asom, from the land of the Thaemanites, reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Asom died; and Adad son of Barad, who cut off Madiam in the plain of Moab, ruled in his stead; and the name of his city was Getthaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Adad died; and Samada of Massecca reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Samada died; and Saul of Rhooboth by the river reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Saul died; and Ballenon the son of Achobor reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Ballenon the son of Achobor died; and Arad the son of Barad reigned in his stead; and the name of his city was Phogor; and the name of his wife was Metebeel, daughter of Matraith, son of Maizoob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} These [are] the names of the chiefs of Esau, in their tribes, according to their place, in their countries, and in their nations; chief Thamna, chief Gola, chief Jether, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} chief Olibema, chief Helas, chief Phinon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} chief Kenez, chief Thaeman, chief Mazar, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} chief Magediel, chief Zaphoin. These are the chiefs of Edom in their dwelling-places in the land of their possession; this is Esau, the father of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Jacob lived in the land where his father sojourned, in the land of Chanaan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Esau, Adah or, Bashemath, Aholibamah; Judith the daughter We ought, most probably, to read here and in, as in, "the son of Zibeon; " which is the reading of the Samaritan, Septuagint (and Syriac, in ), and which Houbigant and Kennicott contend to be genuine. \textsuperscript{6} am cir, 2264, bc cir, 1740 persons Heb. souls; went \textsuperscript{11} am cir, 2270, bc cir, 1734 Zepho; Zephi \textsuperscript{15} First aristocracy of dukes, from am cir, 2429, to am cir, 2471; from bc cir. 1575, to bc cir. 1533. dukes The word duke is from the Latin dux, a captain or leader, from duco, to lead, guide; which is the exact import of the Hebrew ( ΰμεσ ), alluph, from ΰμσ, to lead, guide; and is here applied to heads of families, chieftains, or princes, who were military leaders.; Eliphaz; duke Teman \textsuperscript{16} Duke Korah As it is certain from, that Eliphaz was Esau's son by Adah, and from and, that Eliphaz had but six sons, "Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, and Amalek; " as is also certain, from and, that Korah was the son of Esau (not Eliphaz) by Aholibamah; and as the words duke Korah are omitted by both the Samaritan text and version, Dr. Kennicott pronounces them to be an interpolation. duke \textsuperscript{22} am cir, 2248, bc 1756 Hemam, Homan Timna \textsuperscript{23} Alvan, Alian Shepho or, Shephi \textsuperscript{30} From am cir, 2093, to am cir, 2429; from bc cir, 1911, to bc cir, 1575 dukess in the \textsuperscript{31} the kings, ; before there Moses may here allude to the promise which God made to Jacob ( ), that kings should proceed from him; and here states that these kings reigned before that prophecy began to be fulfilled. \textsuperscript{33} am cir, 2135, bc cir, 1869 Bozrah, Bezer, or Bostra, was situated in Arabia Deserta, and the eastern part of Edom; and, according to Eusebius, was 24 miles from Edrei. It afterwards belonged to Moab, and was given by Moses to Reuben, but again reverted to Edom. It is now called Boszra; and is described by Burckhardt as the largest town in the Haouran, including its ruins, though only inhabited by about twelve or fifteen families. It is situated in the open plain, two hours distant from Aare, and is at present the last inhabited place in the south-east extremity of the Haouran. It is of an oval shape, it greatest length being from east to west; and its circumference three quarters of an hour. \textsuperscript{34} am cir, 2177, bc cir, 1827 Temani Eusebius places Teman, or Theman, which probably gave name to "the land of Temani, " in Arabia Petrea, five miles from Petra, and says there was a Roman garrison there. \textsuperscript{37} am cir, 2303, bc cir, 1701 Rehoboth \textsuperscript{39} am cir, 2387, bc cir, 1617 Hadar, Hadad Pai, After his death was an aristocracy. \textsuperscript{40} Second aristocracy of dukes, from am cir, 2471, bc cir, 1533; to am cir. 2513, bc cir. 1491. And these.; dukes; Alvah or, Aliah \textsuperscript{43} the dukes, ; their; father, ; the Edomites Heb. Edom\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 37}
\markright{GENESIS 37}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these are the generations of Jacob. And Joseph was seventeen years old, feeding the sheep of his father with his brethren, being young; with the sons of Balla, and with the sons of Zelpha, the wives of his father; and Joseph brought to Israel their father their evil reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was to him the son of old age; and he made for him a coat of many colors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his brethren having seen that his father loved him more than all his sons, hated him, and could not speak anything peaceful to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Joseph dreamed a dream, and reported it to his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to them, Hear this dream which I have dreamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I thought you⌃ were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and my sheaf stood up and was erected, and your sheaves turned round, and did obeisance to my sheaf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And his brethren said to him, Shall you indeed reign over us, or shall you indeed be lord over us? And they hated him still more for his dreams and for his words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he dreamed another dream, and related it to his father, and to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed another dream: as it were the sun, and the moon, and the eleven stars did me reverence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And his father rebuked him, and said to him, What is this dream which you have dreamed? shall indeed both I and your mother and your brethren come and bow before you to the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And his brethren went to feed the sheep of their father to Sychem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Israel said to Joseph, Do not your brethren feed their flock in Sychem? Come, I will send you to them; and he said to him, Behold, I [am here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Israel said to him, Go and see if your brethren and the sheep are well, and bring me word; and he sent him out of the valley of Chebron, and he came to Sychem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And a man found him wandering in the field; and the man asked him, saying, What seek you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said, I am seeking my brethren; tell me where they feed [their flocks]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the man said to him, They have departed hence, for I heard them saying, Let us go to Dothaim; and Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they spied him from a distance before he drew near to them, and they wickedly took counsel to kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And each said to his brother, Behold, that dreamer comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now then come, let us kill him, and cast him into one of the pits; and we will say, An evil wild beast has devoured him; and we shall see what his dreams will be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ruben having heard it, rescued him out of their hands, and said, Let us not kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Ruben said to them, Shed not blood; cast him into one of these pits in the wilderness, but do not lay [your] hands upon him; that he might rescue him out of their hands, and restore him to his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass, when Joseph came to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his many-coloured coat that was upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they took him and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, it had not water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they sat down to eat bread; and having lifted up their eyes they saw, and behold, Ismaelitish travellers came from Galaad, and their camels were heavily loaded with spices, and resin, and myrrh; and they went to bring them to Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Judas said to his brethren, What profit is it if we kill our brother, and conceal his blood? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Come, let us sell him to these Ismaelites, but let not our hands be upon him, because he is our brother and our flesh; and his brethren listened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the men, the merchants of Madian, went by, and they drew and lifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ismaelites for twenty pieces of gold; and they brought Joseph down into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Ruben returned to the pit, and sees not Joseph in the pit; and he tore his garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he returned to his brethren and said, The boy is not; and I, whither am I yet to go? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And having taken the coat of Joseph, they killed a kid of the goats, and stained the coat with the blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they sent the coat of many colors; and they brought it to their father, and said, This have we found; know if it be your son's coat or no. And he recognized it, and said, It is my son's coat, an evil wild beast has devoured him; a wild beast has carried off Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Jacob tore his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And all his sons and his daughters gathered themselves together, and came to comfort him; but he would not be comforted, saying, I will go down to my son mourning to Hades; and his father wept for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Madianites sold Joseph into Egypt; to Petephres, the eunuch of Pharao, captain of the guard.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: yareach (יָרֵחַ) = moon. Common English renderings: moon. Important for calendars, feasts, and poetic imagery. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: ga’ar (גָּעַר) = to rebuke. Common English renderings: rebuke. Strong word for authoritative reprimand. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: baqash (בָּקַשׁ) = to seek. Common English renderings: seek. Often used of seeking God, wisdom, or someone’s life. \textsuperscript{34} Gk. vocab: sakkos (σάκκος) = sackcloth. Common English renderings: sackcloth. Associated with mourning, grief, and repentance.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2276, bc 1728 wherein his father was a stranger Heb. of his father's sojournings, *marg. \textsuperscript{3} loved, son a coat; colours Kethoneth passim, a coat made of stripes of different coloured cloth. \textsuperscript{4} hated him, ; , and could not speak peaceably unto him Or, rather, "and they could not speak peace to him, " i.e., they would not accost him in a friendly manner. They would not even wish him well, in the eastern mode of salutation of, Peace be to thee! It is not an unusual thing for an Arab or Turk to hesitate to return the salâm, if given by a Christian, or by one of whom he has not a favourable opinion; and this may always be considered as an act of hostility. \textsuperscript{9} another dream, the sun, ; stars \textsuperscript{14} see whether it be well with Heb. see the peace of thy brethren, etc.; Hebron \textsuperscript{19} Behold Simulated Irony: Where the words in question are used by man either in dissimulation or hypocrisy. For other instances of this figure, see note on; . dreamer Heb. master of dreams, *marg. \textsuperscript{20} and let;, ; Some; and we \textsuperscript{21} Reuben heard, not kill him Heb. nephesh \textsuperscript{25} they sat; Ishmeelites, ; Gilead; spicery Nechoth, is rendered by the LXX "incense; " Syriac, "resin; " Samaritan, "balsam; " Acquila, "storax; " which is followed by Bochart. This drug is abundant in Syria, and here Moses joins with it resin, honey, and myrrh; which agrees with the nature of the storax, which is the resin of a tree of the same name, of a reddish colour, and peculiarly pleasant fragrance. balm Tzeri, which in Arabic, as a verb, is to flow, seems to be a common name, as balm or balsam with us, for many of those oily, resinous substances, which flow spontaneously, or by incision, from various trees or plants; accordingly the ancients have generally interpreted it resin. myrrh Lot, is probably, as Junius, Deut. Dieu, Celsius, and Ursinus contend, the same as the Arabic ladan, Greek λαδανον, and Latin ladanum . \textsuperscript{27} sell him; let not; he is our, were content Heb. hearkened \textsuperscript{35} his daughters, rose up; For I\par}
