\subsection*{Genesis 38}
\markright{GENESIS 38}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass at that time that Judas went down from his brethren, and came as far as to a certain man of Odollam, whose name was Iras. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Judas saw there the daughter of a Chananitish man, whose name was Sava; and he took her, and went in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And she conceived and bore a son, and called his name, Er. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And she conceived and bore a son again; and called his name, Aunan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she again bore a son; and called his name, Selom: and she was in Chasbi when she bore them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Judas took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Thamar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Er, the firstborn of Judas, was wicked before the Lord; and God killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Judas said to Aunan, Go in to your brother's wife, and marry her as her brother-in-law, and raise up seed to your brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Aunan, knowing that the seed should not be his—it came to pass when he went in to his brother's wife, that he spilled [it] upon the ground, so that he should not give seed to his brother's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And his doing this appeared evil before God; and he killed him also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Judas said to Thamar, his daughter-in-law, Sit you a widow in the house of your father-in-law, until Selom my son be grown; for he said, lest he also die as his brethren; and Thamar departed, and sat in the house of her father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the days were fulfilled, and Sava the wife of Judas died; and Judas, being comforted, went to them that sheared his sheep, himself and Iras his Shepherd the Odollamite, to Thamna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it was told Thamar his daughter-in-law, saying, Behold, your father-in-law goes up to Thamna, to shear his sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And having taken off the garments of her widowhood from her, she put on a veil, and ornamented her face, and sat by the gates of Aenan, which is in the way to Thamna, for she saw that Selom was grown; but he gave her not to him for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when Judas saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; for she covered her face, and he knew her not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he went out of his way to her, and said to her, Let me come in to you; for he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law; and she said, What will you give me if you should come in to me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, I will send you a kid of the goats from my flock; and she said, [Well], if you will give me an earnest, until you send it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said, What is the earnest that I shall give you? and she said, Your ring, and your bracelet, and the staff in your hand; and he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And she arose and departed, and took her veil from off her, and put on the garments of her widowhood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Judas sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd the Odollamite, to receive the pledge from the woman; and he found her not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he asked the men of the place, Where is the harlot who was in Aenan by the wayside? and they said, There was no harlot here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he returned to Judas, and said, I have not found her; and the men of the place say, There is no harlot here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Judas said, Let her have them, but let us not be ridiculed; I sent this kid, but you have not found her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it came to pass after three months, that it was told Judas, saying, Thamar your daughter-in-law has grievously played the harlot, and behold she is with child by whoredom; and Judas said, Bring her out, and let her be burnt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And as they were bringing her, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, I am with child by the man whose these things are; and she said, See whose is this ring and bracelet and staff. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Judas knew [them], and said, Thamar is cleared rather than I, forasmuch as I gave her not to Selom my son: and he knew her not again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass when she was in labor, that she also had twins in her womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it came to pass as she was bringing forth, one thrust forth his hand, and the midwife having taken hold of it, bound upon his hand a scarlet [thread], saying, This one shall come out first. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And when he drew back his hand, then immediately came forth his brother; and she said, Why has the barrier been cut through because of you? and she called his name, Phares. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And after this came forth his brother, on whose hand was the scarlet thread; and she called his name, Zara.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Gk. vocab: kakia (κακία) = badness; malice. Common English renderings: malice; evil. Often denotes moral badness or malice. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: almanah (אַלְמָנָה) = widow. Common English renderings: widow. Another key vulnerable class under divine concern. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: matteh (מַטֶּה) = staff; tribe. Common English renderings: rod; tribe. Overlaps with tribe terminology and authority symbolism. Heb. vocab: chatam (חָתַם) = to seal. Common English renderings: seal. Used for sealing documents, certainty, and concealment. \textsuperscript{24} Gk. vocab: porneia (πορνεία) = sexual immorality. Common English renderings: fornication. A broad sexual-sin term shaped by biblical moral law. \textsuperscript{26} Gk. vocab: dikaioō (δικαιόω) = to justify; declare righteous. Common English renderings: justify. A crucial judicial and theological verb represented by its lexical form.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 39}
\markright{GENESIS 39}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Petephres the eunuch of Pharao, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ismaelites, who brought him down there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house with his lord the Egyptian. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and the Lord prospers in his hands whatever he happens to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joseph found grace in the presence of his lord, and was well-pleasing to him; and he set him over his house, and all that he had he gave into the hand of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass after that he was set over his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the Lord was on all his possessions in the house, and in his field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he committed all that he had into the hands of Joseph; and he knew not of anything that belonged to him, save the bread which he himself ate. And Joseph was handsome in form, and exceedingly beautiful in countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, Lie with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But he would not; but said to his master's wife, If because of me my master knows nothing in his house, and has given into my hands all things that belong to him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and in this house there is nothing above me, nor has anything been kept back from me, but you, because you are his wife—how then shall I do this wicked thing, and sin against God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when she talked with Joseph day by day, and he listened not to her to sleep with her, so as to be with her, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} it came to pass on a certain day, that Joseph went into the house to do his business, and there was no one of the household within. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And she caught hold of him by his clothes, and said, Lie with me; and having left his clothes in her hands, he fled, and went forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his clothes in her hands, and fled, and gone forth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} that she called those that were in the house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he has brought in to us a Hebrew servant to mock us—he came in to me, saying, Lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, having left his clothes with me, he fled, and went forth out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So she leaves the clothes by her, until the master came to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, whom you brought in to us, came in to me to mock me, and said to me, I will lie with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, having left his clothes with me, he fled and departed forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass, when his master heard all the words of his wife, that she spoke to him, saying, Thus did your servant to me, that he was very angry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And his master took Joseph, and cast him into the prison, into the place where the king's prisoners are kept, there in the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord was with Joseph, and poured down mercy upon him; and he gave him favor in the sight of the chief keeper of the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the chief keeper of the prison gave the prison into the hand of Joseph, and all the prisoners as many as were in the prison; and all things whatever they do there, he did them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Because of him the chief keeper of the prison knew nothing, for all things were in the hand of Joseph, because the Lord was with him; and whatever things he did, the Lord made them to prosper in his hands.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2276, bc 1728 Joseph; the Ishmeelites \textsuperscript{6} he left, ; save; a goodly person Yephaih toar, weephaih maraih, "beautiful in person and beautiful in countenance." Joseph's beauty is so celebrated in the East, that a handsome man is frequently compared to him; and the Persian poets vie with each other in descriptions of his comeliness. \textsuperscript{10} as she spake;, or to be \textsuperscript{14} he hath The base affection of this woman being disappointed, was changed into rancorous hatred, and she exults in the opportunity of being revenged on Joseph. She begins her accusation in the affected language of offended modesty, rage, and disdain, by charging her husband, whom we may reasonably assume she did not greatly love, with being an accessory to the indignity she pretended to have received: "He hath brought in a Hebrew, " a very abomination to an Egyptian, "to mock us, " insult and treat me in a base, unworthy manner. an Hebrew, ; he came; , loud Heb. great \textsuperscript{20} into the prison Baith hassohar, "the round house, " from the form of the building according to some; or, "the watch or guard house, " from the Arabic sahara, to watch, according to others.; the king's \textsuperscript{21} the Lord, ; , showed him mercy Heb. extended kindness unto him gave him\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 40}
\markright{GENESIS 40}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after these things, that the chief cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker trespassed against their lord the king of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Pharao was angry with his two eunuchs, with his chief cupbearer, and with his chief baker. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he put them in ward, into the prison, into the place whereinto Joseph had been led. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the chief keeper of the prison committed them to Joseph, and he stood by them; and they were [some] days in the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they both had a dream in one night; and the vision of the dream of the chief cupbearer and chief baker, who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were in the prison, was this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Joseph went in to them in the morning, and saw them, and they had been troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he asked the eunuchs of Pharao who were with him in the prison with his master, saying, Why is it that your countenances are sad today? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said to him, We have seen a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, Is not the interpretation of them through god? tell [them] than to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the chief cupbearer related his dream to Joseph, and said, In my dream a vine was before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And in the vine [were] three stems; and it budding shot forth blossoms; the clusters of grapes were ripe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the cup of Pharao was in my hand; and I took the bunch of grapes, and squeezed it into the cup, and gave the cup into Pharao's hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Joseph said to him, This is the interpretation of it. The three stems are three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Yet three days and Pharao shall remember your office, and he shall restore you to your place of chief cupbearer, and you shall give the cup of Pharao into his hand, according to your former high place, as you were wont to be cupbearer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But remember me of yourself, when it shall be well with you, and you shall deal mercifully with me, and you shall make mention of me to Pharao, and you shall bring me forth out of this dungeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For surely I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here I have done nothing, but they have cast me into this pit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the chief baker saw that he interpreted aright; and he said to Joseph, I also saw a dream, and I thought I took up on my head three baskets of mealy food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And in the upper basket there was the work of the baker of every kind which Pharao eats; and the fowls of the air ate them out of the basket that was on my head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joseph answered and said to him, This is the interpretation of it; The three baskets are three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Yet three days, and Pharao shall take away your head from off you, and shall hang you on a tree, and the birds of the sky shall eat your flesh from off you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass on the third day that it was Pharao's birth-day, and he made a banquet for all his servants, and he remembered the office of the cupbearer and the office of the baker in the midst of his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he gave the cup into Pharao's hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph, interpreted to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Yet did not the chief cupbearer remember Joseph, but forgot him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: patar (פָּתַר) = to interpret. Common English renderings: interpret. Especially associated with dream interpretation. \textsuperscript{10} Gk. vocab: anthos (ἄνθος) = flower; blossom. Common English renderings: flower. A natural image often associated with transience. \textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: potērion (ποτήριον) = cup. Common English renderings: cup. Literal cup and figurative portion both occur. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: shakach (שָׁכַח) = to forget. Common English renderings: forget. Used literally and covenantally for neglect or unfaithfulness.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} it came; the butler Mashkeh, from shakah, to give drink, is the same as saky among the Arabians and Persians, and signifies a cup-bearer. \textsuperscript{2} wroth;, ; the chief of the butlers \textsuperscript{3} the place, where Joseph was bound Or, "where Joseph was confined, " for he doubtless had his personal liberty. This place, we learn from the preceding chapter ( ), was the king's prison. All the officers in the employment of the ancient kings of Egypt, according to Diodorus Siculus, were taken from the most illustrious families of the priesthood in the country; no slave or common person being ever permitted to serve in the presence of the king. As these persons were of the most noble families, it is natural to expect they would be put, when accused, into the state prison. \textsuperscript{4} the captain, ; a season Yamim, literally days; how long is uncertain, though the word may signify, as many suppose, a complete year (see note on and see note on ); and as Pharaoh called them to an account on his birthday ( ), Calmet supposes they had offended on the preceding birthday, and thus had been one whole year in prison. \textsuperscript{7} Wherefore; look ye so sadly to day Heb. are your faces evil \textsuperscript{11} And I took etc. From this we find that wine anciently was the mere expressed juice of the grape, without fermentation. The saky, or cup-bearer, took the bunch, pressed the juice into the cup, and instantly delivered it to his master. pressed; hand \textsuperscript{13} within shall; lift up thine head or, reckon, *marg. *marg. \textsuperscript{14} think on me Heb. remember me with thee on me; show \textsuperscript{16} the chief white baskets or, baskets full of holes \textsuperscript{17} bakemeats Heb. meat of Pharaoh, the work of a baker, or cook \textsuperscript{19} within lift up thy head from off thee or, reckon thee and take thy office from thee hang thee; and the birds \textsuperscript{20} third day, birthday; lifted up or, reckoned, *marg.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 41}
\markright{GENESIS 41}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after two full years that Pharao had a dream. He thought he stood upon [the bank of] the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And behold, there came up as it were out of the river seven cows, fair in appearance, and choice of flesh, and they fed on the sedge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And other seven cows came up after these out of the river, ill-favoured and lean-fleshed, and fed by the [other] cows on the bank of the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the seven ill-favoured and lean cows devoured the seven well-favoured and choice-fleshed cows; and Pharao awoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he dreamed again. And, behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, choice and good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And, behold, seven ears thin and blasted with the wind, grew up after them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the seven thin ears and blasted with the wind devoured the seven choice and full ears; and Pharao awoke, and it was a dream. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it was morning, and his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt, and all her wise men; and Pharao related to them his dream, and there was no one to interpret it to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharao, saying, I this day remember my fault: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Pharao was angry with his servants, and put us in prison in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And we had a dream both in one night, I and he; we saw, each according to his dream. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew servant of the captain of the guard; and we related to him [our dreams], and he interpreted [them] to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass, as he interpreted them to us, so also it happened, both that I was restored to my office, and that he was hanged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Pharao having sent, called Joseph; and they brought him out from the prison, and shaved him, and changed his dress, and he came to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Pharao said to Joseph, I have seen a vision, and there is no one to interpret it; but I have heard say concerning you that you did hear dreams and interpret them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joseph answered Pharao and said, Without God an answer of safety shall not be given to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Pharao spoke to Joseph, saying, In my dream I thought I stood by the bank of the river; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and there came up as it were out of the river, seven cows well-favoured and choice-fleshed, and they fed on the sedge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And behold seven other cows came up after them out of the river, evil and ill-favoured and lean-fleshed, such that I never saw worse in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the seven ill-favoured and thin cows ate up the seven first good and choice cows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they went into their bellies; and it was not perceptible that they had gone into their bellies, and their appearance was ill-favoured, as also at the beginning; and after I awoke I slept, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and saw again in my sleep, and as it were seven ears came up on one stem, full and good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And other seven ears, thin and blasted with the wind, sprang up close to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the seven thin and blasted ears devoured the seven fine and full ears: so I spoke to the interpreters, and there was no one to explain it to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joseph said to Pharao, The dream of Pharao is one; whatever God does, he has shown to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream of Pharao is one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the seven thin kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven thin and blasted ears are seven years; there shall be seven years of famine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And as for the word which I have told Pharao, whatever God intends to do, he has shown to Pharao: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} behold, for seven years there is coming great plenty in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But there shall come seven years of famine after these, and they shall forget the plenty that shall be in all Egypt, and the famine shall consume the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of the famine that shall be after this, for it shall be very grievous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And concerning the repetition of the dream to Pharao twice, [it is] because the saying which is from God shall be true, and God will hasten to accomplish it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Now then, look out a wise and prudent man, and set him over the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And let Pharao make and appoint local governors over the land; and let them take up a fifth part of all the produce of the land of Egypt for the seven years of the plenty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And let them gather all the food of these seven good years that are coming, and let the corn be gathered under the hand of Pharao; let food be kept in the cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the stored food shall be for the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; and the land shall not be utterly destroyed by the famine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the word was pleasing in the sight of Pharao, and in the sight of all his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Pharao said to all his servants, Shall we find such a man as this, who has the Spirit of God in him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Pharao said to Joseph, Since God has showed you all these things, there is not a wiser or more prudent man than you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} You shall be over my house, and all my people shall be obedient to your word; only in the throne will I excel you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Pharao said to Joseph, Behold, I set you this day over all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Pharao took his ring off his hand, and put it on the hand of Joseph, and put on him a robe of fine linen, and put a necklace of gold about his neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And he mounted him on the second of his chariots, and a herald made proclamation before him; and he set him over all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Pharao said to Joseph, I am Pharao; without you no one shall lift up his hand on all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And Pharao called the name of Joseph, Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Aseneth, the daughter of Petephres, priest of Heliopolis, to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharao, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharao, and went through all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And the land produced, in the seven years of plenty, [whole] handfuls [of corn]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And he gathered all the food of the seven years, in which was the plenty in the land of Egypt; and he laid up the food in the cities; the food of the fields of a city round about it he laid up in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And Joseph gathered very much corn as the sand of the sea, until it could not be numbered, for there was no number [of it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And to Joseph were born two sons, before the seven years of famine came, which Aseneth, the daughter of Petephres, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And Joseph called the name of the firstborn, Manasse; for God, [said he], has made me forget all my toils, and all my father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And he called the name of the second, Ephraim; for God, [said he], has increased me in the land of my humiliation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And the seven years of plenty passed away, which were in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And the seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph said; and there was a famine in all the land; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And all the land of Egypt was hungry; and the people cried to Pharao for bread. And Pharao said to all the Egyptians, Go to Joseph, and do whatever he shall tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And the famine was on the face of all the earth; and Joseph opened all the granaries, and sold to all the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And all countries came to Egypt to buy of Joseph, for the famine prevailed in all the earth.\par

Associated with kneeling or subjection. \textsuperscript{55} Heb. vocab: ra’ev (רָעֵב) = to hunger. Common English renderings: hunger. Used of famine and individual need.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2289, bc 1715 two full years Shenathayim yamim, "two years of days, " two complete solar revolutions; as a month of days is a full month. that Pharaoh, ; 7:1-8:27; the river \textsuperscript{2} there came a meadow Or, rather, "on, or among the reeds or sedges; " for so achoo is generally supposed to denote (see note on ); so called, according to Mr. Parkhurst, from its fitness for making ropes, or the like, to connect or join things together, from achah, to join, connect. Thus the Latin juncus, a bulrush, a jungendo, from joining, for the same reason. He supposes it to be that sort of reed growing near the Nile which Hasselquist describes as "having scarce any branches, but numerous leaves, which are narrow, smooth, channelled on the upper surface, and the plant about eleven feet high. The Egyptians make ropes of the leaves." \textsuperscript{5} seven ears A species of wheat, which grows in Egypt, bears, when perfect, seven ears on one stalk, as its natural conformation. It differs from ours in having a solid stem, or at least a stem full of pith, in order to yield sufficient nourishment and support to so great a weight as the ears which it bears. rank Heb. fat \textsuperscript{8} his spirit;, ; the magicians of Egypt The word here used ( chartummim ) may mean no more than interpreters of abstruse or difficult subjects; especially of dreams and visions, which formed a considerable part of the ancient pagan religion; and the Egyptian priests were the first who professed this art. The word may be of affinity with, or derived from, the Persian chiradmand, wise, learned, judicious, intelligent, from chirad, understanding, judgment, and mand, endowed with. They seem to have been such persons as Josephus calls sacred scribes; or professors of sacred learning., ; , ; the wise men; but there \textsuperscript{14} sent; and they brought him hastily Heb. made him run; he shaved \textsuperscript{15} I have heard; that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it or, when thou hearest a dream, thou canst interpret it \textsuperscript{21} eaten them up Heb. come to the inward parts of them; still \textsuperscript{23} withered or, small thin; , blasted All the mischief done to corn or fruit by blasting, smutting, mildew, etc. are attributed to the east wind (see parallel passages). In Egypt it is peculiarly destructive, because it comes through the parched deserts of Arabia, often destroying vast numbers of people. The destructive nature of the Sam, Simoom, Smoom, or Samiel, is mentioned by almost all travellers. When this pestilential wind advances, its approach is indicated by a redness in the air. The principal stream of the blast always moves in a line of about 20 yards in breadth, and 12 feet above the surface of the earth; but its parching influence pervades all places to a considerable distance. The only means of preservation from its noxious influence is to lie flat, with the face upon the ground, till the blast be over. Camels and other animals instinctively perceive its approach, and bury their mouths and nostrils in the ground. It rarely last more than seven or eight minutes, but so poisonous are its effects, that it instantly suffocates those who are unfortunate enough to inhale it. \textsuperscript{26} are or, signify, ; good ears are seven the dream is one \textsuperscript{30} seven years; shall be; consume \textsuperscript{31} the plenty It is well known, that in Egypt there is scarcely any rain, the country depending for its fertility upon the overflowing of the Nile; and that the fertility is in proportion to the duration and quality of the overflow, in order to saturate the land and prepare for the seed. Pliny has given a scale, by which the plenty or dearth may be ascertained; which may be considered as perfectly correct. The ordinary height of the inundations is 16 cubits. When the waters are lower than this standard, they do not overflow the whole ground; when above this standard they are too long in running off. In the first case, the ground is not saturated; by the second, the waters are detained so long on the ground that seed-time is lost. The province marks both. If it rise only 12 cubits, a famine is the consequence; at 13 hunger prevails; 14 produces general rejoicing; 15 perfect security; and 16 all the luxuries of life. grievous Heb. heavy \textsuperscript{32} doubled; it is because; established by or, prepared of \textsuperscript{34} officers or, overseers; and take \textsuperscript{36} that the perish not Heb. be not cut off \textsuperscript{40} Thou shalt, ; , be ruled Heb. be armed, or kiss \textsuperscript{42} his ring, ; fine linen or, silk, a gold chain \textsuperscript{43} and they Bow the knee or, Tender father, Heb. Abrech, ruler \textsuperscript{45} Zaphnathpaaneah Which in Coptic signifies a revealer of secrets, or, the man to whom secrets are revealed. Jerome says this name signified in Egyptian, Savatorem mundi, "the Saviour of the world; " and Psotem - phaneh, in Coptic, is certainly "salvation of the world, " from C Ω T, for σωτηρια, salvation, em, the sign of the genitive case, and ΦΕΝΕΗ, world. If this interpretation be correct, Pharaoh must have meant Egypt by the world, or which Joseph might be justly termed the Saviour. We know that the Romans called their empire Universis Orbis-Orbis Terrarum, "all the world:" the Chinese say the same of their empire at the present day, and the phrase is used in the East: Nadir Shah is described on his coins as "Conqueror of the World, " i.e., Persia. \subsection*{Genesis 42}
\markright{GENESIS 42}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob having seen that there was a sale [of corn] in Egypt, said to his sons, Why are you⌃ indolent? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt; go down there, and buy for us a little food, that we may live, and not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the ten brethren of Joseph went down to buy corn out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But [Jacob] sent not Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, with his brethren; for he said, Lest, haply, disease befall him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sons of Israel came to buy with those that came, for the famine was in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joseph was ruler of the land; he sold to all the people of the land. And the brethren of Joseph, having come, did reverence to him, [bowing] with the face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when Joseph saw his brethren, he knew them, and estranged himself from them, and spoke hard words to them; and said to them, Whence are you⌃ come? And they said, Out of the land of Chanaan, to buy food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joseph remembered his dream, which he saw; and he said to them, You⌃ are spies; to observe the marks of the land are you⌃ come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But they said, Nay, Sir, we your servants are come to buy food; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} we are all sons of one man; we are peaceful, your servants are not spies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said to them, Nay, but you⌃ are come to observe the marks of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they said, We your servants are twelve brethren, in the land of Chanaan; and, behold, the youngest is with our father today, but the other one is not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Joseph said to them, This is it that I spoke to you, saying, you⌃ are spies; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} herein shall you⌃ be manifested; by the health of Pharao, you⌃ shall not depart hence, unless your younger brother come here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Send one of you, and take your brother; and go you⌃ to prison, till your words be clear, whether you⌃ speak the truth or not; but, if not, by the health of Pharao, verily you⌃ are spies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he put them in prison three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to them on the third day, This do, and you⌃ shall live, for I fear God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} If you⌃ be peaceful, let one of your brethren be detained in prison; but go you⌃, and carry back the corn you⌃ have purchased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And bring your younger brother to me, and your words shall be believed; but, if not, you⌃ shall die. And they did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And each said to his brother, Yes, indeed, for we are in fault concerning our brother, when we disregarded the anguish of his soul, when he implored us, and we listened not to him; and therefore has this affliction come upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Ruben answered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Hurt not the boy, and you⌃ heard me not? and, behold, his blood is required. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But they knew not that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Joseph turned away from them, and wept; and again he came to them, and spoke to them; and he took Symeon from them, and bound him before their eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joseph gave orders to fill their vessels with corn, and to return their money to each into his sack, and to give them provision for the way; and it was so done to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And having put the corn on the asses, they departed thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And one having opened his sack to give his asses fodder, at the place where they rested, saw also his bundle of money, for it was on the mouth of his sack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he said to his brethren, My money has been restored to me, and behold this is in my sack. And their heart was wonder-struck, and they were troubled, saying one to another, What is this that God has done to us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they came to their father, Jacob, into the land of Chanaan, and reported to him all that had happened to them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The man, the lord of the land, spoke harsh words to us, and put us in prison as spies of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And we said to him, We are men of peace, we are not spies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} We are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is with his father today in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, Herein shall I know that you⌃ are peaceful; leave one brother here with me, and having taken the corn you⌃ have purchased for your family, depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And bring to me your younger brother; then I shall know that you⌃ are not spies, but that you⌃ are men of peace: and I will restore you your brother, and you⌃ shall trade in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And it came to pass as they were emptying their sacks, there was each man's bundle of money in his sack; and they and their father saw their bundles of money, and they were afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And their father Jacob said to them, You⌃ have bereaved me. Joseph is not, Symeon is not, and will you⌃ take Benjamin? all these things have come upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Ruben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to you; give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} But he said, My son shall not go down with you, because his brother is dead, and he only has been left; and [suppose] it shall come to pass that he is afflicted by the way by which you⌃ go, then you⌃ shall bring down my old age with sorrow to Hades.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when Jacob; saw i.e. heard, from the report of others, that there was plenty in Egypt. The operations of one sense are frequently put for those of another in Hebrew (see the parallel passages).; Why do ye \textsuperscript{6} governor Shallit, an intendant, protector, ruler, from shalat, to be over or a protector, to rule. Hence the Arabic salita, to obtain and exercise dominion, rule; and sultân, ruler, lord, prince, and king., ; he it was bowed \textsuperscript{7} roughly unto them Heb. hard things with them \textsuperscript{9} remembered Ye are spies Persons who, under the pretence of wishing to buy corn, desire only to find out whether the land be so defenceless that the tribes to which you belong may attack it successfully, drive out the inhabitants, and settle themselves in it; or, having plundered it, retire into their deserts. This is a frequent custom among the Arabs to the present day., ; nakedness \textsuperscript{11} We are etc. We do not belong to different tribes; and it is not likely that one family would make a hostile attempt upon a whole kingdom; nor, if any serious design had been intended, that one man would have sent his sons on so hazardous an expedition. true men \textsuperscript{13} Thy servants, ;, ; 1Chr. 2:1-8:40 one is not \textsuperscript{16} kept in prison Heb. bound \textsuperscript{21} they said; we saw; this distress \textsuperscript{23} he spake unto them by an interpreter Heb. an interpreter was between them, The mailitz does not seem to have been an interpreter in our sense of the term; as we have many evidences in this book that the Egyptians, Hebrews, Canaanites, and Syrians, could understand each other in a general way; and it appears from several passages in this very chapter (particularly ), that Joseph and his brethren understood each others' language, as his brethren and Joseph's steward also did (, etc; compare and ). It seems to denote an officer who is called in Abyssinia, according to Mr. Bruce, Kal Hatze, "the voice or word of the king, " who always stands at the side of a lattice window of a balcony, within which the king sits; who is never seen, but who speaks through a hole in the side of it, covered in the inside with a curtain, to this officer, by whom he speaks to the persons present. \textsuperscript{25} commanded; to give them; and thus \textsuperscript{27} the inn; inn Malon, from loon, to stay, abide, lodge, denotes any place to stay and lodge in, particularly a place where travellers usually stop to lodge, which is generally near a well, where they fill their girbehs, or leathern bottles, with fresh water, and having unladen and clogged their camels, asses, etc., permit them to crop any little verdure there may be in the place, keeping watch over them by turns. Our word inn here gives us a false idea, there were no such places of entertainment in the desert which Joseph's brethren had to pass; nor are there any at the present day. The only accommodation such a place affords is either a well, or a khan, or caravanserai, which is generally no more than four bare walls, perfectly exposed, the place being open at the top, and furnishing a wretched lodging, and even these, it is probable, were not in use at this early period. \textsuperscript{28} their heart; failed them Heb. went forth, This refers to the spasmodic affection which is felt in the breast at any sudden alarm or fright. What is \textsuperscript{30} roughly to us Heb. with us hard things \textsuperscript{36} Me have ye, all these things are against me Alay hayoo cullanah, literally, "upon me are all these things:" rendered by the Vulgate, in me hec omnia mala reciderunt, "all these evils fall back upon me; " they lie upon me as heavy loads, hastening my death. They are more than I can bear. \textsuperscript{38} his brother, if mischief, bring\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 43}
\markright{GENESIS 43}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But the famine prevailed in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass, when they had finished eating the corn which they had brought out of Egypt, that their father said to them, Go again; buy us a little food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Judas spoke to him, saying, The man, the lord of the country, positively testified to us, saying, You⌃ shall not see my face, unless your younger brother be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If, then, you send our brother with us, we will go down, and buy you food; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} but if you send not our brother with us, we will not go: for the man spoke to us, saying, You⌃ shall not see my face, unless your younger brother be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Israel said, Why did you⌃ harm me, inasmuch as you⌃ told the man that you⌃ had a brother? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they said, The man closely questioned us about our family also, saying, Does your father yet live, and have you⌃ a brother? and we answered him according to this question: did we know that he would say to us, Bring your brother? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Judas said to his father Israel, Send the boy with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you, and our store. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I engage for him; at my hand do you require him; if I bring him not to you, and place him before you, I shall be guilty toward you for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For if we had not tarried, we should now have returned twice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Israel, their father, said to them, If it be so, do this; take of the fruits of the earth in your vessels, and carry down to the man presents of gum and honey, and frankincense, and stacte, and turpentine, and walnuts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And take double money in your hands, and the money that was returned in your sacks, carry back with you, lest perhaps it is a mistake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And take your brother; and arise, go down to the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And my God give you favor in the sight of the man, and send away your other brother, and Benjamin, for I accordingly as I have been bereaved, am bereaved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the men having taken these presents, and the double money, took in their hands also Benjamin; and they rose up and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joseph saw them and his brother Benjamin, born of the same mother; and he said to the steward of his household, Bring the men into the house, and kill beasts and make ready, for the men are to eat bread with me at noon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the man did as Joseph said; and he brought the men into the house of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the men, when they perceived that they were brought into the house of Joseph, said, We are brought in because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first; even in order to inform against us, and lay it to our charge; to take us for servants, and our asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And having approached the man who was over the house of Joseph, they spoke to him in the porch of the house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} saying, We pray [you], Sir; we came down at first to buy food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass, when we came to unlade, and opened our sacks, [there was] also this money of each in his sack; we have now brought back our money by weight in our hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And we have brought other money with us to buy food; we know not who put the money into our sacks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he said to them, [God deal] mercifully with you; be not afraid; your God, and the God of your fathers, has given you treasures in your sacks, and I have enough of your good money. And he brought Symeon out to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he brought water to wash their feet; and gave provender to their asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they prepared their gifts, until Joseph came at noon, for they heard that he was going to dine there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joseph entered into the house, and they brought him the gifts which they had in their hands, into the house; and they did him reverence with their face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he asked them, How are you⌃? and he said to them, Is your father, the old man of whom you⌃ spoke, well? Does he yet live? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they said, Your servant our father is well; he is yet alive. And he said, Blessed be that man by God; —and they bowed, and did him reverence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Joseph lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, born of the same mother; and he said, Is this your younger brother, whom you⌃ spoke of bringing to me? and he said, God have mercy on you, my son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Joseph was troubled, for his bowels yearned over his brother, and he sought to weep; and he went into his chamber, and wept there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he washed his face and came out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they set on [bread] for him alone, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians feasting with him by themselves, for the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for it is an abomination to the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his seniority, and the younger according to his youth; and the men looked with amazement every one at his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And they took their portions from him to themselves; but Benjamin's portion was five times as much as the portions of [the others]. And they drank and were filled with drink with him.\par

Devash, honey, is supposed by some not to have been that produced by bees, but a syrup produced from ripe dates. The Jewish doctors observe, that the word in signifies dates; and the Arabians, at this day, call the choicest dates preserved with butter, dabous, and the honey obtained from them, dibs, or dabs . Benanim, nuts signifies pistachio nuts, the finest thing found in Syria; but, according to the others, a small nut, the produce of a species of the turpentine tree. But, as we learn from, compared with this verse, that the provision for the entertainment of the Egyptians themselves was animal food, this reason cannot be just. The true reason seems to be that assigned by the LXX, Βδελυγμα γαρ εστιν τοις Αιγυπτιοις πας ποιμην προβατων; "For every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians." \textsuperscript{34} messes was five times Sir John Chardin observes, that "in Persia, Arabia, and the Indies, there are some houses where they place several plates in large salvers, and set one of these before each person, or before two or three, according to the magnificence of each house. \subsection*{Genesis 44}
\markright{GENESIS 44}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joseph charged the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put the money of each in the mouth of his sack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And put my silver cup into the sack of the youngest, and the price of his corn. And it was done according to the word of Joseph, as he said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The morning dawned, and the men were sent away, they and their asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when they had gone out of the city, [and] were not far off, then Joseph said to his steward, Arise, and pursue after the men; and you shall overtake them, and say to them, Why have you⌃ returned evil for good? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Why have you⌃ stolen my silver cup? is it not this out of which my lord drinks? and he divines augury with it; you⌃ have accomplished evil in that which you⌃ have done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he found them, and spoke to them according to these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they said to him, Why does our lord speak according to these words? far be it from your servants to do according to this word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If we brought back to you out of the land of Chanaan the money which we found in our sacks, how should we steal silver or gold out of the house of your lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} With whoever of your servants you shall find the cup, let him die; and, moreover, we will be servants to our lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said, Now then it shall be as you⌃ say; with whoever the cup shall be found, he shall be my servant, and you⌃ shall be clear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they hasted, and took down every man his sack on the ground, and they opened every man his sack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he searched, beginning from the oldest, until he came to the youngest; and he found the cup in Benjamin's sack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they tore their garments, and laid each man his sack on his ass, and returned to the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Judas and his brethren came in to Joseph, while he was yet there, and fell on the ground before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joseph said to them, What is this thing that you⌃ have done? know you⌃ not that a man such as I can surely divine? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Judas said, What shall we answer to our lord, or what shall we say, or wherein should we be justified? whereas God has revealed the unrighteousness of your servants; behold, we are slaves to our lord, both we and he with whom the cup has been found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Joseph said, Far be it from me to do this thing; the man with whom the cup has been found, he shall be my servant; but do you⌃ go up with safety to your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Judas drew near him, and said, I pray, Sir, let your servant speak a word before you, and be not angry with your servant, for you are next to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Sir, you asked your servants, saying, Have you⌃ a father or a brother? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And we said to [my] lord, We have a father, an old man, and he has a son of his old age, a young one, and his brother is dead, and he alone has been left behind to his mother, and his father loves him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you said to your servants, Bring him down to me, and I will take care of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And we said to [my] lord, The child will not be able to leave his father; but if he should leave his father, he will die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But you said to your servants, Except your younger brother come down with you, you⌃ shall not see my face again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it came to pass, when we went up to your servant our father, we reported to him the words of our lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And our father said, Go again, and buy us a little food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And we said, We shall not be able to go down; but if our younger brother go down with us, we will go down; for we shall not be able to see the man's face, our younger brother not being with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And your servant our father said to us, You⌃ know that my wife bore me two [sons]; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and one is departed from me; and you⌃ said that he was devoured of wild beasts, and I have not seen him until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} If then you⌃ take this one also from my presence, and an affliction happen to him by the way, then shall you⌃ bring down my old age with sorrow to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Now then, if I should go in to your servant, and our father, and the boy should not be with us, (and his life depends on this [lad's] life) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} —it shall even come to pass, when he sees the boy is not with us, [that] he will die, and your servants will bring down the old age of your servant, and our father, with sorrow to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For your servant has received the boy [in charge] from his father, saying, If I bring him not to you, and place him before you, I shall be guilty towards my father for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Now then I will remain a servant with you instead of the lad, a domestic of my lord; but let the lad go up with his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} For how shall I go up to my father, the lad not being with us? lest I behold the evils which will befall my father.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: zakhah (זָכָה) = to be clean; innocent. Common English renderings: be pure; innocent. Used for acquittal or purity.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the steward Heb. him that was over his house, Fill the \textsuperscript{5} divineth or, maketh trial, *marg.; In the East, there is an ancient tradition, that there was a Cup which possessed the strange property of representing in it the whole world, and all the things which were then doing. The cup is called Jami Jemsheed, "the cup of Jemsheed, " a very ancient king of Persia; and they say that it was discovered, filled with the elixir of immortality, when digging to lay the foundations of Persepolis. The Persian poets are full of allusions to this cup, which they style Jem jehan nima, the cup shewing the universe; and to it they ascribe all the prosperity of their ancient monarchs. Many of the Mahometan princes and governors affect still to have information by means of a cup. Now, though it cannot be admitted that Joseph practised divination, yet, according to the superstition of those times, supernatural influence might be attributed to HIS CUP. \textsuperscript{15} What, wot ye not; divine or, make trial \textsuperscript{16} Judah, What shall we say; God hath; iniquity; behold \textsuperscript{17} God forbid; he shall in peace \textsuperscript{18} Oh my Lord "No paraphrase, " says Dr. A. Clarke, "can heighten the effect of Judah's address to Joseph. To add, would be to diminish its excellence; to attempt to explain, would be to obscure its beauties; to clothe the ideas in other language than that of Judah, and his translators in our Bible, would ruin its energy, and destroy its influence. It is perhaps one of the most tender, affecting pieces of natural oratory ever spoken or penned, and we need not wonder to find that, when Joseph heard it, he could not refrain himself, but wept aloud. His soul must have been insensible beyond what is common to human nature, had he not immediately yielded to a speech so delicately tender, and so powerfully impressive." let thy; anger; as Pharaoh \textsuperscript{20} we said Every word in this verse is simplicity and pathos itself. No man of the least sensibility can read it without great emotion. Indeed the whole speech is exquisitely beautiful, and perhaps the most complete pattern of genuine natural eloquence extant in any language. When we read this generous speech, we forgive Judah all the past, and cannot refuse to say, "Thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise." a child, and his brother, he alone \textsuperscript{31} when he; servants shall, ; grave \textsuperscript{33} therefore What must Benjamin have felt when he heard his brother conclude his speech by a proposal which could never have been thought of if it had not been actually made! Perhaps the annals of the whole world do not produce an instance of so heroic and disinterested affection in any mere man. I pray thee; instead \textsuperscript{34} lest; come on Heb. find; *marg.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 45}
\markright{GENESIS 45}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joseph could not refrain himself when all were standing by him, but said, Dismiss all from me; and no one stood near Joseph, when he made himself known to his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he uttered his voice with weeping; and all the Egyptians heard, and it was reported to the house of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joseph said to his brethren, I am Joseph; does my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joseph said to his brethren, Draw near to me; and they drew near; and he said, I am your brother Joseph, whom you⌃ sold into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now then be not grieved, and let it not seem hard to you that you⌃ sold me hither, for God sent me before you for life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For this second year there is famine on the earth, and there are yet five years remaining, in which there is to be neither plowing, nor mowing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For God sent me before you, that there might be left to you a remnant upon the earth, even to nourish a great remnant of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now then you⌃ did not send me hither, but God; and he has made me as a father of Pharao, and lord of all his house, and ruler of all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Hasten, therefore, and go up to my father, and say to him, These things says your son Joseph; God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore to me, and wait not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall dwell in the land of Gesem of Arabia; and you shall be near me, you and your sons, and your sons' sons, your sheep and your oxen, and whatever things are your. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will nourish you there: for the famine is yet for five years; lest you be consumed, and your sons, and all your possessions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Report, therefore, to my father all my glory in Egypt, and all things that you⌃ have seen, and make haste and bring down my father hither. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept on him; and Benjamin wept on his neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he kissed all his brethren, and wept on them; and after these things his brethren spoke to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the report was carried into the house of Pharao, saying, Joseph's brethren are come; and Pharao was glad, and his household. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Pharao said to Joseph, Say to your brethren, Do this; fill your wagons, and depart into the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And take up your father, and your possessions, and come to me; and I will give you of all the goods of Egypt, and you⌃ shall eat the marrow of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And do you charge them thus; that they should take for them wagons out of the land of Egypt, for your little ones, and for your wives; and take up your father, and come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And be not sparing in regard to your property, for all the good of Egypt shall be yours. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the children of Israel did so; and Joseph gave to them wagons, according to the words spoken by king Pharao; and he gave them provision for the journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he gave to them all two sets of raiment apiece; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of gold, and five changes of raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And to his father he sent [presents] at the same rate, and ten asses, bearing some of all the good things of Egypt, and ten mules, bearing bread for his father for your journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he sent away his brethren, and they went; and he said to them, Be not angry by the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Chanaan, to Jacob their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they reported to him, saying, Your son Joseph is living, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt; and Jacob was amazed, for he did not believe them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But they spoke to him all the words uttered by Joseph, whatever he said to them; and having seen the chariots which Joseph sent to take him up, the spirit of Jacob their father revived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Israel said, It is a great thing for me if Joseph my son is yet alive. I will go and see him before I die.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{20} Heb. vocab: chamal (חָמַל) = to spare; pity. Common English renderings: spare; pity. Used for compassion or withholding destruction. \textsuperscript{23} Gk. vocab: trophē (τροφή) = food; nourishment. Common English renderings: food; nourishment. A general noun for nourishment.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} wept aloud Heb. gave forth his voice in weeping, "This, " says Sir J. Chardin, "is exactly the genius of the people of Asia; their sentiments of joy or grief are properly transports, and their transports are ungoverned, excessive, and truly outrageous. When anyone returns from a long journey or dies, his family burst into cries that may be heard twenty doors off; and this is renewed at different times, and continues many days, according to the vigour of the passion. Sometimes they cease all at once, and then begin as suddenly, with a greater shrillness and loudness than one could easily imagine." \textsuperscript{3} I am Joseph; for they; troubled or, terrified \textsuperscript{5} be not grieved; nor angry with yourselves Heb. neither let there be anger in your eyes God \textsuperscript{6} two years, earing Earing means ploughing or seed-time from the Anglo-Saxon erian, probably from aro, to plough; and agrees with αροω, Greek, charatha, Arabic, and charash, Hebrew. \textsuperscript{7} to preserve you a posterity Heb. to put for you a remnant, to save. \textsuperscript{10} in the land, ; Goshen was the most eastern district of Lower Egypt, and the frontier of that country and Arabia, not far from the Arabian gulf, and lying next to Canaan; for Jacob went directly thither when he came into Egypt, from which it was about eighty miles distant, though Hebron was distant from the Egyptian capital about three hundred miles. be near \textsuperscript{12} your eyes; my mouth Not as \textsuperscript{16} it pleased Pharaoh well Heb. was good in the eyes of Pharaoh \textsuperscript{20} regard not Heb. let not your eye spare, etc., ;, stuff; the good \textsuperscript{22} To all It is a common custom with all the Asiatic sovereigns to give both garments and money to ambassadors and persons of distinction, whom they particularly wish to honour. De la Motraye says, "that they then clothed them (the ambassadors) with caffetans (long vests of gold or silver brocade) with large silk flowers." each; to Benjamin \textsuperscript{23} laden with Heb. carrying, good things; meat As mazon is derived from zoon, to prepare, provide, Dr. A. Clarke thinks it may mean here prepared meat; some made-up dish, delicacies, confectionaries, etc. In Asiatic countries they have several curious methods of preserving flesh by potting, by which it may be kept, for any length of time, sweet and wholesome. Some delicacy, similar to the savoury meat which Isaac loved, may here be intended; sent to Jacob in consideration of his age, and to testify the respect of his son; for of other kinds of meat he could have no need, as he had large flocks and herds, and could kill a lamb, kid, etc. when he pleased. \textsuperscript{26} Joseph and he is; And Jacob's Heb. And his, ; he believed\par}
