\subsection*{Genesis 46}
\markright{GENESIS 46}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Israel departed, he and all that he had, and came to the well of the oath; and he offered sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And God spoke to Israel in a night vision, saying, Jacob, Jacob; and he said, What is it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he says to him, I am the God of your fathers; fear not to go down into Egypt, for I will make you there a great nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will go down with you into Egypt, and I will bring you up at the end; and Joseph shall put his hands on your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jacob rose up from the well of the oath; and the sons of Israel took up their father, and the baggage, and their wives on the wagons, which Joseph sent to take them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they took up their goods, and all their property, which they had gotten in the land of Chanaan; they came into the land of Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The sons, and the sons of his sons with him; [his] daughters, and the daughters of his daughters; and he brought all his seed into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And these are the names of the sons of Israel that went into Egypt with their father Jacob—Jacob and his sons. The firstborn of Jacob, Ruben. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the sons of Ruben; Enoch, and Phallus, Asron, and Charmi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and the sons of Symeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Aod, and Achin, and Saar, and Saul, the son of a Chananitish woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the sons of Levi; Gerson, Cath, and Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the sons of Judas; Er, and Aunan, and Selom, and Phares, and Zara: and Er and Aunan died in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the sons of Phares [were] Esron, and Jemuel. And the sons of Issachar; Thola, and Phua, and Asum, and Sambran. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the sons of Zabulun, Sered, and Allon, and Achoel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} These [are] the sons of Lea, which she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, and Dina his daughter; all the souls, sons and daughters, thirty-three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the sons of Gad; Saphon, and Angis, and Sannis, and Thasoban, and Aedis, and Aroedis, and Areelis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the sons of Aser; Jemna, Jessua, and Jeul, and Baria, and Sara their sister. And the sons of Baria; Chobor, and Melchiil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} These [are] the sons of Zelpha, which Laban gave to his daughter Lea, who bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob; Joseph, and Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And there were sons born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Aseneth, the daughter of Petephres, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him, [even] Manasses and Ephraim. And there were sons born to Manasses, which the Syrian concubine bore to him, [even] Machir. And Machir begot Galaad. And the sons of Ephraim, the brother of Manasses; Sutalaam, and Taam. And the sons of Sutalaam; Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and the sons of Benjamin; Bala, and Bochor, and Asbel. And the sons of Bala were Gera, and Noeman, and Anchis, and Ros, and Mamphim. And Gera begot Arad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} These [are] the sons of Rachel, which she bore to Jacob; all the souls eighteen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the sons of Dan; Asom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the sons of Nephthalim; Asiel, and Goni, and Issaar, and Sollem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} These [are] the sons of Balla, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel, who bore these to Jacob; all the souls, seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And all the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, who came out of his loins, besides the wives of the sons of Jacob, [even] all the souls were sixty-six. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the sons of Joseph, who were born to him in the land of Egypt, were nine souls; all the souls of the house of Jacob who came with Joseph into Egypt, were seventy-five souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he sent Judas before him to Joseph, to meet him to the city of Heroes, into the land of Ramesses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Joseph having made ready his chariots, went up to meet Israel his father, at the city of Heroes; and having appeared to him, fell on his neck, and wept with abundant weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Israel said to Joseph, After this I will [gladly] die, since I have seen your face, for you are yet living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Joseph said to his brethren, I will go up and tell Pharao, and will say to him, My brethren, and my father's house, who were in the land of Chanaan, are come to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the men are shepherds; for they have been feeders of cattle, and they have brought with them their cattle, and their kine, and all their property. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} If then Pharao call you, and say to you, What is you occupation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} You⌃ shall say, We your servants are herdsmen from our youth until now, both we and our fathers: that you⌃ may dwell in the land of Gesem of Arabia, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2298, bc 1706 Beersheba, ; and offered, ; unto \textsuperscript{3} the God fear not, ; I will \textsuperscript{4} will go; and I will, ; and Joseph This last and most solemn office, as Mr. Hewlett observes, that could be paid to a parent, was generally performed by the nearest relation of the deceased. This promise must have given great consolation to the venerable patriarch's mind. \textsuperscript{10} Simeon, ;, ; Jemuel or, Nemuel Jachin or, Jarib Zohar or, Zerah, Canaanitish \textsuperscript{13} Issachar, ; , Phuvah or, Puah Job or, Jashub \textsuperscript{16} sons of, ; Ziphion or, Zephon Ezbon or, Ozni Arodi or, Arod \textsuperscript{20} Manasseh, ; priest or, prince, *marg. \textsuperscript{21} the sons; Ehi, Ahiram Muppim, Shupham, Shuppim Huppim, Hupham \textsuperscript{27} threescore and ten Threescore and six were before mentioned ( ), so that Joseph and his two sons, together with Jacob himself, complete the seventy persons here enumerated; and the number in, and amount to that number. The addition of five persons in the LXX in, was either the cause or the consequence of another difference here; for in that version the number is seventy-five (, ). \textsuperscript{28} Judah, to direct Goshen seems to have been a city, after which the land of Goshen was called. The LXX render it by Ηρωωνπολις, Heroonpolis, "city of Heroon; " which by some writers is simply called Heroum, and is by the ancient geographers placed in the eastern part of Egypt, not far from the Arabian Gulf. \textsuperscript{32} shepherds, ; their trade hath been to feed cattle Heb. they are men of cattle, ; and they \textsuperscript{34} Thy servants', for every From the fragments of Manetho, preserved in Josephus and Africanus, it appears that hordes of marauders, call hycassos, or shepherd kings, whose chief occupation, like the Bedouin Arabs of the present day, was to keep flocks, made a powerful irruption into Egypt, which they subdued, and ruled, by a succession of kings, with great tyranny for 259 years. Hence the persons, and even the very name of shepherds were execrated, and held in the greatest odium by the Egyptians.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 47}
\markright{GENESIS 47}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joseph came and told Pharao, [saying], My father, and my brethren, and their cattle, and their oxen, and all their possessions, are come out of the land of Chanaan, and behold, they are in the land of Gesem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he took of his brethren five men, and set them before Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Pharao said to the brethren of Joseph, What is your occupation? and they said to Pharao, Your servants are shepherds, both we and our father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they said to Pharao, We are come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for the flocks of your servants, for the famine has prevailed in the land of Chanaan; now then, we will dwell in the land of Gesem. And Pharao said to Joseph, Let them dwell in the land of Gesem; and if you know that there are among them able men, make them overseers of my cattle. So Jacob and his sons came into Egypt, to Joseph; and Pharao, king of Egypt, heard [of it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Pharao spoke to Joseph, saying, Your father, and your brethren, are come to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brethren in the best land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharao; and Jacob blessed Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Pharao said to Jacob, How many are the years of the days of your life? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jacob said to Pharao, The days of the years of my life, wherein I sojourn, are one hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, they have not attained to the days of the life of my fathers, in which days they sojourned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Jacob blessed Pharao, and departed from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Joseph settled his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best land, in the land of Ramesses, as Pharao commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Joseph gave provision to his father, and his brethren, and to all the house of his father, corn for each person. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there was no corn in all the land, for the famine prevailed greatly; and the land of Egypt, and the land of Chanaan, fainted for the famine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Joseph gathered all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and the land of Chanaan, [in return for] the corn which they bought, and he distributed corn to them; and Joseph brought all the money into the house of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And all the money failed out of the land of Egypt, and out of the land of Chanaan; and all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, Give us bread, and why do we die in your presence? for our money is spent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joseph said to them, Bring your cattle, and I will give you bread for your cattle, if your money is spent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they brought their cattle to Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in return for their horses, and for their sheep, and for their oxen, and for their asses; and Joseph maintained them with bread for all their cattle in that year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And that year passed, and they came to him in the second year, and said to him, Must we then be consumed from before our lord? for if our money has failed, and our possessions, and our cattle, [brought] to you our lord, and there has not been left to us before our lord more than our own bodies and our land, [we are indeed destitute]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} In order, then, that we die not before you, and the land be made desolate, buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharao: give seed that we may sow, and live and not die, so our land shall not be made desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Joseph bought all the land of the Egyptians, for Pharao; for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharao; for the famine prevailed against them, and the land became Pharao's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he brought the people into bondage to him, for servants, from one extremity of Egypt to the other, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} except only the land of the priests; Joseph bought not this, for Pharao gave a portion in the way of gift to the priests; and they ate their portion which Pharao gave them; therefore they sold not their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joseph said to all the Egyptians, Behold, I have bought you and your land this day for Pharao; take seed for you, and sow the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And there shall be the fruits of it; and you⌃ shall give the fifth part to Pharao, and the four [remaining] parts shall be for yourselves, for seed for the earth, and for food for you, and all that are in your houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they said, You have saved us; we have found favor before our lord, and we will be servants to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joseph appointed it to them for an ordinance until this day; to reserve a fifth part for Pharao, on the land of Egypt, except only the land of the priests, that was not Pharao's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Israel lived in Egypt, in the land of Gesem, and they gained an inheritance upon it; and they increased and multiplied very greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Jacob survived seventeen years in the land of Egypt; and Jacob's days of the years of his life were one hundred and forty-seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and the days of Israel drew near for him to die: and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, If I have found favor before you, put your hand under my thigh, and you shall execute mercy and truth toward me, so as not to bury me in Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But I will sleep with my fathers, and you shall carry me up out of Egypt, and bury me in their sepulchre. And he said, I will do according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said, Swear to me; and he swore to him. And Israel did reverence, leaning on the top of his staff.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{18} Gk. vocab: sōma (σῶμα) = body. Common English renderings: body. The usual term for the body. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: choq (חֹק) = statute; fixed decree. Common English renderings: statute; ordinance. Often denotes a fixed prescribed regulation. \textsuperscript{31} Gk. vocab: klinē (κλίνη) = bed; couch. Common English renderings: bed. A bed or reclining couch.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} For to; for the famine; let thy \textsuperscript{6} is, ; Goshen, men of activity Anshey chayil, men of strength, power, ability, or prowess. It implies both fitness of mind and body; and so valour, prudence, diligence, and virtue. rulers; cattle Mikneh, from kanah, to posses, signifies property or possession of any kind, though it frequently is used for cattle, because in ancient times they constituted the principal part of a man's possessions. \textsuperscript{8} How old art thou Heb. How many are the days of the years of thy life \textsuperscript{9} The days; an hundred; have not \textsuperscript{12} nourished his father; , according to their families or, as a little child is nourished, Heb. according to the little ones \textsuperscript{13} am 2300, bc 1704 so that; fainted \textsuperscript{15} am 2301, bc 1703 Give us bread \textsuperscript{16} Give your cattle This was the wisest measure that could be adopted, both for the preservation of the people and the cattle. As the people had not grain for their own sustenance, consequently they could have none for their cattle. Hence they were in the most imminent danger of starving; and the people also were in equal danger; as they must have divided a portion of that bought for themselves with the cattle, which, for the sake of tillage, etc., they wished of course to preserve till the seven years' famine should end. \textsuperscript{17} for horses; fed them Heb. led them \textsuperscript{21} am 2303, bc 1701 And as It is highly probable, that Joseph was influenced by no political motive in removing the people to the cities, but merely by motives of prudence and humanity; for, as the corn was laid up in the cities, it would be more eligible to bring then from distant towns and villages to places where they might be more conveniently supplied with food. to cities \textsuperscript{22} of the priests or, princes, *marg. for the priests \textsuperscript{25} Thou hast, *marg.; let us \textsuperscript{26} made it a law From this history, and from Diodorus Siculus (lib. i.), we learn that the land of Egypt was divided into three parts: one belonged to the Priests ( and ); a second was the king's (which appears to have been the land of Rameses, or Goshen, ); the remainder was the subjects'. Now Joseph, having purchased the land of the people ( and ), restored it, on the condition of their paying a fifth part of the produce to the king, beyond which he appears to have made no demand. except; priests or, princes \textsuperscript{28} am 2315, bc 1689 seventeen the whole age Heb. the days of the years of his life, *marg. \textsuperscript{29} must die, ; , ; put deal kindly bury me not \textsuperscript{31} Swear And Israel bowed As shachah, which primarily signifies to bow, denotes also to worship; and as mittah, a bed, pronounced matteh, is a staff; the LXX have taken the passage in the latter sense, and rendered it και προσεκυνησεν Ισραηλ επι το ακρον της ραβδου αυτου, "and Israel worshipped upon the top of his staff, " which is literally copied by the apostle Paul, in his Epistle to the Hebrews. The present reading is, however, supported by the Masoretic pointing and the Targums; and is most probably correct, as it would appear that Jacob was confined to his bed.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 48}
\markright{GENESIS 48}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after these things, that it was reported to Joseph, Behold, your father is ill; and, having taken his two sons, Manasse and Ephraim, he came to Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it was reported to Jacob, saying, Behold, your son Joseph comes to you; and Israel having strengthened himself, sat upon the bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jacob said to Joseph, My God appeared to me in Luza, in the land of Chanaan, and blessed me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and said to me, Behold, I will increase you, and multiply you, and will make of you multitudes of nations; and I will give this land to you, and to your seed after you, for an everlasting possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now then your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt, before I came to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasse, as Ruben and Symeon they shall be mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children which you shall beget hereafter, shall be in the name of their brethren; they shall be named after their inheritances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And as for me, when I came out of Mesopotamia of Syria, Rachel, your mother, died in the land of Chanaan, as I drew near to the horse-course of Chabratha of the land [of Chanaan], so as to come to Ephratha; and I buried her in the road of the course; this is Bethlehem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he said, Who are these to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joseph said to his father, They are my sons, whom God gave me here; and Jacob said, Bring me them, that I may bless them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now the eyes of Israel were dim through age, and he could not see; and he brought them near to him, and he kissed them, and embraced them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I have not been deprived of [seeing] your face, and behold! God has showed me your seed also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Joseph brought them out from [between] his knees, and they did reverence to him, with their face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joseph took his two sons, both Ephraim in his right hand, but on the left of Israel, and Manasse on his left hand, but on the right of Israel, and brought them near to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But Israel having stretched out his right hand, laid it on the head of Ephraim, and he was the younger; and his left hand on the head of Manasse, [guiding] his hands crosswise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he blessed them and said, The God in whose sight my fathers were well pleasing, [even] Abraam and Isaac, the God who continues to feed me from my youth until this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} the angel who delivers me from all evils, bless these boys, and my name shall be called upon them, and the name of my fathers, Abraam and Isaac; and let them be increased to a great multitude on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Joseph having seen that his father put his right hand on the head of Ephraim—it seemed grievous to him; and Joseph took hold of the hand of his father, to remove it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joseph said to his father, Not so, father; for this is the firstborn; lay your right-hand upon his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he would not, but said, I know it, son, I know it; he also shall be a people, and he shall be exalted, but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he blessed them in that day, saying, In you shall Israel be blessed, saying, God make you as Ephraim and Manasse; and he set Ephraim before Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die; and God shall be with you, and restore you to the land of your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I give to you Sicima, a select portion above your brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorites with my sword and bow.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: gaal (גָּאַל) = to redeem; act as kinsman-redeemer. Common English renderings: redeem. A family-redemption term important in law, narrative, and theology. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: tamak (תָּמַךְ) = to support; uphold. Common English renderings: uphold. A support and sustaining term.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 49}
\markright{GENESIS 49}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jacob called his sons, and said to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Assemble yourselves, that I may tell you what shall happen to you in the last days. Gather yourselves together, and hear me, sons of Jacob; hear Israel, hear your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Ruben, you [are] my firstborn, you my strength, and the first of my children, hard to be endured, [hard and] self-willed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You were insolent like water, burst not forth with violence, for you went up to the bed of your father; then you defiled the couch, whereupon you went up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Symeon and Levi, brethren, accomplished the injustice of their cutting off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let not my soul come into their counsel, and let not my inward parts contend in their conspiracy, for in their wrath they killed men, and in their passion they houghed a bull. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Cursed be their wrath, for it was willful, and their anger, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Juda, your brethren have praised you, and your hands shall be on the back of your enemies; your father's sons shall do you reverence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Juda is a lion's whelp: from the tender plant, my son, you are gone up, having couched you lie as a lion, and as a whelp; who shall stir him up? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A ruler shall not fail from Juda, nor a prince from his loins, until there come the things stored up for him; and he is the expectation of nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Binding his foal to the vine, and the foal of his ass to the branch [of it], he shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} His eyes shall be more cheering than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Zabulon shall dwell on the coast, and he [shall be] by a haven of ships, and shall extend to Sidon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Issachar has desired that which is good; resting between the inheritances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And having seen the resting place that it was good, and the land that it was fertile, he subjected his shoulder to labor, and became a husbandman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Dan shall judge his people, as one tribe too in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And let Dan be a serpent in the way, besetting the path, biting the heel of the horse (and the rider shall fall backward), {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} waiting for the salvation of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Gad, a plundering troop shall plunder him; but he shall plunder him, [pursuing him] closely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Aser, his bread [shall be] fat; and he shall yield dainties to princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Nephthalim is a spreading stem, bestowing beauty on its fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Joseph is a son increased; my dearly loved son is increased; my youngest son, turn to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Against whom men taking evil counsel reproached [him], and the archers pressed hard upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But their bow and arrows were mightily consumed, and the sinews of their arms were slackened by the hand of the mighty one of Jacob; thence is he that strengthened Israel from the God of your father; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and my God helped you, and he blessed you with the blessing of heaven from above, and the blessing of the earth possessing all things, because of the blessing of the breasts and of the womb, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} the blessings of your father and your mother—it has prevailed above the blessing of the lasting mountains, and beyond the blessings of the everlasting hills; they shall be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the head of the brothers of whom he took the lead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Benjamin, as a ravening wolf, shall eat still in the morning, and at evening he gives food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} All these [are] the twelve sons of Jacob; and their father spoke these words to them, and he blessed them; he blessed each of them according to his blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he said to them, I am added to my people; you⌃ shall bury me with my fathers in the cave, which is in the field of Ephron the Chettite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} in the double cave which is opposite Mambre, in the land of Chanaan, the cave which Abraam bought of Ephron the Chettite, for a possession of a sepulchre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} There they buried Abraam and Sarrha his wife; there they buried Isaac, and Rebecca his wife; there they buried Lea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} in the portion of the field, and of the cave that was in it, [purchased] of the sons of Chet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Jacob ceased giving charges to his sons; and having lifted up his feet on the bed, he died, and was gathered to his people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: sod (סוֹד) = council; secret counsel. Common English renderings: secret; counsel. Can refer to confidential counsel or divine council. Heb. vocab: ratson (רָצוֹן) = favor; goodwill; acceptance. Common English renderings: favor; pleasure. Can indicate favorable will or acceptable status. \textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: shevet (שֵׁבֶט) = tribe; staff; scepter. Common English renderings: tribe; rod; sceptre. Can refer to tribal unit or symbol of rule. \textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: saval (סָבַל) = to bear a load. Common English renderings: bear. Burden-bearing term with physical and metaphorical uses. Heb. vocab: menuchah (מְנוּחָה) = resting place; rest. Common English renderings: rest. Rest as settled repose or inheritance. Heb. vocab: no’am (נֹעַם) = pleasantness; favor. Common English renderings: beauty; pleasantness. Can denote pleasantness, delight, or gracious beauty. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: yeshuah (יְשׁוּעָה) = salvation; deliverance. Common English renderings: salvation; deliverance. Key noun for divine rescue and victory. Gk. vocab: sōtēria (σωτηρία) = salvation; deliverance. Common English renderings: salvation; deliverance. Can refer to rescue, deliverance, or salvation in a fuller theological sense. \textsuperscript{24} Name of God: Avir Yaakov (אֲבִיר יַעֲקֹב) — Mighty One of Jacob Common English renderings: mighty God of Jacob; mighty One of Jacob. A poetic title of covenant strength and sustaining power. Heb. vocab: zeroa (זְרוֹעַ) = arm. Common English renderings: arm. A symbol of strength, especially divine power. \textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: shalal (שָׁלַל) = spoil; plunder. Common English renderings: spoil. Used for booty after victory.\par}

\subsection*{Genesis 50}
\markright{GENESIS 50}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept on him, and kissed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to embalm his father; and the embalmers embalmed Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they fulfilled forty days for him, for so are the days of embalming numbered; and Egypt mourned for him seventy days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when the days of mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the princes of Pharao, saying, If I have found favor in your sight, speak concerning me in the ears of Pharao, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} My father adjured me, saying, In the sepulchre which I dug for myself in the land of Chanaan, there you shall bury me; now then I will go up and bury my father, and return again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Pharao said to Joseph, Go up, bury your father, as he constrained you to swear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So Joseph went up to bury his father; and all the servants of Pharao went up with him, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all the household of Joseph, and his brethren, and all the house of his father, and his kindred; and they left behind the sheep and the oxen in the land of Gesem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there went up with him also chariots and horsemen; and there was a very great company. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan; and they bewailed him with a great and very sore lamentation; and he made a mourning for his father seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the inhabitants of the land of Chanaan saw the mourning at the floor of Atad, and said, This is a great mourning to the Egyptians; therefore he called its name, The mourning of Egypt, which is beyond Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And thus his sons did to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So his sons carried him up into the land of Chanaan, and buried him in the double cave, which cave Abraam bought for possession of a burying place, of Ephrom the Chettite, before Mambre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brethren, and those that had gone up with him to bury his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when the brethren of Joseph saw that their father was dead, they said, [Let us take heed], lest at any time Joseph remember evil against us, and recompense to us all the evils which we have done against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they came to Joseph, and said, Your father adjured [us] before his death, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Thus say you⌃ to Joseph, Forgive them their injustice and their sin, forasmuch as they have done you evil; and now pardon the injustice of the servants of the God of your father. And Joseph wept while they spoke to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they came to him and said, We, these [persons], are your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Joseph said to them, Fear not, for I am God's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You⌃ took counsel against me for evil, but God took counsel for me for good, that [the matter] might be as [it is] today, and much people might be fed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said to them, Fear not, I will maintain you, and your families: and he comforted them, and spoke kindly to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joseph lived in Egypt, he and his brethren, and all the family of his father; and Joseph lived one hundred and ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joseph saw the children of Ephraim to the third generation; and the sons of Machir the son of Manasse were borne on the sides of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Joseph spoke to his brethren, saying, I die, and God will surely visit you, and will bring you out of this land to the land concerning which God swore to our fathers, Abraam, Isaac, and Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joseph adjured the sons of Israel, saying, At the visitation with which God shall visit you, then you⌃ shall carry up my bones hence with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joseph died, aged one hundred and ten years; and they prepared his corpse, and put him in a coffin in Egypt.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the physicians The Hebrew ropheim, from rapha, to heal, is literally the healers, those whose business it was to heal, or restore the body from sickness, by administering proper medicines; and when death took place, to heal or preserve it from decomposition by embalming. The word chanat, to embalm, is also used in Arabic to express the reddening of leather; somewhat analogous to our tanning; which is probably the grand principal in embalming. embalmed \textsuperscript{3} forty days We learn from the Greek historians, that the time of mourning was while the body remained with the embalmers, which Herodotus says was seventy days. During this time the body lay in nitre, the use of which was to dry up all its superfluous and noxious moisture, and when, in the space of 30 days, this was sufficiently effected, the remaining forty, the time mentioned by Diodorus, were employed in anointing it with gums and spices to preserve it, which was properly the embalming. This sufficiently explains the phraseology of the text. mourned Heb. wept threescore \textsuperscript{4} the days Joseph found grace \textsuperscript{5} made me I die, ; I have; bury me; , let me go \textsuperscript{10} the threshingfloor This place was situated, according to Jerome, between the Jordan and the city of Jericho, two miles from the former, and three from the latter, where Bethagla was afterwards built. Procopius of Gaza states the same. As aataad signifies thorns, the place might have been remarkable for their production; though all the versions except the Arabic consider it as a proper name. As Moses wrote or revised his history on the east side of Jordan, the term beyond Jordan, in his five books, means westward of Jordan; but in other parts of Scripture it generally means eastward. beyond; seven days \textsuperscript{11} the Canaanites, Abelmizraim i.e. The mourning of the Egyptians, beyond Jordan \textsuperscript{17} Forgive, ; they did; servants; wept \textsuperscript{19} fear not; for am I It belongs to God to execute vengeance, and Joseph did not intend to usurp his prerogative. Thus he instructed his brethren not to fear him, but to fear God; to humble themselves before God, and to seek his forgiveness. \textsuperscript{21} I will nourish; kindly unto them Heb. to their hearts; *marg. \textsuperscript{22} an hundred Joseph's life was the shortest of all the patriarchs; for which Bp. Patrick gives this reason, he was the son of his father's old age. \textsuperscript{23} the children; brought up Heb. born Joseph's \textsuperscript{24} I die; visit you; you out, ; sware \textsuperscript{26} being an hundred and ten years old Ben meah weaiser shanim; "the son of an hundred and ten years; " the period he lived being personified., ; they embalmed\par}

\section*{Exodus Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Moses\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Received as Mosaic in Jewish and Christian tradition; Exodus is part of the law of Moses.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Jesus treats the bush narrative as Mosaic in Mark 12:26; see also Luke 20:37 and John 5:46-47.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 1446-1406 BC during the wilderness period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places the exodus in the Mosaic generation and preserves the shorter genealogical framework reflected in the standard Hebrew text.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX wording often expands or smooths details, but the historical setting remains the Mosaic exodus and Sinai covenant.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Israel's redemption from Egypt, covenant-making at Sinai, and the erection of the tabernacle.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To record the LORD's redemption, covenant law, and dwelling among His people.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} redemption; Passover; covenant; law; tabernacle; priesthood; divine presence\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Bondage and deliverance 1-15; Covenant at Sinai 16-24; Tabernacle instructions 25-31; Apostasy and renewal 32-34; Tabernacle construction 35-40.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 7Q1 Greek Exodus fragment late 2nd to early 1st century BC | Subst. 4Q paleoGenesis-Exodus and other Qumran Exodus witnesses Hasmonean period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus, with Codex Alexandrinus also preserving Exodus 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Exagoge by Ezekiel the Tragedian (3rd-2nd century BC)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Exodus is preserved in both Hebrew and Greek streams; some early Greek witnesses show readings nearer the Hebrew tradition in places, while the LXX also preserves distinctive renderings and expansions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Because Christ appeals to Moses in the Torah, this edition receives Exodus as Mosaic and originally inerrant in wording; later transmissional divergence is treated as a textual issue, not an authorship issue.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Exodus 1}
\markright{EXODUS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} These are the names of the sons of Israel that came into Egypt together with Jacob their father; they came in each with their whole family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Judas, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Issachar, Zabulon, Benjamin, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Dan and Nephthalim, Gad and Aser. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But Joseph was in Egypt. And all the souls [born] of Jacob were seventy-five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the children of Israel increased and multiplied, and became numerous and grew exceedingly strong, and the land multiplied them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And there arose up another king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to his nation, Behold, the race of the children of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} come then, let us deal craftily with them, lest at any time they be increased, and whenever war shall happen to us, these also shall be added to our enemies, and having prevailed against us in war, they will depart out of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he set over them taskmasters, who should afflict them in their works; and they built strong cities for Pharao, both Pitho, and Ramesses, and On, which is Heliopolis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But as they humbled them, by so much they multiplied, and grew exceedingly strong; and the Egyptians greatly abhorred the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Egyptians tyrannized over the children of Israel by force. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they embittered their life by hard labors, in the clay and in brick-making, and all the works in the plains, according to all the works, wherein they caused them to serve with violence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews; the name of the one was, Sepphora; and the name of the second, Phua. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said, When you⌃ do the office of midwives to the Hebrew women, and they are about to be delivered, if it be a male, kill it; but if a female, save it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt appointed them; and they saved the male children alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king of Egypt called the midwives, and said to them, Why is it that you⌃ have done this thing, and saved the male children alive? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the midwives said to Pharao, The Hebrew women are not as the women of Egypt, for they are delivered before the midwives go in to them. So they bore children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And God did well to the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very strong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And as the midwives feared God, they established for themselves families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Pharao charged all his people, saying, Whatever male [child] shall be born to the Hebrews, cast into the river; and every female, save it alive.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: chadash (חָדָשׁ) = new. Common English renderings: new. \subsection*{Exodus 2}
\markright{EXODUS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a certain man of the tribe of Levi, who took as wife one of the daughters of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And she conceived, and bore a male child; and having seen that he was fair, they hid him three months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when they could no longer hide him, his mother took for him an ark, and besmeared it with bitumen, and cast the child into it, and put it in the ooze by the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his sister was watching from a distance, to learn what would happen to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the daughter of Pharao came down to the river to bathe; and her maids walked by the river's side, and having seen the ark in the ooze, she sent her maid, and took it up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And having opened it, she sees the babe weeping in the ark: and the daughter of Pharao had compassion on it, and said, This [is one] of the Hebrew's children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And his sister said to the daughter of Pharao, Will you that I call to you a nurse of the Hebrews, and shall she suckle the child for you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the daughter of Pharao said, Go: and the young woman went, and called the mother of the child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the daughter of Pharao said to her, Take care of this child, and suckled it for me, and I will give you the wages; and the woman took the child, and suckled it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when the boy was grown, she brought him to the daughter of Pharao, and he became her son; and she called his name, Moses, saying, I took him out of the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass in that length of time, that Moses having grown, went out to his brethren the sons of Israel: and having noticed their distress, he sees an Egyptian striking a certain Hebrew of his brethren the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And having looked round this way and that way, he sees no one; and he struck the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And having gone out the second day he sees two Hebrew men fighting; and he says to the injurer, Therefore smite you your neighbor? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said, Who made you a ruler and a judge over us? will you kill me as you yesterday killed the Egyptian? Then Moses was alarmed, and said, If [it be] thus, this matter has become known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Pharao heard this matter, and sought to kill Moses; and Moses departed from the presence of Pharao, and lived in the land of Madiam; and having come into the land of Madiam, he sat on the well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priest of Madiam had seven daughters, feeding the flock of their father Jothor; and they came and drew water until they filled their pitchers, to water the flock of their father Jothor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the shepherds came, and were driving them away; and Moses rose up and rescued them, and drew water for them, and watered their sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they came to Raguel their father; and he said to them, Why have you⌃ come so quickly today? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they said, An Egyptian delivered us from the shepherds, and drew water for us and watered our sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said to his daughters, And where is he? and why have you⌃ left the man? call him therefore, that he may eat bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses was established with the man, and he gave Sepphora his daughter to Moses to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the woman conceived and bore a son, and Moses called his name Gersam, saying, I am a sojourner in a strange land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And in those days after a length of time, the king of Egypt died; and the children of Israel groaned because of their tasks, and cried, and their cry because of their tasks went up to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And God heard their groanings, and God remembered his covenant made with Abraam and Isaac and Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And God looked upon the children of Israel, and was made known to them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Gk. vocab: brephos (βρέφος) = infant; babe. Common English renderings: babe; infant. Used for very young children and infants. \textsuperscript{10} Name meaning: Moses (Mosheh) — Drawn out Drawn out of the Nile; drew Israel out of Egypt. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: rasha (רָשָׁע) = wicked; guilty. Common English renderings: wicked; ungodly. Describes moral guilt and opposition to righteousness. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: za’aq (זָעַק) = to cry out. Common English renderings: cry. Near-synonym of צעק in distress contexts.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2432, bc 1572 of the house \textsuperscript{3} could not; an ark bulrushes Gome, is the papyrus, so famous in all antiquity. It grows on the banks of the Nile, and in marshy grounds; the stalk rises to the height of six or seven cubits above the water, is triangular, and terminates in a crown of small filaments, resembling hair. This reed was of the greatest use to the Egyptians; the pith serving them for food, and the woody part to build vessels with; which vessels frequently appear on various monuments of Egyptian antiquity. That boats were made of this reed is also attested by Pliny and others. with slime \textsuperscript{5} daughter herself As the word herself is not in the original, Dr. A. Clarke is of opinion that it was for the purpose of washing, not her person, but her clothes, that Pharaoh's daughter came to the river; which was an employment not beneath even king's daughters in those primitive times. when she \textsuperscript{10} and he; Moses Drawn out Because \textsuperscript{12} he looked slew If the Egyptian killed the Hebrew, Moses only acted agreeably to the divine law ( ) in thus slaying the Egyptian; nor did he violate the law of Egypt; for, according to Diodorus Siculus (1. 1. § 17), "he who saw a man killed, or violently assaulted on the highway, and did not rescue him, if he could, was punished with death." Moses, therefore, in this transaction, acted as a brave and good man; especially as at this time there was little probability of obtaining justice on an Egyptian murderer. \textsuperscript{14} Who, ; a prince Heb. a man a prince Moses \textsuperscript{16} the priest or, prince; *marg. they came \textsuperscript{22} Gershom i.e. a stranger here, for he said \textsuperscript{23} am cir, 2504, bc cir, 1500 in process; the king; sighed; cry \textsuperscript{25} looked; God For elohim, God, Houbigant reads aleyhem, unto them; which is countenanced by the LXX, Vulgate, Chaldee, Coptic, and Arabic, and appears to have been the original reading. had respect Heb. knew\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 3}
\markright{EXODUS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses was feeding the flock of Jothor his father-in-law, the priest of Madiam; and he brought the sheep near to the wilderness, and came to the mount of Choreb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in flaming fire out of the bush, and he sees that the bush burns with fire, —but the bush was not consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses said, I will go near and see this great sight, why the bush is not consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when the Lord saw that he drew near to see, the Lord called him out of the bush, saying, Moses, Moses; and he said, What is it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said, Draw not near hither: loose your sandals from off your feet, for the place whereon you stand is holy ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said, I am the God of your father, the God of Abraam, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; and Moses turned away his face, for he was afraid to gaze at God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord said to Moses, I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Egypt, and I have heard their cry [caused] by their taskmasters; for I know their affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land, and to bring them into a good and wide land, into a land flowing with milk and honey, into the place of the Chananites, and the Chettites, and Amorites, and Pherezites, and Gergesites, and Evites, and Jebusites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come to me, and I have seen the affliction with which the Egyptians afflict them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now come, I will send you to Pharao king of Egypt, and you shall bring out my people the children of Israel from the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses said to God, Who am I, that I should go to Pharao king of Egypt, and that I should bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And God spoke to Moses, saying, I will be with you, and this shall be the sign to you that I shall send you forth, —when you bring out my people out of Egypt, then you⌃ shall serve God in this mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses said to God, Behold, I shall go forth to the children of Israel, and shall say to them, The God of our fathers has sent me to you; and they will ask me, What is his name? What shall I say to them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And God spoke to Moses, saying, I am THE BEING; and he said, Thus shall you⌃ say to the children of Israel, THE BEING has sent me to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And God said again to Moses, Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel, The Lord God of our fathers, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, has sent me to you: this is my name for ever, and my memorial to generations of generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Go then and gather the elders of the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, The Lord God of our fathers has appeared to me, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, saying, I have surely looked upon you, and upon all the things which have happened to you in Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians to the land of the Chananites and the Chettites, and Amorites and Pherezites, and Gergesites, and Evites, and Jebusites, to a land flowing with milk and honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall listen to your voice, and you and the elders of Israel shall go in to Pharao king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, The God of the Hebrews has called us; we will go then a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But I know that Pharao king of Egypt will not let you go, save with a mighty hand; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and I will stretch out my hand, and strike the Egyptians with all my wonders, which I shall work among them, and after that he will send you forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and whenever you⌃ shall escape, you⌃ shall not depart empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But [every] woman shall ask of her neighbor and fellow lodger, articles of gold and silver, and apparel; and you⌃ shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters, —and spoil you⌃ the Egyptians.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{5} Heb. vocab: qodesh (קֹדֶשׁ) = holiness; holy thing; sanctuary. Common English renderings: holiness; holy place; sanctuary. Related noun denoting holiness or holy sphere. Heb. vocab: qadosh (קָדוֹשׁ) = holy; set apart. Common English renderings: holy. The core Hebrew holiness term for what is set apart to God. Gk. vocab: hagios (ἅγιος) = holy. Common English renderings: holy; saint. A major holiness term for what is set apart to God. \textsuperscript{6} Name of God: Elohe Yaakov (אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב) — God of Jacob Common English renderings: God of Jacob. A key covenant formula tying God’s present action to His promises to the fathers. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: lachats (לָחַץ) = to oppress; press. Common English renderings: oppress. Pressure imagery behind oppression language. \textsuperscript{14} Name of God: Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh (אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה) — I AM THAT I AM; I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE Common English renderings: I AM THAT I AM. God’s self-revelation to Moses from the burning bush, emphasizing His self-existence and faithfulness.\par}

The other ancient versions are the same as the Hebrew. spoil; the Egyptians or, Egypt\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 4}
\markright{EXODUS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses answered and said, If they believe me not, and do not listen to my voice (for they will say, God has not appeared to you), what shall I say to them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to him, What is this thing that is in your hand? and he said, A rod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said, Cast it on the ground: and he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch forth your hand, and take hold of its tail: so he stretched forth his hand and took hold of the tail, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and it became a rod in his hand, —that they may believe you, that the God of your fathers has appeared to you, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord said again to him, Put your hand into your bosom; and he put his hand into his bosom, and brought his hand out of his bosom, and his hand became as snow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said again, Put your hand into your bosom; and he put his hand into his bosom, and brought his hand out of his bosom, and it was again restored to the complexion of his [other] flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if they will not believe you, nor listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe you [because] of the voice of the second sign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall come to pass if they will not believe you for these two signs, and will not listen to your voice, that you shall take of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water which you shall take from the river shall be blood upon the dry land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses said to the Lord, I pray, Lord, I have not been sufficient in former times, neither from the time that you have begun to speak to your servant: I am weak in speech, and slow-tongued. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to Moses, Who has given a mouth to man, and who has made the very hard of hearing, and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? have not I, God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now go and I will open your mouth, and will instruct you in what you shall say. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses said, I pray you, Lord, appoint another able [person] whom you shall send. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord was greatly angered against Moses, and said, Behold! is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he will surely speak to you; and, behold, he will come forth to meet you, and beholding you he will rejoice within himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall speak to him; and you shall put my words into his mouth, and I will open your mouth and his mouth, and I will instruct you in what you⌃ shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be your mouth, and you shall be for him in things pertaining to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And this rod that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand, wherewith you shall work miracles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Moses went and returned to Jothor his father-in-law, and says, I will go and return to my brethren in Egypt, and will see if they are yet living. And Jothor said to Moses, Go in health. And in those days after some time, the king of Egypt died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord said to Moses in Madiam, Go, depart into Egypt, for all that sought your life are dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Moses took his wife and his children, and mounted them on the beasts, and returned to Egypt; and Moses took the rod [which he had] from God in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord said to Moses, When you go and return to Egypt, see—all the miracles I have charged you with, you shall work before Pharao: and I will harden his heart, and he shall certainly not send away the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall say to Pharao, These things says the Lord, Israel [is] my firstborn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I said to you, Send away my people, that they may serve me: now if you will not send them away, see, I will kill your firstborn son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it came to pass [that] the angel of the Lord met him by the way in the inn, and sought to kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and Sepphora having taken a stone cut off the foreskin of her son, and fell at his feet and said, The blood of the circumcision of my son is staunched: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and he departed from him, because she said, The blood of the circumcision of my son is staunched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses; and he went and met him in the mount of God, and they kissed each other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the Lord, which he sent, and all the things which he charged him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses and Aaron went and gathered the elders of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Aaron spoke all these words, which God spoke to Moses, and wrought the miracles before the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and the people believed and rejoiced, because God visited the children of Israel, and because he saw their affliction: and the people bowed and worshipped.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{14} Name meaning: Aaron (Aharon) — Exalted; mountain of strength; teacher First high priest; exalted to lead worship. \textsuperscript{21} Heb. vocab: mofet (מוֹפֵת) = wonder; portent. Common English renderings: wonder; sign. Often paired with signs in Exodus tradition.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} put forth; And he put \textsuperscript{9} the water shall become Heb. shall be, and shall be blood \textsuperscript{10} eloquent Heb. a man of words; heretofore Heb. since yesterday, nor since the third day, slow of speech \textsuperscript{13} send; wilt send or, shouldest \textsuperscript{15} and put; and I, ; will teach \textsuperscript{18} Jethro Heb. Jether, Let me go and see; Go in peace; In the LXX and Coptic, the following addition is made to this verse: Μετα δε τας ημερας τας πολλας εκεινας ετελευτησεν ο βασιλευς Αιγυπτου, "After these many days, the king of Egypt died." This was probably an ancient side-note, which crept into the text, as it appeared to throw light on the next verse. \textsuperscript{19} Midian A country in Arabia Petrea, on the eastern coast of the Red Sea, near Mount Sinai. This place is still called by the Arabs the Land of Midian, or of Jethro. Abulfeda, speaking of Midian, says, "Madyan is a city, in ruins, on the shore of the Red Sea, on the opposite side to Tabuc, from which it is distant about six days' journey. At Midian may be seen the famous well at which Moses watered the flocks of Shoaib (Jethro). This city was the capital of the tribe of Midian in the days of the Israelites." for all \textsuperscript{24} the inn; The account in this and the two following verses, although rather obscure, seems to imply, that on their way to the land of Egypt, an angel appeared to Moses, and sought to kill his son, on account of his father's non-observance of the Lord's positive command to Abraham, that every man child of the Jewish nation, or born in his house in servitude, should be circumcised on the eighth day; and the Zipporah, at the command of Moses, immediately fulfilled the injunction, and thus averted the wrath of God, denounced against the disobedient: "The uncircumcised man child, whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people." the Lord; sought \textsuperscript{25} a sharp stone or, knife, cast it Heb. made it touch. a bloody \textsuperscript{27} Go into; the mount, ; kissed him\par}
