\subsection*{Exodus 5}
\markright{EXODUS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after this went in Moses and Aaron to Pharao, and they said to him, These things says the Lord God of Israel, Send my people away, that they may keep a feast to me in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Pharao said, Who is he that I should listen to his voice, so that I should send away the children of Israel? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they say to him, The God of the Hebrews has called us to him: we will go therefore a three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest at any time death or slaughter happen to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king of Egypt said to them, Why do you⌃, Moses and Aaron, turn the people from their works? depart each of you to your works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Pharao said, Behold now, the people is very numerous; let us not then give them rest from their work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Pharao gave orders to the taskmasters of the people and the accountants, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You⌃ shall no longer give straw to the people for brick-making as yesterday and the third day; but let them go themselves, and collect straw for themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall impose on them daily the rate of brick-making which they perform: you shall not abate anything, for they are idle; therefore have they cried, saying, Let us arise and do sacrifice to our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let the works of these men be made grievous, and let them care for these things, and not care for vain words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the taskmasters and the accountants hastened them, and they spoke to the people, saying, thus says Pharao, I [will] give you straw no longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Go you⌃, yourselves, get for yourselves straw wherever you⌃ can find it, for nothing is diminished from your rate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So the people were dispersed in all the land of Egypt, to gather stubble for straw. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and the taskmasters hastened them, saying, Fulfil your regular daily tasks, even as when straw was given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the accountants of the race of the children of Israel, who were set over them by the masters of Pharao, were scourged, [[and questioned,] men] saying, Why have you⌃ not fulfilled your rates of brick work as yesterday and the third day, today also? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the accountants of the children of Israel went in and cried to Pharao, saying, Why do you act thus to your servants? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Straw is not given to your servants, and they tell us to make brick; and behold your servants have been scourged: you will therefore injure your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said to them, You⌃ are idle, you⌃ are idlers: therefore you⌃ say, Let us go [and] do sacrifice to our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now then go and work, for straw shall not be given to you, yet you⌃ shall return the rate of bricks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the accountants of the children of Israel saw themselves in an evil plight, [men] saying, You⌃ shall not fail to deliver the daily rate of the brick-making. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they met Moses and Aaron coming forth to meet them, as they came forth from Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they said to them, The Lord look upon you and judge you, for you⌃ have made our savor abominable before Pharao, and before his servants, to put a sword into his hands to kill us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Moses turned to the Lord, and said, I pray, Lord, why have you afflicted this people? and therefore have you sent me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For from the time that I went to Pharao to speak in your name, he has afflicted this people, and you have not delivered your people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: sheqer (שֶׁקֶר) = falsehood; lie. Common English renderings: lie; falsehood. Moral and legal term for deception.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Who; , I know not; neither \textsuperscript{4} wherefore; let Taphreeoo, from pard, to loose, disengage; and which we render let, from the Anglo-Saxon lettan, to hinder. Ye hinder the people from their work: "Get you unto your burdens." "Let religion alone and mind your work." The language not only of tyranny, but of thoughtless irreligion. burdens \textsuperscript{6} taskmasters Nogesim, literally, exactors, oppressors. These taskmasters were Egyptians ( ), but the officers were Hebrews. ., ; officers Shoterim, from the Arabic saytara, to overlook, superintend, seems to denote, as musaytar in Arabic also does, overseers, superintendents. They may have been somewhat like the chiefs of trades, who are found in every city in the East; where every trade has a head, who is entrusted with authority over them, and is in some measure answerable for them to Government. Compare . \textsuperscript{7} straw The straw was mixed with clay, in order to make the bricks. This is expressly affirmed by Philo (vit. Mos.) who was himself a native of Alexandria, in Egypt. He says, describing the oppression of the Israelites, that some were obliged to work in clay, and others to gather straw for the formation of bricks, πλινθου γαρ αχυρα δεσμος, because straw is the binding of the brick. Philo's account is confirmed by Dr. Shaw, who says that "some of the Egyptian pyramids are made of brick, the composition whereof is only a mixture of clay, mud, and straw, slightly blended and kneaded together, and afterwards baked in the sun. The straw, which keeps the bricks together, and still preserves its original colour, seems to be a proof that these bricks were never burnt or made in kilns." The same materials are now used for building in Egypt. Mr. Baumgarten says, "The houses are for the most part of bricks that are only hardened by the heat of the sun, and mixed with straw to make them firm." \textsuperscript{8} tale Tale denotes number, from the Anglo-Saxon taellan, to number, count, etc. ye shall lay \textsuperscript{9} Let there more work be laid upon the men Heb. Let the work be heavy upon the men vain words \textsuperscript{13} daily tasks Heb. a matter of a day in his day \textsuperscript{21} The Lord; our savour; to be abhorred Heb. to stink \textsuperscript{23} in thy name; neither hast thou delivered Heb. delivering, thou hast not delivered\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 6}
\markright{EXODUS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, Now you shall see what I will do to Pharao; for he shall send them forth with a mighty hand, and with a high arm shall he cast them out of his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And God spoke to Moses and said to him, I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I appeared to Abraam and Isaac and Jacob, being their God, but I did not manifest to them my name Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of the Chananites, the land wherein they sojourned, in which also they lived as strangers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I listened to the groaning of the children of Israel (the affliction with which the Egyptians enslave them) and I remembered the covenant with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Go, speak to the children of Israel, saying, I [am] the Lord; and I will lead you forth from the tyranny of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from bondage, and I will ransom you with a high arm, and great judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I will take you to me a people for myself, and will be your God; and you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the tyranny of the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out my hand to give it to Abraam and Isaac and Jacob, and I will give it you for an inheritance: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses spoke thus to the sons of Israel, and they listened not to Moses for faint-heartedness, and for their hard tasks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Go in, speak to Pharao king of Egypt, that he send forth the children of Israel out of his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Moses spoke before the Lord, saying, Behold, the children of Israel listened not to me, and how shall Pharao listen to me? and I am not eloquent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and gave them a charge to Pharao king of Egypt, that he should send forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And these are the heads of the houses of their families: the sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel; Enoch and Phallus, Asron, and Charmi, this is the kindred of Ruben. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of Symeon, Jemuel and Jamin, and Aod, and Jachin and Saar, and Saul the son of a Phoenician woman, these are the families of the sons of Symeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their kindred, Gedson, Caath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these are the sons of Gedson, Lobeni and Semei, the houses of their family. And the sons of Caath, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Ambram and Issaar, Chebron, and Oziel; and the years of the life of Caath were a hundred and thirty-three years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sons of Merari, Mooli, and Omusi, these are the houses of the families of Levi, according to their kindred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Ambram took as wife Jochabed the daughter of his father's brother, and she bore to him both Aaron and Moses, and Mariam their sister: and the years of the life of Ambram were a hundred and thirty-two years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the sons of Issaar, Core, and Naphec, and Zechri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the sons of Oziel, Misael, and Elisaphan, and Segri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Aaron took to himself to wife Elisabeth daughter of Aminadab sister of Naasson, and she bore to him both Nadab and Abiud, and Eleazar and Ithamar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the sons of Core, Asir, and Elkana, and Abiasar, these are the generations of Core. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Eleazar the son of Aaron took to himself for a wife [one] of the daughters of Phutiel, and she bore to him Phinees. These are the heads of the family of the Levites, according to their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} This is Aaron and Moses, whom God told to bring out the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their forces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} These are they that spoke with Pharao king of Egypt, and Aaron himself and Moses brought out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} in the day in which the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, I am the Lord: speak to Pharao king of Egypt whatever I say to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Moses said before the Lord, Behold, I am not able in speech, and how shall Pharao listen to me?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Now shalt; with a strong; drive them \textsuperscript{2} I am the Lord or, Jehovah \textsuperscript{3} God Almighty El shadday, God Almighty; for shadday is evidently of affinity with the Arabic shadid, strong, mighty, and shiddat, strength, might; so the LXX in Job render it παντοκρατωρ, Vulgate, in Pentateuch, Omnipotens, and Syriac, in Job, chasino ., but by my name If Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, did not know the name Jehovah, then Moses must have used it in Genesis by prolepsis, or anticipation. Mr. Locke and others read it interrogatively, for the negative particle, lo, not, has frequently this power in Hebrew: "I appeared unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, and by my name Jehovah was I not also made known unto them?" Jehovah; JAH \textsuperscript{4} established, ; the land of their \textsuperscript{5} the groaning; I have remembered \textsuperscript{6} I am the Lord, ; I will bring; redeem \textsuperscript{7} will take;, ; I will be; from under \textsuperscript{8} swear Heb. lift up my hand, The ancient mode of appealing to God was by lifting up the right hand, and was considered as a form of swearing. Hence yamin, in Hebrew the right hand, is in Arabic an oath, and as a verb, to take an oath. A similar custom prevailed among the heathens. See Virg. Ζn. 1. xii. v. 196.;, to give;, I am \textsuperscript{9} hearkened; anguish Heb. shortness, or, straitness \textsuperscript{12} children, am The italics shew that this word has been supplied by our translators; hence it may be inferred by some that Moses was uncircumcised. The difficulty is in some measure cleared away, by using the word uncircumcised in the sense of unsuitable or incapacitated (see note on ), which agrees with where Moses complains of want of eloquence; but by substituting is for am in this place, the connection with the former part of the verse is preserved; "For if the chosen seed, the circumcised sons of Jacob, refuse to hear me, " as though Moses had said, "how can I expect to make uncircumcised Pharaoh pay attention to me?" \textsuperscript{14} the heads;, The sons; these be \textsuperscript{18} sons, Izehar; and the years \textsuperscript{20} Amram; and the years The Samaritan, LXX, Syriac, and one Hebrew manuscript add, "And Miriam their sister; " which some of the best critics suppose to have been originally in the text.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 7}
\markright{EXODUS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Behold, I have made you a god to Pharao, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall say to him all things that I charge you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharao, that he should send forth the children of Israel out of his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will harden the heart of Pharao, and I will multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Pharao will not listen to you, and I will lay my hand upon Egypt; and will bring out my people the children of Israel with my power out of the land of Egypt with great vengeance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, stretching out my hand upon Egypt, and I will bring out the children of Israel out of the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded them, so did they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron his brother was eighty-three years old, when he spoke to Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now if Pharao should speak to you, saying, Give us a sign or a wonder, then shall you say to your brother Aaron, Take your rod and cast it upon the ground before Pharao, and before his servants, and it shall become a serpent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharao, and [before] his servants, and they did so, as the Lord commanded them; and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharao, and before his servants, and it became a serpent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But Pharao called together the wise men of Egypt, and the sorcerers, and the charmers also of the Egyptians did likewise with their sorceries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they cast down each his rod, and they became serpents, but the rod of Aaron swallowed up their rods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he listened not to them, as the Lord charged them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and the Lord said to Moses, The heart of Pharao is made hard, so that he should not let the people go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Go to Pharao early in the morning: behold, he goes forth to the water; and you shall meet him on the bank of the river, and you shall take in your hand the rod that was turned into a serpent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall say to him, The Lord God of the Hebrews has sent me to you, saying, Send my people away, that they may serve me in the wilderness, and, behold, hitherto you have not listened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} These things says the Lord: Hereby shall you know that I am the Lord: behold, I strike with the rod that is in my hand on the water which is in the river, and it shall change it into blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall stink thereupon, and the Egyptians shall not be able to drink water from the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord said to Moses, Say to your brother Aaron, Take your rod in your hand, and stretch forth your hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and over their canals, and over their ponds, and over all their standing water, and it shall become blood: and there was blood in all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and of stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and Moses and Aaron did so, as the Lord commanded them; and [Aaron] having lifted up [his hand] with his rod, struck the water in the river before Pharao, and before his servants, and changed all the water in the river into blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the fish in the river died, and the river stank thereupon; and the Egyptians could not drink water from the river, and the blood was in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the charmers also of the Egyptians did so with their sorceries; and the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not listen to them, even as the Lord said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Pharao turned and entered into his house, nor did he fix his attention even on this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And all the Egyptians dug round about the river, so as to drink water, for they could not drink water from the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and seven days were fulfilled after the Lord has struck the river.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} that I, ; armies, by great \textsuperscript{10} as the Lord it became \textsuperscript{11} wise men;, ; sorcerers Mechashshaphim, probably from the Arabic kashapha, to discover, reveal, signifies diviners, or those who pretended to reveal futurity, to discover things lost, or to find hidden treasures. they also, ; enchantments By the word lahatim, from lahat, to burn, may be meant such incantations as required lustral fires, fumigations, etc. \textsuperscript{16} The Lord, ; Let my, ; serve \textsuperscript{18} the fish Egyptians "The water of Egypt, " says Abbe Mascrier, "is so delicious, that one would not wish the heat to be less, or to be delivered from the sensation of thirst. The Turks find it so exquisite, that they excite themselves to drink of it by eating salt." "A person, " adds Mr. Harmer, "who never before heard of the deliciousness of the Nile water, and of the large quantities which on that account are drunk of it, will, I am sure, find an energy in those words of Moses to Pharaoh, the Egyptians shall loathe to drink of the water of the river, which he never did before." shall loathe \textsuperscript{19} stretch, their pools Heb. gathering of their waters \textsuperscript{20} he lifted; all the waters As the Nile was held sacred by the Egyptians, as well as the animals it contained, to which they annually sacrificed a girl, or as others say, both a boy and girl, God might have designed this plague as a punishment for such idolatry and cruelty; and to shew them the baseness of those elements which they reverenced, and the insufficiency of the gods in which they trusted. All the punishments brought upon them bore a strict analogy to their crimes. \textsuperscript{21} The first miracle of Christ turned water into wine, the first plague upon Egypt turned all their water into blood. \textsuperscript{22} magicians; and Pharaoh's as the\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 8}
\markright{EXODUS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharao, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord: send forth my people, that they may serve me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if you will not send them forth, behold, I afflict all your borders with frogs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and the river shall teem with frogs, and they shall go up and enter into your houses, and into your bed-chambers, and upon your beds, and upon the houses of your servants, and of your people and on your dough, and on your ovens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And upon you, and upon your servants, and upon your people, shall the frogs come up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron your brother, Stretch forth with the hand your rod over the rivers, and over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Aaron stretched forth his hand over the waters of Egypt, and brought up the frogs: and the frog was brought up, and covered the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the charmers of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries, and brought up the frogs on the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said, Pray for me to the Lord, and let him take away the frogs from me and from my people; and I will send them away, and they shall sacrifice to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses said to Pharao, Appoint me [a time] when I shall pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, to cause the frogs to disappear from you, and from your people, and from your houses, only in the river shall they be left behind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said, On the morrow: he said therefore, As you have said; that you may know, that there is no other [God] but the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the frogs shall be removed away from you, and from your houses and from the villages, and from your servants, and from your people, only in the river they shall be left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Moses and Aaron went forth from Pharao, and Moses cried to the Lord concerning the restriction of the frogs, as Pharao appointed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord did as Moses said, and the frogs died out of the houses, and out of the villages, and out of the fields. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when Pharao saw that there was relief, his heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord spoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, Stretch forth your rod with your hand and strike the dust of the earth; and there shall be lice both upon man, and upon quadrupeds, and in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So Aaron stretched out his rod with his hand, and struck the dust of the earth; and the lice were on men and on quadrupeds, and in all the dust of the earth there were lice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the charmers also did so with their sorceries, to bring forth the louse, and they could not. And the lice were both on the men and on the quadrupeds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} So the charmers said to Pharao, This is the finger of God. But the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he listened not to them, as the Lord said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord said to Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharao: and behold, he will go forth to the water, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord: Send away my people, that they may serve me in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if you will not let my people go, behold, I send upon you, and upon your servants, and upon your people, and upon your houses, the dog-fly; and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with the dog-fly, even throughout the land upon which they are. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and I will distinguish marvelously in that day the land of Gesem, on which my people dwell, in which the dog-fly shall not be: that you may know that I am the Lord the God of all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I will put a difference between my people and your people, and on the morrow shall this be on the land. And the Lord did thus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the dog-fly came in abundance into the houses of Pharao, and into the houses of his servants, and into all the land of Egypt; and the land was destroyed by the dog-fly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, saying, Go and sacrifice to the Lord your God in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Moses said, It can’t be so, for we shall sacrifice to the Lord our God the abominations of the Egyptians; for if we sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians before them, we shall be stoned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, as the Lord said to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Pharao said, I [will] let you go, and do you⌃ sacrifice to your God in the wilderness, but do not go very far away: pray then for me to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses said, I then will go forth from you and pray to God, and the dog-fly shall depart both from your servants, and from your people to-morrow. Do not you, Pharao, deceive again, so as not to send the people away to do sacrifice to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Moses went out from Pharao, and prayed to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the Lord did as Moses said, and removed the dog-fly from Pharao, and from his servants, and from his people, and there was not one left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Pharao hardened his heart, even on this occasion, and he would not send the people away.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: pa’ar (פָּאַר) = to glorify; beautify. Common English renderings: glorify; beautify. Used of honor and adornment, especially in Isaiah. \textsuperscript{19} Gk. vocab: daktylos (δάκτυλος) = finger. Common English renderings: finger. Used literally and in the phrase finger of God.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} refuse, frogs The Hebrew tzephardêim is evidently the same with the Arabic zafda, Chaldaic oordeânaya, and Syriac oordeai, all of which denote frogs, as almost all interpreters, both ancient and modern, agree to render it; Bochart conceives, from tzifa, a bank, and rada, mud, because of delighting in muddy and marshy places. \textsuperscript{6} and the frogs Whether the frog among the Egyptians was an object of reverence or abhorrence is uncertain. It might have been both at the same time, as many objects are known to have been among particular nations; for proof of which see the very learned Jacob Bryant, on the Plagues of Egypt, pp. 31-34. \textsuperscript{8} Entreat, ; and I will, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{9} Glory over me or, Have this honour over me; when or, against when to destroy Heb. to cut of \textsuperscript{10} To morrow or, against to-morrow; there is none \textsuperscript{16} Stretch, lice The word kinnim is rendered by the LXX σκιφες, σκιπες, or σκνηφες, and by the Vulgate sciniphes, Gnats; and Mr. Harmer supposes he has found out the true meaning in the word tarrentes, a species of worm. Bochart, however, seems to have proved that lice, and not gnats, are meant; because: 1. They sprang from the dust, and not from the waters; 2. They were on both man and beast, which cannot be said of gnats; 3. Their name is derived from koon, to make firm, fix, establish, which cannot agree with gnats, flies, etc., which are ever changing place, and almost constantly on the wing; 4. The term kinnah is used by the Talmudists to express the louse. This insect must have been a very dreadful and afflicting plague to the Egyptians, and especially to the priests, who were obliged to shave all their hair off, and to wear a single linen tunic, to prevent vermin harbouring about them. \textsuperscript{21} swarms or, a mixture of noisome beasts, etc. The word arov is rendered κυνομυια, kunomuia, the dog-fly, by the LXX (who are followed by the learned Bochart), which must have been particularly hateful to the Egyptians, because they held dogs in the highest veneration, under which form they worshipped Anubis. \textsuperscript{23} a division Heb. a redemption to morrow or, by to-morrow \textsuperscript{24} there; the land How intolerable a plague of flies can prove, is evident from the fact that whole districts have been laid waste by them. The inhabitants have been forced to quit their cities, not being able to stand against the flies and gnats with which they were pestered. Hence different people had deities whose office it was to defend them against flies. Among these may be reckoned Baalzebub, the fly-god of Ekron; Hercules, muscarum abactor, Hercules the expeller of flies; and hence Jupiter had the titles of απομυιος, μυιαγρος, μυιοχορος, because he was supposed to expel flies, and especially clear his temples of these insects. See Bryant. corrupted or destroyed \textsuperscript{26} It is not; we shall; the abomination i.e. The animals which they worshipped; for an account of which, see note on . \textsuperscript{27} three days', as he shall\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 9}
\markright{EXODUS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharao, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord God of the Hebrews; Send my people away that they may serve me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If however you will not send my people away, but yet detain them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} behold, the hand of the Lord shall be upon your cattle in the fields, both on the horses, and on the asses, and on the camels and oxen and sheep, a very great mortality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will make a marvelous distinction in that time between the cattle of the Egyptians, and the cattle of the children of Israel: nothing shall die of all that is of the children's of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And God fixed a limit, saying, To-morrow the Lord will do this thing on the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord did this thing on the next day, and all the cattle of the Egyptians died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel there died not one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when Pharao saw, that of all the cattle of the children of Israel there died not one, the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not let the people go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, Take you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses scatter it toward heaven before Pharao, and before his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let it become dust over all the land of Egypt, and there shall be upon men and upon beasts sore blains breaking forth both on men and on beasts, in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So he took of the ashes of the furnace before Pharao, and Moses scattered it toward heaven, and it became sore blains breaking forth both on men and on beasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the sorcerers could not stand before Moses because of the sores, for the sores were on the sorcerers, and in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord hardened Pharao's heart, and he listened not to them, as the Lord appointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord said to Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharao; and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord God of the Hebrews, Send away my people that they may serve me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For at this present time do I send forth all my plagues into your heart, and the heart of your servants and of your people; that you may know that there is not another such as I in all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For now I will stretch forth my hand and strike you and kill your people, and you shall be consumed from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And for this purpose have you been preserved, that I might display in you my strength, and that my name might be published in all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Do you then yet exert yourself to hinder my people, so as not to let them go? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold, to-morrow at this hour I will rain a very great hail, such as has not been in Egypt, from the time it was created until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now then hasten to gather your cattle, and all that you have in the fields; for all the men and cattle as many as shall be found in the fields, and shall not enter into a house, (but the hail shall fall upon them,) shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He of the servants of Pharao that feared the word of the Lord, gathered his cattle into the houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he that did not attend in his mind to the word of the Lord, left the cattle in the fields. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch out your hand to heaven, and there shall be hail on all the land of Egypt, both on the men and on the cattle, and on all the herbage on the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses stretched forth his hand to heaven, and the Lord sent thunderings and hail; and the fire ran along upon the ground, and the Lord rained hail on all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} So there was hail and flaming fire mingled with hail; and the hail was very great, such as was not in Egypt, from the time there was a nation upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt both man and beast, and the hail struck all the grass in the field, and the hail broke in pieces all the trees in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Only in the land of Gesem where the children of Israel were, the hail was not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Pharao sent and called Moses and Aaron, and said to them, I have sinned this time: the Lord [is] righteous, and I and my people are wicked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Pray then for me to the Lord, and let him cause the thunderings of God to cease, and the hail and the fire, and I will send you forth and you⌃ shall remain no longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses said to him, When I shall have departed from the city, I will stretch out my hands to the Lord, and the thunderings shall cease, and the hail and the rain shall be no longer, that you may know that the earth [is] the Lord's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But as for you and your servants, I know that you⌃ have not yet feared the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was advanced, and the flax was seeding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But the wheat and the rye were not struck, for they were late. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Moses went forth from Pharao out of the city, and stretched out his hands to the Lord, and the thunders ceased and the hail, and the rain did not drop on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And when Pharao saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders ceased, he continued to sin; and [he] hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not send forth the children of Israel, as the Lord said to Moses.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: makkah (מַכָּה) = blow; plague. Common English renderings: plague; stroke. Term for inflicted blow, wound, or plague.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the hand; murrain We may observe a particular scope and meaning in this calamity, if we consider it in regard to the Egyptians, which would not have existed in respect to any other people. They held in idolatrous reverence almost every animal, but some they held in particular veneration; as the ox, cow, and ram. Among these, Apis and Mnevis are well known; the former being a sacred bull, worshipped at Memphis, as the latter was at Heliopolis. A cow or heifer had the like honours at Momemphis; and the same practice seems to have been adopted in most of the Egyptian nomes . By the infliction of this judgment, the Egyptian deities sank before the God of the Hebrews. See Bryant, pp. 87-93. \textsuperscript{8} Take to This was a significant command; not only referring to the fiery furnace, which was a type of the slavery of the Israelites, but to a cruel rite common among the Egyptians. They had several cities styled Typhonian, in which at particular seasons they sacrificed men, who were burnt alive; and the ashes of the victim were scattered upwards in the air, with the view, probably, that where any atom of dust was carried, a blessing was entailed. The like, therefore, was done by Moses, though with a different intention, and more certain effect. See Bryant, pp. 93-106. \textsuperscript{12} Hardness of heart is a figurative expression, denoting that insensibility of mind upon which neither judgments nor mercies make any abiding impressions; but the conscience being stupefied, the obdurate rebel persists in determined disobedience. \textsuperscript{16} deed; raised thee up Heb. made thee stand for to, ; that my \textsuperscript{18} to morrow; I will cause This must have been a circumstance of all others the most incredible to an Egyptian; for in Egypt there fell no rain, the want of which was supplied by dews, and the overflowing of the Nile. The Egyptians must, therefore, have perceived themselves particularly aimed at in these fearful events, especially as they were very superstitious. There seems likewise a propriety in their being punished by fire and water, as they were guilty of the grossest idolatry towards these elements. Scarcely anything could have distressed the Egyptians more than the destruction of the flax, as the whole nation wore linen garments. The ruin of their barley was equally fatal, both to their trade and to their private advantage. See Bryant, pp. 108-117. \textsuperscript{21} regarded not Heb. set not his heart unto; *marg.; *marg. \textsuperscript{23} the Lord sent; and hail \textsuperscript{28} Entreat, ; mighty thunderings Heb. voices of God, ye shall \textsuperscript{31} flax The word pishteh, flax, Mr. Parkhurst thinks may be derived from pashat, to strip, because the substance which we call flax is properly the filaments of the bark or rind of the vegetable, stripped off the stalks. From time immemorial, Egypt was celebrated for the production and manufacture of flax; and hence the linen and fine linen of Egypt, so often spoken of in scripture and ancient authors. the barley The Hebrew seorah, barley, in Arabic shair, and shairat, is so called from its rough, bristly beard, with which the ears are covered and defended; from saâr, to stand on end as the hair of the head. Hence seâr, the hair of the head. So its Latin name hordeum is from horreo, to stand on end as the hair. Dr. Pococke has observed that there is a double seed time and harvest in Egypt; rice, India wheat, and a grain called the corn of Damascus, are sown and reaped at a very different time from wheat, barley, and flax. The first are sown in March, before the overflowing of the Nile, and reaped about October; whereas the wheat and barley are sown in November and December, as soon as the Nile has gone off, and reaped before May. \textsuperscript{32} not grown up Heb. hidden, or dark\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 10}
\markright{EXODUS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Go in to Pharao: for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that these signs may come upon them; in order {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that you⌃ may relate in the ears of your children, and to your children's children, in how many things I have mocked the Egyptians, and my wonders which I wrought among them; and you⌃ shall know that I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharao, and they said to him, These things says the Lord God of the Hebrews, How long do you refuse to reverence me? Send my people away, that they may serve me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But if you will not send my people away, behold, at this hour to-morrow I will bring an abundance of locusts upon all your coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall cover the face of the earth, and you shall not be able to see the earth; and they shall devour all that is left of the abundance of the earth, which the hail has left you, and shall devour every tree that grows for you on the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians; things which your fathers have never seen, nor their forefathers, from the day that they were upon the earth until this day. And Moses turned away and departed from Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the servants of Pharao say to him, How long shall this be a snare to us? send away the men, that they may serve their God; will you know that Egypt is destroyed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they brought back both Moses and Aaron to Pharao; and he said to them, Go and serve the Lord your God; but who are they that are going with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses said, We will go with the young and the old, with our sons, and daughters, and sheep, and oxen, for it is a feast of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said to them, So let the Lord be with you: as I [will] send you away, [must I send away] you store also? see that evil is attached to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Not so, but let the men go and serve God, for this you⌃ yourselves seek; and they cast them out from the presence of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let the locust come up on the land, and it shall devour every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees, which the hail left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses lifted up his rod towards heaven, and the Lord brought a south wind upon the earth, all that day and all that night: the morning dawned, and the south wind brought up the locusts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and brought them up over all the land of Egypt. And they rested in very great abundance over all the borders of Egypt. Before them there were not such locusts, neither after them shall there be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they covered the face of the earth, and the land was wasted, and they devoured all the herbage of the land, and all the fruit of the trees, which was left by the hail: there was no green thing left on the trees, nor on all the herbage of the field, in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Pharao hasted to call Moses and Aaron, saying, I have sinned before the Lord your God, and against you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} pardon therefore my sin yet this time, and pray to the Lord your God, and let him take away from me this death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Moses went forth from Pharao, and prayed to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord brought in the opposite direction a strong wind from the sea, and took up the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea, and there was not one locust left in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not send away the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch out your hand to heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt—darkness that may be felt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Moses stretched out his hand to heaven, and there was darkness very black, even a storm over all the land of Egypt three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And for three days no man saw his brother, and no man rose up from his bed for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in all the places where they were. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, saying, Go, serve the Lord your God, only leave your sheep and your oxen, and let your store depart with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses said, Nay, but you shall give to us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, which we will sacrifice to the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And our cattle shall go with us, and we will not leave a hoof behind, for of them we will take to serve the Lord our God: but we know not in what manner we shall serve the Lord our God, until we arrive there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he would not let them go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Pharao says, Depart from me, beware of seeing my face again, for in what day you shall appear before me, you shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses says, You have said, I will not appear in your presence again.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: gever (גֶּבֶר) = man; strong man. Common English renderings: man. Often emphasizes male strength or adulthood.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I have hardened, ; that I \textsuperscript{4} morrow, locusts The word arbeh, Locust, is derived from ravah, to multiply, be numerous, etc., because they are more prolific than any other insect, and because of the immense swarms of them by which different countries, especially the East, are infested. The locust, in entomology, belongs to a genus of insects known among naturalists by the name of Grylli; which includes three species, crickets, grasshoppers, and locusts. The common great brown locust is about three inches in length; has two antennae about an inch long, and two pair of wings. The head and horns are brown; the mouth and inside of the larger legs bluish; the upper side of the body and upper wings brown, the former spotted with black, and the latter with dusky spots. The back is defended by a shield of a greenish hue. The under wings are of a light brown, tinctured with green, and nearly transparent. It has a large open mouth, in the two jaws of which it has four teeth, which traverse each other like scissors, being calculated, from their mechanism, to gripe or cut. The general appearance of the insect is that of the grasshopper. The Egyptians had gods in whom they trusted to deliver them from these terrible invaders; but by this judgment they were taught that it was impossible to stand before Moses, the servant of Jehovah. \textsuperscript{5} face Heb. eye, the residue \textsuperscript{7} How long snare; that Egypt \textsuperscript{8} brought, who Heb. who, and who, etc \textsuperscript{9} We will go; our flocks a feast \textsuperscript{10} be so, look to it \textsuperscript{14} the locusts; very grievous; before \textsuperscript{16} called for Heb. hastened to call I have \textsuperscript{17} forgive and entreat; this death \textsuperscript{19} a mighty cast Heb. fastened the Red sea \textsuperscript{21} Stretch darkness As the Egyptians not only worshipped the light and sun, but also paid the same veneration to night and darkness, nothing could be more terrible than this punishment of palpable and coercive darkness, such as their luminary Osiris could not dispel. See Bryant, pp. 141-160., ; even darkness which may be felt Heb. that one may feel darkness \textsuperscript{24} Go ye, flocks little ones \textsuperscript{25} us Heb. into our hands sacrifices, 36:1-40:38 \textsuperscript{28} Get thee for in that\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 11}
\markright{EXODUS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, I will yet bring one plague upon Pharao and upon Egypt, and after that he will send you forth thence; and whenever he sends you forth with every thing, he will indeed drive you out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak therefore secretly in the ears of the people, and let every one ask of his neighbor jewels of silver and gold, and raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord gave his people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and the man Moses was very great before the Egyptians, and before Pharao, and before his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses said, These things says the Lord, About midnight I go forth into the midst of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharao that sits on the throne, even to the firstborn of the woman-servant that is by the mill, and to the firstborn of all cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there shall be a great cry through all the land of Egypt, such as has not been, and such shall not be repeated any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But among all the children of Israel shall not a dog snarl with his tongue, either at man or beast; that you may know how wide a distinction the Lord will make between the Egyptians and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all these your servants shall come down to me, and do me reverence, saying, Go forth, you and all the people over whom you preside, and afterwards I will go forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses went forth from Pharao with wrath. And the Lord said to Moses, Pharao will not listen to you, that I may greatly multiply my signs and wonders in the land [of] Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses and Aaron wrought all these signs and wonders in the land [of] Egypt before Pharao; and the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not listen to send forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.\par

\subsection*{Exodus 12}
\markright{EXODUS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} This month [shall be] to you the beginning of months: it is the first to you among the months of the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, On the tenth of this month let them take each man a lamb according to the houses of their families, every man a lamb for his household. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if they be few in a household, so that there are not enough for the lamb, he shall take with himself his neighbor that lives near to him, —as to the number of souls, every one according to that which suffices him shall make a reckoning for the lamb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} It shall be to you a lamb unblemished, a male of a year old: you⌃ shall take it of the lambs and the kids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it shall be kept by you till the fourteenth of this month, and all the multitude of the congregation of the children of Israel shall kill it toward evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they shall take of the blood, and shall put it on the two door-posts, and on the lintel, in the houses in which soever they shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they shall eat the flesh in this night roast with fire, and they shall eat unleavened [bread] with bitter herbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You⌃ shall not eat of it raw nor sodden in water, but only roast with fire, the head with the feet and the appurtenances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Nothing shall be left of it till the morning, and a bone of it you⌃ shall not break; but that which is left of it till the morning you⌃ shall burn with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And thus shall you⌃ eat it: your loins girded, and your sandals on your feet, and your staves in your hands, and you⌃ shall eat it in haste. It is a passover to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and I will go throughout the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt both man and beast, and on all the gods of Egypt will I execute vengeance: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the blood shall be for a sign to you on the houses in which you⌃ are, and I will see the blood, and will protect you, and there shall not be on you the plague of destruction, when I strike in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And this day shall be to you a memorial, and you⌃ shall keep it a feast to the Lord through all your generations; you⌃ shall keep it a feast for a perpetual ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Seven days you⌃ shall eat unleavened bread, and from the first day you⌃ shall utterly remove leaven from your houses: whoever shall eat leaven, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be a holy convocation to you: you⌃ shall do no servile work on them, only as many things as will [necessarily] be done by every soul, this only shall be done by you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you⌃ shall keep this commandment, for on this day will I bring out your force out of the land of Egypt; and you⌃ shall make this day a perpetual ordinance for you throughout your generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Beginning the fourteenth day of the first month, you⌃ shall eat unleavened bread from evening, till the twenty-first day of the month, till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses; whoever shall eat anything leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, both among the occupiers of the land and the original inhabitants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You⌃ shall eat nothing leavened, but in every habitation of yours you⌃ shall eat unleavened bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses called all the elders of the children of Israel, and said to them, Go away and take to yourselves a lamb according to your kindred, and kill the passover. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you⌃ shall take a bunch of hyssop, and having dipped it into some of the blood that is by the door, you⌃ shall touch the lintel, and [shall put it] upon both door-posts, even of the blood which is by the door; but you⌃ shall not go out every one from the door of his house till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord shall pass by to strike the Egyptians, and shall see the blood upon the lintel, and upon both the door-posts; and the Lord shall pass by the door, and shall not suffer the destroyer to enter into your houses to strike [you]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And keep you⌃ this thing as an ordinance for yourself and for your children for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if you⌃ should enter into the land, which the Lord shall give you, as he has spoken, keep this service. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it shall come to pass, if your sons say to you, What is this service? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} that you⌃ shall say to them, This passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, as he defended the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, but delivered our houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the people bowed and worshipped. And the children of Israel departed and did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it came to pass at midnight that the Lord struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao that sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the captive-maid in the dungeon, and the firstborn of all cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Pharao rose up by night, and his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in all the land of Egypt, for there was not a house in which there was not one dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Pharao called Moses and Aaron by night, and said to them, Rise and depart from my people, both you⌃ and the children of Israel. Go and serve the Lord your God, even as you⌃ say. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And take with you your sheep, and your oxen: bless me also, I pray you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the Egyptians constrained the people, so that they cast them out of the land with haste, for they said, We all shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the people took their dough before their meal was leavened, bound up [as it was] in their garments, on their shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the children of Israel did as Moses commanded them, and they asked of the Egyptians articles of silver and gold and apparel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the Lord gave his people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and they spoiled the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the children Israel departed from Ramesses to Socchoth, to [the full number of] six hundred thousand footmen, even men, besides the baggage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And a great mixed [company] went up with them, and sheep and oxen and very much cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And they baked the dough which they brought out of Egypt, unleavened cakes, for it had not been leavened; for the Egyptians cast them out, and they could not remain, neither did they prepare provision for themselves for the journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the sojourning of the children of Israel, while they sojourned in the land of Egypt and the land of Chanaan, [was] four hundred and thirty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And it came to pass after the four hundred and thirty years, all the forces of the Lord came forth out of the land of Egypt by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} It is a watch kept to the Lord, so that he should bring them out of the land of Egypt; that very night is a watch kept to the Lord, so that it should be to all the children of Israel to their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, This is the law of the passover: no stranger shall eat of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And every slave or servant bought with money—him you shall circumcise, and then shall he eat of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} A sojourner or hireling shall not eat of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} In one house shall it be eaten, and you⌃ shall not carry of the flesh out from the house; and a bone of it you⌃ shall not break. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} All the congregation of the children of Israel shall keep it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And if any proselyte shall come to you to keep the passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male of him, and then shall he approach to sacrifice it, and he shall be even as the original inhabitant of the land; no uncircumcised person shall eat of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} There shall be one law to the native, and to the proselyte coming among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron for them, so they did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And it came to pass in that day that the Lord brought out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt with their forces.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: edah (עֵדָה) = congregation; company. Common English renderings: congregation. Corporate term for the community of Israel. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: pesach (פֶּסַח) = Passover. Common English renderings: Passover. Festival memorializing deliverance from Egypt. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: pasach (פָּסַח) = to pass over; spare. Common English renderings: pass over. Source of Passover terminology. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: chuqqah (חֻקָּה) = statute; ordinance. Common English renderings: statute; ordinance. Common feminine form for prescribed regulation. \textsuperscript{15} Gk. vocab: zymē (ζύμη) = leaven; yeast. Common English renderings: leaven. Frequently used literally and in moral or doctrinal metaphor. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: nagaph (נָגַף) = to strike; smite. Common English renderings: smite; plague. Frequently used in judgment or military defeat. \textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: latreia (λατρεία) = service; worship. Common English renderings: service; worship. A term for sacred service or worship. \textsuperscript{49} Heb. vocab: torah (תּוֹרָה) = instruction; law. Common English renderings: law; instruction. Broader than legal code; can mean teaching or revealed instruction. Gk. vocab: nomos (νόμος) = law. Common English renderings: law. Usually denotes law or legal norm; often the Mosaic law in biblical context.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} am 2513, bc 1491, An, Exod, Isr, 1, Abib or Nisan \textsuperscript{3} Speak ye, ; in the tenth; take to; , lamb or, kid, The word seh means the young of both sheep and goats, and may be indifferently rendered either lamb or kid. It is evident from that the Hebrews might take either; but they generally preferred a lamb, from being of a more gentle nature.; an house The Israelites were divided into twelve tribes, these tribes into families, the families into houses, and the houses into particular persons. \textsuperscript{5} be without, ; a male of the first year Heb. son of a year; *marg. \textsuperscript{6} fourteenth; the whole; , ;, in the evening Heb. between the two evenings, The Jews divided the day into morning and evening. Till the sun passed the meridian, all was morning or forenoon; after that, all was evening or afternoon. Their first evening began just after twelve o'clock, and continued till sunset; their second evening began at sunset, and continued till night, i.e., during the whole time of twilight; between twelve o'clock, therefore, and the termination of twilight, the passover was to be offered (see parallel passages). \textsuperscript{8} eat the; roast; unleavened, ; with bitter \textsuperscript{11} loins; shoes; it is the \textsuperscript{12} pass; will smite, against; gods or, princes, ; I am the Lord \textsuperscript{13} the blood; and when; to destroy you Heb. for a destruction \textsuperscript{14} memorial; a feast; by an ordinance \textsuperscript{16} first day, ;, no manner, ; man Heb. soul \textsuperscript{17} in this selfsame; an ordinance \textsuperscript{21} elders, ; and take; lamb or, kid, *marg. the passover That is, the lamb which was called the paschal, or passover lamb; the animal sacrificed obtaining the name of the institution. St. Paul copies the expression in . \textsuperscript{22} a bunch; , ; hyssop The word aizov, which has been variously rendered, most probably denotes Hyssop; whence are derived the Chaldee aizova, Syriac zupha, Arabic zupha, Ethiopic azab, and hushopa, Greek υσσωπος, hussopos, Latin hyssopus, German usop, and our hyssop, a name retained, with little variation, in all the western languages. It is a plant of the gymnospermia (naked seeded) order, belonging to the didynamia class. It has bushy stalks, growing a foot and a half high; small spear-shaped, close-sitting, and opposite leaves, with several smaller ones rising from the same joint; and all the stalks and branches terminated by erect whorled spikes of flowers, of different colours in the varieties of the plant. The leaves have an aromatic smell, and a warm, pungent taste. Its detersive, cleansing, and medicinal qualities were probably the reason why it was so particularly recommended in Scripture. strike and none \textsuperscript{23} will pass through and will not \textsuperscript{27} It is the sacrifice, ; bowed \textsuperscript{29} at midnight, ; the Lord smote The infliction of this judgment on the Egyptians was most equitable; because, after their nation had been preserved by one of the Israelitish family, they had, contrary to all right, and in defiance of original stipulation, enslaved the people to whom they had been so much indebted, had murdered their offspring, and made their bondage intolerable. See Bryant, p. 160., ;, ; the firstborn of Pharaoh, dungeon Heb. house of the pit \textsuperscript{30} and there was a great cry No people were more remarkable and frantic in their mournings than the Egyptians. When a relative died, every one left the house, and the women, with their hair loose, and their bosoms bare, ran wild about the street. The men also, with their apparel equally disordered, kept them company; all shrieking, howling, and beating themselves. What a scene of horror and distress must now have presented itself, when there was not a family in Egypt where there was not one dead! \textsuperscript{31} called Rise up, ; the children \textsuperscript{34} kneading troughs, or, dough; Probably like the kneading-troughs of the Arabs; comparatively small wooden bowls, which also serve them for dishes. Their being bound up in their clothes may mean no more than their being wrapped up in their hykes, or long, loose, garments. See Shaw's Travels, p. 224, 4to. edit. \textsuperscript{37} the children, Rameses; six hundred \textsuperscript{38} And a mixed multitude Heb. a great mixture \textsuperscript{40} The Samaritan Pentateuch reads, "Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, and of their fathers in the land of Canaan and in the land of Egypt, was 430 years." The Alexandrine copy of the LXX has the same reading; and the same statement is made by the apostle Paul, in, who reckons from the promise made to Abraham to the giving of the law. That these three witnesses have the truth, the chronology itself proves; for it is evident that the descendants of Israel did not dwell 430 years in Egypt; while it is equally evident, that the period from Abraham's entry into Canaan to the Exodus, is exactly that number. Thus, from Abraham's entrance into the promised land to the birth of Isaac, was 25 years; Isaac was 60 at the birth of Jacob; Jacob was 130 at his going into Egypt; where he and his children continued 215 years more; making in the whole 430 years. See Kennicott's Dissertation on the Hebrew Text. sojourning; four hundred \textsuperscript{42} a night to be much observed Heb. a night of observations, observed. \textsuperscript{47} All the; keep it Heb. do it \textsuperscript{48} a stranger; let all; shall be \textsuperscript{50} as the Lord; by their armies\par}
