\subsection*{Exodus 13}
\markright{EXODUS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Sanctify to me every firstborn, first produced, opening every womb among the children of Israel both of man and beast: it is mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses said to the people, Remember this day, in which you⌃ came forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for with a strong hand the Lord brought you forth thence; and leaven shall not be eaten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For on this day you⌃ go forth in the month of new [corn]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it shall come to pass when the Lord your God shall have brought you into the land of the Chananites, and the Chettites, and Amorites, and Evites, and Jebusites, and Gergesites, and Pherezites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Six days you⌃ shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a feast to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Seven days shall you⌃ eat unleavened bread; nothing leavened shall be seen with you, neither shall you have leaven in all your borders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall tell your son in that day, saying, Therefore the Lord dealt thus with me, as I was going out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall be to you a sign upon your hand and a memorial before your eyes, that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth, for with a strong hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And preserve you⌃ this law according to the times of the seasons, from year to year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it shall come to pass when the Lord your God shall bring you into the land of the Chananites, as he swore to your fathers, and shall give it you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that you shall set apart every [offspring] opening the womb, the males to the Lord, every one that opens the womb out of the herds or among your cattle, as many as you shall have: you shall sanctify the males to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Every [offspring] opening the womb of the ass you shall change for a sheep; and if you will not change it, you shall redeem it: every firstborn of man of your sons shall you redeem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if your son should ask you hereafter, saying, What is this? then you shall say to him, With a strong hand the Lord brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when Pharao hardened [his heart so as not] to send us away, he killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man and the firstborn of beast; therefore do I sacrifice every [offspring] that opens the womb, the males to the Lord, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it shall be for a sign upon your hand, and immovable before your eyes, for with a strong hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when Pharao sent forth the people, God led them not by the way of the land of the Phylistines, because it was near; for God said, Lest at any time the people repent when they see war, and return to Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And God led the people round by the way to the wilderness, to the Red Sea: and in the fifth generation the children of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had solemnly adjured the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and you⌃ shall carry up my bones hence with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the children of Israel departed from Socchoth, and encamped in Othom by the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And God led them, in the day by a pillar of cloud, to show them the way, and in the night by a pillar of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the pillar of cloud failed not by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, before all the people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: petach rechem (פָּתַח רֶחֶם) = opening of the womb. Common English renderings: openeth the womb. Technical phrase for the firstborn issue of the womb. \textsuperscript{13} Heb. vocab: padah (פָּדָה) = to ransom; redeem. Common English renderings: redeem. Emphasizes redemption by payment, substitution, or deliverance. \textsuperscript{21} Heb. vocab: anan (עָנָן) = cloud. Common English renderings: cloud. Associated with divine presence and guidance. Gk. vocab: nephelē (νεφέλη) = cloud. Common English renderings: cloud. Frequently associated with divine presence.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Sanctify The word kadash is to consecrate, separate, and set apart a person or thing from all common or secular purposes to some religious use; and exactly answers to the Greek αγιαζω, from α, privative, and γη, the earth; because everything offered or consecrated to God was separated from all earthly uses. \textsuperscript{3} Remember, ;, ; out of the;, ; bondage Heb. servants strength; there \textsuperscript{5} shall bring;, ; sware;, ;, a land thou shalt keep \textsuperscript{9} a sign This expression, says Michaelis, alludes to the custom of the Orientals, of burning in their right hand all kinds of marks with the ashes of henna, which gives an indelible colour; and this is done even to this day. They were likewise accustomed to write all kinds of sayings, and frequently superstitious words, on slips or pieces of linen, which they wore as ornaments on their foreheads.; may be; strong hand \textsuperscript{12} thou shalt, ; set apart Heb. cause to pass over openeth \textsuperscript{13} of an ass; lamb or, kid, shalt thou \textsuperscript{14} thy son; in time to come Heb. tomorrow; By strength \textsuperscript{15} the Lord slew therefore I \textsuperscript{16} a token, frontlets; for by \textsuperscript{18} led the; harnessed or, by five in a rank \textsuperscript{22} He took pillar of fire\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 14}
\markright{EXODUS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and let them turn and encamp before the village, between Magdol and the sea, opposite Beel-sepphon: before them shall you encamp by the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Pharao will say to his people, As for these children of Israel, they are wandering in the land, for the wilderness has shut them in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will harden the heart of Pharao, and he shall pursue after them; and I will be glorified in Pharao, and in all his host, and all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord. And they did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled: and the heart of Pharao was turned, and that of his servants against the people; and they said, What is this that we have done, to let the children of Israel go, so that they should not serve us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Pharao yoked his chariots, and led off all his people with himself: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} having also taken six hundred chosen chariots, and all the cavalry of the Egyptians, and rulers over all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao king of Egypt, and of his servants, and he pursued after the children of Israel; and the children of Israel went forth with a high hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Egyptians pursued after them, and found them encamped by the sea; and all the cavalry and the chariots of Pharao, and the horsemen, and his host [were] before the village, over against Beel-sepphon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Pharao approached, and the children of Israel having looked up, saw, and the Egyptians encamped behind them: and they were very greatly terrified, and the children of Israel cried to the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and said to Moses, Because there were no graves in the land of Egypt, have you brought us forth to kill [us] in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, having brought us out of Egypt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Is not this the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, Let us alone that we may serve the Egyptians? for it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses said to the people, Be of good courage: stand and see the salvation which is from the Lord, which he will work for us this day; for as you⌃ have seen the Egyptians today, you⌃ shall see them again no more for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord shall fight for you, and you⌃ shall hold your peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the Lord said to Moses, Why do you cry to me? speak to the children of Israel, and let them proceed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And do you lift up your rod, and stretch forth your hand over the sea, and divide it, and let the children of Israel enter into the midst of the sea on the dry land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And behold! I will harden the heart of Pharao and of all the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them; and I will be glorified upon Pharao, and on all his host, and on his chariots and his horses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I am glorified upon Pharao and upon his chariots and his horses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the angel of God that went before the camp of the children of Israel removed and went behind, and the pillar of the cloud also removed from before them and stood behind them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it went between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and stood; and there was darkness and blackness; and the night passed, and they came not near to one another during the whole night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the Lord carried back the sea with a strong south wind all the night, and made the sea dry, and the water was divided. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry land, and the water of it was a wall on the right hand and a wall on the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Egyptians pursued them and went in after them, and every horse of Pharao, and his chariots, and his horsemen, into the midst of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it came to pass in the morning watch that the Lord looked forth on the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and cloud, and troubled the camp of the Egyptians, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and bound the axle-trees of their chariots, and caused them to go with difficulty; and the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch forth your hand over the sea, and let the water be turned back to its place, and let it cover the Egyptians [coming] both upon the chariots and the riders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the water returned to its place toward day; and the Egyptians fled from the water, and the Lord shook off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and the water returned and covered the chariots and the riders, and all the forces of Pharao, who entered after them into the sea: and there was not left of them even one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But the children of Israel went along dry land in the midst of the sea, and the water was to them a wall on the right hand, and a wall on the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So the Lord delivered Israel in that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead by the shore of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Israel saw the mighty hand, the [things] which the Lord did to the Egyptians; and the people feared the Lord, and they believed God and Moses his servant.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{4} Gk. vocab: doxazō (δοξάζω) = to glorify; honor. Common English renderings: glorify. A verb for giving glory or being glorified. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: lacham (לָחַם) = to fight; wage war. Common English renderings: fight. Verb for battle, also a different root in noun bread. \textsuperscript{30} Heb. vocab: yasha (יָשַׁע) = to save; deliver. Common English renderings: save. The principal Hebrew salvation verb, denoting rescue and deliverance.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} that they; Pi-hahiroth Pi̇hachiroth, "the mouth of Chiroth, " as it is rendered by the LXX. Dr. Shaw is of opinion, that Chiroth denotes the valley which extends from the wilderness of Etham to the Red Sea. "This valley, " he observes, "ends at the sea in a small bay made by the eastern extremities of the mountains (of Gewoubee and Attackah, between which the valley lies) which I have been describing, and is called Tiah - Beni - Israel, i.e., the road of the Israelites, by a tradition that is still kept up by the Arabs, of their having passed through it; so it is also called Baideah, from the new and unheard of miracle that was wrought near it, by dividing the Red sea, and destroying therein Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen." Migdol The word Migdol signifies a tower, and hence some have supposed that it was a fortress which served to defend the bay. But the LXX render it Μαγδωλος, Magdolus, which is mentioned by Herodotus, Hecateus, and others, and is expressly said by Stephanus (de Urb.) to be πολις Αιγυπτον, "a city of Egypt." This Bochart conjectures to have been the same as Migdol (see the parallel passages).; Heb Baalzephon This may have been the name of a town or city in which Baal was worshipped; and probably called zephon, from being situated on the north point of the Red sea, near the present Suez. \textsuperscript{4} harden, ; I will be, ; that the Egyptians \textsuperscript{5} and the heart; Why have we \textsuperscript{8} the Lord with an high hand \textsuperscript{12} Is not this, Let us alone;, For it had \textsuperscript{13} Fear ye not; , ; see the; for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day or, for whereas ye have seen the Egyptians to-day, etc ye shall see \textsuperscript{16} lift, the sea This sea was what is called in Scripture yam suph, "the sea of weeds; " so called, according to Mr. Bruce, from the vast quantity of coral which grows in it. In the LXX it is called θαλασσα ερυθρα, and by the Latins Rubrum mare, and we from them the Red Sea; so called it is supposed, from Edom (red) or Esau, whose territories extend to its coasts. It separates Arabia from Egypt and Ethiopia, and is computed to be 150 leagues in length from Suez to the straits of Babelmandel. The upper part is divided into two gulfs, that to the East called the Elanitic, from the city Elana at the northern extremity, and that to the west, the Heroopolitic, from the city of Heroopolis. The former is called by the Arabians Bahr el Akaba, the sea of Akaba; and the latter Bahr el Kolzum, the sea of destruction, or Clysmζ; which was that which the Israelites passed. and the \textsuperscript{17} behold; , ; I will, and I will \textsuperscript{19} the angel, ; and the pillar \textsuperscript{22} the children; and the waters This verse demonstrates that this event was wholly miraculous, and cannot be ascribed, as some have supposed, to an extraordinary ebb, which happened just then to be produced by a strong east wind. For this would not have caused the waters, contrary to every law of fluids, to stand as a wall on the right hand and the left. a wall \textsuperscript{24} that in the looked unto;, through and troubled \textsuperscript{25} took off; that they drave them heavily or, and made them to go heavily Let us flee, ;, for the Lord \textsuperscript{27} and the sea; Lord overthrew Heb. shook off \textsuperscript{31} work Heb. hand feared; believed\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 15}
\markright{EXODUS 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song to God, and spoke, saying, Let us sing to the Lord, for he is very greatly glorified: horse and rider he has thrown into the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He was to me a helper and protector for salvation: this is my God and I will glorify him; my father's God, and I will exalt him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord bringing wars to nothing, the Lord [is] his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He has cast the chariots of Pharao and his host into the sea, the chosen mounted captains: they were swallowed up in the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He covered them with the sea: they sank to the depth like a stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Your right hand, O God, has been glorified in strength; your right hand, O God, has broken the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And in the abundance of your glory you have broken the adversaries to pieces: you sent forth your wrath, it devoured them as stubble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And by the breath of your anger the water parted asunder; the waters were congealed as a wall, the waves were congealed in the midst of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoils; I will satisfy my soul, I will destroy with my sword, my hand shall have dominion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You sent forth your wind, the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Who is like to you among the gods, O Lord? who is like to you? glorified in holiness, marvelous in glories, doing wonders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You stretched forth your right hand, the earth swallowed them up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You have guided in your righteousness this your people whom you have redeemed, by your strength you have called them into your holy resting-place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The nations heard and were angry, pangs have seized on the dwellers among the Phylistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then the princes of Edom, and the chiefs of the Moabites hasted; trembling took hold upon them, all the inhabitants of Chanaan melted away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Let trembling and fear fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm, let them become as stone; till your people pass over, O Lord, till this your people pass over, whom you have purchased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Bring them in and plant them in the mountain of their inheritance, in your prepared habitation, which you, O Lord, have prepared; the sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands have made ready. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The Lord reigns for ever and ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the horse of Pharao went in with the chariots and horsemen into the sea, and the Lord brought upon them the water of the sea, but the children of Israel walked through dry land in the midst of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Mariam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, having taken a timbrel in her hand—then there went forth all the women after her with timbrels and dances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Mariam led them, saying, Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been very greatly glorified: the horse and rider has he cast into the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So Moses brought up the children of Israel from the Red Sea, and brought them into the wilderness of Sur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and they came to Merrha, and could not drink of Merrha, for it was bitter; therefore he named the name of that place, Bitterness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses cried to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree, and he cast it into the water, and the water was sweetened: there he established to him ordinances and judgments, and there he proved him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and said, If you will indeed hear the voice of the Lord your God, and do things pleasing before him, and will listen to his commands, and keep all his ordinances, no disease which I have brought upon the Egyptians will I bring upon you, for I am the Lord your God that heals you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they came to Aelim, and there were there twelve fountains of water, and seventy stems of palm-trees; and they encamped there by the waters.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Name of God: Yah (יָהּ) — Short form of Yahweh Common English renderings: LORD. A poetic shortened form of the divine name, especially found in praise formulas like Hallelujah. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: tehillah (תְּהִלָּה) = praise. Common English renderings: praise. Noun often used in psalmic worship. Heb. vocab: pele (פֶּלֶא) = wonder; marvel. Common English renderings: wonderful; miracle. Conveys something extraordinary or incomprehensible. \textsuperscript{17} Heb. vocab: nachalah (נַחֲלָה) = inheritance; allotted possession. Common English renderings: inheritance. Key term for tribal land and covenant inheritance. \textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: dikaiōma (δικαίωμα) = ordinance; righteous requirement. Common English renderings: ordinance. Can refer to a statute, ordinance, or righteous requirement. \textsuperscript{26} Name of God: Yahweh Rapha (יְהוָה רֹפְאֶךָ) — The LORD who heals Common English renderings: the LORD that healeth thee. Reveals God as healer, both physically and covenantally. Heb. vocab: yashar (יָשָׁר) = upright; straight. Common English renderings: upright; right. Moral and directional term for straightness and rectitude.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} strength, ; song; my salvation; my God; an habitation; my father's God exalt him \textsuperscript{7} the greatness; them that, ; consumed \textsuperscript{9} I will pursue; destroy or, repossess \textsuperscript{10} blow; the sea; they sank \textsuperscript{11} like unto thee; , gods or, mighty ones glorious; fearful \textsuperscript{15} dukes; Moab; all the, melt; *marg. \textsuperscript{20} prophetess; sister; a timbrel Toph, in Arabic called duff or diff, and in Spanish adduffa, is the tabret used in the East; being a thin, broad, wooden hoop, with parchment extended over one side of it, to which small pieces of brass, tin, etc., are attached, which make a jingling noise. It is held up with one hand and beaten upon with the other, and is precisely the same as the tambourine. all the \textsuperscript{22} wilderness of Shur This lay on the eastern shore of the Heroopolitic gulf of the Red Sea, and is still called the desert of Shur, according to Dr. Shaw.; three days \textsuperscript{25} cried; a tree; a statute proved \textsuperscript{26} If thou;, and wilt; diseases;, for I am \textsuperscript{27} Elim This was on the northern skirts of the desert of Sin, and, according to Dr. Shaw, two leagues from Tor, and near 30 from Corondel, which he conjectures to be Marah, where there is a small rill, which is brackish. He found but nine of the wells, the other three being filled up with sand; but the 70 palm trees had increased into more than 2, 000.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 16}
\markright{EXODUS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And they departed from Aelim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Aelim and Sina; and on the fifteenth day, in the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the children of Israel said to them, Would we had died struck by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh-pots, and ate bread to satiety! for you⌃ have brought us out into this wilderness, to kill all this congregation with hunger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, I [will] rain bread upon you out of heaven: and the people shall go forth, and they shall gather their daily portion for the day, that I may try them whether they will walk in my law or not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it shall come to pass on the sixth day that they shall prepare whatever they have brought in, and it shall be double of what they shall have gathered for the day, daily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses and Aaron said to all the congregation of the children of Israel, At even you⌃ shall know that the Lord has brought you out of the land of Egypt; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and in the morning you⌃ shall see the glory of the Lord, inasmuch as he hears your murmuring against God; and who are we, that you⌃ continue to murmur against us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses said, [This shall be] when the Lord gives you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety, because the Lord has heard your murmuring, which you⌃ murmur against us: and what are we? for your murmuring is not against us, but against God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses said to Aaron, Say to all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before God; for he has heard your murmuring. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when Aaron spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and they turned toward the wilderness, then the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I have heard the murmuring of the children of Israel: speak to them, saying, Towards evening you⌃ shall eat flesh, and in the morning you⌃ shall be satisfied with bread; and you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it was evening, and quails came up and covered the camp: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} in the morning it came to pass as the dew ceased round about the camp, that, behold, on the face of the wilderness [was] a small thing like white coriander seed, as frost upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, What is this? for they knew not what it was; and Moses said to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} This [is] the bread which the Lord has given you to eat. This is that which the Lord has appointed: gather of it each man for his family, a homer for each person, according to the number of your souls, gather each of you with his fellow-lodgers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the children of Israel did so, and gathered some much and some less. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And having measured the homer [full], he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that had gathered less had no lack; each gathered according to the need of those who belonged to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Moses said to them, Let no man leave of it till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But they did not listen to Moses, but some left of it till the morning; and it bred worms and stank: and Moses was irritated with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they gathered it every morning, each man what he needed, and when the sun waxed hot it melted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it came to pass on the sixth day, they gathered double what was needed, two homers for one [man]; and all the chiefs of the synagogue went in and reported it to Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses said to them, Is not this the word which the Lord spoke? To-morrow [is] the sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord: bake that you⌃ will bake, and seethe that you⌃ will seethe, and all that is over leave to be laid by for the morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they left of it till the morning, as Moses commanded them; and it stank not, neither was there a worm in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses said, Eat [that] today, for today is a sabbath to the Lord: [it] shall not be found in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Six days you⌃ shall gather it, and on the seventh day is a sabbath, for there shall be none on that [day]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass on the seventh day [that] some of the people went forth to gather, and found none. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the Lord said to Moses, How long are you⌃ unwilling to listen to my commands and my law? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} See, for the Lord has given you this day [as] the sabbath, therefore he has given you on the sixth day the bread of two days: you⌃ shall sit each of you in your houses; let no one go forth from his place on the seventh day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the people kept sabbath on the seventh day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the children of Israel called the name of it Man; and it was as white coriander seed, and the taste of it as a wafer with honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Moses said, This [is] the thing which the Lord has commanded, Fill an homer with manna, to be laid up for your generations; that they may see the bread which you⌃ ate in the wilderness, when the Lord led you forth out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Moses said to Aaron, Take a golden pot, and cast into it one full homer of manna; and you shall lay it up before God, to be kept for your generations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} as the Lord commanded Moses: and Aaron laid it up before the testimony to be kept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the children of Israel ate manna forty years, until they came to the land they ate the manna, until they came to the region of Phoenicia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Now the homer was the tenth part of three measures.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: kavod (כָּבוֹד) = glory; honor; weight. Common English renderings: glory; honour. Its root sense of weight helps explain its use for honor and divine glory. \textsuperscript{23} Heb. vocab: shabbat (שַׁבָּת) = sabbath; cessation. Common English renderings: sabbath; rest. Weekly sacred rest, also emblematic of covenant identity. \textsuperscript{34} Heb. vocab: edut (עֵדוּת) = testimony; witness. Common English renderings: testimony; witness. Often linked with covenant stipulations and the ark.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2513, bc 1491, An, Ex, Is 1, Ijar took; Sin This desert was traversed by Dr. Shaw in nine hours. He was all the day diverted by varieties of lizards and vipers, which abound there. \textsuperscript{3} Would; we had; flesh; to kill; hunger \textsuperscript{4} I will rain; a certain rate every day Heb. the portion of a day in his day; prove them \textsuperscript{7} the morning ye shall, ; what are we \textsuperscript{8} the Lord heareth; but against \textsuperscript{12} I have At even in the morning ye shall know \textsuperscript{13} the quails The Latin selav, Chaldee selaiv, Syriac and Arabic selwa, is without doubt the quail, so the LXX render it ορτυγομητρα, a large kind of quail. Josephus, ορτυξ, Ethopic, ferferat, and Vulgate, coturnices, quails, with which agree Philo and the Rabbins. The quail is a bird of the gallinaceous kind, somewhat less than a pigeon, but larger than a sparrow. Hasselquist describes the quail of the larger kind as very much resembling the red partridge, but not larger than the turtle dove; found in Judea as well as in the deserts of Arabia Petrζa and Egypt; and affording a most agreeable and delicate dish.; the dew \textsuperscript{14} the dew; the hoar frost \textsuperscript{15} It is manna or, What is this, or, It is a portion, ; This is \textsuperscript{16} omer, for every man Heb. by the poll, or head persons Heb. souls. \textsuperscript{22} What the substance called manna was, is utterly unknown, but, from the circumstances in the text, it is evident that it was not a natural production, but was miraculously sent by Jehovah. These the learned Abarbinel, a most judicious Jewish interpreter, has thus enumerated: - The natural manna was never found in the desert where this fell where the common manna does fall; - It is only in the spring time, in March and April, whereas this fell throughout all the months in the year; - The ordinary manna does not melt in the sun, as this did ( ); - It does not stink and breed worms, as this did, when kept till the morning ( ); - It cannot be ground or beaten in a mortar, so as to make cakes, as this was; - The common manna is medicinal and purgative, and cannot be used for food and nutriment, as this was; - This fell in a double proportion on the sixth day, and not on the sabbath, as it certainly would have done had it fallen naturally; - It followed them in all their journeys, where ever they pitched their tents; and - It ceased at the very time of the year when the other falls, namely, in March, when the Israelites were come to Gilgal. Whatever this substance was, it does not appear to have been common to the wilderness. From, it is evident that the Israelites never saw it before; and from a pot of it being preserved, it is certain that nothing of the kind ever appeared again. \textsuperscript{31} called the name In consequence of the term manna having been given to a drug which is now much used in England, many persons have ignorantly supposed it to be the same sort of thing as that miraculously sent for the sustenance of the children of Israel in the wilderness. The manna of commerce comes from Calabria and Sicily, where it oozes out of a kind of ash tree, from the end of June to the end of July, and is a thick, clammy, sweet juice, partly drawn from the tree by the rays of the sun, partly by the puncture of insects, and partly by artificial means. The European manna is not so good as the Oriental, which is gathered in Syria, Arabia, and Persia, from the Oriental oak, and from a shrub which is called in Persia teranjabin . and it was \textsuperscript{35} forty years; until they came to the borders\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 17}
\markright{EXODUS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin, according to their encampments, by the word of the Lord; and they encamped in Raphidin: and there was no water for the people to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the people reviled Moses, saying, Give us water, that we may drink; and Moses said to them, Why do you⌃ revile me, and why tempt you⌃ the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people thirsted there for water, and there the people murmured against Moses, saying, Why is this? have you brought us up out of Egypt to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses cried to the Lord, saying, What shall I do to this people? yet a little while and they will stone me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord said to Moses, Go before this people, and take to yourself of the elders of the people; and the rod with which you struck the river, take in your hand, and you shall go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Behold, I stand there before you [come], on the rock in Choreb, and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out from it, and the people shall drink. And Moses did so before the sons of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he called the name of that place, Temptation, and Reviling, because of the reviling of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us or not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Amalec came and fought with Israel in Raphidin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses said to Joshua, Choose out for yourself mighty men, and go forth and set the army in array against Amalec to-morrow; and, behold, I [shall] stand on the top of the hill, and the rod of God [will be] in my hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joshua did as Moses said to him, and he went out and set the army in array against Amalec, and Moses and Aaron and Or went up to the top of the hill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hands, Amalec prevailed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But the hands of Moses were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat upon it; and Aaron and Or supported his hands one on this side and the other on that, and the hands of Moses were supported till the going down of the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joshua routed Amalec and all his people with the slaughter of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord said to Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and speak [this] in the ears of Joshua; for I will utterly blot out the memorial of Amalec from under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Moses built an altar to the Lord, and called the name of it, The Lord my Refuge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For with a secret hand the Lord wages war upon Amalec to all generations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: tsur (צוּר) = rock. Common English renderings: rock. Used for literal rock and as a divine title in poetry. Gk. vocab: petra (πέτρα) = rock. Common English renderings: rock. Usually denotes bedrock or a rocky mass. \textsuperscript{9} Name meaning: Joshua (Yehoshua) — Yahweh saves Led Israel into the Promised Land; his name points to the ultimate Savior. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: emunah (אֱמוּנָה) = faithfulness; firmness; steadiness. Common English renderings: faithfulness. Often denotes steadiness, fidelity, or faithfulness rather than mere belief. \textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: katav (כָּתַב) = to write. Common English renderings: write. Basic writing verb in law and history. \textsuperscript{15} Name of God: Yahweh Nissi (יְהוָה נִסִּי) — The LORD is my banner Common English renderings: The LORD my banner. Moses’ altar-name after victory over Amalek, portraying God as the standard and rallying point of His people. Heb. vocab: nas (נָס) = banner; signal pole. Common English renderings: ensign; banner. Related to rallying and public signal imagery.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the people, ;, Give us; wherefore \textsuperscript{6} I will the rock This rock, which is a vast block of red granite, 15 feet long, 10 broad, and 12 high, lies in the wilderness of Rephidim, to the west of Mount Horeb, a part of Sinai. There are abundant traces of this wonderful miracle remaining at this day. This rock has been visited, drawn, and described by Dr. Shaw and others; and holes and channels appear in the stone, which could only have been formed by the bursting out and running of water. in Horeb and thou; , ; that the people \textsuperscript{7} Massah i.e. Temptation; Meribah that is, Chiding or Strife; chiding tempted; Is the Lord \textsuperscript{9} unto Joshua;, Oshea, Jehoshua, Hoshea, Called Jesus; Choose the rod \textsuperscript{12} Moses' hands; stayed up his hands \textsuperscript{14} memorial, ; for I will;, ; the remembrance \textsuperscript{15} Jehovahnissi i.e. the Lord my banner \textsuperscript{16} Because etc. or, Because the hand of Amalek is against the throne of the Lord, therefore, etc. the Lord, etc. Heb. the hand upon the throne of the Lord.; will have war\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 18}
\markright{EXODUS 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jothor the priest of Madiam, the father-in-law of Moses, heard of all that the Lord did to his people Israel; for the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses, took Sepphora the wife of Moses after she had been sent away, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and her two sons: the name of the one was Gersam, [his father] saying, I was a sojourner in a strange land; — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and the name of the second Eliezer, saying, For the God of my father [is] my helper, and he has rescued me out of the hand of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses, and his sons and his wife, went forth to Moses into the wilderness, where he encamped on the mount of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it was told Moses, saying, Behold, your father-in-law Jothor is coming to you, and your wife and two sons with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses went forth to meet his father-in-law, and did him reverence, and kissed him, and they embraced each other, and he brought them into the tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses related to his father-in-law all things that the Lord did to Pharao and all the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and all the labor that had befallen them in the way, and that the Lord had rescued them out of the hand of Pharao, and out of the hand of the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jothor was amazed at all the good things which the Lord did to them, forasmuch as he rescued them out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Jothor said, Blessed be the Lord, because he has rescued them out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now know I that the Lord is great above all gods, because of this, wherein they attacked them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for God, for Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass after the morrow that Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood by Moses from morning till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jothor having seen all that [Moses] did to the people, says, What is this that you do to the people? therefore sit you alone, and all the people stand by you from morning till evening? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Moses says to his father-in-law, Because the people come to me to seek judgment from God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For whenever there is a dispute among them, and they come to me, I give judgment upon each, and I teach them the ordinances of God and his law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, You do not this thing rightly, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} you will wear away with intolerable weariness, both those and all this people which is with you: this thing is hard, you will not be able to endure it yourself alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now then listen to me, and I will advise you, and God shall be with you: be you to the people in the things pertaining to God, and you shall bring their matters to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you shall testify to them the ordinances of God and his law, and you shall show to them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And do you look out for yourself out of all the people able men, fearing God, righteous men, hating pride, and you shall set over the people captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they shall judge the people at all times, and the too burdensome matter they shall bring to you, but they shall judge the smaller cases; so they shall relieve you and help you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} If you will do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to attend, and all this people shall come with peace into their own place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did whatever he said to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses chose out able men out of all Israel, and he made them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties and captains of tens over the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they judged the people at all times; and every too burdensome matter they brought to Moses, but every light matter they judged themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Moses dismissed his father-in-law, and he returned to his own land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{19} Heb. vocab: etsah (עֵצָה) = counsel; plan. Common English renderings: counsel. Wisdom and divine-plan term. Heb. vocab: ya’ats (יָעַץ) = to counsel; advise. Common English renderings: counsel. Verb for giving advice or forming a plan. Gk. vocab: boulē (βουλή) = counsel; purpose. Common English renderings: counsel. A term for plan, counsel, or resolve. \textsuperscript{21} Gk. vocab: pleonexia (πλεονεξία) = greed; covetousness. Common English renderings: covetousness. Literally the desire to have more.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 19}
\markright{EXODUS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in the third month of the departure of the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, on the same day, they came into the wilderness of Sina. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they departed from Raphidin, and came into the wilderness of Sina, and there Israel encamped before the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses went up to the mount of God, and God called him out of the mountain, saying, These things shall you say to the house of Jacob, and you shall report them to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ have seen all that I have done to the Egyptians, and I took you up as upon eagles' wings, and I brought you near to myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And now if you⌃ will indeed hear my voice, and keep my covenant, you⌃ shall be to me a peculiar people above all nations; for the whole earth is mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall be to me a royal priesthood and a holy nation: these words shall you speak to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses came and called the elders of the people, and he set before them all these words, which God appointed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all the people answered with one accord, and said, All things that God has spoken, we will do and listen to: and Moses reported these words to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord said to Moses, Behold! I come to you in a pillar of a cloud, that the people may hear me speaking to you, and may believe you for ever: and Moses reported the words of the people to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said to Moses, Go down and solemnly charge the people, and sanctify them today and to-morrow, and let them wash their garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And let them be ready against the third day, for on the third day the Lord will descend upon mount Sina before all the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall separate the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves that you⌃ go not up into the mountain, nor touch any part of it: every one that touches the mountain shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A hand shall not touch it, for [every one that touches] shall be stoned with stones or shot through with a dart, whether beast or whether man, it shall not live: when the voices and trumpets and cloud depart from off the mountain, they shall come up on the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified them, and they washed their clothes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to the people, Be ready: for three days come not near to a woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass on the third day, as the morning drew near, there were voices and lightnings and a dark cloud on mount Sina: the voice of the trumpet sounded loud, and all the people in the camp trembled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Moses led the people forth out of the camp to meet God, and they stood by under the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The mount of Sina was altogether on a smoke, because God had descended upon it in fire; and the smoke went up as the smoke of a furnace, and the people were exceedingly amazed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sounds of the trumpet were waxing very much louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord came down upon mount Sina on the top of the mountain; and the Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And God spoke to Moses, saying, Go down, and solemnly charge the people, lest at any time they draw near to God to gaze, and a multitude of them fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And let the priests that draw near to the Lord God sanctify themselves, destroy some of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses said to God, The people will not be able to approach to the mount of Sina, for you have solemnly charged us, saying, Set bounds to the mountain and sanctify it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Lord said to him, Go, descend, and come up you and Aaron with you; but let not the priests and the people force their way to come up to God, lest the Lord destroy some of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses went down to the people, and spoke to them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: qadosh (קָדוֹשׁ) = holy. Common English renderings: holy. Conveys separateness and consecration to God.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2513, bc 1491, An, Ex, Is, 1, Sivan the third; came \textsuperscript{2} Rephidim, the desert Mount Sinai, called by the Arabs Jibbel Mousa, the Mountain of Moses, and sometimes by way of eminence, El Tor, the Mount, is a range of mountains in the peninsula formed by the gulfs of the Red Sea. It consists of several peaks, the principal of which are Horeb and Sinai; the former, still called Oreb, being on the west, and the latter, called Tur Sina, on the east, at the foot of which is the convent of St. Catherine. Dr. Shaw conceives that the wilderness of Sinai, properly so called, is that part which is to the eastward of this mount; so that the removal of the Israelites from Rephidim, which was on the West, to the desert of Sinai, was only removing from one part of the mountain to another. camped \textsuperscript{4} seen Exod. 7:1-14:31; I bare you \textsuperscript{5} if ye; keep; a peculiar, ; all the earth \textsuperscript{12} set bounds; Take; or touch \textsuperscript{13} whether; when the trumpet or, cornet \textsuperscript{15} Be ready; the third, come not \textsuperscript{16} thunders, ; , ;, thick; voice, all the people \textsuperscript{18} mount Sinai; , in fire; as the smoke; whole \textsuperscript{20} the Lord came; Moses went up \textsuperscript{24} and thou but let; lest\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 20}
\markright{EXODUS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke all these words, saying: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You shall have no other gods beside me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You shall not make to yourself an idol, nor likeness of anything, whatever things are in the heaven above, and whatever are in the earth beneath, and whatever are in the waters under the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them; for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, recompensing the sins of the fathers upon the children, to the third and fourth generation to them that hate me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and bestowing mercy on them that love me to thousands [of them], and on them that keep my commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain; for the Lord your God will not acquit him that takes his name in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remember the sabbath day to keep it holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Six days you shall labor, and shall perform all your work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But on the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord your God; on it you shall do no work, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your servant nor your maidservant, your ox nor your ass, nor any cattle of yours, nor the stranger that sojourns with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For in six days the Lord made the heaven and the earth, and the sea and all things in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore the Lord blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Honor your father and your mother, that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the good land, which the Lord your God gives to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall not commit adultery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not steal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall not kill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall not covet your neighbor's wife; you shall not covet your neighbor's house; nor his field, nor his servant, nor his maid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any of his cattle, nor whatever belongs to your neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all the people perceived the thundering, and the flashes, and the voice of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and all the people feared and stood afar off, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and said to Moses, Speak you to us, and let not God speak to us, lest we die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Moses says to them, Be of good courage, for God is come to you to try you, that his fear may be among you, that you⌃ sin not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the people stood afar off, and Moses went into the darkness where God was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord said to Moses, Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob, and you shall report it to the children of Israel, You⌃ have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} You⌃ shall not make to yourselves gods of silver, and gods of gold you⌃ shall not make to yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You⌃ shall make to me an altar of earth; and upon it you⌃ shall sacrifice your whole burnt offerings, and your peace-offerings, and your sheep and your calves in every place, where I shall record my name; and I will come to you and bless you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if you will make to me an altar of stones, you shall not build them hewn [stones]; for you have lifted up your tool upon them, and they are defiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} You shall not go up to my altar by steps, that you may not uncover your nakedness upon it.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: naqah (נָקָה) = to be clean; free from guilt. Common English renderings: be guiltless; cleanse. Often used in legal acquittal or non-acquittal formulas. \textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: moicheia (μοιχεία) = adultery. Common English renderings: adultery. The standard term for violation of the marriage bond. \textsuperscript{24} Heb. vocab: shelem (שֶׁלֶם) = peace offering. Common English renderings: peace offering. Related to wholeness and fellowship.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 21}
\markright{EXODUS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the ordinances which you shall set before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If you buy a Hebrew servant, six years shall he serve you, and in the seventh year he shall go forth free for nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If he should have come in alone, he shall also go forth alone; and if his wife should have gone in together with him, his wife also shall go out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Moreover, if his master give him a wife, and she have [born] him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall be his master's; and he shall go forth alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if the servant should answer and say, I love my master and wife and children, I will not go away free; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} his master shall bring him to the judgment-seat of God, and then shall he bring him to the door, —to the door-post, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if any one sell his daughter as a domestic, she shall not depart as the maidservants depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If she be not pleasing to her master, after she has betrothed herself to him, he shall let her go free; but he is not at liberty to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has trifled with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if he should have betrothed her to his son, he shall do to her according to the right of daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if he take another to himself, he shall not deprive her of necessaries and her apparel, and her companionship [with him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And if he will not do these three things to her, she shall go out free without money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if any man strike another and he die, let him be certainly put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But as for him that did it not willingly, but God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place whither the slayer may flee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if any one lie in wait for his neighbor to kill him by craft, and he go for refuge, you shall take him from my altar to put him to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Whoever smites his father or his mother, let him be certainly put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} He that reviles his father or his mother shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Whosoever shall steal one of the children of Israel, and prevail over him and sell him, and he be found with him, let him certainly die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if two men revile each other and strike the one the other with a stone or his fist, and he die not, but be laid upon his bed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} if the man arise and walk abroad on his staff, he that struck him shall be clear; only he shall pay for his loss of time, and for his healing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if a man strike his man-servant or his maidservant, with a rod, and [the party] die under his hands, he shall be surely punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But if [the servant] continue to live a day or two, let not [the master] be punished; for he is his money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if two men strive and strike a woman with child, and her child be born imperfectly formed, he shall be forced to pay a penalty: as the woman's husband may lay upon him, he shall pay with a valuation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But if it be perfectly formed, he shall give life for life, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if one strike the eye of his man-servant, or the eye of his maidservant, and put it out, he shall let them go free for their eye's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And if he should strike out the tooth of his man-servant, or the tooth of his maidservant, he shall send them away free for their tooth's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And if a bull gore a man or woman and they die, the bull shall be stoned with stones, and his flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall be clear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But if the bull should have been given to goring in former time, and men should have told his owner, and he have not removed him, but he should have slain a man or woman, the bull shall be stoned, and his owner shall die also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And if a ransom should be imposed on him, he shall pay for the ransom of his soul as much as they shall lay upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And if [the bull] gore a son or daughter, let them do to him according to this ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And if the bull gore a man-servant or maidservant, he shall pay to their master thirty silver didrachmas, and the bull shall be stoned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And if any one open a pit or dig a cavity in stone, and cover it not, and an ox or an ass fall in there, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} the owner of the pit shall make compensation; he shall give money to their owner, and the dead shall be his own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And if any man's bull gore the bull of his neighbor, and it die, they shall sell the living bull and divide the money, and they shall divide the dead bull. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But if the bull be known to have been given to goring in time past, and they have testified to his owner, and he have not removed him, he shall repay bull for bull, but the dead shall be his own.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{22} Gk. vocab: zēmia (ζημία) = loss; damage. Common English renderings: loss. A term for forfeiture, damage, or loss. \textsuperscript{30} Heb. vocab: kofer (כֹּפֶר) = ransom; covering price. Common English renderings: ransom; satisfaction. Related to atonement and compensation contexts. Gk. vocab: lytron (λύτρον) = ransom price. Common English renderings: ransom. A redemption term for ransom price.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} an Hebrew; and in the \textsuperscript{3} by himself Heb. with his body \textsuperscript{5} And if; shall plainly say Heb. saying shall say \textsuperscript{6} the judges, ; bore his ear This significant ceremony was intended as a mark of permanent servitude, and was calculated to impress the servant with the duty of hearing all his master's orders, and obeying them punctually. for ever \textsuperscript{8} please not Heb. be evil in the eyes of, etc.; *marg. who hath, seeing \textsuperscript{10} her food Sheairah, "her flesh; " he shall not only afford her a sufficient quantity of food, as before, but of the same quality. She is not to be fed, like a common slave, with a sufficiency of bread, vegetables, milk, etc., but with her customary supply of flesh, and other agreeable articles of food. \textsuperscript{13} lie not; God, ; I will appoint \textsuperscript{15} To smite either father or mother, in a manner which indicated either contempt or malice, or left marks of violence, was deemed a proof of so ungrateful and unnatural a disposition, that no provocation was admitted as an excuse, but the offence was made capital. Nay, he who cursed his father or mother, who uttered imprecations, ill wishes, or revilings, against a parent, was included in the same sense; though few crimes were made capital by the law of Moses. The law of God, as delegated to parents is honoured when they are honoured, and despised when they are despised, and to rebel against the lawful exercise of this authority is rebellion against God. - Rev. T.
