\subsection*{Exodus 22}
\markright{EXODUS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if one steal an ox or a sheep, and kill it or sell it, he shall pay five calves for a calf, and four sheep for a sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if the thief be found in the breach [made by himself] and be struck and die, there shall not be blood shed for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But if the sun be risen upon him, he is guilty, he shall die instead; and if a thief have nothing, let him be sold in compensation for what he has stolen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if the thing stolen be left and be in his hand alive, whether ox or sheep, he shall restore them two-fold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if any one should feed down a field or a vineyard, and should send in his beast to feed down another field, he shall make compensation of his own field according to his produce; and if he shall have fed down the whole field, he shall pay for compensation the best of his own field and the best of his vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if fire have gone forth and caught thorns, and should also set on fire threshing-floors or ears of corn or a field, he that kindled the fire shall make compensation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if any one give to his neighbor money or goods to keep, and they be stolen out of the man's house, if the thief be found he shall repay double. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But if the thief be not found, the master of the house shall come forward before God, and shall swear that surely he has not wrought wickedly in regard of any part of his neighbor's deposit, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} according to every injury alleged, both concerning a calf, and an ass, and a sheep, and a garment, and every alleged loss, whatever in fact it may be, —the judgment of both shall proceed before God, and he that is convicted by God shall repay to his neighbor double. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if any one give to his neighbor to keep a calf or sheep or any beast, and it be wounded or die or be taken, and no one know, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} an oath of God shall be between both, [each swearing] that he has surely not at all been guilty in the matter of his neighbor's deposit; and so his master shall hold him guiltless, and he shall not make compensation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if it be stolen from him, he shall make compensation to the owner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if it be seized of beasts, he shall bring him to [witness] the prey, and he shall not make compensation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if any one borrow [ought] of his neighbor, and it be wounded or die or be carried away, and the owner of it be not with it, he shall make compensation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if the owner be with it, he shall not make compensation: but if it be a hired thing, there shall be [a compensation] to him instead of his hire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if any one deceive a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her for a wife to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if her father positively refuse, and will not consent to give her to him for a wife, he shall pay compensation to her father according to the amount of the dowry of virgins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You⌃ shall not save the lives of sorcerers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Every one that lies with a beast you⌃ shall surely put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He that sacrifices to any gods but to the Lord alone, shall be destroyed by death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you⌃ shall not hurt a stranger, nor afflict him; for you⌃ were strangers in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You⌃ shall hurt no widow or orphan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And if you⌃ should afflict them by ill-treatment, and they should cry aloud to me, I will surely hear their voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I will be very angry, and will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children orphans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if you should lend money to your poor brother who is by you, you shall not be hard upon him you shall not exact usury of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if you take your neighbor's garment for a pledge, you shall restore it to him before sunset. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For this is his clothing, this is the only covering of his nakedness; wherein shall he sleep? If then he shall cry to me, I will listen to him, for I am merciful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} You shall not revile the gods, nor speak ill of the ruler of your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} You shall not keep back the first fruits of your threshing floor and press. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So shall you do with your calf and your sheep and your ass; seven days shall it be under the mother, and the eighth day you shall give it to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you⌃ shall be holy men to me; and you⌃ shall not eat flesh taken of beasts, you⌃ shall cast it to the dog.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: klopē (κλοπή) = theft. Common English renderings: theft. The noun for stealing or theft. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: yatom (יָתוֹם) = orphan; fatherless. Common English renderings: fatherless. One of the classic vulnerable groups in Torah. \textsuperscript{25} Heb. vocab: ani (עָנִי) = poor; afflicted. Common English renderings: poor; afflicted. Often the oppressed person needing justice.\par}

The reason of the former is, as Maimonides explains it, because money, goods, etc., are better guarded in houses and cities, than cattle in a field; which consequently can be more easily stolen. \subsection*{Exodus 23}
\markright{EXODUS 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You shall not receive a vain report: you shall not agree with the unjust [man] to become an unjust witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You shall not associate with the multitude for evil; you shall not join yourself with a multitude to turn aside with the majority so as to shut out judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall not spare a poor man in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if you meet your enemy's ox or his ass going astray, you shall turn them back and restore them to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if you see your enemy's ass fallen under its burden, you shall not pass by it, but shall help to raise it with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You shall not wrest the sentence of the poor in his judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall abstain from every unjust thing: you shall not kill the innocent and just, and you shall not justify the wicked for gifts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall not receive gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of the seeing, and corrupt just words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you⌃ shall not afflict a stranger, for you⌃ know the heart of a stranger; for you⌃ were yourselves strangers in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Six years you shall sow your land, and gather in the fruits of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But in the seventh year you shall let it rest, and leave it, and the poor of your nation shall feed; and the wild beasts of the field shall eat that which remains: thus shall you do to your vineyard and to your oliveyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Six days shall you do your works, and on the seventh day there shall be rest, that your ox and your ass may rest, and that the son of your maidservant and the stranger may be refreshed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Observe all things whatever I have commanded you; and you⌃ shall make no mention of the name of other gods, neither shall they be heard out of your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Keep you⌃ a feast to me three times in the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Take heed to keep the feast of unleavened bread: seven days you⌃ shall eat unleavened bread, as I charged you at the season of the month of new [corn], for in it you came out of Egypt: you shall not appear before me empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall keep the feast of the harvest of first fruits of your labors, whatever you shall have sown in your field, and the feast of completion at the end of the year in the gathering in of your fruits out of your field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Three times in the year shall all your males appear before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For when I shall have cast out the nations from before you, and shall have widened your borders, you shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven, neither must the fat of my feast abide till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You shall bring the first-offerings of the first fruits of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not seethe a lamb in its mother's milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And, behold, I send my angel before your face, that he may keep you in the way, that he may bring you into the land which I have prepared for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Take heed to yourself and listen to him, and disobey him not; for he will not give way to you, for my name is on him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} If you⌃ will indeed hear my voice, and if you will do all the things I shall charge you with, and keep my covenant, you⌃ shall be to me a peculiar people above all nations, for the whole earth is mine; and you⌃ shall be to me a royal priesthood, and a holy nation: these words shall you⌃ speak to the children of Israel, If you⌃ shall indeed hear my voice, and do all the things I shall tell you, I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For my angel shall go as your leader, and shall bring you to the Amorite, and Chettite, and Pherezite, and Chananite, and Gergesite, and Evite, and Jebusite, and I will destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You shall not worship their gods, nor serve them: you shall not do according to their works, but shall utterly destroy them, and break to pieces their pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread and your wine and your water, and I will turn away sickness from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} There shall not be on your land one that is impotent or barren. I will surely fulfil the number of your days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And I will send terror before you, and I will strike with amazement all the nations to which you shall come, and I will make all your enemies to flee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And I will send hornets before you, and you shall cast out the Amorites and the Evites, and the Chananites and the Chettites from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} I will not cast them out in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} By little [and little] I will cast them out from before you, until you shall be increased and inherit the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And I will set your borders from the Red Sea, to the sea of the Phylistines, and from the wilderness to the great river Euphrates; and I will give into your hand those that dwell in the land, and will cast them out from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} You shall make no covenant with them and their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they shall not dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me; for if you should serve their gods, these will be an offense to you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: dal (דַּל) = low; poor. Common English renderings: poor. Often paired with justice concerns. Gk. vocab: ptōchos (πτωχός) = poor; destitute. Common English renderings: poor. A major social-ethical term for the poor.\par}

"It was a custom with the ancient heathens, when they had gathered in all their fruits, to take a kid, and boil it in the dam's milk; and then in a magical way, to go about and sprinkle all their trees, and fields, and gardens, and orchards with it, thinking by these means, that they should make them fruitful, and bring forth more abundantly in the following year. Wherefore, God forbad his people, the Jews, at the time of their in-gathering, to use any such superstitious or idolatrous rite." \textsuperscript{21} Beware of him; provoke him not; he will not; my name \textsuperscript{22} an enemy; an adversary unto thine adversaries or, I will afflict them that afflict thee \textsuperscript{23} mine Angel; thee in; the Hivites The LXX, Samaritan, Coptic, and one Hebrew manuscript add, "and the Girgashite; " thus making the seven nations. \textsuperscript{24} shalt not do after; overthrow \textsuperscript{25} And ye, ;, ; he shall; I will take \textsuperscript{27} my fear; destroy backs Heb. neck \textsuperscript{28} hornets Tzirâh, The hornet, may be so called from the Arabic zaraâ, to lay prostrate, strike down, because of the destruction occasioned by the violence of its sting. The hornet, in natural history, belongs to the species Crabro, of the genus Vespa or Wasp. \subsection*{Exodus 24}
\markright{EXODUS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And to Moses he said, Go up to the Lord, you and Aaron and Nadab and Abiud, and seventy of the elders of Israel: and they shall worship the Lord from a distance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Moses alone shall draw near to God; and they shall not draw near, and the people shall not come up with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses went in and related to the people all the words of God and the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, saying, All the words which the Lord has spoken, we will do and be obedient. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord; and Moses rose up early in the morning, and built an altar under the mountain, and [set up] twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he sent forth the young men of the children of Israel, and they offered whole burnt offerings, and they sacrificed young calves as a peace-offering to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses took half the blood and poured it into bowls, and half the blood he poured out upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he took the book of the covenant and read it in the ears of the people, and they said, All things whatever the Lord has spoken we will do and listen therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord has made with you concerning all these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses went up, and Aaron, and Nadab and Abiud, and seventy of the elders of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they saw the place where the God of Israel stood; and under his feet was as it were a work of sapphire slabs, and as it were the appearance of the firmament of heaven in its purity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And of the chosen ones of Israel there was not even one missing, and they appeared in the place of God, and did eat and drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord said to Moses, Come up to me into the mountain, and be there; and I will give you the tables of stone, the law and the commandments, which I have written to give them laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses rose up and Joshua his attendant, and they went up into the mount of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And to the elders they said, Rest there till we return to you; and behold, Aaron and Or are with you: if any man have a cause to be tried, let them go to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Moses and Joshua went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the glory of God came down upon the mount Sina, and the cloud covered it six days; and the Lord called Moses on the seventh day out of the midst of the cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was as burning fire on the top of the mountain, before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and went up to the mountain, and was there in the mountain forty days and forty nights.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} all the judgments Exod. 21:1-23:33;, All the words \textsuperscript{4} wrote; and builded twelve pillars, ; according \textsuperscript{5} young men burnt offerings; peace offerings \textsuperscript{6} the blood he, ; on the altar \textsuperscript{7} the book; read; All that \textsuperscript{10} saw, ; of a sapphire stone The Hebrew sappir, is without doubt the sapphire; which is a most beautiful precious stone of a fine blue colour, second only to the diamond in lustre, hardness, and value. The ancient oriental sapphire is supposed to have been the same as the lapis lazuli . It glitters with golden spots; and is of an azure or sky-blue colour, but rarely intermixed with purple. \subsection*{Exodus 25}
\markright{EXODUS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and take first fruits of all, who may be disposed in their heart to give; and you⌃ shall take my first fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And this is the offering which you⌃ shall take of them; gold and silver and brass, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and blue, and purple, and double scarlet, and fine spun linen, and goats' hair, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and rams' skins dyed red, and blue skins, and incorruptible wood, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and oil for the light, incense for anointing oil, and for the composition of incense, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and sardius stones, and stones for the carved work of the breast-plate, and the full-length robe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall make me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall make for me according to all things which I show you in the mountain; even the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its furniture: so shall you make it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall make the ark of testimony of incorruptible wood; the length of two cubits and a half, and the breadth of a cubit and a half, and the height of a cubit and a half. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall gild it with pure gold, you shall gild it within and without; and you shall make for it golden wreaths twisted round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall cast for it four golden rings, and shall put them on the four sides; two rings on the one side, and two rings on the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you shall make staves [of] incorruptible wood, and shall gild them with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you shall put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The staves shall remain fixed in the rings of the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall put into the ark the testimonies which I shall give you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you shall make a propitiatory, a lid of pure gold; the length of two cubits and a half, and the breadth of a cubit and a half. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall make two cherubs graven in gold, and you shall put them on both sides of the propitiatory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They shall be made, one cherub on this side, and another cherub on the other side of the propitiatory; and you shall make the two cherubs on the two sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The cherubs shall stretch forth their wings above, overshadowing the propitiatory with their wings; and their faces shall be toward each other, the faces of the cherubs shall be toward the propitiatory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you shall set the propitiatory on the ark above, and you shall put into the ark the testimonies which I shall give you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will make myself known to you from thence, and I will speak to you above the propitiatory between the two cherubs, which are upon the ark of testimony, even in all things which I shall charge you concerning the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you shall make a golden table of pure gold, in length two cubits, and in breadth a cubit, and in height a cubit and a half. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you shall make for it golden wreaths twisted round about, and you shall make for it a crown of an hand-breadth round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall make a twisted wreath for the crown round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall make four golden rings; and you shall put the four rings upon the four parts of its feet under the crown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the rings shall be for bearings for the staves, that they may bear the table with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And you shall make the staves of incorruptible wood, and you shall gild them with pure gold; and the table shall be borne with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you shall make its dishes and its censers, and its bowls, and its cups, with which you shall offer drink-offerings: of pure gold shall you make them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you shall set upon the table show bread before me continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you shall make a candlestick of pure gold; you shall make the candlestick of graven work: its stem and its branches, and its bowls and its knops and its lilies shall be of one piece. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And six branches proceeding sideways, three branches of the candlestick from one side of it, and three branches of the candlestick from the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And three bowls fashioned like almonds, on each branch a knop and a lily; so to the six branches proceeding from the candlestick, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} and in the candlestick four bowls fashioned like almonds, in each branch knops and the flowers of the same. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} A knop under two branches out of it, and a knop under four branches out of it; so to the six branches proceeding from the candlestick; and in the candlestick four bowls fashioned like almonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Let the knops and the branches be of one piece, altogether graven of one piece of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And you shall make its seven lamps: and you shall set on [it] the lamps, and they shall shine from one front. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And you shall make its funnel and its snuff-dishes of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} All these articles [shall be] a talent of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} See, you shall make them according to the pattern showed you in the mount.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: qetoret (קְטֹרֶת) = incense. Common English renderings: incense. Aromatic offering term tied to sanctuary worship. Gk. vocab: thymiama (θυμίαμα) = incense. Common English renderings: incense. A cultic term for incense. \textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: mishkan (מִשְׁכָּן) = dwelling; tabernacle. Common English renderings: tabernacle; dwelling. Term for the sanctuary as God’s dwelling among Israel. \textsuperscript{17} Gk. vocab: hilastērion (ἱλαστήριον) = place or means of propitiation. Common English renderings: propitiation. In the Greek Bible commonly the mercy seat; in the New Testament a major atonement term. \textsuperscript{39} Gk. vocab: talanton (τάλαντον) = talent; weight. Common English renderings: talent. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} they; bring me Heb. take for me offering or, heave offering, willingly \textsuperscript{3} brass Nechosheth, rather, copper; as brass is a factitious metal, composed of copper, and the oxide or ore of zinc, called lapis calaminaris . \textsuperscript{4} blue Techaileth, generally supposed to mean an azure or sky-colour; rendered by the LXX, υακινθον, uakinthon, and Vulgate, hyacinthum . fine linen or, silk \textsuperscript{8} a sanctuary; I may dwell \textsuperscript{9} the pattern of the tabernacle \textsuperscript{10} an ark Aron denotes a chest, or coffer, in general; but is applied particularly to the chest or ark in which the testimony or two tables of the covenant were laid up; on the top of which was the propitiatory or mercy seat; and at the end of which were the cherubim of gold; between whom the visible sign of the presence of God appeared as seated upon his throne. \textsuperscript{19} of the or, of the matter of the \textsuperscript{23} a table; shittim wood Shittim wood is probably the acacia Nilotica . St. Jerome says, that the shittim wood grows in the deserts of Arabia, and is like white thorn, as to its colour and leaves; but the tree is so large as to furnish very long planks. The wood is hard, tough, and extremely beautiful. It is thought he means the black acacia, because that is the most common tree in the deserts of Arabia. It is of the size of a large mulberry tree. The spreading branches and larger limbs are armed with thorns, which grow three together. The bark is rough; and the leaves are oblong, standing opposite each other. The flowers, though sometimes white, are generally of a bright yellow; and the fruit, which resembles a bean, is contained in pods like those of the lupin. "The acacia, " says Dr. Shaw, "being by much the largest and most common tree in the deserts, " ( Arabia Petrζa ), we have some reason to conjecture that the shittim wood was the wood of the acacia, especially as its flowers are of an excellent smell; for the shittah tree is, in, joined with the myrtle and other fragrant shrubs. It may be remarked, that of the two Hebrew names, shittim is masculine, and shittah feminine. So Mr. Bruce says, "the male is called saiel; from it proceeds the gula Arabic, on incision with an axe." \textsuperscript{25} a golden crown to the border \textsuperscript{27} for places of the staves \textsuperscript{29} the;, ; to cover or, to pour out \textsuperscript{37} seven;, they shall; light or, cause to ascend give; it Heb. the face of it \textsuperscript{40} that thou make; was showed thee in the mount Heb. thou wast caused to see in the mount\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 26}
\markright{EXODUS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And you shall make the tabernacle, ten curtains of fine linen spun, and blue and purple, and scarlet spun [with] cherubs; you shall make them with work of a weaver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The length of one curtain shall be eight and twenty cubits, and one curtain shall be the breadth of four cubits: there shall be the same measure to all the curtains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the five curtains shall be joined one to another, and [the other] five curtains shall be closely connected the one with the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall make for them loops of blue on the edge of one curtain, on one side for the coupling, and so shall you make on the edge of the outer curtain for the second coupling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Fifty loops shall you make for one curtain, and fifty loops shall you make on the part of the curtain answering to the coupling of the second, opposite [each other], corresponding to each other at each point. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall make fifty golden rings; and you shall join the curtains to each other with the rings, and it shall be one tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall make for a covering of the tabernacle skins with the hair on, you shall make them eleven skins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The length of one skin thirty cubits, and the breadth of one skin four cubits: there shall be the same measure to the eleven skins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall join the five skins together, and the six skins together; and you shall double the sixth skin in front of the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall make fifty loops on the border of one skin, which is in the midst for the joinings; and you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the second skin that joins it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall make fifty brazen rings; and you shall join the rings by the loops, and you shall join the skins, and they shall be one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall fix at the end that which is over in the skins of the tabernacle; the half of the skin that is left shall you fold over, according to the overplus of the skins of the tabernacle; you shall fold it over behind the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A cubit on this side, and a cubit on that side of that which remains of the skins, of the length of the skins of the tabernacle: it shall be folding over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and that side, that it may cover it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you shall make for a covering of the tabernacle rams' skins dyed red, and blue skins as coverings above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall make the posts of the tabernacle of incorruptible wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Of ten cubits shall you make one post, and the breadth of one post of a cubit and a half. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Two joints shall you make in one post, answering the one to the other: so shall you do to all the posts of the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall make posts to the tabernacle, twenty posts on the north side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall make to the twenty posts forty silver sockets; two sockets to one post on both its sides, and two sockets to the other post on both its sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And for the next side, toward the south, twenty posts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and their forty silver sockets: two sockets to one post on both its sides, and two sockets to the other post on both its sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And on the back of the tabernacle at the part which is toward the [west] you shall make six posts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you shall make two posts on the corners of the tabernacle behind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it shall be equal below, they shall be equal toward the same part from the heads to one joining; so shall you make to both the two corners, let them be equal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there shall be eight posts, and their sixteen silver sockets; two sockets to one post on both its sides, and two sockets to the other post. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall make bars of incorruptible wood; five to one post on one side of the tabernacle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and five bars to one post on the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars to the hinder posts, on the side of the tabernacle toward the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And let the bar in the middle between the posts go through from the one side to the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you shall gild the posts with gold; and you shall make golden rings, into which you shall introduce the bars, and you shall gild the bars with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you shall set up the tabernacle according to the pattern showed you in the mount. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you shall make a veil of blue and purple and scarlet woven, and fine linen spun: you shall make it cherubs [in] woven work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you shall set it upon four posts of incorruptible wood overlaid with gold; and their tops [shall be] gold, and their four sockets [shall be] of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And you shall put the veil on the posts, and you shall carry in there within the veil the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall make a separation for you between the holy and the holy of holies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And you shall screen with the veil the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And you shall set the table outside the veil, and the candlestick opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; and you shall put the table on the north side of the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And you shall make a screen for the door of the tabernacle of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet and fine linen spun, the work of the embroiderer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And you shall make for the veil five posts, and you shall gild them with gold; and their capitals shall be gold; and you shall cast for them five brazen sockets.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the tabernacle with ten curtains The word mishcan, from shachan, to dwell, means simply a dwelling-place, or habitation. "When God had brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, " says the very learned Dr. Cudworth, "resolving to manifest himself in a peculiar manner present among them, he thought good to dwell amongst them in a visible and external manner; and therefore, while they were in the wilderness, and sojourned in tents, he would have a tent or tabernacle built, to sojourn with them also. - Now, the tabernacle being thus a house for God to dwell in visibly, to make up the notion of dwelling or habitation complete, there must be all things suitable to a house belonging to it. Hence, in the holy place, there must be a table and a candlestick, because these were the ordinary furniture of a room. The table must have its dishes, and spoons, and bowls, and covers, belonging to it, though they were never used; and always be furnished with bread upon it. The candlestick must have its lamps continually burning, etc.", ; fine twined linen, ; cherubims cunning work Heb. the work of a cunning workman, or embroiderer \textsuperscript{6} taches of gold, one tabernacle \textsuperscript{7} curtains; goats' hair Izzim, goats, but used here elliptically for goats' hair. In different parts of Asia Minor, Syria, Cilicia, and Phrygia, the goats have long, fine, and beautiful hair; in some cases, almost as fine as silk, which is shorn at proper times, and manufactured into garments., ; a; eleven \textsuperscript{13} a cubit, of that which remaineth Heb. in the remainder or surplusage \textsuperscript{14} a covering; rams' skins dyed red Oroth ailim meoddamim, literally, the skins of red rams. It is a fact, attested by many respectable travellers, that in the Levant, sheep are often met with having red or violet coloured fleeces. Almost all ancient writers speak of the same thing., ; badgers' skins Oroth techashim, which nearly all the ancient versions have taken to be the name of a colour, though they differ very much with regard to the particular colour intended: the LXX, Vulgate, and Coptic, have skins dyed of a violet colour; the Syriac, azure; and the Arabic, black; and Bochart contends for the hysginus, a very deep blue. It may, however, denote an animal; for Dr. Geddes remarks, had the sacred writer meant to express only a variety of colour, he would hardly have repeated oroth, skins, after meoddamim, red, in . \textsuperscript{21} two sockets under one board \textsuperscript{24} be coupled Heb. twined and they shall be coupled together above \textsuperscript{29} overlay the boards with gold \textsuperscript{30} rear up the tabernacle; according to the fashion \textsuperscript{31} a veil of, ; blue, purple Argaman, a very precious colour, extracted from the purpura, or murex, a species of shell-fish; and supposed to be the same with the costly and much celebrated Tyrian purple. scarlet Tolaâth; properly the worm whence the scarlet colour was produced; which grew in a coccus, or excrescence, of a shrub of the ilex kind, like the cochineal worm in the Opuntia of America; which is arranged under the same genus as the Arabic Kermez, which also denotes this colour. cunning work, ; cherubims shall it be made \textsuperscript{32} pillars of shittim; their hooks shall be of gold The Hebrew waveyhem, which we translate their hooks, is rendered by the LXX κεφαλιδες, and by the Vulgate, capiata, capitals. Hence Calmet contends: 1. That if Moses does not mean the capitals of the pillars by this word, he mentions them nowhere else; and it would seem strange, that while he describes them with so much exactness, that he should not mention the capitals; or that pillars every way so correctly formed, should have been destitute of this necessary ornament. 2. As Moses was commanded to make the wavim of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver ( ), and the wavim of the pillars of the vail of gold ( ), and that 1, 775 shekels were employed in making them, overlaying their chapiters, rasheyhem, their heads, and filleting them ( ), it is more reasonable to suppose that all this is spoken of the capitals of pillars, than of any kind of hooks, especially as hooks are mentioned under the word taches or clasps. But as the root wavah seems to signify to connect (for yww, in Arabic, is to marry a wife), and as the letter ww, wav, if it has not its name from its hook-like form, is yet used as a connective particle, it would rather appear to denote hooks, which connected the curtains or vails to the pillars. The LXX also render it αγκυλαι, "handles", and κρικοι, "rings" or "clasps". \textsuperscript{33} the taches, within the veil the ark of the testimony, the holy place \textsuperscript{36} hanging This may be termed the first vail, as it occupied the door or entrance to the tabernacle; the vail that separated the Holy of Holies is called the second vail, . Mr. Morier (Second Journey Through Persia, p. 251), describing the tent of a chief of the Eelauts, says, "It was composed of a wooden frame of circular laths, which were fixed on the ground, and then covered over with large felts, that were fastened down by a cord, ornamented by tassels of various colours. A curtain, curiously worked by the women, with coarse needle-work of various colours, was suspended over the door. In the king of Persia's tents, magnificent perdahs, or hangings of needle-work, are suspended, as well as on the doors of the great mosques in Turkey; and these circumstances combined, will, perhaps, illustrate ."; the tent, ; of blue\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 27}
\markright{EXODUS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And you shall make an altar of incorruptible wood, of five cubits in the length, and five cubits in the breadth; the altar shall be square, and the height of it shall be of three cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall make the horns on the four corners; the horns shall be of the same piece, and you shall overlay them with brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall make a rim for the altar; and its covering and its cups, and its flesh hooks, and its fire-pan, and all its vessels shall you make of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall make for it a brazen grate with network; and you shall make for the grate four brazen rings under the four sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall put them below under the grate of the altar, and the grate shall extend to the middle of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall make for the altar staves of incorruptible wood, and you shall overlay them with brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall put the staves into the rings; and let the staves be on the sides of the altar to carry it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You shall make it hollow with boards: according to what was showed you in the mount, so you shall make it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall make a court for the tabernacle, curtains of the court of fine linen spun on the south side, the length of one hundred cubits for one side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And their pillars twenty, and twenty brazen sockets for them, and their rings and their clasps of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus [shall there be] to the side toward the north curtains of one hundred cubits in length; and their pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty of brass, and the rings and the clasps of the pillars, and their sockets overlaid with silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And in the breadth of the tabernacle toward the west curtains of fifty cubits, their pillars ten and their sockets ten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And in the breadth of the tabernacle toward the south, curtains of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their sockets ten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the height of the curtains [shall be] of fifty cubits for the one side [of the gate]; their pillars three, and their sockets three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And [for] the second side the height of the curtains [shall be] of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And a veil for the door of the court, the height [of it] of twenty cubits of blue linen, and of purple, and spun scarlet, and of fine linen spun with the art of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} All the pillars of the court round about overlaid with silver, and their capitals silver and their brass sockets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the length of the court [shall be] one hundred [cubits] on each side, and the breadth fifty on each side, and the height five cubits of fine linen spun, and their sockets of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And all the furniture and all the instruments and the pins of the court [shall be] of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And do you charge the children of Israel, and let them take for you refined pure olive-oil beaten to burn for light, that a lamp may burn continually {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} in the tabernacle of the testimony, without the veil that is before the [ark of the] covenant, shall Aaron and his sons burn it from evening until morning, before the Lord: it is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations of the children of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} horns of it upon the four corners thereof The horns might have been designed not only for ornament, but to prevent the sacrifices from falling off, and to tie the victim to, previous to its being sacrificed.;, ; overlay it with brass \textsuperscript{3} his shovels; basins fleshhooks; firepans \textsuperscript{4} a grate of network, rings in the four corners thereof \textsuperscript{8} as it was showed Heb. he shewed \textsuperscript{10} sockets shall be of brass fillets shall be of silver \textsuperscript{18} length of the court fifty every where Heb. fifty by fifty \textsuperscript{20} pure oil olive beaten That is, such oil as could be easily expressed from the olives, after they had been bruised in a mortar; and which is much purer than that obtained after the olives are put under the press.; for the light to cause the lamp Josephus says, that the whole of the seven lamps burned all night; and that in the morning four were extinguished, and three burned the whole of the day. Such might have been the practice in his time; but it appears sufficiently evident from, and, that they were anciently extinguished in the morning. to burn Heb. to ascend up \textsuperscript{21} the tabernacle of the congregation; without the veil, testimony, Aaron; evening; a statute for ever\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 28}
\markright{EXODUS 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And do you take to yourself both Aaron your brother, and his sons, even [them] of the children of Israel; so that Aaron, and Nadab and Abiud, and Eleazar and Ithamar, sons of Aaron, may minister to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall make holy apparel for Aaron your brother, for honor and glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And speak you to all those who are wise in understanding, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom and perception; and they shall make the holy apparel of Aaron for the sanctuary, in which [apparel] he shall minister to me as priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And these are the garments which they shall make: the breast-plate, and the shoulder-piece, and the full-length robe, and the tunic with a fringe, and the tire, and the girdle; and they shall make holy garments for Aaron and his sons to minister to me as priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they shall make the shoulder-piece of fine linen spun, the woven work of the embroiderer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined together, fastened on the two sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the woven work of the shoulder-pieces which is upon it, shall be of one piece according to the work, of pure gold and blue and purple, and spun scarlet and fine twined linen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall take the two stones, the stones of emerald, and you shall grave on them the names of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Six names on the first stone, and the other six names on the second stone, according to their births. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [It shall be] the work of the stone-engraver's art; as the graving of a seal you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall put the two stones on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece: they are memorial-stones for the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel before the Lord on his two shoulders, a memorial for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you shall make circlets of pure gold; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and you shall make two fringes of pure gold, variegated with flowers wreathen work; and you shall put the wreathen fringes on the circlets, fastening them on their shoulder-pieces in front. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall make the oracle of judgment, the work of the embroiderer: in keeping with the ephod, you shall make it of gold, and blue and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine linen spun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall make it square: it shall be double; of a span the length of it, and of a span the breadth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you shall interweave with it a texture of four rows of stone; there shall be a row of stones, a sardius, a topaz, and emerald, the first row. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the second row, a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the third row, a ligure, an agate, an amethyst: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the fourth row, a chrysolite, and a beryl, and an onyx stone, set round with gold, bound together with gold: let them be according to their row. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And let the stones of the names of the children of Israel be twelve according to their names, engravings as of seals: let them be for the twelve tribes each according to the name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall make on the oracle woven fringes, a chain-work of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Aaron shall take the names of the children of Israel, on the oracle of judgment on his breast; a memorial before God for him as he goes into the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you shall put the fringes on the oracle of judgment; you shall put the wreaths on both sides of the oracle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and you shall put the two circlets on both the shoulders of the ephod in front. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall put the Manifestation and the Truth on the oracle of judgment; and it shall be on the breast of Aaron, when he goes into the holy place before the Lord; and Aaron shall bear the judgments of the children of Israel on his breast before the Lord continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And you shall make the full-length tunic all of blue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the opening of it shall be in the middle having a fringe round about the opening, the work of the weaver, woven together in the joining of the same piece that it might not be torn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And under the fringe of the robe below you shall make as it were pomegranates of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine linen spun, under the fringe of the robe round about: golden pomegranates of the same shape, and bells round about between these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A bell by the side of a golden pomegranate, and flower-work on the fringe of the robe round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the sound of Aaron shall be audible when he ministers, as he goes into the sanctuary before the Lord, and as he goes out, that he die not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you shall make a plate [of] pure gold, and you shall grave on it [as] the graving of a signet, Holiness of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And you shall put it on the spun blue cloth, and it shall be on the mitre: it shall be in the front of the mitre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And it shall be on the forehead of Aaron; and Aaron shall bear away the sins of their holy things, all that the children of Israel shall sanctify of every gift of their holy things, and it shall be on the forehead of Aaron continually acceptable for them before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the fringes of the garments [shall be] of fine linen; and you shall make a tire of fine linen, and you shall make a girdle, the work of the embroiderer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics and girdles, and you shall make for them tires for honor and glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And you shall put them on Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, and you shall anoint them and fill their hands: and you shall sanctify them, that they may minister to me in the priest's office. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And you shall make for them linen drawers to cover the nakedness of their flesh; they shall reach from the loins to the thighs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Aaron shall have them, and his sons, whenever they enter into the tabernacle of witness, or when they shall advance to the altar of the sanctuary to minister, so they shall not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die: [it is] a perpetual statute for him, and for his seed after him.\par

A major biblical term for wisdom, skill, and God-given understanding. \textsuperscript{35} Gk. vocab: leitourgia (λειτουργία) = service; ministry. Common English renderings: service; ministry. A public or sacred service term. Gk. vocab: leitourgos (λειτουργός) = minister; servant. Common English renderings: minister. One who performs public or sacred service.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} a breastplate Choshen, in Hebrew is used for the square breast-plate of the high priest, in which were set twelve precious stones, each being engraved with the name of one of the sons of Jacob.; ephod The ephod seems to have been a short cloak, without sleeves., ;, ; a robe The word meil, from âlah, to ascend, go up on, may be considered as an upper garment that goes up or over the rest, a surtout., broidered; a mitre; a girdle \textsuperscript{11} engravings of a signet; ouches of gold \textsuperscript{12} the shoulders; Aaron shall bear, for a memorial \textsuperscript{17} thou shalt, ; set in it settings of stones Heb. fill in its fillings of stone the first row; a sardius or, ruby, The Hebrew odem, from adam, to be red, ruddy, seems to denote the ruby; as adam does in Persian a beautiful gem, of a fine deep red colour, with a mixture of purple.;, ; a topaz Pitdah, is constantly rendered by the LXX τοπαζιον, and Vulgate, topazius, with which agrees Josephus. The topaz is a precious stone, of a pale, dead green, with a mixture of yellow, sometimes of a fine yellow; and hence called chrysolyte by the moderns, from its gold colour.; a carbuncle Bareketh, from barak, to lighten, glitter, a very elegant gem, of a deep red colour, with a mixture of scarlet. \textsuperscript{18} emerald Nophech, an emerald, the same with the ancient smaragdus; one of the most beautiful of all the gems, and of a bright green colour, without any mixture.; sapphire; diamond \textsuperscript{20} a beryl; an onyx a jasper, enclosings Heb. fillings \textsuperscript{21} twelve according to the twelve \textsuperscript{25} wreathen chains, on the shoulder pieces of the ephod \textsuperscript{30} the Urim and Thummim, ΰϊ ΰεψιν εΰϊ δϊξιν the Urim and Thummim, lights and perfections; rendered by the LXX δηλωσιϚ και αληθεια, manifestation and truth; and, by the Vulgate, doctrina et veritas, doctrine and truth. Among the various and contradictory opinions respecting the form and substance of these mysterious appendages, the most probable seems to be that of Josephus, Philo, Bp. Patrick, Parkhurst, and the Jewish writers generally; who state, that they were no other than the twelve precious stones of the high priest's breastplate. In support of this statement, it is observed: 1. That in the description of the high priest's breastplate, et seq., the Urim and Thummim are not mentioned, but only the rows of stones; and on the contrary, in, the Urim and Thummim are expressly mentioned, but not a word is said of the four rows of stones. 2. As Moses has given such a particular description of every thing relative to the high priest's dress, these would certainly have been described had they been different from what was previously mentioned.; , ; bear the judgment upon his heart \textsuperscript{32} as it were; that it be not rent \textsuperscript{33} And hem or, skirts pomegranates; bells \textsuperscript{36} a plate of pure gold The word tzitz, which we translate a plate, properly signifies a flower. It is rendered by the LXX πεταλον, a leaf, and is called nezer, a crown in and διαδημα, a diadem, by the author of the book of Wisdom, 28:24. Josephus says that it was adorned with three rows of the flower which the Greeks call κυανος . It was two fingers broad, of a circular form, suited to the shape of the head, and so long that it reached from ear to ear, and was fastened upon a blue lace or ribband, which was tied behind the head; and as the plate reached only half round the head, the remaining part of the ribband was highly ornamented with artificial flowers. grave upon it, HOLINESS\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 29}
\markright{EXODUS 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these are the things which you shall do to them: you shall sanctify them, so that they shall serve me in the priesthood; and you shall take one young calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and unleavened loaves kneaded with oil, and unleavened cakes anointed with oil: you shall make them [of] fine flour of wheat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall put them on one basket, and you shall offer them on the basket, and the young calf and the two rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and you shall wash them with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And having taken the garments, you shall put on Aaron your brother both the full-length robe and the ephod and the oracle; and you shall join for him the oracle to the ephod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall put the mitre on his head; and you shall put the plate, [even] the Holiness, on the mitre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall take of the anointing oil, and you shall pour it on his head, and shall anoint him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and you shall bring his sons, and put garments on them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall gird them with the girdles, and put the tires upon them, and they shall have a priestly office to me for ever; and you shall fill the hands of Aaron and the hands of his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall bring the calf to the door of the tabernacle of witness; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the calf, before the Lord, by the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall kill the calf before the Lord, by the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall take of the blood of the calf, and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, but all the rest of the blood you shall pour out at the foot of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you shall take all the fat that is on the belly, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and shall put them upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But the flesh of the calf, and his skin, and his dung, shall you burn with fire without the camp; for it is an [offering on account] of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall take one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall kill it, and take the blood and pour it on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you shall divide the ram by his several limbs, and you shall wash the inward parts and the feet with water, and you shall put them on the divided parts with the head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall offer the whole ram on the altar, a whole burnt offering to the Lord for a sweet smelling savor: it is an offering of incense to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you shall kill it, and take of the blood of it, and put it on the tip of Aaron's right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot, and on the tips of the right ears of his sons, and on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the great toes of their right feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you shall take of the blood from the altar, and of the anointing oil; and you shall sprinkle it upon Aaron and on his garments, and on his sons and on his sons' garments with him; and he shall be sanctified and his apparel, and his sons and his sons' apparel with him: but the blood of the ram you shall pour round about upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall take from the ram its fat, both the fat that covers the belly, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder, for this is a consecration. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And one cake [made] with oil, and one cake from the basket of unleavened bread set forth before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you shall put them all on the hands of Aaron, and on the hands of his sons, and you shall separate them as a separate offering before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall take them from their hands, and shall offer them up on the altar of whole burnt offering for a sweet smelling savor before the Lord: it is an offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall take the breast from the ram of consecration which is Aaron's, and you shall separate it as a separate offering before the Lord, and it shall be to you for a portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And you shall sanctify the separated breast and the shoulder of removal which has been separated, and which has been removed from the ram of consecration, of the portion of Aaron and of [that of] his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it shall be a perpetual statute of the children of Israel to Aaron and his sons, for this is a separate offering; and it shall be a special offering from the children of Israel, from the peace-offerings of the children of Israel, a special offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the apparel of the sanctuary which is Aaron's shall be his son's after him, for them to be anointed in them, and to fill their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The priest his successor from among his sons who shall go into the tabernacle of witness to minister in the holies, shall put them on seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you shall take the ram of consecration, and you shall boil the flesh in the holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the loaves in the basket, by the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} They shall eat the offerings with which they were sanctified to fill their hands, to sanctify them; and a stranger shall not eat of them, for they are holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And if [anything] be left of the flesh of the sacrifice of consecration and of the loaves until the morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire: it shall not be eaten, for it is a holy thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And thus shall you do for Aaron and for his sons according to all things that I have commanded you; seven days shall you fill their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And you shall sacrifice the calf of the sin-offering on the day of purification, and you shall purify the altar when you do perform consecration upon it, and you shall anoint it so as to sanctify it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Seven days shall you purify the altar and sanctify it; and the altar shall be most holy, every one that touches the altar shall be hallowed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And these are the offerings which you shall offer upon the altar; two unblemished lambs of a year old daily on the altar continually, a constant offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} One lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer in the evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And a tenth measure of fine flour mingled with the fourth part of an hin of beaten oil, and a drink-offering the fourth part of a hin of wine for one lamb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And you shall offer the second lamb in the evening, after the manner of the morning-offering, and according to the drink-offering of the morning lamb; you shall offer it an offering to the Lord for a sweet smelling savor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} a perpetual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the door of the tabernacle of witness before the Lord; wherein I will be known to you from thence, so as to speak to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And I will there give orders to the children of Israel, and I will be sanctified in my glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And I will sanctify the tabernacle of testimony and the altar, and I will sanctify Aaron and his sons, to minister as priests to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And I will be called upon among the children of Israel, and will be their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, to be called upon by them, and to be their God.\par

And the sprinkling might further teach him, that he could neither hear, work, nor walk profitably, uprightly, and well pleasingly in the sight of God, without the application of the blood of the sacrifice.; sprinkle \textsuperscript{21} the anointing oil; shall be \textsuperscript{22} Also thou; the rump Alyah is the large tail of a species of eastern sheep. "This tail, " says Dr. Russell, "is very broad and large, terminating in a small appendix that turns back upon it. It is of a substance between fat and marrow, and is not eaten separately, but mixed with lean meat in many of their dishes, and also often used instead of butter. A common sheep of this sort, without the head, feet, skin, and entrails, weighs about twelve or fourteen Aleppo rotoloes, (a rotoloe is five pounds), of which the tail is usually three rotoloes or upwards; but such as are of the largest breed, and have been fattened, will sometimes weigh about thirty rotoloes, and the tails of these ten.", right shoulder \textsuperscript{24} put wave them Heb. shake to and fro a wave \textsuperscript{25} thou; for a sweet offering \textsuperscript{26} the breast it shall be thy \textsuperscript{27} the breast, ; the wave offering The wave offering and heave offering are thus distinguished by the Jewish writers. The former, called tenoophah, from nooph, to move, toss, was waved horizontally towards the four cardinal points, to signify that He to whom it was consecrated was the Lord of the whole earth; the latter, called teroomah, from room, to be elevated, was lifted perpendicularly upward and downward, in token of its being devoted to the God of heaven. the ram of the consecration Ail milluim, literally, "the ram of filling; " so called, according to some, because at the consecration of the priests, certain pieces of the sacrifice were put into their hands ( ); on which account their consecration itself is called "filling their hands" ( ). Rabbi Solomon gives a different reason for the ram being so called, from malai, to be full, complete; because the sacrifice completed the consecration, and thereupon the priests were fully invested in their office.
