\subsection*{Exodus 30}
\markright{EXODUS 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And you shall make the altar of incense of incorruptible wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall make it a cubit in length, and a cubit in breadth: it shall be square; and the height of it shall be of two cubits, its horns shall be of the same piece. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall gild its grate with pure gold, and its sides round about, and its horns; and you shall make for it a wreathen border of gold roundabout. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall make under its wreathen border two rings of pure gold; you shall make it to the two corners on the two sides, and they shall be bearings for the staves, so as to bear it with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall make the staves of incorruptible wood, and shall gild them with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall set it before the veil that is over the ark of the testimonies, wherein I will make myself known to you from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Aaron shall burn upon it fine compound incense every morning; whenever he trims the lamps he shall burn incense upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when Aaron lights the lamps in the evening, he shall burn incense upon it; a constant incense-offering always before the Lord for their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall not offer strange incense upon it, [nor] an offering made by fire, [nor] a sacrifice; and you shall not pour a drink-offering upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And once in the year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns, he shall purge it with the blood of purification for their generations: it is most holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If you take account of the children of Israel in the surveying of them, and they shall give every one a ransom for his soul to the Lord, then there shall not be among them a destruction in the visiting of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And this is what they shall give, as many as pass the survey, half a didrachm which is according to the didrachm of the sanctuary: twenty oboli [go to] the didrachm, but the half of the didrachm is the offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Every one that passes the survey from twenty years old and upwards shall give the offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than the half didrachm in giving the offering to the Lord, to make atonement for your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall take the money of the offering from the children of Israel, and shall give it for the service of the tabernacle of testimony; and it shall be to the children of Israel a memorial before the Lord, to make atonement for your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Make a brazen laver, and a brazen base for it, for washing; and you shall put it between the tabernacle of witness and the altar, and you shall pour forth water into it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet with water from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whenever they shall go into the tabernacle of witness, they shall wash themselves with water, so they shall not die, whenever they advance to the altar to do service and to offer the whole burnt offerings to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They shall wash their hands and feet with water, whenever they shall go into the tabernacle of witness; they shall wash themselves with water, that they die not; and it shall be for them a perpetual statute, for him and his posterity after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Do you also take sweet herbs, the flower of choice myrrh five hundred shekels, and the half of this two hundred and fifty shekels of sweet smelling cinnamon, and two hundred and fifty shekels of sweet smelling calamus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and of cassia five hundred shekels of the sanctuary, and a hin of olive oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall make it a holy anointing oil, a perfumed ointment [tempered] by the art of the perfumer: it shall be a holy anointing oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall anoint with it the tabernacle of witness, and the ark of the tabernacle of witness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and all its furniture, and the candlestick and all its furniture, and the altar of incense, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its furniture, and the table and all its furniture, and the laver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you shall sanctify them, and they shall be most holy: every one that touches them shall be hallowed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify them that they may minister to me as priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, This shall be to you a holy anointing oil throughout your generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} On man's flesh it shall not be poured, and you⌃ shall not make [any] for yourselves according to this composition: it is holy, and shall be holiness to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Whosoever shall make it in like manner, and whoever shall give of it to a stranger, shall be destroyed from among his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the Lord said to Moses, Take for yourself sweet herbs, stacte, onycha, sweet galbanum, and transparent frankincense; there shall be an equal weight of each. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they shall make with it perfumed incense, tempered with the art of a perfumer, a pure holy work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And of these you shall beat some small, and you shall put it before the testimonies in the tabernacle of testimony, whence I will make myself known to you: it shall be to you a most holy incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} You⌃ shall not make any for yourselves according to this composition; it shall be to you a holy thing for the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Whosoever shall make any in like manner, so as to smell it, shall perish from his people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: qatar (קָטַר) = to burn incense; make smoke. Common English renderings: burn incense; burn. Cultic burning term especially for incense. \textsuperscript{15} Gk. vocab: plousios (πλούσιος) = rich; wealthy. Common English renderings: rich. The adjective for wealthy or rich.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} The Samaritan inserts the first ten verses of this chapter after . an altar, ; to burn incense Where so many sacrifices were offered, it was essentially necessary to have some pleasing perfume to counteract the disagreeable smells that must have arisen from the slaughter of so many animals, the burning of so much flesh, the sprinkling of the blood. No blood was ever sprinkled on this altar, except once a year, on the grand day of expiation. It was called also the golden altar ( ); and the incense was as constantly burnt on it every day, as the morning and evening sacrifice of a lamb was burnt on the brazen altar. \textsuperscript{3} overlay it, top Heb. roof sides Heb. walls \textsuperscript{4} rings, two corners Heb. ribs \textsuperscript{6} veil, ; before the mercy seat that is over the testimony The words μτπι δλτψϊ ΰωΡψ ςμ δςγϊ, liphney haccapporeth asher al haaiduth, "before the mercy-seat that is over the testimony, " are thought to be a repetition of the preceding clause, μτπι δτψλϊ ΰωΡψ ςμ ΰψο δςψϊ, liphney happarocheth asher al aron haaiduth, "before the vail that is by the ark of the testimony; the word δτψλϊ, happarocheth, "the vail, " being corrupted, by transposing the letters into δλτψϊ, hacapporeth, "the mercy-seat, " and the word ΰψο, aron, "ark, " omitted. This repetition, as Dr. Kennicott observes, places the altar of incense before the mercy-seat, and consequently in the Holy of Holies! Now this could not be, as the altar of incense was attended every day, and the Holy of Holies entered only once in the year. The five words which appear to be a repetition are wanting in twenty-six of Kennicott's and Rossi's manuscripts and in the Samaritan Text.; I will \textsuperscript{7} sweet incense Heb. incense of spices, dresseth \textsuperscript{8} lighteth or, setteth up, Heb. causeth to ascend at even Heb. between the two evens. *marg. a perpetual \textsuperscript{12} takest; their number Heb. them that are to be numbered a ransom; no plague \textsuperscript{13} a shekel is; an half shekel; *Gr. \textsuperscript{15} rich; give more Heb. multiply give less than Heb. diminish, an atonement. \textsuperscript{18} a laver; *Gr: put it \textsuperscript{23} thee principal; pure myrrh Myrrh is a white gum, issuing from the trunk and larger branches of a thorny tree resembling the acacia, growing in Arabia, Egypt, and Abyssinia. Its taste is extremely bitter; but its smell, though strong, is agreeable; and it entered into the composition of the most costly ointments among the ancients. The epithet deror, rendered pure, properly denotes fluid, from the Arabic darra, to flow; by which is meant the finest and most excellent kind, called stacte, which issues of itself from the bark without incision. cinnamon Kinnamon bosem, odoriferous or spicy cinnamon, is the bark of the canella, a small tree of the size of a willow growing in the island of Ceylon. sweet calamus Kenaih bosem, calamus aromaticus, or odoriferous cane, is a reed growing in Egypt, Syria, and India, about two feet in height, bearing from the root a knotted stalk, quite round, containing in its cavity a soft white pith. It is said to scent the air while growing; and when cut down, dried, and powdered, makes an ingredient in the richest perfumes. \textsuperscript{25} apothecary or, perfumer, an holy \textsuperscript{33} compoundeth; a stranger cut off \textsuperscript{34} unto thee, stacte Heb. nataph, The Jews and others suppose it to be what was afterwards called the balm of Jericho, or Gilead. onycha The word shechaileth is generally allowed to denote onycha (nail-fish, from its form), as it is rendered by the LXX and Vulgate. It is the shell of the purpura, and of the whole class of murex; and serves as the basis of the principal perfumes in India. galbanum Chelbenah, (probably from chalay, milk or gum, and lavan, white), is the gummy, resinous juice of an umbelliferous plant, the bubon gumniferum of Linneus, growing in Syria, Persia, and Africa. It rises with a ligneous stalk from eight to ten feet, and is garnished with leaves at every joint. The top of the stalk is terminated by an umbel of yellow flowers which are succeeded by oblong channelled seeds, which have a thin membrane or wing on their border. When any part of the plant is broken, there issues out a little thin juice, of a cream colour, of a fat, tough substance, like gum ammoniac, composed of many small, shining grains, of a strong, piercing smell and a sharp, warm taste. frankincense \textsuperscript{35} perfume; after the tempered Heb. salted \textsuperscript{36} the testimony where I will\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 31}
\markright{EXODUS 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, I have called by name Beseleel the son of Urias the son of Or, of the tribe of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I have filled him [with] a divine spirit of wisdom, and understanding, and knowledge, to invent in every work, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and to frame works, to labor in gold, and silver, and brass, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and works in stone, and for artificers' work in wood, to work at all works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I have appointed him and Eliab the [son] of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan, and to every one understanding in heart I have given understanding; and they shall make all things as many as I have appointed you, — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} the tabernacle of witness, and the ark of the covenant, and the propitiatory that is upon it, and the furniture of the tabernacle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and the altars, and the table and all its furniture, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the pure candlestick and all its furniture, and the laver and its base, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and Aaron's robes of ministry, and the robes of his sons to minister to me as priests, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and the anointing oil and the compound incense of the sanctuary; according to all that I have commanded you shall they make them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Do you also charge the children of Israel, saying, Take heed and keep my sabbaths; [for] they are a sign with me and among you throughout your generations, that you⌃ may know that I am the Lord that sanctifies you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you⌃ shall keep the sabbaths, because this is holy to the Lord for you; he that profanes it shall surely be put to death: every one who shall do a work on it, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Six days you shall do works, but the seventh day is the sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord; every one who shall do a work on the seventh day shall be put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the children of Israel shall keep the sabbaths, to observe them throughout their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} It is a perpetual covenant with me and the children of Israel, it is a perpetual sign with me; for in six days the Lord made the heaven and the earth, and on the seventh day he ceased, and rested. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he gave to Moses when he left off speaking to him in mount Sina the two tables of testimony, tables of stone written [upon] with the finger of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{13} Name of God: Yahweh Mekaddishkem (יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם) — The LORD who sanctifies you Common English renderings: the LORD that doth sanctify you. Stresses that holiness is not self-produced but given by God.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} filled; the spirit of God Ruach Elohim, rather, "a spirit of God; " which is a usual Hebraism, signifying "an excellent spirit; " or, as we should now say, "a distinguished genius for the work he had to perform." No man, by course of reading or study, ever acquired a genius of any kind. We call it natural, and say it was born with the man: Moses teaches us to consider it divine. The prophet Isaiah ( ), pointedly refers to this sort of teaching as coming from God, even in the most common and less difficult arts of life. Dark as the heathens were, yet they acknowledged that all talents and the seeds of all arts came from God. \textsuperscript{6} I have given; Aholiab, wise hearted, ; that they Exod. 37:1-38:31; 1Kings 6:1-8:66; 2Chr. 3:1-4:22; Ezek. 43:1-48:35 \textsuperscript{7} tabernacle, ark, furniture Heb. vessels \textsuperscript{8} the table, pure candlestick, the altar \textsuperscript{13} Verily;, a sign;, that ye may \textsuperscript{15} Six days, ; the sabbath; *Gr. holy Heb. holiness whosoever \textsuperscript{17} a sign; six days; and was refreshed God, in condescension to human weakness, applies to himself here what belongs to man; though it may refer to the delight and satisfaction with which he contemplated the completion of all his works, and pronounced them very good.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 32}
\markright{EXODUS 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, the people combined against Aaron, and said to him, Arise and make us gods who shall go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us forth out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what is become of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Aaron says to them, Take off the golden ear-rings which are in the ears of your wives and daughters, and bring them to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all the people took off the golden ear-rings that were in their ears, and brought them to Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he received them at their hands, and formed them with a graving tool; and he made them a molten calf, and said, These [are] your gods, O Israel, which have brought you up out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Aaron having seen it built an altar before it, and Aaron made proclamation saying, To-morrow [is] a feast of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And having risen early on the morrow, he offered whole burnt offerings, and offered a peace-offering; and the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Go quickly, descend hence, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have transgressed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} they have quickly gone out of the way which you commanded; they have made for themselves a calf, and worshipped it, and sacrificed to it, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now let me alone, and I will be very angry with them and consume them, and I will make you a great nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses prayed before the Lord God, and said, Therefore, O Lord, are you very angry with your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great strength, and with your high arm? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [Take heed] lest at any time the Egyptians speak, saying, With evil intent he brought them out to kill them in the mountains, and to consume them from off the earth; cease from your wrathful anger, and be merciful to the sin of your people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} remembering Abraam and Isaac and Jacob your servants, to whom you have sworn by yourself, and have spoken to them, saying, I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven for multitude, and all this land which you spoke of to give to them, so that they shall possess it for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord was prevailed upon to preserve his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tables of testimony were in his hands, tables of stone written on both their sides: they were written within and without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the tables were the work of God, and the writing the writing of God written on the tables. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Joshua having heard the voice of the people crying, says to Moses, There is a noise of war in the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And [Moses] says, It is not the voice of them that begin the battle, nor the voice of them that begin [the cry] of defeat, but the voice of them that begin [the banquet] of wine do I hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And when he drew near to the camp, he sees the calf and the dances; and Moses being very angry cast the two tables out of his hands, and broke them to pieces under the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And having taken the calf which they made, he consumed it with fire, and ground it very small, and scattered it on the water, and made the children of Israel to drink it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses said to Aaron, What has this people done to you, that you have brought upon them a great sin? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Aaron said to Moses, Be not angry, [my] lord, for you know the impetuosity of this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For they say to me, Make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this man Moses, who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what is become of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I said to them, If any one has golden ornaments, take them off; and they gave them me, and I cast them into the fire, and there came out this calf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And when Moses saw that the people was scattered, —for Aaron [had] scattered them [so as to be] a rejoicing to their enemies, — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} then stood Moses at the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come to me. Then all the sons of Levi came to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he says to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, Put every one his sword on his thigh, and go through and return from gate to gate through the camp, and kill every one his brother, and every one his neighbor, and every one him that is nearest to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the sons of Levi did as Moses spoke to them, and there fell of the people in that day to the [number of] three thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses said to them, You⌃ have filled your hands this day to the Lord each one on his son or on his brother, so that blessing should be given to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it came to pass after the morrow [had begun], that Moses said to the people, You⌃ have sinned a great sin; and now I will go up to God, that I may make atonement for your sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Moses returned to the Lord and said, I pray, O Lord, this people has sinned a great sin, and they have made for themselves golden gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And now if you will forgive their sin, forgive [it]; and if not, blot me out of your book, which you have written. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the Lord said to Moses, If any one has sinned against me, I will blot them out of my book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And now go, descend, and lead this people into the place of which I spoke to you: behold, my angel shall go before your face; and in the day when I shall visit I will bring upon them their sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Lord struck the people for the making the calf, which Aaron made.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Heb. vocab: mikhtav (מִכְתָּב) = writing; written document. Common English renderings: writing. Noun for written form or document. Gk. vocab: gramma (γράμμα) = letter; writing. Common English renderings: letter. Can mean a written character or written document.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2513, bc 1491, An, Ex, Is 1, Ab delayed; Up; make;, which shall, the man, ; we wot \textsuperscript{4} fashioned; a graving, calf; , These; which brought \textsuperscript{5} Aaron; made proclamation, ; a feast \textsuperscript{6} offered sat down No doubt at this feast they sacrificed after the manner of the Egyptians. \textsuperscript{8} have turned; which I, These be \textsuperscript{9} I have seen; a stiffnecked \textsuperscript{10} let me alone; my wrath, and I will \textsuperscript{11} besought; the Lord his God Heb. the face of the Lord why doth; which thou \textsuperscript{13} Remember; to whom; I will multiply \textsuperscript{17} Joshua had waited patiently during all the forty days, in the place where Moses had left him - below the summit of the mount, at a distance from the people, and out of the way of temptation. Joshua, they shouted; There is a noise \textsuperscript{18} being overcome Heb. weakness but the \textsuperscript{19} he saw; the dancing; anger; brake them \textsuperscript{20} took the calf How truly contemptible must the object of their idolatry appear, when they were obliged to drink their god, reduced to powder, and strewed on the water! Some have asked, how gold, the most ductile and ponderous of all metals, could have been stamped into dust, and strewed on the water. In, this is fully explained. I took, says Moses, your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire; that is, melted it down, probably into ingots or gross plates, and stamped it, beat it into thin lamine, something like our gold leaf, and ground it very small, even until it was as small as dust, which might be very easily done by the action of the hands, when beat into thin plates or leaves as the original words ekkoth, and dak, imply., ; made the \textsuperscript{25} naked The term naked may mean either that they were unarmed and defenceless, or ashamed from the consciousness of guilt.; Aaron; shame; their enemies Heb. those that rose up against them \textsuperscript{29} Or, another reading of this verse is, and Moses said, Consecrate yourselves to-day to the Lord; because every man hath been against his son and against his brother, etc. Moses; Consecrate Heb. fill your hands \textsuperscript{30} Ye have; peradventure; an atonement \textsuperscript{32} if thou; blot me Allusion may be made to the registry of births, in which those born of a particular tribe were entered in the list of their respective families under that tribe. This was the book of life; and when any died, his name might be considered as blotted out of this list. But as Moses addressed the Lord, he undoubtedly referred, by faith, to the book of God's remembrance.\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 33}
\markright{EXODUS 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, Go forward, go up hence, you and your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, into the land which I swore to Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I will give it to your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I will send at the same time my angel before your face, and he shall cast out the Amorite and the Chettite, and the Pherezite and Gergesite, and Evite, and Jebusite, and Chananite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will bring you into a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up with you, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you by the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the people having heard this grievous saying, mourned in mourning apparel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For the Lord said to the children of Israel, You⌃ are a stiff-necked people; take heed lest I bring on you another plague, and destroy you: now then put off your glorious apparel, and [your] ornaments, and I will show you what I will do to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So the sons of Israel took off their ornaments and their array at the mount of Choreb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses took his tabernacle and pitched it without the camp, at a distance from the camp; and it was called the Tabernacle of Testimony: and it came to pass [that] every one that sought the Lord went forth to the tabernacle which was without the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And whenever Moses went into the tabernacle without the camp, all the people stood every one watching by the doors of his tent; and when Moses departed, they took notice until he entered into the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when Moses entered into the tabernacle, the pillar of the cloud descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and [God] talked to Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all the people saw the pillar of the cloud standing by the door of the tabernacle, and all the people stood and worshipped every one at the door of his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as if one should speak to his friend; and he retired into the camp: but his servant Joshua the son of Naue, a young man, departed not forth from the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Moses said to the Lord, Behold! you say to me, Lead on this people; but you have not showed me whom you will send with me, but you have said to me, I know you above all, and you have favor with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} If then I have found favor in your sight, reveal yourself to me, that I may evidently see you; that I may find favor in your sight, and that I may know that this great nation [is] your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he says, I myself will go before you, and give you rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he says to him, If you go not up with us yourself, bring me not up hence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And how shall it be surely known, that both I and this people have found favor with you, except only if you go with us? So both I and your people shall be glorified beyond all the nations, as many as are upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord said to Moses, I will also do for you this thing, which you have spoken; for you have found grace before me, and I know you above all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And [Moses] says, Manifest yourself to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And [God] said, I will pass by before you with my glory, and I will call by my name, the Lord, before you; and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and will have pity on whom I will have pity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And [God] said, You shall not be able to see my face; for no man shall see my face, and live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord said, Behold, [there is] a place by me: you shall stand upon the rock; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and when my glory shall pass by, then I will put you into a hole of the rock; and I will cover you over with my hand, until I shall have passed by. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I will remove my hand, and then shall you see my back parts; but my face shall not appear to you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Depart thou hast, the land;, Unto \textsuperscript{3} a land; for I, ; stiffnecked; lest I \textsuperscript{5} Ye are; in a moment; put off I may \textsuperscript{7} the tabernacle Eth haohel, the Tent, not eth hammishcan, the Tabernacle, for this was not erected; but probably the tent of Moses, which was before in the midst of the camp, and to which the people came for judgment; and where, no doubt, God frequently met his servant. This situation, as well as the superior elegance, of a chief's tent, was one mode by which he was honoured. afar off; the Tabernacle of sought; went out \textsuperscript{11} spake; his friend; his servant \textsuperscript{13} if, show, ; that I; consider \textsuperscript{17} I will do; thou hast \textsuperscript{19} all my goodness; *marg.; proclaim;, I will be \textsuperscript{20} Thou canst not This is well explained by Rabbi Jehudah, in Sepher Cosri (P. iv. § 3): "Of that divine glory mentioned in the Scripture, there is one degree which the eyes of the prophets were able to explore; another which all the Israelites saw, as the cloud and consuming fire; the third is so bright, and so dazzling, that no mortal is able to comprehend it; but should anyone venture to look on it, his whole frame would be dissolved." In such inconceivable splendour is the Divine Majesty revealed to the inhabitants of the celestial world, where he is said to "dwell in the light which no man can approach unto" ( ). By the "face of God, " therefore, we are to understand that light inaccessible before which angels may stand, but which would be so insufferable to mortal eyes, that no man could see it and live. \textsuperscript{22} in a clift; cover thee; The rock on which Moses stood, and in the clift of which he was sheltered, was doubtless an emblem of Christ; in whose person, character, and salvation alone, sinners may by faith see the glory of God, and live; for there it appears in softened splendour; as the sun, when his brightness is diminished by a mist, is beheld more distinctly by the human eye. - Scott\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 34}
\markright{EXODUS 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Moses, Hew for yourself two tables of stone, as also the first were, and come up to me to the mountain; and I will write upon the tables the words, which were on the first tables, which you broke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And be ready by the morning, and you shall go up to the mount Sina, and shall stand there for me on the top of the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And let no one go up with you, nor be seen in all the mountain; and let not the sheep and oxen feed near that mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [Moses] hewed two tables of stone, as also the first were; and Moses having arisen early, went up to the mount Sina, as the Lord appointed him; and Moses took the two tables of stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord descended in a cloud, and stood near him there, and called by the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord passed by before his face, and proclaimed, The Lord God, pitiful and merciful, longsuffering and very compassionate, and true, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and keeping justice and mercy for thousands, taking away iniquity, and unrighteousness, and sins; and he will not clear the guilty; bringing the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and to the children's children, to the third and fourth generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses hasted, and bowed to the earth and worshipped; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and said, If I have found grace before you, let my Lord go with us; for the people is stiff-necked: and you shall take away our sins and our iniquities, and we will be yours. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, I establish a covenant for you in the presence of all your people; I will do glorious things, which have not been done in all the earth, or in any nation; and all the people among whom you are shall see the works of the Lord, that they are wonderful, which I will do for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Do you take heed to all things whatever I command you: behold, I cast out before your face the Amorite and the Chananite and the Pherezite, and the Chettite, and Evite, and Gergesite and Jebusite: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} take heed to yourself, lest at any time you make a covenant with the dwellers on the land, into which you are entering, lest it be to you a stumbling block among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You⌃ shall destroy their altars, and break in pieces their pillars, and you⌃ shall cut down their groves, and the graven images of their gods you⌃ shall burn with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For you⌃ shall not worship strange gods, for the Lord God, a jealous name, is a jealous God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} lest at any time you make a covenant with the dwellers on the land, and they go a whoring after their gods, and sacrifice to their gods, and they call you, and you should eat of their feasts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and you should take of their daughters to your sons, and you should give of your daughters to their sons; and your daughters should go a whoring after their gods, and your sons should go a whoring after their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you shall not make to yourself molten gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall keep the feast of unleavened bread: seven days shall you eat unleavened bread, as I have charged you, at the season in the month of new [corn]; for in the month of new [corn] you came out from Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The males [are] mine, everything that opens the womb; every firstborn of oxen, and [every] firstborn of sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the firstborn of an ass you shall redeem with a sheep, and if you will not redeem it you shall pay a price: every firstborn of your sons shall you redeem: you shall not appear before me empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest: [there shall be] rest in seed time and harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall keep to me the feast of weeks, the beginning of wheat harvest; and the feast of ingathering in the middle of the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Three times in the year shall every male of yours appear before the Lord the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For when I shall have cast out the nations before your face, and shall have enlarged your coasts, no one shall desire your land, whenever you may go up to appear before the Lord your God, three times in the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifices with leaven, neither shall the sacrifices of the feast of the passover remain till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The first fruits of your land shall you put into the house of the Lord your God: you shall not boil a lamb in his mother's milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord said to Moses, Write these words for yourself, for on these words I have established a covenant with you and with Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Moses was there before the Lord forty days, and forty nights; he did not eat bread, and he did not drink water; and he wrote upon the tables these words of the covenant, the ten sayings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And when Moses went down from the mountain, [there were] the two tables in the hands of Moses, —as then he went down from the mountain, Moses knew not that the appearance of the skin of his face was glorified, when God spoke to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Aaron and all the elders of Israel saw Moses, and the appearance of the skin of his face was made glorious, and they feared to approach him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Moses called them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the synagogue turned towards him, and Moses spoke to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And afterwards all the children of Israel came to him, and he commanded them all things, whatever the Lord had commanded him in the mount of Sina. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And when he ceased speaking to them, he put a veil on his face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak to him, he took off the veil till he went out, and he went forth and spoke to all the children of Israel whatever the Lord commanded him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that it was glorified; and Moses put the veil over his face, till he went in to speak with him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: salach (סָלַח) = to forgive. Common English renderings: forgive; pardon. Commonly used with God as subject of forgiveness.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Hew, ; I will; the words which \textsuperscript{6} passed; proclaimed; The Lord merciful; , ; abundant; truth \textsuperscript{7} Keeping; forgiving; that will by no means clear the guilty The Hebrew nakkeh lo yenakkeh, has been rendered "Acquitting him who is not innocent." Nothing can more strongly express the goodness of God to frail mortals than this declaration, "which has been misunderstood and misinterpreted by all our translators."; , ; visiting \textsuperscript{9} If now, let my Lord; stiffnecked; pardon; take us \textsuperscript{10} I make;, I will do marvels; a terrible \textsuperscript{13} ye shall; images Heb. statutes \textsuperscript{15} make, ; whoring; call thee; eat \textsuperscript{20} firstling; lamb or, kid All the; none \textsuperscript{22} feast of weeks; year's end Heb. revolution of the year \textsuperscript{28} forty days;, he wrote, ; commandments Heb. words \textsuperscript{29} am 2513, bc 1491, An, Ex, Is, 1, Elul Two tables wist; the skin; face shone As the original word karan, signifies to shine out, or dart forth, as horns on the head of an animal, or rays of light reflected from a polished surface, we may suppose that the heavenly glory which filled the soul of this holy man, darted out from his face in coruscations, in the manner in which light is generally represented. The Vulgate renders it, et ignorabat quod cornuta esset facies sua, "and he did not know that his face was horned; " which version, misunderstood, has induced painters to represent Moses with two very large horns, one proceeding from each temple!\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 35}
\markright{EXODUS 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel together, and said, These are the words which the Lord has spoken for [you] to do them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Six days shall you perform works, but on the seventh day [shall be] rest—a holy sabbath—a rest for the Lord: every one that does work on it, let him die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You⌃ shall not burn a fire in any of your dwellings on the sabbath-day; I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This [is] the thing which the Lord has appointed you, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Take of yourselves an offering for the Lord: every one that engages in his heart shall bring the first fruits to the Lord; gold, silver, brass, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} blue, purple, double scarlet spun, and fine linen spun, and goats' hair, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and rams' skins dyed red, and skins [dyed] blue, and incorruptible wood, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and sardine stones, and stones for engraving for the shoulder-piece and full-length robe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And every man that is wise in heart among you, let him come and work all things whatever the Lord has commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The tabernacle, and the cords, and the coverings, and the rings, and the bars, and the posts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and the ark of the testimony, and its staves, and its propitiatory, and the veil, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and the curtains of the court, and its posts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and the emerald stones, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and the incense, and the anointing oil, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the table and all its furniture, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and the candlestick for the light and all its furniture, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and the altar and all its furniture; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the holy garments of Aaron the priest, and the garments in which they shall do service; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the garments of priesthood for the sons of Aaron and the anointing oil, and the compound incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all the congregation of the children of Israel went out from Moses. And they brought, they whose heart prompted them, and they to whoever it seemed good in their mind, each and offering: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and they brought an offering to the Lord for all the works of the tabernacle of witness, and all its services, and for all the robes of the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the men, even every one to whom it seemed good in his heart, brought from the women, [even] brought seals and ear-rings, and finger-rings, and necklaces, and bracelets, every article of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And all as many as brought ornaments of gold to the Lord, and with whoever fine linen was found; and they brought skins [dyed] blue, and rams' skins dyed red. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And every one that offered an offering brought silver and brass, the offerings to the Lord; and [they] with whom was found incorruptible wood; and they brought [offerings] for all the works of the preparation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And every woman skilled in her heart to spin with her hands, brought spun [articles], the blue, and purple, and scarlet and fine linen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And all the women to whom it seemed good in their heart in their wisdom, spun the goats' hair. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the rulers brought the emerald stones, and the stones for setting in the ephod, and the oracle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and the compounds both for the anointing oil, and the composition of the incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And every man and woman whose mind inclined them to come in and do all the works as many as the Lord appointed them to do by Moses—[they] the children of Israel brought an offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Moses said to the children of Israel, Behold, God has called by name Beseleel the [son] of Urias the [son of] Or, of the tribe of Juda, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and has filled him with a divine spirit of wisdom and understanding, and knowledge of all things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} to labor skillfully in all works of cunning workmanship, to form the gold and the silver and the brass, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} and to work in stone, and to fashion the wood, and to work in every work of wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And [God] gave improvement in understanding both to him, and to Eliab the [son] of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And [God] filled them with wisdom, understanding [and] perception, to understand to work all the works of the sanctuary, and to weave the woven and embroidered work with scarlet and fine linen, to do all work of curious workmanship [and] embroidery.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Six days, ; an holy day Heb. holiness whosoever \textsuperscript{11} tabernacle, taches Keraism, from karas, to bend, so called from their curved form; hooks, clasps, or anything used for the purpose of fastening. The word taches is formed by apheresis from the French attacher, to fasten. They were equivalent, perhaps, to our hooks-and-eyes. \textsuperscript{14} candlestick Menorah, rather, a chandelier, which was of pure gold, and is described as having one shaft, with six branches proceeding from it, adorned at equal distances with six flowers, like lilies, with as many bowls and knops placed alternately. \textsuperscript{18} The pins These, as Dr. Wall observes, were not particularly mentioned. Josephus says, that to every board of the tabernacle, and to every pillar of the hangings of the court, there were ropes or cords, fastened at the top of the board or pillar, and that the other end of the rope was fastened to a πασσαλος, a nail, or pin, which, at a good distance off, was driven into the ground up to the head, a cubit deep. This was to keep the tabernacle from being blown down by the wind. Dr. Shaw, describing the tents of the Bedouins, says, "These tents are kept firm and steady by bracing or stretching down their eaves with cords tied to wooden hooked pins, well pointed, which they drive into the ground with a mallet; one of these pins answering to the nail, as the mallet does to the hammer, which Jael used in fastening to the ground the temples of Sisera" ( ). \textsuperscript{22} bracelets Chach, either a hook or clasp to join garments together; fibula, as Montanus renders; or bracelets, which are hooked or clasped together; so Vulgate, armillas .; tablets Kumoz, as Bochart thinks, a kind of girdle, swathe, or zone. every man \textsuperscript{31} And he, ; wisdom Chochmah, (from chacham, to be wise, skilful, prudent), wisdom, denoting the compass of mind and strength of capacity necessary to form a wise man; hence our word wisdom is the power of judging what is wise, or best to be done; from the Saxon wisedom, the doom or judgment of the well taught, wise, or prudent man, from wisan, to teach, advise, and deman, to judge. understanding Tevoonah, (from boon, to separate, distinguish, discern), understanding, discernment, capacity to comprehend the different parts of a work, how to connect, arrange, etc., in order to make a complete whole. knowledge Daâth, (from yadâ, to know, be acquainted with), knowledge, or a particular acquaintance with a person or thing, practical, experimental knowledge. \textsuperscript{35} he filled, ; the cunning;, ; of the weaver\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 36}
\markright{EXODUS 36}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Beseleel wrought, and Eliab and every one wise in understanding, to whom was given wisdom and knowledge, to understand to do all the works according to the holy offices, according to all things which the Lord appointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Moses called Beseleel and Eliab, and all that had wisdom, to whom God gave knowledge in [their] heart, and all who were freely willing to come forward to the works, to perform them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they received from Moses all the offerings, which the children of Israel brought for all the works of the sanctuary to do them; and they continued to receive the gifts brought, from those who brought them in the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there came all the wise men who wrought the works of the sanctuary, each according to his own work, which they wrought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And one said to Moses, The people bring an abundance [too great] in proportion to all the works which the Lord has appointed [them] to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses commanded, and proclaimed in the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman any longer labor for the offerings of the sanctuary; and the people were restrained from bringing any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they had materials sufficient for making the furniture, and they left some besides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And every wise one among those that wrought made the robes of the holy places, which belong to Aaron the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he made the ephod of gold, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine linen twined. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the plates were divided, the threads of gold, so as to interweave with the blue and purple, and with the spun scarlet, and the fine linen twined, they made it a woven work; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} shoulder-pieces joined from both sides, a work woven by mutual twisting of the parts into one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They made it of the same material according to the making of it, of gold, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine linen twined, as the Lord commanded Moses; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and they made the two emerald stones clasped together and set in gold, graven and cut after the cutting of a seal with the names of the children of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and he put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, [as] stones of memorial of the children of Israel, as the Lord appointed Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they made the oracle, a work woven with embroidery, according to the work of the ephod, of gold, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine linen twined. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They made the oracle square [and] double, the length of a span, and the breadth of a span, —double. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And there was interwoven with it a woven work of four rows of stones, a series of stones, the first row, a sardius and topaz and emerald; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the second row, a carbuncle and sapphire and jasper; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the third row, a ligure and agate and amethyst; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the fourth row a chrysolite and beryl and onyx set round about with gold, and fastened with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the stones were twelve according to the names of the children of Israel, graven according to their names like seals, each according to his own name for the twelve tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they made on the oracle turned wreaths, wreathen work, of pure gold, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and they made two golden circlets and two golden rings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they put the two golden rings on both the [upper] corners of the oracle; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and they put the golden wreaths on the rings on both sides of the oracle, and the two wreaths into the two couplings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they put them on the two circlets, and they put them on the shoulders of the ephod opposite [each other] in front. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they made two golden rings, and put them on the two projections on the top of the oracle, and on the top of the hinder part of the ephod within. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they made two golden rings, and put them on both the shoulders of the ephod under it, in front by the coupling above the connexion of the ephod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he fastened the oracle by the rings that were on it to the rings of the ephod, which were fastened with [a string] of blue, joined together with the woven work of the ephod; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and their girdles of fine linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet spun, the work of an embroiderer, according as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And they made the golden plate, a dedicated thing of the sanctuary, of pure gold; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and he wrote upon it graven letters [as] of a seal, Holiness to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And they put it on the border of blue, so that it should be on the mitre above, as the Lord commanded Moses.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} An, Ex, Is, 1, Tisri to Adar Bezaleel, wise hearted man, for the service; according \textsuperscript{6} When God puts grace into the heart, the hands will be diligently employed in every good work. \textsuperscript{8} wise, made; cherubims Keroovim, cherubim, not cherubims. What these were we cannot determine. Some, observing that the verb kerav in Syriac, sometimes means to resemble, make like, conceive the noun keroov signifies no more than an image, figure, or representation of anything. Josephus says they were flying animals, like none of those which are seen by man, but such as Moses saw about the throne of God. In another place he says, "As for the cherubim, nobody can tell or conceive what they were like." These symbolical figures, according to the description of them by Ezekiel (; ), were creatures with four heads and one body; and the animals of which these forms consisted were the noblest of their kind; the lion among the wild beasts; the bull among the tame ones; the eagle among the birds, and man at the head of all. Hence some have conceived them to be somewhat of the shape of flying oxen; and it is alleged in favour of this opinion, that the far more common meaning of the verb kerav, in Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic, being to plough, the natural meaning of keroov, is a creature used in ploughing. This seems to have been the ancient opinion which tradition had handed down, concerning the shape of the cherubim with the flaming sword, that guarded the tree of life ( ). \textsuperscript{19} covering rams' skins dyed red This was the third covering of the tabernacle. The first and lowermost was made of fine linen, richly embroidered with figures of cherubim, in shades of blue, purple, and scarlet ( ). It is reasonable to suppose, that the right side of this curtain was undermost, and so it formed a beautiful ceiling in the inside of the tabernacle. The second covering, which lay over the embroidered one, was made of a sort of mohair ( ), and the fourth, or uppermost one, which was to keep the others from the weather, was made of tachash, or badgers' skins. \textsuperscript{21} The length Each of these boards, taking the cubit at nearly twenty-two inches, was about eighteen feet long, and two feet nine inches broad. As these boards are said to be standing up ( ), their length was consequently the height of the tabernacle; and as the two sides were composed of twenty of these, standing up ( and ), and the west end of six, with two boards to project at the corners ( and ), the tabernacle must therefore, have been thirty cubits, or fifty-five feet long, and about ten cubits, or eighteen feet broad. These boards were fastened at the bottom by two tenons in each board, which fitted into two mortices in the foundation, at the top by links or hasps, and on the sides by five wooden bars, which ran through rings or staples in each of the boards. The boards and bars were all overlaid with gold; and their rings for the staves, and their hasps at top, were of the same metal. The foundation on which they stood consisted of about ninety-six solid blocks of silver, two under each board, about eighteen inches long, and of a suitable thickness; and each weighing a talent, or about a hundred weight. Four blocks of silver formed the bases of the columns which supported the curtain that divided the inside of the tabernacle into two rooms. \textsuperscript{30} under every board two sockets Heb. two sockets two sockets under one board \textsuperscript{35} veil of blue Parachoth, from parach, to separate, divide, make a distinction between somewhat, the inner vail, which divided the tabernacle into two, and separated, and made a distinction between the Holy place and the Holy of Holies. This vail was made of the same rich materials as the inner covering of the tabernacle, and curiously embroidered with cherubim and other ornaments. Though it does not appear from Scripture at what distance from either end of the tabernacle this vail was hung, yet is reasonably conjectured, that it divided it in the same proportion in which the temple, built after this model, was divided; that is, two-thirds of the whole length were allotted to the first room, and one-third to the second; so that the room beyond the vail, the Holy of Holies, was exactly square, being ten cubits each way, and the first room, the sanctuary, was twice as long as it was broad. \textsuperscript{37} an hanging This vail was a fine embroidered curtain, of the same materials and of the same workmanship as the inner vail and inner covering of the tabernacle. The text does not say how low it hung. Philo makes it touch the ground; but Josephus will have it to come down but half way, so that the people might have a view of the inside of the tabernacle; but then he says there was another curtain over that, which came to the ground, to keep it from the weather, and was drawn aside on the sabbath and other festivals., of needlework Heb. the work of a needle worker, or embroider\par}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{8} on the end or, out of, etc on the other end or, out of, etc. \textsuperscript{9} cherubims spread; to the mercy seatward \textsuperscript{10} Nothing but the ark of the covenant, with the mercy-seat, was put within the most holy place; but without the vail this "table of shittim wood" was fixed, of the same height as the ark, but neither so long nor so broad. It was made of the same materials as the ark, and with a golden cornice; but it had also another cornice below the edge, and one at the bottom, with a border between the two of a hand breadth; though some think one border only was below the edge, and that this was towards the bottom, to keep the feet or legs more closely united. The table also had rings and staves for the convenience of removing it. To it were annexed several vessels; as dishes, in which some think the shewbread was placed; or, according to others, the flour of which it was made, or the oil used for various purposes; spoons, which were employed about the incense offered on the golden altar, or carried within the vail in a censer on the day of atonement. Some have supposed the word to denote vials, as we read of vials full of odours and incense ( ): covers, which seem to have been put over both the loaves and the incense, yet some suppose they were vessels used in drink-offerings; but that is more reasonably considered as the use of the bowls. \textsuperscript{16} dishes; cover withal or, pour out withal\par}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the altar This altar consisted of four boards of shittim (acacia) wood, covered with brass, and hollow in the middle; but it is supposed to have been filled up with earth when used, for it is expressly said ( ) that the altar is to be of earth. As it was five cubits long and five cubits broad, and three cubits high, if the cubit be reckoned at 21 inches, it must have been eight feet nine inches square, and about five feet three inches in height., ; foursquare; and three cubits the height thereof \textsuperscript{8} the laver, ; looking glasses, or, brazen glasses, The word maroth, from raah, to see, denotes reflectors, or mirrors, of any kind. That these could not have been looking glasses, as in our translation, is sufficiently evident, not only from the glass not being then in use, but also from the impossibility of making the brazen laver of such materials. The first mirrors known among men, were the clear fountain and unruffled lake. The first artificial ones were made of polished brass, afterwards of steel, and when luxury increased, of silver; but at a very early period, they were made of a mixed metal, particularly of tin and copper, the best of which, as Pliny informs us, were formerly manufactured at Brundusium. When the Egyptians went to their temples, according to St. Cyril, they always carried their mirrors with them. The Israelitish women probably did the same; and Dr. Shaw says, that looking-glasses are still part of the dress of Moorish women, who carry them constantly hung at their breasts. assembling Heb. assembling by troops, It is supposed that these women kept watch during the night. Among the ancients, women were generally employed as door-keepers. See note on . \textsuperscript{21} tabernacle of testimony, ;, ; The word tabernacle is used in many different senses, and signifies: 1. A tent or pavilion -; 2. A house or dwelling -, 3. A kind of tent, which is designated, to speak after the manner of the men, the palace of the Most High, the dwelling of the God of Israel -; 4. Christ's human nature, of which the Jewish tabernacle was a type, wherein God dwells really, substantially, and personally -, 5. The true church militant - 6. Our natural body, in which the soul lodges as in a tabernacle -; 7. The token of God's gracious presence - by the hand; Ithamar \textsuperscript{22} Bezaleel, ; The supernatural qualifications of Bezaleel and Aholiab proved their divine appointment; yet they had an express nomination to their work. They were also miraculously qualified to instruct their assistants, as well as to superintend them. Christ alone builds the Temple of the Lord, and bears the glory; but ministers and private Christians, under his direction and by his grace, may be fellow-workers together with him. They who, in mean employments, are diligent and humbly contented, are equally acceptable with those who are engaged in more splendid services. The women who spun the goats' hair were wise-hearted, as well as the persons who presided over the work of the tabernacle, or as Aaron, who burnt incense there, because they did it heartily unto the Lord. Our wisdom and duty consist in giving God the glory and use of our talents, be they more or less; neither abusing nor burying them, but occupying with them until our Lord shall come; being satisfied that it is better to be a door-keeper in his service, than the most mighty and renowned of the ungodly. - Scott. all that the Lord \textsuperscript{24} All the gold If we follow the estimation of the learned Dean Prideaux, the value of the twenty-nine talents, and 730 shekels of gold, will be 198, 347£. 12s. 6d. The value of the silver contributed by 603, 550; Israelites, at half a shekel, or 1s. 6d. per man, will amount to 45, 266£. 5s. The value of the 70 talents, 2, 400 shekels of brass, will be 513£. 17s. The gold weighed 4, 245 pounds; the silver, 14, 603 pounds; and the brass, 10, 277 pounds, troy weight. The total value of all the gold, silver, and brass, will consequently amount to 244, 127£. 14s. 6d.; and the total weight of these three metals will amount to 29, 124 pounds troy, which reduced to avoirdupois weight, is equal to fourteen tons, 226 pounds! - It may, perhaps, seem difficult to imagine how the Israelites should be possessed of so much wealth in the desert; but it should be remembered, that their ancestors were opulent men before they came into Egypt; that they were further enriched by the spoils of the Egyptians and Amalekites; and that it is probable, they traded with the neighbouring nations who bordered on the wilderness. There appear to be three reasons why so much riches should have been employed in the construction of the tabernacle, etc. 1. To impress the people's minds with the glory and dignity of the Divine Majesty, and the importance of his service. 2. To take out of their hands the occasion of covetousness. 3. To prevent pride and vain glory, by leading them to give up to the divine service even the ornaments of their persons.; offering, the shekel \textsuperscript{26} bekah, every man Heb. a poll, six hundred\par}

\subsection*{Exodus 39}
\markright{EXODUS 39}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} All the gold that was employed for the works according to all the fabrication of the holy things, was of the gold of the offerings, twenty-nine talents, and seven hundred and twenty shekels according to the holy shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the offering of silver from the men that were numbered of the congregation one hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, one drachm apiece, even the half shekel, according to the holy shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Every one that passed the survey from twenty years old and upwards to the [number of] six hundred thousand, and three thousand five hundred and fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the hundred talents of silver went to the casting of the hundred capitals of the tabernacle, and to the capitals of the veil; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} one hundred capitals to the hundred talents, a talent to a chapiter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he formed into hooks for the pillars, and he gilt their capitals and adorned them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the brass of the offering [was] seventy talents, and a thousand five hundred shekels; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and they made of it the bases of the door of the tabernacle of witness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the bases of the court round about, and the bases of the gate of the court, and the pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court round about; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and the brazen appendage of the altar, and all the vessels of the altar, and all the instruments of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses, so did they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And of the gold that remained of the offering they made vessels to minister with before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the blue that was left, and the purple, and the scarlet they made [into] garments of ministry for Aaron, so that he should minister with them in the sanctuary; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and they brought the garments to Moses, and the tabernacle, and its furniture, its bases and its bars and the posts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the ark of the covenant, and its bearers, and the altar and all its furniture. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they made the anointing oil, and the incense of composition, and the pure candlestick, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and its lamps, lamps for burning, and oil for the light, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the table of show bread, and all its furniture, and the show bread upon it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the garments of the sanctuary which belong to Aaron, and the garments of his sons, for the priestly ministry; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the curtains of the court, and the posts, and the veil of the door of the tabernacle, and the gate of the court, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and all the vessels of the tabernacle and all its instruments: and the skins, even rams' skins dyed red, and the blue coverings, and the coverings of the other things, and the pins, and all the instruments for the works of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Whatsoever things the Lord appointed Moses, so did the children of Israel make all the furniture. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses saw all the works;
