{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the blue, cloths, holy place; the holy \textsuperscript{6} onyx stones The meaning of the word shoham is not easily determined. It has been variously rendered a beryl, emerald, prasius, sapphire, sardius, ruby, carnelian, onyx, and sardonyx. It may signify both the onyx and sardonyx. The latter stone is a mixture of the chalcedony and carnelian, sometimes in strata, and at other times blended together, and is found striped with white and red strata, or layers. It is generally allowed that there is no real difference, except in hardness, between the carnelian, chalcedony, agate, sardonyx, and onyx. The onyx is of a darkish horny colour, resembling the nail or hoof, from which circumstance it has its name ( ονυξ ). It has often a plate of a blueish white or red in it, and when on one or both sides of this white there appears a plate of a reddish colour, the jewellers call the stone a sardonyx., ; ouches Mishbetzoth, strait places, sockets, to insert the stones in, from shavatz, to straiten, enclose. \textsuperscript{10} the first row; sardius or, ruby \textsuperscript{11} a diamond; The word yahalom may mean the diamond, from halam, to beat, smite, because of its extreme hardness, by which it will beat to pieces the other stones. It is a fine pellucid substance never debased with any admixture of other matter; susceptible of elegant tinges from metal-line particles; giving fire with steel; not fermenting with acid menstrua; scarcely calcinable by any degree of fire; and of one simple and permanent appearance in all lights. It is the hardest and most valuable of all gems; when pure, perfectly clear and pellucid as the clearest water, and eminently distinguished from all other substances by its vivid splendour, and the brightness of its reflections. \textsuperscript{12} a ligure Leshem, the ligure, the same as the jacinth, or hyacinth, a precious stone of a deep red, with a considerable tinge of yellow. Theophrastus and Pliny say it resembles the carbuncle, of a brightness sparkling like fire. an agate Shevo, the agate, a semi-pellucid compound gem, formed of different simple minerals, as chalcedony, cornelian, jasper. horn-stone, quartz, amethyst, opal, etc.; joined irregularly or in layers. It is of a white, reddish, yellowish, or greenish ground; and so variously figured in its substance as to represent plants, trees, animals, and other objects. an amethyst Achlamah, an amethyst, a transparent gem, composed of a strong blue and deep red; and according as either prevails, affording different tinges of purple, sometimes approaching to violet, and sometimes even fading to a pale rose colour. \textsuperscript{13} a beryl Tarshish, a pellucid gem, of a sea or blueish green colour. a jasper Yaspeh, the jasper, a hard stone, of which there are not less than fifteen varieties of colour, as green, red, yellow, brown, black, etc.\par}

\section*{Leviticus Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Moses\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Received as Mosaic in Jewish and Christian tradition; Leviticus stands within the law delivered through Moses.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The NT repeatedly treats the Mosaic law as Mosaic; see Mark 1:44, Matthew 8:4, and John 7:19-23.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 1445-1406 BC at Sinai and in the wilderness\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Leviticus immediately after the tabernacle's erection and before the Sinai departure narratives in Numbers.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same wilderness setting, while sometimes differing in detail and wording from the later MT tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Priestly legislation delivered from the tabernacle after the covenant at Sinai.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To set forth holy worship, priesthood, sacrifice, purity, atonement, and covenant holiness before a holy God.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} holiness; sacrifice; priesthood; purity; atonement; Day of Atonement; covenant worship\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Sacrifices 1-7; Priesthood 8-10; Clean and unclean 11-15; Atonement 16; Holiness laws 17-27.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Leviticus and related early Qumran Leviticus fragments Hasmonean period | Subst. 11Q paleoLeviticus a, a substantial early witness written in paleo-Hebrew script Herodian period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus, with Codex Alexandrinus also preserving Leviticus 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Discussion of the translated Mosaic law by Letter of Aristeas (mid-2nd century BC)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Leviticus is important for comparing priestly terminology across Hebrew and Greek; some Greek renderings illuminate how Second Temple readers understood cultic vocabulary.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Leviticus as Mosaic law from God through Moses; holiness legislation is treated as divinely given, not as a late priestly invention.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Leviticus}
\markboth{LEVITICUS}{}
\subsection*{Leviticus 1}
\markright{LEVITICUS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord called Moses again and spoke to him out of the tabernacle of witness, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If [any] man of you shall bring gifts to the Lord, you⌃ shall bring your gifts of the cattle and of the oxen and of the sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If his gift be a whole burnt offering, he shall bring an unblemished male of the herd to the door of the tabernacle of witness, he shall bring it as acceptable before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering as a thing acceptable for him, to make atonement for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall kill the calf before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron the priests shall bring the blood, and they shall pour the blood round about on the altar, which [is] at the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And having flayed the whole burnt offering, they shall divide it by its limbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Aaron the priests shall put fire on the altar, and shall pile wood on the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the sons of Aaron the priests shall pile up the divided parts, and the head, and the fat on the wood on the fire, [the wood] which is on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the entrails and the feet they shall wash in water, and the priests shall put all on the altar: it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice, a smell of sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if his gift [be] of the sheep to the Lord, or of the lambs, or of the kids for whole burnt offerings, he shall bring it a male without blemish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he shall lay his hand on its head; and they shall kill it by the side of the altar, toward the north before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall pour its blood on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they shall divide it by its limbs, and its head and its fat, and the priests shall pile them up on the wood which is on the fire, on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they shall wash the entrails and the feet with water, and the priest shall bring all the [parts] and put them on the altar: it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice, a smell of sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if he bring his gift, a burnt offering to the Lord, of birds, then shall he bring his gift of doves or pigeons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the priest shall bring it to the altar, and shall wring off its head; and the priest shall put it on the altar, and shall wring out the blood at the bottom of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he shall take away the crop with the feathers, and shall cast it forth by the altar toward the east to the place of the ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he shall break it off from the wings and shall not separate it, and the priest shall put it on the altar on the wood which is on the fire: it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice, a sweet smelling savor to the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} If any; an offering Korban, from karav to approach, an introductory offering, or offering of access, in allusion to the present which is always required in the East, on being introduced to a superior. \textsuperscript{3} a burnt, ;, ;, ;, ; a male, ; his own, ;, ; at the \textsuperscript{9} inwards, ; burn all, ; a sweet \textsuperscript{10} of the flocks; a burnt sacrifice Olah, a burnt offering, from âlah, to ascend, because this offering ascended, as it were, to God in flame and smoke, being wholly consumed; for which reason its is called in the Septuagint, ολοκαυτωμα, a whole burnt offering. This was the most important of all the sacrifices; and no part of it was eaten either by the priest or the offerer, but the whole was offered to God. It has been sufficiently shown by learned men, that almost every nation of the earth, in every age, had their burnt offerings, from the persuasion that there was no other way to appease the incensed gods; and they even offered human sacrifices, because they imagined that life was necessary to redeem life, and that the gods would be satisfied with nothing less. a male \textsuperscript{11} he shall; northward, and the \textsuperscript{15} wring off his head or, pinch off the head with the nail; Matt. 26:1-27:66 \textsuperscript{16} his feathers or, the filth thereof; by the place\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 2}
\markright{LEVITICUS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if a soul bring a gift, a sacrifice to the Lord, his gift shall be fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and shall put frankincense on it: it is a sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he shall bring it to the priests the sons of Aaron: and having taken from it a handful of the fine flour with the oil, and all its frankincense, then the priest shall put the memorial of it on the altar: [it is] a sacrifice, an odour of sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the remainder of the sacrifice shall be for Aaron and his sons, a most holy portion from the sacrifices of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if he bring as a gift a sacrifice baked from the oven, a gift to the Lord of fine flour, [he shall bring] unleavened bread kneaded with oil, and unleavened cakes anointed with oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if your gift [be] a sacrifice from a pan, it is fine flour mingled with oil, unleavened [offerings]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall break them into fragments and pour oil upon them: it is a sacrifice to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if your gift be a sacrifice from the hearth, it shall be made of fine flour with oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he shall offer the sacrifice which he shall make of these to the Lord, and shall bring it to the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the priest shall approach the altar, and shall take away from the sacrifice a memorial of it, and the priest shall place it on the altar: a burnt offering, a smell of sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And that which is left of the sacrifice [shall be] for Aaron and his sons, most holy from the burnt offerings of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You⌃ shall not leaven any sacrifice which you⌃ shall bring to the Lord; for [as to] any leaven, or any honey, you⌃ shall not bring of it to offer a gift to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You⌃ shall bring them in the way of fruits to the Lord, but they shall not be offered on the altar for a sweet smelling savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And every gift of your sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt; omit not the salt of the covenant of the Lord from your sacrifices: on every gift of yours you⌃ shall offer salt to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if you would offer a sacrifice of first fruits to the Lord, [it shall be] new grains ground [and] roasted for the Lord; so sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priest shall offer the memorial of it [taken] from the grains with the oil, and all its frankincense: it is a burnt offering to the Lord.\par

and they shall kill it before the Lord by the doors of the tabernacle of witness; and the priests the sons of Aaron shall pour out the blood on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he shall offer of it a burnt offering to the Lord, [even] the fat that covers the belly, and all the fat that is on the belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And both the kidneys, and all the fat that is upon them, that which is upon the thighs, and the caul of the liver with the kidneys, shall he take away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priest shall offer it upon the altar: [it is] a burnt offering, a smell of sweet savor to the Lord. All the fat [belongs] to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [It is] a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your habitations; you⌃ shall eat no fat and no blood.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} caul above the liver, with the kidneys or, midriff over the liver, and over the kidneys, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{6} a sacrifice; be of, ; male he shall \textsuperscript{8} he shall, ; kill it; sprinkle \textsuperscript{9} the fat; the whole rump To what has already been said on the tails of eastern sheep, we may add the testimony of Ludolf, who states that they are so very large, some of them weighing from twelve to fourteen pounds, "that the owners are obliged to tie a little cart behind them, whereupon they put the tail of the sheep, as well for the convenience of carriage, and to ease the poor creatures, as to preserve the wool from dirt, and the tail from being torn among the bushes and stones." The same is testified by Dr. Russell, who says, "In some other places where they feed in the fields, the shepherds are obliged to fix a piece of thin board to the under part of the tail, to prevent its being torn by bushes, thistles, etc., as it is not covered underneath with thick wool, like the upper part; and some have small wheels to facilitate the dragging of the board after them." \textsuperscript{16} it is the food all the fat \textsuperscript{17} a perpetual, ; eat neither That is, neither the blood which is contained in the larger veins and arteries, nor the fat or suet which is within the animal, which exists in a separate or unmixed state, as the omentum or caul, the fat of the mesentery, or fatty part of the substance which connects the convolutions of the alimentary canal or small intestines, the fat of the kidneys, and whatever else of the internal fat was easily separable, together with the whole of the tail already described; for the blood which assumes the form of gravy, and the fat which is intermixed with the other flesh, might be eaten. This law not only related to the sacrifices, but to all the cattle which the Israelites slaughtered for food.; blood\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 4}
\markright{LEVITICUS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, saying, If a soul shall sin unwillingly before the Lord, in any of the commandments of the Lord concerning things which he ought not to do, and shall do some of them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} if the anointed priest sin so as to cause the people to sin, then shall he bring for his sin, which he has sinned, an unblemished calf of the herd to the Lord for his sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he shall bring the calf to the door of the tabernacle of witness before the Lord, and he shall put his hand on the head of the calf before the Lord, and shall kill the calf in the presence of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the anointed priest who has been consecrated having received of the blood of the calf, shall then bring it into the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priest shall dip his finger into the blood, and sprinkle of the blood seven times before the Lord, over against the holy veil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the priest shall put of the blood of the calf on the horns of the altar of the compound incense which is before the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of witness; and all the blood of the calf shall he pour out by the foot of the altar of whole burnt offerings, which is by the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and all the fat of the calf of the sin-offering shall he take off from it; the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is on the inwards, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, which is on the thighs, and the caul that is on the liver with the kidneys, them shall he take away, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} as he takes it away from the calf of the sacrifice of peace-offering, so shall the priest offer it on the altar of burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And [they shall take] the skin of the calf, and all his flesh with the head and the extremities and the belly and the dung, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and they shall carry out the whole calf out of the camp into a clean place, where they pour out the ashes, and they shall consume it there on wood with fire: it shall be burnt on the ashes poured out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if the whole congregation of Israel trespass ignorantly, and a thing should escape the notice of the congregation, and they should do one thing forbidden of any of the commands of the Lord, which ought not to be done, and should transgress: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and the sin wherein they have sinned should become known to them, then shall the congregation bring an unblemished calf of the herd for a sin-offering, and they shall bring it to the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the calf before the Lord, and they shall kill the calf before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the anointed priest shall bring in of the blood of the calf into the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the priest shall dip his finger into some of the blood of the calf, and shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the veil of the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of the incense of composition, which is before the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of witness; and he shall pour out all the blood at the bottom of the altar of whole burnt offerings, which is by the door of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he shall take away all the fat from it, and shall offer it up on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he shall do to the calf as he did to the calf of the sin-offering, so shall it be done; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and the trespass shall be forgiven them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they shall carry forth the calf whole without the camp, and they shall burn the calf as they burnt the former calf: it is the sin-offering of the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if a ruler sin, and break one of all the commands of the Lord his God, [doing the thing] which ought not to be done, unwillingly, and shall sin and trespass, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and his trespass wherein he has sinned, be known to him, then shall he offer for his gift a kid of the goats, a male without blemish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he shall lay his hand on the head of the kid, and they shall kill it in the place where they kill the [victims for] whole burnt offerings before the Lord; it is a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin-offering with his finger on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offering; and he shall pour out all its blood by the bottom of the altar of whole burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he shall offer up all his fat on the altar, as the fat of the sacrifice of peace-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and it shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And if a soul of the people of the land should sin unwillingly, in doing a thing [contrary to] any of the commandments of the Lord, which ought not to be done, and shall transgress, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and his sin should be known to him, wherein he has sinned, then shall he bring a kid of the goats, a female without blemish shall he bring for his sin, which he has sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he shall lay his hand on the head of his sin-offering, and they shall kill the kid of the sin-offering in the place where they kill the [victims for] whole burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the priest shall take of its blood with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and all its blood he shall pour forth by the foot of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he shall take away all the fat, as the fat is taken away from the sacrifice of peace-offering, and the priest shall offer it on the altar for a smell of sweet savor to the Lord; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and [his sin] shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And if he should offer a lamb for his sin-offering, he shall offer it a female without blemish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin-offerings, and they shall kill it in the place where they kill the [victims for] whole burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin-offering with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings, and he shall pour out all its blood by the bottom of the altar of whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he shall take away all his fat, as the fat of the lamb of the sacrifice of peace-offering is taken away, and the priest shall put it on the altar for a whole burnt offering to the Lord; and the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: mashiach (מָשִׁיחַ) = anointed one. Common English renderings: anointed; Messiah. Used of priests, kings, and in later expectation of the Messiah.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the priest; a young bullock, ; for a sin \textsuperscript{6} dip, ; seven times The number seven is what is called a number of perfection among the Hebrews; and is often used to denote the completion, fulness, or perfection of a thing. \textsuperscript{7} the horns, ; all the blood \textsuperscript{12} without the camp Heb. to without the camp, This was intended, figuratively, to express the enormity of this sin, and the availableness of the atonement. The sacrifice, as having the sin of the priest transferred from himself to it, by his confession and imposition of hands, was become unclean and abominable, and was carried, as it were, out of God's sight; and thus its own offensiveness was removed, with the sin of the person in whose behalf it was offered.;, the ashes burn him; where the ashes are poured out Heb. at the pouring out of the ashes \textsuperscript{13} the whole congregation This may refer to some oversight in acts of religious worship, or to some transgression of the letter of the law, which arose out of the peculiar circumstances in which they were found, as in the case mentioned in, et seq. The sacrifices and rites in this case were the same as in the preceding; only here the elders laid their hands on the head of the victim, in the name of all the congregation. through ignorance, ; and are guilty, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{18} upon the and shall pour out The reason for pouring out the blood, which is so constantly and strictly required by the law, was in opposition to an idolatrous custom of the ancient Zabii, who "were accustomed to eat of the blood of their sacrifices, because they imagined this to be the food of their gods, with whom they thought they had such communion, by eating their meat, that they revealed to them future things." - Maimonides \textsuperscript{21} as he a sin offering \textsuperscript{22} a ruler hath sinned Under the term nasi, that is, one preferred or elevated above others, from nasa, to exalt, it is probable that any person is meant who held any kind of political dignity among the people; and it evidently means the head of a tribe as in; . But the Rabbins generally understand it of the prince of the great sanhedrin, who, when they were under the regal form of government, was the king. A kid of the goats was the sacrifice in this case; and the rites were nearly the same as in the preceding, only the fat was burnt as that of the peace offering ( ).; and done \textsuperscript{23} if his sin; a kid \textsuperscript{24} And he; in the place, ; it is a sin \textsuperscript{26} the fat, See note on . an atonement \textsuperscript{27} any one Heb. any soul; common people Heb. people of the land, Amos haaretz; that is, any individual who was not a priest, king, or ruler among the people; an ordinary person. Any of these having transgressed, was obliged to bring a lamb or kid, the ceremonies being nearly the same as in the preceding cases. \textsuperscript{30} upon the horns; pour out There may have been some place at the bottom of the altar to receive and carry off the blood. \textsuperscript{31} all the fat, a sweet, ; , ; and the priest \textsuperscript{34} the horns of the altar \textsuperscript{35} And he according Lev. 1:1-6:19 and the priest shall make\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 5}
\markright{LEVITICUS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and he is a witness or has seen or been conscious, if he do not report it, he shall bear his iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That soul which shall touch any unclean thing, or carcass, or [that which is] unclean being taken of beasts, or the dead bodies of abominable [reptiles] which are unclean, or carcasses of unclean cattle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} or should touch the uncleanness of a man, or whatever kind, which he may touch and be defiled by, and it should have escaped him, but afterwards he should know, —then he shall have transgressed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That unrighteous soul, which determines with his lips to do evil or to do good according to whatever a man may determine with an oath, and it shall have escaped his notice, and he shall [afterwards] know [it], and [so] he should sin in some one of these things: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} —then shall he declare his sin in the things wherein he has sinned by that sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he shall bring for his transgressions against the Lord, for his sin which he has sinned, a ewe lamb of the flock, or a kid of the goats, for a sin-offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him for his sin which he has sinned, and his sin shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if he can’t afford a sheep, he shall bring for his sin which he has sinned, two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the Lord; one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall bring the sin-offering first; and the priest shall pinch off the head from the neck, and shall not divide the body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin-offering on the side of the altar, but the rest of the blood he shall drop at the foot of the altar, for it is a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he shall make the second a whole burnt offering, as it is fit; and the priest shall make atonement for his sin which he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And if he can’t afford a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then shall he bring as his gift for his sin, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin-offering; he shall not pour oil upon it, nor shall he put frankincense upon it, because it is a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he shall bring it to the priest; and the priest having taken a handful of it, shall lay the memorial of it on the altar of whole burnt offerings to the Lord; it is a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, which he has sinned in one of these things, and it shall be forgiven him; and that which is left shall be the priest's, as an offering of fine flour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The soul which shall be really unconscious, and shall sin unwillingly in any of the holy things of the Lord, shall even bring to the Lord for his transgression, a ram of the flock without blemish, valued according to shekels of silver according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for his [transgression] wherein he transgressed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he shall make compensation for that wherein he has sinned in the holy things; and he shall add the fifth part to it, and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of transgression, and [his sin] shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the soul which shall sin, and do one thing [against] any of the commandments of the Lord, which it is not right to do, and has not known it, and shall have transgressed, and shall have contracted guilt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} he shall even bring a ram without blemish from the flock, [valued] at a price of silver for his transgression to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for his trespass of ignorance, wherein he ignorantly trespassed, and he knew it not; and it shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For he has surely been guilty of transgression before the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: akatharsia (ἀκαθαρσία) = uncleanness; impurity. Common English renderings: uncleanness. A ceremonial and moral impurity term.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a soul, ; hear; the voice of swearing Kol alah, rather, "the voice of adjuration, " φωνην ορκισμου, as the LXX render; for this does not relate to the duty of informing against a common swearer, but to the case of a person who, being adjured by the civil magistrate to answer upon oath, refuses to declare what he knows upon the subject - such an one shall bear his iniquity - shall be considered as guilty in the sight of God of the transgression which he has endeavoured to conceal, and must expect to be punished for hiding the iniquity with which he was acquainted. bear \textsuperscript{4} if a soul This relates to rash oaths or vows, which a man was afterwards unable, or which it would have been sinful, to perform. to do evil \textsuperscript{6} trespass offering It is remarkable, that in this and the following verse, the sacrifice offered is indifferently called asham, a trespass offering, and chattath, a sin offering; yet the Marginal References show that these differ in several respects. Sin offerings were sometimes offered for the whole congregation; trespass offerings never, but only for particular persons. Bullocks were sometimes used for sin offerings, never for trespass offerings. The blood of the sin offerings was put on the horns of the altar, that of the trespass offerings was only sprinkled round the bottom of the altar. The sin offering seems to have been for the expiation of offences committed in matters of religion, from a mistake or inadvertency respecting the law; but the trespass offering was required for the casual deviations from the ritual law, when well known, or for crimes against moral precepts, implying injustice to man., ; a female, the priest \textsuperscript{7} he be not able to bring a lamb Heb. his hand cannot reach to the sufficiency of a lamb, ; two turtledoves; one \textsuperscript{10} offer; manner or, ordinance, make, ; it \textsuperscript{11} But if the tenth part, fine flour;, no oil, ; for it is \textsuperscript{15} a soul, in the, ;, ram; thy estimation, the shekel \textsuperscript{16} make; the fifth, ; and the priest \textsuperscript{17} a soul sin This case is supposed to differ from the preceding, merely in that the person concerned was not certain whether he had or had not committed the trespass. It is therefore called by the Hebrews a doubtful trespass offering., though; yet is he \textsuperscript{18} And he for a trespass; and the priest\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 6}
\markright{LEVITICUS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The soul which shall have sinned, and willfully overlooked the commandments of the Lord, and shall have dealt falsely in the affairs of his neighbor in the matter of a deposit, or concerning fellowship, or concerning plunder, or has in anything wronged his neighbor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} or has found that which was lost, and shall have lied concerning it, and shall have sworn unjustly concerning [any] one of all the things, whatever a man may do, so as to sin hereby; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} it shall come to pass, whenever he shall have sinned, and transgressed, that he shall restore the plunder which he has seized, or [redress] the injury which he has committed, or restore the deposit which was entrusted to him, or the lost article which he has found of any kind, about which he swore unjustly, he shall even restore it in full; and he shall add to it a fifth part besides; he shall restore it to him whose it is in the day in which he happens to be convicted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shall bring to the Lord for his trespass, a ram of the flock, without blemish, of value to the amount of the thing in which he trespassed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven for any one of all the things which he did and trespassed in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Charge Aaron and his sons, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} This [is] the law of whole burnt offering; this is the whole burnt offering in its burning on the altar all the night till the morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn on it, it shall not be put out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the priest shall put on the linen tunic, and he shall put the linen drawers on his body; and shall take away that which has been thoroughly burnt, which the fire shall have consumed, even the whole burnt offering from the altar, and he shall put it near the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he shall put off his robe, and put on another robe, and he shall take forth the offering that has been burnt without the camp into a clean place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, and shall not be extinguished; and the priest shall burn on it wood every morning, and shall heap on it the whole burnt offering, and shall lay on it the fat of the peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the fire shall always burn on the altar; it shall not be extinguished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} This is the law of the sacrifice, which the sons of Aaron shall bring near before the Lord, before the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the sacrifice with its oil, and with all its frankincense, which are upon the sacrifice; and he shall offer up on the altar a burnt offering as a sweet smelling savor, a memorial of it to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Aaron and his sons shall eat that which is left of it: it shall be eaten without leaven in a holy place, they shall eat it in the court of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as a portion to them of the burnt offerings of the Lord: it is most holy, as the offering for sin, and as the offering for trespass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Every male of the priests shall eat it: it is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations of the burnt offerings of the Lord; whoever shall touch them shall be hallowed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This is the gift of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer to the Lord in the day in which you shall anoint him; the tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sacrifice continually, the half of it in the morning, and the half of it in the evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} It shall be made with oil in a frying-pan; he shall offer it kneaded [and] in rolls, an offering of fragments, an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The anointed priest who is in his place, [one] of his sons, shall offer it: it is a perpetual statute, it shall all be consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And every sacrifice of a priest shall be thoroughly burnt, and shall not be eaten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is the law of the sin-offering; —in the place where they kill the whole burnt offering, they shall kill the sin-offerings before the Lord: they are most holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The priest that offers it shall eat it: in a holy place it shall be eaten, in the court of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Every one that touches the flesh of it shall be holy, and on whoever’s garment any of its blood shall have been sprinkled, whoever shall have it sprinkled, shall be washed in the holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the earthen vessel, in whichever it shall have been sodden, shall be broken; and if it shall have been sodden in a brazen vessel, he shall scour it and wash it with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Every male among the priests shall eat it: it is most holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And no offerings for sin, of whose blood there shall be brought any into the tabernacle of witness to make atonement in the holy place, shall be eaten: they shall be burned with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And this [is] the law of the ram for the trespass-offering; it is most holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} In the place where they kill the whole burnt offering, they shall kill the ram of the trespass-offering before the Lord, and he shall pour out the blood at the bottom of the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he shall offer all the fat from it; and the loins, and all the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that which is upon the thighs, and the caul upon the liver with the kidney, he shall take them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the priest shall offer them on the altar a burnt offering to the Lord; it is for trespass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Every male of the priest shall eat them, in the holy place they shall eat them: they are most holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} As the sin-offering, so also [is] the trespass-offering. There is one law of them; the priest who shall make atonement with it, his it shall be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And [as for] the priest who offers a man's whole burnt offering, the skin of the whole burnt offering which he offers, shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And every sacrifice which shall be prepared in the oven, and every one which shall be prepared on the hearth, or on a frying-pan, it is the property of the priest that offers it; it shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And every sacrifice made up with oil, or not made up [with oil], shall belong to the sons of Aaron, an equal portion to each.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: osheq (עֹשֶׁק) = oppression; extortion. Common English renderings: oppression. Often used for unjust exploitation. Gk. vocab: paraptōma (παράπτωμα) = trespass; offense. Common English renderings: trespass. A term for transgression or offense. Gk. vocab: koinōnia (κοινωνία) = sharing; fellowship; participation. Common English renderings: fellowship; communion. A term of participation or shared relation.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} commit; lie; in that in fellowship or, in dealing, Heb. in putting of the hand, ; deceived \textsuperscript{5} restore;, ; in the principal The property itself, if still remaining, or its full value, to which a fifth part more was to be added, to compensate the owner for the loss he had sustained by being deprived of the use of his goods. He must also bring a trespass offering to the Lord; which was intended to show that disobedience to God is the great evil, even of those crimes which are injurious to man, and that repentance, and even restitution, though needful in order to (obtain) forgiveness, cannot atone for sin. of his trespass offering or, of his being found guilty, Heb. of trespass. \textsuperscript{8} At this verse the Jews begin the twenty-fifth section of the law, and also, in the best Hebrew Bibles, the sixth chapter, which undoubtedly ought to begin here, as the inspired writer enters upon a new subject; the former part of the book being intended for the instruction of the people relative to the several sacrifices to be brought; but this for the instruction of the priests respecting some particulars of their official services. \textsuperscript{9} of the burnt; because of the burning or, for the burning \textsuperscript{10} linen garment; , consumed, ; *marg. beside \textsuperscript{12} the fire; burn wood, ; The efficacy of the priesthood and mediation of Christ is perpetual, and we can never approach to God in his name, by day or night, unseasonably. The ministers of Christ should have the fire of their zeal constantly burning. \textsuperscript{16} the remainder, ; unleavened; shall it \textsuperscript{17} baken; I have it is most holy \textsuperscript{18} the males; It shall every one Kol asher yiggâ bahem yikdash, "all (whether person or thing) that toucheth them shall be (or must be) holy; " that is, the priests must not eat of these oblations when under any ceremonial defilement, and the sacred utensils used about them must not be employed for any other purpose, or in any other way. \textsuperscript{20} the offering This oblation, which the Jews call a mincha of initiation, seems to have been required of the high priest alone "on the day in which he was anointed, " and from that time, every morning and evening, as long as he continued in office, and then in like manner of his successor; for, by "the sons of Aaron, " may be understood his descendants and successors in the high priesthood, in their generations.;, in the day The word beyom signifies not only in the day, but from that day forward; for it was a daily oblation, and for them and their successors, a statue forever. the tenth; a meat offering \textsuperscript{23} shall be The meat offering of the people was eaten by the priests, who typically bore and expiated their sins; but as no priest, being a sinner, could make atonement for himself, his meat offering must not be eaten, but wholly burnt on the altar, which was a typical transfer of his guilt to the great antitype who actually bore and expiated it. it shall not be \textsuperscript{25} the law, In the, it is \textsuperscript{26} priest; in the holy in the court\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 7}
\markright{LEVITICUS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This [is] the law of the sacrifice of peace-offering, which they shall bring to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If a man should offer it for praise, then shall he bring, for the sacrifice of praise, loaves of fine flour made up with oil, and unleavened cakes anointed with oil, and fine flour kneaded with oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} With leavened bread he shall offer his gifts, with the peace-offering of praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he shall bring one of all his gifts, a separate offering to the Lord: it shall belong to the priest who pours forth the blood of the peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the flesh of the sacrifice of the peace-offering of praise shall be his, and it shall be eaten in the day in which it is offered: they shall not leave of it till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if it be a vow, or he offer his gift of his own will, on whatever day he shall offer his sacrifice, it shall be eaten, and on the morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And that which is left of the flesh of the sacrifice till the third day, shall be consumed with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if he do at all eat of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for him that offers: it shall not be reckoned to him, it is pollution; and whatever soul shall eat of it, shall bear his iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And whatever flesh shall have touched any unclean thing, it shall not be eaten, it shall be consumed with fire; every one that is clean shall eat the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And whatever soul shall eat of the flesh of the sacrifice of the peace-offering which is the Lord's, and his uncleanness be upon him, that soul shall perish from his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And whatever soul shall touch any unclean thing, either of the uncleanness of a man, or of unclean quadrupeds, or any unclean abominable thing, and shall eat of the flesh of the sacrifice of the peace-offering, which is the Lord's, that soul shall perish from his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Speak to the children of Israel, saying, You⌃ shall eat no fat of oxen or sheep or goats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the fat of such animals as have died of themselves, or have been seized of beasts, may be employed for any work; but it shall not be eaten for food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Every one that eats fat off the beasts, from which he will bring a burnt offering to the Lord—that soul shall perish from his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You⌃ shall eat no blood in all your habitations, either of beasts or of birds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Every soul that shall eat blood, that soul shall perish from his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You shall also speak to the children of Israel, saying, He that offers a sacrifice of peace-offering, shall bring his gift to the Lord also from the sacrifice of peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} His hands shall bring the burnt offerings to the Lord; the fat which is on the breast and the lobe of the liver, he shall bring them, so as to set them for a gift before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the priest shall offer the fat upon the altar, and the breast shall be Aaron's and his sons, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and you⌃ shall give the right shoulder for a choice piece to the priest of your sacrifices of peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He that offers the blood of the peace-offering, and the fat, of the sons of Aaron, his shall be the right shoulder for a portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For I have taken the wave-breast and shoulder of separation from the children of Israel from the sacrifices of your peace-offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons, a perpetual ordinance [due] from the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} This is the anointing of Aaron, and the anointing of his sons, [their portion] of the burnt offerings of the Lord, in the day in which he brought them forward to minister as priests to the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} as the Lord commanded to give to them in the day in which he anointed them of the sons of Israel, a perpetual statute through their generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} This [is] the law of the whole burnt offerings, and of sacrifice, and of sin-offering, and of offering for transgression, and of the sacrifice of consecration, and of the sacrifice of peace-offering; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} as the Lord commanded Moses in the mount Sina, in the day in which he commanded the children of Israel to offer their gifts before the Lord in the wilderness of Sina.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: todah (תּוֹדָה) = thanksgiving; confession. Common English renderings: thanksgiving; praise. Often a thanksgiving offering or expression.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the law Lev. 5:1-6:7, ;, it is \textsuperscript{2} in the place, ; and the \textsuperscript{6} male; it is most holy \textsuperscript{8} even the priest All the flesh of the burnt offerings being consumed upon the altar, as well as the fat, there could nothing fall to the share of the priest but the skin; which must have been very valuable, as they were used as mattresses ( ), or as carpets to sit upon in the day. They are still used for the same purpose by some of the inhabitants and dervishes of the East. Bishop Patrick remarks, that Adam himself offered the first sacrifice, and had the skin given him by God, to make garments for him and his wife; in conformity with which, the priests ever after had the skin of the whole burnt offerings for their portion. skin \textsuperscript{9} the meat; in the pan or, on the flat plate, or slice, *marg. shall be \textsuperscript{16} be a vow;, ; a voluntary; also the \textsuperscript{18} it shall, ; be imputed; an abomination; bear \textsuperscript{21} the uncleanness, 12:1-13:59, ; any unclean;, abominable, ; cut off \textsuperscript{23} fat Any other fat they might eat; but the fat of these was sacred, because they were the only animals which were offered in sacrifice, though many others ranked among the clean animals as well as these. This prohibition may, however, be understood of these animals when offered in sacrifice, and then only in reference to the inward fat, described in . Of the fat in any other circumstances, it cannot be intended, as it was one of the especial blessings which God gave to his people - "Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, " were the provision which he graciously bestowed on his followers. (See note on .) \textsuperscript{26} ye shall eat The prohibition of the fat or suet, which was restricted to animals offered in sacrifice, taught reverence to the altar and ordinances of God; but that of blood, which was extended to all land animals, had especial respect to the atoning blood of the sacrifice, and of the great antitype which the sacrifice prefigured. \textsuperscript{27} that soul; shall be Shall be excommunicated or cut off from the people of God, and so deprived of any part of their inheritance or of their blessings.\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 8}
\markright{LEVITICUS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Take Aaron and his sons, and his robes and the anointing oil, and the calf for the sin-offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and assemble the whole congregation at the door of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses did as the Lord appointed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Moses said to the congregation, This is the thing which the Lord has commanded you to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses brought near Aaron and his sons, and washed them with water, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and put on him the coat, and girded him with the girdle, and clothed him with the tunic, and put on him the ephod; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and girded him [with a girdle] according to the make of the ephod, and clasped him closely with it: and put upon it the oracle, and put upon the oracle the Manifestation and the Truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he put the mitre on his head, and put upon the mitre in front the golden plate, the most holy thing, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses took of the anointing oil, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and sprinkled of it seven times on the altar; and anointed the altar, and hallowed it, and all things on it, and the laver, and its foot, and sanctified them; and anointed the tabernacle and all its furniture, and hallowed it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Moses poured of the anointing oil on the head of Aaron; and he anointed him and sanctified him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses brought the sons of Aaron near, and put on them coats and girded them with girdles, and put on them bonnets, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Moses brought near the calf for the sin-offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he killed it; and Moses took of the blood, and put it on the horns of the altar round about with his finger; and he purified the altar, and poured out the blood at the bottom of the altar, and sanctified it, to make atonement upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Moses took all the fat that was upon the inwards, and the lobe on the liver, and both the kidneys, and the fat that was upon them, and Moses offered them on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But the calf, and his hide, and his flesh, and his dung, he burnt with fire without the camp, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Moses brought near the ram for a whole burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram. And Moses killed the ram: and Moses poured the blood on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he divided the ram by its limbs, and Moses offered the head, and the limbs, and the fat; and he washed the belly and the feet with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar: it is a whole burnt offering for a sweet smelling savor; it is a burnt offering to the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses brought the second ram, the ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram, and [he] killed him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and Moses took of his blood, and put it upon the tip of Aaron's right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses brought near the sons of Aaron; and Moses put of the blood on the tips of their right ears, and on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the great toes of their right feet, and Moses poured out the blood on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he took the fat, and the rump, and the fat on the belly, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And from the basket of consecration, which was before the Lord, he also took one unleavened loaf, and one loaf made with oil, and one cake; and put [them] upon the fat, and the right shoulder: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and put them all on the hands of Aaron, and upon the hands of his sons, and offered them up for a wave-offering before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Moses took them at their hands, and Moses offered them on the altar, on the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a smell of sweet savor: it is a burnt offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Moses took the breast, and separated it for a heave-offering before the Lord, from the ram of consecration; and it became Moses' portion, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses took of the anointing oil, and of the blood that was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron, and on his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he sanctified Aaron and his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Moses said to Aaron and to his sons, Boil the flesh in the tent of the tabernacle of witness in the holy place; and there you⌃ shall eat it and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as it has been appointed me, [the Lord] saying, Aaron and his sons shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And that which is left of the flesh and of the loaves burn you⌃ with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And you⌃ shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle of witness for seven days, until the day be fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for in seven days shall he consecrate you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} as he did in this day on which the Lord commanded me to do so, to make an atonement for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And you⌃ shall remain seven days at the door of the tabernacle of witness, day and night; you⌃ shall observe the ordinances of the Lord, that you⌃ die not; for so has the Lord God commanded me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Aaron and his sons performed all these commands which the Lord commanded Moses.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} Lord commanded to be done \textsuperscript{7} he put, ; the ephod The ephod seems to have been a garment worn by persons of distinction of various characters ( ); the description of which in the book of Exodus (, etc.) relates only to its materials. As to its shape, the LXX calls it επωμις, which signifies that it was worn on the shoulders. So also Josephus, who says it was a cubit long. St. Jerome compares it with the Roman caracalla, which was a sort of short cloak, only that it had a head or hood, which the ephod had not. \textsuperscript{8} the breast plate, ; the Urim \textsuperscript{13} Moses, ; coats The kethoneth, or coat, was made of linen; but the form of it is no where described in Scripture, except in the visionary appearance of Christ to St. John, in the form and habit of a priest ( ); where he is said to be ενδεδυμενος ποδηρη, "clothed with a garment down to the feet, " which perfectly agrees with the description the Jewish writers give of it; who also say, that it had sleeves which came down to the wrist, and was tied about the neck; so that it was not unlike a long shirt. It was common to all the priests; but the tunic of the high priest was made of finer linen, or wove in a more curious manner ( ). put Heb. bound bonnets The migbaôth, or bonnets, are described by Josephus as being like helmets of linen, one wreath being plaited and folded over another and a thin cap, suited to its shape, put over all, to prevent its unfolding. \textsuperscript{15} he slew it, ; Moses, ; to make; The beginning of this verse may be rendered, "And Moses slew it, and took the blood, " etc. We find it expressly said in Exodus, that Moses slew the sacrifices.; Yet, in general, the offerer seems to have killed his own sacrifice. \textsuperscript{22} the ram of consecration, ; "The ram of consecration" was evidently a sacrifice of peace offering though presented on a particular occasion. Part of the blood was applied, not as that of the sin offering, to the horns of the altar, but to Aaron and his sons; to the tips of their right ears, the thumbs of their right hands, and the great toes of their right feet. Implying their obligation to hearken diligently to the word of God - to do his work in the best manner which they could, and to walk in his ways with steady perseverance; and also, that they could not do these things acceptably except through the atoning blood, received and applied by faith. Then part of the blood reserved upon the altar, probably in a basin for that purpose, was mingled with the holy anointing oil, and sprinkled on the garments both of Aaron and his sons, to hallow them to the Lord. "This may be looked upon as a lively representation of our purification by the blood of jesus Christ, through his Holy Spirit." - Bp. Patrick \textsuperscript{36} Aaron This was necessary to be added, to show the exact fulfilment of the commandments delivered to Moses, and which are recorded in; and consequently the complete consecration and preparation of Aaron and his sons to fill the awfully important office of priests and mediators between God and the children of Israel, to offer sacrifices, and make atonement for the sins of the people.\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 9}
\markright{LEVITICUS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and Moses said to Aaron, Take to yourself a young calf of the herd for a sin-offering, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and offer them before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And speak to the elders of Israel, saying, Take one kid of the goats for a sin-offering, and a young calf, and a lamb of a year old for a whole burnt offering, spotless, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and a calf and a ram for a peace offering before the Lord, and fine flour mingled with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they took as Moses commanded them before the tabernacle of witness, and all the congregation drew near, and they stood before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses said, This is the thing which the Lord has spoken; do [it], and the glory of the Lord shall appear among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses said to Aaron, Draw near to the altar, and offer your sin-offering, and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself, and for your house; and offer the gifts of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Aaron drew near to the altar, and killed the calf of his sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood, and put it on the horns of the altar, and he poured out the blood at the bottom of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he offered up on the altar the fat and the kidneys and the lobe of the liver of the sin-offering, according as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire outside of the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he killed the whole burnt offering; and the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he poured it on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they brought the whole burnt offering, according to its pieces; them and the head he put upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he washed the belly and the feet with water, and he put them on the whole burnt offering on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he brought the gift of the people, and took the goat of the sin-offering of the people, and killed it, and purified it as also the first. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he brought the whole burnt offering, and offered it in due form. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he brought the sacrifice and filled his hands with it, and laid it on the altar, besides the morning whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he killed the calf, and the ram of the sacrifice of peace-offering of the people; and the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he poured it out on the altar round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And [he took] the fat of the calf, and the hind quarters of the ram, and the fat covering the belly, and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them, and the caul on the liver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he put the fat on the breasts, and offered the fat on the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Aaron separated the breast and the right shoulder as a choice-offering before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Aaron lifted up his hands on the people and blessed them; and after he had offered the sin-offering, and the whole burnt offerings, and the peace-offerings, he came down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses and Aaron entered into the tabernacle of witness. And they came out and blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And fire came forth from the Lord, and devoured the offerings on the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fat; and all the people saw, and were amazed, and fell upon their faces.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the eighth day Not on the eighth day of the month, but on the first day after their consecration, which occupied seven days, and before which they were deemed unfit to minister in holy things, being considered in a state of imperfection. All creatures, for the most part, were considered as in a state of uncleanness and imperfection, seven days, and perfected on the eighth. (See note on; .) \textsuperscript{2} a young, ; , and a ram \textsuperscript{3} Take ye, ; a kid As the offering here is a kid, which was the sacrifice of the sin of the ruler, some think that the reading of the Samaritan and the LXX is to be preferred: "Speak unto the Elders of Israel." a calf both \textsuperscript{4} a bullock and a meat; to day \textsuperscript{10} the fat, ; as the Lord \textsuperscript{17} the meat; took an handful thereof Heb. filled his hand out of it, beside. \textsuperscript{21} the breasts, ; as Moses commanded The Samaritan text, and thirty manuscripts have, kaasher tzivvah yehowah eth Moshe, "as Jehovah commanded Moses; " which is also the reading of the LXX, Arabic, and Targum of Onkelos, and seems to be the true reading, being supported, not only by these authorities, but by the whole chapter itself. \textsuperscript{22} his hand or, as the Greek has it, "his hands", Menachem gives reason why it is written hand, to signify the right hand, because that was lifted up higher than the left. The lifting up of the hand was a gesture used in speaking, and signifying any weighty thing; and particularly in swearing; praying; and blessing, either of God, or of men, as in this place. Paul, speaking of prayer, uses the phrase, "lifting up holy hands; " as also David: "Let the lifting up of my hands be as the evening sacrifice." \textsuperscript{24} there came a fire These victims were consumed by a fire of no human kindling. Josephus says that "a fire proceeded from the victims themselves, of its own accord, which had the appearance of a flash of lightning, and consumed all that was upon the altar."; *marg. they shouted\par}
