\subsection*{Leviticus 17}
\markright{LEVITICUS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Every man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers dwelling among you, who shall kill a calf, or a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or who shall kill it out of the camp, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and shall not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of witness, so as to sacrifice it for a whole burnt offering or peace-offering to the Lord to be acceptable for a sweet smelling savor: and whoever shall kill it without, and shall not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of witness, so as to offer it as a gift to the Lord before the tabernacle of the Lord; blood shall be imputed to that man, he has shed blood; that soul shall be cut off from his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} That the children of Israel may offer their sacrifices, all that they shall kill in the fields, and bring them to the Lord to the doors of the tabernacle of witness to the priest, and they shall sacrifice them as a peace-offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priest shall pour the blood on the altar round about before the Lord by the doors of the tabernacle of witness, and shall offer the fat for a sweet smelling savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they shall no longer offer their sacrifices to vain [gods] after which they go a whoring; it shall be a perpetual statute to you for your generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall say to them, Whatever man of the children of Israel, or of the sons of the proselytes dwelling among you, shall offer a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and shall not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of witness to sacrifice it to the Lord, that man shall be destroyed from among his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And whatever man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers dwelling among you, shall eat any blood, I will even set my face against that soul that eats blood, and will destroy it from its people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the life of flesh is its blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for its blood shall make atonement for the soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore I said to the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood, and the stranger that abides among you shall not eat blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And whatever man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers dwelling among you shall take any animal in hunting, beast, or bird, which is eaten, then shall he pour out the blood, and cover it in the dust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the blood of all flesh is its life; and I said to the children of Israel, You⌃ shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood: every one that eats it shall be destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And every soul which eats that which has died of itself, or is taken of beasts, either among the natives or among the strangers, shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening: then shall he be clean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But if he do not wash his garments, and do not bathe his body in water, then shall he bear his iniquity.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} be of, that killeth an \textsuperscript{4} bringeth; , blood shall; he hath be cut off \textsuperscript{5} in the open, ; and offer them \textsuperscript{7} unto devils; devils Seirim, properly signifies hairy or hairy ones; and hence is used not only for he-goats, but also for some fabulous beings or sylvan gods, to whom was ascribed the form of goats. Maimonides says that the Zabian idolaters worshipped demons under the form of goats; and that this custom being spread among other nations, gave occasion to this precept. He-goats, however, are probably intended here, which were objects of divine honour among the Egyptians under the name of honour among the Egyptians under the name of Mendes. Herodotus says that all goats were worshipped in Egypt; but particularly he-goats. From these seem to have sprung Pan, Silenus, and the innumerable herd of those imaginary beings, fauns, satyrs, dryads, etc., all woodland gods, and held in veneration by the Greeks and Romans. gone a whoring Though this phrase is equivalent, in Scripture, to that of committing idolatry, yet it is to be taken sometimes in a literal sense. Baalpeor and Ashtaroth were worshipped with obscene rite; and public prostitution formed a great part of the worship among the Egyptians, Moabites, Canaanites, Greeks, and Romans. \textsuperscript{11} the life This sentence, which contains a most important truth, had existed in the Mosaic writings for more than 3, 000 years, before the attention of any philosopher was drawn to the subject. That the blood actually possesses a living principle, and that the life of the whole body is derived from it, is a doctrine of revelation, and a doctrine which the experiments of the most accurate anatomists have served strongly to confirm. The proper circulation of this important fluid through the whole human system was first taught by Solomon in figurative language ( ), and discovered, as it is called, and demonstrated by Dr. Harvey in 1628; though some Italian philosophers had the same notion a little before. This accurate anatomist was the first who fully revived the Mosaic notion of the vitality of the blood; which was afterwards adopted by the justly celebrated Dr. John Hunter, professor of anatomy, and established by him, by a great variety of strong reasoning and accurate experiments. \subsection*{Leviticus 18}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You⌃ shall not do according to the devices of Egypt, in which you⌃ lived: and according to the devices of the land of Chanaan, into which I bring you, you⌃ shall not do; and you⌃ shall not walk in their ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ shall observe my judgments, and shall keep my ordinances, and shall walk in them: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So you⌃ shall keep all my ordinances, and all my judgments, and do them; which if a man do, he shall live in them: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} No man shall draw near to any of his near kindred to uncover their nakedness; I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, or the nakedness of your mother, for she is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is your father's nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The nakedness of your sister by your father or by your mother, born at home or abroad, their nakedness you shall not uncover. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The nakedness of your son's daughter, or your daughter's daughter, their nakedness you shall not uncover; because it is your nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife; she is your sister by the same father: you shall not uncover her nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is near akin to your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is near akin to your mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, and you shall not go in to his wife; for she is your relation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, for she is your son's wife, you shall not uncover her nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife: it is your brother's nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The nakedness of a woman and her daughter shall you not uncover; her son's daughter, and her daughter's daughter, shall you not take, to uncover their nakedness, for they are your kinswomen: it is impiety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You shall not take a wife in addition to her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness in opposition to her, while she is yet living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall not go in to a woman under separation for her uncleanness, to uncover her nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you shall not lie with your neighbor's wife, to defile yourself with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you shall not give of your seed to serve a ruler; and you shall not profane my holy name; I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall not lie with a man as with a woman, for it is an abomination. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Neither shall you lie with any quadruped for copulation, to be polluted with it: neither shall a woman present herself before any quadruped to have connexion with it; for it is an abomination. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Do not defile yourselves with any of these things; for in all these things the nations are defiled, which I drive out before you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and the land is polluted; and I have recompensed their iniquity to them because of it, and the land is aggrieved with them that dwell upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you⌃ shall keep all my statutes and all my ordinances, and you⌃ shall do none of these abominations; neither the native, nor the stranger that joins himself with you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} (for all these abominations the men of the land did who were before you, and the land was defiled,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and lest the land be aggrieved with you in your polluting it, as it was aggrieved with the nations before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For whoever shall do any of these abominations, the souls that do them shall be destroyed from among their people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you⌃ shall keep my ordinances, that you⌃ may not do any of the abominable practices, which have taken place before your time: and you⌃ shall not be polluted in them; for I [am] the Lord your God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} which if a man do, ; I am the Lord \textsuperscript{6} near to kin Heb. remainder of his flesh. Notwithstanding the prohibitions here, it must be evident, that in the infancy of the world, persons very near of kin, and even brothers and sisters, must have joined in matrimonial alliances; and therefore we cannot pronounce them immoral in themselves. But, in these first instances, necessity required it; but when this necessity no longer existed, the thing became inexpedient and improper for: 1. As human nature now is, it is very expedient that those who are so much together in youth, should, by such a restriction be taught to look upon all such intercourse as prohibited and incestuous; for unless such restrictions are made, it would be impossible to prevent the prevalence of very early corruption among young persons. (See Michaelis on the laws of Moses, Art. 108.) 2. That the duties owing by nature to relatives might not be confounded with those of a social or political kind; for could a man be a brother and a husband, or a son and a husband at the same time, and fulfil the duties of both? Impossible. 3. That by intermarrying with other families, relationship and its endearments might be diffused. These prohibitions are, therefore, to be considered so eminently moral obligations as to be observed by all mankind. to uncover \textsuperscript{17} a woman; it is wickedness \textsuperscript{18} wife or, one wife to another, ; to vex her \textsuperscript{21} pass through Molech signifies a king, or governor, of similar import with Baal, lord, or governor; and it is generally supposed that the sun was worshipped under this name; and more particularly as the fire appears to have been so much employed in his worship. It seems clear that children were not only consecrated to him by passing through the fire, which appears to be alluded to here, but that they were actually made a burnt offering to him (see the parallel passages). That the several abominations afterwards mentioned were actually practised by many heathen nations is abundantly attested by their own writers.; to Molech; Moloch. profane \textsuperscript{30} abominable, ; that ye defile I am\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 19}
\markright{LEVITICUS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the congregation of the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, You⌃ shall be holy; for I the Lord your God [am] holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let every one of you reverence his father and his mother; and you⌃ shall keep my sabbaths: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ shall not follow idols, and you⌃ shall not make to yourselves molten gods: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if you⌃ will sacrifice a peace-offering to the Lord, you⌃ shall offer it acceptable from yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In what day soever you⌃ shall sacrifice it, it shall be eaten; and on the following day, and if any of it should be left till the third day, it shall be thoroughly burnt with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if it should be at all eaten on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice: it shall not be accepted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he that eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat it shall be destroyed from among their people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when you⌃ reap the harvest of your land, you⌃ shall not complete the reaping of your field with exactness, and you shall not gather that which falls from your reaping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall not go over the gathering of your vineyard, neither shall you gather the remaining grapes of your vineyard: you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You⌃ shall not steal, you⌃ shall not lie, neither shall one bear false witness as an informer against his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you⌃ shall not swear unjustly by my name, and you⌃ shall not profane the holy name of your God: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall not injure your neighbor, neither do you rob [him], neither shall the wages of your hireling remain with you until the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not revile the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block in the way of the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall not act unjustly in judgment: you shall not accept the person of the poor, nor admire the person of the mighty; with justice shall you judge your neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall not walk deceitfully among your people; you shall not rise up against the blood of your neighbor: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall not hate your brother in your heart: you shall in any wise rebuke your neighbor, so you shall not bear sin on his account. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And your hand shall not avenge you; and you shall not be angry with the children of your people; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You⌃ shall observe my law: you shall not let your cattle gender with one of a different kind, and you shall not sow your vineyard with diverse seed; and you shall not put upon yourself a mingled garment woven of two [materials]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if any one lie carnally with a woman, and she should be a home-servant kept for a man, and she has not been ransomed, [and] her freedom has not been given to her, they shall be visited [with punishment]; but they shall not die, because she was not set at liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he shall bring for his trespass to the Lord to the door of the tabernacle of witness, a ram for a trespass-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass-offering, before the Lord, for the sin which he sinned; and the sin which he sinned shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And whenever you⌃ shall enter into the land which the Lord your God gives you, and shall plant any fruit tree, then shall you⌃ purge away its uncleanness; its fruit shall be three years uncleansed to you, it shall not be eaten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a subject of praise to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And in the fifth year you⌃ shall eat the fruit, its produce is an increase to you. I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Eat not on the mountains, nor shall you⌃ employ auguries, nor divine by inspection of birds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} You⌃ shall not make a round cutting of the hair of your head, nor disfigure your beard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And you⌃ shall not make cuttings in your body for a [dead] body, and you⌃ shall not inscribe on yourselves any marks. I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} You shall not profane your daughter to prostitute her; so the land shall not go a whoring, and the land be filled with iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} You⌃ shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuaries: I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} You⌃ shall not attend to those who have in them divining spirits, nor attach yourselves to enchanters, to pollute yourselves with them: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} You shall rise up before the hoary head, and honor the face of the old man, and shall fear your God: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And if there should come to you a stranger in your land, you⌃ shall not afflict him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The stranger that comes to you shall be among you as the native, and you shall love him as yourself; for you⌃ were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} You⌃ shall not act unrighteously in judgment, in measures and weights and scales. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} There shall be among you just balances and just weights and just liquid measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And you⌃ shall keep all my law and all my ordinances, and you⌃ shall do them: I am the Lord your God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Heb. vocab: qatsar (קָצַר) = to reap. Common English renderings: reap. Harvest language often appears in law, narrative, and prophecy. \textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: kazav (כָּזָב) = lie; deception. Common English renderings: lie; falsehood. Near-synonym of שקר, often poetic. \textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: skandalon (σκάνδαλον) = stumbling block; snare. Common English renderings: offence; stumblingblock. A cause of stumbling, whether literal or moral. Gk. vocab: skandalizō (σκανδαλίζω) = to cause to stumble; offend. Common English renderings: offend. Represented here by its lexical form; tied to causing spiritual or moral stumbling. \textsuperscript{20} Gk. vocab: eleutheria (ἐλευθερία) = freedom; liberty. Common English renderings: liberty. A term for freedom or liberty.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} a sacrifice, ; ye shall, your own will The Hebrews had several kinds of offerings, which they called corban . Some were free-will offerings, and others were of obligation. The first fruits, the tenths, the sin-offerings, were of obligation; the peace-offerings, vows, offerings of oil, wine, bread, and other things which were made to the temple, or to the ministers of the Lord, were offerings of devotion; these constituted the greater part. They indeed were a shadow of good things to come, which we enjoy in full fruition through THE ONE great SACRIFICE, even Jesus Christ. "Aaron must lay his robes away, His mitre and his vest, When God himself comes down to be The offering and the priest." \textsuperscript{9} ye reap the harvest In what code of laws merely human, is a requisition to be found so counteracting to selfishness, so encouraging to liberality, and so beneficently considering to the poor and needy? But the Mosaic dispensation, like the Christian, breathed with love to God, and benevolence to man. To the honour of the public and charitable spirit of the English, this merciful law is, in general, as much attended to as if it had been incorporated with the gospel. \textsuperscript{17} hate;, rebuke; and not suffer sin upon him or, that thou bear not sin for him \textsuperscript{19} thy cattle gender These practices might have been considered as altering the original constitution of God in creation; and this is the view which the Jews, and also Josephus and Philo, take of the subject. There were, probably, also both moral and political reasons for these prohibitions. With respect to heterogenous mixtures among cattle, it was probably forbidden, to prevent excitements to the abominations condemned in the preceding chapter. As to seeds, in many cases, it would be highly improper to sow different kinds in the same plot of ground. If oats and wheat, for instance, were sown together, the latter would be injured, and the former ruined. This prohibition may therefore be regarded as a prudential agricultural maxim. As to different kinds of garments, the prohibition might be intended against pride and vanity in clothing.; mingled \textsuperscript{20} betrothed to an husband or, abused by any, Heb. reproached by, or, for man she shall be scourged or, they, Heb. there shall be a scourging. they shall. \textsuperscript{24} all the; holy to praise the Lord withal Heb. holiness of praises to the Lord \textsuperscript{26} with the blood, ; use; nor \textsuperscript{29} prostitute Heb. profane to cause \textsuperscript{33} And if; vex him or, oppress him \textsuperscript{36} Just balances weights Heb. stones I am\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 20}
\markright{LEVITICUS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You shall also say to the children of Israel, If [there shall be] any of the children of Israel, or of those who have become proselytes in Israel, who shall give of his seed to Moloch, let him be surely put to death; the nation upon the land shall stone him with stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will set my face against that man, and will cut him off from his people, because he has given of his seed to Moloch, to defile my sanctuary, and profane the name of them that are consecrated to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if the natives of the land should in anyway overlook that man in giving of his seed to Moloch, so as not to put him to death; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} then will I set my face against that man and his family, and I will destroy him, and all who have been of one mind with him, so that he should go a whoring to the princes, from their people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the soul that shall follow those who have in them divining spirits, or enchanters, so as to go a whoring after them; I will set my face against that soul, and will destroy it from among its people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you⌃ shall be holy, for I the Lord your God [am] holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you⌃ shall observe my ordinances, and do them: I [am] the Lord that sanctifies you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Every man who shall speak evil of his father or of his mother, let him die the death; has he spoken evil of his father or his mother? he shall be guilty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Whatever man shall commit adultery with the wife of a man, or whoever shall commit adultery with the wife of his neighbor, let them die the death, the adulterer and the adulteress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And if any one should lie with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness: let them both die the death, they are guilty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if any one should lie with his daughter-in-law, let them both be put to death; for they have wrought impiety, they are guilty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And whoever shall lie with a male as with a woman, they have both wrought abomination; let them die the death, they are guilty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whosoever shall take a woman and her mother, it is iniquity: they shall burn him and them with fire; so there shall not be iniquity among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And whoever shall lie with a beast, let him die the death; and you⌃ shall kill the beast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And whatever woman shall approach any beast, so as to have connexion with it, you⌃ shall kill the woman and the beast: let them die the death, they are guilty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Whosoever shall take his sister by his father or by his mother, and shall see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness, it is a reproach: they shall be destroyed before the children of their family; he has uncovered his sister's nakedness, they shall bear their sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And whatever man shall lie with a woman that is set apart [for a flux], and shall uncover her nakedness, he has uncovered her fountain, and she has uncovered the flux of her blood: they shall both be destroyed from among their generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, or of the sister of your mother; for that man has uncovered the nakedness of one near akin: they shall bear their iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whosoever shall lie with his near kinswoman, has uncovered the nakedness of one near akin to him: they shall die childless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Whoever shall take his brother's wife, it is uncleanness; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall die childless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And keep you⌃ all my ordinances, and my judgments; and you⌃ shall do them, and the land shall not be aggrieved with you, into which I bring you to dwell upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And walk you⌃ not in the customs of the nations which I drive out from before you; for they have done all these things, and I have abhorred them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and I said to you, You⌃ shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you for a possession, [even] a land flowing with milk and honey: I [am] the Lord your God, who have separated you from all people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you⌃ shall make a distinction between the clean and the unclean cattle, and between clean and unclean birds; and you⌃ shall not defile your souls with cattle, or with birds, or with any creeping things of the earth, which I have separated for you by reason of uncleanness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you⌃ shall be holy to me; because I the Lord your God [am] holy, who separated you from all nations, to be mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And [as for] a man or woman whoever of them shall have in them a divining spirit, or be an enchanter, let them both die the death: you⌃ shall stone them with stones, they are guilty.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Whosoever, giveth; , ; Moloch. Molech The Rabbins describe this idol as made of brass sitting upon a throne of the same metal, in the form of a man, with the head of a calf, adorned with a royal crown, and his arms extended as if to embrace any one. When they offered any children to him, they heated the statue by a great fire kindled within, and the victim was put into his arms, and thus consumed. Others relate, that the idol, which was hollow, was divided into seven compartments within; in one of which they put flour, in the second turtles, in the third a ewe, in the fourth a ram, in the fifth a calf, in the sixth an ox, and the seventh a child; which were all burnt together by heating the statue inside. The account which Diodorus (l. xx.) gives of the statue of Saturn, to which the Carthaginians, descendants of the Canaanites, sacrificed their children, is very similar. For they had a brazen stature of Saturn, stretching out his hands towards the ground, in such a manner that the children placed within them tumbled down into a pit full of fire. To this account Milton alludes, in Paradise Lost, B. 1. 392. the people \textsuperscript{3} I will set; to defile; profane \textsuperscript{5} I will against his; whoring \textsuperscript{6} familiar, ; go; cut him; In the days of Moses, superstition was almost the sensus communis of the human race, which then made severe punishment necessary. By means of the Christian dispensation such errors are now exploded, the cultivation of philosophy and natural history having harmonised and contributed their feebler share of light, so that we no longer have to deplore mischiefs occasioned by the silly curiosity attempting to unfold future events. \textsuperscript{9} curseth The term yekallel signifies not only to curse, but to speak contemptuously, disrespectfully, or to make light of a person, so that all speeches which have a tendency to lessen our parents in the eyes of others, or to render their judgment, piety, etc., suspected or contemptible, is here included; though the act of cursing, or of treating the parent with injurious or opprobrious language, is what is particularly intended. He who conscientiously keeps the fifth commandment, can be in no danger of the judgment here denounced.; his blood \textsuperscript{16} And if a woman We are assured by Herodotus (in Euterp) that the abominations here referred to existed among the Egyptians, and even formed part of their superstitious religious system, and we have reason to believe that they were not uncommon among the Canaanites. (See note on ). Need we wonder then, that God should have made laws of this nature, and appointed the punishment of death for these crimes? This one observation will account for many of those strange prohibitions which we find in the Mosaic law. and the beast \textsuperscript{18} having; discovered Heb. made naked \textsuperscript{21} his brother's; an unclean thing Heb. a separation \textsuperscript{24} But I, a land Milk and honey were the chief dainties of the ancients as they are now among the Arabs, particularly the Bedouins. Hence not only the Hebrews, but also the Greeks and Romans, painted the highest pleasantness and fertility by an abundance of milk and honey. The image used in the text, and frequently by ancient authors on similar subjects, is a metaphor, derived from a breast, producing copious streams of milk. which \textsuperscript{25} put difference; abominable creepeth or, moveth\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 21}
\markright{LEVITICUS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the priests the sons of Aaron, and you shall tell them [that] they shall not defile themselves in their nation for the dead, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} but [they may mourn] for a relative who is very near to them, for a father and mother, and sons and daughters, for a brother, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and for a virgin sister that is near to one, that is not espoused to a man; for these one shall defile himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He shall not defile himself suddenly among his people to profane himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you⌃ shall not shave your head for the dead with a baldness on the top; and they shall not shave their beard, neither shall they make gashes on their flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God; for they offer the sacrifices of the Lord as the gifts of their God, and they shall be holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They shall not take a woman who is a harlot and profaned, or a woman put away from her husband; for he is holy to the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall hallow him; he offers the gifts of the Lord your God: he shall be holy, for I the Lord that sanctify them [am] holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if the daughter of a priest should be profaned to go a whoring, she profanes the name of her father: she shall be burnt with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the priest that is chief among his brethren, the oil having been poured upon the head of the anointed one, and he having been consecrated to put on the garments, shall not take the mitre off his head, and shall not rend his garments: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} neither shall he go in to any dead body, neither shall he defile himself for his father or his mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he shall not go forth out of the sanctuary, and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, because the holy anointing oil of God [is] upon him: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He shall take for a wife a virgin of his own tribe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But a widow, or one that is put away, or profaned, or a harlot, these he shall not take; but he shall take for a wife a virgin of his own people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he shall not profane his seed among his people: I [am] the Lord that sanctifies him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Say to Aaron, A man of your tribe throughout your generations, who shall have a blemish on him, shall not draw near to offer the gifts of his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} No man who has a blemish on him shall draw near; a man blind, lame, with his nose disfigured, or his ears cut, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} a man who has a broken hand or a broken foot, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} or humpbacked, or blear-eyed, or that has lost his eye-lashes, or a man who has a malignant ulcer, or tetter, or one that has lost a testicle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Whoever of the seed of Aaron the priest has a blemish on him, shall not draw near to offer sacrifices to your God, because he has a blemish on him; he shall not draw near to offer the gifts of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The gifts of God [are] most holy, and he shall eat of the holy things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Only he shall not approach the veil, and he shall not draw near to the altar, because he has a blemish; and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, for I am the Lord that sanctifies them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{8} Gk. vocab: hagiasmos (ἁγιασμός) = sanctification; holiness. Common English renderings: sanctification. Denotes consecration and holy setting apart.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} Or, the verse may be read, being an husband among his people, he shall not defile himself for his wife, etc. \textsuperscript{5} not make baldness This custom is also called rounding the corners of the head ( ), and seems to have been performed in honour of some idol.; the corner The Hebrew peath zakon, may denote the whiskers; as the Syriac phatho signifies. These are by the Arabs, according to Niebuhr, still cut entirely off, or worn quite short; and hence they are called by Jeremiah, χφεφι τΰδ, those with cropped whiskers. Perhaps some superstition, of which we are ignorant, was connected with this; but whether or not, it was the object of Moses to keep the Israelites distinct from other nations. \textsuperscript{7} that is a whore; put away \textsuperscript{9} the daughter, ; she shall be burnt \textsuperscript{10} upon, ; consecrated; uncover; not rend; All human corpses were considered as unclean. Whoever touched one was unclean for seven days, and was obliged on the third and seventh day to purify himself according to the Mosaic instructions. In the case of the priest it went still farther; insomuch, that even mourning for the dead by any external sign, such as tearing their clothes, defiled them. Hence such mournings were absolutely forbidden to be used in any case, and by the other priests also, except in the case of their very nearest relations, for whom they were allowed to mourn. This statue is founded on the importance of sustaining the decency and purity of Divine worship. The servants of the Deity were to keep themselves at a distance from every thing that in the least degree savoured of uncleanness. \textsuperscript{12} go out for the crown \textsuperscript{17} blemish; let him; bread or, food \textsuperscript{20} a dwarf or, too slender or hath \textsuperscript{21} a blemish In the above list of blemishes, we meet with some that might render the priest contemptible in the eyes of men; and others that would be very great impediments in the discharge of his ministerial duties. to offer \textsuperscript{22} both, ; and of the holy \textsuperscript{23} go in; profane, for I the Lord\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and let them take heed concerning the holy things of the children of Israel, so they shall not profane my holy name in any of the things which they consecrate to me: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Say to them, Every man throughout your generations, whoever of all your seed shall approach to the holy things, whatever the children of Israel shall consecrate to the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be cut off from me: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the man of the seed of Aaron the priest, if he should have leprosy or issue of the reins, shall not eat of the holy things, until he be cleansed; and he that touches any uncleanness of a dead body, or the man whose seed of copulation shall have gone out from him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} or whoever shall touch any unclean reptile, which will defile him, or [who shall touch] a man, whereby he shall defile him according are his bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He shall not eat that which dies of itself, or is taken of beasts, so that he should be polluted by them: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they shall keep my ordinances, that they do not bear iniquity because of them, and die because of them, if they shall profane them: I [am] the Lord God that sanctifies them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And no stranger shall eat the holy things: one that sojourns with a priest, or a hireling, shall not eat the holy things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But if a priest should have a soul purchased for money, he shall eat of his bread; and they that are born in his house, they also shall eat of his bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if the daughter of a priest should marry a stranger, she shall not eat of the offerings of the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if the daughter of priest should be a widow, or put away, and have no seed, she shall return to her father's house, as in her youth: she shall eat of her father's bread, but no stranger shall eat of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the man who shall ignorantly eat holy things, shall add the fifth part to it, and give the holy thing to the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So should they bring upon themselves the iniquity of trespass in their eating their holy things: for I [am] the Lord that sanctifies them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say to them, Any man of the children of {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{40} Heb. vocab: samach (שָׂמַח) = to rejoice. Common English renderings: rejoice; be glad. Joy term with celebratory and covenantal resonance.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the feasts God appointed several festivals among the Jews. The Passover was celebrated on the 14th, or rather 15th day of the first month in the ecclesiastical year, which was the seventh of the civil year, and lasted seven days. The Pentecost was celebrated on the fiftieth day after the passover, in memory of the law's being given to Moses on Mount Sinai, fifty days, or seven weeks after the departure out of Egypt. The word is derived from the Greek word Πεντηκοστη, which signifies the fiftieth. The Hebrews call it the feast of weeks, . The feast of trumpets, celebrated on the first day of the civil year, when a trumpet was sounded, to proclaim its commencement, which was in the month Tisri, answering to our September, . The new moons, or first days of every month, were, in some sort, a consequence of the feast of trumpets. God ordained that, by giving him the first-fruits of every month they should acknowledge him as the Lord of all their time, and own his providence, by which all times and seasons are ordered. The feast of expiation or atonement was kept on the 10th day of Tisri or September: the Hebrews call it Kippur, i.e., pardon or expiation, because it was instituted for the expiation of their sins. The feast of tents or tabernacles was so called, because the Israelites kept it under green tents or arbours, in memory of their dwelling in their passage through the wilderness. It was celebrated on the 15th day of Tisri, and continued eight days. The first and last days are the most solemn. Besides the feasts mentioned by Moses, we find the feast of lots, or Purim, which was celebrated among the Jews of Shushan on the 14th of Adar, which answers to our February. The feast of the dedication of the temple, or rather, of the restoration of the temple, which had been profaned by Antiochus Epiphanes, which is thought to be the feast mentioned in the gospel, was celebrated in the winter. Moâdim, properly means assemblies, convened at an appointed time and place.; proclaim \textsuperscript{10} When and shall;, ; sheaf or, handful, Heb. omer, the first fruits, This offering was a public acknowledgment of the bounty and goodness of God for the kindly fruits of the earth. From the practice of the people of God, the heathen borrowed a similar one, founded on the same reason. \textsuperscript{13} the meat; the drink;, the fourth \textsuperscript{17} two wave leaven; the firstfruits \textsuperscript{22} To the institution of the feast of pentecost is annexed a repetition of that law, by which they were required to leave the gleanings of their fields, and the corn that grew on the ends of the butts, for the poor. It may come in here as a thing which the priests must take occasion to remind the people of, when they brought their first-fruits, intimating to them, that to obey even in this small matter was better than sacrifice; and that unless they were obedient, their offerings should not be accepted. It also taught them that the joy of harvest should express itself in charity to the poor, who must have their due out of what we have, as well as God his. They that are truly sensible of the mercy they receive from God, will without grudging shew mercy to the poor. \textsuperscript{24} In the seventh; a memorial Zichron terooâh, here rendered "a memorial of blowing the trumpets" properly signifies a memorial of triumph or shouting for joy. This festival is generally called the feast of trumpets; and, though the Scriptures have not expressly declared the reason of its celebration, yet, as it fell in the seventh month of the sacred year, which was the first of the civil year, that is, the month Tisri, answering to our September, the opinion very generally embraced by both Jews and Christians is, that it was a memorial of the creation of the world, at which "the sons of God shouted for joy, " ( ); and which is supposed, not altogether without reason, to have been at this season of the year. The month Tisri was not only anciently, but still is, reckoned by the Jews the first month of the year; and the feast of tabernacles, kept in this month, was said to be, as it is correctly rendered in the margin, "at the revolution of the year, " ( ); importing, that at this season the year had revolved, and was beginning anew. So that this feast was the new year's day, on which the people rejoiced in a grateful remembrance of God's benefits, and implored his blessing for the future year. \textsuperscript{29} that shall; he shall be \textsuperscript{32} a sabbath; afflict;, ; celebrate your sabbath Heb. rest \textsuperscript{34} The fifteenth; the feast of tabernacles This feast was celebrated in commemoration of the Israelites' dwelling in tents in the wilderness for forty years; and was kept with greater hilarity than any of the other festivals. Hence, in the Talmud, it is often called chag, the feast, by way of excellence; and by Philo, εορτων μεγιστην, the greatest of the feasts; it was therefore more noticed by the heathen than any other. It is probable that Cecrops borrowed from it the law which he made in Athens, "that the master of every family should after harvest make a feast for his servants, and eat together with them who had taken pains with him in tilling his grounds." \textsuperscript{36} Seven the eighth; solemn Heb. day of restraint; *marg. \textsuperscript{40} the boughs Heb. fruit; of palm trees; rejoice\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 24}
\markright{LEVITICUS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Charge the children of Israel, and let them take for you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to burn a lamp continually, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} outside the veil in the tabernacle of witness; and Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord continually, a perpetual statute throughout your generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ shall burn the lamps on the pure lamp-stand before the Lord till the morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you⌃ shall take fine flour, and make of it twelve loaves; each loaf shall be of two tenth parts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall put them [in] two rows, each row [containing] six loaves, on the pure table before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you⌃ shall put on [each] row pure frankincense and salt; and [these things] shall be for loaves for a memorial, set forth before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} On the sabbath-day they shall be set forth before the Lord continually before the children of Israel, for an everlasting covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat them in the holy place: for this is their most holy portion of the offerings made to the Lord, a perpetual statute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And there went forth a son of an Israelitish woman, and he was son of an Egyptian man among the sons of Israel; and they fought in the camp, the son of the Israelitish woman, and a man who was an Israelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the son of the Israelitish woman named THE NAME and curse; and they brought him to Moses: and his mother's name was Salomith, daughter of Dabri of the tribe of Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they put him in ward, to judge him by the command of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Bring forth him that cursed outside the camp, and all who heard shall lay their hands upon his head, and all the congregation shall stone him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, Whosoever shall curse God shall bear his sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he that names the name of the Lord, let him die the death: let all the congregation of Israel stone him with stones; whether he be a stranger or a native, let him die for naming the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And whoever shall strike a man and he die, let him die the death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And whoever shall strike a beast, and it shall die, let him render life for life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And whoever shall inflict a blemish on his neighbor, as he has done to him, so shall it be done to himself in return; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} bruise for bruise, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as any one may inflict a blemish on a man, so shall it be rendered to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Whosoever shall strike a man, and he shall die, let him die the death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} There shall be one judgment for the stranger and the native, for I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and they brought him that had cursed out of the camp, and stoned him with stones: and the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: blasphēmia (βλασφημία) = blasphemy; slander. Common English renderings: blasphemy. Against God it is blasphemy; against people it can be slander.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} that they, ; the lamps; , ; burn continually Heb. ascend \textsuperscript{5} The loaves of bread which the officiating priest placed every sabbath day upon the golden table in the Sanctum, before the Lord, were twelve in number, representing the twelve tribes of Israel. The loaves must have been large, since two tenth deals (about six pints) of flour were used for each, . They were served up hot on the sabbath day in the Sanctum, when the stale ones, which had been exposed the whole week, were taken away, and none but the priests were allowed to eat them. In an extraordinary extremity, David and his men partook of the shew-bread (see note on ), the urgent necessity alone justifying the act. The Hebrew signifies bread of faces, or, of the face. \textsuperscript{7} pure; the bread, a memorial \textsuperscript{11} blasphemed; , ; the name Houbigant and others think that the name which this man blasphemed was the name of the god of his native land. But that hashshem THE NAME, denotes Jehovah, appears from its being used in the latter part of, as equivalent to "the name of Jehovah, " in the former part. The Jews also frequently use hashshem for Jehovah. cursed, ; brought him \textsuperscript{12} that the mind of the Lord might be showed them Heb. to expound unto them according to the mouth of the Lord \textsuperscript{14} without; all that, let all the \textsuperscript{16} blasphemeth As the word nakav not only signifies to curse, or blaspheme, but also to express, or distinguish by name ( . . ), hence the Jews, at a very early period, understood this law as prohibiting them from uttering the name Jehovah, on any other than sacred occasions. The Septuagint, which was made at least 250 years before Christ, renders it Ονομαζων δε το ονομα Κυριου, θανατω θανατουσθω, "Whosoever nameth the name of the Lord, let him die; " from which we see that the Jews at this time were accustomed to pronounce adonay, or Lord, instead of Jehovah; for in place of it the Septuagint always put ο Κυριος . \textsuperscript{17} And he; killeth any man Heb. smiteth the life of a man \textsuperscript{18} that killeth; beast for beast Heb. life for life\par}

\subsection*{Leviticus 25}
\markright{LEVITICUS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses in the mount Sina, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, Whenever you⌃ shall have entered into the land, which I give to you, then the land shall rest which I give to you, for its sabbaths to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vine, and gather in its fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But in the seventh year [shall be] a sabbath, it shall be a rest to the land, a sabbath to the Lord: you shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall not gather the spontaneous produce of your field, and you shall not gather fully the grapes of your dedication: it shall be a year of rest to the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the sabbaths of the land shall be food for you, and for your man-servant, and for your maidservant, and your hireling, and the stranger that abides with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And for your cattle, and for the wild beats that are in your land, shall every fruit of it be for food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall reckon to yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years; and they shall be to you seven weeks of years, nine and forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you⌃ shall make a proclamation with the sound of a trumpet in all your land; on the day of atonement you⌃ shall make a proclamation with a trumpet in all your land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you⌃ shall sanctify the year, the fifties year, and you⌃ shall proclaim a release upon the land to all that inhabit it; it shall be given a year of release, a jubilee for you; and each one shall depart to his possession, and you⌃ shall go each to his family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} This is a jubilee of release, the year shall be to you the fifties year: you⌃ shall not sow, nor reap the produce that comes of itself from the land, neither shall you⌃ gather its dedicated fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For it is a jubilee of release; it shall be holy to you, you⌃ shall eat its fruits off the fields. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} In the year of the release [even] the jubilee of it, shall [each] one return to his possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if you should sell a possession to your neighbor, or if you should buy of your neighbor, let not a man oppress his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} According to the number of years after the jubilee shall you buy of your neighbor, according to the number of years of the fruits shall he sell to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} According as [there may be] a greater number of years he shall increase [the value of] his possession, and according as [there may be] a less number of years he shall lessen [the value of] his possession; for according to the number of his crops, so shall he sell to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let not a man oppress his neighbor, and you shall fear the Lord your God: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you⌃ shall keep all my ordinances, and all my judgments; and do you⌃ observe them, and you⌃ shall keep them, and dwell securely in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the land shall yield her increase, and you⌃ shall eat to fullness, and shall dwell securely in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if you⌃ should say, What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we do not sow nor gather in our fruits? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then will I send my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and the land shall produce its fruits for three years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you⌃ shall sow in the eighth year, and eat old fruits till the ninth year: until its fruit come, you⌃ shall eat old fruits of the old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the land shall not be sold for a permanence; for the land is mine, because you⌃ are strangers and sojourners before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And in every land of your possession, you⌃ shall allow ransoms for the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if your brother who is with you be poor, and should have sold [part] of his possession, and his kinsman who is near to him come, then he shall redeem the possession which his brother has sold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if one have no near kinsman, and he prosper with his hand, and he find sufficient money, [even] his ransom; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} then shall he calculate the years of his sale, and he shall give what is due to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall return to his possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if his hand have not prospered sufficiently, so as that he should restore the money to him, then he that bought the possessions shall have them till the sixth year of the release; and it shall go out in the release, and the owner shall return to his possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And if any one should sell an inhabited house in a walled city, then there shall be the ransom of it, until [the time] is fulfilled: its time of ransom shall be a full year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And if it be not ransomed until there be completed of its time a full year, the house which is in the walled city shall be surely confirmed to him that bought it, throughout his generations; and it shall not go out in the release. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But the houses in the villages which have not a wall round about them, shall be reckoned as the fields of the country: they shall always be redeemable, and they shall go out in the release. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities in their possession, shall be always redeemable to the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And if any one shall redeem a house of the Levites, then shall their sale of the houses of their possession go out in the release; because the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the lands set apart for their cities shall not be sold, because this is their perpetual possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And if your brother who is with you become poor, and he fail in resources with you, you shall help him as a stranger and a sojourner, and your brother shall live with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} You shall not receive from him interest, nor increase: and you shall fear your God: I [am] the Lord: and your brother shall live with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} You shall not lend your money to him at interest, and you shall not lend your meat to him to be returned with increase. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} I [am] the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Chanaan, so as to be your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And if your brother by you be lowered, and be sold to you, he shall not serve you with the servitude of a slave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} He shall be with you as a hireling or a sojourner, he shall work for you till the year of release: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} and he shall go out in the release, and his children with him; and he shall go to his family, he shall hasten back to his patrimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Because these are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; such an one shall not be sold as a [common] servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} You shall not oppress him with labor, and shall fear the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And whatever number of menservants and maidservants you shall have, you shall purchase male and female servants from the nations that are round about you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And of the sons of the sojourners that are among you, of these you⌃ shall buy and of their relations, all that shall be in your lands; let them be to you for a possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And you⌃ shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be to you permanent possessions for ever: but of your brethren the children of Israel, one shall not oppress his brother in labors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And if a stranger or sojourner with you wax rich, and your brother in distress be sold to the stranger or the sojourner that is with you, or to a proselyte by extraction; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} after he is sold to him there shall be redemption for him, one of his brethren shall redeem him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} A brother of his father, or a son of his father's brother shall redeem him; or let one of his near kin of his tribe redeem him, and if he should be rich and redeem himself, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} then shall he calculate with his purchaser from the year that he sold himself to him until the year of release: and the money of his purchase shall be as that of a hireling, he shall be with him from year to year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And if any have a greater number of years [than enough], according to these he shall pay his ransom out of his purchase-money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And if but a little time be left of the years to the year of release, then shall he reckon to him according to his years, and shall pay his ransom {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} as a hireling; he shall be with him from year to year; you shall not oppress him with labor before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And if he do not pay his ransom accordingly, he shall go out in the year of his release, he and his children with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} For the children of Israel are my servants: they are my attendants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{10} Gk. vocab: aphesis (ἄφεσις) = release; forgiveness. Common English renderings: remission; forgiveness. The term can mean release from debt or bondage and forgiveness of sins.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} When ye; keep Heb. rest, *marg. a sabbath \textsuperscript{5} groweth; thy vine undressed Heb. the separation \textsuperscript{9} jubilee, ; of the jubilee to sound Heb. loud of sound; the day \textsuperscript{10} proclaim; , ; every man, ye shall return \textsuperscript{11} A jubilee Respecting the literal meaning of the word ιεαμ, yobel, or yovel, critics are not agreed. The most natural derivation of the word seems to be from δεαιμ, hovil, the Hiphil form of ιαμ, yaval, to recall, restore, or bring back, because this year restored all slaves to their liberty, and brought back all alienated estates to their primitive owners. Accordingly the LXX render it here αφεσις, a "remission"; and Josephus says it signifies ελευθεριαν, liberty. ye shall \textsuperscript{21} I will As it is here graciously promised, that the sixth year was to bring forth fruits for three years, not merely for two, it is evident that both the sabbatical year and the year of jubilee were distinctly provided for. They were not to sow from the sixth to the eighth year, omitting two seed times; nor reap from the sixth to the ninth, omitting two harvests. No legislator, unless conscious of being divinely commissioned, would have committed himself by enacting such a law as this; nor would any people have submitted to receive it, except in consequence of the fullest conviction that a divine authority had dictated it. It therefore stands as a proof that Moses acted by the express direction of the Almighty, and that the people were fully persuaded of the reality of his divine mission by the miracles he wrought.; three years \textsuperscript{23} The land; for ever or, to be quite cut off, Heb. for cutting off, for the land.; for ye are \textsuperscript{26} himself be able to redeem it Heb. his hand hath attained, and found sufficiency, *marg. \textsuperscript{28} and in the he shall \textsuperscript{29} A very proper difference is here made between houses in a city and houses in the country. The former might be redeemed any time in the course of a year; but after that time could not be redeemed, or go out with the Jubilee. The latter might be redeemed at any time; and if not redeemed must go out with the jubilee. The reason in both cases is sufficiently evident; the house in the city might be built merely for the purposes of trade or traffic - the house in the country was builded on, or attached to, the inheritance which God had divided to the respective families. It was therefore necessary that the same law should apply to the house as to the inheritance; which necessity did not exist with regard to the house in the city. And, as the house in the city might be purchased for the purpose of trade, it would be very inconvenient for the purchaser, when his business was established, to be obliged to remove. \textsuperscript{31} they may be redeemed Heb. redemption belongeth unto it \textsuperscript{32} the cities As the Levites had no inheritance in Israel, but only cities to dwell in; and consequently the houses in these cities were all they could call their own, therefore they could not be ultimately alienated. \textsuperscript{33} a man purchase of the Levites or, one of the Levites redeem them shall go for the houses \textsuperscript{35} thy brother; fallen in decay Heb. his hand faileth then, ; relieve Heb. strengthen a stranger \textsuperscript{39} be sold; compel him to serve as Heb. serve thyself with him with the service of, etc. *marg. \textsuperscript{42} my servants; as bondmen Heb. with the sale of a bondman \textsuperscript{46} And ye shall they shall be your bondmen for ever Heb. ye shall serve yourselves with them, ye shall not rule \textsuperscript{47} sojourner or stranger wax rich Heb. the hand of a stranger, etc. obtain, etc. \textsuperscript{50} reckon price of his sale This was a very equitable law, both to the sojourner to whom the man was sold, and to the Israelite who had been sold. The Israelite might redeem himself, or one of his kindred might redeem him; but this must not be done to the prejudice of his master. They were therefore to reckon the years he must have served, from that time till the jubilee; and then taking the current wages of a servant, per year, at that time, multiply the remaining years by that sum, and the aggregate was to be given to his master for his redemption. The Jews hold that the kindred of such a person were bound, if in their power, to redeem him, lest he should be swallowed up among the heathen; and we find ( ) that this was done by the Jews on their return from the Babylonish captivity. according to the time \textsuperscript{52} jubilee The jubilee was a wonderful institution, and of great service to the religion, freedom, and independence of the Hebrews. It was calculated to prevent the rich from oppressing the poor, and reducing them to perpetual slavery; and to hinder their obtaining possession of all the lands by purchase, mortgage, or usurpation. It was further intended, that debts should not be multiplied too much, lest the poor should be entirely ruined; that slaves should not always continue in servitude; that personal liberty, equality of property, and the regular order of families might, as much as possible, be preserved; and that the people might thus be strongly attached to their country, lands, and inheritances. \textsuperscript{54} in these years or, by these means then\par}
