\subsection*{Leviticus 26}
\markright{LEVITICUS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I [am] the Lord your God: you⌃ shall not make to yourselves gods made with hands, or graven; neither shall you⌃ rear up a pillar for yourselves, neither shall you⌃ set up a stone [for] an object in your land to worship it: I am the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You⌃ shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuaries: I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If you⌃ will walk in my ordinances, and keep my commandments, and do them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} then will I give you the rain in its season, and the land shall produce its fruits, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And your threshing time shall overtake the vintage, and your vintage shall overtake your seed time; and you⌃ shall eat your bread to the full; and you⌃ shall dwell safely upon your land, and war shall not go through your land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will give peace in your land, and you⌃ shall sleep, and none [shall] make you afraid; and I will destroy the evil beasts out of your land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and you⌃ shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you with slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And five of you shall chase one hundred, and one hundred of you shall chase tens of thousands; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will look upon you, and increase you, and multiply you, and establish my covenant with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you⌃ shall eat that which is old and very old, and bring forth the old to make way for the new. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will set my tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not abhor you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and I will walk among you, and be your God, and you⌃ shall be my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, where you⌃ were slaves; and I broke the band of your yoke, and brought you forth openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But if you⌃ will not listen to me, nor obey these my ordinances, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} but disobey them, and your soul should loathe my judgments, so that you⌃ should not keep all my commands, so as to break my covenant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} then will I do thus to you: I will even bring upon you perplexity and the itch, and the fever that causes your eyes to waste away, and [disease] that consumes your life; and you⌃ shall sow your seeds in vain, and your enemies shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I will set my face against you, and you⌃ shall fall before your enemies, and they that hate you shall pursue you; and you⌃ shall flee, no one pursuing you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if you⌃ still refuse to listen to me, then will I chasten you yet more even seven times for your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And I will break down the haughtiness of your pride; and I will make your heaven iron, and your earth as it were brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And your strength shall be in vain; and your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if after this you⌃ should walk perversely, and not be willing to obey me, I will further bring upon you seven plagues according to your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will send upon you the wild beasts of the land, and they shall devour you, and shall consume your cattle: and I will make you few in number, and your ways shall be desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And if hereupon you⌃ are not corrected, but walk perversely towards me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} I also will walk with you with a perverse spirit, and I also will strike you seven times for your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I will bring upon you a sword avenging the cause of [my] covenant, and you⌃ shall flee for refuge to your cities; and I will send out death against you, and you⌃ shall be delivered into the hands of your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} When I afflict you with famine of bread, then ten women shall bake your loaves in one oven, and they shall render your loaves by weight; and you⌃ shall eat, and not be satisfied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And if hereupon you⌃ will not obey me, but walk perversely towards me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} then will I walk with you with a froward mind, and I will chasten you sevenfold according to your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you⌃ shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters shall you⌃ eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And I will render your pillars desolate, and will utterly destroy your wooden [images] made with hands; and I will lay your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols, and my soul shall loathe you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And I will lay your cities waste, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell the savor of your sacrifices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And I will lay your land desolate, and your enemies who dwell in it shall wonder at it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword shall come upon you and consume you; and your land shall be desolate, and your cities shall be desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Then the land shall enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And you⌃ shall be in the land of your enemies; then the land shall keep its sabbaths, and the land shall enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation: it shall keep sabbaths which it kept not among your sabbaths, when you⌃ lived in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And to those who are left of you I will bring bondage into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from war, and shall fall when none pursues them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And brother shall disregard brother as in war, when none pursues; and you⌃ shall not be able to withstand your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And you⌃ shall perish among the Gentiles, and the land of your enemies shall devour you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And those who are left of you shall perish, because of their sins, and because of the sins of their fathers: in the land of their enemies shall they consume away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And they shall confess their sins, and the sins of their fathers, that they have transgressed and neglected me, and that they have walked perversely before me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} and I walked with them with a perverse mind; and I will destroy them in the land of their enemies: then shall their uncircumcised heart be ashamed, and then shall they acquiesce in [the punishment of] their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And I will remember the covenant of Jacob, and the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraam will I remember. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And I will remember the land, and the land shall be left of them; then the land shall enjoy her sabbaths, when it is deserted through them: and they shall accept [the punishment of] their iniquities, because they neglected my judgments, and in their soul loathed my ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And yet not even thus, while they were in the land of their enemies, did I overlook them, nor did I loathe them so as to consume them, to break my covenant made with them; for I am the Lord their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And I will remember their former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage before the nation, to be their God; I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} These are my judgments and my ordinances, and the law which the Lord gave between himself and the children of Israel, in the mount Sina, by the hand of Moses.\par

\subsection*{Leviticus 27}
\markright{LEVITICUS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, Whosoever shall vow a vow as the valuation of his soul for the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the valuation of a male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be his valuation shall be fifty didrachmas of silver by the standard of the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the valuation of a female shall be thirty didrachmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if it be from five years old to twenty, the valuation of a male shall be twenty didrachmas, and of a female ten didrachmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And from a month old to five years old, the valuation of a male shall be five didrachmas, and of a female, three didrachmas of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if from sixty year [old] and upward, if it be a male, his valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver, and if a female, ten didrachmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if the man be too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest; and the priest shall value him: according to what the man who has vowed can afford, the priest shall value him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if it be from the cattle that are offered as a gift to the Lord, whoever shall offer one of these to the Lord, it shall be holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He shall not change it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if he do at all change it, a beast for a beast, it and the substitute shall be holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And if it be any unclean beast, of which none are offered as a gift to the Lord, he shall set the beast before the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the priest shall make a valuation between the good and the bad, and accordingly as the priest shall value it, so shall it stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if [the worshipper] will at all redeem it, he shall add the fifth part to its value. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And whatever man shall consecrate his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall make a valuation of it between the good and the bad: as the priest shall value it, so shall it stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And if he that has sanctified it should redeem his house, he shall add to it the fifth part of the money of the valuation, and it shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if a man should hallow to the Lord a part of the field of his possession, then the valuation shall be according to its seed, fifty didrachmas of silver for a homer of barley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if he should sanctify his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to his valuation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if he should sanctify his field in the latter time after the release, the priest shall reckon to him the money for the remaining years, until the [next] year of release, and it shall be deducted as an equivalent from his full valuation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if he that sanctified the field would redeem it, he shall add to its value the fifth part of the money, and it shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if he do not redeem the field, but should sell the field to another man, he shall not after redeem it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But the field shall be holy to the Lord after the release, as separated land; the priest shall have possession of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if he should consecrate to the Lord of a field which he has bought, which is not of the field of his possession, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} the priest shall reckon to him the full valuation from the year of release, and he shall pay the valuation in that day [as] holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And in the year of release the land shall be restored to the man of whom the other bought it, whose the possession of the land was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And every valuation shall be by holy weights: the didrachm shall be twenty oboli. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And every firstborn which shall be produced among your cattle shall be the Lord's, and no man shall sanctify it: whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But if he should redeem an unclean beast, according to its valuation, then he shall add the fifth part to it, and it shall be his; and if he redeem it not, it shall be sold according to its valuation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And every dedicated thing which a man shall dedicate to the Lord of all that he has, whether man or beast, or of the field of his possession, he shall not sell it, nor redeem it: every devoted thing shall be most holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And whatever shall be dedicated of men, shall not be ransomed, but shall be surely put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Every tithe of the land, both of the seed of the land, and of the fruit of trees, is the Lord's, holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And if a man should at all redeem his tithe, he shall add the fifth part to it, and it shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And every tithe of oxen, and of sheep, and whatever may come in numbering under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} You shall not change a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if you should at all change it, its equivalent also shall be holy, it shall not be redeemed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} These are the commandments which the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel in mount Sina.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Gk. vocab: timē (τιμή) = honor; value; price. Common English renderings: honor; price. Can denote honor or assessed value.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} When; a singular vow A vow is a religious promise made to God, for the most part with prayer, and paid with thanksgiving. Vows were either of abstinence ( and ), or the devoting of something to the Lord, as sacrifices ( ), or the value of persons, beasts, houses, or lands, concerning which the law is here given. A man might vow or devote himself, his children, his domestics, his cattle, his goods, etc.; and respecting the redemption of all these, rules are laid down in this chapter. But if, after consecrating these things, he refused to redeem them, they then became the Lord's property forever. The persons continued all their lives devoted to the sanctuary, the goods were sold for the profit of the temple, or the priests; and the animals, if clean, were offered in sacrifice; and if not proper for sacrifice, were sold, and the proceeds devoted to sacred uses. This is a general view of the different laws relative to vows, mentioned in this chapter. \textsuperscript{3} And thy estimation, ; *marg. fifty shekels i.e, At three shillings each, 7£. 10s. sterling. after the \textsuperscript{4} thirty shekels i.e., 4£. 10s. sterling, A little more than one-half the value of a man; for this obvious reason, that a woman, if employed, would not be of so much use in the sanctuary as the man. \textsuperscript{5} twenty shekels i.e. 3£, sterling ten shekels i.e. 1£, 10s. sterling \textsuperscript{6} from, the male The male five shekels, 15s., the female three shekels, 9s. Being both in infancy they were nearly of an equal value. \textsuperscript{7} from fifteen The old man and the old woman, being almost past labour, were nearly of an equal value; the former being estimated at 15 shekels, and the latter at 10. \textsuperscript{9} all is holy, i.e. separated and devoted; it cannot be redeemed like a human being, a house, or a field (Young) \textsuperscript{12} as thou valuest it, who art the priest Heb. according to thy estimation, O priest, etc. \textsuperscript{16} some part Though the words "some part" are not expressed, yet it is generally allowed that they should be supplied here; as it was not lawful for a man to alienate in this manner his whole patrimony. He might express his good will for the house of God but he must not impoverish his own family. of a field, an homer or, the land of an homer, etc. i.e. as much land as required a homer of barley to sow it, The homer was very different from the omer; the latter held about three quarts, the former seventy-five gallons three pints. \textsuperscript{21} when, devoted It is cherem, a thing so devoted to God, as never more to be capable of being redeemed.; *marg. priest's \textsuperscript{25} And all to the shekel A standard shekel; the standard being kept in the sanctuary, to try and regulate all the weights in the land by. twenty \textsuperscript{26} the firstling Heb. first born, etc. As these firstlings were the Lord's before, it would have been a solemn mockery to pretend to make them a matter of a singular vow; for they were already appointed, if clean, to be sacrificed. which \textsuperscript{27} and shall add This was probably intended to prevent rash vows and covetous redemptions. The priest alone was to value the thing; and to whatever his valuation was, a fifth part must be added by him who wished to redeem it. \textsuperscript{28} no devoted This is the cherem, the absolute, irredeemable grant to God. \textsuperscript{29} None; which shall be devoted That is, either that every person devoted to the service of God shall not be redeemed, but die in that devoted state, or, that such as were devoted to death by appointment and law of God, as the Canaanites were, shall be put to death. \textsuperscript{32} passeth under the rod The Rabbins say, that when a man gave the tithe of his sheep or calves, he shut them in one fold, in which was a narrow door, to let out but one at a time. He then stood by the door, with a rod dipped in vermilion in his hand, and as they passed he counted them with the rod; and when the tenth came he touched it, by which it was distinguished as the tithe calf, sheep, etc.\par}

\section*{Numbers Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Moses\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Received as Mosaic in Jewish and Christian tradition; the wilderness census and journey record belong to Moses' law-history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Jesus and the apostles consistently subsume the wilderness law-history under Moses; see John 5:46-47 and 1 Corinthians 10's use of the wilderness narratives.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 1445-1406 BC during Israel's wilderness wanderings\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology keeps the wilderness events in a tighter chronological framework from Sinai to the plains of Moab.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX follows the same wilderness sequence but often reflects different numerical, lexical, or stylistic decisions in individual passages.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} From Sinai through the wilderness to the plains of Moab east of Jordan.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To show the ordering, testing, judgment, preservation, and preparation of the covenant people on the way to the land.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} wilderness testing; census; priestly order; rebellion; judgment; preservation; Balaam; inheritance\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} First generation ordered 1-10; Wilderness rebellion 11-25; Second generation prepared 26-36.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Numbers fragments such as 4QNumbers Hasmonean period | Subst. Several Qumran Numbers manuscripts provide substantial early Hebrew witnesses Hasmonean-Herodian periods | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus, with Codex Alexandrinus also preserving Numbers 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Chronographic use of wilderness and Mosaic material by Demetrius the Chronographer (late 3rd century BC)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Numbers contains several places where textual comparison of MT and LXX affects chronology, figures, or wording; these deserve close apparatus work in a study edition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Numbers as Mosaic and historically grounded; numerical and textual differences between witnesses are treated as transmissional, not as evidence against inspiration.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} wilderness; tabernacle; on the first day As the tabernacle was erected on the first day of the first month, in the second year of their departure from Egypt ( ), and this happened on the first day of the second month, in the same year, it is evident that the transactions related in the preceding book must all have taken place in the space of one month, and during the time the Israelites were encamped at mount Sinai. \textsuperscript{2} Take ye the sum This numbering was probably intended to illustrate the Divine faithfulness in thus increasing the seed of Abraham; to prepare them to preserve due order in their march; and to distinguish the tribes and families.; the children; after \textsuperscript{14} Eliasaph, Son of Reuel, Deuel As the γ, daleth is very like the ψ, resh, they might be easily mistaken for each other; and hence this person being called both Deuel and Reuel, may be easily accounted for. The Septuagint and Syriac have Reuel, in this chapter; and in, the Samaritan, Vulgate, and Arabic have Deuel, instead of Reuel, with which reading a vast number of manuscripts concur, and which is also supported by, . We may therefore safely conclude, the Deuel, and not Reuel, was the original reading. \textsuperscript{16} the renowned Keruey haâidah, literally "the called of the congregation, " those who were summoned by name to attend., ; heads \textsuperscript{18} their pedigrees; *marg. by the according from twenty In this census no women were reckoned, nor children, nor minors, nor strangers, nor Levites, nor old men; which, collectively, must have formed an immense multitude; the Levites alone amounted to 22, 300 men. \textsuperscript{21} That a comparative view may be easily taken of the state of the tribes, we will here produce them, compared with that of the second census ( ), in their decreasing proportion, beginning with the greatest and proceeding to the least. Thus we find Judah the most populous tribe, and Manasseh the least so; the difference between them being as great as 42, 000. Jacob had given Judah the pre-eminence in his prophetic blessing; and that tribe was to have the precedency in the encampments of Israel. Accordingly God had increased them more than any of their brethren. Ephraim and Manasseh, according to the same prophecy, were numbered as distinct tribes, Ephraim having the superiority, as it was foretold; and Joseph indeed appears "a fruitful bough." \textsuperscript{24} The tribe of Gad marched, along with that of Simeon, under the standard of Reuben; and it seems, on that account, to have been introduced in this order. The other tribes also, are here classed together according to their encampments, and the order of their subsequent march. \textsuperscript{46} What an astonishing increase from seventy persons who went down into Egypt about 215 years before, where they had latterly endured the greatest hardships! \subsection*{Numbers 2}
\markright{NUMBERS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let the children of Israel encamp fronting [each other], every man keeping his own rank, according to [their] standards, according to the houses of their families; the children of Israel shall encamp round about the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they that encamp first toward the east [shall be] the order of the camp of Juda with their host, and the prince of the sons of Juda, Naasson the son of Aminadab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} His forces that were numbered, were seventy-four thousand and six hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they that encamp next [shall be] of the tribe of Issachar, and the prince of the sons of Issachar [shall be] Nathanael the son of Sogar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} His forces that were numbered, were fifty-four thousand and four hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they that encamp next [shall be] of the tribe of Zabulon, and the prince of the sons of Zabulon [shall be] Eliab the son of Chaelon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} His forces that were numbered, were fifty-seven thousand and four hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} All that were numbered of the camp of Juda were one hundred and eighty thousand and six thousand and four hundred: they shall move first with their forces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [This is] the order of the camp of Ruben; their forces [shall be] toward the south, and the prince of the children of Ruben [shall be] Elisur the son of Sediur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} His forces that were numbered, were forty-six thousand and five hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they that encamp next to him [shall be] of the tribe of Symeon, and the prince of the sons of Symeon [shall be] Salamiel the son of Surisadai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} His forces that were numbered, were fifty-nine thousand and three hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they that encamp next to them [shall be] the tribe of Gad; and the prince of the sons of Gad, Elisaph the son of Raguel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} His forces that were numbered, were forty-five thousand and six hundred and fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} All who were numbered of the camp of Ruben, were one hundred and fifty-one thousand and four hundred and fifty: they with their forces shall proceed in the second place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And [then] the tabernacle of witness shall be set forward, and the camp of the Levites [shall be] between the camps; as they shall encamp, so also shall they commence their march, each one next in order to his fellow according to their companies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The station of the camp of Ephraim [shall be] westward with their forces, and the head of the children of Ephraim [shall be] Elisama the son of Emiud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} His forces that were numbered, are forty thousand and five hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they that encamp next [shall be] of the tribe of Manasse, and the prince of the sons of Manasse, Gamaliel the son of Phadassur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} His forces that were numbered, were thirty-two thousand and two hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they that encamp next [shall be] of the tribe of Benjamin, and the prince of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gadeoni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} His forces that were numbered, were thirty-five thousand and four hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} All that were numbered of the camp of Ephraim, were one hundred and eight thousand and one hundred: they with their forces shall set out third. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The order of the camp of Dan [shall be] northward with their forces; and the prince of the sons of Dan, Achiezer the son of Amisadai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} His forces that were numbered, were sixty-two thousand and seven hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they that encamp next to him [shall be] the tribe of Aser; and the prince of the sons of Aser, Phagiel the son of Echran. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} His forces that were numbered, were forty-one thousand and five hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they that encamp next [shall be] of the tribe of Nephthali; and the prince of the children of Nephthali, Achire son Aenan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} His forces that were numbered were fifty-three thousand and four hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} All that were numbered of the camp of Dan, [were] one hundred and fifty-seven thousand and six hundred: they shall set out last according to their order. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} This [is] the numbering of the children of Israel according to the houses of their families: all the numbering of the camps with their forces, [was] six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But the Levites were not numbered with them, as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the children of Israel did all things that the Lord commanded Moses; thus they encamped in their order, and thus they began their march in succession each according to their divisions, according to the houses of their families.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{31} Heb. vocab: acharón (אַחֲרוֹן) = last; latter. Common English renderings: last; latter. Contrasts with former or first.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Every man The Israelites, it appears, encamped in four grand divisions, with the tabernacle in the centre; though at some distance from it. The form of the camp was quadrangular, containing, according to Scheuchzer, a little more than twelve square miles. Under each of the four divisions, three tribes were placed, under one general standard. Between these four great camps and the tabernacle, were pitched four smaller camps of the priests and Levites, who were in immediate attendance upon it; the camp of Moses, and of Aaron and his sons, being on the east side of the tabernacle, where the entrance was. Judah was placed on the east, and under him he had Issachar and Zebulun; on the south was Reuben, and under him Simeon and Gad; on the west was Ephraim, and under him Manasseh and Benjamin; and Dan was on the north, and under him Asher and Naphtali. Every tribe had its particular standard, probably with the name of the tribe embroidered with large letters. It seems highly improbable that the figures of animals should have been painted on them, as the Jewish writers assert; for even in after ages, when Vitellius wished to march through Judea, their great men besought him to march another way, as the law of the land did not permit images (such as were on the Roman standard) to be brought into it. Josephus Ant. 1. xviii. c. 5 sec. 3. shall pitch, the ensign; far off Heb. over against, about the\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 3}
\markright{NUMBERS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the generations of Aaron and Moses, in the day in which the Lord spoke to Moses in mount Sina. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And these [are] the names of the sons of Aaron; Nadab the firstborn; and Abiud, Eleazar and Ithamar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} These [are] the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests whom they consecrated to the priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Nadab and Abiud died before the Lord, when they offered strange fire before the Lord, in the wilderness of Sina; and they had no children; and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priests' office with Aaron their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Take the tribe of Levi, and you shall set them before Aaron the priest, and they shall minister to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and shall keep his charges, and the charges of the children of Israel, before the tabernacle of witness, to do the works of the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they shall keep all the furniture of the tabernacle of witness, and the charges of the children of Israel as to all the works of the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall give the Levites to Aaron, and to his sons the priests; they are given for a gift to me of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the tabernacle of witness; and they shall keep their charge of priesthood, and all things belonging to the altar, and within the veil; and the stranger that touches them shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Behold, I have taken the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel, instead of every male that opens the womb from among the children of Israel: they shall be their ransom, and the Levites shall be mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For every firstborn [is] mine; in the day in which I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified to myself every firstborn in Israel: both of man and beast, they shall be mine: I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sina, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Take the number of the sons of Levi, according to the houses of their families, according to their divisions; number you⌃ them every male from a month old and upwards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Moses and Aaron numbered them by the word of the Lord, as the Lord commanded them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these were the sons of Levi by their names; Gedson, Caath, and Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And these [are] the names of the sons of Gedson according to their families; Lobeni and Semei: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the sons of Caath according to their families; Amram and Issaar, Chebron and Oziel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the sons of Merari according to their families, Mooli and Musi; these are the families of the Levites according to the houses of their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} To Gedson belongs the family of Lobeni, and the family of Semei: these are the families of Gedson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The numbering of them according to the number of every male from a month old and upwards, their numbering [was] seven thousand and five hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the sons of Gedson shall encamp westward behind the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the ruler of the household of the family of Gedson [was] Elisaph the son of Dael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the charge of the sons of Gedson in the tabernacle of witness [was] the tent and the veil, and the covering of the door of the tabernacle of witness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and the curtains of the court, and the veil of the door of the court, which is by the tabernacle, and the remainder of all its works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} To Caath [belonged] one division, that of Amram, and another division, that of Issaar, and another division, that of Chebron, and another division, that of Oziel: these are the divisions of Caath, according to number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Every male from a month old and upward, eight thousand and six hundred, keeping the charges of the holy things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} The families of the sons of Caath, shall encamp beside the tabernacle toward the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the chief of the house of the families of the divisions of Caath, [was] Elisaphan the son of Oziel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And their charge [was] the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and all the vessels of the sanctuary wherewith they do holy service, and the veil, and all their works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the chief over the chief of the Levites, [was] Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, appointed to keep the charges of the holy things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} To Merari [belonged] the family of Mooli, and the family of Musi: these are the families of Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The mustering of them according to number, every male from a month old and upwards, [was] six thousand and fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the head of the house of the families of the division of Merari, was Suriel the son of Abichail: they shall encamp by the side of the tabernacle northwards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} The oversight of the charge of the sons of Merari [included] the capitals of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets, and all their furniture, and their works, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and the pillars of the court round about, and their bases, and their pins, and their cords. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} They that encamp before the tabernacle of witness on the east [shall be] Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charges of the sanctuary according to the charges of the children of Israel; and the stranger that touches them, shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} All the numbering of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered by the word of the Lord, according to their families, every male from a month old and upwards, [were] two and twenty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Count every firstborn male of the children of Israel from a month old and upwards, and take the number by name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And you shall take the Levites for me—I [am] the Lord—instead of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the cattle of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Moses counted, as the Lord commanded him, every firstborn among the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And all the male firstborn in number by name, from a month old and upwards, were according to their numbering twenty-two thousand and two hundred and seventy-three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle, and the Levites shall be mine; I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And for the ransoms of the two hundred and seventy-three which exceed the Levites in number of the firstborn of the sons of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} you shall even take five shekels a head; you shall take them according to the holy didrachm, twenty oboli to the shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And you shall give the money to Aaron and to his sons, the ransom of those who exceed in number among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And Moses took the silver, the ransom of those that exceeded in number the redemption of the Levites. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the priests, ;, whom he consecrated Heb. whose hand he filled; Lev. 8:1-9:24 \textsuperscript{6} The word hakraiv, here rendered bring near, is properly a sacrificial word, and signifies the presenting of a sacrifice or offering to the Lord. As an offering, the tribe of Levi was entirely given up to the service of the sanctuary, to be no longer their own, but the Lord's. \textsuperscript{10} they shall; and the stranger \textsuperscript{12} When God miraculously destroyed all the first-born of the Egyptians ( ), he spared those of the Israelites; and, in commemoration of that event, he was pleased to appoint that all the first-born males "should be set apart unto himself" ( ). God is here pleased to relinquish this claim, and to appoint the whole tribe of Levi to attend his immediate service in their stead. \textsuperscript{22} from a month old The males of all the other tribes were numbered from twenty years old and upwards; but, had the Levites been numbered in this way, they would not have been nearly equal in number to the first-born of the twelve tribes. Add to this, that as there must have been first-born of all ages in the other tribes, it was necessary that the Levites, who were to be their substitutes, should also be of all ages; and it appears to have been partly on this ground, that the Levites were numbered from a month old and upwards. \textsuperscript{24} Lael i.e. unto, by, because of God, . \textsuperscript{25} the charge From this and the next chapter, we see the very severe labour which the Levites were to perform, while the journeyings of the Israelites lasted. When we consider, that there was not less than 14 tons 266 lbs. of metal employed in the tabernacle (see note on ), besides the immense weight of the skins, hangings, cords, boards, and posts, we shall find it was no easy matter to transport this moveable temple from place to place. The Gershonites, who were 7, 500 in number had to carry the tent, coverings, vail, hangings of the court, cords, etc. ( and ); the Kohathites, who were 8, 600, the ark, table, candlestick, altars, and instruments of the sanctuary ( ); and the Merarites, who were 6, 200, the boards, bars, sockets, and all matters connected with these belonging to the tabernacle, with the pillars of the court, their sockets, pins, and cords ( and )., ; the tabernacle and, and the hanging \textsuperscript{31} the ark; 31:1-35:29, the altars, and the hanging \textsuperscript{36} under the custody and charge Heb. the office of the charge, the boards. \textsuperscript{38} toward, keeping; for the charge \textsuperscript{39} and Aaron The word εΙΰΙδΙψΙοΙ, weaharon, "and Aaron, " has a point over each of its letters, probably designed as a mark of spuriousness. The word is wanting in the Samaritan, Syriac, and Coptic, and also in eight of Dr. Kennicott's and in four of De Rossi's manuscripts. Moses alone, as Houbigant observes, was commanded to number the Levites (, ) for as the money with which the first-born were redeemed was to be paid to Aaron and his sons ( ), it was decent that he, whose advantage it was that the number of the first-born should exceed, should not be authorized to take that number himself. twenty and two thousand. This total does not agree with the particulars; for the Gershonites were 7, 500, the Kohathites 8, 600, and the Merarites 6, 200, which make a total of 22, 300. Several methods of solving this difficulty have been proposed by learned men. Houbigant supposes there is an error in the enumeration of the Kohathites in; the numeral shesh, "six, " being written instead of shalosh, "three, " before "hundred." Dr. Kennicott's mode of reconciling the discrepancy, however, is the most simple. He supposes that an error has crept into the number of the Gershonites in, where instead of 7, 500 we should read 7, 200, as κ, caph final, which stands for 500, might have been easily mistaken for ψ, resh, 200 (Dr. Kennicott on the Hebrew Text, vol. II. p. 212). Either of these modes will equally reconcile the difference. \textsuperscript{46} redeemed; the two hundred As the number of the Levites was 22, 000, and the first-born males of the Israelites were 22, 273, there were therefore 372 more of the latter than of the former, which are here ordered to be redeemed. The price of redemption is fixed at five shekels, or about 15s. each, in . This money, amounting to 1, 365 shekels, equal to £204, 15s English, was taken of the first-born. There is some difficulty, however, in determining which of the first-born should be redeemed by paying this sum, and which should be exchanged for the Levites; for every Israelite, no doubt, would rather have his first-born redeemed by a Levite, than pay five shekels; and yet some of them must have incurred this expense. Rabbi Solomon Jarchi says, to prevent contention, Moses took 22, 000 slips of parchment, and wrote on each a son of Levi, and 273 more, on which he wrote five shekels; then putting them in an urn, and shaking them together, he ordered every one of the first-born to draw out a slip. If he drew out one with the first inscription, he said to him, a Levite hath redeemed thee, but if he drew out one of the latter, he said, pay the price. This is pronounced by Dr. A. Clarke to be a stupid, silly tale; but when we know that the determination by lot was used among the Israelites, it does not seem improbable that it was now resorted to, though we cannot vouch for the accuracy of the detail. This species of redeeming men is referred to by St. Peter in his 1st Epistle . which are\par}

That exception, therefore, is here expressly made; and the directions given respecting it must be religiously observed, or the service could not be safely performed. Eleazar exercised this authority in general, as next in succession to Aaron, and he in particular was placed over the Kohathites; while Ithamar, his younger brother, commanded the Gershonites and Merarites ( ). \textsuperscript{32} and by name An inventory was taken of every particular, even to the very pins belonging to each part, that nothing might be wanting when the tabernacle was set up. the instruments \textsuperscript{36} In the third chapter we have an account of the whole number of the Levites; and here of those only who were able to serve the Lord in the sanctuary. By comparing the two places, we find the number of the effective and ineffective males. Thus we find that the whole number of the Levites amounted to 22, 300; of whom 8, 580 were fit for service and 13, 720 unfit, being either too old or too young. What an astonishing number of men, all performing some service by which God was glorified, and the congregation at large benefited! \textsuperscript{44} The family of Merari, though smaller than either of the other families of Levi, yet had a greater number of able men than any of them; for out of 6, 200 males of a month old and upwards, we find 3, 200 who were neither too young nor too old for the service of the sanctuary; which was more than one-half of their whole number. In this the wisdom and providence of God appear most conspicuously; for the Merarites were charged with the heaviest part of the sanctuary, as the boards, bars, sockets, etc; and though waggons were afterwards provided for them, yet the loading and unloading of the sockets, and other things of great weight, would require much strength, both bodily and numerical. (Compare and, with, .) Thus God ever manifests his wisdom, in fitting men for the work to which they are appointed, whether with respect to number or gifts: "For to one is given, by the Spirit, the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge, by the same Spirit; to another faith, by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing, by the same Spirit; to another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues, but all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will." \textsuperscript{49} According to the, every one, ; as the Lord\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 5}
\markright{NUMBERS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Charge the children of Israel, and let them send forth out of the camp every leper, and every one who has a discharge, and every one who is unclean from a dead body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Whether male or female, send them forth out of the camp; and they shall not defile their camps in which I dwell among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the children of Israel did so, and sent them out of the camp: as the Lord said to Moses, so did the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Every man or woman who shall commit any sin that is common to man, or if that soul shall in anyway have neglected the commandment and transgressed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [that person] shall confess the sin which he has committed, and shall make satisfaction for his trespass: he [shall pay] the principal, and shall add to it the fifth part, and shall make restoration to him against whom he has trespassed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But if a man have no near kinsman, so as to make satisfaction for his trespass to him, the trespass-offering paid to the Lord shall be for the priest, besides the ram of atonement, by which he shall make atonement with it for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And every first fruits in all the sanctified things among the children of Israel, whatever they shall offer to the Lord, shall be for the priest himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the hallowed things of every man shall be his; and whatever man shall give [any thing] to the priest, the gift shall be his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, Whosesoever wife shall transgress against him, and slight and despise him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and [supposing] any one shall lie with her carnally, and the thing shall be hid from the eyes of her husband, and she should conceal it and be herself defiled, and there be no witness with her, and she should not be taken; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and there should come upon him a spirit of jealousy, and he should be jealous of his wife, and she be defiled; or there should come upon him a spirit of jealousy, and he should be jealous of his wife, and she should not be defiled; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} then shall the man bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring his gift for her, the tenth part of an ephah of barley-meal: he shall not pour oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it; for it is a sacrifice of jealousy, a sacrifice of memorial, recalling sin to remembrance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priest shall bring her, and cause her to stand before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the priest shall take pure running water in an earthen vessel, and he shall take of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle of witness, and the priest having taken it shall cast it into the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the priest shall cause the woman to stand before the Lord, and shall uncover the head of the woman, and shall put into her hands the sacrifice of memorial, the sacrifice of jealousy; and in the hand of the priest shall be the water of this conviction that brings the curse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the priest shall adjure her, and shall say to the woman, If no one has lain with you, and if you have not transgressed so as to be polluted, being under the power of your husband, be free from this water of the conviction that causes the curse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But if being a married woman you have transgressed, or been polluted, and any one has lain with you, beside your husband: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} then the priest shall adjure the woman by the oaths of this curse, and the priest shall say to the woman, The Lord bring you into a curse and under an oath in the midst of your people, in that the Lord should cause your thigh to rot and your belly to swell; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and this water bringing the curse shall enter into your womb to cause your belly to swell, and your thigh to rot. And the woman shall say, So be it, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the priest shall write these curses in a book, and shall blot them out with the water of the conviction that brings the curse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he shall cause the woman to drink the water of the conviction that brings the curse; and the water of the conviction that brings the curse shall enter into her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the priest shall take from the hand of the woman the sacrifice of jealousy, and shall present the sacrifice before the Lord, and shall bring it to the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the priest shall take a handful of the sacrifice as a memorial of it, and shall offer it up upon the altar; and afterwards he shall cause the woman to drink the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it shall come to pass, if she be defiled, and have altogether escaped the notice of her husband, then the water of the conviction that brings the curse shall enter into her; and she shall swell in her belly, and her thigh shall rot, and the woman shall be for a curse in the midst of her people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if the woman have not been polluted, and be clean, then shall she be guiltless and shall conceive seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} This is the law of jealousy, wherein a married woman should happen to transgress, and be defiled; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} or in the case of a man on whoever the spirit of jealousy should come, and he should be jealous of his wife, and he should place his wife before the Lord, and the priest shall execute towards her all this law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then the man shall be clear from sin, and that woman shall bear her sin.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{14} Heb. vocab: qin’ah (קִנְאָה) = jealousy; zeal. Common English renderings: jealousy; zeal. Used for divine zeal and human jealousy. \textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: amen (אָמֵן) = truly; so be it. Common English renderings: Amen. Response of affirmation, agreement, and certainty.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} put out of the camp The camp of Israel being now formed, with the sanctuary of God in the centre, orders were given that the lepers and unclean persons should be excluded from the camp, according to the laws given at different times on these subjects. (See the marginal references.) This expulsion was founded: 1. On a purely physical reason; for the diseases were contagious, and therefore there was a necessity of putting those afflicted with them apart, that the infection might not be communicated. 2. There was also a spiritual reason. The camp was the habitation of God; and therefore, in honour of Him who had thus condescended to dwell with them, nothing impure should be permitted to remain. 3. Further, there was a typical reason; for the camp was the emblem of the church, where nothing that is defiled should enter, and in which nothing that is unholy should be tolerated.; and every and whosoever \textsuperscript{3} without; defile not; in the midst \textsuperscript{6} When, and that person This expression does not merely refer to the actual criminality of the person, but to his consciousness of guilt respecting it. For this case must be distinguished from that of a person detected in dishonesty, which he attempted to conceal. \textsuperscript{7} confess; and he shall Not only confession, but restitution, in every possible case, is necessary in order to obtain forgiveness. with the principal \textsuperscript{8} have no beside the ram \textsuperscript{14} Rooach kinah, either a supernatural diabolic influence, exciting him to jealousy, or, rather, the passion or affection of jealousy. \textsuperscript{15} her offering for her This coarse offering, without oil or frankincense, implied the baseness of the crime of which the woman was suspected, and the mournful state of her family. It was not an atoning sacrifice, but an oblation for a memorial, as solemnly referring the decision to God, and calling upon him either to acquit or punish.; bringing \textsuperscript{16} bring her near or, rather, "bring it near; " i. e. her offering set her Rather, "set it, " i.e., the offering; for the woman is afterwards ordered to be set before the Lord ( ). \textsuperscript{17} holy water That is, water from the laver; called holy, because separated from common to sacred uses. This is the most ancient account of the trial by ordeal, which obtained so generally among various nations; and it was calculated to fortify the minds of the Israelitish women in the hour of temptation, and to render them watchful against all occasions of exciting suspicion in the breasts of their husbands.; of the dust \textsuperscript{18} the priest; uncover; and put, the bitter water So called from the bitter effects which it had upon the guilty. \textsuperscript{19} charge her with another or, being in the power of thy husband, Heb. under thy husband. *Gr. \textsuperscript{21} an oath; The Lord make; rot Heb. fall \textsuperscript{22} go into; the woman; Amen, ;, *Gr. \textsuperscript{27} if she be defiled; the woman \textsuperscript{29} the law, when a wife goeth\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 6}
\markright{NUMBERS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, Whatsoever man or woman shall specially vow a vow to separate oneself with purity to the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} he shall purely abstain from wine and strong drink; and he shall drink no vinegar of wine or vinegar of strong drink; and whatever is made of the grape he shall not drink; neither shall he eat fresh grapes or raisins, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} all the days of his vow: he shall eat no one of all the things that come from the vine, wine from the grape-stones to the husk, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} all the days of his separation:—a razor shall not come upon his head, until the days be fulfilled which he vowed to the Lord: he shall be holy, cherishing the long hair of the head, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} all the days of his vow to the Lord: he shall not come near to any dead body, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} to his father or his mother, or to his brother or his sister; he shall not defile himself for them, when they have died, because the vow of God is upon him on his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} All the days of his vow he shall be holy to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if any one should die suddenly by him, immediately the head of his vow shall be defiled; and he shall shave his head in whatever day he shall be purified: on the seventh day he shall be shaved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the priest, to the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the priest shall offer one for a sin-offering; and the other for a whole burnt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him in the things wherein he sinned respecting the dead body, and he shall sanctify his head in that day, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} in which he was consecrated to the Lord, [all] the days of his vow; and he shall bring a lamb of a year old for a trespass-offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, because the head of his vow was polluted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And this is the law of him that has vowed: in whatever day he shall have fulfilled the days of his vow, he shall himself bring his gift to the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he shall bring his gift to the Lord; one he-lamb of a year old without blemish for a whole burnt offering, and one ewe-lamb of a year old without blemish for a sin-offering, and one ram without blemish for a peace-offering; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, [even] loaves kneaded with oil, and unleavened cakes anointed with oil, and their meat-offering, and their drink-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priest shall bring them before the Lord, and shall offer his sin-offering, and his whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he shall offer the ram as a sacrifice of peace-offering to the Lord with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall offer its meat-offering and its drink-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he that has vowed shall shave the head of his consecration by the doors of the tabernacle of witness, and shall put the hairs on the fire which is under the sacrifice of peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the priest shall take the sodden shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened cake, and shall put them on the hands of the votary after he has shaved off his {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the priest shall present them as an offering before the Lord; it shall be the holy portion for the priest beside the breast of the heave-offering and beside the shoulder of the wave-offering: and afterwards the votary shall drink wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} This is the law of the votary who shall have vowed to the Lord his gift to the Lord, concerning his vow, besides what he may be able to afford according to the value of his vow, which he may have vowed according to the law of separation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, Thus you⌃ shall bless the children of Israel, saying to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The Lord bless you and keep you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} the Lord make his face to shine upon you, and have mercy upon you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I the Lord will bless them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} When; separate themselves The word yaphli, rendered "shall separate themselves, " signifies, "the doing of something extraordinary, " and is the same word as is used concerning the making a singular vow. ( ); it seems to convey the idea of a person's acting from extraordinary zeal for God and religion. to vow; to separate themselves or, to make themselves Nazarites, Lahazzir, from nazar, to be separate; hence nazir, a Nazarite, i.e., a person separated; one peculiarly devoted to the service of God by being separated from all servile employments. The Nazarites were of two kinds. Such as were devoted to God by their parents in their infancy, or even sometimes before they were born; and such as devoted themselves. The former were Nazarites for life; and the latter commonly bound themselves to observe the laws of the Nazarites for a limited time. The Nazarites for life were not bound to the same strictness as the others, concerning whom the laws relate. \textsuperscript{3} Besides the religious nature of this institution, it seems to have been partly of a civil and prudential use. The sobriety and temperance which the Nazarites were obliged to observe were very conducive to health. Accordingly, they were celebrated for their fair and ruddy complexion; being said to be both whiter than milk and more ruddy than rubies ( ); the sure signs of a sound and healthy constitution. It may here be observed, that when God intended to raise up Samson, by his strength of body, to scourge the enemies of Israel, he ordered, that from his infancy he should drink no wine, but live by the rule of the Nazarites, because that would greatly contribute to make him strong and healthy; intending, after nature had done her utmost to form this extraordinary instrument of his providence, to supply her defect by his own supernatural power. See Jenning's Jewish Antiquities, B. I. c. 8. \textsuperscript{4} separation or, Nazariteship, vine tree Heb. vine of the wine \textsuperscript{7} unclean; consecration Heb. separation, This expression, "the consecration, or separation, of God is on his head, " denotes his hair, which was the proof and emblem of his separation, and of his subjection to God through all the peculiarities of his Nazarate. St. Paul probably alludes to this circumstance in by considering a married woman as a Nazarite for life, i.e., separated from all others, and united to her husband, to whom she is subject. \textsuperscript{12} a trespass, but the; lost Heb. fall \textsuperscript{14} one he; one ewe, ; one ram \textsuperscript{18} shave the head The hair, which was permitted to grow for this purpose, was shaven off, as a token that the vow was accomplished.;, and put it \textsuperscript{20} the priest shall;, with the wave; and after \textsuperscript{27} put my, ; and I will\par}
