one silver bowl of seventy shekels according to the holy shekel; both full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{80}} One golden censer of ten shekels, full of incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{81}} One calf of the herd, one ram, one he-lamb of a year old for a whole burnt offering, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{82}} and one kid of the goats for a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{83}} And for a sacrifice of peace-offering, two heifers, five rams, five he-goats, five ewe-lambs of a year old: this [was] the gift of Achire the son of Aenan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{84}} This was the dedication of the altar in the day in which [Moses] anointed it, by the princes of the sons of Israel; twelve silver chargers, twelve silver bowls, twelve golden censers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{85}} each charger of one hundred and thirty shekels, and each bowl of seventy shekels: all the silver of the vessels [was] two thousand four hundred shekels, the shekels according to the holy shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{86}} Twelve golden censers full of incense: all the gold of the shekels, one hundred and twenty shekels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{87}} All the cattle for whole burnt offerings, twelve calves, twelve rams, twelve he-lambs of a year old, and their meat-offerings, and their drink-offerings: and twelve kids of the goats for sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{88}} All the cattle for a sacrifice of peace-offering, twenty-four heifers, sixty rams, sixty he-goats of a year old, sixty ewe-lambs of a year old without blemish: this is the dedication of the altar, after that [Moses] consecrated [Aaron], and after he anointed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{89}} When Moses went into the tabernacle of witness to speak to God, then he heard the voice of the Lord speaking to him from off the mercy-seat, which is upon the ark of the testimony, between the two cherubs; and he spoke to him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} had fully anointed it; sanctified them \textsuperscript{2} the princes, and were over etc. Heb. who stood offered \textsuperscript{3} covered wagons The Hebrew egloth tzav, signifies "tilted wagons; " so LXX αμαξας λαμπηνικας, with which the Coptic agrees. These were given for the more convenient exporting of the heavier parts of the tabernacle. \textsuperscript{5} Take it; give them i.e. distribute them among the Levites as they need them; giving most to those who have the heaviest burdens to bear. \textsuperscript{7} Two wagons, sons of Gershon The Gershonites being fewest in number of able men, had the less burdensome things to carry; for they carried only the curtains, coverings, and hangings (, ). And although this was a cumbersome carriage, and they needed waggons, yet it was not a heavy one, and they needed few. \textsuperscript{8} four wagons, the sons Though the Merarites were the most numerous, yet they had the greatest burden, namely, the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets, to carry (, ). Therefore they had double the number of waggons to what the Gershonites had assigned them. \textsuperscript{9} unto the Because they had the charge of the ark, table, candlestick, altars, etc. ( ), which were to be carried upon their shoulders. For those sacred things must not be drawn by beasts. because \textsuperscript{10} princes Every prince, or chief, offered in the behalf, and doubtless at the expense, of his whole tribe. dedicating; *title \textsuperscript{13} charger; the shekel; a meat offering \textsuperscript{17} peace; this was the offering It is worthy of remark, that the different tribes are represented here as bringing their offerings precisely in the same order in which they encamped about the tabernacle (see and ), beginning at the East, then proceeding to the South, then to the West, and ending with the North, according to the course of the sun. Thus God evinces that he "is not the author of confusion, but of peace" ( ). It is also worthy of remark, that every tribe offers the same kind of offering, and in the same quantity, to shew, that as every tribe was equally indebted to God for its support, so each should testify an equal sense of obligation. Besides, the vessels were all sacrificial vessels, and the animals were all clean animals, such as were proper for sacrifices; and therefore everything was intended to point out, that the people were to be a holy people, fully dedicated to God, and that God was to dwell among them. Thus, as the priests, altar, etc. were anointed, and the tabernacle dedicated, so the people, by this offering, became consecrated to God. Therefore every act here was a religious act. \textsuperscript{31} offering charger Kaârah, in Arabic, kâran, from kuâra, to be deep, a large deep dish or bowl. It appears by the metal of which this charger and bowl were made, that they were for the use of the altar of burnt offerings in the outer court; for all the vessels of the sanctuary were of gold. It was probably used for receiving the flesh of the sacrifices upon which the priests feasted, or the fine flour for the meat offerings. Bowl Mizrak, from zarak, to sprinkle, a bowl or bason, used in sprinkling the blood of the sacrifice ( ). \textsuperscript{32} spoon Kaph, in Syriac, kaphtho, a pan or censer, on which the incense was put. Both the metal of which it was made, and that which it contained, shew that it was for the use of the golden altar in the sanctuary. incense \textsuperscript{35} And for a sacrifice These sacrifices were more numerous than the burnt offering or the sin offering; because the priests, the princes, and as many of the people as they invited, had a share of them, and feasted, with great rejoicing, before the Lord. This custom, as Mr. Shelden observes, seems to have been imitated by the heathen, who dedicated their altars, temples, statues, etc., with much ceremony. \textsuperscript{48} On the seventh Both Jewish and Christian writers have been surprised that this work of offering went forward on the seventh day (which they suppose to have been a sabbath), as well as on the other days. But: 1. There is no absolute proof that this seventh day of offering was a sabbath. 2. Were it even so, could the people be better employed than in thus consecrating themselves and their services to the Lord? We have already seen that every act was a religious act; and we may rest assured, that no day was too holy for the performance of such acts as are here recorded. Here it may be observed, that Moses has thought fit to set down distinctly, and at full length, the offerings of the princes of each tribe, though, as we have already observed, they were the very same, both in quantity and quality, that an honourable mention might be made of every one apart, and that none might think himself in the least neglected. Elishama \textsuperscript{51} Whether there were any prayers made for the gracious acceptance of the sacrifices which should be hereafter offered on the altar, we are not informed; but the sacrifices themselves were of the nature of supplications, and it is probable, that they who offered them, made humble petitions along with them. \textsuperscript{66} On the tenth day When the twelve days of the dedication commenced cannot be easily determined; but the computation of F. Scacchus seems highly probable. He supposes, that the tabernacle being erected the first day of the first month of the second year after the departure from Egypt, seven days were spent in the consecration of it, and the altar, etc.; and that on the eight day, Moses began to consecrate Aaron and his sons, which lasted seven days more. Then, on the fourteenth day of that month, was the feast day of unleavened bread; which God commanded to be observed in the first month ( ), and which lasted till the 22nd. The rest of the month, we may well suppose, was spent in giving, receiving, and delivering the laws contained in the book of Leviticus; after which, on the first day of the second month, Moses began to number the people, according to the command in the beginning of this book; which may be supposed to have lasted three days. On the fourth, the Levites were numbered; on the next day we may suppose they were offered to God, and given to the Priests; and on the sixth, they were expiated and consecrated, as we read in the following chapter. On the seventh day, their several charges were assigned them ( ); after which, he supposes the princes began to offer, on the eight day of the second month, for the dedication of the altar, which lasted till the nineteenth day inclusively; and on the twentieth day of this month, they removed from Sinai to the wilderness of Paran ( ). Ahiezer \textsuperscript{72} eleventh day Dr. Adam Clarke remarks, that the Hebrew form of expression here, and in, has something curious in it; beyom âshtey âsar yom, "in the day, the first and tenth day; " beyom shenim âsar yom, "in the day, two and tenth day." But this is the idiom of the language; and to an original Hebrew, our almost anomalous words eleventh and twelfth, would appear as strange. Pagiel \textsuperscript{73} The oblations and sacrifices enumerated in were simple and plain, though costly and magnificent. On this occasion we find there were offered 12 silver chargers, each weighing 130 shekels; 12 silver bowls, each 70 shekels; 12 golden spoons, each 10 shekels; making the total amount of silver vessels 2, 400 shekels, and that of golden vessels, 120 shekels. A silver charger, at 130 shekels, reduced to troy weight, makes 75 oz. 9 dwts. 16, 8/31 gr.; and a silver bowl, at 70 shekels, amounts to 40 oz. 12 dwts. 21, 21/31 gr. The total weight of the 12 chargers is therefore 905 oz. 16 dwts. 3, 3/31 gr.; and that of the 12 bowls, 487 oz. 14 dwts. 20; 4/31 gr.; making the total weight of silver vessels 1, 393 oz. 10 dwts. 23, 7/31 gr. The golden spoons, allowing each to be 5 oz. 16 dwts. 3, 3/31 gr., amount to 69 oz. 3 dwts. 13, 5/31 gr. Besides these, there were for sacrifice -parBullocks, 12 Rams, 12 Lambs, 12 Goats, 24 Rams, 60 He goats, 60 Lambs, 60 By this we may at once see, that though the place in which they now sojourned was a wilderness as to cities, villages, and regular inhabitants, yet there was plenty of pasturage; else the Israelites could not have furnished these cattle, with all the sacrifices necessary for different occasions, and especially for the passover, which must of itself have required an immense number of lambs, when each family of 600, 000 males was obliged to provide one ( ). \textsuperscript{85} two thousand, ; after the shekel \textsuperscript{89} to speak; him that is, God he heard; two cherubims\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to Aaron, and you shall say to him, Whenever you shall set the lamps in order, the seven lamps shall give light opposite the candlestick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Aaron did so: on one side opposite the candlestick he lighted its lamps, as the Lord appointed Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And this [is] the construction of the candlestick: [it is] solid, golden—its stem, and its lilies—all solid: according to the pattern which the Lord showed Moses, so he made the candlestick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Take the Levites out of the midst of the children of Israel, and you shall purify them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And thus shall you perform their purification: you shall sprinkle them with water of purification, and a razor shall come upon the whole of their body, and they shall wash their garments, and shall be clean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they shall take one calf of the herd, and its meat-offering, fine flour mingled with oil: and you shall take a calf of a year old of the herd for a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall bring the Levites before the tabernacle of witness; {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} When this was spoken, says Bp. Patrick, is not certain. If Moses went into the tabernacle immediately after the princes had offered ( ), it may be thought he then spake these things unto him; but both this and what follows, concerning the Levites, seem rather to have been delivered after the order for giving them to the priests, and appointing their several charges ( and ). But some other things intervening, which depended upon what had been ordered respecting their camp, and that of the Israelites, Moses omits this until he had stated them, and some other matters which he had received from God. (See note on .) \textsuperscript{4} this work, beaten work, the pattern \textsuperscript{7} Sprinkle; water, ; let them shave Heb. let them cause a razor to pass over, etc. wash their \textsuperscript{8} a young; his meat; another \textsuperscript{9} thou shalt bring, shalt gather the whole The words, kol âdath, which are rendered "the whole assembly, " often signify all the elders, or principal persons in the several tribes (; ). And they cannot well have any other sense here; for it would be impossible for all the children of Israel to put their hands on the Levites, as stated in the next verse. \textsuperscript{11} offer Heb. wave offering Heb. wave-offering, Not that they were actually waved, but they were presented to God, as the God of heaven, and the Lord of the whole earth, as the wave offerings were; and in calling them wave-offerings, it was intimated to them that they must move to and fro with readiness in the business of their profession.;, they may execute Heb. they may be to execute, etc. \textsuperscript{13} offer them Wehainaphta othom tenoophath, literally, as in, "and thou shalt wave them for a wave-offering; " manifestly in allusion to the ancient sacrificial rite of waving the sacrifices before the Lord; and it is probable, that some significant action, analogous to the waving of the sacrifice, was employed on this occasion; for the Levites were considered as an offering to the Lord, to whose service they were wholly dedicated. To this the apostle Paul manifestly alludes, when, in writing to the Romans, he says ( ), "I beseech you, therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service." \textsuperscript{16} wholly given Nethunim, nethunim, "given, given." The word being repeated, "because, " says Bp. Patrick, "the children of Israel had devoted them to him, by laying their hands upon them ( ), and Aaron had waved them as a wave-offering to the Lord" ( ). instead of such Houbigant, on the authority of the Samaritan, reads, "instead of every first-born of the children of Israel, who openeth the womb." \textsuperscript{17} all the; on the day; I sanctified \textsuperscript{19} I have given; a gift Heb. given that there \textsuperscript{21} were purified, offered, Aaron made \textsuperscript{22} after that;, as the Lord \textsuperscript{24} from twenty In, the Levites are appointed to the service of the tabernacle at the age of 30 years; and in, they are ordered to commence their work at 20 years of age. In order to reconcile this apparent discrepancy, it is to be observed: 1. At the time of which Moses speaks in, the Levitical service was exceedingly severe, and consequently required full grown, robust men, to perform it; the age of 30 was therefore appointed as the period for commencing this service, the weightier part of which was probably there intended. 2. In this place God seems to speak of the service in a general way. Hence the age of 25 is fixed. 3. In David's time, and afterwards, in the fixed tabernacle and temple, the laboriousness of the service no longer existed, and hence 20 years was the age appointed.;, wait upon Heb. war the warfare of, etc. \textsuperscript{25} cease waiting upon the service thereof Heb. return from the warfare of the service; The Levites, above fifty years of age, might superintend and assist their junior brethren in the ordinary offices, and give them and the people counsel and instruction; but they were exempted from carrying the tabernacle and from other laborious services. It is remarkable, that no law was made concerning the age at which the priests should begin to officiate, and though various blemishes disqualified them for the service of the sanctuary, yet they continued their ministrations till death, if capable. On the other hand, nothing is said concerning any bodily defects or blemishes disqualifying the Levites; but the time of their service is expressly settled. Their work was far more laborious than that of the priests; it is therefore likely that the priests would not begin very early to officiate; and the wisdom and experience of age would increase, rather than diminish, their fitness for the sacred duties of their office.\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 9}
\markright{NUMBERS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sina in the second year after they had gone forth from the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak, and let the children of Israel keep the passover in its season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} On the fourteenth day of the first month at even, you shall keep it in its season; you shall keep it according to its law, and according to its ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses ordered the children of Israel to sacrifice the passover, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} on the fourteenth day of the first month in the wilderness of Sina, as the Lord appointed Moses, so the children of Israel did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there came men who were unclean by reason of a dead body, and they were not able to keep the passover on that day; and they came before Moses and Aaron on that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And those men said to Moses, We are unclean by reason of the dead body of a man: shall we therefore fail to offer the gift to the Lord in its season in the midst of the children of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses said to them, stand there, and I will hear what charge the Lord will give concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Whatever man shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or on a journey far off, among you, or among your posterity; he shall then keep the passover to the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} in the second month, on the fourteenth day; in the evening they shall offer it, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs shall they eat it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They shall not leave of it until the morrow, and they shall not break a bone of it; they shall sacrifice it according to the ordinance of the passover. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And whatever man shall be clean, and is not far off on a journey, and shall fail to keep the passover, that soul shall be cut off from his people, because he has not offered the gift to the Lord in its season: that man shall bear his iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if there should come to you a stranger in your land, and should keep the passover to the Lord, he shall keep it according to the law of the passover and according to its ordinance: there shall be one law for you, both for the stranger, and for the native of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And in the day in which the tabernacle was pitched the cloud covered the tabernacle, the place of the testimony; and in the evening there was upon the tabernacle as the appearance of fire till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So it was continually: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when the cloud went up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel departed; and in whatever place the cloud rested, there the children of Israel encamped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The children of Israel shall encamp by the command of the Lord, and by the command of the Lord they shall remove: all the days in which the cloud overshadows the tabernacle, the children of Israel shall encamp. And whenever the cloud shall be drawn over the tabernacle for many days, then the children of Israel shall keep the charge of God, and they shall not remove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it shall be, whenever the cloud overshadows the tabernacle a number of days, they shall encamp by the word of the Lord, and shall remove by the command of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it shall come to pass, whenever the cloud shall remain from the evening till the morning, and in the morning the cloud shall go up, then shall they remove by day or by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} When the cloud continues a full month overshadowing the tabernacle, the children of Israel shall encamp, and shall not depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For they shall depart by the command of the Lord: - they kept the charge of the Lord by the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.\par

\subsection*{Numbers 10}
\markright{NUMBERS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Make to yourself two silver trumpets: you shall make them of beaten work; and they shall be to you for the purpose of calling the assembly, and of removing the camps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall sound with them, and all the congregation shall be gathered to the door of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if they shall sound with one, all the rulers even the princes of Israel shall come to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you⌃ shall sound an alarm, and the camps pitched eastward shall begin to move. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall sound a second alarm, and the camps pitched southward shall move; and you⌃ shall sound a third alarm, and the camps pitched westward shall move forward; and you⌃ shall sound a fourth alarm, and they that encamp toward the north shall move forward: they shall sound an alarm at their departure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And whenever you⌃ shall gather the assembly, you⌃ shall sound, but not an alarm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the priests the sons of Aaron shall sound with the trumpets; and it shall be a perpetual ordinance for you throughout your generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if you⌃ shall go forth to war in your land against your enemies that are opposed to you, then shall you⌃ sound with the trumpets; and you⌃ shall be had in remembrance before the Lord, and you⌃ shall be saved from your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And in the days of your gladness, and in your feasts, and in your new moons, you⌃ shall sound with the trumpets at your whole burnt offerings, and at the sacrifices of your peace-offerings; and there shall be a memorial for you before your God: I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud went up from the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the children of Israel set forward with their baggage in the wilderness of Sina; and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Pharan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the first rank departed by the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they first set in motion the order of the camp of the children of Juda with their host; and over their host [was] Naasson, son of Aminadab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And over the host of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, [was] Nathanael son of Sogar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zabulon, [was] Eliab the son of Chaelon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they shall take down the tabernacle, and the sons of Gedson shall set forward, and the sons of Merari, who bear the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the order of the camp of Ruben set forward with their host; and over their host [was] Elisur the son of Sediur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And over the host of the tribe of the sons of Symeon, [was] Salamiel son of Surisadai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad, [was] Elisaph the son of Raguel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the sons of Caath shall set forward bearing the holy things, and [the others] shall set up the tabernacle until they arrive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the order of the camp of Ephraim shall set forward with their forces; and over their forces [was] Elisama the son of Semiud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And over the forces of the tribes of the sons of Manasse, [was] Gamaliel the [son] of Phadassur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And over the forces of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, [was] Abidan the [son] of Gadeoni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the order of the camp of the sons of Dan shall set forward the last of all the camps, with their forces: and over their forces [was] Achiezer the [son] of Amisadai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And over the forces of the tribe of the sons of Aser, [was] Phageel the son of Echran. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And over the forces of the tribe of the sons of Nephthali, [was] Achire the son of Aenan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} These [are] the armies of the children of Israel; and they set forward with their forces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses said to Obab the son of Raguel the Madianite, the father-in-law of Moses, We are going forward to the place concerning which the Lord said, This will I give to you: Come with us, and we will do you good, for the Lord has spoken good concerning Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he said to him, I will not go, but [I will go] to my land and to my kindred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said, Leave us not, because you have been with us in the wilderness, and you shall be an elder among us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And it shall come to pass if you will go with us, it shall even come to pass that in whatever things the Lord shall do us good, we will also do you good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they departed from the mount of the Lord a three days' journey; and the ark of the covenant of the Lord went before them a three days' journey to provide rest for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the cloud overshadowed them by day, when they departed from the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And it came to pass when the ark set forward, that Moses said, Arise, O Lord, and let your enemies be scattered: let all that hate you flee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And in the resting he said, Turn again, O Lord, the thousands [and] tens of thousands in Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{10} Gk. vocab: anamnesis (ἀνάμνησις) = remembrance; memorial. Common English renderings: remembrance. A memorial or recollective remembrance.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} two trumpets The necessity of such instruments will at once appear, when the amazing extent of this army is considered. There were various kinds of trumpets among the ancients, of different forms and materials, as Eustathius shews on Homer, where he mentions six; the second of which was στρογγυλη, turned up round, like a ram's horn; which he says the Egyptians used (from being invented by Osiris) when they assembled the people to their sacrifices. But in opposition to that form, Moses commands these to be made long, in the shape of those used at present. So Josephus informs us, who says they were near a cubit long; the tube of the thickness of a common pipe or flute; the mouth no wider than just to admit blowing into them; and their ends wide like those of a modern trumpet.; of a whole piece; the calling \textsuperscript{6} ye blow A single alarm was a signal for the eastward division to march; two such alarms the signal for the south; and probably three for the west, and four for the North. \subsection*{Numbers 11}
\markright{NUMBERS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the people murmured sinfully before the Lord; and the Lord heard [them] and was very angry; and fire was kindled among them from the Lord, and devoured a part of the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the people cried to Moses: and Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire was quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the name of that place was called Burning; for a fire was kindled among them from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the mixed multitude among them lusted exceedingly; and they and the children of Israel sat down and wept and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt freely; and the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the garlic, and the onions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But now our soul is dried up; our eyes [turn] to nothing but to the manna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the manna is as coriander seed, and the appearance of it the appearance of hoarfrost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the people went through the field, and gathered, and ground it in the mill, or pounded it in a mortar, and baked it in a pan, and made cakes of it; and the sweetness of it was as the taste [of] wafer made with oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when the dew came upon the camp by night, the manna came down upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses heard them weeping by their families, every one in his door: and the Lord was very angry; and the thing was evil in the sight of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses said to the Lord, Why have you afflicted your servant, and why have I not found grace in your sight, that you should lay the weight of this people upon me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Have I conceived all this people, or have I born them? that you say to me, Take them into your bosom, as a nurse would take her suckling, into the land which you swore to their fathers? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whence have I flesh to give to all this people? for they weep to me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I shall not be able to bear this people alone, for this thing is too heavy for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And if you do thus to me, kill me utterly, if I have found favor with you, that I may not see my affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord said to Moses, Gather me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you yourself know that they are the elders of the people, and their scribes; and you shall bring them to the tabernacle of witness, and they shall stand there with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I will go down, and speak there with you; and I will take of the spirit that is upon you, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear together with you the burden of the people, and you shall not bear them alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And to the people you shall say, Purify yourselves for the morrow, and you⌃ shall eat flesh; for you⌃ wept before the Lord, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: and the Lord shall allow you to eat flesh, and you⌃ shall eat flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You⌃ shall not eat one day, nor two, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} you⌃ shall eat for a full month, until [the flesh] come out at your nostrils; and it shall be nausea to you, because you⌃ disobeyed the Lord, who is among you, and wept before him, saying, What had we to do to come out of Egypt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Moses said, The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand footmen; and you said, I will give them flesh to eat, and they shall eat a whole month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Shall sheep and oxen be slain for them, and shall it suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, and shall it suffice them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord said to Moses, Shall not the hand of the Lord be fully sufficient? now shall you know whether my word shall come to pass to you or not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Moses went out, and spoke the words of the Lord to the people; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and he set them round about the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and put it upon the seventy men that were elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied and ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And there were two men left in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Modad; and the spirit rested upon them, and these were of the number of them that were enrolled, but they did not come to the tabernacle; and they prophesied in the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And a young man ran and told Moses, and spoke, saying, Eldad and Modad prophesy in the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Joshua the son of Naue, who attended on Moses, the chosen one, said, [My] lord Moses, forbid them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Moses said to him, Are you jealous on my account? and would that all the Lord's people were prophets; whenever the Lord shall put his spirit upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Moses departed into the camp, himself and the elders of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And there went forth a wind from the Lord, and brought quails over from the sea; and it brought them down upon the camp a day's journey on this side, and a day's journey on that side, round about the camp, as it were two cubits from the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the people rose up all the day, and all the night, and all the next day, and gathered quails; he that gathered least, gathered ten measures; and they refreshed themselves round about the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The flesh was yet between their teeth, before it failed, when the Lord was angry with the people, and the Lord struck the people with a very great plague. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the name of that place was called the Graves of Lust; for there they buried the people that lusted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} The people departed from the Graves of Lust to Aseroth; and the people halted at Aseroth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And when, ;, ; complained or, were as it were complainers it displeased the Lord Heb. it was evil in the ears of the Lord; *marg. and the fire; the uttermost \textsuperscript{2} cried; prayed; the fire; was quenched Heb. sunk \textsuperscript{3} Taberah that is, a burning \textsuperscript{4} the mixed; fell a lusting Heb. lusted a lust the children wept again Heb. returned and wept Who shall \textsuperscript{5} the fish; the cucumbers In Hebrew, kishshuim, in Arabic, kiththa, Chaldee, keta, and Syriac, kati, a species of cucumber peculiar to Egypt, smooth, of a longish cylindrical shape, and about a foot long. Prosper Alpinus says that it differs from the common sort by its size, colour, and softness; that its leaves are smaller, whiter, softer, and rounder; its fruit larger, greener, smoother, softer, sweeter, and more easy of digestion than ours. Hasselquist describes it in the same manner; and adds, that it is very little watery, but firm like a melon, sweet and cool to the taste, but not so cold as the watermelon, which is meant by the avutichim of the text. \textsuperscript{7} the manna; colour thereof as the colour of Heb. eye of it as the eye of bdellium \textsuperscript{8} the people; baked it taste of it \textsuperscript{10} weep throughout, ; the anger; Moses \textsuperscript{11} Wherefore hast thou The complaint and remonstrance of Moses in these verses serve at once to shew the deeply distressed state of his mind, and the degradation of the minds of the people.; , ; wherefore have \textsuperscript{12} Carry them; as a nursing; the land \textsuperscript{15} kill me; let me not; my wretchedness Two of Dr. Kennicott's manuscripts read, "their wretchedness." The Jerusalem Targum has the same, and adds, by way of explanation, "who are thine own people." \textsuperscript{17} I will come; talk with;, I will take; they shall \textsuperscript{18} Sanctify; ye have wept; it was well \textsuperscript{19} About a year before this, the people had been thus feasted for one day ( ); but now such plenty was to be afforded them for a whole month, and they should use it so greedily, that at last they should entirely loathe the food for which they had so inordinately craved. \textsuperscript{20} whole month Heb. month of days, and it; despised \textsuperscript{22} There is certainly a considerable measure of weakness and unbelief manifested in these complaints and questions of Moses; but his conduct appears at the same time so very simple, honest, and affectionate, that we cannot but admire it, while we wonder that he had not stronger confidence in that God, whose stupendous miracles he had so often witnessed in Egypt. \textsuperscript{23} Is the Lord's That is, "Is the power of the Lord diminished?" That power which has been so signally displayed on your behalf, and which is as unchangeable as it is unlimited.; thou shalt \textsuperscript{25} came down; took; gave it From this place, Origen and Theodoret take occasion to compare Moses to a lamp, at which seventy others were lighted, without any diminution of its lustre. they prophesied By prophesying here we are to understand, their performing those civil and sacred functions for which they were qualified; exhorting the people to quiet and peaceable submission, and to trust and confidence in the providence of God. \textsuperscript{31} a wind, ; and brought; quails That the word selav means the quail, we have already had occasion to observe; to which we subjoin the authority of Mr. Maundrell, who visited Naplosa (the ancient Sichem), where the Samaritans live. Mr. Maundrell asked their chief priest what sort of animal he took the selav to be. He answered, they were a sort of fowls; and, by the description Mr. Maundrell perceived he meant the same kind with our quails. a day's journey Heb. the way of a day and as it were two cubits That is, as the Vulgate renders, Volabantque in aere duobus cubitis altitudine super terram, "and they flew in the air, at the height of two cubits above the ground." \textsuperscript{34} Kibrothhattaavah that is, the graves of lust \textsuperscript{35} journeyed unto Hazeroth; abode at Heb. they were in, etc.\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 12}
\markright{NUMBERS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Mariam and Aaron spoke against Moses, because of the Ethiopian woman whom Moses took; for he had taken an Ethiopian woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they said, Has the Lord spoken to Moses only? has he not also spoken to us? and the Lord heard it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the man Moses was very meek beyond all the men that were upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said immediately to Moses and Aaron and Mariam, Come forth all three of you to the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the three came forth to the tabernacle of witness; and the Lord descended in a pillar of a cloud, and stood at the door of the tabernacle of witness; and Aaron and Mariam were called; and both came forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to them, Hear my words: If there should be of you a prophet to the Lord, I will be made known to him in a vision, and in sleep will I speak to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} My servant Moses [is] not so; he is faithful in all my house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I will speak to him mouth to mouth apparently, and not in dark speeches; and he has seen the glory of the Lord; and why were you⌃ not afraid to speak against my servant Moses? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the great anger of the Lord [was] upon them, and he departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the cloud departed from the tabernacle; and, behold, Mariam was leprous, [white] as snow; and Aaron looked upon Mariam, and, behold, she [was] leprous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Aaron said to Moses, I beseech you, my lord, do not lay sin upon us, for we were ignorant wherein we sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let her not be as it were like death, as an abortion coming out of his mother's womb, when [the disease] devours the half of the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses cried to the Lord, saying, O God, I beseech you, heal her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord said to Moses, If her father had only spit in her face, would she not be ashamed seven days? let her be set apart seven days without the camp, and afterwards she shall come in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Mariam was separated without the camp seven days; and the people moved not forward till Mariam was cleansed.\par

\subsection*{Numbers 13}
\markright{NUMBERS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And afterwards the people set forth from Aseroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Pharan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Send for you men, and let them spy the land of the Chananites, which I give to the sons of Israel for a possession; one man for a tribe, you shall send them away according to their families, every one of them a prince. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moses sent them out of the wilderness of Pharan by the word of the Lord; all these [were] the princes of the sons of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And these [are] their names: of the tribe of Ruben, Samuel the son of Zachur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Of the tribe of Symeon, Saphat the son of Suri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Of the tribe of Judah, Chaleb the son of Jephonne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Of the tribe of Issachar, Ilaal the son of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Of the tribe of Ephraim, Ause the son of Naue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Of the tribe of Benjamin, Phalti the son of Raphu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Of the tribe of Zabulon, Gudiel the son of Sudi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Of the tribe of Joseph of the sons of Manasse, Gaddi the son of Susi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Of the tribe of Dan, Amiel the son of Gamali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Of the tribe of Aser, Sathur the son of Michael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Of the tribe of Nephthali, Nabi the son of Sabi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Of the tribe of Gad, Gudiel the son of Macchi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} These [are] the names of the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land; and Moses called Ause the son of Naue, Joshua. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Chanaan, and said to them, Go up by this wilderness; and you⌃ shall go up to the mountain, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and you⌃ shall see the land, what it is, and the people that dwells on it, whether it is strong or weak, or [whether] they are few or many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And what the land is on which they dwell, [whether] it is good or bad; and what the cities are wherein these dwell, whether they dwell in walled [cities] or unwalled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And what the land is, whether rich or poor; whether there are trees in it or no: and you⌃ shall persevere and take of the fruits of the land: and the days [were] the days of spring, the forerunners of the grape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they went up and surveyed the land from the wilderness of Sin to Rhoob, as men go in to Aemath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they went up by the wilderness, and departed as far as Chebron; and there [was] Achiman, and Sessi, and Thelami, the progeny of Enach. Now Chebron was built seven years before Tanin of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they came to the valley of the cluster and surveyed it; and they cut down thence a bough and one cluster of grapes upon it, and bore it on staves, and [they took] of the pomegranates and the figs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they called that place, The valley of the cluster, because of the cluster which the children of Israel cut down from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they returned from thence, having surveyed the land, after forty days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they proceeded and came to Moses and Aaron and all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Pharan Cades; and they brought word to them and to all the congregation, and they showed the fruit of the land: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and they reported to him, and said, We came into the land into which you sent us, a land flowing with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Only the nation that dwells upon it is bold, and they have very great and strong walled towns, and we saw there the children of Enach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Amalec dwells in the land toward the south: and the Chettite and the Evite, and the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwells in the hill country: and the Chananite dwells by the sea, and by the river Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Chaleb stayed the people from speaking before Moses, and said to him, Nay, but we will go up by all means, and will inherit it, for we shall surely prevail against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But the men that went up together with him said, We will not go up, for we shall not by any means be able to go up against the nation, for it is much stronger than we. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they brought a horror of that land which they surveyed upon the children of Israel, saying, The land which we passed by to survey it, is a land that eats up its inhabitants; and all the people whom we saw in it are men of extraordinary stature. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And there we saw the giants; and we were before them as locusts, yes even so were we before them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Name meaning: Caleb (Kalev) — Whole-hearted; dog Followed the LORD fully; faithful like a dog.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Send thou; of every, a ruler \textsuperscript{3} The wilderness of Paran, says Dr. Wells, seems to have been taken in a larger, and in a stricter sense. In the larger sense, it seems to have denoted all the desert and mountainous tract, lying between the wilderness of Shur westward, and mount Seir, or the land of Edom, eastward, the land of Canaan northward, and the Red sea southward. And in this sense, it seems to have comprehended the wilderness of Sin, and the wilderness of Sinai, also the adjoining tract wherein lay Kibroth-hattaavah and Hazeroth. In this sense it may be understood in, where, by "that great and terrible wilderness, " is intended the wilderness of Paran in its largest acceptation; for, in its stricter acceptation, it seems not to have been so great and terrible a wilderness; but is taken to denote more peculiarly that part of Arabia Petrea which lies between mount Sinai and Hazeroth west, and mount Seir east. \textsuperscript{20} whether it be; good courage;, ; the firstripe \textsuperscript{21} from the wilderness of Zin The wilderness of Zin, is different from that called Sin ( ). The latter was near Egypt, but the former was near Kadesh Barnea, not far from the borders of Canaan. It seems to be the valley mentioned by Burckhardt; which, under the names of El Ghor and El Araba, form a continuation of the valley of the Jordan, extending from the Dead sea to the eastern branch of the Red sea. The whole plain presents to the view an appearance of shifting sands, whose surface is broken by innumerable undulations and low hills. A few talk, tamarisk, and rethem trees grow among the sand hills; but the depth of sand precludes all vegetation of herbage., ; Rehob was a city, afterwards given to the tribe of Asher, situated near mount Lebanon, at the northern extremity of the Promised Land, on the road which leads to Hamath, and west of Laish or Dan. Compare; . \subsection*{Numbers 14}
\markright{NUMBERS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried; and the people wept all that night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron; and all the congregation said to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Would we had died in the land of Egypt! or in this wilderness, would we had died! and why does the Lord bring us into this land to fall in war? our wives and our children shall be for a prey: now then it is better to return into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they said one to another, Let us make a ruler, and return into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Moses and Aaron fell upon their face before all the congregation of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But Joshua the [son] of Naue, and Chaleb the [son] of Jephonne, of [the number of] them that spied out the land, tore their garments, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, The land which we surveyed is indeed extremely good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If the Lord choose us, he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which flows with milk and honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Only depart not from the Lord; and fear you⌃ not the people of the land, for they are meat for us; for the season [of prosperity] is departed from them, but the Lord [is] among us: fear them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all the congregation bade stone them with stones; and the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud on the tabernacle of witness to all the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to Moses, How long does this people provoke me? and how long do they refuse to believe me for all the signs which I have wrought among them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I will strike them with death, and destroy them; and I will make of you and of your father's house a great nation, and much greater than this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Moses said to the Lord, So Egypt shall hear, for you have brought up this people from them by your might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Moreover all the dwellers upon this land have heard that you are Lord in the midst of this people, who, O Lord, are seen [by them] face to face, and your cloud rests upon them, and you go before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And [if] you shall destroy this nation as one man; then all the nations that have heard your name shall speak, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Because the Lord could not bring this people into the land which he swore to them, he has overthrown them in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And now, O Lord, let your strength be exalted, as you spoke, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The Lord [is] longsuffering and merciful, and true, removing transgressions and iniquities and sins, and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Forgive this people their sin according to your great mercy, as you were favourable to them from Egypt until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord said to Moses, I am gracious to them according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But [as] I live and my name is living, so the glory of the Lord shall fill all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For all the men who see my glory, and the signs which I wrought in Egypt, and in the wilderness, and have tempted me this tenth time, and have not listened to my voice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} surely they shall not see the land, which I swore to their fathers; but their children which are with me here, as many as know not good or evil, every inexperienced youth, to them will I give the land; but none who have provoked me shall see it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But my servant Chaleb, because there was another spirit in him, and he followed me, I will bring him into the land into which he entered, and his seed shall inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But Amalec and the Chananite dwell in the valley: to-morrow turn and depart for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} How long [shall I endure] this wicked congregation? I have heard their murmurings against me, [even] the murmuring of the children of Israel, which they have murmured concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Say to them, [As] I live, says the Lord: surely as you⌃ spoke into my ears, so will I do to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness; and all those of you that were reviewed, and those of you that were numbered from twenty years old and upward, all that murmured against me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} you⌃ shall not enter into the land for which I stretched out my hand to establish you upon it; {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} It is very probable, that the transactions recorded in this and the four following chapters took place during the time the Israelites abode in Kadesh ( ). \textsuperscript{3} will make, ;, a burnt a sacrifice; performing Heb. separating, or in a freewill;, in your, ; a sweet; the herd Under the term bakar, are comprehended the ox, heifer, etc; and under tzon, are included sheep and goats. The animals enjoined in the Levitical law are the very same which commanded Abraham to offer ( ). Hence it is evident, that God delivered to the patriarchs an epitome of that law which was afterwards given in detail to Moses, the essence of which consisted in its sacrifices; and these sacrifices were of clean animals, the most perfect, useful, and healthy of all that are brought under the immediate government of man. Gross feeding and ferocious animals were all excluded, as well as all birds of prey. \textsuperscript{19} The oblation before prescribed seems to have been a general acknowledgment from the people at large; but this was an oblation from every one that reaped a harvest. Who was required, previously to tasting it himself, to offer a portion of dough as a heave-offering to the Lord. This is supposed to have been given to the priests in their several cities, and not carried to the tabernacle. \textsuperscript{20} a cake; the heave offering \textsuperscript{22} This law concerning sins of ignorance, being entirely diverse from one before considered, occasions considerable difficulty ( ). Some explain that law as relating to sins of commission, this to sins of omission. Others explain the one of inadvertent violations of the moral law, and the other of the transgressions of the ceremonial law, and some think that related to the whole nation, this to any one tribe; or that to the bulk of the nation, this to the rulers and elders. The Jews say, that the former law referred to such national transgressions through heedlessness, as consisted with the maintenance of the prescribed worship in the main; but that this especially respected the case of the nation, when through inattention, and the example and authority of wicked rulers, they had turned aside and committed idolatry, or conducted their worship directly contrary to law; yet through a culpable ignorance, and not in presumption. This was evidently the case under several of their kings; and the explanation seems well grounded. \textsuperscript{24} if ought without Heb. from the eyes one young bullock with his manner or, ordinance one kid \textsuperscript{29} one law; sinneth Heb. doeth \textsuperscript{30} doeth ought; presumptuously Heb. with an high hand, That is, bold, daring, deliberate acts of transgression against the fullest evidence, and in despite of the Divine authority. Such conduct "reproacheth the Lord, " as if his commands were needless, unreasonable, and inimical to the happiness of man; his favour were not desirable, or his wrath not to be feared. In short, as if it were more advantageous to rebel against him than to serve him. Such acts admitted of no atonement. The person was condemned to bear his own iniquity, and to be cut off. reproacheth \textsuperscript{32} they found a man This example seems to have been evidently introduced to illustrate the foregoing law. The man despised the word of the Lord, presumptuously broke his commandment, and on this ground was punished with death. \textsuperscript{38} fringes in the borders The word tzitzith properly denotes an ornament resembling a flower. From, we learn that these were emblematical of the commands of God. That there is any analogy between a fringe and a precept, it would be bold to assert; but when a thing is appointed to represent another, no matter how different, that first object becomes the legitimate representative or sign of the other. \textsuperscript{39} remember; ye seek not; go a whoring\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 16}
\markright{NUMBERS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Core the son of Isaar the son of Caath the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiron, sons of Eliab, and Aun the son of Phaleth the son of Ruben, spoke; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and rose up before Moses, and two hundred and fifty men of the sons of Israel, chiefs of the assembly, chosen councillors, and men of renown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} They rose up against Moses and Aaron, and said, Let it be enough for you that all the congregation [are] holy, and the Lord [is] among them; and why do you⌃ set up yourselves against the congregation of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when Moses heard it, he fell on his face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he spoke to Core and all his assembly, saying, God has visited and known those that are his and who are holy, and has brought them to himself; and whom he has chosen for himself, he has brought to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} This do you⌃: take to yourselves censers, Core and all his company; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and put fire on them, and put incense on them before the Lord to-morrow; and it shall come to pass that the man whom the Lord has chosen, he shall be holy: let it be enough for you, you⌃ sons of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses said to Core, Listen to me, you⌃ sons of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Is it a little thing for you, that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, and brought you near to himself to minister in the services of the tabernacle of the Lord, and to stand before the tabernacle to minister for them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he has brought you near and all your brethren the sons of Levi with you, and do you⌃ seek to be priests also? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus [it is with] you and all your congregation which is gathered together against God: and who is Aaron, that you⌃ murmur against him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiron sons of Eliab; and they said, We will not go up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Is it a little thing that you have brought us up to a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, [and] that you altogether rule over us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You are a prince, and have you brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, and have you given us an inheritance of land and vineyards? would you have put out the eyes of those men? we will not go up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Moses was exceeding indignant, and said to the Lord, Do you take no heed to their sacrifice: I have not taken away the desire of any one of them, neither have I hurt any one of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Moses said to Core, Sanctify your company, and be ready before the Lord, you and Aaron and they, to-morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And take each man his censer, and you⌃ shall put incense upon them, and shall bring each one his censer before the Lord, two hundred and fifty censers, and you and Aaron shall bring each his censer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And each man took his censer, and they put on them fire, and laid incense on them; and Moses and Aaron stood by the doors of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Core raised up against them all his company by the door of the tabernacle of witness; and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Separate your selves from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them at once. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they fell on their faces, and said, O God, the God of spirits and of all flesh, if one man has sinned, [shall] the wrath of the Lord [be] upon the whole congregation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Speak to the congregation, saying, Depart from the company of Core round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Moses rose up and went to Dathan and Abiron, and all the elders of Israel went with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he spoke to the congregation, saying, Separate yourselves from the tents of these stubborn men, and touch nothing that belongs to them, lest you⌃ be consumed with them in all their sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they stood aloof from the tent of Core round about; and Dathan and Abiron went forth and stood by the doors of their tents, and their wives and their children and their store. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Moses said, Hereby shall you⌃ know that the Lord has sent me to perform all these works, that [I have] not [done them] of myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} If these men shall die according to the death of all men, if also their visitation shall be according to the visitation of all men, then the Lord has not sent me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But if the Lord shall show by a wonder, and the earth shall open her mouth and swallow them up, and their houses, and their tents, and all that belongs to them, and they shall go down alive into Hades, then you⌃ shall know that these men have provoked the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And when he ceased speaking all these words, the ground clave asunder beneath them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the ground opened, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that were with Core, and their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they went down and all that they had, alive into Hades; and the ground covered them, and they perished from the midst of the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And all Israel round about them fled from the sound of them, for they said, Lest the earth swallow us up [also]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And fire went forth from the Lord, and devoured the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the Lord said to Moses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, Take up the brazen censers out of the midst of the men that have been burnt, and scatter the strange fire yonder, for they have sanctified the censers {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} of these sinners against their own souls, and do you make them beaten plates a covering to the altar, because they were brought before the Lord and hallowed; and they became a sign to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest took the brazen censers, which the men who had been burnt brought near, and they put them as a covering on the altar: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} a memorial to the children of Israel that no stranger might draw near, who is not of the seed of Aaron, to offer incense before the Lord; so he shall not be as Core and as they that conspired with him, as the Lord spoke to him by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And the children of Israel murmured the next day against Moses and Aaron, saying, You⌃ have killed the people of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And it came to pass when the congregation combined against Moses and Aaron, that they ran impetuously to the tabernacle of witness; and the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And Moses and Aaron went in, in front of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Depart out of the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them at once: and they fell upon their faces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Moses said to Aaron, Take a censer, and put on it fire from the altar, and put incense on it, and carry it away quickly into the camp, and make atonement for them; for wrath is gone forth from the presence of the Lord, it has begun to destroy the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And Aaron took as Moses spoke to him, and ran among the congregation, for already the plague had begun among the people; and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides those that died on account of Core. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And Aaron returned to Moses to the door of the tabernacle of witness, and the plague ceased.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Korah; sons of Reuben; took men As the word men is not in the text, some read "took counsel; " and some "took courage." Houbigant renders yikkach, rebellionem fecerunt, "they rebelled; " which scarcely any rule of criticism can ever justify. Dr. Geddes' translation is, "Another insurrection was raised against Moses by Korah, " etc. Others think that it may mean, "behaved with insolence." But, as Dr. A. Clarke observes, the verb wyyikkach, "and he took" which though at the end of the sentence in English, is the first word in Hebrew, is not in the plural, but the singular; and hence cannot be applied to the acts of all these chiefs. In every part of the Scripture, where this rebellion is referred to, it is attributed to Korah, therefore the verb here belongs to him; and the whole verse should be translated, "Now Korah, son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, he took even Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, son of Reuben, and they rose up, " etc.; reading, with some manuscripts, the Samaritan, and Septuagint, ben, son, instead of beney, sons. \textsuperscript{3} gathered, ; Ye take too much upon you Heb. It is much for you all the; the Lord \textsuperscript{5} the Lord; who is holy; will cause; even him \textsuperscript{7} that the man; too much \textsuperscript{13} a small out of a;, to kill; thou make \textsuperscript{14} Moreover; put out Heb. bore out \textsuperscript{15} very wroth; Respect; I have not Though Moses was their ruler, under God, yet, so far from oppressing them, he had not imposed the smallest tax, nor taken, as a present, so much as an ass from one of them. The common present that is now made to the great, in these countries, is a horse; but there is reason to believe, that an ass might formerly have answered the same purpose. "If it is a visit of ceremony from a bashaw, " says Dr. Russell, "or other person in power, a fine horse, sometimes with furniture, or some such valuable present, is made to him at his departure." As asses were esteemed no dishonourable beasts for the saddle, Sir. J. Chardin, in his manuscript, supposes, that when Samuel disclaimed having taken the ass of any one ( ), he is to be understood of not having taken any ass for his riding. In the same light, he considers this similar declaration of Moses. His reason is "asses being then esteemed very honourable creatures for riding on (; ), as they are at this very time in Persia, being rode with saddles." \textsuperscript{22} they fell, the God; one man sin \textsuperscript{24} It should seem that Dathan and Abiram had set up a spacious tabernacle in the midst of the tents of their families, where they kept court, met in council, and hung out their flag of defiance against Moses; it is here called the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. There, as in the place of rendezvous, Dathan and Abiram stayed, when Korah and his friends went up to the tabernacle of the Lord, waiting the issue of their trial; but here we are told how they had their business done, before that trial was over.
