\subsection*{Numbers 17}
\markright{NUMBERS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, and take rods of them, according to the houses of their families, a rod from all their princes, according to the houses of their families, twelve rods, and write the name of each on his rod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And write the name of Aaron on the rod of Levi; for it is one rod [for each]: they shall give [them] according to the tribe of the house of their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall put them in the tabernacle of witness, before the testimony, where I will be made known to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it shall be, the man whom I shall choose, his rod shall blossom; and I will remove from me the murmuring of the children of Israel, which they murmur against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and all their chiefs gave him a rod [each], for one chief a rod, according to the house of their families, twelve rods; and the rod of Aaron [was] in the midst of the rods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses laid up the rods before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi blossomed, and put forth a bud, and bloomed blossoms and produced almonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses brought forth all the rods from before the Lord to all the sons of Israel; and they looked, and each one took his rod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said to Moses, Lay up the rod of Aaron before the testimonies to be kept as a sign for the children of the disobedient; and let their murmuring cease from me, and they shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded Moses, so did they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the children of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, Behold, we are cut off, we are destroyed, we are consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Every one that touches the tabernacle of the Lord, dies: shall we die utterly?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a rod The word matteh signifies a staff, or sceptre, which the prince or chief of each tribe bore, and which was the sign of office or royalty among almost all the people of the earth. all their princes, twelve rods \textsuperscript{5} Whom I blossom;, ; I will; they murmur \textsuperscript{6} a rod apiece, for each prince one Heb. a rod for one prince, a rod for one prince \textsuperscript{8} the rod of Aaron This fact was so unquestionably miraculous, that no doubt could remain on the minds of the people, or the envious chiefs, of the divine appointment of Aaron, and as there were buds, blossoms, and fruit on the rod at the same time, which was never the case with branches in the natural and ordinary course, this evidently proved the miracle, and took away all suspicion of the fraud which has been impiously suggested, that Moses had taken away Aaron's rod in the night time, and put a living branch of an almond tree in the room of it. A sceptre or staff of office resuming its vegetative life, was considered an absolute impossibility among the ancients; and as they were accustomed to swear by their sceptres, this circumstance was added to confirm the oath. budded \textsuperscript{10} Bring Aaron's for a token; rebels Heb. children of rebellion, ; and thou \textsuperscript{12} Behold; we die Gawanoo, "we expire:" it signifies not so much to die simply, as to feel an extreme difficulty in breathing, which producing suffocation, ends at last in death. See the folly and extravagance of this sinful people, in thus rebelling against the authority of those whom Jehovah had appointed to be their rulers.\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 18}
\markright{NUMBERS 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying, You and your sons and your father's house shall bear the sins of the holy things, and you and your sons shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And take to yourself your brethren the tribe of Levi, the family of your father, and let them be joined to you, and let them minister to you; and you and your sons with you [shall minister] before the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they shall keep your charges, and the charges of the tabernacle; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, so both they and you shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they shall be joined to you, and shall keep the charges of the tabernacle of witness, in all the services of the tabernacle; and a stranger shall not approach to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you⌃ shall keep the charges of the holy things, and the charges of the altar, and [so] there shall not be anger among the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I have taken your brethren the Levites out of the midst of the children of Israel, a present given to the Lord, to minister in the services of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you and your sons after you shall keep up your priestly ministration, according to the whole manner of the altar, and that which is within the veil; and you⌃ shall minister in the services as the office of your priesthood; and the stranger that comes near shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord said to Aaron, And, behold, I have given you the charge of the first fruits of all things consecrated to me by the children of Israel; and I have given them to you as an honor, and to your sons after you for a perpetual ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let this be to you from all the holy things that are consecrated [to me, even] the burnt offerings, from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every trespass-offering of theirs, and from all their sin-offerings, whatever things they give to me of all their holy things, they shall be yours and your sons'. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the most holy place shall you⌃ eat them; every male shall eat them, you and your sons: they shall be holy to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And this shall be to you of the first fruits of their gifts, of all the wave-offerings of the children of Israel; to you have I given them and to your sons and your daughters with you, a perpetual ordinance; every clean person in your house shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Every first-offering of oil, and every first-offering of wine, their first fruits of corn, whatever they may give to the Lord, to you have I given them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} All the first fruits that are in their land, whatever they shall offer to the Lord, shall be yours: every clean person in your house shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Every devoted thing among the children of Israel shall be yours. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And every thing that opens the womb of all flesh, whatever they bring to the Lord, whether man or beast, shall be yours: only the firstborn of men shall be surely redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the redemption of them [shall be] from a month old; their valuation of five shekels—it is twenty oboli according to the holy shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves and the firstborn of sheep and the firstborn of goats; they are holy: and you shall pour their blood upon the altar, and you shall offer the fat as a burnt offering for a smell of sweet savor to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the flesh shall be yours, as also the breast of the wave-offering and as the right shoulder, it shall be yours. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Every special offering of the holy things, whatever the children of Israel shall specially offer to the Lord, I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you, a perpetual ordinance: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, for you and your seed after you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord said to Aaron, You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any portion among them; for I [am] your portion and your inheritance in the midst of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And, behold, I have given to the sons of Levi every tithe in Israel for an inheritance for their services, whenever they perform ministry in the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the children of Israel shall no more draw near to the tabernacle of witness to incur fatal guilt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Levite himself shall perform the service of the tabernacle of witness; and they shall bear their iniquities, it is a perpetual statute throughout their generations; and in the midst of the children of Israel they shall not receive an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Because I have given as a distinct portion to the Levites for an inheritance the tithes of the children of Israel, whatever they shall offer to the Lord; therefore I said to them, In the midst of the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} You shall also speak to the Levites, and shall say to them, If you⌃ take the tithe from the children of Israel, which I have given you from them for an inheritance, then shall you⌃ separate from it a heave-offering to the Lord, a tenth of the tenth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And your heave-offerings shall be reckoned to you as corn from the floor, and an offering from the wine-press. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So shall you⌃ also separate them from all the offerings of the Lord out of all your tithes, whatever you⌃ shall receive from the children of Israel; and you⌃ shall give of them an offering to the Lord to Aaron the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Of all your gifts you⌃ shall offer an offering to the Lord, and of every first-fruit the consecrated part from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you shall say to them, When you⌃ shall offer the first fruits from it, then shall it be reckoned to the Levites as produce from the threshing floor, and as produce from the wine-press. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you⌃ shall eat it in any place, you⌃ and your families; for this is your reward for your services in the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you⌃ shall not bear sin by reason of it, for you⌃ shall have offered an offering of first fruits from it, and you⌃ shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, that you⌃ die not.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Thou, ; shall bear To counterbalance the high honour conferred on Aaron and his family, and to allay the fears and abate the envy of the people, it is here declared, that the priest must bear the blame of everything which was not properly conducted in the sanctuary. \textsuperscript{2} joined unto thee There is a fine paronomasia in the original. Levi is desired from lawah, to join, couple, associate; hence Moses says, the Levites yillawoo, "shall be joined, " or associated, with the priests. They shall conjointly perform the sacred office, but the priests shall be principal, the Levites their associates or assistants.; minister, but thou \textsuperscript{6} And I; I have, given \textsuperscript{7} Therefore thou, within; as a service; the stranger \textsuperscript{9} every meat, every sin, every trespass \textsuperscript{11} the heave; unto thee; every one \textsuperscript{12} best of the oil Heb. fat, the firstfruits \textsuperscript{16} shalt thou redeem Redemption of the firstborn is one of the rites which are still practised among the Jews. According to Leo of Modena, it is performed in the following manner: - When the child is thirty days old, the father sends for one of the descendants of Aaron. Several persons being assembled on the occasion, the father brings a cup, containing several pieces of gold and silver coin. The priest then takes the child into his arms, and addressing himself to the mother, he says, "Is this thy son?" Mother. "Yes." Priest. "Hast thou never had another child, male or female, a miscarriage, or untimely birth?" Mother. "No." Priest. "This being the case, this child, as firstborn, belongs to me." Then turning to the father, he says, "If it be thy desire to have this child, thou must redeem it." Father. "I present thee with this gold and silver for this purpose." Priest. "Thou dost wish, therefore, to redeem this child?" Father. "I do wish so to do." The priest then turning himself to the assembly, says, "Very well. This child, as first-born, is mine; as it is written in Bemidbar ( ), Thou shalt redeem the first-born of a month old for five shekels; but I shall content myself with this in exchange." He then takes two gold crowns, or thereabouts, and returns the child to his parents. according; which is \textsuperscript{19} the heave, ; it is a \textsuperscript{20} Thou shalt have The principal part of what was offered to God was the portion of the priests; who had no inheritance of land in Israel. The Rabbins say, 24 gifts were given to the priests; all of which are expressed in the law. 1. The flesh of the sin-offering, 2. The flesh of the trespass-offering, 3. The peace-offering of the congregation, 4. The remainder of the sheaf, 5. The remnants of the meat-offerings, 6. The two loaves, 7. The shew-bread, 8. The log of oil offered by the leper, 9. The breast and shoulder of the peace-offerings, 10. The heave-offering of confession, 11. The heave-offering of the Nazarite's ram, 12. The firstling, 13. The first-fruits, 14. The heave-offering of first-fruits, 15. Of the tithe, Lev. 28 16. The cake, 17. The first of the fleece, 18. The field of possession, Lev. 35 19. The gifts of slain beasts, 20. The redemption of the first-born, 21. The lamb for a firstling ass, 22. That taken by violence from a stranger, 23. All devoted things 24. \subsection*{Numbers 19}
\markright{NUMBERS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} This is the constitution of the law, as the Lord has commanded, saying, Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them take for you a red heifer without spot, which has no spot on her, and on which no yoke has been put. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall give her to Eleazar the priest; and they shall bring her out of the camp into a clean place, and shall kill her before his face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Eleazar shall take of her blood, and sprinkle of her blood seven times in front of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall burn her to ashes before him; and her skin and her flesh and her blood, with her dung, shall be consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet wool, and they shall cast them into the midst of the burning of the heifer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the priest shall wash his garments, and bathe his body in water, and afterwards he shall go into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he that burns her shall wash his garments, and bathe his body, and shall be unclean till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And a clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up in a clean place outside the camp; and they shall be for the congregation of the children of Israel to keep: it is the water of sprinkling, a purification. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he that gathers up the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments, and shall be unclean until evening; and it shall be a perpetual statute for the children of Israel and for the strangers joined to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He that touches the dead body of any man, shall be unclean seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He shall be purified on the third day and the seventh day, and shall be clean; but if he be not purged on the third day and the seventh day, he shall not be clean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Every one that touches the carcass of the person of a man, if he should have died, and [the other] not have been purified, has defiled the tabernacle of the Lord: that soul shall be cut off from Israel, because the water of sprinkling has not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And this [is] the law; if a man die in a house, every one that goes into the house, and all things in the house, shall be unclean seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And every open vessel which has not a covering bound upon it, shall be unclean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And every one who shall touch a man slain by violence, or a corpse, or human bone, or sepulchre, shall be unclean seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they shall take for the unclean of the burnt ashes of purification, and they shall pour upon them running water into a vessel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And a clean man shall take hyssop, and dip it into the water, and sprinkle it upon the house, and the furniture, and all the souls that are therein, and upon him that touched the human bone, or the slain man, or the corpse, or the tomb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the clean man shall sprinkle [the water] on the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall purify himself; and [the other] shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And whatever man shall be defiled and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord, because the water of sprinkling has not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it shall be to you a perpetual statute; and he that sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his garments; and he that touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And whatever the unclean man shall touch shall be unclean, and the soul that touches it shall be unclean till evening.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the ordinance; a red heifer The following curious particulars have been remarked in this ordinance: 1. A heifer was appointed for sacrifice, in opposition to the Egyptian superstition, which held these sacred, and worshipped their goddess Isis under this form; and this appears the more likely, because males only were chosen for sacrifice. So Herodotus says, they sacrifice males, both old and young; but it is not lawful for them to offer females. 2. It was to be a red heifer, because the Egyptians sacrificed red bulls to the evil demon Typhon. 3. It was to be without spot, having no mixture of any other colour. Plutarch says, the Egyptians "sacrifice red bulls, and select them with such scrupulous attention, that if the animal has a single black or white hair, they reckon it αθυτον, unfit to be sacrificed." 4. Without blemish. (See note on .) 5. On which never came yoke. Because an animal which had been used for a common purpose was deemed improper for sacrifice.; no blemish; upon which \textsuperscript{9} clean; lay them up a water of separation That is, water prepared by being mixed with the ashes of the heifer, and set apart for the special purpose of being sprinkled on those who had contracted any legal defilement. To this rite the apostle Paul, in his epistle to the Hebrews. ( ), pointedly alludes: "For if, " says he, "the blood of bulls and of goats, " alluding, probably, to the sin-offerings and the scape-goat, "and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh; how much more shall the blood of Christ, who, through the eternal Spirit, offered himself without spot unto God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God." \textsuperscript{10} wash his, it shall be \textsuperscript{11} toucheth the dead He who touched a dead beast was only unclean for one day (, ); but he who touches a dead man is unclean for seven days. This was certainly designed to show the peculiar impurity and sinfulness of man, and the hatefulness of sin, seven times worse than the vilest animal!, ; man Heb. soul of man \textsuperscript{12} He shall purify Yithchatta, literally, "he shall sin himself, " i.e., not add sin, but take it away, purify. So we say to fleece, and to skin, which do not signify to add a fleece, or a skin, but to take one away.; third day \textsuperscript{13} purifieth;, ;, the water, his uncleanness \textsuperscript{16} toucheth, a bone a grave \textsuperscript{17} ashes Heb. dust, running water shall be put thereto Heb. living waters shall be given, *marg. \textsuperscript{19} shall sprinkle; on the seventh day he\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 20}
\markright{NUMBERS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the children of Israel, [even] the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Sin, in the first month, and the people abode in Cades; and Mariam died there, and was buried there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was no water for the congregation: and they gathered themselves together against Moses and Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people reviled Moses, saying, Would we had died in the destruction of our brethren before the Lord! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And therefore have you⌃ brought up the congregation of the Lord into this wilderness, to kill us and our cattle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And therefore [is] this? You⌃ have brought us up out of Egypt, that we should come into this evil place; a place where there is no sowing, neither figs, nor vines, nor pomegranates, neither is there water to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Moses and Aaron went from before the assembly to the door of the tabernacle of witness, and they fell upon their faces; and the glory of the Lord appeared to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Take your rod, and call the assembly, you and Aaron your brother, and speak you⌃ to the rock before them, and it shall give forth its waters; and you⌃ shall bring forth for them water out of the rock, and give drink to the congregation and their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses took his rod which was before the Lord, as the Lord commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses and Aaron assembled the congregation before the rock, and said to them, Hear me, you⌃ disobedient ones; must we bring you water out of this rock? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses lifted up his hand and struck the rock with his rod twice; and much water came forth, and the congregation drank, and their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, Because you⌃ have not believed me to sanctify me before the children of Israel, therefore you⌃ shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This is the water of Strife, because the children of Israel spoke insolently before the Lord, and he was sanctified in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Moses sent messengers from Cades to the king of Edom, saying, Thus says your brother Israel; You know all the distress that has come upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And [how] our fathers went down into Egypt, and we sojourned in Egypt many days, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And we cried to the Lord, and the Lord heard our voice, and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt; and now we are in the city of Cades, at the extremity of your coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} We will pass through your land: we will not go through the fields, nor through the vineyards, nor will we drink water out of your cistern: we will go by the king's highway; we will not turn aside to the right hand or to the left, until we have passed your borders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Edom said to him, You shall not pass through me, and if otherwise, I will go forth to meet you in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the children of Israel say to him, We will pass by the mountain; and if I and my cattle drink of your water, I will pay you: but it is no matter of importance, we will go by the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said, You shall not pass through me; and Edom went forth to meet him with a great host, and a mighty hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his borders, and Israel turned away from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they departed from Cades; and the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came to Mount Or. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in mount Or, on the borders of the land of Edom, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Let Aaron be added to his people; for you⌃ shall certainly not go into the land which I have given the children of Israel, because you⌃ provoked me at the water of strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Take Aaron, and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to the mount Or before all the congregation; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and take Aaron's apparel from off him, and put it on Eleazar his son: and let Aaron die there and be added to [his people]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and took him up to mount Or, before all the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he took Aaron's garments off him, and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died on the top of the mountain; and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead: and they wept for Aaron thirty days, [even] all the house of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: sela (סֶלַע) = crag; rock. Common English renderings: rock. Often a rocky cliff or crag. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: ya’an (יַעַן) = because. Common English renderings: because. Causal conjunction often in divine speeches.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} An, Ex, Is, 40 Then This was the first month of the fortieth year after the departure from Egypt. (Compare, with of this chapter and .) This year was the last of their journeyings, for from the going out of the spies ( ) unto this time, was about thirty-eight years., into, ; Kadesh This Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, is different from Kadesh-barnea, lying in, or adjoining to the wilderness of Paran, about eight leagues south of Hebron. (See note on ., .) Kadesh is called Rekam, by the Targumists, Rekem, in the Syriac, and Rakim, in Arabic. Rekem, says Rabbi Nissin (in Gittin, chapter 1) is on the east, meaning of the land of Israel.; Miriam \textsuperscript{5} this evil; no place of i.e. "no place for sowing" \textsuperscript{8} the rod;, speak; bring forth \textsuperscript{12} Because ye believed; sanctify; ye shall \textsuperscript{13} the water; Meribah i.e. Strife; Meribah-Kadesh he was \textsuperscript{14} Moses thy brother; befallen us Heb. found us \textsuperscript{15} our fathers; dwelt; vexed us \textsuperscript{22} Kadesh, ; mount Hor Mount Hor was situated in Arabia Petrea, on the confines of Edom. It is described by Burckhardt, as being situated on the western side of a valley called Wady Mousa; in which are found the ruins of the ancient Petra, and which is two long days' journey north-east of Accaba (on the northern point of the Elanitic gulf of the Red sea), in the Djebel Shera, or mount Seir, and on the east side of the Araba, the valley which forms the continuation of that of the Jordan. On the summit of the mountain is the tomb of Haroun, or Aaron, which is held in great veneration by the Arabs; which agrees with the testimonies of Josephus, Eusebius, and Jerome, all persons well acquainted with these countries, who agree in proving that the sepulchre of Aaron, in mount Hor, was near Petra. When visited by Mr. Legh, it was attended by a crippled Arab hermit, about 80 years of age, who conducted them into a small white building, crowned by a cupola, that contains the tomb of Aaron. The monument is of stone, about three feet high; and round the chamber where it stood were suspended beads, etc., the votive offerings of the devotees. \textsuperscript{24} gathered;, ; because ye word Heb. mouth, *marg. \textsuperscript{28} Moses; put them; died there\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 21}
\markright{NUMBERS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Arad the Chananitish king who lived by the wilderness, heard that Israel came by the way of Atharin; and he made war on Israel, and carried off some of them captives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Israel vowed a vow to the Lord, and said, If you will deliver this people into my power, I will devote it and its cities [to you]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord listened to the voice of Israel, and delivered the Chananite into his power; and [Israel] devoted him and his cities, and they called the name of that place Anathema. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And having departed from mount Or by the way [leading] to the Red Sea, they compassed the land of Edom, and the people lost courage by the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the people spoke against God and against Moses, saying, Why is this? Have you brought us ought of Egypt to kill us in the wilderness? for there is not bread nor water; and our soul loathes this light bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord sent among the people deadly serpents, and they bit the people, and much people of the children of Israel died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the people came to Moses and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against you: pray therefore to the Lord, and let him take away the serpent from us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Moses prayed to the Lord for the people; and the Lord said to Moses, Make you a serpent, and put it on a signal-[staff]; and it shall come to pass that whenever a serpent shall bite a man, every one [so] bitten that looks upon it shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a signal-[staff]: and it came to pass that whenever a serpent bit a man, and he looked on the brazen serpent, he lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the children of Israel departed, and encamped in Oboth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And having departed from Oboth, they encamped in Achalgai, on the farther side in the wilderness, which is opposite Moab, toward the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And thence they departed, and encamped in the valley of Zared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they departed thence and encamped on the other side of Arnon in the wilderness, [the country] which extends from the coasts of the Amorites; for Arnon is the borders of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore it is said in a book, A war of the Lord has set on fire Zoob, and the brooks of Arnon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he has appointed brooks to cause Er to dwell [there]; and it lies near to the coasts of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And thence [they came to] the well; this [is] the well of which the Lord said to Moses, Gather the people, and I will give them water to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then Israel sang this song at the well, Begin [to sing] of the well; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} the princes digged it, the kings of the nations in their kingdom, in their lordship sank it in the rock: and [they went] from the well to Manthanain, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and from Manthanain to Naaliel, and from Naaliel to Bamoth, and from Bamoth to Janen, which is in the plain of Moab [as seen] from the top of the quarried [rock] that looks toward the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Moses sent ambassadors to Seon king of the Amorites, with peaceful words, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} We will pass through your land, we will go by the road; we will not turn aside to the field or to the vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} We will not drink water out of your well; we will go by the king's highway, until we have past your boundaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Seon did not allow Israel to pass through his borders, and Seon gathered all his people, and went out to set the battle in array against Israel into the wilderness; and he came to Jassa, and set the battle in array against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Israel struck him with the slaughter of the sword, and they became possessors of his land, from Arnon to Jaboc, as far as the children of Amman, for Jazer is the borders of the children of Amman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Israel took all their cities, and Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Esebon, and in all cities belonging to it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For Esebon is the city of Seon king of the Amorites; and he before fought against the king of Moab, and they took all his land, from Aroer to Arnon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Therefore say they who deal in dark speeches, Come to Esebon, that the city of Seon may be built and prepared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For a fire has gone forth from Esebon, a flame from the city of Seon, and has consumed as far as Moab, and devoured the pillars of Arnon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Woe to you, Moab; you are lost, you people of Chamos: their sons are sold for preservation, and their daughters are captives to Seon king of the Amorites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And their seed shall perish [from] Esebon to Daebon; and their women have yet farther kindled a fire against Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Moses sent to spy out Jazer; and they took it, and its villages, and cast out the Amorite that lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And having returned, they went up the road that leads to Basan; and Og the king of Basan went forth to meet them, and all his people to war to Edrain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the Lord said to Moses, Fear him not; for I have delivered him and all his people, and all his land, into your hands; and you shall do to him as you did to Seon king of the Amorites, who lived in Esebon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he struck him and his sons, and all his people, until he left none of his to be taken alive; and they inherited his land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: mashal (noun) (מָשָׁל) = proverb; parable. Common English renderings: proverb; parable. Wisdom and poetic comparison term.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Arad; the way of the spies Dr. Kennicott remarks, that the word atharim, rendered spies in our version, is in the Greek a proper name ( Αθαρειν, ( Atharim )., then \textsuperscript{3} hearkened, and they utterly Wyyacharem, rather with the LXX και ανεθεματισεν, "and they anathematised, or devoted them to destruction; " for it is certain that these Canaanites and Arad were not utterly destroyed till the time of Joshua ( ). the name; Hormah, that is, utter destruction. Chormah, rather a devoting to destruction, so LXX Αναθεμα, and Tremellius, devotio sive anathema . \textsuperscript{4} mount Hor, by the way; compass; the soul; discouraged or, grieved, Heb. shortened \textsuperscript{7} We have; pray; And Moses \textsuperscript{9} A serpent of; when he; he lived \textsuperscript{11} Oboth Probably Oboda, a city of Arabia Petrea, mentioned by Ptolemy. Pliny assigns it to the Helmodians; but Stephanus to the Nabatheans. Ijeabarim or, heaps of Abarim \textsuperscript{12} the valley of Zared, the brook Zered \textsuperscript{14} in the book; What he did or, Vaheb in Suphah, The following seems to be the sense of this passage: "From Vaheb in Suphah, and the torrents of Arnon, even the effusion of the torrents, which goeth down to the dwelling of Ar, and lieth for the boundary of Moab; even from thence to the well; (which is the well of which Jehovah spake unto Moses, Gather the people, and I will give them water. Then sang Israel this song: Spring up, O Well! Answer ye to it. The well, princes digged it; even nobles of the people digged it, by a decree, upon their borders); and from the wilderness (or the well, as in LXX) to Mattanah; and from Mattanah, " etc. The whole of this, from, is a fragment from "the book of the wars of Jehovah, " probably a book of remembrances or directions written by Moses for the use of Joshua, and describes the several boundaries of the land of Moab. This rendering removes every obscurity, and obviates every difficulty. \textsuperscript{17} sang; Spring up Heb. ascend sing ye or answer \textsuperscript{18} princes; the lawgiver; And from \textsuperscript{20} country Heb. field, ; to the;, Pisgah or the hill Jeshimon or, the wilderness \textsuperscript{25} dwelt; in Heshbon was situated, according to Eusebius, twenty miles east of Jordan; and Jerome, who places it at the same distance, says it was, in his time, a very considerable city. It still subsists, in ruins, under the name of Heshban.;, villages Heb. daughters \textsuperscript{26} Arnon is a stream which takes its rise in the mountains of Moab, and, by a north-west course, during which it receives the waters of several streams, runs into the Dead sea. It is now called Wady Modjeb, and divides the province of Pelka from that of Kerek, as it formerly divided the kingdoms of the Moabites and Amorites. Its principal source is at a short distance to the north-east of Katrane, a station of the Syrian Hadj, where it is called Seyl Sayde; and lower down it receives the name of Esseim el Kereim, or Szefye. \textsuperscript{28} a fire; , Ar of Moab \textsuperscript{34} Fear him;, ; for I have; thou shalt; as thou\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 22}
\markright{NUMBERS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the children of Israel departed, and encamped on the west of Moab by Jordan toward Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when Balac son of Sepphor saw all that Israel did to the Amorite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} then Moab feared the people exceedingly because they were many; and Moab was grieved before the face of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Moab said to the elders of Madiam, Now shall this assembly lick up all that are round about us, as a calf would lick up the green [herbs] of the field:—and Balac son of Sepphor was king of Moab at that time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he sent ambassadors to Balaam the son of Beor, to Phathura, which is on a river of the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, a people is come out of Egypt, and behold it has covered the face of the earth, and it has encamped close to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now come, curse me this people, for it is stronger than we; if we may be able to strike some of them, and I will cast them out of the land: for I know that whoever you do bless, they are blessed, and whoever you do curse, they are cursed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the elders of Moab went, and the elders of Madiam, and their divining [instruments were] in their hands; and they came to Balaam, and spoke to him the words of Balac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said to them, Tarry here the night, and I will answer you the things which the Lord shall say to me; and the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God came to Balaam, and said to him, Who are these men with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Balaam said to God, Balac son of Sepphor, king of Moab, sent them to me, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, a people has come forth out of Egypt, and has covered the face of the land, and it has encamped near to me; and now come, curse it for me, if indeed I shall be able to strike it, and cast it out of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And God said to Balaam, You shall not go with them, neither shall you curse the people; for they are blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Balaam rose up in the morning, and said to the princes of Balac, Depart quickly to your lord; God does not permit me to go with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the princes of Moab rose, and came to Balac, and said, Balaam will not come with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Balac yet again sent more princes and more honorable than they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they came to Balaam, and they say to him, Thus says Balac the son of Sepphor: I beseech you, delay not to come to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For I will greatly honor you, and will do for you whatever you shall say; come then, curse me this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Balaam answered and said to the princes of Balac, If Balac would give me his house full of silver and gold, I shall not be able to go beyond the word of the Lord God, to make it little or great in my mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now do you⌃ also wait here this night, and I shall know what the Lord will yet say to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And God came to Balaam by night, and said to him, If these men are come to call you, rise and follow them; nevertheless the word which I shall speak to you, it shall you do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And God was very angry because he went; and the angel of the Lord rose up to withstand him. Now he had mounted his ass, and his two servants were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when the ass saw the angel of God standing opposite in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand, then the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field; and [Balaam] struck the ass with his staff to direct her in the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the angel of the Lord stood in the avenues of the vines, a fence [being] on this side and a fence on that. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And when the ass saw the angel of God, she thrust herself against the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall, and he struck her again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the angel of the Lord went farther, and came and stood in a narrow place where it was impossible to turn to the right or the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And when the ass saw the angel of God, she lay down under Balaam; and Balaam was angry, and struck the ass with his staff. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And God opened the mouth of the ass, and she says to Balaam, What have I done to you, that you have struck me this third time? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Balaam said to the ass, Because you have mocked me; and if I [had] had a sword in my hand, I would now have killed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the ass says to Balaam, [Am] not I your ass on which you have ridden since your youth till this day? did I ever do thus to you, utterly disregarding [you]? and he said, No. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And God opened the eyes of Balaam, and he sees the angel of the Lord withstanding [him] in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand, and he stooped down and worshipped on his face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the angel of God said to him, Why have you struck your ass this third time? and, behold, I came out to withstand you, for your way was not seemly before me; and when the ass saw me, she turned away from me this third time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And if she had not turned out of the way, surely now, I should have slain you, and should have saved her alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing opposite in the way to meet [me]; and now if it shall not be pleasing to you [for me to go on], I will return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the angel of the Lord said to Balaam, Go with the men: nevertheless the word which I shall speak to you, that you shall take heed to speak. And Balaam went with the princes of Balac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And when Balac heard that Balaam was come, he went out to meet him, to a city of Moab, which is on the borders of Arnon, which is on the [extreme] part of the borders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Balac said to Balaam, Did I not send to you to call you? why have you not come to me? shall I not indeed be able to honor you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Balaam said to Balac, Behold, I am now come to you: shall I be able to say anything? the word which God shall put into my mouth, that I shall speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Balaam went with Balac, and they came to the cities of streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Balac offered sheep and calves, and sent to Balaam and to his princes who were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And it was morning; and Balac took Balaam, and brought him up to the pillar of Baal, and showed him thence a part of the people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{22} Heb. vocab: satan (שָׂטָן) = adversary; accuser. Common English renderings: adversary; Satan. Can be a common noun or later a personal title. \textsuperscript{25} Heb. vocab: chomah (חוֹמָה) = wall. Common English renderings: wall. Protective city wall term, also metaphorical.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the children, ; on this side \textsuperscript{4} elders, ; Now shall; And Balak \textsuperscript{5} sent; son of Bosor; Pethor Dr. Kennicott justly remarks, that "the description now given of Balaam's residence, instead of being particular, agrees with any place, in any country where there is a river; for he lived by 'Pethor, which is by the river of the land of his people.' But was Pethor, then, near the Nile in Egypt? Or in Canaan, near Jordan? Or in Mesopotamia, near the Euphrates, and belonging to the Ammonites? This last was in fact the case; and therefore, it is well that twelve Hebrew manuscripts (with two of De Rossi's) confirm the Samaritan text here, in reading instead of âmmo, 'his people, ' Ammon, with the Syriac and Vulgate versions." Houbigant justly contends for this reading; and necessity urges the propriety of adopting it, and it thus agrees with . Ptolemy calls Pethor, Pachura, and Eusebius, Pathura; who places it in upper Mesopotamia. Calmet is of opinion, that it was situated towards Thapsacus, beyond the Euphrates.; they cover; face Heb. eye \textsuperscript{11} able to overcome them Heb. prevail in fighting against them \textsuperscript{12} Thou shalt; thou shalt not curse, ; for they \textsuperscript{16} Let nothing etc. Heb. Be not thou letted from, etc. \textsuperscript{17} I will promote; and I will do; come curse me An erroneous opinion prevailed, both in those days and in after ages, that some men had the power, by the help of their gods, to devote, not only particular persons, but cities and whole armies, to destruction. This they are said to have done sometimes by words of imprecation; of which there was a set form among some people, which Ζschines calls διοριζομενην αραν, "the determinate curse." Macrobius has a whole chapter on this subject. He gives us two of the ancient forms used in reference to the destruction of Carthage; the first, which was only pronounced by the dictator, or general, was to call over the protecting deities to their side, and the other to devote the city to destruction, which they were supposed to have abandoned. The Romans held, that no city would be taken till its tutelary god had forsaken it; or if it could be taken, it would be unlawful, as it would be sacrilege to lead the gods into captivity. Virgil intimates, that Troy was destroyed because Excessere omnes adytis, arisque relictis dii, quibus imperium hoc steterat, "All the gods, by whose assistance the empire had hitherto been preserved, forsook their altars and temples." See more on this subject in Dr. A. Clarke, Bp. Patrick, and Burder's Oriental Customs, No. 734. \textsuperscript{20} God If the men; but yet \textsuperscript{22} God's; and the angel; stood \textsuperscript{23} the ass saw; the ass turned \textsuperscript{28} the Lord opened And where is the wonder of all this? If the ass had opened her own mouth, and reproved the rash prophet, we might well be astonished; but when God opens the mouth, an ass can speak as well as a man. It is to no purpose to speak of the construction of the ass's mouth, of the formation of the tongue and jaws being unfit for speaking; for an adequate cause is assigned for this wonderful effect, "The Lord opened the mouth of the ass"; and no one who believes in a God, can doubt of his power to do this and much more.; What have I \textsuperscript{30} the ass said upon which thou hast ridden Heb. who hast ridden upon me, ever since I was thine. or, ever since thou wast, unto, etc. \textsuperscript{31} opened *marg.; bowed down; fell flat on his face or, bowed himself \textsuperscript{32} Wherefore; withstand thee Heb. be an adversary unto thee, thy way; before me \textsuperscript{34} I Have sinned;, ; if it displease thee Heb. be evil in thine eyes, ; *marg. I will get \textsuperscript{39} Kirjathhuzoth or, a city of streets, Probably Rabbath-Moab, now called Rabba, the capital of the Moabites; and being the royal city, distinguished by its streets. \textsuperscript{41} high places Bamoth baal, "the high places of Baal, " probably the same as Bamoth mentioned in; evidently not far from Baal-meon, in the mountains of Abarim. For the Israelites were now encamped in the plains of Moab, which these mountains overlook. Baal, which signifies a lord or governor, was a name common to many idols; and probably here was the same as Chemosh, the god of Moab.; utmost\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Balaam said to Balac, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven calves, and seven rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Balac did as Balaam told him; and he offered up a calf and a ram on [every] altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Balaam said to Balac, Stand by your sacrifice, and I will go and see if God will appear to me and meet me, and the word which he shall show me, I will report to you. And Balac stood by his sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Balaam went to enquire of God; and he went straight forward, and God appeared to Balaam; and Balaam said to him, I have prepared the seven altars, and have offered a calf and a ram on [every] altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And God put a word into the mouth of Balaam, and said, you shall return to Balac, and thus shall you speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he returned to him, and moreover he stood over his whole burnt offerings, and all the princes of Moab with him; and the Spirit of God came upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he took up his parable, and said, Balac king of Moab sent for me out of Mesopotamia, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse me Jacob, and Come, call for a curse for me upon Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} How can I curse whom the Lord curses not? or how can I devote whom God devotes not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For from the top of the mountains I shall see him, and from the hills I shall observe him: behold, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who has exactly calculated the seed of Jacob, and who shall number the families of Israel? let my soul die with the souls of the righteous, and let my seed be as their seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Balac said to Balaam, What have you done to me? I called you to curse my enemies, and behold you have greatly blessed [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Balaam said to Balac, Whatsoever the Lord shall put into my mouth, shall I not take heed to speak this? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Balac said to him, Come yet with me to another place where you shall not see the people, but only you shall see a part of them, and shall not see them all; and curse me them from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he took him to a high place of the field to the top of the quarried [rock], and he built there seven altars, and offered a calf and a ram on [every] altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Balaam said to Balac, Stand by your sacrifice, and I will go to enquire of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And God met Balaam, and put a word into his mouth, and said, return to Balac, and thus shall you speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he returned to him: and he also was standing by his whole burnt sacrifice, and all the princes of Moab with him; and Balac said to him, What has the Lord spoken? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he took up his parable, and said, rise up, Balac, and hear; listen as a witness, you son of Sepphor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} God is not as man to waver, nor as the son of man to be threatened; shall he say and not perform? shall he speak and not keep [to his word]? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Behold, I have received [commandment] to bless: I will bless, and not turn back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} There shall not be trouble in Jacob, neither shall sorrow be seen in Israel: the Lord his God [is] with him, the glories of rulers [are] in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} It was God who brought him out of Egypt; he has as it were the glory of a unicorn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For there is no divination in Jacob, nor enchantment in Israel; in season it shall be told to Jacob and Israel what God shall perform. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Behold, the people shall rise up as a lion's whelp, and shall exalt himself as a lion; he shall not lie down till he have eaten the prey, and he shall drink the blood of the slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Balac said to Balaam, Neither curse the people at all for me, nor bless them at all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Balaam answered and said to Balac, Spoke I not to you, saying, Whatsoever thing God shall speak to me, that will I do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Balac said to Balaam, Come [and] I will remove you to another place, if it shall please God, and curse me them from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Balac took Balaam to the top of Phogor, which extends to the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Balaam said to Balac, build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven calves, and seven rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Balac did as Balaam told him, and offered a calf and a ram on [every] altar.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Build me; seven altars; seven oxen \textsuperscript{3} Stand burnt, ; peradventure, went to an high place or, went solitary \textsuperscript{7} he took, ; parable The word mashal, which as a verb is to rule, have authority, and also to compare, as a noun signifies whatever is expressed in parabolic or figurative language. All these oracular speeches of Balaam are in hemistich metre in the original. They are highly dignified and sublime; and may be considered as immediate poetic productions of the Spirit of God ( ). Aram; Come, ; defy Israel \textsuperscript{9} the people They shall ever be a distinct nation. This prophecy has been literally fulfilled, through a period of 3, 300 years, to the present day. dwell alone; shall not \textsuperscript{10} can count, the dust i.e. The posterity of Jacob, which was to be so numerous as to resemble the dust. the fourth, me Heb. my soul, or, my life the death \textsuperscript{13} unto; utmost and curse me \textsuperscript{14} Pisgah or, the hill; *marg., *marg. built seven \textsuperscript{21} hath not; the Lord, ; the shout \textsuperscript{22} God; the strength; unicorn The reaim, most probably denotes the rhinoceros, so called from the horn on its nose. In size he is only exceeded by the elephant; and in strength and power inferior to none. He is at least twelve feet in length, from the snout to the tail; six or seven feet in height; and the circumference of the body is nearly equal to his length. He is particularly distinguished from all other animals by the remarkable and offensive weapon he carries on his nose; which is very hard horn, solid throughout, directed forward. He principally feeds upon large succulent plants, prickly shrubs, and branches; and delights in marshy places. \textsuperscript{23} no enchantment; against or, in according; What hath \textsuperscript{24} as a great; he shall\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 24}
\markright{NUMBERS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when Balaam saw that it pleased God to bless Israel, he did not go according to his custom to meet the omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and sees Israel encamped by their tribes; and the Spirit of God came upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he took up his parable and said, Balaam son of Beor says, the man who sees truly says, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} he says who hears the oracle of the Mighty One, who saw a vision of God in sleep; his eyes were opened: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} How goodly [are] your habitations, Jacob, and your tents, Israel! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} as shady groves, and as gardens by a river, and as tents which God pitched, and as cedars by the waters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} There shall come a man out of his seed, and he shall rule over many nations; and the kingdom of Gog shall be exalted, and his kingdom shall be increased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} God led him out of Egypt; he has as it were the glory of a unicorn: he shall consume the nations of his enemies, and he shall drain their marrow, and with his darts he shall shoot through the enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He lay down, he rested as a lion, and as a young lion; who shall stir him up? they that bless you are blessed, and they that curse you are cursed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Balac was angry with Balaam, and clapped his hands together; and Balac said to Balaam, I called you to curse my enemy, and behold you have decidedly blessed [him] this third time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now therefore flee to your place: I said, I will honor you, but now the Lord has deprived you of glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Balaam said to Balac, Did I not speak to your messengers also whom you sent to me, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} If Balac should give me his house full of silver and gold, I shall not be able to transgress the word of the Lord to make it good or bad by myself; whatever things God shall say, them will I speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And now, behold, I return to my place; come, I will advise you of what this people shall do to your people in the last days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he took up his parable and said, Balaam the son of Beor says, the man who sees truly says, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} hearing the oracles of God, receiving knowledge from the Most High, and having seen a vision of God in sleep; his eyes were opened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I will point to him, but not now; I bless him, but he draws not near: a star shall rise out of Jacob, a man shall spring out of Israel; and shall crush the princes of Moab, and shall spoil all the sons of Seth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Edom shall be an inheritance, and Esau his enemy shall be an inheritance [of Israel], and Israel wrought valiantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And [one] shall arise out of Jacob, and destroy out of the city him that escapes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And having seen Amalec, he took up his parable and said, Amalec [is] the first of the nations; yet his seed shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And having seen the Kenite, he took up his parable and said, your dwelling-place [is] strong; yet though you should put your nest in a rock, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and though Beor should have a skillfully contrived hiding-place, the Assyrians shall carry you away captive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he looked upon Og, and took up his parable and said, Oh, oh, who shall live, when God shall do these things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And one shall come forth from the hands of the Citians, and shall afflict Assur, and shall afflict the Hebrews, and they shall perish together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Balaam rose up and departed and returned to his place, and Balac went to his own home.\par

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} saw, ; at other times, to seek for enchantments Heb. to the meeting of enchantments \textsuperscript{3} he took up, whose eyes are open hath said Heb. who had his eyes shut, but now opened \textsuperscript{6} as gardens; as the trees Ahalim, "lign-aloe trees." This tree, which grows in the East Indies, is described as being eight or ten feet in height, with a stem the thickness of a man's thigh. At the top grows a large tuft of jagged and thick leaves, thick and indented, broad at the bottom, but growing narrower towards the point, and about four feet in length. The blossoms are red, intermingled with yellow, and double like cloves; from which comes a red and white fruit, of the size of a pea, oblong and triangular, with three apartments filled with seed. The tree has a very beautiful appearance; and a forest of them is said to bear a resemblance to a numerous encampment.; which the; as cedar \textsuperscript{7} pour; many waters; his king; Agag, his kingdom \textsuperscript{8} God, shall eat; break; pierce \textsuperscript{14} I will advertise; the latter \textsuperscript{17} I shall see him The Targum of Onkelos translates this passage in the following manner: "I shall see him, but not now; I shall behold him, but he is not near. When a king shall arise from the house of Jacob, and the Messiah be anointed from the house of Israel; he shall slay the princes of Moab, and rule over all the children of men." \subsection*{Numbers 25}
\markright{NUMBERS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Israel sojourned in Sattin, and the people profaned itself by going a-whoring after the daughters of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they called them to the sacrifices of their idols; and the people ate of their sacrifices, and worshipped their idols. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Israel consecrated themselves to Beel-phegor; and the Lord was very angry with Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Moses, Take all the princes of the people, and make them examples [of judgment] for the Lord in the face of the sun, and the anger of the Lord shall be turned away from Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Moses said to the tribes of Israel, Slay you⌃ every one his friend that is consecrated to Beel-phegor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And, behold, a man of the children of Israel came and brought his brother to a Madianitish woman before Moses, and before all the congregation of the children of Israel; and they were weeping at the door of the tabernacle of witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Phinees the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, and rose out of the midst of the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and went in after the Israelitish man into the chamber, and pierced them both through, both the Israelitish man, and the woman through her womb; and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And those that died in the plague were four and twenty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest has caused my wrath to cease from the children of Israel, when I was exceedingly jealous among them, and I did not consume the children of Israel in my jealousy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Thus do you say [to him], Behold, I give him a covenant of peace: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and he and his seed after him shall have a perpetual covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now the name of the struck Israelitish man, who was struck with the Madianitish woman, [was] Zambri son of Salmon, prince of a house of the tribe of Symeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the name of the Madianitish woman who was struck, [was] Chasbi, daughter of Sur, a prince of the nation of Ommoth: it is a chief house among the people of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Plague the Madianites as enemies, and strike them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} for they are enemies to you by the treachery wherein they ensnare you through Phogor, and through Chasbi their sister, daughter of a prince of Madiam, who was struck in the day of the plague because of Phogor.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: zēlos (ζῆλος) = zeal; jealousy. Common English renderings: zeal; envy. Can be positive zeal or negative jealousy.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} all the heads; and hang Dr. Kennicott remarks, that the Samaritan and Hebrew Texts must be united to make the sense of this verse complete: "And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto all the heads of the people; and let them slay the men that were joined to Baal-peor; and hang them up before the Lord, against the sun, " etc., ; that the fierce \textsuperscript{6} a Midianitish, in the sight of Moses;, ; weeping \textsuperscript{9} St. Paul reckons only 23, 000: Moses includes in the 24, 000 he names, the 1, 000 men who were slain in consequence of the judicial examination ( ), as well as the 23, 000 who died of the plague; while St. Paul only refers to the latter. \textsuperscript{11} turned my; for my sake Heb. with my zeal, that I \textsuperscript{13} his seed; an everlasting; zealous; atonement \textsuperscript{14} a prince; chief house Heb. house of a father the Simeonites \textsuperscript{17} Balaam's counsel seems to have been first given to Balak, king of Moab; but probably the Midianitish women, especially of the higher ranks, as Cozbi was, were the principal tempters; and the nation of Midian seems to have come into the execrable measure more generally and heartily than that of Moab. They were therefore first selected to be made examples of, for a warning to the Moabites, who were spared at this time.\par}

\subsection*{Numbers 26}
\markright{NUMBERS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after the plague, that the Lord spoke to Moses and Eleazar the priest, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, according to the houses of their lineage, every one that goes forth to battle in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke in Araboth of Moab at the Jordan by Jericho, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [This is the numbering] from twenty years old and upward as the Lord commanded Moses. And the sons of Israel that came out of Egypt [are as follows]: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Ruben [was] the firstborn of Israel: and the sons of Ruben, Enoch, and the family of Enoch; to Phallu belongs the family of the Phalluites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} To Asron, the family of Asroni: to Charmi, the family of Charmi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} These [are] the families of Ruben; and their numbering was forty-three thousand and seven hundred and thirty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the sons of Phallu [were] Eliab, — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the sons of Eliab, Namuel, and Dathan, and Abiron: these [are] renowned men of the congregation; these are they that rose up against Moses and Aaron in the gathering of Core, in the rebellion against the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up them and Core, when their assembly perished, when the fire devoured the two hundred and fifty, and they were made a sign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the sons of Core died not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the sons of Symeon:—the family of the sons of Symeon: to Namuel, [belonged] the family of the Namuelites;
