\subsection*{Deuteronomy 3}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And we turned and went by the way leading to Basan; and Og the king of Basan came out to meet us, he and all his people, to battle at Edraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to me, Fear him not, for I have delivered him, and all his people, and all his land, into your hands; and you shall do to him as you did to Seon king of the Amorites who lived in Esebon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord our God delivered him into our hands, even Og the king of Basan, and all his people; and we struck him until we left none of his seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And we mastered all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we took not from them; sixty cities, all the country round about Argob, belonging to king Og in Basan: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} all strong cities, lofty walls, gates and bars; besides the very many cities of the Pherezites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} We utterly destroyed [them] as we dealt with Seon the king of Esebon, so we utterly destroyed every city in order, and the women and the children, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and all the cattle; and we took for a prey to ourselves the spoil of the cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And we took at that time the land out of the hands of the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond Jordan, [extending] from the brook of Arnon even to Aermon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Phoenicians call Aermon Sanior, but the Amorite has called it Sanir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All the cities of Misor, and all Galaad, and all Basan as far as Elcha and Edraim, cities of the kingdom of Og in Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For only Og the king of Basan was left of the Raphain: behold, his bed [was] a bed of iron; behold, [it is] in the chief city of the children of Ammon; the length of it [is] nine cubits, and the breadth of it four cubits, according to the cubit of a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And we inherited that land at that time from Aroer, which is by the border of the torrent Arnon, and half the mount of Galaad; and I gave his cities to Ruben and to Gad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the rest of Galaad, and all Basan the kingdom of Og I gave to the half-tribe of Manasse, and all the country round about Argob, all that Basan; it shall be accounted the land of Raphain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jair the son of Manasse took all the country round about Argob as far as the borders of Gargasi and Machathi: he called them by his name Basan Thavoth Jair until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And to Machir I gave Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And to Ruben and to Gad I gave [the land] under Galaad as far as the brook of Arnon, the border between the brook and as far as Jaboc; the brook [is] the border to the children Amman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Araba and Jordan [are] the boundary of Machanareth, even to the sea of Araba, the salt sea under Asedoth Phasga eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I charged you at that time, saying, The Lord your God has given you this land by lot; arm yourselves, every one [that is] powerful, and go before your brethren the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Only your wives and your children and your cattle (I know that you⌃ have much cattle), let them dwell in your cities which I have given you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} until the Lord your God give your brethren rest, as also he has given to you, and they also shall inherit the land, which the Lord our God gives them on the other side of Jordan; then you⌃ shall return, each one to his inheritance which I have given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Your eyes have seen all things, which the Lord our God did to these two kings: so shall the Lord our God do to all the kingdoms against which you cross over there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You⌃ shall not be afraid of them, because the Lord our God himself shall fight for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I implored the Lord at that time, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Lord God, you have begun to show to your servant your strength, and your power, and your mighty hand, and your high arm: for what God is there in heaven or on the earth, who will do as you have done, and according to your might? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I will therefore go over and see this good land that is beyond Jordan, this good mountain and Antilibanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Lord because of you did not regard me, and listened not to me; and the Lord said to me, Let it suffice you, speak not of this matter to me any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Go up to the top of the quarried rock, and look with your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold [it] with your eyes, for you shall not go over this Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And charge Joshua, and strengthen him, and encourage him; for he shall go before the face of this people, and he shall give them the inheritance of all the land which you have seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And we abode in the valley near the house of Phogor.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Bashan, one of the most fertile districts of the Holy Land, was bounded on the west by the Jordan and lake of Gennesareth, on the east by Trachonitis, on the south by the brook Jabbok, and on the north by mount Hermon; and seems to have been composed of two or three districts, on the south the land of Gilead, on the north the region of Argob, and east of both, the plain of Hauran. (See note on, see note on, and see note on .) The scenery of this elevated tract is described by Mr. Buckingham as extremely beautiful. Its plains covered with a fertile soil; its hills covered with forests, and at every new turn presenting the most beautiful landscapes that can be imagined. Og, ; Edrei This town is placed by Eusebius about 25 miles northward from Bostri; and mentioned by Burckhardt under the name of Draa. \textsuperscript{4} all his cities; all the region \textsuperscript{6} we utterly; as we did \textsuperscript{9} Hermon Mount Hermon is the south-eastern branch of Lebanon, beyond Jordan. The Chaldee Targumist, who places it at Cesarea and Samaritan interpreter call it toor talga, "the mountain of snow, " because of its being always covered with snow; and Jerome informs us, that it lies higher than Paneas or Cζsarea Philippi, and that in the summer time snow used to be carried from thence to Tyre. It is now call El Heish, and is comprised in the district of Kanneytra.; Shenir; Senir \textsuperscript{11} giants Rabbath; Rabbah nine cubits \textsuperscript{13} the rest; which was called Michaelis says, "The tradition that giants formerly dwelt in this part, still remains in Arabia, only that it makes them rather taller than Moses does Og, and calls the land in which they lived, not Bashan, but Hadrach, which name occurs in . I received this information from the verbal communication of a credible Arab, who was born on the other side of Jordan, about three-days journey from Damascus." \textsuperscript{17} Chinnereth; the sea; , ; Ashdothpisgah or, the springs of Pisgah, or, the hill \textsuperscript{18} I commanded;, meet for the war Heb. sons of power \textsuperscript{22} shall not for the Lord \textsuperscript{25} the good land; Lebanon is a long chain of limestone mountains, extending from near the coast of the Mediterranean on the west to the plains of Damascus on the east, and forming the extreme northern boundary of the Holy Land. It is divided into two principal ridges, running parallel to each other in a north-north-east direction; the most westerly of which was properly called Libanus, and the easterly Anti-Libanus. The Hebrews did not make this distinction. It is computed to be fifteen or sixteen hundred fathoms in height. They are by no means barren, but are almost all well cultivated and well peopled; their summits being in many parts level, and forming extensive plains, in which are sown corn and all kinds of pulse. Vineyards, and plantations of olive, mulberry, and fig trees, are also cultivated in terraces formed by walls; and the soil of the declivities and hollows is most excellent, and produces abundance of corn, oil, and wine. \textsuperscript{27} thee up; Pisgah or, the hill, lift up \textsuperscript{28} charge Joshua, ;, ; for he shall; Jesus\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 4}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And now, Israel, hear the ordinances and judgments, all that I teach you this day to do: that you⌃ may live, and be multiplied, and that you⌃ may go in and inherit the land, which the Lord God of your fathers gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You⌃ shall not add to the word which I command you, and you⌃ shall not take from it: keep the commandments of the Lord our God, all that I command you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Your eyes have seen all that the Lord our God did in [the case of] Beel-phegor; for every man that went after Beel-phegor, the Lord your God has utterly destroyed him from among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But you⌃ that kept close to the Lord your God are all alive today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Behold, I have shown you ordinances and judgments as the Lord commanded me, that you⌃ should do so in the land into which you⌃ go to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall keep and do them: for this is your wisdom and understanding before all nations, as many as shall hear all these ordinances; and they shall say, Behold, this great nation [is] a wise and understanding people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For what manner of nation [is so] great, which has God so near to them as the Lord our God [is] in all things in whatever we may call upon him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And what manner of nation [is so] great, which has righteous ordinances and judgments according to all this law, which I set before you this day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Take heed to yourself, and keep your heart diligently: forget not any of the things, which your eyes have seen, and let them not depart from your heart all the days of your life; and you shall teach your sons and your sons' sons, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [even the things that happened in] the day in which you⌃ stood before the Lord our God in Choreb in the day of the assembly; for the Lord said to me, Gather the people to me, and let them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days which they live upon the earth, and they shall teach their sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you⌃ drew near and stood under the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire up to heaven: [there was] darkness, blackness, [and] tempest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord spoke to you out of the midst of the fire a voice of words, which you⌃ heard: and you⌃ saw no likeness, only [you⌃ heard] a voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he announced to you his covenant, which he commanded you to keep, even the ten commandments; and he wrote them on two tables of stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord commanded me at that time, to teach you ordinances and judgments, that you⌃ should do them on the land, into which you⌃ go to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And take good heed to your hearts, for you⌃ saw no similitude in the day in which the Lord spoke to you in Choreb in the mountain out of the midst of the fire: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} lest you⌃ transgress, and make to yourselves a carved image, any kind of figure, the likeness of male or female, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} the likeness of any beast of those that are on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird which flies under heaven, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} the likeness of any reptile which creeps on the earth, the likeness of any fish of those which are in the waters under the earth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and lest having looked up to the sky, and having seen the sun and the moon and the stars, and all the heavenly bodies, you should go astray and worship them, and serve them, which the Lord your God has distributed to all the nations under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But God took you, and led you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be to him a people of inheritance, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord God was angry with me for the things said by you, and swore that I should not go over this Jordan, and that I should not enter into the land, which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For I am to die in this land, and shall not pass over this Jordan; but you⌃ are to pass over, and shall inherit this good land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Take heed to yourselves, lest you⌃ forget the covenant of the Lord our God, which he made with you, and you⌃ transgress, and make to yourselves a graven image of any of the things concerning which the Lord your God commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And when you shall have begotten sons, and shall have sons' sons, and you⌃ shall have lived a long time on the land, and shall have transgressed, and made a graven image of any thing, and shall have done wickedly before the Lord your God to provoke him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I call heaven and earth this day to witness against you, that you⌃ shall surely perish from off the land, into which you⌃ go across Jordan to inherit it there; you⌃ shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall be utterly cut off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord shall scatter you among all nations, and you⌃ shall be left few in number among all the nations, among which the Lord shall bring you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And you⌃ shall there serve other gods, the works of the hands of men, wood and stones, which can’t see, nor can they hear, nor eat, nor smell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And there you⌃ shall seek the Lord your God, and you⌃ shall find him whenever you⌃ shall seek him with all your heart, and with all your soul in your affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And all these things shall come upon you in the last days, and you shall turn to the Lord your God, and shall listen to his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Because the Lord your God [is] a God of pity: he will not forsake you, nor destroy you; he will not forget the covenant of your fathers, which the Lord swore to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Ask of the former days which were before you, from the day when God created man upon the earth, and [beginning] at the [one] end of heaven to the other end of heaven, if there has happened any thing like to this great event, if such a thing has been heard: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} if a nation have heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard and have lived; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} if God has assayed to go and take to himself a nation out of the midst of [another] nation with trial, and with signs, and with wonders, and with war, and with a mighty hand, and with a high arm, and with great sights, according to all the things which the Lord our God did in Egypt in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} So that you should know that the Lord your God he is God, and there is none beside him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} His voice was made audible from heaven to instruct you, and he showed you upon the earth his great fire, and you heard his words out of the midst of the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Because he loved your fathers, he also chose you their seed after them, and he brought you himself with his great strength out of Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} to destroy nations great and stronger than you before your face, to bring you in, to give you their land to inherit, as you have it this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And you shall know this day, and shall consider in your heart, that the Lord your God he [is] God in heaven above, and on the earth beneath, and there is none else but he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And keep you⌃ his commandments, and his ordinances, all that I command you this day; that it may be well with you, and with your sons after you, that you⌃ may be long-lived upon the earth, which the Lord your God gives you for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Then Moses separated three cities beyond Jordan on the east, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} that the slayer might flee there, who should have slain his neighbor unintentionally, and should not have hated him in times past, and he shall flee to one of these cities and live: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Bosor in the wilderness, in the plain country of Ruben, and Ramoth in Galaad [belonging to] Gad, and Gaulon in Basan [belonging to] Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} This [is] the law which Moses set before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} These [are] the testimonies, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} on the other side of Jordan, in the valley near the house of Phogor, in the land of Seon king of the Amorites, who lived in Esebon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck when they came out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And they inherited his land, and the land of Og king of Basan, two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond Jordan eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} From Aroer, which is on the border of the brook Arnon, even to the mount of Seon, which is Aermon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} All Araba beyond Jordan eastward under Asedoth hewn in the rock.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: lamad (לָמַד) = to learn; teach. Common English renderings: learn; teach. Core educational verb in covenant formation. \textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: binah (בִּינָה) = understanding; discernment. Common English renderings: understanding. Closely associated with wisdom and interpretation. \textsuperscript{10} Gk. vocab: ekklēsia (ἐκκλησία) = assembly; congregation. Common English renderings: church; assembly. In the Greek Bible this term first denotes an assembly before becoming the standard word for the church. \textsuperscript{30} Gk. vocab: thlipsis (θλῖψις) = affliction; tribulation. Common English renderings: tribulation; affliction. A pressure word often used for distress and tribulation. \textsuperscript{34} Gk. vocab: peirasmos (πειρασμός) = trial; temptation. Common English renderings: temptation. Can mean testing or temptation according to context.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} unto the statutes Statutes, every thing that concerned morals and the rites and ceremonies of religion; judgments, all matters of civil right and wrong., ; that ye may \textsuperscript{3} what the; for all the men It appears from this appeal, that the pestilence, as well as the sword of the magistrates, singled out the guilty persons and spared the rest ( ). The legislator, in order to deter the Jews from idolatry, alludes to this fact, but he notices no circumstance but one, which, though in the original narrative was not stated, was infinitely the most important to advert to on this occasion; but which no persons, but spectators of the fact, and perfectly acquainted with every individual concerned in it, could possibly feel the truth of. \textsuperscript{5} The people had been often ready to conclude that Moses taught them by his own authority; but at the close of his life he solemnly assured them that he had instructed them exactly as the Lord had commanded him, neither more, nor less, nor otherwise. This is a most express declaration that he was divinely inspired, and utterly incompatible with his integrity of character, if he was not. Scott. \textsuperscript{9} keep thy soul; lest they;, ; teach them \textsuperscript{12} the Lord, no similitude; only ye heard a voice Heb. save a voice \textsuperscript{13} And he; ten; he wrote \textsuperscript{16} corrupt; the likeness Such as Baal-peor, the Roman Priapus; Ashtaroth or Astarte, the Greek and Roman Venus, and many others. \textsuperscript{17} In these verses there is an evident allusion to the idolatrous worship in Egypt. Among the Egyptians, almost everything in nature was the object of their idolatry; among beasts were oxen, heifers, sheep, goats, lions, dogs, monkeys, and cats; among birds, the ibis, crane, and hawk; among reptiles, the crocodile, serpents, frogs, flies, and beetles; all the fish of the Nile, and the Nile itself; besides the sun, moon, planets, stars, fire, light, air, darkness, and night. These are all included in the very circumstantial prohibition in the text, and very forcibly in the general terms of, the reason of which prohibition becomes self-evident, when the various objects of Egyptian idolatry are considered. \textsuperscript{19} when thou; the host; which the Lord; divided or, imparted \textsuperscript{23} heed, ; lest ye forget, ; make you \textsuperscript{24} thy God; a jealous God \textsuperscript{26} I call heaven A most solemn method of adjuration, in use among all the nations in the world; God and man being called upon to bear testimony to the truth of what was spoken, that if there was any flaw or insincerity it might be detected, and if any crime, it might not go unpunished. Such appeals to God shew at once the origin and use of oaths., ; ye shall \textsuperscript{30} all these; are come upon thee Heb. have found thee; *marg. in the latter; if thou; obedient \textsuperscript{32} ask now; from the one \textsuperscript{34} take him, temptations; by signs; by a mighty, ; and by great \textsuperscript{37} because, ; and brought, in his sight; with his \textsuperscript{43} Bezer is the same as Bozra, formerly a royal city of Edom. See note on . Ramoth was a celebrated city in the mountains of Gilead, placed by Eusebius fifteen miles east from Philadelphia or Ammon, and by Jerome in the neighbourhood of Jabbok, and consequently north of Philadelphia.; Golan This city gave name to the district of Gaulonitis, now called Djolan, which comprises the plain to south of Djedour or Iturea, and to the west of Haouran. Its southern frontier is the Nahar Aweired, by which it is separated from the district of Erbad, and the Sheriat el Mandhour, which separates it from the district of El Kefarat. On the west it is limited by the territory of Feik, and on the north-west by Djebel Heish, or mount Hermon. \textsuperscript{44} This is evidently an introduction to the discourse of the subsequent chapters. Moses having practically improved some particulars in the history of Israel, proceeded to repeat and enforce the laws which he had delivered before, with additions and explanations, beginning with the ten commandments. \textsuperscript{46} On this side, ; over Bethpeor Beth-peor was a city which was situated, according to Eusebius, opposite Jericho, and six miles above Livias. As the name signifies "the house of Peor, " it is probable that there was a temple to Peor, situated in this place, full in view of the people, while Moses was pressing upon them the worship of Jehovah alone; and perhaps the very temple where so many had sinned to their own destruction. \subsection*{Deuteronomy 5}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses called all Israel, and said to them, Hear, Israel, the ordinances and judgments, all that I speak in your ears this day, and you⌃ shall learn them, and observe to do them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The Lord your God made a covenant with you in Choreb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord did not make this covenant with your fathers, but with you: you⌃ are all here alive this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The Lord spoke to you face to face in the mountain out of the midst of the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I stood between the Lord and you at that time to report to you the words of the Lord, (because you⌃ were afraid before the fire, and you⌃ went not up to the mountain) saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall have no other gods before my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You shall not make to yourself an image, nor likeness of any thing, whatever things [are] in the heaven above, and whatever [are] in the earth beneath, and whatever [are] in the waters under the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you serve them; for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation to them that hate me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and doing mercifully to thousands of them that love me, and that keep my commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord your God will certainly not acquit him that takes his name in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it, as the Lord your God commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Six days you shall work, and you shall do all your works; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} but on the seventh day [is] the sabbath of the Lord your God: you shall do in it no work, you, and your son, and your daughter, your man-servant, and your maidservant, your ox, and your ass, and all your cattle, and the stranger that sojourns in the midst of you; that your man-servant may rest, and your maid, and your ox, as well as you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out thence with a mighty hand, and a high arm: therefore the Lord appointed you to keep the sabbath day and to sanctify it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you; that it may be well with you, and that you may live long upon the land, which the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall not commit murder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You shall not commit adultery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You shall not steal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You shall not covet your neighbor's wife; you shall not covet your neighbor's house, nor his field, nor his man-servant, nor his maid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any beast of his, nor any thing that is your neighbor's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} These words the Lord spoke to all the assembly of you in the mountain out of the midst of the fire—[there was] darkness, blackness, storm, a loud voice—and he added no more, and he wrote them on two tables of stone, and he gave them to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass when you⌃ heard the voice out of the midst of the fire, for the mountain burned with fire, that you⌃ came to me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and you⌃ said, Behold, the Lord our God has shown us his glory, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire: this day we have seen that God shall speak to man, and he shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now let us not die, for this great fire will consume us, if we shall hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, and we shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For what flesh [is there] which has heard the voice of the living God, speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we [have heard], and shall live? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Do you draw near, and hear all that the Lord our God shall say, and you shall speak to us all things whatever the Lord our God shall speak to you, and we will hear, and do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the Lord heard the voice of your words as you⌃ spoke to me; and the Lord said to me, I have heard the voice of the words of this people, even all things that they have said to you. [They have] well [said] all that they have spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} O that there were such a heart in them, that they should fear me and keep my commands always, that it might be well with them and with their sons for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Go, say to them, Return you⌃ to your houses; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} but stand you here with me, and I will tell you all the commands, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which you shall teach them, and let them do so in the land which I give them for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you⌃ shall take heed to do as the Lord your God commanded you; you⌃ shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} according to all the way which the Lord your God commanded you to walk in it, that he may give you rest; and that it may be well with you, and you⌃ may prolong your days on the land which you⌃ shall inherit.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} all Israel, Hear keep, and Heb. keep to \textsuperscript{6} I am the; brought bondage Heb. servants \textsuperscript{9} shalt not the Lord On the import of the word yehowah, which we translate Lord, see note on . The word elohim, which is rendered God, in the singular, eloah, and in Arabic allah, is derived from the Arabic alaha, he worshipped, adored, was struck with astonishment, fear, or terror, and hence, he adored with sacred honour and veneration. It also signifies, he succoured, liberated, kept in safety, or defended. Here we learn that elohim denotes the sole object of adoration; the perfections of whose nature must astonish all who contemplate them, and fill with horror all who rebel against him; that consequently he must be worshipped with reverence and religious fear; and that every sincere worshipper may expect help in all his weaknesses, etc., freedom from the power, guilt, and consequences of sin, and support and defence to the uttermost. a jealous God visiting \textsuperscript{14} the sabbath; thy stranger, thy manservant \textsuperscript{24} we have heard; he liveth \textsuperscript{25} this great; hear Heb. add to hear \textsuperscript{26} who is It seems to have been a general opinion, that if God appeared to men, it was for the purpose of destroying them. And indeed most of the extraordinary manifestations of God were in the way of judgment; but here it was widely different. God did appear in a sovereign and extraordinary manner; but it was for the instruction, direction, deliverance, and support of his people. 1. They heard this voice speaking with them in a distinct, articulate manner. 2. They saw the fire, the symbol of his presence, the appearances of which demonstrated it to be supernatural. 3. Notwithstanding God appeared so terrible, yet no person was destroyed; for he came not to destroy but to save. all flesh; living \textsuperscript{28} they have well said all \textsuperscript{29} The language of the original is emphatic: Mee yittain wehayah levavom zeh lahem, literally, "Who will give that there may be such a heart in them?" They refuse to receive such a heart from me, who then can supply it? O that there; keep all; that it might\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 6}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the commands, and the ordinances, and the judgments, as many as the Lord our God gave commandment to teach you to do so in the land on which you⌃ enter to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That you⌃ may fear the Lord your God, keep you⌃ all his ordinances, and his commandments, which I command you today, you, and your sons, and your sons' sons, all the days of your life, that you⌃ may live many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Hear, therefore, O Israel, and observe to do them, that it may be well with you, and that you⌃ may be greatly multiplied, as the Lord God of your fathers said that he would give you a land flowing with milk and honey: and these [are] the ordinances, and the judgments, which the Lord commanded the children of Israel in the wilderness, when they had gone forth from the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Hear, O Israel, The Lord our God is one Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and all your strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And these words, all that I command you this day, shall be in your heart and in your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall teach them to your children, and you shall speak of them sitting in the house, and walking by the way, and lying down, and rising up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall fasten them for a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immoveable before your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you⌃ shall write them on the lintels of your houses and of your gates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it shall come to pass when the Lord your God shall have brought you into the land which he swore to your fathers, to Abraam, and to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you great and beautiful cities which you did not build, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} houses full of all good things which you did not fill, wells dug in the rock which you did not dig, vineyards and olive yards which you did not plant, then having eaten and been filled, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} beware lest you forget the Lord your God that brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall fear the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve; and you shall cleave to him, and by his name you shall swear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Go you⌃ not after other gods of the gods of the nations round about you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} for the Lord your God in the midst of you [is] a jealous God, lest the Lord your God be very angry with you, and destroy you from off the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall not tempt the Lord your God, as you⌃ tempted him in the temptation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall by all means keep the commands of the Lord your God, the testimonies, and the ordinances, which he commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall do that which is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, that it may be well with you, and that you may go in and inherit the good land, which the Lord swore to your fathers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} to chase all your enemies from before your face, as the Lord said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it shall come to pass when your son shall ask you at a future time, saying, What are the testimonies, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which the Lord our God has commanded us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then shall you say to your son, We were slaves to Pharao in the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought us forth thence with a mighty hand, and with a high arm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord wrought signs and great and grievous wonders in Egypt, on Pharao and on his house before us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he brought us out thence to give us this land, which he swore to give to our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Lord charged us to observe all these ordinances; to fear the Lord our God, that it may be well with us for ever, that we may live, as even today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there shall be mercy to us, if we take heed to keep all these commands before the Lord our God, as he has commanded us.\par

"Hear, Israel, Jehovah, our God, is one Jehovah." On this passage the Jews lay great stress; and it is one of the four passages which they write on their phylacteries. On the word Elohim, Simeon ben Joachi says: "Come and see the mystery of the word Elohim . There are three degrees, and each degree is by itself alone, and yet they are all one, and joined together in one, and are not divided from each other." the Lord \textsuperscript{5} thou shalt; God with all \textsuperscript{7} And thou shalt, ; teach Heb. whet, or sharpen shalt talk \textsuperscript{12} bondage Heb. bondmen, or servants \textsuperscript{13} fear, ; and serve him Our Saviour quotes these words thus: "And him only ( αυτω μονω ), shalt thou serve; " from which it would appear, that the word levaddo was anciently in the Hebrew Text, as it was in the Septuagint, Coptic, Vulgate ( illi soli ), and Anglo-Saxon. Dr. Kennicott argues that without the word only, the text would not have conclusive for the purpose for which our Lord advanced it. It is proper, however, to observe, that the word levaddo is not found in any manuscript yet collated, though retained in the above versions. shalt swear \textsuperscript{14} not go; of the gods \textsuperscript{15} is a jealous; lest; destroy \textsuperscript{18} shalt do, ; , ; that it may \textsuperscript{20} when thy son; in time to come Heb. to-morrow \textsuperscript{21} We were, with a mighty \textsuperscript{22} showed; Exod. 7:1-12:51; sore Heb. evil before \textsuperscript{24} to fear for our good; he might\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 7}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when the Lord your God shall bring you into the land, into which you go to possess it, and shall remove great nations from before you, the Chettite, and Gergesite, and Amorite, and Chananite, and Pherezite, and Evite, and Jebusite, seven nations [more] numerous and stronger than you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and the Lord your God shall deliver them into your hands, then you shall strike them: you shall utterly destroy them: you shall not make a covenant with them, neither shall you⌃ pity them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} neither shall you⌃ contract marriages with them: you shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter to your son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For he will draw away your son from me, and he will serve other gods; and the Lord will be very angry with you, and will soon utterly destroy you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But thus shall you⌃ do to them; you⌃ shall destroy their altars, and shall break down their pillars, and shall cut down their groves, and shall burn with fire the graven images of their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For you are a holy people to the Lord your God; and the Lord your God chose you to be to him a peculiar people beyond all nations that [are] upon the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} It was not because you⌃ are more numerous than all [other] nations that the Lord preferred you, and the Lord made choice of you: for you⌃ are fewer in number than all [other] nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But because the Lord loved you, and as keeping the oath which he swore to your fathers, the Lord brought you out with a strong hand, and the Lord redeemed you from the house of bondage, out of the hand of Pharao king of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You shall know therefore, that the Lord your God, he [is] God, a faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy for them that love him, and for those that keep his commandments to a thousand generations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and who recompenses them that hate him to their face, to destroy them utterly; and will not be slack with them that hate him: he will recompense them to their face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall keep therefore the commands, and the ordinances, and these judgments, which I command you this day to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall come to pass when you⌃ shall have heard these ordinances, and shall have kept and done them, that the Lord your God shall keep for you the covenant and the mercy, which he swore to your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he will love you, and bless you, and multiply you; and he will bless the off-spring of your body, and the fruit of your land, your corn, and your wine, and your oil, the herds of your oxen, and the flocks of your sheep, on the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall be blessed beyond all nations; there shall not be among you an impotent or barren one, or among your cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord your God shall remove from you all sickness; and none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you have seen, and all that you have known, will he lay upon you; but he will lay them upon all that hate you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall eat all the spoils of the nations which the Lord your God gives you; your eye shall not spare them, and you shall not serve their gods; for this is an offense to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But if you should say in your heart, This nation [is] greater than I, how shall I be able to destroy them utterly? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} you shall not fear them; you shall surely remember all that the Lord your God did to Pharao and to all the Egyptians: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} the great temptations which your eyes have seen, those signs and great wonders, the strong hand, and the high arm; how the Lord your God brought you forth: so the Lord your God will do to all the nations, whom you fear in their presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord your God shall send against them the hornets, until they that are left and they that are hidden from you be utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You shall not be wounded before them, because the Lord your God in the midst of you [is] a great and powerful God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord your God shall consume these nations before you by little and little: you shall not be able to consume them speedily, lest the land become desert, and the wild beasts of the field be multiplied against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord your God shall deliver them into your hands, and you shall destroy them with a great destruction, until you⌃ shall have utterly destroyed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he shall deliver their kings into your hands, and you⌃ shall destroy their name from that place; none shall stand up in opposition before you, until you shall have utterly destroyed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} You⌃ shall burn with fire the graven images of their gods: you shall not covet [their] silver, neither shall you take to yourself gold from them, lest you should offend thereby, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, so should you be an accursed thing like it; you shall utterly hate it, and altogether abominate it, because it is an accursed thing.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{15} Heb. vocab: choli (חֹלִי) = sickness. Common English renderings: sickness; disease. Used for physical affliction. Gk. vocab: nosos (νόσος) = disease. Common English renderings: disease. A general term for sickness or disease.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the Lord, ; the Hittites With respect to the situation of these nations in the land of Canaan, Calmet remarks, that the Canaanites chiefly inhabited Phoenecia; the Hittites, the mountains south of the promised land; the Hivites, mount Ebal, and Gerizim, and towards Hermon; the Girgashites, beyond Jordan, towards the lake of Gennesareth, the Jebusistes, about Jerusalem; the Amorites, the mountains west of the Dead Sea, and part of the land of Moab; and that the Perizzites were probably not a distinct nation, but villagers scattered through the country.; greater \textsuperscript{5} destroy; images Heb. statues, or pillars; and cut burn \textsuperscript{6} an holy, ; to be a special \textsuperscript{9} the faithful; which keepeth; a thousand \textsuperscript{13} he will love; , he will also \textsuperscript{15} will put none The Israelites, if obedient, would have been subject to no maladies but those common to fallen man, and generally very healthy and long lived; being exempted from pestilential diseases, which have often most tremendously scourged guilty nations; and from such maladies in particular, as they had witnessed in Egypt, by which God afflicted their cruel oppressors ( ). This must be referred to the national covenant; for though godliness often secures the most solid temporal advantages, yet temporal blessings were not, even among them, uniformly dispensed to individuals according to their obedience; but they were to the nation, with an exactness which is not observed towards any other people. will put none \textsuperscript{16} consume thine eye, ; for that will \textsuperscript{21} the Lord, ; a mighty God \textsuperscript{22} put out Heb. pluck off thou mayest As the Israelites were not yet sufficiently numerous to fill the whole land occupied by these nations; and as wild and ferocious animals might be expected to multiply where the place was but thinly peopled, therefore God informs them that their extermination from before them should be gradual. Haynes says, "The approaching to Cana, at the close of the day, as we did, is at once terrifying and dangerous. The surrounding country swarms with wild beasts, such as tigers, leopards, jackals, etc., whose cries and howling, I doubt not, would strike the boldest traveller, who had not been frequently in a like situation, with the deepest sense of horror." \textsuperscript{23} the Lord unto thee Heb. before thy face, shall destroy \textsuperscript{24} he shall, their name, ; there shall \textsuperscript{25} graven; thou shalt, snared; an abomination\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 8}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You⌃ shall observe to do all the commands which I charge you today, that you⌃ may live and be multiplied, and enter in and inherit the land, which the Lord your God swore [to give] to your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall remember all the way which the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, that he might afflict you, and try you, and that the things in your heart might be made manifest, whether you would keep his commandments or no. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he afflicted you and straitened you with hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers knew not; that he might teach you that man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God shall man live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Your garments grew not old from off you, your shoes were not worn from off you, your feet were not [painfully] hardened, behold! these forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall know in your heart, that as if any man should chasten his son, so the Lord your God will chasten you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall keep the commands of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the Lord your God will bring you into a good and extensive land, where there are torrents of waters, and fountains of deep places issuing through the plains and through the mountains: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} a land of wheat and barley, [wherein are] vines, figs, pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} a land on which you shall not eat your bread with poverty, and you shall not lack any thing upon it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of its mountains you shall dig brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall eat and be filled, and shall bless the Lord your God on the good land, which he has given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Take heed to yourself that you forget not the Lord your God, so as not to keep his commands, and his judgments, and ordinances, which I command you this day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} lest when you have eaten and are full, and have built goodly houses, and lived in them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and your oxen and your sheep are multiplied to you, and your silver and your gold are multiplied to you, and all your possessions are multiplied to you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} you should be exalted in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} who brought you through that great and terrible wilderness, where [is] the biting serpent, and scorpion, and drought, where there was no water; who brought you a fountain of water out of the flinty rock: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which you knew not, and your fathers knew not; that he might afflict you, and thoroughly try you, and do you good in your latter days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Lest you should say in your heart, My strength, and the power of my hand have wrought for me this great wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But you shall remember the Lord your God, that he gives you strength to get wealth; even that he may establish his covenant, which the Lord swore to your fathers, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it shall come to pass if you do at all forget the Lord your God, and should go after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you⌃ shall surely perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As also the other nations which the Lord God destroys before your face, so shall you⌃ perish, because you⌃ listened not to the voice of the Lord your God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} remember; led thee, ; to humble, ; prove thee; to know \textsuperscript{4} Many have attempted to give the following meaning to this text - "God so amply provided for them all the necessaries of life, that they never were obliged to wear tattered garments, nor were their feet injured for lack of shoes or sandals." Now, though the Israelites doubtless brought out of Egypt more raiment than what they had upon them; and they might manufacture the fleeces of their flocks in the wilderness; and also might be favoured by Providence with other supplies from the neighbouring nations or travelling hordes of Arabs; yet, when we consider their immense numbers, their situation and long continuance in the wilderness, and the very strong expressions made use of in the text, why should we question the extraordinary and miraculous interposition of God in this respect, as well as in others, not less stupendous in their nature, or constant in their supply? \textsuperscript{8} wheat; barley; vines; oil olive Heb. olive tree of oil \textsuperscript{12} Lest when, ; and hast built \textsuperscript{15} led thee; fiery serpents; who brought \textsuperscript{16} fed thee; he might to do thee \textsuperscript{18} he that; that he may\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 9}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Hear, O Israel: You go this day across Jordan to inherit nations greater and stronger than yourselves, cities great and walled up to heaven; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} a people great and many and tall, the sons of Enac, whom you know, and concerning whom you have heard [say], Who can stand before the children of Enac? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall know today, that the Lord your God he shall go before your face: he is a consuming fire; he shall destroy them, and he shall turn them back before you, and shall destroy them quickly, as the Lord said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Speak not in your heart, when the Lord your God has destroyed these nations before your face, saying, For my righteousness the Lord brought me in to inherit this good land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Not for your righteousness, nor for the holiness of your heart, do you go in to inherit their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the Lord will destroy them from before you, and that he may establish the covenant, which the Lord swore to our fathers, to Abraam, and to Isaac, and to Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall know today, that [it is] not for your righteousnesses the Lord your God gives you this good land to inherit, for you are a stiff-necked people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember, forget not, how much you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness: from the day that you⌃ came forth out of Egypt, even till you⌃ came into this place, you⌃ continued to be disobedient toward the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Also in Choreb you⌃ provoked the Lord, and the Lord was angry with you to destroy you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} when I went up into the mountain to receive the tables of stone, the tables of the covenant, which the Lord made with you, and I was in the mountain forty days and forty nights, I ate no bread and drank no water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord gave me the two tables of stone written with the finger of God, and on them there had been written all the words which the Lord spoke to you in the mountain in the day of the assembly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two tables of stone, the tables of the covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord said to me, Arise, go down quickly from hence, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have transgressed; they have gone aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them, and have made themselves a molten image. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord spoke to me, saying, I have spoken to you once and again, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiff-necked people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And now suffer me utterly to destroy them, and I will blot out their name from under heaven, and will make of you a nation great and strong, and more numerous than this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I turned and went down from the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire to heaven; and the two tables of the testimonies [were] in my two hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when I saw that you⌃ had sinned against the Lord your God, and had made to yourselves a molten image, and had gone astray out of the way, which the Lord commanded you to keep; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} then I took hold of the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and broke them before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I made my petition before the Lord as also at the first forty days and forty nights: I ate no bread and drank no water, on account of all your sins which you⌃ sinned in doing evil before the Lord God to provoke him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And I was greatly terrified because of the wrath and anger, because the Lord was provoked with you utterly to destroy you; yet the Lord listened to me at this time also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he was angry with Aaron to destroy him utterly, and I prayed for Aaron also at that time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And your sin which you⌃ had made, [even] the calf, I took, and burnt it with fire, and pounded it and ground it down till it became fine; and it became like dust, and I cast the dust into the brook that descended from the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Also in the burning, and in the temptation, and at the graves of lust, you⌃ provoked the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when the Lord sent you forth from Cades Barne, saying, Go up and inherit the land which I give to you, then you⌃ disobeyed the word of the Lord your God, and believed him not, and listened not to his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You⌃ were disobedient in the things relating to the Lord from the day in which he became known to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I prayed before the Lord forty days and forty nights, the number that I prayed [before], for the Lord said that he would utterly destroy you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And I prayed to God, and said, O Lord, King of gods, destroy not your people and your inheritance, whom you did redeem, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with your great power, and with your strong hand, and with your high arm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Remember Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob your servants, to whom you swore by yourself: look not upon the hardness of heart of this people, and their impieties, and their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Lest the inhabitants of the land whence you brought us out speak, saying, Because the Lord could not bring them into the land of which he spoke to them, and because he hated them, has he brought them forth to kill them in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And these [are] your people and your portion, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with your great strength, and with your mighty hand, and with your high arm.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} to pass, ;, this day The Hebrew hyyom, "this day, " frequently denotes, as here, this time. They had come, 38 years before this, nearly to the verge of the promised land, but were not permitted, because of their unbelief and rebellion, at that day or time, to enter; but this time they shall certainly pass over. This was spoken in the eleventh month of the fortieth year of their journeying; and it was on the first month of the following year they passed over, and during this interval Moses died. nations, cities \textsuperscript{3} Understand; goeth over, ; a consuming fire;, ; he shall \textsuperscript{4} Speak not, ; for the wickedness \textsuperscript{5} Not for Though the Canaanites were expelled for their wickedness, it does not follow, that the Israelites were established in their room on account of any distinguished virtue, or because they deserved it. On many occasions, it may be seen in the history of the world, that God punishes the wicked by the instrumentality of other men, who are as wicked as themselves. Not the Israelites' righteousness, but the wickedness of the inhabitants, and the promise of God to their fathers, was the cause of their obtaining Canaan. that he may \textsuperscript{6} Understand; giveth thee Moses repeats this a third time, that, if it were possible, he might root out of the Israelites the opinion of their own deserts, before God rooted out the Canaanites from their country. a stiffnecked \textsuperscript{7} Remember In order to destroy the opinion which the Israelites had of their own righteousness, it was necessary to call to mind some of their most notorious provocations and rebellions, which Moses exhorts them to preserve in their mind, as a means to keep them humble.; from the day \textsuperscript{8} Also in Horeb Or rather, "Even at Horeb, " for there is a peculiar emphasis here, even there where they had lately received the law, attended with the most astonishing appearances and circumstances. \textsuperscript{9} I was, the tables; then I; I neither \textsuperscript{10} the Lord written with; all the words \textsuperscript{11} the tables of the covenant \textsuperscript{14} Let me; blot; and I will \textsuperscript{17} cast them Moses might have done this through distress and anguish of spirit, on beholding their abominable idolatry and dissolute conduct; or probably he did it emblematically, and perhaps by the direction of God; intimating thereby, that as by this act of his the tables were broken in pieces, on which the Law of God was written, so they, by their present conduct, had made a breach in the covenant, and broken the laws of their Maker and Sovereign. \textsuperscript{18} I fell down The transgressions of the people rendered this second forty days' fasting necessary to Moses. Their pardon was indeed in some sense obtained before he ascended the mount; yet probably much of the time which he spent there was employed in supplication, and when he descended the second time, with the tables of the law in his hands, the pardon was, as it were, ratified and sealed. \textsuperscript{21} I took; the brook This was the stream which flowed from the rock that Moses smote with his rod ( ), and to which the Psalmist alludes in; . Philo relates, that upon Moses' striking the rock, the water poured out like a torrent, affording not only a sufficient quantity for allaying their present thirst, but to fill their water vessels, to carry with them on their journey. \textsuperscript{23} Likewise; ye rebelled; ye believed \textsuperscript{26} prayed; thine inheritance which thou hast redeemed; which thou hast brought forth\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 10}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} At that time the Lord said to me, Hew for yourself two stone tables as the first, and come up to me into the mountain, and you shall make for yourself an ark of wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall write upon the tables the words which were on the first tables which you did break, and you shall put them into the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So I made an ark of boards of incorruptible wood, and I hewed tables of stone like the first, and I went up to the mountain, and the two tables were in my hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he wrote upon the tables according to the first writing the ten commandments, which the Lord spoke to you in the mountain out of the midst of the fire, and the Lord gave them to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I turned and came down from the mountain, and I put the tables into the ark which I had made; and there they were, as the Lord commanded me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Israel departed from Beeroth of the sons of Jakim [to] Misadai: there Aaron died, and there he was buried, and Eleazar his son was priest in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Thence they departed to Gadgad; and from Gadgad to Etebatha, a land [wherein are] torrents of water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand near before the Lord, to minister and bless in his name to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore the Levites have no part nor inheritance among their brethren; the Lord himself [is] their inheritance, as he said to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I remained in the mount forty days and forty nights: and the Lord heard me at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to me, Go, set out before this people, and let them go in and inherit the land, which I swore to their fathers to give to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his ordinances, all that I charge you today, that it may be well with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord your God, the earth and all things that are in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Only the Lord chose your fathers to love them, and he chose out their seed after them, [even] you, beyond all nations, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore you⌃ shall circumcise the hardness of your heart, and you⌃ shall not harden your neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the Lord your God, he [is] God of gods, and the Lord of lords, the great, and strong, and terrible God, who does not accept persons, nor will he by any means accept a bribe: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} executing judgment for the stranger and orphan and widow, and he loves the stranger to give him food and raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you⌃ shall love the stranger; for you⌃ were strangers in the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You shall fear the Lord your God, and serve him, and shall cleave to him, and shall swear by his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He [is] your boast, and he [is] your God, who has wrought in the midst of you these great and glorious things, which your eyes have seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} With seventy souls your fathers went down into Egypt; but the Lord your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.\par
