\subsection*{Deuteronomy 11}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore you shall love the Lord your God, and shall observe his appointments, and his ordinances, and his commandments, and his judgments, always. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you⌃ shall know this day; for [I speak] not to your children, who know not and have not seen the discipline of the Lord your God, and his wonderful works, and his strong hand, and his high arm, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and his miracles, and his wonders, which he wrought in the midst of Egypt on Pharao king of Egypt, and all his land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and what he did to the host of the Egyptians, and to their chariots, and their cavalry, and their host; how he made the water of the Red Sea to overwhelm the face of them as they pursued after you, and the Lord destroyed them until this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and all the things which he did to you in the wilderness until you⌃ came into this place; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and all the things that he did to Dathan and Abiron the sons of Eliab the son of Ruben, whom the earth opening her mouth swallowed up, and their houses, and their tents, and all their substance that was with them, in the midst of all Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} for your eyes have seen all the mighty works of the Lord, which he wrought among you today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you⌃ shall keep all his commandments, as many as I command you today, that you⌃ may live, and be multiplied, and that you⌃ may go in and inherit the land, into which you⌃ go across Jordan to inherit it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} that you⌃ may live long upon the land, which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them, and to their seed after them, a land flowing with milk and honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the land into which you go to inherit it, is not as the land of Egypt, whence you⌃ came out, whenever they sow the seed, and water it with their feet, as a garden of herbs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} but the land into which you go to inherit it, is a land of mountains and plains; it shall drink water of the rain of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A land which the Lord your God surveys continually, the eyes of the Lord your God are upon it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now if you⌃ will indeed listen to all the commands which I charge you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve him with all your heart, and with all your soul, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} then he shall give to your land the early and latter rain in its season, and you shall bring in your corn, and your wine, and your oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he shall give food in your fields to your cattle; and when you have eaten and are full, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} take heed to yourself that your heart be not puffed up, and you⌃ transgress, and serve other gods, and worship them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and the Lord be angry with you, and restrain the heaven; and there shall not be rain, and the earth shall not yield its fruit, and you⌃ shall perish quickly from off the good land, which the Lord has given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you⌃ shall store these words in your heart and in your soul, and you⌃ shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and it shall be fixed before your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you⌃ shall teach them to your children, so as to speak about them when you sit in the house, and when you walk by the way, and when you sleep, and when you rise up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you⌃ shall write them on the lintels of your houses, and on your gates; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} that your days may be long, and the days of your children, upon the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them, as the days of heaven upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it shall come to pass that if you⌃ will indeed listen to all these commands, which I charge you to observe this day, to love the Lord our God, and to walk in all his ways, and to cleave close to him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} then the Lord shall cast out all these nations before you, and you⌃ shall inherit great nations and stronger than yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Every place whereon the sole of your foot shall tread shall be yours; from the wilderness and Antilibanus, and from the great river, the river Euphrates, even as far as the west sea shall be your coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} No one shall stand before you; and the Lord your God will put the fear of you and the dread of you on the face of all the land, on which you⌃ shall tread, as he told you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Behold, I set before you this day the blessing and the curse; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} the blessing, if you⌃ listen to the commands of the Lord your God, all that I command you this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and the curse, if you⌃ do not listen to the commands of the Lord our God, as many as I command you this day, and you⌃ wander from the way which I have commanded you, having gone to serve other gods, which you⌃ know not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it shall come to pass when the Lord your God shall have brought you into the land into which you go over to inherit it, then you shall put blessing on mount Garizin, and the curse upon mount Gaebal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Behold! are not these beyond Jordan, behind, westward in the land of Chanaan, which lies westward near Golgol, by the high oak? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For you⌃ are passing over Jordan, to go in and inherit the land, which the Lord our God gives you to inherit always, and you⌃ shall dwell in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you⌃ shall take heed to do all his ordinances, and these judgments, as many as I set before you today.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Heb. vocab: musar (מוּסָר) = discipline; correction. Common English renderings: instruction; chastening. A major wisdom term for formative discipline.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} thou shalt This verse is the practical improvement of the conclusion of the foregoing chapter; while the next verse begins another view of the subject., ; keep; his statutes \textsuperscript{2} And know Moses seems here to have addressed himself particularly to the elders, who had in their youth witnessed the wonderful works which Jehovah had wrought both for them and among them; and who were bound to remember them for their own warning, and testify them to the rising generation who had not been eye-witnesses.; the chastisement his greatness, his mighty \textsuperscript{6} he did unto, ; substance or, living substance which followed them in their possession Heb. at their feet \textsuperscript{10} wateredst it with thy foot Rain seldom falls in Egypt; the land being chiefly watered by the inundations of the Nile. In order to water the grounds where the inundations do not extend, water is collected in ponds, and directed in streamlets to the different parts of the field where irrigation is necessary. It is no unusual thing in the East to see a man, with a small mattock, making a little trench for the water to run into; and, as he opens the passage, the water following, he uses his foot to raise up the mould against the side of this little channel, to prevent the water from being shed unnecessarily, before it reaches the place of its destination. Hence he may justly be said to water the ground with his foot. \textsuperscript{12} careth for Heb. seeketh the eyes \textsuperscript{15} And I will; send Heb. give eat and be full \textsuperscript{16} Take heed;, your heart; and serve \textsuperscript{17} the Lord's, shut up; ye perish \textsuperscript{18} ye lay up; a sign \textsuperscript{21} your days, ;, as the days \textsuperscript{22} if ye shall, to love; to cleave \textsuperscript{25} There shall;, as he hath \textsuperscript{29} put the blessing; Gerizim and Ebal, mountains west of Jordan, and in the tribe of Ephraim, are opposite, or parallel to each other, extending from east to west; mount Gerizim being on the south, and mount Ebal on the north. They are separated by the beautiful valley in which Shechem or Nablous is situated, which is only about 200 paces in width. Both mountains are much alike in length, height, and figure; being about a league in length, in the form of a semicircle, and so steep, on the side of Shechem, that there is scarcely any shelving. Their altitude appeared to Mr. Buckingham nearly equal, not exceeding 700 or 800 feet from the level of the valley, which is itself elevated. But though they resemble each other in these particulars, yet in another they are very dissimilar; for, says Maundrell, "though neither of the mountains has much to boast of as to its pleasantness, yet, as one passes between them, Gerizim seems to discover a somewhat more verdant, fruitful aspect then Ebal. The reason of which may be, because fronting towards the north, it is sheltered from the heat of the sun by its own shade; whereas Ebal, looking southward, and receiving the sun that comes directly upon it, must by consequence be rendered more scorched and unfruitful."\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 12}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the ordinances and the judgments, which you⌃ shall observe to do in the land, which the Lord God of your fathers gives you for an inheritance, all the days which you⌃ live upon the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You⌃ shall utterly destroy all the places in which they served their gods, whose [land] you⌃ inherit, on the high mountains and on the hills, and under the thick tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you⌃ shall destroy their altars, and break in pieces their pillars, and you⌃ shall cut down their groves, and you⌃ shall burn with fire the graven images of their gods, and you⌃ shall abolish their name out of that place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ shall not do so to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But in the place which the Lord your God shall choose in one of your cities to name his name there, and to be called upon, you⌃ shall even seek [him] out and go there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall carry there your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your first fruits, and your vowed-offerings, and your free will offerings, and your offerings of thanksgiving, the firstborn of your herds, and of your flocks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you⌃ shall eat there before the Lord your God, and you⌃ shall rejoice in all the things on which you⌃ shall lay your hand, you⌃ and your houses, as the Lord your God has blessed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You⌃ shall not do altogether as we do here today, every man that which is pleasing in his own sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For hitherto you⌃ have not arrived at the rest and the inheritance, which the Lord our God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you⌃ shall go over Jordan, and shall dwell in the land, which the Lord our God takes as an inheritance for you; and he shall give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you⌃ shall dwell safely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And there shall be a place which the Lord your God shall choose for his name to be called there, there shall you⌃ bring all things that I order you today; your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes, and the first fruits of your hands, and every choice gift of yours, whatever you⌃ shall vow to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you⌃ shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you⌃ and your sons, and your daughters, and your menservants and your maidservants, and the Levite that is at your gates; because he has no portion or inheritance with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Take heed to yourself that you offer not your whole burnt offerings in any place which you shall see; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} save in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, in one of your tribes, there shall you⌃ offer your whole burnt offerings, and there shall you do all things whatever I charge you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But you shall kill according to all your desire, and shall eat flesh according to the blessing of the Lord your God, which he has given you in every city; the unclean that is within you and the clean shall eat it on equal terms, as the doe or the stag. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Only you⌃ shall not eat the blood; you⌃ shall pour it out on the ground as water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall not be able to eat in your cities the tithe of your corn, and of your wine, and of your oil, the firstborn of your herd and of your flock, and all [your] vows as many as you⌃ shall have vowed, and your thank-offerings, and the first fruits of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But before the Lord your God you shall eat it, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for himself, you, and your son, and your daughter, your man-servant, and your maidservant, and the stranger that is within your gates; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, on whatever you shall lay your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Take heed to yourself that you do not desert the Levite all the time that you live upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if the Lord your God shall enlarge your borders, as he said to you, and you shall say, I will eat flesh; if your soul should desire to eat flesh, you shall eat flesh according to all the desire of your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if the place be far from you, which the Lord your God shall choose for himself, that his name be called upon it, then you shall kill of your herd and of your flock which God shall have given you, even as I commanded you, and you shall eat in your cities according to the desire of your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} As the doe and the stag are eaten, so shall you eat it; the unclean in you and the clean shall eat it in like manner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Take diligent heed that you eat no blood, for blood [is] the life of it; the life shall not be eaten with the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You⌃ shall not eat [it]; you⌃ shall pour it out on the ground as water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} You shall not eat it, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, if you shall do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But you shall take your holy things, if you have any, and your vowed-offerings, and come to the place which the Lord your God shall choose to have his name named upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And you shall sacrifice your whole burnt offerings, you shall offer the flesh upon the altar of the Lord your God; but the blood of your sacrifices you shall pour out at the foot of the altar of the Lord your God, but the flesh you shall eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Beware and listen, and you shall do all the commands which I charge you, that it may be well with you and with your sons for ever, if you shall do that which is pleasing and good before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And if the Lord your God shall utterly destroy the nations, to whom you go in there to inherit their land, from before you, and you shall inherit it, and dwell in their land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} take heed to yourself that you seek not to follow them after they are destroyed before you, saying, How do these nations act towards their gods? I will do likewise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} You shall not do so to your God; for they have sacrificed to their gods the abominations of the Lord which he hates, for they burn their sons and their daughters in fire to their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Every word that I command you this day, it shall you observe to do: you shall not add to it, nor diminish from it.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the statutes, all the days \textsuperscript{3} ye shall; overthrow Heb. break down and burn; and destroy \textsuperscript{11} a place, ; your choice Heb. the choice of your \textsuperscript{12} And ye; the Levite, forasmuch \textsuperscript{13} This was directly opposed to the customs of the heathen idolaters, in offering their sacrifices on the tops of hills and mountains. \textsuperscript{15} whatsoever the unclean, ; Of the propriety of eating clean animals there could be no question, but the blood must be poured out. Yet there were cases when they might kill and eat in all their gates such as the roebuck and the hart, or all clean wild beasts; for these being taken in hunting, and frequently shot by arrows, their blood could not be poured out at the altar \textsuperscript{19} Take; as long etc. Heb. all thy days \textsuperscript{20} shall as he hath; I will \textsuperscript{23} sure Heb. strong the blood is \textsuperscript{27} thy burnt, and the blood \textsuperscript{29} cut off; succeedest Heb. inheritest, or, possessest \textsuperscript{30} that thou; by following Heb. after How did \textsuperscript{31} Thou; abomination to the Heb. abomination of the even their sons The unnatural and horrid practice of offering human sacrifices not only existed, but universally prevailed among ancient nations. We have already (See note on ) referred to the custom among the Phoenicians and Carthaginians, descendants from the Canaanitish nations, of sacrificing their children to Moloch, or Saturn; and we will now cite a passage from Diodorus Siculus (lib. xx.) which immediately precedes that already produced relative to this barbarous custom. He states that the Carthaginians imputed their being besieged by Agathocles to the anger of Saturn, because, instead of sacrificing the best of their own children, as formerly, they had sacrificed children bought for that purpose. "In haste, therefore, to rectify their errors, they chose 200 of the noblest children, and publicly sacrificed them! Others, accused of irreligion, voluntarily gave themselves up, to the number of no less than 300!"\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 13}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if there arise within you a prophet, or one who dreams a dream, and he gives you a sign or a wonder, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and the sign or the wonder come to pass which he spoke to you, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which you⌃ know not; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} you⌃ shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or the dreamer of that dream, because the Lord your God tries you, to know whether you⌃ love your God with all your heart and with all your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You⌃ shall follow the Lord your God, and fear him, and you⌃ shall hear his voice, and attach yourselves to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And that prophet or that dreamer of a dream, shall die; for he has spoken to make you err from the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, who redeemed you from bondage, to thrust you out of the way which the Lord your God commanded you to walk in: so shall you abolish the evil from among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if your brother by your father or mother, or your son, or daughter, or your wife in your bosom, or friend who is equal to your own soul, entreat you secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which neither you nor your fathers have known, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} of the gods of the nations that are round about you, who are near you or at a distance from you, from one end of the earth to the other; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} you shall not consent to him, neither shall you listen to him; and your eye shall not spare him, you shall feel no regret for him, neither shall you at all protect him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} you shall surely report concerning him, and your hands shall be upon him among the first to kill him, and the hands of all the people at the last. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, because he sought to draw you away from the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall not again do according to this evil thing among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if in one of your cities which the Lord God gives you to dwell therein, you shall hear men saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Evil men have gone out from you, and have caused all the inhabitants of their land to fall away, saying, Let us go and worship other gods, whom you⌃ knew not, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} then you shall enquire and ask, and search diligently, and behold, [if] the thing is clearly true, and this abomination has taken place among you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} you shall utterly destroy all the dwellers in that land with the edge of the sword; you⌃ shall solemnly curse it, and all things in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And all its spoils you shall gather into its public ways, and you shall burn the city with fire, and all its spoils publicly before the Lord your God; and it shall be uninhabited for ever, it shall not be built again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And there shall nothing of the cursed thing cleave to your hand, that the Lord may turn from his fierce anger, and show you mercy, and pity you, and multiply you, as he swore to your fathers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} if you will hear the voice of the Lord your God, to keep his commandments, all that I charge you this day, to do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a prophet That is, one pretending to the divine inspiration and authority of the prophetic office, or a dreamer of dreams, one who pretends that some deity has spoken to him in the night season, and giveth thee a sign, oth, what appears to be a miraculous proof of his mission, or a wonder, mopheth, some portentous sign, such as an eclipse, which he, who knew when it would happen, might predict to the people, who knew nothing of the matter, and thereby accredit his pretensions. \subsection*{Deuteronomy 14}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You⌃ are the children of the Lord your God: you⌃ shall not make any baldness between your eyes for the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God has chosen you to be a peculiar people to himself of all the nations on the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You⌃ shall not eat any abominable thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} These [are] the beasts which you⌃ shall eat; the calf of the herd, and lamb of the sheep, and kid of the goats; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} the stag, and doe, and pygarg, and wild goat, and camelopard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Every beast that divides the hoofs, and makes claws of two divisions, and that chews the cud among beasts, these you⌃ shall eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And these you⌃ shall not eat of them that chew the cud, and of those that divide the hoofs, and make distinct claws; the camel, and the hare, and the rabbit; because they chew the cud, and do not divide the hoof, these are unclean to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And as for the swine, because he divides the hoof, and makes claws of the hoof, yet he chews not the cud, he is unclean to you; you⌃ shall not eat of their flesh, you⌃ shall not touch their dead bodies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And these you⌃ shall eat of all that are in the water, you⌃ shall eat all that have fins and scales. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all that have not fins and scales you⌃ shall not eat; they are unclean to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You⌃ shall eat every clean bird. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And these of them you⌃ shall not eat; the eagle, and the ossifrage, and the sea-eagle, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and the vulture, and the kite and the like to it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the sparrow, and the owl, and the cormorant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and the heron, and the swan, and the stork, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and the cormorant, and the hawk, and its like, and the hoopoe, and the raven, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the pelican, and the diver and the like to it, and the red-bill and the bat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} All winged animals that creep are unclean to you; you⌃ shall not eat of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You⌃ shall eat every clean bird. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You⌃ shall eat nothing that dies of itself; it shall be given to the sojourner in your cities and he shall eat it, or you shall sell it to a stranger, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in his mother's milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You shall tithe a tenth of all the produce of your seed, the fruit of your field year by year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you shall eat it in the place which the Lord your God shall choose to have his name called there; you⌃ shall bring the tithe of your corn and of your wine, and of your oil, the firstborn of your herd and of your flock, that you may learn to fear the Lord your God always. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And if the journey be too far for you, and you are not able to bring them, because the place [is] far from you which the Lord your God shall choose to have his name called there, because the Lord your God will bless you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} then you shall sell them for money, and you shall take the money in your hands, and you shall go to the place which the Lord your God shall choose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall give the money for whatever your soul shall desire, for oxen or for sheep, or for wine, or [you shall lay it out] on strong drink, or on whatever your soul may desire, and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and you shall rejoice and your house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and the Levite that is in your cities, because he has not a portion or inheritance with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} After three years you shall bring out all the tithes of your fruits, in that year you shall lay it up in your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the Levite shall come, because he has no part or lot with you, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow which is in your cities; For their support, the Levites had: 1. The tenth of all the productions of the land. 2. Forty-eight cities, each forming a square of 4, 000 cubits. 3. Two thousand cubits of ground round each city; total of land, 53, 000 acres. 4. The first-fruits, and certain parts of all the animals killed in the land. But though this was a very small proportion for a whole tribe that had consented to annihilate its political existence, that it might wait upon the service of God, yet, let it be considered, that what they possessed was the best of the land, and while it was slender remuneration for their services, yet their portion was such as rendered them independent, and kept them comfortable; so that they could wait on God, and labour in his work, without distraction. \textsuperscript{29} he hath, the stranger, ; that the Lord\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 15}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Every seven years you shall make a release. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And this [is] the ordinance of the release: you shall remit every private debt which your neighbor owes you, and you shall not ask payment of it from your brother; for it has been called a release to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Of a stranger you shall ask again whatever he has of yours, but to your brother you shall remit his debt to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For [thus] there shall not be a poor person in the midst of you, for the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you by inheritance, that you should inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if you⌃ shall indeed listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all these commandments, as many as I charge you this day, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} (for the Lord your God has blessed you in the way of which he spoke to you,) then you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if there shall be in the midst of you a poor [man] of your brethren in one of your cities in the land, which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, neither shall you by any means close up your hand from your brother who is in lack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You shall surely open your hands to him, and shall lend to him as much as he wants according to his need. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Take heed to yourself that there be not a secret thing in your heart, an iniquity, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye shall be evil to your brother that is in lack, and you shall not give to him, and he shall cry against you to the Lord, and there shall be great sin in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You shall surely give to him, and you shall lend him as much as he wants, according as he is in need; and you shall not grudge in your heart as you give to him, because on this account the Lord your God will bless you in all your works, and in all things on which you shall lay your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the poor shall not fail off your land, therefore I charge you to do this thing, saying, You shall surely open your hands to your poor brother, and to him that is distressed upon your land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if your brother [or sister], a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, be sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him out free from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And when you shall send him out free from you, you shall not send him out empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall give him provision for the way from your flock, and from your corn, and from your wine; as the Lord your God has blessed you, you shall give to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you from thence; therefore I charge you to do this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if he should say to you, I will not go out from you, because he continues to love you and your house, because he is well with you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} then you shall take an awl, and bore his ear through to the door, and he shall be your servant for ever; and in like manner shall you do to your maidservant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} It shall not seem hard to you when they are sent out free from you, because [your servant] has served you six years according to the annual hire of a hireling; so the Lord your God shall bless you in all things whatever you may do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Every firstborn that shall be born among your kine and your sheep, you shall sanctify the males to the Lord your God; you shall not work with your firstborn calf, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You shall eat it before the Lord year by year in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, you and your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if there be in it a blemish, if it be lame or blind, an evil blemish, you shall not sacrifice it to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You shall eat it in your cities; the unclean in you and the clean shall eat it in like manner, as the doe or the stag. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Only you⌃ shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out on the earth as water.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{4} Heb. vocab: evyon (אֶבְיוֹן) = needy. Common English renderings: needy; poor. Highlights socioeconomic vulnerability.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} creditor that lendeth Heb. master of the lending of his hand exact it \textsuperscript{4} Save etc. or, To the end that there be no poor among you, Houbigant follows this marginal reading, to which he joins the end of the, considering it as explanatory of the law; as if he had said, "Thou shalt not exact the debt that is due from thy brother, but thy hand shall release him, for this reason, that there may be no poor among you through your severity." He justly contends that the phrase ephes kee, can here only mean, "to the end that, " being equivalent to the French afin que . greatly bless \textsuperscript{6} thou shalt lend; thou shalt reign \textsuperscript{7} there be Lest the preceding law might render the Israelites cautious in lending to the poor, Moses here warns them against being led by so mean a principle; but to lend liberally, and God would reward them. thou shalt \textsuperscript{9} Beware; thought etc. Heb. word with thine heart of Belial thine eye; he cry; sin unto thee \textsuperscript{11} the poor Although Moses, by the statutes relative to the division of the land, and inheritance, and the inalienable nature of it, had studied to prevent any Israelite from being born poor, yet he exhorts them to the exercise of the tenderest compassion and most benevolent actions; and not to refuse assistance to the decayed Israelite, though the sabbatical year drew nigh.; Thou shalt \textsuperscript{13} This is a most humane and merciful addition to the law in; enforced upon the Israelites by the consideration of their Egyptian bondage. As a faithful servant has made no property for himself while honestly serving his master, so now, when he quits his service, he has nothing to begin the world with except what the kindness of his master may bestow upon him as a remuneration for his zeal and fidelity. Though what was to be bestowed upon servants is not fixed, yet they were to be liberally supplied ( ). \textsuperscript{19} the firstling, ; thou shalt do \textsuperscript{22} the unclean, the roebuck Tzevee, in Arabic zaby, Chaldee and Syriac tavya, denotes the gazelle or antelope, so called from its stately beauty, as the word imports. In size it is smaller than the roe, of an elegant form, and it motions are light and graceful. It bounds seemingly without effort, and runs with such swiftness that few creatures can exceed it ( ). Its fine eyes are so much celebrated as even to become a proverb; and its flesh is much esteemed for food among eastern nations, having a sweet, musky taste, which is highly agreeable to their palates ( ). If to these circumstances we add, that they are gregarious, and common all over the East, whereas the roe is either not known at all, or else very rare in these countries, little doubt can remain that the gazelle and not the roe is intended by the original word.\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 16}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Observe the month of new [corn], and you shall sacrifice the passover to the Lord your God; because in the month of new [corn] you came out of Egypt by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall sacrifice the passover to the Lord your God, sheep and oxen in the place which the Lord your God shall choose to have his name called upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You shall not eat leaven with it; seven days shall you eat unleavened [bread] with it, bread of affliction, because you⌃ came forth out of Egypt in haste; that you⌃ may remember the day of your coming forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Leaven shall not be seen with you in all your borders for seven days, and there shall not be left of the flesh which you shall sacrifice at even on the first day until the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} you shall not have power to sacrifice the passover in any of the cities, which the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, to have his name called there, you shall sacrifice the passover at even at the setting of the sun, at the time when you came out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall boil and roast and eat it in the place, which the Lord your God shall choose; and you shall return in the morning, and go to your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Six days shall you eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a holiday, a feast to the Lord your God: you shall not do in it any work, save what must be done by any one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Seven weeks shall you number to yourself; when you have begun [to put] the sickle to the corn, you shall begin to number seven weeks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall keep the feast of weeks to the Lord your God, accordingly as your hand has power in as many things as the Lord your God shall give you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your son, and your daughter, your man-servant and your maidservant, and the Levite, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow which dwells among you, in whatever place the Lord your God shall choose, that his name should be called there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and you shall observe and do these commands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall keep for yourself the feast of tabernacles seven days, when you gather in [your produce] from your corn-floor and your wine-press. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, your man-servant, and your maidservant, and the Levite, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow that is in your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Seven days shall you keep a feast to the Lord your God in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for himself; and if the Lord your God shall bless you in all your fruits, and in every work of your hands, then you shall rejoice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Three times in the year shall all your males appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: you shall not appear before the Lord your God empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Each one according to his ability, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which he has given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You shall make for yourself judges and officers in your cities, which the Lord your God gives you in [your] tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} they shall not wrest judgment, nor favor persons, nor receive a gift; for gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You shall justly pursue justice, that you⌃ may live, and go in and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You shall not plant for yourself a grove; you shall not plant for yourself any tree near the altar of your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the Lord your God hates.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the month; the passover This word comes from the Hebrew verb pasach, to pass, to leap or skip over. The destroying angel passed over the houses marked with the blood of the Paschal Lamb, so the wrath of God passes over those whose souls sprinkled with the blood of Christ. . As the paschal lamb was killed before Israel was delivered, so by the death of Christ, we have redemption through his blood. It was killed before the tables of the law were delivered to Moses, or Aaron's sacrifices were enjoined; thus deliverance comes to men, not by the works of the law, but by the only true passover, the Lamb of God. . . It was killed the first month of the year, which prefigured that Christ should suffer death in that month. . it was killed in the evening. . Christ suffered at that time of the day. . . At even the sun sets; at Christ's passion, universal darkness was upon the whole earth. The passover was roasted with fire, denoting the sharp and dreadful pains that Christ should suffer, not only from men, but God also. It was to be eaten with bitter herbs; not only to put them in remembrance of their bitter bondage in Egypt, but also to testify our mortification to sin, and readiness to undergo afflictions for Christ; and likewise to teach us the absolute necessity of true repentance in all that would profitably feed by faith on Christ, the true paschal lamb. for in \textsuperscript{2} sacrifice; in the place which \textsuperscript{3} eat no, ; the bread; for thou camest, mayest \textsuperscript{8} Six days; solemn assembly Heb. restraint; *marg. \textsuperscript{10} a tribute or, sufficiency;, *marg.; according \textsuperscript{13} the feast; corn and thy wine Heb. floor and thine wine-press \textsuperscript{16} Three times; and they shall \textsuperscript{17} as he is able Heb. according to the gift of his hand \textsuperscript{18} Judges, ; in all thy gates This expression may refer to the gate of the city, as the forum or place of public concourse among the Israelites, where a court of judicature was held, to try all causes and decide all affairs. The same practice obtained among other Eastern nations. The Ottoman court, it is well known, derived its appellation of the Porte, from the distribution of justice and the dispatch of public business at its gates. And the square tower which forms the principal entrance to the Alhamra, or red palace of the Moorish kings of Grenada, retains to this day the appellation of the Gate of judgment, from its having been the place where justice was at one period summarily administered. \textsuperscript{19} wrest; respect; words or, matters \textsuperscript{20} That which etc. Heb. Justice, justice; live \textsuperscript{22} image or, statue, or pillar; which\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 17}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a calf or a sheep, in which there is a blemish, [or] any evil thing; for it is an abomination to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if there should be found in any one of your cities, which the Lord your God gives you, a man or a woman who shall do that which is evil before the Lord your God, so as to transgress his covenant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and they should go and serve other gods, and worship them, the sun, or the moon, or any of the host of heaven, which he commanded you not to do, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and it be told you, and you shall have enquired diligently, and, behold, the thing really took place, this abomination has been done in Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} then shall you bring out that man, or that woman, and you⌃ shall stone them with stones, and they shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He shall die on the testimony of two or three witnesses; a man who is put to death shall not be put to death for one witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the hand of the witnesses shall be upon him among the first to put him to death, and the hand of the people at the last; so shall you remove the evil one from among yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if a matter shall be too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, and between cause and cause, and between stroke and stroke, and between contradiction and contradiction, matters of judgment in your cities; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} then you shall arise and go up to the place which the Lord your God shall choose, and you shall come to the priests the Levites, and to the judge who shall be in those days, and they shall search out [the matter] and report the judgment to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall act according to the thing which they shall report to you out of the place which the Lord your God shall choose, and you shall observe to do all whatever shall have been by law appointed to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall do according to the law and to the judgment which they shall declare to you: you shall not swerve to the right hand or to the left from any sentence which they shall report to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the man whoever shall act in haughtiness, so as not to listen to the priest who stands to minister in the name of the Lord your God, or the judge who shall preside in those days, that man shall die, and you shall remove the evil one out of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And all the people shall hear and fear, and shall no more commit impiety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when you shall enter into the land which the Lord your God gives you, and shall inherit it and dwell in it, and shall say, I will set a ruler over me, as also the other nations round about me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} you shall surely set over you the ruler whom the Lord God shall choose: of your brethren you shall set over you a ruler; you shall not have power to set over you a stranger, because he is not your brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For he shall not multiply to himself horses, and he shall by no means turn the people back to Egypt, lest he should multiply to himself horses; for the Lord said, You⌃ shall not any more turn back by that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he shall not multiply to himself wives, lest his heart turn away; and he shall not greatly multiply to himself silver and gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And when he shall be established in his government, then shall he write for himself this repetition of the law into a book by the hands of the priests the Levites; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord your God, and to keep all these commandments, and to observe these ordinances: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he depart not from the commandments on the right hand or on the left; that he and his sons may reign long in his dominion among the children of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Thou shalt sheep or, goat, any evil favouredness, for that \textsuperscript{2} within any of thy gates The expression, "within any of thy gates, " denoted all residing in the cities, and all who went in and came out at the gates of them; so that it included the inhabitants of the whole land. man, in transgressing \textsuperscript{7} of the witnesses; So thou \textsuperscript{8} arise; between blood;, ;, get thee up \textsuperscript{11} According to; to the right \textsuperscript{12} will do; and will not hearken Heb. not to hearken, the priest, ; that man thou shalt \textsuperscript{14} When thou, ; I will set \textsuperscript{15} whom, ; from among; not set \textsuperscript{16} multiply horses Multiplying horses for chariots of war and cavalry, or for luxury, would increase the splendour of a monarch, and form a ground of confidence distinct from a proper confidence in God, and inconsistent with it, and with considering him as the glory of Israel. Egypt abounded in horses; and the desire of multiplying these would induce the prince to encourage a trade with that kingdom; and this might make way for the Israelites being again subjugated by the Egyptians, or at least corrupted by their idolatries and vices. Whereas, it was the command of God that they should no more return thither, but be totally detached from them. Besides, they might be tempted to extend their dominion by means of cavalry, and so get scattered among the surrounding idolatrous nations, and thus cease to be that distinct, separate people, which God intended they should be.; cause; Ye shall henceforth \textsuperscript{17} multiply wives; neither shall he \textsuperscript{18} that he shall a copy Mishneh hattorah hazzoth, "a duplicate of this law." translated by the Septuagint, το δευτερονομιον τουτο, this Deuteronomy. \subsection*{Deuteronomy 18}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The priests, the Levites, even the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; the burnt offerings of the Lord [are] their inheritance, they shall eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they shall have no inheritance among their brethren; the Lord himself [is] his portion, as he said to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And this [is] the due of the priests in the things coming from the people from those who offer sacrifices, whether it be a calf or a sheep; and you shall give the shoulder to the priest, and the cheeks, and the great intestine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and the first fruits of your corn, and of your wine, and of your oil; and you shall give to him the first fruits of the fleeces of your sheep: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} because the Lord has chosen him out of all your tribes, to stand before the Lord your God, to minister and bless in his name, himself and his sons among the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if a Levite come from one of the cities of all the children of Israel, where he himself dwells, accordingly as his mind desires, to the place which he shall have chosen, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} he shall minister to the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites, who stand there present before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He shall eat an allotted portion, besides the sale of his hereditary property. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when you shall have entered into the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} There shall not be found in you one who purges his son or his daughter with fire, one who uses divination, who deals with omens, and augury, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} a sorcerer employing incantation, one who has in him a divining spirit, an observer of signs, questioning the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For every one that does these things is an abomination to the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord will destroy them from before your face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall be perfect before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For all these nations whose [land] you shall inherit, they will listen to omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not permitted you so [to do]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The Lord your God shall raise up to you a prophet of your brethren, like me; him shall you⌃ hear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} according to all things which you did desire of the Lord your God in Choreb in the day of the assembly, saying, We will not again hear the voice of the Lord your God, and we will not any more see this great fire, and [so] we shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord said to me, They have spoken rightly all that they have said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I will raise up to them a prophet of their brethren, like you; and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them as I shall command him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And whatever man shall not listen to whatever words that prophet shall speak in my name, I will take vengeance on him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But the prophet whoever shall impiously speak in my name a word which I have not commanded him to speak, and whoever shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But if you shall say in your heart, How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Whatsoever words that prophet shall speak in the name of the Lord, and they shall not come true, and not come to pass, this [is] the thing which the Lord has not spoken; that prophet has spoken wickedly: you⌃ shall not spare him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{6} come and come with, ; unto the place \textsuperscript{8} like portions; that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony Heb. his sales by the fathers \textsuperscript{10} maketh; that useth divination The precise import of the terms here used to express these unhallowed practices cannot be clearly ascertained. He that useth divination, kosaim, kesamim, seems a general term for the various species after specified; observer of times, meonain, one who pretends to foretell by the clouds, planets, etc.; enchanter menachesh, a diviner, either by means of serpents, or by inspecting the entrails of beasts, the flight of birds, etc.; a witch, mecashsheph, one who used magical fumigations, etc.; a charmer, chover chaver, one who uses spells, or a peculiar conjunction of words, or tying knots, etc.; a consulter with familiar spirits, shoel ov, a pythoness; a wizard, yidoni, a cunning man; necromancer, doresh el hammaithim one who seeks enquiries of the dead. \textsuperscript{13} Thou shalt; perfect or, upright, or, sincere \textsuperscript{14} possess or, inherit hath not suffered \textsuperscript{15} a Prophet; like unto me; , unto him \textsuperscript{16} in Horeb Let me not hear \textsuperscript{18} raise them; like unto; will put; he shall \textsuperscript{20} the prophet;, ; in the name \textsuperscript{22} speaketh; if the thing; presumptuously; shalt not\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 19}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when the Lord your God shall have destroyed the nations, which God gives you, [even] the land, and you⌃ shall inherit them, and dwell in their cities, and in their houses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} you shall separate for yourself three cities in the midst of your land, which the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Take a survey of your way, and you shall divide the coasts of your land, which the Lord your God apportions to you, into three parts, and there shall be there a refuge for every manslayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And this shall be the ordinance of the manslayer, who shall flee there, and shall live, whoever shall have struck his neighbor ignorantly, whereas he hated him not in times past. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And whoever shall enter with his neighbor into the thicket, to gather wood, if the hand of him that cuts wood with the axe should be violently shaken, and the axe head falling off from the handle should light on his neighbor, and he should die, he shall flee to one of these cities, and live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Lest the avenger of blood pursue after the slayer, because his heart is hot, and overtake him, if the way be too long, and kill him, though there is to this man no sentence of death, because he hated him not in time past. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore I charge you, saying, You shall separate for your self three cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if the Lord shall enlarge your borders, as he swore to your fathers, and the Lord shall give to you all the land which he said he would give to your fathers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} if you shall listen to do all these commands, which I charge you this day, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways continually; you shall add for yourself yet three cities to these three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So innocent blood shall not be spilled in the land, which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, and there shall not be in you one guilty of blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But if there should be in you a man hating his neighbor, and he should lay wait for him, and rise up against him, and strike him, that he die, and he should flee to one of these cities, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} then shall the elders of his city send, and take him thence, and they shall deliver him into the hands of the avengers of blood, and he shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Your eye shall not spare him; so shall you purge innocent blood from Israel, and it shall be well with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not move the landmarks of your neighbor, which your fathers set in the inheritance, in which you have obtained a share in the land, which the Lord your God gives you to inherit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} One witness shall not stand to testify against a man for any iniquity, or for any fault, or for any sin which he may commit; by the mouth of two witnesses, or by the mouth of three witnesses, shall every word be established. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if an unjust witness rise up against a man, alleging iniquity against him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} then shall the two men between whom the controversy is, stand before the Lord, and before the priests, and before the judges, who may be in those days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the judges shall make diligent inquiry, and, behold, [if] an unjust witness has borne unjust testimony; [and] has stood up against his brother; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} then shall you⌃ do to him as he wickedly devised to do against his brother, and you shall remove the evil from yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the rest shall hear and fear, and do no more according to this evil thing in the midst of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Your eye shall not spare him: [you shall exact] life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} hath cut, succeedest Heb. inheritest, or possessest \textsuperscript{2} separate three cities Unquestionably in imitation of these cities, the heathen had their asyla, and the Roman Catholics their privileged altars, and similar traditions seem to obtain in many barbarous nations, for "the North American Indian nations have most of them either a house or town of refuge, which is a sure asylum to protect a manslayer, or the unfortunate captive, if he once enter it. In almost every Indian nation, there are several towns, which are called old beloved, ancient, holy, or white towns (white being their fixed emblem of peace, friendship, prosperity, happiness, purity, etc.). They seem to have been formerly towns of refuge; for it is not in the memory of the oldest people that human blood was shed in them." \textsuperscript{4} the slayer; in time past Heb. from yesterday the third day; *marg. \textsuperscript{5} head Heb. iron, helve Heb. wood lighteth Heb. findeth he shall flee \textsuperscript{6} the avenger; slay him Heb. smite him in life not worthy; in time past Heb. from yesterday the third day \textsuperscript{9} If thou shalt, then shalt thou \textsuperscript{11} But if any; mortally Heb. in life \textsuperscript{14} shalt not remove Before the extensive use of fences, landed property was marked out by stones or posts, set up so as to ascertain the divisions of family estates. It was easy to remove one of these landmarks, and set it in a different place; and thus a dishonest man might enlarge his own estate by contracting that of his neighbour. Hence it was a matter of considerable importance to prevent this crime among the Israelites; among whom, removing them would be equivalent to forging, altering, destroying, or concealing the title-deeds of an estate among us. Accordingly, by the Mosaic law, it was not only prohibited in the commandment against covetousness, but we find a particular curse expressly annexed to it in . Josephus considers this law a general prohibition, intended not only to protect private property, but also to preserve the boundaries of kingdoms and countries inviolable. \textsuperscript{16} a false witness; that which is wrong or, falling away\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 20}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if you should go forth to war against your enemies, and should see horse, and rider, and a people more numerous than yourself; you shall not be afraid of them, for the Lord your God [is] with you, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it shall come to pass whenever you shall draw near to battle, that the priest shall draw near and speak to the people, and shall say to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Hear, O Israel; you⌃ are going this day to battle against your enemies: let not your heart faint, fear not, neither be confounded, neither turn aside from their face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For [it is] the Lord your God who advances with you, to fight with you against your enemies, [and] to save you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the scribes shall speak to the people, saying, What man [is] he that has built a new house, and has not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war, and another man dedicate it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And what man [is] he that has planted a vineyard, and not been made merry with it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man be made merry with it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And what man [is] he that has betrothed a wife, and has not taken her? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the scribes shall speak further to the people, and say, What man [is] he that fears and is cowardly in his heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest he make the heart of his brother fail, as his own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall come to pass when the scribes shall have ceased speaking to the people, that they shall appoint generals of the army to be leaders of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if you shall draw near to a city to overcome them by war, then call them out peaceably. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If then they should answer peaceably to you, and open to you, it shall be that all the people found in it shall be tributary and subject to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But if they will not listen to you, but wage war against you, you shall invest it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} until the Lord your God shall deliver it into your hands, and you shall strike every male of it with the edge of the sword: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} except the women and the stuff: and all the cattle, and whatever shall be in the city, and all the plunder you shall take as spoil for yourself, and shall eat all the plunder of your enemies whom the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Thus shall you do to all the cities that are very far off from you, not [being] of the cities of these nations which the Lord your God gives you to inherit their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [Of these] you⌃ shall not take any thing alive; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} but you⌃ shall surely curse them, the Chettite, and the Amorite, and the Chananite, and the Pherezite, and the Evite, and the Jebusite, and the Gergesite; as the Lord your God commanded you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} that they may not teach you to do all their abominations, which they did to their gods, and [so] you⌃ should sin before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if you should besiege a city many days to prevail against it by war to take it, you shall not destroy its trees, by applying an iron tool to them, but you shall eat of it, and shall not cut it down: Is the tree that is in the field a man, to enter before you into the work of the siege? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But the tree which you know to be not fruit-bearing, this you shall destroy and cut down; and you shall construct a mound against the city, which makes war against you, until it be delivered up.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} goest out, horses, ; the Lord \textsuperscript{3} let not; faint Heb. be tender tremble Heb. make haste, be ye terrified \textsuperscript{6} eaten of it Heb. made it common, Deut. 28:1-30:20; lest he die \textsuperscript{7} betrothed a wife It was customary among the Jews to contract matrimony, espouse, or betroth, and for a considerable time to leave the parties in the houses of the respective parents; and when the bridegroom had made proper preparations, then the bride was brought home to his house, and the marriage consummated. The provisions in this verse refer to a case of this kind; though the Jews extend it to him who had newly consummated his marriage, and even to him who had married his brother's wife. It was deemed a peculiar hardship for a person to be obliged to go to battle, who had left a house unfinished, newly purchased land half tilled, or a wife with whom he had just contracted marriage.; lest he die \textsuperscript{8} fearful; lest his brethren's, ; faint Heb. melt, *marg. \textsuperscript{9} to lead the people Heb. to be in the head of the people \textsuperscript{14} the women, ; take unto thyself Heb. spoil thou shalt eat \textsuperscript{19} thou shalt not, ; for the tree etc. or, for, O man, the tree of the field is to be employed in the siege, The original is exceedingly difficult. The LXX has it, "Is the tree in the field a man, to enter the trench before thee?" The Latin Vulgate: "For it is a tree, and not a man, neither can it increase the number of those who war against thee; " Onkelos, "For the tree of the field is not as a man, that it should come against thee in the siege; " and to the same purpose the Arabic, Philo, and Josephus who say, "If trees could speak, they would cry out, that it is unjust that they, who were no cause of the war, should suffer the miseries of it." However rendered, the sense is sufficiently clear, and it is a merciful provision to spare all the fruit trees for the support of both the besieged and besiegers. to employ etc. Heb. to go from before thee \textsuperscript{20} thou shalt build; be subdued Heb. come down\par}
