\subsection*{Deuteronomy 21}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if one be found slain with the sword in the land, which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, having fallen in the field, and they do not know who has struck [him]; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} your elders and your judges shall come forth, and shall measure the distances of the cities round about the slain man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and it shall be that the city which is nearest to the slain man the elders of that city shall take a heifer of the herd, which has not laboured, and which has not borne a yoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the elders of that city shall bring down the heifer into a rough valley, which has not been tilled and is not sown, and they shall kill the heifer in the valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the priests the Levites shall come, because the Lord God has chosen them to stand by him, and to bless in his name, and by their word shall every controversy and every stroke be [decided]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all the elders of that city who draw near to the slain man shall wash their hands over the head of the heifer which was slain in the valley; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and they shall answer and say, Our hands have not shed this blood, and our eyes have not seen [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be merciful to your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, O Lord, that innocent blood may not be charged on your people Israel: and the blood shall be atoned for to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you shall take away innocent blood from among you, if you should do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if when you go out to war against your enemies, the Lord your God should deliver them into your hands, and you should take their spoil, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and should see among the spoil a woman beautiful in countenance, and should desire her, and take her to yourself for a wife, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and should bring her within your house: then shall you shave her head, and pare her nails; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and shall take away her garments of captivity from off her, and she shall abide in your house, and shall bewail her father and mother the days of a month; and afterwards you shall go in to her and dwell with her, and she shall be your wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it shall be if you do not delight in her, you shall send her out free; and she shall not by any means be sold for money, you shall not treat her contemptuously, because you have humbled her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And if a man have two wives, the one loved and the other hated, and both the loved and the hated should have born him [children], and the son of the hated should be firstborn; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} then it shall be that whenever he shall divide by inheritance his goods to his sons, he shall not be able to give the right of the firstborn to the son of the loved one, having overlooked the son of the hated, which is the firstborn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But he shall acknowledge the firstborn of the hated one to give to him double of all things which shall be found by him, because he is the first of his children, and to him belongs the birthright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if any man has a disobedient and contentious son, who hearkens not to the voice of his father and the voice of his mother, and they should correct him, and he should not listen to them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} then shall his father and his mother take hold of him, and bring him forth to the elders of his city, and to the gate of the place: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and they shall say to the men of their city, This our son is disobedient and contentious, he hearkens not to our voice, he is a reveler and a drunkard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; and you shall remove the evil one from yourselves, and the rest shall hear and fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if there be sin in any one, [and] the judgment of death [be upon him], and he be put to death, and you⌃ hang him on a tree: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but you⌃ shall by all means bury it in that day; for every one that is hanged on a tree is cursed of God; and you⌃ shall by no means defile the land which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} a rough valley As the word nachal signifies both a torrent, and the valley or glen through which it flows, nachal aithan may be rendered a rapid torrent. Many torrents in Judea are dry during a great part of the year; when not only their banks but their beds may be ploughed, and yield a crop. Hence there is no impropriety in specifying that such a place should be one that "is neither cared nor sown; " while the circumstance that the elders were to wash their hands over the heifer, whose head had been struck off into the stream, confirms this interpretation. The spot of ground where this sacrifice was made must be uncultivated, because it was considered as a sacrifice for the atonement of murder, and, consequently, would pollute the land. shall strike \textsuperscript{5} for them; by their word; word Heb. mouth \textsuperscript{6} wash their hands Washing the hands was anciently a symbolical action, denoting that the person was innocent of the crime in question. \textsuperscript{8} lay not; unto thy people Heb. in the midst \textsuperscript{9} shalt thou when thou shalt \textsuperscript{12} and she shall This was in token of renouncing her religion, and becoming a proselyte to that of the Jews. This is still a custom in the East. When a Christian turns Mohammedan, his head is shaved, and he is carried through the city, crying, la eelah eela allah wemochammed resoolullahee, "There is no God but the God, and Mohammed is the prophet of God."; pare her nails or, suffer to grow, Heb. make, or dress, Weâsethah eth tzipparneyha, "and she shall make her nails; " i.e., probably neither paring nor letting them grow, but dressing or beautifying them as the Eastern women still do by tinging them with the leaves of an odoriferous plant called alhenna, which Hasselquist (p. 246) informs us, "grows in India and in upper and lower Egypt, flowering from May to August. The leaves are pulverized and made into a paste with water. They bind this paste on the nails of their hands and feet, and keep it on all night. This gives them a deep yellow, which is greatly admired by Eastern nations. The colour lasts for three or four weeks before there is occasion to renew it. The custom is so ancient in Egypt, that I have seen the nails of mummies dyed in this manner." \textsuperscript{17} by giving, ; that he hath Heb. that is found with him the beginning; the right \textsuperscript{18} have a stubborn, ; obey the voice; when they;, ; will not \textsuperscript{20} he will not he is a glutton \textsuperscript{21} all the men; so shalt thou, all Israel \textsuperscript{22} So in, we read, "And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads (chief men) of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel." Among the Romans, in after ages, they hanged, or rather fastened to the tree ALIVE; and such was the cruel death of our blessed Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.; , worthy of death Heb. of the judgment of death, The Hebrews understand this not of putting to death by hanging, but of hanging a man up after he was stoned to death; which was done more ignominiously of some heinous malefactors. We have the examples of Rechab and Baanah, who, for murdering Ish-bosheth, were slain by David's commandment, their hand and feet cut off, and then hanged up. thou hang \textsuperscript{23} he that is hanged is accursed of God Heb. the curse of God, That is, it is the highest degree of reproach that can attach to a man, and proclaims him under the curse of God as much as any external punishment can. They that see him thus hanging between heaven and earth, will conclude him abandoned of both, and unworthy of either. Bp. Patrick observes, that this passage is applied to the death of Christ; not only because he bare our sins and was exposed to shame, as these malefactors were that were accursed of God, but because he was in the evening taken down from the cursed tree and buried (and that by the particular care of the Jews, with an eye to this law, ), in token, that now the guilt being removed, the law was satisfied, as it was when the malefactors had hanged till sun-set. It demanded no more. Then he, and those that are his, ceased to be a curse. And as the land of Israel was pure and clean when the body was buried, so the church is washed and cleansed by the complete satisfaction which Christ thus made.; thy land\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 22}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} When you see the calf of your brother or his sheep wandering in the way, you shall not overlook them; you shall by all means turn them back to your brother, and you shall restore them to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if your brother do not come near you, and you do not know him, you shall bring it into your house within; and it shall be with you until your brother shall seek them, and you shall restore them to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Thus shall you do to his ass, and thus shall you do to his garment, and thus shall you do to every thing that your brother has lost; whatever shall have been lost by him, and you shall have found, you shall not have power to overlook. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You shall not see the ass of your brother, or his calf, fallen in the way: you shall not overlook them, you shall surely help him to raise them up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The apparel of a man shall not be on a woman, neither shall a man put on a woman's dress; for every one that does these things is an abomination to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if you should come upon a brood of birds before your face in the way or upon any tree, or upon the earth, young or eggs, and the mother be brooding on the young or the eggs, you shall not take the dam with the young ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall by all means let the mother go, but you shall take the young to yourself; that it may be well with you, and that you may live long. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If you should build a new house, then shall you make a parapet to your house; so you shall not bring blood-guiltiness upon your house, if one should in any wise fall from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You shall not sow your vineyard with diverse seed, lest the fruit be devoted, and whatever seed you may sow, with the fruit of your vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall not wear a mingled [garment], woollen and linen together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You shall make fringes on the four borders of your garments, with which soever you may be clothed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if any one should take a wife, and dwell with her, and hate her, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and attach to her reproachful words, and bring against her an evil name, and say, I took this woman, and when I came to her I found not her tokens of virginity: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} then the father and the mother of the damsel shall take and bring out the damsel's tokens of virginity to the elders of the city to the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the father of the damsel shall say to the elders, I gave this my daughter to this man for a wife; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and now he has hated her, and attaches reproachful words to her, saying, I have not found tokens of virginity with your daughter; and these [are] the tokens of my daughter's virginity. And they shall unfold the garment before the elders of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the elders of that city shall take that man, and shall chastise him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and shall fine him one hundred shekels, and shall give [them] to the father of the damsel, because he has brought forth an evil name against a virgin of Israel; and she shall be his wife: he shall never be able to put her away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But if this report be true, and the tokens of virginity be not found for the damsel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} then shall they bring out the damsel to the doors of her father's house, and shall stone her with stones, and she shall die; because she has wrought folly among the children of Israel, to defile the house of her father by whoring: so you shall remove the evil one from among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if a man be found lying with a woman married to a man, you⌃ shall kill them both, the man that lay with the woman, and the woman: so shall you remove the wicked one out of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And if there be a young damsel espoused to a man, and a man should have found her in the city and have lain with her; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} you⌃ shall bring them both out to the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones, and they shall die; the damsel, because she cried not in the city; and the man, because he humbled his neighbor's spouse: so shall you remove the evil one from yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But if a man find in the field a damsel that is betrothed, and he should force her and lie with her, you⌃ shall kill the man that lay with her only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the damsel has not [committed] a sin worthy of death; as if a man should rise up against his neighbor, and kill him, so [is] this thing; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} because he found her in the field; the betrothed damsel cried, and there was none to help her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And if any one should find a young virgin who has not been betrothed, and should force [her] and lie with her, and be found, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} the man who lay with her shall give to the father of the damsel fifty silver didrachmas, and she shall be his wife, because he has humbled her; he shall never be able to put her away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{6} young ones thou shalt not \textsuperscript{7} But thou shalt The extirpation of any species of birds, whether edible or birds of prey, is often attended with serious consequences, and is always productive of evil; to prevent which was the object of this law. Palestine is situated in a climate producing poisonous snakes and scorpions, and between deserts and mountains, from which it would be inundated by them, as well as with immense swarms of flies, locusts, and mice, if the birds which feed upon them were extirpated. In a moral point of view, it may have been intended to inculcate a spirit of mercy and kindness, and to prevent the exercise of cruelty even towards a sparrow; for he who is guilty of such cruelty will, if circumstances be favourable, be cruel to his fellow-creatures. that it may thou mayest \textsuperscript{8} then thou shalt The eastern houses being built with flat roofs, which were used for various purposed, as walking, sleeping, etc., it was therefore necessary to have a sort of battlement, or balustrade, to prevent accidents, by people falling off.; thy roof; thou bring \textsuperscript{9} shalt not sow; fruit of thy seed Heb. fulness of thy seed \textsuperscript{10} Two different species cannot associate comfortably together, nor pull pleasantly either in cart or plough; and the ass being lower than the ox, when yoked, he must bear the principal part of the weight. \textsuperscript{21} stone her, ; she hath wrought; shalt thou \textsuperscript{24} and ye shall stone In these laws, the betrothed damsel was considered as the wife of the man to whom she was engaged, though they had not come together; and therefore the crime was adjudged adultery. But a charitable supposition is admitted in the damsel's favour, in case she was found in a solitary place. he hath humbled; so thou shalt put \textsuperscript{25} force her or, take strong hold of her \textsuperscript{30} a man shall This is to be understood as referring to the case of a stepmother. A man in his old age may have married a young woman, and on his dying, his son by another, or a former wife, may desire to espouse her; which is here forbidden.; discover\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 23}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that is fractured or mutilated in his private parts shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [One born] of a harlot shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Ammanite and Moabite shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord, even until the tenth generation he shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord, even for ever: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} because they met you not with bread and water by the way, when you⌃ went out of Egypt; and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor of Mesopotamia to curse you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the Lord your God would not listen to Balaam; and the Lord your God changed the curses into blessings, because the Lord your God loved you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You shall not speak peaceably or profitably to them all your days for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You shall not abhor an Edomite, because he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If sons be born to them, in the third generation they shall enter into the assembly of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if you should go forth to engage with your enemies, then you shall keep you from every wicked thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If there should be in you a man who is not clean by reason of his issue by night, then he shall go forth out of the camp, and he shall not enter into the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it shall come to pass toward evening he shall wash his body with water, and when the sun has gone down, he shall go into the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall have a place outside of the camp, and you shall go out there, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and you shall have a trowel on your girdle; and it shall come to pass when you would relieve yourself abroad, that you shall dig with it, and shall bring back the earth and cover your nuisance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Because the Lord your God walks in your camp to deliver you, and to give up your enemy before your face; and your camp shall be holy, and there shall not appear in you a disgraceful thing, and [so] he shall turn away from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall not deliver a servant to his master, who [coming] from his master attaches himself to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} He shall dwell with you, he shall dwell among you where he shall please; you shall not afflict him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} There shall not be a harlot of the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a fornicator of the sons of Israel; there shall not be an idolatress of the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be an initiated person of the sons of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You shall not bring the hire of a harlot, nor the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God, for any vow; because even both are an abomination to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You shall not lend to your brother on usury of silver, or usury of meat, or usury of any thing which you may lend out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You may lend on usury to a stranger, but to your brother you shall not lend on usury; that the Lord your God may bless you in all your works upon the land, into which you are entering to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if you will vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it; for the Lord your God will surely require it of you, and [otherwise] it shall be sin in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But if you should be unwilling to vow, it is not sin in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} You shall observe the words that proceed from between your lips; and as you have vowed a gift to the Lord God, [so] shall you do that which you have spoken with your mouth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} wounded; shall not enter It is evident that his law was not meant to exclude such Israelites either from the common benefits of civil society, or any essential religious advantages; but merely to lay them under a disgraceful distinction. This would tend to discourage parents from thus treating their children; a practice which was exceedingly common in those ages and countries. To this they were induced by the custom which prevailed, of employing such in the houses of the great and the courts of princes; so that they often rose to the highest posts of honour and authority. Some expositors therefore consider the phrase, "shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, " as meaning, that they should be incapable of bearing any office in that government which was placed over the people of God, who must thus enter a protest against this custom, and deliver selfish parents from this temptation. \textsuperscript{3} Ammonite These nations were subjected for their impiety, wickedness, and enmity to Israel ( and ), to peculiar disgrace; and on this account were not permitted to hold any office among the Israelites. This did not, however, disqualify them from becoming proselytes; for Ruth, who was a Moabitess, was married to Boaz, and became one of the progenitors of our Lord. \textsuperscript{4} Because they met; because they hired \textsuperscript{6} Thou shalt; prosperity Heb. good \textsuperscript{7} he is thy; because thou \textsuperscript{11} when evening, cometh on Heb. turneth toward wash himself \textsuperscript{12} In such a vast camp as that of the Israelites (see and ), and indeed, as Scheuchzer remarks, in every well regulated camp, cleanliness is considered as indispensably necessary. \textsuperscript{13} wilt ease thyself Heb. sittest down cover that \textsuperscript{14} walketh; unclean thing Heb. nakedness of any thing \textsuperscript{15} We cannot suppose that this law required the Israelites to entertain slaves who had robbed their masters, or left their service without cause; but such only as were cruelly treated, and fled to them for protection, especially from the neighbouring nations. To such they were commanded to afford shelter, and shew great kindness. \textsuperscript{16} shall dwell; liketh him best Heb. is good for him thou shalt not \textsuperscript{17} There shall be etc. The prohibition in the text, like many others, has no direct application to practices that were common among the Israelites at that time; but was intended to guard them against the enormities which were practised among the surrounding nations.; whore or, sodomitess, sodomite\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 24}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if you should go into the corn field of your neighbor, then you may gather the ears with your hands; but you shall not put the sickle to your neighbor's corn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if you should go into the vineyard of your neighbor, you shall eat grapes sufficient to satisfy your desire; but you may not put them into a vessel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And if any one should take a wife, and should dwell with her, then it shall come to pass if she should not have found favor before him, because he has found some unbecoming thing in her, that he shall write for her a bill of divorcement, and give it into her hands, and he shall send her away out of his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [if] she should go away and be married to another man; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and the last husband should hate her, and write for her a bill of divorcement; and should give it into her hands, and send her away out of his house, and the last husband should die, who took her to himself for a wife; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the former husband who sent her away shall not be able to return and take her to himself for a wife, after she has been defiled; because it is an abomination before the Lord your God, and you⌃ shall not defile the land, which the Lord your God gives you to inherit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if any one should have recently taken a wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall any thing be laid upon him; he shall be free in his house; for one year he shall cheer his wife whom he has taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You shall not take for a pledge the under millstone, nor the upper millstone; for he who does so takes life for a pledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if a man should be caught stealing one of his brethren of the children of Israel, and having overcome him he should sell him, that thief shall die; so shall you remove that evil one from yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Take heed to yourself in [regard of] the plague of leprosy: you shall take great heed to do according to all the law, which the priests the Levites shall report to you; take heed to do, as I have charged you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Remember all that the Lord your God did to Mariam in the way, when you⌃ were going out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If your neighbor owe you a debt, any debt whatever, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} you shall stand without, and the man who is in your debt shall bring the pledge out to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if the man be poor, you shall not sleep with his pledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall surely restore his pledge at sunset, and he shall sleep in his garment, and he shall bless you; and it shall be mercy to you before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You shall not unjustly withhold the wages of the poor and needy of your brethren, or of the strangers who are in your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You shall pay him his wages the same day, the sun shall not go down upon it, because he is poor and he trusts in it; and he shall cry against you to the Lord, and it shall be sin in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, and the sons shall not be put to death for the fathers; every one shall be put to death for his own sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You shall not wrest the judgment of the stranger and the fatherless, and widow; you shall not take the widow's garment for a pledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you shall remember that you were a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you from thence; therefore I charge you to do this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And when you shall have reaped corn in your field, and shall have forgotten a sheaf in your field, you shall not return to take it; it shall be for the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow, that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And if you should gather your olives, you shall not return to collect the remainder; it shall be for the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, and you shall remember that you were a bondman in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when soever you shall gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean what you have left; it shall be for the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and you shall remember that you were a bondman in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} hath taken; uncleanness Heb. matter of nakedness then let him; divorcement Heb. cutting off, send her \textsuperscript{5} a man; neither etc. Heb. not anything shall pass upon him cheer up \textsuperscript{6} shall take Small hand-mills, which ground at one time only a sufficient quantity for a day's consumption; hence they were forbidden to take either of the stones to pledge, because if they did, they would be deprived of the means of preparing their necessary food, and the family be without bread. On this account they are called in the text, a man's life. The same reason holds good against receiving in pledge, or distraining for debt, any instrument of labour, by which men earn their livelihood.; life \textsuperscript{7} found; then that, and thou shalt \textsuperscript{10} When lend thy brother any thing Heb. lend the loan of anything to thy brother \textsuperscript{13} deliver;, ; the sun; in his own raiment The raiment here referred to was most likely the same as the hyke of the Arabs, a long kind of blanket, resembling a Highland plaid, generally about six yards in length, and five or six feet broad; in which they often carry their provisions, as well as wrap themselves in, in the day, and sleep in at night, it being their only substitute for a bed. How necessary, then, it was to restore the hyke to a poor man before the going down of the sun, that he might have something to repose on, will sufficiently appear from these considerations. shall be \textsuperscript{15} At his; setteth his heart upon it Heb. lifteth his soul unto it, lest he \textsuperscript{19} When thou; it shall be, may bless \textsuperscript{20} go over the boughs again Heb. bough it after thee \textsuperscript{21} gatherest; afterward Heb. after thee\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 25}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And if there should be a dispute between men, and they should come forward to judgment, and [the judges] judge, and justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} then it shall come to pass, if the unrighteous should be worthy of stripes, you shall lay him down before the judges, and they shall scourge him before them according to his iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they shall scourge him with forty stripes in number, they shall not inflict more; for if you should scourge him [with] more stripes beyond these stripes, your brother will be disgraced before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the corn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if brethren should live together, and one of them should die, and should not have seed, the wife of the deceased shall not marry out [of the family] to a man not related: her husband's brother shall go in to her, and shall take her to himself for a wife, and shall dwell with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it shall come to pass that the child which she shall bear, shall be named by the name of the deceased, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if the man should not be willing to take his brother's wife, then shall the woman go up to the gate to the elders, and she shall say, My husband's brother will not raise up the name of his brother in Israel, my husband's brother has refused. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him; and if he stand and say, I will not take her: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} then his brother's wife shall come forward before the elders, and shall loose one shoe from off his foot, and shall spit in his face, and shall answer and say, Thus shall they do to the man who will not build his brother's house in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that has had his shoe loosed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And if men should strive together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them should advance to rescue her husband out of the hand of him that smites him, and she should stretch forth her hand, and take hold of his private parts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not spare her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You shall not have in your bag various weights, a great and a small. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not have in your house various measures, a great and a small. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall have a true and just weight, and a true and just measure, that you may live long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For every one that does this [is] an abomination to the Lord your God, even every one that does injustice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Remember what things Amalec did to you by the way, when you went forth out of the land of Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} how he withstood you in the way, and harassed your rear, [even] those that were weary behind you, and you did hunger and was weary; and he did not fear God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it shall come to pass whenever the Lord your God shall have given you rest from all your enemies round about you, in the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, you shall blot out the name of Amalec from under heaven, and shall not forget [to do it].\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} not exceed vile unto thee That is, be beaten so cruelly, that, by retaining the marks, he become contemptible in the eyes of his brethren. Amendment, and not this, was the object of the punishment. We should hate and despise the sin, but not the sinner. \textsuperscript{4} shalt not In Judea, as well as in Egypt, Greece, and Italy, they made use of beeves to tread out the corn; and the same mode of threshing still obtains in Arabia, Barbary, and other eastern countries, to the present day. The sheaves lie open and expanded on the threshing floors, and the cattle continually move round them, and thus tread out the grain. The natives of Aleppo still religiously observe the ancient humane practice, inculcated by this law, of permitting the oxen to remain unmuzzled when treading out the corn. muzzle; treadeth out Heb. thresheth \textsuperscript{5} brethren; husband's brother or, next kinsman \textsuperscript{6} the firstborn that his name;, brother's wife, or, next kinsman's wife, go up \textsuperscript{9} loose his shoe Pulling off the shoe seems to express his being degraded to the situation of slaves, who generally went barefoot; and spitting in or rather before ( biphney ) his face, was a mark of the utmost ignominy.; spit; So shall \textsuperscript{13} in thy bag; divers weights Heb. a stone and a stone, Aivenwaaiven; because weights were anciently made of stone. Hence the expression, a stone weight, which is still in use, though the matter of which it is made be lead or iron, and the name itself shews us that a stone of a certain weight was formerly used. \textsuperscript{14} divers measures Heb. an ephah and an ephah, Aiphah waaiphah; for this was the cost common measure among the Israelites, by which all the others were made and adjusted. They are not only forbidden to use divers weights and measures, one large or heavy to buy with, and another small and light to sell with, but they were not even allowed to keep such in the house. It is observable also, that these too common but dishonest actions are branded as "an abomination to the Lord, " equally with idolatry, and other scandalous crimes.\par}

\markright{DEUTERONOMY 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded, saying, Keep all these commands, all that I command you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it shall come to pass in the day when you⌃ shall cross over Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, that you shall set up for yourself great stones, and shall plaster them with plaster. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall write on these stones all the words of this law, as soon as you⌃ have crossed Jordan, when you⌃ are entered into the land, which the Lord God of your fathers gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, according as the Lord God of your fathers said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it shall be as soon as you⌃ are gone over Jordan, you⌃ shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, on mount Gaebal, and you shall plaster them with plaster. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And you shall build there an altar to the Lord your God, an altar of stones; you shall not lift up iron upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Of whole stones shall you build an altar to the Lord your God, and you shall offer upon it whole burnt offerings to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall there offer a peace-offering; and you shall eat and be filled, and rejoice before the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall write upon the stones all this law very plainly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses and the priests the Levites spoke to all Israel, saying, Be silent and hear, O Israel; this day you are become a people to the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and shall do all his commands, and his ordinances, as many as I command you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses charged the people on that day, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} These shall stand to bless the people on mount Garizin having gone over Jordan; Symeon, Levi, Judas, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these shall stand for cursing on mount Gaebal; Ruben, Gad, and Aser, Zabulon, Dan, and Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Levites shall answer and say to all Israel with a loud voice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Cursed [is] the man whoever shall make a graven or molten image, an abomination to the Lord, the work of the hands of craftsmen, and shall put it in a secret place: and all the people shall answer and say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Cursed is the man that dishonors his father or his mother: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Cursed is he that removes his neighbor's landmarks: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Cursed is he that makes the blind to wander in the way: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Cursed is every one that shall pervert the judgment of the stranger, and orphan, and widow: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Cursed is he that lies with his father's wife, because he has uncovered his father's skirt: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Cursed is he that lies with any beast: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Cursed is he that lies with his sister by his father or his mother: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Cursed is he that lies with his daughter-in-law: and all the people shall say, So be it. Cursed is he that lies with his wife's sister: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Cursed is he that smites his neighbor secretly: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Cursed is he whoever shall have taken a bribe to kill an innocent man: and all the people shall say, So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Cursed is every man that continues not in all the words of this law to do them: and all the people shall say, So be it.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} on the day, ;, unto the, great stones, and plaster Houbigant and others are of opinion that the original words, wesadta othom beseed, should be rendered "thou shalt cement them with cement, " because this was intended to be a durable monument. Some suppose that the writing was to be in relievo, and that the spaces were to be filled up by the mortar or cement; as is frequently the case with eastern inscriptions. \textsuperscript{3} thou shalt; this law This law probably means only the blessings and curses mentioned in this and the following chapter; which indeed contain an epitome of the whole law. a land \textsuperscript{4} in mount Ebal The Samaritan text has in mount Gerizim; which has given rise to a violent controversy. Dr. Kennicott suppose that the Jews corrupted this passage out of their enmity to the Samaritans, who had their temple on mount Gerizim; while Dr. Parry and H. Verschuir defend the present reading. To the writings of these authors the reader is referred. \textsuperscript{5} And there; thou shalt not \textsuperscript{12} upon mount Gerizim Mount Gerizim and mount Ebal being only separated by a narrow valley, not above a furlong broad, what was spoken with a loud voice on the one might be heard on the other (see note on ). It is probable, however, that the particle âl should be rendered by, as it frequently signifies; for when this direction was reduced to practice ( ), it seems that the people did not stand on the mountains, but over against them in the plain. But the Talmud says, that six tribes went up on each, while the priest and Levites and the ark remained beneath.; Simeon \textsuperscript{13} mount Ebal; to curse Heb. for a cursing Reuben \textsuperscript{15} Cursed be; maketh;, ; an abomination; and putteth; And all; Amen To each of the curses the people were to say Amen, as well as to the blessings; to denote a profession of their faith in the truth of them, that they were the real declarations of the wrath of God; and an acknowledgment of the equity of these curses. It was such an imprecation upon themselves, as strongly obliged them to have nothing to do with those evil practices on which the curse is entailed. We read of those who entered a curse to walk in God's law. . All the people, by saying this Amen, became bound one for another, that they would observe God's laws, by which every man was obliged, as far as he could, to prevent his neighbour from breaking these laws, and to reprove those that had offended, lest they should bear sin and the curse for them.\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 28}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it shall come to pass, if you will indeed hear the voice of the Lord your God, to observe and do all these commands, which I charge you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you on high above all the nations of the earth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and all these blessings shall come upon you, and shall find you. If you will indeed hear the voice of the Lord your God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} blessed [shall] you [be] in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Blessed shall be the offspring of your body, and the fruits of your land, and the herds of your oxen, and the flocks of your sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Blessed shall be your barns, and your stores. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Blessed shall you be in your coming in, and blessed shall you be in your going out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord deliver your enemies that withstand you utterly broken before your face: they shall come out against you one way, and they shall flee seven ways from before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Lord send upon you his blessing in your barns, and on all on which you shall put your hand, in the land which the Lord your God gives you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Lord raise you up for himself a holy people, as he swore to your fathers; if you will hear the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in all his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all the nations of the earth shall see you, that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall stand in awe of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord your God shall multiply you for good in the offspring of your body, and in the offspring of your cattle, and in the fruits of your land, on your land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} May the Lord open to you his good treasure, the heaven, to give rain to your land in season: may he bless all the works of your hands: so shall you lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall then be above and you shall not be below, if you will listen to the voice of the Lord your God, in all things that I charge you this day to observe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall not turn aside from any of the commandments, which I charge you this day, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But it shall come to pass, if you will not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to observe all his commandments, as many as I charge you this day, then all these curses shall come on you, and overtake you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Cursed [shall] you [be] in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Cursed shall be your barns and your stores. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Cursed shall be the offspring of your body, and the fruits of your land, the herds of your oxen, and the flocks of your sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Cursed shall you be in your coming in, and cursed shall you be in your going out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The Lord send upon you lack, and famine, and consumption of all things on which you shall put your hand, until he shall have utterly destroyed you, and until he shall have consumed you quickly because of your evil devices, because you have forsaken me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The Lord cause the pestilence to cleave to you, until he shall have consumed you off the land into which you go to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The Lord strike you with distress, and fever, and cold, and inflammation, and blighting, and paleness, and they shall pursue you until they have destroyed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you shall have over your head a sky of brass, and the earth under you shall be iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The Lord your God make the rain of your land dust; and dust shall come down from heaven, until it shall have destroyed you, and until it shall have quickly consumed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The Lord give you up for slaughter before your enemies: you shall go out against them one way, and flee from their face seven ways; and you shall be a dispersion in all the kingdoms of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And your dead men shall be food to the birds of the sky, and to the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to scare them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The Lord strike you with the botch of Egypt in the seat, and with a malignant scab, and itch, so that you can not be healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The Lord strike you with insanity, and blindness, and astonishment of mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you shall grope at mid-day, as a blind man would grope in the darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways; and then you shall be unjustly treated, and plundered continually, and there shall be no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} you shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and you shall not dwell in it; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather the grapes of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Your calf [shall be] slain before you, and you shall not eat of it; your ass shall be violently taken away from you, and shall not be restored to you: your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and you shall have no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Your sons and your daughters shall be given to another nation, and your eyes wasting away shall look for them: your hand shall have no strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} A nation which you know not shall eat the produce of your land, and all your labors; and you shall be injured and crushed always. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And you shall be distracted, because of the sights of your eyes which you shall see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} The Lord strike you with an evil sore, on the knees and the legs, so that you shall not be able to be healed from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} The Lord carry away you and your princes, whom you shall set over you, to a nation which neither you nor your fathers know; and you shall there serve other gods, wood and stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And you shall be there for a wonder, and a parable, and a tale, among all the nations, to which the Lord your God shall carry you away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} You shall carry forth much seed into the field, and you shall bring in little, because the locust shall devour it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} You shall plant a vineyard, and dress it, and shall not drink the wine, neither shall you delight yourself with it, because the worm shall devour it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} You shall have olive trees in all your borders, and you shall not anoint you with oil, because your olive shall utterly cast [its fruit]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} You shall beget sons and daughters, and they shall not be [yours], for they shall depart into captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} All your trees and the fruits of your land shall the blight consume. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} The stranger that is within you shall get up very high, and you shall come down very low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him: he shall be the head, and you shall be the tail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And all these curses shall come upon you, and shall pursue you, and shall overtake you, until he shall have consumed you, and until he shall have destroyed you; because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep his commands, and his ordinances which he has commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And [these things] shall be signs in you, and wonders among your seed for ever; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} because you did not serve the Lord your God with gladness and a good heart, because of the abundance of all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And you shall serve your enemies, which the Lord will send forth against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in the lack of all things; and you shall wear upon your neck a yoke of iron until he shall have destroyed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} The Lord shall bring upon you a nation from the extremity of the earth, like the swift flying of an eagle, a nation whose voice you shall not understand; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} a nation bold in countenance, which shall not respect the person of the aged and shall not pity the young. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And it shall eat up the young of your cattle, and the fruits of your land, so as not to leave to you corn, wine, oil, the herds of your oxen, and the flocks of your sheep, until it shall have destroyed you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} and have utterly crushed you in your cities, until the high and strong walls be destroyed, in which you trust, in all your land; and it shall afflict you in your cities, which he has given to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And you shall eat the fruit of your body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters, all that he has given you, in your straitness and your affliction, with which your enemy shall afflict you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} He that is tender and very delicate within you shall look with an evil eye upon his brother, and the wife in his bosom, and the children that are left, which may have been left to him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} so as [not] to give to one of them of the flesh of his children, whom he shall eat, because of his having nothing left him in your straitness, and in your affliction, with which your enemies shall afflict you in all your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And she that is tender and delicate among you, whose foot has not assayed to go upon the earth for that comes out between her feet, and the child which she shall bear; for she shall eat them because of the lack of all things, secretly in your straitness, and in your affliction, with which your enemy shall afflict you in your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} If you will not listen to do all the words of this law, which have been written in this book, to fear this glorious and wonderful name, the Lord your God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} then the Lord shall magnify your plagues, and the plagues of your seed, great and wonderful plagues, and evil and dwelling diseases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} And he shall bring upon you all the evil pain of Egypt, of which you were afraid, and they shall cleave to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And the Lord shall bring upon you every sickness, and every plague that is not written, and every one that is written in the book of this law, until he shall have destroyed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And you⌃ shall be left few in number, whereas you⌃ were as the stars of the sky in multitude; because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} And it shall come to pass that as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you; and you⌃ shall be quickly removed from the land, into which you⌃ go to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all nations, from one end of the earth to the other; and you shall there serve other gods, wood and stone, which you have not known, nor your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} Moreover among those nations he will not give you quiet, neither by any means shall the sole of your foot have rest; and the Lord shall give you there another and a misgiving heart, and failing eyes, and a wasting soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} And your life shall be in suspense before your eyes; and you shall be afraid by day and by night, and you shall have no assurance of your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} In the morning you shall say, Would it were evening! and in the evening you shall say, Would it were morning! for the fear of your heart with which you shall fear, and for the sights of your eyes which you shall see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} And the Lord shall bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I said, You shall not see it again; and you⌃ shall be sold there to your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and none shall buy you.\par

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 29}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} These [are] the words of the covenant, which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which he made with them in Choreb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Moses called all the sons of Israel and said to them, You⌃ have seen all things that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you to Pharao and his servants, and all his land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the great temptations which your eyes have seen, the signs, and those great wonders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Yet the Lord God has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old, and your sandals were not worn away off your feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You⌃ did not eat bread, you⌃ did not drink wine or strong drink, that you⌃ might know that I [am] the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you⌃ came as far as this place; and there came forth Seon king of Esebon, and Og king of Basan, to meet us in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And we struck them and took their land, and I gave it for an inheritance to Ruben and Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you⌃ shall take heed to do all the words of this covenant, that you⌃ may understand all things that you⌃ shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You⌃ all stand today before the Lord your God, the heads of your tribes, and your elders, and your judges, and your officers, every man of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} your wives, and your children, and the stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from your hewer of wood even to your drawer of water, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that you should enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into his oaths, as many as the Lord your God appoints you this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} that he may appoint you to himself for a people, and he shall be your God, as he said to you, and as he swore to your fathers, Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I do not appoint to you alone this covenant and this oath; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} but to those also who are here with you today before the Lord your God, and to those who are not here with you today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For you⌃ know how we lived in the land of Egypt, how we came through the midst of the nations through whom you⌃ came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you⌃ saw their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Lest there be among you man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose heart has turned aside from the Lord your God, having gone to serve the gods of these nations; lest there be in you a root springing up with gall and bitterness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it shall be if one shall hear the words of this curse, and shall flatter himself in his heart, saying, Let good happen to me, for I will walk in the error of my heart, lest the sinner destroy the guiltless with [him]: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} God shall by no means be willing to pardon him, but then the wrath of the Lord and his jealousy shall flame out against that man; and all the curses of this covenant shall attach themselves to him, which are written in this book, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord shall separate that man for evil of all the children of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that are written in the book of this law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And another generation shall say—even your sons who shall rise up after you, and the stranger who shall come from a land afar off, and shall see the plagues of that land and their diseases, which the Lord has sent upon it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} brimstone and burning salt, (the whole land shall not be sown, neither shall any green thing spring, nor rise upon it, as Sodom and Gomorrha were overthrown, Adama and Seboim, which the Lord overthrew in his wrath and anger:)— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and all the nations shall say, Why has the Lord done thus to this land? what [is] this great fierceness of anger? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And [men] shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers, the things which he appointed to their fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and they went and served other gods, which they knew not, neither did he assign [them] to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord was exceedingly angry with that land to bring upon it according to all the curses which are written in the book of this law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the Lord removed them from their land in anger, and wrath, and very great indignation, and cast them out into another land as at present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} The secret things [belong] to the Lord our God, but the things that are revealed [belong] to us and to our children for ever, to do all the words of this law.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} I have led, your clothes; and thy shoe \textsuperscript{12} thou shouldest; enter Heb. pass, This is an allusion to the solemn ceremony used by several ancient nations, when they entered into a covenant with each other. The victims, slain as a sacrifice on this occasion, were divided, and parts laid asunder. The contracting parties then passed between them, imprecating, as a curse on those who violated the sacred compact, that they might in like manner be cut asunder ( ). St. Cyril, in his work against Julian, shows that passing between the divided parts of a victim was used also among the Chaldeans and other people. into his oath \textsuperscript{18} among you man, ; among you a root; gall and wormwood or, a poisonful herb, Heb. rosh \textsuperscript{19} this curse; that he bless;, ;, ; though I walk; imagination or, stubborness, *marg. to add A very forcible metaphor, denoting the natural progress and increasing avidity of sinful passions and depraved inclinations; which lead men to drink down iniquity as the drunkard does his liquor, without regard to the consequences. Some render, "to add thirst to drunkenness; " and then it implies the insatiableness of men's sinful passions, which hanker for more and more indulgence after the greatest excesses. drunkenness to thirst Heb. the drunken to the thirsty \textsuperscript{20} will not spare; , ; the anger his jealousy; , ; smoke; all the curses, blot out \textsuperscript{21} separate; , are written Heb. is written \textsuperscript{22} which the Lord hath laid upon it Heb. wherewith the Lord hath made it sick \textsuperscript{26} they went; gods whom he had etc. or, who had not given to them any portion, given. Heb. divided. \textsuperscript{28} rooted them, ; as it is this day \textsuperscript{29} secret; revealed; and to our\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 30}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it shall come to pass when all these things shall have come upon you, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before your face, and you shall call [them] to mind among all the nations, wherein the Lord shall have scattered you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and shall return to the Lord your God, and shall listen to his voice, according to all things which I charge you this day, with all your heart, and with all your soul; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} then the Lord shall heal your iniquities, and shall pity you, and shall again gather you out from all the nations, among which the Lord has scattered you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If your dispersion be from one end of heaven to the other, thence will the Lord your God gather you, and thence will the Lord your God take you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord your God shall bring you in from thence into the land which your fathers have inherited, and you shall inherit it; and he will do you good, and multiply you above your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord shall purge your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord your God will put these curses upon your enemies, and upon those that hate you, who have persecuted you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall return and listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and shall keep his commands, all that I charge you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord your God shall bless you in every work of your hands, in the offspring of your body, and in the offspring of your cattle, and in the fruits of your land, because the Lord your God will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} if you will listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep his commandments, and his ordinances, and his judgments written in the book of this law, if you turn to the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For this command which I give you this day is not grievous, neither is it far from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} It is not in heaven above, [as if there were one] saying, Who shall go up for us into heaven, and shall take it for us, and we will hear and do it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither is it beyond the sea, saying, Who will go over for us to the other side of the sea, and take it for us, and make it audible to us, and we will do it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The word is very near you, in your mouth, and in your heart, and in your hands to do it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Behold, I have set before you this day life and death, good and evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} If you will listen to the commands of the Lord your God, which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his ordinances, and his judgments; then you⌃ shall live, and shall be many in number, and the Lord your God shall bless you in all the land into which you go to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But if your heart change, and you will not listen, and you shall go astray and worship other gods, and serve them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I declare to you this day, that you⌃ shall utterly perish, and you⌃ shall by no means live long upon the land, into which you⌃ go over Jordan to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I call both heaven and earth to witness this day against you, I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse: choose you life, that you and your seed may live; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} to love the Lord your God, to listen to his voice, and cleave to him; for this [is] your life, and the length of your days, that you should dwell upon the land, which the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} it shall come; the blessing, 27:1-28:65; thou shalt call; whither \textsuperscript{2} return unto; with all thine heart \textsuperscript{3} then the; , gather thee This seems to refer to a more extensive captivity than that which the Jews suffered in Babylon. \textsuperscript{4} unto; thence will the As this promise refers to a return from a captivity among all nations, consequently it cannot be exclusively the Babylonish captivity which is intended; and the repossession of their land must be different from that which was consequent on their return from Babylon. Nor at that period could it be said that they were multiplied more than their fathers, or, as the Hebrew imports, made greater than their fathers, when after their return they were tributary to the Persians, and afterwards fell under the power of the Greeks, under whom they suffered much; nor have their hearts, as a nation, yet been circumcised. \textsuperscript{6} will circumcise; to love the Lord \textsuperscript{9} make thee;, rejoice over thee \textsuperscript{11} it is not hidden Or as the word niphlaith implies, not too wonderful for thee to comprehend or perform; but easily to be acquainted with, and understood, because clearly revealed. Neither is it afar off; it was proclaimed in you ears from mount Sinai, and is now proclaimed in the sanctuary. It is not in heaven; for it has been already revealed.
