\subsection*{Deuteronomy 31}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses finished speaking all these words to all the children of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and said to them, I am this day one hundred and twenty years [old]; I shall not be able any longer to come in or go out; and the Lord said to me, You shall not go over this Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord your God who goes before you, he shall destroy these nations before you, and you shall inherit them: and [it shall be] Joshua that goes before your face, as the Lord has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord your God shall do to them as he did to Seon and Og the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond Jordan, and to their land, as he destroyed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord has delivered them to you; and you⌃ shall do to them, as I charged you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Be courageous and strong, fear not, neither be cowardly neither be afraid before them; for [it is] the Lord your God that advances with you in the midst of you, neither will he by any means forsake you, nor desert you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses called Joshua, and said to him before all Israel, Be courageous and strong; for you shall go in before this people into the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them, and you shall give it to them for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord that goes with you shall not forsake you nor abandon you; fear not, neither be afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it to the priests the sons of Levi who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to the elders of the sons of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Moses charged them in that day, saying, After seven years, in the time of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} when all Israel come together to appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose, you⌃ shall read this law before all Israel in their ears, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} having assembled the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the stranger that is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall listen to do all the words of this law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And their sons who have not known shall hear, and shall learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land, into which you⌃ go over Jordan to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, the days of your death are at hand; call Joshua, and stand you⌃ by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and I will give him a charge. And Moses and Joshua went to the tabernacle of testimony, and stood by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord descended in a cloud, and stood by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony; and the pillar of the cloud stood by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and this people will arise and go a whoring after the strange gods of the land, into which they are entering: and they will forsake me, and break my covenant, which I made with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I will be very angry with them in that day, and I will leave them and turn my face away from them, and they shall be devoured; and many evils and afflictions shall come upon them; and they shall say in that day, Because the Lord my God is not with me, these evils have come upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I will surely turn away my face from them in that day, because of all their evil doings which they have done, because they turned aside after strange gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now write the words of this song, and teach it to the children of Israel, and you⌃ shall put it into their mouth, that this song may witness for me among the children of Israel to their face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For I will bring them into the good land, which I swore to their fathers, to give to them a land flowing with milk and honey: and they shall eat and be filled and satisfy [themselves]; then will they turn aside after other gods, and serve them, and they will provoke me, and break my covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And this song shall stand up to witness against them; for they shall not forget it out of their mouth, or out of the mouth of their seed; for I know their wickedness, what they are doing here this day, before I have brought them into the good land, which I swore to their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he charged Joshua, and said, Be courageous and strong, for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land, which the Lord swore to them, and he shall be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And when Moses finished writing all the words of this law in a book, even to the end, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} then he charged the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Take the book of this law, and you⌃ shall put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there among you for a testimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For I know your provocation, and your stiff neck; for yet during my life with you at this day, you⌃ have been provoking in your conduct toward God: how shall you⌃ not also be so after my death? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Gather together to me the heads of your tribes, and your elders, and your judges, and your officers, that I may speak in their ears all these words; and I call both heaven and earth to witness against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For I know that after my death you⌃ will utterly transgress, and turn aside out of the way which I have commanded you; and evils shall come upon you in the latter days, because you⌃ will do evil before the Lord, to provoke him to anger by the works of your hands. And Moses spoke all the words of this song even to the end, in the ears of the whole assembly.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Heb. vocab: amets (אַמֵּץ) = to be strong; courageous. Common English renderings: be strong; courage. Often paired with חזק in exhortations.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} I am an The life of Moses, the great prophet of Jehovah and lawgiver of the Jews, was exactly the same in length as the time Noah employed in preaching righteousness to the antediluvian world. These one hundred and twenty years were divided into three remarkable periods. Forty years he lived in Egypt, in the court of Pharaoh, acquiring all the learning and wisdom of the Egyptians (, ); forty years he sojourned in Midian, in a state of preparation for his great and important mission ( ); and forty years he guided, led, and governed the Israelites under the express direction and authority of God. \subsection*{Deuteronomy 32}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Attend, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words out of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let my speech be looked for as the rain, and my words come down as dew, as the shower upon the herbage, and as snow upon the grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I have called on the name of the Lord: assign you⌃ greatness to our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [As for God], his works [are] true, and all his ways [are] judgment: God [is] faithful, and there is no unrighteousness [in him]; just and holy [is] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They have sinned, not [pleasing] him; spotted children, a froward and perverse generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Do you⌃ thus recompense the Lord? [is the] people thus foolish and unwise? did not he himself your father purchase you, and make you, and form you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember the days of old, consider the years for past ages: ask your father, and he shall relate to you, your elders, and they shall tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And his people Jacob became the portion of the Lord, Israel was the line of his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He maintained him in the wilderness, in burning thirst and a dry land: he led him about and instructed him, and kept him as the apple of an eye. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} As an eagle would watch over his brood, and yearns over his young, receives them having spread his wings, and takes them up on his back: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} the Lord alone led them, there was no strange god with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He brought them up on the strength of the land; he fed them with the fruits of the fields; they sucked honey out of the rock, and oil out of the solid rock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Butter of cows, and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, of calves and kids, with fat of kidneys of wheat; and he drank wine, the blood of the grape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he became thick and broad: then he forsook the God that made him, and departed from God his Saviour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They provoked me to anger with strange gods; with their abominations they bitterly angered me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They sacrificed to devils, and not to God; to gods whom they knew not: new and fresh [gods] came in, whom their fathers knew not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You have forsaken God that begot you, and forgotten God who feeds you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord saw, and was jealous; and was provoked by the anger of his sons and daughters, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and said, I will turn away my face from them, and will show what shall happen to them in the last days; for it is a perverse generation, sons in whom is no faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They have provoked me to jealousy with [that which is] not God, they have exasperated me with their idols; and I will provoke them to jealousy with them that are no nation, I will anger them with a nation void of understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For a fire has been kindled out of my wrath, it shall burn to hell below; it shall devour the land, and the fruits of it; it shall set on fire the foundations of the mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} I will gather evils upon them, and will fight with my weapons against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [They shall be] consumed with hunger and the devouring of birds, and there shall be irremediable destruction: I will send forth against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the rage of [serpents] creeping on the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Without, the sword shall bereave them of children, and terror [shall issue] out of the secret chambers; the young man shall perish with the virgin, the suckling with him who has grown old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I said, I will scatter them, and I will cause their memorial to cease from among men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Were it not for the wrath of the enemy, lest they should live long, lest their enemies should combine against them; lest they should say, Our own high arm, and not the Lord, has done all these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} It is a nation that has lost counsel, neither is there understanding in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} They had not sense to understand: let them reserve these things against the time to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} How should one pursue a thousand, and two rout tens of thousands, if God had not sold them, and the Lord delivered them up? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For their gods are not as our God, but our enemies [are] void of understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For their vine [is] of the vine of Sodom, and their vine-branch of Gomorrha: their grape [is] a grape of gall, their cluster [is] one of bitterness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Their wine [is] the rage of serpents, and the incurable rage of asps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Behold! are not these things stored up by me, and sealed among my treasures? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} In the day of vengeance I will recompense, whenever their foot shall be tripped up; for the day of their destruction [is] near to them, and the judgments at hand are close upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For the Lord shall judge his people, and shall be comforted over his servants; for he saw that they were utterly weakened, and failed in the hostile invasion, and were become feeble: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and the Lord said, Where are their gods on whom they trusted? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} the fat of whose sacrifices you⌃ ate, and you⌃ drank the wine of their drink-offerings? let them arise and help you, and be your protectors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Behold, behold that I am [he], and there is no god beside me: I kill, and I will make to live: I will strike, and I will heal; and there is none who shall deliver out of my hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For I will lift up my hand to heaven, and swear by my right hand, and I will say, I live for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} For I will sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand shall take hold of judgment; and I will render judgment to my enemies, and will recompense them that hate me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} I will make my weapons drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh, [it shall glut itself] with the blood of the wounded, and from the captivity of the heads of [their] enemies that rule over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Rejoice, you⌃ heavens, with him, and let all the angels of God worship him; rejoice you⌃ Gentiles, with his people, and let all the sons of God strengthen themselves in him; for he will avenge the blood of his sons, and he will render vengeance, and recompense justice to his enemies, and will reward them that hate him; and the Lord shall purge the land of his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it to the children of Israel; and Moses went in and spoke all the words of this law in the ears of the people, he and Joshua the [son] of Naue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And Moses finished speaking to all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And he said to them, Take heed with your heart to all these words, which I testify to you this day, which you⌃ shall command your sons, to observe and do all the words of this law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} For this [is] no vain word to you; for it [is] your life, and because of this word you⌃ shall live long upon the land, into which you⌃ go over Jordan to inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And the Lord spoke to Moses in this day, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Go up to the mount Abarim, this mountain Nabau which is in the land of Moab over against Jericho, and behold the land of Chanaan, which I give to the sons of Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} and die in the mount whither you go up, and be added to your people; as Aaron your brother died in mount Or, and was added to his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Because you⌃ disobeyed my word among the children of Israel, at the waters of strife of Cades in the wilderness of Sin; because you⌃ sanctified me not among the sons of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} You shall see the land before [you], but you shall not enter into it.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{4} Name of God: Tsur (צוּר) — Rock Common English renderings: Rock. A foundational metaphor for God’s stability, faithfulness, justice, and protection. \textsuperscript{6} Gk. vocab: mōros (μωρός) = foolish. Common English renderings: foolish. The adjective for foolish, dull, or senseless. \textsuperscript{15} Name of God: Eloah (אֱלוֹהַּ) — God; mighty one Common English renderings: God. A singular poetic form related to Elohim, used especially in elevated or wisdom-style passages. \textsuperscript{20} Gk. vocab: apistia (ἀπιστία) = unbelief; faithlessness. Common English renderings: unbelief. Can denote disbelief or lack of fidelity. \textsuperscript{37} Heb. vocab: chasah (חָסָה) = to seek refuge. Common English renderings: trust; take refuge. Often describes taking refuge in God.\par}

As the word paira signifies the hair of the head, both in Hebrew and Arabic, Mr. Parkhurst and others render mairosh parôth, "from the hairy head; " but to have this sense, the words should rather have been mipparôth rosh, according the Hebrew idiom. The word farôu, in Arabic, however, also denotes a prince or chief; and the words may be literally rendered, with the LXX, απο κεφαλης αρχοντων εχθρων, "from the head of the chiefs of the enemies." The hyperbaton, or transposition of words from their grammatical order, is very observable in this verse; the third member forming a continuation of the first, and the fourth of the second. \textsuperscript{43} Rejoice or, Praise his people, ye nations; or, Sing ye, O ye nations.; avenge; , render will be \textsuperscript{48} am 2553, bc 1451, An, Ex, Is, 40, Adar \textsuperscript{51} ye trespassed;, Meribah-Kadesh or, strife at Kadesh, because ye\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 33}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And this [is] the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said, The Lord is come from Sina, and has appeared from Seir to us, and has hasted out of the mount of Pharan, with the ten thousands of Cades; on his right hand [were] his angels with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he spared his people, and all his sanctified ones [are] under your hands; and they are under you; and he received of his words {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} the law which Moses charged us, an inheritance to the assemblies of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shall be prince with the beloved one, when the princes of the people are gathered together with the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let Ruben live, and not die; and let him be many in number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And this [is the blessing] of Juda; Hear, Lord, the voice of Juda, and do you visit his people: his hands shall contend for him, and you shall be a help from his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And to Levi he said, Give to Levi his manifestations, and his truth to the holy man, whom they tempted in the temptation; they reviled him at the water of strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who says to his father and mother, I have not seen you; and he knew not his brethren, and he refused to know his sons: he kept your oracles, and observed your covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} They shall declare your ordinances to Jacob, and your law to Israel: they shall place incense in [the time of] your wrath continually upon your altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Bless, Lord, his strength, and accept the works of his hands; break the loins of his enemies that have risen up against him, and let not them that hate him rise up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And to Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in confidence, and God overshadows him always, and he rested between his shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And to Joseph he said, His land [is] of the blessing of the Lord, of the seasons of sky and dew, and of the deeps of wells below, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and of the fruits of the changes of the sun in season, and of the produce of the months, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} from the top of the ancient mountains, and from the top of the everlasting hills, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and of the fullness of the land in season: and let the things pleasing to him that lived in the bush come on the head of Joseph, and on the crown [of him who was] glorified above his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} His beauty [is as] the firstling of his bull, his horns [are] the horns of a unicorn; with them he shall thrust the nations at once, even from the end of the earth: these [are] the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these [are] the thousands of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And to Zabulon he said, Rejoice, Zabulon, in your going out, and Issachar in his tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They shall utterly destroy the nations, and you⌃ shall call [men] there, and there offer the sacrifice of righteousness; for the wealth of the sea shall suckle you, and so shall the marts of them that dwell by the sea-coast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And to Gad he said, Blessed [be] he that enlarges Gad: as a lion he rested, having broken the arm and the ruler. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he saw his first fruits, that there the land of the princes gathered with the chiefs of the people was divided; the Lord wrought righteousness, and his judgment with Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And to Dan he said, Dan [is] a lion's whelp, and shall leap out of Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And to Nephthali he said, Nephthali [has] the fulness of good things; and let him be filled with blessing from the Lord: he shall inherit the west and the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And to Aser he said, Aser [is] blessed with children; and he shall be acceptable to his brethren: he shall dip his foot in oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} His sandal shall be iron and brass; as your days, so [shall be] your strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} There is not [any such] as the God of the beloved; he who rides upon the heaven [is] your helper, and the magnificent One of the firmament. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the rule of God shall protect you, and [that] under the strength of the everlasting arms; and he shall cast forth the enemy from before your face, saying, Perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Israel shall dwell in confidence alone on the land of Jacob, with corn and wine; and the sky [shall be] misty with dew upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Blessed [are] you, O Israel; who [is] like to you, O people saved by the Lord? your helper shall hold his shield over you, and [his] sword [is] your boast; and your enemies shall speak falsely to you, and you shall tread upon their neck.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Gk. vocab: plērōma (πλήρωμα) = fullness; totality. Common English renderings: fulness. A term for fullness or that which fills. \textsuperscript{27} Heb. vocab: machaseh (מַחֲסֶה) = refuge. Common English renderings: refuge. A frequent poetic image for God as shelter.\par}

\subsection*{Deuteronomy 34}
\markright{DEUTERONOMY 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moses went up from Araboth Moab to the mount of Nabau, to the top of Phasga, which is before Jericho; and the Lord showed him all the mount of Galaad to Dan, and all the land of Nephthali, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and all the land of Ephraim and Manasse, and all the land of Juda to the farthest sea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and the wilderness, and the country round about Jericho, the city of palm-trees, to Segor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Moses, This [is] the land of which I swore to Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob, saying, To your seed will I give it: and I have showed it to your eyes, but you shall not go in there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So Moses the servant of the Lord died in the land of Moab by the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they buried him in Gai near the house of Phogor; and no one has seen his sepulchre to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Moses was one hundred and twenty years old at his death; his eyes were not dimmed, nor were his natural powers destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Israel wept for Moses in Araboth of Moab at Jordan near Jericho thirty days; and the days of the sad mourning for Moses were completed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joshua the son of Naue was filled with the spirit of knowledge, for Moses had laid his hands upon him; and the children of Israel listened to him; and they did as the Lord commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And there rose up no more a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} in all the signs and wonders, which the Lord sent him to work in Egypt on Pharao, and his servants, and all his land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} the great wonders, and the mighty hand which Moses displayed before all Israel.\par

\section*{Joshua Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Joshua with possible inspired final notices by Eleazar or Phinehas\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book naturally reads as Joshua's conquest record with brief closing notices after his death.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct saying of Jesus names Joshua as author, but the OT historical books are treated as truthful covenant history; see Hebrews 4:8 for Joshua's historical role.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 1406-1380 BC during and shortly after the conquest\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Joshua immediately after Moses and before the judges in Israel's settlement of Canaan.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same conquest setting, though some speech and place-name details differ from the MT in spots.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Israel's entry into, conquest of, and initial allotment within Canaan under Joshua.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To show the LORD's covenant faithfulness in giving the land and to call Israel to obedient covenant fidelity.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} conquest; covenant faithfulness; land promise; holy war; inheritance; covenant renewal\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Entry and conquest 1-12; Land allotment 13-21; Covenant charge and renewal 22-24.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Joshua a (4Q47) ca. 200-100 BC | Subst. 4Q Joshua a and b preserve substantial early Hebrew portions of Joshua Hasmonean period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus, with Codex Alexandrinus also preserving Joshua 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Retelling of Israel's conquest traditions by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Joshua's textual witnesses show the usual MT/LXX differences in wording and arrangement; some Qumran evidence helps illuminate earlier Hebrew forms behind later traditions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Joshua as fundamentally authored within Joshua's lifetime, with any brief posthumous notices understood as inspired completion, not a denial of substantial Joshuanic authorship.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Joshua 1}
\markright{JOSHUA 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after the death of Moses, that the Lord spoke to Joshua the son of Naue, the minister of Moses, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Moses my servant is dead; now then arise, go over Jordan, you and all this people, into the land, which I give them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Every spot on which you⌃ shall tread I will give it to you, as I said to Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The wilderness and Antilibanus, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, and as far as the extremity of the sea; your coasts shall be from the setting of the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Not a man shall stand against you all the days of your life; and as I was with Moses, so will I also be with you, and I will not fail you, or neglect you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Be strong and quit yourself like a man, for you shall divide the land to this people, which I swore to give to your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Be strong, therefore, and quit yourself like a man, to observe and do as Moses my servant commanded you; and you shall not turn therefrom to the right hand or to the left, that you may be wise in whatever you may do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the book of this law shall not depart out of your mouth, and you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may know how to do all the things that are written [in it]; then shall you prosper, and make your ways prosperous, and then shall you be wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Behold! I have commanded you; be strong and courageous, be not cowardly nor fearful, for the Lord your God is with you in all places whither you go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joshua commanded the scribes of the people, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Go into the midst of the camp of the people, and command the people, saying, Prepare provisions; for yet three days and you⌃ shall go over this Jordan, entering in to take possession of the land, which the Lord God of your fathers gives to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And to Ruben, and to Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasse, Joshua said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Remember the word which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, saying, the Lord your God has caused you to rest, and has given you this land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let your wives and your children and your cattle dwell in the land, which he has given you; and you⌃ shall go over well armed before your brethren, every one of you who is strong; and you⌃ shall fight on their side; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} until the Lord your God shall have given your brethren rest, as also to you, and they also shall have inherited the land, which the Lord your God gives them; then you⌃ shall depart each one to his inheritance, which Moses gave you beyond Jordan eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they answered Joshua and said, We will do all things which you command us, and we will go to every place whither you shall send us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Whereinsoever we listened to Moses we will listen to you; only let the Lord our God be with you, as he was with Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And whoever shall disobey you, and whoever shall not listen to your words as you shall command him, let him die; but be you strong and courageous.\par

\subsection*{Joshua 2}
\markright{JOSHUA 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joshua the son of Naue sent out of Sattin two young men to spy [the land], saying, Go up and view the land and Jericho: and the two young men went and entered into Jericho; and they entered into the house of a harlot, whose name [was] Raab, and lodged there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it was reported to the king of Jericho, saying, Men of the sons of Israel have come in hither to spy the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king of Jericho sent and spoke to Raab, saying, Bring out the men that entered into your house this night; for they are come to spy out the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the woman took the two men and hid them; and she spoke to the messengers, saying, The men came in to me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} but when the gate was shut in the evening, the men went out; I know not whither they are gone: follow after them, if you⌃ may overtake them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But she [had] brought them up upon the house, and hid them in the flax-stalks that were spread by her on the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the men followed after them in the way to Jordan to the fords; and the gate was shut. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass when the men who pursued after them were gone forth, and before the spies had lain down to sleep, that she came up to them on the top of the house; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and she said to them, I know that the Lord has given you the land; for the fear of you has fallen upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For we have heard that the Lord God dried up the Red Sea before you, when you⌃ came out of the land of Egypt, and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond Jordan, to Seon and Og, whom you⌃ utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when we heard it we were amazed in our heart, and there was no longer any spirit in any of us because of you, for the Lord your god [is] God in heaven above, and on the earth beneath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now swear to me by the Lord God; since I deal mercifully with you, so do you⌃ also deal mercifully with the house of my father: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and save alive the house of my father, my mother, and my brethren, and all my house, and all that they have, and you⌃ shall rescue my soul from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the men said to her, Our life for yours [even] to death: and she said, When the Lord shall have delivered the city to you, you⌃ shall deal mercifully and truly with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And she let them down by the window; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and she said to them, Depart into the hill-country, lest the pursuers meet you, and you⌃ shall be hidden there three days until your pursuers return from after you, and afterwards you⌃ shall depart on your way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the men said to her, We are clear of this your oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold, we shall enter into a part of the city, and you shall set a sign; you shall bind this scarlet cord in the window, by which you have let us down, and you shall bring in to yourself, into your house, your father, and your mother, and your brethren, and all the family of your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it shall come to pass that whoever shall go outside the door of your house, his guilt shall be upon him, and we shall be quit of this your oath; and we will be responsible for all that shall be found with you in your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But if any one should injure us, or betray these our matters, we shall be quit of this your oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she said to them, Let it be according to your word; and she sent them out, and they departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they came to the hill-country, and remained there three days; and the pursuers searched all the roads, and found them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the two young men returned, and came down out of the mountain; and they went over to Joshua the son of Naue, and told him all things that had happened to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they said to Joshua, The Lord has delivered all the land into our power, and all the inhabitants of that land tremble because of us.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: Rahab (Rachav) — Broad; spacious God’s mercy was broad enough to save a Canaanite prostitute. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: tiqvah (תִּקְוָה) = hope; cord. Common English renderings: hope. Used for expectation and also a literal cord in narrative.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} sent or, had sent Shittim, to spy secretly; even Jericho, harlot's house Though the word zonah generally denotes a prostitute, yet many very learned men are of opinion that it should be here rendered an innkeeper or hostess, from zoon, to furnish or provide food. In this sense it was understood by the Targumist, who renders it, ittetha pundekeetha, "a woman, a tavern-keeper, " and so St. Chrysostome, in his second sermon on Repentance, calls her πανδοκευτρια . The Greek πορνη, by which the LXX render it, and which is adopted by the Apostles, is derived from περναω, to sell, and is also supposed to denote a tavern keeper. Among the ancients, women generally kept houses of entertainment. Herodotus says, "Among the Egyptians, the women carry on all commercial concerns, and keep taverns, while the men continue at home and weave." The same custom prevailed among the Greeks.; Rachab; lodged Heb. lay \textsuperscript{5} of shutting; the men went out \textsuperscript{6} to the roof; hid them \textsuperscript{9} I know; that the Lord; your terror; faint Heb. melt \textsuperscript{10} For we; what ye did \textsuperscript{11} our hearts, ; did there remain Heb. rose up, for the Lord \textsuperscript{12} swear; that ye will; my father's; give me \textsuperscript{13} my father It is observable that in this enumeration of her kindred, there is no mention made of a husband. It is most likely that she was a single woman or widow, who obtained an honest livelihood by keeping a house for the entertainment of strangers; and not a woman of ill fame, as some have supposed. The spies sent on this occasion were certainly some of the most confidential persons that Joshua had in his host, and their errand was of the greatest importance; is it then not most likely that they lodged at an inn? \textsuperscript{14} for yours Heb. instead of you to die, when the Lord \textsuperscript{15} she let them; for her house \textsuperscript{18} scarlet thread; bring Heb. gather thy father \textsuperscript{19} whosoever; his blood; his blood \textsuperscript{20} And if thou we will be quit \textsuperscript{24} Truly the Lord; all the inhabitants; faint Heb. melt\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 3}
\markright{JOSHUA 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and departed from Sattin; and they came as far as Jordan, and lodged there before they crossed over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass after three days, [that] the scribes went through the camp; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and they charged the people, saying, When you⌃ shall see the ark of the covenant of the Lord our God, and our priests and the Levites bearing it, you⌃ shall depart from your places, and you⌃ shall go after it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But let there be a distance between you and it; you⌃ shall stand as much as two thousand cubits [from it]. Do not draw near to it, that you⌃ may know the way which you⌃ are to go; for you⌃ have not gone the way before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Joshua said to the people, Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow, for to-morrow the Lord will do wonders among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joshua said to the priests, Take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and go before the people: and the priests took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and went before the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord said to Joshua, This day do I begin to exalt you before all the children of Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so will I also be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now charge the priests that bear the ark of the covenant, saying, As soon as you⌃ shall enter on a part of the water of Jordan, then you⌃ shall stand in Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joshua said to the children of Israel, Come hither, and listen to the word of the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Hereby you⌃ shall know that the living God [is] among you, and will utterly destroy from before our face the Chananite, and the Chettite and Pherezite, and the Evite, and the Amorite, and the Gergesite, and the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes over Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Choose for yourselves twelve men of the sons of Israel, one of each tribe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it shall come to pass, when the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord of the whole earth rest in the water of Jordan, the water of Jordan [below] shall fail, and the water coming down from above shall stop. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the people removed from their tents to cross over Jordan, and the priests bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord before the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when the priests that bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord entered upon Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord were dipped in part of the water of Jordan; (now Jordan overflowed all its banks about the time of wheat harvest:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} then the waters that came down from above stopped; there stood one solid heap very far off, as far as the region of Kariathiarim, and the lower part came down to the sea of Araba, the salt sea, till it completely failed; and the people stood opposite Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the priests that bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood on dry land in the midst of Jordan; and all the children of Israel went through on dry land, until all the people had completely gone over Jordan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} rose early Archbishop Usher supposes, that this was upon Wednesday, the 28th of April, am 2553, the fortieth year of the Exodus from Egypt. From Shittim, where the israelites had been encamped for about two months ( ), to the Jordan, was, according to Josephus, about sixty stadia; that is, between seven and eight English miles.; Shittim; Jordan, called by the Arabs El Sharia, takes its rise in Anti-Libanus, about twelve miles north of Cesarea Philippi, now Banias; and, having run about twelve miles southward, it receives a considerable stream, which is now called the Moiet Hasbeia. About 15 miles farther, it forms the waters of Merom or Semechon, now Houle; and, after running about 28 miles more, it passes through the lake of Gennesareth, and thence runs southward till it loses itself in the Dead Sea; its whole course being about 160 miles. \textsuperscript{3} When ye see the priests, ; ye shall remove \textsuperscript{4} a space; heretofore Heb. since yesterday and the third day; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} magnify thee; as I was \textsuperscript{10} Hereby ye; living; among; drive out from \textsuperscript{13} the soles; of the Lord stand upon \textsuperscript{15} the feet; Jordan overfloweth The ordinary current of the Jordan, near where the Israelites crossed, is said by Maundrell, to be about twenty yards across, deeper than a man's height, and so rapid, that there is no swimming against it. It has, however, two banks; the first, or inner one, is that of the river in its natural state, and the second, or outer one, about a furlong distant, is that of its overflowings, which it does when the summer's sun has melted the snow on mount Lebanon and Hermon, in the months of March and April. And this was the time which God chose that the Israelites should pass over it; that a miraculous interposition might be necessary; and that, by the miracle, they might be convinced of his omnipotence.; all the time \textsuperscript{16} rose up; Zaretan, Zartanah, Zarthan the salt sea; The passage through the Red Sea took place in the night, when the Israelites were fleeing from the Egyptians with great trepidation, but they passed Jordan in the day-time, with previous warning, leisurely, directly opposite to Jericho, and with a triumphant defiance of the Canaanites; this passage into the promised land evidently typifying the believer's passage through death to heaven. \textsuperscript{17} the priests stood firm; all the Israelites\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 4}
\markright{JOSHUA 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when the people had completely passed over Jordan, the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Take men from the people, one of each tribe, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and charge them; and you⌃ shall take out of the midst of Jordan twelve fit stones, and having carried them across together with yourselves, place them in your camp, where you⌃ shall encamp for the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joshua having called twelve men of distinction among the children of Israel, one of each tribe, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} said to them, Advance before me in the presence of the Lord into the midst of Jordan, and each having taken up a stone from thence, let him carry it on his shoulders, according to the number of the twelve tribes of Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} that these may be to you continually for an appointed sign, that when your son asks you in future, saying, What are these stones to us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} then you may explain to your son, saying, The river Jordan was dried up from before the ark of the covenant of the Lord of the whole earth, when it passed it: and these stones shall be for a memorial for you for the children of Israel for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Israel did so, as the Lord commanded Joshua; and they took up twelve stones out of the midst of Jordan, (as the Lord commanded Joshua, when the children of Israel had completely passed over,) and carried these stones with them into the camp, and laid them down there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joshua set also other twelve stones in Jordan itself, in the place that was under the feet of the priests that bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and there they are to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the priests that bore the ark of the covenant stood in Jordan, until Joshua [had] finished all that the Lord commanded him to report to the people; and the people hasted and passed over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass when all the people had passed over, that the ark of the covenant of the Lord passed over, and the stones before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse passed over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses commanded them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Forty thousand armed for battle went over before the Lord to war, to the city of Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} In that day the Lord magnified Joshua before all the people of Israel; and they feared him, as [they did] Moses, as long as he lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Charge the priests that bear the ark of the covenant of the testimony of the Lord, to go up out of Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Joshua charged the priests, saying, Go up out of Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass when the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord were gone up out of Jordan, and set their feet upon the land, [that] the water of Jordan returned impetuously to its place, and went as before over all its banks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the people went up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month; and the children of Israel encamped in Galgala in the region eastward from Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Joshua set these twelve stones which he took out of Jordan, in Galgala, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} saying, When your sons ask you, saying, What are these stones? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Tell your sons, that Israel went over this Jordan on dry land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} when the Lord our God had dried up the water of Jordan from before them, until they had passed over; as the Lord our God did to the Red Sea, which the Lord our God dried up from before us, until we passed over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} That all the nations of the earth might know, that the power of the Lord is mighty, and that you⌃ might worship the Lord our God in every work.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the priests feet twelve stones; leave them \textsuperscript{6} a sign; when your; in time to come Heb. to-morrow \textsuperscript{9} set up twelve; and they are there These words might be written by Joshua at the close of his life, or perhaps be added by some later prophet. It seems from this verse, that there were two sorts of stones erected as a memorial of this great event. Twelve at Gilgal ( ), and twelve in the bed of the Jordan; which last might have been placed on a base of strong stone work, so high as always to be visible, and serve to mark the very spot where the priests stood with the ark. Drs. Kennicott and Shuckford, however, would read here with the Syriac, mittoch, "from the midst, " instead of bethoch, "in the midst; " and render, "And Joshua took up the twelve stones (taken) from the midst of Jordan, " etc. But this reading is unsupported by any manuscript yet collated; and it appears wholly unnecessary. \textsuperscript{10} stood in the midst; Moses; hasted \textsuperscript{13} prepared for war or, ready armed, to the plains \textsuperscript{18} the soles, lifted up Heb. plucked up that the waters As soon as the priests and the ark were come up out of Jordan, the waters of the river, which had stood on a heap, flowed down according to their natural and usual course, and again soon filled the channel. This make it abundantly evident, that the miraculous change which had been given to the river was not from any secret natural cause, but solely by the power of God, and for the sake of his chosen people; for when Israel's host had passed through, and the token of his presence was removed, immediately the waters went forward again, so that if it be asked, "What aileth thee, O Jordan, that thou wast driven back?" it must be answered, it was in obedience to the God of Israel, and in kindness to the Israel of God. and flowed Heb. went \textsuperscript{19} first month Gilgal That is, the place afterwards called Gilgal; for it is so called here by anticipation. It was about ten furlongs east from Jericho, and fifty west from the Jordan. See Josephus and Calmet. \textsuperscript{21} When your; in time to come Heb. to-morrow \textsuperscript{23} as the Lord The parents must take that occasion to tell their children of the drying up of the Red Sea forty years before: "As the Lord your God did to the Red Sea." It greatly magnifies later mercies to compare them with those before enjoyed; for, by making the comparison, it appears that God is the same yesterday, to-day, and forever. Later blessings should also bring to remembrance former mercies, and revive thankfulness for them. which he dried \textsuperscript{24} all the people; , that it is; ye might; for ever Heb. all days\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 5}
\markright{JOSHUA 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when the kings of the Amorites who were beyond Jordan heard, and the kings of Phoenicia by the sea, that the Lord God had dried up the river Jordan from before the children of Israel when they passed over, that their hearts failed, and they were terror-stricken, and there was no sense in them because of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And about this time the Lord said to Joshua, Make you stone knives of sharp stone, and sit down and circumcise the children of Israel the second time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joshua made sharp knives of stone, and circumcised the children of Israel at the place called the “Hill of Foreskins.” {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [this is] the way in which Joshua purified the children of Israel; as many as were born in the way, and as many as were uncircumcised of them that came out of Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} all these Joshua circumcised; for forty and two years Israel wondered in the wilderness of Mabdaris— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore most of the fighting men that came out of the land of Egypt, were uncircumcised, who disobeyed the commands of God; concerning whom also he determined that they should not see the land, which the Lord swore to give to their fathers, [even] a land flowing with milk and honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And in their place he raised up their sons, whom Joshua circumcised, because they were uncircumcised, having been born by the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when they had been circumcised they rested continuing there in the camp till they were healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord said to Joshua the son of Naue, On this day have I removed the reproach of Egypt from you: and he called the name of that place Galgala. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the children of Israel kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, to the westward of Jericho on the opposite side of the Jordan in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they ate of the grain of the earth unleavened and new [corn]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} In this day the manna failed, after they had eaten of the corn of the land, and the children of Israel no longer had manna: and they took the fruits of the land of the Phoenicians in that year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass when Joshua was in Jericho, that he looked up with his eyes and saw a man standing before him, and [there was] a drawn sword in his hand; and Joshua drew near and said to him, Are you for us or on the side of our enemies? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said to him, I am now come, the chief captain of the host of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joshua fell on his face upon the earth, and said to him, Lord, what command you your servant? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the captain of the Lord's host said to Joshua, Loose your shoe off your feet, for the place whereon you now stand is holy.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} all the kings; Canaanites; which were by; heard; neither was \textsuperscript{2} sharp knives or, knives of flints, Before the use of iron was common, all the nations of the earth had their edge tools made of stones, flints, etc. Our ancestors had their arrows and spearheads made of flint; which are frequently turned up by the plough. And even when iron became more common, stone knives seem to have been preferred for making incisions in the human body. The Egyptians used such to open the bodies for embalming; and the tribe of Alnajab in Ethiopia, who follow the Mosaic institution, perform the rite of circumcision, according to Ludolf, cultris lapidibus, with knives made of stone. circumcise \textsuperscript{3} Joshua; the hill of the foreskins or, Gibeah haaraloth \textsuperscript{6} walked;, ; sware that; a land \textsuperscript{8} when they etc. Heb. when the people had made an end to be circumcised till they were whole \textsuperscript{9} I rolled away; Gilgal That is, rolling. \textsuperscript{11} old corn The people would find abundance of old corn in the deserted granaries of the affrighted inhabitants, and the barley harvest being ripe, after offering the sheaf of first-fruits, they ate also new parched corn; and thus the manna being no longer necessary, ceased, after having been sent them regularly for almost forty years. To Christians the manna for their souls shall never fail, till they arrive at the Canaan above, to feast on its rich and inexhaustible provisions. unleavened cakes \textsuperscript{12} the manna; but they did eat \textsuperscript{13} he lifted; a man; his sword;, Art thou for us \textsuperscript{14} but as captain or, Prince; fell on his; What saith; my lord \textsuperscript{15} Loose; And Joshua Many persons have been puzzled to know what was intended by this extraordinary appearance of the angel to Joshua, because they supposed that the whole business ends with the chapter; whereas it is continued in the succeeding one, the first verse of which is a mere parenthesis, simply relating to the state of Jericho at the time when Joshua was favoured with this encouraging vision; by which he was shewn that their help came from God alone, and that it was not by human might or power, but by the Lord of hosts they were to obtain the victory.\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 6}
\markright{JOSHUA 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now Jericho was closely shut up and besieged, and none went out of it, and none came in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to Joshua, Behold, I deliver Jericho into your power, and its king in it, [and its] mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And do you set the men of war round about it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it shall be [that] when you⌃ shall sound with the trumpet, all the people shall shout together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when they have shouted, the walls of the city shall fall of themselves; and all the people shall enter, each one rushing direct into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joshua the [son] of Naue went in to the priests, and spoke to them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And let seven priests having seven sacred trumpets proceed thus before the Lord, and let them sound loudly; and let the ark of the covenant of the Lord follow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Charge the people to go round, and encompass the city; and let your men of war pass on armed before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let the men of war proceed before, and the priests bringing up the rear behind the ark of the covenant of the Lord [proceed] sounding the trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joshua commanded the people, saying, Cry not out, nor let any one hear your voice, until he himself declare to you the time to cry out, and then you⌃ shall cry out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the ark of the covenant of God having gone round immediately returned into the camp, and lodged there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And on the second day Joshua rose up in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets went on before the Lord; and afterwards the men of war went on, and the remainder of the multitude went after the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the priests sounded with the trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the rest of the multitude compassed the city six times from within a short distance, and went back again into the camp; this they did six days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And on the seventh day they rose up early, and compassed the city on that day seven times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass at the seventh circuit the priests blew the trumpets; and Joshua said to the children of Israel, Shout, for the Lord has given you the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the city shall be devoted, it and all things that are in it, to the Lord of Hosts: only do you⌃ save Raab the harlot, and all things in her house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But keep yourselves strictly from the accursed thing, lest you⌃ set your mind upon and take of the accursed thing, and you⌃ make the camp of the children of Israel an accursed thing, and destroy us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And all the silver, or gold, or brass, or iron, shall be holy to the Lord; it shall be carried into the treasury of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the priests sounded with the trumpets: and when the people heard the trumpets, all the people shouted at once with a loud and strong shout; and all the wall fell round about, and all the people went up into the city: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and Joshua devoted it to destruction, and all things that were in the city, man and woman, young man and old, and calf and ass, with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joshua said to the two young men who had acted a spies, Go into the house of the woman, and bring her out thence, and all that she has. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the two young men who had spied out the city entered into the house of the woman, and brought out Raab the harlot, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and her kindred, and all that she had; and they set her without the camp of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the city was burnt with fire with all things that were in it; only of the silver, and gold, and brass, and iron, they gave to be brought into the treasury of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joshua saved alive Raab the harlot, and all the house of her father, and caused her to dwell in Israel until this day, because she hid the spies which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joshua adjured [them] on that day before the Lord, saying, Cursed [be] the man who shall build that city: he shall lay the foundation of it in his firstborn, and he shall set up the gates of it in his youngest son. And so did Hozan of Baethel; he laid the foundation in Abiron his firstborn, and set up the gates of it in his youngest surviving son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord was with Joshua, and his name was in all the land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} was straitly Heb. did shut up, and was shut up; because \textsuperscript{2} the Lord I have, ; , the king \textsuperscript{4} trumpets of rams' The words shopheroth hyyovelim, should rather be rendered jubilee, trumpets, i.e., such as were used on the jubilee, which were probably made of horn or silver. For the entrance of the Israelites into Canaan was indeed a jubilee to them (see note on ). Instead of the dreadful trumpet of war, they were ordered to sound the trumpet of joy, as already conquerors.; , ; seven times \textsuperscript{5} make a long; the people; and the wall The words wenaphelah chomath hair tachteyha, are literally, "and the wall of the city shall fall down under itself; " which appears simply to mean, that the wall shall fall down from its very foundation; which was probably the case in every part, though large breaches in different places might have been amply sufficient first to admit the armed men, after whom the host might enter to destroy the city. There is no ground for the supposition that the walls sunk into the earth.; flat Heb. under it \textsuperscript{9} and the rereward Heb. gathering, host \textsuperscript{10} any noise with your voice Heb. your voice to be heard; until the day \textsuperscript{15} about the dawning; only on that day \textsuperscript{17} accursed or, devoted; *marg.; only Rahab because \textsuperscript{18} in any wise; lest ye make, ; make the camp; and trouble it \textsuperscript{19} all the silver;, ; consecrated Heb. holiness, *marg. the treasury \textsuperscript{20} the wall; flat Heb. under it \textsuperscript{21} And they The Canaanites were ripe for destruction; and God was pleased, instead of destroying them by a pestilence, a famine, or an earthquake, to employ the Israelites as the executioners of his vengeance. Had an angel been commissioned to slay them, who would have charged him with iniquity or cruelty? In all public calamities infants are involved; and tens of thousands of infants die in great agony every year. Now, either God is not the agent in these calamities (which opinion, though often implied in men's reasonings on these subjects, is not far from atheism); or they must consist with the most perfect justice and goodness. utterly \textsuperscript{22} Joshua, as ye sware unto her \textsuperscript{23} out Rahab; kindred Heb. families left them \textsuperscript{25} Rahab; she dwelleth unto because \textsuperscript{26} adjured This is to be regarded as a prediction, that he who rebuilded this city should lose all his children in the interim between the laying of the foundation to the completion of the walls.; Cursed\par}
