\subsection*{Joshua 7}
\markright{JOSHUA 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But the children of Israel committed a great trespass, and purloined [part] of the accursed thing; and Achar the son of Charmi, the son of Zambri, the son of Zara, of the tribe of Juda, took of the accursed thing; and the Lord was very angry with the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joshua sent men to Gai, which is by Baethel, saying, Spy out Gai: and the men went up and spied Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they returned to Joshua, and said to him, Let not all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and take the city by siege: carry not up there the whole people, for [the enemy] are few. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there went up about three thousand men, and they fled from before the men of Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the men of Gai killed of them to the number of thirty-six men, and they pursued them from the gate, and destroyed them from the steep hill; and the heart of the people was alarmed and became as water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joshua tore his garments; and Joshua fell on the earth on his face before the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they cast dust on their heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Joshua said, I pray, Lord, therefore has your servant brought this people over Jordan to deliver them to the Amorite to destroy us? would we had remained and settled ourselves beyond Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And what shall I say since Israel has turned his back before his enemy? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when the Chananite and all the inhabitants of the land hear it, they shall compass us round and destroy us from off the land: and what will you do [for] your great name? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said to Joshua, Rise up; why have you fallen upon your face? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The people has sinned, and transgressed the covenant which I made with them; they have stolen from the cursed thing, and put it into their store. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the children of Israel will not be able to stand before their enemies; they will turn their back before their enemies, for they have become an accursed thing: I will not any longer be with you, unless you⌃ remove the cursed thing from yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Rise, sanctify the people and tell them to sanctify themselves for the morrow: thus says the Lord God of Israel, The accursed thing is among you; you⌃ shall not be able to stand before your enemies, until you⌃ shall have removed the cursed thing from among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you⌃ shall all be gathered together by your tribes in the morning, and it shall come to pass that the tribe which the Lord shall show, you⌃ shall bring by families; and the family which the Lord shall show, you⌃ shall bring by households; and the household which the Lord shall show, you⌃ shall bring man by man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the man who shall be pointed out, shall be burnt with fire, and all that he has; because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord, and has wrought wickedness in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joshua rose up early, and brought the people by their tribes; and the tribe of Juda was pointed out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it was brought by their families, and family of the Zaraites was pointed out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it was brought man by man, and Achar the son of Zambri the son of Zara was pointed out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Joshua said to Achar, Give glory this day to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession; and tell me what you have done, and hide it not from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Achar answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel: thus and thus have I done: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I saw in the spoil an embroidered mantle, and two hundred didrachmas of silver, and one golden wedge of fifty didrachmas, and I desired them and took them; and, behold, they are hid in my tent, and the silver is hid under them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent into the camp; and these things were hidden in his tent, and the silver under them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they brought them out of the tent, and brought them to Joshua and the elders of Israel, and they laid them before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Joshua took Achar the son of Zara, and brought him to the valley of Achor, and his sons, and his daughters, and his calves, and his asses, and all his sheep, and his tent, and all his property, and all the people [were] with him; and he brought them to Emec Achor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joshua said to Achar, Why have you destroyed us? the Lord destroy you as at this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they set up over him a great heap of stones; and the Lord ceased from his fierce anger. Therefore he called the place Emecachor until this day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} committed; for Achan; Achar, Zimri took the anger \textsuperscript{2} to Ai; Hai, Aija Bethaven; Go up \textsuperscript{3} about two Heb. about 2, 000 men, or about 3, 000 men, labour. \textsuperscript{5} for they the going down or, Morad wherefore \textsuperscript{6} rent; fell; until the eventide, ; put dust Rending the clothes, beating the breast, tearing the hair, throwing dust upon the head, and falling prostrate, were usual signs of deep affliction and distress among the ancient Israelites. In illustration of this custom, see note on, when the messenger brought tidings to Eli of the discomfiture of the armies of Israel by the Philistines; again, in the case of Tamar, and in, when a whole nation, "assembled with fasting, and with sackcloth, and earth upon them." In the case of Mordecai, see note on . See note on, where his friends abased themselves to comfort him. See note on, see note on, and see note on . In each of these instances it is worthy of remark, that putting dust on the head generally follows rending of the clothes, and was the usual mode of evincing poignant sorrow. \textsuperscript{7} wherefore; to deliver; would to and dwelt \textsuperscript{8} what shall; backs Heb. necks \textsuperscript{9} shall hear; environ, what wilt thou \textsuperscript{11} Israel, transgressed; the accursed, stolen; dissembled; among \textsuperscript{12} the children; they were; neither \textsuperscript{13} sanctify; an accursed; take away \textsuperscript{15} he that is; he hath wrought; folly or, wickedness \textsuperscript{19} My son; give; make; tell me \textsuperscript{21} I saw; Babylonish garment Addereth shinâr, "a splendid or costly robe of Shinar, " the plain in which Babylon stood. Bochart and Calmet have shewn at large, that Babylonish robes were very splendid, and in high reputation. Calmet says, they are generally allowed to have been of various colours, though some suppose they were woven thus; others, that they were embroidered with the needle; and others, that they were painted. Silius Italicus seems to think they were woven. Martial supposes them to have been embroidered with the needle; and Pliny and Apuleius speak of them as painted. *marg. wedge Heb. tongue I coveted; took them; they are hid \textsuperscript{23} laid them out Heb. poured \textsuperscript{24} took Achan; his sons; the valley \textsuperscript{25} Why hast; all Israel;, burned \textsuperscript{26} raised; So the Lord; The valley; Achor that is, Trouble\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 8}
\markright{JOSHUA 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Joshua, Fear not, nor be timorous: take with you all the men of war, and arise, go up to Gai; behold, I have given into your hands the king of Gai, and his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall do to Gai, as you did to Jericho and its king; and you shall take to yourself the spoil of its cattle; set now for yourself an ambush for the city behind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joshua and all the men of war rose to go up to Gai; and Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men, and he sent them away by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he charged them, saying, Do you⌃ lie in ambush behind the city: do not go far from the city, and you⌃ shall all be ready. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I and all with me will draw near to the city: and it shall come to pass when the inhabitants of Gai shall come forth to meet us, as before, that we will flee from before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when they shall come out after us, we will draw them away from the city; and they will say, These men flee from before us, as also before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you⌃ shall rise up out of the ambuscade, and go into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You⌃ shall do according to this word, behold! I have commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joshua sent them, and they went to lie in ambush; and they lay between Baethel and Gai, westward of Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and numbered the people; and he went up, he and the elders before the people to Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the men of war went up with him, and they went forward and came over against the city eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the ambuscade [was] on the west side of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it came to pass when the king of Gai saw [it], he hasted and went out to meet them direct to the battle, he and all the people [that were] with him: and he knew not that there was an ambuscade [formed] against him behind the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joshua and Israel saw, and retreated from before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they pursued after the children of Israel, and they themselves went to a distance from the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} There was no one left in Gai who did not pursue after Israel; and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord said to Joshua, Stretch forth your hand with the spear that is in your hand toward the city, for I have delivered it into your hands; and the liers in wait shall rise up quickly out of their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Joshua stretched out his hand [and] his spear toward the city, and the ambuscade rose up quickly out of their place; and they came forth when he stretched out his hand; and they entered into the city, and took it; and they hasted and burnt the city with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when the inhabitants of Gai looked round behind them, then they saw the smoke going up out of the city to heaven, and they were no longer able to flee this way or that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambuscade had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city went up to heaven; and they turned and struck the men of Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And these came forth out of the city to meet them; and they were in the midst of the army, some [being] on this side, and some on that; and they struck them until there was not left of them one who survived and escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they took the king of Gai alive, and brought him to Joshua. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And when the children of Israel had ceased slaying all that were in Gai, and in the fields, and in the mountain on the descent, from whence they pursued them [even] to the end, then Joshua returned to Gai, and struck it with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they that fell in that day, men and women, were twelve thousand: [they killed] all the inhabitants of Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Beside the spoils that were in the city, all things which the children of Israel took as spoil for themselves according to the command of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Joshua. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Joshua burnt the city with fire: he made it an uninhabited heap for ever, [even] to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he hanged the king of Gai on a gallows; and he remained on the tree till evening: and when the sun went down, Joshua gave charge, and they took down his body from the tree, and cast it into a pit, and they set over him a heap of stones until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel in mount Gaebal, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the law of Moses, an altar of unhewn stones, on which iron had not been lifted up; and he offered there whole burnt offerings to the Lord, and a peace-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Joshua wrote upon the stones a copy of the law, even the law of Moses, before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And all Israel, and their elders, and their judges, and their scribes, passed on one side and on the other before the ark; and the priests and the Levites took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and the stranger and the native were there, who were half of them near mount Garizin, and half near mount Gaebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded at first, to bless the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And afterwards Joshua read accordingly all the words of this law, the blessings and the curses, according to all things written in the law of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} There was not a word of all that Moses charged Joshua, which Joshua read not in the ears of all the assembly of the children of Israel, the men, and the women, and the children, and the strangers that joined themselves to Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Fear not, ; take all It would seem, from this verse, that all that were capable of bearing arms were to march out of the camp on this occasion: 30, 000 formed an ambuscade in one place; and 5, 000 were placed in another, who all gained their positions in the night. With the rest of the army, Joshua appeared the next morning before Ai, which the men of that city would naturally suppose was the whole of the Israelitish force and, consequently, be the more emboldened to come out and attack them. Some, however, think that 30, 000 men were the whole that were employed on this occasion, 5, 000 of whom were placed in ambush on the west of the city, between Bethel and Ai ( ), and, with the rest, Joshua appeared before the city in the morning. The king, seeing but about 25, 000 coming against him, though he had but 12, 000 persons in the whole city ( ), determined to risk a battle, issued out, and was defeated by stratagem. I have \textsuperscript{2} do to Ai, . See note on, see note on, see note on, and see note on . only the spoil; lay thee \textsuperscript{4} lie in wait;, ; go not \textsuperscript{5} as at that we will \textsuperscript{6} drawn Heb. pulled, They flee \textsuperscript{8} set the city, I have \textsuperscript{12} five thousand of the city or, of Ai \textsuperscript{14} Ai saw it, he wist not \textsuperscript{17} a man, ; Bethel is not mentioned in the Greek version, and some, with Houbigant and Pilkington, think it was not originally in the Hebrew; because, had the men of Bethel pursued, as well as those of Ai, it would have been said that they left the cities, and not the city, open. The principal strength of Bethel might have been previously taken into Ai, as the strongest place to make a stand in; Bethel being but about three miles westward from Ai. \textsuperscript{18} Stretch; the spear The word keedon is rendered clypeum, a shield or buckler, by the Vulgate but the LXX translate it γαισον, which Suidas says, signifies a kind of weapon, οιον δορατος, like a spear. It may denote a short spear, javelin, or lance; for it is evident that it signifies neither the larger spear nor the shield, because it is distinguished from both., ; Joshua may have had a flag or ensign at the end of the spear, which might be seen at a considerable distance when extended, which was the sign agreed upon by him and the ambush. \textsuperscript{20} the smoke; and they had; power Heb. hand \textsuperscript{24} returned unto Ai This must refer to the women, children, and old persons left behind; for it seems that all the effective men had sallied out when they imagined the Israelites had fled ( ). \textsuperscript{28} an heap; unto this day \textsuperscript{29} the king The kings of Canaan lay under the same curse as their subjects and probably were more deeply criminal. The reserving of the king of Ai for a solemn execution, would tend to strike terror into the other kings, contribute to the success of Israel, and give their proceedings the stamp of a judicial process, and of executing the vengeance of God upon his enemies., ; as soon a great heap \textsuperscript{30} built an altar, in mount Ebal Moses himself had twice given express orders for this solemnity; once, in which he pointed out the very place where it was to be performed; and again, at the, there is a renewal of the instructions to Joshua, with special reference to minute particulars. It was a federal transaction. The covenant was now renewed between God and Israel upon their taking possession of the land of promise, that they might be encouraged in the conquest of it, and might know upon what terms they held it, and come under fresh obligations to obedience. \textsuperscript{31} as it is; altar; and they offered \textsuperscript{33} all Israel; priests, ; stranger; Moses \textsuperscript{35} was not; women; strangers were Heb. walked conversant The word conversant, from the Latin conversor, is here used in the classical sense of having intercourse with.\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 9}
\markright{JOSHUA 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when the kings of the Amorites on the other side of Jordan, who were in the mountain country, and in the plain, and in all the coast of the great sea, and those who were near Antilibanus, and the Chettites, and the Chananites, and the Pherezites, and the Evites, and the Amorites, and the Gergesites, and the Jebusites, heard [of it], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} they came all together at the same time to make war against Joshua and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the inhabitants of Gabaon heard of all that the Lord did to Jericho and Gai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they also wrought craftily, and they went and made provision and prepared themselves; and having taken old sacks on their shoulders, and old and torn and patched bottles of wine, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and the upper part of their shoes and their sandals old and clouted on their feet, and their garments old upon them—and the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy and corrupt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they came to Joshua into the camp of Israel to Galgala, and said to Joshua and Israel, We are come from a far land: now then make a covenant with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the children of Israel said to the Chorrhaean, Peradventure you dwell among us; and how should I make a covenant with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said to Joshua, We are your servants: and Joshua said to them, Whence are you⌃, and whence have you⌃ come? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they said, Your servants are come from a very far country in the name of the Lord your God: for we have heard his name, and all that he did in Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and all that he did to the kings of the Amorites, who were beyond Jordan, to Seon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Basan, who lived in Astaroth and in Edrain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And our elders and all that inhabit our land when they heard spoke to us, saying, Take to yourselves provision for the way, and go to meet them; and you⌃ shall say to them, We are your servants, and now make a covenant with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} These [are] the loaves—we took them hot for our journey on the day on which we came out to come to you; and now they are dried and become mouldy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these [are] the skins of wine which we filled when new, and they are torn; and our garments and our shoes are worn out because of the very long journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the chiefs took of their provision, and asked not [counsel of] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joshua made peace with them, and they made a covenant with them to preserve them; and the princes of the congregation swore to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were near neighbors, and that they lived among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the children of Israel departed and came to their cities; and their cities [were] Gabaon, and Kephira, and Berot, and the cities of Jarin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the children of Israel fought not with them, because all the princes swore to them by the Lord God of Israel; and all the congregation murmured at the princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the princes said to all the congregation: We have sworn to them by the Lord God of Israel, and now we shall not be able to touch them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This we will do; take them alive, and we will preserve them: so there shall not be wrath against us by reason of the oath which we swore to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They shall live, and shall be hewers of wood and drawers of water to all the congregation, as the princes said to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joshua called them together and said to them, Why have you⌃ deceived me, saying, We live very far from you; whereas you⌃ are fellow-countrymen of those who dwell among us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now you⌃ are cursed: there shall not fail of you a slave, or a hewer of wood, or a drawer of water to me and my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they answered Joshua, saying, It was reported to us what the Lord your God charged his servant Moses, to give you this land, and to destroy us and all that lived on it from before you; and we feared very much for our lives because of you, and [therefore] we did this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now, behold, we [are] in your power; do to us as it is pleasing to you, and as it seems [good] to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they did so to them; and Joshua rescued them in that day out of the hands of the children of Israel, and they did not kill them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Joshua made them in that day hewers of wood and drawers of water to the whole congregation, and for the altar of God: therefore the inhabitants of Gabaon became hewers of wood and drawers of water for the altar of God until this day, even for the place which the Lord should choose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} [Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel in mount Gebal, ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} [as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded the children of Israel, as it was written in the law of Moses, an altar of unhewn stones, on which iron had not been lifted up: and he offered there whole burnt offerings to the Lord, and a piece offering. And Joshua wrote upon the stones a copy of the law, even the law of Moses, before the children of Israel. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} [And all Israel, and their elders, and their judges, and their scribes, passed on one side and on the other, before the ark; and the priests and the levites took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and the stranger and the native were there, who were half of them near mount Gebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded at first, to bless the people. ]\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} all the kings, on this, ; of the great, ; Lebanon, ; Hittite \textsuperscript{4} work wilily; ambassadors The word tzir, an ambassador, properly denotes a hinge; because an ambassador is a person upon whom the business turns as upon a hinge. So the Latin Cardinalis, from cardo, a hinge, was the title of the prime minister of the emperor Theodosius, though now applied only to the Pope's electors and counsellors. wine bottles These bottles being made of skin, were consequently liable to be rent, and capable of being mended; which is done, according to Chardin, by putting in a piece, or by gathering up the wounded piece in the manner of a purse; and sometimes by inserting a flat piece of wood. \textsuperscript{5} old shoes; clouted The word clouted signifies here patched, from the Anglo-Saxon clut, a clout or rag; and not nailed from the French clou, a nail. \textsuperscript{6} the camp, We be; make ye Kirthoo lanoo berith, "cut or divide with us a covenant, " or rather the covenant sacrifice offered on these occasions. (See note on .) \textsuperscript{9} From a because; we have \textsuperscript{11} our elders Take; with you Heb. in your hand, We are your \textsuperscript{14} the men took of their victuals or, they received the men by reason of their victuals asked not \textsuperscript{21} let them; as the princes \textsuperscript{22} Wherefore, ; We are, ye dwell \textsuperscript{23} cursed This may refer to the original curse pronounced against the descendants of Canaan. Both of them seem to have implied nothing else than perpetual slavery. The Gibeonites were brought, no doubt, under tribute; performed the meanest offices for the Israelites; being in the same condition as the servile class of Hindoos, called the Chetrees; had their national importance annihilated, and yet were never permitted to incorporate themselves with the Israelites. none of you be freed Heb. not be cut off from you hewers In the East, collecting wood for fuel, and carrying water, are the peculiar employment of females. The Arab women of Barbary, and the daughters of the Turcomans, are thus employed. Hence Mr. Harmer concludes, that the bitterness of the doom of the Gibeonites does not seem to have consisted in the labouriousness of the service enjoined them, but its disgracing them from the characteristic employment of men, that of bearing arms, and condemning them and their posterity for ever to the employment of females. \textsuperscript{24} the Lord;, we were sore \textsuperscript{25} we are; as it seemeth \textsuperscript{27} made them Heb. gave, or delivered to be, ; , Nethinim in the place\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 10}
\markright{JOSHUA 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when Adoni-bezec king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Gai, and had destroyed it, as he did to Jericho and its king, even so they did to Gai and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gabaon had gone over to Joshua and Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} then they were greatly terrified by them, for [the king] knew that Gabaon [was] a great city, as one of the chief cities, and all its men [were] mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So Adoni-bezec king of Jerusalem sent to Elam king of Hebron, and to Phidon king of Jerimuth, and to Jephtha king of Lachis, and to Dabin king of Odollam, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Come up hither to me, and help me, and let us take Gabaon; for the Gabaonites have gone over to Joshua and to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the five kings of the Jebusites went up, the king of Jerusalem, and the king of Chebron, and the king of Jerimuth, and the king of Lachis, and the king of Odollam, they and all their people; and encamped around Gabaon, and besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the inhabitants of Gabaon sent to Joshua into the camp to Galgala, saying, Slack not your hands from your servants: come up quickly to us, and help us, and rescue us; for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country are gathered together against us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Joshua went up from Galgala, he and all the people of war with him, every one mighty in strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord said to Joshua, Fear them not, for I have delivered them into your hands; there shall not one of them be left before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when Joshua came suddenly upon them, he [had] advanced all the night out of Galgala. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord struck them with terror before the children of Israel; and the Lord destroyed them with a great slaughter at Gabaon; and they pursued them by the way of the going up of Oronin, and they struck them to Azeca and to Makeda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when they fled from the face of the children of Israel at the descent of Oronin, then the Lord cast upon them hailstones from heaven to Azeca; and they were more that died by the hailstones, than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword in the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then Joshua spoke to the Lord, in the day in which the Lord delivered the Amorite into the power of Israel, when he destroyed them in Gabaon, and they were destroyed from before the children of Israel: and Joshua said, Let the sun stand over against Gabaon, and the moon over against the valley of Aelon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the sun and the moon stood still, until God executed vengeance on their enemies; and the sun stood still in the midst of heaven; it did not proceed to set till the end of one day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And there was not such a day either before or after, so that God should listen to a man, because the Lord fought on the side of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And these five kings fled, and hid themselves in a cave that is in Makeda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it was told Joshua, saying, The five kings have been found hid in the cave that is in Makeda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joshua said, Roll stones to the mouth of the cave, and set men to watch over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But do not you⌃ stand, but pursue after your enemies, and attack the rear of them, and do not suffer them to enter into their cities; for the Lord our God has delivered them into our hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when Joshua and all Israel ceased destroying them utterly with a very great slaughter, that they that escaped took refuge in the strong cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all the people returned safe to Joshua to Makeda; and no one of the children of Israel murmured with his tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joshua said, Open the cave, and bring out these five kings out of the cave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they brought out the five kings out of the cave, the king of Jerusalem, and the king of Chebron, and the king of Jerimuth, and the king of Lachis, and the king of Odollam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And when they brought them out to Joshua, then Joshua called together all Israel, and the chiefs of the army that went with him, saying to them, Come forward and set your feet on their necks; and they came and set their feet on their necks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joshua said to them, Do not fear them, neither be cowardly; be courageous and strong, for thus the Lord will do to all your enemies, against whom you⌃ fight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joshua killed them, and hanged them on five trees; and they hung upon the trees until the evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass toward the setting of the sun, Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees, and cast them into the cave into which they [had] fled for refuge, and rolled stones to the cave, [which remain] till this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they took Makeda on that day, and killed the inhabitants with the edge of the sword, and they utterly destroyed every living thing that was in it; and there was none left in it that was preserved and had escaped; and they did to the king of Makeda, as they did to the king of Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Joshua and all Israel with him departed out of Makeda to Lebna, and besieged Lebna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the Lord delivered it into the hands of Israel: and they took it, and its king, and killed the inhabitants with the edge of the sword, and every thing breathing in it; and there was not left in it any that survived and escaped; and they did to its king, as they did to the king of Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Joshua and all Israel with him departed from Lebna to Lachis, and he encamped about it, and besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the Lord delivered Lachis into the hands of Israel; and they took it on the second day, and they put the inhabitants to death with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed it, as they had done to Lebna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then Elam the king of Gazer went up to help Lachis; and Joshua struck him and his people with the edge of the sword, until there was not left to him one that was preserved and escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Joshua and all Israel with him departed from Lachis to Odollam, and he besieged it and took it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Lord delivered it into the hand of Israel; and he took it on that day, and killed the inhabitants with the edge of the sword, and killed every thing breathing in it, as they did to Lachis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Joshua and all Israel with him departed to Chebron, and encamped about it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And he struck it with the edge of the sword, and all the living creatures that were in it; there was no one preserved: they destroyed it and all things in it, as they did to Odollam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Joshua and all Israel returned to Dabir; and they encamped about it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and they took it, and its king, and its villages: and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and they destroyed it, and every thing breathing in it; and they did not leave in it any one that was preserved: as they did to Chebron and her king, so they did to Dabir and her king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Joshua struck all the land of the hill country, and Nageb and the plain country, and Asedoth, and her kings, they did not leave of them one that was saved: and they utterly destroyed every thing that had the breath of life, as the Lord God of Israel commanded, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} from Cades Barne to Gaza, all Gosom, as far as Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Joshua struck, once for all, all their kings, and their land, because the Lord God of Israel fought on the side of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Heb. vocab: Yerushalayim (יְרוּשָׁלַםִם) = Jerusalem. Common English renderings: Jerusalem. Central city of Davidic kingship and temple worship.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Adoni-zedec; as he had, how the \textsuperscript{2} they feared; Gibeon was situated on an eminence, as its name imports, 40 furlongs north from Jerusalem, according to Josephus. the royal cities Heb. cities of the kingdom \textsuperscript{3} king of Jerusalem, Hebron was situated on an eminence, 20 miles south of Jerusalem, and the same distance north of Beersheba. It is now called El Khalil, "the well-beloved, " the usual epithet which the Turks and Arabs apply to Abraham, whose sepulchral cave they still shew; over which St. Helena built a magnificent church Its original site was on an eminence, at the southern foot of which the present village is pleasantly situated, on which are the remains of an ancient castle, its sole defence.; Lachish \textsuperscript{6} to the camp, Slack from thy; mountains \textsuperscript{10} the Lord; , at Gibeon Bethhoron, ; Azekah; Makkedah \textsuperscript{12} Sun Joshua doubtless acted, on this occasion, by an immediate impulse upon his mind from the Spirit of God. The terms here employed to record the miracle, agree with the accustomed manner in which the motions of the earth and sun are described in our own day. The sun apparently moves, but really is stationary; while the diurnal movement of the earth on its axis is by us unnoticed, and would not have been known except by astronomical science. The sun appeared to the Israelites over Gibeon, and the moon over the valley of Ajalon, and there they stayed in their course for "a whole day." Many vain enquiries have been made concerning the way in which this miracle was wrought, and many difficulties and objections have been urged against understanding it literally. But the fact is authenticated by the Divine testimony; and the manner in which it was accomplished lies entirely out of our province, because beyond our comprehension.; stand thou Heb. be silent, *marg. Ajalon; Aijalon \textsuperscript{13} until; Jasher or, the upright; So the sun \textsuperscript{14} there was; the Lord; for the Lord \textsuperscript{16} and hid; in a cave \textsuperscript{17} This information brought to Joshua, is an evidence that there were those of the country, who knew the holes and fastnesses of it, that were in his interests. And the care Joshua took to secure them there, as it is an instance of his policy and presence of mind, even in the heat of action; so, in the success of their project, it shews how they who think to hide themselves from God, not only deceive, but destroy themselves. Their refuge of lies will but bind them over to God's judgment. \textsuperscript{19} stay ye; smite Heb. cut off the tail, suffer them \textsuperscript{25} Fear not; be strong thus shall \textsuperscript{27} they took; until this very day \textsuperscript{28} Makkedah Situated, according to Eusebius, 8 miles east from Eleutheropolis. It was afterwards assigned to the tribe of Judah. them, ; and he did \textsuperscript{29} Libnah This city was situated in the south of Judah, and in the district of Eleutheropolis, according to Eusebius and Jerome. It is probably the Libnah in the neighbourhood of which the Israelites encamped., ; as he did \textsuperscript{31} Lachish was also situated in the south of Judah, seven miles south from Eleutheropolis, according to Eusebius and Jerome. It appears to have been anciently a very strong place; for though the people were panic struck, and the Israelites flushed with success, yet Joshua could not reduce it till the second day; and the king of Assyria afterwards was obliged to raise the siege. \textsuperscript{33} Gezer was situated on the confines of Ephraim and Manasseh, between Beth-horon and the sea; and is evidently the village of Gazara mentioned by Eusebius, four miles (north) from Nicopolis or Emmaus. \textsuperscript{34} Eglon This town appears to have been no great distance from Lachish, with which it is mentioned, as one of the cities given to Judah. \textsuperscript{37} the king From, we learn that the king of Hebron was one of the five whom Joshua slew and hanged on five trees at Makkedah. This slaying of the king of Hebron, therefore, must either refer to what had already been done, or the Hebronites had set up another, whom Joshua now slew when he took the city. according \textsuperscript{38} Debir was situated in the south of the tribe of Judah, near Hebron. The expression of Joshua's returning to Debir, probably denotes, that having carried his conquests in the southern parts as far as Gaza ( ), which was in the south-west angle of Canaan, he then marched back to besiege Debir. \textsuperscript{40} all the country, utterly; as the Lord \textsuperscript{41} Kadeshbarnea; Gaza; all the country The country of Goshen, mentioned here, seems to have been in the south of Judah; and to have taken its name from the city of Goshen, situated in the same tribe., Gibeon\par}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} on the other, from the; unto the mount \textsuperscript{3} sea of Chinneroth This inland sea, or rather lake, which drives its several names, the Lake of Tiberias, Sea of Galilee, Lake of Gennesareth, from the territory which forms its western and south-western border, is computed to be between seventeen and eighteen miles in length, and from five to six in breadth. The waters of this lake, which are sweet and agreeable, lie in a deep basin, surrounded with lofty hills, except at the north and south, where it is a plain country or level. There is a current through the whole lake even to the shore; and the Jordan through it is discernible by the smoothness of the surface in that part. Its appearance from the north- western extremity is said by Mr. Buckingham to be exceedingly grand; but the barren aspect of the mountains on each side, and the total absence of wood, give a cast of dullness to the picture.; Sea of Tiberias the sea, ; Bethjeshimoth the south or, Teman Ashdothpisgah or, the springs of Pisgah, or, the hill; *marg. \textsuperscript{4} the coast; the remnant; dwelt \textsuperscript{7} on this side, Baalgad, Seir, ; Joshua gave, 13:1-19:51 \textsuperscript{11} Jarmuth Placed by Eusebius and Jerome four miles from Eleutheropolis, near Eshtaol; but, in Jermus, which is probably the same, they state it to be ten miles from Eleutheropolis, towards Jerusalem; which is supposed to be nearer the truth. Lachish Eusebius and Jerome say it was a village in their time, seven miles south from Eleutheropolis. \textsuperscript{12} Eglon, Gezer appears to have situated in the tribe of Ephraim, near Beth-horon, between it and the sea. Eusebius and Jerome place it four miles north of Nicopolis or Emmaus. \textsuperscript{14} Hormah, Arad Eusebius places this city in the neighbourhood of Kadesh, four miles from Malathis, and twenty from Hebron. \textsuperscript{15} Libnah Eusebius and Jerome inform us, that Libnah was a town or village in their time, lying in the district of Eleutheropolis. \subsection*{Joshua 13}
\markright{JOSHUA 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joshua [was] old and very advanced in years; and the Lord said to Joshua, You are advanced in years, and there is much land left to inherit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And this [is] the land that is left: the borders of the Phylistines, the Gesirite, and the Chananite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} from the wilderness before Egypt, as far as the borders of Accaron on the left of the Chananites [the land] is reckoned to the five principalities of the Phylistines, to the inhabitant of Gaza, and of Azotus, and of Ascalon, and of Geth, and of Accaron, and to the Evite; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} from Thaeman even to all the land of Chanaan before Gaza, and the Sidonians as far as Aphec, as far as the borders of the Amorites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And all the land of Galiath of the Phylistines, and all Libanus eastward from Galgal, under the mountain Aermon as far as the entering in of Emath; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} every one that inhabits the hill country from Libanus as far as Masereth Memphomaim. All the Sidonians, I will destroy them from before Israel; but do you give them by inheritance to Israel, as I charged you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now divide this land by lot to the nine tribes, and to the half tribe of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} From Jordan to the great sea westward you shall give it [them]: the great sea shall be the boundary. [But] to the two tribes and to the half tribe of Manasse, to Ruben and to Gad Moses gave [an inheritance] beyond Jordan: Moses the servant of the Lord gave [it] to them eastward, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} from Aroer, which is on the bank of the brook of Arnon, and the city in the midst of the valley, and all Misor from Maedaban. The village Afka, situated in the bottom of a valley, and hour and three quarters from Akoura, and three hours' distance from Lake Liemoun, is supposed to occupy its site. Burckhardt, however, could not hear of any remains of antiquity in it neighbourhood.; the Amorites \textsuperscript{5} Giblites Probably the inhabitants of the country, around Gebal ( ), or Byblos, as the LXX render, a city of Phoenicia, situated on the Mediterranean, between Sidon and Tripoli, on the north of the river Adonis. It is now called Gibyle, of Djebail, situated about a day's journey south of Tripoli. Its walls are about a mile in circumference, with square towers about every forty yards' distance. Anciently it must have been a place of no mean extent and of considerable beauty, from the ruins still visible. *marg.; Lebanon, Baalgad under mount unto the \textsuperscript{17} Dibon Eusebius says the city was situated in the plain of Arnon. \subsection*{Joshua 14}
\markright{JOSHUA 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] they of the children of Israel that received their inheritance in the land of Chanaan, to whom Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the [son] of Naue, and the heads of the families of the tribes of the children of Israel, gave inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} They inherited according to their lots, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Joshua to the nine tribes and the half tribe, on the other side of Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the sons of Joseph were two tribes, Manasse and Ephraim; and there was none inheritance in the land given to the Levites, only cities to dwell in, and their suburbs separated for the cattle, and their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} As the Lord commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel; and they divided the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Juda came to Joshua in Galgal, and Chaleb the [son] of Jephone the Kenezite said to him, You know the word that the Lord spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and you in Cades Barne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For I was forty years old when Moses the servant of God sent me out of Cades Barne to spy out the land; and I returned him an answer according to his mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} My brethren that went up with me turned away the heart of the people, but I applied my self to follow the Lord my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Moses swore on that day, saying, The land on which you are gone up, it shall be your inheritance and your children's for ever, because you have applied yourself to follow the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now the Lord has kept me alive as he said: this [is] the forty-fifth year since the Lord spoke that word to Moses; and Israel journeyed in the wilderness; and now, behold, I [am] this day eighty-five years old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I am still strong this day, as when the Lord sent me: just so strong am I now to go out and to come in for war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now I ask of you this mountain, as the Lord said in that day; for you heard this word on that day; and now the Enakim are there, cities great and strong: if then the Lord should be with me, I will utterly destroy them, as the Lord said to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joshua blessed him, and gave Chebron to Chaleb the son of Jephone the son of Kenez for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore Chebron became the inheritance of Chaleb the [son] of Jephone the Kenezite until this day, because he followed the commandment of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the name of Chebron before was the city Argob, it [is] the metropolis of the Enakim: and the land rested from war.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} lot Though God had sufficiently pointed out by the predictions of Jacob and Moses what portions he designed for each tribe, yet we readily discern an admirable proof of His wisdom, in the orders he gave to decide them by lot. By this means the false interpretations which might have been given to the words of Jacob and Moses were prevented; and by striking at the root of whatever might occasion jealousies and disputes among the tribes, he evidently secured the honesty of those appointed to distribute the conquered lands of Canaan. Besides, the success of this method gave a fresh proof of the divinity of the Jewish religion, and the truth of its oracles. Each tribe finding itself placed by lot exactly in the spot where Jacob and Moses foretold, it was evident that Providence had equally directed both the predictions and that lot; and it would be the greatest folly and presumption not to acknowledge the inspiration of God in the words of Jacob and Moses; the direction of his hand in the lot, and his providence in the event. \textsuperscript{6} Gilgal, Caleb, Kenezite; Thou knowest; the man; , ; *title; Kadeshbarnea \textsuperscript{12} the Anakims; if so be; I shall \textsuperscript{15} And the name; And the land\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 15}
\markright{JOSHUA 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the borders of the tribe of Juda according to their families were from the borders of Idumea from the wilderness of sin, as far as Cades southward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And their borders were from the south as far as a part of the salt sea from the high country that extends southward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they proceed before the ascent of Acrabin, and go out round Sena, and go up from the south to Cades Barne; and go out to Asoron, and proceed up to Sarada, and go out by the way that is west of Cades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they go out to Selmona, and issue at the valley of Egypt; and the termination of its boundaries shall be at the sea: these are their boundaries southward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And their boundaries eastward [are] all the salt sea as far as Jordan; and their borders from the north, and from the border of the sea, and from part of Jordan— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the borders go up to Baethaglaam, and they go along from the north to Baetharaba, and the borders go on up to the stone of Baeon the son of Ruben. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the borders continue on to the fourth part of the valley of Achor, and go down to Galgal, which is before the approach of Adammin, which is southward in the valley, and terminate at the water of the fountain of the sun; and their going forth shall be the fountain of Rogel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the borders go up to the valley of Ennom, behind Jebus southward; this is Jerusalem: and the borders terminate at the top of the mountain, which is before the valley of Ennom toward the sea, which is by the side of the land of Raphain northward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the border [going forth] from the top of the mountain terminates at the fountain of the water of Naphtho, and terminates at mount Ephron; and the border will lead to Baal; this is the city of Jarim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the border will go round from Baal to the sea, and will go on to the mount of Assar behind the city of Jarin northwards; this is Chaslon: and it will come down to the city of Sun, and will go on to the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the border terminates behind Accaron northward, and the borders will terminate at Socchoth, and the borders will go on to the south, and will terminate at Lebna, and the issue of the borders will be at the sea; and their borders [shall be] toward the sea, the great sea shall be the boundary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} These [are] the borders of the children of Juda round about according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And to Chaleb the son of Jephone he gave a portion in the midst of the children of Juda by the command of God; and Joshua gave him the city of Arboc the metropolis of Enac; this is Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Chaleb the son of Jephone destroyed thence the three sons of Enac, Susi, and Tholami, and Achima. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Chaleb went up thence to the inhabitants of Dabir; and the name of Dabir before was the city of Letters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Chaleb said, Whosoever shall take and destroy the city of Letters, and master it, to him will I give my daughter Ascha to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Gothoniel the son of Chenez the brother of Chaleb took it; and he gave him Ascha his daughter to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass as she went out that she counselled him, saying, I will ask of my father a field; and she cried from off her ass; and Chaleb said to her, What is it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And she said to him, Give me a blessing, for you have set me in the land of Nageb; give me Botthanis: and he gave her Gonaethla the upper, and Gonaethla the lower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And their cities were cities belonging to the tribe of the children of Juda on the borders of Edom by the wilderness, and Baeseleel, and Ara, and Asor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and Icam, and Regma, and Aruel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and Cades, and Asorionain, and Maenam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and Balmaenan, and their villages, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and the cities of Aseron, this [is] Asor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and Sen, and Salmaa, and Molada, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and Seri, and Baephalath, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and Cholaseola, and Beersabee; and their villages, and their hamlets, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Bala and Bacoc, and Asom, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and Elboudad, and Baethel, and Herma, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and Sekelac, and Macharim, and Sethennac, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} and Labos, and Sale, and Eromoth; twenty-nine cities, and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} In the plain country Astaol, and Raa, and Assa, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} and Ramen, and Tano, and Iluthoth, and Maeani, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} and Jermuth, and Odollam, and Membra, and Saocho, and Jazeca. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Sacarim and Gadera, and its villages; fourteen cities, and their villages; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Senna, and Adasan, and Magadalgad, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} and Dalad, and Maspha, and Jachareel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and Basedoth, and Ideadalea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} and Chabra, and Maches, and Maachos, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} and Geddor, and Bagadiel, and Noman, and Machedan: sixteen cities, and their villages; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Lebna, and Ithac, and Anoch, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} and Jana, and Nasib, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} and Keilam, and Akiezi, and Kezib, and Bathesar, and Aelom: ten cities, and their villages; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Accaron and her villages, and their hamlets: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} from Accaron, Gemna, and all the cities that are near Asedoth; and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Asiedoth, and her villages, and her hamlets; Gaza, and its villages and its hamlets as far as the river of Egypt, and the great sea is the boundary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And in the hill country Samir, and Jether, and Socha, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} and Renna and the city of Letters, this [is] Dabir; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Aerem, and Remna, and Soma, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} and Jemain, and Baethachu, and Phacua, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} and Euma, and the city Arboc, this is Chebron, and Soraith: nine cities and their villages: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Maor, and Chermel, and Ozib, and Itan, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} and Jariel, and Aricam, and Zacanaim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} and Gabaa, and Thamnatha; Many of the ancient towns and villages have had their names so totally changed that their former appellations are no longer discernible; several lie buried under their own ruins, and others have been so long destroyed that not a vestige of them remains. On these accounts it is very difficult to ascertain the precise situation of many places mentioned in these chapters; but this cannot in any measure affect the truth of the narrative.; even to the \textsuperscript{2} the salt sea; bay Heb. tongue \textsuperscript{3} Maalehacrabbim or, the going up to Acrabbim; Zin; Adar Probably the same as Hazar-addar, . Karkaa Supposed to be the Coracea of Ptolemy, in Arabia Petrea Eusebius places a castle called Carcaria at the distance of a day's journey from Petra. \textsuperscript{4} Azmon The last city they possessed towards Egypt; east of the River of Egypt or Rhinocorura. river \textsuperscript{6} Bethhogla Probably the Bethagla mentioned by Jerome is the same as the "threshing-floor of Atad, " ( ), situated three miles from Jericho, and two from Jordan; and belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, though serving as a frontier to the tribe of Judah. the stone \textsuperscript{7} Debir, the valley; Gilgal, Adummim A town and mountain of Benjamin ( ), near Jericho, towards Jerusalem. Enshemesh Situated east of Jerusalem, on the confines of Judah and Benjamin. Enrogel Supposed to be the same as the fountain of Siloam, east of Jerusalem, at the foot of mount Zion. \textsuperscript{8} valley of the son A valley near to Jerusalem.; , the Jebusite;, valley of the giants Situated apparently west of Jerusalem and mount Moriah.; the valley of Rephaim \textsuperscript{9} Nephtoah Baalah A city near Bethshemesh, and, according to Eusebius, nine miles from Jerusalem, in going towards Diospolis.; Kirjathjearim \textsuperscript{10} Bethshemesh Placed by Eusebius ten miles east from Eleutheropolis, towards Nicopolis. Timnah \textsuperscript{13} Caleb; the city of Arba or, Kirjath-arba \textsuperscript{19} Give me a blessing; *marg. \textsuperscript{23} Kedesh; Hazor The LXX read Ασοριωναιν, for Hazar-Ithnan, regarding these two as one city. \textsuperscript{24} Ziph Eusebius and Jerome say, that Ziph was a village in their time eight miles east from Hebron., ; *title Telem \textsuperscript{25} Hazor Or, rather, Hazar-hadattah, or, as the LXX, Alexandrian, and Vulgate render Ασωρ η καινη, Asor nova, "New Hazor, " to distinguish it from the preceding ( ), and following Hazor. Bethpalet \textsuperscript{28} Hazarshual; Beersheba;, Bizjothjah Instead of Bizjothjah, the LXX read, "and their towns and villages." \textsuperscript{32} Ain Probably the βηθανιν of Eusebius, four miles from Hebron. Rimmon \textsuperscript{33} Eshtaol This town is placed by Eusebius ten mile from Eleutheropolis, towards Nicopolis, and it is supposed to be a wretched village, called Esdad, about 15 miles south of Yebna.; Zoreah A town near to Eshtaol, placed at ten miles' distance n of Eleutheropolis by Eusebius. \textsuperscript{35} Jarmuth, ; Adullam; Socoh Eusebius says, there were two cities of Socoh, an upper and lower, nine miles from Eleutheropolis, towards Jerusalem.; Azekah Eusebius and Jerome say there was a town of this name in their time, between Jerusalem and Eleutheropolis. \textsuperscript{36} Sharaim Adithaim Eusebius mentions two cities, called Adatha, one towards Gaza, and the other east of Lydda. and Gederothaim or, or, fourteen cities, There are fifteen in all; but the two last seem to be only two names of the same city. \textsuperscript{46} near Heb. by the place of \textsuperscript{62} the city of This city was situated somewhere in the vicinity, west of the lake Asphaltites; and supposed by some to be the same as Zoar. Engedi En-gedi, or Hazazon-Tamar, was situated, according to Eusebius, in the desert west of the Dead Sea. Josephus says it was 300 stadia from Jerusalem, and not far from the lake Asphaltites; and consequently it could not have been far from Jericho and the mouth of the Jordan. It was celebrated for the abundance of its palm-trees.\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 16}
\markright{JOSHUA 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the borders of the children of Joseph were from Jordan by Jericho eastward; and they will go up from Jericho to the hill country, to the wilderness, to Baethel Luza. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they will go out to Baethel, and will proceed to the borders of Achatarothi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they will go across to the sea to the borders of Aptalim, as far as the borders of Baethoron the lower, and the going forth of them shall be to the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the sons of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasse, took their inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the borders of the children of Ephraim were according to their families, and the borders of their inheritance were eastward to Ataroth, and Eroc as far as Baethoron the upper, and Gazara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the borders will proceed to the sea to Icasmon north of Therma; they will go round eastward to Thenasa, and Selles, and will pass on eastward to Janoca, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and to Macho, and Ataroth, and [these are] their villages; and they will come to Jericho, and will issue at Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the borders will proceed from Tapho to the sea to Chelcana; and their termination will be at the sea; this [is] the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the cities separated to the sons of Ephraim [were] in the midst of the inheritance of the sons of Manasse, all the cities and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Ephraim did not destroy the Chananite who lived in Gazer; and the Chananite lived in Ephraim until this day, until Pharao the king of Egypt went up and took it, and burnt it with fire; and the Chananites, and Pherezites, and the dwellers in Gaza they destroyed, and Pharao gave them for a dowry to his daughter.\par

Of which the one, called upper Beth-horon, from its situation, was built (rebuilt) by Solomon, and the other, called nether Beth-horon, was given to the Levites. Josephus places Beth-oron about 100 furlongs from Jerusalem. \subsection*{Joshua 17}
\markright{JOSHUA 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the borders of the tribe of the children of Manasse, (for he [was] the firstborn of Joseph,) [assigned] to Machir the firstborn of Manasse the father of Galaad, for he was a warrior, [were] in the land of Galaad and of Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was [land] assigned to the other sons of Manasse according to their families; to the sons of Jezi, and to the sons of Kelez, and to the sons of Jeziel, and to the sons of Sychem, and to the sons of Symarim, and to the sons of Opher: these [are] the males according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Salpaad the sons of Opher had no sons but daughters: and these [are] the names of the daughters of Salpaad; Maala, and Nua, and Egla, and Melcha, and Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they stood before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua, and before the rulers, saying, God gave a charge by the hand of Moses, to give us an inheritance in the midst of our brethren: so there was given to them by the command of the Lord an inheritance among the brethren of their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And their lot fell [to them] from Anassa, and [to the] plain of Labec of the land of Galaad, which is beyond Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the daughters of the sons of Manasse inherited a portion in the midst of their brethren, and the land of Galaad was assigned to the remainder of the sons of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the borders of the sons of Manasse were Delanath, which is before the sons of Anath, and it proceeds to the borders [even] to Jamin and Jassib to the fountain of Thaphthoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} It shall belong to Manasse, and Thapheth on the borders of Manasse [shall belong] to the sons of Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the borders shall go down to the valley of Carana southward by the valley of Jariel, ([there is] a turpentine tree [belonging] to Ephraim between [that and] the city of Manasse:) and the borders of Manasse [are] northward to the brook; and the sea shall be its termination. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Southward [the land belongs] to Ephraim, and northward to Manasse; and the sea shall be their cost; and northward they shall border upon Aseb, and eastward upon Issachar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Manasses shall have in [the portion of] Issachar and Aser Baethsan and their villages, and the inhabitants of Dor, and its villages, and the inhabitants of Mageddo, and its villages, and the third part of Mapheta, and its villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the sons of Manasse were not able to destroy these cities; and the Chananite began to dwell in that land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass that when the children of Israel were strong, they made the Chananites subject, but they did not utterly destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the sons of Joseph answered Joshua, saying, Therefore have you caused us to inherit one inheritance, and one line? whereas I am a great people, and God has blessed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joshua said to them, If you be a great people, go up to the forest, and clear [the land] for yourself, If mount Ephraim be too little for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they said, The mount of Ephraim does not please us, and the Chananite dwelling in it in Baethsan, and in its villages, [and] in the valley of Jezrael, has choice cavalry and iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Joshua said to the sons of Joseph, If you are a great people, and have great strength, you shall not have [only] one inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For you shall have the wood, for there is a wood, and you shall clear it, and [the land] shall be yours; even when you shall have utterly destroyed the Chananite, for he has chosen cavalry; yet you are stronger than he.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the rest the children; Abiezer, Jeezer children of Asriel children of Hepher \textsuperscript{5} ten portions As there were six sons and five daughters, among whom this division was to be made, there should be eleven portions, but Zelophehad, son of Hepher, having left five daughters in his place, neither he nor Hepher is reckoned. The lot of Manasseh therefore was divided into ten parts; five for the five sons of Gilead, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, and Shemida; and five for the five daughters of Zelophehad, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah., beside \textsuperscript{7} Asher Eusebius says this was a town in his time not far from Neapolis, towards Scythopolis or Bethshan; between which towns it is also placed by the old Jerusalem Itinerary. Michmethah Situated, probably, east of Shechem, though its precise situation, as well as that of many others, cannot, at this distance of time, be ascertained. Many of these towns were small, and we may rationally conclude, slightly built; and consequently have perished more than two thousand years ago. It would therefore be useless now to look for such places; though in many instances, their ancient names have been preserved, and their sites identified. Several towns even in England, mentioned by Cesar and other ancient writers, are no longer discernible; several have changed their names, and not a few their situation. Shechem \textsuperscript{9} river Kanah or, brook of reeds, The brook Kanah seem to be what is now called Nahr el Kasab, which falls into the Mediterranean a few miles south of Cesarea of Palestine, mentioned by the Hon. C. L. Irby, and J. Mangles. these cities the outgoings, the sea The Mediterranean \textsuperscript{11} Manasseh; Beth-shean, the Scythopolis of the Greek and Roman writers, was situated in the plain of Jordan, west of that river, 120 furlongs (south) from Tiberias, according to Josephus, and 600 furlongs (north) from Jerusalem ( ). It was the largest city of the Decapolis, and the only one on that side of Jordan. It is now called Bisan, 8 hours or 24 miles from Tiberias; and described by Dr. Richardson, exclusive of its ruins, as a "collection of miserable hovels, containing 200 inhabitants.", Beth-shan, Ibleam; Bileam Dor, according to Eusebius, was situated on the Mediterranean, nine miles from Cesarea Palestine, towards Carmel.
