\subsection*{Joshua 18}
\markright{JOSHUA 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the congregation of the children of Israel were assembled at Selo, and there they pitched the tabernacle of witness; and the land was subdued by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the sons of Israel remained, [even] those who [had] not received their inheritance, seven tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joshua said to the sons of Israel, How long will you⌃ be slack to inherit the land, which the Lord our God has given you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Appoint of yourselves three men of each tribe, and let them rise up and go through the land, and let them describe it before me, as it will be proper to divide it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they came to him: and he divided to them seven portions, [saying], Juda shall stand to them a border southward, and the sons of Joseph shall stand to them northward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And do you⌃ divide the land into seven parts, and bring the description hither to me, and I will give you a lot before the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the sons of Levi have no part among you; for the priesthood of the Lord [is] his portion; and Gad, and Ruben, and the half tribe of Manasse, have received their inheritance beyond Jordan eastward, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the men rose up and went; and Joshua charged the men who went to explore the land, saying, Go and explore the land, and come to me, and I will bring you forth a lot here before the Lord in Selo. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they went, and explored the land: and they viewed it, and described it according to the cities, seven parts in a book, and brought [the book] to Joshua. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joshua cast the lot for them in Selo before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the lot of the tribe of Benjamin came forth first according to their families: and the borders of their lot came forth between the children of Juda and the children of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And their borders were northward: the borders shall go up from Jordan behind Jericho northward, and shall go up to the mountain westward, and the issue of it shall be Baethon of Mabdara. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the borders will go forth thence to Luz, behind Luz, from the south of it; this is Baethel: and the borders shall go down to Maatarob Orech, to the hill country, which is southward of Baethoron the lower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the borders shall pass through and proceed to the part that looks toward the sea, on the south, from the mountain in front of Baethoron southward, and its termination shall be at Cariath-Baal, this is Cariath-Jarin, a city of the children of Juda; this is the part toward the west. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the south side on the part of Cariath-Baal; and the borders shall go across to Gasin, to the fountain of the water of Naphtho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the borders shall extend down on one side, this is in front of the forest of Sonnam, which is on the side of Emec Raphain northward, and it shall come down to Gaeenna behind Jebusai southward: it shall come down to the fountain of Rogel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And [the borders] shall go across to the fountain of Baethsamys: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and shall proceed to Galiloth, which is in front by the going up of Aethamin; and they shall come down to the stone of Baeon of the sons of Ruben; and shall pass over behind Baetharaba northward, and shall go down to the borders behind the sea northward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the termination of the borders shall be at the creek of the salt sea northward to the side of Jordan southward: these are their southern borders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jordan shall be their boundary on the east: this [is] the inheritance of the children of Benjamin, these [are] their borders round about according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the cities of the children of Benjamin according to their families [were] Jericho, and Bethagaeo, and the Amecasis, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and Baethabara, and Sara, and Besana, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and Aeein, and Phara, and Ephratha, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and Carapha, and Cephira, and Moni, and Gabaa, twelve cities and their villages: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Gabaon, and Rama, and Beerotha; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and Massema, and Miron, and Amoke; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and Phira, and Caphan, and Nacan, and Selecan, and Thareela, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and Jebus (this is Jerusalem); and Gabaoth, Jarim, thirteen cities, and their villages; this [is] the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin according to their families.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Shiloh was situated on a hill in the tribe of Ephraim, though near the borders of Benjamin, about fifteen miles north of Jerusalem, and, according to Eusebius, twelve, or according to Jerome, ten miles (south) from Shechem or Nablous. It was but a little north from Bethel or Ai, and near the road from Shechem to Jerusalem ( ). In Jerome's time, Shiloh was ruined; and nothing remarkable was extant, but the foundations of the altar of burnt offerings which had been erected when the tabernacle stood there., set up \textsuperscript{5} Judah shall, the house Josh. 16:1-17:18 \textsuperscript{8} Go that I may here \textsuperscript{9} described The surveyors seem to have formed some kind of map of the country, as well as a description of it in writing. The Egyptians, from the situation of their fields, as annually overflowed by the Nile, acquired great skill in mensuration and land surveying; and some of the Israelites had, no doubt, learned these from them, without a knowledge of which they could not properly have divided the land. This is probably the first act of surveying on record. into seven \textsuperscript{10} cast lots; before the Lord \textsuperscript{16} the valley of the son; , ; the valley of the giants See note on .; Jebusi Mount zion, south of Jerusalem; for Jebusi or Jebus was the ancient name of that city.;, Enrogel \textsuperscript{17} Enshemesh The fountain of the Sun; whether a town, or simply a fountain, is uncertain. Geliloth is probably the same as Gilgal; though as the word may signify border or limits, some think that it is probably not the proper name of a place: "And went forth towards the borders which are over against the ascent to Adummim." Others render Geliloth circuits or roundings, or the hills about Jordan, tumuli Jordanis . Vulgate: pertransit usque ad tumulos . the stone \textsuperscript{19} bay Heb. tongue, *marg. the salt; this was the The borders of this tribe on the north were the same as those of Ephraim on the south, and his southern boundaries the same as the northern borders of Judah; but drawn from west to east, instead of from east to west (; ). As the inheritance of Benjamin did not extend to the Mediterranean sea, and no other sea or lake is known to have been in those parts, perhaps this depression, "compassed the corner of the sea southward, " ( ), should be rendered, "made a circuit on the side next the sea towards the south; " for it seems to connect the northern border, in the preceding verses, with the southern which follows. \textsuperscript{23} Ophrah Situated, according to Eusebius, five miles east of Bethel. \textsuperscript{24} Ophni Probably the same as Gophna ( ς being often pronounced as G); which, according to Josephus, was about fifteen miles from Jerusalem, towards Shechem, says Eusebius (Onom. in φαραγξ βοτρους. ) Gaba or Geba, according to Josephus, was not far from Rama, forty stadia from Jerusalem, and, according to Eusebius, five miles from Gophna, towards Shechem. \textsuperscript{25} Gibeon; Ramah Situated, according to Eusebius, six miles from Jerusalem towards Bethel; though Jerome places it near Gaba, seven miles from Jerusalem., Ramathaim-zophim, ; Arimathea Beeroth Eusebius says Beeroth was seven miles from Jerusalem, towards Nicopolis or Emmaus. Jerome, however, reads Neapolis or Shechem; but Reland prefers the former. \textsuperscript{26} Mizpeh Situated not far from Rama, forty stadia from Jerusalem. \subsection*{Joshua 19}
\markright{JOSHUA 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the second lot came out for the children of Symeon; and their inheritance was in the midst of the lots of the children of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And their lot was Beersabee, and Samaa, and Caladam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and Arsola, and Bola, and Jason, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and Erthula, and Bula, and Herma, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and Sikelac, and Baethmachereb, and Sarsusin, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and Batharoth, and their fields, thirteen cities, and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Eremmon, and Thalcha, and Jether, and Asan; four cities and their villages, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} round about their cities as far as Balec as [men] go to Bameth southward: this [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Symeon according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The inheritance of the tribe of the children of Symeon [was a part] of the lot of Juda, for the portion of the children of Juda was greater than theirs; and the children of Symeon inherited in the midst of their lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the third lot came out to Zabulon according to their families: the bounds of their inheritance shall be—Esedekgola shall be their border, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} the sea and Magelda, and it shall reach to Baetharaba in the valley, which is opposite Jekman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the border returned from Sedduc in a contrary direction eastward from Baethsamys, to the borders of Chaselothaith, and shall pass on to Dabiroth, and shall proceed upward to Phangai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And thence it shall come round in the opposite direction eastward to Gebere to the city of Catasem, and shall go on to Remmonaa Matharaoza. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the borders shall come round northward to Amoth, and their going out shall be at Gaephael, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and Catanath, and Nabaal, and Symoon, and Jericho, and Baethman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Zabulon according to their families, [these] cities and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the fourth lot came out to Issachar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And their borders were Jazel, and Chasaloth, and Sunam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and Agin, and Siona, and Reeroth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and Anachereth, and Dabiron, and Kison, and Rebes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and Remmas, and Jeon, and Tomman, and Aemarec, and Bersaphes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the boundaries shall border upon Gaethbor, and upon Salim westward, and Baethsamys; and the extremity of his bounds shall be Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the fifth lot came out to Aser according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And their borders were Exeleketh, and Aleph, and Baethok, and Keaph, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and Elimelech, and Amiel, and Maasa, and the lot will border on Carmel westward, and on Sion, and Labanath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it will return westward from Baethegeneth, and will join Zabulon and Ekgai, and Phthaeel northwards, and the borders will come to Saphthaebaethme, and Inael, and will go on to Chobamasomel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and Elbon, and Raab, and Ememaon, and Canthan to great Sidon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the borders shall turn back to Rama, and to the fountain of Masphassat, and the Tyrians; and the borders shall return to Jasiph, and their going forth shall be the sea, and Apoleb, and Echozob, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and Archob, and Aphec, and Raau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Aser according to their families, the cities and their villages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the sixth lot came out to Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And their borders were Moolam, and Mola, and Besemiin, and Arme, and Naboc, and Jephthamai, as far as Dodam; and their goings out were Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the coasts will return westward by Athabor, and will go out thence to Jacana, and will border on Zabulon southward, and Aser will join [it] westward, and Jordan eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the walled cities of the Tyrians, Tyre, and Omathadaketh, and Kenereth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} and Armaith, and Areal, and Asor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and Cades, and Assari, and the well of Asor; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} and Keroe, and Megalaarim, and Baetthame, and Thessamys. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the seventh lot came out to Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And their borders were Sarath, and Asa, and the cities of Sammaus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} and Salamin, and Ammon, and Silatha, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} and Elon, and Thamnatha, and Accaron; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} and Alcatha, and Begethon, and Gebeelan, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} and Azor, and Banaebacat, and Gethremmon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And westward of Hieracon the border [was] near to Joppa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan, according to their families, these [are] their cities and their villages: and the children of Dan did not drive out the Amorite who afflicted them in the mountain; and the Amorite would not suffer them to come down into the valley, but they forcibly took from them the border of their portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And the sons of Dan went and fought against Lachis, and took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword; and they lived in it, and called the name of it Lasendan: and the Amorite continued to dwell in Edom and in Salamin: and the hand of Ephraim prevailed against them, and they became tribute to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And they proceeded to take possession of the land according to their borders, and the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Naue among them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} by the command of God, and they gave him the city which he asked for, Thamnasarach, which is in the mount of Ephraim; and he built the city, and lived in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} These [are] the divisions which Eleazar the priest divided by lot, and Joshua the [son] of Naue, and the heads of families among the tribes of Israel, according to the lots, in Selo before the Lord by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and they went to take possession of the land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Beersheba Sheba and Moladah; Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel \textsuperscript{11} the river The river Kishon, which empties itself into the Mediterranean near mount Carmel, in the vicinity of which Jokneam was situated. Jokneam; Jokmeam \textsuperscript{12} Chislothtabor Called Chasalus by Eusebius and Jerome, and placed at the foot of mount Tabor, eight miles east of Diocesarea.; Daberath Josephus, who calls this town Dabaritta, or Darabitta, places it in the plain of Jezreel, or Esdraelon, on the confines of Samaria and Galilee. It is probably the Dabira which Jerome place towards amount Tabor, in the district of Diocesarea; and the Debora or Daboura, mentioned by travellers as a village at the foot of mount Tabor., Dabareh, Japhia Probably Japha, a city of Galilee, near Jotapata, mentioned by Josephus. \textsuperscript{13} Gittahhepher Placed by Jerome two miles from Sephoris, or Diocesarea, towards Tiberias., Gath-hepher, methoar, or, which is drawn \textsuperscript{15} Kattath etc.; . Nahalol Shimron, Bethlehem \textsuperscript{18} Jezreel; Chesulloth Probably the same as Chisloth-tabor. Shunem \textsuperscript{19} Haphraim A town called Aiphraim, in the time of Eusebius, six miles north of Legio. Shihon A town called Seon by Eusebius, at the foot of mount Tabor. \textsuperscript{24} The lot Asher lay upon the coast of the great sea. We read of only one remarkable person of this tribe, and that was Anna, the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, a widow of about four-score and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. \textsuperscript{25} Helkath Beten Probably the same as Bebeten or Batnai, mentioned by Eusebius, eight miles east from Ptolemais; and perhaps the Ecbatana which Pliny places not far from Ptolemais. Achshaph \textsuperscript{26} Misheal Situated, according to Eusebius, near mount Carmel, on the sea coast.; Marshal Carmel \textsuperscript{27} Bethdagon Zebulun Situated on the sea coast, near Ptolemais. valley Cabul Supposed to be the same town which Josephus calls Χωβουλο, and which he says was situated near the sea side, near Ptolemais. \textsuperscript{28} Rehob Kanah This seems a different Cana from that in Lower Galilee; and to be that which is placed in some maps east of Tyre, between Libanus and Antilibanus, and south of the river Cassimer, or Leitani., Cana great \textsuperscript{29} Ramah Probably the Rama mentioned by Theodoret as a city of Syria; and placed in some maps between Sarepta and Sidon, eastward, near Lebanon. Tyre Heb. Tzor; Ezek. 26:1-28:26 Achzib \textsuperscript{34} turneth Aznothtabor Apparently the same as Azanoth, which Eusebius places in the plain not far from Diocesarea or Sephoris., Judah As it is certain that the tribe of Naphtali did not border upon that of Judah, there being several tribes between, we should probably omit Judah, with the Septuagint; though it may have been a town so called. \textsuperscript{35} Hammath; Hamath Chinnereth, Chinneroth; Gennesaret \textsuperscript{38} Bethanath Eusebius mentions a town of the name of Βαταναιαν, fifteen miles from Cesarea. (Diocesarea or Sephoris probably.) Bethshemesh \textsuperscript{41} Zorah Situated on the frontiers of Dan and Judah, tens miles north from Eleutheropolis, towards Nicoplis, according to Eusebius, not far from Caphar Sorek., Zoreah, ; Irshemesh Supposed by some to be the same as Beth-shemesh in the tribe of Judah; but this latter city is evidently distinguished from it by being assigned by the tribe of Judah to the Levites ( ). Ir-shemesh rendered πολις Σαμμαυς by the LXX, seems to be the same as Emmaus or Nicopolis, 22 miles south-east from Lydda, according to the Old Jerusalem Itinerary. \textsuperscript{42} Shaalabbin Eusebius calls it Σαλαβα, and places it in Samaria, and Jerome calls it Salebi ( ), and joins it to Ajalon and Emmaus., Shaalbim Ajalon This appears to be the Ajalon which Jerome places two miles from Nicopolis or Emmaus, in the road to Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{43} Thimnathah; Timnath Ekron is placed by Eusebius between Ashdod and Jamnia, eastward; and probably the ruined village of Tookrair, mentioned by Dr. Richarson, situated on the top of a hill, and which he says seems to have been a place of considerable consequence, occupies its site. \textsuperscript{46} before or, over against Japho or, Joppa \textsuperscript{47} the coast, called Leshem, Laish\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 20}
\markright{JOSHUA 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Assign the cities of refuge, [of] which I spoke to you by Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [Even] a refuge to the slayer who has struck a man unintentionally; and the cities shall be to you a refuge, and the slayer shall not be put to death by the avenger of blood, until he have stood before the congregation for judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joshua separated Cades in Galilee in the mount Nephthali, and Sychem in the mount Ephraim, and the city of Arboc; this is Chebron, in the mountain of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And beyond Jordan he appointed Bosor in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Ruben, and Aremoth in Galaad out of the tribe of Gad, and Gaulon in the country of Basan out of the tribe of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} These [were] the cities selected for the sons of Israel, and for the stranger dwelling among them, that every one who smites a soul unintentionally should flee there, that he should not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he should stand before the congregation for judgment.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} at the entering; take that he may\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Josh 5:14; Josh 6:2; Josh 7:10; Josh 13:1-7 \textsuperscript{2} Exod 21:13-14; Num 35:6; Num 35:11-14; Deut 4:41-43; Deut 19:2-13; Rom 8:1; Rom 8:33-34; Heb 6:18-19; Num 35:15-24 \textsuperscript{4} Ruth 4:1-2; Job 5:4; Job 29:7; Prov 31:23; Jer 38:7; Ps 26:9; Heb 6:18 \textsuperscript{5} Num 35:12; Num 35:25 \textsuperscript{6} Num 35:12; Num 35:24-25; Heb 9:26\par}
\subsection*{Joshua 21}
\markright{JOSHUA 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the heads of the families of the sons of Levi drew near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the [son] of Naue, and to the heads of families of the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they spoke to them in Selo in the land of Chanaan, saying, The Lord gave commandment by Moses to give us cities to dwell in, and the country round about for our cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So the children of Israel gave to the Levites in their inheritance by the command of the Lord the cities and the country round. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the lot came out for the children of Caath; and the sons of Aaron, the priests the Levites, had by lot thirteen cities out of the tribe of Juda, and out of the tribe of Symeon, and out of the tribe of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And to the sons of Caath that were left were [given by] lot ten cities, out of the tribe of Ephraim, and out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half tribe of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the sons of Gedson had thirteen cities, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Aser, and out of the tribe of Nephthali, and out of the half tribe of Manasse in Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Merari according to their families had by lot twelve cities, out of the tribe of Ruben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities and their suburbs, as the Lord commanded Moses, by lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the tribe of the children of Juda, and the tribe of the children of Symeon, and [part] of the tribe of the children of Benjamin gave these cities, and they were assigned {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} to the sons of Aaron of the family of Caath of the sons of Levi, for the lot fell to these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they gave to them Cariatharboc the metropolis of the sons of Enac; this is Chebron in the mountain [country] of Juda, and the suburbs round it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But the lands of the city, and its villages Joshua gave to the sons of Chaleb the son of Jephonne for a possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And to the sons of Aaron he gave the city of refuge for the slayer, Chebron, and the suburbs belonging to it; and Lemna and the suburbs belonging to it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and Aelom and its suburbs; and Tema and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and Gella and its suburbs; and Dabir and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and Asa and its suburbs; and Tany and its suburbs; and Baethsamys and its suburbs: nine cities from these two tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And from the tribe of Benjamin, Gabaon and its suburbs; and Gatheth and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and Anathoth and its suburbs; and Gamala and its suburbs; four cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} All the cities of the sons of Aaron the priests, thirteen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And to the families, [even] the sons of Caath the Levites, that were left of the sons of Caath, there was [given] their priests' city, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} out of the tribe of Ephraim; and they gave them the slayer's city of refuge, Sychem, and its suburbs, and Gazara and its appendages, and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and Baethoron and its suburbs: four cities: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and the tribe of Dan, Helcothaim and its suburbs; and Gethedan and its suburbs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and Aelon and its suburbs; and Getheremmon and its suburbs: four cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And out of the half tribe of Manasse, Tanach and its suburbs; and Jebatha and its suburbs; two cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} In all [were given] ten cities, and the suburbs of each belonging to them, to the families of the sons of Caath that remained. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And [Joshua gave] to the sons of Gedson the Levites out of the other half tribe of Manasse cities set apart for the slayers, Gaulon in the country of Basan, and its suburbs; and Bosora and its suburbs; two cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kison and its suburbs; and Debba and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and Remmath and its suburbs; and the well of Letters, and its suburbs; four cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And out of the tribe of Aser, Basella and its suburbs; and Dabbon and its suburbs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and Chelcat and its suburbs; and Raab and its suburbs; four cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And of the tribe of Nephthali, the city set apart for the slayer, Cades in Galilee, and its suburbs; and Nemmath, and its suburbs; and Themmon and its suburbs; three cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} All the cities of Gedson according to their families [were] thirteen cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And to the family of the sons of Merari the Levites that remained, [he gave] out of the tribe of Zabulon, Maan and its suburbs; and Cades and its suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} and Sella and its suburbs: three cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And beyond Jordan over against Jericho, out of the tribe of Ruben, the city of refuge for the slayer, Bosor in the wilderness; Miso and its suburbs; and Jazer and its suburbs; and Decmon and its suburbs; and Mapha and its suburbs; four cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And out of the tribe of Gad the city of refuge for the slayer, both Ramoth in Galaad, and its suburbs; Camin and its suburbs; and Esbon and its suburbs; and Jazer and its suburbs: the cities [were] four in all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} All [these] cities [were given] to the sons of Merari according to the families of them that were left out of the tribe of Levi; and their limits were the twelve cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the children of Israel, [were] forty-eight cities, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} and their suburbs round about these cities: a city and the suburbs round about the city to all these cities: and Joshua ceased dividing the land by their borders: and the children of Israel gave a portion to Joshua because of the commandment of the Lord: they gave him the city which he asked: they gave him Thamnasachar in mount Ephraim; and Joshua built the city, and lived in it: and Joshua took the knives of stone, wherewith he circumcised the children of Israel that were born in the desert by the way, and put them in Thamnasachar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} So the Lord gave to Israel all the land which he swore to give to their fathers: and they inherited it, and lived in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the Lord gave them rest round about, as he swore to their fathers: not one of all their enemies maintained his ground against them; the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} There failed not one of the good things which the Lord spoke to the children of Israel; all came to pass.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} the children; the tribe These tribes furnished more habitation to the Levites, in proportion, than any of the other tribes, because they possessed a more extensive inheritance, agreeably to what Moses had commanded ( ). It is worthy of remark, that the principal part of this tribe, whose business was to minister at the sanctuary, which sanctuary was afterwards established at Jerusalem, had their appointment nearest to that city; so that they were always within reach of the sacred work which God had appointed them. \textsuperscript{8} by lot; as the Lord \textsuperscript{9} these cities; mentioned Heb. called \textsuperscript{11} And they the city of Arba or, Kirjath-arba, ; is Hebron, in the hill \textsuperscript{13} they gave Hebron a city; Libnah \textsuperscript{14} Jattir or Jether, according to Eusebius, was situated in the district of Daroma, or the southern part of Judah, 20 miles (south) from Eleutheropolis, towards the city of Malatha.; Eshtemoa Eusebius says Eshtemoa, or Esthema, was a great city in the south of Judah, and in the district of Eleutheropolis, north of that city., Eshtemoh \textsuperscript{16} Ain; Ashan Juttah Eusebius says Juttah was a great town 18 miles south from Eleutheropolis. Bethshemesh \textsuperscript{18} Anathoth was situated about three miles northward from Jerusalem according to Eusebius and Jerome (in Jer. 1:20); or twenty furlongs, according to Josephus. Ant. I. x. c. 7 sec. 3.; Almon, Alemeth \textsuperscript{23} Eltekeh Gibbethon Probably the Gabatha mentioned by Eusebius and Jerome, as situated in the south of Judah, 12 miles from Eleutheropolis, where the prophet Habakkuk's sepulchre was shown. \textsuperscript{24} Aijalon, Ajalon, Gathrimmon is said by Jerome to be a great town 10 miles from Diospolis, or Lydda, towards Eleutheropolis. \textsuperscript{25} Aner and Bileam are mentioned in Chronicles, instead of Tanach and Gath-rimmon ( ). Either the cities had at this time different names, or afterwards their names were changed; or the Levites, being by some means dispossessed of the cities first assigned them, received others from their brethren. A careful examination of the marginal references will discover other variations of this kind, which may be accounted for in the same manner. Tanach \textsuperscript{27} And unto Golan; Beeshterah It is very probable that Beesh-terah is a contraction of baith ashtaroth, "the house of Ashtaroth, " and the same as Ashtaroth, which is the reading in . \textsuperscript{29} Jarmuth This seems to be the same city with Remeth, and Ramoth, mentioned with Engannim. \textsuperscript{32} Kedesh; Hammothdor Supposed by many to be the same as Tiberias; so called from the hot-baths, as the word Chammoth may denote, in its vicinity., Hammath Kartan Supposed to be the same as Kirjathaim. \textsuperscript{35} Dimnah This and the following verse are wholly omitted by the Masora, and many Hebrew Bibles which are esteemed very highly; though, without them, neither the twelve cities of the Merarites in particular ( ), nor the forty-eight Levitical cities in general ( ), nor the six cities of refuge, can be made up. But these two verses, are thus absolutely necessary for the truth and consistency of this chapter, are happily preserved in no less than 149 manuscripts collated by Dr. Kennicott, and upwards of 40 collated by De Rossi. \textsuperscript{41} within; forty At the last census, the tribe of Levi amounted only to 23, 000 ( ); and it is thought by some that forty-eight cities was too great a proportion for this tribe. But it should be considered, that cities in ancient times were little more than villages.\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 22}
\markright{JOSHUA 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Joshua called together the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and said to them, You⌃ have heard all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and you⌃ have listened to my voice in all that he commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You⌃ have not deserted your brethren these many days: until this day you⌃ have kept the commandment of the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And now the Lord our God has given our brethren rest, as he told them: now then return and depart to your homes, and to the land of your possession, which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But take great heed to do the commands and the law, which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you to do; to love the Lord our God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commands, and to cleave to him, and serve him with all your mind, and with all your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joshua blessed them, and dismissed them; and they went to their homes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And to [one] half the tribe of Manasse Moses gave a portion in the land of Basan, and to [the other] half Joshua gave a portion with his brethren on the other side of Jordan westward: and when Joshua sent them away to their homes, then he blessed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they departed with much wealth to their houses, and they divided the spoil of their enemies with their brethren; very much cattle, and silver, and gold, and iron, and much raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse, departed from the children of Israel in Selo in the land of Chanaan, to go away into Galaad, into the land of their possession, which they inherited by the command of the Lord, by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they came to Galaad of Jordan, which is in the land of Chanaan: and the children of Ruben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to look at. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the children of Israel heard say, Behold, the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse have built an altar at the borders of the land of Chanaan at Galaad of Jordan, on the opposite side to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all the children of Israel gathered together to Selo, so as to go up and fight against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the children of Israel sent to the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and to the sons of the half tribe of Manasse into the land of Galaad, both Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and ten of the chiefs with him; [there was] one chief of every household out of all the tribes of Israel; (the heads of families are the captains of thousands in Israel.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they came to the sons of Ruben, and to the sons of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasse into the land of Galaad; and they spoke to them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus says the whole congregation of the Lord, What [is] this transgression that you⌃ have transgressed before the God of Israel, to turn away today from the Lord, in that you⌃ have built for yourselves an altar, so that you⌃ should be apostates from the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Is the sin of Phogor too little for you, whereas we have not been cleansed from it until this day, though there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you⌃ have this day revolted from the Lord; and it shall come to pass if you⌃ revolt this day from the Lord, that to-morrow there shall be wrath upon all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now if the land of your possession [be too] little, cross over to the land of the possession of the Lord, where the tabernacle of the Lord dwells, and receive you⌃ an inheritance among us; and do not become apostates from God, neither do you⌃ apostatize from the Lord, because of your having built an altar apart from the altar of the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Behold! did not Achar the [son] of Zara commit a trespass [taking] of the accursed thing, and there was wrath on the whole congregation of Israel? and he himself died alone in his own sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the sons of Ruben, and the sons of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse answered, and spoke to the captains of the thousands of Israel, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} God [even] God is the Lord, and God [even] God himself knows, and Israel he shall know; if we have transgressed before the Lord by apostasy, let him not deliver us this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And if we have built to ourselves an altar, so as to apostatize from the Lord our God, so as to offer upon it a sacrifice of whole burnt offerings, so as to offer upon it a sacrifice of peace-offering, —the Lord shall require it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But we have done this for the sake of precaution [concerning this] thing, saying, Lest hereafter your sons should say to our sons, What have you⌃ to do with the Lord God of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whereas the Lord has set boundaries between us and you, even Jordan, and you⌃ have no portion in the Lord: so your sons shall alienate our sons, that they should not worship the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And we gave orders to do thus, to build this altar, not for burnt offerings, nor for meat-offerings; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} but that this may be a witness between you and us, and between our posterity after us, that we may do service to the Lord before him, with our burnt offerings and our meat-offerings and our peace-offerings: so your sons shall not say to our sons, hereafter, You⌃ have no portion in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And we said, If ever it should come to pass that they should speak [so] to us, or to our posterity hereafter; then shall they say, Behold the likeness of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for the sake of burnt offerings, nor for the sake of meat-offerings, but it is a witness between you and us, and between our sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Far be it from us therefore that we should turn away from the Lord this day so as to apostatize from the Lord, so as that we should build an altar for burnt offerings, and for peace-offerings, besides the altar of the Lord which is before his tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Phinees the priest and all the chiefs of the congregation of Israel who were with him heard the words which the children of Ruben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse spoke; and it pleased them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Phinees the priest said to the sons of Ruben, and to the sons of Gad, and to the half of the tribe of Manasse, To-day we know that the Lord [is] with us, because you⌃ have not trespassed grievously against the Lord, and because you⌃ have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} So Phinees the priest and the princes departed from the children of Ruben, and from the children of Gad, and from the half tribe of Manasse out of Galaad into the land of Chanaan to the children of Israel; and reported the words to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it pleased the children of Israel; and they spoke to the children of Israel, and blessed the God of the children of Israel, and told them to go up no more to war against the others to destroy the land of the children of Ruben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse: so they lived upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Joshua gave a name to the altar of the children of Ruben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasse; and said, It is a testimony in the midst of them, that the Lord is their God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{5} Gk. vocab: spoudē (σπουδή) = diligence; zeal; earnestness. Common English renderings: diligence. A term for earnest effort or zeal.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Joshua; Reubenites We have already seen, that a detachment of 40, 000 men, of the tribes of Reuben and Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh, had passed over Jordan armed, with their brethren, according to their agreement with Moses. The war being now concluded, the land divided, and their brethren settled, Joshua assembles these warriors; and with commendations for their services and fidelity, he dismisses them, having fist given them the most pious and suitable instructions. They had now been about seven years absent from their respective families; and though there was only the river Jordan between the camp of Gilgal and their own inheritance, yet it does not appear that they had, during that time, ever revisited their home, which they might have done at any time of the year, except the harvest, as the river was at other times easily fordable. \textsuperscript{10} the children This verse should probably be rendered, "And when they came to the borders of Jordan, that are in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh, Then built an altar by (or beyond, al ) Jordan, a great altar to the view." It would appear, that when they came to the river, they formed the purpose of building the altar; and when they crossed it they put that purpose into execution. It is evident that they did not build it west of the Jordan, for that was not in their territories, and the next verse expressly says that it was built over against the land of Canaan. built \textsuperscript{12} the whole Supposing they had built this altar for sacrifice, in opposition to the command of God, they considered them as rebels against God and the Israelitish constitution. \textsuperscript{14} chief house Heb. house of the father an head \textsuperscript{15} the whole; trespass, ; to turn; rebel \textsuperscript{17} Is the iniquity; from which \textsuperscript{18} following; and it will he will be \textsuperscript{21} Then the children The conduct and answer of these Reubenites and the associates are worthy of admiration and imitation. Though conscious of their innocence, they permitted Phinehas to finish his speech, though composed of little else than accusations, without any interruption; and taking in good part the suspicions, reproofs, and even harshness of their brethren, with the utmost meekness and solemnity they explain their intention, give all the satisfaction in their power, and with great propriety and reverence, appeal to that God against whom they were supposed to have rebelled. answered, ; heads \textsuperscript{22} Lord God ιδεδ ΰμδιν ΰμ, El Elohim Yehowah, literally "The strong God, Elohim Jehovah, " which is nearly the version of Luther, der starke Gott, der Herr, "The strong God, the Lord.";, ; he knoweth; Israel; if it be \textsuperscript{24} for fear In time to come Heb. To-morrow; *marg. \textsuperscript{30} it pleased them Heb. it was good in their eyes, It is remarkable, that Joshua is not once named in this transaction; but this only shews, that he did not in his old age assume any regal authority, but left the elders and magistrates to conduct the general business, only acting himself when great occasions made it necessary. Yet we cannot doubt, that his wisdom and piety influenced the counsels of the elders and people at this time.; *marg. \textsuperscript{31} the Lord is; now Heb. then \textsuperscript{34} Ed i.e. a witness, The word witness, or testimony, is not found in the common editions of the Hebrew Bible; and is supplied in Italics by our venerable translators, at least in our modern copies; for in the first edition of this translation, it stands in the text without any note of this kind; but it is found in several of Kennicott's and De Rossi's manuscripts, and also in the Syriac and Arabic. Several also of the early printed editions of the Hebrew Bible have the word ed, either in the text or in the margin; and it must be allowed to be necessary to complete the sense. It is very probable that an inscription was put on this altar, signifying the purpose for which it was erected. Thus was this affair most happily terminated.; the Lord is God Several manuscripts read more emphatically, ΰμδιν δεΰ ιδεδ, Yehowah, hoo Elohim, "Jehovah he is God."\par}

\subsection*{Joshua 23}
\markright{JOSHUA 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after many days after the Lord had given Israel rest from all his enemies round about, that Joshua was old and advanced in years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joshua called together all the children of Israel, and their elders, and their chiefs, and their judges, and their officers; and said to them, I am old and advanced in years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you⌃ have seen all that the Lord our God has done to all these nations before us; [for it] is the Lord your God who has fought for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} See, that I have given to you these nations that are left to you by lots to your tribes, all the nations beginning at Jordan; and [some] I have destroyed; and the boundaries shall be at the great sea westward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord our God, he shall destroy them before us, until they utterly perish; and he shall send against them the wild beasts, until he shall have utterly destroyed them and their kings from before you; and you⌃ shall inherit their land, as the Lord our God said to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Do you⌃ therefore strive diligently to observe and do all things written in the book of the law of Moses, that you⌃ turn not to the right hand or to the left; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} that you⌃ go not in among these nations that are left; and the names of their gods shall not be named among you, neither shall you⌃ serve them, neither shall you⌃ bow down to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But you⌃ shall cleave to the Lord our God, as you⌃ have done until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord shall destroy them before you, [even] great and strong nations; and no one has stood before us until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} One of you has chased a thousand, for the Lord our God, he fought for you, as he said to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And take you⌃ great heed to love the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For if you⌃ shall turn aside and attach yourselves to these nations that are left with you, and make marriages with them, and become mingled with them and they with you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} know that the Lord will no more destroy these nations from before you; and they will be to you snares and stumbling blocks, and nails in your heels, and darts in your eyes, until you⌃ be destroyed from off this good land, which the Lord your God has given you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But I hasten to go the way [of death], as all that are upon the earth also [do]: and you⌃ know in your heart and in your soul, that not one word has fallen [to the ground] of all the words which the Lord our God has spoken respecting all that concerns us; there has not one of them failed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it shall come to pass, that as all the good things are come upon us which the Lord God will bring upon you all the evil things, until he shall have destroyed you from off this good land, which the Lord has given you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} when you⌃ transgress the covenant of the Lord our God, which he has charged us, and go and serve other gods, and bow down to them.\par

\subsection*{Joshua 24}
\markright{JOSHUA 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joshua gathered all the tribe of Israel to Selo, and convoked their elders, and their officers, and their judges, and set them before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joshua said to all the people, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, Your fathers at first sojourned beyond the river, [even] Thara, the father of Abraam and the father of Nachor; and they served other gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I took your father Abraam from the other side of the river, and I guided him through all the land, and I multiplied his seed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and I gave to him Isaac, and to Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I gave to Esau mount Seir for him to inherit: and Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt, and became there a great and populous and mighty nation: and the Egyptians afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I struck Egypt with the wonders that I wrought among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And afterwards [God] brought out our fathers from Egypt, and you⌃ entered into the Red Sea; and the Egyptians pursued after our fathers with chariots and horses into the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And we cried aloud to the Lord; and he put a cloud and darkness between us and the Egyptians, and he brought the sea upon them, and covered them; and your eyes have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt; and you⌃ were in the wilderness many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he brought us into the land of the Amorites that lived beyond Jordan, and the Lord delivered them into our hands; and you⌃ inherited their land, and utterly destroyed them from before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Balac, king of Moab, son of Sepphor, rose up, and made war against Israel, and sent and called Balaam to curse us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But the Lord your God would not destroy you; and he greatly blessed us, and rescued us out of their hands, and delivered them [to us]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you⌃ crossed over Jordan, and came to Jericho; and the inhabitants of Jericho fought against us, the Amorite, and the Chananite, and the Pherezite, and the Evite, and the Jebusite, and the Chettite, and the Gergesite, and the Lord delivered them into our hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he sent forth the hornet before you; and he drove them out from before you, [even] twelve kings of the Amorites, not with your sword, nor with your bow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he gave you a land on which you⌃ did not labor, and cities which you⌃ did not build, and you⌃ were settled in them; and you⌃ eat [of] vineyards and olive yards which you⌃ did not plant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And now fear the Lord, and serve him in righteousness and justice; and remove the strange gods, which our fathers served beyond the river, and in Egypt; and serve the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if it seem not good to you to serve the Lord, choose to yourselves this day whom you⌃ will serve, whether the gods of your fathers that were on the other side of the river, or the gods of the Amorites, among whom you⌃ dwell upon their land: but I and my house will serve the Lord, for he is holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the people answered and said, Far be it from us to forsake the Lord, so as to serve other gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The Lord our God, he is God; he brought up us and our fathers from Egypt, and kept us in all the way wherein we walked, and among all the nations through whom we passed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord cast out the Amorite, and all the nations that inhabited the land from before us: yes, we will serve the Lord, for he is our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Joshua said to the people, Indeed you⌃ will not be able to serve the Lord, for God is holy; and he being jealous will not forgive your sins and your transgressions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whenever you⌃ shall forsake the Lord and serve other gods, then he shall come upon you and afflict you, and consume you, because he has done you good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the people said to Joshua, Nay, but we will serve the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joshua said to the people, You⌃ [are] witnesses against yourselves, that you⌃ have chosen the Lord to serve him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now take away the strange gods that are among you, and set your heart right toward the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the people said to Joshua, We will serve the Lord, and we will listen to his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day, and gave them a law and an ordinance in Selo before the tabernacle of the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he wrote these words in the book of the laws of God: and Joshua took a great stone, and set it up under the oak before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Joshua said to the people, Behold, this stone shall be among you for a witness, for it has heard all the words that have been spoken to it by the Lord; for he has spoken to you this day; and this [stone] shall be among you for a witness in the last days, whenever you⌃ shall deal falsely with the Lord my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Joshua dismissed the people, and they went every man to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it came to pass after these things that Joshua the son of Naue the servant of the Lord died, [at the age] of one hundred and ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And they buried him by the borders of his inheritance in Thamnasarach in the mount of Ephraim, northward of the mount of Galaad: there they put with him into the tomb in which they buried him, the knives of stone with which he circumcised the children of Israel in Galgala, when he brought them out of Egypt, as the Lord appointed them; and there they are to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that lived as long as Joshua, and all that knew all the works of the Lord which he wrought for Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the children of Israel brought up the bones of Joseph out of Egypt, and buried [them] in Sicima, in the portion of the land which Jacob bought of the Amorites who lived in Sicima for one hundred ewe-lambs; and he gave it to Joseph for a portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it came to pass afterwards that Eleazar the high-priest the son of Aaron died, and was buried in Gabaar of Phinees his son, which he gave him in mount Ephraim. In that day the children of Israel took the ark of God, and carried it about among them; and Phinees exercised the priest's office in the room of Eleazar his father till he died, and he was buried in his own place Gabaar: but the children of Israel departed every one to their place, and to their own city: and the children of Israel worshipped Astarte, and Astaroth, and the gods of the nations round about them; and the Lord delivered them into the hands of Eglom king of Moab and he ruled over them eighteen years.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Joshua This must have been a different assembly from that mentioned in the preceding chapter, though probably held not long after the former. Shechem As it is immediately added, that "they presented themselves before God, " which is supposed to mean at the tabernacle; some are of opinion that Joshua caused it to be conveyed from Shiloh to Shechem on this occasion, to give the greater solemnity to his last meeting with the people. The Vatican and Alexandrian copies of the Septuagint, however, read Σηλω, both here and in; which many suppose to have been the original reading. Dr. Shuckford supposes that the covenant was made at Shechem, and that the people went to Shiloh to confirm it. But the most probable opinion seems to be that of Dr. Kennicott, that when all the tribes were assembled as Shechem, Joshua called the chiefs to him on that mount, which had before been consecrated by the law, and by the altar which he had erected., ; called; presented \textsuperscript{2} Your fathers, ; served other gods In the case of Abraham this was probably the case, till he was called to the knowledge of God, when above 70 years old. \textsuperscript{4} unto Isaac unto Esau; Jacob \textsuperscript{7} And when he put brought your eyes; ye dwelt \textsuperscript{14} fear; serve; put From this exhortation of Joshua, we not only learn that the Israelites still retained some relics of idolatry, but to what gods they were attached. 1. Those whom their fathers worshipped on the other side of the food, or the river Euphrates, i.e., the gods of the Chaldeans, fire, light, the sun, etc. 2. \section*{Judges Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Samuel (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Jewish and Christian tradition often ascribes Judges to Samuel; the recurring refrain fits an early-monarchy perspective looking back on the pre-kingdom period.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the human writer, but Judges is received as truthful sacred history within the same covenant-historical stream Christ and the apostles endorse.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} early monarchy\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} likely ca. 11th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology presents Judges as the era between Joshua and Samuel/Saul, though exact lengths within the book are debated.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The LXX preserves the same judges-era framework while differing from the MT in various details and some plus/minus readings.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} The unsettled tribal era between Joshua and the rise of the monarchy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To show Israel's cycle of apostasy, oppression, crying out, and deliverance, and the need for righteous covenant leadership.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} apostasy; deliverance; covenant discipline; tribal disorder; need for godly rule\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Introduction and incomplete conquest 1-3; Major judges 3-16; Epilogue of social and cultic disorder 17-21. 1Q Judges a (1Q6) and 4Q Judges fragments | Subst. before 68 BC Early Qumran Judges manuscripts preserve portions of the book in Hebrew | Heb. Hasmonean-Herodian periods Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus preserve Judges in Greek\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Retelling of judges-era history (Josephus)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1st century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Judges contains significant textual variation in a number of scenes, and the LXX can preserve readings useful for evaluating difficult MT passages.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Judges 1}
\markright{JUDGES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after the death of Joshua, that the children of Israel enquired of the Lord, saying, Who shall go up for us first against the Chananites, to fight against them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said, Judas shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Judas said to his brother Symeon, Come up with me into my lot, and let us array ourselves against the Chananites, and I also will go with you into your lot: and Symeon went with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Judas went up; and the Lord delivered the Chananite and the Pherezite into their hands, and they struck them in Bezek to [the number of] ten thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they overtook Adonibezek in Bezek, and fought against him; and they struck the Chananite and the Pherezite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Adonibezek fled, and they pursued after him, and took him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Adonibezek said, Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered [their food] under my table: as I therefore have done, so God has recompensed me: and they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Judas fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and struck with the edge of the sword, and they burnt the city with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And afterwards the children of Judas went down to fight with the Chananite dwelling in the hill country, and the south, and the plain country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Judas went to the Chananite who lived in Chebron; and Chebron came out against him; [and the name of Chebron before was Cariatharbocsepher:] and they struck Sessi, and Achiman, and Tholmi, children of Enac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they went up thence to the inhabitants of Dabir; but the name of Dabir was before Cariathsepher, the city of Letters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Chaleb said, Whosoever shall strike the city of Letters, and shall first take it, I will give to him Ascha my daughter to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gothoniel the younger son of Kenez the brother of Chaleb took it; and Chaleb gave him his daughter Ascha to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it came to pass as she went in, that Gothoniel urged her to ask a field of her father; and she murmured and cried from off her ass, You have sent me forth into a south land: and Chaleb said to her, What is your request? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Ascha said to him, Give me, I pray you, a blessing, for you have sent me forth into a south land, and you shall give me the ransom of water: and Chaleb gave her according to her heart the ransom of the upper [springs] and the ransom of the low [springs]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the children of Jothor the Kenite the father-in-law of Moses went up from the city of palm-trees with the children of Judas, to the wilderness that is in the south of Juda, which is at the descent of Arad, and they lived with the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Judas went with Symeon his brother, and struck the Chananite that inhabited Sepheth, and they utterly destroyed them; and they called the name of the city Anathema. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But Judas did not inherit Gaza nor her coasts, nor Ascalon nor her coasts, nor Accaron nor her coasts, [nor] Azotus nor the lands around it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord was with Judas, and he inherited the mountain; for they were not able to destroy the inhabitants of the valley, for Rechab prevented them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they gave Chebron to Chaleb, as Moses said; and thence he inherited the three cities of the children of Enac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But the children of Benjamin did not take the inheritance of the Jebusite who lived in Jerusalem; and the Jebusite lived with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the sons of Joseph, they also went up to Baethel; and the Lord was with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they encamped and surveyed Baethel: and the name of the city before was Luza. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the spies looked, and behold, a man went out of the city, and they took him; and they said to him, Show us the way into the city, and we will deal mercifully with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he showed them the way into the city; and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but they let go the man and his family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the man went into the land of Chettin, and built there a city, and called the name of it Luza; this [is] its name until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Manasse did not drive out [the inhabitants of] Baethsan, which is a city of Scythians, nor her towns, nor her suburbs; nor Thanac, nor her towns; nor the inhabitants of Dor, nor her suburbs, nor her towns; nor the inhabitant of Balac, nor her suburbs, nor her towns; nor the inhabitants of Magedo, nor her suburbs, nor her towns; nor the inhabitants of Jeblaam, nor her suburbs, nor her towns; and the Chananite began to dwell in this land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it came to pass when Israel was strong, that he made the Chananite tributary, but did not utterly drive them out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Ephraim did not drive out the Chananite that lived in Gazer; and the Chananite lived in the midst of him in Gazer, and became tributary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Zabulon did not drive out the inhabitants of Kedron, nor the inhabitants of Domana: and the Chananite lived in the midst of them, and became tributary to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Aser did not drive out the inhabitants of Accho, and [that people] became tributary to him, nor the inhabitants of Dor, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor the inhabitants of Dalaph, nor Aschazi, nor Chebda, nor Nai, nor Ereo. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Aser lived in the midst of the Chananite who inhabited the land, for he could not drive him out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Nephthali did not drive out the inhabitants of Baethsamys, nor the inhabitants of Baethanach; and Nephthali lived in the midst of the Chananite who inhabited the land: but the inhabitants of Bethsamys and of Baetheneth became tributary to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the Amorite drove out the children of Dan into the mountains, for they did not suffer them to come down into the valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Amorite began to dwell in the mountain of shells, in which [are] bears, and foxes, in Myrsinon, and in Thalabin; and the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy upon the Amorite, and he became tributary to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the border of the Amorite [was] from the going up of Acrabin, from the rock and upwards.\par
