\subsection*{Judges 2}
\markright{JUDGES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And an angel of the Lord went up from Galgal to the [place of] weeping, and to Baethel, and to the house of Israel, and said to them, Thus says the Lord, I brought you up out of Egypt, and I brought you into the land which I swore to your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant that I have made with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you⌃ shall make no covenant with them that dwell in this land, neither shall you⌃ worship their gods; but you⌃ shall destroy their graven images, you⌃ shall pull down their altars: but you⌃ listened not to my voice, for you⌃ did these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I said, I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be for a distress to you, and their gods shall be to you for an offense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass when the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they named the name of that place Weepings; and they sacrificed there to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joshua dismissed the people, and they went every man to his inheritance, to inherit the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the people served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that lived many days with Joshua, as many as knew all the great work of the Lord, what things he had wrought in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Joshua the son of Naue, the servant of the Lord, died, one hundred and ten years old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they buried him in the border of his inheritance, in Thamnathares, in mount Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all that generation were laid to their fathers: and another generation rose up after them, who knew not the Lord, nor yet the work which he wrought in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the children of Israel wrought evil before the Lord, and served Baalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and walked after other gods, of the gods of the nations round about them; and they worshipped them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they provoked the Lord, and forsook him, and served Baal and the Astartes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel; and he gave them into the hands of the spoilers, and they spoiled them; and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, and they could not any longer resist their enemies, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} among whoever they went; and the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord spoke, and as the Lord swore to them; and he greatly afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Lord raised up judges, and the Lord save them out of the hands of them that spoiled them: and yet they listened not to the judges, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} for they went a whoring after other gods, and worshipped them; and they turned quickly out of the way in which their fathers walked to listen to the words of the Lord; they did not so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And because the Lord raised them up judges, so the Lord was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the Lord was moved at their groaning by reason of them that besieged them and afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass when the judge died, that they went back, and again corrupted [themselves] worse than their fathers to go after other gods to serve them and to worship them: they abandoned not their devices nor their stubborn ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and said, Forasmuch as this nation has forsaken my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not listened to my voice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} therefore I will not any more cast out a man of the nations before their face, which Joshua the son of Naue left in the land. And [the Lord] left [them], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} to prove Israel with them, whether they would keep the way of the Lord, to walk in it, as their fathers kept it, or no. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So the Lord will leave these nations, so as not to cast them out suddenly; and he delivered them not into the hand of Joshua.\par

\subsection*{Judges 3}
\markright{JUDGES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the nations which the Lord left to prove Israel with them, all that had not known the wars of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Only for the sake of the generations of Israel, to teach them war, only the men before them knew them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The five lordships of the Phylistines, and every Chananite, and the Sidonian, and the Evite who lived in Libanus from the mount of Aermon to Laboemath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [this] was done in order to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would obey the commands of the Lord, which he charged their fathers by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the children of Israel lived in the midst of the Chananite, and the Chettite, and the Amorite, and the Pherezite, and the Evite, and the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they took their daughters for wives to themselves, and they gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgot the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and sold them into the hand of Chusarsathaim king of Syria of the rivers: and the children of Israel served Chusarsathaim eight years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the children of Israel cried to the Lord; and the Lord raised up a savior to Israel, and he saved them, Gothoniel the son of Kenez, the brother of Chaleb younger than himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war against Chusarsathaim: and the Lord delivered into his hand Chusarsathaim king of Syria of the rivers, and his hand prevailed against Chusarsathaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the land was quiet forty years; and Gothoniel the son of Kenez died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the children of Israel continued to do evil before the Lord: and the Lord strengthened Eglom king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he gathered to himself all the children of Ammon and Amalec, and went and struck Israel, and took possession of the city of Palm-trees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the children of Israel served Eglom the king of Moab eighteen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the children of Israel cried to the Lord; and he raised up to them a savior, Aod the son of Gera a son of Jemeni, a man who used both hands alike: and the children of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglom king of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Aod made himself a dagger of two edges, of a span long, and he girded it under his cloak upon his right thigh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he went, and brought the presents to Eglom king of Moab, and Eglom [was] a very handsome man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass when [Aod] had made an end of offering his gifts, that he dismissed those that brought the gifts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he himself returned from the quarries that are by Galgal; and Aod said, I have a secret errand to you, O king! and Eglom said to him, Be silent: and he sent away from his presence all who waited upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Aod went in to him; and he sat in his own upper summer chamber quite alone; and Aod said, I have a message from God to you, O king: and Eglom rose up from his throne near him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass as he arose, that Aod stretched forth his left hand, and took the dagger off his right thigh, and plunged it into his belly; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and drove in also the haft after the blade, and the fat closed in upon the blade, for he drew not out the dagger from his belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Aod went out to the porch, and passed out by the appointed [guards], and shut the doors of the chamber upon him, and locked [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he went out: and Eglom's servants came, and saw, and behold, the doors of the upper chamber [were] locked; and they said, Does he not uncover his feet in the summer-chamber? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they waited till they were ashamed, and, behold, there was no one that opened the doors of the upper chamber; and they took the key, and opened them; and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Aod escaped while they were in a tumult, and no one paid attention to him; and he passed the quarries, and escaped to Setirotha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass when Aod came into the land of Israel, that he blew the horn in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came down with him from the mountain, and he [was] before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he said to them, Come down after me, for the Lord God has delivered our enemies, even Moab, into our hand; and they went down after him, and seized on the fords of Jordan before Moab, and he did not suffer a man to pass over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they struck Moab on that day about ten thousand men, every [lusty] person and every mighty man; and not a man escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So Moab was humbled in that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years; and Aod judged them till he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And after him rose up Samegar the son of Dinach, and struck the Philistines to the number of six hundred men with a plowshare [such as is drawn by] oxen; and he too delivered Israel.\par

Aram \textsuperscript{12} am 2662, bc 1342, An, Ex, Is, 148 did evil; and the Lord; the king \textsuperscript{15} am 2679, bc 1325, An, Ex, Is, 166 cried unto; a Benjamite or, the son of Jemini lefthanded Heb. shut of his right hand, This Hebrew phrase intimates that, either through disease or disuse, he made little or no use of the right hand, but of his left only, and so was the less fit for war, because he would most likely wield a dagger awkwardly. Yet God chose this left-handed man to be the minister of his retributive justice. It was God's right hand that gained Israel the victory; not the right hand of the instruments he employed.; sent a present \textsuperscript{19} quarries or graven images, a secret; And all that \textsuperscript{20} a summer parlour Heb. a parlour of cooling, The aleeyah, or upper chamber, seems to have been of the same description as the oleah of the Arabs, but properly ventilated, described by Dr. Shaw, who says, that to most of their houses there is a smaller one annexed, which sometimes rises one story higher than the house; at other times, it consists of one or two rooms only, and a terrace; while others that are built, as they frequently are, over the porch or gateway, have, if we except the ground floor, which they want, all the conveniences that belong to the house itself. There is a door of communication from them into the gallery of the house; besides another, which opens immediately from a private staircase, down into the porch or street, without giving the least disturbance to the house. In these back houses strangers are usually lodged and entertained; and to them likewise the men are wont to retire from the noise and hurry of their families, to be more at leisure for mediation or diversions. He measured several, and "found them about eight feet long; and at the bigger end about six inches in circumference. They were armed at the lesser end with a sharp prickle for driving the oxen; and at the other end with a small paddle of iron, strong and massive, for cleansing the plough from the clay. In the hand of a powerful man such an instrument must be more dangerous and fatal than a sword."; also Israel "So part is called Israel.", ; "It seems to concern only the country next to the Philistines."\par}

\subsection*{Judges 4}
\markright{JUDGES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the children of Israel continued to do evil against the Lord; and Aod was dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord sold the children of Israel into the hand of Jabin king of Chanaan, who ruled in Asor; and the chief of his host was Sisara, and he lived in Arisoth of the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the children of Israel cried to the Lord, because he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and he mightily oppressed Israel twenty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Debbora, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, —she judged Israel at that time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she sat under the palm tree of Debbora between Rama and Baethel in mount Ephraim; and the children of Israel went up to her for judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Debbora sent and called Barac the son of Abineem out of Cades Nephthali, and she said to him, Has not the Lord God of Israel commanded you? and you shall depart to mount Thabor, and shall take with yourself ten thousand men of the sons of Nephthali and of the sons of Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I will bring to you to the torrent of Kison Sisara the captain of the host of Jabin, and his chariots, and his multitude, and I will deliver them into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Barac said to her, If you will go with me, I will go; and if you will not go, I will not go; for I know not the day on which the Lord prospers his messenger with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And she said, I will surely go with you; but know that your honor shall not attend on the expedition on which you go, for the Lord shall sell Sisara into the hands of a women: and Debbora arose, and went with Barac out of Cades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Barac called Zabulon and Nephthali out of Cades, and there went up at his feet ten thousand men, and Debbora went up with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Chaber the Kenite had removed from Caina, from the sons of Jobab the father-in-law of Moses, and pitched his tent by the oak of the covetous ones, which is near Kedes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it was told Sisara that Barac the son of Abineem was gone up to mount Thabor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Sisara summoned all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron and all the people with him, from Arisoth of the Gentiles to the brook of Kison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Debbora said to Barac, Rise up, for this [is] the day on which the Lord has delivered Sisara into your hand, for the Lord shall go forth before you: and Barac went down from mount Thabor, and ten thousand men after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord discomfited Sisara, and all his chariots, and all his army, with the edge of the sword before Barac: and Sisara descended from off his chariot, and fled on his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Barac pursued after the chariots and after the army, into Arisoth of the Gentiles; and the whole army of Sisara fell by the edge of the sword, there was not one left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Sisara fled on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Chaber the Kenite his friend: for there was peace between Jabin king of Asor and the house of Chaber the Kenite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jael went, out to meet Sisara, and said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me, fear not: and he turned aside to her into the tent; and she covered him with a mantle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Sisara said to her, Give me, I pray you, a little water to drink, for I am thirsty: and she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him to drink, and covered him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Sisara said to her, Stand now by the door of the tent, and it shall come to pass if any man come to you, and ask of you, and say, Is there [any] man here? then you shall say, There is not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Jael the wife of Chaber took a pin of the tent, and took a hammer in her hand, and went secretly to him, and fastened the pin in his temple, and it went through to the earth, and he fainted away, and darkness fell upon him and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And, behold, Barac [was] pursuing Sisara: and Jael went out to meet him, and she said to him, Come, and I will show you the man whom you seek: and he went in to her; and, behold, Sisara was fallen dead, and the pin [was] in his temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So God routed Jabin king of Chanaan in that day before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin king of Chanaan, until they utterly destroyed Jabin king of Chanaan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2699, bc 1305, An, Ex, Is, 186 did evil \textsuperscript{2} sold; "It seems to concern only north Israel." Hazor, Sisera; Harosheth \textsuperscript{4} am 2719, bc 1285, An, Ex, Is, 206 \textsuperscript{5} the palm between, ;, ; came up \textsuperscript{6} Barak; Kedeshnaphtali, Hath; Tabor; ten thousand \textsuperscript{11} Heber; Hobab, Zaanaim, Zaanannim Kedesh \textsuperscript{13} gathered Heb. gathered by cry, or proclamation nine, chariots of iron Probably chariots armed with iron scythes, projecting from the axle on each side, by which the infantry might be easily cut down or thrown into confusion. The ancient Britons are said to have had such chariots. \textsuperscript{14} Up; for this This is exactly the purpose for which the Septuagint states, that Barak wished Deborah to accompany him: "Because I know not the day in which God will send his angel to give me prosperity." is not; mount Mount Tabor, called by the Arabs Djebel Tour, is almost entirely insulated, and rises up in the plain of Esdraelon, about six miles from Nazareth, in a conical form, somewhat like a sugar-loaf. Josephus states its height to be thirty stadia, with a plain of 26 stadia in circumference on its top, on which was formerly a city, which was used as a military post. It is described as an exceedingly beautiful mountain, having a rich soil, producing excellent herbage, and adorned with groves and clumps of trees. \textsuperscript{16} pursued; there a man left Heb. unto one \textsuperscript{18} Jael mantle or, rug, or blanket \textsuperscript{21} took, ; a nail One of the spikes of the tent. \subsection*{Judges 5}
\markright{JUDGES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Debbora and Barac son of Abineem sang in that day, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A revelation was made in Israel when the people were made willing: Praise you⌃ the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Hear, you⌃ kings, and listen, rulers: I will sing, it is I [who will sing] to the Lord, it is I, I will sing a psalm to the Lord the god of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O Lord, in your going forth on Seir, when you went forth out of the land of Edom, the earth quaked and the heaven dropped dews, and the clouds dropped water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The mountains were shaken before the face of the Lord Eloi, this Sina before the face of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In the days of Samegar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, they deserted the ways, and went in by-ways; they went in crooked paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The mighty men in Israel failed, they failed until Debbora arose, until she arose a mother in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They chose new gods; then the cities of rulers fought; there was not a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} My heart [inclines] to the orders given in Israel; you⌃ that are willing among the people, bless the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You⌃ that mount a she-ass at noon-day, you⌃ that sit on the judgment-seat, and walk by the roads of them that sit in judgment by the way; declare {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [you⌃ that are delivered] from the noise of disturbers among the drawers of water; there shall they relate righteous acts: O Lord, increase righteous acts in Israel: then the people of the Lord went down to the cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Awake, awake, Debbora; awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barac, and lead your captivity captive, son of Abineem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then went down the remnant to the strong, the people of the Lord went down for him among the mighty ones from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Ephraim rooted them out in Amalec, behind you was Benjamin among your people: the inhabitants of Machir came down with me searching out the enemy, and from Zabulon came they that draw with the scribe's pen of record. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And princes in Issachar were with Debbora and Barac, thus she sent Barac on his feet in the valleys into the portions of Ruben; great [pangs] reached to the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Why did they sit between the sheepfolds to hear the bleating of flocks for the divisions of Ruben? [there were] great searchings of heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Galaad [is] on the other side of Jordan where he pitched his tents; and why does Dan remain in ships? Aser sat down on the sea-coasts, and he will tabernacle at his ports. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The people Zabulon exposed their soul to death, and Nephthali came to the high places of their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Kings set themselves in array, then the kings of Chanaan fought in Thanaach at the water of Mageddo; they took no gift of money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The stars from heaven set themselves in array, they set themselves [to fight] with Sisara out of their paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The brook of Kison swept them away, the ancient brook, the brook Kison: my mighty soul will trample him down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} When the hoofs of the horse were entangled, his mighty ones earnestly hasted {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} to curse Meroz: Curse you⌃ [it], said the angel of the Lord; cursed [is] every one that dwells in it, because they came not to the help of the Lord, to his help among the mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Blessed among women be Jael wife of Chaber the Kenite; let her be blessed above women in tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He asked for water, she gave him milk in a dish; she brought butter of princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} She stretched forth her left hand to the nail, and her right to the hand workman's hammer, and she struck Sisara with it, she nailed through his head and struck him; she nailed through his temples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He rolled down between her feet; he fell and lay between her feet; he bowed and fell: where he bowed, there he fell dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The mother of Sisara looked down through the window out of the loophole, [saying], Why was his chariot ashamed? why did the wheels of his chariots wait? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Her wise ladies answered her, and she returned answers to herself, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Will they not find him dividing the spoil? he will surely be gracious to every man: [there are] spoils of dyed garments for Sisara, spoils of various dyed garments, dyed embroidered garments, they [are] the spoils for his neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Thus let all your enemies perish, O Lord: and they that love him shall be as the going forth of the sun in his strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the land had rest forty years.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Heb. vocab: zamar (זָמַר) = to sing praise; make music. Common English renderings: sing praise. Music and praise term used especially in poetry.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Sang Deborah This verse briefly recites the subject of this inspired song, which consists of eight stanzas: The first opens with a devout thanksgiving. The second describes the magnificent scenes at Mount Sinai, etc. The third states the apostasy and consequent punishment of the Israelites. The fourth contrasts their present happy state. The fifth censures the recreant tribes of Reuben, Gad, etc. The sixth records the defeat of the confederate kings of Canaan. The seventh contains a panegyric on Jael. And the eight describes the fond anticipations and disappointment of the mother of Sisera.; *title \textsuperscript{3} O ye kings;, even I \textsuperscript{5} mountains; melted Heb. flowed that Sinai \textsuperscript{6} Shamgar Jael the highways; travellers Heb. walkers of paths byways Heb. crooked ways \textsuperscript{10} Speak or, Meditate, ride, ye that sit \textsuperscript{11} the noise, in the places Dr. Shaw mentions a beautiful rill of water in Barbary, which runs into a large bason, called shrub we krub, "drink and be off, " because of the danger of meeting with robbers and assassins in this place, who fall upon those who come to drink.; righteous acts Heb. righteousnesses; villages go down \textsuperscript{14} of Ephraim, Amalek; after, Machir handle the pen Heb. draw with the pen \textsuperscript{15} the princes Barak, foot Heb. his feet, Beraglaiv, rather, "with his footmen, " so LXX Alex. πεζους αυτου, and Luther, mit feinem Fubvolt . For the or, In the divisions, etc. thoughts Heb. impressions \textsuperscript{16} sheepfolds; For or, In, *marg. great \textsuperscript{17} Gilead, Asher sea shore or, sea-port breaches or, creeks \textsuperscript{18} Zebulun jeoparded Heb. exposed to reproach. their lives; in the high \textsuperscript{20} fought; the stars courses Heb. paths \textsuperscript{22} horsehoofs Anciently, horses were not shod; nor are they at the present day in some parts of the East. The flight was so rapid that the hoofs of their horses were splintered and broken by the roughness of the roads; in consequence of which they became lame, and could not carry off their riders., ; prancings or, tramplings, or, plungings mighty ones Or, as Dr. Waterland renders, "mighty horses, " or "strong steeds, " as Dr. Kennicott, i.e., their war-horses, which gives great energy to the text, and renders it perfectly intelligible. \textsuperscript{23} Curse ye; Meroz This city of Meroz seems to have been, at this time, a place of considerable importance, since something great was expected from it; but probably, after the angel of the Lord had pronounced this curse, it dwindled and like the fig-tree which Christ cursed, withered away; so that we never read of it after this in Scripture. the angel, ; they came; to the help \textsuperscript{25} asked butter Chemah, may signify buttermilk, which is made by the Arabs by agitating the milk in a leathern bag; and is highly esteemed because of its refreshing and cooling qualities. \textsuperscript{26} with the Heb. She hammered she smote off Or rather, "she smote his head, then she struck through and pierced his temples:" which is more consonant to the original, and to fact, as it does not appear that she smote off his head. \textsuperscript{27} At Heb. Between where; dead Heb. destroyed \textsuperscript{30} Have they not sped; every man Heb. the head of a man of divers \textsuperscript{31} So let, ; them that; the sun; And the land The victory here celebrated in this song, was of such happy consequence to Israel, that for the principal part of one age, they enjoyed the peace to which it had been the means of opening the way. The land had rest forty years, that is, so long it was from this victory to the raising up of Gideon. And well would it have been for the Israelites, if while the tribes had rest, they had taken advantage of the cessation from war, and had walked in the fear of the Lord.\par}

\subsection*{Judges 6}
\markright{JUDGES 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of Madiam seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the hand of Madiam prevailed against Israel: and the children of Israel made for themselves because of Madiam the caves in the mountains, and the dens, and the holes in the rocks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass when the children of Israel sowed, that Madiam and Amalec went up, and the children of the east went up together with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they encamped against them, and destroyed their fruits until they came to Gaza; and they left not the support of life in the land of Israel, not even ox or ass among the herds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For they and their stock came up, and their tents were with them, as the locust in multitude, and there was no number to them and their camels; and they came to the land of Israel, and laid it waste. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Israel was greatly impoverished because of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the children of Israel cried to the Lord because of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord sent a prophet to the children of Israel; and he said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I am he that brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and I brought you up out of the house of your bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I delivered you out of the hand of Egypt, and out of the hand of all that afflicted you, and I cast them out before you; and I gave you their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I said to you, I [am] the Lord your God: you⌃ shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you⌃ dwell; but you⌃ listened not to my voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And an angel of the Lord came, and sat down under the fir tree, which was in Ephratha in the land of Joas father of Esdri; and Gedeon his son [was] threshing wheat in a wine-press in order to escape from the face of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said to him, The Lord [is] with you, you mighty in strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gedeon said to him, [Be gracious] with me, my Lord: but if the Lord is with us, why have these evils found us? and where are all his miracles, which our fathers have related to us, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt? and now he has cast us out, and given us into the hand of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the angel of the Lord turned to him, and said, Go in this your strength, and you shall save Israel out of the hand of Madiam: behold, I have sent you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Gedeon said to him, [Be gracious] with me, my Lord: whereby shall I save Israel? behold, my thousand is weakened in Manasse, and I am the least in my father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the angel of the Lord said to him, The Lord shall be with you, and you shall strike Madiam as one man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Gedeon said to him, If now I have found mercy in your eyes, and you will do this day for me all that you have spoken of with me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} depart not hence until I come to you, and I will bring forth an offering and offer it before you: and he said, I will remain until you return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Gedeon went in, and prepared a kid of the goats, and an ephah of fine flour unleavened; and he put the flesh in the basket, and poured the broth into the pot, and brought them forth to him under the turpentine tree, and drew near. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the angel of God said to him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and put them on that rock, and pour out the broth close by: and he did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the angel of the Lord stretched out the end of the rod that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened bread; and fire came up out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened bread, and the angel of the Lord vanished from his sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Gedeon saw that he was an angel of the Lord; and Gedeon said, Ah, ah, Lord my God! for I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord said to him, Peace be to you, fear not, you shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Gedeon built there an altar to the Lord, and called it The peace of the Lord, until this day, as it is still in Ephratha of the father of Esdri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass in that night, that the Lord said to him, Take the young bullock which your father has, even the second bullock of seven years old, and you shall destroy the altar of Baal which your father has, and the grove which is by it you shall destroy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall build an altar to the Lord your God on the top of this Maozi in the ordering[it], and you shall take the second bullock, and shall offer up whole burnt offerings with the wood of the grove, which you shall destroy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Gedeon took ten men of his servants, and did as the Lord spoke to him: and it came to pass, as he feared the house of his father and the men of the city if he should do it by day, that he did it by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the men of the city rose up early in the morning; and behold, the altar of Baal had been demolished, and the grove by it had been destroyed; and they saw the second bullock, which Gedeon offered on the altar that had been built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And a man said to his neighbor, Who has done this thing? and they enquired and searched, and learned that Gedeon the son of Joas had done this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the men of the city said to Joas, Bring out your son, and let him die, because he has destroyed the altar of Baal, and because he has destroyed the grove that is by it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Gedeon the son of Joas said to all the men who rose up against him, Do you⌃ now plead for Baal, or will you⌃ save him? whoever will plead for him, let him be slain this morning: if he be a god let him plead for himself, [because] one has thrown down his altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he called it in that day Jerobaal, saying, Let Baal plead thereby, because his altar has been thrown down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And all Madiam, and Amalek, and the sons of the east gathered themselves together, and encamped in the valley of Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gedeon, and he blew with the horn, and Abiezer came to help after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And [Gedeon] sent messengers into all Manasse, and into Aser, and into Zabulon, and into Nephthali; and he went up to meet them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Gedeon said to God, If you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} behold, I put the fleece of wool in the threshing floor: if there be dew on the fleece only, and drought on all the ground, I shall know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And it was so: and he rose up early in the morning, and wrung the fleece, and dew dropped from the fleece, a bowl full of water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Gedeon said to God, Let not, I pray you, your anger be kindled with me, and I will speak yet once; I will even yet make one trial more with the fleece: let now the drought be upon the fleece only, and let there be dew on all the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And God did so in that night; and there was drought on the fleece only, and on all the ground there was dew.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{24} Name of God: Yahweh Shalom (יְהוָה שָׁלוֹם) — The LORD is peace Common English renderings: The LORD is peace. Gideon’s altar-name after encountering God’s reassurance in fearful days.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} did evil; delivered When God judges, he will overcome; and sinners shall be made either to bend or break before him. See the ensuing history. Midian \textsuperscript{2} the hand; prevailed Heb. was strong dens Dr. Shaw says, that a great way on each side Joppa, on the sea coast, there is a range of mountains and precipices; and in these high situations are generally found the dens, holes, or caves, which are so frequently mentioned in Scripture; and which were formerly the lonesome retreats of the distressed Israelites. \textsuperscript{4} destroyed; till thou come The Midianites dwelt beyond the eastern borders of the land of Canaan, east of the Dead Sea, and Gaza was on the Mediterranean, on the west, so that these invaders ravaged the whole breadth of the land., left no; sheep or, goat \textsuperscript{5} tents; as grasshoppers; their camels; to destroy \textsuperscript{8} am 2759, bc 1245, An, Ex, Is, 246 a prophet Heb. a man a prophet Thus saith \textsuperscript{10} I am the fear not; ye have \textsuperscript{11} an angel, ; Abiezrite; Gideon, Gedeon, hide it, Heb. cause it to flee \textsuperscript{13} if the Lord; why then; our fathers, forsaken us \textsuperscript{15} wherewith; my family is poor Heb. my thousand is the meanest; the least \textsuperscript{18} bring;, present or, meat offering \textsuperscript{19} and made Dr. Shaw observes, "Besides a bowl of milk, and a basket of figs, raisins, or dates, which upon our arrival were presented to us, to stay our appetite, the master of the tent fetched us from his flock, according to the number of our company, a kid or a goat, a lamb or a sheep; half of which was immediately seethed by his wife, and served up with cucasoe; the rest was made kaḃab, i.e., cut to pieces and roasted, which we reserved for our breakfast or dinner next day." May we not suppose, says Mr. Harmer, that Gideon presented some slight refreshment to the supposed prophet, according to the present Arab mode, and desired him to stay till he could provide something more substantial; that he immediately killed a kid, seethed a part of it, and when ready brought the stewed meat in a pot, with unleavened cakes of bread, which he had baked; and the other part, the kaḃab, in a basket for him to carry with him, for some after repast in his journey?; a kid Heb. a kid of the goats unleavened cakes \textsuperscript{24} built; Jehovahshalom that is, The Lord send peace; Ophrah \textsuperscript{25} Take thy father's; even or, and, throw; thy father; cut down \textsuperscript{26} build rock Heb. strong place the ordered place or, an orderly manner \textsuperscript{27} and did; he did it \textsuperscript{31} Will ye plead The words are very emphatic: "Will ye plead in earnest ( tereevoon ) for Baal? Will ye really save ( tosheeoon ) him? If he be God ( Elohim, ) let him contend for himself, seeing his altar is thrown down."; let him be; if he be \textsuperscript{32} Jerubbaal that is, Let Baal plead; Jerubbesheth, that is, Let the shameful thing plead \textsuperscript{33} Then all, ; children; went over; the valley \textsuperscript{34} the Spirit, ; came upon Heb. clothed; blew; Abiezer; was gathered Heb. was called\par}

\subsection*{Judges 7}
\markright{JUDGES 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jerobaal rose early, the same is Gedeon, and all the people with him, and encamped at the fountain of Arad; and the camp of Madiam was to the north of him, [reaching] from Gabaathamorai, in the valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to Gedeon, The people with you [are] many, so that I may not deliver Madiam into their hand, lest at any time Israel boast against me, saying, My hand has saved me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And now speak in the ears of the people, saying, Who [is] afraid and fearful? let him turn and depart from mount Galaad: and there returned of the people twenty-two thousand, and ten thousand were left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Gedeon, The people is yet numerous; bring them down to the water, and I will purge them there for you: and it shall come to pass that of whoever I shall say to you, This one shall go with you, [even] he shall go with you; and of whoever I shall say to you, This one shall not go with you, [even] he shall not go with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he brought the people down to the water; and the Lord said to Gedeon, Whosoever shall lap of the water with his tongue as if a dog should lap, you shall set him apart, and [also] whoever shall bow down upon his knees to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the number of those that lapped with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men; and all the rest of the people bowed upon their knees to drink water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord said to Gedeon, I will save you by the three hundred men that lapped, and I will give Madiam into your hand; and all the [rest of the] people shall go every one to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they took the provision of the people in their hand, and their horns; and he sent away every man of Israel each to his tent, and he strengthened the three hundred; and the army of Madiam were beneath him in the valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass in that night that the Lord said to him, Arise, go down into the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if you are afraid to go down, go down you and your servant Phara into the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall hear what they shall say, and afterwards your hands shall be strong, and you shall go down into the camp: and he went down and Phara his servant to the extremity of the [companies of] fifty, which were in the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Madiam and Amalec and all the children of the east [were] scattered in the valley, as the locust for multitude; and there was no number to their camels, but they were as the sand on the seashore for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gedeon came, and behold a man [was] relating to his neighbor a dream, and he said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream, and behold, a cake of barley bread rolling into the camp of Madiam, and it came as far as a tent, and struck it, and it fell, and it turned it up, and the tent fell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And his neighbor answered and said, This is none other than the sword of Gedeon, son of Joas, a man of Israel: God has delivered Madiam and all the host into his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass when Gedeon heard the account of the dream and the interpretation of it, that he worshipped the Lord, and returned to the camp of Israel, and said, Rise, for the Lord has delivered the camp of Madiam into our hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and put horns in the hands of all, and empty pitchers, and torches in the pitchers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and he said to them, You⌃ shall look at me, and so shall you⌃ do; and behold, I will go into the beginning of the host, and it shall come to pass [that] as I do, so shall you⌃ do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I will sound with the horn, and all you⌃ with me shall sound with the horn round about the whole camp, and you⌃ shall say, For the Lord and Gedeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Gedeon and the hundred men that were with him came to the extremity of the army in the beginning of the middle watch; and they completely roused the guards, and sounded with the horns, and they broke the pitchers that were in their hands, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the three companies sounded with the horns, and broke the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands, and in their right hands their horns to sound with; and they cried out, A sword for the Lord and for Gedeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And [every] man stood in his place round about the host; and all the host ran, and sounded [an alarm], and fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they sounded with the three hundred horns; and the Lord set [every] man's sword in all the host against his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the host fled as far as Bethseed Tagaragatha Abel-meula to Tabath; and the men of Israel from Nephthali, and from Aser, and from all Manasse, came to help, and followed after Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Gedeon sent messengers into all mount Ephraim, saying, Come down to meet Madiam, and take to yourselves the water as far as Baethera and Jordan: and every man of Ephraim cried out, and they took the water before hand to Baethera and Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they took the princes of Madiam, even Oreb and Zeb; and they killed Oreb in Sur Oreb, and they killed Zeb in Jakephzeph; and they pursued Madiam, and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeb to Gedeon from beyond Jordan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Jerubbaal It appears that Jerubbaal had now become the surname of Gideon. He is mentioned by Sanchoniathon, quoted by Eusebius, who lived in the reign of Ithobal, king of Tyre, and consequently a little after the time of Gideon, by the name of Jerombalus, a priest of Jeuo or Jao. rose up; Moreh \textsuperscript{2} too many; Israel; Mine own \textsuperscript{3} Whosoever; mount Gilead Gideon was certainly not at mount Gilead, east of Jordan at this time; but rather near mount Gilboa, west of Jordan. Calmet thinks there must either have been two Gileads, which does not appear from Scripture to have been the case, or that the Hebrew Text is corrupt, and that for Gilead we should read Gilboa. This reading, though adopted by Houbigant, is not confirmed by an manuscript or version. Dr. Hales endeavours to reconcile the whole, by the supposition that in Gideon's army there were many eastern Manassites from mount Gilead, near the Midianites; and therefore proposes to read, "Whosoever from mount Gilead is fearful and afraid, let him return (home) and depart early." twenty \textsuperscript{5} lappeth The original word yalok, is precisely the sound which the dog makes in lapping. It appears that it is not unusual for the Arabs to drink water out of the palms of their hands; and, from this account, we learn that the Israelites did so occasionally. Dr. A. Clarke, in his edition of Harmer, has presented us with the following curious manuscript note from Dr. Russell. "When they take water with the palms of their hands, they naturally place themselves on their hams, to be nearer the water; but when they drink from a pitcher or gourd, fresh filled, they do not sit down on purpose to drink, but drink standing, and very often put the sleeve of their shirt over the mouth of the vessel, by way of strainer, lest small leeches might have been taken up with the water. For the same reason they often prefer taking the water with the palm of the hand to lapping it from the surface." From the letters of Busbequius we learn, that the Eastern people are not in the habit of drinking standing. The 300 men, who satisfied their thirst in the most expeditious manner, by this sufficiently indicated their spirit, and alacrity to follow Gideon in his dangerous enterprise; while the rest shewed their love of ease, self-indulgence, effeminacy, and want of courage. \textsuperscript{9} the same; Arise; I have delivered \textsuperscript{11} thou shalt; thine hands; armed men or, ranks by five, *marg. \textsuperscript{14} his fellow, ; into his hand \textsuperscript{15} interpretation thereof Heb. breaking thereof, worshipped; Arise \textsuperscript{16} three companies This small number of men, thus divided, would be able to encompass the whole camp of the Midianites. Concealing the lamps in the pitchers, they would pass unobserved to their appointed stations; then, in the dead of the night, when most of the enemy were fast asleep, all at once breaking their pitchers one against another, with as much noise as they could, and blowing the trumpets and shouting; they would occasion an exceedingly great alarm. The obedience of faith alone could have induced such an expedient, which no doubt God directed Gideon to employ. - Scott. a trumpet Heb. trumpets in the hand of all of them empty lamps or, fire-brands, or torches \textsuperscript{18} blow ye the sword The word cherev, "sword, " necessarily implied, and rightly supplied by our venerable translators from, is found in this place, in the Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic, and in eight manuscripts; and evidently appears to be genuine. \textsuperscript{19} in the beginning; they blew brake \textsuperscript{20} blew How astonishing and overwhelming must the effect be, in a dark night, of the sudden glare of 300 torches, darting their splendour in the same instant on the half-awakened eyes of the terrified Midianites; accompanied with the clangor of 300 trumpets, alternately mingled with the thundering shout of cherav yehovah oolegidon, "The sword of Jehovah and of Gideon!"; brake \textsuperscript{22} blew, ; the Lord; in or, toward Zererath Probably the same as Zartanah. border Heb. lip Abelmeholah Situated, according to Eusebius 16 miles south from Scythopolis, or Bethshan., Tabbath Probably the town of Οηβης, mentioned by Eusebius, 13 miles from Neapolis, or Shechem, towards Scythopolis. \textsuperscript{24} sent; take before, Bethbarah Probably the same as Betha-bara, beyond Jordan, and at the ford where the Hebrews passed under the direction of Joshua. \textsuperscript{25} two princes; rock; Oreb Eusebius and Jerome speak of a small place called Araba, three miles west from Scythopolis, which is supposed by some to have had its name from Oreb. and brought Among ancient nations, the head of the conquered chief was usually brought to the conqueror. Thus Pompey's head was brought to Cesar, Cicero's head to Mark Anthony, and the heads of Ahab's children to Jehu. These barbarities are seldom practised now, except among the Mahommedans, or the savages of Africa and America; and for the credit of human nature, it is to be wished that such atrocities had never been committed. on the other side The words maiaiver lyyarden, may denote at the passage of Jordan, or from beyond Jordan. Gideon does not appear to have yet passed the Jordan.\par}

\subsection*{Judges 8}
\markright{JUDGES 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the men of Ephraim said to Gedeon, What [is] this [that] you have done to us, in that you did not call us when you went to fight with Madiam? and they chode with him sharply. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said to them, What have I now done in comparison of you? [is] not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord has delivered into your hand the princes of Madiam, Oreb and Zeb; and what could I do in comparison of you? Then was their spirit calmed toward him, when he spoke this word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Gedeon came to Jordan, and went over, himself and the three hundred with him, hungry, yet pursuing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to the men of Socchoth, Give, I pray you, bread to feed this people that follow me; because they are faint, and behold, I am following after Zebee and Salmana, kings of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the princes of Socchoth said, [Are] the hands of Zebee and Salmana now in your hand, that we should give bread to your host? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Gedeon said, Therefore when the Lord gives Zebee and Salmana into my hand, then will I tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness, and the Barkenim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he went up thence to Phanuel, and spoke to them likewise: and the men of Phanuel answered him as the men of Socchoth [had] answered him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Gedeon said to the men of Phanuel, When I return in peace, I will break down this tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Zebee and Salmana [were] in Carcar, and their host [was] with them, about fifteen thousand, all that were left of all the host of the aliens; and they that fell [were] one hundred and twenty thousand men that drew the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Gedeon went up by the way of them that lived in tents, eastward of Nabai and Jegebal; and he struck the host, and the host was secure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Zebee and Salmana fled; and he pursued after them, and took the two kings of Madiam, Zebee and Salmana, and discomfited all the army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gedeon the son of Joas returned from the battle, down from the battle of Ares. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he took prisoner a young lad of the men of Socchoth, and questioned him; and he wrote to him the names of the princes of Socchoth and of their elders, seventy-seven men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Gedeon came to the princes of Socchoth, and said, Behold Zebee and Salmana, about whom you⌃ reproached me, saying, [Are] the hands of Zebee and Salmana now in your hand, that we should give bread to your men that are faint? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he took the elders of the city with the thorns of the wilderness and the Barkenim, and with them he tore the men of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he overthrew the tower of Phanuel, and killed the men of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to Zebee and Salmana, Where [are] the men whom you⌃ killed in Thabor? and they said, As you, so [were] they, according to the likeness of the son of a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Gedeon said, They were my brethren and the sons of my mother: [as] the Lord lives, if you⌃ had preserved them alive, I would not have slain you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said to Jether his firstborn, Rise and kill them; but the lad drew not his sword, for he was afraid, for he was yet very young. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Zebee and Salmana said, Rise you and fall upon us, for your power [is] as that of a man; and Gedeon arose, and killed Zebee and Salmana: and he took the round ornaments that were on the necks of their camels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the men of Israel said to Gedeon, Rule, [my] lord, over us, both you, and your son, and your son's son; for you have saved us out of the hand of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Gedeon said to them, I will not rule, and my son shall not rule among you; the Lord shall rule over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Gedeon said to them, I will make a request of you, and do you⌃ give me every man an earring out of his spoils: for they had golden earrings, for they were Ismaelites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they said, We will certainly give them: and he opened his garment, and each man cast therein an earring of his spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the weight of the golden earrings which he asked, was a thousand and seven hundred pieces of gold, besides the crescents, and the chains, and the garments, and the purple cloths that were on the kings of Madiam, and besides the chains that were on the necks of their camels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Gedeon made an ephod of it, an set it in his city in Ephratha; and all Israel went there a whoring after it, and it became a stumbling block to Gedeon and his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Madiam, was straitened before the children of Israel, and they did not lift up their head any more; and the land had rest forty years in the days of Gedeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Jerobaal the son of Joas went and sat in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Gedeon had seventy sons begotten of his body, for he had many wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And his concubine was in Sychem, and she also bore him a son, and gave him the name Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Gedeon son of Joas died in his city, and he was buried in the sepulchre of Joas his father in Ephratha of Abi-Esdri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it came to pass when Gedeon was dead, that the children of Israel turned, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made for themselves a covenant with Baal that he should be their god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the children of Israel remembered not the Lord their God who had delivered them out of the hand of all that afflicted them round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they did not deal mercifully with the house of Jerobaal, (the same is Gedeon) according to all the good which he did to Israel.\par

Gideon was a mighty man of valour, a true patriot, evidently disinterested and void of ambition. He loved his country, and hazarded his life for it; but refused the kingdom, when offered to him and his heirs. The act of making the ephod was totally wrong; yet, probably it was done with no reprehensible design.\par}
