\subsection*{Judges 9}
\markright{JUDGES 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abimelech son of Jerobaal went to Sychem to his mother's brethren; and he spoke to them and to all the kindred of the house of his mother's father, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Sychem, saying, Which [is] better for you, that seventy men, even all the sons of Jerobaal, should reign over you, or that one man should reign over you? and remember that I am your bone and your flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his mother's brethren spoke concerning him in the ears of all the men of Sychem all these words; and their heart turned after Abimelech, for they said, He is our brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they gave him seventy [pieces] of silver out of the house of Baalberith; and Abimelech hired for himself vain and cowardly men, and they went after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he went to the house of his father to Ephratha, and killed his brethren the sons of Jerobaal, seventy men upon one stone; but Joatham the youngest son of Jerobaal was left, for he hid himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all the men of Sicima, and all the house of Bethmaalo, were gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king by the oak of Sedition, which was at Sicima. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it was reported to Joatham, and he went and stood on the top of mount Garizin, and lifted up his voice, and wept, and said to them, Hear me, you⌃ men of Sicima, and God shall hear you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them; and they said to the olive, Reign over us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But the olives said to them, Shall I leave my fatness, with which men shall glorify God, and go to be promoted over the trees? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the trees said to the fig tree, Come, reign over us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the fig tree said to them, Shall I leave my sweetness and my good fruits, and go to be promoted over the trees? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the trees said to the vine, Come, reign over us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the vine said to them, Shall I leave my wine that cheers God and men, and go to be promoted over the trees? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then all the trees said to the bramble, Come you and [reign] over us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the bramble said to the trees, If you⌃ in truth anoint me to reign over you, come, stand under my shadow; and if not, let fire come out from me and devour the cedars of Libanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now, if you⌃ have done it in truth and integrity, and have made Abimelech king, and if you⌃ have wrought well with Jerobaal, and with his house, and if you⌃ have done to him according to the reward of his hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} as my father fought for you, and put his life in jeopardy, and delivered you out of the hand of Madiam; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and you⌃ are risen up this day against the house of my father, and have slain his sons, being seventy men, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech the son of his bondwoman king over the men of Sicima, because he is your brother: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} if then you⌃ have done truly and faithfully with Jerobaal, and with his house this day, rejoice you⌃ in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice over you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Sicima, and the house of Bethmaalo; and let fire come out from the men of Sicima and from the house of Bethmaalo, and devour Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Joatham fled, and ran away, and went as far as Baeer, and lived there out of the way of his brother Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Abimelech reigned over Israel three years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Sicima; and the men of Sicima dealt treacherously with the house of Abimelech: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} to bring the injury done to the seventy sons of Jerobaal, and to lay their blood upon their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and upon the men of Sicima, because they strengthened his hands to kill his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the men of Sicima set liers in wait against him on the top of the mountains, and robbed every one who passed by them on the way; and it was reported to the king Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Gaal son of Jobel came, and his brethren, and passed by Sicima, and the men of Sicima trusted in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they went out into the field, and gathered their grapes, and trod them, and made merry; and they brought [the grapes] into the house of their god, and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Gaal the son of Jobel said, Who is Abimelech, and who is the son of Sychem, that we should serve him? [Is he] not the son of Jerobaal, and [is] not Zebul his steward, his servant with the son of Emmor the father of Sychem? and why should we serve him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And would that this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech, and I would say to him, Multiply your host, and come out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Jobel, and he was very angry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, Behold, Gaal the son of Jobel and his brethren are come to Sychem; and behold, they have besieged the city against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And now rise up by night, you and the people with you, and lay wait in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it shall come to pass in the morning at sunrising, you shall rise up early and draw toward the city; and behold, he and the people with him will come forth against you, and you shall do to him according to your power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Abimelech and all the people with him rose up by night, and formed an ambuscade against Sychem in four companies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Gaal the son of Jobel went forth, and stood by the door of the gate of the city: and Abimelech and the people with him rose up from the ambuscade. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Gaal the son of Jobel saw the people, and said to Zebul, Behold, a people comes down from the top of the mountains: and Zebul said to him, You see the shadow of the mountains as men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Gaal continued to speak and said, Behold, a people comes down westward from the part bordering on the middle of the land, and another company comes by the way of Helon Maonenim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Zebul said to him, And where is your mouth as you spoke, Who is Abimelech that we should serve him? [Is] not this the people whom you despised? go forth now, and set the battle in array against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Gaal went forth before the men of Sychem, and set the battle in array against Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from before him; and many fell down slain as far as the door of the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Abimelech entered into Arema, and Zebul cast out Gaal and his brethren, so that they should not dwell in Sychem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And it came to pass on the second day that the people went out into the field, and [one] brought word to Abimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And he took the people, and divided them into three companies, and formed an ambush in the field; and he looked, and, behold, the people went forth out of the city, and he rose up against them, and struck them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Abimelech and the chiefs of companies that were with him rushed forward, and stood by the door of the gate of the city; and the two [other] companies rushed forward upon all that were in the field, and struck them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and took the city, and killed the people that were in it, and destroyed the city, and sowed it with salt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And all the men of the tower of Sychem heard, and came to the gathering of Baethel-berith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And it was reported to Abimelech, that all the men of the tower of Sychem were gathered together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And Abimelech went up to the mount of Selmon, and all the people that were with him; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand, and cut down a branch of a tree, and took it, and laid it on his shoulders; and said to the people that were with him, What you⌃ see me doing, do quickly as I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And they cut down likewise even every man a branch, and went after Abimelech, and laid them against the place of gathering, and burnt the place of gathering over them with fire; and they died, even all the men of the tower of Sicima, about a thousand men and women. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And Abimelech went out of Baethel-berith, and encamped against Thebes, and took it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And there was a strong tower in the midst of the city; and there all the men and the women of the city fled, and shut [the door] without them, and went up on the roof of the tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And Abimelech drew near to the tower, and they besieged it; and Abimelech drew near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon the head of Abimelech, and broke his skull. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And he cried out quickly to the young man his armor-bearer, and said to him, Draw your sword, and kill me, lest at any time they should say, A woman killed him: and his young man thrust him through and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead; and they went each to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} So God requited the wickedness of Abimelech, which he wrought against his father, in slaying his seventy brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And all the wickedness of the men of Sychem God requited upon their head; and the curse of Joatham the son of Jerobaal came upon them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Whether etc. Heb. What is good whether etc threescore your bone \textsuperscript{3} spake; to follow Heb. after our brother \textsuperscript{4} house, vain etc. Anashim raikim oophochozim, "worthless and dissolute men; " persons who were living on the public, and had nothing to lose. Such was the foundation of his Babel government. By a cunning management of such unprincipled men most revolutions are brought about. \textsuperscript{6} the house; Millo Probably the name of a person of note in Shechem. plain or, oak \textsuperscript{8} The trees This is the most ancient fable or apologue extant; and is extremely beautiful, apposite, and intelligible.; olive tree The zayith, or olive tree, in the Linnean system, is a genus of the diandra monogynia class of plants. It is of a moderate height, and grows best in sunny places. Its trunk is knotty; bark smooth, of an ash colour. Wood solid and yellowish; leaves oblong, almost like those of the willow, of a dark green colour on the upper side, and whitish below. In June it puts forth white flowers, growing in bunches, each of one piece, widening towards the top, and dividing into four parts. After this succeeds the fruit, which is oblong and plump; first green, then pale, and when quite ripe, black. Within it is enclosed a hard stone, filled with oblong seeds. It was the most useful of all trees in the forest; as the bramble was the meanest and most worthless. Reign \textsuperscript{9} wherewith, ; God Elohim, rather gods; the parable being adapted to the idolatrous Shechemites. to be promoted over the trees Heb. up and down for other trees \textsuperscript{15} shadow; let fire; the cedars \textsuperscript{17} fought, adventured his life Heb. cast his life \textsuperscript{21} Beer Probably the Beer mentioned by Mr. Maundrell, three hours and a half, or about ten miles, north of Jerusalem, towards Shechem. It is situated toward the south, on an easy declivity; and has a fountain of excellent water at the bottom of the hill, from which it has taken its name. Close to the well are the mouldering walls of a ruined khan; and on the summit of the hill two large arches still remain of a ruined convent. Dr. Richardson says, that it seems to have been once a place of considerable consequence. \textsuperscript{23} am 2771, bc 1233 God That is, God permitted the evil spirit of jealousy, treachery, and discord, to break out between Abimelech and the Shechemites.; An Ex, Is, 258 dealt \textsuperscript{24} That the; aided him in the killing of Heb. strengthened his hands to kill, Sooner or later, God will make inquisition for blood, and will return it on the heads of those that shed it. Accessories will be reckoned with, as well as principals, in that and other sins. The Shechemites, who countenanced Abimelech's pretensions, aided and abetted him in his bloody project, and avowed the fact by making him king after he had done it, must fall with him, fall by him, and fall first. Those that combine together to do wickedly, are justly dashed in pieces one against another. Blood cannot be a lasting cement to any interest. \textsuperscript{27} merry or, songs, ; the house; did eat; cursed \textsuperscript{29} would to God The very words and conduct of a sly, hypocritical demagogue.; And he said Rather, "and I would say to Abimelech, " as the LXX renders; for as Dr. Wall observes, this was probably not said in the presence of Abimelech; but at an intemperate feast, in his absence, when he boasted he would challenge him. Increase thine army \textsuperscript{31} privily Heb. craftily, or, to Tormah they fortify Under pretence of repairing the walls and towers, they were actually putting the place in a state of defence, intending to seize on the government as soon as they found Abimelech coming against them. \textsuperscript{33} as thou shalt find Heb. as thine hand shall find, *marg. \textsuperscript{35} Gaal Of this person we know no more than is here recorded. He was probably one of the descendants of the Canaanites, who hoped, from the state of the public mind and their disaffection to Abimelech, to cause a revolution, and thus to restore the ancient government as it was under Hamor, the father of Shechem. Josephus says he was a man of authority, who sojourned with them, with his armed men and kinsmen; and that the Shechemites desired that he would allow them a guard during the vintage. the people \textsuperscript{36} seest the shadow Doubdan states, that in some parts of the Holy Land there are many detached rocks scattered up and down, some growing out of the ground, and others fragments broken off from rocky precipices, the shadow of which, it appears, Josephus thought might be most naturally imagined to look like troops of men at a distance, rather than that of the mountains; for he represents Zebul as saying to Gaal, that he mistook the shadow of the rocks for men. \textsuperscript{37} middle Heb. navel Meonenim or, the regarders of the times \textsuperscript{41} Arumah This place appears from the next verse to have been near Shechem; and is perhaps the same as Ruma, a village of Galilee, mentioned by Josephus, Bell. 1. iii. c. 7. Zebul \textsuperscript{45} he took beat; *marg.; sowed Salt in small quantities renders land extremely fertile; but too much of it destroys vegetation. Every place, says Pliny, in which salt is found is barren, and produces nothing. Hence the sowing of a place with salt was a custom in different nations to express permanent desolation. Sigonius observes, that when Milan was taken, ad 1162, the walls were razed, and it was sown with salt. And Brantome informs us, that it was an ancient custom in France, to sow the house of a man with salt, who had been declared a traitor to his king. Charles IX., king of France, the most base and perfidious of human beings, caused the house of Admiral Coligni (whom he and the Duke of Guise caused to be murdered, with thousands more of Protestants, on the eve of St. Bartholomew, 1572), to be sown with salt! \textsuperscript{48} Zalmon What ye; me do Heb. I have done \textsuperscript{50} Thebez According to Eusebius, thirteen miles from Shechem, towards Scythopolis. \textsuperscript{53} woman; and all to An antiquated expression, meaning "full intention" to complete an object. "All to, " observes Dr. Johnson, "is a particle of mere enforcement." The original is wattaritz eth gulgalto, which is simply as the LXX render και εκλασε το κρανιον αυτου, "and she brake his skull." Plutarch relates, that Pyrrhus was killed at the siege of Thebes, by a piece of a tile, which a woman threw upon his head. \textsuperscript{54} Draw thy And his young man It was a disgrace to be killed by a woman. \textsuperscript{56} God rendered Both the fratricide Abimelech and the unprincipled men of Shechem had the iniquity visited upon them of which they had been guilty. Man's judgment may be avoided; but there is no escape from that of God. How many houses have been sown with salt in France, by the just judgment of God, for the massacre of the Protestants on the eve of St. Bartholomew! See note on .\par}

\subsection*{Judges 10}
\markright{JUDGES 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after Abimelech Thola the son of Phua rose up to save Israel, [being] the son of his father's brother, a man of Issachar; and he lived in Samir in mount Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and died, and was buried in Samir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And after him arose Jair of Galaad, and he judged Israel twenty-two years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he had thirty-two sons riding on thirty-two colts, and they had thirty-two cities; and they called them Jair's towns until this day in the land of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jair died, and was buried in Rhamnon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim, and Astaroth, and the gods of Aram, and the gods of Sidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Phylistines; and they forsook the Lord, and did not serve him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and sold them into the hands of the Phylistines, and into the hand of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they afflicted and bruised the children of Israel at that time eighteen years, all the children of Israel beyond Jordan in the land of the Amorite in Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the children of Ammon went over Jordan to fight with Juda, and Benjamin, and with Ephraim; and the children of Israel were greatly afflicted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the children of Israel cried to the Lord, saying, We have sinned against you, because we have forsaken God, and served Baalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to the children of Israel, Did I not [save you] from Egypt and from the Amorite, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Phylistines, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and from the Sidonians, and Amalec, and Madiam, who afflicted you? and you⌃ cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Yet you⌃ forsook me and served other gods; therefore I will not save you any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Go, and cry to the gods whom you⌃ have chosen to yourselves, and let them save you in the time of your affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the children of Israel said to the Lord, We have sinned: do you to us according to all [that is] good in your eyes; only deliver us this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they put away the strange gods from the midst of them, and served the Lord only, and his soul was pained for the trouble of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the children of Ammon went up, and encamped in Galaad; and the children of Israel were gathered together and encamped on the hill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the people the princes of Galaad said every man to his neighbor, Who [is] he that shall begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall even be head over all that dwell in Galaad.\par

But the Maonites might be a tribe of Arabs, inhabitants of Maon ( .; ), which assisted Moab. \textsuperscript{15} We have sinned; do thou; seemeth etc. Heb. is good in thine eyes deliver \textsuperscript{16} they put, ; strange gods Heb. gods of strangers his soul; grieved Heb. shortened, Not that there is any grief in God; he has infinite joy and happiness in himself, which cannot be broken in upon by either the sins or the miseries of his creatures. Not that there is any change in God; for he is of one mind, and who can turn him? But his goodness is his glory; by it he proclaims his name, and magnifies it; and as he is pleased to put himself into the relation of a father to his people, so he is pleased to represent his goodness to them by the compassion of a father to his children; for as he is the Father of lights, so is he the Father of mercies. \textsuperscript{17} gathered together Heb. cried together Mizpeh \textsuperscript{18} What man; he shall be\par}

\subsection*{Judges 11}
\markright{JUDGES 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jephthae the Galaadite [was] a mighty man; and he [was] the son of a harlot, who bore Jephthae to Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the wife of Galaad bore him sons; and the sons of his wife grew up, and they cast out Jephthae, and said to him, You shall not inherit in the house of our father, for you are the son of a concubine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jephthae fled from the face of his brethren, and lived in the land of Tob; and vain men gathered to Jephthae, and went out with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass when the children of Ammon prepared to fight with Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} that the elders of Galaad went to fetch Jephthae from the land of Tob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they said to Jephthae, Come, and be our head, and we will fight with the sons of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jephthae said to the elders of Galaad, Did you⌃ not hate me, and cast me out of my father's house, and banish me from you? and therefore are you⌃ come to me now when you⌃ lack me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the elders of Galaad said to Jephthae, Therefore have we now turned to you, that you should go with us, and fight against the sons of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabitants of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jephthae said to the elders of Galaad, If you⌃ turn me back to fight with the children of Ammon, and the Lord should deliver them before me, then will I be your head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the elders of Galaad said to Jephthae, The Lord be witness between us, if we shall not do according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jephthae went with the elders of Galaad, and the people made him head and ruler over them: and Jephthae spoke all his words before the Lord in Massepha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Jephthae sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What have I to do with you, that you have come against me to fight in my land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king of the children of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthae, Because Israel took my land when he went up out of Egypt, from Arnon to Jaboc, and to Jordan: now then return them peaceably and I will depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jephthae again sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and said to him, Thus says Jephthae, Israel took not the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} for in their going up out of Egypt Israel went in the wilderness as far as the sea of Siph, and came to Cades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, I will pass, if it please you, by your land: and the king of Edom complied not: and [Israel] also sent to the king of Moab, and he did not consent; and Israel sojourned in Cades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And [they] journeyed in the wilderness, and compassed the land of Edom and the land of Moab: and they came by the east of the land of Moab, and encamped in the country beyond Arnon, and came not within the borders of Moab, for Arnon [is] the border of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Israel sent messengers to Seon king of the Amorite, king of Esbon, and Israel said to him, Let us pass, we pray you, by your land to our place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Seon did not trust Israel to pass by his coast; and Seon gathered all his people, and they encamped at Jasa; and he set the battle in array against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord God of Israel delivered Seon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck him; and Israel inherited all the land of the Amorite who lived in that land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} from Arnon and to Jaboc, and from the wilderness to Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now the Lord God of Israel has removed the Amorite from before his people Israel, and shall you inherit his [land]? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Will you not inherit those possessions which Chamos your god shall cause you to inherit; and shall not we inherit the [land of] all those whom the Lord our God has removed from before you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now are you any better than Balac son of Sepphor, king of Moab? did he indeed fight with Israel, or indeed make war with him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} when [Israel] lived in Esebon and in its coasts, and in the land of Aroer and in its coasts, and in all the cities by Jordan, three hundred years? and therefore did you not recover them in that time? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And now I have not sinned against you, but you wrong me in preparing war against me: may the Lord the Judge judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But the king of the children of Ammon listened not to the words of Jephthae, which he sent to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthae, and he passed over Galaad, and Manasse, and passed by the watch-tower of Galaad to the other side of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Jephthae vowed a vow to the Lord, and said, If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} then it shall come to pass that whoever shall first come out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, he shall be the Lord's: I will offer him up for a whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jephthae advanced to meet the sons of Ammon to fight against them; and the Lord delivered them into his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he struck them from Aroer till [one] comes to Arnon, in number twenty cities, and as far as Ebelcharmim, with a very great destruction: and the children of Ammon were straitened before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Jephthae came to Massepha to his house; and behold, his daughter came forth to meet him with timbrels and dances; and she was his only child, he had not another son or daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And it came to pass when he saw her, that he tore his garments, and said, Ah, ah, my daughter, you have indeed troubled me, and you were the cause of my trouble; and I have opened my mouth against you to the Lord, and I shall not be able to return from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And she said to him, Father, have you opened your mouth to the Lord? Do to me accordingly as [the word] went out of your mouth, in that the Lord has wrought vengeance for you on your enemies of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And she said to her father, Let my father now do this thing: let me alone for two months, and I will go up and down on the mountains, and I will bewail my virginity, I and my companions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he said, Go: and he sent her away for two months; and she went, and her companions, and she bewailed her virginity on the mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And it came to pass at the end of the two months that she returned to her father; and he performed upon her his vow which he vowed; and she knew no man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} and it was an ordinance in Israel, [That] the daughters of Israel went from year to year to bewail the daughter of Jephthae the Galaadite for four days in a year.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Jephthah, called Jephthae a mighty; an harlot Heb. a woman an harlot Probably zonah should be rendered as in, a hostess, or inn-keeper, so Targum of Jonathan, wehoo bar ittetha pundekeetha, "and he was the son of a woman, a tavern-keeper." She was very probably a Canaanite, as she is called, a strange woman, ishah achereth, "a woman of another race; " and on this account his brethren drove him from the family, as not having a full right to the inheritance. \textsuperscript{3} from his brethren Heb. from the face of Tob Probably the same as Ish-Tob; and appears to have been a part of Syria, near Zobah, Rehob, and Maachah, east of Jordan, and in the most northern part of the portion of Manasseh. If so, it could not be far from Gilead, the country of Jephthah. This country is called Tobie or Tubin; and the Jews who inhabited this district Tubieni, . . vain men \textsuperscript{4} am 2817, bc 1187, An, Ex, Is, 304 in process of time Heb. after days. \textsuperscript{10} The Lord; be witness be the hearer, ; if we do \textsuperscript{11} head uttered; Jephthah uttered That is, upon his elevation, he immediately retired to his devotion, and in prayer spread the whole matter before God, both his choice to the office, and his execution of the office, as one that had his eye ever toward the Lord, and would do nothing without him; that leaned not to his own understanding or courage, but depended on the Almighty God, and his favour. This is an ensample worthy of universal imitation; in All Our Ways, whether great or apparently subordinate, let us acknowledge God and seek his direction. So shall we make our way prosperous, and obtain that peace which passeth all understanding. Jephthah opened his campaign with prayer. before; Mizpeh This Mizpeh was east of Jordan in the mountains of Gilead ( ); and hence called Mizpeh of Gilead ( ), to distinguish it from another place of the same name, west of Jordan, in the tribe of Judah. \textsuperscript{12} sent messengers In this Jephthah acted in accordance with the law of Moses; and hence the justice of his cause would appear more forcibly to the people.; What hast \textsuperscript{13} Because Israel; from Arnon That is, all the land which had belonged to the Amorites and Moabites. Jabbok \textsuperscript{16} But when The whole of these messages shew, Jephthah had well studied the book of Moses. His arguments also are very clear and cogent, and his demands reasonable; for he only required that the Ammonites should cease to harass a people who had neither injured them, nor intended to do so. walked; came \textsuperscript{17} sent messengers; the king abode \textsuperscript{18} went, ; compassed came by pitched \textsuperscript{20} Lord God;, they smote; so Israel \textsuperscript{22} And they from the wilderness From Arabia Deserta on the east, to Jordan on the west. \textsuperscript{23} Jephthah shews that the Israelites did not take the land of the Moabites or Ammonites, but that of the Amorites, which they had conquered from Sihon their king; and although the Amorites had taken the lands in question from the Ammonites, yet the title by which Israel held them was good, because they took them, not from the Ammonites, but from the Amorites. \textsuperscript{24} Wilt not thou possess This is simply an argumentum ad hominem; in which Jephthah argues on this principles recognized by the king of Ammon. As if he had said, "You suppose that the land which you possess was given you by your god Chemosh; and therefore will not relinquish what you believe you hold by a divine right. Now we know that Jehovah, our God, has given us the land of the Israelites; and therefore we will not give it up." Chemosh; whomsoever \textsuperscript{29} the spirit, ; Jephthah "Jephthah seems to have been judge only of north-east Israel." over Mizpeh \textsuperscript{31} whatsoever etc. Heb. that which cometh forth, which shall come forth shall surely;, ; and I will or, or I will, etc. Wehaaleetheehoo olah, rather, as Dr. Randolph and others contend, "and I will offer Him (or to Him, i.e., Jehovah) a burnt offering; " for hoo may with much more propriety be referred to the person to whom the sacrifice was to be made, than to the thing to be sacrificed. Unless understood in this way, or as the marginal reading, it must have been the vow of a heathen or a madman. If a dog, or other uncleaned animal had met him, he could not have made it a burnt offering; or if his neighbour's wife, sons, etc., his vow gave him no right over them. \textsuperscript{33} Aroer Minnith Situated, according to Eusebius, four miles from Heshbon, towards Philadelphia or Rabbath. the plain or, Abel \textsuperscript{34} Mizpeh, his daughter; beside her or, he had not of his own either son or daughter, Heb. of himself neither \textsuperscript{35} rent his clothes, ; have opened; I cannot \textsuperscript{37} go up and down Heb. go and go down bewail \textsuperscript{39} did with That Jephthah did not sacrifice his daughter, but consecrated her to the service of God in the tabernacle, in a state of celibacy, will we imagine be evident from the following consideration - 1. Human sacrifices were ever an abomination to Jehovah, of which Jephthah could not be ignorant; and consequently he would neither have made such a vow, nor carried it into execution. 2. We are expressly told ( ) that Jephthah was under the influence of the Spirit of God, which would effectually prevent him from embruing his hands in the blood of his own child. 3. He had it in his power to redeem his daughter ( ); and surely his only child must have been of more value than thirty shekles. 4. Besides, who was to perform the horrid rite? Not Jephthah himself, who was no priest, and in whom it would have been most unnatural and inhuman; and the priests would certainly have dissuaded him from it. 5. The sacred historian informs us, that she bewailed her virginity, that she knew no man, and that the Israelitish women went yearly to comfort or lament with her.; to his vow, custom or, ordinance \textsuperscript{40} yearly Heb. from year to year lament or, to talk with, four days\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the men of Ephraim assembled [themselves], and passed on to the north, and said to Jephthae, Therefore did you go over to fight with the children of Ammon, and did not call us to go with you? we will burn your house over you with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jephthae said to them, I and my people and the children of Ammon were very much engaged in war; and I called for you, and you⌃ did not save me out of their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I saw that you were no helper, and I put my life in my hand, and passed on to the sons of Ammon; and the Lord delivered them into my hand: and therefore are you⌃ come up against me this day to fight with me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jephthae gathered all the men of Galaad, and fought with Ephraim; and the men of Galaad struck Ephraim, because they that were escaped of Ephraim said, You⌃ [are] of Galaad in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Galaad took the fords of Jordan before Ephraim; and they that escaped of Ephraim said to them, Let us go over: and the men of Galaad said, Are you an Ephrathite? and he said, No. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then they said to him, Say now Stachys; and he did not rightly pronounce it so: and they took him, and killed him at the fords of Jordan; and there fell at that time of Ephraim two and forty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jephthae judged Israel six years; and Jephthae the Galaadite died, and was buried in his city Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And after him Abaissan of Bethleem judged Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he had thirty sons, and thirty daughters, whom he sent forth; and he brought in thirty daughters for his sons from without; and he judged Israel seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abaissan died, and was buried in Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And after him Aelom of Zabulon judged Israel ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Aelom of Zabulon died, and was buried in Aelom in the land of Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And after him Abdon the son of Ellel, the Pharathonite, judged Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he had forty sons, and thirty grandsons, that rode upon seventy colts: and he judged Israel eight years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Abdon the son of Ellel, the Pharathonite, died, and was buried in Pharathon in the land of Ephraim in the mount of Amalec.\par

It is well known that several nations cannot pronounce certain letters. The sound of th cannot be pronounced by the Persians, no more than by some of our Continental neighbours; though it is a common sound among the Arabians. To this day, many of the German Jews cannot articulate ϊ th, for which they substitute ss; thus for baith, a house, they say baiss . there fell; forty Arbaim ooshenayim aleph, "forty and two thousand." Here the ε, and, may mean simple addition; and this number may denote 2, 040 and not 42, 000. \subsection*{Judges 13}
\markright{JUDGES 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the children of Israel yet again committed iniquity before the Lord; and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Phylistines forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was a man of Saraa, of the family of the kindred of Dan, and his name was Manoe, and his wife was barren, and bore not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And an angel of the Lord appeared to the woman, and said to her, Behold, you are barren and have not born; yet you shall conceive a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And now be very cautious, and drink no wine nor strong drink, and eat no unclean thing; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} for behold, you are with child, and shall bring forth a son; and there shall come no razor upon his head, for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb; and he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Phylistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the woman went in, and spoke to her husband, saying, A man of God came to me, and his appearance [was as] of an angel of God, very dreadful; and I did not ask him whence he was, and he did not tell me his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said to me, Behold, you are with child, and shall bring forth a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, and eat no unclean thing; for the child shall be holy to God from the womb until the day of his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Manoe prayed to the Lord and said, I pray you, O Lord my lord, [concerning] the man of God whom you sent; let him now come to us once more, and teach us what we shall do to the child about to be born. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord heard the voice of Manoe, and the angel of God came yet again to the woman; and she sat in the field, and Manoe her husband was not with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the woman hasted, and ran, and brought word to her husband, and said to him, Behold the man who came in [the other] day to me has appeared to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Manoe arose and followed his wife, and came to the man, and said to him, Are you the man that spoke to the woman? and the angel said, I [am]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Manoe said, Now shall [your] word come to pass: what shall be the ordering of the child, and our dealings with him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe, Of all things concerning which I spoke to the woman, she shall beware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} She shall eat of nothing that comes of the vine yielding wine, and let her not drink wine or strong liquor, and let her not eat anything unclean: all things that I have charged her she shall observe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord, Let us detain you here, and prepare before you a kid of the goats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe, If you should detain me, I will not eat of your bread; and if you would offer a whole burnt offering, to the Lord you shall offer it: for Manoe knew not that he [was] an angel of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord, What [is] your name, that [when] your word shall come to pass, we may glorify you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the angel of the Lord said to him, Why do you thus ask after my name; whereas it is wonderful? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Manoe took a kid of the goats and its meat-offering, and offered it on the rock to the Lord; and [the angel] wrought a distinct work, and Manoe and his wife were looking on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when the flame went up above the altar toward heaven, that the angel of the Lord went up in the flame; and Manoe and his wife were looking, and they fell upon their face to the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the angel appeared no more to Manoe and to his wife: then Manoe knew that this [was] an angel of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Manoe said to his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But his wife said to him, If the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received of our hand a whole burnt offering and a meat-offering; and he would not have shown us all these things, neither would he have caused us to hear all these things {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the woman brought forth a son, and she called his name Sampson; and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the Spirit of the Lord began to go out with him in the camp of Dan, and between Saraa and Esthaol.\par

\subsection*{Judges 14}
\markright{JUDGES 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Sampson went down to Thamnatha, and saw a woman in Thamnatha of the daughters of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he went up and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Thamnatha of the daughters of the Phylistines; and now take her to me for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his father and his mother said to him, Are there no daughters of your brethren, and [is there not] a woman of all my people, that you go to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Sampson said to his father, Take her for me, for she [is] right in my eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord, that he sought to be revenged on the Philistines: and at that time the Philistines lorded it over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Sampson and his father and his mother went down to Thamnatha, and he came to the vineyard of Thamnatha; and behold, a young lion roared in meeting him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon him, and he crushed him as he would have crushed a kid of the goats, and there was nothing in his hands: and he told not his father and his mother what he had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was pleasing in the eyes of Sampson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And after some time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion; and behold, a swarm of bees, and honey [were] in the mouth of the lion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he took it into his hands, and went on eating, and he went to his father and his mother, and gave to them, and they did eat; but he told them not that he took the honey out of the mouth of the lion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And his father went down to the woman, and Sampson made there a banquet for seven days, for so the young men are used to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass when they saw him, that they took thirty guests, and they were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Sampson said to them, I propound you a riddle: if you⌃ will indeed tell it me, and discover it within the seven days of the feast, I will you give thirty sheets and thirty changes of raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if you⌃ can’t tell it me, you⌃ shall give me thirty napkins and thirty changes of apparel: and they said to him, Propound your riddle, and we will hear it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said to them, Meat came forth of the eater, and sweetness out of the strong: and they could not tell the riddle for three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass on the fourth day, that they said to the wife of Sampson, Deceive now your husband, and let him tell you the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire: did you⌃ invite us to do us violence? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Sampson's wife wept before him, and said, You do but hate me, and love me not; for the riddle which you have propounded to the children of my people you have not told me: and Sampson said to her, If I have not told it to my father and my mother, shall I tell it to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And she wept before him the seven days, during which their banquet lasted: and it came to pass on the seventh day, that he told her, because she troubled him; and she told it to the children of her people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before sunrise, What [is] sweeter than honey? and what [is] stronger than a lion? and Sampson said to them, If you⌃ had not plowed with my heifer, you⌃ would not have known my riddle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him powerfully, and he went down to Ascalon, and destroyed of the inhabitants thirty men, and took their garments, and gave the changes of raiment to them that told the riddle; and Sampson was very angry, and went up to the house of his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the wife of Sampson was [given] to one of his friends, with whom he was on terms of friendship.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{10} Heb. vocab: bachur (בָּחוּר) = young man; chosen one. Common English renderings: young man; choice one. Often denotes a vigorous young male. \textsuperscript{12} Heb. vocab: chidah (חִידָה) = riddle; dark saying. Common English renderings: riddle; hard question. Used in wisdom and poetic discourse. \textsuperscript{18} Heb. vocab: cheres (חֶרֶס) = sun; earthenware. Common English renderings: sun; potsherd. Context determines sense; rare and varied term.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} thy brethren, uncircumcised; , ; she pleaseth me well Heb. she is right in mine eyes \textsuperscript{4} it was of the Lord That is, God permitted it, that it might be a means of bringing about the deliverance of Israel. Such marriages were forbidden to the Israelites, to keep them separate from the idolatrous nations.; had dominion \textsuperscript{5} against him Heb. in meeting him \textsuperscript{6} the Spirit, ; rent him Now it is not intimated that he did this by his own natural strength; but by the supernatural strength communicated by the Spirit of the Lord coming mightily upon him; which strength was not at his own command, but was, by the will of God, attached to his hair and nazarate., ; he told \textsuperscript{8} to take her; a swarm It is probable, that the flesh had been entirely consumed off the bones, which had become dry; and the body having been throw into some private place (for Samson turned aside to visit it), a swarm of bees had formed their combs in the cavity of the dry ribs, or region of the thorax; nor was it a more improper place than a hollow rock. \textsuperscript{12} a riddle; *marg. the seven; sheets or, shirts. This will receive illustration from Mr. Jackson's description of the Moorish dress: "It resembles that of the ancient patriarchs, as represented in paintings (but the paintings are taken from Asiatic models); that of the men consists of a red cap and turban, a ( kumja ) shirt, which hangs outside of the drawers, and comes below the knee; a ( caftan ) coat, which buttons close before, and down to the bottom with large open sleeves; over which, when they go out of doors, they throw carelessly, and sometimes elegantly, a hayk, or garment of white cotton, silk, or wool, five or six yards long, and five feet wide. The Arabs often dispense with the caftan, and even with the shirt, wearing nothing but the hayk ."; change \textsuperscript{14} Out of the eater; they could \textsuperscript{15} on the seventh day The LXX reads "on the fourth day; " with which the Syriac and Arabic agree. This, as Dr. Wall observes, is certainly right; for it appears from, that she wept the remainder of the seven days; for which there could have been no time, if they did not threaten her till the seventh. Entice; lest we burn, take that we have Heb. possess us, or, impoverish us \textsuperscript{16} Thou dost I have not \textsuperscript{17} the seven or, the rest of the seven days she lay, ; and she told \textsuperscript{19} the Spirit, ; spoil or, apparel\par}

\subsection*{Judges 15}
\markright{JUDGES 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after a time, in the days of wheat harvest, that Sampson visited his wife with a kid, and said, I will go in to my wife even into the chamber: but her father did not suffer him to go in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And her father spoke, saying, I said that you did surely hate her, and I gave her to one of your friends: [is] not her younger sister better than she? let her be to you instead of her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Sampson said to them, Even for once am I guiltless with regard to the Philistines, in that I do mischief among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Sampson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch between two tails, and fastened it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he set fire to the torches, and sent [the foxes] into the corn of the Philistines; and every thing was burnt from the threshing floor to the standing corn, and even to the vineyard and olives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Philistines said, Who [has done] these things? and they said, Sampson the son-in-law of the Thamnite, because he has taken his wife, and given her to one of his friends; and the Philistines went up, and burnt her and her father's house with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Sampson said to them, Though you⌃ may have dealt thus with her, verily I will be avenged of you, and afterwards I will cease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he struck them leg on thigh [with] a great overthrow; and went down and lived in a cave of the rock Etam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Philistines went up, and encamped in Juda, and spread themselves abroad in Lechi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the men of Juda said, Why are you⌃ come up against us? and the Philistines said, We are come up to bind Sampson, and to do to him as he has done to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the three thousand men of Juda went down to the hole of the rock Etam, and they said to Sampson, Know you not that the Philistines rule over us? and what [is] this [that] you have done to us? and Sampson said to them, As they did to me, so have I done to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they said to him, We are come down to bind you to deliver you into the hand of the Philistines: and Sampson said to them, Swear to me that you⌃ will not fall upon me yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they spoke to him, saying, Nay, but we will only bind you fast, and deliver you into their hand, and will by no means kill you: and they bound him with two new ropes, and brought him from that rock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they came to Lechi: and the Philistines shouted, and ran to meet him: and the Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him, and the ropes that were upon his arms became as tow which is burnt with fire; and his bonds were consumed from off his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he found the jaw-bone of an ass that had been cast away, and he put forth his hand and took it, and struck with it a thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Sampson said, With the jaw-bone of an ass I have utterly destroyed them, for with the jaw-bone of an ass I have struck a thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass when he ceased speaking, that he cast the jaw-bone out of his hand; and he called that place the Lifting of the jaw-bone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he was very thirsty, and wept before the Lord, and said, You have been well pleased to grant this great deliverance by the hand of your servant, and new shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And God broke open a hollow place in the jaw, and there came thence water, and he drank; and his spirit returned and he revived: therefore the name of the fountain was called 'The well of the invoker,' which is in Lechi, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a kid; I will go \textsuperscript{2} I verily; I gave; take her Heb. let her be thine \textsuperscript{3} Now shall etc. or, Now shall I be blameless from the Philistines though etc. \textsuperscript{4} caught three Dr. Kennicott and others contend, that for shualim, "foxes, " we should read shoalim, "handfuls, " or sheaves of corn. But: 1. The word lachad, rendered caught, never signifies simply to get or take but always to catch, seize, or take by assault or stratagem. 2. Though the proposed alteration is sanctioned by seven manuscripts, yet all the versions are on the other side. 3. Admitting this alteration, it will be difficult to prove that the word shoal means either a sheaf or a handful of corn in the ear, and straw. It occurs but thrice in Scriptures ( . . ): where it evidently means as much as can be contained in the hollow of the hand; but when handfuls of grain in the shock, or sheaves are intended, very different words are used. See note on, etc. 4. It is not hinted that Samson collected them alone, or in one day; he might have employed many hands and several days in the work. 5. The word shual properly denotes the jackal, which travellers describe as an animal in size between the wolf and fox, gregarious, as many as 200 having been seen together, and the most numerous of any in eastern countries; so that Samson might have caught many of them together in nets.; firebrands or, torches \textsuperscript{11} went Heb. went down the rock Etam Probably near the town Etam, mentioned in . Philistines \textsuperscript{14} the Philistines; the Spirit, ; the cords; loosed Heb. were melted \textsuperscript{15} new jawbone Heb. moist slew, ; a thousand Some would render the words aileph ish, "a chief; " but it is alluph, and not aileph, which signifies a chief; besides which, the Hebrew idiom would, even in that case, require it to be ish alluph, "a man, a chief, " and not alluph ish, "a chief, a man." Add to which, that every version renders it "a thousand men." \textsuperscript{16} with the jawbone There is here a fine paronomasia upon the word chamor, "an ass, " which also signifies "a heap; " bilchee hachamor, chamor chamorathayim, "With the jaw-bone of an ass, a heap upon two heaps." heaps upon heaps Heb. an heap, two heaps \textsuperscript{17} Ramathlehi that is, the lifting up of the jaw-bone, or, the casting away of the jaw-bone \textsuperscript{18} he was sore; Thou hast given, shall; and fall; the uncircumcised \textsuperscript{19} the jaw or, Lehi, This reading is certainly preferable. It was in the place called Lehi where a spring was supernaturally opened. there came his spirit; Enhakkore Samson gave this expressive name to the miraculously springing water, to be as a memorial of the goodness of God to him. En-hakkore, the well of him that cried, which kept him in remembrance both of his own distress which caused him to cry, and the favour of Jehovah to him in answer to his cry. Many a spring of comfort God opens to his people, which may fitly be called by the name En-hakkore, and this instance of Samson's relief should encourage us to trust in God, for when he pleases he can open rivers in high places.; Samson at first gave the name of Ramath-lehi (the lifting up of the jaw-bone) which denoted him great and triumphant, but now he gives it another name, En-hakkore, which denotes him wanting and dependent. \textsuperscript{20} "He seems to have judged South-west Israel during twenty years of their servitude of the Philistines."\par}

\subsection*{Judges 16}
\markright{JUDGES 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Sampson went to Gaza, and saw there a harlot, and went in to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, Sampson is come here: and they compassed him and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and they were quiet all the night, saying, Let us wait till the dawn appear, and we will kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Sampson slept till midnight, and rose up at midnight, and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city with the two posts, and lifted them up with the bar, and laid them on his shoulders, and he went up to the top of the mountain that is before Chebron, and laid them there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass after this that he loved a woman in Alsorech, and her name [was] Dalida. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the princes of the Philistines came up to her, and said to her, Beguile him, and see wherein his great strength [is], and wherewith we shall prevail against him, and bind him to humble him; and we will give you each eleven hundred [pieces] of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Dalida said to Sampson, Tell me, I pray you, wherein [is] your great strength, and wherewith you shall be bound that you may be humbled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Sampson said to her, If they bind me with seven moist cords that have not been spoiled, then shall I be weak and be as one of ordinary men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the princes of the Philistines brought to her seven moist cords that had not been spoiled, and she bound him with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the liers in wait remained with her in the chamber; and she said to him, the Philistines [are] upon you, Sampson: and he broke the cords as if any one should break a thread of tow when it has touched the fire, and his strength was not known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Dalida said to Sampson, Behold, you have cheated me, and told me lies; now then tell me wherewith you shall be bound. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said to her, If they should bind me fast with new ropes with which work has not been done, then shall I be weak, and shall be as another man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Dalida took new ropes, and bound him with them, and the liers in wait came out of the chamber, and she said, The Philistines [are] upon you, Sampson: and he broke them off his arms like a thread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Dalida said to Sampson, Behold, you have deceived me, and told me lies; tell me, I entreat you, wherewith you may be bound: and he said to her, If you should weave the seven locks of my head with the web, and should fasten them with the pin into the wall, then shall I be weak as another man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it came to pass when he was asleep, that Dalida took the seven locks of his head, and wove them with the web, and fastened them with the pin into the wall, and she said, The Philistines [are] upon you, Sampson: and he awoke out of his sleep, and carried away the pin of the web out of the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Dalida said to Sampson, How say you, I love you, when your heart is not with me? this third time you have deceived me, and have not told me wherein [is] your great strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass as she pressed him sore with her words continually, and straitened him, that his spirit failed almost to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then he told her all his heart, and said to her, A razor has not come upon my head, because I have been a holy [one] of God from my mother's womb; if then I should be shaven, my strength will depart from me, and I shall be weak, and I shall be as all [other] men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Dalida saw that he told her all his heart, and she sent and called the princes of the Philistines, saying, Come up yet this once; for he has told me all his heart. And the chiefs of the Philistines went up to her, and brought the money in their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Dalida made Sampson sleep upon her knees; and she called a man, and he shaved the seven locks of his head, and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Dalida said, The Philistines [are] upon you, Sampson: and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at former times, and shake myself; and he knew not that the Lord was departed from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he ground in the prison-house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the hair of his head began to grow as before it was shaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the chiefs of the Philistines met to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon, and to make merry; and they said, God has given into our hand our enemy Sampson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the people saw him, and sang praises to their god; for our god, [said they], has delivered into our hand our enemy, who wasted our land, and who multiplied our slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And when their heart was merry, then they said, Call Sampson out of the prison-house, and let him play before us: and they called Sampson out of the prison-house, and he played before them; and they struck him with the palms of their hands, and set him between the pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Sampson said to the young man that held his hand, Suffer me to feel the pillars on which the house [rests], and I will stay myself upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the house [was] full of men and women, and there were all the chiefs of the Philistines, and on the roof [were] about three thousand men and women looking at the sports of Sampson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Sampson wept before the Lord, and said, O Lord, my lord, remember me, I pray you, and strengthen me, O God, yet this once, and I will requite one recompense to the Philistines for my two eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Sampson took hold of the two pillars of the house on which the house stood, and leaned on them, and laid hold of one with his right hand, and the other with his left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Sampson said, Let my soul perish with the Philistines: and he bowed himself mightily; and the house fell upon the princes, and upon all the people that were in it: and the dead whom Sampson killed in his death were more than those whom he killed in his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And his brethren and his father's house went down, and they took him; and they went up and buried him between Saraa and Esthaol in the sepulchre of his father Manoe; and he judged Israel twenty years.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Gaza, a city of great antiquity, was situated between Raphia and Askelon, twenty-two miles north of the former, and sixteen south of the latter, according to the Antonine Itinerary; three miles from the sea, according to Arrian, and thirty-four from Ashdod or Azotus, according to Diodorus Siculus. It was a place of great strength and importance; and successively belonged to the Philistines, Hebrews, Chaldeans, and Persians; which latter defended it for two months against Alexander the great, who finally took and destroyed it. It was afterwards rebuilt, and alternately possessed by the Egyptians, Syrians, and Jews. The present town, which the Arabs call Razza, is situated on an eminence, and is rendered picturesque by the number of fine minarets which rise majestically above the buildings, with beautiful date trees interspersed. It contains upwards of 2, 000 inhabitants.; an harlot Heb. a woman an harlot and went \textsuperscript{2} compassed; quiet Heb. silent kill him \textsuperscript{3} took; bar and all Heb. with the bar \textsuperscript{4} he loved;, ; in the valley or, by the brook \textsuperscript{5} the lords; Entice;, ; afflict or, humble we will \textsuperscript{7} If they bind; green withs or, new cords, Heb. moist another Heb. one. \textsuperscript{11} If they bind me, ; that never etc. Heb. wherewith work hath not been done \textsuperscript{13} with the web It is evident that this verse ends abruptly, and does not contain a full sense. Houbigant has particularly noticed this, and corrected the text from the Septuagint, which adds after these words: και εγκρουσης τω πασσαλω εις τον τοιχον, και εσομαι ως εις των ανθρωπων ασθενης και εγενετο εν τω κοιμασθαι αυτον και ελαβε Δαλιδα τας επτα σειρας της κεφαλης αυτου, και υφανεν εν τω διασματι, κ.τ.λ . "and shall fasten them with the pin in the wall, I shall become weak like other men, and so it was, that when he slept, Dalida took the seven locks of his head, and wove them with the web, " etc. This is absolutely necessary to complete the sense; else Delilah would appear to do something she was not ordered to do, and to omit what she was commanded. Dr. Kennicott very judiciously observes, that the omission, for such it appears to be, begins and ends with the same word; and that the same word occurring in different places, is a very common cause of omission in Hebrew manuscripts. \textsuperscript{16} she pressed; vexed Heb. shortened, *marg. \textsuperscript{17} all his heart; There hath \textsuperscript{20} I will go, ; the Lord \textsuperscript{21} and put out Heb. and bored out, bound him; grind \textsuperscript{22} the hair; after he was shaven or, as when he was shaven \textsuperscript{24} praised; which slew many of us Heb. and who multiplied our slain \textsuperscript{25} their hearts, ; them Heb. before them sport \textsuperscript{27} and there "Samson, therefore, " says Dr. Shaw, "must have been in a court or area below; and consequently the temple will be of the same kind with the ancient, τεμενη, or sacred enclosures, which were only surrounded either in part, or on all sides, with some plain or cloistered buildings. Several palaces, doutwanas, (as the courts of justice are called in those countries) are built in this fashion. On their public festivals and rejoicings, the roofs of these cloisters are crowded with spectators. I have often seen numbers of people diverted in this manner on the roof of the dey's palace at Algiers; which, like many others, has an advanced cloister, over against the gate of the palace, like a long pent-house, supported by one or two contiguous pillars in front, or centre." the roof \textsuperscript{28} called; remember me; that I may \textsuperscript{29} on which it was borne up or, he leaned on them \textsuperscript{30} me Heb. my soul die; and the house; So the dead \textsuperscript{31} his brethren between Zorah; And he judged\par}
