\subsection*{Judges 17}
\markright{JUDGES 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a man of mount Ephraim, and his name was Michaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said to his mother, The eleven hundred pieces of silver which you took of yourself, and [about which] you cursed me, and spoke in my ears, behold, the silver [is] with me; I took it: and his mother said, Blessed [be] my son of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he restored the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother; and his mother said, I had wholly consecrated the money to the Lord out of my hand for my son, to make a graven and a molten [image], and now I will restore it to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver, and gave them to a silversmith, and he made it a graven and a molten image; and it was in the house of Michaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the house of Michaias [was] to him the house of God, and he made an ephod and theraphin, and he consecrated one of his sons, and he became to him a priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And in those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there was a young man in Bethleem of the tribe of Juda, and he [was] a Levite, and he was sojourning there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the man departed from Bethleem the city of Juda to sojourn in whatever place he might find; and he came as far as mount Ephraim, and to the house of Michaias to accomplish his journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Michaias said to him, Whence come you? and he said to him, I am a Levite of Bethleem Juda, and I go to sojourn in any place I may find. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Michaias said to him, Dwell with me, and be to me a father and a priest; and I will give you ten pieces of silver by the year, and a change of raiment, and your living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Levite went and began to dwell with the man; and the young man was to him as one of his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Michaias consecrated the Levite, and he became to him a priest, and he was in the house of Michaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Michaias said, Now I know that the Lord will do me good, because a Levite has become my priest.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2585, bc 1419, An, Ex, Is, 72 there was It is extremely difficult to fix the chronology of this and the following transactions. Some think them to be here in their natural order; others that they happened in the time of Joshua, or immediately after the ancients who outlived him. All that can be said with certainly is, that they happened when there was no king in Israel; that is, about the time of the judges, or in some time of the anarchy ( .) mount \textsuperscript{2} about etc. Houbigant renders this, "and for which you put me to my oath." cursedst; I took it Blessed \textsuperscript{3} I had wholly; a graven image \textsuperscript{5} an house of gods or, as baith Elohim may also signify, "a house of God."; ephod; teraphim, *marg. consecrated Heb. filled the hand; his sons \textsuperscript{7} Beth-lehem-judah; of the family That is, of the tribe of Judah by his mother; and of that of Levi by his father. \textsuperscript{8} departed; as he journeyed Heb. in making his way \textsuperscript{10} a father; I will give; a suit of apparel or, a double suit, etc. Heb. an order of garments\par}

\subsection*{Judges 18}
\markright{JUDGES 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In those days there was no king in Israel; and in those days the tribe of Dan sought for itself an inheritance to inhabit, because no inheritance had fallen to it until that day in the midst of the tribes of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the sons of Dan sent from their families five men of valour, from Saraa and from Esthaol, to spy out the land and to search it; and they said to them, Go and search out the land. And they came as far as the mount of Ephraim to the house of Michaias and they lodged there, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} in the house of Michaias, and they recognized the voice of the young man the Levite, and turned in there; and said to him, Who brought you in hither? and what do you in this place? and what have you here? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he said to them, Thus and thus did Michaias to me, and he hired me, and I became his priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they said to him, Enquire now of God, and we shall know whether our way will prosper, on which we are going. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priest said to them, Go in peace; your way in which you⌃ go, [is] before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the five men went on, and came to Laisa; and they saw the people in the midst of it dwelling securely, at ease as [is] the manner of the Sidonians, and there is no one perverting or shaming a matter in the land, no heir extorting treasures; and they are far from the Sidonians, and they have no intercourse with any one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the five men came to their brethren to Saraa and Esthaol, and said to their brethren, Why sit you⌃ here [idle]? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they said, Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and, behold, [it is] very good, yet you⌃ are still: delay not to go, and to enter in to possess the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And whenever you⌃ shall go, you⌃ shall come in upon a people secure, and the land [is] extensive, for God has given it into your hand; a place where there is no lack of anything that the earth affords. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And there departed thence of the families of Dan, from Saraa and from Esthaol, six hundred men, girded with weapons of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they went up, and encamped in Cariathiarim in Juda; therefore it was called in that place the camp of Dan, until this day: behold, [it is] behind Cariathiarim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they went on thence to the mount of Ephraim, and came to the house of Michaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the five men who went to spy out the land of Laisa answered, and said to their brethren, You⌃ know that there is in this place an ephod, and theraphin, and a graven and a molten image; and now consider what you⌃ shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they turned aside there, and went into the house of the young man, the Levite, [even] into the house of Michaias, and asked him how he was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the six hundred men of the sons of Dan who were girded with their weapons of war stood by the door of the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the five men who went to spy out the land went up, and entered into the house of Michaias, and the priest stood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they took the graven image, and the ephod, and the theraphin, and the molten image; and the priest said to them, What are you⌃ doing? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they said to him, Be silent, lay your hand upon your mouth, and come with us, and be to us a father and a priest: [is it] better for you to be the priest of the house of one man, or to be the priest of a tribe and house for a family of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the heart of the priest was glad, and he took the ephod, and the theraphin, and the graven image, and the molten image, and went in the midst of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So they turned and departed, and put their children and their property and their baggage before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} They went some distance from the house of Michaias, and, behold, Michaias and the men in the houses near Michaias' house, cried out, and overtook the children of Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the children of Dan turned their face, and said to Michaias, What is the matter with you that you have cried out? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Michaias said, Because you⌃ have taken my graven image which I made, and my priest, and are gone; and what have I remaining? and what [is] this [that] you⌃ say to me, Why cry you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the children of Dan said to him, Let not your voice be heard with us, lest angry men run upon you, and take away your life, and the lives of your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the children of Dan went their way; and Michaias saw that they were stronger than himself, and he returned to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the children of Dan took what Michaias had made, and the priest that he had, and they came to Laisa, to a people quiet and secure; and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And there was no deliverer, because [the city] is far from the Sidonians, and they have no intercourse with men, and it [is] in the valley of the house of Raab; and they built the city, and lived in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; and the name of the city was Ulamais before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the children of Dan set up the graven image for themselves; and Jonathan son of Gerson son of Manasse, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan till the time of the carrying away of the nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they set up for themselves the graven image which Michaias made, all the days that the house of God was in Selom; and it was so in those days [that] there was no king in Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Heb. vocab: batach (בָּטַח) = to trust; feel secure. Common English renderings: trust. Confidence term often directed toward God or false securities.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} no king The word mailech, which generally means a king, is sometimes taken for a supreme ruler, governor, or judge (see note on, and see note on ); and it is probable it should be so understood here, and in the parallel passages., the tribe for unto \textsuperscript{2} men Heb. sons Zorah, ; to spy; mount \textsuperscript{3} they knew They knew by his dialect or mode of pronunciation, that he was not an Ephraimite (see the parallel texts).; and what hast \textsuperscript{6} Go in peace, ; before; the Lord As the Levite uses the word Jehovah, and as the Danites succeeded according to the oracle delivered by him, some learned men are of opinion, that the worship established by Micah was not of an idolatrous kind. \textsuperscript{7} Laish, called Leshem how they; magistrate Heb. possessor, or, heir of restraint; and had no In the most correct copies of the LXX this clause stands thus; και λογος ουκ ην αυτοις μετα Συριας; "and they had no transactions with Syria; " evidently reading instead of ΰγν, adam, man, ΰψν, aram, Syria; words so nearly similar that the only difference between them is in the ψ, raish, and γ, daleth, which in both manuscripts and printed books is sometimes indiscernible. Laish was situated on the frontiers of Syria. \textsuperscript{9} Arise; are ye still be not \textsuperscript{10} secure, God hath; where there \textsuperscript{12} Kirjathjearim A city of Judah, on the confines of Benjamin; distant nine miles from Alia or Jerusalem, in going towards Diospolis or Lydda, according to Eusebius.; Mahanehdan *marg. \textsuperscript{14} Then in these, now therefore \textsuperscript{15} saluted him Heb. asked him of peace, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{19} lay thine This was the token of silence. These men were evidently very ignorant; and absurdly concluded that they should, by taking Micah's gods, secure the presence and favour of the God of Israel, in their expedition and settlement. They perhaps supposed the piety of their motives, and the goodness of their end, would justify the means. But it was a base robbery of Micah, aggravated by the Levite's ingratitude, and their menaces., ; a father \textsuperscript{20} heart; went He was glad of his preferment among the Danites; and went into the crowd, that he might not be discovered by Micah or his family. \textsuperscript{21} and put These men were so confident of success, that they removed their whole families, household goods, cattle, and all. the carriage Kevoodah, from kavad, to be heavy, denotes the luggage or baggage. \textsuperscript{23} What aileth; comest Heb. art gathered together \textsuperscript{25} angry Heb. bitter of soul; *marg. \textsuperscript{28} And there *marg.; far from Probably the people of Laish were originally a colony of the Zidonians; who being an opulent people, and in possession of a strong city, lived in a state of security, not being afraid of their neighbours. In this the Leshemites imitated them, though they appear not to have had the same reason for their confidence; and though they might naturally expect help from their countrymen, yet as they lived at a considerable distance from Sidon, the Danites saw they could strike the blow before the news of the invasion could reach that city.; Bethrehob, Rehob \textsuperscript{29} Dan; who was; Laish, or Dan, was situated at the northern extremity of the land of Canaan, in a beautiful and fertile plain, at the foot of mount Lebanon, on the springs of Jordan, and, according to Eusebius, four miles from Cesarea Philippi, or Paneas, now Banias (with which some have confounded it), towards Tyre. Burckhardt says, that the source of the river El Dhan, or Jordan, is at an hour's distance from Banias, which agrees with Eusebius. \textsuperscript{30} set up;, ; God had graciously performed his promise, in putting these Danites in possession of that which fell to their lot, obliging them thereby to be faithful to him who had been so to them; they inherited the labour of the people, that they might observe his statues. . But the first thing they do after they are settled is to break his laws, by setting up the graven image, attributing their success to that idol, which, if God had not been infinitely patient, would have been their ruin. Thus a prosperous idolater goes on to offend, imputing this his power unto his God. Instead of Manasseh, some would read Moses; as it is found in some manuscripts, in the Vulgate and in the concessions of the most intelligent Jews. But Bp. Patrick takes this to be an idle conceit of the Rabbins, and supposes this Jonathan to be of some other family of the Levites. Yet Kimchi acknowledges, that the Jews, deeply concerned for the honour of their lawgiver, to whom they thought it would be a great dishonour to have a grandson who was an idolater, suspended the letter, π, noon, over the word ξωΡ, Moses, thus ξπωΡδ, as it is found in the Hebrew Bibles; which, by means of the points, they have changed into Manasseh. until; the land Houbigant contends, that, instead of haaretz, "the land, " we should read haaron, "the ark; " for the ε, wav, and ο, noon final, might easily be mistaken for υ, tzadday final; which is the only difference between the two words. This conjecture is the more likely, as the next verse tells us, that Micah's graven image continued at Dan "all the time that the house of God was at Shiloh; " which was till the ark was taken by the Philistines.\par}

\subsection*{Judges 19}
\markright{JUDGES 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a Levite sojourning in the sides of mount Ephraim, and he took to himself a concubine from Bethleem Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And his concubine departed from him, and went away from him to the house of her father to Bethleem Juda, and she was there four months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And her husband rose up, and went after her to speak kindly to her, to recover her to himself; and he had his young man with him, and a pair of asses; and she brought him into the house of her father; and the father of the damsel saw him, and was well pleased to meet him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his father-in-law, the father of the damsel, constrained him, and he stayed with him for three days; and they ate and drank, and lodged there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass on the fourth day that they rose early, and he stood up to depart; and the father of the damsel said to his son-in-law, Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterwards you⌃ shall go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So they two sat down together and ate and drank: and the father of the damsel said to her husband, Tarry now the night, and let your heart be merry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the man rose up to depart; but his father-in-law constrained him, and he stayed and lodged there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the father of the damsel said, Strengthen now your heart, and quit yourself as a soldier till the day decline; and the two ate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the man rose up to depart, he and his concubine, and his young man; but his father-in-law the father of the damsel said to him, Behold now, the day has declined toward evening; lodge here, an let your heart rejoice; and you⌃ shall rise early to-morrow for your journey, and you shall go to your habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But the man would not lodge there, but he arose and departed, and came to the part opposite Jebus, (this is Jerusalem,) and [there was] with him a pair of asses saddled, and his concubine [was] with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they came as far as Jebus: and the day had far advanced, and the young man said to his master, Come, I pray you, and let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusites, and let us lodge in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And his master said to him, We will not turn aside to a strange city, where there is not one of the children of Israel, but we will pass on as far as Gabaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to his young man, Come, and let us draw near to one of the places, and we will lodge in Gabaa or in Rama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they passed by and went on, and the sun went down upon them near to Gabaa, which is in Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they turned aside thence to go in to lodge in Gabaa; and they went in, and sat down in the street of the city, and there was no one who conducted them into a house to lodge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And behold, an old man came out of the field from his work in the evening; and the man was of mount Ephraim, and he sojourned in Gabaa, and the men of the place [were] sons of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he lifted up his eyes, and saw a traveller in the street of the city; and the old man said to him, Whither go you, and whence come you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to him, We are passing by from Bethleem Juda to the sides of mount Ephraim: I am from thence, and I went as far as Bethleem Juda, and I am going home, and there is no man to take me into his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Yet is there straw and food for our asses, and bread and wine for me and my handmaid and the young man with your servants; there is no lack of anything. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the old man said, Peace [be] to you; only be every lack of your upon me, only do you by no means lodge in the street. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he brought him into his house, and made room for his asses; and they washed their feet, and ate and drank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they [were] comforting their heart, when, behold, the men of the city, sons of transgressors, compassed the house, knocking at the door: and they spoke to the old man the owner of the house, saying, Bring out the man who came into your house, that we may know him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the master of the house came out to them, and said, Nay, brethren, do not you⌃ wrong, I pray you, after this man has come into my house; do not you⌃ this folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Behold my daughter a virgin, and the man's concubine: I will bring them out, and humble you⌃ them, and do to them that which is good in your eyes; but to this man do not this folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But the men would not consent to listen to him; so the man laid hold of his concubine, and brought her out to them; and they knew her, and abused her all night till the morning, and let her go when the morning dawned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the woman came toward morning, and fell down at the door of the house where her husband was, until it was light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And her husband rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went forth to go on his journey; and, behold, the woman his concubine had fallen down by the doors of the house, and her hands were on the threshold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he said to her, Rise, and let us go; and she answered not, for she was dead: and he took her upon his ass, and went to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he took his sword, and laid hold of his concubine, and divided her into twelve parts, and sent them to every coast of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it was so, that every one who saw it said, [Such a day] as this has not happened nor has been seen from the day of the going up of the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt until this day: take you⌃ counsel concerning it, and speak.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when there, mount; a concubine Heb. a woman or, a wife.;, ; Beth-lehem-judah \textsuperscript{2} played; four whole months or, a year and four months, Heb. days, four months \textsuperscript{3} went speak; friendly unto her Heb. to her heart, to bring his servant \textsuperscript{5} Comfort Heb. Srengthen; with a morsel \textsuperscript{6} let thine heart, ; , until afternoon, Heb. till the day declined, Merely that they might avoid the heat of the day, which would have been very inconvenient in travelling. \textsuperscript{9} the day draweth etc. Heb. is weak the day groweth to an end Heb. it is the pitching time of the day, . That is, it was near the time in which travellers ordinarily pitched their tents, to take up their lodging for the night. In the latter part of the afternoon, eastern travellers begin to look out for a place for this purpose. So Dr. Shaw observes, "Our constant practice was to rise at break of day, set forward with the sun, and travel to the middle of the afternoon; at which time we began to look out for encampments of Arabs; who, to prevent such parties as ours from living at free charges upon them, take care to pitch in woods, valleys, or places the least conspicuous." to morrow; home Heb. to thy tent \textsuperscript{10} over against Heb. to over against Jebus \textsuperscript{12} Gibeah, a city of Benjamin, and the birth-place of Saul, was situated near Rama and Gibeon, according to Josephus, thirty furlongs north from Jerusalem; or, according to Jerome, about two leagues. \textsuperscript{15} no man There was probably no inn, or house of public entertainment in this place; and therefore they could not have a lodging unless furnished by mere hospitality. But these Benjamites seem to have added to their other vices, avarice and inhospitality, like the inhabitants of Akoura in mount Lebanon, mentioned by Burckhardt. \textsuperscript{18} I am now The LXX read, εις τον οικον μου εγω πορευομαι; "I am going to my own house; " which is probably the true reading, as we find ( ) that he really went home; yet he might have gone previously to Shiloh, or to "the house of the Lord, " because that was also in mount Ephraim. the house; receiveth Heb. gathereth \textsuperscript{19} straw and provender In those countries principally devoted to pasturage, they made little or no hay, but as they raised corn, they took great care of their straw for cattle, which by their mode of threshing was chopped very small. See note on . \textsuperscript{20} Peace be; let all thy wants Here was genuine hospitality: "Keep your bread and wine for yourselves, and your straw and provender for your asses; you may need them before you finish your journey: I will supply all your wants for this night; only do not lodge in the street."; lodge not \textsuperscript{21} So he brought, they washed \textsuperscript{22} they were, the men; sons of Belial;, ; Bring forth \textsuperscript{23} the man do not this folly \textsuperscript{24} Behold The rites of hospitality are regarded as sacred and inviolable in the East, and a man who has admitted a stranger under his roof, is bound to protect him even at the expense of his life. On these high notions only, the influence of which an Asiatic mind alone can appreciate, can the present transaction be either excused or palliated. them; humble ye *marg. so vile a thing Heb. the matter of this folly \textsuperscript{29} divided her It is probable, that with the pieces he sent to each tribe a circumstantial account of the barbarity of the men of Gibeah; and that they considered each of the pieces as expressing an execration. That a similar custom prevailed in ancient times is evident from . It had an inhuman appearance, thus to mangle the corpse of this unhappy woman; but it was intended to excite a keener resentment against so horrible a crime, which called for a punishment proportionally severe.; with her bones\par}

\subsection*{Judges 20}
\markright{JUDGES 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the children of Israel went out, and all the congregation was gathered as one man, from Dan even to Bersabee, and in the land of Galaad, to the Lord at Massepha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all the tribes of Israel stood before the Lord in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Massepha: and the children of Israel came and said, Tell us, where did this wickedness take place? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered and said, I and my concubine went to Gabaa of Benjamin to lodge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the men of Gabaa rose up against me, and compassed the house by night against me; they wished to kill me, and they have humbled my concubine, and she is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I laid hold of my concubine, and divided her in pieces, and sent [the parts] into every coast of the inheritance of the children of Israel; for they have wrought lewdness and abomination in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold, all you⌃ [are] children of Israel; and consider and take counsel here among yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all the people rose up as one man, saying, No one of us shall return to his tent, and no one of us shall return to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now this [is] the thing which shall be done in Gabaa; we will go up against it by lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Moreover we will take ten men for one hundred for all the tribes of Israel, and one hundred for a thousand, and a thousand for ten thousand, to take provision, to cause them to come to Gabaa of Benjamin, to do to it according to all the abomination, which they wrought in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the men of Israel were gathered to the city as one man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the tribes of Israel sent men through the whole tribe of Benjamin, saying, What [is] this wickedness that has been wrought among you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now then give up the men the sons of transgressors that are in Gabaa, and we will put them to death, and purge out wickedness from Israel: but the children of Benjamin consented not to listen to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the children of Benjamin were gathered from their cities to Gabaa, to go forth to fight with the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the children of Benjamin from their cities were numbered in that day, twenty-three thousand, [every] man drawing a sword, besides the inhabitants of Gabaa, who were numbered seven hundred chosen men of all the people, able to use both hands alike; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} All these could sling with stones at a hair, and not miss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the men of Israel, exclusive of Benjamin, were numbered four hundred thousand men that drew sword; all these [were] men of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they arose and went up to Baethel, and enquired of God: and the children of Israel said, Who shall go up for us first to fight with the children of Benjamin? And the Lord said, Juda shall go up first as leader. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the children of Israel rose up in the morning, and encamped against Gabaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they went out, all the men of Israel, to fight with Benjamin, and engaged with them at Gabaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the sons of Benjamin went forth from Gabaa, and they destroyed in Israel on that day two and twenty thousand men down to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the men of Israel strengthened themselves, and again engaged in battle in the place where they had engaged on the first day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the children of Israel went up, and wept before the Lord till evening, and enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall we again draw near to battle with our brethren the children of Benjamin? and the Lord said, Go up against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the children of Israel advanced against the children of Benjamin on the second day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the children of Benjamin went forth to meet them from Gabaa on the second day, and destroyed of the children of Israel yet further eighteen thousand men down to the ground: all these drew sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the children of Israel and all the people went up, and came to Baethel; and they wept, and sat there before the Lord; and they fasted on that day until evening, and offered whole burnt offerings and perfect sacrifices, before the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} for the ark of the Lord God [was] there in those days, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron stood before it in those days; and the children of Israel enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall we yet again go forth to fight with our brethren the sons of Benjamin? and the Lord said, Go up, to-morrow I will give them into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the children of Israel set an ambush against Gabaa round about [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and arrayed themselves against Gabaa as before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the children of Benjamin went out to meet the people, and were all drawn out of the city, and began to strike and kill the people as before in the roads, whereof one goes up to Baethel, and one to Gabaa in the field, about thirty men of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the children of Benjamin said, They fall before us as at the first: but the children of Israel said, Let us flee, and draw them out from the city into the roads; and they did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And all the men rose up out of their places, and engaged in Baal Thamar; and the liers in wait of Israel advanced from their place from Maraagabe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And there came over against Gabaa ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel; and the fight [was] severe; and they knew not that evil was coming upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Lord struck Benjamin before the children of Israel; and the children of Israel destroyed of Benjamin in that day one hundred and twenty-five thousand men: all these drew sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the children of Benjamin saw that they were struck; and the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambuscade which they had prepared against Gabaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And when they retreated, then the liers in wait rose up, and they moved toward Gabaa, and the whole ambush came forth, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the children of Israel had a signal of battle with the liers in wait, that they should send up a signal of smoke from the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And the children of Israel saw that the liers in wait had seized Gabaa, and they stood in line of battle; and Benjamin began to strike down wounded ones among the men of Israel about thirty men; for they said, Surely they fall again before us, as in the first battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the signal went up increasingly over the city as a pillar of smoke; and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold the destruction of the city went up to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And the men of Israel turned back, and the men of Benjamin hasted, because they saw that evil had come upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And they turned to the way of the wilderness from before the children of Israel, and fled: but the battle overtook them, and they from the cities destroyed them in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And they cut down Benjamin, and pursued him from Nua closely till they came opposite Gabaa on the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And there fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand men: all these [were] men of might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And the rest turned, and fled to the wilderness to the rock of Remmon; and the children of Israel picked off of them five thousand men; and the children of Israel went down after them as far as Gedan, and they struck of them two thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And all that fell of Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men that drew sword in that day: all these were men of might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And the rest turned, and fled to the wilderness to the rock of Remmon, even [six] hundred men; and they sojourned four months in the rock of Remmon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And the children of Israel returned to the children of Benjamin, and struck them with the edge of the sword from the city of Methla, even to the cattle, and every thing that was found in all the cities: and they burnt with fire the cities they found.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{26} Heb. vocab: tsum (צוּם) = to fast. Common English renderings: fast. Important for repentance, mourning, and seeking God. Gk. vocab: nēsteia (νηστεία) = fasting. Common English renderings: fasting. A term for fasting in repentance, mourning, or devotion.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Then all, ; as one man; from Dan; with the; unto the, in Mizpeh; It does not appear that the Israelites on this occasion, were summoned by the authority of any one common head, but they came together by the consent and agreement, as it were, of one common heart, fired with a holy zeal for the honour of God and Israel. The place of their meeting was Mizpeh; they gathered together unto the Lord there; for Mizpeh was so very near to Shiloh, that their encampment might very well be supposed to reach from Mizpeh to Shiloh. Shiloh was a small town, and therefore, when there was a general meeting of the people to present themselves before God, they chose Mizpeh for their head quarters, which was the next adjoining city of note; perhaps, because they were not willing to give that trouble to Shiloh, which so great an assembly would occasion; it being the residence of the priests that attended the tabernacle. \textsuperscript{3} the children of Benjamin; how was \textsuperscript{4} the Levite Heb. the man the Levite I came \textsuperscript{5} And the men beset and my concubine forced Heb. humbled \textsuperscript{6} cut her folly in Israel \textsuperscript{7} ye are all;, give here \textsuperscript{8} as one man, We will not \textsuperscript{13} deliver children of Belial; put away, ; would not; The conduct of the Israelites was very equitable in this demand; but perhaps the rulers or elders of Gibeah ought previously to have been applied to, to deliver up the criminals to justice. However, the refusal of the Benjamites, and their protection of those who had committed this horrible wickedness, because they were of their own tribe, prove them to have been deeply corrupted, and (all their advantages considered) as ripe for divine vengeance as the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah had been. Confiding in their own valour and military skill, they seen to have first prepared for battle in this unequal contest with such superior numbers. \textsuperscript{16} lefthanded Itter yad yemeeno, "obstructed in his right hand; " so the Chaldee Targum, gemid beedaih deyammeena, contracted or impeded in his right hand." Lev. Clerc observes, that the 700 men left-handed seem therefore to have been made slingers, because they could not use the right hand, which is employed in managing heavier arms; and they could discharge the stones from the sling in a direction against which their opponents were not upon their guard, and thus do the greater execution.; sling stones The sling was a very ancient warlike instrument; and, in the hands of those who were skilled in the use of it, produced astonishing effects. The inhabitants of the islands of Baleares, now Majorca and Minorca, were the most celebrated slingers of antiquity. They did not permit their children to break their fast, till they had struck down the bread they had to eat from the top of a pole, or some distant eminence. Vegetius tells us, that slingers could in general hit the mark at 600 feet distance. \textsuperscript{23} wept; And the It seems most evident that the Israelites did not seek the protection of God. When they "went to the house of God, " ( ), it was not to enquire concerning the expediency of the war, nor of its success, but which of the tribes should begin the attack, and here the question is, "Shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother?" Having so much right on their side, they had no doubt of the justice of their cause, and the propriety of their conduct; and having such a superiority of numbers, they had no doubt of success. But God humbled them, and delivered them into the hands of their enemies; and shewed them that the race was not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong. \textsuperscript{27} inquired; the ark; The loss of two battles at length brought this stiff-necked people to enquire of the Lord; for all the company at this time met at Shiloh, and kept a day of fasting and prayer with great earnestness and solemnity. "Behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear." \textsuperscript{28} Phinehas It is evident, from this mention of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, that these transactions must have taken place not long after the death of Joshua.;, stood, Shall I yet; Go up \textsuperscript{29} Israel Though God had promised them success, they knew they could expect it only by the use of proper means. Hence they used all prudent precaution, and employed all their military skill. liers \textsuperscript{31} drawn smite of the people, and kill, as at Heb. smite of the people wounded as at, etc the house of God or, Beth-el, Gibeah.; thirty \textsuperscript{32} Let us flee This was done, not only because they had placed an ambuscade behind Gibeah, which was to enter and burn the city as soon as the Benjamites left it; but it would seem, that the slingers, by being within the city and its fortifications, had great advantage over the Israelites by their slings, when they could not come among them with their swords, unless they got them in the plain country. \textsuperscript{33} rose up put themselves There appear to have been three divisions of the Israelitish army. One at Baal-tamar (which was situated, says Eusebius, near Gibeah); a second behind the city in ambush; and a third, who skirmished with the Benjamites before Gibeah. \textsuperscript{35} twenty; Though the numbers of the Israelites were immensely superior to those of Benjamin, though the stratagem was well laid and ingeniously executed, and the battle bravely fought, yet the inspired historian ascribes the victory to the hand of the Lord, as entirely as if he had smitten the Benjamites by a miracle. \textsuperscript{37} the liers in wait hasted drew themselves along or, made a long sound with the trumpets \textsuperscript{38} Now there From this verse to the end of the chapter, we have the details of the same operations which are mentioned, in a general way, in the preceding verses of this chapter. sign or, time; *marg. and Heb. with flame Heb. elevation \textsuperscript{39} And when smite and kill Heb. smite the wounded \textsuperscript{40} a pillar; looked flame Heb. whole consumption \textsuperscript{41} were amazed; was come upon them Heb. touched them \textsuperscript{43} enclosed with ease or, from Menuchah, etc over against Heb. unto over against \textsuperscript{47} six hundred; rock of Rimmon, The rock Rimmon was doubtless a strong place; but it is uncertain where situated. It is probable however, that it was near, and took its name from, the village of Remmon, mentioned by Eusebius, fifteen miles north from Jerusalem. It appears that rocks are still resorted to in the East, as places of security; and some of them are even capable of sustaining a siege. Deut. Lam. Roque says, that "The Grand Seignior, wishing to seize the person of the emir (Fakr-eddin, prince of the Druses), gave orders to the pacha to take him prisoner. He accordingly came in search of him, with a new army, in the district of Chouf, which is part of mount Lebanon, wherein is the village of Gesin, and close to it, the rock which served for a retreat to the emir. It is named in Arabic, Magara Gesin, i.e., the cavern of Gessin, by which name it is famous. The pacha pressed the emir so closely, that this unfortunate prince was obliged to shut himself up in the cleft of a great rock, with a small number of his officers. The pacha besieged him there several months; and was going to blow up the rock by a mine, when the emir capitulated." \textsuperscript{48} smote them; came to hand Heb. was found they came to Heb. were found\par}

\subsection*{Judges 21}
\markright{JUDGES 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now the children of Israel swore in Massephath, saying, No man of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the people came to Baethel, and sat there until evening before God: and they lifted up their voice and wept with a great weeping; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and said, Therefore, O Lord God of Israel, has this come to pass, that today one tribe should be counted [as missing] from Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass on the morrow that the people rose up early, and built there an altar, and offered up whole burnt offerings and peace offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the children of Israel said, Who of all the tribes of Israel, went not up in the congregation to the Lord? for there was a great oath concerning those who went not up to the Lord to Massephath, saying, He shall surely be put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Israel relented toward Benjamin their brother, and said, To-day one tribe is cut off from Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} What shall we do for wives for the rest that remain? whereas we have sworn by the Lord, not to give them of our daughters for wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said, What one [man is there] of the tribes of Israel, who went not up to the Lord to Massephath? and, behold, no man came to the camp from Jabis Galaad to the assembly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the people were numbered, and there was not there a man from the inhabitants of Jabis Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men of the strongest, and they charged them, saying, Go you⌃ and strike the inhabitants of Jabis Galaad with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And this shall you⌃ do: every male and every woman that has known the lying with man you⌃ shall devote [to destruction], but the virgins you⌃ shall save alive: and they did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they found among the inhabitants of Jabis Galaad four hundred young virgins, who had not known man by lying with him; and they brought them to Selom in the land of Chanaan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And all the congregation sent and spoke to the children of Benjamin in the rock Remmon, and invited them to [make] peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Benjamin returned to the children of Israel at that time, and the children of Israel gave them the women whom they [had] save alive of the daughters of Jabis Galaad; and they were content. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the people relented for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do for wives for them that remain? for the women have been destroyed out of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they said, [There must be] an inheritance of them that are escaped of Benjamin; and [so] a tribe shall not be destroyed out of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For we shall not be able to give them wives of our daughters, because we swore among the children of Israel, saying, Cursed [is] he that gives a wife to Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they said, Behold! now [there is] a feast of the Lord from year to year in Selom, which is on the north of Baethel, eastward on the way that goes up from Baethel to Sychem, and from the south of Lebona. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they charged the children of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in wait in the vineyards; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and you⌃ shall see; and behold! if there come out the daughters of the inhabitants of Selom to dance in dances, then shall you⌃ go out of the vineyards and seize for yourselves every man a wife of the daughters of Selom, and go you⌃ into the land of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it shall come to pass, when their fathers or their brethren come to dispute with us, that we will say to them, Grant them freely to us, for we have not taken every man his wife in the battle: because you⌃ did not give to them according to the occasion, you⌃ transgressed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the children of Benjamin did so; and they took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they seized: and they went and returned to their inheritance, and built the cities, and lived in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the children of Israel went thence at that time every man to his tribe and his kindred; and they went thence every man to his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And in those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own sight.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} had sworn, ; There; his daughter \textsuperscript{8} Jabeshgilead This place, as its name imports, was situated in Gilead, east of Jordan. Eusebius and Jerome say it was a great town in their time, standing upon a hill, six miles south from Pella, in the way to Geresa, now Djerash. The Wady Yabes, mentioned by Burckhardt, which empties itself into the Jordan, in the neighbourhood of Bisan or Beth-shan (see note on ), and upon which Pella was situated (celebrated by Pliny, 1. v. c. 18, for its fine waters), seems to have taken its name from Jabesh. Near this spot, we must therefore look for its site; and the place called Kalaat Rabbad seems to correspond, very nearly, to the spot; though it probably still retains among the Arabs its ancient name. \textsuperscript{10} Go and smite As they had sworn to destroy those who would not assist in the war ( ), they determined to destroy the men of Jabesh, and to leave none except the virgins; and to give these to the 600; Benjamites who had escaped to the rock of Rimmon. The whole account is dreadful. The crime of the men of Gibeah was of the deepest dye; the punishment involving both the guilty and innocent, was extended to the most criminal excess, and their mode of remedying the evil they had occasioned was equally abominable. \textsuperscript{11} every male; hath lain by man Heb. knoweth the lying with man \textsuperscript{12} virgins Heb. women virgins Shiloh \textsuperscript{13} to speak Heb. and spake and called the rock Rimmon; call peaceably or, proclaim peace \textsuperscript{19} a feast;, ;, ; yearly Heb. from year to year on the east side or, toward the sun rising of the highway or, on Lebonah Maundrell supposes, that either Khan Leban, which is situated on the eastern side of a "delicious vale, " four leagues south from Shechem, and two leagues north from Bethel, or the village of Leban, which is on the opposite side, occupies the site of the ancient Lebonah. It is eight hours, or about 24 miles, from Jerusalem, according to Dr. Richardson. \textsuperscript{22} Be favourable unto them or, Gratify us in them, each man; give unto \textsuperscript{23} and they went It appears that the Benjamites acted in the most honourable way to the women they had thus violently carried off, and we may rest assured, that they took them to an inheritance more than equal to their own. But this transaction, as well as the indiscriminate massacre of the people of Jabesh-gilead, as Dr. Gray observes, was certainly stamped with injustice and cruelty; and must be condemned on those principles which the Scriptures elsewhere furnish. repaired\par}

\section*{Ruth Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Samuel (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Ancient Jewish tradition commonly linked Ruth with Samuel; the Davidic genealogy and early-monarchy perspective fit that setting.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT statement names Ruth's writer, but Matthew 1 confirms Ruth's place in the true messianic genealogy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} early monarchy\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} likely 11th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology places Ruth in the days of the judges, with the genealogy reaching David in the monarchy's opening era.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The LXX preserves the same judges-era setting and Davidic trajectory, with only limited textual divergence from the MT.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} A famine-era Bethlehem setting during the judges, leading to the Davidic line through Ruth and Boaz.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To display covenant kindness, providence, and the inclusion of Ruth the Moabitess in the line of David and Messiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} kindness; redemption; providence; Davidic line; kinsman-redeemer; covenant mercy\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Naomi's emptiness 1; Ruth and Boaz meet 2; Redemption arranged 3; Redemption completed and genealogy 4. 4Q Ruth a (4Q104) | Subst. about 50 BC 4Q Ruth fragments provide the earliest Hebrew witness to the book | Heb. 1st century BC Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus preserve Ruth in Greek\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Retelling of Ruth within Israel's sacred history (Josephus)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1st century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Ruth is comparatively stable textually, though Qumran and Greek evidence remain useful at individual points.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Ruth 1}
\markright{RUTH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land: and a man went from Bethleem Juda to sojourn in the land of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the man's name [was] Elimelech, and his wife's name Noemin, and the names of his two sons Maalon and Chelaion, Ephrathites of Bethleem of Juda: and they came to the land of Moab, and remained there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Elimelech the husband of Noemin died; and she was left, and her two sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they took to themselves wives, women of Moab; the name of the one [was] Orpha, and the name of the second Ruth; and they lived there about ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And both Maalon and Chelaion died also; and the woman was left of her husband and her two sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And she rose up and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned out of the country of Moab, for she heard in the country of Moab that the Lord [had] visited his people to give them bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And she went forth out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her: and they went by the way to return to the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Noemin said to her daughter-in-law, Go now, return each to the house of her mother: the Lord deal mercifully with you, as you⌃ have dealt with the dead, and with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Lord grant you that you⌃ may find rest each of you in the house of her husband: and she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice, and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they said to her, We will return with you to your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Noemin said, Return now, my daughters; and why do you⌃ go with me? have I yet sons in my womb to be your husbands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Turn now, my daughters, for I am too old to be married: for I said, Suppose I were married, and should bear sons; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} would you⌃ wait for them till they should be grown? or would you⌃ refrain from being married for their sakes? Not so, my daughters; for I am grieved for you, that the hand of the Lord has gone forth against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they lifted up their voice, and wept again; and Orpha kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people; but Ruth followed her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Noemin said to Ruth, Behold, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; turn now you also after your sister-in-law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave you, or to return from following you; for wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you lodge, I will lodge; your people [shall be] my people, and your God my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And wherever you die, I will die, and there will I be buried: the Lord do so to me, and more also, [if I leave you], for death [only] shall divide between me and you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Noemin seeing that she was determined to go with her, ceased to speak to her any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they went both of them until they came to Bethleem: and it came to pass, when they arrived at Bethleem, that all the city rang with them, and they said, Is this Noemin? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And she said to them, Nay, do not call me Noemin; call me 'Bitter,' for the Mighty One has dealt very bitterly with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty: and why call you⌃ me Noemin, whereas the Lord has humbled me and the Mighty One has afflicted me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So Noemin and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, returned from the country of Moab; and they came to Bethleem in the beginning of barley harvest.\par

\subsection*{Ruth 2}
\markright{RUTH 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Noemin had [a friend] an acquaintance of her husband, and the man [was] a mighty man of the kindred of Elimelech, and his name [was] Booz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ruth the Moabitess said to Noemin, Let me go now to the field, and I will glean among the ears behind the man with whoever I shall find favor: and she said to her, Go, daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And she went; and came and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and she happened by chance to come on a portion of the land of Booz, of the kindred of Elimelech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And, behold, Booz came from Bethleem, and said to the reapers, The Lord [be] with you: and they said to him, The Lord bless you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Booz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, Whose [is] this damsel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And his servant who was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel who returned with Noemin out of the land of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the reapers: and she came and stood from morning till evening, and rested not [even] a little in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Booz said to Ruth, Have you not heard, [my] daughter? go not to glean in another field; and depart not you hence, join yourself here with my damsels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} [Let] your eyes [be] on the field where [my men] shall reap, and you shall go after them: behold, I have charged the young men not to touch you: and when you shall thirst, then you shall go to the vessels, and drink of that which the young men shall have drawn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And she fell upon her face, and did reverence to the ground, and said to him, How is it that I have found grace in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, whereas I am a stranger? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Booz answered and said to her, It has fully been told me how you have dealt with your mother-in-law after the death of your husband; and how you did leave your father and your mother, and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you knew not before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The Lord recompense your work; may a full reward be given you of the Lord God of Israel, to whom you have come to trust under his wings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And she said, Let me find grace in your sight, my lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken kindly to your handmaid, and behold, I shall be as one of your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Booz said to her, Now [it is] time to eat; come here, and you shall eat of the bread, and you shall dip your morsel in the vinegar: and Ruth sat by the side of the reapers: and Booz handed her meal, and she ate, and was satisfied, and left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And she rose up to glean; and Booz charged his young men, saying, Let her even glean among the sheaves, and reproach her not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And do you⌃ by all means carry it for her, and you⌃ shall surely let fall for her some of that which is heaped up; {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} kinsman, a mighty; Boaz, according the Targumist, was the same as Ibzan.; Booz \textsuperscript{3} gleaned; hap was Heb. hap happened \textsuperscript{6} the servant This seems to have been a kind of steward, who had the under- management of the estate., ; It is the \textsuperscript{7} I pray; continued; in the house It seems that the reapers were now resting in a tent, erected for that purpose; and that Ruth had just gone in with them, to take her rest also. \textsuperscript{13} Let me find or, I find favour, ; friendly Heb. to the heart; not like \textsuperscript{14} At mealtime; dip thy morsel Vinegar, robb of fruits, etc., are used for this purpose in the East to the present day; into which, says Dr. Shaw, they dip the bread and hand together. parched; she did; was sufficed \textsuperscript{15} glean The word glean comes from the French glaner to gather ears or grains of corn. This was formerly a general custom in England and Ireland. The poor went into the fields, and collected the straggling ears of corn after the reapers; and it was long supposed that this was their right, and that the law recognized it; but although it has been an old custom, it is now settled by a solemn judgment of the Court of Common Pleas, that a right to glean in the harvest field cannot be claimed by any person at common law. Any person may permit or prevent it on his own grounds. By the Irish Acts, 25; Henry VIII. c. 1, and 28; Henry VIII. c. 24, gleaning and leasing are so restricted as to be in fact prohibited in that part of the United Kingdom. reproach Heb. shame \textsuperscript{20} Blessed; hath not; one of our or, one that hath right to redeem \textsuperscript{21} Thou shalt; young men The word hannearim should be translated the servants; both male and female being included in it, the latter especially (see note on, see note on, and see note on ). \textsuperscript{22} Ruth is said, by the Targumist, to have been the daughter of Eglon, king of Moab. It is good; meet or, fall not upon thee\par}

\subsection*{Ruth 3}
\markright{RUTH 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And she lodged with her mother-in-law: and Noemin her mother-in-law said to her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And now [is] not Booz our kinsman, with whose damsels you were? behold, he winnows barley this night in the floor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But do you wash, and anoint yourself, and put your raiment upon you, and go up to the threshing floor: do not discover yourself to the man until he has done eating and drinking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it shall come to pass when he lies down, that you shall mark the place where he lies down, and shall come and lift up the covering of his feet, and shall lie down; and he shall tell you what you shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Ruth said to her, All that you shall say, I will do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And she went down to the threshing floor, and did according to all that her mother-in-law enjoined her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Booz ate and drank, and his heart was glad, and he came to lie down by the side of the heap of corn; and she came secretly, and lifted up the covering of his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass at midnight that the man was amazed, and troubled, and behold, a woman lay at his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said, Who are you? and she said, I am your handmaid Ruth; spread therefore your skirt over your handmaid, for you are a near relation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Booz said, Blessed [be] you of the Lord God, [my] daughter, for you have made your latter kindness greater than the former, in that you follow not after young men, whether [any be] poor or rich. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now fear not, my daughter, whatever you shall say I will do to you; for all the tribe of my people knows that you are a virtuous woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now I am truly akin to you; nevertheless there is a kinsman nearer than I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Lodge [here] for the night, and it shall be in the morning, if he will do the part of a kinsman to you, well—let him do it: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to you, I will do the kinsman's part to you, [as] the Lord lives; lie down till the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And she lay at his feet until the morning; and she rose up before a man could know his neighbor; and Booz said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to her, Bring the apron that is upon you: and she held it, and he measured six measures of barley, and put them upon her, and she went into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Ruth went in to her mother-in-law, and she said to her, [My] daughter! and [Ruth] told her all that the man had done to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And she said to her, He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said to me, Go not empty to your mother-in-law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she said, Sit still, [my] daughter, until you shall know how the matter will fall out; for the man will not rest until the matter be accomplished this day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Gk. vocab: pteryx (πτέρυξ) = wing; edge; extremity. Common English renderings: wing. Can denote a literal wing or a figurative covering edge.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} shall I not; may be \textsuperscript{2} is not Boaz; with whose, he winnoweth It is probable that the winnowing of grain was effected by taking up a portion of the corn in a sieve, and letting it down slowly in the wind; thus the grain would, by its own weight, fall in one place, while the chaff, etc., would be carried a distance by the wind. It is said here that this was done at night; probably what was threshed out in the day was winnowed in the evening, when the sea breeze set in, which was common in Palestine. \textsuperscript{4} uncover his feet or, lift up the clothes that are on his feet \textsuperscript{7} his heart;, ; , ; went to lie Such was the simplicity of those early times, that the most wealthy persons looked after their own affairs, both at home and in the field. These threshing-floors were covered at top to keep off the rain, but lay open on all sides, that the wind might come in freely, for winnowing the corn; which being done, it is probable they were shut up at night, with doors fitted to them, that if any one lay there he might be kept warm, and the corn be secured from robbers. \textsuperscript{9} Ruth; spread therefore Hebrew "spread thy wing; " the emblem of protection; and a metaphor taken from the young of fowls, which run under the wings of their mother from birds of prey. Even to the present day, when a Jew marries a woman, he throws the skirts of his talith over her, to signify that he has taken her under his protection. a near kinsman or, one that has right to redeem \textsuperscript{13} if he will; the Lord liveth \textsuperscript{15} veil or sheet, or apron, The word mitpachath has been variously rendered. The LXX translate it περιζωμα, an apron, and Vulgate, pallium, a cloak. By the circumstances of the story, it must have been of a considerable size; and accordingly Dr. Shaw thinks it was no other than the hyke, the finer sort of which, such as are still worn by ladies and persons of distinction among the Arabs, he takes to answer to the πεπλος, or robe, of the ancient Greeks. he measured; six measures The quantity of this barley is uncertain. The Targum renders it, shith sein, "six seahs ." A seah contained about two gallons and a half, six of which must have been a very heavy load for a woman, and so the Targumist thought, for he adds, "And she received strength from the Lord to carry it." \textsuperscript{16} Who art thou Or, as the Vulgate renders, Quid egisti filiȧ "What hast thou done, my daughter?"\par}

For this relative was not a brother, but simply a kinsman; and the shoe was not pulled off by Ruth, but by the kinsman himself. The Targumist, instead of his shoe, renders "his right hand glove, " it probably being the custom, in his time, to give that instead of a shoe. Jarchi says, "When we purchase anything new, it is customary to give, instead of a shoe, a handkerchief or veil." \textsuperscript{10} have I; the name; ye are witnesses \textsuperscript{11} the Lord; Rachel, ; build; do thou worthily or, get thee riches, or power Ephratah; be famous Heb. proclaim thy name \textsuperscript{12} the house; whom; of the seed \textsuperscript{13} am 2697, bc 1307, An, Ex, Is, 184 Boaz the Lord \textsuperscript{14} the women; Blessed; which hath left thee Heb. caused to cease unto thee kinsman or, redeemer that his \textsuperscript{15} a nourisher etc. Heb. to nourish thy grey hairs, ; for thy better \textsuperscript{17} the women Obed That is, δουλευων, serving, or a servant, as Josephus interprets it. \textsuperscript{20} Nahshon; Naasson Salmon or, Samlah \textsuperscript{21} Salmon, Salma; and Boaz; Booz\par}
