\section*{1 Samuel Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Samuel with later prophetic completion by Nathan and Gad\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Conservative tradition often understands Samuel to have written the early material, with Nathan and Gad completing the later record; compare 1 Chronicles 29:29.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The NT treats the Samuel narrative as real sacred history; Acts 3:24 names Samuel prominently among the prophets.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 11th-10th century BC across Samuel's ministry into David's early reign\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology covers the transition from judgeship to monarchy, from Samuel to Saul and David.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same transition period but sometimes preserves notable readings differing from the MT, especially in Samuel.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Israel's transition from tribal confederation to monarchy under Samuel, Saul, and David.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To show the rise of the monarchy under God's sovereign rule, the failure of Saul, and the divine choice of David.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} prophetic leadership; kingship; covenant obedience; rejection of Saul; rise of David\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Samuel and Eli 1-7; Saul's rise and fall 8-15; David's rise under Saul's shadow 16-31.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Samuel b (4Q52) about 250 BC | Subst. 4Q Samuel a and related Samuel manuscripts preserve extensive early Hebrew evidence of both 1 and 2 Samuel 3rd-1st centuries BC | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve Samuel in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Retelling of Samuel-Saul-David history by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Samuel is one of the most textually important books in MT/LXX comparison; 4QSamuel often aligns with the LXX against the MT and can preserve older readings.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives the Samuel corpus as truthful prophetic history and treats the strong Qumran-LXX evidence as valuable for recovering earlier Hebrew readings where the MT appears secondary.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Kings I}
\markboth{KINGS I}{}
\subsection*{Kings I 1}
\markright{KINGS I 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There was a man of Armathaim Sipha, of mount Ephraim, and his name [was] Helkana, a son of Jeremeel the son of Elias the son of Thoke, in Nasib Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he [had] two wives; the name of the one [was] Anna, and the name of the second Phennana. And Phennana had children, but Anna had no child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the man went up from year to year from his city, from Armathaim, to worship and sacrifice to the Lord God of Sabaoth at Selom: and [there were] Heli and his two sons Ophni and Phinees, the priests of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the day came, and Helkana sacrificed, and gave portions to his wife Phennana and her children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And to Anna he gave a prime portion, because she had no child, only Helkana loved Anna more than the other; but the Lord [had] closed her womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the Lord gave her no child in her affliction, and according to the despondency of her affliction; and she was dispirited on this account, that the Lord shut up her womb so as not to give her a child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So she did year by year, in going up to the house of the Lord; and she was dispirited, and wept, and did not eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Helkana her husband said to her, Anna: and she said to him, Here [am] I, my lord: and he said to her, What ails you that you weep? and why do you not eat? and why does your heart strike you? [am] I not better to you than ten children? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Anna rose up after they had eaten in Selom, and stood before the Lord: and Heli the priest [was] on a seat by the threshold of the temple of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And she [was] very much grieved in spirit, and prayed to the Lord, and wept abundantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, O Lord God of Sabaoth, if you welt indeed look upon the humiliation of your handmaid, and remember me, and give to your handmaid a boy, then will I indeed dedicate him to you till the day of his death; and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink, and no razor shall come upon his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it came to pass, while she was long praying before the Lord, that Heli the priest marked her mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And she was speaking in her heart, and her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: and Heli accounted her a drunken woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the servant of Heli said to her, How long will you be drunken? take away your wine from you, and go out from the presence of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Anna answered and said, Nay, my lord, [I live] in a hard day, and I have not drunk wine or strong drink, and I pour out my soul before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Count not your handmaid for a pestilent woman, for by reason of the abundance of my importunity I have continued [my prayer] until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Heli answered and said to her, Go in peace: the God of Israel give you all your petition, which you have asked of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she said, Your handmaid has found favor in your eyes: and the woman went her way, and entered into her lodging, and ate and drank with her husband, and her countenance was no more sad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they rise early in the morning, and worship the Lord, and they go their way: and Helkana went into his house at Armathaim, and knew his wife Anna; and the Lord remembered her, and she conceived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when the time was come, that she brought forth a son, and called his name Samuel, and said, Because I asked him of the Lord God of Sabaoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the man Helkana and all his house went up to offer in Selom the yearly sacrifice, and his vows, and all the tithes of his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But Anna did not go up with him, for she said to her husband, [I will not go up] until the child goes up, when I have weaned him, and he shall be presented before the Lord, and he shall abide there continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Helkana her husband said to her, Do that which is good in your eyes, abide still until you shall have weaned him; but may the Lord establish that which comes out of your mouth: and the woman tarried, and suckled her son until she had weaned him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And she went up with him to Selom with a calf of three years old, and loaves, and an ephah of fine flour, and a bottle of wine: and she entered into the house of the Lord in Selom, and the child with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they brought him before the Lord; and his father killed his offering which he offered from year to year to the Lord; and he brought near the child, and killed the calf; and Anna the mother of the child brought him to Heli. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And she said, I pray you, my lord, as your soul lives, I [am] the woman that stood in your presence with you while praying to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For this child I prayed; and the Lord has given me my request that I asked of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And I lend him to the Lord all his days that he lives, a loan to the Lord: and she said,\par

\subsection*{Kings I 2}
\markright{KINGS I 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God; my mouth is enlarged over my enemies, I have rejoiced in your salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For there is none holy as the Lord, and there is none righteous as our God; there is none holy besides you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Boast not, and utter not high things; let not high-sounding words come out of your mouth, for the Lord [is] a God of knowledge, and God prepares his own designs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The bow of the mighty has waxed feeble, and the weak have girded themselves with strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They that were full of bread are brought low; and the hungry have forsaken the land; for the barren has born seven, and she that abounded in children has waxed feeble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to the grave, and brings up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord makes poor, and makes rich; he brings low, and lifts up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He lifts up the poor from the earth, and raises the needy from the dunghill; to seat him with the princes of the people, and causing them to inherit the throne of glory: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} granting his petition to him that prays; and he blesses the years of the righteous, for by strength can’t man prevail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The Lord will weaken his adversary; the Lord [is] holy. Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor let the mighty man boast in his strength, and let not the rich man boast in his wealth; but let him that boasts boast in this, to understand and know the Lord, and to execute judgment and justice in the midst of the earth. The Lord has gone up to the heavens, and has thundered: he will judge the extremities of the earth, and he gives strength to our kings, and will exalt the horn of his Christ. And she left him there before the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and departed to Armathaim: and the child ministered in the presence of the Lord before Heli the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the sons of Heli the priest [were] evil sons, not knowing the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the priest's claim from every one of the people that sacrificed [was this:] the servant of the priest came when the flesh was in seething, and a flesh-hook of three teeth [was] in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he struck it into the great caldron, or into the brazen vessel, or into the pot, and whatever came up with the flesh-hook, the priest took for himself: so they did to all Israel that came to sacrifice to the Lord in Selom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And before the fat was burnt for a sweet savor, the servant of the priest would come, and say to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest, and I will by no means take of you sodden flesh out of the caldron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And [if] the man that sacrificed said, First let the fat be burned, as it is fit, and take for yourself of all things which your soul desires: then he would say, Nay, for you shall give it me now; and if not I will take it by force. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord, for they set at nothing the offering of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Samuel ministered before the Lord, a child girded with a linen ephod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And his mother made him a little doublet, and brought it to him from year to year, in her going up in company with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Heli blessed Helcana and his wife, saying The Lord recompense to you seed of this woman, in return for the loan which you have lent to the Lord: and the man returned to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord visited Anna, and she bore yet three sons, and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Heli [was] very old, and he heard what his sons did to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he said to them, Why do you⌃ according to this thing, which I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Nay [my] sons, for the report which I hear [is] not good; do not so, for the reports which I hear [are] not good, so that the people do not serve God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} If a man should at all sin against another, then shall they pray for him to the Lord; but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall entreat for him? But they listened not to the voice of their father, because the Lord would by all means destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the child Samuel advanced, and was in favor with God and with men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And a man of God came to Heli, and said, Thus says the Lord, I plainly revealed myself to the house of your father, when they were servants in Egypt to the house of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And I chose the house of your father out of all the tribes of Israel to minister to me in the priest's office, to go up to my altar, and to burn incense, and to wear an ephod. And I gave to the house of your father all the offerings by fire of the children of Israel for food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And therefore have you looked upon my incense-offering and my meat-offering with a shameless eye, and have honored your sons above me, so that they should bless themselves with the first fruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel, I said, Your house and the house of your father shall pass before me for ever: but now the Lord says, That be far from me; for I will only honor them that honor me, and he that sets me at nothing shall be despised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Behold, the days come when I will destroy your seed and the seed of your father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And you shall not have an old man in my house for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And [if] I do not destroy a man of your from my altar, [it shall be] that his eyes may fail and his soul may perish; and every one that remains in your house shall fall by the sword of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And this which shall come upon your two sons Ophni and Phinees shall be a sign to you; in one day they shall both die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And I will raise up to myself a faithful priest, who shall do all that is in my heart and in my soul; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before my Christ for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And it shall come to pass that he that survives in your house, shall come to do obeisance before him for a little piece of silver, saying, Put me into one of your priest's offices to eat bread.\par

\subsection*{Kings I 3}
\markright{KINGS I 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the child Samuel ministered to the Lord before Heli the priest: and the word of the Lord was precious in those days, there was no distinct vision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass at that time that Heli was sleeping in his place; and his eyes began to fail, and could not see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the lamp of God [was burning] before it was trimmed, and Samuel slept in the temple, where [was] the ark of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord called, Samuel, Samuel; and he said, Behold, [here am] I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he ran to Heli, and said, [Here am] I, for you did call me: and he said, I did not call you; return, go to sleep; and he returned and went to sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord called again, Samuel, Samuel: and he went to Heli the second time, and said, Behold [here am] I, for you did call me: and he said, I called you not; return, go to sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And [it was] before Samuel knew the Lord, and [before] the word of the Lord was revealed to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord called Samuel again for the third time: and he arose and went to Heli, and said, Behold, I [am here], for you did call me: and Heli perceived that the Lord [had] called the child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said, Return, child, go to sleep; and it shall come to pass if he shall call you, that you shall say, Speak for your servant hears: and Samuel went and lay down in his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord came, and stood, and called him as before: and Samuel said, Speak, for your servant hears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I execute my words in Israel; whoever hears them, both his ears shall tingle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} In that day I will raise up against Heli all things that I have said against his house; I will begin, and I will make an end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I have told him that I will be avenged on his house perpetually for the iniquities of his sons, because his sons spoke evil against God, and he did not admonish them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And [it shall] not [go on] so; I have sworn to the house of Eli, the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be atoned for with incense or sacrifices for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Samuel slept till morning, and rose early in the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to tell [Heli] the vision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Heli said to Samuel, Samuel, [my] son; and he said, Behold, [here am] I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, What [was] the word that was spoken to you? I pray you hide it not from me: may God do these things to you, and more also, if you hide from me any thing of all the words that were spoken to you in your ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Samuel reported all the words, and hid them not from him. And Heli said, He [is] the Lord, he shall do that which is good in his sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and there did not fall one of his words to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all Israel knew from Dan even to Bersabee, that Samuel [was] faithful as a prophet to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord manifested himself again in Selom, for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel; and Samuel was accredited to all Israel as a prophet to the Lord from one end of the land to the other: and Heli [was] very old, and his sons kept advancing [in wickedness], and their way [was] evil before the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} ere Before sun-rise. For it is probable the lamps were extinguished before the rising of the sun; see the parallel passages. the lamp; the temple \textsuperscript{7} Now Samuel Or, Thus did Samuel before he knew the Lord, and before the word of the Lord was revealed unto him. did not yet Samuel was not destitute of the knowledge of God, in that sense which implies the total absence of true piety, as Eli's sons were; for he knew and worshipped the God of Israel, but he did not know him as communicating special revelations of his will to him, in the manner in which he made it known to the prophets. \textsuperscript{8} the third; Although Samuel did not apprehend the way in which God reveals himself to his servants the prophets - by the "still small voice" - yet when this direct communication from the Almighty was made the third time, in a way altogether new and strange to him, it seems astonishing that he did not immediately apprehend. Perhaps he would have been sooner aware of a divine revelation, had it come in a dream or a vision. Those who have the greatest knowledge of divine things, should remember the time when they were as babes, unskilful in the word of righteousness. \textsuperscript{10} the Lord came This seems to imply a visible appearance, as well as an audible voice. as at other; Samuel did not now rise and run as before, when thought he Eli called, but lay still and listened. All must be silent, when God speaks. Observe, however, Samuel in his reply left out one word. He did not say, Speak, Lord, but only Speak, for thy servant heareth; perhaps, as Bp. Patrick suggests, out of uncertainty, whether it was God that spake to him or not. However, by this answer way was made for the message he was now to receive, and Samuel was brought acquainted with the words of God and visions of the Almighty. \textsuperscript{11} I will do; both the ears \textsuperscript{12} I will perform; when I begin etc. Heb. beginning and ending \textsuperscript{13} For I have told him or, And I will tell him, etc., I will; which he knoweth; his sons, vile or, accursed restrained them not Heb. frowned not upon them \textsuperscript{15} opened; Samuel reverenced Eli as a father, and feared to distress him by shewing what God had purposed to do. It does not appear that God commanded Samuel to deliver this message; he therefore did not attempt it till adjured by Eli. It might be supposed that Samuel would have been so full of ecstasy as to have forgotten his ordinary service, and run amongst his friends to tell them of the converse he had with God in the night, but he modestly keeps it to himself. Our secret communion with God is not to be proclaimed on the house-top. feared \textsuperscript{17} I pray thee; God; more also Heb. so add thing or, word \textsuperscript{18} every whit Heb. all the things, or, words, Whit, or wid, comes from the Anglo-Saxon wiht, which signifies person, thing, etc.. Every whit is every thing: equivalent to every jot. \subsection*{Kings I 4}
\markright{KINGS I 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered themselves together against Israel to war; and Israel went out to meet them and encamped at Abenezer, and the Philistines encamped in Aphec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Philistines prepare to fight with Israel, and the battle was turned against them; and the men of Israel fell before the Philistines, and there were struck in the battle in the field four thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people came to the camp, and the elders of Israel said, Why has the Lord caused us to fall this day before the Philistines? let us take the ark of our God out of Selom, and let it proceed from the midst of us, and it shall save us from the hand of our enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the people sent to Selom, and they take thence the ark of the Lord who dwells between the cherubs: and both the sons of Heli, Ophni and Phinees, [were] with the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass when the ark of the Lord entered into the camp, that all Israel cried out with a loud voice, and the earth resounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Philistines heard the cry, and the Philistines said, What [is] this great cry in the camp of the Hebrews: and they understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Philistines feared, and said, These are the Gods that are come to them into the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Woe to us, O Lord, deliver us today for such a thing has not happened aforetime: woe to us, who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these [are] the Gods that struck Egypt with every plague, and in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Strengthen yourselves and behave yourselves like men, O you⌃ Philistines, that you⌃ may not serve the Hebrews as they have served us, but be you⌃ men and fight with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they fought with them; and the men of Israel fall, and they fled every man to his tent; and there was a very great slaughter; and there fell of Israel thirty thousand fighting men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the ark of God was taken, and both the sons of Heli, Ophni, and Phinees, died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the battle, and he came to Selom on that day: and his clothes [were] torn, and earth [was] upon his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he came, an behold, Heli was upon the seat by the gate looking along the way, for his heart was greatly alarmed for the ark of God: and the man entered into the city to bring tidings; and the city cried out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Heli heard the sound of the cry, and said, What [is] the voice of this cry? and the men hasted and went in, and reported to Heli. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Now Heli [was] ninety years old, and his eyes were fixed, and he saw not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Heli said to them that stood round about him, What [is] the voice of this sound? And the man hasted and advanced to Heli, and said to him, I am he that is come out of the camp, and I have fled from the battle today: and Heli said, What [is] the even, [my] son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they young man answered and said, The men of Israel fled from the face of the Philistines, and there was a great slaughter among the people, and both your sons are dead, and the ark of God is taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass, when he mentioned the ark of God, that he fell from the seat backward near the gate, and his back was broken, and he died, for [he was] an old man and heavy: and he judged Israel twenty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And his daughter-in-law the wife of Phinees [was] with child, [about] to bring forth; and she heard the tidings, that the ark of God was taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead; and she wept and was delivered, for her pains came upon her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And in her time she was at the point of death; and the women that stood by her, said to her, Fear not, for you have born a son: but she answered not, and her heart did not regard it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she called the child Uaebarchaboth, because of the ark of God, and because of her father-in-law, and because of her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they said, The glory of Israel is departed, forasmuch as the ark of the Lord is taken.\par

\subsection*{Kings I 5}
\markright{KINGS I 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it from Abenezer to Azotus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Philistines took the ark of the Lord, and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people of Azotus rose early, and entered into the house of Dagon; and looked, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the Lord: and they lifted up Dagon, and set him in his place. And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the Azotians, and he plagued them, and he struck them in their secret parts, Azotus and her coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass when they rose early in the morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands [were] cut off each before the threshold, and both the wrists of his hands had fallen on the floor of the porch; only the stump of Dagon was left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Therefore the priests of Dagon, and every one that enters into the house of Dagon, do not tread upon the threshold of the house of Dagon in Azotus until this day, for they step over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon Azotus, and he brought evil upon them, and it burst out upon them into the ships, and mice sprang up in the midst of their country, and there was a great and indiscriminate mortality in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the men of Azotus saw that [it was] so, and they said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us, for his hand [is] heavy upon us and upon Dagon our god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they send and gather the lords of the Philistines to them, and say, What shall we do to the ark of the God of Israel? and the Gittites say, Let the ark of God come over to us; and the ark of the God of Israel came to Geth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass after it went about to Geth, that the hand of the Lord comes upon the city, a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city small and great, and struck them in their secret parts: and the Gittites made to themselves images of tumors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and it came to pass when the ark of God went into Ascalon, that the men of Ascalon cried out, saying, Why have you⌃ brought back the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they send and gather the lords of the Philistines, and they said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it lodge in its place; and let it not kill us and our people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For there was a very great confusion in all the city, when the ark of the God of Israel entered there; and those, who lived and died not were struck with tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} took, ; Ebenezer, Ashdod, called Azotus by the Greeks, was one of the five satrapies of the Philistines, and a place of great strength and consequence. It was situated near the Mediterranean, between Askelon and Jamnia, thirty-four miles north of Gaza, according to Diodorus Siculus, and the Antonine and Jerusalem Itineraries. It is now called Shdood; and Dr. Richardson says they neither saw nor heard of any ruins there. "The ground, " he observes, "around Ashdod is beautifully undulating, but not half stocked with cattle. The site of the town is on the summit of a grassy hill; and, if we are to believe historians, was anciently as strong as it was beautiful."; Azotus \textsuperscript{4} the head; of Dagon The name of this idol, Dagon, signifies a fish, and it is supposed to be the Atergatis of the Syrians, corruptly called Derceto by the Greeks, which had the upper part like a woman, and the lower part like a fish; as Lucian informs us: Δερκετους δε ειδος εν Φοινικη εθεησαμην, θεημα ξενον; ημισεη μεν γυνη; το δε οκοσον εκ μηρων ες ακρους ποδας, ιχθυος ουρη αποτεινεται . "In Phoenicia I saw the image of Derceto; a strange sight truly! For she had the half of a woman, but from the thighs downward a fish's tail." Diodorus (1. ii.) describing the same idol, as represented at Askelon, says, το μεν προσωπον εχει γυναικος, το δἀλλο σωμα παν ιχθυος . "It had the head of a woman, but all the rest of the body a fish's." Probably Horace alludes to this idol, in De Art. Poet. 4; Desinat in piscem, mulier formosa superne ." "The upper part a handsome woman, and the lower part a fish." If such was the form of this idol, then everything that was human was broken off from what resembled a fish. the stump or, the fishy part \textsuperscript{6} the hand; emerods, ; thereof The LXX and Vulgate add: Και μεσον της χωρας αυτης ανεφυησαν μυες και εγενετο συγχυσις θανατου μεγαλη εν τη πολει . ( Et ebullierunt ville et agri in medio regionis illius, et nati sunt mures; et facta est confusio mortis magne in civitate ). "And [the cities and fields in Vulg.] the midst of that region produced mice; [Vulg. burst up, and mice were produced; ] and there was the confusion of a great death in the city." \textsuperscript{7} saw;, The ark; upon Dagon our god \textsuperscript{9} the hand, ; with a very and they had emerods \textsuperscript{10} God to Ekron; us, to slay us and our people Heb. me, to slay me and my people \textsuperscript{11} us not, and our people Heb. me not, and my people a deadly; the hand\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 6}
\markright{KINGS I 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the ark was seven months in the country of the Philistines, and their land brought forth swarms of mice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Philistines call their priests, and their prophets, and their enchanters, saying, What shall we do to the ark of the Lord? teach us wherewith we shall send it away to its place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they said, If you⌃ send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, do not on any account send it away empty, but by all means render to it an offering for the plague; and then shall you⌃ be healed, and an atonement shall be made for you: should not his hand be [thus] stayed from off you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they say, What [is] the offering for the plague [which] we shall return to it? and they said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} According to the number of the lords of the Philistines, five golden tumors, for the plague was on you, and on your rulers, and on the people; and golden mice, the likeness of the mice that destroy your land: and you⌃ shall give glory to the Lord, that he may lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And why do you⌃ harden your hearts, as Egypt and Pharao hardened their hearts? [was it] not [so] when he mocked them, [that] they let the people go, and they departed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now take wood and make a new wagon, and take two cows, that have calved for the first time, without their calves; and do you⌃ yoke the cows to the wagon, and lead away the calves from behind them home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you⌃ shall take the ark and put it on the wagon; and you⌃ shall restore to it the golden articles for the trespass-offering in a coffer by the side of it: and you⌃ shall let it go, and sent it away, and you⌃ shall depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you⌃ shall see, if it shall go the way of its coasts along by Baethsamys, he has brought upon us this great affliction; and if not, then shall we know that his hand has not touched us, but this [is a] chance [which] has happened to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Philistines did so; and they took two cows that had calved for the first time, and yoked them to the wagon, and shut up their calves at home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they set the ark of the Lord, and the coffer, and the golden mice, on the wagon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the cows went straight on the way to the way of Baethsamys, they went along one track; and laboured, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, and the lords of the Philistines went after it as far as the coasts of Baethsamys. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the men of Baethsamys were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark of the Lord, and rejoiced to meet it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the wagon entered into the field of Osee, which was in Baethsamys, and they set there by it a great stone; and they split the wood of the wagon, and offered up the cows for a whole burnt offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord, and the coffer with it, and the golden articles upon it, and placed them on the great stone, and the men of Baethsamys offered whole burnt offerings and meat offerings on that day to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these [are] the golden tumors which the lords of the Philistines gave as a trespass-offering to the Lord; for Azotus one, for Gaza one, for Ascalon one, for Geth one, for Accaron one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the golden mice according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines, belonging to the five lords, from the fenced city to the village of the Pherezite, and to the great stone, on which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that was in the field of Osee the Baethsamysite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Baethsamys, because they saw the ark of the Lord; and [the Lord] struck among them seventy men, and fifty thousand men: and the people mourned, because the Lord had inflicted on the people, a very great plague. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the men of Baethsamys said, Who shall be able to pass before this holy Lord God? and to whom shall the ark of the Lord go up from us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they send messengers to the inhabitants of Cariathiarim, saying, The Philistines have brought back the ark of the Lord, go down and take it home to yourselves.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2864, bc 1140, An, Ex, Is, 351 the ark \textsuperscript{4} Five golden, ; you all Heb. them \textsuperscript{5} mice Bochart has collected many curious accounts relative to the terrible devastations made by these mischievous animals. William, Archbishop of Tyre, records, that in the beginning of the twelfth century, a penitential council was held at Naplouse, where five and twenty canons were framed for the correction of the manners of the inhabitants of the Christian kingdom of Jerusalem, who they apprehended had provoked to bring upon them the calamities of earthquakes, war, and famine. This last he ascribes to locusts and devouring mice, which had for four years together so destroyed the fruits of the earth as to cause an almost total failure of their crops. It was customary for the ancient heathen to offer to their gods such monuments of their deliverance as represented the evils from which they had been rescued; and Tavernier informs us, that among the Indians, when a pilgrim goes to one of the pagodas for a cure, he brings the figure of the member affected, made of gold, silver, or copper, according to his circumstances, which he offers to his god., ; give glory; *marg.; lighten; off your \textsuperscript{6} harden; the Egyptians, wonderfully or, reproachfully did they not the people Heb. them \textsuperscript{9} Bethshemesh, he or, it, we shall not his hand a chance \textsuperscript{17} these Ashdod; Gaza; Askelon; Gath; Ekron \textsuperscript{18} the five lords; great stone of or, great stone \textsuperscript{19} he smote; fifty thousand As it is very improbable that the village of Beth-shemesh should contain, or be capable of employing, 50, 070 men in the fields at wheat harvest, much less that they could all peep into the ark, and from the uncommon manner in which it is expressed in the original, it is generally allowed that there is some corruption in the text, or that some explanatory word is omitted. The Hebrew is shivim ish, chamishim aileph ish, literally, "seventy men, fifty thousand men." So LXX εβδομηκοντα ανδρας και πεντηκοντα χιλιαδας ανδρων . Vulgate, septuaginta viros, et quinquaginta millia plebis . "70 (chief) men, and 50, 000 common people." Targum, besabey amma, "of the elders of the people 70 men, ovekahala, and in the congregation 50, 000 men." But the Syriac, chamsho alphin weshivin gavrin, "5, 000 and 70 men; " with which the Arabic agrees; while Josephus has only εβδομηκοντα, seventy men; and three reputable manuscripts of Dr. Kennicott's also omit "50, 000 men." Some learned men, however, would render, by supplying ξ, mem, "70 men; fifty out of a thousand; " which supposes about 1, 400 present, and that a twentieth part were slain.\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 7}
\markright{KINGS I 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the men of Cariathiarim come, and bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord: and they bring it into the house of Aminadab in the hill; and they sanctified Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the covenant of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass from the time that the ark was in Cariathiarim, the days were multiplied, and [the time] was twenty years; and all the house of Israel looked after the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, If you⌃ do with all your heart return to the Lord, take away the strange gods from the midst of you, and the groves, and prepare your hearts to [serve] the Lord, and serve him only; and he shall deliver you from the hand of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the children of Israel took away Baalim and the groves of Astaroth, and served the Lord only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Massephath, and I will pray for you to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they were gathered together to Massephath, and they drew water, and poured it out upon the earth before the Lord. And they fasted on that day, and said, We have sinned before the Lord. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Massephath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Philistines heard that all the children of Israel were gathered together to Massephath: and the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel: and the children of Israel heard, and they feared before the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Cease not to cry to the Lord your God for us, and he shall save us out of the hand of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it up as a whole burnt offering with all the people to the Lord: and Samuel cried to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Samuel was offering the whole burnt offering; and the Philistines drew near to war against Israel; and the Lord thundered with a mighty sound in that day upon the Philistines, and they were confounded and overthrown before Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the men of Israel went forth out of Massephath, and pursued the Philistines, and struck them to the parts under Baethchor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Samuel took a stone, and set it up between Massephath and the old [city]; and he called the name of it Abenezer, stone of the helper; and he said, Hitherto has the Lord helped us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So the Lord humbled the Philistines, and they did not anymore come into the border of Israel; and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the cities which the Philistines took from the children of Israel were restored; and they restored them to Israel from Ascalon to Azob: and they took the coast of Israel out of the hand of the Philistines; and there was peace between Israel and the Amorite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he went year by year, and went round Baethel, and Galgala, and Massephath; and he judged Israel in all these consecrated places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And his return was to Armathaim, because there was his house; and there he judged Israel, and built there an altar to the Lord.\par

Others suppose that it was done emblematically, to represent the contrition of their hearts, and their desire to wash away their past offences. \subsection*{Kings I 8}
\markright{KINGS I 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And these [are] the names of his sons; Joel the firstborn, and the name of the second Abia, judges in Bersabee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his sons did not walk in his way; and they turned aside after gain, and took gifts, and perverted judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the men of Israel gather themselves together, and come to Armathaim to Samuel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and they said to him, Behold, you are grown old, and your sons walk not in your way; and now set over us a king to judge us, as also the other nations [have]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the thing [was] evil in the eyes of Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us: and Samuel prayed to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord said to Samuel, Hear the voice of the people, in whatever they shall say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from reigning over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} According to all their doings which they have done to me, from the day that I brought them out of Egypt until this day, even [as] they have deserted me, and served other gods, so they do also to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now listen to their voice; only you shall solemnly testify to them, and you shall describe to them the manner of the king who shall reign over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Samuel spoke every word of the Lord to the people who asked of him a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said, This shall be the manner of the king that shall rule over you: he shall take your sons, and put them in his chariots, and among his horsemen, and running before his chariots, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and [his manner shall be] to make them to himself captains of hundreds and captains of thousands; and to reap his harvest, and gather his vintage, and prepare his instruments of war, and the implements of his chariots. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, and cooks, and bakers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he will take your fields, and your vineyards, and your good olive yards, and give them to his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he will take the tithe of your seeds and your vineyards, and give [it] to his eunuchs, and to his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he will take your servants, and your handmaids, and your good herds and your asses, and will take the tenth of them for his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he will tithe your flocks; and you⌃ shall be his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you⌃ shall cry out in that day because of your king whom you⌃ have chosen to yourselves, and the Lord shall not hear you in those days, because you⌃ have chosen to yourselves a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But the people would not listen to Samuel; and they said to him, Nay, but there shall be a king over us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} An we also will be like all the nations; and our king shall judge us, and shall go out before us, and fight our battles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and spoke them in the ears of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord said to Samuel, Listen to their voice, and appoint them a king. And Samuel said to the men of Israel, Let each man depart to his city.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2892, bc 1112, An, Ex, Is, 379 made his; sons judges \textsuperscript{6} displeased Heb. was evil in the eyes of, prayed \textsuperscript{9} hearken unto or, obey howbeit etc. or, notwithstanding when thou hast solemnly protested against them, then thou shalt shew, etc. the manner \textsuperscript{11} This will; He will take;, ; run \textsuperscript{18} cry out and the Lord "Hitherto, " says Puffendorf, "the people of Israel had lived under governors raised up by God, who had exacted no tribute of them, nor put them to any charge; but little content with this form of government, they desire to have a king like other nations, who should live in magnificence and pomp, keep armies, and be able to resist any invasion. Samuel informs them what it was they desired; that, when they understood it, they might consider whether they would persist in their choice. If they would have a king splendidly attended, he tells them that he would take their sons for his chariots, etc.. If they would have him keep up constant forces, then he would appoint them for colonels and captains, and employ those in his wars who were accustomed to follow their family business; and since, after the manner of other kings, he must keep a stately court, they must be content that their daughters should serve in several offices, which the king would think below the dignity of his wives and daughters ( ). In one word, that, to sustain his dignity, their king would exact the tenth of all they possessed, and be maintained in a royal manner out of their estates." will not hear\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 9}
\markright{KINGS I 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And [there was] a man of the sons of Benjamin, and his name [was] Kis, the son of Abiel, the son of Jared, the son of Bachir, the son of Aphec, the son of a Benjamite, a man of might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And this man [had] a son, and his name was Saul, of great stature, a goodly man; and there was not among the sons of Israel a goodlier than he, high above all the people from his shoulders and upward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the asses of Kis the father of Saul were lost; and Kis said to Saul his son, Take with you one of the young men, and arise you⌃, and go seek the asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they went through mount Ephraim, and they went through the land of Selcha, and found them not: and they passed through the land of Segalim, and they were not there: and they passed through the land of Jamin, and found them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when they came to Siph, then Saul said to his young man that was with him, Come and let us return, lest my father leave the asses, and take care for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the young man said to him, Behold now, [there is] a man of God in this city, and the man [is] of high repute; all that he shall speak will surely come to pass: now then let us go, that he may tell us our way on which we have set out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Saul said to his young man that was with him, Behold, then, we will go; but what shall we bring the man of God? for the loaves are spent out of our vessels, and we have nothing more with us that belongs to us to bring to the man of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the young man answered Saul again, and said, Behold, there is found in my hand a fourth part of a shekel of silver; and you shall give it to the man of God, and he shall tell us our way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now before time in Israel every one in going to enquire of God said, Come and let us go to the seer; for the people beforetime called the prophet, the seer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Saul said to his servant, Well said, come and let us go: and they went to the city where the man of God was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} As they went up the ascent to the city, they find virgins who had come out to draw water, and they say to them, Is the seer here? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the virgins answered them, and they say to them, He is: behold, [he is] before you: now he is coming to the city, because of the day, for today [there is] a sacrifice for the people in Bama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} As soon as you⌃ shall enter into the city, so shall you⌃ find him in the city, before he goes up to Bama to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes in, for he blesses the sacrifice, and afterwards the guests eat; now then go up, for you⌃ shall find him because of the holiday. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they go up to the city; and as they were entering into the midst of the city, behold, Samuel came out to meet them, to go up to Bama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came to him, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} At this time to-morrow I will send to you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be ruler over my people Israel, and he shall save my people out of the hand of the Philistines; for I have looked upon the humiliation of my people, for their cry is come to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Samuel looked upon Saul, and the Lord answered him, Behold the man of whom I spoke to you, this one shall rule over my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Saul drew near to Samuel into the midst of the city, and said, Tell me now which [is] the house of the seer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am he: go up before me to Bama, and eat with me today, and I will send you away in the morning, and I will tell you all that is in your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And concerning your asses that have been lost now these three days, care not for them, for they are found. And to whom does the excellency of Israel belong? does it not to you and to your father's house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Saul answered and said, Am not I the son of a Benjamite, the least tribe of the people of Israel? and of the least family of the whole tribe of Benjamin? and why have you spoken to me according to this word? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them to the inn, and set them there a place among the chief of those that were called, about seventy men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Samuel said to the cook, Give me the portion which I gave you, which I told you to set by you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Now the cook [had] boiled the shoulder, and he set it before Saul; and Samuel said to Saul, Behold that which is left: set before you, and eat; for it is set you for a testimony in preference to the others; take [of it]: and Saul ate with Samuel on that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he went down from Bama into the city; and they prepared a lodging for Saul on the roof, and he lay down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it came to pass when the morning dawned, that Samuel called Saul on the roof, saying, Rise up, and I will dismiss you. And Saul arose, and he and Samuel went out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} As they went down to a part of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Speak to the young man, and let him pass on before us; and do you stand as today, and listen to the word of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Kish; Cis a Benjamite or, the son of a man of Jemini power or, substance. \textsuperscript{6} city; an honourable, all that he saith \textsuperscript{7} what shall;, spent in Heb. gone out of, etc there is not We are not to suppose from this that the prophets took money to predict future events: Saul only refers to an invariable custom, that no man approached a superior without some present or another, however small in value. Dr. Pococke tells us of a present of fifty radishes! Other authors mention a flower, an orange, or similar trifles; and Mr. Bruce says, that one who wished to solicit a favour from him, presented him with about a score of dates! "I mention this trifling circumstance, " says Mr. B. "to shew how essential to human and civil intercourse presents are considered to be in the East; whether it be dates, or whether it be diamonds, they are so much a part of their manners, that without them, an inferior will never be at peace in his own mind, or think that he has hold of his superior for protection. But superiors give no presents to their inferiors." Presents then are tokens of honour; not intended as offers of payment or enrichment. have we Heb. is with us \textsuperscript{8} I have here at hand Heb. there is found in my hand \textsuperscript{10} Well said Heb. Thy word is good \textsuperscript{11} the hill to the city Heb. in the ascent of the city, found. \textsuperscript{12} sacrifice or, feast; the high place \textsuperscript{13} he doth bless; this time Heb. to-day \textsuperscript{15} the Lord; told Samuel in his ear Heb. revealed the ear of Samuel; *marg. \textsuperscript{17} Behold; reign over Heb. restrain in \textsuperscript{19} the seer The word roaih literally signifies one who sees; particularly preternatural sights. A seer and a prophet were the same in most cases; only with this difference, the seer was always a prophet, but the prophet was not always a seer. A seer seems to imply one who frequently met with and saw some symbolical representation of God. All prophets, true or false, profess to see God (see, . ); and diviners, in their enthusiastic flights, boasted that they had those things exhibited to their sight which should come to pass. and will tell \textsuperscript{20} three days ago Heb. to-day three days, set not *marg.; on whom \textsuperscript{21} a Benjamite; my family, ; so to me Heb. according to this word \textsuperscript{24} the shoulder Probably the shoulder was set before Saul, not because it was the best part, but because it was an emblem of the government to which he was now called. (See note on .); left or, reserved \textsuperscript{26} Samuel Saul had no doubt slept there all night, as is usual in the East; and now, being the break of day, "Samuel called to Saul on the top of the house:" there was no calling him to the top of the house a second time; he was sleeping there, and Samuel called him up. Up \textsuperscript{27} Bid the servant; a while Heb. to-day that I may\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 10}
\markright{KINGS I 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured [it] on his head, and kissed him, and said to him, Has not the Lord anointed you for a ruler over his people, over Israel? and you shall rule among the people of the Lord, and you shall save them out of the hand of their enemies; and this [shall be] the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you for a ruler over his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [As soon] as you shall have departed this day from me, you shall find two men by the burial-place of Rachel on the mount of Benjamin, exulting greatly; and they shall say to you, The asses are found which you⌃ went to seek; and, behold, your father has given up the matter of the asses, and he is anxious for you, saying, What shall I do for my son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall depart thence, and shall go beyond that as far as the oak of Thabor, and you shall find there three men going up to God to Baethel, one bearing three kids, and another bearing three vessels of bread, and another bearing a bottle of wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they shall ask you how you do, and shall give you two presents of bread, and you shall receive them of their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And afterward you shall go to the hill of God, where is the encampment of the Philistines; there [is] Nasib the Philistine: and it shall come to pass when you⌃ shall have entered into the city, that you shall meet a band of prophets coming down from the Bama; and before them will be lutes, and a drum, and a pipe, and a harp, and they shall prophesy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Spirit of the Lord shall come upon you, and you shall prophesy with them, and shall be turned into another man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it shall come to pass when these signs shall come upon you, —[then] do you whatever your hand shall find, because God [is] with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall go down in front of Galgal, and behold, I come down to you to offer a whole burnt offering and peace-offerings: seven days shall you wait until I shall come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass when he turned his back to depart from Samuel, God gave him another heart; and all these signs came to pass in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he comes thence to the hill, and behold a band of prophets opposite to him; and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all that had known him before came, and saw, and behold, he [was] in the midst of the prophets: and the people said every one to his neighbor, What [is] this that has happened to the son of Kis? [is] Saul also among the prophets? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And one of them answered and said, And who [is] his father? and therefore it became a proverb, [Is] Saul also among the prophets? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he ceased prophesying, and comes to the hill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And his kinsman said to him and to his servant, Whither went you⌃? and they said, To seek the asses; and we saw that they were lost, and we went in to Samuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And his kinsman said to Saul, Tell me, I pray you, What did Samuel say to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Saul said to his kinsman, he verily told me that the asses were found. But the matter of the kingdom he told him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Samuel summoned all the people before the Lord to Massephath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to the children of Israel, Thus has the Lord God of Israel spoken, saying, I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, and I rescued you out of the hand of Pharao king of Egypt, and out of all the kingdoms that afflicted you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you⌃ have this day rejected God, who is himself your Deliverer out of all your evils and afflictions; and you⌃ said, Nay, but you shall set a king over us: and now stand before the Lord according to your tribes, and according to your families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin is taken by lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he brings near the tribe of Benjamin by families, and the family of Mattari is taken by lot: and they bring near the family of Mattari, man by man, and Saul the son of Kis is taken; and he sought him, but he was not found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Samuel asked yet again of the Lord, Will the man come here? and the Lord said, Behold, he is hid among the stuff. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he ran and took him thence, and he set him in the midst of the people; and he was higher than all the people by his shoulders and upwards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Samuel said to all the people, Have you⌃ seen whom the Lord has chosen to himself, that there is none like to him among you all? And all the people took notice, and said, Let the king live! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Samuel told the people the manner of the king, and wrote it in a book, and set it before the Lord: and Samuel sent away all the people, and each went to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Saul departed to his house to Gabaa; and there went with Saul mighty men whose hearts God had touched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But evil men said, Who [is] this man [that] shall save us? and they despised him, and brought him no gifts.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a vial, ; kissed him; captain, ; his inheritance \textsuperscript{2} Rachel's; Zelzah The asses, care Heb. business \textsuperscript{4} salute thee Heb. ask thee of peace \textsuperscript{5} hill of God, a company;, a psaltery \textsuperscript{7} let it be Heb. it shall come to pass that, etc signs; that thou do as occasion etc. Heb. do for thee as thine hand shall find, God \textsuperscript{9} back Heb. shoulder gave Heb. turned another heart and all those signs The following history of Saul is given by the Afghans, a people generally supposed to be of Jewish origin: "In a war which raged between the children of Israel and the Amalekites, the latter being victorious, plundered the Jews, and obtained possession of the ark of the covenant. Considering this (as) the God of the Jews, they threw it into the fire, which did not affect it. They afterwards attempted to cleave it with axes, but without success. Every individual who treated it with indignity, was punished for his temerity. They then placed it in their temple; but all their idols bowed to it. At length they fastened it upon a cow, which they turned loose in the wilderness. When the prophet Samuel arose, the children of Israel said to him, 'We have been totally subdued by the Amalekites, and have no king. Raise to us a king, that we may be enabled to contend for the glory of God.' Samuel said, 'In case you are led out to battle, are you determined to fight?' They answered, 'What has befallen us, that we should not fight against infidels? That nation has banished us from our country and children.' At this time the angel Gabriel descended, and delivering a wand, said, 'It is the command of God, that the person whose stature shall correspond with this wand, shall be king of Israel.' Melec Talut was at that time a man of inferior condition, and performed the humble employment of feeding the goats and cows of others. One day, a cow under his charge was accidentally lost. Being disappointed in his searches, he was greatly distressed, and applied to Samuel saying, 'I have lost a cow, and I do not possess the means of satisfying the owner. Pray for me that I may be extricated from this difficulty.' Samuel perceiving that he was a man of lofty stature, asked his name. He answered, Talut. Samuel then said, 'Measure Talut with the wand which the angel Gabriel brought.' His stature was equal to it. Samuel then said, 'God has raised Talut to be your king.' The children of Israel answered, 'We are greater than our king. We are men of dignity, and he is of inferior condition. How shall he be our king?' Samuel informed them, they should know that God had constituted Talut king, by his restoring the ark of the covenant. He accordingly restored it, and they acknowledged him their sovereign." Asiatic Researches, vol. ii. p. 119, et seq. \textsuperscript{11} when all; one to another Heb. a man to his neighbour What is this;, Is Saul \textsuperscript{12} of the same place Heb. from thence who is their \textsuperscript{14} And he said no where \textsuperscript{19} And ye have, by your tribes \textsuperscript{24} See ye him; God save the king Heb. Let the king live \textsuperscript{27} children; brought him; he held his peace or, he was as though he had been deaf\par}
