\subsection*{Kings I 11}
\markright{KINGS I 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass about a month after this, that Naas the Ammanite went up, and encamped against Jabis Galaad: and all the men of Jabis said to Naas the Ammanite, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Naas the Ammanite said to them, On these terms will I make a covenant with you, that I should put out all your right eyes, and I will lay a reproach upon Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the men of Jabis say to him, Allow us seven days, and we will send messengers into all the coasts of Israel: if there should be no one to deliver us, we will come out to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the messengers came to Gabaa to Saul, and they speak the words into the ears of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice, and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And, behold, Saul came after the early morning out of the field: and Saul said, Why does the people week? and they tell him the words of the men of Jabis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Spirit of the Lord came upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he took two cows, and cut them in pieces, and sent them into all the coasts of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, Whoso comes not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall they do to his oxen: and a transport from the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they came out to battle as one man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he reviews them at Bezec in Bama, every man of Israel six hundred thousand, and the men of Juda seventy thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to the messengers that came, Thus shall you⌃ say to the men of Jabis, To-morrow you⌃ shall have deliverance when the sun is hot; and the messengers came to the city, and told the men of Jabis, and they rejoiced. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the men of Jabis said to Naas the Ammanite, To-morrow we will come forth to you, and you⌃ shall do to us what seems good in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass on the morrow, that Saul divided the people into three companies, and they go into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and they struck the children of Ammon until the day was hot; at it came to pass that those who were left were scattered, and there were not left among them two together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the people said to Samuel, Who has said that Saul shall not reign over us? Give up the men, and we will put them to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Saul said, No man shall die this day, for today the Lord has wrought deliverance in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Samuel spoke to the people, saying, Let us go to Galgala, and there renew the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And all the people went to Galgala, and Samuel anointed Saul there to be king before the Lord in Galgala, and there he offered meat-offerings and peace-offerings before the Lord: and Samuel and all Israel rejoiced exceedingly.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Nahash In the Vulgate this chapter begins thus: Et factum est quasi post mensem, "And it came to pass about a month after; " which is also the reading of the principal copies of the Septuagint; and is also found in Josephus, though it appears to be of little authority.; Jabeshgilead; Make \textsuperscript{3} Give us Heb. Forbear us \textsuperscript{5} after the herd; What aileth \textsuperscript{6} Spirit of God;, his anger \textsuperscript{7} he took The sending the pieces of the oxen was an act similar to that of the Levite (see note on ). An eminent Scotch writer describes the rites, incantations, and imprecations used prior to the fiery cross being circulated, to summon the rough warriors of ancient times to the service of their chief; and he alludes to this ancient custom, which in comparatively modern times, has been practised in Scotland; and proves that a similar punishment of death, or destruction of their houses, for disobeying the summons, was inflicted by the ancient Scandinavians, as recorded by Olaus Magnus, in his History of the Goths. This bears a striking similarity to the ancient custom of the Israelites. With the Highlanders, a goat was slain; with the Israelites, an ox. The exhibition of a cross, stained with the blood of the sacrificed animal, was the summons of the former, while part of the animal, was the mandate of the latter. Disobedience in one nation was punished with the death of themselves or oxen, and burning of their dwellings in the other. hewed Whosoever the fear; with one consent Heb. as one man \textsuperscript{11} on the morrow; in three, morning slew; so that two \textsuperscript{15} before the Lord sacrificed; rejoiced greatly\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 12}
\markright{KINGS I 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Samuel said to all Israel, Behold, I have listened to your voice in all things that you⌃ have said to me, and I have set a king over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And now, behold, the king goes before you; and I am grown old and shall rest; and, behold, my sons [are] among you; and, behold, I have gone about before you from my youth to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, [here am] I, answer against me before the Lord and before his anointed: whose calf have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom of you have I oppressed? or from whose hand have I taken a bribe, even [to] a sandal? bear witness against me, and I will make restitution to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they said to Samuel, You have not injured us, and you have not oppressed us; and you have not afflicted us, and you have not taken anything from any one's hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Samuel said to the people, The Lord [is] witness among you, and his anointed [is] witness this day, that you⌃ have not found anything in my hand: and they said, [He is] witness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Samuel spoke to the people, saying, The Lord who appointed Moses and Aaron [is] witness, who brought our fathers up out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now stand still, and I will judge you before the Lord; and I will relate to you all the righteousness of the Lord, the things which he has wrought among you and your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} When Jacob and his sons went into Egypt, and Egypt humbled them, then our fathers cried to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron; and they brought our fathers out of Egypt, and he made them to dwell in this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they forgot the Lord their God, and he sold them into the hands of Sisara captain of the host of Jabis king of Asor, and into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the king of Moab; and he fought with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they cried to the Lord, and said, We have sinned, for we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and the groves: and now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he sent Jerobaal, and Barac, and Jephthae, and Samuel, and rescued us out of the hand of our enemies round about, and you⌃ lived in security. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you⌃ saw that Naas king of the children of Ammon came against you, and you⌃ said, Nay, none but a king shall reign over us; whereas the Lord our God [is] our king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And now behold the king whom you⌃ have chosen; and behold, the Lord has set a king over you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} If you⌃ should fear the Lord, and serve him, and listen to his voice, and not resist the mouth of the Lord, and you⌃ and your king that reigns over you should follow the Lord, [well]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if you⌃ should not listen to the voice of the Lord, and you⌃ should resist the mouth of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be upon you and upon your king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now stand still, and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [Is it] not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; and know you⌃ and see, that your wickedness [is] great which you⌃ have wrought before the Lord, having asked for yourselves a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Samuel called upon the Lord, and the Lord sent thunders and rain in that day; and all the people feared greatly the Lord and Samuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And all the people said to Samuel, Pray for your servants to the Lord your God, and let us not die; for we have added to all our sins this iniquity, in asking for us a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Samuel said to the people, Fear not: you⌃ have [indeed] wrought all this iniquity; only turn not from following the Lord, and serve the Lord with all your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And turn not aside after the [gods] that are nothing, who will do nothing, and will not deliver [you], because they are nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For the Lord will not cast off his people for his great name's sake, because the Lord graciously took you to himself for a people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And far be it from me to sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will serve the Lord, and show you the good and the right way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Only fear the Lord, and serve him in truth and with all your heart, for you⌃ see what great things he has wrought with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But if you⌃ continue to do evil, then shall you⌃ and your king be consumed.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} walketh; I am old; my sons, I have walked \textsuperscript{3} his anointed, ; whose ox; bribe Heb. ransom blind mine eyes or, that I should hide mine eyes at him; I will \textsuperscript{5} The Lord, his anointed ye have; in my hand \textsuperscript{6} It is the Lord;, ; advanced or, made \textsuperscript{7} reason; righteous acts Heb. righteousnesses or benefits, to Heb. with \textsuperscript{8} Jacob; cried, sent Moses;, brought, made them \textsuperscript{9} forgat; he sold; of the Philistines, into the \textsuperscript{11} Jerubbaal, Bedan, whose name occurs no where else as a judge of Israel, Bp. Patrick and others suppose to be a contraction of ben Dan, "the son of Dan; " by which they suppose Samson is meant, as the Targum reads. The LXX, Syriac, and Arabic, however, instead of Bedan read Barak; and the two latter versions, instead of Samuel have Samson. These readings are adopted by Houbigant, and appear to be genuine; for it is not probable that Samuel would enumerate himself. Judg. 13:1-16:31 Jephthah Samuel \textsuperscript{12} Nahash Nay, ; when the Lord \textsuperscript{13} behold, whom ye, have desired \textsuperscript{14} If ye will; commandment Heb. mouth continue Heb. be after \textsuperscript{17} Is it In northern latitudes, thunder and rain are far from being un-common during harvest. But rain is hardly ever known in Palestine during that season, which commences about the end of June, or beginning of July. This fact is abundantly confirmed by modern travellers, and is demonstrative to every unprejudiced reader of the Holy Scriptures, that the thunder and rain, which at Samuel's invocation, was sent at this season of the year, was a miraculous interposition of the power of God; for we read in, it was a "great thing which the Lord will do." Thus were the Israelites warned of their sin in having asked a king, and of the omnipotence of that God, whose gracious promises they virtually neglected by this act. \subsection*{Kings I 13}
\markright{KINGS I 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Saul chooses for himself three thousand men of the men of Israel: and there were with Saul two thousand who were in Machmas, and in mount Baethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gabaa of Benjamin: and he sent the rest of the people every man to his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jonathan struck Nasib the Philistine that lived in the hill; and the Philistines hear of it, and Saul sounds the trumpet through all the land, saying, The servants have despised [us]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And all Israel heard say, Saul has struck Nasib the Philistine; now Israel had been put to shame before the Philistines; and the children of Israel went up after Saul in Galgala. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Philistines gather together to war with Israel; and then come up against Israel thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand by the seashore for multitude: and they come up, and encamp in Machmas, opposite Baethoron southward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait so that they could not draw near, and the people hid themselves in caves, and sheepfolds, and rocks, and ditches, and pits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they that went over went over Jordan to the land of Gad and Galaad: and Saul was yet in Galgala, and all the people followed after him in amazement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he continued seven days for the appointed testimony, as Samuel told him, and Samuel came not to Galgala, and his people were dispersed from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Saul said, Bring hither [victims], that I may offer whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings: and he offered the whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass when he had finished offering the whole burnt offering, that Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to meet him, [and] to bless him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Samuel said, What have you done? and Saul said, Because I saw how the people were scattered from me, and you were not present as you purposed according to the set time of the days, and the Philistines were gathered to Machmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then I said, Now will the Philistines come down to me to Galgala, and I have not sought the face of the Lord: so I forced myself and offered the whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Samuel said to Saul, You have done foolishly; for you have not kept my command, which the Lord commanded you, as now the Lord would have confirmed your kingdom over Israel for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But now your kingdom shall not stand to you, and the Lord shall seek for himself a man after his own heart; and the Lord shall appoint him to be a ruler over his people, because you have not kept all that the Lord commanded you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Samuel arose, and departed from Galgala, and the remnant of the people went after Saul to meet [him] after the men of war, when they had come out of Galgala to Gabaa of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were found with him, about six hundred men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Saul and Jonathan his son, and the people that were found with them, halted in Gabaa, of Benjamin; and they wept: and the Philistines had encamped in Machmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And men came forth to destroy out of the land of the Philistines in three companies; one company turning by the way of Gophera toward the land of Sogal, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and another company turning the way of Baethoron, and another company turning by the way of Gabae that turns aside to Gai of Sabim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And there was not found a smith in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make themselves sword or spear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all Israel went down to the Land of the Philistines to forge every one his reaping-hook and his tool, and every one his axe and his sickle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it was near the time of vintage: and their tools were [valued at] three shekels for a plowshare, and there was the same rate for the axe and the sickle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it came to pass in the days of the war of Machmas, that there was not a sword or spear found in the hand of all the people, that were with Saul and Jonathan; but with Saul and Jonathan his son was there found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And there went out some from the camp of the Philistines to the place beyond Machmas.\par

This is probably the true reading; for it does not appear that Samuel went to Gibeah, which was Saul's usual residence; and the Hebrew copyist, as Dr. Wall observes, seems to have missed a line, and added to the sentence concerning Samuel, that which ended the sentence concerning Saul. \subsection*{Kings I 14}
\markright{KINGS I 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when a certain day arrived, Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man that bore his armor, Come, and let us go over to Messab of the Philistines that is on the other side yonder; but he told not his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Saul sat on the top of the hill under the pomegranate tree that is in Magdon, and there were with him about six hundred men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Achia son of Achitob, the brother of Jochabed the son of Phinees, the son of Heli, [was] the priest of God in Selom wearing an ephod: and the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in the midst of the passage whereby Jonathan sought to pass over to the encampment of the Philistines, there was both a sharp rock on this side, and a sharp rock on the other side: the name of the one [was] Bases, and the name of the other Senna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The one way [was] northward to one coming to Machmas, and the other way [was] southward to one coming to Gabae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Jonathan said to the young man that bore his armor, Come, let us go over to Messab of these uncircumcised, if [perhaps] the Lord may do something for us; for the Lord is not straitened to save by many or by few. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And his armor-bearer said to him, Do all that your heart inclines toward: behold, I [am] with you, my heart [is] as your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Jonathan said, Behold, we will go over to the men, and will come down suddenly upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If they should say thus to us, Stand aloof there until we shall send you word; then we will stand still by ourselves, and will not go up against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [But] if they should say thus to us, Come up to us; then will we go up, for the Lord has delivered them into our hands; this [shall be] a sign to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they both went in to Messab of the Philistines; and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of their Caves, where they had hidden themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the men of Messab answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will show you a thing: and Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, Come up after me, for the Lord has delivered them into the hands of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Jonathan went up on his hands and feet, and his armor-bearer with him; and they looked on the face of Jonathan, and he struck them, and his armor-bearer did strike [them] after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the first slaughter which Jonathan and his armor-bearer effected was twenty men, with darts and slings, and pebbles of the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And there was dismay in the camp, and in the field; and all the people in Messab, and the spoilers were amazed; and they would not act, and the land was terror-struck, and there was dismay from the lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the watchmen of Saul looked in Gabaa of Benjamin, and, behold, the army was thrown into confusion on every side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Saul said to the people with him, Number yourselves now, and see who has gone out from you: and they numbered themselves, and behold, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Saul said to Achia, Bring the ephod; for he wore the ephod in that day before Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass while Saul was speaking to the priest, that the sound in the camp of the Philistines continued to increase greatly; and Saul said to the priest, Withdraw your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Saul went up and all the people that were with him, and they come to the battle: and, behold, [every] man's sword was against his neighbor, a very great confusion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the servants who had been before with the Philistines, who had gone up to the army, turned themselves also to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And all the Israelites who were hidden in mount Ephraim heard also that the Philistines fled; and they also gather themselves after them to battle: and the Lord saved Israel in that day; and the war passed through Bamoth; and all the people with Saul were about ten thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the battle extended itself to every city in the mount Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Saul committed a great trespass of ignorance in that day, and he lays a curse on the people, saying, Cursed [is] the man who shall eat bread before the evening; so I will avenge myself on my enemy: and none of the people tasted bread, though all the land was dining. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Jaal was a wood abounding in swarms of bees on the face of the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the people went into the place of the bees, and, behold, they continued speaking; and, behold, there was none that put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Jonathan had not heard when his father adjured the people; and he reached forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, an dipped it into the honeycomb, and returned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes recovered their sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And one of the people answered and said, Your father solemnly adjured the people, saying, Cursed [is] the man who shall eat bread today. And the people were very faint, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and Jonathan knew it, and said, My father has destroyed the land: see how my eyes have received sight [now] that I have tasted a little of this honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Surely if the people had this day eaten freely of the spoils of their enemies which they found, the slaughter among the Philistines would have been greater. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And on that day he struck some of the Philistines in Machmas; and the people were very weary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the people turned to the spoil; and the people took flocks, and herds, and calves, and killed them on the ground, and the people ate with the blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it was reported to Saul, saying, The people have sinned against the Lord, eating with the blood: and Saul said, Out of Getthaim roll a great stone to me hither. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and tell them to bring hither every one his calf, and every one his sheep: and let them kill it on this [stone] and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood: and the people brought each one that which was in his hand, and they killed [them] there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Saul built an altar there to the Lord: this was the first altar that Saul built to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines this night, and let us plunder among them till the day break, and let us not leave a man among them. And they said, Do all that is good in your sight: and the priest said, let us draw near hither to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Saul enquired of God, If I go down after the Philistines, will you deliver them into the hands of Israel? And he answered him not in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Saul said, Bring hither all the chiefs of Israel, and know and see by whom this sin has been committed this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} For as the Lord lives who has saved Israel, if answer should be against my son Jonathan, he shall surely die. And there was no one that answered out of all the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And he said to all the men of Israel, You⌃ shall be under subjection, and I an Jonathan my son will be under subjection: and the people said to Saul, Do that which is good in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Saul said, O Lord God of Israel, why have you not answered your servant this day? [is] the iniquity in me, or in Jonathan my son? Lord God of Israel, give clear [manifestations]; and if [the lot] should declare this, give, I pray you, to your people of Israel, give, I pray, holiness. And Jonathan and Saul are taken, and the people escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Saul said, Cast [lots] between me and my son Jonathan: whoever the Lord shall cause to be taken by lot, let him die: and the people said to Saul, This thing is not [to be done]: and Saul prevailed against the people, and they cast [lots] between him and Jonathan his son, and Jonathan is taken by lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what you have done: and Jonathan told him, and said, I did indeed taste a little honey, with the end of my staff that was in my hand, and, behold! I [am to] die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Saul said to him, God do so to me, and more also, you shall surely die today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And the people said to Saul, Shall he that has wrought this great salvation in Israel be put to death this day? [As] the Lord lives, there shall not fall to the ground one of the hairs of his head; for the people of God have wrought successfully this day. And the people prayed for Jonathan in that day, and he died not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Saul went up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines departed to their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And Saul received the kingdom, by lot he inherits the office [of ruling] over Israel: and he fought against all his enemies round about, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against the children of Edom, and against Baethaeor, and against the king of Suba, and against the Philistines: wherever he turned, he was victorious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And he wrought valiantly, and struck Amalec, and rescued Israel out of the hand of them that trampled on him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Jessiu, and Melchisa: and [these were] the names of his two daughters, the name of the firstborn Merob, and the name of the second Melchol. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And the name of his wife was Achinoom, the daughter of Achimaa: and the name of his captain of the host was Abenner, the son of Ner, son of a kinsman of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And Kis [was] the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abenezer, [was] son of Jamin, son of Abiel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And the war was vehement against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and when Saul saw any mighty man, and any valiant man, then he took them to himself.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2917, bc 1087, An, Ex, Is 404 it came to pass upon a day or, there was a day Jonathan, ; he told not \textsuperscript{2} in the uttermost; a pomegranate The word rimmon, in Arabic romman, whence the Portuguese romaa, denotes the pomegranate, both tree and fruit; called by naturalists malus punica or malo-granatum . It is, according to the Linnean system, a genus of the icosandria monogynia class of plants; and is a low tree, growing very common in Palestine, and other parts of the East. It has several small angular boughs, very thick and bushy, covered with a reddish bark, and some of them armed with sharp thorns. They are garnished with small, narrow, spear-shaped leaves, like those of the myrtle, but not so sharp, of a green colour, inclining to red. Its blossoms are large, beautiful, of an elegant red colour, inclining to purple, composed of several stalks resembling a rose, in the hollow of the cup. This cup is oblong, hard, purple, having a figure somewhat like that of a bell. It is chiefly valued for its fruit, which is exceedingly beautiful, of the form and size of a large apple, with a reddish rind, and red within; being full of small kernels, with red grains, replenished with a generous liquor, of which, Sir John Chardin informs us, they still make considerable quantities of wine in the East, particularly in Persia. But as the pomegranate tree, from its low growth, is but little adapted for pitching a tent under, it is probable that Rimmon here is the name of the rock mentioned in . \textsuperscript{3} Ahiah, called Ahimelech. Ichabod's wearing \textsuperscript{5} forefront Heb. tooth, Bozez, i.e. shining, Seneh, i.e. a bush or tooth \textsuperscript{6} Come This action of Jonathan's was totally contrary to the laws of war; no military operation should be undertaken without the knowledge and command of the general. But it is highly probable, that this gallant man was led to undertake the hazardous enterprise by an immediate divine impulse; and by the same influence was kept from informing the soldiers, and even from consulting his father, who might have opposed his design. uncircumcised; it may be; for there is no restraint Where there is a promise of defense and support, the weakest, in the face of the strongest enemy, may rely upon it with the utmost confidence. \textsuperscript{9} they; Tarry Heb. Be still \textsuperscript{10} this shall be a sign \textsuperscript{12} Come up to us Meaning, that they would cause them to repent of their audacity. This was the favourable sign which Jonathan had requested.; Come up after me \textsuperscript{14} an half acre of land or, half a furrow of an acre of land, The original is obscure and variously understood; but it is probably a proverbial expression for a small space. \textsuperscript{15} there was trembling; the spoilers, the earth quaked; very great trembling Heb. trembling of God; God will in some way or other direct the steps of those who acknowledge him in all their ways, and seek unto him for direction with full purpose of heart. Sometimes we find most comfort in that which is least our own doing, and into which we have been led by the unexpected, but well observed, turns of Providence. \textsuperscript{18} Bring hither The Septuagint reads Προσαγαγε το εφουδ, οτι αυτος ηρε το εφουδ εν τη ημερα εκεινη ενωπιον Ισραηλ . "Bring hither the ephod; for he bore the ephod on that day before Israel, " which Houbigant and others think is the true reading. Finding that his son Jonathan and his armour-bearer were absent, Saul wished to consult the high-priest; but the tumult increasing, he says to him, "Withdraw thine hand:" i.e., desist form consulting the ephod on the present occasion, and immediately hastened to make the best use he could of this astonishing victory.; For the ark \textsuperscript{20} assembled themselves Heb. were cried together every man's \textsuperscript{21} the Hebrews Probably such as they held in bondage, or who were their servants. Instead of ( haivrim ) "the Hebrews, " the LXX evidently read haavdim, for they have οι δουλοι, "the slaves; " but this reading is not countenanced by any other version, nor by any manuscript \textsuperscript{22} hid themselves, the battle The LXX and Vulgate add here, και πας ο λαος ην μετα Σαουλ ως δεκα χιλιαδες ανδρων, Et erant cum Saul, quasi decem millia virorum . "And (all the people who were, LXX) there were with Saul about ten thousand men; " but this is supported by no other authority. \textsuperscript{25} all they; honey This was wild honey, which to this day abounds in Judea; and bursting from the comb, runs down the hollow trees, rocks, etc. \textsuperscript{29} My father see It is well known, that hunger and fatigue produce faintness and dim the sight; and on taking a little food, this affection is immediately removed. \textsuperscript{31} from Michmash The distance, Calmet states to be three or four leagues. Aijalon \textsuperscript{32} flew the people The people having abstained from food the whole of the day, and being now faint through hunger and fatigue, they flew upon the cattle, and not taking time to bleed them properly, they eagerly devoured the flesh with the blood, directly contrary to the law - another bad effect of Saul's rash adjuration. did eat \textsuperscript{34} with him Heb. in his hand \textsuperscript{35} built It is probable that Saul converted the great stone, on which the cattle had been slaughtered, into an altar, on which sacrifices were offered, before the people attempted to proceed any further. This we are told was the first he had built. Samuel, as a prophet and priest, had hitherto erected the altars, but Saul seems to have thought he had sufficient authority to erect one himself, without the prophet, as he had once offered sacrifice without him.; the same etc. Heb. that altar he began to build unto the Lord \textsuperscript{36} Let us go; let us not leave; Then said the priest It is evident that Ahiah, who had before been interrupted by Saul's impatience, doubted of the propriety of pursuing the Philistines that night, and properly counselled them to enquire of the Lord. \textsuperscript{37} Shall I go, ; he answered \textsuperscript{38} Draw ye near; chief Heb. corners \textsuperscript{41} Therefore Both the Septuagint and Vulgate add much to this verse: Και ειπε Σαουλ, Κυριε ο Θεος Ισραηλ, τι οτι ουκ απεκριθης τω δουλω σου σημερον; ει εν εμοι η εν Ιωναθαν τω υιω μου η αδικια, Κυριε ο Θεος Ισραηλ δος δηλους και εαν ταδε ειπη, δος δη τω λαω σου Ισραηλ, δος δη οσιοτητα, κ.τ.λ. Et dixit Saul ad Dominum Deum Israel; Domine Deus Israel da indicium: quid est quod non responderis servo tuo hodie? Si in me, aut in Jonatha filio meo est iniquitas hec, da ostensionem. Aut si hec iniquitas est in populo tuo, da sanctitatem, etc . "And Saul said (to the Lord God of Israel, Vulg.) Lord God of Israel (give a sign, Vulg.). Why is it that thou has not answered thy servant today? If the iniquity be in me, or in my son Jonathan, (O Lord God of Israel, LXX) make it manifest; and if thou say thus, give to thy people Israel, give mercy, " etc., (but Vulg. Or, if this iniquity be in thy people, give sanctification, " etc.) Give a perfect lot or, Shew the innocent; And Saul; escaped Heb. went forth \textsuperscript{43} Tell me; I did but \textsuperscript{45} who hath; there shall not The people judged rightly, that the guilt was contracted by Saul, and not by Jonathan; and therefore they rescued him from the hands of his rash and severe father.; he hath; the people \textsuperscript{48} gathered an host or, wrought mightily smote \textsuperscript{49} Jonathan; name of the firstborn \textsuperscript{50} the name of the captain; Abner Heb. \subsection*{Kings I 15}
\markright{KINGS I 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Samuel said to Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint you king over Israel: and now hear the voice of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus said the Lord of hosts, Now will I take vengeance for what Amalec did to Israel, when he met him in the way as he came up out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And now go, and you shall strike Amalec and Hierim and all that belongs to him, and you shall not save anything of him alive, but you shall utterly destroy him: and you shall devote him and all his to [destruction], and you shall spare nothing belonging to him; and you shall kill both man and woman, and infant and suckling, and calf and sheep, and camel and ass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Saul summoned the people, and he numbered them in Galgala, four hundred thousand regular troops, and Juda thirty thousand regular troops. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Saul came to the cities of Amalec, and laid wait in the valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Saul said to the Kinite, Go, and depart out of the midst of the Amalekites, lest I put you with them; for you dealt mercifully with the children of Israel when they went up out of Egypt. So the Kinite departed from the midst of Amalec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Saul struck Amalec from Evilat to Sur fronting Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he took Agag the king of Amalec alive, and he killed all the people and Hierim with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Saul and all the people saved Agag alive, and the best of the flocks, and of the herds, and of the fruits, of the vineyards, and of all the good things; and they would not destroy them: but every worthless and refuse thing they destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I have repented that I have made Saul to be king: for he has turned back from following me, and has not kept my word. And Samuel was grieved, and cried to the Lord all night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Samuel rose early and went to meet Israel in the morning, and it was told Saul, saying, Samuel has come to Carmel, and he has raised up help for himself: and he turned his chariot, and came down to Galgala to Saul; and, behold, he was offering up a whole burnt offering to the Lord, the chief of the spoils which he brought out of Amalec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said to him, Blessed [are] you of the Lord: I have performed all that the Lord said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Samuel said, What then [is] the bleating of this flock in my ears, and the sound of the oxen which I hear? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Saul said, I have brought them out of Amalec, that which the people preserved, even the best of the sheep, and of the cattle, that it might be sacrificed to the Lord your God, and the rest have I utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Samuel said to Saul, Stay, and I will tell you what the Lord has said to me this night: and he said to him, Say on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Samuel said to Saul, Are you not little in his eyes, [though] a leader of one of the tribes of Israel? and [yet] the Lord anointed you to be king over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord sent you on a journey, and said to you, Go, and utterly destroy: you shall kill the sinners against me, [even] the Amalekites; and you shall war against them until you have consumed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And why did not you listen to the voice of the Lord, but did haste to fasten upon the spoils, and did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Saul said to Samuel, Because I listened to the voice of the people: yet I went the way by which the Lord sent me, and I brought Agag the king of Amalec, and I destroyed Amalec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But the people took of the spoils the best flocks and herds [out] of that which was destroyed, to sacrifice before the Lord our God in Galgal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Samuel said, Does the Lord take pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in hearing the words of the Lord? behold, obedience [is] better than a good sacrifice, and hearkening than the fat of rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For sin is [as] divination; idols bring on pain and grief. Because you have rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord also shall reject you from being king over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Saul said to Samuel, I have sinned, in that I have transgressed the word of the Lord and your direction; for I feared the people, and I listened to their voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now remove, I pray you, my sin, and turn back with me, and I will worship the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Samuel said to Saul, I will not turn back with you, for you have rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord will reject you from being king over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Samuel turned his face to depart, and Saul caught hold of the skirt of his garment, and tore it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Samuel said to him, The Lord has torn your kingdom from Israel out of your hand this day, and will give it to your neighbor who is better than you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Israel shall be divided to two: and [God] will not turn nor repent, for he is not as a man to repent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Saul said, I have sinned; yet honor me, I pray you, before the elders of Israel, and before my people; and turn back with me, and I will worship the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} So Samuel turned back after Saul, and he worshipped the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Samuel said, Bring me Agag the king of Amalec: and Agag came to him trembling; and Agag said Is death thus bitter? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Samuel said to Agag, As your sword has bereaved women of their children, so shall your mother be made childless among women: and Samuel killed Agag before the Lord in Galgal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Samuel departed to Armathaim, and Saul went up to his house at Gabaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Samuel did not see Saul again till the day of his death, for Samuel mourned after Saul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2925, bc 1079, An, Ex, Is, 412 The Lord, hearken \textsuperscript{3} Now go The Amalekites, a people of Arabia Petrea, who inhabited a tract of country on the frontiers of Egypt and Canaan, had acted with great cruelty towards the Israelites on their coming out of Egypt, and God then purposed that Amalek, as a nation, should be blotted out from under heaven; but it had been spared till it had filled up the measure of its iniquities, and now this purpose is carried into effect by Saul, upwards of 400 years afterwards! Nothing could justify such an exterminating decree but the absolute authority of God; and this was given. All the reasons of it we do not know; but this we know well, the Judge of all the earth doeth right. utterly destroy; slay; ox and sheep \textsuperscript{6} the Kenites; depart; ye showed \textsuperscript{7} smote; Havilah This Havilah was probably situated in Arabia, and the district of Chaulon may mark the spot. It seems different from that encompassed by the river Pison, one of the rivers of Eden., Shur \textsuperscript{9} the best, ; the fatlings or, the second sort \textsuperscript{11} repenteth me; turned;, ; hath not performed, it grieved; he cried \textsuperscript{12} Carmel; he set him; a place Yad, Literally as the LXX render χειρα, a hand; probably because the trophy or monument of victory was in the shape of a large hand, the emblem of power, erected on a pillar. These memorial pillars were anciently much in use; and the figure of a hand, by its emblematical meaning, was well adapted to preserve the remembrance of a victory. Niebuhr, speaking of the Mesjed Ali, or Mosque of Ali, says that, "at the top of the dome, where one generally sees on the Turkish mosques a crescent, or only a pole, there is here a hand stretched out, to represent that of Ali." Another writer informs us, that at the Alhamra, or red palace of the Moorish kings in Grenada, "on the key-stone of the outward arch [of the present principal entrance] is sculptured the figure of an arm, the symbol of strength and dominion." \textsuperscript{18} the sinners; they be consumed Heb. they consume them \textsuperscript{23} rebellion; witchcraft Heb. divination; stubbornness; thou hast rejected \textsuperscript{24} I have sinned; I feared; obeyed \textsuperscript{26} I will not; for thou \textsuperscript{28} The Lord; hath given; a neighbour \textsuperscript{29} Strength or, Eternity, or, Victory; will not lie \textsuperscript{30} honour me now; that I may worship \textsuperscript{33} As thy sword; Samuel It has been a matter of wonder to many, how Samuel could thus slay a captive prince, even in the presence of Saul, who from motives of clemency had spared him; but it should be remarked, that what Samuel did here, he did in his magisterial capacity; and that Agag had been a cruel tyrant, and therefore was cut off for his merciless cruelties. Farther, it is not likely that he did it by his own sword, but by that of the executioner. What kings, magistrates, and generals do, in an official way, by their subjects, servants, or soldiers, they are said to do themselves - qui facit per alterum, facit per se . hewed\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 16}
\markright{KINGS I 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to Samuel, How long do you mourn for Saul, whereas I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, I will send you to Jessae, to Bethleem; for I have seen among his sons a king for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Samuel said, How can I go? whereas Saul will hear of it, and kill me: and the Lord said, Take a heifer in your hand and you shall say, I am come to sacrifice to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall call Jessae to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; and you shall anoint him whom I shall mention to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Samuel did all that the Lord told him; and he came to Bethleem: and the elders of the city were amazed at meeting him, and said, Do you come peaceably, you Seer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice to the Lord. Sanctify yourselves, and rejoice with me this day: and he sanctified Jessae and his sons, and he called them to the sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass when they came in, that he saw Eliab, and said, Surely the Lord's anointed [is] before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the Lord said to Samuel, Look not on his appearance, nor on his stature, for I have rejected him; for God sees not as man looks; for man looks at the outward appearance, but God looks at the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Jessae called Aminadab, and he passed before Samuel: and he said, Neither has God chosen this one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jessae caused Sama to pass by: and he said, Neither has God chosen this one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Jessae caused his seven sons to pass before Samuel: and Samuel said, the Lord has not chosen these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Samuel said to Jessae, Have you no more sons? And Jessae said, [There is] yet a little one; behold, he tends the flock. And Samuel said to Jessae, Send and fetch him for we may not sit down till he comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he sent and fetched him: and he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes, and very goodly to behold. And the Lord said to Samuel, Arise, and anoint David, for he is good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward: and Samuel arose, and departed to Armathaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord tormented him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Saul's servants said to him, Behold now, an evil spirit from the Lord torments you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Let now your servants speak before you, and let them seek for our lord a man skilled to play on the harp; and it shall come to pass when an evil spirit comes upon you and he shall play on his harp, that you shall be well, and he shall refresh you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Saul said to his servants, Look now out for me a skillful player, and bring him to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And one of his servants answered and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jessae the Bethleemite, and he understands playing [on the harp], and the man [is] prudent, and a warrior, and wise in speech, and the man [is] handsome, and the Lord [is] with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Saul sent messengers to Jessae, saying, Send to me your son David who is with your flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jessae took a homer of bread, and a bottle of wine, and one kid of the goats, and sent them by the hand of his son David to Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David went in to Saul, and stood before him; and he loved him greatly; and he became his armor-bearer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Saul sent to Jessae, saying, Let David, I pray you, stand before me, for he has found grace in my eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass when the evil spirit was upon Saul, that David took his harp, and played with his hand: and Saul was refreshed, and [it was] well with him, and the evil spirit departed from him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2941, bc 1063, An, Ex, Is, 428 How long; seeing, ; horn with oil;, Jesse \textsuperscript{2} How can I go; Take an heifer For the prudent management of the affair, and to avoid suspicion, Samuel was directed to go to Bethlehem to sacrifice, as he probably did from time to time in many different places; and the answer which he was instructed to return was strictly true though he did not tell the principal design of his coming; for though no man in any circumstances should tell a lie, yet, in all circumstances, he is not bound to tell the whole truth, though he must tell nothing but the truth, and so tell that truth that the hearer shall not believe a lie by it. with thee Heb. in thine hand, I am come \textsuperscript{3} call Jesse; and I will show; anoint \textsuperscript{4} trembled; coming Heb. meeting Comest \textsuperscript{7} Look not; seeth not; looketh; outward appearance Heb. eyes on the heart \textsuperscript{11} There remaineth; down Heb. round \textsuperscript{12} ruddy; of a beautiful countenance Heb. fair of eyes, And the Lord anoint him \textsuperscript{14} the Spirit, ; evil spirit The evil spirit was either sent immediately from the Lord, or permitted to come; but whether this was a diabolic possession, or a mere mental malady, is not agreed. It seems to have partaken of both. That Saul had fallen into a deep melancholy, there is little doubt; and that an evil spirit might work more effectually on such a state of mind, there can be little question. His malady appears to have been of a mixed kind, natural and diabolical. There is too much of apparent nature in it to permit us to believe it was all spiritual; and there is too much of apparently supernatural influence, to suffer us to believe it was all natural.; troubled or, terrified \textsuperscript{18} a mighty; and prudent matters or, speech. a comely the Lord \textsuperscript{20} an ass laden Chamor lechem, literally, "an ass of bread, " rendered by the LXX γομορ αρτων, a gomor of bread; meaning, probably, not an animal, but a vessel containing a certain measure of bread. \textsuperscript{21} stood before him; loved him\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 17}
\markright{KINGS I 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Philistines gather their armies to battle, and gather themselves to Socchoth of Judaea, and encamp between Socchoth and Azeca Ephermen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Saul and the men of Israel gather together, and they encamp in the valley, and set the battle in array against the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Philistines stand on the mountain on one side, and Israel stands on the mountain on the other side, and the valley was between them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there went forth a mighty man out of the army of the Philistines, Goliath, by name, out of Geth, his height [was] four cubits and a span. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And [he had] a helmet upon his head, and he wore a breastplate of chain armor; and the weight of his breastplate [was] five thousand shekels of brass and iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And greaves of grass [were] upon his legs, and a brazen target [was] between his shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the staff of his spear [was] like a weaver's beam, and the spear's head [was formed] of six hundred shekels of iron; and his armor-bearer went before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he stood and cried to the army of Israel, and said to them, Why are you⌃ come forth to set yourselves in battle array against us? Am not I a Philistine, and you⌃ Hebrews of Saul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if he shall be able to fight against me, and shall strike me, then will we be your servants: but if I should prevail and strike him, you⌃ shall be our servants, and serve us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Philistine said, Behold, I have defied the armies of Israel this very day: give me a man, and we will both of us fight in single combat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed, and greatly terrified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [And David son of an Ephrathite said, this one was of Bethleem Juda, and his name was Jessae, and he had eight sons. And the man passed for an old man among men in the days of Saul. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [And the three elder sons of Jessae went and followed Saul to the war, and the ] [names of his sons that went to the war were, Eliab his first-born, and his second Aminadab, and his third son Samma. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [And David himself ] [was the younger son, and the three elder followed Saul. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [And David departed and returned from Saul, ] [to feed his father’s sheep in Bethleem; ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [And the Philistine advanced morning and evening, and stood up forty days. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [And Jessae said to David, Take now to your brethren an ephah of this meal, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp and give them to your brothers. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} [And you shall carry to the captain of the thousand ] [these ten cheeses of milk, and you shall see how your brethren fare, and learn what they lack. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [And Saul himself and all the men of Israel were in the valley of the Oak, warring with the Philistines. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [And David rose early in the morning, and left the sheep to a keeper, and took and went as Jessae commanded him, and he came to the trench and to the army as it was going out to fight, and they shouted for the battle. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [And Israel and the Philistines formed their lines one opposite the other. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} [And David deposited his burden in the hand of a keeper, and ran to the line, and went and asked his brethren how they Were. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} [And while he was speaking with them, behold the Amessaean advanced, Goliath by name, the Philistine of Geth, of the armies of the Philistines, and he spoke ] [as before, and David heard. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [And all the men of Israel when they saw the man fled from before him, and they were greatly terrified. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} [And the men of Israel said, Have you⌃ seen this man that comes up? for he has reproached Israel and has come up; and it shall be that the man who shall strike him, the king shall enrich him with great wealth and shall give him his daughter, and shall make his father’s house free in Israel. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [and David spoke to the men who stood with him saying, Shall it indeed be done thus to the man who shall strike that Philistine, and take away reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he has defied the army of the living God? ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} [And the people spoke to him according to this Word, saying Thus shall it be done to the man Who shall strike him. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} [And Eliab his elder brother heard as he spoke to the men, and Eliab was very angry with David and said, Why have you thus come down, and with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the naughtiness of your heart, for you are come down to see the battle. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} [And David said what have I done now? ] [Have I no business here? ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} [And he turned from him towards another, and he spoke after the same manner; and the people answered him ] [after the former manner. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} [And the Words which David spoke were heard and were reported ] [to Saul. And he took him to himself. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And David said to Saul, Let not, I pray you, the heart of my lord be dejected within him: your servant will go, and fight with this Philistine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Saul said to David, You will not in anyway be able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a mere youth, and he a man of war from his youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And David said to Saul, Your servant was tending the flock for his father; and when a lion came and a she-bear, and took a sheep out of the flock, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} then I went forth after him, and struck him, and drew [the spoil] out of his mouth: and as he rose up against me, then I caught hold of his throat, and struck him, and killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Your servant struck both the lion and the bear, and the uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them: shall I not go and strike him, and remove this day a reproach from Israel? For who [is] this uncircumcised one, who has defied the army of the living God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} The Lord who delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this uncircumcised Philistine. And Saul said to David, Go, and the Lord shall be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Saul clothed David with a military coat, and [put] his brazen helmet on his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he girded David with his sword over his coat: and he made trial walking [with them] once and again: and David said to Saul, I shall not be able to go with these, for I have not proved [them]: so they remove them from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And he took his staff in his hand, and he chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the shepherd's scrip which he had for his store, and his sling was in his hand; and he approached the Philistine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} [And the Philistine advanced and drew near to David, and a man bearing his shield went before him, and the Philistine looked on. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Goliath saw David, and despised him; for he was a lad, and ruddy, with a fair countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the Philistine said to David, Am I as a dog, that you come against me with a staff and stones? [and David said, Nay, but worse than a dog.] And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air, and to the beasts of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And David said to the Philistine, You come to me with sword, and with spear, and with shield; but I come to you in the name of the Lord God of hosts of the army of Israel, which you have defied {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} this day. And the Lord shall deliver you this day into my hand; and I will kill you, and take away your head from off you, and will give your limbs and the limbs of the army of the Philistines this day to the birds of the sky, and to the wild beasts of the earth; and all the earth shall know that there is a God in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And all this assembly shall know that the Lord delivers not by sword or spear, for the battle [is] the Lord's, and the Lord will deliver you into our hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And the Philistine arose and went to meet David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And David stretched out his hand to his scrip, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead, and the stone penetrated through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} [So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in the hand of David. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And David ran, and stood upon him, and took his sword, and killed him, and cut off his head: and the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, and they fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And the men of Israel and Juda arose, and shouted and pursued them as far as the entrance to Geth, and as far as the gate of Ascalon: and the slain men of the Philistines fell in the way of the gates, both to Geth, and to Accaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And the men of Israel returned from pursuing after the Philistines, and they destroyed their camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; Cumberland's calculation, the height of Goliath was about eleven feet ten inches; but Parkhurst estimating the ordinary cubit at seventeen inches and a half, calculates that he was nine feet six inches high. Few instances can be produced of men who can be compared with him. Pliny says, "The tallest man that hath been seen in our days was one name Gabara, who, in the days of Claudius, the late Emperor, was brought out of Arabia. He was nine feet nine inches." Josephus mentions a Jew, named Eleazar, whom Vitellius sent to Rome, who was seven cubits, or ten feet two inches high. Becanus saw a man near ten feet, and a woman that was full ten feet. And, to mention no more, a man of the name of John Middleton, born at Hale, near Warrington, in Lancashire, in the reign of James the First, was more than nine feet high. Dr. Plott, in his history of Staffordshire, says, that "his hand, from the carpus to the end of the middle finger, was seventeen inches, his palms eight inches and a half broad, and his whole height was nine feet three inches; wanting but six inches of the height of Goliath of Gath." \textsuperscript{6} target of brass or, gorget \textsuperscript{18} carry cheeses Heb. cheeses of milk; their thousand Heb. a thousand look \textsuperscript{19} the valley Dr. Richardson says, that in about twenty minutes, in an easterly direction, form the cave of St. John (which is about two hours or six miles, in a westerly direction, from Jerusalem), they came to the valley of Elah; which position seems to agree with that of Shochoh and Azekah. He describes it as "a small valley, and the place of the encampment is pointed out where it narrows into a broad, deep ravine; part of it was in crop, and part of it was under the plough, which was drawn by a couple of oxen. A small stream, which had shrunk almost under its stony bed, passes through it from east to west, from which we are informed that David chose out five smooth stones, and hasted and ran to meet the haughty champion of Gath. A well of water under the bank, with a few olive trees above, on the north side of the valley, are said to mark the spot of the shepherd's triumph over his boasting antagonist. Saul and his men probably occupied the side of the valley which is nearest to Jerusalem, on which the ground is higher and more rugged than on the other side." \textsuperscript{20} left the sheep; trench or, place of the carriage; fight or, battle array, or place of fight \textsuperscript{22} his carriage Heb. the vessels from upon him saluted his brethren Heb. asked his brethren of peace \textsuperscript{24} him Heb. his face, sore \textsuperscript{25} the king;, free in Israel \textsuperscript{28} Eliab's anger; with I know \textsuperscript{31} sent for him Heb. took him; The preceding twenty verses, from the to the inclusive, the, and from the to the end of this chapter, with the first and the, 10th, 11th, 18th, and 19th, of, are all wanting in the Vatican copy of the LXX; and they are supposed by Dr. Kennicott, and others, to be an interpolation. But, as Bp. Horsley observes, it appears, from many circumstances of the story, that David's combat with Goliath was many years prior to Saul's madness, and David's introduction to him as a musician. In the first place, David was quite a youth when he engaged with Goliath ( and ). When introduced to Saul he was of full age ( ). Again, this combat was his first appearance in public life, and his first military exploit (, ). When introduced as a musician, he was a man of established character, and a man of war ( ). The Arabs also call the dynasty of the Philistine kings, who reigned in Palestine when the Hebrews came there, Galutiah, or Jalutiah. Achmed Al Fassi says, "Those kings were as well known by the name of Jalaut, as the ancient kings of Egypt by that of Pharaoh. David killed the Jalaut who reigned in his time, and entirely rooted out the Philistines, the rest of whom fled into Africa, and from them descended the Brebers or Berbers, who inhabit the coast of Barbary." It is remarkable that the Berbers themselves should acknowledge their descent from the Philistines. "The name Goliath, which they pronounce Sghialud, is very common among the Brebers, and the history of the champion of the Philistines is very well known to the Moors.
