\subsection*{Kings I 19}
\markright{KINGS I 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, to kill David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David much: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul seeks to kill you: take heed to yourself therefore to-morrow morning, and hide yourself, and dwell in secret. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will go forth, and stand near my father in the field where you shall be, and I will speak concerning you to my father; and I will see what his answer may be, and I will tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jonathan spoke favorably concerning David to Saul his father, and said to him, Let not the king sin against your servant David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds [are] very good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he put his life in his hand, and struck the Philistine, and the Lord wrought a great deliverance; and all Israel saw, and rejoined: why then do you sin against innocent blood, to kill David without a cause? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan; and Saul swore, saying, [As] the Lord lives, he shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jonathan called David, and told him all these words; and Jonathan brought David in to Saul, and he was before him as in former times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And there was again war against Saul; and David did valiantly, and fought against the Philistines, and struck them with a very great slaughter, and they fled from before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And an evil spirit from God was upon Saul, and he was resting in his house, and a spear [was] in his hand, and David was playing on the harp with his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Saul sought to strike David with the spear; and David withdrew [suddenly] from the presence of Saul; and he drove the spear into the wall; and David retreated and escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass in that night, that Saul sent messengers to the house of David to watch him, in order to kill him in the morning; and Melchol David's wife told him, saying, Unless you save your life this night, to-morrow you shall be slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So Melchol lets David down by the window, and he departed, and fled, and escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Melchol took images, and laid them on the bed, and she put the liver of a goat by his head, and covered them with clothes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Saul sent messengers to take David; and they say that he is sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he sends to David, saying, Bring him to me on the bed, that I may kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the messengers come, and, behold, the images [were] on the bed, and the goat's liver at his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Saul said to Melchol, Why have you thus deceived me, and suffered my enemy to depart, and he has escaped? and Melchol said to Saul, He said, let me go, and if not, I will kill you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So David fled, and escaped, and comes to Samuel to Armathaim, and tells him all that Saul had done to him: and Samuel and David went, and lived in Navath in Rama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David [is] in Navath in Rama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Saul sent messengers to take David, and they saw the assembly of the prophets, and Samuel stood [as] appointed over them; and the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they prophesy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it was told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied: and Saul sent again a third set of messengers, and they also prophesied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Saul was very angry, and went himself also to Armathaim, and he comes as far as the well of the threshing floor that is in Sephi; and he asked and said, Where [are] Samuel and David? And they said, Behold, in Navath in Rama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he went thence to Navath in Rama: and there came the Spirit of God upon him also, and he went on prophesying till he came to Navath in Rama. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he took off his clothes, and prophesied before them; and lay down naked all that day and all that night: therefore they said, [Is] Saul also among the prophets?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And Saul's enmity now burst forth, in the avowed purpose of putting David to death; and nothing less than the especial interposition of Providence could have saved David's life, when every officer about the king's person, and every soldier, had positive orders to dispatch him. \textsuperscript{4} spake good; sin against; because his works \textsuperscript{5} put his life; slew wrought, ; sin against innocent; without a cause \textsuperscript{7} in times past Heb. yesterday, third day, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{8} David, him Heb. his face \textsuperscript{10} sought; he slipped; and escaped \textsuperscript{11} sent messengers *title, to watch him \textsuperscript{13} an image Heb. teraphim, *marg., ; a pillow Rather, "the net-work of goat's hair at its (the Teraphim's) pillow; " for the kevir, (whence the Chaldee and Syriac kavreetho, a honey-comb, from its net-like form), seems to have been a kind of mosquito-net, which, says Dr. Shaw, is "a close curtain of gauze, used all over the East, by people of fashion, to keep out the flies." That they had such anciently cannot be doubted. Thus when Judith had beheaded Holofernes in his bed (, ) "she pulled down the canopy (or the mosquito net, το κωνωπειου, from κωνωψ, a gnat, or mosquito, whence our word canopy) wherein he did lie in his drunkenness, from the pillars." \textsuperscript{15} Bring him The eastern beds consist merely of two thick cotton quilts, one of which, folded double, serves as a mattress, the other as a covering. Such seems to have been the bed of David, which could easily have been carried, with himself in it, to the presence of Saul. \textsuperscript{16} And when It is highly probable that David, when supposed to be sick, was thought to be hid in the harem or chamber of Michal. "The harems, " says Deut. Lam. Motraye, "are sanctuaries, as sacred and inviolable, for persons pursed by justice for any crime, debt, etc., as the Roman Catholic churches in Italy, Spain, Portugal, etc." Thus we find, that to effect his purpose, Saul sent messengers to Michal, but they treated her harem with too much respect to enter it at first; but being authorised by Saul, they entered even into her chamber; and during the delay occasioned by respect for the privacy of Michal, David escaped. \textsuperscript{17} Why hast; mine enemy; And Michal He said; why should \textsuperscript{23} the Spirit; until he came \textsuperscript{24} stripped; lay Heb. fell, Is Saul\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 20}
\markright{KINGS I 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David fled from Navath in Rama, and comes into the presence of Jonathan; and he said, What have I done, and what [is] my fault, and wherein have I sinned before your father, that he seeks my life? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jonathan said to him, Far be it from you: you shall not die: behold, my father will not do any thing great or small without discovering it to me; and why should my father hide this matter from me? This thing is not [so]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David answered Jonathan, and said, Your father knows surely that I have found grace in your sight, and he said, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he refuse his consent: but [as] the Lord lives and your soul lives, as I said, [the space] is filled up between me and death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jonathan said to David, What does your soul desire, and what shall I do for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David said to Jonathan, Behold, to-morrow [is] the new moon, and I shall not on any account sit down to eat, but you shall let me go, and I will hide in the plain till the evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if your father do in anyway enquire for me, then shall you say, David earnestly asked leave of me to run to Bethleem his city, for [there is] there, a yearly sacrifice for all the family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} If he shall say thus, Well, — [all is] safe for your servant: but if he shall answer harshly to you, know that evil is determined by him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you shall deal mercifully with your servant; for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself: and if there is iniquity in your servant, kill me yourself; but why do you thus bring me to your father? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jonathan said, That be far from you: for if I surely know that evil is determined by my father to come upon you, although it should not be against your cities, I will tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David said to Jonathan, Who can tell me if your father should answer roughly? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jonathan said to David, Go, and abide in the field. And they went out both into the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Jonathan said to David, the Lord God of Israel knows that I will sound my father as I have an opportunity, three several times, and, behold, [if good] should be determined concerning David, and I do not send to you to the field, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} God do so to Jonathan and more also: as I shall [also] report the evil to you, and make it known to you, and I will let you go; and you shall depart in peace, and the Lord shall be with you, as he was with my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if indeed I continue to live, then shall you deal mercifully with me; and if I indeed die, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} you shall not withdraw your mercy from my house for ever: and if you do not, when the Lord cuts off the enemies of David each from the face of the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [should it happen] that the name of Jonathan be revealed by the house of David, then let the Lord seek out the enemies of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jonathan swore yet again to David, because he loved the soul of him that loved him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jonathan said, To-morrow [is] the new moon, and you will be enquired for, because your seat will be observed as vacant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall stay three days, and watch an opportunity, and shall come to your place where you may hide yourself in the day of your business, and you shall wait by that stone Ezel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And I will shoot three arrows, aiming them at a mark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And behold, I [will] send a lad, saying, Go find me the arrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} If I should expressly say to the lad, The arrow [is] here, and on this side of you, take it; [then] come, for it is well with you, and there is no reason [for fear, as] the Lord lives: [but] if I should say thus to the young man, The arrow [is] on that side of you, and beyond; go, for the Lord has sent you away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And as for the word which you and I have spoken, behold, the Lord [is] witness between me and you for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} So David hides himself in the field, and the [new] month arrives, and the king comes to the table to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he sat upon his seat as in former times, even on his seat by the wall, and he went before Jonathan; and Abenner sat on one side of Saul, and the place of David was empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Saul said nothing on that day, for he said, It seems to have fallen out that he is not clean, because he has not purified himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass on the morrow, on the second day of the month, that the place of David was empty; and Saul said to Jonathan his son, Why has not the son of Jessae attended both yesterday and today at the table? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Jonathan answered Saul, and said to him, David asked leave of me to go as far as Bethleem his city; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and he said, Let me go, I pray you, for we have a family sacrifice in the city, and my brethren have sent for me; and now, if I have found grace in your eyes, I will even go over and see my brethren: therefore he is not present at the table of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Saul was exceedingly angry with Jonathan, and said to him, You son of traitorous damsels! for do I not know that you are an accomplice with the son of Jessae to your shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For so long as the son of Jessae lives upon the earth, your kingdom shall not be established: now then send and take the young man, for he shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jonathan answered Saul, Why is he to die? What has he done? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Saul lifted up his spear against Jonathan to kill him: so Jonathan knew that this evil was determined on by his father to kill David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Jonathan sprang up from the table in great anger, and did not eat bread on the second [day] of the month, for he grieved bitterly for David, because his father determined [on mischief] against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And morning came, and Jonathan went out to the field, as he appointed [to do] for a signal to David, and a little boy [was] with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he said to the boy, Run, find me the arrows which I shoot: and the boy ran, and [Jonathan] shot an arrow, and sent it beyond [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the boy came to the place where the arrow was which Jonathan shot; and Jonathan cried out after the lad, and said, The arrow [is] on that side of you and beyond you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Jonathan cried out after his boy, saying, Make all speed, and stay not. And Jonathan's boy gathered up the arrows, and brought the arrows to his master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And the boy knew nothing, only Jonathan and David [knew]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy, and said to his boy, Go, enter into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And when the lad went in, then David arose from the south, and fell upon his face, and did obeisance to him three times, and they kissed each other, and wept for each other, for a great while. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, and as we have both sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord shall be witness between me and you, and between my seed and your seed for ever—[even so let it be]. And David arose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} God forbid; show it me Heb. uncover mine ear, *marg. \textsuperscript{3} sware; but truly;, as thy soul; but a step \textsuperscript{4} Whatsoever etc. or, Say what is thy mind, and I will do, etc desireth Heb. speaketh, or thinketh \textsuperscript{5} the new moon The months of the Hebrews were lunar months, and they reckoned from one new moon to another. And, as their feasts, particularly the passover, were reckoned according to this, they were very scrupulous in observing the first appearance of each new moon. On these new moons, they offered sacrifices, and feasted together, but the gathering together of all the families of a tribe on such occasions seems to have taken place only once in the year.; that I may \textsuperscript{8} deal kindly; thou hast, if there be; why shouldest \textsuperscript{12} O Lord This verse is evidently deficient. The LXX have Κυριος ο Θεος Ισραηλ οιδεν, "The Lord God of Israel doth know; " the Syraic and Arabic, "The Lord God of Israel is witness; " either of which makes good sense. But two of Dr. Kennicott's manuscripts supply the word chai, "liveth; " and the text reads thus: "As the Lord God of Israel liveth, when I have sounded my father - if there be good unto David, and I then send not unto thee, " etc.; which is a still better sense.; sounded Heb. searched, show it thee Heb. uncover thine ear \textsuperscript{13} The Lord do; the Lord be; he hath been with my father \textsuperscript{16} made Heb. cut; Let the Lord \textsuperscript{17} because he loved him or, by his love toward him for he loved \textsuperscript{18} new moon and thou shalt Among the forms of salutation and compliment used in Persia, one was, according to my mode of notation in italics, Ja i shama khali bud pish yaran, signifying, Thy place or seat was empty among thy friends. This phrase, or the greater part of it, was frequently addressed to myself when coming into a circle of Persian acquaintances, after an absence of several days or weeks. It reminded me of a passage in the First book of Samuel ( ). And thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty. And again, David's place was empty." Sir W. Ouseley's Travels, vol i. preface, p.16. empty Heb. missed \textsuperscript{19} quickly or, diligently, Heb. greatly hide thyself, when the business Heb. in the day of the business Ezel or, that sheweth the way. \textsuperscript{21} no Heb. not any thing as the \textsuperscript{30} Saul's;, ; Thou etc. or, Thou perverse rebel, Heb. Son of perverse rebellion, ; and unto the This reflection on the mother of Jonathan, by the passionate monarch, reflects more dishonour on himself than on his brave and noble minded son. Mungo Park gives an instance of the prevalence of the same principles in Africa; for he says, "Maternal affection is every where conspicuous among the Africans, and creates a correspondent return of tenderness in the child. 'Strike me, ' said my attendant, 'but do not curse my mother.' I found the same sentiment to prevail universally in all parts of Africa." King Saul, unable to villify Jonathan to his own satisfaction by personal reproaches, outstepped the ordinary abuse of his day, and proceeded to that which was designed to produce unusual vexation, and vented the bitterness of his mind by maligning the character of his own wife and Jonathan's mother. \textsuperscript{31} send, shall surely die Heb. is the son of death; *marg. \textsuperscript{32} Wherefore; what hath; cast, ; whereby \textsuperscript{34} in fierce; he was grieved \textsuperscript{36} Run beyond him Heb. to pass over him \textsuperscript{40} artillery Heb. instruments, Rather weapons, as the word kelim also denotes; and here means the bow, quiver, and arrows. This is probably the only place in our language in which the word artillery is not applied to cannon or ordinance, but simply to weapons of war. his lad Heb. the lad that was his \textsuperscript{41} and fell; and they kissed; David exceeded \textsuperscript{42} Go in peace; forasmuch as or, the Lord be witness of that which, etc. And he arose; The separation of two such faithful friends was equally grievous to them both, but David's case was the more deplorable. For when Jonathan was returning to his family and friends, David was leaving all his comforts, even those of God's sanctuary, and therefore his grief exceeded Jonathan's; or, perhaps it was because his temper was more tender and his passions stronger. They referred each other to the covenant of friendship that was between them, both of them being comforted thereby in this very mournful separation - "We have sworn both of us in the name of the Lord, for ourselves and our heirs, that we and they will be faithful and kind to each other from generation to generation."\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David comes to Nomba to Abimelech the priest: and Abimelech was amazed at meeting him, and said to him, Why [are] you alone, and nobody with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David said to the priest, The king gave me a command today, and said to me, Let no one know the matter on which I send you, and concerning which I have charged you: and I have charged my servants [to be] in the place that is called, The faithfulness of God, Phellani Maemoni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And now if there are under your hand five loaves, give into my hand what is ready. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the priest answered David, and said, There are no common loaves under my hand, for I have none but holy loaves: if the young men have been kept at least from women, then they shall eat [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David answered the priest, and said to him, Yes, we have been kept from women for three days: when I came forth for the journey all the young men were purified; but this expedition is unclean, therefore it shall be sanctified this day because of my weapons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Abimelech the priest gave him the show bread; and it is wrapped in a cloth: if you will take it, take it for yourself, for there is no other except it here. And David said, Behold, there is none like it; give it me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he gave it him; and David arose, and fled in that day from he presence of Saul: and David came to Anchus king of Geth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the servants of Anchus said to him, [Is] not this David the king of the land? Did not the dancing women begin the song to him, saying, Saul has struck his thousand, and David his ten thousands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And David laid up the words in his heart, and was greatly afraid of Anchus king of Geth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he changed his appearance before him, and feigned himself a false character in that day; and drummed upon the doors of the city, and used extravagant gestures with his hands, and fell against the doors of the gate, and his spittle ran down upon his beard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Anchus said to his servants, Behold! you⌃ see the man [is] mad: why have you⌃ brought him in to me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [Am] I in lack of madmen, that you⌃ have brought him in to me to play the madman? Jerome says, that in his time the ruins of it might be seen not far from Diospolis or Lydda. But the Rabbins assert that Jerusalem might be seen from this town. It is well known that from all antiquity it was held no crime to tell a lie in order to save life. Thus Diphilon Υπολαμβανω το ψευδας επι σωτηρια λεγομενον, ουδεν περιποιεισθαι δυσχερες . "I hold it right to tell a lie for safety. Nothing should be avoided to save life." A heathen may say or sing thus, but no Christian can act thus and save his soul, though he may save his life. \textsuperscript{3} under thine; present Heb. found \textsuperscript{4} hallowed bread; if the young \textsuperscript{5} the vessels; in a manner though it were sanctified this day in the vessel or, especially when this day there is other sanctified in the vessel. \textsuperscript{9} The sword the valley, behold behind \textsuperscript{10} fled; Achish or, Abimelech; *title Gath Jerome says there was a large town called Gath, in the way from Eleutheropolis to Gaza; and Eusebius speaks of another Gath, five miles from Eleutheropolis, towards Lydda (and consequently different from that mentioned by Jerome); and also of another Gath, between Jamnia and Antipatris. It appears to have been the extreme boundary of the Philistine territory in one direction, as Ekron was on the other (; ), and lay near Mareshah ( . ), which agrees pretty well with the position assigned it by Jerome. But Reland and Dr. Wells agree with Eusebius; and the authors of the Universal History (b. i. c. 7) place it about six miles form Jamnia, fourteen south of Joppa, and thirty-two west of Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{11} the servants *title the king \textsuperscript{13} changed *title; scrabbled or, made marks \textsuperscript{14} is mad or, playeth the madman\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 23}
\markright{KINGS I 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it was told David, saying, behold, the Philistines war in Keila, and they rob, they trample on the threshing-floors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go and strike these Philistines? And the Lord said, Go, and you shall strike these Philistines, and shall save Keila. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the men of David said to him, Behold, we are afraid here in Judea; and how shall it be if we go to Keila? Shall we go after the spoils of the Philistines? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David enquired yet again of the Lord; and the Lord answered him, and said to him, Arise and go down to Keila, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So David and his men with him went to Keila, and fought with the Philistines; and they fled from before him, and he carried off their cattle, and struck them with a great slaughter, and David rescued the inhabitants of Keila. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass when Abiathar the son of Achimelech fled to David, that he went down with David to Keila, having an ephod in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it was told Saul that David was come to Keila: and Saul said, God has sold him into my hands, for he is shut up, having entered into a city that has gates and bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Saul charged all the people to go down to war to Keila, to besiege David and his men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David knew that Saul spoke openly of mischief against him: and David said to Abiathar the priest, Bring the ephod of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David said, Lord God of Israel, your servant has indeed heard, that Saul seeks to come against Keila to destroy the city on my account. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Will [the place] be shut up? And now will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, tell your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord said, It will be shut up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David arose, and the men with him, in number about four hundred, and they went forth from Keila, and went wherever they could go: and it was told Saul that David had escaped from Keila, and he forbore to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he lived in Maserem in the wilderness, in the narrow [passes]; and lived in the wilderness in mount Ziph, in the dry country. And Saul sought him continually, but the Lord delivered him not into his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David perceived that Saul went forth to seek David; and David was in the dry mountain in the New Ziph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jonathan son of Saul rose, and went to David to Caene, and strengthened his hands in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said to him, Fear not, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you; and you shall be king over Israel, and I shall be second to you; and Saul my father knows it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So they both made a covenant before the Lord; and David lived in Caene, and Jonathan went to his home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Ziphites came up out of the dry country to Saul to the hill, saying, Behold, is not David hidden with us in Messara, in the narrows in Caene in the hill of Echela, which is on the right of Jessaemon? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And now [according to] all the king's desire to come down, let him come down to us; they have shut him up into the hands of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Saul said to them, Blessed [be] you⌃ of the Lord, for you⌃ have been grieved on my account. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Go, I pray you, and make preparations yet, and notice his place where his foot shall be, quickly, in that place which you⌃ spoke of, lest by any means he should deal craftily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Take notice, then, and learn, and I will go with you; and it shall come to pass that if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Ziphites arose, and went before Saul: and David and his men [were] in the wilderness of Maon, westward, to the right of Jessaemon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Saul and his men went to seek him: and they brought word to David, and he went down to the rock that was in the wilderness of Maon: and Saul heard, and followed after David to the wilderness of Maon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Saul and his men go on one side of the mountain, and David and his men are on the other side of the mountain: and David was hiding himself to escape from Saul: and Saul and his men encamped against David and his men, in order to take them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And there came a messenger to Saul, saying, Haste you, and come here, for the Philistines have invaded the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So Saul returned from following after David, and went to meet the Philistines: therefore that place was called The divided Rock.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Keilah was a city of Judah, situated, according to Eusebius, eight miles from Eleutheropolis, towards Hebron. Sozomen says that the prophet Habakkuk's tomb was shewn there.; rob the \textsuperscript{2} inquired In what way David made this enquiry we are not told; but it was probably by means of Abiathar; and therefore it would seem, that with Houbigant, we should read the immediately after the . - This adventure was truly noble and patriotic. Had not David loved his country, and been above all motives of private and personal revenge, he would have rejoiced in this invasion of Judea, as producing a strong diversion in his favour, and embroiling his inveterate enemy. In most cases, a man with David's wrongs would have joined with the enemies of his country, and avenged himself on the author of his calamities; but he thinks of nothing but succouring Keilah, and using his power and influence in behalf of his brethren. \textsuperscript{4} yet again; for I will \textsuperscript{7} am 2943, bc 1061, An, Ex, Is 430 God hath, ; he is shut \textsuperscript{12} deliver Heb. shut up, They will \textsuperscript{14} a mountain the wilderness Ziph is mentioned in Joshua with Carmel and Maon, near which it seems to have been situated; and as we have mention of Carmel and Maon in the history of David, as adjoining to Ziph, it cannot be doubted that by the Ziph, in the wilderness of which David now lay, and where was the hill of Hachilah, is to be understood Ziph near Carmel and Maon., Saul; but God \textsuperscript{17} Fear not; shall not; thou shalt be I shall be; that also Saul \textsuperscript{19} the Ziphites; *title; Hachilah Calmet states, that Hachilah was a mountain about ten miles south of Jericho, where Jonathan Maccabeus built the castle of Massada, west of the Dead Sea, and not far from En-gedi., on the south Heb. on the right hand Jeshimon or, the wilderness, Eusebius places Jeshimon ten miles south of Jericho, near the Dead Sea; which agrees extremely well with the position of Hachilah, as stated by Calmet. \textsuperscript{20} all the desire; our part \textsuperscript{22} haunt is Heb. foot shall be \textsuperscript{23} take knowledge; I will search; the thousands \textsuperscript{24} the wilderness Maon, from which the adjoining mountainous district derived its name, was city in the most southern parts of the tribe of Judah, and a neighbouring town to Carmel. Hence Nabal ( ) is described as a man of Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and though he might dwell generally in Maon, yet he is styled Nabal the Carmelite, from the place where his estate lay. Calmet supposes it to be the city Minois, which Eusebius places in the vicinity of Gaza; and the Moenoemi Castrum, which the Theodosian code places near Beersheba. Maon; the south \textsuperscript{25} into a rock or, from the rock \textsuperscript{27} there came; the Philistines; invaded Heb. spread themselves upon \textsuperscript{28} Selahammahlekoth that is, the rock of divisions, Because, says the Targum, "the heart of the king was divided to go hither and thither." Here Saul was obliged to separate himself from David, in order to go and oppose the invading Philistines; which deliverance of David was of such a nature as made the Divine interposition fully visible.\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 24}
\markright{KINGS I 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David rose up from thence, and lived in the narrow passes of Engaddi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass when Saul returned from pursuing after the Philistines, that it was reported to him, saying, David [is] in the wilderness of Engaddi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he took with him three thousand men, chosen out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men in front of Saddaeem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he came to the flocks of sheep that were by the way, and there was a cave there; and Saul went in to make preparation, and David and his men were sitting in the inner part of the cave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the men of David said to him, Behold, this [is] the day of which the Lord spoke to you, that he would deliver your enemy into your hands; and you shall do to him as [it is] good in your sight. So David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul's garment secretly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass after this that David's heart struck him, because he had cut off the skirt of his garment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David said to his men, The Lord forbid it me, that I should do this thing to my lord the anointed of the Lord, to lift my hand against him; for he is the anointed of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So David persuaded his men by [his] words, and did not suffer them to arise and kill Saul: and Saul arose and went his way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David rose up [and went] after him out of the cave: and David cried after Saul, saying, [My] lord, [O] king! and Saul looked behind him, and David bowed with his face to the ground, and did obeisance to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David said to Saul, Why do you listen to the words of the people, saying, Behold, David seeks your life? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, your eyes have seen this day how that the Lord has delivered you this day into my hands in the cave; and I would not kill you, but spared you, and said, I will not lift up my hand against my lord, for he is the Lord's anointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And behold, the skirt of your mantle [is] in my hand, I cut off the skirt, and did not kill you: know then and see today, there is no evil in my hand, nor impiety, nor rebellion; and I have not sinned against you, yet you lay snares for my soul to take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The Lord judge between me and you, and the Lord requite you on yourself: but my hand shall not be upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As the old proverb says, Transgression will proceed from the wicked ones: but my hand shall not be upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now after whom do you come forth, O king of Israel? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog, and after a flea? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The Lord be judge and umpire between me and you, the Lord look upon and judge my cause, and rescue me out of your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, [Is] this your voice, Son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Saul said to David, You [are] more righteous that I, for you have recompensed me good, but I have recompensed you evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you have told me today what good you have done me, how the Lord shut me up into your hands today, and you did not kill me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And if any one should find his enemy in distress, and should send him forth in a good way, then the Lord will reward him good, as you have done this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And now, behold, I know that you shall surely reign, and the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Now then swear to me by the Lord, that you will not destroy my seed after me, that you will not blot out my name from the house of my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So David swore to Saul: and Saul departed to his place, and David and his men went up to the strong-hold of Messera.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when Saul following Heb. after it was told; the wilderness \textsuperscript{2} Saul took and went, the rocks \textsuperscript{3} the sheepcotes Caves in the rocks, in which it is still common for shepherds and their flocks to lodge. Dr. Pococke observes, "Beyond the valley [of Tekoa], there is a very large grotto, which the Arabs call El-Maamah, a hiding place. The high rocks on each side of the valley are almost perpendicular; and the way to the grotto is by a terrace formed in the rock, which is very narrow. There are two entrances into it; we went by the farthest, which leads by a narrow passage into a very large grotto, the rock being supported by natural pillars; the top of it rises in several places like domes; the grotto is perfectly dry. There is a tradition, that the people of the country, to the number of 30, 000, retired into this grotto, to avoid a bad air. This place is so strong, that one would imagine it to be one of the strong holds of En-gedi, to which David and his men fled from Saul, and possibly it may be that very cave in which he cut off Saul's skirt; for David and his men might, with good ease, lie hid there and not be seen by him." \subsection*{Kings I 25}
\markright{KINGS I 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Samuel died, and all Israel assembled, and bewailed him, and they bury him in his house in Armathaim: and David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Maon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was a man in Maon, and his flocks were in Carmel, and [he was] a very great man; and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand she-goats: and he happened to be shearing his flock in Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the man's name [was] Nabal, and his wife's name [was] Abigaia: and his wife [was] of good understanding and very beautiful in person: but the man [was] harsh, and evil in his doings, and the man [was] churlish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David heard in the wilderness, that Nabal the Carmelite was shearing his sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David sent ten young men, and he said to the young men, Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and ask him in my name how he is. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And thus shall you⌃ say, May you and your house seasonably prosper, and all yours be in prosperity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now, behold, I have heard that your shepherds who were with us in the wilderness are shearing your sheep, and we hindered them not, neither did we demand any thing from them all the time they were in Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Ask your servants, and they will tell you. Let then your servants find grace in your eyes, for we are come on a good day; give we pray you, whatever your hand may find, to your son David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So the servants come and speak these words to Nabal, according to all these words in the name of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Nabal sprang up, and answered the servants of David, and said, Who [is] David? and who [is] the son of Jessae? Now-a-days there is abundance of servants who depart every one from his master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And shall I take my bread, and my wine, and my beasts that I have slain for my shearers, and shall I give them to men of whom I know not whence they are? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So the servants of David turned back, and returned, and came and reported to David according to these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said to his men, Gird on every man his sword. And they went up after David, about four hundred men: and two hundred abode with the stuff. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And one of the servants reported to Abigaia the wife of Nabal, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our lord; but he turned away from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the men were very good to us; they did not hinder us, neither did they demand from us any thing all the days that we were with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when we were in the field, they were as a wall round about us, both by night and by day, all the days that we were with them feeding the flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And now do you consider, and see what you will do; for mischief is determined against our lord and against his house; and he [is] a vile character, and one can’t speak to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Abigaia hasted, and took two hundred loaves, and two vessels of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five ephahs of fine flour, and one homer of dried grapes, and two hundred cakes of figs, and put them upon asses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And she said to her servants, Go on before me, and behold I come after you: but she told not her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when she had mounted her ass and was going down by the covert of the mountain, behold, David and his men came down to meet her, and she met them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David said, Perhaps I have kept all his possessions in the wilderness that he should wrong me, and we did not order the taking anything of all his goods; yet he has rewarded me evil for good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So God do to David and more also, if I leave one male of all that belong to Nabal until the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Abigaia saw David, and she hasted and alighted from her ass; and she fell before David on her face, and did obeisance to him, [bowing] to the ground {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [even] to his feet, and said, On me, my lord, be my wrong: let, I pray you, your servant speak in your ears, and hear you the words of your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let not my lord, I pray you, take to heart this pestilent man, for according to his name, so is he; Nabal [is] his name, and folly [is] with him: but I your handmaid saw not the servants of my lord whom you did send. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And now, my lord, [as] the Lord lives, and your soul lives, as the Lord has kept you from coming against innocent blood, and from executing vengeance for yourself, now therefore let your enemies, and those that seek evil against my lord, become as Nabal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And now accept this token of goodwill, which your servant has brought to my lord, and you shall give it to the servants that wait on my lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Remove, I pray you, the trespass of your servant; for the Lord will surely make for my lord a sure house, for the Lord fights the battles of my lord, and there shall no evil be ever found in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And [if] a man shall rise up persecuting you and seeking your life, yet shall the life of my lord be bound up in the bundle of life with the Lord God, and you shall whirl the life of your enemies [as] in the midst of a sling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it shall be when the Lord shall have wrought for my lord all the good things he has spoken concerning you, and shall appoint you to be ruler over Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} then this shall not be an abomination and offense to my lord, to have shed innocent blood without cause, and for my lord to have avenged himself: and so may the Lord do good to my lord, and you shall remember your handmaid to do her good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And David said to Abigaia, Blessed [be] the Lord God of Israel, who sent you this very day to meet me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} and blessed [be] your conduct, and blessed [be] you, who have hindered me this very day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But surely as the Lord God of Israel lives, who hindered me this day from doing you harm, if you had not hasted and come to meet me, then I said, There shall [surely] not be left to Nabal till the morning one male. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And David took of her hand all that she brought to him, and said to her, Go in peace to your house: see, I have listened to your voice, and accepted your petition. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Abigaia came to Nabal: and, behold, he had a banquet in this house, as the banquet of a king, and the heart of Nabal [was] merry within him, and he [was] very drunken: and she told him nothing great or small till the morning light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And it came to pass in the morning, when Nabal recovered from his wine, his wife told him these words; and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And it came to pass after about ten days, that the Lord struck Nabal, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And David heard it and said, Blessed [be] the Lord, who has judged the cause of my reproach at the hand of Nabal, and has delivered his servant from the power of evil; and the Lord has returned the mischief of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and spoke concerning Abigaia, to take her to himself for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So the servants of David came to Abigaia to Carmel, and spoke to her, saying, David has sent us to you, to take you to himself for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And she arose, and did reverence with her face to the earth, and said, Behold, your servant [is] for an handmaid to wash the feet of your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Abigaia arose, and mounted her ass, and five damsels followed her: and she went after the servants of David, and became his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And David took Achinaam out of Jezrael, and they were both his wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Saul gave Melchol his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Amis who was of Romma.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2944, bc 1060, An, Ex, Is 431 Samuel lamented; in his house; the wilderness \textsuperscript{2} Maon possessions were or, business was Carmel Not the famous mount Carmel, in the north of Canaan, and in the tribe of Asher; but a city, on a mountain of the same name, in the south of Judah, which seems to have given name to the surrounding territory. Eusebius and Jerome inform us, that there was in their time a town called Carmelia, ten miles east from Hebron, where the Romans kept a garrison, whose position well agrees with this Carmel. man; three thousand; shearing This was a very ancient custom, and appears to have been always attended with festivity. The ancient Romans, however, used to pluck off the wool from the sheep's backs; and hence a fleece was called vellus, a vellendo, from plucking it off. Pliny says, that in his time sheep were not shorn every where, but in some places the wool was still plucked off.; Carmel \textsuperscript{3} good, was churlish; and he was Wehoo calibbee, literally, "and he was a Calebite; " but as the word cailev signifies a dog, the Septuagint has understood it as implying a man of canine disposition, and translated it, και ανθρωπος κυνικος, "and he was a doggish man." It is understood in the same way by the Syriac and Arabic. \textsuperscript{5} greet him etc. Heb. ask him in my name of peace \textsuperscript{6} liveth; Peace be both *marg. \textsuperscript{7} thy shepherds In those times, and at the present day, wandering Arabs, under their several chiefs, think that they have a right to exact contributions of provisions, etc., wherever they come. But David, though he lived in the wilderness like the Arab emirs, had not adopted their manners. One of them, at the head of 600 men, would have demanded, from time to time, some provision or present from Nabal's servants, for permitting them to feed at quiet; and would have driven them away from the watering place upon any dislike. David had done nothing of this kind; but had protected them against those who would. we hurt Heb. we shamed \textsuperscript{8} a good day; thy son \textsuperscript{9} ceased Heb. rested, or, became quiet \textsuperscript{10} Who is David; there be \textsuperscript{11} Shall I then; flesh Heb. slaughter give it; whom \textsuperscript{13} Gird ye;, ; David also; two hundred \textsuperscript{14} railed on them Heb. flew upon them \textsuperscript{15} very good; hurt Heb. shamed \textsuperscript{17} evil, ; a son of Belial; that a man \textsuperscript{18} made haste; took two The Eastern bread is generally both thin and small; and answers to our cakes.; two bottles That is, two goatskins' full. five sheep Not one sheep to one hundred men. clusters Heb. lumps, Raisins dried in the sun, cakes of figs Figs cured and then pressed together. Now all this provision was a matter of little worth; and had it been granted in the first instance, it would have perfectly satisfied David, and secured his good offices. \textsuperscript{20} rode she came down David was coming down mount Paran; Abigail was coming down from Carmel. \textsuperscript{22} So and more Nothing can justify this conduct of David, which was rash, unjust, and cruel in the extreme. David himself condemns it, and thanks God for being prevented from executing this evil ( )., ; if I leave any that pisseth etc. This seems to have been a proverbial expression among the Israelites; and may with the utmost propriety be read "any male." \textsuperscript{24} fell; Upon; let thine; audience Heb. ears \textsuperscript{25} regard Heb. lay it to his heart; man of Belial, Nabal that is, fool \textsuperscript{26} as the Lord liveth; and as thy the Lord hath; from avenging thyself Heb. saving thyself, now let \textsuperscript{27} blessing or, present; follow Heb. walk at the feet of, *marg. \textsuperscript{28} forgive the Lord; fighteth; evil hath \textsuperscript{29} bound The metaphors in this verse are derived from the consideration, that things of value are collected together, and often tied up in bundles, like sheaves of corn, to prevent their being scattered and lost, and that whatever is put into a sling is not intended to be preserved, but to be thrown away.; with the Lord, ; sling out as out of the middle of a sling Heb. in the midst of the bow of a sling \textsuperscript{31} grief Heb. staggering, or, stumbling; avenged, ; remember \textsuperscript{32} David overlooks the rich and seasonable present of Abigail, though pressed with hunger and wearied with travel; but her advice, which disarmed his rage, and calmed his revenge, draws forth these high and affectionate gratulations. These were his joyful and glorious trophies; not over his enemies, but over himself. \textsuperscript{34} kept me back hasted; there had \textsuperscript{36} a feast; merry; she told him \textsuperscript{37} had told him, his heart \textsuperscript{39} Blessed; pleaded; kept his servant; hath returned; to take her It is probable that David had heard that Saul, to cut off his pretensions to the throne, had married Michal to Phalti; and this justified him in taking Abigail, it not being then unlawful for a man to have several wives. This conduct of David's corresponds with the manner in which the Oriental princes generally form their matrimonial alliances. "The king of Abyssinia, " says Mr. Bruce, "sends an officer to the house where the lady lives, who announces to her that it is the king's pleasure she should remove instantly to the palace. She then dresses herself in the best manner, and immediately obeys. Thenceforward he assigns her an apartment in the palace, and gives her a house elsewhere in any part she chooses." \textsuperscript{42} Abigail; after her Heb. at her feet \textsuperscript{44} But Saul Rather, "For Saul, " etc., as the particle ε, wav, frequently signifies; this being the cause why David took another wife. Michal, Phalti, Phaltiel Gallim This town appears to have been situated in the tribe of Benjamin, as it is mentioned in, with Michmash, Geba, etc.\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 26}
\markright{KINGS I 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Ziphites come out of the dry country to Saul to the hill, saying, Behold, David hides himself with us in the hill Echela, opposite Jessemon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him [went] three thousand men chosen out of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Saul encamped in the hill of Echela in front of Jessemon, by the way, and David lived in the wilderness: and David saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David sent spies, and ascertained that Saul was come prepared out of Keila. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David arose secretly, and goes into the place where Saul was sleeping, and there [was] Abenner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul was sleeping in a chariot, and the people had encamped along round about him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David answered and spoke to Abimelech the Chettite, and to Abessa the son Saruia the brother of Joab, saying, Who will go in with me to Saul into the camp? And Abessa said, I will go in with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So David and Abessa go in among the people by night: and behold, Saul was fast asleep in the chariot, and his spear was stuck in the ground near his head, and Abenner and his people slept round about him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abessa said to David, The Lord has this day shut up your enemy into your hands, and now I will strike him to the earth with the spear to the ground once [for all], and I will not strike him again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David said to Abessa, Do not lay him low, for who shall lift up his hand against the anointed of the Lord, and be guiltless? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David said, [As] the Lord lives, if the Lord strike him not, or his day come and he die, or he go down to battle and be added [to his fathers, do not so]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The Lord forbid it me that I should lift up my hand against the anointed of the Lord: and now take, I pray you, the spear from his bolster, and the pitcher of water, and let us return home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So David took the spear, and the pitcher of water from his bolster, and they went home: and there was no one that saw, and no one that knew, and there was no one that awoke, all being asleep, for a stupor from the Lord had fallen upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of a hill afar off, and [there was] a good distance between them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David called to the people, and spoke to Abenner, saying, Will you not answer, Abenner? and Abenner answered and said, Who are you that call? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David said to Abenner, [Are] not you a man? and who [is] like you in Israel? Why then do you not guard your lord the king? for one out of the people went in to destroy your lord the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And this thing [is] not good which you have done. [As] the Lord lives, you⌃ are worthy of death, you⌃ who guard your lord the king, the anointed of the Lord: and now behold, I pray you, the spear of the king, and the cruse of water: where are the articles that should be at his head? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Saul recognized the voice of David, and said, [Is] this your voice, son David? and David said, I [am] your servant, [my] lord, O king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said, Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? for in what have I sinned? and what unrighteousness has been found in me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant. If God stirs you up against me, let your offering be acceptable: but if the sons of men, they [are] cursed before the Lord, for they have cast me out this day so that I should not be established in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other Gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And now let not my blood fall to the ground before the Lord, for the king of Israel has come forth to seek your life, as the night hawk pursues [its prey] in the mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Saul said, I have sinned: turn, son David, for I will not hurt you, because my life was precious in your eyes; and today I have been foolish and have erred exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And David answered and said, Behold, the spear of the king: let one of the servants come over and take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord shall recompense each according to his righteousness and his truth, since the Lord delivered you this day into my hands, and I would not lift my hand against the Lord's anointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And, behold, as your life has been precious this very day in my eyes, so let my life be precious before the Lord, and may he protect me, and deliver me out of all affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Saul said to David, Blessed [be] you, [my] son; and you shall surely do valiantly, and surely prevail. And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} Abner, ;, ; trench or, midst of his carriages; The word maugal never signifies a ditch or rampart, but a chariot or waggon way. Nor does it seem to denote a ring of carriages, as Buxtorf and others interpret the word; for it is not probable that Saul would encumber his army with baggage in so rapid a pursuit, nor that so mountainous a country was practicable for waggons. It appears simply to mean here, the circular encampment (from agal, "round") which these troops formed, in the midst of which, as being the place of honour, Saul reposed. An Arab camp, D'Arvieux informs us, is always circular, when the disposition of the ground will permit, the prince being in the middle, and the troops at a respectful distance around him. Add to which, their lances are fixed near them in the ground all the day long, ready for action. \textsuperscript{6} Hittite;, to Abishai, ; Zeruiah Who will go \textsuperscript{8} God, ; delivered Heb. shut up; *marg. the second time \textsuperscript{10} the Lord liveth, ; his day; he shall descend \textsuperscript{12} So David, a deep sleep \textsuperscript{13} the top; David, by retiring to a place of safety before he called to Abner, seems to have manifested more distrust of Saul than he had done on a former occasion. Yet he desired that Saul and all Israel should be informed of his conduct at this time. Abner and his soldiers, by neglecting to guard Saul when he slept, had exposed his life, and merited to be treated as his enemies, though he confided in them as friends; for, although their sound sleep was undoubtedly supernatural, yet there might be a neglect of placing sentinels, arising from contempt of David's small company. Saul also deemed David his enemy, though he had before spared and protected his life. \textsuperscript{16} worthy to die Heb. the sons of death; *marg. Lord's \textsuperscript{19} let my lord; stirred; accept Heb. smell; cursed; they have driven; abiding Heb. cleaving the inheritance \textsuperscript{20} let not my, the king; a flea Parosh, (in Arabic borghooth, Syriac, poorthano, ) the well known little contemptible and troublesome insect, the flea, seems to be so called from its agility in leaping and skipping, from para, "free, " and raash, "to leap, bound." David, by comparing himself to this insect, seems to import, that while it would cost Saul much pains to catch him, he would obtain but very little advantage from it. a partridge Korai certainly denotes the partridge, which is called in Arabic, kiraa . It seems to be so called from the cry or cur which it utters when calling its young. \textsuperscript{21} I have sinned, ; I will no my soul \textsuperscript{24} as thy life; let him deliver; *title\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 27}
\markright{KINGS I 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David said in his heart, Now shall I be one day delivered [for death] into the hands of Saul; and there is no good thing for me unless I should escape into the land of the Philistines, and Saul should cease from seeking me through every coast of Israel: so I shall escape out of his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} So David arose, and the six hundred men that were with him, and he went to Anchus, son Ammach, king of Geth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David lived with Anchus, he and his men, each with his family; and David and both his wives, Achinaam, the Jezraelitess, and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it was told Saul that David had fled to Geth; and he no longer sought after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David said to Anchus, If now your servant has found grace in your eyes, let them give me, I pray you, a place in one of the cities in the country, and I will dwell there: for why does your servant dwell with you in a royal city? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he gave him Sekelac in that day: therefore Sekelac came into possession of the king of Judea to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the number of the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was four months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David and his men went up, and made an attack on all the Gesirites and on the Amalekites: and behold, the land was inhabited, (even the land from Gelampsur) by those who come from the fortified [cities] even to the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he struck the land, and saved neither man nor woman alive; and they took flocks, and herds, and asses, and camels, and raiment; and they returned and came to Anchus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Anchus said to David, On whom have you⌃ made an attack today? And David said to Anchus, On the south of Judea, and on the south of Jesmega, and on the south of the Kenezite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I have not saved man or woman alive to bring them to Geth, saying, Lest they carry a report to Geth against us, saying, These things David does. And this was his manner all the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So David had the full confidence of Anchus, who said, He is thoroughly disgraced among his people in Israel and he shall be my servant for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2946, bc 1058, An, Ex, Is 433 And David, ; I shall This was a rash conclusion: God had caused him to be anointed king of Israel, and promised his accession to the throne, and had so often interposed in his behalf, that he was authorised to believe the very reverse. perish Heb. be consumed there is nothing; into the land \textsuperscript{2} David This measure of David's, in uniting himself to the enemies of his God and people, was highly blameable; was calculated to alienate the affections of the Israelites; and led to equivocation, if not downright falsehood. the six, Achish \textsuperscript{6} Ziklag was at first given to the tribe of Judah, but was afterwards ceded to that of Simeon; but as it bordered on the Philistines, if they had ever been expelled, they had retaken it. Eusebius simply says it was situated in the south of Canaan. \textsuperscript{7} the time Heb. the number of days a full year Heb. a year of days \textsuperscript{8} am 2948, bc 1056, An, Ex, Is, 435 the Geshurites;, ; Gezrites or, Gerzites, These people seem to be the Gerrhenians ( ) whose chief city, Gerrha, is mentioned by Strabo as lying between Gaza and Pelusium in Egypt. the Amalekites; as thou goest \textsuperscript{9} left neither; and the camels \textsuperscript{10} Whither etc. or, Did you not make a road And David; Against David here meant the Geshurites, and Gezrites, and Amalekites, which people occupied that part of the country which lies to the south of Judah. But Achish, as was intended, understood him in a different sense, and believed that he had attacked his own countrymen. David's answer, therefore, though not an absolute falsehood, was certainly an equivocation intended to deceive, and therefore incompatible with that sense of truth and honour which became him as a prince, and a professor of true religion. From these, and similar passages, we may observe the strict impartiality of the Sacred Scriptures. They present us with the most faithful delineation of human nature; they exhibit the frailties of kings, priests, and prophets, with equal truth; and examples of vice and frailty, as well as of piety and virtue, are held up, that we may guard against the errors to which the best men are exposed. the Jerahmeelites, Kenites \textsuperscript{12} utterly to abhor Heb. to stink\par}
