\subsection*{Kings I 28}
\markright{KINGS I 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered themselves together with their armies to go out to fight with Israel; and Anchus said to David, Know surely, that you shall go forth to battle with me, [you], and your men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David said to Anchus, Thus now you shall know what your servant will do. And Anchus said to David, So will I make you captain of my body-guard continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Samuel died, and all Israel lamented for him, and they bury him in his city, in Armathaim. And Saul had removed those who had in them divining spirits, and the wizards, out of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Philistines assemble themselves, and come and encamp in Sonam: and Saul gathers all the men of Israel, and they encamp in Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was alarmed, and his heart was greatly dismayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Saul enquired of the Lord; and the Lord answered him not by dreams, nor by manifestations, nor by prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then Saul said to his servants, Seek for me a woman who has in her a divining spirit, and I will go to her, and enquire of her: and his servants said to him, Behold, [there is] a woman who has in her a divining spirit at Aendor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he goes, and two men with him, and they come to the woman by night; and he said to her, Divine to me, I pray you, by the divining spirit within you, and bring up to me him whom I shall name to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the woman said to him, Behold now, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those who had in them divining spirits, and the wizards from the land, and why do you spread a snare for my life to destroy it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Saul swore to her, and said, [As] the Lord lives, no injury shall come upon you on this account. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the woman said, Whom shall I bring up to you? and he said, Bring up to me Samuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the woman saw Samuel, and cried out with a loud voice: and the woman said to Saul, Why have you deceived me? for you are Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king said to her, Fear not; tell me whom you have seen. And the woman said to him, I saw gods ascending out of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said to her, What did you perceive? and she said to him, An upright man ascending out of the earth, and he [was] clothed with a mantle. And Saul knew that this was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the earth, and did obeisance to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Samuel said, Why have you troubled me, that I should come up? And Saul said, I am greatly distressed, and the Philistines war against me, and God has departed from me, and no longer hearkens to me either by the hand of the prophets or by dreams: and now I have called you to tell me what I shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Samuel said, Why asked you me, whereas the Lord has departed from you, and taken part with your neighbor? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord has done to you, as the Lord spoke by me; and the Lord will rend your kingdom out of your hand, and will give it to your neighbor David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and did not execute his fierce anger upon Amalec, therefore the Lord has done this thing to you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord shall deliver Israel with you into the hands of the Philistines, and to-morrow you and your sons with you shall fall, and the Lord shall deliver the army of Israel into the hands of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Saul instantly fell at his full length upon the earth, and was greatly afraid because of the words of Samuel; and there was no longer any strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all that day, and all that night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the woman went in to Saul, and saw that he was greatly disquieted, and said to him, Behold now, your handmaid has listened to your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have heard the words which you have spoken to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And now listen, I pray you, to the voice of your handmaid, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, and you shall be strengthened, for you will be going on your way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But he would not eat; so his servants and the woman constrained him, and he listened to their voice, and rose up from the earth, and sat upon a bench. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the woman had a fat heifer in the house; and she hasted and killed it; and she took meal and kneaded it, and baked unleavened cakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And she brought [the meat] before Saul, and before his servants; and they ate, and rose up, and departed that night.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} that the, Philistines thou shalt go \textsuperscript{6} inquired; by dreams; by Urim; by prophets \textsuperscript{7} Seek me; a familiar spirit; that I may; Endor En-dor, a city of Manasseh, was situated in the plain of Jezreel; and Eusebius and Jerome inform us, that it was a great town in their days, four miles south from Mount Tabor, near Nain, towards Scythopolis. This agrees with Maundrell, who says, that not many miles eastward of Tabor, you see mount Hermon, at the foot of which is seated Nain and Endor; and Burckhardt says, that in two hours and a half from Nazareth, towards Scythopolis or Bisan, they came to the village of Denouny, near which are the ruins of Endor; where the witch's grotto is shewn. \textsuperscript{8} disguised, ; I pray thee; bring me \textsuperscript{14} What form is he of Heb. What is his form a mantle \textsuperscript{15} Why hast, I am sore; the Philistines God; answereth, prophets Heb. the hand of prophets therefore \textsuperscript{17} to him or, for himself, The LXX read σοι, and the Vulgate tibi, to thee; which is the reading of five of Dr. Kennicott's and De Rossi's manuscripts, as well as both the Bibles printed at Venice in 1518, where we read lecha, "to thee, " for lo, "to him; " and as the words are spoken to Saul, this seems to be evidently the correct reading. as he spake, me Heb. mine hand thy neighbour \textsuperscript{19} the Lord; and to morrow There is considerable diversity of opinion, both among learned and pious men, relative to this appearance to Saul. But the most probable opinion seems to be, that Samuel himself did actually appear to Saul, not by the power of enchantment, but by the appointment and especial mercy of God, to warn this infatuated monarch of his approaching end, that he might be reconciled with his Maker. There is not the smallest intimation of chicanery or Satanic influence given in the text; but on the contrary, from the plain and obvious meaning of the language employed, it is perfectly evident that it was Samuel himself, Shemooel hoo, as it is expressed in . Indeed the very soul of Samuel seems to breathe in his expressions of displeasure against the disobedience and wickedness of Saul; while the awful prophetic denunciations which accordingly came to pass, were such as neither human nor diabolical wisdom could foresee, and which could only be known to God himself, and to those to whom he chose to reveal them. \textsuperscript{20} fell straightway Heb. made haste and fell with the fullness of his stature sore afraid\par}

\subsection*{Kings I 29}
\markright{KINGS I 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Philistines gather all their armies to Aphec, and Israel encamped in Aendor, which is in Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the lords of the Philistines went on by hundreds and thousands, and David and his men went on in the rear with Anchus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the lords of the Philistines said, Who [are] these that pass by? And Anchus said to the captains of the Philistines, [Is] not this David the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with us some time, even this second year, and I have not found any fault in him from the day that he attached himself to me even until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the captains of the Philistines were displeased at him, and they say to him, Send the man away, and let him return to his place, where you did set him; and let him not come with us to the war, and let him not be a traitor in the camp: and wherewith will he be reconciled to his master? Will it not be with the heads of those men? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [Is] not this David whom they celebrated in dances, saying, Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Anchus called David, and said to him, [As] the Lord lives, you [are] right and approved in my eyes, and [so is] your going out and your coming in with me in the army, and I have not found [any] evil to charge against you from the day that you came to me until this day: but you are not approved in the eyes of the lords. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now then return and go in peace, thus you shall not do evil in the sight of the lords of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David said to Anchus, What have I done to you? and what have you found in your servant from the [first] day that I was before you even until this day, that I should not come and war against the enemies of the lord my king? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Anchus answered David, I know that you [are] good in my eyes, but the lords of the Philistines say, He shall not come with us to the war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now then rise up early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord that are come with you, and go to the place where I appointed you, and entertain no evil thought in your heart, for you [are] good in my sight: and rise early for your journey when it is light, and depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So David arose early, he and his men, to depart and guard the land of the Philistines: and the Philistines went up to Jezrael to battle.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} Is not this David These words seem to mark no definite time; and may be understood thus: "Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me for a considerable time?" these days found \textsuperscript{4} Make this fellow The princes reasoned wisely, according to the common practice of mankind; and it was well for David that they were such good politicians. It was ordered by a gracious Providence that they refused to let David go with them to this battle, in which he must have been either an enemy to his country, or false to his friends and to his trust. Had he fought for the Philistines, he would have fought against God and his country; and had he in the battle gone over to the Israelites, he would have deceived and become a traitor to the hospitable Achish. God therefore delivered him from such disgrace; and by the same kind Providence he was sent back to rescue his wives, and the wives and children of his people, from captivity. \textsuperscript{6} the Lord; thou hast; thy going; I have not the lords favour etc. Heb. thou art not good in the eyes of the lords; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} displease Heb. do not evil in the eyes of the lords \textsuperscript{8} But what have, with Heb. before that I may not \textsuperscript{9} as an angel, ; the princes \textsuperscript{11} And the Philistines; Jezreel, or Esdrelon, was a city of Issachar, afterwards celebrated as the residence of the kings of Israel, delightfully situated in the extensive and fertile plain of the same name, which extends from Scythopolis or Bethshan on the east to mount Carmel on the west. Eusebius and Jerome inform us, that it was in their time a place of considerable consequence, lying between Scythopolis on the east and Legio on the west; and the latter (on ). informs us that it was pretty near Maximianopolis. The Jerusalem Itinerary places it ten miles west from Scythopolis; and William of Tyre says it was called Little Gerinum in his time, and that there was a fine fountain in it, whose waters fell into the Jordan near Scythopolis. See note on .\par}

\markright{KINGS I 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when David and his men had entered Sekelac on the third day, that Amalec had made an incursion upon the south, and upon Sekelac, and struck Sekelac, and burnt it with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And as to the women and all things that were in it, great and small, they killed neither man nor woman, but carried them captives, and went on their way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David and his men came into the city, and, behold, it was burnt with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters were carried captive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David and his men lifted up their voice, and wept till there was no longer any power within them to weep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And both the wives of David were carried captive, Achinaam, the Jezraelitess, and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David was greatly distressed, because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, each for his sons and his daughters: but David strengthened himself in the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David said to Abiathar the priest the son of Achimelech, Bring near the ephod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? and he said to him, Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them, and you shall surely rescue [the captives]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So David went, he and the six hundred men with him, an they come as far as the brook Bosor, and the superfluous ones stopped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he pursued them with four hundred men; and there remained behind two hundred men, who tarried on the other side of the brook Bosor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they find an Egyptian in the field, and they take him, and bring him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they caused him to drink water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and he ate, and his spirit was restored in him; for he had not eaten bread, and had not drunk water three days and three nights. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said to him, Whose are you? and whence are you? and the young man the Egyptian said, I am the servant of an Amalekite; and my master left me, because I was taken ill three days ago. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And we made an incursion on the south of the Chelethite, and on the parts of Judea, and on the south of Chelub, and we burnt Sekelac with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David said to him, Will you bring me down to this troop? And he said, Swear now to me by God, that you will not kill me, and that you will not deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down upon this troop. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So he brought him down there, and behold, they [were] scattered abroad upon the surface of the whole land, eating and drinking, and feasting by [reason of] all the great spoils which they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David came upon them, and struck them from the morning till the evening, and on the next day; and not one of them escaped, except four hundred young men, who were mounted on camels, and fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued both his wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And nothing was lacking to them of great or small, either of the spoils, or the sons and daughters, or anything that they had taken of theirs; and David recovered all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he took all the flocks, and the herds, and led them away before the spoils: and it was said of these spoils, These [are] the spoils of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David comes to the two hundred men who were left behind that they should not follow after David, and he had caused them to remain by the brook of Bosor; and they came forth to meet David, and to meet his people with him: and David drew near to the people, and they asked him how he did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then every ill-disposed and bad man of the soldiers who had gone with David, answered and said, Because they did not pursue together with us, we will not give them of the spoils which we have recovered, only let each one lead away with him his wife and his children, and let them return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And David said, You⌃ shall not do so, after the Lord has delivered [the enemy] to us, and guarded us, and the Lord has delivered into our hands the troop that came against us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And who will listen to these your words? for they are not inferior to us; for according to the portion of him that went down to the battle, so shall be the portion of him that abides with the baggage; they shall share alike. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass from that day forward, that it became an ordinance and a custom in Israel until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And David came to Sekelac, and sent of the spoils to the elders of Juda, and to his friends, saying, Behold [some] of the spoils of the enemies of the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} to those in Baethsur, and to those in Rama of the south, and to those in Gethor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And to those in Aroer, and to those in Ammadi, and to those in Saphi, and to those in Esthie, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and to those in Geth, and to those in Cimath, and to those in Saphec, and to those in Themath, and to those in Carmel, and to those in the cities of Jeremeel, and to those in the cities of the Kenezite; \subsection*{Kings I 31}
\markright{KINGS I 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Philistines fought with Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and they fall down wounded in the mountain in Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Philistines press closely on Saul and his sons, and the Philistines strike Jonathan, and Aminadab, and Melchisa son of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the battle prevails against Saul, and the shooters with arrows, even the archers find him, and he was wounded under the ribs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Saul said to his armor-bearer, Draw your sword and pierce me through with it; lest these uncircumcised come and pierce me through, and mock me. But his armor-bearer would not, for he feared greatly: so Saul took his sword and fell upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he fell also himself upon his sword, and died with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, in that day together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, and those beyond Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead; and they leave their cities and flee: and the Philistines come and dwell in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass on the morrow that the Philistines come to strip the dead, and they find Saul and his three sons fallen on the mountains of Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they turned him, and stripped off his armor, and sent it into the land of the Philistines, sending round glad tidings to their idols and to the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they set up his armor at the temple of Astarte, and they fastened his body on the wall of Baethsam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the inhabitants of Jabis Galaad hear what the Philistines did to Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they rose up, [even] every man of might, and marched all night, and took the body of Saul and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Baethsam; and they bring them to Jabis, and burn them there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they took their bones, and buried them in the field that is in Jabis, and fasted seven days.\par

\section*{2 Samuel Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Nathan and Gad continuing the Samuel corpus\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Conservative tradition commonly reads 1-2 Samuel as one prophetic history completed after Samuel's death by Nathan and Gad; compare 1 Chronicles 29:29.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The David narratives are treated throughout the NT as real sacred history grounding the messianic hope.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 10th century BC during David's reign\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology covers David's reign over Judah and all Israel, the covenant promise, and the later court narratives.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same Davidic framework, though Samuel remains one of the books with major textual interest between MT and Greek tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} David's reign in Hebron and Jerusalem, including covenant promise, sin, chastening, and kingdom consolidation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To present the establishment of David's kingdom, the Davidic covenant, and the moral seriousness of sin even in the Lord's chosen king.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} Davidic covenant; kingship; sin and repentance; providence; kingdom consolidation; messianic promise\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} David's ascent 1-5; Ark and covenant promise 6-7; Royal victories 8-10; David's sin and its consequences 11-20; Final words and appendices 21-24.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Samuel a (4Q51) preserves extensive 2 Samuel material about 50 BC | Subst. 4Q Samuel manuscripts are the earliest substantial Hebrew witnesses to large portions of 2 Samuel 3rd-1st centuries BC | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve 2 Samuel in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Retelling of David's reign by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Samuel contains major text-critical loci, and Qumran plus LXX evidence is often crucial where the MT is difficult or abbreviated.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 2 Samuel as prophetic court history standing within the inspired Samuel corpus and treats textual divergence as a preservation issue, not a challenge to inerrancy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Kings II}
\markboth{KINGS II}{}
\subsection*{Kings II 1}
\markright{KINGS II 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after Saul was dead, that David returned from striking Amalec, and David abode two days in Sekelac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came from the camp, from the people of Saul, and his garments were torn, and earth [was] upon his head: and it came to pass when he went in to David, that he fell upon the earth, and did obeisance to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David said to him, Whence come you? and he said to him, I have escaped out of the camp of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David said to him, What [is] the matter? tell me. And he said, The people fled out of the battle, and many of the people have fallen and are dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David said to the young man who brought him the tidings, How know you that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the young man that brought the tidings, said to him, I happened accidentally to be upon mount Gelbue; and, behold, Saul was leaning upon his spear, and, behold, the chariots and captains of horse pressed hard upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he looked behind him, and saw me, and called me; and I said, Behold, [here am] I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said to me, Who are you? and I said, I am an Amalekite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to me, Stand, I pray you, over me, and kill me, for a dreadful darkness has come upon me, for all my life [is] in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew he would not live after he was fallen; and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was upon his arm, and I have brought them hither to my lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And David laid hold of his garments, and tore them; and all the men who were with him tore their garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they lamented, and wept, and fasted till evening, for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Juda, and for the house of Israel, because they were struck with the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said to the young man who brought the tidings to him, Whence are you? and he said, I am the son of an Amalekite sojourner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David said to him, How was it you were not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the anointed of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David called one of his young men, and said, Go and fall upon him: and he struck him, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And David said to him, Your blood [be] upon your own head; for your mouth has testified against you, saying, I have slain the anointed of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he gave orders to teach it the sons of Juda: behold, it is written in the book of Right. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Set up a pillar, O Israel, for the slain that died upon your high places: how are the mighty fallen! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Tell it not in Geth, and tell it not as glad tidings in the streets of Ascalon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You⌃ mountains of Gelbue, let not dew no rain descend upon you, nor fields of first fruits [be upon you], for there the shield of the mighty ones has been grievously assailed; the shield of Saul was not anointed with oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} From the blood of the slain, and from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan returned not empty; and the sword of Saul turned not back empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and the beautiful, were not divided: comely [were they] in their life, and in their death they were not divided: [they were] swifter than eagles, and they were stronger than lions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you with scarlet together with your adorning, who added golden ornaments to your apparel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, even the slain ones upon your high places! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I am grieved for you, my brother Jonathan; you were very lovely to me; your love to me was wonderful beyond the love of women. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the third; a man clothes; and earth he fell \textsuperscript{4} How went Heb. What was, etc. *marg. the people \textsuperscript{6} As I happened The story of this young man appears to be wholly a fiction, formed for the purpose of ingratiating himself with David, as the next probable successor to the crown. There is no fact in the case, except for the bringing of the diadem and bracelets of Saul, as a sufficient evidence of his death, which, as he appears to been a plunderer of the slain, he seems to have stripped from the dead body of the unfortunate monarch It is remarkable, that Saul, who had forfeited his crown by his disobedience and ill-timed clemency with respect to the Amalekites, should now have the insignia of royalty stripped from his person by one of those very people.; mount; Saul \textsuperscript{7} Here am I Heb. When the Khalif Cayem Bemrillah granted the investiture of certain dominions to an Eastern prince, the ceremony was performed by sending him letters patent, a crown, chain, and bracelets. The bracelet, says Mr. Morier, are ornaments fastened above the elbows, composed of precious stones of great value, and are only worn by the king and his sons. \textsuperscript{18} teach; bow Kasheth, or the bow, was probably the title of the following threnody; so called, in the oriental style, because Saul's death was occasioned by that weapon, and because the bow of Jonathan, out of which "the arrow was shot beyond the lad, " ( ), is celebrated in this song. the book Jasher or, the upright, So LXX επι βιβλιου τον ευθους; Targum, siphra deooritha, "the book of the law; " the Arabic, "the book of Ashee. This is the book of Samuel." \noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after this that David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into one of the cities of Juda? and the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? and he said, To Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David went up there to Chebron, [he] and both his wives, Achinaam the Jezraelitess, and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and the men that were with him, every one and his family; and they lived in the cities of Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the men of Judea come, and anoint David there to reign over the house of Juda; and they reported to David, saying, The men of Jabis of the country of Galaad have buried Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David sent messengers to the rulers of Jabis of the country of Galaad, and David said to them, Blessed be you⌃ of the Lord, because you⌃ have wrought this mercy toward your lord, even toward Saul the anointed of the Lord, and you⌃ have buried him and Jonathan his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now may the Lord deal in mercy and truth towards you: and I also will requite towards you this good deed, because you⌃ have done this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now let your hands be made strong, and be valiant; for your master Saul is dead, and moreover the house of Juda have anointed me to be king over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But Abenner, the son of Ner, the commander-in-chief of Saul's army, took Jebosthe son of Saul, and brought him up from the camp to Manaem {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and made him king over the land of Galaad, and over Thasiri, and over Jezrael, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Jebosthe, Saul's son [was] forty years old, when he reigned over Israel; and he reigned two years, but not over the house of Juda, who followed David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the days which David reigned in Chebron over the house of Juda were seven years and six months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Abenner the son of Ner went forth, and the servants of Jebosthe the son of Saul, from Manaem to Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joab the son of Saruia, and the servants of David, went forth from Chebron, and met them at the fountain of Gabaon, at the same place: and these sat down by the fountain on this side, and those by the fountain on that side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abenner said to Joab, Let now the young men arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And there arose and passed over by number twelve of the children of Benjamin, belonging to Jebosthe the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they seized every one the head of his neighbor with his hand, and his sword [was thrust] into the side of his neighbor, and they fall down together: and the name of that place was called The portion of the treacherous ones, which is in Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the battle was very severe on that day; and Abenner and the men of Israel were worsted before the servants of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there were there the three sons of Saruia, Joab, and Abessa, and Asael: and Asael was swift in his feet as a roe in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Asael followed after Abenner, and turned not to go to the right hand or to the left from following Abenner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Abenner looked behind him, and said, Are you Asael himself? and he said, I am. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Abenner said to him, Turn you to the right hand or to the left, and lay hold for yourself on one of the young men, and take to yourself his armor: but Asel would not turn back from following him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Abenner said yet again to Asael, Stand aloof from me, lest I strike you to the ground? and how should I lift up my face to Joab? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And what does this mean? return to Joab your brother? But he would not stand aloof; and Abenner smites him with the hinder end of the spear on the loins, and the spear went out behind him, and he falls there and dies on the spot: and it came to pass that every one that came to the place where Asael fell and died, stood still. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Joab and Abessa pursued after Abenner, and the sun went down: and they went as far as the hill of Amman, which is in the front of Gai, by the desert way of Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the children of Benjamin who followed Abenner gather themselves together, and they formed themselves into one body, and stood on the top of a hill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Abenner called Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour perpetually? know you not that it will be bitter at last? How long then will you refuse to tell the people to turn from following our brethren? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Joab said, As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, even from the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Joab sounded the trumpet, and all the people departed, and did not pursue after Israel, and did not fight any longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Abenner and his men departed at evening, [and went] all that night, and crossed over Jordan, and went along the whole adjacent [country], and they come to the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Joab returned from following Abenner, and he assembled all the people, and there were missing of the people of David, nineteen men, and Asael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the servants of David struck of the children of Benjamin, of the men of Abenner, three hundred and sixty men belonging to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they take up Asael, and bury him in the tomb of his father in Bethleem. And Joab and the men with him went all the night, and the morning rose upon them in Chebron.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} the men of Judah, ; anointed, ; the men of Jabeshgilead \textsuperscript{5} David This was a generous and noble act, highly indicative of the grandeur of David's mind. He respected Saul, though he had been greatly injured by him, as the anointed king of Israel, and once his legitimate sovereign; and he loved Jonathan as his most intimate friend. Blessed \textsuperscript{7} let your; valiant Heb. the sons of valour \textsuperscript{8} Abner, Saul's host Heb. the host which was Saul's Ishbosheth;, Esh-baal Mahanaim \textsuperscript{9} Gilead; Ashurites The LXX read τον Θασιρι, Thasiri; and the Vulgate Gessuri, "Geshurites; " but it is probable that for ashuri, "Ashurites, " we should read ashairi, "Asherites, " or those of the tribe of Asher.; over Jezreel \textsuperscript{10} two years Houbigant proposes to read shesh shanah, "six years" instead of shetayim shanim, "two years, " of the text, which he contends is a solecism; for, in pure Hebrew, the words should be shetayim shanah; and this is the reading of twenty manuscripts; but two is acknowledged by all the versions and manuscripts yet collated. \textsuperscript{11} time Heb. number of days \textsuperscript{12} am 2951, bc 1053, An, Ex, Is, 438 Mahanaim; Gibeon \textsuperscript{13} Joab, ; together Heb. them together pool \textsuperscript{16} by the head Probably by the beard or hair of the head. Plutarch, in his Apophthegms, informs us, that all things being ready for a battle, Alexander's captains asked him whether he had anything else to command them. "Nothing, " said he, "but that the Macedonians shave their beards." Parmenio wondering what he meant, "Dost thou not know, " said he, "that in fight, there is no better hold than the beard?" Helkathhazzurim that is, the field of strong men \textsuperscript{18} three, was as light; foot Heb. his feet a wild roe Heb. one of the roes that is in the field; The word tzevee, rather denotes the gazelle or antelope (see note on .) \textsuperscript{19} turned; following Abner Heb. after Abner \textsuperscript{21} and take thee It seems that Asahel wished to get the armour of Abner as a trophy. armour or, spoil \textsuperscript{23} the fifth rib, stood still \textsuperscript{26} Shall; sword;, ; it will be; how long \textsuperscript{27} As God This was spoken in allusion to the proposal of Abner ( ), which led to the slaughter of twelve young men of each party, and thus provoked the battle. It is probable, that Joab had orders simply to act on the defensive, and would not have attacked the Israelites that day unless compelled; therefore the blame lay upon Abner and Israel.; unless;, ; in the morning Heb. from the morning gone up or, gone away \textsuperscript{29} Bithron or Bether is probably the same as Betarus, which is placed in the Antonine Itinerary between Caesarea of Palestine and Diospolis or Lydda, 18 miles from the former, and 22 from the latter. The Jerusalem Itinerary mentions a place called Bethar, 16 miles from Caesarea, and 20 from Diospolis, which is probably the same. The Talmudists say that it was four miles distant from the sea., Bether Mahanaim \textsuperscript{31} three hundred The slain of Israel, though greatly exceeding those of Judah, were not great. This might be owing to the directions given by David, to be as lenient as possible; but the death of Asahel seems to have stopped the pursuers, and greatly favoured the escape of the vanquished.\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 3}
\markright{KINGS II 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was war for a long time between the house of Saul and the house of David; and the house of David grew continually stronger; but the house of Saul grew continually weaker. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And sons were born to David in Chebron: and his firstborn was Ammon the son of Achinoom the Jezraelitess. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his second son [was] Daluia, the son of Abigaia the Carmelitess; and the third, Abessalom the son of Maacha the daughter of Tholmi the king of Gessir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the fourth [was] Ornia, the son of Aggith, and the fifth [was] Saphatia, the son of Abital. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sixth [was] Jetheraam, the son of Aegal the wife of David. These were born to David in Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abenner was governing the house of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Saul had a concubine, Respha, the daughter of Jol; and Jebosthe the son of Saul said to Abenner, Why have you gone in to my father's concubine? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abenner was very angry with Jebosthe for this saying; and Abenner said to him, Am I a dog's head? I have this day wrought kindness with the house of Saul your father, and with his brethren and friends, and have not gone over to the house of David, and do you this day seek a charge against me concerning injury to a woman? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} God do thus and more also to Abenner, if as the Lord swore to David, so do I not to him this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} to take away the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to raise up the throne of David over Israel and over Juda from Dan to Bersabee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jebosthe could not any longer answer Abenner a word, because he feared him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Abenner sent messengers to David to Thaelam where he was, immediately, saying, Make your covenant with me, and, behold, my hand [is] with you to bring back to you all the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said, With a good will I will make with you a covenant: only I demand one condition of you, saying, You shall not see my face, unless you bring Melchol the daughter of Saul, when you come to see my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David sent messengers to Jebosthe the son of Saul, saying, Restore me my wife Melchol, whom I took for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jebosthe sent, and took her from her husband, [even] from Phaltiel the son of Selle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And her husband went with her weeping behind her as far as Barakim. And Abenner said to him, Go, return; and he returned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abenner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, In former days you⌃ sought David to reign over you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and now perform [it]: for the Lord has spoken concerning David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save Israel out of the hand of all their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Abenner spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abenner went to speak in the ears of David at Chebron, all that seemed good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the house of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Abenner came to David to Chebron, and with him twenty men: and David made for Abenner and his men with him a banquet of wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Abenner said to David, I will arise now, and go, and gather to my lord the king all Israel; and I will make with him a covenant, and you shall reign over all whom your soul desires. And David sent away Abenner, and he departed in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And, behold, the servants of David and Joab arrived from their expedition, and they brought much spoil with them: and Abenner was not with David in Chebron, because he had sent him away, and he had departed in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joab and all his army came, and it was reported to Joab, saying, Abenner the son of Ner is come to David, and David has let him go, and he has departed in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Joab went in to the king, and said, What [is] this [that] you have done? behold, Abenner came to you; and why have you let him go, and he has departed in peace? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Know you not the mischief of Abenner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all things that you do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joab returned from David, and sent messengers to Abenner after [him]; and they bring him back from the well of Seiram: but David knew [it] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he brought back Abenner to Chebron, and Joab caused him to turn aside from the gate to speak to him, laying wait for him: and he struck him there in the loins, and he died for the blood of Asael the brother of Joab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And David heard [of it] afterwards, and said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before the Lord even for ever of the blood of Abenner the son of Ner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Let it fall upon the head of Joab, and upon all the house of his father; and let there not be lacking of the house of Joab one that has an issue, or a leper, or that leans on a staff, or that falls by the sword, or that wants bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For Joab and Abessa his brother laid wait continually for Abenner, because he killed Asael their brother at Gabaon in the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And David said to Joab and to all the people with him, Rend your garments, and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and lament before Abenner. And king David followed the bier. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they bury Abenner in Chebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at his tomb, and all the people wept for Abenner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the king mourned over Abenner, and said, Shall Abenner die according to the death of Nabal? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Your hands were not bound, and your feet [were] not [put] in fetters: [one] brought [you] not near as Nabal; you did fall before children of iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And all the people assembled to weep for him. And all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was yet day: and David swore, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if I eat bread or any thing else before the sun goes down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And all the people took notice, and all things that the king did before the people were pleasing in their sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} So all the people and all Israel perceived in that day, that it was not of the king to kill Abenner the son of Ner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the king said to his servants, Know you⌃ not that a great prince is this day fallen in Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And that I am this day a [mere] kinsman [of his], and [as it were] a subject; but these men the sons of Saruia are too hard for me: the Lord reward the evil-doer according to his wickedness.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} long war, between; David waxed \textsuperscript{3} Chileab, Daniel Abigail; Absalom, Talmai Geshur \textsuperscript{7} Rizpah Wherefore This action of Abner's seems a most evident proof that he intended to seize on the government; and it was so understood by Ish-bosheth; see parallel texts. gone in \textsuperscript{8} Abner; Amos I a dog's head This was a proverbial expression among the Hebrews to denote whatever was deemed worthless and contemptible. Something similar to this was the answer of the Turkish commander at Beer, on the Euphrates, to a request made to see the castle. "Do they, " said he, "take me for a child, or an ass's head, that they would feed me with sweet meats, and dupe me with a bit of cloth? No, they shall not see the castle."; do show \textsuperscript{9} So do God; as the Lord \textsuperscript{13} that is Heb. saying Thou shalt, except As Michal was not divorced, but violently separated from David, he had a legal right to demand her, and was justified in receiving her again. It is probable, also, that her marriage with Phaltiel was a force upon her inclinations; and whatever affections he might have for her, it was highly criminal for him to take another man's wife. David required Michal probably both out of affection for her, and to strengthen his interest, by asserting his affinity with the house of Saul. Michal \textsuperscript{16} along weeping Heb. going and weeping, Bahurim \textsuperscript{17} in times past Heb. both yesterday and the third day \textsuperscript{18} for the Lord;, ; By the hand \textsuperscript{24} What hast Joab and his brother Abishai, David's nephews, had been very faithful and highly useful to him in his distresses; and, from gratitude and natural affection, he had inadvertently permitted them to assume almost as much ascendancy over him as Abner had over the pusillanimous Ishbosheth. He trusted and feared them too much, and allowed them all the importance they claimed; which had emboldened them, especially Joab, to a high degree of presumption. \textsuperscript{25} that he came; *marg.; and to know \textsuperscript{27} took him; quietly or, peaceably, and smote Joab was afraid that Abner, after rendering such essential service to David, would be made the general of the army; and therefore, under pretence of avenging the death of his brother, he treacherously assassinated the unsuspecting and too-confiding Abner, and such was the power of this cool-blooded and nefarious murderer, that the king dared not bring him to justice for his crime. But, while Joab's conduct cannot be too severely reprobated, the justice of God is apparent in Abner's punishment; who, from ambition, had pertinaciously, against his conscience, opposed the declared will of God; and was induced by base resentment to desert Ish-bosheth, and offer his services to David. See note on, and see note on . for the blood \textsuperscript{28} guiltless; blood Heb. bloods, *marg. \textsuperscript{29} rest; let there; fail Heb. be cut off an issue \textsuperscript{31} And David, intending no doubt to punish Joab, and to lessen his authority with the people, commanded him to take upon him the office of chief mourner; but, as his revenge was gratified, his rival removed, and no heavier punishment inflicted, it is probable his hardened mind would feel but little objection to the ceremony. Rend; bier Heb. bed \textsuperscript{33} as a fool dieth That is, as a bad man, as the word frequently signifies in Scripture. \textsuperscript{34} hands The hand of malefactors were usually secured with cords, and their feet with fetters; a custom to which David affectingly alludes in his lamentation over the dust of Abner. Thy hands, O Abner, were not bound, as found to be a malefactor, nor thy feet put in fetters; thou was treated with honour by him whose business it was to judge thee, and thy attachment to the house of Saul was esteemed rather generous than culpable. As the best of men may fall, so thou fellest by the sword of treachery, not of justice.; wicked men Heb. children of iniquity; wept \textsuperscript{35} cause; So do; till the \textsuperscript{36} pleased them Heb. was good in their eyes as \textsuperscript{39} I am; weak Heb. tender; *marg. the sons too hard, the Lord\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 4}
\markright{KINGS II 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Jebosthe the son of Saul heard that Abenner the son of Ner had died in Chebron; and his hands were paralyzed, and all the men of Israel grew faint. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jebosthe the son of Saul had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one [was] Baana, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Remmon the Berothite of the children of Benjamin; for Beroth was reckoned to the children of Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Berothites ran away to Gethaim, and were sojourners there until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jonathan Saul's son [had] a son lame of his feet, five years old, and he was [in the way] when the news of Saul and Jonathan his son came from Jezrael, and his nurse took him up, and fled; and it came to pass as he hasted and retreated, that he fell, and was lamed. And his name [was] Memphibosthe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Rechab and Baana the sons of Remmon the Berothite went, and they came in the heat of the day into the house of Jebosthe; and he was sleeping on a bed at noon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And, behold, the porter of the house winnowed wheat, and he slumbered and slept: and the brothers Rechab and Baana went privily into the house: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jebosthe was sleeping on his bed in his chamber: and they strike him, and kill him, and take off his head: and they took his head, and went all the night by the western road. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they brought the head of Jebosthe to David to Chebron, and they said to the king, Behold the head of Jebosthe the son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life; and the Lord has executed for my lord the king vengeance on his enemies, as [it is] this day: even on Saul your enemy, and on his seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David answered and Rechab and Baana his brother, the sons of Remmon the Berothite, and said to them, [As] the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all affliction; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} he that reported to me that Saul was dead, even he was as one bringing glad tidings before me: but I seized him and killed him in Sekelac, to whom I ought, [as he thought], to have given a reward for his tidings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now evil men have slain a righteous men in his house on his bed: now then I will require his blood of your hand, and I will destroy you from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And David commanded his young men, and they kill them, and cut off their hands and their feet; and they hung them up at the fountain in Chebron: and they buried the head of Jebosthe in the tomb of Abenezer the son of Ner.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} captains; other Heb. second Beeroth \textsuperscript{4} Jonathan when the tidings, Mephibosheth, Meribbaal \textsuperscript{5} went, lay on a bed It is customary, in all hot countries, to travel or work very early and very late, and to rest at noon, at which time the heat most prevails. \textsuperscript{6} as though It is still the custom of the East, according to Dr. Perry, to allow the soldiers a certain quantity of corn, with other articles of provision, together with some pay, and as it was the custom also to grind the corn, as needed, at the break of day, these two captains very naturally went the day before to the palace, where the king's stores appear to have been kept, to fetch wheat, in order to distribute it to the soldiers under them, to be ground at the accustomed hour in the morning. The princes of the East, in those days, as appears from the history of David, reposed on their couches till the cool of the evening. They therefore came in the heat of the day, when they knew their master would be resting on his bed; and as it was a necessary to have the corn before it was needed, their coming at this time, though it might be earlier than usual, excited no suspicion. under \textsuperscript{7} took his head; When those difficulties dispirit us which should rather invigorate us and sharpen our endeavours, we betray a carelessness of character which is soon taken advantage of by our more watchful neighbours. Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty and ruin. The idle soul is an easy prey to the destroyer. \textsuperscript{10} one thinking etc. Heb. he was in his own eyes, as a bringer, etc. who thought, etc. or, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings. \textsuperscript{12} slew them; hanged; in the sepulchre\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 5}
\markright{KINGS II 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all the tribes of Israel come to David to Chebron, and they said to him, Behold, we [are] your bone and your flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And heretofore Saul being king over us, you were he that did lead out and bring in Israel: and the Lord said to you, You shall feed my people Israel, and you shall be for a leader to my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all the elders of Israel come to the king to Chebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Chebron before the Lord; and they anoint David king over all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} David [was] thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Seven years and six months he reigned in Chebron over Juda, and thirty-three years he reigned over all Israel and Juda in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David and his men, departed to Jerusalem, to the Jebusite that inhabited the land: and it was said to David, You shall not come in hither: for the blind and the lame withstood him, saying, David shall not come in hither. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David took first the hold of Sion: this [is] the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David said on that day, Every one that smites the Jebusite, let him attack with the dagger both the lame and the blind, and those that hate the soul of David. Therefore they say, The lame and the blind shall not enter into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David lived in the hold, and it was called the city of David, and he built the city itself round about from the citadel, and [he built] his own house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David advanced and became great, and the Lord Almighty [was] with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Chiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar wood, and carpenters, and stone-masons: and they built a house for David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And David knew that the Lord had prepared him to be king over Israel, and that his kingdom was exalted for the sake of his people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David took again wives and concubines out of Jerusalem, after he came from Chebron: and David had still more sons and daughters born to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And these [are] the names of those that were born to him in Jerusalem; Sammus, and Sobab, and Nathan, and Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Ebear, and Elisue, and Naphec, and Jephies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Elisama, and Elidae, and Eliphalath, Samae, Jessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Jebaar, Theesus, Eliphalat, Naged, Naphec, Janathan, Leasamys, Baalimath, Eliphaath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over Israel; and all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the strong hold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Philistines came, and assembled in the valley of the giants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? and will you deliver them into my hands? and the Lord said to David, Go up, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And David came from Upper Breaches, and struck the Philistines there: and David said, The Lord has destroyed the hostile Philistines before me, as water is dispersed; therefore the name of that place was called Over Breaches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they leave there their gods, and David and his men with him took them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Philistines came up yet again, and assembled in the valley of Giants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And David enquired of the Lord: and the Lord said, You shall not go up to meet them: turn from them, and you shall meet them near the place of weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it shall come to pass when you hear the sound of a clashing together from the grove of weeping, then you shall go down to them, for then the Lord shall go forth before you to make havoc in the battle with the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And David did as the Lord commanded him, and struck the Philistines from Gabaon as far as the land of Gazera.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} leddest out; feed; a captain \textsuperscript{3} So all; made; before; anointed \textsuperscript{6} Jerusalem; the Jebusites;, which spake etc. Dr. Kennicott's amended translation is as follows: "Who spake unto David, saying, Thou shalt not come in hither; for the blind and the lame shall drive thee away, by saying, David shall not come in hither" . "And David said, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, and through the subterraneous passage reacheth the lame and the blind, who hate the life of David (because the blind and the lame said, he shall not come into the house), shall be chief and captain. So Joab, the son of Zeriah, went up first, and was chief." Except thinking, David cannot or, saying, David shall not, etc \textsuperscript{8} Whosoever; he shall be Wherefore etc. or, Because they had said, even the blind and the lame, he shall not come into the house \textsuperscript{10} went on, and grew great Heb. went going and growing; the Lord \textsuperscript{11} Hiram; masons Heb. hewers of the stone of the wall they built \textsuperscript{14} the names, Shammuah or, Shimea, Nathan; Solomon \textsuperscript{16} Eliada or, Beeliada, Eliphalet Eliphelet \textsuperscript{20} Baalperazim that is, The plain of breaches \textsuperscript{21} David; burned them or, took them away \textsuperscript{23} inquired fetch; the mulberry trees The word bechaim, rendered mulberry trees, is rendered by Aquila, απιων, pear-trees, as the LXX also render in; and so the Vulgate in both places has pyrorum . The Rabbins, however, believe bacha signifies the mulberry-tree; with whom Ursinus agrees. It more probably denotes a large shrub which the Arabs still call baca, from its distilling an odoriferous gum, from bachah to distil, as tears. Of this opinion is Celsius, who quotes a passage from Abulfadi, who describes it as a balsam shrub, having longish leaves, and bearing a large fruit with an acrid taste. M. Forskal mentions a tree by the name of beca, with leaves rather ovated, smooth, entire. Its berries are poisonous to the sheep.\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 6}
\markright{KINGS II 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David again gathered all the young men of Israel, about seventy thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David arose, and went, he and all the people that were with him, and some of the rulers of Juda, on an expedition [to a distant place], to bring back thence the ark of God, on which the name of the Lord of Host who dwells between the cherubs upon it is called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they put the ark of the Lord on a new wagon, and took it out of the house of Aminadab who lived on the hill, and Oza and his brethren the sons of Aminadab drove the wagon with the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his brethren went before the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David and the children of Israel [were] playing before the Lord on well-tuned instruments mightily, and with songs, and with harps, and with lutes, and with drums, and with cymbals, and with pipes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they come as far as the threshing floor of Nachor: and Oza reached forth his hand to the ark of God to keep it steady, and took hold of it; for the ox shook it out of its place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord was very angry with Oza; and God struck him there: and he died there by the ark of the Lord before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David was dispirited because the Lord made a breach upon Oza; and that place was called the breach of Oza until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David feared the Lord in that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come in to me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David would not bring in the ark of the covenant of the Lord to himself into the city of David: and David turned it aside into the house of Abeddara the Gethite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the ark of the Lord lodged in the house of Abeddara the Gethite three months, and the Lord blessed all the house of Abeddara, and all his possessions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it was reported to king David, saying, The Lord has blessed the house of Abeddara, and all that he has, because of the ark of the Lord. And David went, and brought up the Ark of the Lord from the house of Abeddara to the city of David with gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there were with him bearing the ark seven bands, and for a sacrifice a calf and lambs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David sounded with well-tuned instruments before the Lord, and David [was] clothed with a fine long robe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of a trumpet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass as the ark arrived at the city of David, that Melchol the daughter of Saul looked through the window, and saw king David dancing and playing before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they bring the ark of the Lord, and set it in its place in the midst of the tabernacle which David pitched for it: and David offered whole burnt offerings before the Lord, [and] peace-offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And David made an end of offering the whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of Hosts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he distributed to all the people, even to all the host of Israel from Dan to Bersabee, both men and women, to every one a cake of bread, and a joint of meat, and a cake from the frying-pan: and all the people departed every one to his home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And David returned to bless his house. And Melchol the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and saluted him, and said, How was the king of Israel glorified today, who was today uncovered in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the dancers wantonly uncovers himself! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David said to Melchol, I will dance before the Lord. Blessed [be] the Lord who chose me before your father, and before all his house, to make me head over his people, even over Israel: therefore I will play, and dance before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will again uncover myself thus, and I will be vile in your eyes, and with the maidservants by whom you said that I was not had in honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Melchol the daughter of Saul had no child till the day of her death.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Baale, Baalah, i.e. Kirjath-jearim; whose name etc. or, at which the name, even the name of the Lord of hosts, was called upon; dwelleth \textsuperscript{3} set etc. Heb. made the ark of God to ride, ; Gibeah or, the hill \textsuperscript{5} David; , ; on all manner This place should doubtless be corrected from the parallel place; where, instead of bechol âtzey beroshim, which is literally, "with all trees or wood of fir, " we read bechol ôz oovesheerim, "with all their might, and with songs." This makes a good sense, while the former makes none: the LXX have the same reading here, εν ισχυι, και εν ωδαις . \textsuperscript{6} Nachon's, he is called Chidon put forth Even the Kohathites, who were appointed to carry the ark, after it was covered by the priests, were forbidden to touch it on pain of death; but Uzzah, who certainly was no priest, probably with some degree of irreverence, having presumed to lay his hand upon the ark, which perhaps was not covered, thus incurred the penalty due to his rashness., shook it or, stumbled \textsuperscript{7} God smote; error or, rashness \textsuperscript{8} displeased; made Heb. broken Perezuzzah that is, The breach of Uzzah \textsuperscript{14} danced; with all his; girded \textsuperscript{15} David with shouting, ;, the sound \textsuperscript{17} they brought; pitched Heb. stretched offered \textsuperscript{19} he dealt; So all the \textsuperscript{20} bless; *title Michal; glorious; uncovered We are only to understand by this expression that David had divested himself of his royal robes, in order to appear humble before the Lord, by assimilating himself to the condition of one of the priests or Levites. For we find that he was "girded with a linen ephod; " and consequently no part of his body was exposed, having only put off his outer garments. The terms uncovered or naked frequently mean no more than this in Scripture.; vain fellows; shamelessly or, openly \textsuperscript{22} more vile; in mine; maidservants or, handmaids I be had\par}
