\subsection*{Kings II 7}
\markright{KINGS II 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when the king sat in his house, and the Lord had given him an inheritance on every side [free] from all his enemies round about him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold now, I live in a house of cedar, and the ark of the Lord dwells in the midst of a tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Nathan said to the king, Go and do all that [is] in your heart, for the Lord [is] with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass in that night, that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Go, and say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord, You shall not build me a house for me to dwell in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For I have not lived in a house from the day that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt to this day, but I have been walking in a lodge and in a tent, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} wherever I went with all Israel. Have I ever spoken to any of the tribes of Israel, which I commanded to tend my people Israel, saying, Why have you⌃ not built me a house of Cedar? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now thus shall you say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord Almighty, I took you from the sheep-cote, that you should be a prince over my people, over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I was with you wherever you went, and I destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned according to the renown of the great ones on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves, and shall be no more distressed; and the son of iniquity shall no more afflict them, as he [has done] from the beginning, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel: and I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will tell you that you shall build a house to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall come to pass when your days shall have been fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, even your own issue, and I will establish his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He shall build for me a house to my name, and I will set up his throne even for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. And when he happens to transgress, then will I chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the sons of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But my mercy I will not take from him, as I took it from those whom I removed from my presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And his house shall be made sure, and his kingdom for ever before me, and his throne shall be set up for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And king David came in, and sat before the Lord, and said, Who am I, O Lord, my Lord, and what [is] my house, that you have loved me hitherto? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Whereas I was very little before you, O Lord, my Lord, yet you spoke concerning the house of your servant for a long time to [to come]. And [is] this the law of man, O Lord, my Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And what shall David yet say to you? and now you know your servant, O Lord, my Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you have wrought for your servant's sake, and according to your heart you have wrought all this greatness, to make it known to your servant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} that he may magnify you, O my Lord; for there is no one like you, and there is no God, but you among all of whom we have heard with our ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And what other nation in the earth [is] as your people Israel? whereas God was his guide, to redeem for himself a people to make you a name, to do mightily and nobly, so that you should cast out nations and [their] tabernacles from the presence of your people, whom you did redeem for yourself out of Egypt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you have prepared for yourself your people Israel to be a people for ever, and you, Lord, are become their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now, O my Lord, the Almighty Lord God of Israel, confirm the word for ever which you have spoken concerning your servant and his house: and now as you have said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Let your name be magnified for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Almighty Lord God of Israel, you have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, I will build you a house: therefore your servant has found [in] his heart to pray this prayer to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And now, O Lord my Lord, you are God; and your words will be true, and you have spoken these good things concerning your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And now begin and bless the house of your servant, that it may continue for ever before you; for you, O Lord, my Lord, have spoken, and the house of your servant shall be blessed with your blessing so as to continue for ever.\par

\subsection*{Kings II 8}
\markright{KINGS II 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after this, that David struck the Philistines, and put them to flight, and David took the tribute from out of the hand of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David struck Moab, and measured them out with lines, having laid them down on the ground: and there were two lines for slaying, and two lines he kept alive: and Moab became servants to David, yielding tribute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David struck Adraazar the son of Raab king of Suba, as he went to extend his power to the river Euphrates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David took a thousand of his chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all his chariot [horses], and he reserved to himself one hundred chariots. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Syria of Damascus comes to help Adraazar king of Suba, and David struck twenty-two thousand men belonging to the Syrian. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David placed a garrison in Syria near Damascus, and the Syrians became servants and tributaries to David: and the Lord preserved David wherever he went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David took the golden bracelets which were on the servants of Adraazar king of Suba, and brought them to Jerusalem. And Susakim king of Egypt took them, when he went up to Jerusalem in the days of Roboam son of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And king David took from Metebac, and from the choice cities of Adraazar, very much brass: with that Solomon made the brazen sea, and the pillars, and the lavers, and all the furniture. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And You the king of Hemath heard that David had struck all the host of Adraazar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And You sent Jedduram his son to king David, to ask him of his welfare, and to congratulate him on his fighting against Adraazar and striking him, for he was an enemy to Adraazar: and in his hands were vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And these king David consecrated to the Lord, with the silver and with the gold which he consecrated out of all the cities which he conquered, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} out of Idumea, and out of Moab, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalec, and from the spoils of Adraazar son of Raab king of Suba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David made [himself] a name: and when he returned he struck Idumea in Gebelem to [the number of] eighteen thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he set garrisons in Idumea, even in all Idumea: and all the Idumeans were servants to the king. And the Lord preserved David wherever he went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David reigned over all Israel: and David wrought judgment and justice over all his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joab the son of Saruia [was] over the host; and Josaphat the son of Achilud [was keeper] of the records. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Sadoc the son of Achitob, and Achimelech son of Abiathar, [were] priests; and Sasa [was] the scribe, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and Banaeas son of Jodae [was] councillor, and the Chelethite and the Phelethite, and the sons of David, were princes of the court.\par

The letter ζ, zayin, with a dot upon it stands for seven thousand, and the final letter ο, noon, for seven hundred. \subsection*{Kings II 9}
\markright{KINGS II 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David said, Is there yet any one left in the house of Saul, that I may deal kindly with him for Jonathan's sake? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was a servant of the house of Saul, and his name was Siba: and they call him to David; and the king said to him, Are you Siba? and he said, I [am] your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king said, Is there yet a man left of the house of Saul, that I may act towards him with the mercy of God? and Siba said to the king, There is yet a son of Jonathan, lame [of] his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king said, Where [is] he? and Siba said to the king, Behold, [he is] in the house of Machir the son of Amiel of Lodabar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And king David went, and took him out of the house of Machir the son Amiel of Lodabar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Memphibosthe the son of Jonathan the son of Saul comes to the king David, and he fell upon his face and did obeisance to him: and David said to him, Memphibosthe: and he said, Behold your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David said to him, Fear not, for I will surely deal mercifully with you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul the father of your father; and you shall eat bread at my table continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Memphibosthe did obeisance, and said, Who am I your servant, that you have looked upon a dead dog like me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king called Siba the servant of Saul, and said to him, All that belonged to Saul and to all his house have I given to the son of your lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you, and your sons, and your servants, shall till the land for him; and you shall bring in bread to the son of your lord, and he shall eat bread: and Memphibosthe the son of your lord shall eat bread continually at my table. Now Siba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Siba said to the king, According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so will your servant do. And Memphibosthe did eat at the table of David, as one of the sons of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Memphibosthe had a little son, and his name [was] Micha: and all the household of Siba [were] servants to Memphibosthe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Memphibosthe lived in Jerusalem, for he continually ate at the table of the king; and he was lame in both his feet.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the kindness of God That is, the highest degree of kindness; as the hail of God is very great hail; the mountains of God exceeding high mountains; besides which, this kindness was according to the covenant of God made between him and Jonathan.; yet a son \textsuperscript{4} Machir Lodebar This place appears to have been situated beyond Jordan; and was probably, as Reland supposes, the same as Debir or Lidbir, . \textsuperscript{6} Mephibosheth, called Meribbaal he fell \textsuperscript{7} Fear not, ; for I will; eat bread \textsuperscript{10} shall eat bread The eating at courts was of two kinds; the one public and ceremonious, the other private. Sir John Chardin understands those passages which speak of a right to eat at the royal table, as pointing out a right to a seat there, when the repast was public and solemn. So in a manuscript Note on, he tells us that it was to be understood of the majilis, (the term for an assembly of lords, or a public feast), and not of the daily and ordinary repast. Hence, though Mephibosheth was to eat at all public times at the king's table, yet he would want the produce of his lands for food at other times, which it was necessary for Ziba to understand. \textsuperscript{13} he did eat, was lame\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 10}
\markright{KINGS II 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after this that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Annon his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David said, I will show mercy to Annon the son of Naas, as his father dealt mercifully with me. And David sent to comfort him concerning his father by the hand of his servants; and the servants of David came into the land of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Annon their lord, [Is it] to honor your father before you that David has sent comforters to you? Has not David rather sent his servants to you that they should search the city, and spy it out and examine it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Annon took the servants of David, and shaved their beards, and cut off their garments in the midst as far as their haunches, and sent them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they brought David word concerning the men; and he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly dishonored: and the king said, Remain in Jericho till your beards have grown, and [then] you⌃ shall return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Ammon saw that the people of David were ashamed; and the children of Ammon sent, and hired the Syrians of Baethraam, and the Syrians of Suba, and Roob, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Amalec with a thousand men, and Istob with twelve thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David heard, and sent Joab and all his host, [even] the mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Ammon went forth, and set the battle in array by the door of the gate: [those] of Syria, Suba, and Roob, and Istob, and Amalec, being by themselves in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him from that which was opposed in front and from behind, and he chose out [some] of all the young men of Israel, and they set themselves in array against Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the rest of the people he gave into the hand of Abessa his brother, and they set the battle in array opposite to the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said, If Syria be too strong for me, then shall you⌃ help me: and if the children of Ammon be too strong for you, then will we be ready to help you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Be you courageous, and let us be strong for our people, and for the sake of the cities of our God, and the Lord shall do that which is good in his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joab and his people with him advanced to battle against Syria, and they fled from before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, and they fled from before Abessa, and entered into the city: and Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Syrians saw that they were worsted before Israel, and they gathered themselves together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Adraazar sent and gathered the Syrians from the other side of the river Chalamak, and they came to Aelam; and Sobac the captain of the host of Adraazar [was] at their head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel, and went over Jordan, and came to Aelam: and the Syrians set the battle in array against David, and fought with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Syria fled from before Israel, and David destroyed of Syria seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and he struck Sobac the captain of his host, and he died there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And all the kings the servants of Adraazar saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, and they went over to Israel, and served them: and Syria was afraid to help the children of Ammon any more.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} AM 2967, bc 1037, An, Ex, Is, 454 king \textsuperscript{2} show kindness; Nahash as his father \textsuperscript{3} Thinkest thou that David doth Heb. In thine eyes doth David not \textsuperscript{4} and shaved The beard is held in high respect and greatly valued in the East. The possessor considers it as his greatest ornament; often swears by it; and, in matters of great importance, pledges it; and nothing can be more secure than such a pledge; for its owner will redeem it at the hazard of his life. The beard was never cut off but in mourning, or as a sign of slavery. It is customary to shave the Ottoman princes, as a mark of their subjection to the reigning emperor. The beard is a mark of authority and liberty among the Mohammedans. The Persians who clip the beard, and shave above the jaw, are reputed heretics. They who serve in the seraglios have their beards shaven, as a sign of servitude; nor do they suffer them to grow till the sultan has set them at liberty. Among the Arabians, it is more infamous for anyone to appear with his beard cut off, than among us to be publicly whipped or branded; and many would prefer death to such a punishment.; cut off \textsuperscript{6} stank; Syrians of Bethrehob, Zobah; Maacah Ishtob or, the men of Tob \textsuperscript{8} at the entering This was at the city of Medeba, a city upon the borders of the Ammonites, and in their possession. Rehob \textsuperscript{12} Be of good This is a very animating address, and equal to anything of the kind in ancient or modern times. Ye fight pro aris et focis; for every good, sacred and civil; for God, for your families, and for your countries. Such harangues, especially in very trying circumstances, are very natural, and may perhaps be found in the records of every nation. Several instances might be quoted from Roman and Grecian history; but few are more remarkable than that of Tyrtaeus, the lame Athenian poet, to whom the command of the army was given in one of the Messenian wars. The Spartans had at that time suffered great losses, and all their stratagems proved ineffectual, so that they began to despair of success; when the poet, by his lectures on honour and courage, delivered in moving verse to the army, ravished them to such a degree with the thoughts of dying for their country, that, rushing on with a furious transport to meet their enemies, they gave them an entire overthrow, and by one decisive battle brought the war to a happy conclusion.; play; the Lord \textsuperscript{15} am 2968, bc 1036, An, Ex, Is, 455 gathered \textsuperscript{16} Hadarezer; the river i.e. Euphrates Shobach or, Shophach\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 11}
\markright{KINGS II 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when the time o the year for kings going out [to battle] had come round, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbath: but David remained at Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass toward evening, that David arose off his couch, and walked on the roof of the king's house, and saw from the roof a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David sent and enquired about the woman: and [one] said, [Is] not this Bersabee the daughter of Eliab, the wife of Urias the Chettite? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David sent messengers, and took her, and went in to her, and he lay with her: and she was purified from her uncleanness, and returned to her house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, I am with child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Urias the Chettite; and Joab sent Urias to David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Urias arrived and went in to him, and David asked him how Joab was, and how the people were, and how the war went on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David said to Urias, Go to your house, and wash your feet: and Urias departed from the house of the king, and a portion [of meat] from the king followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Urias slept at the door of the king with the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they brought David word, saying, Urias has not gone down to his house. And David said to Urias, Are you not come from a journey? why have you not gone down to your house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Urias said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Juda dwell in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; and shall I go into my house to eat and drink, and lie with my wife? how [should I do this? as] your soul lives, I will not do this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And David said to Urias, Remain here today also, and to-morrow I will let you go. So Urias remained in Jerusalem that day and the day following. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David called him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk: and he went out in the evening to lie upon his bed with the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the morning came, and David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Urias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he wrote in the letter, saying, Station Urias in front of the severe [part] of the fight, and retreat from behind him, so shall he be wounded and die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass while Joab was watching against the city, that he set Urias in a place where he knew that valiant men were. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and some of the people of the servants of David fell, and Urias the Chettite died also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joab sent, and reported to David all the events of the war, so as to tell them to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he charged the messenger, saying, When you have finished reporting all the events of the war to the king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} then it shall come to pass if the anger of the king shall arise, and he shall say to you, Why did you⌃ draw near to the city to fight? knew you⌃ not that they would shoot from off the wall? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerobaal son of Ner? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from above the wall, and he died in Thamasi? why did you⌃ draw near to the wall? then you shall say, Your servant Urias the Chettite is also dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the messenger of Joab went to the king to Jerusalem, and he came and reported to David all that Joab told him, all the affairs of the war. And David was very angry with Joab, and said to the messenger, Why did you⌃ draw near to the wall to fight? knew you⌃ not that you⌃ would be wounded from off the wall? Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerobaal? did not a woman cast upon him a piece of millstone from the wall, and he died in Thamasi? why did you⌃ draw near to the wall? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the messenger said to David, The men prevailed against us, and they came out against us into the field, and we came upon them even to the door of the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the archers shot at your servants from off the wall, and some of the king's servants died, and your servant Urias the Chettite is dead also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And David said to the messenger, Thus shall you say to Joab, Let not the matter be grievous in your eyes, for the sword devours one way at one time and another way at another: strengthen your array against the city, and destroy it, and strengthen him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the wife of Urias heard that Urias her husband was dead, and she mourned for her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the time of mourning expired, and David sent and took her into his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son: but the thing which David did was evil in the eyes of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2969, bc 1035, An, Ex, Is, 456 after the year etc. Heb. at the return of the year.; at the time The sacred historian seems to intimate that there was one particular time of the year to which military operations were limited; and Josephus informs us that this took place in the beginning of spring. In another part of his works he says, that as soon as spring was begun, Adad levied and led forth his army against the Hebrews. Antiochus also prepared to invade Judea at the first appearance of spring; and Vespasian marched to Antipatris at the commencement of the same season. The kings and armies of the East, says Chardin, do not march but when there is grass, and when they can encamp, which is in April. This rule, however, seems to be disregarded in modern times. \subsection*{Kings II 12}
\markright{KINGS II 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David; and he went in to him, and said to him, There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the rich [man] had very many flocks and herds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But the poor [man had] only one little ewe lamb, which he had purchased, and preserved, and reared; and it grew up with himself and his children in common; it ate of his bread and drank of his cup, and slept in his bosom, and was to him as a daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And a traveller came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his flocks and of his herds, to dress for the traveller that came to him; and he took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man that came to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David was greatly moved with anger against the man; and David said to Nathan, [As] the Lord lives, the man that did this thing shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he shall restore the lamb sevenfold, because he has not spared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Nathan said to David, You are the man that has done this. Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I anointed you to be king over Israel, and I rescued you out the hand of Saul; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and I gave you the house of your lord, and the wives of your lord into your bosom, and I gave to you the house of Israel and Juda; and if that had been little, I would have given you yet more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Why have you set at nothing the word of the Lord, to do that which is evil in his eyes? you have slain Urias the Chettite with the sword, and you have taken his wife to be your wife, and you have slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now therefore the sword shall not depart from your house for ever, because you have set me at nothing, and you have taken the wife of Urias the Chettite, to be your wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus says the Lord, Behold, I will raise up against you evil out of your house, and I will take your wives before your eyes, and will give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing in the sight of all Israel, and before the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said to David, And the Lord has put away your sin; you shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Only because you have given great occasion of provocation to the enemies of the Lord by this thing, your son also that is born to you shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Nathan departed to his house. And the Lord struck the child, which the wife of Urias the Chettite bore to David, and it was ill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And David enquired of God concerning the child, and David fasted, and went in and lay all night upon the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the elders of his house arose [and went] to him to raise him up from the ground, but he would not [rise], nor did he eat bread with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass on the seventh day that the child died: and the servants of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive we spoke to him, and he listened not to our voice; and you should we tell him that the child is dead?—so would he do [himself] harm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And David understood that his servants were whispering, and David perceived that the child was dead: and David said to his servants, Is the child dead? and they said, He is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Then David rose up from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his raiment, and went into the house of God, and worshipped him; and went into his own house, and called for bread to eat, and they set bread before him and he ate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And his servants said to him, What [is] this thing that you have done concerning the child? while it was yet living you did fast, and weep, and watch: and when the child was dead you did rise up, and did eat bread, and drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And David said, While the child yet lived, I fasted and wept; for I said, Who knows if the Lord will pity me, and the child live? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But now it is dead, why should I fast thus? shall I be able to bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And David comforted Bersabee his wife, and he went in to her, and lay with her; and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his named Solomon, and the Lord loved him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and called his name Jeddedi, for the Lord's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Joab fought against Rabbath of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbath, and taken the city of waters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And now gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and take it beforehand; lest I take the city first, and my name be called upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And David gathered all the people, and went to Rabbath, and fought against it, and took it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he took the crown of Molchom their king from off his head, and the weight of it was a talent of gold, with precious stones, and it was upon the head of David; and he carried forth very much spoil of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he brought forth the people that were in it, and put them under the saw, and under iron harrows, and axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick-kiln: and thus he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2970, bc 1034, An, Ex, Is, 457 the Lord; unto David, ; he came *title There were There is nothing in this parable which requires illustration. Its bent is evident; and it was wisely constructed, by not having too near a resemblance, to make David unwittingly pass sentence on himself. The parable was in David's hand what his own letter was in the hands of the brave Uriah. Nathan at length closed in with him in the application of it. In beginning with a parable he shewed his prudence, and great need there is of prudence in giving reproof; but now he speaks as an ambassador from God. He reminds David of the great things God had designed and done for him, and then charges him with a high contempt of the Divine authority, and threatens an entail of judgments upon his family for this sin. Those who despise the word and law of God, despise God himself, and will assuredly suffer for such contempt. \textsuperscript{3} one little; meat Heb. morsel lay in his \textsuperscript{5} David's; As the Lord shall surely die or, is worthy to die, Heb. is a son of death, *marg. \textsuperscript{7} Thou art; I anointed; I delivered;, ; *title \textsuperscript{8} thy master's wives; gave thee; I would \textsuperscript{9} despised, ; to do evil; thou hast \textsuperscript{10} the sword, ; because; hast taken \textsuperscript{11} I will raise, I will take That is, in the course of my providence I will permit this to be done. Such phrases in Scripture do not mean that God either does or can do evil himself; but only that he permits such evil to be done as he foresaw would be done, and which, had he pleased, he might have prevented. \textsuperscript{13} David; I have sinned; The Lord;, ; thou \textsuperscript{14} by this deed; the child \textsuperscript{16} besought; fasted Heb. fasted a fast; lay all night \textsuperscript{18} seventh day vex, Heb. do hurt to \textsuperscript{23} I shall go; he shall not \textsuperscript{24} am 2971, bc 1033, An, Ex, Is, 458 she bare \textsuperscript{25} Nathan; Jedidiah that is, Beloved of the Lord \textsuperscript{26} Joab; Rabbah, or Rabbath-Ammon, also called Philadelphia, from Ptolemy Philadelphus, king of Egypt, was situated east of Jordan, and, according to Eusebius, ten miles east from Jazer. It is sometimes mentioned as belonging to Arabia, sometimes to Coelo-Syria; and was one of the cities of the Decapolis east of Jordan. Josephus extends the region of Perea as far as Philadelphia. It is now, says Burckhardt, called Amman, distant about 19 miles to the se by e of Szalt, and lies along the banks of a river called Moiet Amman, which has its source in a pond, at a few hundred paces from the south-western end of the town, and empties itself in the Zerka, or Jabbok, about four hours to the northward. This river runs in a valley bordered on both sides by barren hills of flint, which advance on the south side close to the edge of the stream. The edifices which still remain, though in a decaying state, from being built of a calcareous stone of moderate hardness, sufficiently attest the former greatness and splendour of this metropolis of the children of Ammon. \textsuperscript{27} Rabbah; the city of waters Probably that part of the city situated near the pond, from which the rest received their water. \textsuperscript{28} it be called after my name Heb. my name be called upon it \textsuperscript{30} took the weight If this talent was only seven pounds, as Whiston says, David might have carried it on his head with little difficulty; but this weight, according to common computation, would amount to nearly 114 pounds! Some, therefore, think, that mishkelah should be taken for its value, not weight; which renders it perfectly plain, as the worth of the crown will be about 5, 074£, 15s, 7d sterling. The ancients mention several such large crowns, made more for sight than use. Atheneus describes a crown of gold that was 24 feet in circumference; and mentions others that were two, some four, and others five feet deep. Pliny takes notice of some that were no less than eight pounds weight. Besides the crown usually worn, it was customary for kings, in some nations, to have such large ones as described, either hung or supported over the throne, where they sat at their coronation or other solemn occasions. in great abundance Heb. very great \textsuperscript{31} and put them Rather, as the particle α frequently signifies, "And he put them to saws, and to harrows, and to axes, " etc., as we say, to put a person to the plough, to the anvil, to the last, etc., Also\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 13}
\markright{KINGS II 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it happened after this that Abessalom the son of David had a very beautiful sister, and her name [was] Themar; and Amnon the son of David loved her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Amnon was distressed even to sickness, because of Themar his sister; for she was a virgin, and it seemed very difficult for Amnon to do anything to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Amnon had a friend, and his name [was] Jonadab, the son of Samaa the brother of David: and Jonadab [was] a very cunning man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he said to him, What ails you that you are thus weak? O son of the king, morning by morning? will you not tell me? and Ammon said, I love Themar the sister of my brother Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jonadab said to him, Lie upon your bed, and make yourself sick, and your father shall come in to see you; and you shall say to him, Let, I pray you, Themar my sister come, and feed me with morsels, and let her prepare food before my eyes, that I may see and eat at her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Ammon lay down, and made himself sick; and the king came in to see him: and Amnon said to the king, Let, I pray you, my sister Themar come to me, and make a couple of cakes in my sight, and I will eat them at her hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David sent to Themar to the house, saying, Go now to your brother's house, and dress him food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Themar went to the house of her brother Amnon, and he [was] lying down: and she took the dough and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And she took the frying pan and poured them out before him, but he would not eat. And Amnon said, Send out every man from about me. And they removed every man from about him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Amnon said to Themar, Bring in the food into the closet, and I will eat of your hand. And Themar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them to her brother Amnon into the chamber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And she brought [them] to him to eat, and he caught hold of her, and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And she said to him, Nay, my brother, do not humble me, for it ought not to be so done in Israel; do not this folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I, whither shall I remove my reproach? and you shall be as one of the fools in Israel. And now, speak, I pray you, to the king, for surely he will not keep me from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But Amnon would not listen to her voice; and he prevailed against her, and humbled her, and lay with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then Amnon hated her with very great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her, for the last wickedness was greater than the first: and Amnon said to her, Rise, and be gone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Themar spoke to him concerning this great mischief, greater, [said she], than the other that you did me, to send me away: but Amnon would not listen to her voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he called his servant who had charge of the house, and said to him, Put now this [woman] out from me, and shut the door after her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she had on her a variegated robe, for so were the king's daughters that were virgins attired in their apparel: and his servant led her forth, and shut the door after her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Themar took ashes, and put them on her head; and she tore the variegated garment that was upon her: and she laid her hands on her head, and went crying continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Abessalom her brother said to her, Has your brother Amnon been with you? now then, my sister, be silent, for he is your brother: be not careful to mention this matter. So Themar lived as a widow in the house of her brother Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And king David heard of all these things, and was very angry; but he did not grieve the spirit of his son Amnon, because be loved him, for he was his firstborn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Abessalom spoke not to Amnon, good or bad, because Abessalom hated Amnon, on account of his humbling his sister Themar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass at the end of two whole years, that they were shearing [sheep] for Abessalom in Belasor near Ephraim: and Abessalom invited all the king's sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Abessalom came to the king, and said, Behold, your servant has a sheep-shearing; let now the king and his servants go with your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the king said to Abessalom, Nay, my son, let us not all go, and let us not be burdensome to you. And he pressed him; but he would not go, but blessed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Abessalom said to him, And if not, let I pray you, my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Abessalom pressed him, and he sent with him Amnon and all the king's sons; and Abessalom made a banquet like the banquet of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Abessalom charged his servants, saying, Mark when the heart of Amnon shall be merry with wine, and I shall say to you, Strike Amnon, and kill him: fear not; for is it not I that command you? Be courageous, and be valiant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the servants of Abessalom did to Amnon as Abessalom commanded them: and all the sons of the king rose up, and they mounted every man his mule, and fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it came to pass, when they were in the way, that a report came to David, saying, Abessalom has slain all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay upon the ground: and all his servants that were standing round him tore their garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jonadab the son of Samaa brother of David, answered and said, Let not my Lord the king say that he has slain all the young men the sons of the king, for Amnon only of them all is dead; for he was appointed [to death] by the mouth of Abessalom from the day that he humbled his sister Themar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And now let not my lord the king take the matter to heart, saying, All the king's sons are dead: for Amnon only of them is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Abessalom escaped: and the young man the watchman, lifted up his eyes, and looked; and, behold, much people went in the way behind him from the side of the mountain in the descent: and the watchman came and told the king, and said, I have seen men by the way of Oronen, by the side of the mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the king's sons are present: according to the word of your servant, so has it happened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And it came to pass when he had finished speaking, that, behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voices and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept with a very great weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} But Abessalom fled, and went to Tholmi son of Emiud the king of Gedsur to the land of Chamaachad: and king David mourned for his son continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} So Abessalom fled, and departed to Gedsur, and was there three years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And king David ceased to go out after Abessalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, touching his death.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2972, bc 1032, A.Ex, Is, 459 Absalom; a fair sister; Tamar; loved her \textsuperscript{2} vexed; Amnon etc. Heb. it was marvellous, or hidden, in the eyes of Amnon \textsuperscript{3} a friend; Shimeah; Shimeah subtil man \textsuperscript{4} Why art; lean Heb. thin from day to day Heb. morning by morning, I love.; my brother \textsuperscript{8} she took Dr. Russell says, "The Eastern ladies often wash their own hands, prepare cakes, pastry, etc. in their apartments; and some few particular dishes are cooked by themselves, but not in their apartments. On such occasions, they go to some room near the kitchen." flour or, paste and made cakes Rather, as Mr. Parkhurst renders, "and tossed it ( wattelabbaiv ) in his sight, and dressed the tossed cakes ( halleveevoth )." This will receive illustration from the account which Mr. Jackson gives of the Arabian manner of kneading and baking. "They have a small place built with clay, between two and three feet high, having a hole at the bottom for the convenience of drawing out the ashes, something similar to that of a brick-kiln. The oven is usually about fifteen inches wide at top, and gradually grows wider to the bottom. It is heated with wood; and when sufficiently hot, and perfectly clear from smoke, having nothing but clear embers at bottom, which continue to reflect great heat, they prepare the dough in a large bowl, and mould the cakes to the desired size on a board or stone placed near the oven. After they have kneaded the cake to a proper consistency, they pat it a little, then toss it about with great dexterity in one hand till it is as thin as they choose to make it. They then wet one side of it with water, at the same time wetting the hand and arm with which they put it into the oven." \textsuperscript{12} force me Heb. humble me; no such thing ought Heb. it ought not so, folly \textsuperscript{15} hated her exceedingly Heb. with great hatred greatly \textsuperscript{20} Amnon Heb. Aminon but hold; regard not Heb. set not thine heart on desolate Heb. and desolate. \textsuperscript{21} he was very wroth The Septuagint and Vulgate add, και ουκ ελυπησε το πνευμα Αμνων του υιου αυτου, οτι ηγαπα αυτον, οτι πρωτοτοκος αυτου ην . et noluit contristare spiritum Amnon filii sui, quoniam diligebat eum, quia primogenituj erat ei . "But he would not grieve the soul of Amnon his son, for he loved him because he was his first-born." The same addition is found in Josephus; and it is probable that it once formed a part of the Hebrew Text. \textsuperscript{23} am 2974, bc 1030, An, Ex, Is 461 sheepshearers; invited \textsuperscript{26} let my brother He urged this with the more plausibility because Amnon was the first-born, and presumptive heir to the crown; and he had dissembled his resentment so long and so well that he was not suspected. \textsuperscript{28} commanded; heart is merry; fear not; have not I or, Will you not, since I have, etc. valiant Heb. sons of valour \textsuperscript{29} servants; gat him up Heb. rode mule \textsuperscript{32} Jonadab Shimeah, Shammah David's brother This was a very bad man. He had given his cousin Amnon the most detestable advice; and here speaks coolly of a most bloody tragedy of which he had been the cause. appointment Heb. mouth determined or, settled \textsuperscript{35} as they servant said, Heb. according to the word of thy servant \textsuperscript{36} very sore Heb. with a great weeping greatly, *marg. \textsuperscript{37} Absalom fled As Absalom had committed wilful murder, he could not avail himself of a city of refuge; but went to Talmai, king of Geshur, his maternal grandfather. \subsection*{Kings II 14}
\markright{KINGS II 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joab the son of Saruia knew that the heart of the king was toward Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joab sent to Thecoe, and took thence a cunning woman, and said to her, Mourn, I pray you, and put on mourning apparel, and anoint you not with oil, and you shall be as a woman mourning for one that is dead thus for many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall go to the king, and speak to him according to this word. And Joab put the words in her mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So the woman of Thecoe went in to the king and fell upon her face to the earth, and did him obeisance, and said, Help, O king, help. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king said to her, What is the matter with you? And she said, I am indeed a widow woman, and my husband is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And moreover your handmaid had two sons, and they fought together in the field, and there was no one to part them; and the one struck the other his brother, and killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And behold the whole family rose up against your handmaid, and they said, Give up the one that struck his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother, whom he killed, and we will take away even your heir: so they will quench my coal that is left, so as not to leave my husband remnant or name on the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king said to the woman, Go in peace to your house, and I will give commandment concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the woman of Thecoe said to the king, On me, my lord, O king, and on my father's house [be] the iniquity, and the king and his throne [be] guiltless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king said, Who was it that spoke to you? you shall even bring him to me, and [one] shall not touch him any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And she said, Let now the king remember concerning his Lord God in that the avenger of blood is multiplied to destroy, and let them not take away my son. And he said, [As] the lord lives, not a hair of your son shall fall to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the woman said, Let now your servant speak a word to my lord the king. And he said, Say on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the woman said, Why have you devised this thing against the people of God? or [is] this word out of the king's mouth as a transgression, so that the king should not bring back his banished? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For we shall surely die, and be as water poured upon the earth, which shall not be gathered up, and God shall take the life, even as he devises to thrust forth from him his outcast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now whereas I came to speak this word to my lord the king, [the reason is] that the people will see me, and your handmaid will say, Let one now speak to my lord the king, if perhaps the king will perform the request of his handmaid; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} for the king will hear. Let him rescue his handmaid out of the hand of the man that seeks to cast out me and my son from the inheritance of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the woman said, If now the word of my lord the king be gracious, —[well]: for as an angel of God, so [is] my lord the king, to hear good and evil: and the Lord your God shall be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king answered, and said to the woman, Hide not from me, I pray you, the matter which I ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king by all means speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the king said, [Is] not the hand of Joab in all this matter with you? and the woman said to the king, [As] your soul lives, my lord, O king, there is no turning to the right hand or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab himself charged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your handmaid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In order that this form of speech might come about [it was] that your servant Joab has framed this matter: and my lord is wise as [is] the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king said to Joab, Behold now, I have done to you according to this your word: go, bring back the young man Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joab fell on his face to the ground, and did obeisance, and blessed the king: and Joab said, To-day your servant knows that I have found grace in your sight, my lord, O king, for my lord the king has performed the request of his servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joab arose, and went to Gedsur, and brought Abessalom to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king said, Let him return to his house, and not see my face. And Abessalom returned to his house, and saw not the king's face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there was not a man in Israel so very comely as Abessalom: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And when he polled his head, (and it was at the beginning of every year that he polled it, because it grew, heavy upon him,) even when he polled it, he weighed the hair of his head, two hundred shekels according to the royal shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And there were born to Abessalom three sons and one daughter, and her name was Themar: she was a very beautiful woman, and she becomes the wife of Roboam son of Solomon, and she bears to him Abia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Abessalom remained in Jerusalem two full years, and he saw not the king's face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Abessalom sent to Joab to bring him in to the king, and he would not come to him: and he sent to him the second time, and he would not come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Abessalom said to his servants, Behold, Joab's portion in the field [is] next to mine, and he has in it barley; go and set it on fire. And the servants of Abessalom set the field on fire: and the servants of Joab come to him with their clothes torn, and they said to him, The servants of Abessalom have set the field on fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Joab arose, and came to Abessalom into the house, and said to him, Why have your servants set my field on fire? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Abessalom said to Joab, Behold, I sent to you, saying, Come hither, and I will send you to the king, saying, Why did I come out of Gedsur? it would have been better for me to have remained there: and now, behold, I have not seen the face of the king; but if there is iniquity in me, then put me to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Joab went in to the king, and brought him word: and he called Abessalom, and he went in to the king, and did him obeisance, and fell upon his face to the ground, even in the presence of the king; and the king kissed Abessalom.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2977, bc 1027, An, Ex, Is, 464 Joab; toward Absalom \textsuperscript{2} to Tekoah was a city of Judah, situated, according to Eusebius and Jerome, twelve miles south of Jerusalem. Josephus says it was not far from the castle of Herodium; and Jerome (Prologue to Amos) says it stood on a hill six miles south from Bethlehem. Dr. Poccocke places it at the same distance; and says there are still considerable ruins on the top of a hill, which is about half a mile long and a furlong broad.; Tekoa mourning \textsuperscript{4} fell on her; Help Heb. Save \textsuperscript{5} I am indeed It is very possible that the principal incidents mentioned here were real; and that Joab found out a person whose circumstances bore a near resemblance to that which he wished to represent. She did not make the similitude too plain and visible, lest the king should see her intention before she had obtained a grant of pardon; and thus her circumstances, her mournful tale, her widow's dress, her aged person (for Josephus says she was advanced in years), and her impressive manner, all combined to make one united irresistible impression on the heart of the aged monarch \textsuperscript{6} and they two; none to part Heb. no deliverer between \textsuperscript{7} the whole; so they; quench upon the earth Heb. upon the face of the earth \textsuperscript{9} the iniquity; and the king \textsuperscript{11} let the king, ; thou etc. Heb. the revenger of blood do not multiply to destroy the revengers; As the Lord; not one hair \textsuperscript{12} Let thine speak one word, ; Say on \textsuperscript{13} Wherefore; people; in that the king \textsuperscript{14} we must; as water; neither etc. or, because God hath not taken away his life, he hath also devised means, etc. God.; he devise \textsuperscript{17} comfortable Heb. for rest as an angel This is very much like the hyperbolical language which is addressed by the Hindoos to an European when they desire to obtain something from him: "Saheb, " say they, "can do every thing. No one can prevent the execution of Saheb's commands. Saheb is God." Though the expression may be imputed to the hyperbolical genius of these countries, yet there was, perhaps, more of real persuasion than we are apt to suppose. Sir John Chardin states, that having found fault with the king of Persia's valuation of a rich trinket, the grand master told him that if a Persian had dared to have done such a thing, it would have been as much as his life was worth. "Know, " said he, "that the kings of Persia have a general and full knowledge of matters, as sure as it is extensive; and that, equally in the greatest and smallest things, there is nothing more just and sure than what they pronounce."; to discern Heb. to hear, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{19} of Joab, ; As thy soul;, ; turn; he put \textsuperscript{22} thanked Heb. blessed; I have found; his or, thy \textsuperscript{25} But in all Israel etc. Heb. And as Absalom there was not a beautiful man in all Israel to praise greatly, ; from the sole \textsuperscript{26} when he polled; two hundred shekels If the shekel be allowed to mean the common shekel, the amount will be utterly incredible; for Josephus says that "two hundred shekels make five mine" and the mina, he says, "weighs two pounds and a half; " which calculation makes Absalom's hair weigh twelve pounds and a half! But it is probable that the king's shekel was that which Epiphanius and Hesychius say was the fourth part of an ounce, half a stater, or two drachmas. The whole amount, therefore, of the 200 shekels is about 50 ounces, which make 4 lb. 2 oz. troy weight, or 3 lb. 2 oz. avoirdupois. This need not be accounted incredible, especially as abundance of oil and ointment was used by the ancients in dressing their heads. Josephus informs us, that the Jews also put gold dust in their hair. \textsuperscript{28} am 2977-2979, bc 1027-1025, An, Ex, Is, 464-466 and saw not \textsuperscript{30} near mine Heb. near my place go and set; And Absalom's \textsuperscript{32} it had been, if there \textsuperscript{33} am 2979, bc 1025, An, Ex, Is, 466 kissed Absalom\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 15}
\markright{KINGS II 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after this that Abessalom prepared for himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Abessalom rose early, and stood by the side of the way of the gate: and it came to pass that every man who had a cause, came to the king for judgment, and Abessalom cried to him, and said to him, Of what city are you? And he said, Your servant [is] of one of the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abessalom said to him, See, your affairs [are] right and clear, yet you have no one [appointed] of the king to hear you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Abessalom said, O that one would make me a judge in the land; then every man who had a dispute or a cause would come to me, and I would judge him! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass when a man came near to do him obeisance, that he stretched out his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Abessalom did after this manner to all Israel that came to the king for judgment; and Abessalom gained the hearts of the men of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass after forty years, that Abessalom said to his father, I will go now, and pay my vows, which I vowed to the Lord in Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For your servant vowed a vow when I lived at Gedsur in Syria, saying, If the Lord should indeed restore me to Jerusalem, then will I serve the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king said to him, Go in peace. And he arose and went to Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abessalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, When you⌃ hear the sound of the trumpet, then shall you⌃ say, Abessalom is become king in Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And there went with Abessalom two hundred chosen men from Jerusalem; and they went in their simplicity, and knew not anything. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Abessalom sent to Achitophel the Theconite, the counsellor of David, from his city, from Gola, where he was sacrificing: and there was a strong conspiracy; and the people with Abessalom were increasingly numerous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there came a messenger to David, saying, the heart of the men of Israel is gone after Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, Rise, and let us flee, for we have no refuge from Abessalom: make haste and go, lest he overtake us speedily, and bring evil upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king's servants said to the king, In all things which our lord the king chooses, behold [we are] your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the king and all his house went out on foot: and the king left ten women of his concubines to keep the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king and all his servants went out on foot; and abode in a distant house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all his servants passed on by his side, and every Chelethite, and every Phelethite, and they stood by the olive tree in the wilderness: and all the people marched near him, and all his court, and all the men of might, and all the men of war, six hundred: and they were present at his side: and every Chelethite, and every Phelethite, and all the six hundred Gittites that came on foot out of Geth, and they went on before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the king said to Ethi, the Gittite, Why do you also go with us? return, and dwell with the king, for you are a stranger, and you have come forth as a sojourner out of your place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whereas you came yesterday, shall I today cause you to travel with us, and shall you [thus] change your place? you did come forth yesterday, and today shall I set you in motion to go along with us? I indeed will go wherever I may go: return then, and cause your brethren to return with you, and may the Lord deal mercifully and truly with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ethi answered the king and said, [As] the Lord lives and as my lord the king lives, in the place wherever my lord shall be, whether it be for death or life, there shall your servant be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the king said to Ethi, Come and pass over with me. So Ethi the Gittite and the king passed over, and all his servants, and all the multitude with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And all the country wept with a loud voice. And all the people passed by over the brook of Kedron; and the king crossed the brook Kedron: and all the people and the king passed on toward the way of the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And behold also Sadoc, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Baethar: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had passed out of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the king said to Sadoc, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I should find favor in the eyes of the Lord, then will he bring me back, and he will show me it and its beauty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But if he should say thus, I have no pleasure in you; behold, [here] I am, let him do to me according to that which is good in his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the king said to Sadoc the priest, Behold, you shall return to the city in peace, and Achimaas your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, your two sons with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Behold, I continue in arms in Araboth of the desert, until there come tidings from you to report to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So Sadoc and Abiathar brought back the ark of the Lord to Jerusalem, and it continued there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And David went up by the ascent of [the mount of] Olives, ascending and weeping, and had his head covered, and went barefooted: and all the people that were with him covered [every] man his head; and they went up, ascending and weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it was reported to David, saying, Achitophel also [is] among the conspirators with Abessalom. And David said, O Lord my God, disconcert, I pray you, the counsel of Achitophel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And David came as far as Ros, where he worshipped God: and behold, Chusi the chief friend of David came out to meet him, having torn his garment, and earth [was] upon his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And David said to him, If you should go over with me, then will you be a burden to me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} but if you shall return to the city, and shall say to Abessalom, Your brethren are passed over, and the king your father is passed over after me: and now I am your servant, O king, suffer me to live: at one time even of late I was the servant of your father, and now I [am] your humble servant—so shall you disconcert for me, the counsel of Achitophel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And, behold, [there are] there with you Sadoc and Abiathar the priests; and it shall be that every word that you shall hear of the house of the king, you shall report it to Sadoc and Abiathar the priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Behold, [there are] there with them their two sons, Achimaas the son of Sadoc, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar; and by them you⌃ shall report to me every word which you⌃ shall hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} So Chusi the friend of David went into the city, and Abessalom was lately gone into Jerusalem.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} rose up; came Heb. to come \textsuperscript{3} thy matters; there is etc. or, none will hear thee from the king downward \textsuperscript{4} Oh that I; I would do \textsuperscript{7} am 2983, bc 1021, An, Ex, Is, 470 forty years As David reigned in the whole only forty years, this reading is evidently corrupt, though supported by the commonly printed Vulgate, LXX, and Chaldee. But the Syriac, Arabic, Josephus, Theodoret, the Sixtine edition of the Vulgate, and several manuscripts of the same version, read four years; and it is highly probable that arbaim, forty, is an error for arba, four, though not supported by any Hebrew manuscript yet discovered. Two of those collated by Dr. Kennicott, however, have yom, "day, " instead of shanah, "year, " i.e., forty days instead of forty years; but this is not sufficient to outweigh the other authorities.; let me go pay \textsuperscript{8} thy servant; Geshur, I will serve \textsuperscript{12} Ahithophel, David's; Giloh while he offered, ; the people \textsuperscript{14} Arise; *title bring Heb. thrust; *marg. and smite \textsuperscript{16} the king *title after him Heb. at his feet; *marg. ten women \textsuperscript{20} go up and down Heb. wander in going, ; seeing mercy \textsuperscript{22} and all the little Sir John Chardin informs us, in a manuscript note on this place, that it is usual with the greatest part of the eastern people, especially the Arabs, to carry their whole family with them when they go to war. \textsuperscript{23} all the country the brook The brook Kidron, which is but a few paces broad, runs along the valley of Jehoshaphat, east of Jerusalem, to the south-west corner of the city, and then, turning to the south-east, empties itself into the Dead Sea. Like the Ilissus, it is dry at least nine months in the year, being only furnished with water in the winter, and after heavy rains. Its bed is narrow and deep, which indicates that it must formerly have been the channel for waters which have found some other, and probably subterraneous course. Kidron; Cedron the wilderness \textsuperscript{25} Carry back; he will bring, ; habitation \textsuperscript{30} the ascent;, ; mount Olivet Mount Olivet, so called from its abounding with olive trees, is situated east of Jerusalem, being separated from it only by the valley of Jehoshaphat and the brook Kidron. Josephus says it is five stadia, i.e., 625 geometrical paces from Jerusalem; and St. Luke ( ) says it is a Sabbath day's journey, or about eight stadia distant, i.e., to the summit. It forms part of a ridge of limestone hills, extending from north to south for about a mile; and it is described as having three, or, according to others, four summits; the central and highest of which overlooks the whole of the city, over whose streets and walls the eye roves as if in the survey of a model. and wept as he went up Heb. going up and weeping, ; his head covered This custom was only practised by persons in great distress, or when convicted of great crimes. Thus Darius, when informed by Tyriotes, the eunuch, that his queen was dead, and that she had suffered no violence from Alexander, covered his head, and wept a long time; then throwing off the garment that covered him, he thanked the gods for Alexander's moderation and justice.; barefoot; weeping \textsuperscript{31} Ahithophel;, ; O Lord, turn the counsel \textsuperscript{32} the top; he worshipped;, Hushai Archite coat rent \textsuperscript{34} return; as I have been then mayest\par}
