\subsection*{Kings II 16}
\markright{KINGS II 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David passed on a little way from Ros; and, behold, Siba the servant of Memphibosthe [came] to meet him; and he had a couple of asses laden, and upon them two hundred loaves, and one hundred [bunches of] raisins, and one hundred [cakes of] dates, and bottle of wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king said to Siba, What meanest you by these? and Siba, said, The asses [are] for the household of the king to sit upon, and the loaves and the dates [are] for the young men to eat, and the wine [is] for them that are faint in the wilderness to drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king said, And where [is] the son of your master? and Siba said to the king, Behold, he remains in Jerusalem; for he said, To-day shall the house of Israel restore to me the kingdom of my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king said to Siba, Behold, all Memphibosthe's property [is] your. And Siba did obeisance and said, My lord, O king, let me find grace in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And king David came to Baurim; and, behold, there came out from thence a man of the family of the house of Saul, and his name [was] Semei the son of Gera. He came forth and cursed as he went, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on the right and left hand of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And thus Semei said when he cursed him, Go out, go out, you bloody man, and man of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Lord has returned upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, because you have reigned in his stead; and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Abessalom your son: and, behold, you [are taken] in your mischief, because you [are] a bloody man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abessa the son of Saruia said to the king, Why does this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over now and take off his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king said, What have I to do with you, you⌃ sons of Saruia? even let him alone, and so let him curse, for the Lord has told him to curse David: and who shall say, Why have you done thus? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And David said to Abessa and to all his servants, Behold, my son who came forth out of my bowels seeks my life; still more now may the son of Benjamin: let him curse, because the Lord has told him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If by any means the Lord may look on my affliction, thus shall he return me good for his cursing this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David and all the men with him went on the way: and Semei went by the side of the hill next to him, cursing as he went, and casting stones at him, and sprinkling him with dirt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the king, and all the people with him, came away and refreshed themselves there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Abessalom and all the men of Israel went into Jerusalem, and Achitophel with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass when Chusi the chief friend of David came to Abessalom, that Chusi said to Abessalom, Let the king live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abessalom said to Chusi, [Is] this your kindness to your friend? why went you not forth with your friend? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Chusi said to Abessalom, Nay, but following whom the Lord, and this people, and all Israel have chosen, —his will I be, and with him I will dwell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And again, whom shall I serve? should I not in the presence of his son? As I served in the sight of your father, so will I be in your presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Abessalom said to Achitophel, Deliberate among yourselves concerning what we should do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Achitophel said to Abessalom, Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep his house; and all Israel shall hear that you have dishonored your father; and the hands of all that are with you shall be strengthened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they pitched a tent for Abessalom on the roof, and Abessalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the counsel of Achitophel, which he counselled in former days, [was] as if one should enquire of the word of God: so [was] all the counsel of Achitophel both to David and also to Abessalom.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} little past, Ziba, with a couple; summer These were probably pumpkins, cucumbers, or water-melons; the two latter being extensively used in the East to refresh travellers in the burning heat of the summer; and probably, as Mr. Harmer supposes, called summer fruits on this very account.; a bottle \textsuperscript{2} What meanest; The asses. This is the eastern mode of speaking when presenting anything to a great man: "This is for the slaves of the servants of your majesty; " when at the same time the presents are intended for the sovereign himself, and it is so understood.; for the young that such \textsuperscript{4} Behold; , I humbly beseech thee Heb. I do obeisance \textsuperscript{5} Bahurim This place is supposed to be the same as Almon ( ), and Almeth ( ), a city of Benjamin, north of Jerusalem, and apparently not far from Olivet., whose name;, he came etc. or, he still came forth and cursed \textsuperscript{7} bloody man Heb. man of blood, ; man of Belial \textsuperscript{8} returned; the blood, ; thou etc. or, thee in thy evil \textsuperscript{9} Abishai; dead dog; curse; let me go \textsuperscript{10} What have; so let him; Who shall \textsuperscript{11} Behold came forth; seeketh; the Lord \textsuperscript{12} the Lord; affliction or, tears, Heb. eye requite \textsuperscript{13} cursed cast dust Heb. dusted him with dust; It was an ancient custom, in those warm and arid countries, to lay the dust before a person of distinction, by sprinkling the ground with water. Dr. Pococke and the consul were treated with this respect when they entered Cairo. The same custom is alluded to in the well-known fable of Phedrus, in which a slave is represented going before Augustus and officiously laying the dust. To throw dust in the air while a person was passing was therefore an act of great disrespect; to do so before a sovereign prince, an indecent outrage. But it is probable that Shimei meant more than disrespect and outrage to this afflicted king. Sir John Chardin informs us, that in the East, in general, those who demand justice against a criminal throw dust upon him, signifying that he ought to be put in the grave, and hence the common imprecation among the Turks and Persians, "Be covered with earth, " or, "Earth be upon thy head." \textsuperscript{16} God save the king Heb. let the king live \textsuperscript{17} Is this thy why wentest \textsuperscript{21} Go in, unto thy, ; abhorred; thy father then shall the hands \textsuperscript{23} as if; oracle of God Heb. word of God, so was The first counsel of this sagacious but wicked man to Absalom was more like an oracle of Satan, both for subtlety and atrocity. He advised the shameless measure just detailed, in order to establish Absalom, and to preclude the possibility of a reconciliation with David. The wives of a conquered king were always the property of the conqueror; and in possessing these he appeared to possess the right to the kingdom. all the counsel; both\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 17}
\markright{KINGS II 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Achitophel said to Abessalom, Let me now choose out for myself twelve thousand men, and I will arise and follow after David this night: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and I will come upon him when he [is] weary and weak-handed, and I will strike him with terror; and all the people with him shall flee, and I will strike the king only of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will bring back all the people to you, as a bride returns to her husband: only you seek the life of one man, and all the people shall have peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the saying [was] right in the eyes of Abessalom, and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Abessalom said, Call now also Chusi the Arachite, and let us hear what [is] in his mouth, even in his also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Chusi went in to Abessalom, and Abessalom spoke to him, saying, After this manner spoke Achitophel: shall we do according to his word? but if not, do you speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Chusi said to Abessalom, This counsel which Achitophel has counselled this one time [is] not good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Chusi said, You know your father and his men, that they are very mighty, and bitter in their spirit, as a bereaved bear in the field, [and as a wild boar in the plain]: and your father [is] a man of war, and will not give the people rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For, behold, he is now hidden in one of the hills or in some [other] place: and it shall come to pass when he falls upon them at the beginning, that [some one] will certainly hear, and say, There has been a slaughter among the people that follow after Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then even he [that is] strong, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, —it shall utterly melt: for all Israel knows that your father [is] mighty, and they that are with him [are] mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For thus I have surely given counsel, that all Israel be generally gathered to you from Dan even to Bersabee, as the sand that is upon the sea-shore for multitude: and that your presence go in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And we will come upon him in one of the places where we shall find him, and we will encamp against him, as the dew falls upon the earth; and we will not leave of him and of his men so much as one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if he shall have taken refuge with his army in a city, then shall all Israel take ropes to that city, and we will draw it even into the river, that there may not be left there even a stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Abessalom, and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Chusi the Arachite [is] better than the counsel of Achitophel. For the Lord ordained to disconcert the good counsel of Achitophel, that the Lord might bring all evil upon Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Chusi the Arachite said to Sadoc and Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus Achitophel counselled Abessalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now send quickly and report to David, saying, Lodge not this night in Araboth of the wilderness: even go and make haste, lest [one] swallow up the king, and all the people with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jonathan and Achimaas stood by the well of Rogel, and a maidservant went and reported to them, and they go and tell king David; for they might not be seen to enter into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But a young man saw them and told Abessalom: and the two went quickly, and entered into the house of a man in Baurim; and he had a well in his court, and they went down into it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And a woman took a covering, and spread it over the mouth of the well, and spread out ground corn upon it to dry, and the thing was not known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the servants of Abessalom came to the woman into the house, and said, Where [are] Achimaas and Jonathan? and the woman said to them, They are gone a little way beyond the water. And they sought and found them not, and returned to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass after they were gone, that they came up out of the pit, and went on their way; and reported to king David, and said to David, Arise you⌃ and go quickly over the water, for thus has Achitophel counselled concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And David rose up and all the people with him, and they passed over Jordan till the morning light; there was not one missing who did not pass over Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Achitophel saw that his counsel was not followed, and he saddled his ass, and rose and departed to his house into his city; and he gave orders to his household, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And David passed over to Manaim: and Abessalom crossed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Abessalom appointed Amessai in the room of Joab over the host. And Amessai was the son of a man whose name was Jether of Jezrael: he went in to Abigaia the daughter of Naas, the sister of Saruia the mother of Joab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And all Israel and Abessalom encamped in the land of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass when David came to Manaim, that Uesbi the son of Naas of Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Amiel of Lodabar, and Berzelli the Galaadite of Rogellim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} brought ten embroidered beds, (with double coverings,) and ten caldrons, and earthenware, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and meal, and beans, and pulse, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheeses of kine: and they brought them to David and to his people with him to eat; for [one] said, The people [is] faint and hungry and thirsty in the wilderness.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I will arise; this night \textsuperscript{3} I will bring shall be \textsuperscript{4} the saying; pleased Absalom well Heb. was right in the eyes of Absalom \textsuperscript{5} Hushai, he saith Heb. is in his mouth \textsuperscript{7} given Heb. counselled not good \textsuperscript{8} mighty men, ; chafed in their minds Heb. bitter of soul, as a bear; thy father is \textsuperscript{9} he is hid; some; over thrown Heb. fallen \textsuperscript{10} heart; utterly melt; thy father; and they which \textsuperscript{11} all Israel; as the sand; thou go Heb. they face, or presence go etc in thine \textsuperscript{12} in some place we will light This is a very beautiful and expressive figure. The dew in Palestine, and other warm climates, falls fast, sudden, and heavy; and it falls upon every spot of earth, so that not a blade of grass escapes it. It is therefore no inapt emblem of a numerous and active army; and it was, perhaps, for this reason that the Romans called their light armed forces rorarii . \textsuperscript{13} bring ropes In the same manner the king of Maturan, in Java, proposed pulling down a tower which the Dutch had built, by making his people and elephants pull at a number of chains, and ropes of cocoa-nut bark, thrown around it. one small \textsuperscript{14} the Lord; appointed Heb. commanded; to defeat; good counsel \textsuperscript{16} Lodge but speedily, ; be swallowed \textsuperscript{19} spread a covering, the thing \textsuperscript{20} They be gone; , when they had sought \textsuperscript{22} and they passed; there lacked \textsuperscript{23} saw, followed Heb. done his city put his household in order Heb. gave charge concerning his house, and hanged \textsuperscript{25} Amasa, Ithra, Jether the Ishmaelite Abigail Heb. Abigal Nahash or, Jesse. \textsuperscript{27} the son of Nahash; Machir Barzillai \textsuperscript{28} beds These no doubt consisted of skins of beasts, mats, carpets, and such like.; basins or, cups, Sappoth, probably wooden bowls, such as the Arabs still eat out of, and knead their bread in. earthen vessels Keley yotzair, literally, "vessels of the potter." So when Dr. Perry visited the temple of Luxor in Egypt, he says, "We were entertained by the Caliph here with great civility and favour; he sent us, in return of our presents, several sheep, a good quantity of eggs, bardacks, " etc. The bardacks, he informs us, were earthen vessels, used "to cool and refresh their water in, by means of which it drinks very cool and pleasant in the hottest seasons of the year." See Harmer, chapter vi. wheat Mr. Jones says, "Travellers use zumeet, tumeet, and limereece . Zumeet is flour mixed with honey, butter, and spice; tumeet is flour done up with organ oil, and limereece is flour mixed with water, for drink. This quenches thirst much better than water alone, satisfies a hungry appetite; cools and refreshes tired and weary spirits, " etc. \textsuperscript{29} cheese of kine for David; to eat; The people; in the wilderness\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 18}
\markright{KINGS II 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David numbered the people with him, and set over them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David sent away the people, the third part under the hand of Joab, and the third part under the hand of Abessa the son of Saruia, the brother of Joab, and the third part under the hand of Ethi the Gittite. And David said to the people, I also will surely go out with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they said, You shall not go out: for if we should indeed flee, they will not care for us; and if half of us should die, they will not mind us; for you [are] as ten thousand of us: and now [it is] well that you shall be to us an aid to help us in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king said to them, Whatsoever shall seem good in your eyes I will do. And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king commanded Joab and Abessa and Ethi, saying, Spare for my sake the young man Abessalom. And all the people heard the king charging all the commanders concerning Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all the people went out into the wood against Israel; and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the people of Israel fell down there before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter in that day, [even] twenty thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the battle there was scattered over the face of all the land: and the wood consumed more of the people than the sword consumed among the people in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abessalom went to meet the servants of David: and Abessalom was mounted on his mule, and the mule came under the thick boughs of a great oak; and his head was entangled in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth; and the mule passed on from under him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And a man saw it, and reported to Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Abessalom hanging in an oak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Joab said to the man who reported it to him, And, behold, you did see him: why did you not strike him there to the ground? and I would have given you ten [pieces] of silver, and a girdle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the man said to Joab, Were I even to receive a thousand shekels of silver, I would not lift my hand against the king's son; for in our ears the king charged you and Abessa and Ethi, saying, Take care of the young man Abessalom for me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} so as to do no harm to his life: and nothing of the matter will be concealed from the king, and you will set yourself against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Joab said, I will begin this; I will not thus remain with you. And Joab took three darts in his hand, and thrust them into the heart of Abessalom, while he was yet alive in the heart of the oak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And ten young men that bore Joab's armor compassed Abessalom, and struck him and killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing Israel, for Joab spared the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he took Abessalom, and cast him into a great cavern in the wood, into a deep pit, and set up over him a very great heap of stones: and all Israel fled every man to his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now Abessalom while yet alive had taken and set up for himself the pillar near which he was taken, and set it up so as to have the pillar in the king's dale; for he said he had no son to keep his name in remembrance: and he called the pillar, Abessalom's hand, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Achimaas the son of Sadoc said, Let me run now and carry glad tidings to the king, for the Lord has delivered him from the hand of his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Joab said to him, You [shall] not [be] a messenger of glad tidings this day; you shall bear them another day; but on this day you shall bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Joab said to Chusi, Go, report to the king all that you have seen. And Chusi did obeisance to Joab, and went out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Achimaas the son of Sadoc said again to Joab, Nay, let me also run after Chusi. And Joab said, Why would you thus run, my son? attend, you have no tidings for profit if you go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he said, Why should I not run? and Joab said to him, Run. And Achimaas ran along the way of Kechar, and outran Chusi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And David was sitting between the two gates: and the watchman went up on the top of the gate of the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the watchman cried out, and reported to the king. And the king said, If he be alone, [there are] good tidings in his mouth. And the man came and drew near. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman cried at the gate, and said, And look, another man running alone. And the king said, He also brings glad tidings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the watchman said, I see the running of the first as the running of Achimaas the son of Sadoc. And the king said, He [is] a good man, and will come to [report] glad tidings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Achimaas cried out and said to the king, Peace. And he did obeisance to the king with his face to the ground, and said, Blessed [be] the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men that lifted up their hands against my lord the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the king said, [Is] the young man Abessalom safe? and Achimaas said, I saw a great multitude [at the time] of Joab's sending the king's servant and your servant, and I knew not what was there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the king said, Turn aside, stand still here. And he turned aside, and stood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And, behold, Chusi came up, and said to the king, Let my lord the king hear glad tidings, for the Lord has avenged you this day upon all them that rose up against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the king said to Chusi, Is it well with the young man Abessalom? and Chusi said, Let the enemies of my lord the king, and all whoever have risen up against him for evil, be as that young man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the king was troubled, and went to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and thus he said as he went, My son Abessalom, my son, my son Abessalom; would God I had died for you, [even] I [had died] for you, Abessalom, my son, my son!\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a third part, the hand of Joab Ittai I will surely \textsuperscript{3} Thou shalt if we flee; care for us Heb. set their heart on us but now The particle attah, Now, is doubtless a mistake for the pronoun attah, Thou, and so it appears to have been read by the LXX, Vulgate, and Chaldee, and by two of Kennicott's and De Rossi's manuscripts. worth etc. Heb. as ten thousand of us, succour Heb. be to succour \textsuperscript{4} by the gate; by hundreds David's small company, by this time, was greatly recruited; but what its number was we cannot tell. Josephus says it amounted only to 4, 000 men. \textsuperscript{5} Deal gently, ; all the people \textsuperscript{6} wood of Ephraim The wood of Ephraim was evidently beyond Jordan, and apparently not far from Mahanaim; and it is supposed to be the place where the Ephraimites were slain by Jephthah. \textsuperscript{7} the people, a great, twenty thousand men \textsuperscript{8} in the wood, That is, probably, many more were slain in pursuit through the wood than in the battle, by falling into swamps, pits, etc., and being entangled and cut down by David's men. Such is the relation of Josephus; but the Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic state, that they were devoured by wild beasts in the wood.; devoured more Heb. multiplied to devour \textsuperscript{9} his head Riding furiously under the thick boughs of a great oak, which hung low and had never been cropped, either the twisted branches, or some low forked bough of the tree, caught him by the neck, or, as some think, by the loops into which his long hair had been pinned, which had been so much his pride, and was now justly made a halter for him. He may have hung so low from the bough, in consequence of the length of his hair, that he could not use his hands to help himself, or so entangled that his hands were bound, so that the more he struggled the more he was embarrassed. This set him up as a fair mark to the servants of David; and although David would have spared his rebellious son, if his orders had been executed, yet he could not turn the sword of Divine justice, in executing the just, righteous sentence of death on this traitorous son., ; taken up \textsuperscript{12} receive etc. Heb. weigh upon mine hand in our hearing Beware etc. Heb. Beware, whosoever ye be, of the, etc \textsuperscript{13} wrought, for there is no \textsuperscript{14} with thee Heb. before thee thrust them; midst Heb. heart \textsuperscript{17} laid This was the ancient method of burying, whether heroes or traitors; the heap of stones being designed to perpetuate the memory of the event, whether good or bad. The Arabs in general make use of no other monument than a heap of stones over a grave. Thus, in an Arabic poem, it is related, that Hatim the father, and Adi the grandfather of Kais, having been murdered, at a time before Kais was capable of reflection, his mother kept it a profound secret; and in order to guard him against having any suspicion, she collected a parcel of stone on two hillocks in the neighbourhood, and told her son that the one was the grave of his father, and the other of his grandfather. The ancient cairns in Ireland and Scotland, and the tumuli in England, are of this kind. \textsuperscript{18} reared up the king's I have no son; he called; Absalom's place Josephus says there was in his time, about two furlongs from Jerusalem, a marble pillar called Absalom's hand, as it is in the Hebrew (see note on ); and there is one shown to the present day, in the valley of Jehoshaphat, which, though comparatively a modern structure, probably occupies the site of the original one set up by Absalom. \textsuperscript{19} Ahimaaz, avenged him Heb. judged him from the hand, etc. \textsuperscript{20} bear tidings Heb. be a man of tidings, because \textsuperscript{22} howsoever Heb. be what may ready or, convenient \textsuperscript{27} thinketh Heb. I see, He is a good \textsuperscript{28} All is well or, Peace be to thee, Heb. Peace, he fell down upon his face, This act was not only in reverence to the king, but in humble adoration of God, whose name he praises for this victory. The more our hearts are fixed and enlarged, in thanksgiving to God for our mercies, the better disposed we shall be to bear with patience the afflictions mixed with them., Blessed; delivered up Heb. shut up \textsuperscript{29} Is the young man Absalom safe Heb. is there peace to, etc. I saw a great. \textsuperscript{31} Tidings Heb. Tidings is brought the Lord, ; Cushi was the man Joab ordered to carry the tidings to David. He was an Ethiopian, as his name signifies, and some think he was so by birth - a black, who waited on Joab, probably one of the ten who had helped to dispatch Absalom; though it was dangerous for one of those to bring the news to David, lest his fate should be the same with theirs that reported the death of Saul and Ishbosheth to him. \textsuperscript{32} The enemies Thus Cushi obliquely and slowly informs David of the death of his son Absalom. \textsuperscript{33} O my son would God\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 19}
\markright{KINGS II 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And they brought Joab word, saying, Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the victory was turned that day into mourning to all the people, for the people heard say that day, The king grieves after his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people stole away that day to go into the city, as people steal away when they are ashamed as they flee in the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king hid his face: and the king cried with a loud voice, My son Abessalom! Abessalom my son! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Joab went in to the king, into the house, and said, You have this day shamed the faces of all your servants that have delivered you this day, and [have saved] the lives of your sons and of your daughters, and the lives of your wives, and of your concubines, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} forasmuch as you love them that hate you, and hate them that love you; and you have this day declared, that your princes and your servants are nothing [in your sight]: for I know this day, that if Abessalom were alive, [and] all of us dead today, then it would have been right in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now arise, and go forth, and speak comfortably to your servants; for I have sworn by the Lord, that unless you will go forth today, there shall not a man remain with you this night: and know for yourself, this thing [will] indeed [be] evil to you beyond all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then the king arose, and sat in the gate: and all the people reported, saying, Behold, the king sits in the gate. And all the people went in before the king to the gate; for Israel had fled every man to his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And all the people disputed among all the tribes of Israel, saying, King David delivered us from all our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines: and now he has fled from the land, and from his kingdom, and from Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Abessalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle: and now why are you⌃ silent about bringing back the king? And the word of all Israel came to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And king David sent to Sadoc and Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Israel, saying, Why are you⌃ the last to bring back the king to his house? whereas the word of all Israel is come to the king to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You⌃ [are] my brethren, you⌃ [are] my bones and my flesh: why are you⌃ the last to bring back the king to his house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you⌃ shall say to Amessai, [Are] you not my bone and my flesh? and now God do so to me, and more also, if you shall not be commander of the host before me continually in the room of Joab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he bowed the heart of all the men of Juda as that of one man; and they sent to the king, saying, Return you, and all your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king returned, and came as far as Jordan. And the men of Juda came to Galgala on their way to meet the king, to cause the king to pass over Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Semei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, of Baurim, hasted and went down with the men of Juda to meet king David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And a thousand men of Benjamin [were] with him, and Siba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons with him, and his twenty servants with him: and they went directly down to Jordan before the king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and they performed the service of bringing the king over; and there went over a ferry-boat to remove the household of the king, and to do that which was right in his eyes. And Semei the son of Gera fell on his face before the king, as he went over Jordan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and said to the king, Let not my lord now impute iniquity, and remember not all the iniquity of your servant in the day in which my lord went out from Jerusalem, so that the king should mind it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For your servant knows that I have sinned: and, behold, I am come today before all Israel and the house of Joseph, to go down and meet my lord the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Abessai the son of Saruia answered and said, Shall not Semei therefore be put to death, because he cursed the Lord's anointed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And David said, What have I to do with you, you⌃ sons of Saruia, that you⌃ as it were lie in wait against me this day? today no man in Israel shall be put to death, for I know not if I this day reign over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the king said to Semei, You shall not die: and the king swore to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Memphibosthe the son of Saul's son went down to meet the king, and had not dressed his feet, nor pared his nails, nor shaved himself, neither had he washed his garments, from the day that the king departed, until the day when he arrived in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass when he went into Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Memphibosthe? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Memphibosthe said to him, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me; for your servant said to him, Saddle me the ass, and I will ride upon it, and go with the king; for your servant [is] lame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he has dealt deceitfully with your servant to my lord the king: but my lord the king [is] as an angel of God, and do you that which is good in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For all the house of my father were but as dead men before my lord the king; yet you have set your servant among them that eat at your table: and what right have I any longer even to cry to the king? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the king said to him, Why speak you any longer of your matters? I have said, You and Siba shall divide the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Memphibosthe said to the king, Yes, let him take all, since my lord the king has come in peace to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Berzelli the Galaadite came down from Rogellim, and crossed over Jordan with the king, that he might conduct the king over Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Berzelli was a very old man, eighty years old; and he had maintained the king when he lived in Manaim; for he was a very great man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the king said to Berzelli, You shall go over with me, and I will nourish your old age with me in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Berzelli said to the king, How many [are] the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} I am this day eighty years old: can I then distinguish between good and evil? Can your servant taste any longer what I eat or drink? can I any longer hear the voice of singing men or singing women? and therefore shall your servant any longer be a burden to my lord the king? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Your servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why does the king return me this recompense? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Let, I pray you, your servant remain, and I will die in my city, by the tomb of my father and of my mother. And, behold, your servant Chamaam shall go over with my lord the king; and do you to him as it seems good in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the king said, Let Chamaam go over with me, and I will do to him what is good in my sight; and whatever you shall choose at my hand, I will do for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And all the people went over Jordan, and the king went over; and the king kissed Berzelli, and blessed him; and he returned to his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the king went over to Galgala, and Chamaam went over with him: and all the men of Juda went over with the king, and also half the people of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, Why have our brethren the men of Juda stolen you away, and caused the king and all his house to pass over Jordan, and all the men of David with him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And all the men of Juda answered the men of Israel, and said, Because the king is near of kin to us: and why were you thus angry concerning this matter? have we indeed eaten of the king's food? or has he given us a gift, or has he sent us a portion? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the men of Israel answered the men of Juda, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we are older than you, we have also an interest in David above you: and why have you⌃ thus insulted us, and why was not our advice taken before that of Juda, to bring back our king? And the speech of the men of Juda was sharper than the speech of the men of Israel.\par

But, in his manner, Joab far exceeded the bounds of that reverence which a servant owes to his master, or a subject to his prince. saved \textsuperscript{6} In that etc. Heb. By loving, etc thou regardest etc. Heb. princes or servants are not to thee. then it had. \textsuperscript{7} comfortably unto thy Heb. to the heart of thy; *marg. there all the evil \textsuperscript{8} sat in the gate How prudently and mildly David took the reproof and counsel given him! He shook off his grief, anointed his head, and washed his face, that he might not appear unto men to mourn, and then made his appearance at the gate of the city, which was the public place of resort for the hearing of causes and giving judgment, as well as a place to ratify special bargains. Thither the people flocked to congratulate him on his and their safety, and that all was well. When we are convinced of a fault, we must amend, though we are told of it by our inferiors in a way which is peculiarly painful to our natural feelings. This ancient custom still obtains in the East; for when Dr. Pococke returned from viewing the town of ancient Byblus, he says, "The sheik and the elders were sitting in the gate of the city, after the ancient manner, and I sat awhile with them.", for Israel \textsuperscript{9} strife; The king;, he is fled \textsuperscript{10} whom; is dead speak ye not a word Heb. are ye silent \textsuperscript{13} Amasa; God; room of Joab \textsuperscript{14} he bowed The measures that he pursued were the best calculated that could be adopted for accomplishing this salutary end. David appears to take no notice of their infidelity, but rather to place confidence in them, that their confidence in him might be naturally excited; and to oblige them yet farther, purposes to make Amasa general of the army, instead of Joab. even \textsuperscript{16} Shimei It appears that Shimei was a powerful chieftain in the land; for he had here in his retinue no less than a thousand men.; hasted \textsuperscript{18} And there The LXX connecting this the with preceding verse, render, και κατευθυναν τον Ιορδανην εμπροσθεν του βασιλεως, και ελειτουργησαν την λειτουργιαν του διαβιβασαι τον βασιλεα, "and they made ready Jordan before the king, and did the necessary service to bring over the king." The Vulgate has: et irrumpentes Jordanem, ante regem transierunt vada, ut traducerent domum regis, "and breaking into Jordan, they passed the fords before the king, to bring over the king's household." Josephus says they prepared a bridge over the Jordan, to facilitate his passage. what he thought good Heb. the good in his eyes fell down \textsuperscript{19} And said Let not; remember; did perversely; take it \textsuperscript{22} What have; shall there any man \textsuperscript{24} Mephibosheth, dressed his feet Literally, made his feet, which seems to mean washing the feet paring the nails, and perhaps anointing or otherwise perfuming them, if not tinging the nails with henna; see note on . Sir John Chardin, in his manuscript note on this place, informs us, that it is customary in the East to have as much care of the feet as the hands; and that their barbers cut and adjust the nails with a proper instrument, because they often go barefoot. The nails of the toes of the mummies inspected in London in 1763, of which an account is given in the Philosophical Transactions for 1764, seem to have been tinged with some reddish colour.; trimmed Literally, made his beard, which may mean, combing, curling, and perfuming it. But Mr. Morier says that they almost universally dye the beard black, by successive layers of a paste made of henna, and another made of the leaf of the indigo. How many days are the years of my life \textsuperscript{35} can I discern; taste I hear; a burden \textsuperscript{37} Let thy The whole of this little episode is extremely interesting, and contains an affecting description of the infirmities of old age. The venerable and kind Barzillai was fourscore years old; his ear was become dull of hearing, and his relish for even royal dainties was gone. The evil days had arrived in which he was constrained to say, "I have no pleasure in them" ( ). As he was too old either to enjoy the pleasures of a court, or to be of any further service to the king, he finishes his affecting address to the aged monarch with the request, that he would suffer him to enjoy what old men naturally desire, to "die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and mother; " at the same time commending his son Chimham to his kind offices. I may die; by the grave, ; Chimham \textsuperscript{39} the king The kiss was the token of friendship and farewell; the blessing was a prayer to God for his prosperity. Probably a prophetical benediction. kissed Barzillai; blessed, ;, ; returned \textsuperscript{40} Chimham Heb. \subsection*{Kings II 20}
\markright{KINGS II 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a transgressor [so] called there, and his name was Sabee, a Benjamite, the son of Bochori: and he blew the trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have we [any] inheritance in the son of Jessae: to your tents, O Israel, every one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all the men of Israel went up from following David after Sabee the son of Bochori: but the men of Juda adhered to their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David went into his house at Jerusalem: and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and he put them in a place of custody, and maintained them, and went not in to them; and they were kept living as widows, till the day of their death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king said to Amessai, Call to me the men of Juda for three days, and do you be present here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Amessai went to call Juda, and delayed beyond the time which David appointed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David said to Amessai, Now shall Sabee the son of Bochori do us more harm than Abessalom: now then take you with you the servants of your lord, and follow after him, lest he find for himself strong cities, so will he blind our eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there went out after him Amessai and the men of Joab, and the Cherethites, and the Phelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sabee the son of Bochori. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they [were] by the great stone that is in Gabaon: and Amessai went in before them: and Joab had upon him a military cloak over his apparel, and over it he was girded with a dagger fastened upon his loins in its scabbard: and the dagger came out, it even came out and fell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joab said to Amessai, Are you in health, [my] brother? and the right hand of Joab took hold of the beard of Amessai to kiss him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Amessai observed not the dagger that was in the hand of Joab: and Joab struck him with it on the loins, and his bowels were shed out upon the ground, and he did not repeat the blow, and he died: and Joab and Abessai his brother pursued after Sabee the son of Bochori. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And there stood over him one of the servants of Joab, and said, Who [is] he that is for Joab, and who [is] on the side of David following Joab? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Amessai [was] weltering in blood in the midst of the way. And a man saw that all the people stood still; and he removed Amessai out of the path into a field, and he cast a garment upon him, because he saw every one that came to him standing still. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And when he was quickly removed from the road, every man of Israel passed after Joab to pursue after Sabee the son of Bochori. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Bethmacha; and all in Charri too were assembled, and followed after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they came and besieged him in Abel and Phermacha: and they raised a mound against the city and it stood close to the wall; and all the people with Joab proposed to throw down the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And a wise woman cried from the wall, and said, Hear, hear; say, I pray you⌃, to Joab, Draw near hither, and I will speak to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he drew near to her, and the woman said to him, Are you Joab? and he said, I [am]. And she said to him, Hear the words of your handmaid; and Joab said, I do hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she spoke, saying, Of old time they said thus, Surely one was asked in Abel, and Dan, whether the faithful in Israel failed in what they purposed; they will surely ask in Abel, even in like manner, whether they have failed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I am a peaceful one of the strong ones in Israel; but you seek to destroy a city and a mother city in Israel: why do you seek to ruin the inheritance of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should ruin or destroy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Is not the case thus, that a man of mount Ephraim, Sabee, son of Bochori by name, has even lifted up his hand against king David? Give him only to me, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the woman went in to all the people, and she spoke to all the city in her wisdom; and they took off the head of Sabee the son of Bochori; and took it away and threw it to Joab: and he blew the trumpet, and the people separated from the city away from him, every man to his tent: and Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joab [was] over all the forces of Israel: and Banaias the son of Jodae [was] over the Cherethites and over the Phelethites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Adoniram [was] over the tribute: and Josaphath the son of Achiluth [was] recorder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Susa [was] scribe: and Sadoc and Abiathar [were] priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Moreover Iras the [son of] Iarin was priest to David.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And there; a man; he blew; We have \textsuperscript{2} every man; the men; from Jordan \textsuperscript{3} ten women, and put The confinement and retired maintenance of these women was the only measure which in justice and prudence could be adopted. In China, when an emperor dies, all his women are removed to an edifice called the palace of chastity, situated within the palace, in which they are shut up for the remainder of their lives. ward Heb. an house of ward, shut Heb. bound living in widowhood Heb. in widowhood of life \textsuperscript{6} Abishai, ; do us thy lord's; escape us Heb. deliver himself from our eyes \textsuperscript{9} Art thou; took Amasa Thevenot says, that among the Turks it is a great affront to take one by the beard, unless it be to kiss him, in which case they often do it. D'Arvieux, describing an assembly of Arab emirs at an entertainment, says, "After the usual civilities, caresses, kissings of the beard, and of the hand, which every one gave and received according to his rank and dignity, they sat down upon mats." The doing this by the Arab emirs corresponds with the conduct of Joab, and illustrates this horrid assassination. to kiss him \textsuperscript{10} in Joab's; he smote; and shed struck him not again Heb. doubled not his stroke \textsuperscript{14} Abel Or rather, probably, Abel of Beth-Maachah, as in the next verse. It appears, from Joab having marched "through all the tribes of Israel, " to have been situated in the northern confines of the land of Israel, and in the half tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan, as that was the situation of Maachah, to which it belonged. This agrees with the situation of the Abila which Eusebius and Jerome place between Paneas, or Cesarea Philippi, and Damascus. Josephus says it was a fortified city, and a metropolis of the Israelites; and also that it belonged to the ten tribes, having been taken from the king of Damascus.; Berites, Beeroth \textsuperscript{15} cast up; a bank So LXX generally render solelah, by προσχωμα or χωμα; which latter is described by Potter as "a mount, which was raised so high as to equal, if not exceed, the top of the besieged walls. The sides were walled in with bricks or stones, or secured with strong rafters; the fore part only, being by degrees to be moved near the walls, remained bare." it stood in the trench or, it stood against the outmost wall battered etc. Heb. marred to throw down \textsuperscript{18} They were wont etc. or, They plainly spake in the beginning, saying, Surely they will ask of Abel, and so make an end. \textsuperscript{19} peaceable; a mother; swallow; the inheritance \textsuperscript{20} Far be it; that I should \textsuperscript{21} a man; by name Heb. by his name lifted; his head \textsuperscript{22} in her wisdom, he blew, retired Heb. were scattered And Joab \textsuperscript{26} Ira; Ithrite Jairite chief ruler or, prince; The Hebrew is cohen ledawid, which might be rendered, a priest of David; and so the Septuagint, Vulgate, Syriac, and Arabic. The Chaldee has rav, a chief or prince. Probably he was a kind of domestic chaplain or seer to the king.\par}

\subsection*{Kings II 21}
\markright{KINGS II 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David sought the face of the Lord. And the Lord said, [There is] guilt upon Saul and his house because of his bloody murder, whereby he killed the Gabaonites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And King David called the Gabaonites, and said to them; —(now the Gabaonites are not the children of Israel, but [are] of the remnant of the Amorite, and the children of Israel had sworn to them: but Saul sought to strike them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Juda.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David said to the Gabaonites, What shall I do to you? and wherewithal shall I make atonement, that you⌃ may bless the inheritance of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Gabaonites said to him, We have no [question about] silver or gold with Saul and with his house; and there is no man for us to put to death in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said, What say you⌃? speak, and I will do it for you. And they said to the king, The man who would have made an end of us, and persecuted us, who plotted against us to destroy us, let us utterly destroy him, so that he shall have no standing in all the coasts of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let one give us seven men of his sons, and let us hang them up in the sun to the Lord in Gabaon of Saul, as chosen out for the Lord. And the king said, I will give [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the king spared Memphibosthe son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the oath of the Lord that was between them, even between David and Jonathan the son of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king took the two sons of Respha the daughter of Aia, whom she bore to Saul, Hermonoi and Memphibosthe, and the five sons of Michol daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Esdriel son of Berzelli the Moulathite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he gave them into the hand of the Gabaonites, and they hanged them up to the sun in the mountain before the lord: and they fell, even the seven together: moreover they were put to death in the days of harvest at the commencement, in the beginning of barley harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Respha the daughter of Aia took sackcloth, and fixed it for herself on the rock in the beginning of barley harvest, until water dropped upon them out of heaven: and she did not suffer the birds of the air to rest upon them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it was told David what Respha the daughter of Aia the concubine of Saul had done, [and they were faint, and Dan, the son of Joa of the offspring of the giants overtook them.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And David went and took the bones of Saul, and the bones of Jonathan his son, from the men of the sons of Jabis Galaad, who stole them from the street of Baethsan; for the Philistines set them there in the day in which the Philistines struck Saul in Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he carried up thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and gathered the bones of them that had been hanged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they buried the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and the bones of them that had been hanged, in the land of Benjamin in the hill, in the sepulchre of Cis his father; and they did all things that the king commanded: and after this God listened to [the prayers of] the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And there was yet war between the Philistines and Israel: and David went down and his servants with him, and they fought with the Philistines, and David went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jesbi, who was of the progeny of Rapha, and the head of whose spear [was] three hundred shekels of brass in weight, who also was girded with a club, even he thought to strike David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abessa the son of Saruia helped him and struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David swore, saying, You shall not any longer go out with us to battle, and you shall not quench the lamp of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And after this there was a battle again with the Philistines in Geth: then Sebocha the Astatothite killed Seph of the progeny of Rapha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And there was a battle in Rom with the Philistines; and Eleanan son of Ariorgim the Bethleemite killed Goliath the Gittite; and the staff of his spear [was] as a weaver's beam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And there was yet a battle in Geth: and there was a man of stature, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet [were] six on each, four and twenty in number: and he also was born to Rapha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he defied Israel, and Jonathan son of Semei brother of David, struck him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} These four were born descendants of the giants in Geth, the family of Rapha; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.\par

\subsection*{Kings II 22}
\markright{KINGS II 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song, in the day in which the Lord rescued him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the song was thus: O Lord, my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} my God; he shall be to me my guard, I will trust in him: [he is] my protector, and the horn of my salvation, my helper, and my sure refuge; you shall save me from the unjust man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I will call upon the Lord who is worthy to be praised, and I shall be saved from my enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For the troubles of death compassed me, the floods of iniquity amazed me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the pangs of death surrounded me, the agonies of death prevented me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} When I am afflicted I will call upon the Lord, and will cry to my God, and he shall hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry shall come into his ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the earth was troubled and quaked, and the foundations of heaven were confounded and torn asunder, because the Lord was angry with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} There went up a smoke in his wrath, and fire out of his mouth devours: coals were kindled at it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he bowed the heavens, and came down, and [there was] darkness under his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he rode upon the cherubs and did fly, and was seen upon the wings of the wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he made darkness his hiding-place; his tabernacle round about him was the darkness of waters, he condensed it with the clouds of the air. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} At the brightness before him coals of fire were kindled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord thundered out of heaven, and the Most High uttered his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he sent forth arrows, and scattered them, and he flashed lightning, and dismayed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the channels of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were revealed, at the rebuke of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He sent from above and took me; he drew me out of many waters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He delivered me from my strong enemies, from them that hated me, for they were stronger than I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The days of my affliction prevented me; but the Lord was my stay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he brought me into a wide place, and rescued me, because he delighted in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord recompensed me according to my righteousness; even according to the purity of my hands did he recompense me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Because, I kept the ways of the Lord, and did not wickedly depart from my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For all his judgments and his ordinances [were] before me: I departed not from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I shall be blameless before him, and will keep myself from my iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the Lord will recompense me according to my righteousness, and according to the purity of my hands in his eye-sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} With the holy you will be holy, and with the perfect man you will be perfect, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and with the excellent you will be excellent, and with the froward you will be froward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And you will save the poor people, and will bring down the eyes of the haughty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For you, Lord, [are] my lamp, and the Lord shall shine forth to me in my darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For by you shall I run [as] a girded man, and by my God shall I leap over a wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} As for the Mighty One, his way [is] blameless: the word of the Lord [is] strong [and] tried in the fire: he is a protector to all that put their trust in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Who [is] strong, but the Lord? and who will be a Creator except our God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} [It is] the Mighty One who strengthens me with might, and has prepared my way without fault. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} He makes my feet like hart's feet, and sets me upon the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} He teaches my hands to war, and has broken a brazen bow by my arm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And you have given me the shield of my salvation, and your propitious dealing has increased me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} so as to make room under me for my going, and my legs did not totter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} I will pursue my enemies, and will utterly destroy them; and I will not turn again till I have consumed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And I will crush them, and they shall not rise; and they shall fall under my feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And you shall strengthen me with power for the war; you shall cause them that rise up against me to bow down under me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And you have caused my enemies to flee before me, even them that hated me, and you have slain them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} They shall cry, and there shall be no helper; to the Lord, but he hearkens not to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And I ground them as the dust of the earth, I beat them small as the mire of the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And you shall deliver me from the striving of the peoples, you shall keep me [to be] the head of the Gentiles: a people which I knew not served me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} The strange children feigned [obedience] to me; they listened to me as soon as they heard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} The strange children shall be cast away, and shall be overthrown out of their hiding places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} The Lord lives, and blessed [be] my guardian, and my God, my strong keeper, shall be exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} The Lord who avenges me [is] strong, chastening the nations under me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} and bringing me out from my enemies: and you shall set me on high from among those that rise up against me: you shall deliver me from the violent man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Therefore will I confess to you, O Lord, among the Gentiles, and sing to your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} He magnifies the salvation of his king, and works mercy for his anointed, even for David and for his seed for ever.\par

\subsection*{Kings II 23}
\markright{KINGS II 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the last words of David. Faithful [is] David the son of Jessae, and faithful the man whom the Lord raised up to be the anointed of the God of Jacob, and beautiful [are] the psalms of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The Spirit of the Lord spoke by me, and his word [was] upon my tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The God of Israel says, A watchman out of Israel spoke to me a parable: I said among men, How will you⌃ strengthen the fear of the anointed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in the morning light of God, let the sun arise in the morning, from the light of which the Lord passed on, and as it were from the rain of the tender grass upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For my house [is] not so with the Mighty One: for he has made an everlasting covenant with me, ready, guarded at every time; for all my salvation and all my desire [is], that the wicked should not flourish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} All these [are] as a thorn thrust forth, for they shall not be taken with the hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and a man shall not labor among them; and [one shall have] that which is fully armed with iron, and the staff of a spear, and he shall burn them with fire, and they shall be burnt in their shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} These [are] the names of the mighty men of David: Jebosthe the Chananite is a captain of the third [part]: Adinon the Asonite, he drew his sword against eight hundred soldiers at once. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And after him Eleanan the son of his uncle, son of Dudi who was among the three mighty men with David; and when he defied the Philistines they were gathered there to war, and the men of Israel went up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He arose an struck the Philistines, until his hand was weary, and his hand clave to the sword: and the Lord wrought a great salvation in that day, and the people rested behind him only to strip [the slain]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And after him Samaia the son of Asa the Arachite: and the Philistines were gathered to Theria; and there was there a portion of ground full of lentiles; and the people fled before the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he stood firm in the midst of the portion, and rescued it, and struck the Philistines; and the Lord wrought a great deliverance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And three out of the thirty went down, and came to Cason to David, to the cave of Odollam; and [there was] an army of the Philistines, and they encamped in the valley of Raphain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David [was] then in the strong hold, and the garrison of the Philistines [was] then in Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And David longed, and said, Who will give me water to drink out of the well that is in Bethleem by the gate? now the band of the Philistines [was] then in Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the three mighty men broke through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well that was in Bethleem in the gate: and they took it, and brought it to David, and he would not drink it, but poured it out before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, O Lord, forbid that I should do this, that I should drink of the blood of the men who went at [the risk of] their lives: and he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Abessa the brother of Joab the son of Saruia, he [was] chief among the three, and he lifted up his spear against three hundred whom he killed; and he had a name among three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Of those three [he was] most honorable, and he became a chief over them, but he reached not to the [first] three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Banaeas the son of Jodae, he was abundant in [mighty] deeds, from Cabeseel, and he struck the two sons of Ariel of Moab: and he went down and struck a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He struck an Egyptian, a wonderful man, and in the hand of the Egyptian [was] a spear as the side of a ladder; and he went down to him with a staff, and snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} These things did Banaeas the son of Jodae, and he had a name among the three mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He was honorable among the [second] three, but he reached not to the [first] three: and David made him his reporter. And these [are] the names of King David's mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Asael Joab's brother; he [was] among the thirty. Eleanan son of Dudi his uncle in Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Saema the Rudaean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Selles the Kelothite: Iras the son of Isca the Thecoite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Abiezer the Anothite, of the sons of the Anothite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Ellon the Aoite; Noere the Netophatite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Esthai the son of Riba of Gabaeth, son of Benjamin the Ephrathite; Asmoth the Bardiamite; Emasu the Salabonite: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Adroi of the brooks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Gadabiel son of the Arabothaeite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} the sons of Asan, Jonathan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Samnan the Arodite; Amnan the son of Arai the Saraurite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Aliphaleth the son of Asbites, the son of the Machachachite; Eliab the son of Achitophel the Gelonite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Asarai the Carmelite the son of Uraeoerchi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Gaal the son of Nathana. The son of much valour, [the son] of Galaaddi. Elie the Ammanite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Gelore the Bethorite, armor-bearer to Joab, son of Saruia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Iras the Ethirite. Gerab the Ethenite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Urias the Chettite: thirty-seven in all.\par
