\subsection*{Kings II 24}
\markright{KINGS II 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord caused his anger to burn forth again in Israel, and [Satan] stirred up David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king said to Joab commander of the host, who was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel and Juda, from Dan even to Bersabee, and number the people, and I will know the number of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joab said to the king, Now may the Lord add to the people one hundred-fold as many as they are, and [may] the eyes of my lord the king see it: but why does my lord the king desire this thing? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Nevertheless the word of the king prevailed against Joab and the captains of the host: And Joab and the captains of the host went out before the king to number the people of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they went over Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right of the city which is in the midst of the valley of Gad and Eliezer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they came to Galaad, and into the land of Thabason, which is Adasai, and they came to Danidan and Udan, and compassed Sidon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they came to Mapsar of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Evite and the Chananite: and they came by the South of Juda to Bersabee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they compassed the whole land; and they arrived at Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joab gave in the number of the census of the people to the king: and Israel consisted of eight hundred thousand men of might that drew sword; and the men of Juda, five hundred thousand fighting men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the heart of David struck him after he had numbered the people; and David said to the Lord, I have sinned grievously, O Lord, [in] what I have now done: remove, I pray you, the iniquity of your servant, for I have been exceedingly foolish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And David rose early in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to the prophet Gad, the seer, saying, Go, and speak to David, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Thus says the Lord, I bring [one of] three things upon you: now choose you one of them, and I will do [it] to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gad went in to David, and told him, and said to him, Choose [one of these things] to befall you, whether there shall come upon you [for] three years famine in your land; or that you should flee three months before your enemies, and they should pursue you; or that there should be [for] three days mortality in your land. Now then decide, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And David said to Gad, On every side I am much straitened: let me fall now into the hands of the Lord, for his compassions [are] very many; and let me not fall into the hands of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So David chose for himself the mortality: and [they were] the days of wheat harvest; and the Lord sent a pestilence upon Israel from morning till noon, and the plague began among the people; and there died of the people from Dan even to Bersabee seventy thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the angel of the Lord stretched out his hand against Jerusalem to destroy it, and the Lord repented of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, [It is] enough now, withhold your hand. And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David spoke to the Lord when he saw the angel striking the people, and he said, Behold, it is I that have done wrong, but these sheep what have they done? Let your hand, I pray you, be upon me, and upon my father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Gad came to David in that day, and said to him, Go up, and set up to the Lord an altar in the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And David went up according to the word of Gad, as the Lord commanded him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Orna looked out, and saw the king and his servants coming on before him: and Orna went forth, and did obeisance to the king with his face to the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Orna said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? and David said, To buy of you the threshing floor, in order to build an altar to the Lord that the plague may be restrained from off the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Orna said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer to the Lord that which is good in his eyes: behold, [here are] oxen for a whole burnt offering, and the wheels and furniture of the oxen for wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Orna gave all to the king: and Orna said to the king, The Lord your God bless you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king said to Orna, Nay, but I will surely buy it of you at a fair price, and I will not offer to the Lord my God a whole burnt offering for nothing. So David purchased the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And David built there an altar to the Lord, and offered up whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings: and Solomon made an addition to the altar afterwards, for it was little at first. And the Lord listened to the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2987, bc 1017, An, Ex, Is, 474 again he This verse, when read without reference to any other part of the word of God, is very difficult to understand, and has been used by those who desire to undermine the justice of God, to shew that he sought occasion to punish - that he incited David to sin; and when he had so incited him, gave to him the dreadful alternative of choosing one of three scourges by which his people were to be cut off. On the face of the passage these thoughts naturally arise, because "the Lord" is the antecedent to the pronoun "he, " - He moved David. But to those who "search the Scriptures, " this exceedingly difficult passage receives a wonderful elucidation. By referring to, the reader will there find that Satan was the mover, and that the Lord most righteously punished David for the display of pride he had manifested. Oh! that Christians, who sometimes have their minds harassed with doubts, would remember the promise, that what they know not now they shall know hereafter; and if no other instance of elucidation than this passage occurred to them to remove their doubts, let this be a means of stirring them up to dig deeper than ever into the inexhaustible mines of the Inspired Word. moved; number \textsuperscript{2} Joab, Go now etc. or, Compass now all, from Dan; and number We know not in what the sinfulness of this action consisted. Some think it was a contempt of the promise that the Israelites should be innumerable, and that they ought not to have been numbered without an express command, as in the days of Moses. Others suppose with Josephus that it was a kind of sacrilege, in omitting to collect the half-shekel a-piece for the use of the sanctuary. It however would appear that pride and ambition, and a desire of conquest, induced David to this measure, and rendered it so displeasing to God. that I may \textsuperscript{5} Aroer; river or, valley Jazer \textsuperscript{6} Gilead; land of Tahtimhodshi or, nether land newly inhabited, Dan-jaan.; Zidon \textsuperscript{10} David's heart; I have sinned; take away; foolishly \textsuperscript{12} I offer that I may \textsuperscript{14} I am in; for his;, ; great or, many let me not \textsuperscript{15} the Lord; from Dan seventy thousand men \textsuperscript{16} the angel; repented; It is enough; Araunah; Ornan the Jebusite \textsuperscript{17} spake I have sinned; these sheep; let thine \textsuperscript{18} Gad; threshing floor, These, among the ancient Jews, were only round, level plats of ground in the open air, as they are to this day in the East, where the corn was trodden out by oxen. \section*{1 Kings Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Jeremiah (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Jewish and Christian tradition often associates Kings with Jeremiah or a prophetic school around him; the book reads as prophetic covenant history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the human writer, but the Elijah-Elisha and Solomon narratives are received as true sacred history throughout later Scripture.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} exilic or late pre-exilic composition using earlier royal records\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology runs from David's death through Solomon and the divided kingdom down to Ahab and Jehoshaphat's era.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same royal history but differs from the MT in order and detail at several points, especially in the kingdom narratives.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} From Solomon's accession to the divided kingdom and the ministries of Elijah and related prophets.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To explain the monarchy under the covenant, showing blessing for obedience and judgment for apostasy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} kingdom; temple; covenant obedience; idolatry; prophetic warning; Elijah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Solomon's reign 1-11; Divided kingdom beginnings 12-16; Elijah cycle and royal narratives 17-22.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Kings fragments survive only sparsely Second Temple period | Subst. No large Qumran witness survives comparable to Samuel; major evidence comes from the medieval Hebrew tradition and ancient versions n/a | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve 1 Kings in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Retelling of Israel's monarchy by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Kings is important for MT/LXX comparison because the Greek tradition sometimes preserves different order, pluses, or names in the royal accounts.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Kings as prophetic covenant history, historically true and theologically interpretive, not as late fictionalized court legend.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Kings III 1}
\markright{KINGS III 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And king David [was] old and advanced in days, and they covered him with clothes, and he was not warmed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And his servants said, Let them seek for the king a young virgin, and she shall wait on the king, and cherish him, and lie with him, and my lord the king shall be warmed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So they sought for a fair damsel out of all the coasts of Israel; and they found Abisag the Somanite, and they brought her to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the damsel was extremely beautiful, and she cherished the king, and ministered to him, but the king knew her not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Adonias the son of Aggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king; and he prepared for himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And his father never at any time checked him, saying, Why have you done [thus]? and he was also very handsome in appearance, and his mother bore him after Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he conferred with Joab the son of Saruia, and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed after Adonias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But Sadoc the priest, and Banaeas the son of Jodae, and Nathan the prophet, and Semei, and Resi, and the mighty men of David, did not follow Adonias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Adonias sacrificed sheep and calves and lambs by the stone of Zoelethi, which was near Rogel: and he called all his brethren, and all the adult [men] of Juda, servants of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But Nathan the prophet, and Banaeas, and the mighty [men], and Solomon his brother, he did not call. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Nathan spoke to Bersabee the mother of Solomon, saying, Have you not heard that Adonias the son of Aggith reigns, and our lord David knows it not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now come, let me, I pray, give you counsel, and you shall rescue your life, and the life of your son Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Haste, and go in to king David, and you shall speak to him, saying, Have not you, my lord, O king, sworn to your handmaid, saying, Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? why then does Adonias reign? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I also will come in after you, and will confirm your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So Bersabee went in to the king into the chamber: and the king was very old, and Abisag the Somanite was ministering to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Bersabee bowed, and did obeisance to the king; and the king said, What is your request? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And she said, My lord, you did swear by the Lord your God to your handmaid, saying, Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and shall sit upon my throne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And now, behold, Adonias reigns, and you, my lord, O king, know [it] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he has sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance, and has called all the king's sons, and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander-in-chief of the host; but Solomon your servant he has not called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you, my lord, O king, —the eyes of all Israel [are] upon you, to tell them who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it shall come to pass, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, that I and Solomon my son shall be offenders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And behold, while she was yet talking with the king, Nathan the prophet came. And it was reported to the king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Behold, Nathan the prophet [is here]: and he came in to the king's presence, and did obeisance to the king with his face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Nathan said, My lord, O king, did you say, Adonias shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For he has gone down today, and has sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance, and has called all the king's sons, and the chiefs of the army, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and they said, [Long] live king Adonias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But he has not invited me your servant, and Sadoc the priest, and Banaeas the son of Jodae, and Solomon your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Has this matter happened by the authority of my lord the king, and have you not made known to your servant who shall sit upon the have given charge that he should be for a prince over Israel and Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Banaeas the son of Jodae answered the king and said, So let it be: may the Lord God of my lord the king confirm [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} As the Lord was with my lord the king, so let him be with Solomon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Sadoc the priest took the horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon, and blew the trumpet; and all the people said, Let king Solomon live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And all the people went up after him, and they danced in choirs, and rejoiced with great joy, and the {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} and Sadoc the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him in Gion, and have gone up thence rejoicing, and the city resounded: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And the servants of the king have gone in to bless our lord king David, saying, God make the name of Solomon better than your name, \subsection*{Kings III 2}
\markright{KINGS III 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the days of David drew near that he should die: and he addressed his son Solomon, saying, I go the way of all the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} but be you strong, and show yourself a man; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and keep the charge of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, to keep the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments which are written in the law of Moses; that you may understand what you shall do in all things that I command you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} that the Lord may confirm his word which he spoke, saying, If your children shall take heed to their way to walk before me in truth with all their heart, [I promise you], saying, there shall not fail you a man on the throne of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Moreover you know all that Joab the son of Saruia did to me, what he did to the two captains of the forces of Israel, to Abenner the son of Ner, and to Amessai the son of Jether, that he killed them, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put innocent blood on his girdle that was about his loins, and on his sandal that was on his foot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore you shall deal [with him] according to your wisdom, and you shall not bring down his grey hairs in peace to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But you shall deal kindly with the sons of Berzelli the Galaadite, and they shall be among those that eat at your table; for thus they drew near to me when I fled from the face of your brother Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And, behold, [there is] with you Semei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Baurim: and he cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went into the camp; and he came down to Jordan to meet me, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, I will not put you to death with the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But you shall by no means hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man, and will know what you shall do to him, and shall bring down his grey hairs with blood to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the days which David reigned over Israel [were] forty years; he reigned seven years in Chebron, and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was established greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Adonias the son of Aggith came in to Bersabee the mother of Solomon, and did obeisance to her: and she said, Do you enter peaceably? and he said, Peaceably: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I have business with you. And she said to him, Say on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to her, You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel turned their face toward me for a king; but the kingdom was turned [from me] and became my brother's: for it was [appointed] to him from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now I make one request of you, do not turn away your face. And Bersabee said to him, Speak [on]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said to her, Speak, I pray you, to king Solomon, for he will not turn away his face from you, and let him give me Abisag the Somanite for a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Bersabee said, Well; I will speak for you to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Bersabee went in to king Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonias; and the king rose up to meet her, and kissed her, and sat on the throne, and a throne was set for the mother of the king, and she sat on his right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And she said to him, I ask of you one little request; turn not away my face from you. And the king said to her, Ask, my mother, and I will not reject you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she said, Let, I pray you, Abisag the Somanite be given to Adonias your brother to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And king Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why have you asked Abisag for Adonias? ask for him the kingdom also; for he [is] my elder brother, and he has for his companion Abiathar the priest, and Joab the son of Saruia the commander-in-chief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And king Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, God do so to me, and more also, [if it be not] that Adonias has spoken this word against his own life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And now [as] the Lord lives who has established me, and set me on the throne of my father David, and he has made me a house, as the Lord spoke, this day shall Adonias be put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So king Solomon sent by the hand of Banaeas the son of Jodae, and he killed him, and Adonias died in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king said to Abiathar the priest, Depart you quickly to Anathoth to your farm, for you are worthy of death this day; but I will not kill you, because you have borne the ark of the covenant of the Lord before my father, and because you were afflicted in all things wherein my father was afflicted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Solomon removed Abiathar from being a priest of the Lord, that the word of the Lord might be fulfilled, which he spoke concerning the house of Heli in Selom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the report came to Joab son of Saruia; for Joab had turned after Adonias, and he went not after Solomon: and Joab fled to the tabernacle of the Lord, and caught hold of the horns of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it was told Solomon, saying, Joab has fled to the tabernacle of the Lord, and behold! he has hold of the horns of the altar. And king Solomon sent to Joab, saying, What ails you, that you have fled to the altar? and Joab said, Because I was afraid of you, and fled for refuge to the Lord. And Solomon sent Banaeas son of Jodae, saying, Go and kill him, and bury him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Banaeas son of Jodae came to Joab to the tabernacle of the Lord, and said to him, Thus says the king, Come forth. And Joab said, I will not come forth, for I will die here. And Banaeas son of Jodae returned and spoke to the king, saying, Thus has Joab spoken, and thus has he answered me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the king said to him, Go, and do to him as he has spoken, and kill him: and you shall bury him, and you shall remove this day the blood which he shed without cause, from me and from the house of my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the Lord has returned upon his own head the blood of his unrighteousness, inasmuch as he attacked two men more righteous and better than himself, and killed them with the sword, and my father David knew not of their blood, [even] Abenner the son of Ner the commander-in-chief of Israel, and Amessa the son of Jether the commander-in-chief of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And their blood is returned upon his head, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but to David, and his seed, and his house, and his throne, may there be peace for ever from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} So Banaeas son of Jodae went up, and attacked him, and killed him, and buried him in his house in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the king appointed Banaeas son of Jodae in his place over the host; and the kingdom was established in Jerusalem; and [as for] Sadoc the priest, the king appointed him to be high priest in the room of Abiathar. And Solomon son of David reigned over Israel and Juda in Jerusalem: and the Lord gave understanding to Solomon, and very much wisdom, and largeness of heart, as the sand by the sea-shore.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} I go; be thou; and show \textsuperscript{3} And keep;, statutes, testimonies;, written; that thou prosper or, do wisely, *marg., ; whithersoever \textsuperscript{4} That the Lord; his word; walk, ; with all their heart, ; fail etc. Heb. be cut off from thee from the throne \textsuperscript{5} Joab;, Abner Amasa Jether, Ithra shed Heb. put \textsuperscript{7} Barzillai; eat, ; when I fled \textsuperscript{8} Shimei; grievous Heb. strong he came \textsuperscript{9} hold him Do not consider him as an innocent man; for, as thou art a wise man, and knowest how to treat such persons, treat him as he deserves; only, as I have sworn to him that I would not put him to death, "bring not his hoar head down to the grave with blood." So Solomon understood David; for, after he had commanded Joab to be slain, in obedience to his father, he sent for Shimei, and knowing he ought to be well watched, he confined him to Jerusalem for the rest of his life, and so it appears David should be understood; for the negative particle lo, in the former clause, "hold him not guiltless, " should be repeated in the latter clause, though not expressed; instances of which frequently occur in the Hebrew Scriptures. (See note on . .; .; etc). This is the view taken of the subject by Dr. Kennicott, and it seems the best and most correct mode of interpreting the text.; wise, his; with \textsuperscript{12} am 2990, bc 1014, An, Ex, Is, 477 sat Solomon; his kingdom \textsuperscript{15} Thou knowest;, for it was \textsuperscript{16} deny me not Heb. turn not away my face \textsuperscript{23} God; if Adonijah We have already seen, that the whole harem of an eastern monarch was a part of the regal succession (see note on ); and it was treason for a subject to claim any wife or virgin who had once formed a part of it. Solomon evidently considered the request of Adonijah in this light; and was convinced that he was still aiming to seize the crown, to which he considered this as one step. But it is very doubtful, how far the plea either of policy or state necessity can justify Solomon in thus embruing his hands in his brother's blood, whatever might have been his treasonable intentions or conduct. spoken \textsuperscript{24} as the Lord set me; made me; as he promised put \textsuperscript{26} Abiathar, Anathoth; worthy of death Heb. a man of death; *marg. barest; hast been \textsuperscript{27} So Solomon This was for having taken part with Adonijah; but by it a remarkable prophecy was fulfilled. God had told Eli ( ) that the priesthood should depart from his house; Abiathar was the last of the priests of Ithamar, of which family was Eli the high priest. Zadok, who succeeded, was of the family of Eleazar; and by this change the priesthood reverted to its ancient channel. that he;, Shiloh \textsuperscript{31} Do that thou; which and from \textsuperscript{32} return; two men, more righteous; my father, Abner Amasa Jether; Ithra \textsuperscript{33} return upon; upon David; his house \textsuperscript{34} Benaiah, and fell It appears that he slew him at the very altar. The altar was so sacred among all the people, that, in general, even the vilest wretch found safety, if he once reached it. This led to many abuses, and the perversion of public justice; and God decreed ( ) that the presumptuous murderer, who had taken refuge at his altar, should be dragged thence and put to death. buried; in the\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 3}
\markright{KINGS III 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the wisdom of Solomon abounded exceedingly beyond the wisdom of all the ancients, and beyond all the wise men of Egypt: and he took the daughter of Pharao, and brought her into the city of David, until he had finished building his own house, and the house of the Lord first, and the wall of Jerusalem round about. In seven years he made and finished [them]. And Solomon had seventy thousand bearers of burdens, and eight thousand hewers of stone in the mountain: and Solomon made the sea, and the bases, and the great lavers, and the pillars, and the fountain of the court, and the brazen sea— and he built the citadel as a defence above it, he made a breach in the wall of the city of David: thus the daughter of Pharao went up out of the city of David to her house which he built for her. Then he built the citadel: and Solomon offered up three whole burnt offerings in the year, and peace-offerings on the altar which he built to the Lord, and he burnt incense before the Lord, and finished the house. And these are the chief persons who presided over the works of Solomon; three thousand and six hundred masters of the people that wrought the works. And he burit Assur, and Magdo, and Gazer, and upper Baethoron, and Ballath: only after he had built the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem round about, afterwards he built these cities. And when David was yet living, he charged Solomon, saying, Behold, there is with you Semei the son of Gera, of the seed of Benjamin out of Chebron: he cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went into the camp; and he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, He shall not be slain with the sword. But now do not you hold him guiltless, for you are a man of understanding, and you will know what you shall do to him, and you shall bring down his grey hairs with blood to the grave. And the king called Semei, and said to him, Build you a house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and you shall not go out thence any whither. And it shall come to pass in the day that you shall go forth and cross over the brook Kedron, know assuredly that you shall certainly die: your blood shall be upon your head. And the king caused him to swear in that day. And Semei said to the king, Good [is] the word that you have spoken, my lord O king: thus will your servant do. And Semei lived in Jerusalem three years. And it came to pass after the three years, that two servants of Semei ran away to Anchus son of Maacha king of Geth: and it was told Semei, saying, Behold, your servants [are] in Geth. And Semei rose up, and saddled his ass, and went to Geth to Anchus to seek out his servants: and Semei went, and brought his servants out of Geth. And it was told Solomon, saying, Semei is gone out of Jerusalem to Geth, and has brought back his servants. And the king sent and called Semei, and said to him, Did I not adjure you by the Lord, and testify to you, saying, In whatever day you shall go out of Jerusalem, and go to the right or left, know certainly that you shall assuredly die? And why have you not kept the oath of the Lord, and the commandment which I commanded you? And the king said to Semei, You know all your mischief which your heart knows, which you did to David my father: and the Lord has recompensed your mischief on your [own] head. And king Solomon [is] blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the Lord for ever. And Solomon commanded Banaeas the son of Jodae, and he went forth and killed him. And king Solomon was very prudent and wise: and Juda and Israel [were] very many, as the sand which is by the sea for multitude, eating, and drinking, and rejoicing: and Solomon was chief in all the kingdoms, and they brought gifts, and served Solomon all the days of his life. And Solomon began to open the domains of Libanus, and he built Thermae in the wilderness. And this was the daily provision of Solomon, thirty measures of fine flour, and sixty measures of ground meal, ten choice calves, and twenty oxen from the pastures, and one hundred sheep, besides stags, and does, and choice fed birds. For he ruled in all the country on this side the river, from Raphi to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the river: and he was at peace on all sides round about; and Juda and Israel lived safely, every one under his vine and under his fig tree, eating and drinand feasting, from Dan even to Bersabee, all the days of Solomon. And these [were] the princes of Solomon; Azariu son of Sadoc the priest, and Orniu son of Nathan chief of the officers, and he went to his house; and Suba the scribe, and Basa son of Achithalam recorder, and Abi son of Joab commander-in-chief, and Achire son of Edrai [was] over the levies, and Banaeas son of Jodae over the household and over the brick work, and Cachur the son of Nathan [was] counsellor. And Solomon had forty thousand brood mares for his chariots, and twelve thousand horses. And he reigned over all the kings from the river and to the land of the Philistines, and to the borders of Egypt: so Solomon the son of David reigned over Israel and Juda in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Nevertheless the people burnt incense on the high places, because a house had not yet been built to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Solomon loved the Lord, [so as] to walk in the ordinances of David his father; only he sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he arose and went to Gabaon to sacrifice there, for that [was] the highest place, and great: Solomon offered a whole burnt offering of a thousand [victims] on the altar in Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and the Lord said to Solomon, Ask some petition for yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Solomon said, You have dealt very mercifully with your servant David my father according as he walked before you in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with you, and you have kept for him this great mercy, to set his son upon his throne, as [it is] this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now, O Lord my God, you have appointed your servant in the room of David my father; and I am a little child, and know not my going out and my coming in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But your servant [is] in the midst of your people, whom you have chosen, a great people, which as this day can’t be numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You shall give therefore to your servant a heart to hear and to judge your people justly, and to discern between good and evil: for who will be able to judge this your great people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it was pleasing before the Lord, that Solomon asked this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to him, Because you have asked this thing of me, and have not asked for yourself long life, and have not asked wealth, nor have asked the lives of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} behold, I have done according to your word: behold, I have given you an understanding and wise heart: there has not been [any one] like you before you, and after you there shall not arise one like you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I have given you what you have not asked, wealth and glory, so that there has not been any one like you among kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if you will walk in my way, to keep my commandments and my ordinances, as David your father walked, then will I multiply your days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Solomon awoke, and, behold, [it was] a dream: and he arose and came to Jerusalem, and stood before the altar that was in front of the ark of the covenant of the Lord in Sion: and he offered whole burnt offerings, and sacrificed peace-offerings, and made a great banquet for himself and all his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then there appeared two harlots before the king, and they stood before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the one woman said, Hear me, [my] lord; I and this woman lived in one house, and we were delivered in the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass on the third day after I was delivered, this woman also was delivered: and we [were] together; and there was no one with us besides our two selves in the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And this woman's child died in the night; because she overlaid it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and she arose in the middle of the night, and took my son from my arms, and laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and I arose in the morning to suckle my son, and he was dead: and, behold, I considered him in the morning, and, behold, it was not my son whom I bore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the other woman said, No, but the living [is] my son, and the dead [is] your son. So they spoke before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and the king said to them, You say, This [is] my son, [even] the living [one], and this woman's son [is] the dead one: and you say, No, but the living [is] my son, and the dead [is] your son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king said, Fetch a sword. And they brought a sword before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the king said, Divide the live child, the suckling, in two; and give half of it to one, and half of it to the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the woman whose the living child was, answered and said to the king, (for her bowels yearned over her son) and she said, I pray you, [my] lord, give her the child, and in nowise kill it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor hers; divide [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the king answered and said, Give the child to her that said, 'Give it to her, and by no means kill it:' she [is] its mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and all Israel heard this judgment which the king judged, and they feared before the king; because they saw that the wisdom of God [was] in him, to execute judgment.\par

The tabernacle was now at Gibeon ( ), which was therefore called the great high place; whither we find Solomon, without censure, repaired to sacrifice.; was no \textsuperscript{5} the Lord in a dream; , Ask what \textsuperscript{6} thy servant; great, ; mercy or, bounty, ; according, ; that \textsuperscript{7} thou hast, a little; to go \textsuperscript{9} Give therefore; understanding Heb. hearing, to judge; discern; *Gr: who is able \textsuperscript{11} hast not; long life Heb. many days discern Heb. hear, *marg. \textsuperscript{12} I have done; I have given, ; neither \textsuperscript{13} And I; riches; shall not be or, hath not been \textsuperscript{14} if thou; as thy, ; I will lengthen \textsuperscript{15} awoke; before; peace offerings; , a feast \textsuperscript{16} two women; harlots The word zanoth, rendered harlots, is here translated by the Targumist, the best judge in this case, pundekon, "tavern-keepers." See note on, and see note on . Had these women been harlots, it is not likely that they would have dared to appear before Solomon; nor is it likely that such persons would have been permitted in the reign of David. Their husbands might at this time have been following their necessary occupations in distant parts. stood \textsuperscript{25} Divide This was apparently a very strange decision; but Solomon saw that the only way to discover the real mother was by the affection and tenderness should would necessarily shew to her offspring. The plan was tried, and succeeded; and it was a proof of his sound judgment, penetration, and acquaintance with the human heart, or rather, of his extraordinary and supernatural wisdom. See note on . The two following instances are in some faint manner to be compared to Solomon's decision, inasmuch as they also work upon the human sympathies. Suetonius, in his Life of the emperor Claudian, tells us, that this emperor discovered a woman to be the real mother of a young man, whom she refused to acknowledge, by commanding her to marry him, the proofs being doubtful on both sides; for, rather than commit incest, she confessed the truth. Diodorus Siculus also informs us, that Ariopharnes, king of Thrace, being appointed to decided between three young men, each of whom professed to be the son of the deceased king of the Cimmerians, and claimed the succession, discovered the real son by ordering each to shoot an arrow into the dead body of the king. Two of them did this without hesitation; but the real son of the deceased monarch refused. \textsuperscript{26} her bowels; yearned Heb. were hot, give her \textsuperscript{28} feared; the wisdom; in him Heb. in the midst of him to do\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And king Solomon reigned over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And these [are] the princes which he had; Azarias son of Sadoc. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Eliaph, and Achia son of Seba, scribes; and Josaphat son of Achilud, recorder. came to supply for a month in the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And these [were] their names: Been the son of Or in the mount of Ephraim, one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The son of Dacar, in Makes, and in Salabin, and Baethsamys, and Elon as far as Bethanan, one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Bana son of Achiluth [had] Ithaanach, and Mageddo, and [his was] the whole house of San which was by Sesathan below Esrae, and from Bethsan as far as Sabelmaula, as far as Maeber Lucam, one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The son of Naber in Raboth Galaad, to him [fell] the lot of Ergab in Basan, sixty great cities with walls, and brazen bars, one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Achinadab son of Saddo, [had] Maanaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Achimaas [was] in Nephthalim, and he took Basemmath daughter of Solomon to wife, one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Baana son of Chusi, in Aser and in Baaloth, one, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Josaphat son of Phuasud [was] in Issachar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Semei son of Ela, in Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Gaber son of Adai in the land of Gad, [the land] of Seon king of Esebon, and of Og king of Basan, and one officer in the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And thus the officers provided king Solomon: and [they execute] every one in his month all the orders for the table of the king, they omit nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they carried the barley and the straw for the horses and the chariots to the place where the king might be, each according to his charge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And these [were] the requisite supplies for Solomon: in one day thirty measures of fine flour, and sixty measures of fine pounded meal, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and ten choice calves, and twenty pastured oxen, and one hundred sheep, besides stags, and choice fatted does. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For he had dominion on this side the river, and he was at peace on all sides round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the Lord gave understanding to Solomon, and very much wisdom, and enlargement of heart, as the sand on the seashore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Solomon abounded greatly beyond the wisdom of all the ancients, and beyond all the wise men of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he was wiser than all [other] men: and he was wiser than Gaethan the Zarite, and [than] Aenan, and [than] Chalcad and Darala the son of Mal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Solomon spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were five thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he spoke of trees, from the cedar in Libanus even to the hyssop which comes out through the wall: he spoke also of cattle, and of birds, and of reptiles, and of fishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And all the nations came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and [ambassadors] from all the kings of the earth, as many as heard of his wisdom. And Solomon took to himself the daughter of Pharao to wife, and brought her into the city of David until he had finished the house of the Lord, and his own house, and the wall of Jerusalem. Then went up Pharao the king of Egypt, and took Gazer, and burnt it and the Chananite dwelling in Mergab; and Pharao gave them as a dowry to his daughter the wife of Solomon: and Solomon rebuilt Gazer.\par

Niebuhr, Descrip. de l'Arab p. 146. \textsuperscript{24} Azzah; Gaza all the kings; had peace \textsuperscript{29} God, ; , largeness as the sand \textsuperscript{30} the children; the wisdom of Egypt \textsuperscript{31} wiser; Ethan; *title Heman, ; *title his fame \textsuperscript{33} the cedar tree The word airez, whence the Chaldee and Syriac arzo, and the Arabic and Ethiopic arz, and Spanish alerze, unquestionably denotes the cedar; it is thus rendered by the LXX and other versions, κεδρος, and by the Vulgate cedrus; and the inhabitants of mount Lebanon still call it ars . The cedar is a large and nobel evergreen tree, and grows on the most elevated part of the mountain, is taller than the pine, and so thick that five men together could scarcely fathom one. It shoots out its branches at ten or twelve feet from the ground; they are large and distant from each other, and are perpetually green. The wood is of a brown colour, very solid and incorruptible, if preserved from wet. The tree bears a small cone, like that of the pine.; the hyssop; of beasts\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 5}
\markright{KINGS III 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Chiram king of Tyre sent his servants to anoint Solomon in the room of David his father, because Chiram always loved David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Solomon sent to Chiram, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You knew my father David, that he could not build a house to the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that compassed him about, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And now the Lord my God has given me rest round about; there is no one plotting against [me], and there is no evil trespass [against me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And, behold, I intend to build a house to the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord God spoke to my father David, saying, Your son whom I will set on your throne in your place, he shall build a house to my name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now command, and let [men] cut wood for me out of Libanus: and, behold, my servants [shall be] with your servants, and I will give you the wages of your service, according to all that you shall say, because you know that we have no one skilled in cutting timber like the Sidonians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass, as soon as Chiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed [be] God today, who has given to David a wise son over this numerous people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he sent to Solomon, saying, I have listened concerning all that you have sent to me for: I will do all your will: [as for] timber of cedar and fir, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} my servants shall bring them down from Libanus to the sea: I will form them [into] rafts, [and bring them] to the place which you shall send to me [about]; and I will land them there, and you shall take [them] up: and you shall do my will, in giving bread to my household. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So Chiram gave to Solomon cedars, and fir trees, and all his desire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Solomon gave to Chiram twenty thousand measures of wheat as food for his house, and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil thus Solomon gave to Chiram yearly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon as he promised him; and there was peace between Chiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant between them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king raised a levy out of all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he sent them to Libanus, ten thousand taking turn every month: they were a month in Libanus and two months at home: and Adoniram [was] over the levy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Solomon had seventy thousand bearers of burdens, and eighty thousand hewers of stone in the mountain; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} besides the rulers that were appointed over the works of Solomon, [there were] three thousand six hundred masters who wrought in the works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [And the king commanded and they ] [brought great stones, precious stones for the foundation of the house, and unhewn stones. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they prepared the stones and the timber [during] three years.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2990, bc 1014, An, Ex, Is, 477 Hiram, ; Huram sent; for Hiram \textsuperscript{3} could not; the wars, put \textsuperscript{5} behold, purpose Heb. say as the Lord \textsuperscript{6} cedar trees, ; will I give hire; appoint Heb. say that there is not; Sidonians \textsuperscript{7} Blessed; which hath; a wise son \textsuperscript{8} considered Heb. heard timber of fir \textsuperscript{9} Lebanon and I will appoint Heb. send in giving food \textsuperscript{11} measures Heb. cors, *marg. twenty measures "Twenty thousand baths of oil" are mentioned in Chronicles; and the Syriac, Arabic, and Septuagint also have here "twenty thousand measures." But as barley and wine are also spoken of there, it is probable that the wheat mentioned here, and the small quantity of fine oil, were intended for the use of Hiram's own family, while that in Chronicles was for his workmen. \textsuperscript{12} as he promised him; they two \textsuperscript{13} levy Heb. tribute of men, the levy \textsuperscript{15} threescore These were all strangers, or proselytes, dwelling among the Israelites, as we learn from the paralled place in 2Chr. \textsuperscript{16} three thousand In the parallel passage of Chronicles, it is "three thousand six hundred, " which is also the reading of the Septuagint here.\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 6}
\markright{KINGS III 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the four hundred and fortieth year after the departure of the children of Israel out of Egypt, in the fourth year and second month of the reign of king Solomon over Israel, that the king commanded that they should take great [and] costly stones for the foundation of the house, and hewn stones. And the men of Solomon, and the men of Chiram hewed [the stones], and laid them [for a foundation]. In the fourth year he laid the foundation of the house of the Lord, in the month Ziu, even in the second month. In the eleventh year, in the month Baal, this [is] the eighth month, the house was completed according to all its plan, and according to all its arrangement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the house which the king built to the Lord [was] forty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and its height five and twenty cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the porch in front of the temple—twenty cubits [was] its length according to the breadth of the house in front of the house: and he built the house, and finished it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he made to the house secret windows inclining inward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And against the wall of the house he set chambers round about the temple and the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The under side [was] five cubits broad, and the middle [part] six, and the third [was] seven cubits broad; for he formed an interval to the house round about without the house, that they might not touch the walls of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the house was built in the construction of it with rough hewn stones: and there was not heard in the house in the building of it hammer or axe, or any iron tool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the porch of the under side [was] below the right wing of the house, and [there was] a winding ascent into the middle [chamber], and from the middle to the third story. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So he built the house and finished it; and he made the ceiling of the house with cedars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he made the partitions through all the house, each five cubits high, and enclosed each partition with cedar boards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he framed the walls of the house within with cedar boards, from the floor of the house and on to the inner walls and to the beams: he lined the parts enclosed with boards within, and compassed the inward parts of the house with planks of fir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he built the twenty cubits from the top of the wall, one side from the floor to the beams, and he made it from the oracle to the most holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the temple was forty cubits [in extent], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} in front of the oracle in the midst of the house within, [in order] to put there the ark of the covenant of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The length [was] twenty cubits, and the breadth [was] twenty cubits, and the height of it was twenty cubits. And he covered it with perfect gold, and he made an altar in front of the oracle, and covered it with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he covered the whole house with gold, till he had finished [gilding] the whole house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he made in the oracle two cherubs of ten cubits measured size. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the wing of one cherub was five cubits, and his other wing was five cubits; ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Thus it was with the other cherub, both were alike finished with one measure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the height of the one cherub [was] ten cubits, and so [was it] with the second cherub. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And both the cherubs [were] in the midst of the innermost part of the house; and they spread out their wings, and one wing touched the wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; and their wings in the midst of the house touched each other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he covered the cherubs with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} He graved all the walls of the house round about with the graving of cherubs, and [he sculptured] palm trees within and without [the house]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he covered the floor of the house within and without with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And for the door-way of the oracle he made doors of juniper wood, [there were] porches in a four-fold way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} In both the doors [were] planks of fir; the one door had two leaves and their hinges, and the other door had two leaves and turned [on hinges], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} being carved with cherubs, and [there were] palm-trees and open flower-leaves, and it [was] overlaid with gold gilt upon the engraving. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he built the inner court, three rows of hewn stones, and a row of wrought cedar round about, and he made the curtain of the court of the porch of the house that was in front of the temple.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2993, bc 1011, An, Ex, Is, 480 And it came; in the month Zif; began Heb. built, build \textsuperscript{2} the house Ezek. 40:1-41:26 the length According to Bp. Cumberland's estimation of the cubit, its length was 36 yds. 1 ft. 5/28 inch; its breadth 12 yds. 5/76 inch; and its height, 18 yds. 8/64 inch This constituted what is properly called the temple; but, besides this, there were the courts and colonnades, where the people might assemble to perform their devotions, without being exposed to the open air. threescore \textsuperscript{4} windows of narrow lights or, windows broad within, and narrow without; or, skewed and closed \textsuperscript{5} against or, upon, or joining to built, ; , chambers Heb. floors, These appear to have been what we should now call corridors or galleries; in which were apartments for the use of the priests. They consisted of three stories, and increased one cubit in breadth in every story, the wall of the temple being two cubits thicker at the bottom than at the top; and where the wall diminished, a rest was thus formed for the beams of the chambers to lodge upon. oracle, ; chambers Heb. ribs \textsuperscript{6} narrowed rests or, narrowings, or rebatements \textsuperscript{7} built of stone; neither hammer \textsuperscript{8} side Heb. shoulder went up \textsuperscript{9} he built, with beams and boards of cedar or, the vault beams and the ceilings with cedar \textsuperscript{15} he built That is, he lined or wainscoted the walls with cedar, the floor being covered with planks of fir. The marginal reading in this verse is preferable, as it removes every difficulty and obscurity. both the floor of the house, and the walls or, from the floor of the house, unto the walls, etc. and so \textsuperscript{16} built them, ; the oracle The oracle was the sanctuary, or holy of holies, in which there was nothing but the ark of the covenant, including the tables of the law, and into which the high priest alone was to enter but once a year. \textsuperscript{20} twenty cubits pure Heb. shut up the altar \textsuperscript{23} two cherubims These were distinct from, and much larger than those which covered the mercy-seat.; olive tree or, oily trees, Heb. trees of oil \textsuperscript{27} they stretched forth the wings of the cherubims or, the cherubims stretched forth their wings \textsuperscript{29} carved figures; palm trees Tamar, in Ethiopic, tamart, the palm tree, is so called, says Parkhurst, from its straight, upright growth, for which it seems more remarkable than any other tree; and it sometimes rises to the height of more than 100 feet. The trunk is remarkably straight and lofty; and it is crowned at the top with a large tuft of spiring leaves, about four feet long, which never fall off, but always continue in the same flourishing verdure. The stalks are generally full of rugged knots, which are vestiges of decayed leaves. For the trunk of the tree is not solid, but its centre is filled with pith, round which is a tough bark full of strong fibres when young, which, as the tree becomes old, hardens and becomes ligneous. To this bark the leaves are closely joined, which, as the tree becomes old, hardens and becomes ligneous. To this bark the leaves are closely joined, which in the centre rise erect, but after they are advanced above the vagina which surrounds them, they expand very wide on every side of the stem, and as the older leaves decay, the stalk advances in height. The leaves, when the tree has grown to a size for bearing fruit, are six or eight feet long, and very broad when expanded. The fruit, called the date, grows below the leaves in clusters.; open flowers Heb. openings of flowers \textsuperscript{31} doors; a fifth part or, five square \textsuperscript{34} fir tree the two leaves\par}
