\subsection*{Kings III 7}
\markright{KINGS III 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And king Solomon sent, and took Chiram out of Tyre, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} the son of a widow woman; and he [was] of the tribe of Nephthalim, and his father [was] a Tyrian; a worker in brass, and accomplished in are and skill and knowledge to work every work in brass: and he was brought in to king Solomon, and he wrought all the works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he cast the two pillars for the porch of the house: eighteen cubits [was] the height of [each] pillar, and a circumference of fourteen cubits encompassed it, even the thickness of the pillar: the flutings [were] four fingers [wide], and thus [was] the other pillar [formed]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he made two molten capitals to put on the heads of the pillars: five cubits [was] the height of one chapiter, and five cubits [was] the height of the other chapiter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he made two ornaments of network to cover the capitals of the pillars; even a net for one chapiter, and a net for the other chapiter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And hanging work, two rows of brazen pomegranates, formed with network, hanging work, row upon row: and thus he framed [the ornaments] for the second chapiter. And he set up the pillars of the porch of the temple: and he set up the one pillar, and called its name Jachum: and he set up the second pillar, and called its name Boloz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And on the heads of the pillars he made lily-work against the porch, of four cubits, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and a chamber over both the pillars, and above the sides an addition [equal to] the chamber in width. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he made the sea, ten cubits from one rim to the other, the same was completely circular round about: its height [was] five cubits, and its circumference thirty-three cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And stays underneath its rim round about compassed it ten cubits round; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And [there were] twelve oxen under the sea: three looking to the north, and three looking to the west, and three looking to the south, and three looking to the east: and all their hinder parts [were] inward, and the sea [was] above upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and its rim [was] as the work of the rim of a cup, a lily-flower, and the thickness of it [was] a span. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he made ten brazen bases: five cubits [was] the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth of it, and its height [was] six cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And this work of the bases [was] formed with a border the them, and [there was] a border between the ledges. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And upon their borders between the projection [were] lions, and oxen, and cherubs: and on the projections, even so above, and also below [were] the places of lions and oxen, hanging work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And [there were] four brazen wheels to one base; and [there were] brazen bases, and their four sides [answering to them], side pieces under the bases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And [there were] axles in the wheels under the base. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the height of one wheel [was] a cubit and a half. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the work of the wheels [was] as the work of chariot wheels: their axles, and their felloes, and [the rest of] their work, [were] all molten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The four side pieces were at the four corners of each base; its shoulders [were formed] of the base. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And on the top of the base half a cubit [was] the size of it, [there was] a circle on the top of the base, and [there was] the top of its spaces and its borders: and it was open at the top of its spaces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And its borders [were] cherubs, and lions, and palm-trees, upright, each [was] joined in front [and] within and round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} According to the same form he made all the ten bases, [even] one order and one measure to all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he made ten brazen lavers, each laver containing forty baths, [and] measuring four cubits, each laver [placed] on a several base throughout the ten bases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he put five bases on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and the sea was placed on the right side of the house eastward in the direction of the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Chiram made the caldrons, and the pans, and the bowls; and Chiram finished making all the works that he wrought for king Solomon in the house of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} two pillars and the wreathen works of the pillars on the heads of the two pillars; and the two networks to cover both the wreathen works of the flutings that were upon the pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} The four hundred pomegranates for both the networks, two rows of pomegranates for one network, to cover both the wreathen works of the bases belonging to both pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the ten bases, and the ten lavers upon the bases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And the caldrons, and pans, and bowls, and all the furniture, which Chiram made for king Solomon for the house of the Lord: and [there were] eight and forty pillars of the house of the king and of the house of the Lord: all the works of the king which Chiram made were entirely of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} There was no reckoning of the brass of which he made all these works, from the very great abundance, there was no end of the weight of the brass. In the country round about Jordan did he cast them, in the clay land between Socchoth and Sira. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And king Solomon took the furniture which [Chiram] made for the house of the Lord, the golden altar, and the golden table of show bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And [he put] the five candlesticks on the left, and five on the right in front of the oracle, [being] of pure gold, and the lamp-stands, and the lamps, and the snuffers of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And [there were made] the porches, and the nails, and the bowls, and the spoons, and the golden censers, of pure gold: and the panels of the doors of the innermost part of the house, [even] the holy of holies, and the golden doors of the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} So the work of the house of the Lord which Solomon wrought was finished; and Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father, and all the holy things of Solomon; he put the silver, and the gold, and the furniture, into the treasures of the house of the Lord. And Solomon built a house for himself in thirteen years. And he built the house with the wood of Libanus; its length [was] one hundred cubits, and its breadth [was] fifty cubits, and its height [was] of thirty cubits, and [it was made] with three rows of cedar pillars, and the pillars had side-pieces of cedar. And he formed the house with chambers above on the sides of the pillars, and the number of the pillars [was each] row forty and five, and [there were] three chambers, and space against space in three rows. And all the doors and spaces formed like chambers [were] square, and from door to door [was a correspondence] in three rows. And [he made] the porch of the pillars, [they were] fifty [cubits] long and fifty broad, the porch joining them in front; and the [other] pillars and the thick beam [were] in front of the house by the porches. And [there was] the Porch of seats where he would judge, the porch of judgment. And their house where he would dwell, [had] one court communicating with these according to this work; and [he built] the house for the daughter of Pharao whom Solomon had taken, according to this porch. All these [were] of costly stones, sculptured at intervals within even from the foundation even to the top, and outward to the great court, founded with large costly stones, stones of ten cubits and eight cubits [long]. And above with costly stones, according to the measure of hewn stones, and with cedars. [There were] three rows of hewn [stones] round about the great hall, and a row of sculptured cedar: and Solomon finished all his house.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{14} a widow's son Heb. the son of a widow woman tribe The mother of Hiram (not the Tyrian king mentioned before, but an intelligent coppersmith, of Jewish extraction by his mother's side) in Chronicles, is said to have been of "the daughters of Dan; " and she might have been of Naphtali by her father, and of Dan by her mother; or she might originally be of the tribe of Dan, and have been first married to a man of the tribe of Naphtali; and, in either case, she might be indifferently called "of the tribe of Naphtali, " or of "the daughters of Dan." Naphtali his father he was filled \textsuperscript{15} cast Heb. fashioned two pillars; eighteen cubits That is, nearly thirty feet, English measure. But in the parallel place in Chronicles, these pillars are said to thirty-five cubits high. Tremellius reconciles this difference by observing, that the common cubit was but one-half of the cubit of the sanctuary; so that eighteen of the one would make thirty-six of the other; from which, if we deduct one cubit for the base, there will remain thirty-five. Notwithstanding the names of these pillars, they seem to have supported no part of the building, and appear to have been formed for ornament; and were no doubt also emblematical. The right pillar was called Jachin, which signifies, "He will establish; " while that on the left was named Boaz, "In it is strength." Some think they were intended for memorials of the pillars and cloud of fire, which led Israel through the wilderness; but Henry supposes them designed for memorandums to the priests and others that came to worship at God's door. 1. To depend upon God only, and not upon any sufficiency of their own, for strength and establishment in all their religious exercises. 2. It was a memorandum to them of the strength and establishment of the temple of God among them. When the temple was destroyed, particular notice is taken of the breaking up and carrying away of these brazen pillars, which had been the tokens of its establishment, and would have been still so, if they had not forsaken God. \textsuperscript{23} he made, a molten sea; the one brim to the other Heb. his brim to his brim \textsuperscript{26} an hand breadth with flowers, it contained This immense laver, called a sea from it magnitude, held, at a moderate computation, 16, 000 gallons. Besides this great brazen laver, there were in the temple ten lavers of brass of a less size, which moved on wheels, and were ornamented with the figures of various animals, having, probably, always some relation to the cherubim. These lavers were to hold water for the use of the priests in their sacred office, particularly to wash the victims that were to be offered as a burnt offering, as we learn from; but the brazen sea was for the priests to wash in. The knops are supposed to have been in the form of an ox's head ( ); and some think the water flowed out at their mouths. two thousand \textsuperscript{27} ten bases These highly ornamental bases appear to have been square stands, or immense pedestals, for the purpose of supporting the lavers. \textsuperscript{28} bases was on It seems evident that these bases or pedestals rose with steps, and that the ornaments mentioned in the next verse appeared in front, forming so many entablatures. But the description of these bases is very difficult to comprehend: many of the original words are seldom, if at all, used elsewhere; and it would be impossible to give an explanation of each particular, without a labour and prolixity disproportioned to its importance to us. \textsuperscript{30} wheels, had undersetters It is probable that these undersetters were so many strong legs, somewhat shorter than the wheels, and were intended to prevent the laver from tilting, or falling, in case of any accident. \textsuperscript{32} joined to the base Heb. in the base \textsuperscript{36} graved cherubims, ;, proportion Heb. nakedness \textsuperscript{39} side Heb. shoulder he set \textsuperscript{40} Hiram Heb. Hirom, the lavers; the shovels the basins So Hiram \textsuperscript{42} the pillars Heb. the face of the pillars \textsuperscript{45} the pots; bright brass Heb. brass made bright, or scoured \textsuperscript{47} because they were exceeding many Heb. for the exceeding multitude, found out Heb. searched \textsuperscript{49} the candlesticks, ; before the oracle the tongs \textsuperscript{50} spoons; censers Heb. ash pans \textsuperscript{51} was ended; Solomon brought It appears, therefore, that Solomon did not use any of the gold and silver in the structure of the temple which his father had provided. things which David his father had dedicated Heb. holy things of David\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 8}
\markright{KINGS III 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord and his own house after twenty years, then king Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel in Sion, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, this is Sion, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} in the month of Athanin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the priests took up the ark, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and the tabernacle of testimony, and the holy furniture that was in the tabernacle of testimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king and all Israel [were occupied] before the ark, sacrificing sheep [and] oxen, without number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priests bring in the ark into its place, into the oracle of the house, even into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the cherubs spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubs covered the ark and its holy things above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the holy staves projected, and the ends of the holy staves appeared out of the holy places in front of the oracle, and were not seen without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} There was nothing in the ark except the two tables of stone, the tables of the covenant which Moses put [there] in Choreb, which [tables] the Lord made [as a covenant] with the children of Israel in their going forth from the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass when the priests departed out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the king turned his face, and the king blessed all Israel, (and the whole assembly of Israel stood:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and he said, Blessed [be] the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke by his mouth concerning David my father, and has fulfilled it with his hands, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} From the day that I brought out my people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city in [any] one tribe of Israel to build a house, so that my name should be there: but I chose Jerusalem that my name should be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it was in the heart of my father to build a house to the name of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord said to David my father, Forasmuch as it came into your heart to build a house to my name, you did well that it came upon your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Nevertheless you shall not build the house, but your son that has proceeded out of your bowels, he shall build the house to my name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord has confirmed the word that he spoke, and I am risen up in the place of my father David, and I have sat down on the throne of Israel, as the Lord spoke, and I have built the house to the name of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And I have set there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord, which the Lord made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Solomon stood up in front of the altar before all the congregation of Israel; and he spread out his hands toward heaven: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and he said, Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above and on the earth beneath, keeping covenant and mercy with your servant who walks before you with all his heart; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} which you have kept toward your servant David my father: for you have spoken by your mouth and you have fulfilled it with your hands, as [at] this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now, O Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father, [the promises] which you have spoken to him, saying, There shall not be taken from you a man sitting before me on the throne of Israel, provided only your children shall take heed to their ways, to walk before me as you have walked before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And now, O Lord God of Israel, let, I pray you, your word to David my father be confirmed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But will God indeed dwell with men upon the earth? if the heaven and heaven of heavens will not suffice you, how much less even this house which I have built to your name? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Yet, O Lord God of Israel, you shall look upon my petition, to hear the prayer which your servant prays to you in your presence this day, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, even toward the place which you said, My name shall be there, to hear the prayer which your servant prays at this place day and night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And you shall listen to the prayer of your servant, and of your people Israel, which they shall pray toward this place; and you shall hear in your dwelling-place in heaven, and you shall do and be gracious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Whatsoever trespasses any [one] shall commit against his neighbor,—and if he shall take upon him an oath so that he should swear, and he shall come and make confession before your altar in this house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} then shall you hear from heaven, and do, and you shall judge your people Israel, that the wicked should be condemned, to recompense his way upon his head; and to justify the righteous, to give to him according to his righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} When your people Israel falls before enemies, because they shall sin against you, and they shall return and confess to your name, and they shall pray and supplicate in this house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} then shall you hear from heaven, and be gracious to the sins of your people Israel, and you shall restore them to the land which you gave to their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} When the heaven is restrained, and there is no rain, because they shall sin against you, and the shall pray toward this place, and they shall make confession to your name, and shall turn from their sins when you shall have humbled them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} then you shall hear from heaven, and be merciful to the sins of your servant and of your people Israel; for you shall show them the good way to walk in it, and you shall give rain upon the earth which you have given to your people for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} If there should be famine, if there should be death, because there should be blasting, locust, or if there be mildew, and if their enemy oppress them in [any] one of their cities, [with regard to] every calamity, every trouble, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} every prayer, every supplication whatever shall be made by any man, as they shall know each the plague of his heart, and shall spread abroad his hands to this house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} then shall you listen from heaven, out of your established dwelling-place, and shall be merciful, and shall do, and recompense to [every] man according to his ways, as you shall know his heart, for you alone know the heart of all the children of men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} that they may fear you all the days that they live upon the land, which you have given to our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And for the stranger who is not of your people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} when they shall come and pray toward this place, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} then shall you hear [them] from heaven, out of your established dwelling-place, and you shall do according to all that the stranger shall call upon you for, that all the nations may know your name, and fear you, as [do] your people Israel, and may know that your name has been called on this house which I have builded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} [If it be] that your people shall go forth to war against their enemies in the way by which you shall turn them, and pray in the name of the Lord toward the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built to your name, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} then shall you hear from heaven their supplication and their prayer, and shall execute judgment for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} [If it be] that they shall sin against you, (for there is not a man who will not sin,) and you shall bring them and deliver them up before their enemies, and they that take [them] captive shall carry [them] to a land far or near, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} and they shall turn their hearts in the land whither they have been carried captives, and turn in the land of their sojourning, and supplicate you, saying, We have sinned, we have done unjustly, we have transgressed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} and they shall turn to you with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies whither you have carried them captives, and shall pray to you toward their land which you have given to their fathers, and the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built to your name: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} then shall you hear from heaven your established dwelling-place, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} and you shall be merciful to their unrighteousness wherein they have trespassed against you, and according to all their transgressions wherewith they have transgressed against you, and you shall cause them to be pitied before them that carried them captives, and they shall have compassion on them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} for [they are] your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, out of the midst of the furnace of iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And let your eyes and your ears be opened to the supplication of your servant, and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them in all things for which they shall call upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} Because you have set them apart for an inheritance to yourself out of all the nations of the earth, as you spoke by the hand of your servant Moses, when you brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, O Lord God.—Then spoke Solomon concerning the house, when he had finished building it—He manifested the sun in the heaven: the Lord said he would dwell in darkness: build you my house, a beautiful house for yourself to dwell in anew. Behold, is not this written in the book of the song? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And it came to pass when Solomon had finished praying to the Lord all this prayer and supplication, that he rose up from before the altar of the Lord, [after] having knelt upon his knees, and his hands [were] spread out towards heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Blessed [be] the Lord this day, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he said: there has not failed one word among all his good words which he spoke by the hand of his servant Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} May the Lord our God be with us, as he was with our fathers; let him not desert us nor turn from us, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} that he may turn our hearts toward him to walk in all his ways, and to keep all his commandments, and his ordinances which he commanded our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} And let these words, which I have prayed before the Lord our God, [be] near to the Lord our God day and night, to maintain the cause of your servant, and the cause of your people Israel for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} that all the nations of the earth may know that the Lord God, he [is] God, and there is none beside. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And let our hearts be perfect toward the Lord our God, to walk also holily in his ordinances, and to keep his commandments, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And the king and all the children of Israel offered sacrifice before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} And king Solomon offered for the sacrifices of peace-offering which he sacrificed to the Lord, two and twenty thousand oxen, one hundred and twenty thousand sheep: and the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} In that day the king consecrated the middle of the court in the front of the house of the Lord; for there he offered the whole burnt offering, and the sacrifices, and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the brazen altar which was before the Lord [was too] little to bear the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices of peace-offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} And Solomon kept the feast in that day, and all Israel with him, even a great assembly from the entering in of Hemath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God in the house which he built, eating and drinking, and rejoicing before the Lord our God seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} And on the eighth day he sent away the people: and they blessed the king, and each departed to his tabernacle rejoicing, and [their] heart [was] glad because of the good things which the Lord had done to his servant David, and to Israel his people.\par

\subsection*{Kings III 9}
\markright{KINGS III 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the work of Solomon, whatever he wished to perform, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he appeared in Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord said to him, I have heard the voice of your prayer, and your supplication which you made before me: I have done for you according to all your prayer: I have hallowed this house which you have built to put my name there for ever, and my eyes and my heart shall be there always. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if you will walk before me as David your father walked, in holiness of heart and uprightness, and so as to do according to all that I commanded him, and shall keep my ordinances and my commandments: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} then will I establish the throne of your kingdom in Israel for ever, as I spoke to David your father, saying, There shall not fail you a man to rule in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But if you⌃ or your children do in any wise revolt from me, and do not keep my commandments and my ordinances, which Moses set before you, and you⌃ go and serve other gods, and worship them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} then will I cut off Israel from the land which I have given them, and this house which I have consecrated to my name I will cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a desolation and a byword to all nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And this house, which is high, shall be [so that] every one that passes by it shall be amazed, and shall hiss; and they shall say, Therefore has the Lord done thus to this land, and to this house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And [men] shall say, Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought out their fathers from Egypt, out of the house of bondage, and they attached themselves to strange gods, and worshipped them, and served them: therefore the Lord has brought this evil upon them. Then Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharao out of the city of David into his house which he built for himself in those days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [During] twenty years in which Solomon was building the two houses, the house of the Lord, and the house of the king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Chiram king of Tyre helped Solomon with cedar wood, and fir wood, and with gold, and all that he wished for: then the king gave Chiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So Chiram departed from Tyre, and went into Galilee to see the cities which Solomon gave to him; and they pleased him not. And he said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} What [are] these cities which you have given me, brother? And he called them Boundary until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Chiram brought to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} even that for which king Solomon built a ship in Gasion Gaber near Aelath on the shore of the extremity of the sea in the land of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Chiram sent in the ship together with the servants of Solomon servants of his own, mariners to row, men acquainted with the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they came to Sophira, and took thence one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and brought them to king Solomon.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3013, bc 991 it came, ; the house; all Solomon's \textsuperscript{3} I have heard; I have hallowed; to put;, mine eyes \textsuperscript{4} And if thou, ; in integrity \textsuperscript{7} will I cut; this house; , ; and Israel \textsuperscript{10} at the end of twenty \textsuperscript{11} Now Hiram; king Solomon of Galilee \textsuperscript{12} they pleased him not Heb. were not right in his eyes; *marg. \textsuperscript{13} my brother; Cabul that is, Displeasing, or dirty. Josephus says that Cabul, in the Phoenician language, signifies ουκ αρεσκον, displeasing; and that these cities were situated in the neighbourhood of Tyre. Most commentators are persuaded that the city Cabul in the tribe of Asher was one; and probably from this Hiram took occasion to give this name to all the other cities which Solomon had ceded to him. \textsuperscript{26} made a navy, 18-11:4 Eziongeber; Eloth shore Heb. lip\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 10}
\markright{KINGS III 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the queen of Saba heard of the name of Solomon, and the name of the Lord, and she came to try him with riddles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train; and [there came] camels bearing spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and she came in to Solomon, and told him all that was in her heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Solomon answered all her questions: and there was not a question overlooked by the king which he did not answer her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the queen of Saba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he built, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and the provision of Solomon and the sitting of his attendants, and the standing of his servants, and his raiment, and his cupbearers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the house of the Lord, and she was utterly amazed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And she said to king Solomon, [It was] a true report which I heard in my land of your words and your wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But I believed not them that told me, until I came and my eyes saw: and, behold, the words as they reported to me are not the half: you have exceeded in goodness all the report which I heard in my land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Blessed [are] your wives, blessed [are] these your servants who stand before you continually, who hear all your wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Blessed be the Lord your God, who has taken pleasure in you, to set you upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord loved Israel to establish [him] for ever; and he has made you king over them, to execute judgment with justice, and in their causes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And she gave to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones: there had not come any other spices so abundant as those which the queen of Saba gave to king Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the ship of Chiram which brought the gold from Suphir, brought very much hewn timber and precious stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king made the hewn timber [into] buttresses of the house of the Lord and the king's house, and lyres and harps for singers: such hewn timber had not come upon the earth, nor have been seen anywhere until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And king Solomon gave to the queen of Saba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides all that he had given her by the hand of king Solomon: and she returned, and came into her own land, she and her servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Besides the tributes of them that were subjects, both merchants and all the kings of the [country] beyond [the river], and of the princes of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Solomon made three hundred spears of beaten gold: three hundred shekels of gold were upon one spear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And three hundred shields of beaten gold: and three pounds of gold were in one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king made a great ivory throne, and gilded it with pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The throne [had] six steps, and calves in bold relief to the throne behind it, and side-pieces on either hand of the place of the seat, and two lions standing by the side-pieces, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and twelve lions standing there on the six steps on either side: it was not so done in any [other] kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all the vessels made by Solomon [were] of gold, and the lavers [were] golden, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; there was no silver, for it was not accounted of in the days of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For Solomon had a ship of Tharsis in the sea with the ships of Chiram: one ship came to the king every three years out of Tharsis, [laden with] gold and silver, and wrought stones, and hewn stones. This was the arrangement of the provision which king Solomon fetched to build the house of the Lord, and the house of the king, and the wall of Jerusalem, and the citadel; to fortify the city of David, and Assur, and Magdal, and Gazer, and Baethoron the upper, and Jethermath, and all the cities of the chariots, and all the cities of the horsemen, and the fortification of Solomon which he purposed to build in Jerusalem and in all the land, so that none of the people should rule over him that was left of the Chettite and the Amorite, and the Pherezite, and the Chananite, and the Evite, and the Jebusite, and the Gergesite, who were not of the children of Israel, their descendants who had been left with him in the land, whom the children of Israel could not utterly destroy; and Solomon made them tributaries until this day. But of the children of Israel Solomon made nothing; for they were the warriors, and his servants and rulers, and captains of the third order, and the captains of his chariots, and his horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Solomon increased beyond all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom which the Lord [had] put into his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they brought every one their gifts, vessels of gold, and raiment, and stacte, and spices, and horses, and mules, a rate year by year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Solomon had four thousand mares for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen: and he put them in the cities of his chariots, and with the king in Jerusalem: and he ruled over all the kings from the river to the land of the Philistines, and to the borders of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars as the sycamores in the plain for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the goings forth of Solomon's horsemen [was] also out of Egypt, and the king's merchants [were] of Thecue; and they received them out of Thecue at a price. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And that which proceeded out of Egypt went up [thus, even] a chariot for one hundred [shekels] of silver, and a horse for fifty [shekels] of silver: and thus for all the kings of the Chettians, and the kings of Syria, they came out by sea.\par

\subsection*{Kings III 11}
\markright{KINGS III 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And king Solomon was a lover of women. And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines. And he took strange women, as well as the daughter of Pharao, Moabitish, Ammanitish women, Syrians and Idumeans, Chettites, and Amorites; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} of the nations concerning whom the Lord forbade the children of Israel, [saying], You⌃ shall not go in to them, and they shall not come in to you, lest they turn away your hearts after their idols: Solomon clave to these in love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass in the time of the old age of Solomon, that his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as [was] the heart of David his father. And the strange women turned away his heart after their gods. Then Solomon built a high place to Chamos the idol of Moab, and to their king the idol of the children of Ammon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and to Astarte the abomination of the Sidonians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And thus he acted towards all his strange wives, who burnt incense and sacrificed to their idols. And Solomon did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he went not after the Lord, as David his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because he turned away his heart from the Lord God of Israel, who had appeared twice to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and charged him concerning this matter, by no means to go after other gods, but to take heed to do what the Lord God commanded him; neither was his heart perfect with the Lord, according to the heart of David his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord said to Solomon, Because it has been thus with you, and you have not kept my commandments and my ordinances which I commanded you, I will surely rend your kingdom out of your hand, and give it to your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Only in your days I will not do it for David your father's sake: [but] I will take it out of the hand of your son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Only I will not take away the whole kingdom: I will give one tribe to your son for David my servant's sake, and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord raised up an enemy to Solomon, Ader the Idumaean, and Esrom son of Eliadae who [lived] in Raama, [and] Adadezer king of Suba his master; (and men gathered to him, and he was head of the conspiracy, and he seized on Damasec,) and they were adversaries to Israel all the days of Solomon: and Ader the Idumaean [was] of the seed royal in Idumaea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it happened, that while David was utterly destroying Edom, while Joab captain of the host was going to bury the dead, when they killed every male in Idumaea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} (for Joab and all Israel abode there six months in Idumaea, until he utterly destroyed every male in Idumaea;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} that Ader ran away, he and all the Idumaeans of the servants of his father with him; and they went into Egypt; and Ader [was then] a little child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there rise up men out of the city of Madiam, and they come to Pharan, and take men with them, and come to Pharao king of Egypt: and Ader went in to Pharao, and he gave him a house, and appointed him provision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Ader found great favor in the sight of Pharao, and he gave him his wife's sister in marriage, the elder sister of Thekemina. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the sister of Thekemina bore to him, [even] to Ader, Ganebath her son; and Thekemina brought him up in the midst of the sons of Pharao, and Ganebath was in the midst of the sons of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ader heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead; and Ader said to Pharao, Let me go, and I will return to my country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Pharao said to Ader, What lack you with me? that behold! you seek to depart to your country? and Ader said to him, By all means let me go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So Ader returned to his country; this [is] the mischief which Ader did, and he was a bitter enemy of Israel, and he reigned in the land of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Jeroboam the son of Nabat, the Ephrathite of Sarira, the son of a widow, [was] servant of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And this [was] the occasion of his lifting up [his] hands against king Solomon: now king Solomon built the citadel, he completed the fortification of the city of David his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the man Jeroboam was very strong; and Solomon saw the young man that he was active, and he set him over the levies of the house of Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it came to pass at that time, that Jeroboam went forth from Jerusalem, and Achia the Selonite the prophet found him in the way, and caused him to turn aside out of the way: and Achia was clad with a new garment, and they two [were] alone in the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Achia laid hold of his new garment that was upon him, and tore it [into] twelve pieces: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and he said to Jeroboam, Take to yourself ten pieces, for thus says the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give you ten tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Yet he shall have two tribes, for my servant David's sake, and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Because he forsook me, and sacrificed to Astarte the abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chamos, and to the idols of Moab, and to their king the abomination of the children of Ammon, and he walked not in my ways, to do that which was right before me, as David his father [did]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Howbeit I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, (for I will certainly resist him all the days of his life,) for David my servant's sake, whom I have chosen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} But I will take the kingdom out of the hand of his son, and give you ten tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But to his son I will give the two [remaining] tribes, that my servant David may have an establishment continually before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for myself to put my name there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And I will take you, and you shall reign as your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And it shall come to pass, if you will keep all the commandments that I shall give you, and will walk in my ways, and do that which is right before me, to keep my ordinances and my commandments, as David my servant did, that I will be with you, and will build you a sure house, as I built to David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam: but he arose and fled into Egypt, to Susakim king of Egypt, and he was in Egypt until Solomon died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And the rest of the history of Solomon, and all that he did, and all his wisdom, behold are not these things written in the book of the life of Solomon? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the days [during] which Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel [were] forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And Solomon slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David his father. And it came to pass when Jeroboam son of Nabat heard [of it], even while he was yet in Egypt as he fled from the face of Solomon and lived in Egypt, he straightway comes into his own city, into the land of Sarira in the mount of Ephraim. And king Solomon slept with his fathers, and Roboam his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3020-3029, bc 984-975 loved; , ; together with or, beside \textsuperscript{2} Ye shall not go in; surely; Solomon \textsuperscript{4} when Solomon, his wives; his heart \textsuperscript{6} went not fully after Heb. fulfilled not after; *Heb: \textsuperscript{9} angry; his heart; which had appeared \textsuperscript{11} is done of thee Heb. is with thee thou hast not I will surely \textsuperscript{12} in thy days;, for David; I will rend it out \textsuperscript{13} Howbeit; one tribe, for David; for Jerusalem's \textsuperscript{15} when David; *title after he had; every male \textsuperscript{17} Hadad; a little child Naar katon, rather, "a little boy:" one who was apprehensive of his danger, and could, with his father's servants, make his escape. \textsuperscript{18} Midian Probably not the Midian east of the Red Sea, to which Moses fled (, etc.) but the Midian east of the Dead Sea, and south of Moab. These Midianites, whose daughters seduced the Israelites to commit idolatry (; etc.) were descendants of Midian, son of Abraham ( ). Their capital city was called Midian, and its remains were to be seen in the time of Eusebius and Jerome. It was situated on the Arnon, south of the city Ar, or Areopolis.;, Paran Probably the city of Paran, or the district around it, situated in the south of Idumea, and according to Eusebius, three days' journey east from Elah or Elath, at the head of the eastern branch, or Elamitic gulf of the Red Sea. \textsuperscript{19} found; that he gave Tahpenes \textsuperscript{21} Hadad; Let me depart Heb. Send me away \textsuperscript{22} But; Nothing Heb. Not let me go \textsuperscript{26} Jeroboam, an Ephrathite; Solomon's servant \textsuperscript{27} lifted up; Solomon, repaired Heb. closed, the breaches; the city \textsuperscript{28} was industrious Heb. did work, he made charge Heb. burden; the house \textsuperscript{29} Ahijah; Shilonite and they two \textsuperscript{32} he shall for Jerusalem's sake \textsuperscript{35} I will take will give \textsuperscript{36} David; light Heb. lamp, or candle the city \textsuperscript{38} if thou wilt, ; that I will; build the \textsuperscript{40} Solomon sought; Shishak This is the first time we meet with the proper name of an Egyptian king in Scripture, Pharaoh being the general appellation for all the sovereigns of that country. Some are of opinion that Shishak is the same with the celebrated Sesostris of the Greek historians; but it is probable that this king lived long before Solomon's time. Usher thinks him to be Sesonchis, and places the beginning of his reign, am 3026, bc 978. \textsuperscript{41} rest acts or, words, or things \textsuperscript{42} time Heb. days forty years Josephus says fourscore years; which is sufficiently absurd. Calmet supposes him to have been 18 years old when he came to the throne, and 58 when he died. \textsuperscript{43} am 3029, bc 975 slept, ;, buried; Rehoboam; Roboam\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 12}
\markright{KINGS III 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And king Roboam goes to Sikima; for all Israel were coming to Sikima to make him king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people spoke to king Roboam, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} but do you now lighten somewhat of the hard service of your father, and of his heavy yoke which he put upon us, and we will serve you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to them, Depart for three days, and return to me. And they departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the king referred [the matter] to the elders, who stood before Solomon his father while he was yet living, saying, How do you⌃ advise that I should answer this people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they spoke to him, saying, If you will this day be a servant to this people, and will serve them, and will speak to them good words, then will they be your servants continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But he forsook the counsel of the old men which they gave him, and consulted with the young men who were brought up with him, who stood in his presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to them, What counsel do you⌃ give? And what shall I answer to this people who speak to me, saying, Lighten somewhat of the yoke which your father has put upon us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the young men who had been brought up with him, who stood before his face, spoke to him, saying, Thus shall you say to this people who have spoken to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy, and do you now lighten it from off us: thus shall say to them, My little [finger shall be] thicker than my father's loins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I also will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all Israel came to king Roboam on the third day, as the king spoke to them, saying, Return to me on the third day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king answered the people harshly; and Roboam forsook the counsel of the old men which they counselled him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king listened not to the people, because the change was from the Lord, that he might establish his word which he spoke by Achia the Selonite concerning Jeroboam the son of Nabat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them: and the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we any inheritance in the son of Jessae. Depart, O Israel, to your tents: now feed your own house, David. So Israel departed to his tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king sent Adoniram who was over the tribute; and they stoned him with stones, and he died: and king Roboam made haste to rise to flee to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} So Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned out of Egypt, that they sent and called him to the assembly, and they made him king over Israel: and none followed the house of David except the tribe of Juda and Benjamin only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Roboam went into Jerusalem, and he assembled the congregation of Juda, and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred and twenty thousand young men, warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to recover the kingdom to Roboam the son of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the word of the Lord came to Samaia the man of God, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Speak to Roboam the son of Solomon, king of Juda, and to all the house of Juda and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Thus says the Lord, You⌃ shall not go up, neither shall you⌃ fight with your brethren the sons of Israel: return each man to his own home; for this thing is from me; and they listened to the word of the Lord, and they ceased from going up, according to the word of the Lord. So king Solomon sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Roboam his son reigned in his stead in Jerusalem, being sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twelve years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Naanan, daughter of Ana son of Naas king of the children of Ammon. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked not in the way of David his father. And there was a man of mount Ephraim, a servant to Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam: and the name of his mother was Sarira, a harlot: and Solomon made him head of the levies of the house of Joseph: and he built for Solomon Sarira in mount Ephraim; and he had three hundred chariots of horses: he built the citadel with the levies of the house of Ephraim; he fortified the city of David, and aspired to the kingdom, And Solomon sought to kill him; and he was afraid, and escaped to Susakim king of Egypt, and was with him until Solomon died. And Jeroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon was dead: and he spoke in the ears of Susakim king of Egypt, saying, Let me go, and I will depart into my land: and Susakim said to him, Ask and request, and I will grant it you. And Susakim gave to Jeroboam Ano the oldest sister of Thekemina his wife: she was great among the daughters of the king, and she bore to Jerobaom Abia his son: and Jeroboam said to Susakim, Let me indeed go, and I will depart. And Jeroboam departed out of Egypt, and came into the land of Saria that was in mount Ephraim, and there the whole in mount Ephraim, and there the whole tribe of Ephraim assembles, and Jeroboam built a fortress there. And his young child was sick with a very severe sickness; and Jeroboam went to enquire concerning the child: and he said to Ano his wife, Arise, go, enquire of God concerning the child, whether he shall recover from his sickness. Now there was a man in Selom, an his name [was] Achia: and he was sixty years old, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise, and take in your hand loaves for the man of God, and cakes for his children, and grapes, and a pot of honey. And the woman arose, and took in her hand bread, and two cakes, and grapes, and a pot of honey, for Achia: and the man [was] old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see. And she arose, up from Sarira and went; and it came to pass when she had come into the city to Achia the Selonite, that Achia said to his servant, Go out now to meet Ano the wife of Jeroboam, and you shall say to her, Come in, and stand not [still]: for thus says the Lord, I send grievous tidings to you. And Ano went in to the man of God; and Achia said to her, Why have you brought me bread and grapes, and cakes, and a pot of honey? Thus says the Lord, Behold, you shall depart from me, and it shall come to pass when you have entered into the city, [even] into Sarira, that your maidens shall come out to meet you, and shall say to you, The child is dead: for thus says the Lord, Behold, I will destroy every male of Jeroboam, and there shall be the dead of Jeroboam in the city, [them] the dogs shall eat, and him that eat, and he shall lament for the child, saying, [Woe is me], Lord! For there has been found in him some good thing touching the Lord. And the woman departed, when she heard this: and it came to pass as she entered into Sarira, that the child died; and there came forth a wailing to meet [her]. And Jeroboam went to Sikima in mount Ephraim, and assembled there the tribes of Israel; and Roboam the son of Solomon went up there. And the word of the Lord came to Samaias son of Enlami, saying, Take to yourself a new garment which has not gone into the water, and rend it into twelve pieces; and you shall five some to Jeroboam, and shall say to him, thus says the Lord, Take to yourself ten pieces to cover you: and Jeroboam took [them]: and Samaias said, Thus says the Lord concerning the ten tribes of Israel. And the people said to Roboam the son of Solomon, Your father make his yoke heavy upon us, and made the meat of his table heavy; and now you shall lighten them upon us, and we will serve you. And Roboam said to the people, Wait three days, and I will return you an answer: and Roboam said, Bring in to me the elders, and I will take counsel with them what I shall answer to the people on the third day, So Roboam spoke in their ears, as the people sent to him to [say]: and the elders of the people said, Thus the people have spoken to you. And Roboam rejected their counsel, and it pleased him not: and he sent and brought in those who had been brought up with him; and he said to them, Thus and thus has the people sent to me to say: and they that had been brought up with him said, Thus shall you speak to the people saying, My little [finger] shall be thicker than my father's loins; my father scourged you with whips, but I will rule you with scorpions. And the saying pleased Roboam, and he answered the people as the young men, they that were brought up with him, counselled him: and all the people spoke as one man, every one to his neighbor, and they cried out all together, saying, We have no part in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jessae: to they tents, O Israel, every one; for this man is not for a prince or a ruler over us. And all the people was dispersed from Sikima, and they departed every one to his tent: and Roboam strengthened him self and departed, and mounted his chariot, and entered into Jerusalem: and there follow him the whole tribe of Juda, and the whole tribe of Benjamin. And it came to pass at the beginning of the year, that Roboam gathered all the men of Juda and Benjamin, and went up to fight with Jeroboam at Sikima. And the word of the Lord came to Sameas the man of God, saying, Speak to Roboam king of Juda, and to all the house of Juda and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying, Thus says the Lord, You⌃ shall not go up, neither shall you⌃ fight with your brethren the sons of Israel: return every man to his house, for this thing is from me. And they listened to the word of the Lord, and forbore to go up, according to the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Jeroboam built Sikima in mount Ephraim and lived in it, and went forth thence and built Phanuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Jeroboam said in his heart, Behold, now the kingdom will return to the house of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} If this people shall go up to offer sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then the heart of the people will return to the Lord, and to their master, to Roboam king of Juda, and they will kill me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the king took counsel, and went, and made two golden heifers, and said to the people, Let it suffice you to have gone [hitherto] to Jerusalem: behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he put one in Bethel, and he put the other in Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And this thing became a sin; and the people went before one as far as Dan, and left the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he made houses on the high places, and made priests of any part of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jeroboam appointed a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, according to the feast in the land of Juda; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} and went up to the altar which he made in Baethel to sacrifice to the heifers which he made, and he placed in Baethel the priests of the high places which he had made. And he went up to the altar which he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast which he devised out of his own heart; and he made a feast to the children of Israel, and went up to the altar to sacrifice.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{7} If thou wilt; speak good \textsuperscript{10} Thus shalt thou My little finger A proverbial mode of expression: "My little finger is thicker than my father's thigh." As much as the thigh surpasses the little finger in thickness, so much does my power exceed that of my father; and the use I shall make of it to oppress and tax you shall be in proportion. \textsuperscript{11} I will add, ; but I will chastise Should you rebel or become disaffected, my father's whip shall be a scorpion in my hand. His was chastisement, mine shall be punishment. Celsius and Hiller conjecture that âkrabbim denotes a thorny kind of shrub, whose prickles are of a venomous nature, called by the Arabs scorpion thorns, from the exquisite pain which they inflict. But the Chaldee renders it margenin, and the Syriac moragyai, i.e., μαραγναι, scourges; and in the parallel place of Chronicles the Arabic has saut, a scourge. Isidore, and after him Calmet and others, assert that the scorpion was a sort of severe whip, the lashes of which were armed with knots or points that sunk into and tore the flesh. scorpions \textsuperscript{13} answered; , ; roughly Heb. hardly, forsook \textsuperscript{14} the counsel; My father made \textsuperscript{15} the cause The cause of all this confusion and anarchy was Rehoboam's folly, cruelty, and despotic tyranny, and this was certainly not "from the Lord, " nor does the original text speak this doctrine. For an elucidation of a similar passage, see note on . It says, sibbah, (from savav, to turn, change), "the change or Revolution was from the Lord; " which is consistent with all the preceding declarations. God stirred up the people to revolt from a man who had neither skill nor humanity to govern them. God serves his own wise and righteous purpose by the imprudences and iniquities of men, and snares sinners in the work of their own hands. "He maketh the wrath of man to praise him."; , ; that he might \textsuperscript{16} What portion; to your tents, now see, ;, ; So Israel \textsuperscript{18} Adoram, Adoniram; Hadoram all Israel; made speed Heb. strengthened himself flee to Jerusalem \textsuperscript{19} Israel; rebelled or, fell away, unto this day \textsuperscript{20} and made him; none that followed \textsuperscript{24} Ye shall not go up;, for this thing; They hearkened \textsuperscript{26} said in his heart; Now shall \textsuperscript{27} go up, ;, and they shall \textsuperscript{28} took counsel; two calves of gold He invented a political religion, and instituted feasts in his own times, different from those appointed by Jehovah; gave the people certain objects of adoration, and pretended to think that it would be both inconvenient and oppressive to them to go up to Jerusalem to worship. These calves were doubtless of the same kind as the calf which was set up by Aaron; and it is remarkable, that in pointing them out to the people he should use the same words that Aaron used on that occasion, when they must have heard what terrible judgments fell upon their forefathers for this idolatry. Solomon's idolatry, however, had prepared the people for Jeroboam's abominations.; It is too much; behold \textsuperscript{32} like unto; offered upon the altar or, went up to the altar, sacrificing. or, to sacrifice. he placed. \textsuperscript{33} offered upon the altar or, went up to the altar, etc. in the month; he offered; and burnt incense Heb. to burn incense\par}
