\subsection*{Kings III 13}
\markright{KINGS III 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And behold, there came a man of God out of Juda by the word of the Lord to Baethel, and Jeroboam stood at the altar to sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he cried against the altar by the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus says the Lord, Behold, a son is [to be] born to the house of David, Josias by name; and he shall offer upon you the priests of the high places, [even] of them that sacrifice upon you, and [he] shall burn men's bones upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And in that day one shall give a sign, saying, This [is] the word which the Lord has spoken, saying, Behold, the altar is torn, and the fatness upon it shall be poured out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass when king Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who called on the altar that was in Baethel, that the king stretched forth his hand from the altar, saying, Take hold of him. And, behold, his hand, which he stretched forth against him, withered, and he could not draw it back to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the altar was torn, and the fatness was poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God gave by the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And king Jeroboam said to the man of God, Intreat the Lord your God, and let my hand be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the Lord, and he restored the king's hand to him, and it became as before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the king said to the man of God, Enter with me into the house, and dine, and I will give you a gift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the man of God said to the king, If you should give me the half of your house, I would not go in with you, neither will I eat bread, neither will I drink water in this place; for thus the Lord charged me by [his] word, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Eat no bread, and drink no water, and return not by the way by which you came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So he departed by another way, and returned not by the way by which he came to Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And there lived an old prophet in Baethel; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God did on that day in Baethel, and the words which he spoke to the king: and they turned the face of their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And their father spoke to them, saying, Which way went he? and his sons show him the way by which the man of God who came out of Juda went up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to his sons, Saddle me the ass: and they saddled him the ass, and he mounted it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said to him, Are you the man of God that came out of Juda? And he said to him, I [am]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to him, Come with me, and eat bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said, I shall not by any means be able to return with you, neither will I eat bread, neither will I drink water in this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For thus the Lord commanded me by word, saying, Eat not bread there, and drink not water, and return not there by the way by which you came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to him, I also am a prophet as you [are]; and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back to you into your house, and let him eat bread and drink water: but he lied to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he brought him back, and he ate bread and drank water in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass while they were sitting at the table, that the word of the Lord came to the prophet that brought him back; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and he spoke to the man of God that came out of Juda, saying, Thus says the Lord, Because you have resisted the word of the Lord, and have not kept the commandment which the Lord your God commanded you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} but have returned, and eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which he spoke to you, saying, You shall not eat bread, and shall not drink water; [therefore] your body shall in nowise enter into the sepulchre of your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass after he had eaten bread and drunk water, that he saddled the ass for him, and he turned and departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And a lion found him in the way, and killed him; and his body was cast out in the way, and the ass was standing by it, and the lion [also] was standing by the body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And, behold, men [were] passing by, and saw the carcass cast in the way, and the lion was standing near the carcass: and they went in and spoke [of it] in the city where the old prophet lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And [the prophet] that turned him back out of the way heard, and said, This is the man of God who rebelled against the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} [And he spoke to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass, and they saddled it. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he went and found the body cast in the way, and the ass and the lion were standing by the body: and the lion had not devoured the body of the man of God, and had not torn the ass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the prophet took up the body of the man of God, and laid it on his ass; and the prophet brought him back to his city, to bury him in his own tomb, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and they bewailed him, [saying], Alas, brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it came to pass after he had lamented him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, Whenever I die, bury me in this tomb wherein the man of God is buried; lay me by his bones, that my bones may be preserved with his bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For the word will surely come to pass which he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Baethel, and against the high houses in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And after this Jeroboam turned not from his sin, but he turned and made of part of the people priests of the [high places]: whoever would, he consecrated him, and he became a priest for the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And this thing became sin to the house of Jeroboam, even to its destruction and its removal from the face of the earth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} there came; by the word, ; Jeroboam; burn or, offer \textsuperscript{2} O altar; Josiah by name; offer \textsuperscript{6} now, ; besought; Lord Heb. face of the Lord \textsuperscript{7} refresh; I will give As great men in the East make no presents to equals or inferiors when visited, Sir John Chardin thinks that the king intended by this to treat the prophet as his superior. \textsuperscript{11} an old prophet; sons Heb. son came \textsuperscript{17} It was Heb. a word was by the word \textsuperscript{20} the word of the Lord "A great clamour, " says Dr. Kennicott, "has been raised against this part of history, on account of God's denouncing sentence on the true prophet by the mouth of the false prophet; but if we examine with attention the original words here, they will be found to signify either he who brought him back, or, whom he had brought back; for the very same words, asher heshivo, occur again, where they are now translated, whom he had brought back; and where they cannot be translated otherwise. This being the case, we are at liberty to consider the words of the Lord as delivered to the true prophet, thus brought back; and then the sentence is pronounced by God himself, calling to him out of heaven, as in . And that this doom was thus pronounced by God, not by the false prophet, we are assured in . 'The Lord hath delivered him unto the lion, according to the word of the Lord, which He spake unto him.' Josephus (and also the Arabic) asserts, that the sentence was declared by God to the true prophet." \textsuperscript{21} Thus saith; thou hast disobeyed \textsuperscript{26} the man; torn Heb. broken which he spake \textsuperscript{28} the lion had All here was supernatural. The lion, though he had killed the man, yet, contrary to his nature, did not devour him, nor tear the ass, nor meddle with the travellers that passed by; while the ass stood quietly by, not fearing the lion, nor betaking himself to flight. Both stood as guardians of the fallen prophet, till this extraordinary intelligence was carried into the city which rendered the miracle the more illustrious and plainly shewed that this event did not happen by chance. This concatenation of miracles marked the death of the man of God as a Divine rebuke for his disobedience in eating bread at idolatrous Beth-el; and here we see, as in various other cases, that "often judgment begins at the house of God." The true prophet, for suffering himself to be seduced by the old prophet, and for receiving that as a revelation from God which was opposed to the revelation which himself had received, and which was confirmed by so many miracles, is slain by a lion, and his body deprived of the burial of his fathers; while the wicked king and the fallen prophet are both permitted to live.; torn Heb. broken \textsuperscript{32} the saying; the houses; in the cities \textsuperscript{33} am 3030-3050, bc 974-954 Jeroboam; made again Heb. returned and made; *marg. whosoever, consecrated him Heb. filled his hand, *marg. \textsuperscript{34} became sin; to cut it off\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 14}
\markright{KINGS III 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Roboam son of Solomon ruled over Juda. Roboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in the city Jerusalem, which the Lord chose to put his name there out of all the tribes of Israel: and his mother's name [was] Naama the Ammonitess. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Roboam did evil in the sight of the Lord; and he provoked him in all the things which their fathers did in their sins which they sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they built for themselves high places, and pillars, and [planted] groves on every high hill, and under every shady tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And there was a conspiracy in the land, and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord removed from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam, Susakim king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and took all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king's house, and the golden spears which David took out of the hand of the sons of Adrazaar king of Suba, and brought them into Jerusalem, even all that he took, [and] the golden shields which Solomon had made, [and carried them away into Egypt.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And king Roboam made brazen shields instead of them; and the chiefs of the golden shields which Solomon had made, and the chiefs of the body guard, who kept the gate of the house of the king, were placed in charge over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it came to pass when the king went into the house of the Lord, that the body guard took them up, and fixed them in the chamber of the body guard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the rest of the history of Roboam, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And there was war between Roboam and Jeroboam continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Roboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Abiu his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{21} Rehoboam; the city, ; to put his name; Naamah \textsuperscript{23} built; images or, standing images, or statues, groves; under every \textsuperscript{26} he took away; the shields of gold \textsuperscript{29} am 3029-3046, bc 975-958 are they not written \textsuperscript{31} am 3046, bc 958 Rehoboam, ; his mother's Abijam Dr. Kennicott observes, that the name of this king of Judah is now expressed three ways; here and in four other places, it is Abijam; in two others ( ) it is Abijahu; but in eleven others it is Abijah or Abiah, as it is expressed by St. Matthew ( ), Αβια; and this is the reading of thirteen of Kennicott's and De Rossi's manuscripts, and of thirteen respectable editions of the Hebrew Bible. The Syriac is the same. The Septuagint in the London Polyglott has Αβιου, Abihu; but in the Complutensian and Antwerp Polyglotts it has Αβια, Abiah; and the Editio Princeps of the Vulgate, some manuscripts and the text in these two Polyglotts, instead of Abiam, have Abia ., Abia, Abijah, Abia\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 15}
\markright{KINGS III 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nabat, Abiu son of Roboam reigns over Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he reigned three years over Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Maacha, daughter of Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he walked in the sins of his father which he wrought in his presence, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as [was] the heart of his father [David]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Howbeit for David's sake the Lord gave him a remnant, that he might establish his children after him, and might establish Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Forasmuch as David did that which was right in the sight of the Lord: he turned not from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the rest of the history of Abiu, and all that he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? And there was war between Abiu and Jeroboam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Abiu slept with his fathers in the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam; and he is buried with his fathers in the city of David: And Asa his son reigns in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In the four and twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa begins to reign over Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Ana, daughter of Abessalom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Asa did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, as David his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he removed the sodomites out of the land, and abolished all the practices which his fathers had kept up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he removed Ana his mother from being queen, forasmuch as she gathered a meeting in her grove: and Asa cut down her retreats, and burnt them with fire in the brook of Kedron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But he removed not the high places; nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with the Lord all his days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he brought in the pillars of his father, he even brought in his gold and silver pillars into the house of the Lord, and [his] vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And there was war between Asa and Baasa king of Israel all their days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Baasa king of Israel went up against Juda, and built Rama, so that no one should go out or come in for Asa king of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Asa took all the silver and the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house, and gave them into the hands of his servants; and king Asa sent them out to the son of Ader, the son of Taberema son of Azin king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Make a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father: behold! I have sent forth to you gold and silver [for] gifts: come, break your league with Baasa king of Israel, that he may go up from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the son of Ader listened to king Asa, and sent the chiefs of his forces to the cities of Israel; and they struck Ain, Dan, and Abel of the house of Maacha, and all Chennereth, as far as the whole land of Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass when Baasa heard it, that he left off building Rama, and returned to Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And king Asa charged all Juda without exception: and they take up the stones of Rama and its timbers [with] which Baasa was building; and king Asa built with them upon the whole hill of Benjamin, and the watch-tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the rest of the history of Asa, and all his mighty deeds which he wrought, and the cities which he built, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Josaphat his son reigns in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Nabat son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Juda, and he reigned two years in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sins wherein he caused Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Baasa son of Achia, [who was] over the house of Belaan son of Achia, conspired against him, and struck him in Gabathon of the Philistines; for Nabat and all Israel were besieging Gabathon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Baasa killed him in the third year of Asa son of Asa king of Juda; and reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And it came to pass when he reigned, that he struck the whole house of Jeroboam, and left none that breathed of Jeroboam, until he has destroyed him utterly, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by his servant Achia the Selonite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} for the sins of Jeroboam, who led Israel into sin, even by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the rest of the history of Nabat, and all that he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} [And there was a war between Asa and Baasa king of Israel in all their days. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And in the third year of Asa king of Juda, Baasa the son of Achia begins to reign over Israel in Thersa, twenty and four years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and in his sins, as he caused Israel to sin.\par

For Ramah was a city of Benjamin, situated on the confines of both kingdoms, probably on a hill, as the name imports, commanding a narrow defile between the mountains, through which lay the principal road to Jerusalem; so that a fortification being erected here, no communication could be held between the people of Israel and Judah, without Baasha's permission.; he might not suffer \textsuperscript{19} There is a league; break thy league; depart Heb. go up \textsuperscript{20} Ijon Probably the same as Hazar-enan, a frontier town to Damascus ( ); and perhaps the Inna of Coele-Syria, long. 68 degrees and a half, lat. 33 degrees, according to Ptolemy. Dan; Abel-beth-maachah, Cinneroth \textsuperscript{22} made a proclamation exempted Heb. free Geba, Gaba, Mizpah; Mizpeh \textsuperscript{23} rest of all, in the time \textsuperscript{24} am 3090, bc 914 was buried Of his splendid and costly funeral we read in . Jehoshaphat; Josaphat \textsuperscript{25} am 3050-3051, bc 954-953 Nadab, began to reign Heb. reigned \textsuperscript{26} he did evil, walked, in his sin \textsuperscript{27} Baasha the son, conspired; Gibbethon \textsuperscript{30} the sins, by his provocation \textsuperscript{31} am 3050-3051, bc 954-953 are they not written \textsuperscript{32} am 3051-3074, bc 953-930 there was war That is, there was a constant spirit of hostility kept up between the two kingdoms, and no doubt frequent skirmishing between the bordering parties; but there was no open war till Baasha king of Israel began to build Ramah, which was, according to; in the thirty-sixth year of Asa; but according to, his son was killed by Zimri in the twenty-sixth year of Asa, and consequently he could not make war upon him in the thirty-sixth year of his reign. Chronologers endeavour to reconcile this, by saying that the years should be reckoned, not from the beginning of Asa's reign, but from the separation of the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. We must either adopt this mode of solution, or admit that there is a mistake in some of the numbers, probably in the parallel places in Chronicles, but which we have no direct means of correcting.\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 16}
\markright{KINGS III 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Ju son of Anani to Baasa, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Forasmuch as I lifted you up from the earth, and made you ruler over my people Israel; and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam, and have caused my people Israel to sin, to provoke me with their vanities; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, I raise up [enemies] after Baasa, and after his house; and I will make your house as the house of Jeroboam son of Nabat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Him that dies of Baasa in the city the dogs shall devour, and him that dies of his in the field the birds of the sky shall devour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now the rest of the history of Baasa, and all that he did, and his mighty acts, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Baasa slept with his fathers, and they bury him in Thersa; and Ela his son reigns in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord spoke by Ju the son of Anani against Baasa, and against his house, [even] all the evil which he wrought before the Lord to provoke him to anger by the works of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he struck him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Ela son of Baasa reigned over Israel two years in Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Zambri, captain of half his cavalry, conspired against him, while he was in Thersa, drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa the steward at Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Zambri went in and struck him and killed him, and reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass when he reigned, when he sat upon his throne, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that he struck all the house of Baasa, according to the word which the Lord spoke against the house of Baasa, and to Ju the prophet, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} for all the sins of Baasa and Ela his son, as he led Israel astray to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel with their vanities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the rest of the deeds of Ela which he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Zambri reigned in Thersa seven days: and the army of Israel [was] encamped against Gabathon of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the people heard in the army, saying, Zambri has conspired and struck the king: and the people of Israel made Ambri the captain of the host king in that day in the camp over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Ambri went up, and all Israel with him, out of Gabathon; and they besieged Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it came to pass when Zambri saw that his city was taken, that he goes into the inner chamber of the house of the king, and burnt the king's house over him, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Because of his sins which he committed, doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, so as to walk in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and in his sins wherein he caused Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the rest of the history of Zambri, and his conspiracies wherein he conspired, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then the people of Israel divides; half the people goes after Thamni the son of Gonath to make him king; and half the people goes after Ambri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The people that followed Ambri overpowered the people that followed Thamni son of Gonath; and Thamni died and Joram his brother at that time, and Ambri reigned after Thamni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} In the thirty-first year of king Asa, Ambri begins to reign over Israel twelve years: he reigns six years in Thersa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Ambri bought the mount Semeron of Semer the lord of the mountain for two talents of silver; and he built [upon] the mountain, and they called the name of the mountain [on] which he built, after the name of Semer the lord of the mount, Semeron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Ambri did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and wrought wickedly beyond all that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and in his sins wherewith he caused Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel by their vanities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the rest of the acts of Ambri, and all that he did, and all his might, behold, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Ambri slept with his fathers, and is buried in Samaria; and Achaab his son reigns in his stead. And in the eleventh year of Ambri Josaphat the son of Asa reigns, [being] thirty-five years old in the beginning of his reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Gazuba, daughter of Seli. And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and turned not from it, [even] from doing right in the eyes of the Lord: only they removed not [any] of the high places; they sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. Now the engagements which Josaphat made with the king of Israel, and all his mighty deeds which he performed, and the enemies whom he fought against, behold, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? and the remains of the prostitution which they practiced in the days of Asa his father, he removed out of the land: and there was no king in Syria, [but] a deputy. And king Josaphat made a ship at Tharsis to go to Sophir for gold: but it went not, for the ship was broken at Gasion Gaber. Then the king of Israel said to Josaphat, I will send forth your servants and my servants in the ship: but Josaphat would not. And Josaphat slept with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Joram his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} In the second year of Josaphat king of Juda, Achaab son of Ambri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Achaab did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and did more wickedly than all that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, but he took as wife, Jezabel the daughter of Jethebaal king of the Sidonians; and he went and served Baal, and worshipped him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he set up an altar to Baal, in the house of his abominations, which he built in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Achaab made a grove; and Achaab did yet more abominably, to provoke the Lord God of Israel, and [to sin against] his own life so that he should be destroyed: he did evil above all the kings of Israel that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And in his days Achiel the Baethelite built Jericho: he laid the foundation of it in Abiron his firstborn, and he set up the doors of it in Segub his younger son, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by Joshua the son of Naue.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} I exalted thee; thou hast walked, hast made my people \textsuperscript{6} am 3074, bc 930 Baasha, Tirzah, Elah \textsuperscript{7} the hand and against his house in provoking with the work; because he killed him This the Vulgate understands of Jehu the prophet; some think Baasha is intended; others Nadab the son of Jeroboam; and others Jeroboam, whom Baasha destroyed in his posterity by cruelly murdering them all. \textsuperscript{8} am 3075, bc 929 In the twenty Baasha began to reign in the third year of Asa, and reigned 24 years; yet he died and was succeeded by Elah in the 26th year of Asa; and, in like manner, Elah, who began to reign in the 26th year of Asa, and was killed in the 27th, is said to have reigned two years. Thus it is evident that a part of a year is calculated as a whole year. In the Chinese annals, the whole year in which a king dies is ascribed to his reign, the years of the succeeding king being reckoned only from the beginning of the following year. \textsuperscript{9} his servant conspired;, drinking; steward of Heb. which was over \textsuperscript{11} he slew; he left him; neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends or, both his kinsmen and his friends \textsuperscript{12} according by Jehu the prophet Heb. by the hand of Jehu the prophet \textsuperscript{15} seven; And the people were encamped \textsuperscript{18} and burnt the king's house \textsuperscript{23} am 3079-3086, bc 925-918 the thirty As it is stated in and, that Zimri began to reign in the 27th year of Asa; and as he reigned only seven days, and Omri immediately succeeded him, this could not be the 31st, but in the 27th year of Asa. Jarchi, from Sedar Olam, reconciles this, by stating that Tibni and Omri began to reign jointly in the 27th year of Asa; and that Tibni dying about five years afterwards, Omri began to reign alone in the 31st year of Asa. twelve years \textsuperscript{24} the name of the city, ; Samaria Heb. \subsection*{Kings III 17}
\markright{KINGS III 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Eliu the prophet, the Thesbite of Thesbae of Galaad, said to Achaab, As the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be these years dew nor rain, except by the word of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the word of the Lord came to Eliu, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Depart hence eastward, and hide you by the brook of Chorrath, that is before Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it shall be [that] you shall drink water of the brook, and I will charge the ravens to feed you there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Eliu did according to the word of the Lord, and he sat by the brook of Chorrath before Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the ravens brought him loaves in the morning, and flesh in the evening and he drank water of the brook. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass after some time, that the brook was dried up, because there had been no rain upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the word of the Lord came to Eliu, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Arise, and go to Sarepta of the Sidonian [land]: behold, I have there commanded a widow-woman to maintain you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he arose and went to Sarepta, and came to the gate of the city: and, behold, a widow-woman was there gathering sticks; and Eliu cried after her, and said to her, Fetch me, I pray you, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And she went to fetch it; and Eliu cried after her, and said, Bring me, I pray you, a morsel of the bread that is in your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the woman said, [As] the Lord your God lives, I have not a cake, but only a handful of meal in the pitcher, and a little oil in a cruse, and, behold, I am going to gather two sticks, and I shall go in and dress it for myself and my children, and we shall eat it and die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Eliu said to her, Be of good courage, go in and do according to your word: but make me thereof a little cake, and you shall bring [it] out to me first, and you shall make [some] for yourself and your children last. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For thus says the Lord, The pitcher of meal shall not fail, and the cruse of oil shall not diminish, until the day that the Lord gives rain upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the woman went and did [so], and did eat, she, and he, and her children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the pitcher of meal failed not, and the cruse of oil was not diminished, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of Eliu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass afterward, that the son of the woman the mistress of the house was sick; and his sickness was very severe, until there was no breath left in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she said to Eliu, What have I to do with you, O man of God? have you come in to me to bring my sins to remembrance, and to kill my son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Eliu said to the woman, Give me your son. And he took him out of her bosom, and took him up to the chamber in which he himself lodged, and laid him on the bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Eliu cried aloud, and said, Alas, O Lord, the witness of the widow with whom I sojourn, you have wrought evil [for her] in slaying her son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he breathed on the child thrice, and called on the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, let, I pray you, the soul of this child return to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it was so, and the child cried out, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and he brought him down from the upper chamber into the house, and gave him to his mother; and Eliu said, See, your son lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the woman said to Eliu, Behold, I know that you [are] a man of God, and the word of the Lord in your mouth [is] true.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3094, bc 910 Elijah Heb. Elijahu, ;, ; Elias As the Lord God; before whom; dew nor rain \textsuperscript{5} did according; Many learned men have raised doubts on those parts of the Inspired Word, which may, by the perverseness of their argument and the ingenuity of their surmise, be made to appear inconsistent with fact. In this case, they are not satisfied with being expressly told by God that the ravens supplied Elijah with food, while the brook gave him drink, but apparently to mystify a manifest miracle, they suggest whether these ravens might not be merchantmen, or the inhabitants of a neighbouring town. Let any unprejudiced reader and lover of the Bible take the whole history of Elijah, and he will find that his life was almost a daily illustration of the power of God in his miraculous interpositions. Instance the supply of provision in the unwasting barrel of meal and cruse of oil, after the prophet had removed to Zarephath. The power communicated to him to raise the widow's son from death. The wonderful interposition of the Lord to prove the folly of Baal's worshippers, in sending down fire from heaven to consume Elijah's sacrifice and lick up the water, although the sacrifice had been saturated therewith, and the altar surrounded by a deep trench to prevent its running away. The prayer for rain is another instance. The sojourn in Horeb forty days and forty nights, after having eaten of the cake: the destruction of Ahaziah's messengers twice. The smiting of the waters at Jordan. The fall of the mantle on Elisha, and finally, in the closing scene of life, he was taken to glory without tasting the pains of death, the sting was taken away. \textsuperscript{7} am 3095, bc 909 after a while Heb. at the end of days the brook \textsuperscript{9} Zarephath; Sarepta which belongeth widow woman \textsuperscript{11} as she was going; a morsel \textsuperscript{12} As the Lord;, ; but an handful; that we may eat it \textsuperscript{13} Fear not; make me thereof; first \textsuperscript{14} thus saith, The barrel of meal; sendeth Heb. giveth \textsuperscript{15} did according, ; many days or, a full year \textsuperscript{16} the barrel; according by Elijah Heb. by the hand of Elijah \textsuperscript{17} am 3096, bc 908 the son of the woman; that there was; *marg. \textsuperscript{18} What have I; O thou man art thou come \textsuperscript{20} he cried; hast thou also \textsuperscript{21} stretched himself Heb. measured himself; O Lord my God \textsuperscript{22} into him Heb. into his inward parts and he revived \textsuperscript{24} Now by this, the word\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 18}
\markright{KINGS III 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the Lord came to Eliu in the third year, saying, Go, and appear before Achaab, and I will bring rain upon the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Eliu went to appear before Achaab: and the famine [was] severe in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Achaab called Abdiu the steward. Now Abdiu feared the Lord greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass when Jezabel struck the prophets of the Lord, that Abdiu took one hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Achaab said to Abdiu, Come, and let us go through the land, and to the fountains of water, and to the brooks, if by any means we may find grass, and may save the horses and mules, and so they will not perish from the tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they made a division of the way between them to pass through it: Achaab went one way, and Abdiu went by another way alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Abdiu was alone in the way; and Eliu came alone to meet him: and Abdiu hasted, and fell upon his face, and said, My lord Eliu, are you [indeed] he? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Eliu said to him, I [am]: go say to your master, Behold, Eliu [is here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Abdiu said, What sin have I committed, that you give your servant into the hand of Achaab to kill me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [As] the Lord your God lives, there is not a nation or kingdom, whither my lord has not sent to seek you; and if they said, He is not [here], then has he set fire to the kingdom and its territories, because he has not found you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now you say, Go, tell your lord, Behold, Eliu [is here]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall come to pass when I shall have departed from you, that the Spirit of the Lord shall carry you to a land which I know not, and I shall go in to tell the matter to Achaab, and he will not find you and will kill me: yet your servant fears the Lord from his youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Has it not been told to you my lord, what I did when Jezabel killed the prophets of the Lord, that I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And now you say to me, Go, say to your master, Behold, Eliu [is here]: and he shall kill me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Eliu said, [As] the Lord of Hosts before whom I stand lives, today I will appear before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Abdiu went to meet Achaab, and told him: and Achaab hasted forth, and went to meet Eliu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass when Achaab saw Eliu, that Achaab said to Eliu, Are you he that perverts Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Eliu said, I do not pervert Israel; but it is you and your father's house, in that you⌃ forsake the Lord your God, and you have gone after Baalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now send, gather to me all Israel to mount Carmel, and the prophets of shame four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, that eat [at] Jezabel's table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Achaab sent to all Israel, and gathered all the prophets to mount Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Eliu drew near to them all: and Eliu said to them, How long will you⌃ halt on both feet? if the Lord be God, follow him; but if Baal, follow him. And the people answered not a word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Eliu said to the people, I am left, the only one prophet of the Lord; and the prophets of Baal [are] four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the groves four hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Let them give us two oxen, and let them choose one for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire [on] the wood: and I will dress the other bullock, and put on no fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And do you⌃ call loudly on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God, and it shall come to pass that the God who shall answer by fire, he [is] God. And all the people answered and said, The word which you have spoken [is] good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Eliu said to the prophets of shame, Choose to yourselves one calf, and dress it first, for you⌃ [are] many; and call you⌃ on the name of your god; but apply no fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they took the calf and dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning till noon, and said, hear us, O Baal, hear us. And there was no voice, neither was there hearing, and they ran up and down on the altar which they [had] made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it was noon, and Eliu the Thesbite mocked them, and said, Call with a loud voice, for he is a god; for he is meditating, or else perhaps he is engaged in business, or perhaps he is asleep, and is to be awaked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they cried with a loud voice, and cut themselves according to their custom with knives and lancets until the blood gushed out upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they prophesied until the evening came; and it came to pass as it was the time of the offering of the sacrifice, that Eliu the Thesbite spoke to the prophets of the abominations, saying, Stand by for the present, and I will offer my sacrifice. And they stood aside and departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Eliu said to the people, Come near to me. And all the people came near to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Eliu took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord spoke to him, saying, Israel shall be your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he built up the stones in the name of the Lord, and repaired the altar that had been broken down; and he made a trench that would hold two measures of seed round about the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he piled the cleft wood on the altar which he [had] made, and divided the whole burnt offering, and laid [it] on the wood, and laid [it] in order on the altar, and said, Fetch me four pitchers of water, and pour [it] on the whole burnt offering, and on the wood. And they did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he said, Do it the second time. And they did it the second time. And he said, Do it the third time. And they did it the third time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the water ran round about the altar, and they filled the trench with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Eliu cried aloud to the heaven, and said, Lord God of Abraam, and Isaac, and Israel, answer me, O Lord, answer me this day by fire, and let all this people know that you are the Lord, the God of Israel, and I [am] your servant, and for your sake I have wrought these works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Hear me, O Lord, hear me, and let this people know that you are the Lord God, and you have turned back the heart of this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Then fire fell from the Lord out of heaven, and devoured the whole burnt offerings, and the wood and the water that was in the trench, and the fire licked up the stones and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And all the people fell upon their faces, and said, Truly the Lord [is] God; he [is] God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Eliu said to the people, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them; and Eliu brings them down to the brook Kisson, and he killed them there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Eliu said to Achaab, Go up, and eat and drink, for [there is] a sound of the coming of rain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Achaab went up to eat and to drink; and Eliu went up to Carmel, and stooped to the ground, and put his face between his knees, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} and said to his servant, Go up, and look toward the sea. And the servant looked, and said, There is nothing: and Eliu said, Do you then go again seven times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the servant went again seven times: and it came to pass at the seventh time, that, behold, a little cloud like the sole of a man's foot brought water; and he said, Go up, and say to Achaab, make ready your chariot, and go down, lest the rain overtake you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And it came to pass in the meanwhile, that the heaven grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Achaab wept, and went to Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And the hand of the Lord [was] upon Eliu, and he girded up his loins, and ran before Achaab to Jezrael.\par

\subsection*{Kings III 19}
\markright{KINGS III 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Achaab told Jezabel his wife all that Eliu [had] done, and how he [had] slain the prophets with the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jezabel sent to Eliu, and said, If you are Eliu and I am Jezabel, God do so to me, and more also, if I do not make your life by this time to-morrow as the life of one of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Eliu feared, and rose, and departed for his life: and he comes to Bersabee [to] the land of Juda, and he left his servant there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he himself went a day's journey in the wilderness, and came and sat under a juniper tree; and asked concerning his life that he might die, and said, Let it be enough now, O Lord, take, I pray you, my life from me; for I am no better than my fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he lay down and slept there under a tree; and behold, some one touched him, and said to him, Arise and eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Eliu looked, and, behold, at his head there was a cake of meal and a cruse of water; and he arose, and ate and drank, and returned and lay down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the angel of the Lord returned again, and touched him, and said to him, Arise, and eat, for the journey [is] far from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he arose, and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights to mount Choreb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he entered there into a cave, and rested there; and, behold, the word of the Lord [came] to him, and he said, What [do] you here, Eliu? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Eliu said, I have been very jealous for the Lord Almighty, because the children of Israel have forsaken you: they have digged down your altars, and have slain your prophets with the sword; and I only am left alone, and they seek my life to take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said, You shall go forth to-morrow, and shall stand before the Lord in the mount; behold, the Lord will pass by. And, behold, a great [and] strong wind rending the mountains, and crushing the rocks before the Lord; [but] the Lord [was] not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake; [but] the Lord [was] not in the earthquake: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and after the earthquake a fire; [but] the Lord [was] not in the fire: and after the fire the voice of a gentle breeze. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass when Eliu heard, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went forth and stood in the cave: and, behold, a voice [came] to him and said, What [do] you here, Eliu? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Eliu said, I have been very jealous for the Lord Almighty; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, and they have overthrown your altars, and have slain your prophets with the sword! and I am left entirely alone, and they seek my life to take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord said to him, Go, return, and you shall come into the way of the wilderness of Damascus: and you shall go and anoint Azael to be king over Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Ju the son of Namessi shall you anoint to be king over Israel; and Elisaie the son of Saphat shall you anoint to be prophet in your room. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it shall come to pass, that him that escapes from the sword of Azael, Ju shall kill; and him that escapes from the sword of Ju, Elisaie shall kill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall leave in Israel seven thousand men, all the knees which had not bowed themselves to Baal, and every mouth which had not worshipped him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he departed thence, and finds Elisaie the son of Saphat, and he was plowing with oxen; [there were] twelve yoke before him, and he with the twelve, and he passed by to him, and cast his mantle upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Elisaie left the cattle, and ran after Eliu and said, I will kiss my father, and follow after you. And Eliu said, Return, for I have done [a work] for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he returned from following him, and took a yoke of oxen, and killed them, and boiled them with the instruments of the oxen, and gave to the people, and they ate: and he arose, and went after Eliu, and ministered to him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ahab, how he had slain \textsuperscript{2} So let; if I; to morrow \textsuperscript{4} sat down; he requested; for himself Heb. for his life better \textsuperscript{5} as he lay an angel \textsuperscript{7} the angel because the journey \textsuperscript{8} in the strength; forty days; Horeb \textsuperscript{9} unto a cave; What doest thou \textsuperscript{10} very jealous; thrown down, ; I only, ; they seek my life \textsuperscript{11} stand upon the mount, ; the Lord passed; and a great; but the Lord was not in the wind an earthquake \textsuperscript{13} he wrapped his face This he did to signify his reverence; for covering the face was a token of respect among the Asiatics, as uncovering the head is among Europeans. See note on .; What doest \textsuperscript{15} wilderness of Damascus The wilderness of Damascus seems to have been that part of Arabia Deserta which lay on the south-east of that city, and east of the Trachonites, or the Djebel Haouran and El Ledja; at which the prophet could arrive without meeting Jezebel or any of his enemies.; anoint; Hazael \textsuperscript{17} him that escapeth; the sword of Hazael, the sword of Jehu, Elisha slay \textsuperscript{18} Yet I have left or, Yet I will leave, ; the knees; every mouth Idolaters often kissed their hand in honour of their idols; and hence the origin of adoration from ad, to and os, oris, the mouth. Cicero mentions a statue of Hercules, the chin and lips of which were considerably worn by the kissing of his worshippers. \textsuperscript{19} Elisha he with; his mantle \textsuperscript{20} he left, I pray; Go back again Heb. \subsection*{Kings III 20}
\markright{KINGS III 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Nabuthai the Jezraelite had a vineyard, near the threshing floor of Achaab king of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Achaab spoke to Nabuthai, saying, Give me your vineyard, and I will have it for a garden of herbs, for it [is] near my house: and I will give you another vineyard better than it; or if it please you, I will give you money, the price of this your vineyard, and I will have it for a garden of herbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Nabuthai said to Achaab, My God forbid me that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the spirit of Achaab was troubled, and he lay down upon his bed, and covered his face, and ate no bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jezabel his wife went in to him, and spoke to him, [saying], Why [is] your spirit troubled, and [why] do you eat no bread? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to her, Because I spoke to Nabuthai the Jezraelite, saying, Give me your vineyard for money; or if you will, I will give you another vineyard for it: and he said, I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jezabel his wife said to him, Do you now thus act the king over Israel? arise, and eat bread, and be your own [master], and I will give you the vineyard of Nabuthai the Jezraelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And she wrote a letter in the name of Achaab, and sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders, and to the freemen who lived with Nabuthai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it was written in the letters, saying, Keep a fast, and set Naboth in a chief place among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And set two men, sons of transgressors, before him, and let them testify against him, saying, He blessed God and the king: and let them lead him forth, and stone him, and let them die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the men of his city, the elders, and the nobles who lived in his city, did as Jezabel sent to them, and as it had been written in the letters which she sent to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they proclaimed a fast, and set Nebuthai in a chief place among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And two men, sons of transgressors, came in, and sat opposite him, and bore witness against him, saying, You have blessed God and the king. And they led him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they sent to Jezabel, saying, Nabuthai is stoned, and is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass, when Jezabel heard [it], that she said to Achaab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Nabuthai the Jezraelite, who would not sell it to you: for Nebuthai is not alive, for he is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass, when Achaab heard that Nabuthai the Jezraelite was dead, that he tore his garments, and put on sackcloth. And it came to pass afterward, that Achaab arose and went down to the vineyard of Nabuthai the Jezraelite, to take possession of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Lord spoke to Eliu the Thesbite, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Arise, and go down to meet Achaab king of Israel, who is in Samaria, for he [is] in the vineyard of Nabuthai, for he has gone down there to take possession of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall speak to him, saying, Thus says the Lord, Forasmuch as you have slain and taken possession, therefore thus says the Lord, In every place where the swine and the dogs have licked the blood of Nabuthai, there shall the dogs lick your blood; and the harlots shall wash themselves in your blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Achaab said to Eliu, Have you found me, my enemy? and he said, I have found [you]: because you have wickedly sold yourself to work evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} behold, I bring evil upon you: and I will kindle a fire after you, and I will utterly destroy every male of Achaab, and him that is shut up and him that is left in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will make your house as the house of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and as the house of Baasa son of Achia, because of the provocations wherewith you have provoked [me], and caused Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord spoke of Jezabel, saying, The dogs shall devour her within the fortification of Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Him that is dead of Achaab in the city shall the dogs eat, and him that is dead of him in the field shall the birds of the sky eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But Achaab [did] wickedly, in that he sold himself to do that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his wife Jezabel led him astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he did very abominably in following after the abominations, according to all that the Amorite did, whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And because of the word, Achaab was pierced with sorrow before the Lord, and he both went weeping, and tore his garment, and girded sackcloth upon his body, and fasted; he put on sackcloth also in the day that he struck Nabuthai the Jezraelite, and went his way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the word of the Lord came by the hand of his servant Eliu concerning Achaab, and the Lord said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Have you seen how Achaab has been pricked [to the heart] before me? I will not bring on the evil in his days, but in his son's days will I bring on the evil.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3103, bc 901 Benhadad; Thirty and two; and horses; besieged \textsuperscript{6} and they shall search; pleasant Heb. desirable; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} all the elders; Mark seeketh mischief;, ; denied him not Heb. kept not back from him \textsuperscript{10} The gods; if the dust; follow me Heb. are at my feet, *marg. \textsuperscript{11} Let not him etc. This was no doubt a proverbial mode of expression. Jonathan renders it: "Let not him who girds himself, and goes down to battle, boast as one who has conquered and returned from it.", ; harness The word harness is an obsolete word for armour, derived from the French harnois . See note on . \textsuperscript{12} message Heb. word drinking; pavilions or, tents, That persons of regal dignity regaled themselves in this manner, we may learn from Dr. Chandler, who, when he went to visit the Aga of Suki, after his return from hawking, found him vexed and tired; and "a couch was prepared from him beneath a shed made against a cottage, and covered with green boughs to keep off the sun. He entered as we were standing by, and fell down on it to sleep, without taking any notice of us." Set yourselves in array, And they set etc. or, Place the engines, And they placed engines \textsuperscript{13} came Heb. approached Hast thou, ; and thou shalt \textsuperscript{14} young men or, servants; order Heb. bind, or tie \textsuperscript{16} Benhadad; the thirty; The Syrians, the besiegers, had their directions from a drunken king, who gave orders over his cups, while he was drinking at noon. Drunkenness is a sin which is most detestable in all, but more so in a king than in a private individual, inasmuch as the greater weight a man's situation carries, whether from accumulated riches, family connections, hereditary authority, or invested command, so is the influence which his vices must have on those around him. Perhaps it may be said, from past experience, that drunkenness, which is a most heinous sin in the sight of God, may be charged on those who indulge only now and then in that which may eventually lead them into drunkenness; for they shut their eyes against the most palpable facts, and rather than give up the paltry gratification of a debauch, involve thousands by their example to positive harm. Benhadad's drunkenness was the forerunner of his fall. Belshazzar also, we read, drank wine with his princes, his wives, and his concubines, and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone, and in the same hour came forth the finger of a man's hand and wrote his doom on the plaster of the wall. Those who fancy themselves perfectly secure, and above the possibility of falling, are commonly nearest their destruction. There is always an Ahab read to take advantage of and improve the self-imposed imbecility. \textsuperscript{20} they slew; the Syrians; escaped \textsuperscript{22} the prophet, ; strengthen; at the return \textsuperscript{23} Their gods It was the general belief in the heathen world, that each district had its tutelary and protecting deity, who could do nothing out of his own province. \textsuperscript{25} thou hast lost Heb. was fallen and surely \textsuperscript{26} Aphek Supposed to be the Aphek near the river Adonis, between Heliopolis and Biblos, and probably the same place that Paul Lucas mentions in his Voyage to the Levant. It was swallowed up by an earthquake, and formed a lake about nine miles in circumference, in which he says there were several houses still to be seen entire, under the water.; Aphik, ; to fight against Israel Heb. to the war with Israel \textsuperscript{27} were all present or, were victualled; like two \textsuperscript{28} there came, ; Because; therefore will; , ye shall know \textsuperscript{29} seven days; an hundred thousand\par}
