\subsection*{Kings III 21}
\markright{KINGS III 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the son of Ader gathered all his forces, and went up and besieged Samaria, [he] and thirty-two kings with him, and all [his] horse and chariots: and they went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he sent into the city to Achaab king of Israel, and said to him, Thus says the son of Ader, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children are mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king of Israel answered and said, As you have said, my lord, O king, I am yours, and all mine [also]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the messengers came again, and said, Thus says the son of Ader, I sent to you, saying, You shall give me your silver and your gold, and your wives and your children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For at this time to-morrow I will send my servants to you, and they shall search your house, and the houses of your servants, and it shall be that all the desirable objects of their eyes on which they shall lay their hands, they shall even take [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the king of Israel called all the elders of the land, and said, Take notice now and consider, that this man seeks mischief: for he has sent to me concerning my wives, and concerning my sons, and concerning my daughters: I have not kept back from him my silver and my gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the elders and all the people said to him, Listen not, and consent not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to the messengers of the son of Ader, Say to your master, All things that you have sent to your servant about at first I will do; but this thing I shall not be able to do. And the men departed, and carried back the answer to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the son of Ader sent to him, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for foxes to all the people, even my infantry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the king of Israel answered and said, Let it be sufficient; let not the humpbacked boast as he that is upright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it came to pass when he returned him this answer, he and all the kings with him were drinking in tents: and he said to his servants, Form a trench. And they made a trench against the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And, behold, a prophet came to Achaab king of Israel, and said, Thus says the Lord, Have you seen this great multitude? behold, I give it this day into your hands; and you shall know that I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Achaab said, Whereby? And he said, Thus says the Lord, by the young men of the heads of the districts. And Achaab said, Who shall begin the battle? and he said, You. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Achaab numbered the young men the heads of the districts, and they were two hundred and thirty: and afterwards he numbered the people, [even] every man fit for war, seven thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he went forth at noon, and the son of Ader was drinking [and] getting drunk in Socchoth, he and the kings, [even] thirty and two kings, his allies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the young men the heads of the districts went forth first; and they send and report to the king of Syria, saying, There are men come forth out of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to them, If they come forth peaceably, take them alive; and if they come forth to war, take them alive: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and let not the young men the heads of the districts go forth of the city. And the force that was behind them {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} struck each one the man next to him; and each one a second time struck the man next to him: and Syria fled, and Israel pursued them; and the son of Ader, [even] the king of Syria, escapes on the horse of a horseman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king of Israel went forth, and took all the horses and the chariots, and struck [the enemy] with a great slaughter in Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the prophet came to the king of Israel, and said, Strengthen yourself, and observe, and see what you shall do; for at the return of the year the son of Ader king of Syria comes up against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the servants of the king of Syria, even they said, The God of Israel [is] a God of mountains, and not a God of valleys; therefore has he prevailed against us: but if we should fight against them in the plain, verily we shall prevail against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And do you this thing: Send away the kings, each one to his place, and set princes in their stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And we will give you [another] army according to the army that was destroyed, and cavalry according to the cavalry, and chariots according to the chariots, and we will fight against them in the plain, and we shall prevail against them. And he listened to their voice, and did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it came to pass at the return of the year, that the son of Ader reviewed Syria, and went up to Apheca to war against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the children of Israel were numbered, and came to meet them: and Israel encamped before them as two little flocks of goats, but Syria filled the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And there came the man of God, and said to the king of Israel, Thus says the Lord, Because Syria has said, The Lord God of Israel [is] a God of the hills, and he [is] not a God of the valleys, therefore will I give this great army into your hand, and you shall know that I [am] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And they encamp one over against the other before them seven days. And it came to pass on the seventh day that the battle drew on, and Israel struck Syria, [even] one hundred thousand footmen in one day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the rest fled to Apheca, into the city; and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men that were left: and the son of Ader fled, and entered into an inner chamber, into a closet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said to his servants, I know that the kings of Israel are merciful kings: let us now put sackcloth upon our loins, and ropes upon our heads, and let us go forth to the king of Israel, if by any means he will save our souls alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} So they girded sackcloth upon their loins, and put ropes upon their heads, and said to the king of Israel, Your servant the son of Ader says, Let our souls live, I pray you. And he said, Does he yet live? He is my brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the men divined, and offered drink-offerings; and they caught the word out of his mouth, and said, Your brother the son of Ader. And he said, Go you⌃ in and fetch him. And the son of Ader went out to him, and they cause him to go up to him into the chariot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he said to him, The cities which my father took from your father I will restore to you; and you shall make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made streets in Samaria; and I will let you go with a covenant. And he made a covenant with him, and let him go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, Strike me, I pray, And the man would not strike him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he said to him, Because you have not listened to the voice of the Lord, therefore, behold, as you depart from me, a lion shall strike you: and he departed from him, and a lion found him, and struck him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And he finds another man, and says, Strike me, I pray you. And the man struck him, and in striking wounded [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the prophet went and stood before the king of Israel by the way, and bound his eyes with a bandage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And it came to pass as the king passed by, that he cried aloud to the king, and said, Your servant went out to war, and, behold, a man brought [another] man to me, and said to me, Keep his man; and if he should by any means escape, then your life shall go for his life, or you shall pay a talent of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And it came to pass, that your servant looked round this way and that way, and the man was gone. And the king of Israel said to him, Behold, you have also destroyed snares [set] for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And he hasted, and took away the bandage from his eyes; and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And he said to him, Thus says the Lord, Because you have suffered to escape out of your hand a man appointed to destruction, therefore your life shall go for his life, and your people for his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the king of Israel departed confounded and discouraged, and came to Samaria.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Give me The request of Ahab, at first view, appears fair and honourable. But, as he most evidentially wished Naboth to alienate it finally, which was expressly forbidden and provided against in the law of God ( ), it was high iniquity in Ahab to tempt him to do it, and to covet it showed the depravity of his soul.; a garden of herbs; seem good to thee Heb. be good in thine eyes \textsuperscript{3} The Lord; , ; I should give \textsuperscript{4} heavy; I will not; And he laid him \textsuperscript{5} Jezebel, ; Why is thy spirit \textsuperscript{6} Because; I will not give \textsuperscript{7} Dost thou now; I will give thee \textsuperscript{8} she wrote; the elders; the nobles \textsuperscript{9} Proclaim a fast; on high among Heb. in the top of \textsuperscript{10} two men; sons of Belial; Thou didst blaspheme Some, with Parkhurst, would render the original, bairachta elohim wamailech, "Thou hast blessed the gods and Molech; " a sense, however, which seems extremely forced, and is not acknowledged by any of the ancient versions, though the LXX and Vulgate render bairachta by ευλογησε, benedixit, "blessed." It is no unusual thing for a word to have opposite senses. \textsuperscript{13} the men of Belial; , ; blaspheme God, ; the king; they carried him \textsuperscript{19} Hast thou killed; In the place This punishment, on Ahab's humiliation and repentance, was transferred from him to his son Jehoram ( ), in whom it was literally accomplished. See the parallel texts. \textsuperscript{20} Hast thou found me; thou hast sold; to work \textsuperscript{21} Behold;, him that pisseth, him that is shut up \textsuperscript{22} make thine, made Israel to sin \textsuperscript{23} Jezebel; the dogs Shocking as this must appear to minds that have been humanized by the kindly influence of Christianity, we still find similar instances in the accounts of modern travellers. I was miserable, and almost driven to despair, at seeing my hunting dogs, twice let loose by the carelessness of my servants, bringing into the court-yard the heads and arms of slaughtered men, and which I could no way prevent, but by the destruction of the dogs themselves." wall or, ditch. \textsuperscript{25} But there; sell himself; whom Jezebel, ; stirred up or, incited \textsuperscript{27} he rent; lay in sackcloth; went softly \textsuperscript{29} Seest thou; Ahab;, I will not; the evil in his son's days\par}

\subsection*{Kings III 22}
\markright{KINGS III 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he rested three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass in the third year, that Josaphat king of Juda went down to the king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king of Israel said to his servants, Know you⌃ that Remmath Galaad [is] ours, and we are slow to take it out of the hand of the king of Syria? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, Will you go up with us to Remmath Galaad to battle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Josaphat said, As I [am], so [are] you also; as my people, [so is] your people; as my horses, [so are] your horses. And Josaphat king of Juda said to the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray you, of the Lord today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the king of Israel gathered all the prophets together, about four hundred men; and the king said to them, Shall I go up to Remmath Galaad to battle, or shall I forbear? and they said, Go up, and the Lord will surely give [it] into the hands of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Josaphat said to the king of Israel, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may enquire of the Lord by him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, There is one man here [for us] to enquire of the Lord by; but I hate him, for he does not speak good of me, but only evil; Michaias son of Jemblaa. And Josaphat king of Juda said, Let not the king say so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king of Israel called a eunuch and said, [Bring hither] quickly Michaias son of Jemblaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Juda sat, each on his throne, armed in the gates of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Sedekias son of Chanaan made for himself iron horns, and said, Thus says the Lord, With these you shall push Syria, until it be consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all the prophets prophesied in like manner, saying, Go up to Remmath Galaad, and [the thing] shall prosper, and the Lord shall deliver it and the king of Syria into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the messenger that went to call Michaias spoke to him, saying, Behold now, all the prophets speak with one mouth good concerning the king, let now your words be like the words of one of them, and speak good things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Michaias said, [As] the Lord lives, whatever the Lord shall say to me, that will I speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he came to the king: and the king said to him, Michaias, shall I go up to Remmath Galaad to battle, or shall I forbear? and he said, Go up, and the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the king said to him, How often shall I adjure you, that you speak to me truth in the name of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, Not so. I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains as a flock without a shepherd: and the Lord said, [Is] not God lord of these? let each one return to his home in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Juda, Did I not say to you that this man does not prophesy good to me, for [he speaks] nothing but evil? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Michaias said, Not so, [it is] not I: hear the word of the Lord; [it is] not so. I saw the God of Israel sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven stood about him on his right hand and on his left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord said, Who will deceive Achaab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall in Remmath Galaad? and one spoke one way, and another another way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And there came forth a spirit and stood before the Lord, and said, I will deceive him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord said to him, Whereby? And he said, I will go forth, and will be a false spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, You shall deceive him, yes, and shall prevail: go forth, and do so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now, behold, the Lord has put a false spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Sedekias the son of Chanaan came near and struck Michaias on the cheek, and said, What sort of a spirit of the Lord [has] spoken in you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Michaias said, Behold, you shall see in that day, when you shall go into an innermost chamber to hide yourself there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king of Israel said, Take Michaias, and convey him away to Semer the keeper of the city; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and tell Joas the king's son to put this [fellow] in prison, and to feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Michaias said, If you return at all in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So the king of Israel went up, and Josaphat king of Juda with him to Remmath Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Juda, I will disguise myself, and enter into the battle, and do you put on my raiment. So the king of Israel disguised himself, and went into the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the king of Syria had charged the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying, Fight not [against] small or great, but against the king of Israel only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Josaphat king of Juda, that they said, this seems [to be] the king of Israel. And they compassed him about to fight [against] him; and Josaphat cried out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that this was not the king of Israel, that they returned from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And one drew a bow with a good aim, and struck the king of Israel between the lungs and the breast-plate: and he said to his charioteer, Turn your hands, and carry me away out of the battle, for I am wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the war was turned in that day, and the king was standing on the chariot, against Syria from morning till evening; and he shed the blood out of his wound, into the bottom of the chariot, and died at even, and the blood ran out of the wound into the bottom of the chariot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the herald of the army stood at sunset, saying, Let every man go to his own city and his own land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} for the king is dead. And they came to Samaria, and buried the king in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And they washed the chariot at the fountain of Samaria; and the swine and the dogs licked up the blood, and the harlots washed themselves in the blood, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And the rest of the acts of Achaab, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built, and all the cities which he built, behold, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And Achaab slept with his fathers, and Ochozias his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And Josaphat the son of Asa reigned over Juda: in the fourth year of Achaab king of Israel began Josaphat to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Thirty and five years old [was he] when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name [was] Azuba daughter of Salai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And he walked in all the way of Asa his father: he turned not from it, even from doing that which was right in the eyes of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Only he took not away [any] of the high places: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And Josaphat was at peace with the king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And the rest of the acts of Josaphat, and his mighty deeds, whatever he did, behold, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And Josaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried by his fathers in the city of David his father, and Joram his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And Ochozias son of Achaab reigned over Israel in Samaria: in the seventeenth year of Josaphat king of Juda, Ochozias son of Achaab reigned over Israel in Samaria two years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Achaab his father, and in the way of Jezabel his mother, and in the sins of the house of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And he served Baalim, and worshipped them, and provoked the Lord God of Israel, according to all that had been done before him.\par

It may mean, either "The Lord will deliver it (Ramoth Gilead) into the king's (Ahab's) hand; " or, "The Lord will deliver (Israel) into the king's (of Syria) hand." So in the famous reply of the Delphian oracle to Pyrrhus: Aio te Aacida, Romanos vincere posse: Ibis redibis nunquam in bello peribis; "I say to thee, Pyrrhus the Romans shall overcome. Thou shalt go, thou shalt return never in war shalt thou perish." \textsuperscript{8} yet one man, but I hate him, ; , ; good; concerning me; Let not the \textsuperscript{10} having put; void place Heb. floor all the prophets \textsuperscript{11} horns of iron; Thus saith \textsuperscript{15} shall we go Go and prosper This was strong irony; they were the precise words of the false prophets; but were spoken by Micaiah in such a tone and manner as at once shewed Ahab that he did not believe, but ridiculed these words of uncertainty. The reply of the Delphian oracle to Crosesus was as ambiguous as that returned to Pyrrhus, Croesus Halym penetrans magnam pervertet opum vim, "If Croesus crosses the Halys, he will overthrow a great empire." \section*{2 Kings Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Jeremiah (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Conservative tradition reads 1-2 Kings as one prophetic history shaped from royal and prophetic records, commonly linked with Jeremiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Later Scripture consistently treats the fall of Samaria and Jerusalem as real covenant judgments exactly as Kings presents them.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} exilic composition using earlier records and prophetic material\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology runs from Ahaziah and Elisha through the falls of Samaria and Jerusalem and the exile.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same exile-centered history while differing at points from the MT in names, order, and phrasing.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The decline of both kingdoms to exile, with prophetic ministries including Elisha, Isaiah's era, and the final collapse of Judah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To explain exile as covenant judgment while preserving hope through prophetic witness and Davidic continuity.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} exile; covenant curse; prophetic warning; reform; apostasy; remnant\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Elisha and kings 1-8; Jehu and later northern kingdom 9-17; Judah's decline to exile 18-25.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Kings fragments are sparse Second Temple period | Subst. As with 1 Kings, the main early full-book comparison is between the later Hebrew tradition and the ancient Greek witnesses n/a | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve 2 Kings in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Retelling of the exilic catastrophe by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Kings is central to evaluating how MT and LXX preserve royal and exilic history, especially in synchronisms and proper names.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 2 Kings as true prophetic interpretation of Israel's fall under God's covenant sanctions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Kings IV}
\markboth{KINGS IV}{}
\subsection*{Kings IV 1}
\markright{KINGS IV 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Achaab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ochozias fell through the lattice that was in his upper chamber in Samaria and was sick; and he sent messengers, and said to them, Go and enquire of Baal fly, the god of Accaron, whether I shall recover of this my sickness. And they went to enquire of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And an angel of the Lord called Eliu the Thesbite, saying, Arise, and go to meet the messengers of Ochozias king of Samaria, and you shall say to them, [Is it] because there is no God in Israel, [that] you⌃ go to enquire of Baal fly, the God of Accaron? but [it shall] not [be] so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For thus says the Lord, The bed on which you are gone up, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die. And Eliu went, and said [so] to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, Why have you⌃ returned? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they said to him, A man came up to meet us, and said to us, Go, return to the king that sent you, and say to him, Thus says the Lord, [Is it] because there is no God in Israel, [that] you go to enquire of Baal fly, the God of Accaron? [it shall] not [be] so: the bed on which you are gone up, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So they returned and reported to the king as Eliu said: and he said to them, What [was] the manner of the man who went up to meet you, and spoke to you these words? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said to him, [He was] a hairy man, and girded with a leather girdle about his loins. And he said, This is Eliu the Thesbite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he sent to him a captain of fifty and his fifty; and he went up to him: and, behold, Eliu sat on the top of a mountain. And the captain of fifty spoke to him, and said, O man of God, the king has called you, come down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Eliu answered and said to the captain of fifty, And if I [am] a man of God, fire shall come down out of heaven, and devour you and your fifty. And fire came down out of heaven, and devoured him and his fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the king sent a second time to him another captain of fifty, and his fifty. And the captain of fifty spoke to him, and said, O man of God, thus says the king, Come down quickly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Eliu answered and spoke to him, and said, If I [am] a man of God, fire shall come down out of heaven, and devour you and your fifty. And fire came down out of heaven, and devoured him and his fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king sent yet again a captain and his fifty. And the third captain of fifty came, and knelt on his knees before Eliu, and entreated him, and spoke to him and said, O man of God, let my life, and the life of these fifty your servants, be precious in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Behold, fire came down from heaven, and devoured the two first captains of fifty: and now, I pray, let my life be precious in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the angel of the Lord spoke to Eliu, and said, Go down with him, be not afraid of them. And Eliu rose up, and went down with him to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Eliu spoke to him, and said, Thus says the Lord, Why have you sent messengers to enquire of Baal fly, the god of Accaron? [it shall] not [be] so: the bed on which you are gone up, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So he died according to the word of the Lord which Eliu has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the rest of the acts of Ochozias which he did, behold, [are] they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? and Joram son of Achaab reigns over Israel in Samaria twelve years [beginning] in the eighteenth year of Josaphat king of Juda: and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, only not as his brethren, nor as his mother: and he removed the pillars of Baal which his father made, and broke them in pieces: only he was joined to the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who led Israel to sin; he departed not from them. And the Lord was very angry with the house of Achaab.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a lattice The flat roofs of the eastern houses are generally surrounded by a parapet wall breast high; but instead of this, some terraces are guarded with balustrades only, or latticed work. Of the same kind, probably, was the lattice, or net, as the term shevacha seems to import, through which Ahaziah fell into the court. This incident proves the necessity of the law for the formation of battlements for roof ( ), which God graciously dictated from Sinai, which furnishes a beautiful example of his paternal care and goodness; for the terrace was a place where many offices of the family were performed, and business frequently transacted.; was sick *marg.; Baalzebub, ; Beelzebub god; whether \textsuperscript{3} angel; Elijah; Arise it, ; ye go \textsuperscript{4} Thou shalt etc. Heb. The bed whither thou art gone up, thou shalt not come down from it but shalt \textsuperscript{7} What manner of man was he Heb. What was the manner of the man \textsuperscript{8} an hairy man That is, he wore a rough garment, either made of camels' hair, as that of John Baptist, or of a skin, dressed with the hair on. Sir J. Chardin informs us, in a manuscript note on this place, cited by Mr. Harmer, that the eastern dervishes and fakeers are clothed just as Elijah was, with a hairy garment, girded with a leathern girdle. \textsuperscript{9} sent unto;, ; he sat; Thou man \textsuperscript{10} If I be a man; let fire Or, rather, as the original literally imports, and the LXX render, καταβησεται πυρ, fire shall come down; Elijah's words being simply declarative, and not imprecatory.; consumed \textsuperscript{13} he sent again; fell on Heb. bowed, besought; O man of God \textsuperscript{15} be not afraid of him \textsuperscript{16} Forasmuch;, Baalzebub Literally, "the lord of flies; " or, as the LXX render, Βααλ μυεαν θεον, Baal the fly god. See note on . on which thou art gone up In the East there is usually at the end of each chamber a little gallery, raised three or four feet above the floor, with a balustrade in front, to which they go up by a few steps. Here they place their beds; an allusion to which situation is involved in this declaration of Elijah's, and frequently referred to in the Sacred Scriptures. See note on . \textsuperscript{17} Jehoram As it is said in, that he began his reign in the eighteenth of Jehoshaphat, it is supposed that Jehoshaphat admitted his son Jehoram to reign with him eight or nine years before his death. "The second year that Jehoram was Prorex, and the eighteenth of Jehoshaphat." in the second\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 2}
\markright{KINGS IV 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, when the Lord was going to take Eliu with a whirlwind as it were into heaven, that Eliu and Elisaie went out of Galgala. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Eliu said to Elisaie, Stay here, I pray you; for God has sent me to Baethel. And Elisaie said, [As] the Lord lives and your soul lives, I will not leave you; so they came to Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the sons of the prophets who were in Baethel came to Elisaie, and said to him, Do you know, that the Lord this day is going to take your lord away from your head? And he said, Yes, I know [it]; be silent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Eliu said to Elisaie, Stay here, I pray you; for the Lord has sent me to Jericho. And he said, [As] the Lord lives and your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they came to Jericho. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho drew near to Elisaie, and said to him, Do you know that the Lord is about to take away your master today from your head? And he said, Yes, I know [it]; hold your peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Eliu said to him, Stay here, I pray you, for the Lord has sent me to Jordan. And Elisaie said, [As] the Lord lives and your soul lives, I will not leave you: and they both went on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And fifty men of the sons of the prophets [went also], and they stood opposite afar off: and both stood on [the bank] of Jordan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Eliu took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and struck the water: and the water was divided on this side and on that side, and they both went over on dry ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass while they were crossing over, that Eliu said to Elisaie, Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken up from you. And Elisaie said, Let there be, I pray you, a double [portion] of your spirit upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Eliu said, You have asked a hard thing: if you shall see me when I am taken up from you, then shall it be so to you; and if not, it shall not be [so]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass as they were going, they went on talking; and, behold, a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and it separated between them both; and Eliu was taken up in a whirlwind as it were into heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Elisaie saw, and cried, Father, father, the chariot of Israel, and the horseman thereof! And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his garments, and tore them into two pieces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Elisaie took up the mantle of Eliu, which fell from off him upon Elisaie; and Elisaie returned, and stood upon the brink of Jordan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and he took the mantle of Eliu, which fell from off him, and struck the water, and said, Where is the Lord God of Eliu? and he struck the waters, and they were divided hither and there; and Elisaie went over. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho on the opposite side saw him, and said, The spirit of Eliu has rested upon Elisaie. And they came to meet him, and did obeisance to him to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they said to him, Behold now, [there are] with your servants fifty men of strength: let them go now, and seek your lord: perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has taken him up, and cast him into Jordan, or on one of the mountains, or on one of the hills. And Elisaie said, You⌃ shall not send. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they pressed him until he was ashamed; and he said, Send. And they sent fifty men, and sought three days, and found him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they returned to him, for he lived in Jericho: and Elisaie said, Did I not say to you, Go not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the men of the city said to Elisaie, Behold, the situation of the city [is] good, as [our] lord sees; but the waters [are] bad, and the ground barren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Elisaie said, Bring me a new pitcher, and put salt in it. And they took [one], and brought [it] to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Elisaie went out to the spring of the waters, and cast salt therein, and says, Thus says the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be any longer death thence or barren [land]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the waters were healed until this day, according to the word of Elisaie which he spoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he went up thence to Baethel: and as he was going up by the way there came up also little children from the city, and mocked him, and said to him, Go up, bald-head, go up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he turned after them, and saw them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And, behold, there came out two bears out of the wood, and they tore forty and two children of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he went thence to mount Carmel, and returned thence to Samaria.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} take up; by a whirlwind; Elisha Gilgal \textsuperscript{2} Tarry here; As the Lord, ; I will not; Bethel \textsuperscript{3} And the sons, ; thy master \textsuperscript{5} the sons i.e. as the Targumist renders, talmeedey neveeya, "disciples of the prophets, " thy master; , I know it \textsuperscript{7} fifty men; to view afar off Heb. in sight, or over against \textsuperscript{8} his mantle Την μηλωτην αυτου, his sheep skin, says the Septuagint; the skins of sheep being formerly worn by prophets as the simple insignia of their office. See note on ., were \textsuperscript{9} Ask what; , Elisha said; a double portion This probably refers to the law respecting the first-born, who had a double portion of the property of his father. As Elisha may have considered himself as the first-born of Elijah, so he requested a double portion of his spiritual influence. \textsuperscript{10} Thou hast; asked a hard thing Heb. done hard in asking if thou see \textsuperscript{11} by a whirlwind into heaven \textsuperscript{12} saw it My father; he saw him; rent them \textsuperscript{13} the mantle; bank Heb. lip \textsuperscript{15} to view The spirit; bowed \textsuperscript{16} strong men Heb. sons of strength the Spirit;, ; some mountain Heb. one of the mountains \textsuperscript{17} they urged; found him not \textsuperscript{19} my Lord seeth; the water; barren Heb. causing to miscarry \textsuperscript{21} cast; I have healed; there shall \textsuperscript{23} Bethel;, little children The words nearim ketannim not only signify little children but young men; for katon signifies not only little, but young, in opposition to old; and naar signifies not only a child, but a young man grown to years of maturity. Thus Isaac is called naar when twenty-eight years old, Joseph when thirty-nine, and Rehoboam when forty. These idolatrous young men, having heard of the ascension of Elijah, without believing it, blasphemously bade Elisha to follow him. The venerable prophet, from a Divine impulse, pronounced a curse "in the name of the Lord, " which was immediately followed by the most terrible judgment; thus evincing the Source from which it flowed., ; mocked; Go up \textsuperscript{24} cursed them; , ; she bears; children of them\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 3}
\markright{KINGS IV 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Joram the son of Achaab began to reign in Israel in the eighteenth year of Josaphat king of Juda, and he reigned twelve years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, only not as his father, nor as his mother: and he removed the pillars of Baal which his father had made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Only he adhered to the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who made Israel to sin; he departed not from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Mosa king of Moab was a sheep-master, and he rendered to the king of Israel in the beginning [of the year], one hundred thousand lambs, and one hundred thousand rams, with the wool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass, after the death of Achaab, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And king Joram went forth in that day out of Samaria, and numbered Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he went and sent to Josaphat king of Juda, saying, The king of Moab has rebelled against me: will you go with me against Moab to war? And he said, I will go up: you are as I, I am as you; as my people, so [is] your people, as my horses, so [are] your horses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said, What way shall I go up? and he said, The way of the wilderness of Edom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king of Israel went, and the king of Juda, and the king of Edom: and they fetched a compass of seven days' journey; and there was no water for the army, and for the cattle that went with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king of Israel said, Alas! that the Lord should have called the three kings on their way, to give them into the hand of Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Josaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may enquire of the Lord by him? And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, [There is] here Elisaie son of Saphat, who poured water on the hands of Eliu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Josaphat said, He has the word of the Lord. And the king of Israel, and Josaphat king of Juda, and the king of Edom, went down to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Elisaie said to the king of Israel, What have I to do with you? go to the prophets of your father, and the prophets of your mother. And the king of Israel said to him, Has the Lord called the three kings to deliver them into the hands of Moab? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Elisaie said, [As] the Lord of hosts before whom I stand lives, unless I regarded the presence of Josaphat the king of Juda, I would not have looked on you, nor seen you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now fetch me a harper. And it came to pass, as the harper harped, that the hand of the Lord came upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said, Thus says the Lord, Make this valley full of trenches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For thus says the Lord, You⌃ shall not see wind, neither shall you⌃ see rain, yet this valley shall be filled with water, and you⌃, and your flocks, and your cattle shall drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And this [is] a light [thing] in the eyes of the Lord: I will also deliver Moab into your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you⌃ shall strike every strong city, and you⌃ shall cut down every good tree, and you⌃ shall stop all wells of water, and spoil every good piece [of land] with stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass in the morning, when the sacrifice was offered, that, behold! waters came from the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all Moab heard that the three kings were come up to fight against them; and they cried out on every [side, even] all that were girded with a girdle, and they said, Ho! and stood upon the border. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they rose early in the morning, and the sun rose upon the waters, and Moab saw the waters on the opposite side red as blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they said, This [is] the blood of the sword; and the kings have fought, and each man has struck his neighbor; now then to the spoils, Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they entered into the camp of Israel; and Israel arose and struck Moab, and they fled from before them; and they went on and struck Moab as they went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they razed the cities, and cast every man his stone on every good piece [of land] and filled it; and they stopped every well, and cut down every good tree, until they left [only] the stones of the wall cast down; and the slingers compassed [the land], and struck it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king of Moab saw that the battle prevailed against him; and he took with him seven hundred men that drew sword, to cut through to the king of Edom: and they could not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he took his oldest son whom he had designed to reign in his stead, and offered him up for a whole burnt offering on the walls. And there was a great indignation against Israel; and they departed from him, and returned to their land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} wrought, but not, and like; image Heb. statue Baal \textsuperscript{3} he cleaved which made, he departed \textsuperscript{8} the wilderness of Edom The wilderness of Edom was probably the same as that of Zin or Kadesh, through which the children of Israel passed; extending southward from the Dead Sea, to the eastern branch of the Red Sea. See note on . \textsuperscript{9} Edom no water;, that followed them Heb. at their feet, *marg. \textsuperscript{11} Is there not here; that we may;, ;, poured water That is, was his constant and confidential servant. Mr. Hanway, speaking of a Persian supper, says, "Supper being now brought in, a servant presented a basin of water, and a napkin hung over his shoulders; he went to every one in the company, and poured water on their hands to wash." \textsuperscript{13} What; get; the prophets, Nay \textsuperscript{14} As the Lord; I regard; I would not look \textsuperscript{15} bring me This was evidently intended to soothe and tranquillize the prophet's mind, which had been agitated and discomposed with holy indignation by the presence of the idolatrous king, and the recollection of his abomination. The soothing influence of music is generally acknowledged in every civilized nation., ; the hand \textsuperscript{17} Ye shall not;, that ye may \textsuperscript{18} And this; a light; he will \textsuperscript{19} And ye; fell mar Heb. grieve \textsuperscript{20} when the meat; there came water This supply was altogether miraculous; for there was neither wind nor rain, nor any other natural means to furnish it. filled \textsuperscript{21} gathered Heb. were cried together put on armour Heb. gird himself with a girdle. \textsuperscript{23} This is blood, slain Heb. destroyed now therefore \textsuperscript{24} smote the; went forward or, smote in it even \textsuperscript{25} beat down; stopped; and felled only in etc. Heb. until he left the stones thereof in Kir-haraseth Kirharaseth Supposed to be the same as Ar, or Areopolis, the capital of Moab.;, Kir-heres \textsuperscript{26} unto the king of Edom \textsuperscript{27} offered him In cases of great extremity, it was customary in various heathen nations, to offer human sacrifices, and even their own children. This was frequent among the Phoenicians, Greeks, Romans, Scythians, Gauls, Africans, and others; and was the natural fruit of a religious system, which had for the objects of its worship cruel and merciless divinities. The king of Moab, in this case, sacrificed his son to obtain the favour of Chemosh his god, who, being a devil, delighted in blood and murder, and the destruction of mankind. The dearer anything was to them, the more acceptable those idolaters thought the sacrifice, and therefore burnt their children in the fire to their honour.; they departed\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 4}
\markright{KINGS IV 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And one of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried to Elisaie, saying, Your servant my husband is dead; and you know that your servant feared the Lord: and the creditor is come to take my two sons to be his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Elisaie said, What shall I do for you? tell me what you have in the house. And she said, Your servant has nothing in the house, except oil wherewith I anoint myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said to her, Go, borrow for yourself vessels without of all your neighbors, [even] empty vessels; borrow not a few. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall go in and shut the door upon you and upon your sons, and you shall pour forth into these vessels, and remove that which is filled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she departed from him, and shut the door upon herself and upon her sons: they brought the vessels near to her, and she poured in until the vessels were filled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And she said to her sons, Bring me yet a vessel. And they said to her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And she came and told the man of God: and Elisaie said, Go, and sell the oil, and you shall pay your debts, and you and your sons shall live of the remaining oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And a day came, when Elisaie passed over to Soman, and [there was] a great lady there, and she constrained him to eat bread: and it came to pass as often as he went into [the city, that] he turned aside to eat there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the woman said to her husband, See now, I know that this [is] a holy man of God who comes over continually to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let us now make for him an upper chamber, a small place; and let us put there for him a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall come to pass that when he comes in to us, he shall turn in there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And a day came, and he went in there, and turned aside into the upper chamber, and lay there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said to Giezi his servant, Call me this Somanite. and he called her, and she stood before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, you have taken all this trouble for us; what should I do for you? Have you any request [to make] to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she said, I dwell in the midst of my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said to Giezi, What must we do for her? and Giezi his servant said, Indeed she has no son, and her husband [is] old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he called her, and she stood by the door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Elisaie said to her, At this time [next year], as the season [is], you [shall be] alive, and embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, do not lie to your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the woman conceived, and bore a son at the very time, as the season was, being alive, as Elisaie said to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the child grew: and it came to pass when he went out to his father to the reapers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} that he said to his father, My head, my head. and [his father] said to a servant, carry him to his mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he carried him to his mother, and he lay upon her knees till noon, and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she carried him up and laid him on the bed of the man of god; and she shut the door upon him, and went out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And she called her husband, and said, Send now for me one of the young men, and one of the asses, and I will ride quickly to the man of God, and return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he said, Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon, nor the Sabbath. And she said, [It is] well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And she saddled the ass, and said to her servant, Be quick, proceed: spare not on my account to ride, unless I shall tell you. Go, and you shall proceed, and come to the man of God to mount Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And she rode and came to the man of God to the mountain: and it came to pass when Elisaie saw her coming, that he said to Giezi his servant, See now, that Somanite comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Now run to meet her, and you shall say, [Is it] well with you? [is it] well with your husband? [is it] well with the child? and she said, [It is] well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And she came to Elisaie to the mountain, and laid hold of his feet; and Giezi drew near to thrust her away. And Elisaie said, Let her alone, for her soul [is] much grieved in her, and the Lord has hidden [it] from me, and has not told [it] me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And she said, Did I ask a son of my lord? For did I not say, Do not deal deceitfully with me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Elisaie said to Giezi, Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go: if you meet any man, you shall not salute him, and if a man salute you you shall not answer him: and you shall lay my staff on the child's face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the mother of the child said, [As] the Lord lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you. And Elisaie arose, and went after her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Giezi went on before her, and laid his staff on the child's face: but there was neither voice nor any hearing. So he returned to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not awaked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Elisaie went into the house, and, behold, the dead child was laid upon his bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Elisaie went into the house, and shut the door upon themselves, the two, and prayed to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and bowed himself upon him, and the flesh of the child grew warm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he returned, and walked up and down in the house: and he went up, and bowed himself on the child seven times; and the child opened his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Elisaie cried out to Giezi, and said, Call this Somanite. So he called her, and she came in to him: and Elisaie said, Take your son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the woman went in, and fell at his feet, and did obeisance [bowing] to the ground; and she took her son, and went out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Elisaie returned to Galgala: and a famine [was] in the land; and the sons of the prophets sat before him: and Elisaie said to his servant, Set on the great pot, and boil pottage for the sons of the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a vine in the field, and gathered of it wild gourds, his garment full; and he cast it into the caldron of pottage, for they knew [them] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And he poured it out for the men to eat: and it came to pass, when they were eating of the pottage, that behold! they cried out, and said, [There is] death in the pot, O man of God. And they could not eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And he said, Take meal, and cast it into the pot. And Elisaie said to his servant Giezi, Pour out for the people, and let them eat. And there was no longer there any hurtful thing in the pot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And there came a man over from Baetharisa, and brought to the man of God twenty barley loaves and cakes of figs, of the first fruits. And he said, Give to the people, and let them eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And his servant said, Why should I set this before one hundred men? and he said, Give to the people, and let them eat; for thus says the Lord, They shall eat and leave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And they ate and left, according to the word of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3110, bc 894 sons, ; thy servant did fear; , ; the creditor \textsuperscript{2} What shall I; save a pot of oil \textsuperscript{3} empty vessels; borrow not a few Heb. scant not \textsuperscript{4} thou shalt shut; and shalt pour \textsuperscript{6} when the vessels;, ; And the oil \textsuperscript{8} it fell on Heb. there was, Shunem This city was situated in the tribe of Issachar, five miles south from mount Tabor, according to Eusebius; and is probably the place which he calls Sanim, in Acrabatene, in the neighbourhood of Samaria or Sebaste.; a great woman; she constrained him Heb. she laid hold on him \textsuperscript{9} she said; this is; man of God \textsuperscript{10} Let us; a little chamber An aleeyah, or oleah, as the Arabs call it; a small back house annexed to the principal dwelling, in which the prophet could live in a great privacy as in his own house, and to which he could retire at pleasure, without breaking in upon the private affairs of the family, or being in his turn interrupted by them in his devotions. See note on, and see note on \textsuperscript{13} thou hast; to the king; to the captain; I dwell; among mine \textsuperscript{16} About this, season Heb. set time thou shalt; my lord do not lie \textsuperscript{19} My head From this peculiar exclamation, and the season of the year, it is probable he was affected by the coup de soleil, or stroke of the sun, which is by no means uncommon in hot climates, and often proves fatal. \textsuperscript{20} his mother; and then died \textsuperscript{23} new moon; well Heb. peace \textsuperscript{24} Then she; an ass These animals were not anciently, as now, used only by the lower classes, but were in general use among the noble and chief personages of the East, and it was not unusual for even the husband to walk by the side of his wife while thus riding; the driver, as was the custom, following. The Shunammite, when she went to the prophet, did not desire so much attendance; but only requested her husband to send her an ass and its driver. Drive slack not thy riding for me Heb. restrain not for me to ride \textsuperscript{26} Run now Is it well with thee; It is well \textsuperscript{27} him by the feet Heb. by his feet; thrust; Let her alone; vexed Heb. bitter; hid it from me \textsuperscript{28} Did I desire Do not \textsuperscript{29} Gird up thy loins; take my; salute him not lay my staff \textsuperscript{30} As the Lord, I will not \textsuperscript{31} neither voice; hearing Heb. attention, not awaked \textsuperscript{35} to and fro Heb. once hither and once thither and the child opened \textsuperscript{36} Call this Shunammite Take up \textsuperscript{38} Elisha; a dearth; the sons; were sitting;, ; Set on the great pot \textsuperscript{39} a wild vine; wild gourds The word pakkuoth, from peka, in Chaldee, to burst, and in Syriac, to crack, thunder, is generally supposed to be the fruits of the coloquintida, or colocynth; whose leaves are large, placed alternately, very much like those of the vine, whence it might be called a wild vine. The flowers are white, and the fruit of the gourd kind, of the size of a large apple, and when ripe, of a yellow colour, and a pleasant and inviting appearance. It ranks among vegetable poisons, as all intense bitters do; but, judiciously employed, it is of considerable use in medicine. It is said that the fruit, when ripe, is so full of wind that it bursts, and throws its liquor and seeds to a great distance, and if touched, before it breaks of itself, it flies open with an explosion, and discharges its foetid contents in the face of him who touched it. \textsuperscript{41} he cast, ; there harm Heb. evil thing \textsuperscript{42} Baalshalisha, bread; of barley; the husk thereof or, his scrip, or garment, Note: Parched corn, or corn to be parched; full ears before they are ripe, parched on the fire. A very frequent food in the East. The loaves were probably extremely small, as their loaves of bread still are in eastern countries. But small as this may appear, it would be a considerable present in the time of famine; though very inadequate to the number of persons. Baal-shalisha, of which the person who made this seasonable present was an inhabitant, was situated, according to Eusebius and Jerome, fifteen miles north of Diospolis, or Lydda. \textsuperscript{43} his servitor What; They shall eat\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 5}
\markright{KINGS IV 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now Naiman, the captain of the host of Syria, was a great man before his master, and highly respected, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria, and the man was mighty in strength, [but] a leper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Syrians went forth in small bands, and took captive out of the land of Israel a little maid: and she waited on Naiman's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And she said to her mistress, O that my lord were before the prophet of God in Samaria; then he would recover him from his leprosy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And she went in and told her lord, and said, Thus and thus spoke the maid from the land of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king of Syria said to Naiman, Go to, go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel. And he went, and took in his hand ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now then, as soon as this letter shall reach you, behold, I have sent to you my servant Naiman, and you shall recover him from his leprosy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass, when the king of Israel read the letter, [that] he tore his garments, and said, [Am] I God, to kill and to make alive, that this [man] sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy? consider, however, I pray you, and see that this [man] seeks an occasion against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass, when Elisaie heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments, that he sent to the king of Israel, saying, Therefore have you torn your garments? Let Naiman, I pray you, come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So Naiman came with horse and chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisaie. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Elisaie sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash seven times in Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be cleansed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Naiman was angry, and departed, and said, Behold, I said, He will by all means come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of his God, and lay his hand upon the place, and recover the leper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [Are] not the Abana and Pharphar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not go and wash in them, and be cleansed? and he turned and went away in a rage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And his servants came near and said to him, [Suppose] the prophet had spoken a great thing to you, would you not perform it? yet he has but said to you, Wash, and be cleansed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So Naiman went down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the word of Elisaie: and his flesh returned to him as the flesh of a little child, and he was cleansed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he and all his company returned to Elisaie, and he came and stood before him, and said, Behold, I know that there is no God in all the earth, save only in Israel: and now receive a blessing of your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Elisaie said, [As] the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not take [one]. And he pressed him to take [one]: but he would not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Naiman said, Well then, if not, let there be given to your servant, I pray you, the load [of a] yoke of mules; and you shall give me of the red earth: for henceforth your servant will not offer whole burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the Lord by [reason of] this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And let the Lord be propitious to your servant when my master goes into the house of Remman to worship there, and he shall lean on my hand, and I shall bow down in the house of Remman when he bows down in the house of Remman; even let the Lord, I pray, be merciful to your servant in this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Elisaie said to Naiman, Go in peace. And he departed from him a little way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Giezi the servant of Elisaie said, Behold, my Lord has spared this Syrian Naiman, so as not to take of his hand what he has brought: as the Lord lives, I will surely run after him, and take somewhat of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So Giezi followed after Naiman: and Naiman saw him running after him, and turned back from his chariot to meet him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [Giezi] said, All is well: my master has sent me, saying, Behold, now are there come to me two young men of the sons of the prophets from mount Ephraim; give them, I pray you, a talent of silver, and two changes of raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And [Naiman] said, Take two talents of silver. And he took two talents of silver in two bags, and two changes of raiment, and put them upon two of his servants, and they bore them before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he came to a secret place, and took them from their hands, and laid them up in the house, and dismissed the men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he went in himself and stood before his master; and Elisaie said to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Whence [come you], Giezi? and Giezi said, Your servant has not been hither or there. And Elisaie said to him, Went not my heart with you, when the man returned from his chariot to meet you? and now you have received silver, and now you have received raiment, and olive yards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The leprosy also of Naiman shall cleave to you, and to your seed for ever. And he went out from his presence leprous, like snow.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3110, bc 894 Naaman a great; with Heb. before honourable or, gracious, Heb. lifted up, or accepted in countenance by him; deliverance or, victory a leper \textsuperscript{2} by companies; waited on Heb. was before \textsuperscript{3} Would God; with Heb. before he would; recover him of Heb. gather in \textsuperscript{5} go; and took; with him Heb. in his hand ten talents of silver This, at 353£. 11s. 10+d. the talent, would amount to 3, 535£. 18s. 9d. six thousand If shekels are meant, as the Arabic reads, then this, at 1£. 16s. 5d. each, will amount to 10, 925£.; and the whole to 14, 464£. 18s. 9d.. Besides the value of the ten changes of raiment. ten changes \textsuperscript{7} that he rent, ; Amos I God; see how \textsuperscript{8} rent his clothes; let him come, ; and he shall \textsuperscript{10} sent a messenger wash, ; seven times, ; thy flesh \textsuperscript{11} Naaman; went away; Behold; , I thought etc. Heb. I said, etc. or, I said with myself, He will surely come out, etc. strike. Heb. move up and down. \textsuperscript{12} Abana and Pharpar or, Amana, This river is evidently the Barrada, or Barda, as the Arabic renders, the Chrysorrhoas of the Greeks, which taking its rise in Antilibanus, runs eastward towards Damascus, where it is divided into three streams, one of which passes through the city, and the other two through the gardens; which reuniting at the east of the city, forms a lake about five or six leagues to the south-east, called Behairat el Marj, or, Lake of the Meadow. Pharpar was probably one of the branches. better \textsuperscript{13} his servants; My father, ; how much rather, Wash \textsuperscript{14} went he down; according to; his flesh; and he was clean \textsuperscript{15} he returned now I know; a blessing \textsuperscript{16} As the Lord; I will receive \textsuperscript{18} and he leaneth This verse should probably, as many learned men have supposed, be read in the past, and not in the future tense: "In this thing the Lord pardon thy servant, that when my master went into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaned on my hand, and I worshipped in the house of Rimmon; in that I have worshipped in the house of Rimmon, the Lord pardon thy servant in this thing." Rimmon is supposed by Selden to the same with Elion, a god of the Phoenicians, borrowed undoubtedly from the Elyon of the Hebrews, one of the names of God., and I bow; the Lord pardon \textsuperscript{19} he said; Go in peace; little way Heb. a little piece of ground, *marg. \textsuperscript{20} Gehazi, ; my master; as the Lord liveth; and take \textsuperscript{21} he lighted; Is all well Heb. Is there peace \textsuperscript{22} My master; the sons; give them a talent \textsuperscript{23} Be content; And he urged him, bound *marg. and they bare \textsuperscript{24} tower or, secret place and bestowed \textsuperscript{25} stood before; Whence;, Thy servant; no whither Heb. not hither or thither \textsuperscript{26} he said; Went; Is it a time \textsuperscript{27} leprosy; unto thy seed; a leper\par}
