\subsection*{Kings IV 6}
\markright{KINGS IV 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the sons of the prophets said to Elisaie, Behold now, the place wherein we dwell before you is too narrow for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let us go, we pray you, to Jordan, and take thence every man a beam, and make for ourselves a habitation there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said, Go. And one of them said gently, Come with your servants. And he said, I will go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he went with them, and they came to Jordan, and began to cut down wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And behold, one was cutting down a beam, and the axe head fell into the water: and he cried out, Alas! master: and it was hidden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the man of God said, Where did it fall? and he showed him the place: and he broke off a stick, and threw it in there, and the iron came to the surface. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said, Take it up to yourself. And he stretched out his hand, and took it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king of Syria was at war with Israel: and he consulted with his servants, saying, I will encamp in such a place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Elisaie sent to the king of Israel, saying, Take heed that you pass not by that place, for the Syrians are hidden there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king of Israel sent to the place which Elisaie mentioned to him, and saved himself thence not once or twice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the mind of the king of Syria was very much disturbed concerning this thing; and he called his servants, and said to them, Will you⌃ not tell me who betrays me to the king of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And one of his servants said, Nay, my Lord, O king, for Elisaie the prophet that is in Israel reports to the king of Israel all the words whatever you may say in your bedchamber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said, Go, see where this man [is], and I will send and take him. And they sent word to him, saying, Behold, [he is] in Dothaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he sent there horses, and chariots, and a mighty host: and they came by night, and compassed about the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the servant of Elisaie rose up early and went out; and, behold, a host compassed the city, and horses and chariots: and the servant said to him, O master, what shall we do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Elisaie said, Fear not, for they who are with us [are] more than they that are with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Elisaie prayed, and said, Lord, open, I pray you, the eyes of the servant, and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw: and, behold, the mountain [was] full of horses, and there were chariots of fire round about Elisaie. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they came down to him; and he prayed to the Lord, and said, Strike, I pray you, this people with blindness. And he struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisaie. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Elisaie said to them, This [is] not the city, and this [is] not the way: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you⌃ seek. And he led them away to Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it came to pass when they entered into Samaria, that Elisaie said, Open, I pray you, O Lord, their eyes, and let them see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, they were in the midst of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king of Israel said to Elisaie, when he saw them, Shall I [not] verily strike them, [my] father? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he said, You shall not strike them, unless you would strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow: set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink, and depart to their master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank: and he dismissed them and they departed to their master. And the bands of Syria came no longer into the land of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it came to pass after this, that the son of Ader king of Syria gathered all his army, and went up, and besieged Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was [valued] at fifty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung at five pieces of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, and a woman cried to him, saying, Help, my lord, O king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he said to her, Unless the Lord help you, whence shall I help you? from the corn-floor, or from the wine-press? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the king said to her, What is [the matter] with you? And the woman said to him, This [woman] said to me, Give your son, and we will eat him today, and we will eat my son to-morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So we boiled my son, and ate him; and I said to her on the second day, Give your son, and let us eat him: and she has hidden her son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And it came to pass, when the king of Israel heard the words of the woman, [that] he tore his garments; and he passed by on the wall, and the people saw sackcloth within upon his flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said, God do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisaie shall stand upon him this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Elisaie was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him; and [the king] sent a man before him: before the messenger came to him, he also said to the elders, Do you⌃ see that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? See, as soon as the messenger shall have come, shut the door, and forcibly detain him at the door: [is] not the sound of his master's feet behind him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} While he was yet speaking with them, behold, a messenger came to him: and he said, Behold, this evil [is] of the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the sons; the place; too strait for us \textsuperscript{3} Be content; go with thy \textsuperscript{5} ax head Heb. iron; master;, for it was borrowed \textsuperscript{6} he cut down This could have no natural tendency to raise the iron and cause it to swim. It was only a sign, or ceremony, which the prophet chose to employ on the occasion.; the iron This was the real miracle; for the gravity of the metal must otherwise still have kept it at the bottom of the river. \textsuperscript{7} Take it up; put out \textsuperscript{8} the king;, took; camp or, encamping \textsuperscript{10} sent to the place To see if it were so. But the Vulgate renders, misit rex Israel ad locum, et preoccupavit eum; "the king of Israel sent to the place, and pre-occupied it; " which is very likely, though not expressed in the Hebrew Text.; warned him; saved \textsuperscript{12} None Heb. The utmost he ought to have done with these men, when thus brought into his hand, was to make them prisoners of war., shall \textsuperscript{22} wouldest; thy sword; set bread \textsuperscript{23} he prepared; So the bands That is, for a considerable time. They are besides in the greatest repute after they are parched in pans and ovens; then assuming the name leblebby; " and he thinks they were so called from being pointed at one end, and acquiring an ash colour in parching. \textsuperscript{27} If the Lord etc. or, Let not the Lord save thee whence \textsuperscript{28} What aileth thee; Give thy son \textsuperscript{29} next Heb. other she hath hid \textsuperscript{31} God do so; if the head \textsuperscript{32} the elders, ere the messenger, See ye how son of a murderer, the sound \textsuperscript{33} this evil is of the Lord; , ; wait for the\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 7}
\markright{KINGS IV 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elisaie said, Hear you the word of the Lord; Thus says the Lord, As at this time, to-morrow a measure of fine flour [shall be sold] for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gates of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the officer on whose hand the king rested, answered Elisaie, and said, Behold, [if] the Lord shall make flood-gates in heaven, might this thing be? and Elisaie said, Behold, you shall see with your eyes, but shall not eat thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And there were four leprous men by the gate of the city: and one said to his neighbor, Why sit we here until we die? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If we should say, Let us go into the city, then [there is] famine in the city, and we shall die there: and if we sit here, then we shall die. Now then come, and let us fall upon the camp of the Syrians: if they should take us alive, then we shall live; and if they should put us to death, then we shall [only] die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they rose up while it was yet night, to go into the camp of Syria; and they came into a part of the camp of Syria, and behold, there [was] no man there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the Lord had made the army of Syria to hear a sound of chariots, and a sound of horses, [even] the sound of a great host: and [each] man said to his fellow, Now has the king of Israel hired against us the kings of the Chettites, and the kings of Egypt, to come against us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they arose and fled while it was yet dark, and left their tents, and their horses, and their asses in the camp, as they were, and fled for their lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And these lepers entered a little way into the camp, and went into one tent, and ate and drank, and took thence silver, and gold, and raiment; and they went and returned thence, and entered into another tent, and took thence, and went and hid [the spoil]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And [one] man said to his neighbor, We are not doing [well] thus: this day is a day of glad tidings, and we hold our peace, and are waiting till the morning light, and shall find mischief: now them come, and let us go into [the city], and report to the house of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So they went and cried toward the gate of the city, and reported to them, saying, We went into the camp of Syria, and, behold, there is not there a man, nor voice of man, only horses tied and asses, and their tents as they were. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the porters cried aloud, and reported to the house of the king within. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king rose up by night, and said to his servants, I will now tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They knew that we are hungry; and they have gone forth from the camp and hidden themselves in the field, saying, They will come out of the city, and we shall catch them alive, and go into the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And one of his servants answered and said, Let them now take five of the horses that were left, which were left here; behold, they are the number left to all the multitude of Israel; and we will send there and see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So they took two horsemen; and the king of Israel sent after the king of Syria, saying, Go, and see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they went after them even to Jordan: and, behold, all the way was full of garments and vessels, which the Syrians had cast away in their panic. and the messengers returned, and brought word to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the people went out, and plundered the camp of Syria: and a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord, and two measures of barley for a shekel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king appointed the officer on whose hand the king leaned [to have charge] over the gate: and the people trampled on him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God [had] said, who spoke when the messenger came down to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So it came to pass as Elisaie had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley [shall be sold] for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel; and it shall be as at this time to-morrow in the gate of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the officer answered Elisaie, and said, Behold, [if] the Lord makes flood-gates in heaven, shall this thing be? and Elisaie said, Behold, you shall see [it] with your eyes, but you shall not eat thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it was so: for the people trampled on him in the gate, and he died.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Elisha said See note on, and see note on .; To morrow;, ; a measure of fine flour A seah of flour. The seah was about two gallons and a half; the shekel 2s. 4d. at the lowest computation. A wide difference between this and the price of the ass's head.; of barley; in the gate of Samaria From this it appears that the gates were not only used as courts of judicature, but as market-places. So Mr. Morier observes: "In our rides we usually went out of the town at the Derwazeh Shah Abdul Azeem, or the gate leading to the village of Shah Abdul Azeem, where a market was held every morning, particularly of horses, mules, asses, and camels. At about sun-rise, the owners of the animals assemble and exhibit them for sale. But besides, here were sellers of all sorts of goods, in temporary shops and tents, and this, perhaps, will explain the custom alluded to in ." \textsuperscript{2} a lord etc. or, a lord which belonged to the king, leaning on his hand, if the Lord; windows; thou shalt see it \textsuperscript{4} we will enter let us fall; if they save us; we shall but die \textsuperscript{6} the Lord, ; the kingss of the Hittites the kings of the Egyptians \textsuperscript{7} they arose; their horses; and fled for their life \textsuperscript{9} they said one; this day; some mischief will come upon us Heb. we shall find punishment \textsuperscript{10} the porter; no man there \textsuperscript{13} one in the city Heb. in it they are even \textsuperscript{16} spoiled the tents; , according to \textsuperscript{17} the lord the people trode upon him\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 8}
\markright{KINGS IV 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elisaie spoke to the woman, whose son he [had] restored to life, saying, Arise, and go you and your house, and sojourn wherever you may sojourn: for the Lord has called for a famine upon the land; indeed it is come upon the land [for] seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the woman arose, and did according to the word of Elisaie, both she and her house; and they sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass after the expiration of the seven years, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines to the city; and came to cry to the king for her house and for her lands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king spoke to Giezi the servant of Elisaie the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray you, all the great things which Elisaie has done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored to life the dead son, behold, the woman whose son Elisaie restored to life [came] crying to the king for her house and for her lands. And Giezi said, My lord, O king, this [is] the woman, and this [is] her son, whom Elisaie restored to life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the king asked the woman, and she told him: and the king appointed her a eunuch, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field from the day that she left the land until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Elisaie came to Damascus; and the king of Syria the son of Ader was ill, and they brought him word, saying, The man of God is come here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king said to Azael, Take in your hand a present, and go to meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this my disease? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Azael went to meet him, and he took a present in his hand, and all the good things of Damascus, forty camels' load, and came and stood before him, and said to Elisaie, Your son the son of Ader, the king of Syria, has sent me to you to enquire, saying, Shall I recover of this my disease? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Elisaie said, Go, say, You shall certainly live; yet the Lord has showed me that you shall surely die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he stood before him, and fixed [his countenance] till he was ashamed: and the man of God wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Azael said, Why does my lord weep? And he said, Because I know all the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: you will utterly destroy their strong holds with fire, and you will kill their choice men with the sword, and you will dash their infants [against the ground], and their women with child you will rip up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Azael said, Who is your servant? a dead dog, that he should do this thing? And Elisaie said, The Lord has shown me you ruling over Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he departed from Elisaie, and went in to his lord; and he said to him, What said Elisaie to you? and he said, He said to me, You shall surely live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass on the next day that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and put it on his face, and he died: and Azael reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} In the fifth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, and while Josaphat was king of Juda, Joram the son of Josaphat king of Juda began to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Achaab; for the daughter of Achaab was his wife: and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But the Lord would not destroy Juda for David his servant's sake, as he said he would give a light to him and to his sons continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Juda, and they made a king over themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Joram went up to Sior, and all the chariots that were with him: and it came to pass after he had arisen, that he struck Edom who compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Juda till this day. Then Lobna revolted at that time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} So Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David: and Ochozias his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} In the twelfth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, Ochozias son of Joram began to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Twenty and two years old [was] Ochozias when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem: and the name of his mother [was] Gotholia, daughter of Ambri king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he walked in the way of the house of Achaab, and did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as did the house of Achaab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he went with Joram the son of Achaab to war against Azael king of the Syrians in Remmoth Galaad; and the Syrians wounded Joram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And king Joram returned to be healed in Jezrael of the wounds with which they wounded him in Remmoth, when he fought with Azael king of Syria. And Ochozias son of Joram went down to see Joram the son of Achaab in Jezrael, because he was sick.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3113, bc 891 whose son, sojourn, ; the Lord, ; called for a famine seven years \textsuperscript{4} the king As it appears not likely that the king would hold conversation with a leprous man; or, that, knowing Gehazi had been dismissed with the highest disgrace from the prophet's service, he would talk with him concerning his late master; some have supposed that this happened before the cleansing of Naaman. But it agrees better with the chronology to consider it as having taken place after that event; the king, probably, having an insatiable curiosity to know the private history of a man who had done such astonishing things. As to the circumstances of Gehazi's disease, he might overlook that, and converse with him, keeping at a reasonable distance, as nothing but actual contact could defile. The pronoun he is generally referred to Hazael; but Dr. Geddes and others are decidedly of the opinion, that we should understand by it Ben-hadad; who, encouraged by the favourable answer of Elisha, as reported by Hazael, adopted a violent remedy to allay the heat of his fever, and put over his face the keever, or fly-net. (See note on ), dipped in water, which suddenly checked the perspiration, and occasioned his death. so that he died, ; Hazael \textsuperscript{16} am 3112, bc 892 Jehoram; began to reign Heb. reigned, "Began to reign in concert with his father." \textsuperscript{18} in the way; the house, ; the daughter;, his wife \textsuperscript{19} for David; light Heb. candle, or lamp \textsuperscript{21} Zair is supposed by Calmet and others to be the same as Seir, the country of Seir the Horite, inhabited by the Edomites or Idumeans. For his father began to reign when he was thirty-two years old, and reigned eight years, and so died, being forty years old. \subsection*{Kings IV 9}
\markright{KINGS IV 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elisaie the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, Gird up your loins, and take this cruse of oil in your hand, and go to Remmoth Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall enter there, and shall see there Ju the son of Josaphat son of Namessi, and shall go in and make him rise up from among his brethren, and shall bring him into a secret chamber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall take the cruse of oil, and pour [it] on his head, and say you, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you king over Israel: and you shall open the door, and flee, and not wait. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the young man the prophet went to Remmoth Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he went in, and, behold, the captains of the host were sitting; and he said, I have a message to you, O captain. And Ju said, To which of all us? And he said, To you, O captain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he arose, and went into the house: and he poured the oil upon his head, and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed you to be king over the people of the Lord, even over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall utterly destroy the house of Achaab your master from before me, and shall avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord, at the hand of Jezabel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and at the hand of the whole house of Achaab: and you shall utterly cut off from the house of Achaab every male, and him that is shut up and left in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will make the house of Achaab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and as the house of Baasa the son of Achia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the dogs shall eat Jezabel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Ju went forth to the servants of his lord, and they said to him, [Is] all well? Why came this mad fellow in to you? And he said to them, You⌃ know the man, and his communication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they said, [It is] wrong: tell us now. And Ju said to them, Thus and thus spoke he to me, saying, —and he said, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you to be king over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And when they heard it, they hasted, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew with the trumpet, and said, Ju is king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So Ju the son of Josaphat the son of Namessi conspired against Joram, and Joram was defending Remmoth Galaad, he and all Israel, because of Azael king of Syria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And king Joram had returned to be healed in Jezrael of the wounds which the Syrians had given him, in his war with Azael king of Syria. And Ju said, If your heart is with me, let there not go forth out of the city one fugitive to go and report to Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Ju rode and advanced, and came down to Jezrael; for Joram king of Israel was getting healed in Jezrael of the arrow-wounds wherewith the Syrians [had] wounded him in Rammath in the war with Azael king of Syria; for he [was] strong and a mighty man: and Ochozias king of Juda was come down to see Joram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And there went up a watchman upon the tower of Jezrael, and saw the dust [made by] Ju as he approached; and he said, I see dust. And Joram said, Take a horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, Peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there went a horseman to meet them, and said, Thus says the king, Peace. And Ju said, What have you to do with peace? turn behind me. And the watchman reported, saying, The messenger came up to them, and has not returned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he sent another horseman, and he came to him, and said, Thus says the king, Peace. And Ju said, What have you to do with peace? turn behind me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the watchman reported, saying, He came up to them, and has not returned: and the driver drives Ju the son of Namessi, for it is with furious [haste]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Joram said, Make ready. And one made ready the chariot: and Joram the king of Israel went forth, and Ochozias king of Juda, each in his chariot, and they went to meet Ju, and found him in the portion of Nabuthai the Jezraelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it came to pass when Joram saw Ju, that he said, [Is it] peace, Ju? And Ju said, How [can it be] peace? as yet [there are] the whoredoms of your mother Jezabel, and her abundant witchcrafts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joram turned his hands, and fled, and said to Ochozias, Treachery, Ochozias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Ju bent his bow with his full strength, and struck Joram between his arms, and his arrow went out at his heart, and he bowed upon his knees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And [Ju] said to Badecar his chief officer, Cast him into the portion of ground of Nabuthai the Jezraelite, for I and you remember, riding [as we were] on chariots after Achaab his father, that the Lord took up this burden against him, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Surely, I have seen yesterday the blood of Nabuthai, and the blood of his sons, says the Lord; and I will recompense him in this portion, says the Lord. Now then, I pray you, take him up and cast him into the portion, according to the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Ochozias king of Juda saw [it], and fled by the way of Baethgan. And Ju pursued after him, and said, [Slay] him also. And one struck him in the chariot at the going up of Gai, which is Jeblaam: and he fled to Mageddo, and died there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And his servants put him on a chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem, and they buried him in his sepulchre in the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And in the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ochozias began to reign over Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Ju came to Jezrael; and Jezabel heard [of it], and coloured her eyes, and adorned her head, and looked through the window. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Ju entered into the city; and she said, Had Zambri, the murderer of his master, peace? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he lifted up his face toward the window, and saw her, and said, Who are you? Come down with me. And two eunuchs looked down towards him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he said, Throw her [down]. And they threw her [down]; and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses: and they trampled on her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And [Ju] went in and ate and drank, and said, Look now, after this cursed woman, and bury her, for she is a king's daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they went to bury her; but they found nothing of her but the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And they returned and told him. And he said, [It is] the word of the Lord, which he spoke by the hand of Eliu the Thesbite, saying, In the portion of Jezrael shall the dogs eat the flesh of Jezabel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the carcass of Jezabel shall be as dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezrael, so that they shall not say, [This is] Jezabel.\par

In the Agamemnon of Aschylus, the hypocritical Clytemnestra commands the maids to spread carpets before her returning husband, that on his descending from his chariot he may place his foot on "a purple-covered path." We also find this custom among the Romans. Plutarch relates, that when Cato of Utica left the Macedonian army, where he had become legionary tribune, the soldiers spread their clothes in the way.; on the top The ancient fortified cities were generally strengthened with a citadel (, ), commonly built on an eminence, to which they ascended by a flight of stairs ( ). It is extremely probable, therefore, that Ramoth-gilead, being a frontier town of Israel and Syria, had a tower of this nature; and that Jehu was proclaimed king on the top of the stairs by which they ascended the hill on which the tower stood, i.e., in the area before the door of the tower, and consequently the most public place in the city. blew with trumpets; is king Heb. reigneth \textsuperscript{15} Joram Heb. \subsection*{Kings IV 10}
\markright{KINGS IV 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Achaab [had] seventy sons in Samaria. And Ju wrote a letter, and sent it into Samaria to the rulers of Samaria, and to the elders, and to the guardians of [the children of] Achaab, saying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Now then, as soon as this letter shall have reached you, whereas [there are] with you the sons of your master, and with you chariots and horses, and strong cities, and arms, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} do you⌃ accordingly look out the best and fit among your master's sons, and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they feared greatly, and said, Behold, two kings stood not before him: and how shall we stand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So they that were over the house, and they that were over the city, and the elders and the guardians, sent to Ju, saying, We also [are] your servants, and whatever you shall say to us we will do; we will not make [any] man king: we will do that which is right in your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Ju wrote them a second letter, saying, If you⌃ [are] for me, and listen to my voice, take the heads of the men your master's sons, and bring [them] to me at this time to-morrow in Jezrael. Now the sons of the king were seventy men; these great men of the city brought them up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass, when the letter came to them, that they took the king's sons, and killed them, [even] seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezrael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And a messenger came and told [him], saying, They have brought the heads of the king's sons. And he said, Lay them [in] two heaps by the door of the gate until the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the morning came, and he went forth, and stood, and said to all the people, You⌃ are righteous: behold, I conspired against my master, and killed him: but who killed all these? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} See now that there shall not fall to the ground anything of the word of the Lord which the Lord spoke against the house of Achaab: for the Lord has performed all that he spoke of by the hand of his servant Eliu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Ju struck all that were left of the house of Achaab in Jezrael, and all his great men, and his acquaintance, and his priests, so as not to leave him [any] remnant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he arose and went to Samaria, [and] he [was] in the house of sheep-shearing in the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Ju found the brethren of Ochozias king of Juda, and said, Who [are] you⌃? And they said, We [are] the brethren of Ochozias, and we have come down to salute the sons of the king, and the sons of the queen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said, Take them alive. And they killed them at the shearing-house, forty and two men: he left not a man of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he went thence and found Jonadab the son of Rechab [coming] to meet him; and he saluted him, and Ju said to him, Is your heart right with my heart, as my heart [is] with your heart? And Jonadab said, It is. And Ju said, If it is then, give me your hand. And he gave him his hand, and he took him up to him into the chariot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said to him, Come with me, and see me zealous for the Lord. And he caused him to sit in his chariot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he entered into Samaria, and struck all that were left of Achaab in Samaria, until he had utterly destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spoke to Eliu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Ju gathered all the people, and said to them, Achaab served Baal a little; Ju shall serve him much. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now then do all [you⌃] the prophets of Baal call all his servants and his priests to me; let not a man be lacking: for I have a great sacrifice [to offer] to Baal; every one who shall be missing shall die. But Ju did it in subtilty, that he might destroy the servants of Baal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Ju said, Sanctify a solemn festival to Baal, and they made a proclamation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ju sent throughout all Israel, saying, Now then let all [Baal's] servants, and all his priests, and all his prophets [come], let none be lacking: for I am going to offer a great sacrifice; whoever shall be missing, shall not live. So all the servants of Baal came, and all his priests, and all his prophets: there was not one left who came not. And they entered into the house of Baal; and the house of Baal was filled from one end to the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he said to the man who was over the house of the wardrobe, Bring forth a robe for all the servants of Baal. And the keeper of the robes brought forth to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Ju and Jonadab the son of Rechab entered into the house of Baal, and said to the servants of Baal, Search, and see whether there is among you any of the servants of the Lord, or only the servants of Baal, by themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he went in to offer sacrifices and whole burnt offerings; and Ju set for himself eighty men without, and said, Every man who shall escape of the men whom I bring into your hand, the life of him [that spares him] shall go for his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it came to pass, when he had finished offering the whole burnt offering, that Ju said to the footmen and to the officers, Go you⌃ in and kill them; let not a man of them escape. So they struck them with the edge of the sword, and the footmen and the officers cast [the bodies] forth, and went to the city of the house of Baal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they brought out the pillar of Baal, and burnt it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they tore down the pillars of Baal, and made his house a draught-house until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So Ju abolished Baal out of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Nevertheless Ju departed not from following the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin: [these were] the golden heifers in Baethel and in Dan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the Lord said to Ju, Because of all your deeds wherein you have acted well in doing that which was right in my eyes, according to all things which you have done to the house of Achaab [as they were] in my heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But Ju took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: he departed not from following the sins of Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short; and Azael struck them in every coast of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} from Jordan eastward all the land of Galaad belonging to the Gadites, of Gaddi and that of Ruben, and of Manasses, from Aroer, which is on the brink of the brook of Arnon, and Galaad and Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the rest of the acts of Ju, and all that he did, and all his might, and the wars wherein he engaged, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Ju slept with his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria: and Joachaz his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the days which Ju reigned over Israel [were] twenty-eight years in Samaria.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} seventy sons, in Samaria; the rulers; them Heb. nourishers \textsuperscript{6} If ye be mine Heb. If ye be for me; take ye your master's sons; which brought them up "The rich, " says Mr. Morier, "hire a dedeh, or wet nurse for their children. If a boy, the father appoints a steady man from the age of two years to be his laleh, who, I conjecture, must stand in the same capacity as the bringers up of children mentioned in the catastrophe of Ahab's sons. But if it be a daughter, she has a gees sefeed, or white head, attached to her for the same purpose as the laleh ." \textsuperscript{8} there came; Lay ye them Such barbarities are by no means uncommon in the East. "It has been know to occur, " says Mr. Morier, "after the combat was over, that prisoners have been put to death in cold blood, in order that the heads, which are immediately despatched to the king, and deposited in heaps at the place gates, might make a more considerable show." until the morning \textsuperscript{9} Ye be righteous; I conspired \textsuperscript{10} fall unto the earth; the Lord hath done;, by Heb. by the hand of, *marg. \textsuperscript{11} and; kinsfolks or, acquaintance his priests; he left \textsuperscript{12} shearing house Heb. house of shepherds binding sheep \textsuperscript{13} met with Heb. found the brethren, ; salute Heb. the peace of, etc \textsuperscript{14} Take them alive; neither left \textsuperscript{15} lighted on Heb. found, *marg. Jehonadab, Jonadab Rechab saluted Heb. blessed, Is thine heart right; give me; he took him Jehu asked for the hand of Jehonadab not merely for the purpose of assisting him into the chariot, but that he might give him an assurance that he would assist him in the prosecution of his desires; for giving the hand is considered as a pledge of friendship and fidelity, or a form of entering into a contract, among all nations. Mr. Bruce relates, that when he entreated the protection of a sheikh, the great people who were assembled came, "and after joining hands, repeated a kind of prayer, of about two minutes long; by which they declared themselves and their children accursed, if ever they lifted their hands against me in the tell, (or field) in the desert, or on the river; or, in case that I, or mine, should fly to them for refuge, if they did not protect us at the risk of their lives, their families, and their fortunes, or, as they emphatically expressed it, to the death of the last male child among them." Another striking instance occurs in Ockley's History of the Saracens. Telha, just before he died, asked one of Ali's men if he belonged to the emperor of the faithful; and being informed that he did, "Give me then, " said he, "your hand, that I may put mine in it, and by this action renew the oath of fidelity which I have already made to Ali." \textsuperscript{19} all the prophets; all his servants all his priests But Jehu \textsuperscript{21} And they came; the house of Baal full from one end to another or, so full that they stood mouth to mouth \textsuperscript{24} If any of the men \textsuperscript{25} Go in; let; edge Heb. mouth \textsuperscript{26} images Heb. statues, *marg. and burned them \textsuperscript{27} brake down the image; made it a draught house This was an ancient mode of degradation, which still continues in the East; and we are informed, that Abbas the Great, king of Persia, having conquered Bagdad, treated the tomb of Hanifah, one of the fathers of the church among the Turks, in a similar manner. \textsuperscript{29} am 3120-3148, bc 884-856 the sins, ;, made Israel; the golden calves;, in Bethel \textsuperscript{30} Because thou hast; according to all that; thy children \textsuperscript{31} took no heed Heb. observed not, ; walk; he departed \textsuperscript{32} cut Heb. cut off the ends of Hazael \textsuperscript{33} eastward Heb. toward the rising of the sun the land of Gilead; even or, even to \textsuperscript{35} am 3148, bc 856 Jehu slept;, Jehoahaz \textsuperscript{36} the time Heb. the days were\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 11}
\markright{KINGS IV 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Gotholia the mother of Ochozias saw that her son was dead, and she destroyed all the seed royal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Josabee daughter of king Joram, sister of Ochozias, took Joas the son of her brother, and stole him from among the king's sons that were put to death, [secreting] him and his nurse in the bedchamber, and hid him from the face of Gotholia, and he was not slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he remained with her hid in the house of the Lord six years: and Gotholia reigned over the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in the seventh year Jodae sent and took the captains of hundreds of the Chorri and of the Rhasim, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant of the Lord with them, and adjured them, and Jodae showed them the king's son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And charged them, saying, This [is] the thing which you⌃ shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let a third part of you go in [on] the sabbath-day, and keep you⌃ the watch of the king's house in the porch; and another third in the gate of the high way, and a third at the gate behind the footmen; and keep you⌃ the guard of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there [shall be] two parties among you, even every one that goes out on the Sabbath, and they shall keep the guard of the Lord's house before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And do you⌃ compass the king about every man with his weapon in his hand, and he that goes into the ranges shall die: and they shall be with the king in his going out and in his coming in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the captains of hundreds did all things that the wise Jodae commanded; and they took each his men, both those that went in on the sabbath-day, and those that went out on the sabbath-day, and went in to Jodae the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the priest gave to the captains of hundreds the swords and spears of king David that were in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the footmen stood each with his weapon in his hand from the right corner of the house to the left corner of the house, [by] the altar and the house round about the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he brought forth the king's son, and put upon him the crown and [gave him] the testimony; and he made him king, and anointed him: and they clapped [their] hands, and said, Long live the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Gotholia heard the sound of the people running, and she went in to the people to the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And she looked, and, behold, the king stood near a pillar according to the manner; and the singers and the trumpeters were before the king and all the people of the land [even] rejoicing and sounding with trumpets: and Gotholia tore her garments, and cried, A conspiracy, a conspiracy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jodae the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were over the host, and said to them, Bring her forth without the ranges, [and] he that goes in after her shall certainly die by the sword. For the priest said, Let her not however be slain in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they laid hands upon her, and went in by the way of the horses' entrance into the house of the Lord, and she was slain there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jodae made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be the Lord's people; also between the king and the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and tore it down, and completely broke in pieces his altars and his images, and they killed Mathan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he took the captains of the hundreds, and the Chorri, and the Rhasim, and all the people of the land, and brought down the king out of the house of the Lord; and they went in by the way of the gate of the footmen of the king's house, and seated him there on the throne of the kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was at rest: and they killed Gotholia with the sword in the house of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Joas [was] seven years old when he began to reign.\par

Judith "surprised the rock Damo, and slew the whole of the princes, to the number, it is said, of about 400; " while the infant king, Del Naad, was conveyed for safety to a loyal province, and afterwards restored., seed royal Heb. seed of the kingdom, *marg. \textsuperscript{2} Jehosheba, Jehoshabeath Joram, Jehoram Joash, Jehoash they hid him; , in the bedchamber Bachadar hammittoth, "in a chamber of beds; " which Sir J. Chardin thinks does not mean a room to sleep in, but a chamber used as a repository for beds; for, in the East, they sleep upon cotton mattresses, "of which they have several in great houses, against they should have occasion, and a room on purpose for them." \textsuperscript{4} am 3126, bc 878 the seventh rulers; the captains, made a covenant; took an oath \textsuperscript{6} the gate of Sur; that it be not broken down or, from breaking up \textsuperscript{7} parts or, companies, Heb. hands go forth \textsuperscript{10} king David's spears Josephus states that, for fear of creating suspicion, they came unarmed, "and Jehoiada having opened the arsenal in the temple which David had prepared, he divided among the centurions, priests, and Levites, the spears (arrows), and quivers, and all other kinds of weapons which he found there." \textsuperscript{11} every man, corner Heb. shoulder by the altar \textsuperscript{12} he brought; put the crown; the testimony; anointed him; and they clapped Wyyakkoo kaph, "they clapped the hand, " which Mr. Harmer thinks was similar to the mode in which Oriental females express their respect for persons of high rank, by gently applying one of their hands to their mouth. So Pitts relates, that in some of the towns of Barbary, the leaders of the sacred caravan being received with loud acclamations, "the very women get upon the tops of the houses to view the parade, or fine show, where they keep striking their four fingers on their lips, as fast as they can, making a joyful noise all the while."; and said; God save the king Heb. \subsection*{Kings IV 12}
\markright{KINGS IV 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Joas began to reign in the seventh year of Ju, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Sabia of Bersabee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joas did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all the days that Jodae the priest instructed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Only there were not [any] of the high places removed, and the people still sacrificed there, and burned incense on the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joas said to the priests, [As for] all the money of the holy things that is brought into the house of the Lord, the money of valuation, [as] each man brings the money of valuation, all the money which any man may feel disposed to bring into the house of the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} let the priests take it to themselves, every man from [the proceeds of] his sale: and they shall repair the breaches of the house in all [places] wherever a breach shall be found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass in the twenty-third year of king Joas the priests [had] not repaired the breaches of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And king Joas called Jodae the priest, and the [other] priests, and said to them, Why have you⌃ not repaired the breaches of the house? now then receive no [more] money from your sales, for you⌃ shall give it to [repair the] breaches of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the priests consented to receive no more money of the people, and not to repair the breaches of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jodae the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it by the altar in the house of a man [belonging to] the house of the Lord, and the priests that kept the door put [therein] all the money that was found in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass, when they saw that [there was] much money in the chest, that the king's scribe and the high priest went up, and they tied up and counted the money that was found in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they gave the money that had been collected into the hands of them that wrought the works, the overseers of the house of the Lord; and they gave it out to the carpenters and to the builders that wrought in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And to the masons, and to the hewers of stone, to purchase timber and hewn stone to repair the breaches of the house of the Lord, for all that was spent on the house of the Lord to repair [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Only there were not to be made for the house of the Lord silver plates, studs, bowls, or trumpets, any vessel of gold or vessel of silver, of the money that was brought into the house of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} for they were to give it to the workmen, and they repaired therewith the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Also they took no account of the men into whose hands they gave the money to give to the workmen, for they acted faithfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Money for a sin-offering, and money for a trespass-offering, whatever happened to be brought into the house of the Lord, went to the priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then went up Azael king of Syria, and fought against Geth, and took it: and Azael set his face to go against Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joas king of Juda took all the holy things which Josaphat, and Joram, Ochozias, his fathers, and kings of Juda [had] consecrated, and what he had himself dedicated, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the Lord's house and the king's house, and he sent [them] to Azael king of Syria; and he went up from Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the rest of the acts of Joas, and all that he did, behold, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And his servants rose up and made a conspiracy, and struck Joas in the house of Mallo that is in Sela. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Jezirchar the son of Jemuath, and Jezabuth Somer's son, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amessias his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} am 3148, bc 856 said to the priests; the money; dedicated things or, holy things, Heb. holiness, even the money; that every man is set at Heb. of the souls of his estimation, and all the money, ; cometh etc. Heb. ascendeth upon the heart of a man \textsuperscript{5} Let the priests let them repair \textsuperscript{6} three and twentieth year Heb. twentieth year and third year the priests \textsuperscript{7} king Jehoash, Jehoiada; Why repair ye \textsuperscript{9} took a chest; beside the priests, ; door Heb. threshold, *marg. \textsuperscript{10} the king's, ; scribe or, secretary put up Heb. bound up, in bags Sir J. Chardin informs us, "it is a custom of Persia always to seal up bags of money; and the money of the king's treasure is not told, but is received by bags sealed up." These are what are called in the East purses; each of which, as Maillet informs us, contains money to the amount of 1, 500 livres, or about 63£. of our money. The money thus collected for the reparation of the temple, seems, in like manner, to have been reckoned in bags of equal value to each other; as we can scarcely imagine the placing it in bags would otherwise have been mentioned. The value of a Jewish purse is unknown; but the bags mentioned in, amounted to a talent. \textsuperscript{11} gave the money; laid it out Heb. brought it forth \textsuperscript{12} masons; was laid out Heb. went forth \textsuperscript{13} there were not That is, there were no vessels made for the service of the temple till all the outward repairs were completed; but, when this was done, "they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, whereof were made vessels of gold and silver, " ( ), to replace those which had been taken away by Athaliah and her sons. bowls; trumpets \textsuperscript{15} they reckoned for they dealt \textsuperscript{17} am 3164, bc 840 Hazael against Gath; set his face; to Jerusalem \textsuperscript{18} took all the hallowed He dearly bought, by such unhallowed means, a peace which was of short duration; for the next year Hazael returned, and Jehoash having no more treasures, was obliged to hazard a battle, which he lost, and the principal part of his nobility, so that Judah was totally ruined, and Jehoash soon after slain in his bed by his own servants.; went away Heb. went up \textsuperscript{20} his servants;, the house of Millo or, Beth-millo \textsuperscript{21} Jozachar This person is called Zabad in Chronicles, and Shimeath his mother is said to be an Ammonitess; and Jehozabad is said to be the son, not of Shomer, but of Shimrith, a Moabitess. Who the fathers of these two persons were we know not; they were probably foreigners and aliens. Some suppose that they belonged to the king's chamber, and therefore could have easy access to him., Zabad Shomer, Shimrith Amaziah his son\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} 2Kgs 9:27; 2Kgs 11:1; 2Kgs 11:3-4; 2Kgs 11:21; 2Chr 24:1-14; 2Kgs 11:2; 1Chr 3:11 \textsuperscript{2} 2Kgs 14:3; 2Chr 24:2; 2Chr 24:17-22; 2Chr 25:2; 2Chr 26:4 \textsuperscript{3} 2Kgs 14:4; 2Kgs 18:4; 1Kgs 15:14; 1Kgs 22:43; 2Chr 31:4; Jer 2:20 \textsuperscript{4} 2Kgs 22:4; 2Chr 29:4-11; 2Chr 35:2; 2Kgs 12:18; 1Kgs 7:1; 1Chr 18:11; 2Chr 15:18; 2Chr 31:12; Lev 5:15-16; Lev 27:12-27; Lev 27:31; Exod 30:12-16; 2Chr 24:9-10; Lev 27:2-8; Exod 25:1-2; Exod 35:5; Exod 35:22; Exod 35:29; Exod 36:3; 1Chr 29:3-9; 1Chr 29:17; Ezra 1:6; Ezra 2:69; Ezra 7:16; Ezra 8:25-28; Luke 21:4 \textsuperscript{5} 2Chr 24:5; 2Kgs 12:12; 2Kgs 22:5-6; 1Kgs 11:27; 2Chr 24:7; Isa 58:12 \textsuperscript{6} 1Sam 2:29-30; 2Chr 29:34; Isa 56:10-12; Mal 1:10; Phil 2:21; 1Pet 5:2 \textsuperscript{7} 2Chr 24:5; 2Chr 24:6-14; 2Kgs 12:2; 2Kgs 11:4; 2Chr 23:1; 2Chr 24:16; 1Chr 21:3 \textsuperscript{9} 2Chr 24:8-14; Mark 12:41; 2Chr 24:10; 2Kgs 22:4; 2Kgs 23:4; 2Kgs 25:18; 1Chr 15:18; 1Chr 15:24; Jer 35:4; Jer 52:24; Ps 84:10 \textsuperscript{10} 2Kgs 19:2; 2Kgs 22:3; 2Kgs 22:12; 2Sam 8:17; 2Sam 20:25; 2Kgs 5:23 \textsuperscript{11} 2Kgs 22:5-6; 2Chr 24:11-12; 2Chr 34:9-11 \textsuperscript{12} 1Kgs 5:17-18; Ezra 3:7; Ezra 5:8; Luke 21:5 \textsuperscript{13} 2Chr 24:14; Num 7:13-14; 1Kgs 7:48-50; Ezra 1:9-11; Num 10:2 \textsuperscript{15} 2Kgs 22:7; 2Chr 34:12; Neh 7:2; Matt 24:45; Luke 16:1; Luke 16:10-11; 1Cor 4:2-3; 3John 1:5 \textsuperscript{16} Lev 5:15-18; Lev 7:7; Num 5:8-10; Num 18:8-9; Hos 4:8 \textsuperscript{17} 2Kgs 8:12-15; 1Sam 27:2; 1Kgs 2:39-40; 1Chr 8:13; 1Chr 18:1; Jer 42:15; Luke 9:51; Luke 9:53; 2Chr 24:23-24 \textsuperscript{18} 2Kgs 18:15-16; 1Kgs 15:18; 2Chr 16:2 \textsuperscript{19} 2Kgs 8:23; 1Kgs 11:41; 1Kgs 14:19; 1Kgs 14:29 \textsuperscript{20} 2Kgs 14:5; 2Chr 24:24-25; 2Chr 25:27; 2Chr 33:24; Judg 9:6; 2Sam 5:9; 1Kgs 11:27 \textsuperscript{21} 2Chr 24:26; 2Chr 24:27\par}
\subsection*{Kings IV 13}
\markright{KINGS IV 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the twenty-third year of Joas son of Ochozias king of Juda began Joachaz the son of Ju to reign in Samaria, [and he reigned] seventeen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked after the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin; he departed not from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and delivered them into the hand of Azael king of Syria, and into the hand of the son of Ader son of Azael, all their days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joachaz implored the Lord, and the Lord listened to him, for he saw the affliction of Israel, because the king of Syria afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord gave deliverance to Israel, and they escaped from under the hand of Syria: and the children of Israel lived in their tents as heretofore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Only they departed not from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who led Israel to sin: they walked in them—moreover the grove also remained in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Whereas there was not left any army to Joachaz, except fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand infantry: for the king of Syria had destroyed them, and they made them as dust for trampling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the rest of the acts of Joachaz, and all that he did, and his mighty acts [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joachaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria: and Joas his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the thirty-seventh year of Joas king of Juda, Joas the son of Joachaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria sixteen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord; he departed not from all the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin: he walked in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the rest of the acts of Joas, and all that he did, and his mighty acts which he performed together with Amessias king of Juda, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joas slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne, and he was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now Elisaie was sick of his sickness, whereof he died: and Joas king of Israel went down to him, and wept over his face, and said, [My] father, [my] father, the chariot of Israel, and the horseman thereof! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Elisaie said to him, Take bow and arrows. And he took to himself a bow and arrows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said to the king, Put your hand on the bow. And Joas put his hand upon [it]: and Elisaie put his hands upon the king's hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. And Elisaie said, Shoot. And he shot. And [Elisaie] said, The arrow of the Lord's deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria; and you shall strike the Syrians in Aphec until you have consumed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Elisaie said to him, Take bow and arrows. And he took them. And [he] said to the king of Israel, Strike upon the ground. And the king struck three times, and stayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the man of God was grieved at him, and said, If you had struck five or six times, then you should have struck Syria till you had consumed them; but now you shall strike Syria [only] thrice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Elisaie died, and they buried him. And the bands of the Moabites came into the land, at the beginning of the year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it came to pass as they were burying a man, that behold, they saw a band [of men], and they cast the man into the grave of Elisaie: and as soon as he touched the bones of Elisaie, he revived and stood up on his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Azael greatly afflicted Israel all the days of Joachaz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Lord had mercy and compassion upon them, and had respect to them because of his covenant with Abraam, and Isaac, and Jacob; and the Lord would not destroy them, and did not cast them out from his presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Azael king of Syria died, and the son of Ader his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Joas the son of Joachaz returned, and took the cities out of the hand of the son of Ader the son of Azael, which he had taken out of the hand of Joachaz his father in the war: thrice did Joas strike him, and he recovered the cities of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} three and twentieth year Heb. twentieth year, and third year, Jehoahaz \textsuperscript{2} am 3148-3156, bc 856-839 followed Heb. walked after \textsuperscript{3} and he delivered; Hazael, ; Benhadad all their days Rather "all his days; " for Joash son of Jehoahaz delivered Israel from Ben-hadad. \textsuperscript{4} Jehoahaz; the Lord; he saw; because the king \textsuperscript{5} a saviour This saviour was undoubtedly Joash, whose successful wars are subsequently detailed. Houbigant recommends to read the after the ., ; beforetime Heb. yesterday and third day \textsuperscript{6} departed, ; walked Heb. he walked, and there remained Heb. and there stood \textsuperscript{7} fifty horsemen, ; the king, like the dust; *marg. \textsuperscript{9} am 3165, bc 839 buried him; Joash, Jehoash reigned in his stead "Alone." \textsuperscript{10} In the thirty Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, was associated with his father in the government two years before his death. It is this association that is spoken of here. Joash reigned sixteen years which include the years he reigned conjointly with his father. began Jehoash "In consort with his father. ." \textsuperscript{12} am 3163-3179, bc 841-825 the rest, his might \textsuperscript{14} am 3166, bc 838 fallen sick; he died; O my father \textsuperscript{16} Put thine hand Heb. make thine hand to ride Elisha \textsuperscript{17} Open; The arrow This was a symbolical action, indicative of the deliverance of Israel from Syria. It was an ancient custom to shoot an arrow or cast a spear into a country before the commencement of hostilities.; Aphek \textsuperscript{19} the man of God, was wroth; now thou shalt \textsuperscript{20} am 3167, bc 837 buried him; the bands, the Moabites \textsuperscript{21} was let down Heb. went down touched \textsuperscript{23} the Lord; had respect; because of his covenant, ; neither cast he; presence Heb. face \textsuperscript{25} am 3168, bc 836 took again Heb. returned and took, Three times.\par}
