\subsection*{Kings IV 14}
\markright{KINGS IV 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the second year of Joas the son of Joachaz king of Israel, did Amessias also the son of Joas the king of Juda begin to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Joadim of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, but not as David his father: he did according to all things that his father Joas did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Only he removed not the high places: as yet the people sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass when the kingdom was established in his hand, that he killed his servants that had slain the king his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But he killed not the sons of those that had slain him; according as it is written in the book of the laws of Moses, as the Lord gave commandment, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, and the children shall not be put to death for the fathers; but every one shall die for his own sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He struck of Edom ten thousand in the valley of salt, and took the Rock in the war, and called its name Jethoel until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then Amessias sent messengers to Joas son of Joachaz son of Ju king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joas the king of Israel sent to Amessias king of Juda, saying, The thistle that was in Libanus sent to the cedar that was in Libanus, saying, Give my daughter to your son to wife: and the wild beasts of the field that were in Libanus passed by and trod down the thistle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You have struck and wounded Edom, and your heart has lifted you up: stay at home and glorify yourself; for therefore are you quarrelsome to your hurt? So [both] you will fall and Juda with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Nevertheless Amessias listened not: so Joas king of Israel went up, and he and Amessias king of Juda looked one another in the face in Baethsamys of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Juda was overthrown before Israel, and [every] man fled to his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joas king of Israel took Amessias the son of Joas the son of Ochozias, in Baethsamys; and he came to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, [beginning] at the gate of Ephraim as far as the gate of the corner, four hundred cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he took the gold, and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house, and the hostages, and returned to Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the rest of the acts of Joas, [even] all that he did in his might, how he warred with Amessias king of Juda, are not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joas slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Amessias the son of Joas king of Juda lived after the death of Joas son of Joachaz king of Israel fifteen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the rest of the acts of Amessias, and all that he did, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachis: and they sent after him to Lachis, and killed him there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they brought him upon horses; and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all the people of Juda took Azarias, and he was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amessias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He built Aeloth, and restored it to Juda, after the king slept with his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} In the fifteenth year of Amessias son of Joas king of Juda began Jeroboam son of Joas to reign over Israel in Samaria forty and one years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He recovered the coast of Israel from the entering in of Aemath to the sea of Araba, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spoke by his servant Jonas the son of Amathi, the prophet of Gethchopher. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For the Lord saw [that] the affliction of Israel [was] very bitter, and that they were few in number, straitened and in lack, and destitute, and Israel had no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord said that he would not blot out the seed of Israel from under heaven; so he delivered them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, which he achieved in war, and how he recovered Damascus and Aemath to Juda in Israel, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zacharias his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3165, bc 839 Joash, reigned Amaziah \textsuperscript{3} am 3165-3194, bc 839-810 he did; he did according \textsuperscript{5} am 3166, bc 838 that he slew; his servants \textsuperscript{7} am 3177, bc 827 slew; the valley of salt Some suppose that the Valley of Salt was south of the Dead, or Salt Sea, towards the land of Edom; and others suppose it to be the Valley of Salt, about three or four miles south-east of Palmyra, which now supplies, in a great measure, the surrounding country with salt.; *title Selah or, the rock, Selah is generally supposed to be the same as Petra, which in Greek signifies a rock, the celebrated capital of Arabia Petrea. Strabo places it three or four days' journey from Jericho, and five days' journey from the forest of palm trees on the Red Sea. Pliny places it 600 miles from Gaza, and 125 from the Persian Gulf; but Cellarius and Reland very justly consider that the numbers have been changed, and that we ought to read 125 miles from Gaza, and 600 from the Persian Gulf. Eusebius places Beerothbenejaakan 30 miles west from Petra, and Elath ten miles east; and Burckhardt discovered the ruins of this ancient city in a valley called Wady Mousa. Joktheel \textsuperscript{9} The thistle; The word choach, which is rendered here, and in; thistle, in, thicket in, bramble, and in; thorn, is probably the black thorn, or sloe tree, the prunus spinosa of Linneus, as the same word signifies in Arabic. There is a vast deal of insolent dignity in this remonstrance of Jehoash; but it has nothing conciliatory; no proposal of making amends for the injury his army had done to the unoffending inhabitants of Judah ( ). The comparatively useless thorn, which may by chance lacerate the incautious passenger, is made the emblem of the house of Judah and David, while the house of Jehu is represented by the stately cedar. \textsuperscript{10} thine heart; glory of this; home Heb. thy house why shouldest \textsuperscript{12} was put to the worse Heb. was smitten they fled \textsuperscript{13} took Amaziah; the gate of Ephraim; the corner \textsuperscript{14} all the gold;, and hostages *marg. \textsuperscript{16} am 3179, bc 825 Jehoash; was buried Jeroboam \textsuperscript{19} am 3194, bc 810 they made, ; fled to Lachish \textsuperscript{21} Azariah; Uzziah, Ozias made him king \textsuperscript{22} Elath, the Ala or Elana of the Greek and Roman writers, was a celebrated port situated at the extremity of the eastern branch of the Red Sea, hence called the Elanitic Gulf, ten miles east from Petra, according to Eusebius, and 150; Roman miles from Gaza, according to Pliny, but 1, 260 stadia, or 157 miles, according to Strabo and Marcianus Herecleota. It is now called Akaba, and is nothing but a tower or castle, surrounded by a large grove of date trees, the residence of a governor, dependent on him of Grand Cairo.; Eloth \textsuperscript{23} am 3179-3220, bc 825-784 the fifteenth Jeroboam; began to reign "Now he begins to reign alone." \textsuperscript{24} in the sight; he departed \textsuperscript{25} from the entering; unto the sea; Jonah;, Jonas Gathhepher, Gittah-hepher \textsuperscript{26} saw the affliction; not any shut \textsuperscript{27} said not; blot out; he saved \textsuperscript{28} the rest Damascus; which belonged to Judah These places belonged to Judah by David's conquest ( ), but had been repossessed by the Syrians. \textsuperscript{29} am 3220, bc 784 Zachariah reigned "After an interregnum of eleven years."\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 15}
\markright{KINGS IV 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel Azarias the son of Amessias king of Juda began to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Jechelia of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all things that Amessias his father did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Only he took not away [any] of the high places: as yet the people sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord plagued the king, and he was leprous till the day of his death; and he reigned in a separate house. And Joatham the king's son [was] over the household, judging the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the rest of the acts of Azarias, and all that he did, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Azarias slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Joatham his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In the thirty and eighth year of Azarias king of Juda Zacharias the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in Samaria six months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who made Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Sellum the son of Jabis [and others] conspired against him, and they struck him [in] Keblaam, and killed him, and he reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the rest of the acts of Zacharias, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [This was] the word of the Lord which he spoke to Ju, saying, Your sons of the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel: and it was so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Sellum the son of Jabis reigned: and in the thirty and ninth year of Azarias king of Juda began Sellum to reign a full month in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Manaem the son of Gaddi went up out of Tharsila, and came to Samaria, and struck Sellum the son of Jabis in Samaria, and killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the rest of the acts of Sellum, and his conspiracy wherein he was engaged, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then Manaem struck both Thersa and all that was in it, and its borders extending beyond Thersa, because they opened not to him: and he struck it, and ripped up the women with child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} In the thirty and ninth year of Azarias king of Juda began Manaem the son of Gaddi to reign over Israel in Samaria ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} In his days went up Phua king of the Assyrians against the land: and Manaem gave to Phua a thousand talents of silver to aid him with his power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Manaem raised the silver [by a tax] upon Israel, even on every mighty man in wealth, to give to the king of the Assyrians, fifty shekels [levied] on each man; and the king of the Assyrians departed, and remained not there in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the rest of the acts of Manaem, and all that he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Manaem slept with his fathers; and Phakesias his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} In the fifties year of Azarias king of Juda, began Phakesias the son of Manaem to reign over Israel in Samaria two years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who made Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Phakee the son of Romelias, his officer, conspired against him, and struck him in Samaria in the front of the king's house, with Argob and Aria, and with him [there were] fifty men of the four hundred: and he killed him, and reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the rest of the acts of Phakesias, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} In the fifty-second year of Azarias king of Juda began Phakee the son of Romelias to reign over Israel in Samaria twenty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who led Israel to sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} In the days of Phakee king of Israel came Thalgath-phellasar king of the Assyrians, and took Ain, and Abel, and Thamaacha, and Anioch, and Kenez, and Asor, and Galaa, and Galilee, [even] all the land of Nephthali, and carried them away to the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Osee son of Ela formed a conspiracy against Phakee the son of Romelias, and struck him, and killed him, and reigned in his stead, in the twentieth year of Joatham the son of Azarias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the rest of the acts of Phakee, and all that he did, behold, these [are] written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} In the second year of Phakee son of Romelias king of Israel began Joatham the son of Azarias king of Juda to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Jerusa daughter of Sadoc. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all things that his father Azarias did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Nevertheless he took not away the high places: as yet the people sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the Lord's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the rest of the acts of Joatham, and all that he did, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} In those days the Lord began to send forth against Juda Raasson king of Syria, and Phakee son of Romelias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Joatham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Achaz his son reigned in his stead.\par

It is the sixteenth year of Jeroboam's monarchy." Azariah, ;, Uzziah \textsuperscript{5} am 3239-3246, bc 765-758 the Lord; so that; and dwelt; Jotham, judging \textsuperscript{6} Azariah Dr. Kennicott complains loudly here of "the corruption in the name of this king of Judah, who is expressed by four different names in this chapter: Ozriah, Oziah, Ozrihu, and Ozihu. Our oldest Hebrew manuscript relieves us here, by reading truly, in, Uzziah, where the printed text is differently corrupted. This reading is called true: 1. Because it is supported by the Syriac and Arabic versions in these three verses. 2. Because the printed text itself has it so in and of this very chapter. 3. Because it is so expressed in the parallel place in Chronicles. 4. This Pul began to reign according to Usher, am 3237, the fifth year of Menahem; and he is supposed to be the same that reigned in Nineveh, when Jonah preached in that city.; Menahem, ;, to confirm \textsuperscript{20} Menahem exacted Heb. caused to come forth the mighty; of each man etc. Or, rather, as Bishop Patrick renders, "to give to the king of Assyria fifty shekels of silver for each man, " i.e., in his army. It may be supposed, that Menahem compelled "the mighty men of wealth" to give much more a-piece than this sum (somewhat about 5£. sterling each) and each of them in some proportion to his affluence. stayed not \textsuperscript{23} am 3243, bc 761 and reigned two years \textsuperscript{25} am 3245, bc 759 Pekah; a captain; conspired, with Argob From the contstruction of the Hebrew Text, it would appear that Argob and Arieh were slain with the king, and that the fifty Gileadites were conspirators with Pekah. \textsuperscript{27} am 3245-3265, bc 759-739 the two, Pekah \textsuperscript{29} Tiglathpileser Some suppose Tiglath-pileser to be the son of Sardanapalus, but the learned Prideaux makes him the same as Arbaces the Mede, called by Alian, Thelgamus, and by Castor, Ninus Junior, who, with Belesis, headed the conspiracy against Sardanapalus, and fixed his royal seat at Nineveh, as Belesis, called in Scripture Baladan ( ), did his at Babylon. This Jotham died at forty-one. He was too great a blessing to be continued long to such an unworthy people. His death was a judgment, especially considering the character of Ahaz, his son and successor. For we read ( ) Ahaz made his son pass through the fire. \subsection*{Kings IV 16}
\markright{KINGS IV 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the seventeenth year of Phakee son of Romelias began Achaz the son of Joatham king of Juda to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Twenty years old was Achaz when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not that which was right in the eyes of the Lord his God faithfully, as David his father [had done]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, yes, he made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places, and upon the hills, and under every shady tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then went up Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romelias king of Israel against Jerusalem to war, and besieged Achaz, but could not prevail [against him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} At that time Raasson king of Syria recovered Aelath to Syria, and drove out the Jews from Aelath, and the Idumeans came to Aelath, and lived there until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Achaz sent messengers to Thalgath-phellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son: come up, deliver me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Achaz took the silver and the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and of the king's house, and sent gifts to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king of the Assyrians listened to him: and the king of the Assyrians went up to Damascus and took it, and removed the inhabitants, and killed king Raasson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And king Achaz went to Damascus to meet Thalgath-phellasar king of the Assyrians at Damascus; and he saw an altar at Damascus. And king Achaz sent to Urias the priest the pattern of the altar, and its proportions, and all its workmanship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Urias the priest built the altar, according to all [the directions] which king Achaz sent from Damascus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king saw the altar, and went up to it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and offered his whole burnt offering, and his meat-offering, and his drink-offering, and poured out the blood of his peace-offerings on the brazen altar that was before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he brought forward [the one] before the house of the Lord from between the altar and the house of the Lord, and he set it openly by the side of the altar northwards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And king Achaz charged Urias the priest, saying, Offer upon the great altar the whole burnt offering in the morning and the meat-offering in the evening, and the whole burnt offering of the king, and his meat-offering, and the whole burnt offering of all the people, and their meat-offering, and their drink-offering; and you shall pour all the blood of the whole burnt offering, and all the blood of [any other] sacrifice upon it: and the brazen altar shall be for me in the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Urias the priest did according to all that king Achaz commanded him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And king Achaz cut off the borders of the bases, and removed the laver from off them, and took down the sea from the brazen oxen that were under it, and set it upon a base of stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he made a base for the throne in the house of the Lord, and he turned the king's entrance without in the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the rest of the acts of Achaz, even all that he did, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Achaz slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Ezekias his son reigned in his stead.\par

Tilgath-pileser; Tilgath-pilneser I am thy servant, and save \textsuperscript{8} the silver, ; to the king \textsuperscript{9} am 3264, bc 740 went up, Foretold, Damascus Heb. Dammesek Kir Josephus informs us that this place was in Upper Media; and it is clear that it must be understood of some city or country in the dominions of the king of Assyria. It is highly probable that it was the country on the banks of the river Κυρος, Cyrus, or Kyrus, now called Kur, or Kura; and we find cities called Cyropolis, Cyrena, and Carine, mentioned by writers as lying in these parts, and a part of Media, called Syromedia, as it is thought, from the Syrians who were carried captive thither.; slew Rezin \textsuperscript{10} saw an altar; the pattern \textsuperscript{13} he burnt Lev. 1:1-3:16 of his peace offerings Heb. of the peace-offerings which were his \textsuperscript{15} the morning; , the king's burnt; , ; for me to inquire by \textsuperscript{17} am 3265, bc 739 cut off, borders; sea \textsuperscript{18} the covert There are a great number of conjectures concerning this covert; but it is probable that it was either, as Locke supposes, a sort of shelter or canopy erected for the people on the sabbath when the crowd was too great for the porch to contain them; or, as Dr. Geddes supposes, a seat, covered with a canopy, placed on an elevation, for the king and his court, when they attended public worship. \textsuperscript{20} am 3278, bc 726 buried; Hezekiah; Ezekias\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 17}
\markright{KINGS IV 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the twelfth year of Achaz king of Juda began Osee the son of Ela to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, only not as the kings of Israel that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Against him came up Salamanassar king of the Assyrians; and Osee became his servant, and rendered him tribute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king of the Assyrians found iniquity in Osee, in that he sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt, and brought not a tribute to the king of the Assyrians in that year: and the king of the Assyrians besieged him, and bound him in the prison-house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king of the Assyrians went up against all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it [for] three years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In the ninth year of Osee the king of the Assyrians took Samaria, and carried Israel away to the Assyrians, and settled them in Alae, and in Abor, [near] the rivers of Gozan, and [in] the mountains of the Medes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For it came to pass that the children of Israel [had] transgressed against the Lord their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharao king of Egypt, and they feared other gods, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and walked in the statutes of the nations which the Lord cast out before the face of the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel as many as did [such things], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and [in those] of the children of Israel as many as secretly practised customs, not as [they should have done], against the Lord their God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city. And they made for themselves pillars and groves on every high hill, and under every shady tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And burned incense there on all high places, as the nations [did] whom the Lord removed from before them, and dealt with familiar spirits, and they carved [images] to provoke the Lord to anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they served the idols, of which the Lord said to them, You⌃ shall not do this thing [against] the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord testified against Israel and against Juda, even by the hand of all his prophets, [and] of every seer, saying, Turn you⌃ from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my ordinances, and all the law which I commanded your fathers, [and] all that I sent to them by the hand of my servants the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But they listened not, and made their neck harder than the neck of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they kept not any of his testimonies which he charged them; and they walked after vanities, and became vain, and after the nations round about them, concerning which the Lord had charged them not to do accordingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They forsook the commandments of the Lord their God, and made themselves graven images, [even] two heifers, and they made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divinations and auspices, and sold themselves to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight; and there was only left the tribe of Juda quite alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Nay even Juda kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but they walked according to the customs of Israel which they practised, and rejected the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord was angry with the whole seed of Israel, and troubled them, and gave them into the hand of them that spoiled them, until he cast them out of his presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Forasmuch as Israel revolted from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam the son of Nabat king: and Jeroboam drew off Israel from following the Lord, and led them to sin a great sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the children of Israel walked in all the sin of Jeroboam which he committed; they departed not from it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} until the Lord removed Israel from his presence, as the Lord spoke by all his servants the prophets; and Israel was removed from off their land to the Assyrians until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king of Assyria brought from Babylon the men of Chutha, [and men] from Aia, and from Aemath, and Seppharvaim, and they were settled in the cities of Samaria in the place of the children of Israel: and they inherited Samaria, and were settled in its cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And it was so at the beginning of their establishment there [that] they feared not the Lord, and the Lord sent lions among them, and they killed some of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they spoke to the king of the Assyrians, saying, The nations whom you have removed and substituted in the cities of Samaria [for the Israelites], know not the manner of the God of the land: and he has sent the lions against them, and, behold, they are slaying them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, Bring some [Israelites] thence, and let them go and dwell there, and they shall teach them the manner of the God of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they brought one of the priests whom they had removed from Samaria, and he settled in Baethel, and taught them how they should fear the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But the nations made each their own gods, and put them in the house of the high places which the Samaritans [had] made, each nation in the cities in which they lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the men of Babylon made Socchoth Benith, and the men of Chuth made Ergel, and the men of Haemath made Asimath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the Evites made Eblazer and Tharthac, and the [inhabitant] of Seppharvaim [did evil] when they burnt their sons in the fire to Adramelech and Anemelech, the gods of Seppharvaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they feared the Lord, yet they established their abominations in the houses of the high places which they made in Samaria, each nation in the city in which they lived: and they feared the Lord, and they made for themselves priests of the high places, and sacrificed for themselves in the house of the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they feared the Lord, and served their gods according to the manner of the nations, whence [their lords] brought them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Until this day they did according to their manner: they fear [the Lord], and they do according to their customs, and according to their manner, and according to the law, and according to the commandment which the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whose name he made Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the Lord made a covenant with them, and charged them, saying, You⌃ shall not fear other gods, neither shall you⌃ worship them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} but only to the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with a high arm: him shall you⌃ fear, and him shall you⌃ worship; to him shall you⌃ sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} You⌃ shall observe continually the ordinances, and the judgments, and the law, and the commandments which he wrote for you to do; and you⌃ shall not fear other gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Neither shall you⌃ forget the covenant which he made with you: and you⌃ shall not fear other gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But you⌃ shall fear the Lord your God, and he shall deliver you from all your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Neither shall you⌃ comply with their practice, which they follow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} So these nations feared the Lord, and served their graven images: yes, their sons and their son's sons do until this day even as their fathers did.\par

Cuth is probably the Cush watered by the Gihon, or Araxes, now Aras ( ), the ancient country of the Scythians, where we meet with the Quitians, Coethians, or Coete, and Cytheans, and the cities of Cotatis, Cetemane, Cythanum, Cyta, Cethena, etc. Nergal Supposed to denote the solar orb; the emblem of which, according to the Rabbins, was a cock. Ashima Jarchi says this idol was of the form of a goat. \textsuperscript{31} the Avites; Nibhaz Supposed to be the same as the Anubis of the Egyptians; and was in form partly a dog and partly a man. burnt their children \textsuperscript{32} made unto themselves, the houses \textsuperscript{33} They feared; whom they carried etc. or, who carried them away from thence, The new inhabitants of the land imitated the idolatrous Israelites, by associating their idols with Jehovah, as the objects of worship. The remainder, however, of the verses seem to relate to the Israelites after they were carried captive. They still persevered in idolatry and disobedience; and not being purified, were left to be consumed in the furnace. It is said that the Israelites "did not fear the Lord, " yet the heathens, who followed their example, are said "to have feared the Lord." The Israelites did not so much as fear the wrath of Almighty God; but, on the other hand, the poor pagans feared the power of his wrath, and to avert it paid some ignorant worship, according to the wretched instructions given them. As this was an external acknowledgment of his power and Godhead, and a homage paid to him, he was pleased in consequence to withdraw his judgments from them. - Scott \textsuperscript{34} fear not, whom he named Israel \textsuperscript{35} With whom; charged them; fear other gods \textsuperscript{36} a stretched; him shall ye fear \textsuperscript{37} the statutes;, ; wrote for you; and ye shall not \textsuperscript{39} the Lord; he shall deliver \textsuperscript{40} they did not but they did \textsuperscript{41} these nations; unto this day\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 18}
\markright{KINGS IV 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the third year of Osee son of Ela king of Israel [that] Ezekias son of Achaz king of Juda began to reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Five and twenty years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Abu, daughter of Zacharias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father David did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He removed the high places, and broke in pieces the pillars, and utterly destroyed the groves, and the brazen serpent which Moses made: because until those days the children of Israel burnt incense to it: and he called it Neesthan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; and after him there was not any like him among the kings of Juda, nor among those that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he clave to the Lord, he departed not from following him; and he kept his commandments, as many as he commanded Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord was with him; and he was wise in all that he undertook: and he revolted from the king of the Assyrians, and served him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He struck the Philistines [even] to Gaza, and to the border of it, from the tower of the watchmen even to the strong city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Ezekias (this is the seventh year of Osee son of Ela king of Israel,) [that] Salamanassar king of the Assyrians came up against Samaria, and besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he took it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Ezekias, (this [is] the ninth year of Osee king of Israel, when Samaria was taken.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the king of the Assyrians carried away the Samaritans to Assyria, and put them in Alae and in Abor, [by] the river Gozan, and [in] the mountains of the Medes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} because they listened not to the voice of the Lord their God, and transgressed his covenant, [even] in all things that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and listened not [to them], nor did [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And in the fourteenth year of king Ezekias came up Sennacherim king of the Assyrians against the strong cities of Juda, and took them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Ezekias king of Juda sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians to Lachis, saying, I have offended; depart from me: whatever you shall lay upon me, I will bear. And the king of Assyria laid upon Ezekias king of Juda [a tribute of] three hundred talents of silver, and thirty talents of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Ezekias gave all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} At that time Ezekias cut off [the gold from] the doors of the temple, and [from] the pillars which Ezekias king of Juda [had] overlaid with gold, and gave it to the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan and Raphis and Rapsakes from Lachis to king Ezekias with a strong force against Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem, and stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is by the way of the fuller's field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they cried to Ezekias: and there came to him Heliakim the son of Chelcias the steward, and Somnas the scribe, and Joas the son of Saphat the recorder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Rapsakes said to them, Say now to Ezekias, Thus says the king, the great king of the Assyrians, What [is] this confidence wherein you trust? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You have said, (but [they are] mere words,) [I have] counsel and strength for war. Now then in whom do you trust, that you have revolted from me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} See now, are you trusting for yourself on this broken staff of reed, [even] upon Egypt? whoever shall stay himself upon it, it shall even go into his hand, and pierce it: so [is] Pharao king of Egypt to all that trust on him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And whereas you have said to me, We trust on the Lord God: [is] not this he, whose high places and altars Ezekias has removed, and has said to Juda and Jerusalem, You⌃ shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now, I pray you, make and agreement with my lord the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you shall be able on your part to set riders upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} How then will you turn away the face of one petty governor, from among the least of my lord's servants? whereas you trust for yourself on Egypt for chariots and horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Heliakim the son of Chelkias, and Somnas, and Joas, said to Rapsakes, Speak now to your servants in the Syrian language, for we understand it; and speak not with us in the Jewish language: and why do you speak in the ears of the people that are on the wall? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Rapsakes said to them, Has my master sent me to your master, and to you, to speak these words? [has he] not [sent me] to the men who sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own water together with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Rapsakes stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jewish language, and spoke, and said, Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} thus says the king, Let not Ezekias encourage you with words: for he shall not be able to deliver you out of his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And let not Ezekias cause you to trust on the Lord, saying, The Lord will certainly deliver us; this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of the Assyrians: listen not to Ezekias: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} for thus says the king of the Assyrians, Gain my favor, and come forth to me, and every man shall drink [of the wine] of his own vine, and every man shall eat of his own fig tree, and shall drink water out of his own cistern; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} until I come and remove you to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, and bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil, and honey, and you⌃ shall live and not die: and do not you⌃ listen to Ezekias, for he deceives you, saying, The Lord shall deliver you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Have the Gods of the nations at all delivered each their own land out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Where is the god of Haemath, and of Arphad? where is the god of Seppharvaim, Ana, and Aba? for have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Who [is there] among all the gods of the countries, who have delivered their countries out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But [the men] were silent, and answered him not a word: for [there was] a commandment of the king, saying, You⌃ shall not answer him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Heliakim the son of Chelcias, the steward, and Somnas the scribe, and Joas the son of Saphat the recorder came in to Ezekias, having torn their garments; and they reported to him the words of Rapsakes.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3278, bc 726 in the third, Hezekiah; Ezekias \textsuperscript{2} Twenty and five years old As Ahaz was 20 years old when he began to reign, and died when he had reigned 16 years, his whole age only amounted to 36 years; and as Hezekiah was, at least, entering on his 25th year when he began to reign, then Ahaz must have been under 12 years of age when his son was born! This is not at all impossible, and there are well-attested facts of men having children at as early a period, especially in eastern countries., am 3278-3306, bc 726-698 Abi, Abijah \textsuperscript{3} right in the sight; according \textsuperscript{4} removed, ; brake; images Heb. statues the brazen serpent; unto those days Nehushtan That is, a piece of brass. \textsuperscript{6} he clave None of the kings of Judah, from the time of the division of the kingdom, equalled Hezekiah in the stedfastness and simplicity of his dependence upon the Lord; in which he aspired to an equality with his progenitor David, who had reigned over the whole land. Even Asa, through weakness of faith, sought the assistance of a heathen prince; and Jehoshaphat formed an alliance with idolatrous Ahab; but Hezekiah clave to the Lord, in entire confidence and unreserved obedience, to the end of his life.; from following him Heb. from after him kept \textsuperscript{7} And the Lord; he prospered; *marg.; rebelled \textsuperscript{8} the Philistines; Gaza Heb. Azzah from the tower \textsuperscript{9} am 3281, bc 723 the fourth year, Shalmaneser; Shalman \textsuperscript{10} am 3283, bc 721 they took it \textsuperscript{11} the king;, ; Halah It is thought, with much probability, that Halah, or Chalach, is Ptolemy's Calachene, the northern part of Assyria; that Habor, or Chabor, is the mountain or mountainous country, between Media and Assyria, called by Ptolemy, Χαβωρας, Chaboras; and that Gozan is Gauzanitis of Ptolemy, situated between that mountain and the Caspian sea, and between the two channels of the river Cyrus. \textsuperscript{13} am 3291, bc 713 the fourteenth; Sennacherib Heb. Sanherib come up \textsuperscript{17} am 3294, bc 710 the king; Tartan Calmet remarks, that these are not the names of persons, but of offices: Tartan signifies "he who presides over gifts or tribute; " Rabsaris, "the chief of the eunuchs; " and Rabshakeh, "the chief cup-bearer." great Heb. heavy the conduit of the upper pool If the Fuller's field were near En-Rogel, or the Fuller's fountain, east of Jerusalem, as is generally supposed, then the conduit of the upper pool may been an aqueduct that brought the water from the upper or eastern reservoir of that fountain, which had been seized in order to distress the city. \textsuperscript{18} Eliakim;, Shebna the scribe or, secretary, *marg. the recorder \textsuperscript{19} Rabshakeh He was the chief speaker, being a very eloquent man, and, according to the Hebrews, whom Procopius follows, an apostate Jew; which is not improbable, as he spoke Hebrew so fluently; and when he blasphemed the Divine Majesty, the king and nobles rent their clothes, which was usual unless the blasphemer were an Israelite. Thus saith; What confidence \textsuperscript{20} sayest or, talkest vain words Heb. word of the lips, I have counsel and strength for the war. or, but counsel and strength are for the war. rebellest \textsuperscript{21} trustest Heb. trustest thee the staff; upon Egypt, so is Pharaoh \textsuperscript{22} We trust; whose high places \textsuperscript{23} pledges Heb. hostages I will deliver \textsuperscript{24} How then;, thy trust;, ; chariots \textsuperscript{26} Speak Perceiving that the object of this blasphemous caitiff was to stir up the people to sedition, they mildly and reasonably required him to make his proposals in the Syrian language. in the Syrian language \textsuperscript{27} eat; their own piss Heb. the water of their feet \textsuperscript{28} Rabshakeh; the king of Assyria \textsuperscript{31} Make an agreement with me or, Seek my favour, Heb. Make with me a blessing, ; eat ye; cistern or, pit \textsuperscript{32} I come, like your own;, persuadeth or, deceiveth \textsuperscript{34} the gods; Hamath, there is little doubt, was the Epiphania of the Greeks, as Josephus, Theodoret, and Jerome, expressly assert. It was a celebrated city of Syria, situated on the Orontes, and the present Hamah doubtless occupies its site; as Abulfeda, who was prince or emir of Hamah about ad 1345, expressly states, in his Description of Syria, that Hamah is an ancient city mentioned in the writings of the Israelites. It is still a considerable town, situated on both sides of the Orontes, about three days' journey and a half from Tripoli; and must contain, Burckhardt says, at least 30, 000 inhabitants. Arpad is probably the town of Arphas, mentioned by Josephus as limiting the province of Gamalitis, Gaulanitis, Batanea, and Trachonitis, to the ne; and the Raphan, or Raphanea, which Stephanus places near Epiphania. the gods, Ava, have they delivered \textsuperscript{35} Who are; that the Lord\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 19}
\markright{KINGS IV 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when king Ezekias heard it, that he tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth, an went into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he sent Heliakim the steward, and Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, clothed with sackcloth, to Esaias the prophet the son of Amos. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they said to him, Thus says Ezekias, This day [is] a day of tribulation, and rebuke, and provocation: for the children are come to the travail-[pangs], but the mother has no strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Peradventure the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rapsakes, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to reproach the living God and to revile him with the words which the Lord your God has heard: and you shall offer [your] prayer for the remnant that is found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So the servants of king Ezekias came to Esaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esaias said to them, Thus shall you⌃ say to your master, Thus says the Lord, Be not afraid of the words which you have heard, wherewith the servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold, I send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a report, and shall return to his own land; and I will overthrow him with the sword in his own land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So Rapsakes returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Lobna: for he heard that he [had] departed from Lachis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he heard concerning Tharaca king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he is come forth to fight with you: and he returned, and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let not your God on whom you trust encourage you, saying, Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hands of the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians have done in all the lands, to waste them utterly: and shall you be delivered? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Have the gods of the nations at all delivered them, whom my fathers destroyed; both Gozan, and Charran, and Raphis, and the sons of Edem who were in Thaesthen? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Where is the king of Haemath, and the king of Arphad? and where is the king of the city of Seppharvaim, of Ana, and Aba? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Ezekias took the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it: and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Ezekias spread it before the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and said, O Lord God of Israel that dwell over the cherubs, you are the only god in all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear: open, Lord, your eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherim, which he has sent to reproach the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For truly, Lord, the kings of Assyria have wasted the nations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and have cast their gods into the fire: because they are no gods, but the works of men's hands, wood and stone; and they have destroyed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And now, O Lord our God, deliver us out of his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth shall know that you alone [are] the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Esaias the son of Amos sent to Ezekias, saying, Thus says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, I have heard your prayer to me concerning Sennacherim king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} This [is] the word which the Lord has spoken against him; The virgin daughter of Sion has made light of you, and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Whom have you reproached, and whom have you reviled? and against whom have you lifted up your voice, and raised your eyes on high? [Is it] against the Holy One of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} By your messengers you have reproached the Lord, and have said, I will go up with the multitude of my chariots, to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Libanus, and I have cut down the height of his cedar, [and] his choice cypresses; and I have come into the midst of the forest and of Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} I have refreshed [myself], and have drunk strange waters, and I have dried up with the sole of my foot all the rivers of fortified places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I have brought about [the matter], I have brought it to a conclusion; and it is come to the destruction of the bands of warlike prisoners, [even of] strong cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they that lived in them were weak in hand, they quaked and were confounded, they became [as] grass of the field, or [as] the green herb, the grass [growing on] houses, and that which is trodden down by him that stands [upon it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But I know your down-sitting, and your going forth, and your rage against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Because you were angry against me, and your fierceness is come up into my ears, therefore will I put my hooks in your nostrils, and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And this shall be a sign to you; eat this year the things that grow of themselves, and in the second year the things which spring up: and in the third year [let there be] sowing, and reaping, and planting of vineyards, and eat you⌃ the fruit of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he shall increase him that has escaped of the house of Juda: and the remnant [shall strike] root beneath, and it shall produce fruit above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For from Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and he that escapes from the mountain of Sion: the zeal of the Lord of host shall do this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} [Is it] not so? Thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians, He shall not enter into this city, and he shall not shoot an arrow there, neither shall a shield come against it, neither shall he heap a mound against it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} By the way by which he comes, by it shall he return, and he shall not enter into this city, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And I will defend this city as with a shield, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And it came to pass at night that the angel of the Lord went forth, an struck in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred and eighty-five thousand: and they rose early in the morning, and, behold, [these were] all dead corpses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Sennacherim king of the Assyrians departed, and went and returned, and lived in Nineve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And it came to pass, while he was worshipping in the house of Meserach his god, that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Ararath; and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when king he rent; covered; went into \textsuperscript{2} he sent Eliakim; to Isaiah; Esaias the son of Amoz \textsuperscript{3} This day; blasphemy or, provocation; for the children \textsuperscript{4} the Lord; whom the king reprove; lift up; the remnant; left Heb. found \textsuperscript{6} Isaiah, Be not afraid; , the servants \textsuperscript{7} a blast; hear a rumour; I will cause \textsuperscript{9} when he heard When Sennacherib had levied contributions on Hezekiah, he marched his army into Egypt; where, after several successes, he laid siege to Pelusium, and spent much time in it; but hearing that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, whom Strabo calls Therchon, was marching against him with a great army, to assist his kinsman Sevechus, or Sethon, the king of Egypt, he durst not abide his coming, but raised the siege; and returning to Judea, he encamped against Lachish, and afterwards against Libnah. But finding that Tirhakah pursued him as a fugitive, he marched back to encounter him; and having totally routed his army, he returned to wreak his vengeance on Hezekiah.; sent \textsuperscript{12} Have the gods Gozan; Haran; Charran Rezeph was probably either Rezapha, which Ptolemy places in the Palmyrene, west of the Euphrates; or rather, Rezipha, in Mesopotamia, east of the Euphrates. By the hand of messengers; With the multitude; tall cedar trees thereof Heb. tallness of the cedar-trees thereof. the forest of his Carmel. or, the forest, and his fruitful field. \textsuperscript{24} I have digged etc. I have conquered strange countries, and marched through the driest places, in which I have digged wells for my army. with the sole My infantry have been so numerous, that they alone have been sufficient to dry up all the rivers of besieged places, either by drinking them, or by diverting their course into other channels.; besieged places or, fenced places \textsuperscript{25} Hast thou not etc. or, Hast thou not heard how I have made it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? \subsection*{Kings IV 20}
\markright{KINGS IV 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In those days was Ezekias sick [even] to death. And the prophet Esaias the son of Amos came in to him, and said to him, Thus says the Lord, Give charge to your household; [for] you shall die, and not live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ezekias turned to the wall, and prayed to the Lord, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Lord, remember, I pray you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your eyes. And Ezekias wept with a great weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Esaias was in the middle court, and the word of the Lord came to him, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Turn back, and you shall say to Ezekias the ruler of my people, Thus says the Lord God of your father David, I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears: behold, I will heal you: on the third day you shall go up to the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will add to your days fifteen years; and I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and I will defend this city for my own sake, and for my servant's David sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said, Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it upon the ulcer, and he shall be well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Ezekias said to Esaias, What [is] the sign that the Lord will heal me, and I shall go up to the house of the Lord on the third day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Esaias said, This [is] the sign from the Lord, that the Lord will perform the word which he has spoken, the shadow [of the dial] shall advance ten degrees: [or] if it should go back ten degrees [this would also be the sign]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Ezekias said, [It is] a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees: nay, but let the shadow return ten degrees backward on the dial. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Esaias the prophet cried to the Lord: and the shadow returned back ten degrees on the dial. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} At that time Marodach Baladan, son of Baladan king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Ezekias, because he had heard that Ezekias was sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Ezekias rejoiced at them, and showed all the house of his spices, the silver and the gold, the spices, and the fine oil, and the armory, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing which Ezekias did not show them in his house, and in all his dominion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Esaias the prophet went in to king Ezekias, and said to him, What said these men? and whence came they to you? And Ezekias said, they came to me from a distant land, [even] from Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said, What saw they in your house? And he said, They saw all things that [are] in my house: there was nothing in my house which I showed not to them; yes, all that was in my treasures also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Esaias said to Ezekias, Hear the word of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold, the days come, that all things that are in your house shall be taken, and all that your fathers have treasured up until this day, to Babylon; and there shall not fail a word, which the Lord has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And as for your sons which shall come forth of you, which you shall beget, [the enemy] shall take them, and they shall be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Ezekias said to Esaias, Good [is] the word of the Lord which he has spoken: [only] let there be peace in my days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the rest of the acts of Ezekias, and all his might, and all that he made, the fountain and the aqueduct, and [how] he brought water into the city, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ezekias slept with his fathers: and Manasses his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3291, bc 713 was Hezekiah; the prophet, Set thine house in order Heb. Give charge concerning thine house; *marg. thou shalt die \textsuperscript{3} remember;, ;, ; I have walked; in truth; a perfect heart, ; wept sore Heb. wept with a great weeping \textsuperscript{5} Turn again; the captain; the God; I have heard; I have seen, ; I will heal; thou shalt go \textsuperscript{6} I will add; I will defend \textsuperscript{7} Take a lump; the boil The word shechin, from the Arabic sachana, to be hot, signifies an inflammatory tumour, or burning boil; and some think that Hezekiah's malady was a pleurisy; others, that it was the plague; and others, the elephantiasis, a species of leprosy, as one of the Hexapla versions renders in . A poultice of figs might be very proper to maturate a boil, or dismiss any obstinate inflammatory swelling; but we need not discuss its propriety in this case, because it was as much the means which God chose to bless for his recovery, as the clay which Christ moistened to anoint the eyes of the blind man; for in both cases, without Divine interposition the cure could not have been effected. \textsuperscript{11} cried unto; he brought; dial Heb. degrees \textsuperscript{12} am 3292, bc 712 Berodachbaladan, Merodach-baladan king Babylon;, sent letters, for he had heard \textsuperscript{13} showed; precious things or, spicery, armour or, jewels, Heb. vessels there was nothing \textsuperscript{14} came Isaiah What said; a far country \textsuperscript{18} thy sons; they shall be "Fulfilled in ." \textsuperscript{19} Good; Is it not good, etc or, Shall there not be peace and truth, etc. peace and truth \textsuperscript{20} he made a pool, ; the book\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 21}
\markright{KINGS IV 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Manasses [was] twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Apsiba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he built again the high places, which Ezekias his father [had] demolished; and set up an altar to Baal, and made groves as Achaab king of Israel [made them]; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, whereas he had said, In Jerusalem I will place my name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he built an altar to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he caused his sons to pass through the fire, and used divination and auspices, and made groves, and multiplied wizards, so as to do that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he set up the graven image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I even place my name for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, [even of those] who shall keep all that I commanded, according to all the commandments which my servant Moses commanded them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But they listened not; and Manasses led them astray to do evil in the sight of the Lord, beyond the nations whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord spoke by his servants the prophets, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Forasmuch as Manasses the king of Juda has wrought all these evil abominations, beyond all that the Amorite did, who lived before [him], and has led Juda also into sin by their idols, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [it shall] not [be] so. Thus says the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I bring calamities upon Jerusalem and Juda, so that both the ears of every one that hears shall tingle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Achaab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a jar is wiped, and turned upside down in the wiping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will reject the remnant of my inheritance, and will deliver them into the hands of their enemies; and they shall be for a plunder and for a spoil to all their enemies: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} forasmuch as they have done wickedly in my sight, and have provoked me from the day that I brought out their fathers out of Egypt, even until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Moreover Manasses shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem [with it] from one end to the other, beside his sins with which he caused Juda to sin, in doing evil in the eyes of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the rest of the acts of Manasses, and all that he did, and his sin which he sinned, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Manasses slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his house, [even] in the garden of Oza: and Amos his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Twenty and two years old [was] Amos when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Mesollam, daughter of Arus of Jeteba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasses his father did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he walked in all the way in which his father walked, and served the idols which his father served, and worshipped them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he forsook the Lord God of his fathers, and walked not in the way of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the servants of Amos conspired against him, and killed the king in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the people of the land killed all that had conspired against king Amos; and the people of the land made Josias king in his room. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the rest of the acts of Amos, [even] all that he did, behold, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Oza: and Josias his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3306-3361, bc 698-643 was twelve; Manasses Hephzibah; *marg. \textsuperscript{2} And he did, ; after the abominations \textsuperscript{3} the high places; he reared;, a grove Rather, as we have before remarked, Asherah or Astarte. So Castel defines Asherah to be Simulacrum ligneum Astarte dicatum; "A wooden image dedicated to Astarte." Ahab; and worshipped \textsuperscript{6} am 3321, bc 683 he made; observed times; familiar; wrought \textsuperscript{7} am 3306-3327, bc 698-677 he set; In this house \textsuperscript{8} will I make; only if they \textsuperscript{9} they hearkened; seduced; more evil \textsuperscript{10} In the following verses the doom of Judah and Jerusalem is passed, and it is a heavy doom. The prophets were sent in the first place to teach them the knowledge of God, to remind them of their duty, and direct them in it. If they succeeded not in that, their next work was to reprove them for their sins, and to set them in view before them, that they might repent and reform, and return to their duty. If in this they prevailed not, their next work was to foretell the judgments of God, that the terror of them might awaken to repentance those who would not be made sensible of the obligations of his love; or else that the execution of them, in their season, might be a demonstration of the divine mission of the prophets who foretold them. They were made judges to those who would not hear and receive them as teachers. - Henry. \textsuperscript{11} Because; above all; made Judah \textsuperscript{13} I will stretch This metaphor is taken from the custom of using a line in measuring land, and in dividing portions of it among several persons. Samaria was taken, pillaged, and ruined, and its inhabitants carried into captivity: Jerusalem shall have the same measure.; the plummet; I will wipe I will empty Jerusalem of all its wealth and inhabitants, as truly as a dish turned up and wiped is emptied of its contents.; wiping it, and turning it upside down Heb. he wipeth and turneth it upon the face thereof \textsuperscript{14} And I will; the remnant, ; deliver \textsuperscript{16} Manasseh; , ; one end to another Heb. mouth to mouth beside his sin \textsuperscript{18} am 3361, bc 643 and was buried \textsuperscript{19} am 3361-3363, bc 643-641 Amon; two years \textsuperscript{24} the people of the land slew made Josiah\par}
