\subsection*{Kings IV 22}
\markright{KINGS IV 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Josias [was] eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Jedia, daughter of Edeia of Basuroth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in all the way of David his father; he turned not aside to the right hand or to the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass in the eighteenth year of king Josias, in the eighth month, the king sent Sapphan the son of Ezelias the son of Mesollam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Go up to Chelcias the high priest, and take account of the money that is brought into the house of the Lord, which they that keep the door have collected of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And let them give it into the hand of the workmen that are appointed in the house of the Lord. And he gave it to the workmen in the house of the Lord, to repair the breaches of the house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} [even] to the carpenters, and builders, and masons, [and] also to purchase timber and hewn stones, to repair the breaches of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Only they did not call them to account for the money that was given to them, because they dealt faithfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Chelcias the high priest said to Saphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Chelcias gave the book to Sapphan, and he read it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he went into the house of the Lord to the king, and reported the matter to the king, and said, Your servants have collected the money that was found in the house of the Lord, and have given it into the hand of the workmen that are appointed in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Sapphan the scribe spoke to the king, saying, Chelcias the priest has given me a book. And Sapphan read it before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king commanded Chelcias the priest, and Achikam the son of Sapphan, and Achobor the son of Michaias, and Sapphan the scribe, and Asaias the king's servant, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Go, enquire of the Lord for me, and for all the people, and for all Juda, and concerning the words of this book that has been found: for the wrath of the Lord that has been kindled against us [is] great, because our fathers listened not to the words of this book, to do according to all the things written concerning us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So Chelcias the priest went, and Achicam, and Achobor, and Sapphan, and Asaias, to Olda the prophetess, the mother of Sellem the son of Thecuan son of Aras, keeper of the robes; and she lived in Jerusalem in Masena; and they spoke to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And she said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, Say to the man that sent you to me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus says the Lord, Behold, I bring evil upon this place, and upon them that dwell in it, [even] all the words of the book which the king of Juda has read: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} because they have forsaken me, and burnt incense to other gods, that they might provoke me with the works of their hands: therefore my wrath shall burn forth against this place, and shall not be quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And to the king of Juda that sent you to enquire of the Lord, —thus shall you⌃ say to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, [As for] the words which you have heard; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} because your heart was softened, and you were humbled before [me], when you heard all that I spoke against this place, and against the inhabitants of it, that it should be utterly destroyed and accursed, and you did rend your garments, and weep before me; I also have heard, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} It shall not be so [therefore]: behold, I [will] add you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your tomb in peace, and your eyes shall not see [any] among all the evils which I bring upon this place.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3363-3394, bc 641-610 Josiah This prince was one of the best, if not the best, of all the Jewish kings since the time of David. He began well, continued well, and ended well.; Josias eight years old; Boscath This was a city in the plain country of the tribe of Judah; and is mentioned in the parallel passage along with Lachish and Eglon., Bozkath \textsuperscript{4} Hilkiah; that he may Ten years seem to have elapsed since the people began to present the accustomed offerings; yet no one had taken an account of them, nor were they applied to the purpose for which they were given. sum the silver; the keepers; door Heb. threshold \textsuperscript{6} carpenters or, artificers, builders; masons or, repairers of the wall \textsuperscript{8} I have found This certainly was a genuine copy of the divine law, and probably the autograph of Moses, as it is said, in the parallel place of Chronicles, to be the book of the law of the Lord by Moses. It is not probable that this was the only copy of the law in the land, or that Josiah had never before seen the book of Moses; but the fact seems to be, that this was the original of the covenant renewed by Moses in the plains of Moab, and now being unexpectedly found, its antiquity, the occasion of its being made, the present circumstances of the people, the imperfect state in which the reformation was as yet, after all that had been done, would all concur to produce the effect here mentioned on the mind of the pious Josiah. \textsuperscript{9} Shaphan, ;, ; the scribe gathered Heb. melted \textsuperscript{12} the king; Ahikam; Achbor, Abdon Michaiah or, Micah \textsuperscript{13} inquire; great; because our fathers \textsuperscript{14} prophetess; Tikvah, Tikvath, Hasrah wardrobe Heb. garments; college or, second part \textsuperscript{17} have forsaken;, ; the works; therefore shall not be \textsuperscript{18} the king thus shall ye \textsuperscript{19} thine heart;, ; humbled; a desolation; hast rent wept; I also have \textsuperscript{20} I will gather; thou shalt During thy life, none of these calamities shall fall upon thee nor thy people; no adversary shall be permitted to disturb the peace of Judea; and thou shalt at last "be gathered into thy grave in peace." Now, though it is stated that Pharaoh-Necho slew him at Megiddo, yet the Assyrians and the Jews were at peace; and though Josiah might feel it his duty to oppose the Egyptian king's going against his friend and ally, and that, in his endeavours to oppose him, he was mortally wounded at Megiddo, yet certainly he was not killed there, but was brought to Jerusalem, where he died in peace. gathered\par}

\subsection*{Kings IV 23}
\markright{KINGS IV 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} So they reported the word to the king: and the king sent and gathered all the elders of Juda and Jerusalem to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Juda and all who lived in Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people small and great; and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his ordinances with all the heart and with all the soul, to confirm the words of this covenant; [even] the things written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king commanded Chelcias the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and them that kept the door, to bring out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and all the host of heaven, and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kedron, and took the ashes of them to Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he burned the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Juda [had] appointed, (and they burned incense in the high places and in the cities of Juda, and the places around about Jerusalem); and them that burned incense to Baal, and to the sun, and to the moon, and to Mazuroth, and to all the host of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he carried out the grove from the house of the Lord to the brook Kedron, and burned it at the brook Kedron, and reduced it to powder, and cast its powder on the sepulchres of the sons of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he pulled down the house of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove tents for the grove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he brought up all the priest from the cities of Juda, and defiled the high places where the priests burned incense, from Gaebal even to Bersabee; and he pulled down the house of the gates that was by the door of the gate of Joshua the ruler of the city, on a man's left hand at the gate of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Only the priests of the high places went not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, for they only ate leavened bread in the midst of their brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he defiled Taphes which is in the valley of the son of Ennom, [constructed] for a man to cause his son or his daughter to pass through fire to Moloch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he burned the horses which the king of Juda had given to the sun in the entrance of the house of the Lord, by the treasury of Nathan the king's eunuch, in the suburbs; and he burned the chariot of the sun with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the altars that were on the roof of the upper chamber of Achaz, which the kings of Juda had made, and the altars which Manasses had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, did the king pull down and forcibly remove from thence, and cast their dust into the brook of Kedron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king defiled the house that was before Jerusalem, on the right hand of the mount of Mosthath, which Solomon king of Israel built to Astarte the abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chamos the abomination of Moab, and to Moloch the abomination of the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he broke in pieces the pillars, and utterly destroyed the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Also the high altar in Baethel, which Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who made Israel to sin, had made, even that high altar he tore down, and broke in pieces the stones of it, and reduced it to powder, and burnt the grove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Josias turned aside, and saw the tombs that were there in the city, and sent, and took the bones out of the tombs, and burnt them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God spoke, when Jeroboam stood by the altar at the feast: and he turned and raised his eyes to the tomb of the man of God that spoke these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said, What [is] that mound which I see? And the men of the city said to him, [It is the grave of] the man of God that came out of Juda, and uttered these imprecations which he imprecated upon the altar of Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said, Let him alone; let no one disturb his bones. So his bones were spared, together with the bones of the prophet that came out of Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Moreover Josias removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel made to provoke the Lord, and did to them all that he did in Baethel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places that were there on the altars, and burnt the bones of men upon them, and returned to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover to the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For a passover [such as] this had not been kept from the days of the judges who judged Israel, even all the days of the kings of Israel, and of the kings of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But in the eighteenth year of king Josias, was the passover kept to the Lord in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Moreover Josias removed the sorcerers, and the wizards, and the theraphin, and the idols, and all the abominations that had been set up in the land of Juda and in Jerusalem, that he might keep the words of the law that were written in the book, which Chelcias the priest found in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} There was no king like him before him, who turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses; and after him there rose not one like him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Nevertheless the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great anger, wherewith he was angry in his anger against Juda, because of the provocations, wherewith Manasses provoked him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord said, I will also remove Juda from my presence, as I removed Israel, and will reject this city which I have chosen [even] Jerusalem, and the house [of] which I said, My name shall be there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the rest of the acts of Josias, and all that he did, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And in his days went up Pharao Nechao king of Egypt against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates: and Josias went out to meet him: and Nechao killed him in Mageddo when he saw him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And his servants carried him dead from Mageddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his sepulchre: and the people of the land took Joachaz the son of Josias, and anointed him, and made him king in the room of his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Twenty and three years old was Joachaz when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Amital, daughter of Jeremias of Lobna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Pharao Nechao removed him to Rablaam in the land of Emath, so that he should not reign in Jerusalem; and imposed a tribute on the land, one hundred talents of silver, and one hundred talents of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Pharao Nechao made Eliakim son of Josias king of Juda king over them in the place of his father Josias, and he changed his name [to] Joakim, and he took Joachaz and brought him to Egypt, and he died there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Joakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharao; but he assessed the land to give the money at the command of Pharao: they gave the silver and the gold [each] man according to his assessment together with the people of the land to give to Pharao Nechao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Twenty-five years old [was] Joakim when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Jeldaph, daughter of Phadail of Ruma. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the lord, according to all that his fathers had done.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} both small and great Heb. from small even unto great; he read;, the book \textsuperscript{3} stood; made a covenant; to walk his commandments, ; with all their heart, ; And all \textsuperscript{4} priestss of the second order These were either such as occasionally supplied the high priests's office, or those of the second course or order established by David. See the references.; the keepers; to bring;, Baal;, ; Kidron; Cedron Bethel \textsuperscript{5} put down Heb. caused to cease the idolatrous priests Heb. Chemarim. *marg. "Foretold. ." planets or, twelve signs, or constellations, So the Vulgate duodecim signa, "the twelve signs, " i.e., the zodiac; which is the most probable meaning of the word mazzaloth, from the Arabic manzeel, a caravanserai, house, or dwelling, as being the apparent dwellings of the sun in his annual course; and the Targumists and Rabbins often employ the words tereysar mazzalaya, to denote the signs of the zodiac. all the host \textsuperscript{6} the grove Or rather, Asherah, or Astarte.; and burned; the graves; the children Probably the common people. \textsuperscript{7} the sodomites; where; hangings Heb. houses \textsuperscript{8} from etc. The northern and southern borders of Judah. Geba; Beersheba \textsuperscript{9} the priests; but they did \textsuperscript{10} Topheth;, Tophet the valley; *Gr. might make \textsuperscript{11} the sun; house of the Lord Throughout the East, the horse because of his swiftness and utility, was dedicated to the sun; and the Greeks and Romans feigned that the chariot of the sun was drawn by four horses, Pyrous, Eous, Aithon, and Phlegon, and hence also chariots were dedicated to that luminary. Jarchi says, that those who adored the sun had horses, which they mounted every morning, to go out to meet him at his rising. The kings of Judah had imitated these idolatrous customs, and kept the horses of the sun even at the entrance of the temple of the Lord! chamberlain or, eunuch, or officer \textsuperscript{12} on the top; which Manasseh; brake them down from thence or, ran from thence cast \textsuperscript{13} the mount of corruption that is, the mount of Olives, Houbigant, deriving the Hebrew mashchith from mashach, "to anoint, " reads "the Mount of Olives." Jarchi, following the Chaldee, also says this was the Mount of Olives; for this is the mount hammishchah, of unction, but because of the idolatrous purposes for which it was used, the Scripture changed the appellation to the mount of hammashchith, corruption. Solomon; Ashtoreth; Chemosh;, Milcom, Malcham \textsuperscript{14} he brake; images Heb. statues the bones of men \textsuperscript{16} burned; who proclaimed The Septuagint and Hexaplar Syriac at Paris insert, "when Jeroboam stood by the altar at the feast. Κωμη δε εστιν η Ρεβλαθα της νυν καλουμενης Εμεσης . Emesa was a city of Syria, situated on the Orontes, and, according to the Antonine Itinerary, 18 miles from Laodicea ad Libanum. It is now called Homs, or Hems, about eight hours, or twenty-four miles se of Hamah or Hamath, in the road to Damascus. The present town only occupies about one quarter of the space contained within the ancient walls, which apparently date from the time of the Saracens. \subsection*{Kings IV 24}
\markright{KINGS IV 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In his days went up Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and Joakim became his servant three years; and [then] he turned and revolted from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the lord sent against him the bands of the Chaldeans, and the bands of Syria, and the bans of Moab, and the bands of the children of Ammon, and sent them into the land of Juda to prevail [against it], according to the word of the Lord, which he spoke by his servants the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Moreover it was the purpose of the Lord concerning Juda, to remove them from his presence, because of the sins of Manasses, according to all that he did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Moreover he shed innocent blood, and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord would not pardon [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the rest of the acts of Joakim, and all that he did, behold, [are] not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joakim slept with his fathers: and Joachim his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the king of Egypt came no more out of his land: for the king of Babylon took away all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the river of Egypt as far as the river Euphrates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Eighteen years old [was] Joachim when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Nestha, daughter of Ellanastham, of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} At that time went up Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon to Jerusalem, and the city was besieged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Joachim king of Juda came forth to the king of Babylon, he and his servants, and his mother, and his princes, and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he brought forth thence all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king's house, and he cut up all the golden vessels which Solomon the king of Israel [had] made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he carried away [the inhabitants of] Jerusalem, and all the captains, and the mighty men, taking captive ten thousand prisoners, and every artificer and smith: and only the poor of the land were left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he carried Joachim away to Babylon, and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his eunuchs: and he carried away the mighty men of the land into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And all the men of might, even seven thousand, and one thousand artificers and smiths: all [were] mighty [men] fit for war; and the king of Babylon carried them captive to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king of Babylon made Batthanias his son king in his stead, and called his name Sedekias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Twenty and one years old [was] Sedekias when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Amital daughter of Jeremias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Joachim did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For it was according to the Lord's anger against Jerusalem and on Juda, until he cast them out of his presence, that Sedekias revolted against the king of Babylon.\par

In the East, a body exposed during the night would be a prey to wild animals; if any of it were left till the morning, the carnivorous birds would devour it.; Jehoiachin As this man reigned only three months, and was a mere vassal of the king of Babylon, his reign is scarcely reckoned; and therefore Jeremiah ( ) says of Jehoiakim, "he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David." \textsuperscript{7} the king, from the river \textsuperscript{8} Jehoiachin; Jeconiah, Coniah, Jechonias eighteen years In the parallel place, he is said to be only eight years old; but this must be a mistake, for we find that having reigned only three months, he was carried captive to Babylon, and there had wives; and had he been of such a tender age, it could scarcely have been said that, as a king, "he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord." \textsuperscript{9} evil Young renders, "the evil thing, " noting, "that is, idolatry." according \textsuperscript{10} At that time was besieged Heb. came into siege \textsuperscript{12} Jehoiachin; officers or, eunuchs took him; eighth year "Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year." \textsuperscript{13} he carried; and cut; which Solomon \textsuperscript{14} all That is, all the chief men, the nobles, and the artificers. Jerusalem; craftsmen So, the poorest sort \textsuperscript{15} he carried; officers or, eunuchs \textsuperscript{17} the king; his father's brother He was son of Josiah, brother to Jehoiakim, and uncle of Jehoiachin.; changed The change of name was to shew Nebuchadnezzar's supremacy, and that Zedekiah was only his vassal or viceroy. \subsection*{Kings IV 25}
\markright{KINGS IV 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, [that] Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came, and all his host, against Jerusalem; and he encamped against it, and built a mound against it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Sedekias on the ninth day of the month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the city was broken up, and all the men of war went forth by night, by the way of the gate between the walls, this is [the gate] of the king's garden: and the Chaldeans [were set] against the city round about: and [the king] went by the way of the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the force of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army was dispersed from about him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they took the king, and brought him to the king of Babylon to Reblatha; and he gave judgment upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he killed the sons of Sedekias before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Sedekias, and bound him in fetters, and brought him to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month (this [is] the nineteenth year of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon), came Nabuzardan, captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every house did the captain of the guard burn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the force of the Chaldeans pulled down the wall of Jerusalem round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Nabuzardan the captain of the guard removed the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the men who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vine-dressers and husbandmen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Chaldeans broke to pieces the brazen pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the Lord, and carried their brass to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the caldrons, and the shovels, and the bowls, and the censers, and all the brazen vessels with which they minister, he took. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the captain of the guard took the fire-pans, and the gold and silver bowls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Two pillars, and one sea, and the bases which Solomon made for the house of the Lord: there was no weight of the brass of all the vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The height of one pillar [was] eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was of brass: and the height of the chapiter was three cubits: the border, and the pomegranates on the chapiter round about were all of brass: and so it was with the second pillar with its border. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the captain of the guard took Saraias the high-priest, and Sophonias the second in order, and the three doorkeepers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they took out of the city one eunuch who was commander of the men of war, and five men that saw the face of the king, that were found in the city, and the secretary of the commander-in-chief, who took account of the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land that were found in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Nabuzardan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Reblatha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king of Babylon struck them and killed them at Reblatha in the land of Aemath. because they were afraid of the Chaldeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the carrying away of Joachim king of Juda, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, [that] Evialmarodec king of Babylon in the [first] year of his reign lifted up the head of Joachim king of Juda, and brought him out of his prison-house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings that were with him in Babylon; \section*{1 Chronicles Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Ezra (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Conservative tradition often links Chronicles to Ezra; the genealogical and priestly concerns fit a post-exilic covenant-restoration setting.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the human author, but Chronicles participates in the inspired canonical history Christ endorsed in the Hebrew Scriptures.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} post-exilic\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} likely 5th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology surveys from Adam to David, then narrows to David's reign with strong priestly and worship emphasis.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The Greek tradition preserves the same broad shape, though Chronicles has far fewer dramatic MT/LXX divergences than Samuel-Kings.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Post-exilic retelling of sacred history from Adam to David, written for the restored community.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To reframe Israel's history around covenant continuity, temple worship, priesthood, and the Davidic line.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} genealogy; temple worship; Levites; Davidic kingship; covenant continuity\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Genealogies 1-9; David's reign and preparations for worship 10-29. Qumran Chronicles fragments survive only in limited form | Subst. Second Temple period No extensive early Qumran witness comparable to Samuel; the chronicler's text is chiefly known from later Hebrew manuscripts and Greek tradition | Heb. n/a Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Alexandrinus preserves Chronicles in Greek; Vaticanus is defective in parts of the historical books\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 5th century AD by Use of Chronicles material in later Jewish historiography (Josephus)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1st century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Chronicles often preserves an interpretive retelling distinct from Samuel-Kings; textual work must distinguish redactional purpose from transmissional difference.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 2}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} These [are] the names of the sons of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Ruben, Symeon, Levi, Juda, Issachar, Zabulon, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Nephthali, Gad, Aser. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The sons of Juda; Er, Aunan, Selom. [These] three were born to him of the daughter of Sava the Chananitish woman: and Er, the firstborn of Juda, [was] wicked before the Lord, and he killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Thamar his daughter-in-law bore to him Phares, and Zara: all the sons of Juda [were] five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The sons of Phares, Esrom, and Jemuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the sons of Zara, Zambri, and Aetham, and Aemuan, and Calchal, and Darad, [in] all five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Charmi; Achar the troubler of Israel, who was disobedient in the accursed thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the sons of Aetham; Azarias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the sons of Esrom who were born to him; Jerameel, and Aram, and Chaleb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Aram begot Aminadab, and Aminadab begot Naasson, chief of the house of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Naasson begot Salmon, and Salmon begot Booz, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and Booz begot Obed, and Obed begot Jessae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Jessae begot his firstborn Eliab, Aminadab [was] the second, Samaa the third, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Nathanael the fourth, Zabdai the fifth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Asam the sixth, David the seventh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And their sister [was] Saruia, and [another] Abigaia: and the sons of Saruia [were] Abisa, and Joab, and Asael, three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abigaia bore Amessab: and the father of Amessab [was] Jothor the Ismaelite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Chaleb the son of Esrom took Gazuba to wife, and Jerioth: and these [were] her sons; Jasar, and Subab, and Ardon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Gazuba died; and Chaleb took to himself Ephrath, and she bore to him Or. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Or begot Uri, and Uri begot Beseleel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And after this Esron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Galaad, and he took her when he was sixty-five years old; and she bore him Seruch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Seruch begot Jair, and he had twenty-three cities in Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he took Gedsur and Aram, the towns of Jair from them; [with] Canath and its towns, sixty cities. All these [belonged to] the sons of Machir the father of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And after the death of Esron, Chaleb came to Ephratha; and the wife of Esron [was] Abia; and she bore him Ascho the father of Thecoe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the sons of Jerameel the firstborn of Esron [were], the firstborn Ram, and Banaa, and Aram, and Asan his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Jerameel had another wife, and her name [was] Atara: she is the mother of Ozom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerameel were Maas, and Jamin, and Acor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the sons of Ozom were, Samai, and Jadae: and the sons of Samai; Nadab, and Abisur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the name of the wife of Abisur [was] Abichaia, and she bore him Achabar, and Moel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the sons of Nadab; Salad and Apphain; and Salad died without children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the sons of Apphain, Isemiel; and the sons of Isemiel, Sosan; and the sons of Sosan, Dadai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the sons of Dadai, Achisamas, Jether, Jonathan: and Jether died childless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the sons of Jonathan; Phaleth, and Hozam. These were the sons of Jerameel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Sosan had no sons, but daughters. And Sosan had an Egyptian servant, and his name [was] Jochel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Sosan gave his daughter to Jochel his servant to wife; and she bore him Ethi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Ethi begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and Zabed begot Aphamel, and Aphamel begot Obed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Obed begot Jeu, and Jeu begot Azarias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And Azarias begot Chelles, and Chelles begot Eleasa, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} and Eleasa begot Sosomai, and Sosomai begot Salum, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} and Salum begot Jechemias, and Jechemias begot Elisama, and Elisama begot Ismael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the sons of Chaleb the brother of Jerameel [were], Marisa his firstborn, he [is] the father of Ziph:—and the sons of Marisa the father of Chebron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And the sons of Chebron; Core, and Thapphus, and Recom, and Samaa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And Samaa begot Raem the father of Jeclan: and Jeclan begot Samai. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And his son [was] Maon: and Maon [is] the father of Baethsur. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And Gaepha the concubine of Chaleb bore Aram, and Mosa, and Gezue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And the sons of Addai [were] Ragem, and Joatham, and Sogar, and Phalec, and Gaepha, and Sagae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And Chaleb's concubine Mocha bore Saber, and Tharam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} She bore also Sagae the father of Madmena, and Sau the father of Machabena, and the father of Gaebal: and the daughter of Chaleb [was] Ascha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} These were the sons of Chaleb: the sons of Or the firstborn of Ephratha; Sobal the father of Cariathiarim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Salomon the father of Baetha, Lammon the father of Baethalaem, and Arim the father of Bethgedor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And the sons of Sobal the father of Cariathiarim were Araa, and Aesi, and Ammanith, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} and Umasphae, cities of Jair; Aethalim, and Miphithim, and Hesamathim, and Hemasaraim; from these went forth the Sarathaeans, and the sons of Esthaam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} The sons of Salomon; Baethalaem, the Netophathite, Ataroth of the house of Joab, and half of the family of Malathi, Esari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} The families of the scribes dwelling in Jabis; Thargathiim, and Samathiim, and Sochathim, these [are] the Kinaeans that came of Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2252, etc. bc 1752, etc Israel or, Jacob, Reuben \textsuperscript{2} Dan Joseph Benjamin Naphtali Gad Asher \textsuperscript{4} Tamar; Thamar Pharez; Perez; Phares Zerah; Zara \textsuperscript{6} Zimri i.e. snug; my song; my field, ., ;, ; Ethan i.e. perennial, constant; ancient, ., ; *title Heman i.e. faithful, ; *title Calcol i.e. sustenance; comprehended, . Dara i.e. pearl of wisdom, Darda, γψγς, is here called Dara, γψς, by the elision of a γ, daleth, Darda \textsuperscript{7} Carmi Achar Achan is probably called Achar, from the trouble he occasioned., Achan accursed \textsuperscript{9} Jerahmeel Ram; Aram Chelubai, Caleb \textsuperscript{13} his firstborn, Eliab, Elihu Shimma, Shimea, Shammah \textsuperscript{15} David It appears from the parallel places of Samuel, that Jesse had eight sons, of whom David was the eighth and youngest; but one may have died before David came to the throne. \textsuperscript{17} Amasa, ; Jether, ιϊψ, is essentially the same with ιϊψΰ, Ithra, the latter only having the addition of an ΰ aleph; and it is probable, that he was an Ishmaelite by birth but an Israelite by religion., Ithra an Israelite Ishmeelite a descendant of Ishmael \textsuperscript{18} am 2534, etc. bc 1470, etc Caleb, λμα, is the same as Chelubai, λμεαι, the latter simply having a ε, wav inserted, and a ι, yood affixed. This person must have lived some time before Israel left Egypt; for Bezaleel, the principal person employed in constructing the tabernacle, was his grandson., Chelubai \textsuperscript{23} Geshur; Kenath was situated in the tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan. Eusebius says it was called in his time Καναθα, Kanatha; and was a town in the Trachonitis, near Bozra. Josephus places it in Coelo-syria; and Pliny reckons it among the cities of the Decapolis. It was also called Nobah, after Nobah an Israelite, who conquered it ( ); which is placed by Eusebius, eight miles south of Heshbon. see note on . \textsuperscript{25} the sons of Of the persons mentioned in, nothing more is recorded or known. Jerahmeel \textsuperscript{33} Peleth Zaza i.e. going back; brightness; fulness, . \textsuperscript{34} no sons, but daughters, Jarha i.e. increasing moon \textsuperscript{35} Sheshan When the people of the East have no sons, they frequently marry their daughters to their slaves, even when they have much property to bestow upon them. Hassan had been the slave of Kamel, his predecessor; but Kamel, according to the custom of the country, gave him one of his daughters in marriage, and left him at his death one part of his great riches which he had amassed in the course of a long and prosperous life (Maillet, Lett. xi. p. 118). his daughter Attai i.e. opportune \textsuperscript{37} Ephlal i.e. intercession, Obed \textsuperscript{39} Helez i.e. strength, Eleasah i.e. God has wrought \textsuperscript{40} Sisamai i.e. distinguished one; swallow, . Shallum \textsuperscript{41} Jekamiah i.e. let Jah arise, Elishama \textsuperscript{42} Caleb This was not Caleb the son of Jephunneh, but Caleb the son of Hezron, and therefore called the brother of Jerahmeel. See the parallel texts., Chelubai, his firstborn; the father i.e. the founder, Or, as the Targum renders, "the prince of the Ziphites; " for it was usual to call both the founder and the prince of a city its father. Ziph; the father of Hebron \textsuperscript{44} Raham i.e. compassionate, Jorkoam i.e. paleness or spreading of the people, . \textsuperscript{45} Bethzur Beth-zur was situated in the tribe of Judah, twenty miles south from Jerusalem, towards Hebron, according to Eusebius. It was fortified by Rehoboam ( ) and was a fortress of great consequence, principally in the time of the Maccabees.; etc. \textsuperscript{49} the father of Madmannah; Madmannah was a city situated in the southern part of Judah, and towards Gaza, according to Eusebius.; Madmenah Gibea It is probable this was not Gibeah of Benjamin, and the royal residence of Saul, but Gibeah in the tribe of Judah, to which all these other cities belonged.; Gibeah \textsuperscript{50} Caleb This Caleb was the grandson of the preceding, and brother to Uri, the father of Bezaleel. Ephratah, Ephrath Kirjathjearim \textsuperscript{52} Haroeh or, Reaiah; As Haroeh and Reaiah have nearly the same signification, it is probable they were deemed perfectly interchangeable, and indifferently applied. half of the Manahethites or, half of the Menuchites, or, Hatsihammenuchoth. \textsuperscript{54} Bethlehem Netophathites; Ataroth or, Atarites, or crowns of the house of Joab \textsuperscript{55} the scribes; Jabez Kenites; Rechab\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 3}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now these were the sons of David that were born to him in Chebron; the firstborn Amnon, [born] of Achinaam the Jezraelitess; the second Damniel, of Abigaia the Carmelitess. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The third, Abessalom, the son of Mocha the daughter of Tholmai king of Gedsur; the fourth, Adonia the son of Aggith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The fifth, Saphatia, [the son] of Abital; the sixth, Jethraam, [born] of Agla his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Six were born to him in Chebron; and he reigned there seven years and six months: and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And these were born to him in Jerusalem; Samaa, Sobab, Nathan, and Solomon; four [of] Bersabee the daughter of Amiel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and Ebaar, and Elisa, and Eliphaleth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and Nagai, and Naphec, and Japhie, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and Helisama, and Eliada, and Eliphala, nine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} All [these were] the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines, and [there was also] Themar their sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The sons of Solomon; Roboam, Abia his son, Asa his son, Josaphat his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Joram his son, Ochozias his son, Joas his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Amasias his son, Azarias his son, Joathan his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Achaz his son, Ezekias his son, Manasses his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Amon his son, Josia his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of Josia; the firstborn Joanan, the second Joakim, the third Sedekias, the fourth Salum. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the sons of Joakim; Jechonias his son, Sedekias his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the sons of Jechonias; Asir, Salathiel his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Melchiram, and Phadaias, and Sanesar, and Jekimia, and Hosamath, and Nabadias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sons of Phadaias; Zorobabel, and Semei: and the sons of Zorobabel; Mosollam, and Anania, and Salomethi [was] their sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Asube, and Ool, and Barachia, and Asadia, and Asobed, five. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the sons of Anania, Phalettia, and Jesias his son, Raphal his son, Orna his son, Abdia his son, Sechenias his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the son of Sechenias; Samaia: and the sons of Samaia; Chattus, and Joel, and Berri and Noadia, and Saphath, six. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the sons of Noadia: Elithenan, and Ezekia, and Ezricam, three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the sons of Elithenan; Odolia, and Heliasebon, and Phadaia, and Akub, and Joanan, and Dalaaia, and Anan, seven.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2951, etc. bc 1053, etc the sons of David Amnon, Ahinoam, Jezreelitess Daniel It is probable this person had two names. The Targumist says he was "called Chileab, because he was in every respect like his father." of Abigail \textsuperscript{3} Eglah The Targumist, Jarchi, and others, maintain that this was Michal; and though it is stated ( ) that "she had no child to the day of her death, " yet she might have had a child before, at that time living. \textsuperscript{4} there he reigned; and in Jerusalem \textsuperscript{5} Shimea; Shammuah Nathan; Solomon; Bathshua, Bath-sheba, Ammiel, Eliam \textsuperscript{10} Rehoboam, ; Roboam Abia, Abijam, Abijah Asa; Jehoshaphat; Josaphat \textsuperscript{11} Joram; Jehoram Ahaziah; Jehoahaz, Azariah Joash \textsuperscript{12} Amaziah; Azariah; Uzziah, Ozias Jotham; Joatham \textsuperscript{13} Ahaz; Achaz Hezekiah; Ezekias Manasseh; Manasses \textsuperscript{14} Amon; Josiah; Josias, Johanan, or, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Eliakim; Zedekiah, Mattaniah, Shallum, The Targumist says he was called Shallum, "because the kingdom departed from the house of David in his days."; Jehoahaz \textsuperscript{16} Jeconiah, ; Jehoiachin, Coniah, Jechonias Zedekiah As the sons of Jeconiah are enumerated in the succeeding verse, and as Zedekiah is no where else mentioned as the son of Jeconiah, but as the son of Josiah, it is highly probable that son here means successor.; being his uncle \textsuperscript{17} Assir As Salathiel was not the son of Assir, but of Jeconiah, it is probable that the word assir, which signifies a prisoner, is an ephithet applied to Jeconiah, who was a long time prisoner at Babylon. Salathiel, Shealtiel \textsuperscript{19} the sons of Pedaiah As St. Matthew states that Zerubbabel was the son of Salathiel, Houbigant thinks these words should be omitted; and Pedaiah is wanting in the Arabic and Syriac. Zerubbabel; Zorobabel \textsuperscript{22} Hattush six Five only are enumerated in the text, which Houbigant would substitute as the true reading; but probably the father is reckoned with his sons.\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 4}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the sons of Juda; Phares, Esrom, and Charmi, and Or, Subal, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and Rada his son; and Subal begot Jeth; and Jeth begot Achimai, and Laad: these [are] the generations of the Arathites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And these [are] the sons of Aetam; Jezrael and Jesman, and Jebdas: and their sister's name [was] Eselebbon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Phanuel the father of Gedor, and Jazer the father of Osan: these [are] the sons of Or, the firstborn of Ephratha, the father of Baethalaen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Asur the father of Thecoe had two wives, Aoda and Thoada. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Aoda bore to him Ochaia, and Ephal, and Thaeman, and Aasther: all these [were] the sons of Aoda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Thoada; Sereth, and Saar, and Esthanam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Coe begot Enob, and Sabatha, and the progeny of the brother of Rechab, the son of Jarin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Igabes was more famous than his brethren; and his mother called his name Igabes, saying, I have born as a sorrowful one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Igabes called on the God of Israel, saying, O that you would indeed bless me, and enlarge my coasts, and that your hand might be with me, and that you would make me know that you will not grieve me! And God granted him all that he asked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Chaleb the father of Ascha begot Machir; he [was] the father of Assathon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He begot Bathraias, and Bessee, and Thaeman the founder of the city of Naas the brother of Eselom the Kenezite: these [were] the men of Rechab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the sons of Kenez; Gothoniel, and Saraia: and the sons of Gothoniel; Athath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Manathi begot Gophera: and Saraia begot Jobab, the father of Ageaddair, for they were artificers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of Chaleb the son of Jephonne; Er, Ada, and Noom: and the sons of Ada, Kenez. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the sons of Aleel, Zib, and Zepha, and Thiria, and Eserel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the sons of Esri; Jether, Morad, and Apher, and Jamon: and Jether begot Maron, and Semei, and Jesba the father of Esthaemon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And his wife, that [is] Adia, bore Jared the father of Gedor, and Aber the father of Sochon, and Chetiel the father of Zamon: and these [are] the sons of Betthia the daughter of Pharao, whom Mored took. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sons of the wife of Iduia the sister of Nachaim the father of Keila; Garmi, and Esthaemon the Nochathite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the sons of Semon; Amnon, and Ana the son of Phana, and Inon: and the sons of Sei, Zoan, and the sons of Zoab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The sons of Selom the son of Juda; Er the father of Lechab, and Laada the father of Marisa, and the offspring of the family of Ephrathabac [belonging to] the house of Esoba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Joakim, and the men of Chozeba, and Joas, and Saraph, who lived in Moab, and he changed their names to Abederin and Athukiim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} These [are] the potters who lived in Ataim and Gadira with the king: they grew strong in his kingdom, and lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The sons of Semeon; Namuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zares, Saul: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Salem his son, Mabasam his son, Masma his son: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Amuel his son, Sabud his son, Zacchur his son, Semei his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Semei [had] sixteen sons, and six daughters; and his brethren had not many sons, neither did all their families multiply as the sons of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they lived in Bersabee, and Molada, and in Esersual, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and in Balaa, and in Aesem, and in Tholad, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and in Bathuel, and in Herma, and in Sikelag, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and in Baethmarimoth, and Hemisuseosin, and the house of Baruseorim: these [were] their cities until [the time of] king David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And their villages [were] Aetan, and En, Remnon, and Thocca, and Aesar, five cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And all their villages [were] round about these cities, as far as Baal: this [was] their possession, and their distribution. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Mosobab, and Jemoloch, and Josia the son of Amasia; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} and Joel, and Jeu the son of Asabia, the son of Sarau, the son of Asiel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} and Elionai, and Jocaba, and Jasuia, and Asaia, and Jediel, and Ismael, and Banaias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and Zuza the son of Saphai, the son of Alon, the son of Jedia, the son of Semri, the son of Samaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} These went by the names of princes in their families, and they increased abundantly in their fathers' households. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And they went till they came to Gerara, to the east of Gai, to seek pasture for their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And they found abundant and good pastures, and the land before them [was] wide, and [there was] peace and quietness; for [there were] some of the children of Cham who lived there before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And these who are written by name came in the days of Ezekias king of Juda, and they struck the people's houses, and the Minaeans whom they found there, and utterly destroyed them until this day: and they lived in their place, because [there was] pasture there for their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And some of them, [even] of the sons of Symeon, went to mount Seir, [even] five hundred men; and Phalaettia, and Noadia, and Raphaia, and Oziel, sons of Jesi, [were] their rulers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And they struck the remnant that were left of Amalec, until this day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2283, etc. bc 1721, etc Pharez; Phares, Esrom Carmi, Chelubai, Caleb \textsuperscript{8} Probably Jabez should be mentioned here; as otherwise he is as a consequent without an antecedent. \textsuperscript{9} more; Jabez i.e. Sorrowful I bare him \textsuperscript{10} called; the God; Oh that etc. Heb. If thou wilt, etc. bless me; enlarge; thine hand; that thou; keep me Heb. do me that it may, ; God granted \textsuperscript{12} Irnahash or, the city of Nahash \textsuperscript{13} Kenaz; Hathath or, Hathath and Meonathai, who begat, etc \textsuperscript{14} valley or, inhabitants of the valley Charashim that is, craftsmen. \textsuperscript{17} Ezra seems to be the person before called Asareel in . and she bare Miriam It is probable that the latter part of should be transposed before this passage, which Michaelis thinks is its right place; for otherwise we have the pronoun she without an antecedent, and children born without their father's being mentioned. Eshtemoa; Eshtemoh \textsuperscript{18} Jehudijah i.e. Jewess, Jered the father of, ; Gedor was a city in the tribe of Judah; and probably the same which Eusebius calls Κεδους, and Jerome Gedrus, ten miles from Diospolis, or Lydda, towards Eleutheropolis. Heber Socho i.e. inclosure; his branch, .; Shocho, Also, ; Jekuthiel i.e. the fear or veneration or preservation of God; God is almightiness, Bithiah i.e. worshiper of Jah; daughter of Jah, . daughter of Pharaoh., ; Mered \textsuperscript{19} Hodiah or, Jehudijah, mentioned before, Keilah \textsuperscript{20} Shimon is supposed to have been another son of Mered, by Jehudijah. As this latter name signifies a Jewess, it rather favours the opinion that Bithiah was not a Jewess, but an Egyptian. \textsuperscript{24} The sons of Simeon This genealogy differs in many particulars from those in the parallel places; probably being occasioned by the same person's having several names. Nemuel; Jemuel Jarib, Jachin Zerah, Zohar \textsuperscript{28} Beersheba Beer-sheba was situated twenty miles south of Hebron, according to Eusebius and Jerome, in whose time it was occupied by a Roman garrison., Moladah Probably the same as Malatha, so often mentioned by Eusebius; from whom it appears it was situated about twenty miles from Hebron. \textsuperscript{31} and Hazarsusim, Hazar-susah, Beth-lebaoth, Sharuhen \textsuperscript{32} Etam Ether, or Etham, was situated near Malatha, according to Eusebius., Ether, Remmon Ashan Eusebius say Beth-ashan was sixteen miles west of Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{33} Baal, Baalath-beer their genealogy or, as they divided themselves by nations among them \textsuperscript{38} mentioned by their names Heb. coming by names \textsuperscript{39} they went This expedition of the Simeonites took place in the days of Hezekiah, and, as Calmet conjectures, near the time of the captivity of the ten tribes; when the remnant of Simeon would feel themselves obliged to retire more southward into Arabia Petrea, for fear of the Jews, and to seek pasture for their flocks. Gedor; Geder \textsuperscript{40} the land Ham These were probably either Philistines or Egyptians, who dwelt at Gedor. \textsuperscript{41} these written Hezekiah; the habitations Or, the Meunnim, or Maonites.; pasture \textsuperscript{43} the rest That is, those who escaped in the war which Saul, and afterwards David, made against them.; unto this day\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 5}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel (for he [was] the firstborn; but because of his going up to his father's couch, [his father] gave his blessing to his son Joseph, [even] the son of Israel; and he was not reckoned as firstborn; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} for Judas [was] very mighty even among his brethren, and one was to be a ruler out of him: but the blessing [was] Joseph's). {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel; Enoch, and Phallus, Asrom, and Charmi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The sons of Joel; Semei, and Banaia his son: and the sons of Gug the son of Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} His son [was] Micha, his son Recha, his son Joel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} his son Beel, whom Thagla-phallasar king of Assyria carried away captive: he [is] the chief of the Rubenites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And his brethren in his family, in their distribution according to their generations; the chief, Joel, and Zacharia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Balec the son of Azuz, the son of Sama, the son of Joel: he lived in Aroer, and even to Naban, and Beelmasson. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he lived eastward to the borders of the wilderness, from the river Euphrates: for they had much cattle in the land of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And in the days of Saul they made war upon the sojourners [in the land]; and they fell into their hands, all of them dwelling in their tents eastward of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The sons of Gad lived over against them in the land of Basan even to Sela. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Joel the firstborn, and Sapham the second, and Janin the scribe in Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And their brethren according to the houses of their fathers; Michael, Mosollam, and Sebee, and Joree, and Joachan, and Zue, and Obed, seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} These [are] the sons of Abichaia the son of Uri, the son of Idai, the son of Galaad, the son of Michael, the son of Jesai, the son of Jeddai, the son of Buz, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [who was] the brother of the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, [he was] chief of the house of their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They lived in Galaad, in Basan, and in their villages, and [in] all the country round about Saron to the border. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The enumeration of [them] all took place in the days of Joatham king of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The sons of Ruben and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasse, of mighty men, bearing shields and sword, and bending the bow, and skilled in war, [were] forty and four thousand and seven hundred and sixty, going forth to battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they made war with the Agarenes, and Itureans, and Naphiseans, and Nadabeans, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and they prevailed against them: and the Agaraeans were given into their hands, [they] and all their tents: for they cried to God in the battle, and he listened to them, because they trusted on him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they took captive their store; five thousand camels, and two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand asses, and one hundred thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For many fell slain, because the war [was] of God. And they lived in their place until the captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the half-tribe of Manasse lived from Basan to Baal, Ermon, and Sanir, and [to] the mount Aermon: and they increased in Libanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And these were the heads of the houses of their families; Opher, and Sei, and Eliel, and Jeremia, and Oduia, and Jediel, mighty men of valour, men of renown, heads of the houses of their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But they rebelled against the God of their fathers, and went a-whoring after the gods of the nations of the land, whom God cast out from before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phaloch king of Assyria, and the spirit of Thagla-phallasar king of Assyria, and carried away Ruben and Gaddi, and the half-tribe of Manasse, and brought them to Chaach, and Chabor, and to the river Gozan, until this day.\par

Nephish; * Naphish: \textsuperscript{20} And they; for they cried;, in the battle;, because \textsuperscript{21} took away Heb. led captive camels The camel, in Hebrew gamal, retained with little variation in all languages, is, according to the Linnean system, a genus of quadrapeds of the order pecora; comprehending the camel, properly so called, with two prominences; the dromedary, with a single one; the lama, or Peruvian camel, with the back even and the breast gibbose, and the pacos, or camel without any gibbosity. The camel, properly so called, is about 6+ feet in height. Its head is small; ears short; neck long, slender, and bending; legs long and slender, having four callosities on the fore legs and two on the hinder, on which it rests; feet soft, parted, but not thoroughly divided; bottom of the foot tough and pliant; tail about two feet in length, terminating in a tuft; and hair fine, soft, of considerable length, and of a dusky reddish colour. Besides the same internal structure as other ruminating animals, it is furnished with an additional bag for containing a quantity of water till wanted. men Heb. souls of men; souls, Heb. nephesh \textsuperscript{22} the war was of God; they dwelt steads until the captivity \textsuperscript{24} famous men Heb. men of names \textsuperscript{25} and went; a whoring; after the gods \textsuperscript{26} stirred up; Pul, Tiglath pileser and brought them\par}
