\subsection*{Chronicles I 6}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The sons of Levi: Gedson, Caath, and Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the sons of Caath; Ambram, and Issaar, Chebron, and Oziel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the sons of Ambram; Aaron, and Moses, and Mariam: and the sons of Aaron; Nadab, and Abiud, Eleazar, and Ithamar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Eleazar begot Phinees, Phinees begot Abisu; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Abisu begot Bokki, and Bokki begot Ozi; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Ozi begot Zaraia, Zaraia begot Mariel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and Mariel begot Amaria, and Amaria begot Achitob; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and Achitob begot Sadoc, and Sadoc begot Achimaas; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and Achimaas begot Azarias, and Azarias begot Joanan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and Joanan begot Azarias: he ministered as priest in the house which Solomon built in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Azarias begot Amaria, and Amaria begot Achitob; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and Achitob begot Sadoc, and Sadoc begot Salom; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and Salom begot Chelcias, and Chelcias begot Azarias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and Azarias begot Saraia, and Saraias begot Josadac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Josadac went into captivity with Juda and Jerusalem under Nabuchodonosor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The sons of Levi: Gedson, Caath, and Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these [are] the names of the sons of Gedson; Lobeni, and Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The sons of Caath; Ambram, and Issaar, Chebron, and Oziel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The sons of Merari; Mooli and Musi: and these [are] the families of Levi, according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} To Gedson—to Lobeni his son—[were born] Jeth his son, Zammath his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Joab his son, Addi his son, Zara his son, Jethri his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The sons of Caath; Aminadab his son, Core his son, Aser his son; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Helcana his son, Abisaph his son, Aser his son: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Thaath his son, Uriel his son, Ozia his son, Saul his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the sons of Helcana; Amessi, and Achimoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Helcana his son, Suphi his son, Cainaath his son; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Eliab his son, Jeroboam his son, Helcana his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The sons of Samuel; the firstborn Sani, and Abia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} The sons of Merari; Mooli, Lobeni his son, Semei his son, Oza his son; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Samaa his son, Angia his son, Asaias his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And these [were the men] whom David set over the service of the singers in the house of the Lord when the ark was at rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they ministered in front of the tabernacle of witness [playing] on instruments, until Solomon built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; and they stood according to their order for their services. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And these [were the men] that stood, and their sons, of the sons of Caath: Aeman the psalm singer, son of Joel, the son of Samuel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} the son of Helcana, the son of Jeroboam, the son of Eliel, the son of Thoas, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} the son of Suph, the son of Helcana, the son of Maath, the son of Amathi, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} the son of Helcana, the son of Joel, the son of Azarias, the son of Japhanias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} the son of Thaath, the son of Aser, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Core, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} the son of Isaar, the son of Caath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand; Asaph the son of Barachias, the son of Samaa, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} the son of Michael, the son of Baasia, the son of Melchia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} the son of Athani, the son of Zaarai, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} the son of Adai, the son of Aetham, the son of Zammam, the son of Semei, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} the son of Jeeth, the son of Gedson, the son of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the sons of Merari their brethren on the left hand: Aetham the son of Kisa, the son of Abai, the son of Maloch, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} the son of Asebi, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} the son of Amessias, the son of Bani, the son of Semer, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} the son of Mooli, the son of Musi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And their brethren according to the houses of their fathers, [were] the Levites who were appointed to all the work of ministration of the tabernacle of the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And Aaron and his sons [were] to burn incense on the altar of whole burnt offerings, and on the altar of incense, for all the ministry [in] the holy of holies, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all things that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And these [are] the sons of Aaron; Eleazar his son, Phinees his son, Abisu his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Bokki his son, Ozi his son, Saraia his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Mariel his son, Amaria his son, Achitob his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} Sadoc his son, Achimaas his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And these [are] their residences in their villages, in their coasts, to the sons of Aaron, to their family the Caathites: for they had the lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And they gave them Chebron in the land of Juda, and its suburbs round about it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} But the fields of the city, and its villages, they gave to Chaleb the son of Jephonne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And to the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge, [even] Chebron, and Lobna and her suburbs round about, and Selna and her suburbs, and Esthamo and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} and Jethar and her suburbs, and Dabir and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} and Asan and her suburbs, and Baethsamys and her suburbs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} and of the tribe of Benjamin Gabai and her suburbs, and Galemath and her suburbs, and Anathoth and her suburbs: all their cities [were] thirteen cities according to their families. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And to the sons of Caath that were left of their families, [there were given] out of the tribe, [namely], out of the half-tribe of Manasse, by lot, ten cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And to the sons of Gedson according to their families [there were given] thirteen cities of the tribe of Issachar, of the tribe of Aser, of the tribe of Nephthali, of the tribe of Manasse in Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} And to the sons of Merari according to their families [there were given], by lot, twelve cities of the tribe of Ruben, of the tribe of Gad, [and] of the tribe of Zabulon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} So the children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities and their suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} And they gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Juda, and out of the tribe of the children of Symeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities which they call by name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} And [to the members] of the families of the sons of Caath there were also given the cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} And they gave them the cities of refuge, Sychem and her suburbs in mount Ephraim, and Gazer and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} and Jecmaan and her suburbs, and Baethoron and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{69}} and Aelon and her suburbs, and Gethremmon and her suburbs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{70}} and of the half-tribe of Manasse Anar and her suburbs, and Jemblaan and her suburbs, to the sons of Caath that were left, according to [each several] family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{71}} To the sons of Gedson from the families of the half-tribe of Manasse [they gave] Golan of Basan and her suburbs, and Aseroth and her suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{72}} And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedes and her suburbs, and Deberi and her suburbs, and Dabor and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{73}} and Ramoth, and Aenan and her suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{74}} And of the tribe of Aser; Maasal and her suburbs, and Abdon and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{75}} and Acac and her suburbs, and Roob and her suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{76}} And of the tribe of Nephthali; Kedes in Galilee and her suburbs, and Chamoth and her suburbs, and Kariathaim and her suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{77}} To the sons of Merari that were left, [they gave] out of the tribe of Zabulon Remmon and her suburbs, and Thabor and her suburbs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{78}} out of [the country] beyond Jordan; Jericho westward of Jordan: out of the tribe of Ruben; Bosor in the wilderness and her suburbs, and Jasa and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{79}} and Kadmoth and her suburbs, and Maephla and her suburbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{80}} Out of the tribe of Gad; Rammoth Galaad and her suburbs, and Maanaim and her suburbs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{81}} and Esebon and her suburbs, and Jazer and her suburbs.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2304, etc. bc 1700, etc sons of Levi; Gershon, Gershom \textsuperscript{2} the sons of Kohath; Amram, Amminadab \textsuperscript{10} am 3244, bc 760 Johanan is supposed to the same as Jehoiada, as he would otherwise not be mentioned. executed the temple Heb. the house Solomon 1Kings 6:1-7:51 \textsuperscript{14} am 3416, bc 588 Seraiah was carried to Riblah, and there put to death by order of Nebuchadnezzar; so that with him ended the succession of high priests in the first temple. \textsuperscript{15} Jehozadak, Jozadak, Josedech. when the Lord;, by the hand \textsuperscript{16} am 2304, bc 1700, etc Gershom; Gershon \textsuperscript{17} the sons of Gershom; Shimei, Shimi \textsuperscript{21} Joah, Ethan Zerah, Adaiah Jeaterai, Ethni \textsuperscript{25} am 2904, etc. bc 1100, etc Elkanah \textsuperscript{26} Zophai; Zuph Nahath, Toah, Tohu \textsuperscript{27} Eliab, Eliel, Elihu Elkanah; Houbigant says that we may here venture to add, "Samuel his son." \textsuperscript{28} firstborn; Here there is an ellipsis of the name of the firstborn, which the margin correctly supplies as Joel. The word Vashni when otherwise pointed means "second, " so that the verse more properly reads "And the sons of Samuel; the firstborn (Joel) and the second Abiah." Vashni i.e. Jah is strong; wherefore, sleep thou; changed; my year; second; liberal gift of the Lord, . It appears that the Joel is here lost out of the text; and that washni, which signifies "and the second, " and which refers to Abiah, is made into a proper name. The Syriac and Arabic read as in Samuel. The marginal references contain the variation in the names given to the same persons, in different parts of sacred history, as far as it can be ascertained; and nearly the whole, that is at present known concerning them, may be learned by carefully consulting them.; Joel \textsuperscript{30} Haggiah i.e. festival of Jah, Asaiah. \textsuperscript{31} am 2962, bc 1042 whom David, after that \textsuperscript{32} they ministered; with singing until Solomon; and then; , waited Heb. stood; according to their order This order is specified below. \textsuperscript{33} Heman, ; *title Joel, Vashni Shemuel This variation, as well as some others, only exists in the translation; the Hebrew being uniformly Shemuel.;, Samuel \textsuperscript{34} Elkanah Jeroham Eliel, Eliab, Toah i.e. depressing; inclination; sinking, prostration, ., Nahath \textsuperscript{36} Joel While it is sufficiently evident that many of the variations of the names of persons have arisen from the carelessness of transcribers, or the inattention of translators, and others from a difference (probably dialectical) in the pronunciation; it is also evident, that the same persons, as in these instances, must have had two or more totally distinct names ( ), Shaul, Uzziah, Uriel. \textsuperscript{37} Tahath Assir Ebiasaph; Abiasaph Korah;, *titles, *titles \textsuperscript{38} Izhar; Izehar, Kohath Levi Israel \textsuperscript{39} his brother Asaph is probably called his brother, because he was of the same tribe as Heman; or, perhaps, because he was his companion or associate. Asaph, ;, ; , ;, *titles, *titles \textsuperscript{40} Michael Baaseiah i.e. pressing together; work of the Lord, . Malchiah. \textsuperscript{44} Ethan, Jeduthun, *title Kishi, Kushaiah \textsuperscript{49} am 2513, bc 1491 Aaron;, 8:1-10:20, 21:1-22:33; make an atonement, ; *marg. Moses \textsuperscript{50} these are etc. We have already had a list of these, though more extensive. Eleazar; , ; Phinehas \textsuperscript{54} am 2561, bc 1443 these are; castles; of the families for theirs \textsuperscript{57} they gave; the city of refuge; Libnah, Jattir \textsuperscript{58} Hilen i.e. fortress, or, Holon.; This variation simply arises from the introduction of a ι yood, and a change of the vowel points; Holon being written ημο, and Hilen ηιμο .], Holon Debir \textsuperscript{59} Ashan It is probable that either Ain, in Joshua, is a mistake for Ashan, or that it was called by both names.;, Ain Bethshemesh \textsuperscript{60} Geba; Alemeth i.e. covering a hiding place, ., Almon Anathoth; , thirteen cities Here there are only eleven enumerated; but two more are added in the book of Joshua, Juttah and Gibeon, which make thirteen., ; None of the versions give the full number of names, though they all give the whole sum of thirteen; and it is probable that these two cities had been destroyed and lay in ruins when this book was written, and hence were not enumerated. \textsuperscript{61} And unto, left; by lot ten cities \textsuperscript{68} Jokmeam i.e. gathered of the people; he will establish the people, ; Probably the same as Kibzaim, Bethhoron \textsuperscript{70} Aner is probably another name of Tanach, which was a city of the half tribe of Manasseh, west of Jordan; and Eusebius, Jerome, and Procopius of Gaza, say that it was in their time a considerable place, three miles from Legio., Tanach, Gath-rimmon Bileam i.e. devouring; foreigner, . Compare the same Hebrew word rendered Balaam.; Ibleam is here called Bileam, by a transposition of letters common to all languages. It is evident, however, that many of these cities or their names have been changed since the time of Joshua; but, as it has been well observed, Salop and Shrewsbury, Sarum and Salisbury, are as different names as any in these catalogues; yet those who live in their vicinity are not at all confused by them. Some cities also are here mentioned as belonging to Ephraim, which in Joshua are spoken of as cities of Dan; but various changes in such matters would occur in a course of ages., Ibleam \textsuperscript{72} Kedesh, ; Daberath, Kishon, Daberah, Jarmuth, En-gannim \textsuperscript{73} Ramoth i.e. heights; coral, ; Anem i.e. double fountain; two eyes, . \textsuperscript{74} Mashal i.e. entreaty, Mishal \textsuperscript{75} Hukok i.e. a ditch; appointed portion; the engraving, .; Compare, Helkath \textsuperscript{76} Kedesh, ; Kadesh-naphtali Hammon, Hammoth-dor, Kartan Kirjathaim \textsuperscript{77} Unto Rimmon, Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, Nahalal, Tabor; Probably the city on the summit of Tabor, mentioned by Polybius and Josephus, the remains of which still exist. \textsuperscript{78} Bezer; Jahzah i.e. threshing-floor, ; Jahazah\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 7}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And [as] to the sons of Issachar, [they were] Thola, and Phua, and Jasub, and Semeron, four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the sons of Thola; Ozi, Raphaia, and Jeriel, and Jamai, and Jemasan, and Samuel, chiefs of their fathers' houses [belonging to] Thola, men of might according to their generations; their number in the days of David [was] twenty and two thousand and six hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the sons of Ozi; Jezraia: and the sons of Jezraia; Michael, Abdiu, and Joel, and Jesia, five, all rulers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And with them, according to their generations, according to the houses of their families, [were men] mighty to set [armies] in array for war, thirty and six thousand, for they had multiplied [their] wives and children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And their brethren among all the families of Issachar, also mighty men, [were] eighty-seven thousand—[this was] the number of them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The sons of Benjamin; Bale, and Bachir, and Jediel, three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the sons of Bale; Esebon, and Ozi, and Oziel, and Jerimuth, and Uri, five; heads of houses of families, mighty men; and their number [was] twenty and two thousand and thirty-four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the sons of Bachir; Zemira, and Joas, and Eliezer, and Elithenan, and Amaria, and Jerimuth, and Abiud, and Anathoth, and Eleemeth: all these [were] the sons of Bachir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And their number according to their generations, ([they were] chiefs of their fathers' houses, men of might), [was] twenty thousand and two hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the sons of Jediel; Balaan: and the sons of Balaan; Jaus, and Benjamin, and Aoth, and Chanana, and Zaethan, and Tharsi, and Achisaar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All these [were] the sons of Jediel, chiefs of their families, men of might, seventeen thousand and two hundred, going forth to war with might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Sapphin, and Apphin, and the sons of Or, Asom, whose son [was] Aor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The sons of Nephthali; Jasiel, Goni, and Aser, and Sellum, his sons, Balam his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The sons of Manasse; Esriel, whom his Syrian concubine bore; and she bore to him also Machir the father of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Machir took a wife for Apphin and Sapphin, and his sister's name was Moocha; and the name of the second [son] was Sapphaad; and to Sapphaad were born daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Moocha the wife of Machir bore a son, and called his name Phares; and his brother's name [was] Surus; his sons [were] Ulam, and Rocom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the sons of Ulam; Badam. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} whose number This was probably the number returned by Joab and his assistants, when they made that census of the people with which God was so much displeased. We find that the effective men of Issachar amounted to 87, 000 ( ); 22, 600 of whom descended from Tola his eldest son; but whether the 36, 000 ( ) were descendants of Tola by Uzzi, and the 22, 600 his descendants by Tola's other sons; or whether another of Issachar's sons be intended, does not clearly appear; though the former seems the more obvious meaning. \textsuperscript{6} of Benjamin In the parallel place of Genesis, ten sons of Benjamin are reckoned, Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard; and in Numbers, five only are mentioned, Bela, Ashbel, Ahiraim, Shupham, and Hupham; and Ard and Naaman are said to be the sons of Bela, and consequently Benjamin's grandsons. In the beginning of the following chapter, also, five are only mentioned, Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, and Rapha; and Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoha, another Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram, are all represented as grandsons, not sons of Benjamin. Hence we see that in many cases, grandsons are called sons, and both are often confounded in the genealogical tables. It seems, also, that the persons mentioned in the following verses were neither sons nor grandsons of Bela and Becher, but distinguished persons among their descendants.; Jediael \textsuperscript{12} Shuppim; Muppim Huppim, Shupham, Hupham Ir, Iri Aher signifies another, and it has been conjectured that these were Danites, "the sons of another tribe; " especially as Hushim is named as the only son of Dan, . And they suppose that the name of Dan was not mentioned, because his descendants first established idolatry. But Zebulun, as well as Dan, is here omitted, perhaps because none of either of these tribes returned at first from Babylon. Though the Benjamites had been almost destroyed in the first days of the judges, they soon became numerous and powerful., Ahiram \textsuperscript{13} Jahziel; Jahzeel Shallum; Shillem the sons of Bilhah \textsuperscript{14} The sons The text in these two verses seems to be strangely corrupted; and, as it stands, is scarcely intelligible. Probably it should be rendered, "The sons of Manasseh were Ashriel, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him; and Machir the father of Gilead, whom (his wife) bore to him. Machir took for a wife Maachah, sister to Huppim and Shuppim." This is nearly the version of Dr. Geddes. Machir \textsuperscript{15} Huppim and the name It is certain that Zelophehad was not a son, but a descendant of Manasseh's, three generations having intervened; for he was the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. and Zelophehad \textsuperscript{21} because they came Or rather, "when λι, ( kee ) they came down to take away their cattle; " for it does not appear that the sons of Ephraim were the aggressors, but the men of Gath, who appear to have been born in Egypt. This is the only place in the Sacred Writings where this piece of history is mentioned, and the transaction seems to have happened before the Israelites came out of Egypt; for it appears from the following verse, that Ephraim was alive when these children of his were slain. \textsuperscript{23} Beriah that is, In evil because Many similar instances of the naming of children from passing circumstances, occur throughout the sacred volume. See those of a similar character with this verse:, where Rachel, while dying, names her new-born son Ben-oni, or, the son of my sorrow. So in, the wife of Phinehas, on being apprised of the death of Eli and her husband, and that the ark was taken by the Philistines, while in the pains of travail, and dying, named her son I-chabod, or, there is no glory. So also in of this book, we read that Jabez, or, sorrowful, had that name given to him, because his mother "bare him with sorrow." \textsuperscript{27} Non, Nun, Oshea Jehoshuah, ; Joshua; Jesus \textsuperscript{28} Bethel; Naaran, or Naarath, Eusebius says was a town in his time called Νοοραθ, Noorath, five miles from Jericho. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} Addar The variation in this name is occasioned simply by the transposition of a γ, daleth and ψ, raish; being in the parallel passage ΰψγ, Ard, and here ΰγψ, Addar .; Ard \textsuperscript{5} Gera Shephuphan ωΡτν, Shuppim, seems to be merely a contracted form of ωΡτετν, Shupham, or rather, Shephupham, which, by the mutation of ξ, mem, into π, noon, is here changed into ωΡτετο, Shephuphan ., Shuppim, Shupham Huram appears to be an error for Hupham in the parallel passage of Numbers, which, by contraction, is written Huppim. \textsuperscript{9} Hodesh In the preceding verse it is said that "Hushim and Baara were his wives; " and here it said, "he begat of Hodesh his wife, " etc; and then in the, his children by Hushim are mentioned, but not a word of Baara. It is probable, therefore, that Hodesh was another name for Baara; and this is asserted by the Targumist: "And he begat of Baara, that is, of Chodesh, his wife, so called because he espoused her anew." \textsuperscript{10} Jeuz i.e. counselor; he will take counsel, . Shachia i.e. captivation; captive of the Lord; the return of Jah, Mirma i.e. deceit, guile, fraud, . \textsuperscript{12} Ono is stated by Reland to have been three miles from Lydda.;, Lod, or Lydda, was situated about four leagues from Joppa, and a day's journey, or about thirty-two miles nw from Jerusalem; and, according to the Antonine Itinerary, twelve miles from Jamnia, eighteen from Eleutheropolis, and twenty two from Bethar. Josephus says it was a village, not yielding to a city in greatness; and that it was one of three toparchies dismembered from Samaria, and given to the Jews. It was destroyed by Cesitus in the Jewish war, and, when rebuilt, was called Diospolis. It is now called Loudd, and is a poor village, situated in a fine plain about a league to the e-ne of Ramia. \textsuperscript{13} Shema, Shimhi the fathers, Aijalon, Ajalon \textsuperscript{28} dwelt; Jerusalem, the ancient capital of Judea, is situated in long. 35 degrees 20 minutes e, lat. 31 degrees 47 minutes 47 seconds n; and, according to the best authorities, 136 miles sw of Damascus, 34 miles s of Shechem or Nablous, 45 miles e of Jaffa, 27 miles n of Hebron, and about 20 miles w of Jericho. The city of Jerusalem was built on hills, and encompassed with mountains ( ), in a stony and barren soil, and was about sixteen furlongs in length, say Strabo. The ancient city of Jebus, taken by David from the Jebusites, was not large, and stood on a mountain south of that on which the temple was erected. Here David built a new city, called the city of David, wherein was the royal palace. Between these two mountains lay the valley of Millo, filled up by David and Solomon; and after the reign of Manasseh, another city is mentioned, called the second. The Maccabees considerably enlarged Jerusalem on the north, enclosing a third hill; and Josephus mentions a fourth hill, called Bezetha, which Agrippa joined to the former. This new city lay north of the temple, along the brook Kidron. See note on . \textsuperscript{33} Ner; Kish; Cis Saul, Abinadab, Ishui Eshbaal, Ish-bosheth\par}

The list is here nearly the same with those found in Ezra and Nehemiah, and contains those who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, but the list in Nehemiah is more ample, probably because it contains those who came afterwards; the object of the sacred writer here being to give the names of those who came first ( ). These consisted of men belonging not only to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, but to many of the other tribes of Israel, who took advantage of the proclamation of Cyrus to return to Jerusalem. Properly speaking, the divisions mentioned here constituted the whole of the Israelitish people, who were divided into priests, Levites, common Israelites, and Nethinims. the king's; they \textsuperscript{19} Ebiasaph Korah;, *titles gates Heb. thresholds, *marg. over the host; keepers of the entry \textsuperscript{22} in their;, David, 25:1-26:32, Samuel did ordain Heb. founded set office or, trust \textsuperscript{26} set office or, trust chambers or, storehouses, treasuries. \textsuperscript{28} the charge; bring them in and out Heb. bring them in by tale, and carry them out \textsuperscript{29} instruments or, vessels the oil the frankincense \textsuperscript{31} Shallum, set office or, trust, in the pans or, on flat plates, or slices \textsuperscript{32} the sons showbread Heb. bread of ordering to \textsuperscript{33} the singers, ; were free, they etc. Heb. upon them employed A number of Levites were employed by rotation in singing the praises of Jehovah; and they seem to have continued the service day and night. See the references. \textsuperscript{34} chief fathers; Jerusalem We have already seen the situation and extent of this ancient city (see note on ); but the Jerusalem of sacred history is no more. After having been successively destroyed by the Babylonians and Romans, and taken by the Saracens, Crusaders, and Turks, in the possession of the latter of whom it still continues, not a vestige remains of the capital of David and Solomon, not a monument of Jewish times is standing. The very course of the walls is changed, and the boundaries of the ancient city are become doubtful. The monks pretend to shew the sites of the sacred places; but they have not the slightest pretensions to even a probable identity with the real places. The Jerusalem that now is, however, called by the Arabs El Kouds, or "the holy city, " is still a respectable, good-looking town, of an irregular shape. It is surrounded by high embattled walls, enclosing an area not exceeding two miles and a half, and occupying two small hills, having the valley of Jehoshaphat on the east, the valley of Siloam and Gehinnom on the south, and the valley of Rephaim on the west; and containing a population variously estimated at from 20, 000 to 30, 000 souls. \textsuperscript{35} am 2804, etc. bc 1200, etc in Gibeon the father, whose Some editions read achatho, "his sister; " but in the parallel place, it is ishto, "his wife, " which is also the reading of the LXX, Vulgate, Arabic, and Syriac here, and is undoubtedly the true reading. \noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now the Philistines warred against Israel; and they fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Philistines pursued after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines struck Jonathan, and Aminadab, and Melchisue, sons of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the battle prevailed against Saul, and the archers hit him with bows and arrows, and they were wounded of the bows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Saul said to his armor-bearer, Draw your sword, and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me. Saul was dead, and he also fell upon his sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Saul died, and his three sons on that day, and all his family died at the same time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And all the men of Israel that were in the valley saw that Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, and they left their cities, and fled: and the Philistines came and lived in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass on the next [day] that the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his sons fallen on mount Gelbue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they stripped him, and took his head, and his And they put their armor in the house of their god, and they put his head in the house of Dagon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the dwellers in Galaad heard of all that the Philistines had done to Saul and to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all the mighty men rose up from Galaad, and they took the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabis, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabis, and fasted seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So Saul died for his transgressions, wherein he transgressed against God, against the word of the Lord, forasmuch as he kept [it] \subsection*{Chronicles I 11}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And all Israel came to David in Chebron, saying, Behold, we [are] your bones and your flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And heretofore when Saul was king, you were he that led Israel in and out, and the Lord of Israel said to you, You shall feed my people Israel, and you shall be for a ruler over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all the elders of Israel came to the king to Chebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Chebron before the Lord: and they anointed David to be king over Israel, according to the word of the Lord by Samuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king and his men went to Jerusalem, this [is] Jebus; and there the Jebusites the inhabitants of the land said to David, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} You shall not enter in hither. But he took the strong hold of Sion: this [is] the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David said, Whoever first smites the Jebusite, even he shall be chief and captain. And Joab the son of Saruia went up first, and became chief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David lived in the strong hold; therefore he called it the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he fortified the city round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And David continued to increase, and the Lord Almighty [was] with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And these [are] the chiefs of the mighty men, whom David had, who strengthened [themselves] with him in his kingdom, with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the Lord concerning Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And this [is] the list of the mighty [men] of David; Jesebada, son of Achaman, first of the thirty: he drew his sword once against three hundred whom he killed at one time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And after him Eleazar son of Dodai, the Achochite: he was among the three mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He was with David in Phasodamin, and the Philistines were gathered there to battle, and [there was] a portion of the field full of barley; and the people fled before the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he stood in the midst of the portion, and rescued it, and struck the Philistines; and the Lord wrought a great deliverance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to David, to the cave of Odollam, and the camp of the Philistines [was] in the giants' valley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And David [was] then in the hold, and the garrison of the Philistines [was] then in Bethleem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David longed, and said, Who will give me water to drink of the well of Bethleem, that is in the gate? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the three broke through the camp of the Philistines, and they drew water out of the well that was in Bethleem, which was in the gate, and they took it, and came to David: but David would not drink it, and poured it out to the Lord, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} God forbid that I should do this thing: shall I drink the blood of these men with their lives? for with [the peril of] their lives they brought it. So he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty [men]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Abisa the brother of Joab, he was chief of three: he drew his sword against three hundred slain at one time, and he had a name among the [second] three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He was more famous than the two [others] of the three, and he was chief [over] them; yet he reached not to the [first] three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Banaia the son of Jodae was the son of a mighty man: many [were] his acts for Cabasael: he struck two lion-like men of Moab, and he went down and struck a lion in a pit on a snowy day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he struck an Egyptian, a wonderful man five cubits [high]; and in the hand of the Egyptian [there was] a spear like a weavers' beam; and Banaia went down to him with a staff, and took the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} These things did Banaia son of Jodae, and his name [was] among the three mighties. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He was distinguished beyond the thirty, yet he reached not to the [first] three: and David set him over his family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the mighty [men] of the forces [were], Asael the brother of Joab, Eleanan the son of Dodoe of Bethleem, \subsection*{Chronicles I 12}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] they that came to Sikelag, when he yet kept himself close because of Saul the son of Kis; and these [were] among the mighty, aiding [him] in war, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and [using] the bow with the right hand and with the left, and slingers with stones, and [shooters] with bows. Of the brethren of Saul of Benjamin, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the chief [was] Achiezer, and Joas son of Asma the Gabathite, and Joel and Jophalet, sons of Asmoth, and Berchia, and Jeul of Anathoth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and Samaias the Gabaonite a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty; [and] Jeremia, and Jeziel, and Joanan, and Jozabath of Gadarathiim, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Azai and Arimuth, and Baalia, and Samaraia, and Saphatias of Charaephiel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Helcana, and Jesuni, and Ozriel, and Jozara, and Sobocam, and the Corites, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and Jelia and Zabadia, sons of Iroam, and the [men] of Gedor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And from Gad these separated themselves to David from the wilderness, strong mighty men of war, bearing shields and spears, and their faces [were as] the face of a lion, and they were nimble as roes upon the mountains in speed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Aza the chief, Abdia the second, Eliab the third, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Masmana the fourth, Jeremias the fifth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Jethi the sixth, Eliab the seventh, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Joanan the eighth, Eleazer the ninth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Jeremia the tenth, Melchabanai the eleventh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} These [were] chiefs of the army of the sons of Gad, the least one commander of one hundred, and the greatest one of a thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} These [are] the [men] that crossed over Jordan in the first month, and it had overflowed all its banks; and they drove out all the inhabitants of the valleys, from the east to the west. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And there came [some] of the sons of Benjamin and Juda to the assistance of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David went out to meet them, and said to them, If you⌃ are come peaceably to me, let my heart be at peace with you: but if [you⌃ are come] to betray me to my enemies unfaithfully, the God of your fathers look upon it, and reprove it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Spirit came upon Amasai, a captain of the thirty, and he said, Go, David, son of Jesse, you and your people, peace, peace be to you, and peace to your helpers, for your God has helped you. And David received them, and made them captains of the forces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And [some] came to David from Manasse, when the Philistines came against Saul to war: and he helped them not, because the captains of the Philistines took counsel, saying, With the heads of those men will he return to his master Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} When David was going to Sikelag, there came to him of Manasse, Edna and Jozabath, and Rodiel, and Michael, and Josabaith, and Elimuth, and Semathi: [these] are the captains of thousands of Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they fought on the side of David against a troop, for they [were] all men of might; and they were commanders in the army, [because] of [their] might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For daily men came to David, [till they amounted] to a great force, as the force of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And these [are] the names of the commanders of the army, who came to David to Chebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him according to the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The sons of Juda, bearing shields and spears, six thousand and eight hundred mighty in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Of the sons of Symeon mighty for battle, seven thousand and one hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Of the sons of Levi, four thousand and six hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Joadas the chief [of the family] of Aaron, and with him three thousand and seven hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Sadoc, a young [man] mighty in strength, and [there were] twenty-two leaders of his father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And of the sons of Benjamin, the brethren of Saul, three thousand: and still the greater part of them kept the guard of the house of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And of the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand and eight hundred mighty men, famous in the houses of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And of the half-tribe of Manasse, eighteen thousand, even [those] who were named by name, to make David king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And of the sons of Issachar having wisdom with regard to the times, knowing what Israel should do, two hundred; and all their brethren with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And of Zabulon they that went out to battle, with all weapons of war, [were] fifty thousand to help David, not weak-handed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And of Nephthali a thousand captains, and with them [men] with shields and spears, thirty-seven thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And of the Danites [men] ready for war twenty-eight thousand and eight hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And of Aser, they that went out to give aid in war, forty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And from the country beyond Jordan, from Ruben, and the Gadites, and from the half-tribe of Manasse, one hundred and twenty thousand, with all weapons of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} All these [were] men of war, setting [the army] in battle array, with a peaceful mind [towards him], and they came to Chebron to make David king over all Israel: and the rest of Israel [were of] one mind to make David king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And they were there three days eating and drinking, for their brethren [had] made preparations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And their neighbors, as far as Issachar and Zabulon and Nephthali, brought to them upon camels, and asses, and mules, and upon calves, food, meal, cakes of figs, raisins, wine, and oil, calves and sheep abundantly: for [there was] joy in Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} these are; while he yet etc. Heb. being yet shut up, Sometimes, in the East, when a successful prince endeavoured to extirpate the preceding royal family, some of them escaped the slaughter, and secured themselves in an impregnable fortress, or in a place of great secrecy; while others have been known to seek an asylum in a foreign county, from when they have occasioned, from time to time, great anxiety and great difficulties to the usurper of the crown. The expression shut up, so often applied to the extermination of eastern royal families ( .; .; ), strictly speaking, refers to the two first of these cases; but the term may be used in a more extensive sense, for those who, by retiring into deserts, or foreign countries, preserve themselves from being slain by the men who usurp the dominions of their ancestors. Thus the term is here applied to David, though he did not shut himself up, strictly speaking, in Ziklag. It is described as a town in the country, and was probably an unwalled town; and it is certain that he did not confine himself to it, but, on the contrary, was continually making excursions from thence. Saul, the mighty \textsuperscript{3} Shemaah or, Hasmaah Gibeathite; Azmaveth the Antothite \textsuperscript{4} Gibeonite, a mighty man Gederathite \textsuperscript{8} into the hold;, of war Heb. of the host handle; whose faces; as swift as the roes upon the mountains Heb. as the roes upon the mountains to make haste \textsuperscript{14} one of the least was over an hundred, and the greatest over a thousand or, one that was least could resist an hundred, the greatest a thousand. \textsuperscript{15} it had overflown Heb. it had filled over \textsuperscript{17} to meet them Heb. before them If ye be come; heart; knit Heb. one; wrong or, violence God; rebuke it \textsuperscript{18} the spirit; came upon Amasai Heb. clothed Amasai;, Amasa, Thine are we., and on they side; peace; thy God; captains of the band \textsuperscript{19} when he came to the jeopardy of our heads Heb. on our heads \textsuperscript{20} As he went These captains of Manasseh seem to have met David as he was returning from the army of the Philistines to Ziklag. It is probable that they did not bring their companies with them; yet they both assured him of future assistance, and very seasonably helped him against the Amalekites who had spoiled Ziklag. captains \textsuperscript{21} against the band or, with a band, mighty men \textsuperscript{22} day by day; like the host of God That is, says the Targumist, a very numerous army, like the army of the angel of God. \textsuperscript{23} am 2956, bc 1048, An, Ex, Is, 433 the numbers; bands or, captains, or men, Heb. heads came to David Some learned men understand this as relating to the time when David was make king over Judah, on his first coming to Hebron, but it seems wholly to refer to his being made king over all Israel, after the death of Ishbosheth; for there was no such union or assembly of the several tribes on the former occasion, as is here described. to turn according \textsuperscript{29} kindred Heb. brethren; the greatest part of them Heb. a multitude of them \textsuperscript{30} famous Heb. men of names \textsuperscript{32} understanding of the times That is, as the following words indicate, intelligent men, who understood the signs of the times, well versed in political affairs, and knew what was proper to be done in all the exigencies of human life; and who now perceived that it was both the duty and political interest of Israel to advance David to the throne.; to know; all their \textsuperscript{33} expert in war or, rangers of battle, or ranged in battle, keep rank. or, set the battle in array. they were not of double heart. Heb. they were without a heart and a heart. That is, they were all sincerely affected towards David, though so numerous. \textsuperscript{36} expert in war or, keeping their rank \textsuperscript{38} with a perfect heart The meaning of this expression may be inferred from that of a double heart in . If a double heart be expressive of insincerity or duplicity, a perfect heart, which seems to be put in opposition to it, must signify a sincere, faithful, and entire attachment.; all the rest \textsuperscript{40} brought The Septuagint reads εφερον αυτιος, "brought (to) them" which is probably correct; the Hebrew lahem, "to them" might be easily mistaken for lechem, "bread." The passage will then read, "bought them on asses, on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, meat, meal, cakes of figs, " etc., which renders the introduction of and unnecessary. From the mention of oil, figs, and raisins, Mr. Harmer thinks that this assembly was held in autumn., meat, meal or, victual of meal cakes of figs there was joy\par}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} If it seem; and that it be; send abroad Heb. break forth, and send left; the priests; their cities and suburbs Heb. the cities of their suburbs \textsuperscript{3} bring again Heb. bring about the ark; we inquired \textsuperscript{5} David; Shihor; Sihor; Sihor Hemath; Hamath Kirjathjearim \textsuperscript{6} Baalah; Baale that dwelleth; whose name \textsuperscript{7} carried the ark Heb. made the ark to ride, at and again at verse 38. A particular caution is given that strangers must not touch, or even pry into, the most holy things connected with the tabernacle, lest the offender die. In giving the law, also, even a beast which touched Sinai's mount was, by the Almighty's fiat, to be stoned or thrust through with a dart. And again we read ( ) after special orders to Aaron and his sons about covering the sanctuary and all the vessels previously to a removal, that the Kohathites, who were to carry them, "shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die." These were positive commands. May the sin of Uzza in touching the ark, warn Christians to take heed of rashness and irreverence in dealing about holy things. See note on . in a new cart; out of the house \textsuperscript{8} David; singing Heb. songs with harps The word kinnor, in Chaldee, kinnora, in Syraic, kainoro, in Arabic, kinnarat, and in Greek κινυρος, certainly denotes a harp, played on with the hand, according to . The number of strings in the harp was at first three; but afterwards they were increased to four, and at last to seven., ; psalteries Naivel, or naibel, in Greek ναβλα, and in Latin, nablium, was an instrument of the harp kind; having twelve sounds. \textsuperscript{9} Chidon, Nachon stumbled or shook it \textsuperscript{10} he put; there he died \textsuperscript{11} displeased; Perezuzza that is, The breach of Uzza to this day \textsuperscript{13} brought Heb. removed Obededom, ; the Gittite\par}

{\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And David called Sadoc and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites, Uriel, Asaia, and Joel, and Semaia, and Eliel, and Aminadab, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and said to them, You⌃ [are] the heads of the families of the Levites: sanctify yourselves, you and your brethren, and you⌃ shall carry up the ark of the God of Israel, [to the place] which I have prepared for it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For because you⌃ were not [ready] at the first, our God made a breach upon us, because we sought him not according to the ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves, to bring up the ark of the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of the Levites took the ark of God, (as Moses commanded by the word of God according to the scripture) upon their shoulders with staves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And David said to the chiefs of the Levites, Set your brethren the singers with musical instruments, lutes, harps, and cymbals, to sound aloud with a voice of joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So the Levites appointed Aeman the son of Joel; Asaph the son of Barachias [was one] of his brethren; and Aethan the son of Kisaeus was of the sons of Merari their brethren; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and with them their brethren of the second rank, Zacharias, and Oziel, and Semiramoth, and Jeiel, and Elioel, and Eliab, and Banaia, and Maasaia, and Matthathia, and Eliphena, and Makellia, and Abdedom, and Jeiel, and Ozias, the porters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the singers, Aeman, Asaph, and Aethan, with brazen cymbals to make [a sound] to be heard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Zacharias, and Oziel, Semiramoth, Jeiel, Oni, Eliab, Maasaeas, Banaeas, with lutes, on alaemoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Mattathias, and Eliphalu, and Makenia, and Abdedom, and Jeiel, and Ozias, with harps of Amasenith, to make a loud noise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Chonenia chief of the Levites [was] master of the bands, because he was skillful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Barachia and Elcana [were] doorkeepers of the ark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Somnia, and Josaphat, and Nathanael, and Amasai, and Zacharia, and Banaea, and Eliezer, the priests, were sounding with trumpets before the ark of God: and Abdedom and Jeia [were] doorkeepers of the ark of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains of thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant from the house of Abdedom with gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it came to pass when God strengthened the Levites bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that they sacrificed seven calves and seven rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And David [was] girded with a fine linen robe, and all the Levites [who were] bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the singers, and Chonenias the master of the band of singers; also upon David [there was] a robe of fine linen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of a horn, and with trumpets, and with cymbals, playing loudly on lutes and harps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the ark of the covenant of the Lord arrived, and came to the city of David; and Melchol the daughter of Saul looked down through the window, and saw king David dancing and playing: and she despised him in her heart.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles I 16}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} So they brought in the ark of God, and set it in the midst of the tabernacle which David pitched for it; and they offered whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David finished offering up whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he divided to every man of Israel (both men and women), to [every] man one baker's loaf, and a cake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he appointed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, Levites to minister [and] lift up the voice, and to give thanks and praise the Lord God of Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Asaph [was] the chief, and next to him Zacharias, Jeiel, Semiramoth, and Jeiel, Mattathias, Eliab, and Banaeas, and Abdedom: and Jeiel sounding with musical instruments, lutes [and] harps, and Asaph with cymbals: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and Banaeas and Oziel the priests [sounding] continually with trumpets before the ark of the covenant of God in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then David first gave orders to praise the Lord by the hand of Asaph and his brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Song. Give thanks to the Lord, call upon him by his name, make known his designs among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Sing [songs] to him, and sing hymns to him, relate to all [people] his wonderful deeds, which the Lord has wrought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Praise his holy name, the heart that seeks his pleasure shall rejoice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Seek the Lord and be strong, seek his face continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Remember his wonderful works which he has wrought, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [you⌃] seed of Israel his servants, [you⌃] seed of Jacob his chosen ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} He [is] the Lord our God; his judgments [are] in all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Let us remember his covenant for ever, his word which he commanded to a thousand generations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} which he covenanted with Abraham, and his oath [sworn] to Isaac. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He confirmed it to Jacob for an ordinance, to Israel [as] an everlasting covenant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} saying, To you will I give the land of Chanaan, the line of your inheritance: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} when they were few in number, when they were but little, and lived as strangers in it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and went from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He suffered not a man to oppress them, and he reproved kings for their sakes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} saying, Touch not my anointed ones, and deal not wrongfully with my prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Sing you⌃ to the Lord, all the earth; proclaim his salvation from day to day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Declare among the nations his glory, his wondrous deeds among all peoples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For the Lord [is] great, and greatly to be praised: he [is] to be feared above all gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For all the gods of the nations [are] idols; but our God made the heavens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Glory and praise [are] in his presence; strength and rejoicing [are] in his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Give to the Lord, you⌃ families of the nations, give to the Lord glory and strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Give to the Lord the glory [belonging] to his name: take gifts and offer [them] before him; and worship the Lord in his holy courts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Let the whole earth fear before him; let the earth be established, and not be moved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; and let them say among the nations, The Lord reigns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} The sea with its fullness shall resound and the tree of the field, and all things in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then shall the trees of the wood rejoice before the Lord, for he is come to judge the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Give thanks to the Lord, for [it is] good, for his mercy [is] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And say you⌃, Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather us, and rescue us from among the heathen, that we may praise your holy name, and glory in your praises. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Blessed [be] the Lord God of Israel from everlasting and to everlasting: And all the people shall say, Amen. So they praised the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And they left there Asaph and his brethren before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to minister before the ark continually, according to the service of each day: from day to day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Abdedom and his brethren [were] sixty and eight; and Abdedom the son of Idithun, and Osa, [were] to be doorkeepers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And [they appointed] Sadoc the priest, and his brethren the priests, before the tabernacle of the Lord in the high place in Gabaon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} to offer up whole burnt offerings continually morning and evening, and according to all things written in the law of the Lord, which he commanded the children of Israel by Moses the servant of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And with him [were] Aeman and Idithun, and the rest chosen out by name to praise the Lord, for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And with them [there were] trumpets and cymbals to sound aloud, and musical instruments for the songs of God: and the sons of Idithun [were] at the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And all the people went every one to his home: and David returned to bless his house.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles I 17}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass as David lived in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, Behold, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the Lord [is] under [curtains] of skins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Nathan said to David, Do all that is in your heart; for God [is] with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass in that night, that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Go and say to David my servant, Thus said the Lord, You shall not build me a house for me to dwell in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For I have not lived in a house from the day that I brought up Israel until this day, but I have been in a tabernacle and a tent, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} in all places through which I have gone with all Israel: did I ever speak to [any] one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, [Why is it] that you⌃ have not built me a house of cedar? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now thus shall you say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord Almighty, I took you from the sheepfold, from following the flocks, to be a ruler over my people Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and I was with you in all places whither you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you, and I made for you a name according to the name of the great ones that are upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant him, and he shall dwell by himself, and shall no longer be anxious; and the son of iniquity shall no longer afflict him, as at the beginning, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. Also I have humbled all your enemies, and I will increase you, and the Lord will build you a house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it shall come to pass when your days shall be fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, which shall be of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He shall build me a house, and I will set up his throne for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son: and my mercy will I not withdraw from him, as I withdrew [it] from them that were before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will establish him in my house and in his kingdom for ever; and his throne shall be set up for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spoke Nathan to David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And king David came and sat before the Lord, and said, Who am I, O Lord God? and what [is] my house, that you have loved me for ever? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And these things were little in your sight, O God: you have also spoken concerning the house of your servant for a long time to come, and you have looked upon me as a man looks upon his fellow, and have exalted me, O Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} What shall David do more toward you to glorify [you]? and you know your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you have wrought all this greatness according to your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} O Lord, there is none like you, and there is no God beside you, according to all things which we have heard with our ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Neither is there another nation upon the earth [such] as your people Israel, whereas God led him in the way, to redeem a people for himself, to make for himself a great and glorious name, to cast out nations from before your people, whom you redeemed out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you have appointed your people Israel as a people to yourself for ever; and you, Lord, did become a God to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And now, Lord, let the word which you spoke to your servant, and concerning his house, be confirmed for ever, and do you as you have spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And let your name [be] established and magnified for ever, [men] saying, Lord, Lord, Almighty God of Israel: and [let] the house of your servant David [be] established before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For you, O Lord my God, have revealed to the ear of your servant that you will build him a house; therefore your servant has found a willingness to pray before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And now, Lord, you yourself are God, and you have spoken these good things concerning your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And now you have begun to bless the house of your servant, so that it should continue for ever before you: for you, Lord, have blessed [it], and do you bless [it] for ever.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles I 18}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass afterwards, that David struck the Philistines, and routed them, and took Geth and its villages out of the hand of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he struck Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David, [and] tributaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David struck Adraazar king of Suba of Emath, as he was going to establish power toward the river Euphrates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And David took of them a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand infantry: and David houghed all the chariot [horses], but there were reserved of them one hundred chariots. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Syrian came from Damascus to help Adraazar king of Suba; and David struck of the Syrian [army] twenty and two thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David put a garrison in Syria near Damascus; and they became tributary servants to David: and the Lord delivered David wherever he went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David took the golden collars that were on the servants of Adraazar, and brought them to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David took out of Matabeth, and out of the chief cities of Adraazar very much brass: of this Solomon made the brazen sea, and the pillars, and the brazen vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Thoa king of Emath heard that David had struck the whole force of Adraazar king of Suba. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he sent Aduram his son to king David to ask how he was, and to congratulate him because he had fought against Adraazar, and struck him; for Thoa was the enemy of Adraazar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the golden and silver and brazen vessels, even these king David consecrated to the Lord, with the silver and the gold which he took from all the nations; from Idumaea, and Moab, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Abesa son of Saruia struck the Idumeans in the valley of Salt, eighteen thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he put garrisons in the valley; and all the Idumaeans became David's servants: and the Lord delivered David wherever he went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So David reigned over all Israel; and he executed judgment and justice to all his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joab the son of Saruia [was] over the army, and Josaphat the son of Achilud [was] recorder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Sadoc son of Achitob, and Achimelech son of Abiathar, [were] the priests; and Susa [was] the scribe; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and Banaeas the son of Jodae [was] over the Cherethite and the Phelethite, and the sons of David were the chief deputies of the king.\par

The difference arises from the mistake of a ψ, raish, for a γ, daleth, two letters very similar., Hadadezer Zobah; *title by the river \textsuperscript{4} seven thousand, seven hundred David The words wyakker Dawid eth col haraichev, should be rendered, "and David disjointed all the chariots; " which is nearly the rendering of the LXX, και παραλυσε Δανιδ παντα τα αρματα . To have houghed the horses would have been both unreasonable and inhuman; for, as he had gained so complete a victory, there was no danger of their falling into the hands of the enemy; and if he did not choose to keep them, which indeed the law would not permit, he ought to have killed them outright., houghed; an hundred chariots \textsuperscript{5} the Syrians; Damascus Heb.
