\subsection*{Chronicles I 19}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after this, [that] Naas the king of the children of Ammon died, and Anan his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David said, I will act kindly toward Anan the son of Naas, as his father acted kindly towards me. And David sent messengers to condole with him on the death of his father. So the servants of David came into the land of the children of Ammon to Anan, to comfort him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Anan, Is it to honor your father before you, that David has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you that they might search the city, and to spy out the land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Anan took the servants of David, and shaved them, and cut off the half of their garments as far as their tunic, and sent them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And there came men to report to David concerning the men: and he sent to meet them, for they were greatly disgraced: and the king said, Dwell in Jericho until your beards have grown, and return. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the children of Ammon saw that the people of David were ashamed, and Anan and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen out of Syria of Mesopotamia, and out of Syria Maacha, and from Sobal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they hired for themselves two and thirty thousand chariots, and the king of Maacha and his people; and they came and encamped before Medaba: and the children of Ammon assembled out of their cities, and came to fight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David heard, and sent Joab and all the host of mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the children of Ammon came forth, and set themselves in array for battle by the gate of the city: and the kings that were come forth encamped by themselves in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Joab saw that they were fronting [him] to fight against him before and behind, and he chose [some] out of all the young men of Israel, and they set themselves in array against the Syrian. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the rest of the people he gave into the hand of his brother Abesai, and they set themselves in array against the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, If the Syrian should prevail against me, then shall you deliver me: and if the children of Ammon should prevail against you, then will I deliver you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Be of good courage, and let us be strong, for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the Lord shall do what [is] good in his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So Joab and the people that were with him set themselves in battle array against the Syrians, and they fled from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians fled, and they also fled from before Abesai, and from before Joab his brother, and they came to the city: and Joab came to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Syrian saw that Israel had defeated him, and he sent messengers, and they brought out the Syrians from beyond the river; and Sophath the commander-in-chief of the forces of Adraazar [was] before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it was told David; and he gathered all Israel, and crossed over Jordan, and came upon them, and set the battle in array against them. So David set [his army] in array to fight against the Syrians, and they fought against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Syrians fled from before Israel; and David killed of the Syrians seven thousand [riders in] chariots, and forty thousand infantry, and he killed Sophath the commander-in-chief of the forces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the servants of Adraazar saw that they were defeated before Israel, and they made peace with David and served him: and the Syrians would not any more help the children of Ammon.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} I will show; the children \textsuperscript{3} but the princes; Thinkest thou that David Heb. In thine eyes doth David, to search \textsuperscript{4} took David's, shaved them; and cut, sent them \textsuperscript{5} and told David at Jericho; your beards \textsuperscript{6} had made; odious Heb. to stink; *marg. a thousand, ; Syriamaachah Zobah \textsuperscript{7} hired; thirty Thirty-two thousand soldiers, exclusive of the thousand sent by the king of Maachah, are mentioned in the parallel passage ( ); but of chariots or cavalry there is no mention; and the number of chariots stated here is prodigious, and beyond all credibility. But as the word raichev denotes not only a chariot, but a rider (see ), it ought most probably to be rendered here, in a collective sense, cavalry; and then the number of troops will exactly agree with the passage in Samuel. It is probable that they were a kind of auxiliary troops who were usually mounted on horses, or in chariots, but who occasionally served as foot-soldiers. the king of Maachah This variation exists only in the translation, the original being the same in both places, melech maachah, "the king of Maachah.", king Maachah Medeba \textsuperscript{9} put the battle; the kings \textsuperscript{10} when Joab battle Heb. face of the battle set against; choice or, young men \textsuperscript{11} Abishai Heb. Abshai, ; The variation of ΰαιωΡι, Abishai, and ΰαωΡι, Abshai, is simply caused by the elision of ι, yood, which is by no means uncommon. and they set \textsuperscript{13} of good; let us behave etc. In Samuel, "let us play the men; " but the original is the same in both places, nithchazzak . let the Lord \textsuperscript{16} am 2968, bc 1036, An, Ex, Is, 455 and drew; river that is, Euphrates Shophach This variation arises from the permutation of α, baith, and τ, pay; being written in the parallel passage ωΡεακ, Shobach, and here ωΡετκ, Shophach, Shobach. \textsuperscript{17} upon them Instead of alaihem, "upon them, " it is in chelamah, "to Helam:" the one seems evidently to be a mistake for the other. and set \textsuperscript{18} fled before Israel;, seven thousand In the parallel passage, "the men of seven hundred chariots; " which difference probably arose from mistaking ο, noon final, which stands for 700, for ζ, zayin, with a dot above, which denotes 7, 000, or vice versa. The great similarity of these letters might easily cause the one to be mistaken for the other. footmen If these troops were as we have suppose, a kind of dismounted cavalry, the terms footmen and horsemen might be indifferently applied to them., horsemen\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 20}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass at the return of the year, at the [time of the] going forth of kings [to war], that Joab gathered the whole force of the army, and they ravaged the land of the children of Ammon; and he came and besieged Rabba. But David abode in Jerusalem. And Joab struck Rabba and destroyed it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David took the crown of Molchom their king off his head, and the weight of it was found [to be] a talent of gold, and on it were precious stones; and it was [placed] on the head of David: and he brought out the spoils of the city [which were] very great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he brought out the people that were in it, and sawed them asunder with saws, and [cut them] with iron axes, and with harrows: and thus David did to all the children of Ammon. And David and all his people returned to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass afterward that there was again war with the Philistines in Gazer: then Sobochai the Sosathite struck Saphut of the sons of the giants, and laid him low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And there [was] war again with the Philistines; and Eleanan the son of Jair struck Lachmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, and the wood of his spear [was] as a weavers' beam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there was again war in Geth, and there was a man of extraordinary size, and his fingers [and toes were] six on each hand and foot, four and twenty; and he was descended from the giants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he defied Israel, and Jonathan the son of Samaa the brother of David killed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} These were born to Rapha in Geth; all four were giants, and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles I 21}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the devil stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And king David said to Joab and to the captains of the forces, Go, number Israel from Bersabee even to Dan, and bring me [the account], and I shall know their number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Joab said, May the Lord add to his people, one hundred-fold as many as they [are], and [let] the eyes of my lord the king see [it]: all [are] the servants of my lord. Why does my lord seek this thing? [do it not], lest it become a sin to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Nevertheless the king's word prevailed against Joab; and Joab went out and passed through all Israel, and came to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Joab gave the number of the mustering of the people to David: and all Israel was a million and one hundred thousand men that drew sword: and the sons of Juda [were] four hundred and seventy thousand men that drew sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But he numbered not Levi and Benjamin among them; for the word of the king was painful to Joab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And [there was] evil in the sight of the Lord respecting this thing; and he struck Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And David said to God, I have sinned exceedingly, in that I have done this thing: and now, I pray you, remove the sin of your servant; for I have been exceedingly foolish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord spoke to Gad the seer, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Go and speak to David, saying, Thus says the Lord, I bring three things upon you: choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Gad came to David, and said to him, Thus says the Lord, Choose for yourself, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} either three years of famine, or that you should flee three months from the face of your enemies, and the sword of your enemies [shall be employed] to destroy you, or that the sword of the Lord and pestilence [should be] three days in the land, and the angel of the Lord [shall be] destroying in all the inheritance of Israel. And now consider what I shall answer to him that sent the message. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And David said to Gad, They are very hard for me, even [all] the three: let me fall now into the hands of the Lord, for his mercies [are] very abundant, and let me not fall by any means into the hands of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So the Lord brought pestilence upon Israel: and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was destroying, the Lord saw, and repented for the evil, and said to the angel that was destroying, Let it suffice you; withhold your hand. And the angel of the Lord stood by the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And David lifted up his eyes, and saw the angel of the Lord, standing between the earth and the heaven, and his sword drawn in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem: and David and the elders clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David said to God, [Was it] not I [that] gave orders to number the people? and I am the guilty one; I have greatly sinned: but these sheep, what have they done? O Lord God, let your hand be upon me, and upon my father's house, and not on your people for destruction, O Lord! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the angel of the Lord told Gad to tell David, that he should go up to erect an altar to the Lord, in the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And David went up according to the word of Gad, which he spoke in the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Orna turned and saw the king; and he hid himself and his four sons with him. Now Orna was threshing wheat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David came to Orna; and Orna came forth from the threshing floor, and did obeisance to David with his face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And David said to Orna, Give me your place of the threshing floor, and I will build upon it an altar to the Lord: give it me for its worth in money, and the plague shall cease from [among] the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Orna said to David, Take it to yourself, and let my lord the king do what is right in his eyes: see, I have given the calves for a whole burnt offering, and the plow for wood, and the corn for a meat-offering; I have given all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And king David said to Orna, Nay; for I will surely buy it for its worth in money: for I will not take your property for the Lord, to offer a whole burnt offering to the Lord without cost [to myself]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And David gave to Orna for his place six hundred shekels of gold [by] weight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And David built there an altar to the Lord, and offered up whole burnt offerings and peace-offerings: and he cried to the Lord, and he answered him by fire out of heaven on the altar of whole burnt offerings, and [it] consumed the whole burnt offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the Lord spoke to the angel; and he put up the sword into its sheath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} At that time when David saw that the Lord answered him in the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite, he also sacrificed there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the tabernacle of the Lord which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of whole burnt offerings, [were] at that time in the high place at Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And David could not go before it to enquire of God; for he hasted not because of the sword of the angel of the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles I 22}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David said, This is the house of the Lord God, and this [is] the altar for whole burnt offering for Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And David gave orders to gather all the strangers that were in the land of Israel; and he appointed stone-hewers to hew polished stones to build the house to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And David prepared much iron for the nails of the doors and the gate; the hinges also and brass in abundance, there was no weighing [of it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And cedar threes without number: for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar trees in abundance to David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And David said, My son Solomon [is] a tender child, and the house [for me] to build to the Lord [is] for superior magnificence for a name and for a glory through all the earth: I will make preparation for it. And David prepared abundantly before his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he called Solomon his son, and commanded him to build the house for the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And David said to Solomon, [My] child, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the word of the Lord came to me, saying, You have shed blood abundantly, and have carried on great wars: you shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood upon the earth before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Behold, a son shall be born to you, he shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name [shall be] Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He shall build a house to my name; and he shall be a son to me, and I will be a father to him; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom in Israel for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now, my son, the Lord shall be with you, and prosper [you]; and you shall build a house to the Lord your God, as he spoke concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Only may the Lord give you wisdom and prudence, and strengthen you over Israel, both to keep and to do the law of the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then will he prosper [you], if you take heed to do the commandments and judgments which the Lord commanded Moses for Israel: be courageous and strong; fear not, nor be terrified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And, behold, I according to my poverty have prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold, and a million talents of silver, and brass and iron without measure; for it is abundant; and I have prepared timber and stones; and do you add to these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And [of them that are] with you do you add to the multitude of workmen; [let there be] artificers and masons, and carpenters, and every skillful [workman] in every work; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} in gold and silver, brass and iron, [of which] there is no number. Arise and do, and the Lord [be] with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And David charged all the chief men of Israel to help Solomon his son, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} [Is] not the Lord with you? and he has given you rest round about, for he has given into your hands the inhabitants of the land; and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now set your hearts and souls to seek after the Lord your God: and rise, and build a sanctuary to your God to carry in the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the holy vessels of God, into the house that is to be built to the name of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} This is the house David perhaps had some assurance that this was the place on which God designed that His house should be built; and perhaps it was this that induced him to buy not only the threshing-floor, but probably some adjacent ground also, as Calmet supposes, that there might be sufficient room for such a structure.; and this is the altar \textsuperscript{7} it was in, ; unto the name \textsuperscript{8} Thou hast shed; thou shalt not \textsuperscript{9} a son; I will give, ; Solomon that is, Peaceable, I will give peace *marg. \textsuperscript{10} He shall build; he shall be; I will establish \textsuperscript{12} Only the; that thou mayest \textsuperscript{13} Then shalt; *marg.; to fulfil; be strong \textsuperscript{14} trouble or, poverty, an hundred thousand This, at 5, 075£. 15s. 7+d. the talent, would amount to the sum of 507, 578, 125£.; thousand talents of silver This, at 353£. 11s. 10d. the talent, would amount to 353, 591, 666£. 13s. 4d.; and both sums would amount to the immense sum of 868, 169, 791£. 13s. 4d. without weight \textsuperscript{15} hewers and workers of stone and timber that is, masons and carpenters, all manner \textsuperscript{16} the gold, Arise, ; and the Lord \textsuperscript{18} Is not; and hath; before the Lord \textsuperscript{19} set your; *marg. arise; to bring; to the name\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 23}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he assembled all the chief men of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Levites numbered [themselves] from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls amounted to thirty and eight thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Of the overseers over the works of the house of the Lord [there were] twenty-four thousand, and [there were] six thousand scribes and judges; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and four thousand doorkeepers, and four thousand to praise the Lord with instruments which he made to praise the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And David divided them [into] daily courses, for the sons of Levi, for Gedson, Caath, and Merari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And for [the family of] Gedson, Edan, and Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The sons of Edan [were] Jeiel, the chief, and Zethan, and Joel, three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The sons of Semei; Salomith, Jeiel, and Dan, three: these [were] the chiefs of the families of Edan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And to the sons of Semei, Jeth, and Ziza, and Joas, and Beria: these [were] the four sons of Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jeth was the chief, and Ziza the second: and Joas and Beria did not multiply sons, and they became [only] one reckoning according to the house of their father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The sons of Caath; Ambram, Isaar, Chebron, Oziel, four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The sons of Ambram; Aaron and Moses: and Aaron was appointed for the consecration of the most holy things, he and his sons for ever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister and bless in his name for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And [as for] Moses the man of God, his sons were reckoned to the tribe of Levi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The sons of Moses; Gersam, and Eliezer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The sons of Gersam; Subael the chief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the sons of Eliezer were, Rabia the chief: and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rabia were very greatly multiplied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The sons of Isaar; Salomoth the chief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The sons of Chebron; Jeria the chief, Amaria the second, Jeziel the third, Jekemias the fourth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The sons of Oziel; Micha the chief, and Isia the second. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The sons of Merari; Mooli, and Musi: the sons of Mooli; Eleazar, and Kis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, but daughters: and the sons of Kis, their brethren, took them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The sons of Musi; Mooli, and Eder, and Jarimoth, three. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} These [are] the sons of Levi according to the houses of their fathers; chiefs of their families according to their numbering, according to the number of their names, according to their polls, doing the works of service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For David said, The Lord God of Israel has given rest to his people, and has taken up his abode in Jerusalem for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Levites bore not the tabernacle, and all the vessels of it for its service. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For by the last words of David was the number of the Levites [taken] from twenty years old and upward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For he appointed them to wait on Aaron, to minister in the house of the Lord, over the courts, and over the chambers, and over the purification of all the holy things, and over the works of the service of the house of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and for the show-bread, and for the fine flour of the meat-offering, and for the unleavened cakes, and for the fried cake, and for the dough, and for every measure; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks to the Lord, and so in the evening; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and [to be] over all the whole burnt offerings that were offered up to the Lord on the sabbaths, and at the new moons, and at the feasts, by number, according to the order [given] to them, continually before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they are to keep the charge of the tabernacle of witness, and the charge of the holy place, and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brethren, to minister in the house of the Lord.\par

In the time of Moses, the age was from thirty years to fifty. Here this latter period is not mentioned, probably because the service was not so laborious now; for the ark being fixed, they had no longer any burdens to carry; and therefore even an old man might continue to serve. See note on . twenty \textsuperscript{25} The Lord; that they may dwell in Jerusalem or, and he dwelleth in Jerusalem \textsuperscript{27} by the last; numbered Heb. numbers \textsuperscript{28} office was to wait etc. Heb. station was at the hand of Aaron, *marg. for the service; , purifying \textsuperscript{29} for the showbread It was the priests' office to place this bread before the Lord; and it was their privilege to feed on the old loaves when they were replaced by the new.; the fine flour; unleavened, pan or, flat plate for all manner of measure The standards of all weights and measures were in the sanctuary; and therefore the Levites had the inspection of weights and measures of every kind, that no fraud might in this way be committed. Honesty is inseparably connected with piety; and hence the Levites, being sufficiently numerous, were employed to superintend the former, as well as the latter. \textsuperscript{31} in the sabbaths; set feasts; Num. 28:1-29:40 \textsuperscript{32} keep; the charge of the sons\par}

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the divisions There were four classes of these, each of which belonged to the four gates of the temple, which opened to the four cardinal points of heaven. The eastern gate fell to Shelemiah; the northern to Zechariah ( ); the southern to Obed-edom ( ); and the western to Shuppim and Hosah ( ). These several persons were captains of these porter-bands, or door-keepers, at the different gates. There were probably a thousand men under each of these captains; as we find, from, that their whole number was four thousand. the porters, ; Korhites; *titles Meshelemiah ωΡμξιδ, Shelemiah, is merely an abbreviation of ξωΡμξιδ, Meshelemiah, by the apheresis of ξ, mem ., Shelemiah Asaph This variation arises from the rejection of the word ΰα, av, "father, " and the mutation of ι, yood, into ΰ, aleph; being written in the parallel passages ΰαιρσ, Ebiasaph, and here ΰρσ, Asaph ., Ebiasaph \textsuperscript{5} him "That is, Obed-edom, as ." \textsuperscript{6} mighty men of valour They were not only porters, or door keepers, in the ordinary sense of the word, but they were a military guard to the gate, as Dr. Delaney suggests that the word shoarim should be rendered here, and perhaps in this sense alone are we to understand their office, which appears to have been of considerable dignity, and conferred only on men of the first rank. They were appointed to attend the temple, to guard all the avenues to it, to open and shut all the outer gates, and attend at them, not only for state but for service. They were also required to direct and instruct those who were going to worship in the courts of the sanctuary in the conduct they were to observe, to encourage those who were timid, to send back the strangers and unclean, and to guard against thieves and others who were enemies to the house of God.; *marg. \textsuperscript{12} wards That is, classes against each other. Ward formerly signified a class or division. We still apply the term to the different apartments in hospitals, and to the more extensive districts into which the city of London is divided. \textsuperscript{13} as well the small as the great Heb. or, as well for the small as for the great \textsuperscript{15} Asuppim Heb. gatherings, ; Or collections; probably the place where either the supplies of the porters, or the offerings made for the priests and Levites, were laid up. Obed-edom is said to have had the charge of the treasures, etc., in . \textsuperscript{16} Hosah Shallecheth That is, ejection; probably the gate through which all the filth which from time to time might accumulate in the temple and its courts, was cast out. causeway; ward against ward That is, their stations were opposite to each other; as the north to the south, and the east to the west. \textsuperscript{18} Parbar i.e. the outside place; he annulled the corn; a quarter of Jerusalem (Strong), Also, Parbar is most probably the same as parwar, which denotes suburbs ( ), in which sense it is often used in the Chaldee Targums; and consequently this may be considered as leading to the suburbs. \textsuperscript{19} Kore, or rather, Korhi, χψηι, is essentially the same with χψη, Korah, merely having a paragogic ι, yood ., Korah \textsuperscript{20} treasures, ; dedicated things Heb. holy things \textsuperscript{22} Jehieli, ιηιΰμι, is the same as Jehiel, ιηιΰμ, with the addition of ι, yood ., Jehiel over the treasures \textsuperscript{24} Shebuel The difference between ωΡεαΰμ, Shubael, and ωΡαΰμ, Shebuel, simply arises from the elision of ε, wav and a change of vowels., Shubael \textsuperscript{27} Out spoils won in battles Heb. battles and spoils to maintain \textsuperscript{30} the Hebronites, men of valour officers Heb. over the charge \textsuperscript{32} men of valour chief fathers, Reubenites and affairs Heb. and thing; There were more Levites employed as judges with the two tribes and half on the other side of Jordan, than with all the rest of the tribes; there were two thousand seven hundred, whereas on the west side of Jordan there were only one thousand seven hundred. Either those remote tribes were not so well furnished as the rest with judges of their own, or because they lay farthest from Jerusalem, on the borders of the neighbouring nations, and were thus much in danger of being infected with idolatry, they most needed the help of Levites to prevent their running into the abominations of the idolaters.\par}

All these [were] superintendents of the substance of king David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Jonathan, David's uncle by the father's side, [was] a counsellor, a wise man: and Jeel the son of Achami [was] with the king's sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Achitophel [was] the king's counsellor: and Chusi the chief friend of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And after this Achitophel Jodae the son of Banaeas [came] next, and Abiathar: and Joab [was] the king's commander-in-chief.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the chief fathers The patriarchs, chief generals, or generals of brigade. This enumeration is widely different from that of the preceding. In that, we have the order and course of the priests and Levites, in their ecclesiastical ministrations. In this, we have the account of the order of the civil service, what related simply to the political state of the king and kingdom. Twenty-four persons, chosen out of David's worthies, each of whom had a second, were placed over 24, 000 men, who all served a month at a time, in turn; and this was the whole of their service during the year, after which they attended to their own affairs. Thus the king had always on foot a regular force of 24, 000, who served without expense to him or the state, and were not oppressed by the service, which took up only a twelfth part of their time; and by this plan he could, at any time, bring into the field 12 times 24, 000 or 288, 000 fighting men, independently of the 12, 000 officers, which made in the whole an effective force of 300, 000 soldiers; and all these men were prepared, disciplined, and ready at a call, without the smallest expense to the state or the king. These were, properly speaking, the militia of the Israelitish kingdom. captains; served; any matter month \textsuperscript{5} Benaiah Or, "Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the chief priest:" it was Jehoiada, and not Benaiah, who was a priest.; chief priest or, principal officer \textsuperscript{8} Shamhuth If this person was the same as Shammoth the Hararite, or Shammah the Harodite, it is probable that he took the denomination Izrahite, from one of his progenitors of the name Izrah, and derived the other from the place of his residence., Shammoth the Hararite; Shammah the Harodite \textsuperscript{16} Furthermore These persons, called "princes of the tribes, " in, and, appear to have been civil rulers over their several tribes, and honorary men, without pay, not unlike the lords lieutenants of our counties. In this enumeration there is no mention of the tribes of Gad and Asher, probably because they were joined to the neighbouring tribes; or perhaps, the account of these has been lost from the register. \textsuperscript{18} Elihu If Elihu be not a mistake for Eliab, it is probable that he was called by both names., Eliab \textsuperscript{23} David took not It seems probable, from this passage, that Joab began, by David's order, to number the children, as well as adults, but was prevented from finishing the account, probably because the plague had begun. The numbering of the effective men might have been deemed a political expedient; but pride and ostentation alone could dictate the numbering of minors and infants, especially as God had pronounced the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, innumerable. from twenty he would increase \textsuperscript{24} began to number; was the number put Heb. ascended the number \textsuperscript{27} the increase of the vineyards Heb. that which was of the vineyards \textsuperscript{28} And over the sycamore trees The Hebrew shikmin, Syriac shekmo, and Arabic jummeez, is the συκομορος, or sycomore, of the Greeks, so called from συκος, a fig-tree, and μορος a mulberry- tree, because it resembles the latter in its leaves, and the former in its fruits. "The sycamore, " says Mr. Norden, "is of the height of a beech, and bears its fruit in a manner quite different from other trees. It has them on the trunk itself, which shoots out little sprigs, in form of grape stalks, at the end of which grow the fruit close to one another, almost like a cluster of grapes. The tree is always green, and bears fruit several times in the year, without observing any certain seasons; for I have seen some sycamores that have given fruit two months after others. The fruit has the figure and smell of real figs, but is inferior to them in the taste, having a disgusting sweetness. Its colour is a yellow, inclining to an ochre, shadowed by a flesh colour. In the inside it resembles the common figs, excepting that it has a blackish colouring with yellow spots. This sort of tree is pretty common in Egypt; the people, for the greater part, live on its fruit, and think themselves well regaled when they have a piece of bread, a couple of sycamore figs, and a pitcher of water." \textsuperscript{32} uncle, nephew scribe or, secretary son of Hachmoni, or, Hachmonite\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles I 29}
\markright{CHRONICLES I 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And David the king said to all the congregation, Solomon my son, whom the Lord has chosen, [is] young and tender, and the work [is] great; for [it is] not for man, but for the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I have prepared according to all [my] might for the house of my God gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, onyx stones, and costly and variegated stones for setting, and every precious stone, and much Parian [marble]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And still farther, because I took pleasure in the house of my God, I have gold and silver which I have procured for myself, and, behold, I have given them to the house of my God over and above, beyond what I have prepared for the holy house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Three thousand talents of gold of Suphir, and seven thousand talents of fine silver, for the overlaying of the walls of the sanctuary: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [for you to use] the gold for [things of] gold, and the silver for things of silver, and for every work by the hand of the artificers. And who is willing to dedicate himself in work this day for the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then the heads of families, and the princes of the children of Israel, and the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, and the overseers of the works, and the king's builders, offered willingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they gave for the works of the house of the Lord five thousand talents of gold, and ten thousand gold [pieces], and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of brass, and one hundred thousand talents of iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they who had [precious] stone, gave it into the treasuries of the house of the Lord by the hand of Jeiel the Gedsonite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the people rejoiced because of the willingness, for they offered willingly to the Lord with a full heart: and king David rejoiced greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And king David blessed the Lord before the congregation, saying, Blessed are you, O Lord God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting and to everlasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Your, O Lord, [is] the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the might: for you are Lord of all things that are in heaven and upon the earth: before your face every king and nation is troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} From you [come] wealth and glory: you, O Lord, rule over all, the Lord of all dominion, and in your hand [is] strength and rule; and [you are] almighty with your hand to increase and establish all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And now, Lord, we give thanks to you, and praise your glorious name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But who am I, and what [is] my people, that we have been able to be thus forward [in offering] to you? for all things [are] your, and of your own have we given you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} for we are strangers before you, and sojourners, as all our fathers [were]: our days upon the earth [are] as a shadow, and there is no remaining. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} O Lord our God, as for all this abundance which I have prepared that a house should be built to your holy name, it is of your hand, and all [is] your. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I know, Lord, that you are he that searches the hearts, and you love righteousness. I have willingly offered all these things in simplicity of heart; and now I have seen with joy your people here present, willingly offering to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} O Lord God of Abraham, and Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, preserve these things in the thought of the heart of your people for ever, and direct their hearts to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And to Solomon my son give a good heart, to perform your commandments, and [to observe] your testimonies, and your ordinances, and to accomplish the building of your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And David said to the whole congregation, Bless you⌃ the Lord our God. And all the congregation blessed the Lord God of their fathers, and they bowed the knee and worshipped the Lord, and [did obeisance] to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And David sacrificed to the Lord, and offered up whole burnt offerings to the Lord on the morrow after the first day, a thousand calves, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, and their drink-offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they ate and drank joyfully that day before the Lord: and they made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and anointed him king before the Lord, and Sadoc to the priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Solomon sat upon the throne of his father David, and was highly honored; and all Israel obeyed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The princes, and the mighty men, and all the sons of king David his father, were subject to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the Lord magnified Solomon over all Israel, and gave him royal glory, such as was not upon any king before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And David the son of Jessae reigned over Israel forty years; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} seven years in Chebron, and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he died in a good old age, full of days, in wealth, and glory: and Solomon his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the rest of the acts of David, the former and the latter, are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} concerning all his reign, and his power, and the times which went over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the earth.\par

\section*{2 Chronicles Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Ezra (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Traditionally linked with Ezra as part of the same Chronicler history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The NT does not name the human writer, but the temple and Davidic history it preserves is treated as real covenant history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} post-exilic\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} likely 5th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology continues from Solomon through the southern kings to Cyrus's decree.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The Greek tradition preserves the same Judah-centered framework with normal versional differences.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Judah's temple-centered history from Solomon to exile and restoration decree.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To explain Judah's history through worship, reform, apostasy, and the hope of restoration under the Davidic and temple promises.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} temple; reform; apostasy; exile; restoration; Davidic line\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Solomon and temple 1-9; Kings of Judah 10-36; Exile and Cyrus decree 36. Qumran Chronicles fragments are limited | Subst. Second Temple period Early Hebrew evidence is limited; the principal full witnesses are medieval Hebrew plus ancient Greek tradition | Heb. n/a Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Alexandrinus preserves 2 Chronicles in Greek\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 5th century AD by Use of Chronicles history in later Jewish writing (Josephus)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1st century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Chronicles should be read as complementary inspired history with its own theological emphases; textual divergence from Kings does not imply contradiction.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\markboth{CHRONICLES II}{}
\subsection*{Chronicles II 1}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Solomon the son of David was established over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him, and increased him exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the captains of thousands, and to the captains of hundreds, and to the judges, and to all the rulers over Israel, even the heads of the families; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and Solomon and all the congregation went to the high place that was in Gabaon, where was God's tabernacle of witness, which Moses the servant of the Lord made in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But David had brought up the ark of God out of the city of Cariathiarim; for David had prepared a place for it, for he had pitched a tabernacle for it in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the brazen altar which Beseleel the son of Urias, the son of Or, had made, was there before the tabernacle of the Lord: and Solomon and the congregation enquired at it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Solomon brought [victims] there to the brazen altar that was before the Lord in the tabernacle, and offered upon it a thousand whole burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In that night God appeared to Solomon, and said to him, Ask what I shall give you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Solomon said to God, You have dealt very mercifully with my father David, and have made me king in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now, O Lord God, let, I pray you, your name be established upon David my father; for you have made me king over a people numerous as the dust of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now give me wisdom and understanding, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who shall judge this your great people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God said to Solomon, Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked great wealth, nor glory, nor the life of your enemies, and you have not asked long life; but have asked for yourself wisdom and understanding, that you might judge my people, over whom I have made you king: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I give you this wisdom and understanding; and I will give you wealth, and riches, and glory, so that there shall not have been [any] like you among the kings before you, neither shall there be such after you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Solomon came from the high place that was in Gabaon to Jerusalem, [from] before the tabernacle of witness, and reigned over Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Solomon collected chariots and horsemen: and he had fourteen hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen: and he set them in the cities of chariots, and the people [were] with the king in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem [to be] as stones, and cedars in Judea as sycamores in the plain for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Solomon imported horses from Egypt, and the charge of the king's merchants for going [was as follows], and they traded, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and went and brought out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred [pieces] of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty [pieces] of silver: and so they brought for all the kings of the Chettites, and for the kings of Syria by their means.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} was strengthened, the Lord, ; magnified \textsuperscript{2} Then Solomon This seems to have taken place a short time after David's decease, and, according to some, in the second year of Solomon's reign; when being established in his kingdom, he convened his chief men, and spake to them concerning the solemn sacrifice which he purposed to offer to God. to the captains, ;, the chief \textsuperscript{3} Gibeon; the tabernacle, ; the servant \textsuperscript{4} the ark The tabernacle and the brazen altar still remained at Gibeon; but David had brought away the ark out of the tabernacle, and placed it in a tent at Jerusalem.;, for he had pitched \textsuperscript{5} the brazen, Bezaleel; he put or, was there sought unto it went to seek the Lord there \textsuperscript{7} In that night This was the night following the sacrifice which Solomon had offered.; Ask \textsuperscript{8} Thou has showed, ; to reign \textsuperscript{9} let thy promise; for thou hast like the dust Heb. much as the dust \textsuperscript{10} Give me; go out; for who can \textsuperscript{11} Because This does not occur in Kings, and it implies that the request of Solomon, as arising from a spiritual judgment and heart, was peculiarly acceptable to that God who searches, regards, and demands the heart. God promised Solomon all the things which he had not asked, except the life of his enemies; for he was to be a peaceable king, a type of the Prince of peace. this was; that thou mayest \textsuperscript{12} I will give; such as none \textsuperscript{14} Solomon;, the chariot cities Cities where the chariots, and horses belonging to them, were kept. \textsuperscript{15} the king He destroyed its value by making it so exceedingly plentiful.; made Heb. gave sycamore trees \textsuperscript{16} Solomon Heb. the going forth of the horses which was Solomon's; linen yarn The word ξχεΰ, or ξχεδ, mikweh, is regarded by the ancient translators as a proper name. The LXX have εκ Θεκουε, "from Tekoa, " the Vulgate, de Coa, "from Koa, " which is adopted by Dr. Geddes; the Syriac, "from the city Aphelia; " and the Arabic, " ex urbe Australium ." Bochart thinks it signifies a tribute; others suppose that it signifies a string or drove of horses, or as Jarchi says, what the Germans call Stutte, a stud; but Houbigant supposes it to be a corruption for mercavah, "chariots." Our English translation, however, which regards it as synonymous with tikwah, seems by far the best. According to Norden, linen yarn is still one of the principal articles of commerce in Egypt, and is exported in very large quantities, together with unmanufactured flax and spun cotton; and Sanutus, 400 years ago, remarked that though Christian countries abounded in flax, yet the goodness of the Egyptian was such, that it was dispersed even to the west. \textsuperscript{17} the kings means Heb. hand\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 2}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Solomon said that he would build a house to the name of the Lord, and a house for his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Solomon gathered seventy thousand men that bore burdens, and eighty thousand hewers of stone in the mountain, and [there were] three thousand six hundred superintendents over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Solomon sent to Chiram king of Tyre, saying, Whereas you did deal [favourably] with David my father, and did send him cedars to build for himself a house to dwell in, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} behold, I also his son am building a house to the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it to him, to burn incense before him, and [to offer] show bread continually, and to offer up whole burnt offerings continually morning and evening, and on the sabbaths, and at the new moons, and at the feasts of the Lord our God: this [is] a perpetual [statute] for Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the house which I am building [is to be] great: for the Lord our God [is] great beyond all gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And who will be able to build him a house? for the heaven and heaven of heavens do not bear his glory: and who am I, that I should build him a house, save only to burn incense before him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now send me a man wise and skilled to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in blue, and one that knows how to grave together with the craftsmen who are with me in Juda and in Jerusalem, which materials my father David prepared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And send me from Libanus cedar wood, and wood of juniper, and pine; for I know that your servants are skilled in cutting timber in Libanus: and, behold, your servants shall go with my servants, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} to prepare timber for me in abundance: for the house which I am building [must be] great and glorious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And, behold, I have given freely to your servants that work and cut the wood, corn for food, [even] twenty thousand measures of wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand measures of wine, and twenty thousand measures of oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Chiram king of Tyre answered in writing, and sent to Solomon, saying, Because the Lord loved his people, he made you king over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Chiram said, Blessed [be] the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to king David a wise son, and one endowed with knowledge and understanding, who shall build a house for the Lord, and a house for his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And now I have sent you a wise and understanding man [who belonged] to Chiram my father {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} (his mother [was] of the daughters of Dan, and his father [was] a Tyrian), skilled to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in stones and wood; and to weave with purple, and blue, and fine linen, and scarlet; and to engrave, and to understand every device, whatever you shall give him [to do] with your craftsmen, and the craftsmen of my lord David your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now, the wheat, and the barley, and the oil, and the wine which my lord mentioned, let him send to his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And we will cut timber out of Libanus according to all your need, and we will bring it on rafts to the sea of Joppa, and you shall bring it to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Solomon gathered all the foreigners that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering with which David his father numbered them; and there were found one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he made of them seventy thousand burden-bearers, and eighty thousand hewers of stone, and three thousand six hundred taskmasters over the people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} determined for the name, ; an house \textsuperscript{3} Huram, Hiram As thou didst \textsuperscript{4} build; to dedicate to burn sweet incense Heb. incense of spices the continual; the burnt; the solemn feasts; Num. 28:1-29:40 \textsuperscript{5} great; great is our God \textsuperscript{6} But who; is able Heb. hath returned, or obtained strength who am I then; save only \textsuperscript{7} cunning;, to grave Heb. to grave gravings whom David \textsuperscript{8} Send me also algum trees or, algummim, Called in the parallel passage, by a transposition of letters, almuggim, or "almug-trees; " which is rendered by the Vulgate, ligna thyina, the thya or lignum vite wood. Theophrastus say that "the thyon of thya tree grows near the temple of Jupiter Ammon (in Africa), and in the Cyrenaica; that it resembles the cypress in its boughs, leaves, stalk, and fruit; and that its wood (from its close texture) never rots." The LXX render here πευκινα; and Josephus calls it ξυλα πευκινα, torch or pine-trees; but cautions us against supposing that the wood was like what was known in his time by that name; for these "were to the sight like the wood of the fig-tree, but more white and shining." The Syriac version has kaiso dekeėsotho, probably cypress wood; and Dr. Shaw supposes it denotes the cypress. Several critics understand it to mean gummy wood; and Celsius queries whether it may not be the sandal-tree, as the Rabbins and Dr. Geddes suppose., almug-trees \textsuperscript{9} wonderful great Heb. great and wonderful \textsuperscript{10} I will give; baths of wine \textsuperscript{12} Huram; that made heaven Gen. 1:1-2:25;, ; endued etc. Heb. knowing prudence and understanding, an house \textsuperscript{16} we will cut as much as thou shalt need Heb. according to all thy need, Joppa. Heb. Japho. \textsuperscript{17} numbered; the strangers Heb. the men the strangers after the numbering\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 3}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem in the mount of Amoria, where the Lord appeared to his father David, in the place which David had prepared in the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And thus Solomon began to build the house of God: the length in cubits—even the first measurement from end to end, was sixty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the portico in front of the house, its length in front of the breadth of the house [was] twenty cubits, and its height one hundred and twenty cubits: and he gilded it within with pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he lined the great house with cedar wood, and gilded it with pure gold, and carved upon it palm-trees and chains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty; and he gilded it with gold of the gold from Pharuim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he gilded the house, and its [inner] walls, and the door-posts, and the roofs, and the doors with gold; and he carved cherubs on the walls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he built the holy of holies, its length was according to the front [of the other house], the breadth of the house [was] twenty cubits, and the length twenty cubits: and he gilded [it] with pure gold for cherubs, to [the amount of] six hundred talents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the weight of the nails, [even] the weight of each was fifty shekels of gold: and he gilded the upper chamber with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he made two cherubs in the most holy house, wood-work, and he gilded them with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the wings of the cherubs were twenty cubits in length: and one wing of five cubits touched the wall of the house: and the other wing of five cubits touched the wing of the other cherub. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the wings of these cherubs expanded were of the length of twenty cubits: and they stood upon their feet, and their faces were toward the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he made the vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and wove cherubs in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Also he made in front of the house two pillars, in height thirty-five cubits, and their chapters of five cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he made chains, [as] in the oracle, and put [them] on the heads of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right hand and the other on the left: and he called the name of the one on the right hand 'Stability,' and the name of the one on the left 'Strength.'\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2993, bc 1011, An, Ex, Is, 480 Solomon in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David or, which was seen of David Ornan, Araunah \textsuperscript{3} am 2993-3000, bc 1011-1004 Solomon instructed Heb. founded The length the first measure It is supposed, with much probability, that the first measure means the cubit used in the time of Moses, contradistinguished from that used in Babylon, and which the Israelites used after their return from captivity. And, as these Books were written after the captivity, it was necessary for the writer to make this remark, lest it should be thought that the measurement was by the Babylonish cubit, which was a palm or one-sixth shorter than the cubit of Moses; which may serve to reconcile some variations in the historical books, with respect to numbers when applied to measures. \textsuperscript{4} the porch; an hundred and twenty As the height of the temple was only thirty cubits, 120 seems too great a height for the porch; but the Syriac, Arabic, and the LXX in the codex Alexandrinus, have only twenty, probably reading, instead of maiah weesrim, "one hundred and twenty, " ammoth esrim, "twenty cubits; " which brings it within the proportion of the other measures. \textsuperscript{6} garnished Heb. covered precious; Parvaim is supposed by Calmet to be the same as Sepharvaim in Armenia or Media; Bochart is of opinion that it is Taprobanes, now the island of Ceylon, which he drives from taph, a border, and Parvan, i.e., "the coast of Parvan; " but the late Editor of Calmet thinks it the same as the Parvatoi mountains of Ptolemy, at the head of the Indus. \textsuperscript{10} two cherubims image work or, as some think, of movable work \textsuperscript{13} inward or, toward the house \textsuperscript{14} the veil; wrought Heb. caused to ascend \textsuperscript{15} two pillars; thirty The Syriac and Arabic have, agreeably to the parallel passage, "eighteen cubits high; " but the Septuagint, Chaldee, and Vulgate have "thirty and five cubits high." See note on . high Heb. long \textsuperscript{17} reared up Jachin that is, He shall establish Boaz that is, In it is strength\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 4}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he made a brazen altar, the length of it twenty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits, and the height ten cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he made the molten sea, in diameter ten cubits, entirely round, and the height of it five cubits, and the circumference thirty cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And beneath it the likeness of calves, they compass it round about: ten cubits compass the laver round about, they cast the calves two rows in their casting, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} wherein they made them twelve calves, —three looking northwards, and three westwards, and three southwards, and three eastwards: and the sea was upon them above, [and] their hinder parts were inward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And its thickness was a hand-breadth, and its brim as the brim of a cup, graven with flowers of lilies, holding three thousand measures: and he finished [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he made ten lavers, and set five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them the instruments of the whole burnt offerings, and to rinse [the vessels] in them; and the sea [was] for the priests to wash in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he made the ten golden candlesticks according to their pattern, and he put them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he made ten tables, and put them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left: and he made one hundred golden bowls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Also he made the priests' court, and the great court, and doors to the court, and their panels [were] overlaid with brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he set the sea at the corner of the house on the right, as it were fronting the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Chiram made the flesh hooks, and the fire-pans, and the grate of the altar, and all its instruments: and Chiram finished doing all the work which he wrought for king Solomon in the house of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} two pillars, and upon them an embossed work for the capitals on the heads of the two pillars, and two nets to cover the heads of the capitals which are on the heads of the pillars; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and four hundred golden bells for the two nets, and two rows of pomegranates in each net, to cover the two embossed rims of the capitals which are upon the pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he made the ten bases, and he made the lavers upon the bases; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the one sea, and the twelve calves under it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and the foot-baths, and the buckets, and the caldrons, and the flesh hooks, and all their furniture (which Chiram made, and brought to king Solomon in the house of the Lord) of pure brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} In the country round about Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground in the house of Socchoth, and between [that and] Saredatha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance, for the quantity of brass failed not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Solomon made all the vessels of the house of the Lord, and the golden altar, and the tables, and upon them [were to be] the loaves of show bread; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} also the candlesticks, and the lamps to give light according to the pattern, and in front of the oracle, of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And their snuffers, and their lamps [were made], and [he made] the bowls, and the censers, and the fire-pans, of pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [there was] the inner door of the house [opening] into the holy of holies, and [he made] the inner doors of the temple of gold. So all the work which Solomon wrought for the house of the Lord was finished.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a molten sea; brim to brim Heb. his brim to his brim \textsuperscript{3} And under; oxen In the parallel passage of Kings, instead of bekarim, "oxen, " we have pekaim, "knops, " in the form of colocynths. (See note on, and see note on ); which last is supposed by able critics to be the reading which ought to received be here; bekarim, "oxen, " being a mistake for pekaim, "knops." Houbigant, however, contends that the words in both places are right; but that bakar does not signify an ox here, but a large kind of grape, according to its meaning in Arabic. But Dr. A. Clarke states that bakar, or bakarat, has no such meaning in Arabic, though the phrase aino ' lbikri, or "ox-eye, " signifies a species of black grape, very large, and of incredible sweetness; that consequently the criticism of this great man is not solid; and that the likeliest method of reconciling the two places is to suppose a change in the letters as above. \textsuperscript{5} with flowers of lilies or, like a lily flower three thousand baths In the parallel passage, it is said to hold only two thousand baths; which some think may be reconciled by supposing that the quantity of water which was commonly in it was 2, 000 baths, but that, if filled up to the top, it would hold 3, 000. But, as we have already seen that the Babylonish cubit was less than that of the ancient Hebrews, it might be the same with measures of capacity; so that 2, 000 of the ancient Jewish baths might have been equal to 3, 000 of those used after the captivity. The Targum cuts the knot: "It received 3, 000 baths of dry measure, and held 2, 000 of liquid measure." See note on . \textsuperscript{6} ten lavers; such things as they offered for the burnt offering Heb. the work of burnt offering, ; but the sea \textsuperscript{8} ten tables; basins or, bowls \textsuperscript{11} the pots, basins or, bowls finished Heb. finished to make \textsuperscript{13} four hundred; pillars Heb. face of the pillars \textsuperscript{16} pots also; fleshhooks; Huram, Hiram his father bright Heb. made bright, or scoured \textsuperscript{17} clay ground Heb. thicknesses of the ground Zeredathah, Zarthan \textsuperscript{19} all the vessels; the golden; the tables \textsuperscript{20} the candlesticks; burn after the oracle \textsuperscript{21} the flowers Probably each branch of the chandelier was made like a plant in flower; and the opening of the flower was either the lamp, or served to support it.;, perfect gold Heb. perfections of gold, That is, the purest and best gold. \textsuperscript{22} snuffers; basins or, bowls the entry Capellus and others suppose we should read, agreeably to, "The hinges also of the doors of the inner house, " etc.; the word pothoth, "hinges, " being mistaken for paithach, "an entry" or "door-way."\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 5}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Solomon brought in the holy things of his father David, the silver, and the gold, and the [other] vessels, and put them in the treasury of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, [even] the leaders of the families of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, —this [is] Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all Israel were assembled [to] the king in the feast, this [is] the seventh month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And all the elders of Israel came; and all the Levites took up the ark, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and the tabernacle of witness, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle; and the priests and the Levites brought it up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And king Solomon, and all the elders of Israel, and the religious of them, and they of them that were gathered before the ark, [were] sacrificing calves and sheep, which could not be numbered or reckoned for multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place, into the oracle of the house, [even] into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the cherubs stretched out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubs covered the ark, and its staves above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the staves projected, and the heads of the staves were seen from the holy place in front of the oracle, they were not seen without: and there they were to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} There was nothing in the ark except the two tables which Moses placed [there] in Choreb, which God gave in covenant with the children of Israel, when they went out of the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when the priests when out of the holy place, (for all the priests that were found were sanctified, they were not [then] arranged according to their daily course,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that all the singing Levites [assigned] to the sons of Asaph, to Aeman, to Idithun, and to his sons, and to his brethren, of them that were clothed in linen garments, with cymbals and lutes and harps, [were] standing before the altar, and with them one hundred and twenty priests, blowing trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there was one voice in the trumpeting and in the psalm-singing, and in the loud utterance with one voice to give thanks and praise the Lord; and when they raised their voice together with trumpets and cymbals, and instruments of music, and said, Give thanks to the Lord, for [it is] good, for his mercy [endures] for ever:—then the house was filled with the cloud of the glory of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.\par
