\subsection*{Chronicles II 6}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then said Solomon, The Lord said that he would dwell in thick darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But I have built a house to your name, holy to you, and prepared [for you] to dwell in for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king turned his face, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: and all the congregation of Israel stood by. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he said, Blessed [be] the Lord God of Israel: he has even fulfilled with his hands as he spoke with his mouth to my father David, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} From the day when I brought up my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city of all the tribes of Israel, to build a house that my name should be there; neither did I choose a man to be a leader over my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But I chose Jerusalem that my name should be there; and I chose David to be over my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came into the heart of David my father, to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the Lord said to my father David, Whereas it came into your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it came into your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Nevertheless you shall not build the house; for your son who shall come forth out of your loins, he shall build the house for my name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord has confirmed this word, which he spoke; and I am raised up in the room of my father David, and I sit upon the throne of Israel as the Lord said, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and I have set there the ark in which [is] the covenant of the Lord, which he made with Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread out his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For Solomon [had] made a brazen scaffold, and set it in the midst of the court of the sanctuary; the length of it [was] five cubits, and the breadth of it five cubits, and the height of it three cubits: and he stood upon it, and fell upon his knees before the whole congregation of Israel, and spread abroad his hands to heaven, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and said, Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven, or on the earth; keeping covenant and mercy with your servants that walk before you with [their] whole heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Even as you have kept [them] with your servant David my father, as you have spoken to him in words:—you have both spoken with your mouth, and have fulfilled [it] with your hands, as it is this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and now, Lord God of Israel, keep with your servant David my father the things which you spoke to him, saying, There shall not fail you a man before me sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your sons will take heed to their way to walk in my law, as you did walk before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And now, Lord God of Israel, let, I pray you, your word be confirmed, which you have spoken to your servant David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For will God indeed dwell with men upon the earth? if the heaven and the heaven of heavens will not suffice you, what then is this house which I have built? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Yet you shall have respect to the prayer of your servant, and to my petition, O Lord God, so as to listen to the petition and the prayer which your servant prays before you this day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} so that your eyes should be open over this house by day and by night, towards this place, whereon you said your name should be called, so as to hear the prayer which your servant prays towards this house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you shall hear the supplication of your servant, and of your people Israel, whatever prayers they shall make towards this place: and you shall listen in your dwelling-place out of heaven, yes you shall hear, and be merciful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} If a man sin against his neighbor, and he bring an oath upon him so as to make him swear, and he come and swear before the altar in this house; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} then shall you listen out of heaven, and do, and judge your servants, to recompense the transgressor, and to return his ways upon his head: and to justify the righteous, to recompense him according to his righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And if your people Israel should be put to the worse before the enemy, if they should sin against you, and [then] turn and confess to your name, and pray and make supplication before you in this house; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} then shall you listen out of heaven and shall be merciful to the sins of your people Israel, and you shall restore them to the land which you gave to them and to their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} When heaven is restrained, and there is no rain, because they shall have sinned against you, and [when] they shall pray towards this place, and praise your name, and shall turn from their sins, because you shall afflict them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} then shall you listen from heaven, and you shall be merciful to the sins of your servants, and of your people Israel; for you shall show them the good way in which they shall walk; and you shall send rain upon your land, which you gave to your people for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} If there should be famine upon the land, if there should be death, a pestilent wind an blight; if there should be locust and caterpiller, and if the enemy should harass them before their cities: in whatever plague and whatever distress [they may be]; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then whatever prayer and whatever supplication shall be made by any man and all your people Israel, if a man should know his own plague and his own sickness, and should spread forth his hands toward this house; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} then shall you hear from heaven, out of your prepared dwelling-place, and shall be merciful, and shall recompense to the man according to his ways, as you shall know his heart [to be]; for you alone know the heart of the children of men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} that they may reverence all your ways all the days which they live upon the face of the land, which you gave to our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And every stranger who is not himself of your people Israel, and who shall have come from a distant land because of your great name, and your mighty hand, and your high arm; when they shall come and worship toward this place; — {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} then shall you listen out of heaven, out of your prepared dwelling-place, and shall do according to all that the stranger shall call upon you for; that all the nations of the earth may know your name, and that they may fear you, as your people Israel [do], and that they may know that your name is called upon this house which I have built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And if your people shall go forth to war against their enemies by the way by which you shall send them, and shall pray to you toward this city which you have chosen, and [toward] the house which I have built to your name; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} then shall you hear out of heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Whereas if they shall sin against you, (for there is no man who will not sin,) and you shall strike them, and deliver them up before their enemies, and they that take them captive shall carry them away into a land of enemies, to a land far off or near; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and [if] they shall repent in their land whither they were carried captive, and shall also turn and make supplication to you in their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have transgressed, we have wrought unrighteously; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} and [if] they shall turn to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of them that carried them captives, whither they carried them captives, and shall pray toward their land which you gave to their fathers, and the city which you did choose, and the house which I built to your name:— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} then shall you hear out of heaven, out of your prepared dwelling-place, their prayer and their supplication, and you shall execute justice, and shall be merciful to your people that sin against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And now, Lord, let, I pray you, your eyes be opened, and your ears be attentive to the petition [made in] this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And now, O Lord God, arise into your resting-place, you, and the ark of your strength: let your priests, O Lord God, clothe themselves with salvation, and your sons rejoice in prosperity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} O Lord God, turn not away the face of your anointed: remember the mercies of your servant David.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} turned his face blessed; all the congregation \textsuperscript{5} Since the day; my name; neither chose The judges and Saul were chosen by God, for a season, to be rulers of Israel; but not to establish a permanent and hereditary authority over that people, as was the case with David. This clause is wanting in the parallel passage of Kings; but it helps to clear the sense. \textsuperscript{6} But I have chosen Jerusalem This clause is also not found in Kings. Jerusalem was expressly marked out, by the building of the temple, to be the centre of the worship of Israel; as Jehovah had before spoken by Moses. \subsection*{Chronicles II 7}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when Solomon had finished praying, then the fire came down from heaven, and devoured the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices; and the glory of the Lord filled the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the priests could not enter into the house of the Lord at that time, for the glory of the Lord filled the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all the children of Israel saw the fire descending, and the glory of the Lord was upon the house: and they fell upon their face to the ground on the pavement, and worshipped, and praised the Lord; for [it is] good [to do so], because his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king and all the people [were] offering sacrifices before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of calves twenty and two thousand, of sheep one hundred and twenty thousand: so the king and all the people dedicated the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the priests were standing at their watches, and the Levites with instruments of music of the Lord, belonging to king David, to give thanks before the Lord, for his mercy [endures] for ever, with the hymns of David, by their ministry: and the priests were blowing the trumpets before them, and all Israel standing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was in the house of the Lord: for he offered there the whole burnt offerings and the fat of the peace-offerings, for the brazen altar which Solomon had made was not sufficient to receive the whole burnt offerings, and the meat-offerings, and the fat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Solomon kept the feast at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entering in of Aemath, and as far as the river of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And on the eighth day he kept a solemn assembly: for he kept a feast of seven days as the dedication of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he dismissed the people to their tents, rejoicing, and with a glad heart because of the good deeds which the Lord had done to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So Solomon finished the house of the Lord, and the king's house: and in whatever Solomon wished in his heart to do in the house of the Lord and in his own house, he prospered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him, I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place to myself for a house of sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} If I should restrain the heaven and there should be no rain, and if I should command the locust to devour the trees, and if I should send pestilence upon my people; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} then if my people, on whom my name is called, should repent, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their evil ways, I also will hear from heaven, and I will be merciful to their sins, and I will heal their land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now my eyes shall be open, and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now I have chosen and sanctified this house, that my name should be there for ever: and my eyes and my heart shall be there always. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if you will walk before me as David your father [did], and will do according to all that I have commanded you, and will keep my ordinances and my judgments; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} then will I establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, There shall not fail you a man ruling in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But if you⌃ should turn away, and forsake my ordinances and my commandments, which I have set before you, and go and serve other gods, and worship them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} then will I remove you from the land which I gave them; and this house which I have consecrated to my name I will remove out of my sight, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And [as for] this lofty house, every one that passes by it shall be amazed, and shall say, Therefore has the Lord done [thus] to this land, and to this house? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [men] shall say, Because they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they attached themselves to other gods, and worshipped them, and served them: and therefore he has brought upon them all this evil.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when Solomon; the fire; the glory \textsuperscript{3} they bowed; For he is \textsuperscript{4} Then the king They presented the victims to the priests, and they and the Levites slew them, and sprinkled the blood; or, perhaps, the people themselves slew them, and having caught the blood, collected the fat, etc., presented them to the priests to be offered as the law required. \textsuperscript{5} a sacrifice, ; twenty and two The number of sheep and oxen here mentioned has to some appeared incredibly large; but it must be considered that a prodigious number of persons was now at Jerusalem, and that this was the amount of all the victims that had been offered during the seven days of the feast of tabernacles, as well as the time the feast of the dedication lasted. dedicated \textsuperscript{6} the priests, the Levites;, ; which David because his mercy;, ministry Heb. hand, the priests \textsuperscript{8} kept; a very great from the entering That is, from one extremity of the land to another; Hamath being situated on the north, and the river of Egypt on the south. \textsuperscript{9} solemn assembly Heb. restraint; seven days \textsuperscript{10} three and twentieth glad;, ; goodness \textsuperscript{12} the Lord; I have heard; have chosen; an house of sacrifice \textsuperscript{13} If I shut up heaven; I command; I send \textsuperscript{14} my people which are called by my name Heb. upon whom my name is called humble, ; and pray seek my face; turn from; will I hear, heal their land \textsuperscript{15} mine eyes; that is made in this place Heb. of this place \textsuperscript{16} have I chosen; my name, ; eyes \textsuperscript{18} stablish as I have, shall not; fail thee Heb. be cut off to thee \textsuperscript{19} if ye turn away; shall go\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 8}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass after twenty years, in which Solomon built the house of the Lord, and his own house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that Solomon rebuilt the cities which Chiram had given to Solomon, and caused the children of Israel to dwell in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Solomon came to Baesoba, and fortified it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he built Thoedmor in the wilderness, and all the strong cities which he built in Emath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he built Baethoron the upper, and Baethoron the lower, strong cities, —they had walls, gates, and bars; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and Balaath, and all the strong cities which Solomon had, and all his chariot cities, and cities of horsemen, and all things that Solomon desired according to his desire of building, in Jerusalem, and in Libanus, and in all his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [As for] all the people that was left of the Chettites, and the Amorites, and the Pherezites, and the Evites, and the Jebusites, who are not of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} but were of the children of them whom the children Israel destroyed not, that were left after them in the land, even them did Solomon make tributaries to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But Solomon did not make any of the children of Israel servants in his kingdom; for, behold, [they were] warriors and rulers, and mighty [men], and captains of chariots and horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And these are the chiefs of the officers of king Solomon, two hundred and fifty overseeing the work among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharao from the city of David to the house which he had built for her: for he said, My wife shall not dwell in the city of David, the king of Israel, for [the place] is holy into which the ark of the Lord has entered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then Solomon offered up to the Lord whole burnt offerings on the altar which he had built to the Lord before the temple, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} according to the daily rate, to offer up [sacrifices] according to the commandments of Moses, on the sabbaths, and at the new moons, and at the feasts, three times in the year, at the feast of unleavened bread, and at the feast of weeks, and at the feast of tabernacles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he established, according to the order of his father David, the courses of the priests, and [that] according to their public ministrations: and the Levites [were appointed] over their charges, to praise and minister before the priests according to the daily order: and the porters were appointed according to their courses to the different gates: for thus [were] the commandments of David the man of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} They transgressed not the commandments of the king concerning the priests and the Levites with regard to everything else, and with regard to the treasures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now all the work had been prepared from the day when the foundation was laid, until Solomon finished the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then Solomon went to Gasion Gaber, and to Aelath near the sea in the land of Idumea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Chiram sent by the hand of his servants ships, and servants skilled in naval affairs; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Sophira, and brought thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and they came to king Solomon.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} he built Tadmor, the Palmyra of the Greeks, as we learn from Josephus, a celebrated city of Syria, situated in an oasis, or fertile spot of land, surrounded on all sides by a vast sandy desert, like an island in the midst of the ocean; according to Pliny, 337 miles from Seleucia and Tigrim, 203 from the nearest part of the Mediterranean, and 176 from Damascus; according to Josephus, one day's journey west of the Euphrates, and six from Babylon; and according to Ptolemy, in lat. 34 degrees north, or that of Tripoli, and about 4 degrees more easterly; and it is described by Mr. Wood as "situated under a barren ridge of hills to the west, and open on the other sides to the desert; " "about six days' journey from Aleppo, and as much from Damascus, and about twenty leagues west of the Euphrates." Palmyra attained the height of its splendour when the royal city of Zenobia was conquered by the emperor Aurelian; became a Roman colony after the victories of Trajan; and was probably reduced to its present miserable state in the wars of the Saracens. Its magnificent ruins, however, scattered over an extent of several miles, sufficiently attest its former splendour and riches. \textsuperscript{6} Baalath; the store cities; chariot cities; all that Solomon desired to build Heb. all the desire of Solomon which he desired to build; and in Lebanon \textsuperscript{7} As for all the Hittites \textsuperscript{8} whom the children; to pay \textsuperscript{9} But of the; they were men \textsuperscript{11} brought up, holy Heb. holiness \textsuperscript{12} on the altar; before the porch \textsuperscript{13} every day; Num. 28:1-29:40; three times \textsuperscript{14} the courses, ; the Levites;, ; the porters, so had David the man of God commanded Heb. so was the commandment of David the man of God \textsuperscript{18} Hiram Huram, Ophir Conjectures respecting the situation of Ophir are endless. Grotius conjectures it to be a part of Arabia called Aphar by Arrian; while Bochart and others have placed it in the island of Ceylon. Calmet supposes it to have been situated in Armenia; but his late editor places it at the head of the Indus. Josephus says that Ophir is the Indies, called the Gold country; by which he is supposed to mean Chersonesus Aurea, now Malacca, opposite Sumatra; and Lev. Poivre observes that the inhabitants of these places call their gold mines ophirs . took thence\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the queen of Saba heard [of] the name of Solomon, and she came to Jerusalem with a very large force, to prove Solomon with hard questions, and [she had] camels bearing spices in abundance, and gold, and precious stones: and she came to Solomon, and told him all that was in her mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Solomon told her all her words; and there passed not a word from Solomon which he told her not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the queen of Saba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and the meat of the tables, and the sitting of his servants, and the standing of his ministers, and their raiment; and his cupbearers, and their apparel; and the whole burnt offerings which he offered up in the house of the Lord; then she was in ecstasy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she said to the king, [It was] a true report which I heard in my land concerning your words, and concerning your wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Yet I believed not the reports until I came, and my eyes saw: and, behold, the half of the abundance of your wisdom was not told me: you have exceeded the report which I heard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Blessed [are] your men, blessed [are] these your servants, who stand before you continually, and hear your wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Blessed be the Lord your God, who took pleasure in you, to set you upon his throne for a king, to the Lord your God: forasmuch as the Lord your God loved Israel to establish them for ever, therefore he has set you over them for a king to execute judgment and justice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in very great abundance, and precious stones: and there were not [any where else] such spices as those which the queen of Saba gave king Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the servants of Solomon and the servants of Chiram brought gold to Solomon out of Suphir, and pine timber, and precious stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the king made of the pine timber steps to the house of the Lord, and to the king's house, and harps and lutes for the singers: and such were not seen before in the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And king Solomon gave to the queen of Saba all that she requested, besides all that she brought to king Solomon: and she returned to her [own] land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the weight of the gold that was brought to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} besides what the men who were regularly appointed and the merchants brought, and all the kings of Arabia and princes of the land: all brought gold and silver to king Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And king Solomon made two hundred shields of beaten gold: there were six hundred [shekels] of pure gold to one shield. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And three hundred buckles of beaten gold: [the weight] of three hundred gold shekels went to one buckler: and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king made a great throne of ivory, and he gilded it with pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And [there were] six steps to the throne, riveted with gold, and elbows on either side of the seat of the throne, and two lions standing by the elbows: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and twelve lions standing there on the six steps on each side. There was not the like in any [other] kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all king Solomon's vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were covered with gold: silver was not thought anything of in the days of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For a ship went for the king to Tharsis with the servants of Chiram: once every three years came vessels from Tharsis to the king, laden with gold, and silver, and ivory, and apes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Solomon exceeded all [other] kings both in riches and wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they brought every one his gifts, silver vessels and golden vessels, and raiment, myrrh and spices, horses and mules, a rate every year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; and he put them in the chariot cities, and with the king in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he rules over all the kings from the river even to the land of the Philistines, and to the borders of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as the sycamore trees in the plain for abundance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Solomon imported horses from Egypt, and from every [other] country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the rest of the acts of Solomon, the first and the last, behold, these are written in the words of Nathan the prophet, and in the words of Achia the Selonite, and in the visions of Joel the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nabat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Solomon reigned over all Israel forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Solomon fell asleep, and they buried him in the city of David his father: and Roboam his son reigned in his stead.\par

Mr. Bruce has given us the history of her and her descendants from Abyssinian records; and Josephus says that Sheba was the ancient name of the city of Meroe (south of Egypt, and sometimes comprehended in Ethiopia), and that this princess came from thence. Those who think the princess came from Arabia, rely chiefly on the fact that gold, silver, spices, and precious stones, which were the presents she made to Solomon, are the natural products of that country; and that it may well be placed at the uttermost part of the earth, as it borders on the southern ocean, and formerly they knew no land beyond it. \textsuperscript{10} brought gold; algum trees, almug-trees \textsuperscript{11} terraces or, stairs, Heb. highways harps \textsuperscript{18} stays Heb. hands two lions \textsuperscript{20} drinking; pure Heb. shut up none were of silver or, there was no silver in them it was \textsuperscript{21} Tharshish Tarshish Bochart thinks this Tarshish was probably the promontory Cory, on the north of the island of Ceylon, which, according to him, was the land of Ophir. That it was name of a place in the East Indies, seems probable from the articles brought thence, and also from the ships sent thither being built at Ezion-geber, on the Red Sea; though Michaelis supposes that the fleet coasted along the shore of Africa, doubling the Cape of Good Hope, and came to Tartessus, in Spain, and thence back again the same way; that this accounts for their three years' voyage out and home; and that Spain and the coasts of Africa furnish all the commodities which they brought back. ivory or, elephants' teeth peacocks Tukkeeyim is rendered taysin in the Targum, ταωνων, in the Alexandrian manuscript of the LXX, and pavos, "peacocks, " in the Vulgate; with which the Syriac, Arabic, and Rabbins agree. This derives confirmation from the fact, that the peacock is called in Malabaric, Togei . \textsuperscript{26} reigned over; river "That is, Euphrates." \textsuperscript{27} the king; made Heb. gave the sycamore \textsuperscript{28} brought "Moses, " says Bp. Warburton, "had expressly prohibited the multiplying of horses ( ); by which the future king was forbidden to establish a body of calvary, because this could not be effected without sending into Egypt, with which people God had forbidden any communication, as this would be dangerous to religion. When Solomon had violated this law, and multiplied horses to excess ( ), it was soon attended with those fatal consequences that the law foretold: for this wisest of kings having likewise, in violation of another law, married Pharaoh's daughter (the early fruits of this commerce), and then, by a repetition of the same crime, but a transgression of another law, had espoused more strange women (; ), they first, in defiance of a fourth law, persuaded him to build them idol temples for their use; and afterwards, against a fifth law, brought him to erect other temples for his own." \textsuperscript{29} the rest book Heb. words Nathan, ;, ; Ahijah, Iddo\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 10}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Roboam came to Sychem: for all Israel came to Sychem to make him king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass when Jeroboam the son of Nabat heard [it], (now he was in Egypt, forasmuch as he had fled there from the face of king Solomon, and Jeroboam lived in Egypt,) that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they sent and called him: and Jeroboam and all the congregation came to Roboam, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Your father made our yoke grievous: now then abate [somewhat] of your father's grievous rule, and of his heavy yoke which he put upon us, and we will serve you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to them, Go away for three days, and [then] come to me. So the people departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And king Roboam assembled the elders that stood before his father Solomon in his life-time, saying, How do you⌃ counsel [me] to return an answer to this people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they spoke to him, saying, If you would this day befriend this people, and be kind to them, and speak to them good words, then will they be your servants for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But he forsook the advice of the old men, who took counsel with him, and he took counsel with the young men who had been brought up with him, who stood before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to them, What do you⌃ advise that I should answer this people, who spoke to me, saying, Ease [somewhat] of the yoke which your father laid upon us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the young men that had been brought up with him spoke to him, saying, Thus shall you speak to the people that spoke to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy, and do you lighten [somewhat of it] from us; thus shall you say, My little finger [shall be] thicker than my father's loins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And whereas my father chastised you with a heavy yoke, I will also add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, and I will chastise you with scorpions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Jeroboam and all the people came to Roboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, Return to me on the third day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the king answered harshly; and king Roboam forsook the counsel of the old men, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king listened not to the people, for there was a change [of their minds] from God, saying, The Lord has confirmed his word, which he spoke by the hand of Achia the Selonite concerning Jeroboam the son of Nabat, and [concerning] all Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} for the king did not listen to them. And the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David, or inheritance in the son of Jessae? to your tents, O Israel: now see to your own house, David. So all Israel went to their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But the men of Israel, even those who lived in the cities of Juda, [remained] and made Roboam king over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And king Roboam sent to them Adoniram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And king Roboam hasted to mount [his] chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} So Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Rehoboam; Roboam Shechem, Sichem; all \textsuperscript{7} If thou be kind; speak good \textsuperscript{8} he forsook;, ; the young men It was a custom in different countries to educate with the heir to the throne, young noblemen of nearly the same age. This, as Calmet observes, answered two great and important ends: 1. It excited the prince to emulation; that he might, as far as possible, surpass in all manly exercises, and in all acts of prudence and virtue, those whom one day he was to surpass in the elevation and dignity of his station. 2. That he might acquire a correct knowledge of the disposition and views of those who were likely to be, under him, the highest officers of the state, and consequently know the better how to trust and employ them. \textsuperscript{10} Thus shalt; My little finger "My weakness, " says the Targumist, "shall be stronger than the might of my father." \textsuperscript{11} my father put Heb. laded I will put, ; scorpions \textsuperscript{15} the king the cause; that the Lord;, Ahijah \textsuperscript{16} What portion; the son, David; So all Israel \textsuperscript{18} Hadoram, Adoniram, Adoram stoned him; made speed Heb. strengthened himself\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 11}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Roboam came to Jerusalem; and he assembled Juda and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand young men fit for war, and he waged war with Israel to recover the kingdom to Roboam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Word of the Lord came to Samaias the man of God, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Speak to Roboam the [son] of Solomon, and to all Juda and Benjamin, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Thus says the Lord, You⌃ shall not go up, and you⌃ shall not war against your brethren: return every one to his home; for this thing is of me. And they listened to the word of the Lord, and returned from going against Jeroboam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Roboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built walled cities in Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he built Bethleem, and Aetan and Thecoe, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and Baethsura, and Sochoth, and Odollam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and Geth, and Marisa, and Ziph, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and Adorai, and Lachis, and Azeca, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and Saraa, and Aelom, and Chebron, which belong to Juda and Benjamin, walled cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he fortified them with walls, and placed in them captains, and stores of provisions, oil and wine, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} shields and spears in every several city, and he fortified them very strongly, and he had on his side Juda and Benjamin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel were gathered to him out of all the coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the Levites left the tents of their possession, and went to Juda to Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had ejected them so that they should not minister to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he made for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vanities, and for the calves which Jeroboam made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he cast out from the tribes of Israel those who set their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel: and they came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice to the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they strengthened the kingdom of Juda; and [Juda] strengthened Roboam the [son] of Solomon for three years, for he walked three years in the ways of David and Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Roboam took to himself for a wife, Moolath daughter of Jerimuth the son of David, and Abigaia daughter of Heliab the son of Jessae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And she bore him sons; Jeus, and Samoria, and Zaam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And afterwards he took to himself Maacha the daughter of Abessalom; and she bore him Abia, and Jetthi, and Zeza, and Salemoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Roboam loved Maacha the daughter of Abessalom more than all his wives and all his concubines: for he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines; and he begot twenty-eight sons, and sixty daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he made Abia the son of Maacha chief, [even] a leader among his brethren, for he intended to make him king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he was exalted beyond all his [other] sons in all the coasts of Juda and Benjamin, and in the strong cities; and he gave them provisions in great abundance: and he desired many wives.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} against; return; for this thing; they obeyed \textsuperscript{6} Bethlehem, called Bethlehem Judah ( ), to distinguish it from another Bethlehem in Zebulun ( ), and also Ephratah (i.e., fruitful), and by the Arabs, Bait-el-lahm, is situated on a rising ground on the southern side of a deep and extensive valley, and reclining from e to w not quite six miles s of Jerusalem.; Etam; Tekoa \textsuperscript{12} he put shields; having Judah \textsuperscript{13} am 3030, bc 974 resorted to him Heb. presented themselves to him \textsuperscript{15} for the devils The word, seirim literally signifies hairy ones, or goats. \subsection*{Chronicles II 12}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass when the kingdom of Roboam was established, and when he had grown strong, [that] he forsook the commandments of the Lord, and all Israel with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam, Susakim king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horses: and there was no number of the multitude that came with him from Egypt; Libyans, Trogodytes, and Ethiopians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they obtained possession of the strong cities, which were in Juda, and came to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Samaias the prophet came to Roboam, and to the princes of Juda that were gathered to Jerusalem for fear of Susakim, and said to them, Thus said the Lord, You⌃ have left me, and I will leave you in the hand of Susakim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the elders of Israel and the king were ashamed, and said, The Lord [is] righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when the Lord saw that they repented, then came the word of the Lord to Samaias, saying, They have repented; I will not destroy them, but I will set them in safety for a little while, and my wrath shall not be poured out on Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Nevertheless they shall be servants, and know my service, and the service of the kings of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So Susakim king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem, and took the treasures that were in the house of the Lord, and the treasures that were in the king's house: he took all; and he took the golden shields which Solomon had made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And king Roboam made brazen shields instead of them. And Susakim set over him captains of footmen, as keepers of the gate of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when the king went into the house of the Lord, the guards and the footmen went in, and they that returned to meet the footmen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when he repented, the anger of the Lord turned from him, and did not destroy him utterly; for there were good things in Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So king Roboam strengthened [himself] in Jerusalem, and reigned: and Roboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, in the city which the Lord chose out of all the tribes of the children of Israel to call his name there: and his mother's name was Noomma the Ammanitess. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he did evil, for he directed not his heart to seek the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the acts of Roboam, the first and the last, behold, are they not written in the book of Samaia the prophet, and Addo the seer, with his achievements. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Roboam made war with Jeroboam all [his] days. And Roboam died with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abia his son reigned in his stead.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 13}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam Abia began to reign over Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He reigned three years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name [was] Maacha, daughter of Uriel of Gabaon. And there was war between Abia and Jeroboam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Abia set the battle in array with an army, with mighty men of war, [even] four hundred thousand mighty men: and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand, [they were] mighty warriors of the host. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Abia rose up from the mount Somoron, which is in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear you⌃, Jeroboam, and all Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [Is it] not for you to know that the Lord God of Israel has given a king over Israel for ever to David, and to his sons, by a covenant of salt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But Jeroboam the [son] of Nabat, the servant of Solomon [the son] of David, is risen up, and has revolted from his master: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and there are gathered to him pestilent men, transgressors, and he has risen up against Roboam the [son] of Solomon, while Roboam was young and fearful in heart, and he withstood him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now you⌃ profess to resist the kingdom of the Lord in the hand of the sons of David; and you⌃ [are] a great multitude, and with you are golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Did you⌃ not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make to yourselves priests of the people of any [other] land? whoever came to consecrate himself with a calf of the heard and seven rams, he forthwith became a priest to that which is no god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But we have not forsaken the Lord our God, and his priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, minister to the Lord; and in their daily courses {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} they sacrifice to the Lord whole burnt offering, morning and evening, and compound incense, and [set] the show bread on the pure table; and [there is] the golden candlestick, and the lamps for burning, to light in the evening: for we keep the charge of the Lord God of our fathers; but you⌃ have forsaken him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And, behold, the Lord and his priests are with us at our head, and the signal trumpets to sound an alarm over us. Children of Israel, fight not against the Lord God of our fathers; for you⌃ shall not prosper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now Jeroboam had caused an ambush to come round upon him from behind: and he [himself] was before Juda, and the ambush behind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Juda looked back, and, behold, the battle [was] against them before and behind: and they cried to the Lord, and the priests sounded with the trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the men of Juda shouted: and it came to pass, when the men of Juda shouted, that the Lord struck Jeroboam and Israel before Abia and Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the children of Israel fled from before Juda; and the Lord delivered them into their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Abia and his people struck them with a great slaughter: and there fell slain of Israel five hundred thousand mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So the children of Israel were brought low in that day, and the children of Juda prevailed, because they trusted on the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Abia pursued after Jeroboam, and he took from him the cities, Baethel and her towns, and Jesyna and her towns, and Ephron and her towns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jeroboam did not recover strength again all the days of Abia: and the Lord struck him, and he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But Abia strengthened himself, and took to himself fourteen wives, and he begot twenty-two sons, and sixteen daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the rest of the acts of Abia, and his deeds, and his sayings, are written in the book of the prophet Addo.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3046-3049, bc 958-955 in the eighteenth \textsuperscript{2} Michaiah, Maachah the daughter of Absalom, Abishalom Gibeah, Gibeath, ; am 3047, bc 957 And there was \textsuperscript{3} set Heb. bound together, four hundred, ; eight hundred \textsuperscript{4} Zemaraim could not be, as some have supposed, the same as the hill of Samaria, ωΡξψεο, so called from Shemer, in the days of Omri; but was probably a hill on the confines of Ephraim, near Zemaraim, a city of Benjamin, near Bethel.; Hear me \textsuperscript{5} Ought ye not; the Lord; to David; a covenant of salt \textsuperscript{7} vain men; the children of Belial; young; could not \textsuperscript{8} the kingdom; a great multitude, ; with you golden \textsuperscript{9} cast out made you priests, consecrate himself Heb. fill his hand; *marg. young; no gods \textsuperscript{10} the Lord We have not abandoned the Lord; and we still serve him according to His own law. But what Abijah urged concerning the state of religion in Judah was not strictly just; and, as spoken by him, it favoured ostentation. Abijah himself was but an indifferent character; and idolatry was evidently connived at in his days. Yet it was true, that the men of Judah had the priests, ordinances, and worship of Jehovah among them; that there were numbers of pious worshippers in the land; that theirs was the more righteous cause; that Jehovah was on their side as their Captain, while Israel fought against him; and that the presence of the priests with the sacred trumpets was a token of His presence and favour.; the priests \textsuperscript{11} they burn; sweet incense; showbread; the candlestick; we keep \textsuperscript{12} God; for our captain; his priests; fight ye; ye shall not \textsuperscript{14} looked back; cried; the priests \textsuperscript{15} as the men; God smote \textsuperscript{19} took cities, ; Jeshanah, according to the Talmud, was not far from Sephoris. Perhaps it is the Migdal-Senna of Eusebius, eight miles north of Jericho. Ephrain, or Ephron, a city of Benjamin, is placed by Eusebius, eight miles north of Jerusalem, near Bethel. Josephus calls Ephrain and Bethel two little cities; and places the former in the tribe of Benjamin, near the wilderness of Judea, in the way to Jericho.; Ephron\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 14}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Abia died with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In the days of Asa the land of Juda had rest ten years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was good and right in the sight of the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he removed the altars of the strange [gods], and the high places, and broke the pillars in pieces, and cut down the groves: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and he told Juda to seek earnestly the Lord God of their fathers, and to perform the law and commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he removed from all the cities of Juda the altars and the idols, and established in quietness {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} fortified cities in the land of Juda; for the land was quiet, and he had no war in these years; for the Lord gave him rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said to Juda, Let us fortify these cities, and make walls, and towers, and gates, and bars: we shall prevail over the land, for as we have sought out the Lord our God, he has sought out us, and has given us rest round about, and prospered us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Asa had a force of armed men bearing shields and spears in the land of Juda, [even] three hundred thousand, and in the land of Benjamin two hundred and eighty thousand targeteers and archers: all these were mighty warriors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Zare the Ethiopian went out against them, with a force of a million, and three hundred chariots; and came to Maresa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Asa went out to meet him, and set the battle in array in the valley north of Maresa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Asa cried to the Lord his God, and said, O Lord, it is not impossible with you to save by many or by few: strengthen us, O Lord our God; for we trust in you, and in your name have we come against this great multitude. O Lord our God, let not man prevail against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Juda; and the Ethiopians fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Asa and his people pursued them to Gedor; and the Ethiopians fell, so that they could not recover themselves; for they were crushed before the Lord, and before his host; and they took many spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they destroyed their towns roundabout Gedor; for a terror of the Lord was upon them: and they spoiled all their cities, for they had much spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Also they destroyed the tents of cattle, and the Alimazons, and took many sheep and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 15}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Azarias the son of Oded—upon him came the Spirit of the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and he went out to meet Asa, and all Juda and Benjamin, and said, Hear me, Asa, and all Juda and Benjamin. The Lord [is] with you, while you⌃ are with him; and if you⌃ seek him out, he will be found of you; but if you⌃ forsake him, he will forsake you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Israel [has been] a long time without the true God, and without a priest to expound [the truth], and without the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But he shall turn them to the Lord God of Israel, and he will be found of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in that time there is no peace to one going out, or to one coming in, for the terror of the Lord is upon all that inhabit the lands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And nation shall fight against nation, and city against city; for God has confounded them with every [kind of] affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But be you⌃ strong, and let not your hands be weakened: for there is a reward for your work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when [Asa] heard these words, and the prophesy of Adad the prophet, then he strengthened himself, and cast out the abominations from all the land of Juda and Benjamin, and from the cities which Jeroboam possessed, in mount Ephraim, and he renewed the altar of the Lord, which was before the temple of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he assembled Juda and Benjamin, and the strangers that lived with him, of Ephraim, and of Manasse, and of Symeon: for many of Israel were joined to him, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they assembled at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he sacrificed to the Lord in that day of the spoils which they brought, seven hundred calves and seven thousand sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he entered into a covenant that they should seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And that whoever should not seek the Lord God of Israel, should die, whether young or old, whether man or woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they swore to the Lord with a loud voice, and with trumpets, and with cornets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And all Juda rejoiced concerning the oath: for they swore with all their heart, and they sought him with all their desires; and he was found of them: and the Lord gave them rest round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he removed Maacha his mother from being priestess to Astarte; and he cut down the idol, and burnt it in the brook of Kedron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Nevertheless they removed not the high places: they still existed in Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he brought in the holy things of David his father, and the holy things of the house of God, silver, and gold, and vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And there was no war [waged] with him until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 16}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Asa, the king of Israel went up against Juda, and built Rama, so as not to allow egress or ingress to Asa king of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Asa took silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord, and of the king's house, and sent [them] to the son of Ader king of Syria, which lived in Damascus, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Make a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father: behold, I have sent you gold and silver: come, and turn away from me Baasa king of Israel, and let him depart from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the son of Ader listened to king Asa, and sent the captains of his host against the cities of Israel; and struck Aeon, and Dan, and Abelmain, and all the country round Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it came to pass when Baasa heard [it] he left off building Rama, and put a stop to his work: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} then king Asa took all Juda, and took the stones of Rama, and its timber, [with] which Baasa [had] built; and he built with them Gabae and Maspha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And at that time came Anani the prophet to Asa king of Juda, and said to him, Because you did trust on the king of Syria, and did not trust on the Lord your God, therefore the army of Syria is escaped out of your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans a great force, in courage, in horsemen, in great numbers? and did not He deliver them into your hands, because you trusted in the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For the eyes of the Lord look upon all the earth, to strengthen every heart that is perfect toward him. In this you have done foolishly; henceforth there shall be war with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Asa was angry with the prophet, and put him in prison, for he was angry at this: and Asa vexed some of the people at that time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And, behold, the acts of Asa, the first and the last, [are] written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Asa was diseased [in] his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, until he was very ill: but in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the fortieth year of his reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they buried him in the sepulchre which he had dug for himself in the city of David, and they laid him on a bed, and filled [it] with spices and [all] kinds of perfumes of the apothecaries; and they made for him a very great funeral.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 17}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josaphat his son reigned in his stead, Josaphat strengthened himself against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he put garrisons in all the strong cities of Juda, and appointed captains in all the cities of Juda, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord was with Josaphat, for he walked in the first ways of his father, and did not seek to idols; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} but he sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in the commandments of his father, and not according to the works of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord prospered the kingdom in his hand; and all Juda gave gifts to Josaphat; and he had great wealth and glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And his heart was exalted in the way of the Lord; and he removed the high places and the groves from the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And in the third year of his reign, he sent his chief men, and his mighty men, Abdias and Zacharias, and Nathanael, and Michaias, to teach in the cities of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And with them [were] the Levites, Samaias, and Nathanias, and Zabdias, and Asiel, and Semiramoth, and Jonathan, and Adonias, and Tobias, and Tobadonias, Levites, and with them Elisama and Joram, the priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they taught in Juda, and [there was] with them the book of the law of the Lord, and they passed through the cities of Juda, and taught the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And a terror of the Lord was upon all the kingdoms of the land round about Juda, and they made no war against Josaphat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And [some] of the Philistines brought to Josaphat gifts, and silver, and presents; and the Arabians brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Josaphat increased in greatness exceedingly, and built in Judea places of abode, and strong cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he had many works in Judea: and the mighty men of war, [the men] of strength, [were] in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And this [is] their number according to the houses of their fathers; even the captains of thousands in Juda [were], Ednas the chief, and with him mighty men of strength three hundred thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And after him, Joanan the captain, and with him two hundred eighty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And after him Amasias the [son] of Zari, who was zealous for the Lord; and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And out of Benjamin [there was] a mighty man of strength, even Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand archers and targeteers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And after him Jozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand mighty men of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} These were the king's servants besides those whom the king put in the strong cities in all Judea.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} placed forces in the cities \textsuperscript{3} the Lord; he walked;, ; his father David or, his father, and of David, sought \textsuperscript{5} am 3091, bc 913 the Lord; brought Heb. gave presents; he had riches \textsuperscript{6} his heart; lifted up that is, was encouraged in the ways, ; he took away \textsuperscript{7} am 3092, bc 912 he sent In these verse we have an account of a remarkable itinerant ministry established by Jehoshaphat, in which three classes of men were employed: 1. The Princes 2. The Levites 3. The Priests We may presume that the Princes instructed the people in the nature of the civil law and constitution of the kingdom; that the Levites instructed them in every thing that appertained to the temple service, and ritual law; and that the Priests instructed them in the nature and design of their religion. Thus the nation became thoroughly instructed in their duty to God, to the king, and to each other; they therefore became as one man; and against a people thus united, on such principles, no enemy could be successful.; to teach \textsuperscript{9} they taught; the book; throughout \textsuperscript{10} the fear; fell Heb. was so that \textsuperscript{12} am 3092-3115, bc 912-889 waxed great; in Judah, castles or, palaces \textsuperscript{14} the numbers, to the house, three hundred \textsuperscript{15} next to him Heb. at this hand\par}
