\subsection*{Chronicles II 18}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josaphat had yet great wealth and glory, and he connected himself by marriage with the house of Achaab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he went down after a term of years to Achaab to Samaria: and Achaab killed for him sheep and calves, in abundance, and for the people with him, and he much desired him to go up with him to Ramoth of the country of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Achaab king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Juda, Will you go with me to Ramoth of the country of Galaad? And he said to him, As I [am], so also [are] you, as your people, [so] also [is] my people with you for the war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Josaphat said to the king of Israel, Seek, I pray you, the Lord today. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, Shall I go to Ramoth Galaad to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up, and God shall deliver [it] into the hands of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Josaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we may enquire of him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, There is yet one man by whom to enquire of the Lord; but I hate him, for he does not prophesy concerning me for good, for all his days [are] for evil: this [is] Michaias the son of Jembla. And Josaphat said, Let not the king say so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king called an eunuch, and said, [Fetch] quickly Michaias the son of Jembla. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Juda were sitting each on his throne, and clothed in their robes, sitting in the open space at the entrance of the gate of Samaria: and all the prophets were prophesying before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Sedekias son of Chanaan made for himself iron horns, and said, Thus says the Lord, With these you shall thrust Syria until it be consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth Galaad, and you shall prosper; and the Lord shall deliver it into the hands of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the messenger that went to call Michaias spoke to him, saying, Behold, the prophets have spoken favourably concerning the king with one mouth; let now, I pray you, your words be as [the words] of one of them, and do you speak good things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Michaias said, [As] the Lord lives, whatever God shall say to me, that will I speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he came to the king, and the king said to him, Michaias, shall I go up to Ramoth Galaad to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go up, and you shall prosper, and they shall be given into your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the king said to him, How often shall I solemnly charge you that you speak to me nothing but truth in the name of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said, I saw Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep without a shepherd: and the Lord said, These have no commander; let each return to his home in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, Said I not to you, that he would not prophesy concerning me good, but evil? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But he said, Not so. Hear you⌃ the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven stood by on his right hand and on his left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Lord said, Who will deceive Achaab king of Israel, that he may go up, and fall in Ramoth Galaad? And one spoke this way, and another spoke that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will deceive him. And the Lord said, Whereby? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said, I will go forth, and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And [the Lord] said, You shall deceive [him], and shall prevail: go forth, and do so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And now, behold, the Lord has put a false spirit in the mouth of these your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Then Sedekias the son of Chanaan drew near, and struck Michaias on the cheek, and said to him, By what way passed the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Michaias said, Behold, you shall see in that day, when you shall go from chamber to chamber to hide yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the king of Israel said, Take Michaias, and carry him back to Emer the governor of the city, and to Joas the captain, the king's son; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and you⌃ shall say, Thus said the king, Put this fellow into the prison house, and let him eat the bread of affliction, and [drink] the water of affliction, until I return in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Michaias said, If you do at all return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me. And he said, Hear, all you⌃ people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So the king of Israel, and Josaphat king of Juda, went up to Ramoth Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, Disguise me, and I will enter into the battle: and do you put on my raiment. so the king of Israel disguised himself, and entered into the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots that were with him, saying, Fight neither against small nor great, but only against the king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Josaphat, that they said, It is the king of Israel: and they compassed him about to fight against him: and Josaphat cried out, and the Lord delivered him; and God turned them away from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned away from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And a man drew a bow with a good aim, and struck the king of Israel between the lungs and the breast-plate: and he said to the charioteer, Turn your hand, drive me out of the battle, for I am wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the battle turned in that day; and the king of Israel remained on the chariot against Syria until evening, and died at sunset.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3107, bc 897 riches, ; joined affinity He took Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, to be wife to his son Joram ( ); which fatal connection was highly displeasing to God, and Jehoshaphat was severely reproved for it by Jehu the seer, . \textsuperscript{2} after certain years Heb. at the end of years; *marg. he went; Ahab; persuaded, Ramothgilead \textsuperscript{5} prophets; Shall we go, Go up \textsuperscript{6} Is there not; besides Heb. yet, or more \textsuperscript{7} one man, I hate him, ; good; me; Let not the \textsuperscript{8} officers or, eunuchs; *marg.; Fetch quickly Heb. hasten \textsuperscript{9} sat either; clothed; void place or, floor, Threshing-floors, among the ancient Jews, as we have before remarked, were only, as they are to this day in the East, round level plats of ground in the open air. Hence a floor might well be near the gate of Samaria, which was built on a hill, and afford no improper place for the kings of Judah and Israel to give audience to the prophets. all the prophets \textsuperscript{10} horns of iron Mr. Bruce, in describing the head-dress of the governors of Abyssinia, says, "A large broad fillet was bound upon their forehead, and tied behind their head. In the middle of this was a horn, or conical piece of silver, gilt, about four inches long, much in the shape of our common candle extinguishers. This is called kirn, keren, and is only worn in reviews, or parades after victory." Such, it may be supposed, were the horns of iron which Zedekiah (who appears to have acted the hero returning from a military triumph) made for himself, when he presumed, in the name of Jehovah, to flatter his prince with the promise of victory: "Thus saith the Lord, With these thou shalt push Syria, until they be consumed."; Thus, ; they be consumed Heb. thou consume them \textsuperscript{12} Behold; assent Heb. mouth, *marg. \textsuperscript{16} he said as sheep; master \textsuperscript{17} Did I not tell; but evil or, but for evil \textsuperscript{18} hear the word, ; I saw; all the host \textsuperscript{19} Who shall entice; go up \textsuperscript{21} a lying spirit; Thou shalt \textsuperscript{22} the lord hath; and the Lord \textsuperscript{24} Behold;, into an inner chamber or, from chamber to chamber, Heb. into a chamber in a chamber. "In one of the halls of the seraglio at Constantinople, " says Deut. Lam. Motraye, "the eunuch made us pass by several little chambers, with doors shut, like the cells of monks or nuns, as far as I could judge by one that another eunuch opened." This exactly corresponds with the idea of a "chamber within a chamber; " and it would appear that Micaiah predicted that Zedekiah should fly for shelter to a Harem, which we have seen was deemed inviolate. (See note on .) \textsuperscript{26} Put; this fellow; bread of affliction; until I return \textsuperscript{29} I will disguise; put thou on thy robes; the king \textsuperscript{30} Fight ye, small or great \textsuperscript{31} Jehoshaphat; the Lord;, God moved them \textsuperscript{32} from pursuing him Heb. from after him \textsuperscript{33} a certain man at a venture Heb. in his simplicity, between the etc. Heb. between the joints and between the breast plate, The shiryon, in Syriac, sheryono, seems to have covered both the back and breast of the warrior, and was consequently not properly a breast-plate, but a coat of mail or corslet. The corslet was made of flax or of wool woven very thick, of ox-hide, of brass, or of iron. The metallic corslet consisted not of solid piece, but of scales, hooks, or rings, connected like the links of a chain, that the warrior might move with greater ease. It was between the joints of this harness that Ahab received his mortal wound. wounded Heb. made sick\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 19}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josaphat king of Juda returned to his house at Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there went out to meet him Jeu the prophet the son of Anani, and said to him, King Josaphat, do you help a sinner, or act friendly towards one hated of the Lord? Therefore has wrath come upon you from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Nevertheless [some] good things have been found in you, forasmuch as you did remove the groves from the land of Juda, and did direct your heart to seek after the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Josaphat lived in Jerusalem: and he again went out among the people from Bersabee to the mount of Ephraim, and turned them back to the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he appointed judges in all the strong cities of Juda, city by city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to the judges, Take good heed what you⌃ do: for you⌃ judge not for man, but for the Lord, and with you are matters of judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now let the fear of the Lord be upon you, and be wary, and do [your duty]: for there is no unrighteousness with the Lord our God, neither [is it for him] to respect persons, nor take bribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Moreover Josaphat appointed in Jerusalem some of the priests, and Levites, and heads of houses of Israel, for the judgment of the Lord, and to judge the dwellers in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he charged them, saying, Thus shall you⌃ do in the fear of the Lord, in truth and with a perfect heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Whatsoever man of your brethren that dwell in their cities [shall bring] the cause that comes before you, between blood [and] blood, and between precept and commandment, and ordinances and judgments, you⌃ shall even decide for them; so they shall not sin against the Lord, and there shall not be wrath upon you, and upon your brethren: thus you⌃ shall do, and you⌃ shall not sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And, behold, Amarias the priest is head over you in every matter of the Lord; and Zabdias the son of Ismael is head over the house of Juda in every matter of the king; and the scribes and Levites are before you: be strong and active, and the Lord shall be with the good.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 20}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after this came the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them [some] of the Minaeans, against Josaphat to battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they came and told Josaphat, saying, There is come against you a great multitude from Syria, from beyond the sea; and, behold, they are in Asasan Thamar, this is Engadi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Josaphat was alarmed, and set his face to seek the Lord earnestly, and he proclaimed a fast in all Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Juda gathered themselves together to seek after the Lord: even from all the cities of Juda they came to seek the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Josaphat stood up in the assembly of Juda in Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, in front of the new court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said, O Lord God of my fathers, are not you God in heaven above, and are not you Lord of all the kingdoms of the nations? and [is there] not in your hand the might of dominion, and there is no one who can resist you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Are not you the Lord that did destroy the inhabitants of this land before the face of your people Israel, and did give it to your beloved seed of Abraham for ever? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they lived in it, and built in it a sanctuary to your name, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If there should come upon us evils, sword, judgment, pestilence, famine, we will stand before this house, and before you, (for your name [is] upon this house,) and we will cry to you because of the affliction, and you shall hear, and deliver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now, behold, the children of Ammon, and Moab, and mount Seir, with regard to whom you did not permit Israel to pass through their border, when they had come out of the land of Egypt, (for they turned away from them, and did not destroy them;)— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} yet now, behold, they make attempts against us, to come forth to cast us out from our inheritance which you gave us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O Lord our God, will you not judge them? for we have no strength to resist this great multitude that is come against us; and we know not what we shall do to them: but our eyes are toward you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And all Juda was standing before the Lord, and their children, and their wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Oziel the [son] of Zacharias, of the children of Banaias, of the sons of Eleiel, the sons of Matthanias the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, —upon him came the Spirit of the Lord in the assembly: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and he said, Hear you⌃, all Juda, and the dwellers in Jerusalem, and king Josaphat: Thus says the Lord to you, even you, Fear not, neither be alarmed, before all this great multitude; for the battle is not years, but God's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To-morrow go you⌃ down against them: behold, they come up by the ascent of Assis, and you⌃ shall find them at the extremity of the river of the wilderness of Jeriel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} It is not for you to fight: understand these things, and see the deliverance of the Lord with you, Juda and Jerusalem: fear not, neither be afraid to go forth to-morrow to meet them; and the Lord shall be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Josaphat bowed with his face [to the ground] with all Juda and the dwellers in Jerusalem, [and] they fell before the Lord to worship the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the Levites of the children of Caath, and [they] of the sons of Core, rose up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Thecoe: and as they went out, Josaphat stood and cried, and said, Hear me, Juda, and the dwellers in Jerusalem; put your trust in the Lord God, and your trust shall be honored; trust in his prophet, and you⌃ shall prosper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he took counsel with the people, and set appointed men to sing psalms and praises, to give thanks, and sing the holy songs of praise in going forth before the host: and they said, Give thanks to the Lord, for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And when they began the praise and thanksgiving, the Lord caused the children of Ammon to fight against Moab, and [the inhabitants of] mount Seir that came out against Juda; and they were routed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Then the children of Ammon and Moab rose up against the dwellers in mount Seir, to destroy and consume them; and when they had made an end of [destroying] the inhabitants of Seir, they rose up against one another so that they were utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Juda came to the watch-tower of the wilderness, and looked, and saw the multitude, and, behold, [they were] all fallen dead upon the earth, not one escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Josaphat and his people went out to spoil them, and they found much cattle, and furniture, and spoils, and precious things: and they spoiled them, and they were three days gathering the spoil, for it was abundant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it came to pass on the fourth day they were gathered to the Valley of Blessing; for there they blessed the Lord: therefore they called the name of the place the Valley of Blessing, until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And all the men of Juda returned to Jerusalem, and Josaphat led them with great joy; for the Lord gave them joy over their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they entered into Jerusalem with lutes and harps and trumpets, [going] into the house of the lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And there was a terror of the Lord upon all the kingdoms of the land, when they heard that the Lord fought against the enemies of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the kingdom of Josaphat was at peace; and his God gave him rest round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Josaphat reigned over Juda, being thirty-five years [old] when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Azuba, daughter of Sali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he walked in the ways of his father Asa, and turned not aside from doing that which was right in the sight of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} nevertheless the high places yet remained; and as yet the people did not direct their heart to the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And the rest of the acts of Josaphat, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the history of Jeu [the son] of Anani, who wrote the book of the kings of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And afterwards Josaphat king of Juda entered into an alliance with Ochozias king of Israel, (now this was an unrighteous man,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} by acting [with] and going to him, to build ships to go to Tharsis: and he built ships in Gasion Gaber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Eliezer you [son] of Dodia of Marisa prophesied against Josaphat, saying, Forasmuch as you have allied yourself with Ochozias, the Lord has broken your work, and your vessels have been wrecked. And they could not go to Tharsis.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 21}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Joran his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he had brothers, the six sons of Josaphat, Azarias, and Jeiel, and Zacharias, and Azarias, and Michael, and Zaphatias: all these [were] the sons of Josaphat king of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And their father gave them many gifts, silver, and gold, and arms, together with fortified cities in Juda: but he gave the kingdom to Joram, for he [was] the firstborn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Joram entered upon his kingdom, and strengthened himself, and killed all his brothers with the sword, and [some] of the princes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When he was thirty and two years old, Joram succeeded to his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Achaab; for a daughter of Achaab was his wife: and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} nevertheless the Lord would not utterly destroy the house of David, because of the covenant which he made with David, and as he said to him that he would give a light to him and his sons for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In those days Edom revolted from Juda, and they made a king over themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joram went with the princes, and all the cavalry with him: and it came to pass that he arose by night, and struck Edom that compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots, and the people fled to their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Edom revolted from Juda until this day. Then Lomna at that time revolted from [under] his hand, because he forsook the Lord God of his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For he built high places in the cities of Juda, and caused the dwellers in Jerusalem to go a-whoring, and led Juda astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And there came to him [a message] in writing from Eliu the prophet, saying, Thus says the Lord God of your father David, Because you have not walked in the way of your father Josaphat, nor in the ways of Asa king of Juda, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} but have walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and have caused Juda and the dwellers in Jerusalem to go a-whoring, as the house of Achaab caused [Israel] to go a-whoring, and you have slain your brethren, the sons of your father, who were better than yourself; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} behold, the Lord shall strike you with a great plague among your people, and your sons, and your wives, and all your store: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and you [shall be afflicted] with a grievous disease, with a disease of the bowels, until your bowels shall fall out day by day with the sickness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So the Lord stirred up the Philistines against Joram, and the Arabians, and those who bordered on the Aethiopians: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and they went up against Juda, and prevailed against them, and took away all the store which they found in the house of the king, and his sons, and his daughters; and there was no son left to him but Ochozias the youngest of his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And after all these things the Lord struck him in the bowels with an incurable disease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it continued from day to day: and when the time of the days came [to] two years, his bowels fell out with the disease, and he died by a grievous distemper: and his people performed no funeral, like the funeral of his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he departed without honor, and was buried in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3115, bc 889 Jehoshaphat was buried, Jehoram reigned "Alone." \textsuperscript{2} Israel Jehoshaphat was certainly not king of Israel, but of Judah: Yisrael must therefore be a mistake for Yehoodah; which is the reading of thirty-eight of Dr. Kennicott's and De Rossi's manuscripts, and of the Syriac, Arabic, Septuagint, and Vulgate. \textsuperscript{3} gave them; the kingdom He associated him with himself in the kingdom about three years before his death, and in the fifth year of Joram king of Israel; so that Jehoram reigned three years with his father, and five years alone, in all eight years. Jehoram "Jehoram made partner of the kingdom with his father, ." \textsuperscript{5} am 3112-3119, bc 892-885 Jehoram "In consort, ." \textsuperscript{6} in the way he had \textsuperscript{7} Howbeit; because; as he promised; , 18-135:21; light Heb. lamp, or candle \textsuperscript{8} am 3115, bc 889 the Edomites; dominion Heb. hand and made \textsuperscript{12} am 3116, bc 888 a writing "Which was writ before his assumption."; Elijah the prophet If the account of the translation of Elijah be given in the order in which it happened, then it occurred in the reign of Jehoshaphat, the father of Jehoram. Hence, it is probable that he wrote it before his assumption, and left it to be delivered by Elisha or one of the prophets. in the ways of Jehoshaphat; in the ways of Asa \textsuperscript{13} in the way, a whoring; hast slain \textsuperscript{14} plague Heb. stroke, thy people Many of the people had concurred in Jehoram's idolatry, and some of them must have been instruments in his base, unnatural murders; they were therefore joined in his punishment, and he suffered by the loss of his subjects.; thy children \textsuperscript{15} by disease This is supposed to have been a violent dysentery, a disease which is often attended with symptoms similar to those described in the text; by the same death perished Antiochus Ephiphenes, and Herod Agrippa.; thy bowels fall; the sickness \textsuperscript{16} am 3117, bc 887 the Lord; Philistines \textsuperscript{17} carried away Heb. carried captive, his sons also, Jehoahaz, Ahaziah, Azariah \textsuperscript{18} am 3117-3119, bc 887-885 And after all "His son Ahaziah Prorex, soon after." an incurable disease \textsuperscript{20} am 3119, bc 885 Thirty and two without being desired Heb. without desire, That is, without being regretted. No one wished him to live any longer. He was hated while he lived, and neglected when he died.\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 22}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ochozias his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of robbers that came against them, even the Arabians and the Alimazonians, had slain all the elder ones. So Ochozias son of Joram king of Juda reigned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Ochozias began to reign when he was twenty years old, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Gotholia, the daughter of Ambri. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he walked in the way of the house of Achaab; for his mother was his counsellor to do evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord as the house of Achaab [had done]: for they were his counselors after the death of his father to his destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he walked in their counsels, and he went with Joram son of Achaab king of Israel to war against Azael king of Syria to Ramoth Galaad: and the archers struck Joram. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joram returned to Jezrael to be healed of the wounds wherewith the Syrians struck him in Ramoth, when he fought against Azael king of Syria. And Ochozias son of Joram, king of Juda, went down to see Joram the son of Achaab at Jezrael because he was sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And destruction from God came upon Ochozias in [his] coming to Joram; for when he had come, Joram went out with him against Jeu the son of Namessei, the anointed of the Lord against the house of Achaab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass, when Jeu was taking vengeance on the house of Achaab, that he found the princes of Juda and the brethren of Ochozias ministering to Ochozias, and he killed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he gave orders to seek Ochozias: and they took him while he was healing his wounds in Samaria, and they brought him to Jeu, and he killed him; and they buried him, for they said, He is the son of Josaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So there was none in the house of Ochozias to secure their power in the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Gotholia the mother of Ochozias saw that her son was dead, and she arose and destroyed all the seed royal in the house of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But Josabeeth, the daughter of the king, took Joas the son of Ochozias and rescued him secretly out of the midst of the sons of the king that were put to death, and she placed him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Josabeeth daughter of king Joram, sister of Ochozias, wife of Jodae the priest, hid him, and she [even] hid him from Gotholia, and she did not kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he was with him hid in the house of God six years; and Gotholia reigned over the land.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the inhabitants, Ahaziah, Azariah, Jehoahaz; slain \textsuperscript{2} am 3119, 3120, bc 885, 884 Forty and two In the parallel passage (see note on ) he is said to be only twenty-two; and this is doubtless the true reading, as it is supported here by several manuscripts and versions. Athaliah \textsuperscript{5} He walked; went with, 29-9:13 Ramothgilead \textsuperscript{6} And he returned which were given him Heb. wherewith they wounded him, Azariah. Ahaziah, ΰηζιδε, and Jehoahaz, ιδεΰηζ, are essentially the same both in letters and sense, the word ιδε, yeho, or ιδ, yah, being merely transposed, but Azariah, ςζψιδε, seems to have been a distinct name by which he was known., Ahaziah, Jehoahaz to see Jehoram \textsuperscript{7} destruction Heb. treading down, was of God; he went out the Lord had \textsuperscript{9} he sought Ahaziah The account in the parallel passage is somewhat different. "The current of the story at large is this, " says Dr. Lightfoot: "Jehu slayeth Joram in the field of Jezreel, as Ahaziah and Joram were together: Ahaziah seeing this, flies, and gets into Samaria, and hides himself there. Jehu marches to Jezreel, and makes Jezebel dogs' meat. From thence sends to Samaria for the heads of Ahab's children and posterity; which are brought him by night, and shewed to the people in the morning. Then he marches to Samaria, and, by the way, slayeth forty-two of Ahab's kinsmen, and findeth Jehonadab, the father of the Rechabites. Coming into Samaria, he maketh search for Ahaziah. They find him hid, bring him to Jehu, and he commands to carry him towards Gur, by Ibleam, and there to slay him. They do so. Smite him in his chariot, and his charioteer driveth away to Megiddo before he dies." \subsection*{Chronicles II 23}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in the eighth year Jodae strengthened [himself], and took the captains of hundreds, Azarias the son of Joram, and Ismael the son of Joanan, and Azarias the son of Obed, and Maasaeas the son of Adia, and Elisaphan the son of Zacharias, with him to the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they went round about Juda, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Juda, and heads of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and all the congregation of Juda made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he showed them the king's son, and said to them, Behold, let the king's son reign, as the Lord said concerning the house of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now this [is] the thing which you⌃ shall do. Let a third part of you, [even] of the priests and of the Levites, enter in on the sabbath, even into the gates of the entrances; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and let a third part be in the house of the king; and another third at the middle gate: and all the people in the courts of the Lord's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And let not [any one] enter into the house of the Lord, except the priests and the Levites, and the servants of the Levites; they shall enter in, because they are holy: and let all the people keep the watch of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man's weapon in his hand; and whoever [else] goes into the house shall die: but they shall be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Levites and all Juda did according to all that the priest Jodae commanded them, and they took each his men from the beginning of the sabbath to the end of the sabbath, for Jodae the priest did not dismiss the courses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Jodae gave to the men the swords, and the shields, and the arms, which [had] belonged to King David, in the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he set the whole people, every man with his arms, from the right side of the house to the left side of the altar and the house, over against the king round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he brought out the king's son, and put on him the crown and the testimony, and Jodae the priest and his sons proclaimed him king, and anointed him, and said, Long live the king! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Gotholia heard the sound of the people running, and acknowledging and praising the king: and she went in to the king into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And she looked, and, behold, the king [stood] in his place, and the princes and trumpets were at the entrance, and the princes were round the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded the trumpets, and there were the singers singing with instruments, and singing hymns of praise. and Gotholia tore her robe, and cried, you⌃ surely are plotting against [me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jodae the priest went forth, and Jodae the priest charged the captains of hundreds, even the captains of the host, and said to them, Thrust her forth outside the house, and follow her, and let her be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So they let her go [out]; and she went through the horsemen's gate of the house of the king, and they killed her there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jodae made a covenant between himself, and the people, and the king, that the people should be the Lord's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and tore down it and its altars, and they ground his images to powder, and they killed Matthan the priest of Baal before his altars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jodae the priest committed the works of the house of the Lord into the and of the priests and Levites, and he re-established the courses of the priests and Levites which David appointed over the house of the Lord, and [he appointed them] to offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with gladness, and with songs by the hand of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the porters stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, that no one unclean in any respect should enter in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he took the heads of families, and the mighty men, and the chiefs of the people, and all the people of the land, and they conducted the king into the house of the Lord; and he went through the inner gate into the king's house, and they seated the king on the throne of the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all the people of the land rejoiced; and the city was quiet: and they killed Gotholia.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} seventh year covenant with him \textsuperscript{2} went about; the chief of Houbigant omits the words of Israel. Bp. Patrick, however, is of the opinion that Judah is here called by the general name of Israel, but it is probable, that these "chief fathers of Israel, " were the descendants of those priests and Levites, and other pious persons of the ten tribes, who left their cities and possessions, and joined themselves to Judah, in the days of Jeroboam. See the parallel passages. \textsuperscript{3} made a covenant; as the Lord \textsuperscript{4} entering; porters doors Heb. thresholds \textsuperscript{5} the king's house; the gate \textsuperscript{8} the Levites the courses 1Chr. 24:1-26:32 \textsuperscript{9} spears; which were in the house When the soldier retired from the tumults of war to the bosom of his family, he frequently hung up his arms in the temple, as a grateful acknowledgment of the protection he had received, and of the victories he had won. It is highly probable, therefore, that the arms of David which Jehoiada delivered to the captains of hundreds, "which were in the house of God, " were laid up in the tabernacle by David when he resigned the command of his armies to his generals; and there is reason to believe that his conduct, in this respect, was followed by many of his companions in arms. \textsuperscript{10} side of the temple Heb. shoulder of the house, along by \textsuperscript{11} They brought; put upon; the testimony; , anointed him; God save the king Heb. \subsection*{Chronicles II 24}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Joas was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Sabia of Bersabee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Joas did that which right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jodae the priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jodae took to himself two wives, and they bore sons and daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass afterward that it came into the heart of Joas to repair the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he gathered the priests and the Levites, and said to them, Go out into the cities of Juda, and collect money of all Israel to repair the house of the Lord from year to year, and make haste to speak [of it]. But the Levites hasted not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And king Joas called Jodae the chief, and said to him, Why have you not looked after the Levites, so that they should bring from Juda and Jerusalem that which was prescribed by Moses the man of God, when he assembled Israel at the tabernacle of witness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For Gotholia was a transgressor, and her sons tore down the house of God; for they offered the holy things of the house of the Lord to Baalim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king said, Let a box be made, and let it be put at the gate of the house of the Lord without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let [men] proclaim in Juda an in Jerusalem, that [the people] should bring to the Lord, as Moses the servant of God spoke concerning Israel in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all the princes and all the people gave, and brought in, and cast into the box until it was filled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when they brought in the box to the officers of the king by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that the money was more than sufficient, then came the king's scribe, and the officer of the high priest, and emptied the box, and restored it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and collected much money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king and Jodae the priest gave it to the workmen employed in the service of the house of the Lord, and they hired masons and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord, also smiths and braziers to repair the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the workmen wrought, and the works prospered in their hands, and they established the house of the Lord on its foundation, and strengthened [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when they had finished [it], they brought to the king and to Jodae the remainder of the money, and they made vessels for the house of the Lord, vessels of service for whole burnt offerings, and gold and silver [censers]: and they offered up whole burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jodae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jodae grew old, being full of days, and he died, being one hundred and thirty years old at his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they buried him with the kings in the city of David, because he had dealt well with Israel, and with God and his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass after the death of Jodae, [that] the princes of Juda went in, and did obeisance to the king. Then the king listened to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they forsook the house of the Lord God of their fathers, and served the Astartes and idols: and there was wrath upon Juda and Jerusalem in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} yet he sent prophets to them, to turn them to the Lord; but they listened not: and he testified to them, but they obeyed not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Spirit of God came upon Azarias the son of Jodae the priest, and he stood up above the people, and said, Thus says the Lord, Why do you⌃ transgress the commandments of the Lord? so shall you⌃ not prosper; for you⌃ have forsaken the Lord, and he will forsake you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they conspired against him, and stone him by command of king Joas in the court of the Lord's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So Joas remembered not the kindness which his father Jodae had exercised towards him, but killed his son. And as he died, he said, The Lord look upon [it], and judge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass after the end of the year, [that] the host of Syria went up against him, and came against Juda and Jerusalem: and they killed all the chiefs of the people among the people, and all their spoils they sent to the king of Damascus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For the army of Syria came with few men, yet God gave into their hands a very large army, because they had forsaken the God of their fathers; and he brought judgments on Joas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And after they had departed from him, when they had left him in sore diseases, then his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the son of Jodae the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died, and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchre of the kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And they that conspired against him were Zabed the son of Samaath the Ammanite, and Jozabed the son of Samareth the Moabite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And all his sons, and the five came to him: and the other [matters], behold, they are written in the book of the kings. And Amasias his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3126-3165, bc 878-839 Joash, ιεΰωΡ, or ιΰωΡ, is merely an abbreviation of Jehoash, ιδεΰωΡ, by the elision of δ, hay, and here also of ε, wav ., Jehoash, seven years old As Joash was hidden six years in the temple, and was but seven when he came to the throne, he could have been but one year old when secreted by his aunt. \textsuperscript{2} am 3126-3162, bc 878-842 Joash; all the days of Jehoiada \textsuperscript{3} took for him Not for himself, as the Jewish expositors suppose, but for Joash; for Jehoiada's advanced age renders it highly improbable that he should take them for himself. The event soon verified this prediction; for, before the year was expired, the Syrians came up against Jerusalem, and destroyed all the princes of the people, and Joash himself was slain in his bed by his own servants. Many circumstances served to aggravate this barbarous act. Zechariah was a high-priest and a prophet, upright and unblameable in the discharge of his high offices; this murder was perpetrated within the very precincts of the courts of the Lord; and this truly good man was by blood the nearest relative of Joash, and the son of the man who had save him from being murdered, and raised him to the throne!; and require it \textsuperscript{23} am 3165, bc 839 at the end Heb. in the revolution, the host; princes;, Damascus Heb. \subsection*{Chronicles II 25}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Amasias began to reign when he was twenty and five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name [was] Joadaen of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass, when the kingdom was established in his hand, that he killed his servants who had slain the king his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But he killed not their sons, according to the covenant of the law of the Lord, as it is written, [and] as the Lord commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, and the sons shall not die for the fathers, but they shall die each for his own sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Amasias assembled the house of Juda, and appointed them according to the houses of their families for captains of thousands and captains of hundreds in all Juda and Jerusalem: and he numbered them from twenty years old and upwards, and found them three hundred thousand able to go out to war, holding spear and shield. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Also he hired of Israel one hundred thousand mighty [men for] one hundred talents of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the host of Israel go with you; for the Lord is not with Israel, [even] all the sons of Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For if you shall undertake to strengthen [yourself] with these, then the lord shall put you to flight before the enemies: for it is of the Lord both to strengthen and to put to flight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Amasias said to the man of God, But what shall I do [for] the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel? And the man of God said, The Lord can give you much more than these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Amasias separated from the army that came to him from Ephraim, that they might go away to their place; and they were very angry with Juda, and they returned to their place with great wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Amasias strengthened [himself], and took his people, and went to the valley of salt, and struck there the children of Seir ten thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the children of Juda took ten thousand prisoners, and they carried them to the top of the precipice, and cast them headlong from the top of the precipice, and they were all dashed to pieces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the men of the host whom Amasias sent back so that they should not go with him to battle, [went] and attacked the cities of Juda, from Samaria to Baethoron; and they struck three thousand among them, and took much spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And it came to pass, after Amasias had returned from striking Idumea, that he brought home the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up for himself as gods, and bowed down before them, and he sacrificed to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the anger of the Lord came upon Amasias, and he sent him a prophet, and he said to him, Why have you sought the gods of the people, which have not rescued their own people out of your hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass when the prophet was speaking to him, that he said to him, have I made you king's counsellor? take heed lest you be scourged: and the prophet forebore, and said, I know that [God] is disposed against you to destroy you, because you have done this thing, and have not listened to my counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Amasias king of Juda took counsel, and sent to Joas, son of Joachaz, son of Jeu, king of Israel, saying, Come, and let us look one another in the face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Joas king of Israel sent to Amasias king of Juda, saying, The thistle that was in Libanus sent to the cedar that was in Libanus, saying, Give your daughter to my son to wife; but, behold, your wild beasts of the field that are in Libanus shall come: and the wild beasts did come, and trod down the thistle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You have said, Behold, I have struck Idumea, and your stout heart exalts you: now stay at home; for why do you implicate yourself in mischief, that you should fall, and Juda with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Nevertheless Amasias listened not, for it was of the Lord to deliver him into [the enemy's] hands, because he sought after the gods of the Idumeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So Joas king of Israel went up; and they saw one another, he and Amasias king of Juda, in Baethsamys, which is of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Juda was put to flight before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Joas king of Israel took prisoner Amasias king of Juda, [son] of Joas, son of Joachaz, in Baethsamys, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he pulled down [part] of the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And [he took] all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord and with Abdedom, and the treasures of the king's house, and the hostages, and he returned to Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Amasias the [son] of Joas king of Juda lived after the death of Joas the [son] of Joachaz king of Israel fifteen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the rest of the acts of Amasias, the first and the last, Behold! are they not written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And at the time when Amasias departed from the Lord, then they formed a conspiracy against him; and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachis: and they sent after him to Lachis, and killed him there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they took him up on horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of David.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} am 3166, bc 838 Now it came established to him Heb. confirmed upon him he slew; No doubt those wicked men, Jozachar and Jehozabad, who murdered his father, had considerable influence; and therefore he found it dangerous to bring them to justice, till he was assured of the loyalty of his other officers: when this was clear, he called them to an account, and justly put them to death for treason and murder; for, if even these conspirators against Joash intended to avenge upon him the death of Zechariah, they acted without a commission from that God "to whom vengeance belongeth." \textsuperscript{5} am 3177, bc 827 captains over thousands; from twenty three \textsuperscript{6} an hundred talents of silver Estimating the shekel at 2s. 6d., and the talent, being 3, 000 shekels (see ), at 375£, one hundred talents would amount to 37, 500£.; which, divided among 100, 000 men, quotes only 7s. 6d.; hence we may suppose, that this was only an earnest of their pay, or that they expected to be enriched by the plunder of the Edomites. \textsuperscript{7} a man of God; for the Lord \textsuperscript{8} be strong; God hath power; army Heb. band, The Lord \textsuperscript{10} Amaziah home Heb. to their place great anger Heb. heat of anger \textsuperscript{12} And other ten thousand No intimation is given on what account, or on what provocation, this most cruel conduct towards the prisoners of war was adopted. The enmity between Israel and Edom seems to have been reciprocal and deeply malignant. The victorious king and his army considered every individual of Edom as a traitor and rebel; and so adjudged them to death, and acted on this judgment. But their conduct was wholly inexcusable, and could only perpetuate rancour to future generations, and provoke the surviving Edomites to cruel retaliations, whenever they had it in their power. cast them; broken in pieces \textsuperscript{13} soldiers of the army Heb. sons of the band, fell upon the cities These Israelites seem to have returned home, when discharged by Amaziah, whose powerful army deterred them from attempting revenge at that time; but when he was engaged in war with the Edomites, they marched from Samaria, and plundered all the cities till they came to Beth-horon, where they slew 3, 000 of the inhabitants. Samaria, Bethhoron \textsuperscript{15} a prophet, ; Why hast thou sought; the gods which could \textsuperscript{16} Art thou made, ; forbear; determined Heb. counselled \textsuperscript{17} am 3178, bc 826 Amaziah; let us see \textsuperscript{18} thistle or, furze-bush, or thorn; a wild beast Heb. a beast of the field \textsuperscript{19} heart; to boast; why shouldest \textsuperscript{20} it came of God; sought \textsuperscript{21} they saw one another That is, "they fought against each other." To face an enemy, or to face one another, is still a common expression. The reason of this war was evidently the injury the army of Joash had done to the unoffending inhabitants of Judah. The ravages committed by them were totally unprovoked, base, and cowardly: they fell upon women, old men, and children, and butchered them in cold blood, when all the effective men were gone with their king against the Edomites. The quarrel of Amaziah were certainly just, yet he was put to the rout. He fell, and Judah with him, as Joash had said; and the reason was, because "it came of God, that he might deliver them into the hands of their enemies, because they sought after the gods of Edom." This was the reason why the Israelites triumphed. Bethshemesh \textsuperscript{22} put to the worse Heb. smitten, fled \textsuperscript{23} took Amaziah, ; Jehoahaz, Ahaziah, Azariah gate of Ephraim, corner gate Heb. the gate of it that looketh \textsuperscript{24} all the gold; the hostages also It is probable that these hostages were given in order that Amaziah might regain his liberty. \textsuperscript{27} am 3194, bc 810 after the time following Heb. after made Heb. conspired; Lachish \textsuperscript{28} the city of Judah that is, the city of David, as it is\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 26}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then all the people of the land took Ozias, and he was sixteen years old, and they made him king in the room of his father Amasias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He built Aelath, he recovered it to Juda, after the king slept with his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Ozias began to reign at the age of sixteen years, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Jechelia of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Amasias his father did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he sought the Lord in the days of Zacharias, who understood the fear of the Lord; and in his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord prospered him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he went out and fought against the Philistines, and pulled down the walls of Geth, and the walls of Jabner, and the walls of Azotus, and he built cities [near] Azotus, and among the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord strengthened him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that lived on the rock, and against the Minaeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Minaeans gave gifts to Ozias; and his fame spread as far as the entering in of Egypt, for he strengthened [himself] exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Ozias built towers in Jerusalem, both at the gate of the corners, and at the valley gate, and at the corners and he fortified them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he built towers in the wilderness, and dug many wells, for he had many cattle in the low country and in the plain; and vinedressers in the mountain country and in Carmel: for he was a husbandman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Ozias had a host of warriors, and that went out orderly to war, and returned orderly in number; and their number was [made] by the hand of Jeiel the scribe, and Maasias the judge, by the hand of Ananias the king's deputy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The whole number of the chiefs of families of the mighty men of war [was] two thousand six hundred; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and with them was a warrior force, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred: these waged war mightily to help the king against [his] enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Ozias prepared for them, [even] for all the host, shields, and spears, and helmets, and breastplates, and bows, and slings for stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he made in Jerusalem machines invented by a wise contriver, to be upon the towers and upon the corners, to cast darts and great stones: and [the fame] of their preparation was heard at a distance; for he was wonderfully helped, till he was strong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction; and he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to turn incense on the altar of incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And there went in after him Azarias the priest, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they withstood Ozias the king, and said to him, [It is] not for you, Ozias, to burn incense to the Lord, but only for the priests the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to sacrifice: go forth of the sanctuary, for you have departed from the Lord; and this shall not be for glory to you from the Lord god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Ozias was angry, and in his hand [was] the censer to burn incense in the temple: and when he was angry with the priests, then the leprosy rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, over the altar of incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Azarias the chief priest, and the [other] priests, turned [to look] at him, and, behold, he [was] leprous in his forehead; and they got him hastily out thence, for he also hasted to go out, because the Lord had rebuked him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Ozias the king was a leper to the day of his death, and he lived [as] a leper in a separate house; for he was cut off from the house of the Lord: and Joathan his son [was set] over his kingdom, judging the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the rest of the acts of Ozias, the first and the last, [are] written by Jessias the prophet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Ozias slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial [place] of the kings, for they said, He is a leper; and Joatham his son reigned in his stead.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 27}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Joatham [was] twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Jerusa, daughter of Sadoc. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Ozias did: but he went not into the temple of the Lord. And still the people corrupted themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and he built much in the wall of Opel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In the mountain of Juda, and in the woods, [he built] both dwelling-places and towers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He fought against the king of the children of Ammon, and prevailed against him: and the children of Ammon gave him even annually one hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. These the king of the children of Ammon brought to him annually in the first and second and third years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Joatham grew strong, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the rest of the acts of Joatham, and his war, and his deeds, behold, [they are] written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joatham slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Achaz his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3246-3262, bc 753-742 twenty and five; Joatham \textsuperscript{2} And he did; he entered not He copied his father's conduct as far as it was pious and constitutional; and avoided his transgression.; the people \textsuperscript{3} high gate; Ophel or, the tower, "The wall, " says the Targum, "of the interior palace." Ophel appears to have been a tower, or fort, on the city wall, in which we read "the Nehthinim dwelt." \textsuperscript{4} he built cities, the mountains; castles and towers These castles and towers he doubtless built for the protection of the country people against marauders. \textsuperscript{5} the king of the Ammonites We find here, that he brought the Ammonites under a heavy tribute for three years; but whether this was the effect of his prevailing against them, is not so evident. Some think that they paid this tribute for three years, and then revolted; that, in consequence, he attacked them, and their utter subjection was the result.; ten thousand Rather, "ten thousand cors ( korim ) of wheat." The cor was same as the homer, and contained about 32 pecks 1 pint. So much Heb. This \textsuperscript{7} Now the rest, am 3262, bc 742 they are written There is not so much found in the book of Kings, which we have now, as here. In both places we have abridged accounts; the larger histories having been lost.\par}
