\subsection*{Chronicles II 28}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Achaz was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: and he did not that which was right in the sight of the Lord, as David his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, for he made graven images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And [he sacrificed] to their idols in the valley of Benennom, and passed his children through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he burnt incense upon the high places, and upon the roofs, and under every shady tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria; and he struck him, and took captive of them a great band of prisoners, and carried him to Damascus. Also [God] delivered him into the hands of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Phakee the son of Romelias king of Israel, killed in Juda in one day one hundred and twenty thousand mighty men; because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Zechri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maasias the king's son, and Ezrican the chief of his house, and Elcana the king's deputy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the children of Israel took captive of their brethren three hundred thousand, women, and sons, and daughters, and they spoiled them of much property, and brought the spoils to Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there was there a prophet of the Lord, his name [was] Oded: and he went out to meet the host that were coming to Samaria, and said to them, Behold, the wrath of the Lord God of your fathers [is] upon Juda, and he has delivered them into your hands, and you⌃ have slain them in wrath, and it has reached even to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now you⌃ talk of keeping the children of Juda and Jerusalem for servants and handmaidens. Behold, am I not with you to testify for the Lord your God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now listen to me, and restore the prisoners of your brethren whom you⌃ have taken: for the fierce anger of the Lord [is] upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the chiefs of the sons of Ephraim rose up, Udias the son of Joanas, and Barachias the son of Mosolamoth, and Ezekias the son of Sellem, and Amasias the son of Eldai, against those that came from the war, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and said to them, You⌃ shall not bring in hither the prisoners to us, for whereas sin against the Lord [is] upon us, you⌃ mean to add to our sins, and to our trespass: for our sin [is] great, and the fierce anger of the Lord [is] upon Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So the warriors left the prisoners and the spoils before the princes and all the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the men who were called by name rose up, and took hold of the prisoners, and clothed all the naked from the spoils, and gave them garments and shoes, and gave them [food] to eat, and [oil] to anoint themselves [with], and they helped also every one that was weak with asses, and placed them in Jericho, the city of palm-trees, with their brethren; and they returned to Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} At that time king Achaz sent to the king of Assyria to help him, and on this occasion, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} because the Idumeans had attacked [him], and struck Juda, and taken a number of prisoners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Also the Philistines had made an attack on the cities of the plain country, and the cities of the south of Juda, and taken Baethsamys, and [the things in the house of the Lord, and the things in the house of the king, and of the princes: and they gave to the king] Aelon, and Galero, and Socho and her villages, and Thamna and her villages, and Gamzo and her villages: and they lived there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the Lord humbled Juda because of Achaz king of Juda, because he grievously departed from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And there came against him Thalgaphellasar king of Assyria, and he afflicted him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Achaz took the things [that were] in the house of the Lord, and the things in the house of the king, and of the princes, and gave them to the king of Assyria: but he was no help to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} but only [troubled him] in his affliction: and he departed yet more from the Lord, and king Achaz said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} I will seek after the gods of Damascus that strike me. And he said, Forasmuch as the gods of the king of Syria themselves strengthen them, therefore will I sacrifice to them, and they will help me. But they became a stumbling block to him, and to all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Achaz removed the vessels of the house of the Lord, and cut them in pieces, and shut the doors of the house of the Lord, and made to himself altars in every corner in Jerusalem: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and in each several city in Juda he made high places to burn incense to strange gods: and they provoked the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the rest of his acts, and his deeds, the first and the last, behold, [they are] written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Achaz slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; for they did not bring him into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel: and Ezekias his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3262-3278, bc 742-726 Ahaz; like David his father \textsuperscript{2} For he walked; molten images; Baalim \textsuperscript{3} burnt incense or, offered sacrifice the valley;, burnt; after the abominations \textsuperscript{5} his God; delivered him, ; Damascus Heb. Darmesek \textsuperscript{6} Pekah;, an hundred valiant men Heb. sons of valour because \textsuperscript{7} next to the king Heb. the second to the king \textsuperscript{9} he went out; Behold To this beautiful speech nothing can be added by the best comment. It is simple, humane, pious, and overwhelmingly convincing; and it is no wonder that it produced the effect here described. That there was much humanity, as well as firmness, in the heads of the children of Ephraim, who joined with the prophet of Jehovah on this occasion, their subsequent conduct, as detailed in the, sufficiently proves. They did not barely dismiss these most unfortunate captives, but they took that very spoil which their victorious army had taken, and with clothed, shod, fed, and anointed these distressed people, set the feeblest of them upon asses, and escorted them safely to Jericho! We can scarcely find a parallel to this in the universal history of the wars which savage man has carried on against his fellows from the foundation of the world. The compliance also of the whole army, in leaving both the captives and spoil to the disposal of the princes, was really wonderful, and perhaps unparalleled in history. Both the princes and army are worthy to be held up to the admiration and imitation of mankind. because the Lord God; reacheth \textsuperscript{10} keep not with; the Lord \textsuperscript{15} expressed by name clothed; gave them; carried the city \textsuperscript{16} did king; the kings Instead of malchey, "kings, " the Chaldee, Syriac, Arabic, and Vulgate, one manuscript, and the parallel place, have mailech, "king." \textsuperscript{17} the Edomites; captives Heb. a captivity \textsuperscript{18} Philistines, Bethshemesh; Ajalon, Aijalon Gederoth Shocho, Socoh Timnah, Timnath \textsuperscript{19} the Lord; because of Ahaz; Israel made Judah \textsuperscript{20} am 3264, bc 740 Tilgathpilneser, Tiglath-pileser; distressed him \textsuperscript{23} For he sacrificed This passage, says Mr. Hallet, greatly surprised me; for the sacred historian is here represented as saying, "The gods of Damascus had smitten Ahaz." But it is impossible to suppose that an inspired author should say this; for the Scripture every where represents the heathen idols as nothing and vanity, and as incapable of doing either good or hurt. All difficulty is avoided if we follow the old Hebrew copies, from which the Greek translation was made: "And king Ahaz said, I will seek to the gods of Damascus which have smitten me."; Damascus Heb. Darmesek Because the gods sacrifice to them, But they were \textsuperscript{24} cut in pieces, shut up, he made \textsuperscript{27} am 3278, bc 726 they brought, ; the kings of Israel Or, "the kings of Judah; " the name Israel being sometimes applied by the writer of this book, in a general way, to Judah. The Hebrews were accustomed to honour the memory of those kings who had reigned well, by depositing their remains in the royal cemetery. On the contrary, those who died under the disapprobation of the people, as a mark of posthumous disgrace, were denied interment with their predecessors, and were buried in some other place in Jerusalem. So it was with Ahaz, who, though brought into the city, was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings of Judah. It was doubtless with a design to make a suitable impression on the minds of their kings while living, that such distinctions were observed. They might thus restrain them from evil, or excite them to good, according as they were fearful of being execrated, or desirous of being honoured, when dead.\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 29}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Ezekias began to reign at the age of twenty-five years, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Abia, daughter of Zacharias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father David had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass, when he was established over his kingdom, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and put them on the east side, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and said to them, Hear, you⌃ Levites: now sanctify yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and cast out the impurity from the holy places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For our fathers have revolted, and done that which was evil before the Lord our God, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their face from the tabernacle of the Lord, and have turned [their] back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they have shut up the doors of the temple, and put out the lamps, and have not burnt incense, and have not offered whole burnt offerings in the holy [place] to the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord was very angry with Juda and Jerusalem, and made them an astonishment, and a desolation, and a hissing, as you⌃ see with your eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And, behold, your fathers have been struck with the sword, and your sons and your daughters and your wives are in captivity in a land not their own, as it is even now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore it is now in my heart to make a covenant, a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, that he may turn away his fierce wrath from us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now be not lacking [to your duty], for the Lord has chosen you to stand before him to minister, and to be ministers and burners of incense to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then the Levites rose up, Maath the son of Amasi, and Joel the son of Azarias, of the sons of Caath: and of the sons of Merari, Kis the son of Abdi, and Azarias the son of Haelel: and of the sons of Gedsoni, Jodaad the son of Zemmath, and Joadam: these [were] the sons of Joacha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And of the sons of Elisaphan; Zambri, and Jeiel: and of the sons of Asaph; Zacharias, and Matthanias: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and of the sons of Aeman; Jeiel, and Semei: and of the sons of Idithun; Samaisa, and Oziel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they gathered their brethren, and they purified themselves according to the king's command by the order of the Lord, to purify the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the priests entered into the house of the Lord, to purify [it], and they cast out all the uncleanness that was found in the house of the Lord, even into the court of the house of the Lord: and the Levites received [it] to cast into the brook of Kedron without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And [Ezekias] began on the first day, [even] on the new moon of the first month, to purify, and on the eighth day of the month they entered into the temple of the Lord: and they purified the house of the Lord in eight days; and on the thirteenth day of the first month they finished [the work]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they went in to king Ezekias, and said, We have purified all the things in the house of the Lord, the altar of whole burnt offering, and its vessels, and the table of show-bread, and its vessels; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and all the vessels which king Achaz polluted in his reign, in his apostasy, we have prepared and purified: behold, they are before the altar of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And king Ezekias rose early in the morning, and gathered the chief men of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he brought seven calves, seven rams, seven lambs, seven kids of goats for a sin-offering, for the kingdom, and for the holy things, and for Israel: and he told the priests the sons of Aaron to go up to the altar of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they killed the calves, and the priests received the blood, and poured it on the altar: and they killed the rams, and poured the blood upon the altar: also they killed the lambs, and poured the blood round the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they brought the goats for a sin-offering before the king and the congregation; and laid their hands upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the priests killed them, and offered their blood as a propitiation on the altar; and they made atonement for all Israel: for the king said, The whole burnt offering, and the sin-offering [are] for all Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, and lutes, and harps, according to the commandment of king David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet: for by the commandment of the Lord the order [was] in the hand of the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Ezekias told [them] to offer up the whole burnt offering on the altar: and when they began to offer the whole burnt offering, they began to sing to the Lord, and the trumpets [accompanied] the instruments of David king of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And all the congregation worshipped, and the psalm-singers [were] singing, and the trumpets sounding, until the whole burnt sacrifice had been completely offered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And when they had done offering [it], the king and all that were present bowed, and worshipped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And king Ezekias and the princes told the Levites to sing hymns to the Lord in the words of David, and of Asaph the prophet: and they sang hymns with gladness, and fell down and worshipped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then Ezekias answered and said, Now you⌃ have consecrated yourselves to the Lord, bring near and offer sacrifices of praise in the house of the Lord. And the congregation brought sacrifices and thank-offerings into the house of the Lord; and every one who was ready in his heart [brought] whole burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the number of the whole burnt offerings which the congregation brought, was seventy calves, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs: all these [were] for a whole burnt offering to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the consecrated calves were six hundred, [and] the sheep three thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But the priests were few, and could not flay the whole burnt offering, so their brethren the Levites helped them, until the work was finished, and until the priests had purified themselves: for the Levites [more] zealously purified [themselves] than the priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the whole burnt offering [was] abundant, with the fat of the complete peace-offering, and the drink-offerings of the whole burnt sacrifice. So the service was established in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Ezekias and all the people rejoiced, because God has prepared the people: for the thing was done suddenly.\par

The lamps were not lighted, and incense was not burnt. There are still such neglects as these, and they are no less culpable, if the Word be not duly read and opened, answering to the lighting of the lamps, and if prayers and praises be not duly offered up, which was signified by the burning of incense. \textsuperscript{8} Wherefore, ; he hath delivered It is probable Hezekiah refers to that dreadful defeat by the Israelites, in which one hundred and twenty thousand were slain, and two hundred thousand taken prisoners. On this labour they spent eight days. Then they cleansed the interior of the temple; but, as the Levites had no right to enter the temple, the priests carried all the dirt and rubbish to the porch, whence they were collected by the Levites, carried away, and cast into the brook Kidron. In this work, eight more days were occupied; and thus the temple was purified in sixteen days. the inner part; all the uncleanness; Kidron; Cedron \textsuperscript{19} all the vessels did cast away Or, as the LXX, Vulgate, and Targum read, "did pollute, " hizneeach, he rendered them so abominable that they were rejected with abhorrence. \textsuperscript{21} they brought The law only required one bullock for the sins of the high priest, another for the sins of the people, and one he-goat for the sins of the prince, but Hezekiah offered many more, and the reason appears sufficiently evident. The law only speaks of the sins of ignorance, but here there were sins of every dye, idolatry, apostasy from the Divine worship, profanation of the temple, etc., etc. The sin offerings, we are informed, were offered, first, for the Kingdom, for the transgressions of the king and his family; secondly, for the sanctuary, which had been defiled and polluted; and for the priests, who had been profane, negligent, and unholy; and finally, for Judah, for the whole mass of the people, who had been led away into every kind of abomination by the above examples. seven, ; \subsection*{Chronicles II 30}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Ezekias sent to all Israel and Juda, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasse, that they should come into the house of the Lord to Jerusalem, to keep the passover to the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the king, and the princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, designed to keep the passover in the second month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For they could not keep it at that time, because a sufficient number of priest had not purified themselves, and the people was not gathered to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the proposal pleased the king and the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they established a decree that a proclamation should go through all Israel, from Bersabee to Dan, that they should come and keep the passover to the Lord God of Israel at Jerusalem: for the multitude had not done it lately according to the scripture. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the posts went with the letters from the king and the princes to all Israel and Juda, according to the command of the king, saying, Children of Israel, return to the Lord God of Abraam, and Isaac, and Israel, and bring back them that have escaped [even] those that were left of the hand of the king of Assyria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And be not as your fathers, and your brethren, who revolted from the Lord God of their fathers, and he gave them up to desolation, as you⌃ see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now harden not your hearts, as your fathers [did]: give glory to the Lord God, and enter into his sanctuary, which he has sanctified for ever: and serve the Lord your God, and he shall turn away [his] fierce anger from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For when you⌃ turn to the Lord, your brethren and your children shall be pitied before all that have carried them captives, and he will restore [you] to this land: for the Lord our God is merciful and pitiful, and will not turn away his face from you, if we return to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So the posts went through from city to city in mount Ephraim, and Manasse, and as far as Zabulon: and they as it were laughed them to scorn, and mocked them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the men of Aser, and [some] of Manasses and of Zabulon, were ashamed, and came to Jerusalem and Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the hand of the Lord was [present] to give them one heart to come, to do according to the commands of the king and of the princes, by the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And a great multitude were gathered to Jerusalem to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they arose, and took away the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all on which they burnt incense to false [gods] they tore down and cast into the brook Kedron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the second month: and the priests and the Levites repented, and purified [themselves], and brought whole burnt offerings into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they stood at their post, according to their ordinance, according to the commandment of Moses the man of God: and the priests received the blood from the hand of the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For a great part of the congregation was not sanctified; and the Levites were [ready] to kill the passover for every one who could not sanctify himself to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the greatest part of the people of Ephraim, and Manasse, and Issachar, and Zabulon, had not purified [themselves], but ate the passover contrary to the scripture. On this account also Ezekias prayed concerning them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The good Lord be merciful with regard to every heart that sincerely seeks the Lord God of their fathers, and [is] not [purified] according to the purification of the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the Lord listened to Ezekias, and healed the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the children of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great joy; and they continued to sing hymns to the Lord daily, and the priests and the Levites [played] on instruments to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Ezekias encouraged all the Levites, and those that had good understanding of the Lord: and they completely kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, offering peace-offerings, and confessing to the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the congregation purposed together to keep other seven days: and they kept seven days with gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For Ezekias set apart for Juda, [even] for the congregation, a thousand calves and seven thousand sheep; and the princes set apart for the people a thousand calves and ten thousand sheep: and the holy things of the priests abundantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And all the congregation, the priests and the Levites, rejoiced, and all the congregation of Juda, and they that were present of Jerusalem, and the strangers that came from the land of Israel, and the dwellers in Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And there was great joy in Jerusalem: from the days of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not such a feast in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the priests the Levites rose up and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came into his holy dwelling-place, [even] into heaven.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Israel, Ephraim, ;, to the house to keep \textsuperscript{2} the king; in the second month In Ijar, as they could not celebrate in Nisan, the 14th of which month was the proper time. \subsection*{Chronicles II 31}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when all these things were finished, all Israel that were found in the cities of Juda went out, and broke in pieces the pillars, and cut down the groves, and tore down the high places and the altars out of all Judea and Benjamin, also of Ephraim and Manasse, till they made an end: and all Israel returned, every one to his inheritance, and to their cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ezekias appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites, and the courses of each one according to his ministry, to the priests and to the Levites, for the whole burnt offering, and for the peace-offering, and to praise, and to give thanks, and to minister in the gates, [and] in the courts of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king's proportion out of his substance [was appointed] for the whole burnt offerings, the morning and the evening one, and the whole burnt offerings for the sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the feasts that were ordered in the law of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they told the people who lived in Jerusalem, to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be strong in the ministry of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And as he gave the command, Israel brought abundantly first fruits of corn, and wine, and oil, and honey, and every fruit of the field: and the children of Israel and Juda brought tithes of everything abundantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they that lived in the cities of Juda themselves also brought tithes of calves and sheep, and tithes of goats, and consecrated them to the Lord their God, and they brought them and laid them in heaps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In the third month the heaps began to be piled, and in the seventh month they were finished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Ezekias and the princes came and saw the heaps, and blessed the Lord, and his people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then Ezekias enquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Azarias the priest, the chief over the house of Sadoc, spoke to him, and said, From the time that the first fruits began to be brought into the house of the Lord, we have eaten and drunk, and left even abundantly; for the Lord has blessed his people, and we have left to this amount. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Ezekias told them yet farther to prepare chambers for the house of the Lord; and they prepared [them], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and they brought there the first fruits and the tithes faithfully: and Chonenias the Levite was superintendent over them, and Semei his brother was next. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and Jeiel, and Ozias, and Naeth, and Asael, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel, and Samachia, and Maath, and Banaias, and his sons, were appointed by Chonenias and Semei his brother, as Ezekias the king, and Azarias who was over the house of the Lord commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Core, the [son] of Jemna the Levite, the porter eastward, [was] over the gifts, to distribute the first fruits of the Lord, and the most holy things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} by the hand of Odom, and Benjamin, and Jesus, and Semei, and Amarias, and Sechonias, by the hand of the priests faithfully, to give to their brethren according to the courses, as well to great as small; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} besides the increase of males from three years old and upward, to every one entering into the house of the Lord, [a portion] according to a daily rate, for service in the daily courses of their order. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} This [is] the distribution of the priests according to the houses of their families; and the Levites in their daily courses from twenty years old and upward [were] in [their] order, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} to assign stations for all the increase of their sons and their daughters, for the whole number: for they faithfully sanctified the holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} As for the sons of Aaron that executed the priests' office, —even those from their cities the men in each several city who were named expressly, —[were appointed] to give a portion to every male among the priests, and to every one reckoned among the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Ezekias did so through all Juda, and did that which was good and right before the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And in every work which he began in service in the house of the Lord, and in the law, and in the ordinances, he sought his God with all his soul, and wrought, and prospered.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Now when all Israel; present Heb. found; brake, ; images Heb. statues, in Ephraim, ;, until etc. Heb. until to make an end \textsuperscript{2} the courses, ;, 23:1-26:32; to give thanks;, ; in the gates of the tents of the Lord Beshaarey machanoth Yehowah, "within the gates of the camps of Jehovah; " which comprehended the whole of the buildings that surrounded the temple, in which the priests and Levites were stationed, and which resembled military encampments. \textsuperscript{3} the king's;, for the morning; the burnt for the new moons; the set feasts \textsuperscript{4} the portion; that they might; the law \textsuperscript{5} as soon; came abroad Heb. brake forth, the first fruits, ;, ; honey or, dates, The word devash generally denotes the honey produced by bees; but as we have already observed (on ), the Jewish doctors are of opinion that it here signifies dates, of the fruit of the palm tree; which the Arabians call daboos, and the honey produced from them, dibs . "This liquor, " says Dr. Shaw, "which has a more luscious sweetness than honey, is of the consistence of a thin syrup, but quickly grows tart and ropy, acquiring an intoxicating quality, and giving by distillation an agreeable spirit, or araky, according to the general name of these people for all hot liquors, extracted by the alembic." Though Jehovah forbad any devash, or honey, to offered to him upon the altar, yet it appears it might be presented as first-fruits, or in the way of tithes, which were designed for the sustenance of the priests. \textsuperscript{6} the children the tithe; by heaps Heb. heaps and heaps. \textsuperscript{10} Azariah; Since; we have had; the Lord \textsuperscript{13} under Heb. at the commandment, Azariah \textsuperscript{14} the porter, the freewill; to distribute the most \textsuperscript{15} next him Heb. at his hand, *marg. \subsection*{Chronicles II 32}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after these things and this faithful dealing, came Sennacherim king of the Assyrians, and he came to Juda, and encamped against the fortified cities, and intended to take them for himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ezekias saw that Sennacherim was come, and [that] his face [was set] to fight against Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he took counsel with his elders and his mighty [men] to stop the wells of water which were without the city: and they helped him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he collected many people, and stopped the wells of water, and the river that flowed through the city, saying, Lest the king of Assyria come, and find much water, and strengthen [himself]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Ezekias strengthened [himself], and built all the wall that had been pulled down, and the towers, and another wall in front without, and fortified the strong place of the city of David, and prepared arms in abundance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he appointed captains of war over the people, and they were gathered to [meet] him to the open place of the gate of the valley, and he encouraged them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Be strong and courageous, and fear not, neither be dismayed before the King of Assyria, and before all the nation that [is] with him: for [there are] more with us than with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} With him [are] arms of flesh; but with us [is] the Lord our God to save [us], and to fight our battle. And the people were encouraged at the words of Ezekias king of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And afterward Sennacherim king of the Assyrians sent his servants to Jerusalem; and [he went] himself against Lachis, and all his army with him, and sent to Ezekias king of Juda, and to all Juda that [was] in Jerusalem, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Thus says Sennacherim king of the Assyrians, On what do you⌃ trust, that you⌃ will remain in the siege in Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Does not Ezekias deceive you, to deliver you to death and famine and thirst, saying, The Lord our God will deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Is not this Ezekias who has taken down his altars and his high places and has spoken to Juda and the dwellers in Jerusalem, saying, You⌃ shall worship before this altar and burn incense upon it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Know you⌃ not what I and my fathers have done to all the nations of the countries? Could the gods of the nations of all the earth at all rescue their people out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Who is there among all the gods of those nations whom my fathers utterly destroyed, [worthy of trust]? Could they deliver their people out of my hand, that your God should deliver you out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Now then, let not Ezekias deceive you, and let him not make you thus confident, and believe him not: for no god of any kingdom or nation is at all able to deliver his people out of my hand, or the hand of my fathers: therefore your God shall not deliver you out of my hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And his servants continued to speak against the Lord God, and against his servant Ezekias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he wrote a letter to reproach the Lord God of Israel, and spoke concerning him, saying, As the gods of the nations of the earth have not delivered their people out of my hand, so the God of Ezekias shall by no means deliver his people out of my hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language to the people of Jerusalem on the wall, [calling them] to assist them, and pull down [the walls], that they might take the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he spoke against the God of Jerusalem, even as against the gods of the nations of the earth, the works of the hands of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And king Ezekias and Esaias the prophet the son of Amos prayed concerning these things, and they cried to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord sent an angel, and he destroyed every mighty man and warrior, and leader and captain in the camp of the king of Assyria: and he returned with shame of face to his own land and came into the house of his god: and [some] of them that came out of his bowels killed him with the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So the Lord delivered Ezekias and the dwellers in Jerusalem out of the hand of Sennacherim King of Assyria, and out of the hand of all [his enemies], and gave them rest round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And many brought gifts to the Lord to Jerusalem, and presents to Ezekias king of Juda; and he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations after these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} In those days Ezekias was sick even to death, and prayed to the Lord: and he listened to him, and gave him a sign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But Ezekias did not recompense the Lord according to the return which he made him, but his heart was lifted up: and wrath came upon him, and upon Juda and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Ezekias humbled himself after the exaltation of his heart, he and the dwellers in Jerusalem; and the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Ezekias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Ezekias had wealth and very great glory: and he made for himself treasuries of gold, and silver, and precious stones, also for spices, and stores for arms, and for precious vessels; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and cities for the produce of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls and mangers for every [kind of] cattle, and folds for flocks; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and cities which he built for himself, and store of sheep and oxen in abundance, for the Lord gave him a very great store. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The same Ezekias stopped up the course of the water of Gion above, and brought the water down straight south of the city of David. And Ezekias prospered in all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Notwithstanding, in regard to the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who were sent to him to enquire of him [concerning] the prodigy which came upon the land, the Lord left him, to try him, to know what was in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the rest of the acts of Ezekias, and his kindness, behold, they are written in the prophecy of Esaias the son of Amos the prophet, and in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Ezekias slept with his fathers, and they buried him in a high place among the sepulchres of the sons of David: and all Juda and the dwellers in Jerusalem gave him glory and honor at his death. And Manasses his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} these things; king of Assyria, ; win them Heb. break them up \textsuperscript{2} he was purposed to fight Heb. his face was to war \textsuperscript{4} who stopped This was prudently done; for, without water, how could an immense army subsist in ar arid country? No doubt the Assyrian army suffered much through this; as a Christian army did, through the same cause, 1, 800 years afterwards. the brook, ran through the midst of Heb. overflowed kings The Septuagint, Syriac, and Arabic read king, in the singular number.; find \textsuperscript{5} he strengthened, ; that was broken another wall; Millo; darts or, swords, or weapons \textsuperscript{6} he set captains; in the street; comfortably to them Heb. to their heart; *marg. \textsuperscript{7} strong; be not afraid; for there \textsuperscript{8} an arm; with us; to fight; rested Heb. leaned, ; upon the words \textsuperscript{9} am 3294, bc 710 Sennacherib; Lachish, ; power Heb. dominion \textsuperscript{10} Thus saith; siege Heb. strong-hold \textsuperscript{11} to give over; The Lord our God \textsuperscript{12} Hath not; taken away This was artfully malicious. Many of the people had sacrificed to Jehovah on high places ( ); and Hezekiah had removed them, as incentives to idolatry. Hence Rabshakeh insinuates that by so doing he had offended Jehovah, deprived the people of their religious rights, and that, consequently, he could neither expect the blessing of God, nor the cooperation of the people. \subsection*{Chronicles II 33}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Manasses was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord destroyed from before the face of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he returned and built the high places, which his father Ezekias had pulled down, and set up images to Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he built altars in the house of the Lord, concerning which the Lord said, In Jerusalem shall be my name for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He also passed his children through the fire in the valley of Benennom; and he divined, and used auspices, and sorceries, and appointed those who had divining spirits, and enchanters, and wrought abundant wickedness before the Lord, to provoke him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he set the graven [image], the molten [statue], the idol which he made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, if only they will take heed to do all things which I have commanded them, according to all the law and the ordinances and the judgments [given] by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So Manasses led astray Juda and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to do evil beyond all the nations which the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord spoke to Manasses, and to his people: but they listened not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, and they took Manasses in bonds, and bound him in fetters, and brought him to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when he was afflicted, he sought the face of the Lord his God, and was greatly humbled before the face of the God of his fathers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and he prayed to him: and he listened to him, and listened to his cry, and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom: and Manasses knew that the Lord he is God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And afterward he built a wall without the city of David, from the southwest southward in the valleys and at the entrance through the fish-gate, as men go out by the gate round about, even as far as Opel: and he raised it much, and set captains of the host in all the fortified cities in Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he removed the strange gods, and the graven [image] out of the house of the Lord, and all the altars which he had built in the mount of the house of the Lord, and in Jerusalem, and without the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he repaired the altar of the Lord, and offered upon it a sacrifice of peace-offering and thank-offering, and he told Juda to serve the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Nevertheless the people still sacrificed on the high places, only to the Lord their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the rest of the acts of Manasses, and his prayer to God, and the words of the seers that spoke to him in the name of the God of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} behold, [they are] in the account of his prayer; and [God] listened to him. And all his sins, and his backslidings, and the spots on which he built the high places, and set there groves and graven images, before he repented, behold, they are written in the books of the seers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Manasses slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the garden of his house: and Amon his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Amon was twenty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his father Manasses did: and Amon sacrificed to all the idols which his father Manasses had made, and served them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he was not humbled before the Lord as his father Manasses was humbled; for his son Amon abounded in transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And his servants conspired against him, and killed him in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the people of the land killed the men who had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josias his son king in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3306-3361, bc 693-643 Manasseh; Manasses twelve \textsuperscript{3} he built again Heb. he returned and built, which Hezekiah, ; he reared; made groves; the host \textsuperscript{7} he set a carved image The Targumist says, "He set up an image, the likeness of himself, in the house of the sanctuary." In the parallel passage it is, "a graven image of the grove, " or rather, Asherah or Astarte. Manasseh, as Bp. Patrick observes, seems to have studied to find out what God had forbidden in his law, that he might practice it. A most prodigious change from the height of piety in his father's time, into the sink of impiety in this! in the house, God had said; which I have \textsuperscript{8} will I; so that they; to do all, ; by the hand \textsuperscript{9} made Judah; to do worse; the heathen \textsuperscript{11} am 3327, bc 677 the Lord; the captains, of the king Heb. which were the king's, ; among the thorns The word bachochim may possibly here signify with fetters or chains, as the kindred word chachim denotes, . The Syriac and Arabic have alive, probably reading bechayim .; bound him; fetters or, chains \textsuperscript{12} And when; he besought; the Lord humbled \textsuperscript{13} he was entreated; brought him; knew \textsuperscript{14} am 3327-3361, bc 677-643 he built Gihon; fish gate; Ophel or, the tower; put \textsuperscript{16} repaired; peace thank commanded, see note on \textsuperscript{18} am 3306-3361, bc 698-643 the rest, his prayer, the seers; in the book \textsuperscript{19} his prayer also; all his sins; before he, ; the seers or, Hosai, So the Targum and Vulgate. The Syraic has Hanun the prophet; and the Arabic, Saphan the prophet. This record is totally lost; for the captivity and repentance of Manasseh are related no where else; and the prayer of Manasseh in the Apocrypha was probably composed long afterwards. It is not acknowledged as canonical even by the Romish church, though it was anciently used as a form of confession, and as such still received by the Greek church. \textsuperscript{22} as did Manasseh; for Amon sacrificed Amon's conduct is recorded as like his father Manasseh, in sacrificing to graven images; by which some think it is an evidence that Manasseh did not truly repent, but they forget how many good kings had wicked sons. In one point of view Manasseh was defective, although it cannot be supposed that it affected his eternal state; for when he cast out the images, he did not utterly deface and destroy them, according to the law in, which required, moreover, that the graven images should be burnt with fire. How necessary that law was, this instance shows; for the carved images being only thrown aside, and not burnt, Amon knew where to find them, soon set them up, and sacrificed to them. \textsuperscript{23} humbled, ; trespassed more and more Heb. multiplied trespass\par}

\subsection*{Chronicles II 34}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Josias was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of his father David, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And in the eighth year of his reign, and he [being] yet a youth, he began to seek the Lord God of his father David: and in the twelfth year of his reign he began to purge Juda and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the ornaments for the altars, and the molten images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he pulled down the altars of Baalim that were before his face, and the high places that were above them; and he cut down the groves, and the graven images, and broke in pieces the molten images, and reduced them to powder, and cast [it] upon the surface of the tombs of those who [had] sacrificed to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he burnt the bones of the priests upon the altars, and purged Juda and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And [he did so] in the cities of Manasse, and Ephraim, and Symeon, and Nephthali, and the places round about them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he pulled down the altars and the groves, and he cut the idols in small pieces, and cut off all the high places from all the land of Israel, and returned to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And in the eighteenth year of his reign, after having cleansed the land, and the house, he sent Saphan the son of Ezelias, and Maasa prefect of the city, and Juach son of Joachaz his recorder, to repair the house of the Lord his God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they came to Chelcias the high priest, and gave the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the gate collected of the hand of Manasse and Ephraim, and of the princes, and of every one that was left in Israel, and of the children of Juda and Benjamin, and of the dwellers in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they gave it into the hand of the workmen, who were appointed in the house of the Lord, and they gave it to the workmen who wrought in the house of the Lord, to repair and strengthen the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They gave [it] also to the carpenters and builders, to buy squared stones, and timber for beams to cover the houses which the kings of Juda had destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the men [were] faithfully [engaged] in the works: and over them were superintendents, Jeth and Abdias, Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zacharias and Mosollam, of the sons of Caath, [appointed] to oversee; and every Levite, and every one that understood [how] to play on musical instruments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And [overseers were] over the burden-bearers, and over all the workmen in the respective works; and of the Levites [were appointed] scribes, and judges, and porters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when they brought forth the money that had been brought into the house of the Lord, Chelcias the priest found a book of the law of the Lord [given] by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Chelcias answered and said to Saphan the scribe, I have found a book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Chelcias gave the book to Saphan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Saphan brought in the book to the king, and moreover gave an account to the king, [saying, This is] all the money given into the hand of your servants that work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they have collected the money that was found in the house of the Lord, and given it into the hand of the overseers, and into the hand of them that do the work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Saphan the scribe brought word to the king, saying, Chelcias the priest has given me a book. And Saphan read it before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the law, that he tore his garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the king commanded Chelcias, and Achicam the son of Saphan, and Abdom the son of Michaias, and Saphan the scribe, and Asia the servant of the king, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Go, enquire of the Lord for me, and for every one that is left in Israel and Juda, concerning the words of the book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord [which] has been kindled among us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of the Lord, to do according to all the things written in this book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Chelcias went, and [the others] whom the king told, to Olda the prophetess, the wife of Sellem son of Thecoe, son of Aras, who kept the commandments; and she lived in Jerusalem in the second [quarter]: and they spoke to her accordingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And she said to them, Thus has the Lord God of Israel said, Tell the man who sent you to me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Thus says the Lord, Behold, I bring evil upon this place, [even] all the words that are written in the book that was read before the king of Juda: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} because they have forsaken me, and burnt incense to strange gods, that they might provoke me by all the works of their hands; and my wrath is kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And concerning the king of Juda, who sent you to seek the Lord, —thus shall you⌃ say to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, [As for] the words which you have heard, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} forasmuch as your heart was ashamed, and you were humbled before me when you heard my words against this place, and against the inhabitants of it, and you were humbled before me, and did rend your garments, and did weep before me; I also have heard, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Behold, I [will] gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not look upon all the evils which I am bringing upon this place, and upon the inhabitants of it. And they brought back word to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the king sent and gathered the elders of Juda and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the king went up to the house of the Lord, [he] and all Juda, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, and the Levites, and all the people great and small: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that were found in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the king stood at a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk before the Lord, to keep his commandments and testimonies, and his ordinances, with all [his] heart and with all [his] soul, so as to perform the words of the covenant that were written in this book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he caused all that were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord God of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And Josias removed all the abominations out of the whole land which belonged to the children of Israel, and caused all that were found in Jerusalem and in Israel, to serve the Lord their God all his days: he departed not from following the Lord God of his fathers.\par

\subsection*{Chronicles II 35}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josias kept a passover to the Lord his God; and sacrificed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he appointed the priests at their charges, and encouraged them for the services of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he told the Levites that were able [to act] in all Israel, that they should consecrate themselves to the Lord: and they put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built: and the king said, You⌃ must not carry anything on your shoulders: now then minister to the Lord your God, and to his people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And prepare yourselves according to the houses of your families, and according to your daily courses, according to the writing of David king of Israel, and [the order] by the hand of his son Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And stand you⌃ in the house according to the divisions of the houses of your families for your brethren the sons of the people; [so] also let there be for the Levites a division of the house of their family. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And kill you⌃ the passover, and prepare [it] for your brethren, to do according to the word of the Lord, by the hand of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Josias gave as an offering to the children of the people, sheep, and lambs, and kids of the young of the goats, all for the passover, [even for] all that were found, in number [amounting to] thirty thousand, and three thousand calves, these [were] of the substance of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And his princes gave an offering to the people, and to the priests, and to the Levites: and Chelcias and Zacharias and Jeiel the chief men gave to the priests of the house of God, they even gave for the passover sheep, and lambs, and kids, two thousand six hundred, and three hundred calves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Chonenias, and Banaeas, and Samaeas, and Nathanael his brother, and Asabias, and Jeiel, and Jozabad, heads of the Levites, gave an offering to the Levites for the passover, of five thousand sheep and five hundred calves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the service was duly ordered, and the priests stood in their place, and the Levites in their divisions, according to the command of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they killed the passover, and the priests sprinkled the blood from their hand, and the Levites flayed [the victims]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they prepared the whole burnt offering to give to them, according to the division by the houses of families, [even] to the sons of the people, to offer to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And thus [they did] till the morning. And they roasted the passover with fire according to the ordinance; and boiled the holy [pieces] in copper vessels and caldrons, and [the feast] went on well, and they quickly served all the children of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And after they had prepared for themselves and for the priests, for the priests [were engaged] in offering the whole burnt offerings and the fat until night, then the Levites prepared for themselves, and for their brethren the sons of Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the sons of Asaph the psalm-singers [were] at their post according to the commands of David, and Asaph, and Aeman, and Idithom, the prophets of the king: also, the chiefs and the porters of the several gates; —it was not for them to stir from the service of the holy things, for their brethren the Levites prepared for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So all the service of the Lord was duly ordered and prepared in that day, for keeping the passover, and offering the whole burnt sacrifices on the altar of the Lord, according to the command of king Josias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the children of Israel that were present kept the passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there was no passover like it in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet, or any king of Israel: they kept not such a passover as Josias, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Juda and Israel that were present, and the dwellers in Jerusalem, kept to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josias this passover was kept, after all these things that Josias did in the house. And king Josias burnt those who had in them a divining spirit, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and the sodomites which were in the land of Juda and in Jerusalem, that he might confirm the words of the law that were written in the book which Chelcias the priest found in the house of the Lord. There was no [king] like him before him, who turned to the Lord with all his heart, and all his soul, and all his strength, according to all the law of Moses, and after him there rose up none like him. Nevertheless the Lord turned not from the anger of his fierce wrath, wherewith the Lord was greatly angry against Juda, for all the provocations wherewith Manasses provoked him: and the Lord said, I will even remove Juda also from my presence, as I have removed Israel, and I have rejected the city which I chose, [even] Jerusalem, and thehouse of which I said, My name shall be there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Pharao Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates, and king Josias went to meet him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he sent messengers to him, saying, What have I to do with you, O king of Juda? I am not come today to war against you; and God has told me to hasten: beware of the God that is with me, lest he destroy you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} However, Josias turned not his face from him, but strengthened himself to fight against him, and listened not to the words of Nechao by the mouth of God, and he came to fight in the plain of Mageddo. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the archers shot at king Josias; and the king said to his servants, Take me away, for I am severely wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And his servants lifted him out of the chariot, and put him in the second chariot which he had, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died, and was buried with his fathers: and all Juda and Jerusalem lamented over Josias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Jeremias mourned over Josias, and all the chief men and chief women uttered a lamentation over Josias until this day: and they made it an ordinance for Israel, and, behold, it is written in the lamentations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the rest of the acts of Josias, and his hope, are written in the law of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And his acts, the first and the last, behold, [they are] written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Josiah The whole solemnity was performed with great exactness according to the law, and upon that account there was none like it since Samuel's time; for even in Hezekiah's passover there were several irregularities. Bp. Patrick observes, that in this also it exceeded the other passovers which preceding things had kept, that though Josiah was by no means so rich as David, or Solomon, or Jehoshaphat, yet he furnished the congregation with beasts for sacrifice, both paschal and eucharistical, at his own proper cost and charge, which was more than any king ever did before.; the fourteenth; Josiah's solemnization of the passover, which is merely alluded to at, is very particularly related her, while the destruction of idolatry is largely related in the Kings, and here only touched upon. The feasts of the Lord God, appointed by the ceremonial law, were very numerous; but the passover was the chief. It was the first which was solemnized in the night wherein Israel came out of Egypt, and ushered in those which were afterwards instituted, and it was the last great feast which was held in the night wherein Christ was betrayed, before the vail of the temple was rent in twain. Be means of this feast, both Josiah and Hezekiah revived religion in their day. \textsuperscript{3} the Levites; Put, in the house not be; serve now \textsuperscript{4} the houses; after your courses The regulations formed by David, and established by Solomon, concerning the courses of the priests and Levites, were committed to writing, and preserved, for them to refer to continually. Josiah, as well as Hezekiah, required the priests and Levites to attend to their several duties, and encouraged them therein, but he neither added, altered, not retrenched anything. He merely enforced what had been established in the law, and in the regulations made by David and the contemporary prophets: "the commandment of the king....was by the word of the Lord." 1Chr. 23:1-26:32 and according \textsuperscript{5} And stand, families of the fathers Heb. house of the fathers people Heb. sons of the people. \textsuperscript{7} Josiah; gave Heb. offered, thirty thousand According to the calculation, that not fewer than ten, nor more than twenty persons, were to join for one kid or lamb, the numbers given on this occasion would suffice for above 400, 000 persons. the king's substance \textsuperscript{8} his princes;, ; gave Heb. offered willingly, Hilkiah rulers \textsuperscript{13} roasted; sod; divided them speedily Heb. made them run \textsuperscript{15} place Heb. station according;, *titles the porters \textsuperscript{17} present Heb. found the feast \textsuperscript{18} there was no passover Not one on purer principles, more heartily joined in by the people present, more literally or exactly consecrated, according to the law, or more religiously observed. The words do not refer to the number present, but to the manner and spirit.; neither did \textsuperscript{20} am 3394, bc 610 temple Heb. house Necho Pharaoh, the lame, says the Targumist., Pharaoh-necho, Charchemish \textsuperscript{21} What; house wherewith I have war Heb. house of my war God; forbear thee \textsuperscript{22} Nevertheless Josiah's conduct in this affair has been treated with great severity; and he has been charged with engaging rashly in an unjust war, and disregarding the express command of God. But Scripture no where condemns him; and Pharaoh, in marching through Josiah's territories, against his will, certainly committed an act of hostility. It is evident that Josiah was in possession of the whole land of Israel ( ); and probably he held the northern parts of it as a grant from the king of Babylon; and was not only in alliance with him, but bound to guard his frontiers against hostile invaders. He may, therefore, be fairly justified from the charge of unjustly meddling in a war that did not belong him. It is true the ambassadors assured Josiah, that "God had commanded Pharaoh to make haste; " and he is therefore said not to have "hearkened to the words of Necho, from the mouth of God." But Necho produced no proof that he was a prophet of Jehovah; and the word he employed, elohim, may denote gods or idols; and critics have noticed that the expression, "from the mouth of God, " is not used when the true God is meant. but disguised;, the mouth; Megiddo; Megiddon, Armageddon \textsuperscript{23} the archers; wounded Heb. made sick \textsuperscript{24} the second they died; in one of the or, among the, Judah \textsuperscript{25} Jeremiah; all the singing; and made them\par}
