\subsection*{Chronicles II 36}
\markright{CHRONICLES II 36}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the people of the land took Joachaz the son of Josias, and anointed him, and made him king over Jerusalem in the room of his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Joachaz [was] twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Amital, daughter of Jeremias of Lobna. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done. And Pharao Nechao bound him in Deblatha in the land of Aemath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king brought him over to Egypt; and imposed a tribute on the land, one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Pharao Nechao made Eliakim the son of Josias king over Juda in the room of his father Josias, and changed his name [to] Joakim. And Pharao Nechao took his brother Joachaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there: but [he] had given the silver and gold to Pharao. At that time the land began to be taxed to give the money at the command of Pharao; and every one as he could borrowed the silver and the gold of the people of the land, to give to Pharao Nechao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Joachim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name [was] Zechora, daughter of Nerias of Rama. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers did. In his days came Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon into the land, and he served him three years, and [then] revolted from him. And the Lord sent against them the Chaldeans, and plundering parties of Syrians, and plundering parties of the Moabites, and of the children of Ammon, and of Samaria; but after this they departed, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of his servants the prophets. Nevertheless the wrath of the Lord was upon Juda, so that they should be removed from his presence, because of the sins of Manasses in all that he did, and for the innocent blood which Joakim shed, for he had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; yet the Lord would not utterly destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came up against him, and bound him with brazen fetters, and carried him away to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he carried away a part of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon, and put them in his temple in Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the rest of the acts of Joakim, and all that he did, behold, [are] not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda? And Joakim slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in Ganozae: and Jechonias his son reigned in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Jechonias [was] eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And at the turn of the year, king Nabuchodonosor sent, and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of the Lord, and made Sedekias his father's brother king over Juda and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Sedekias [was] twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and be reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God: he was not ashamed before the prophet Jeremias, nor because of the word of the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} in that he rebelled against king Nabuchodonosor, which he adjured him by God [not to do]: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart, so as not to return to the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the great men of Juda, and the priests, and the people of the land transgressed abundantly in the abominations of the heathen, and polluted the house of the Lord which [was] in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord God of their fathers sent by the hand of his prophets; rising early and sending his messengers, for he spared his people, and his sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Nevertheless they sneered at his messengers, and set at nothing his words, and mocked his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord rose up against his people, till there was no remedy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, and killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary, and did not spare Sedekias, and had no mercy upon their virgins, and they led away their old men: he delivered all things into their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all the vessels of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord, and all the treasures of the king and the great men; he brought all to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he burnt the house of the Lord, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt its palaces with fire, and [utterly destroyed] every beautiful vessel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he carried away the remnant to Babylon; and they were servants to him and to his sons until [the establishment of] the kingdom of the Medes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} That the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias might be fulfilled, until the land should enjoy its sabbaths in resting [and] sabbath keeping all the days of its desolation, till the accomplishment of seventy years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, after the fulfillment of the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and told him to make proclamation in writing throughout all his kingdom, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians to all the kingdoms of the earth, The Lord God of heaven has given me [power], and he has commanded me to build a house to him in Jerusalem, in Judea. Who [is there] of you of all his people? His God shall be with him, and let him go up.\par

\section*{Ezra Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Ezra\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book's first-person sections and priestly-scribal perspective support Ezran authorship, with possible final compilation of Ezra-Nehemiah materials.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Ezra's role as priest and scribe is affirmed within the book itself; later Scripture receives the restoration account as true sacred history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 5th century BC in the Persian period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology begins with Cyrus's decree and spans the return, temple rebuilding, and Ezra's reform mission.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The Greek tradition preserves the same Persian-period restoration frame, though 1 Esdras witnesses a related alternate Greek arrangement of some material.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Return from Babylon, temple restoration, and covenant reform under Persian rule.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To show the LORD's faithfulness in restoring His people, temple, and law after exile.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} return; temple; law; reform; covenant restoration; providence under empire\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} First return and temple rebuilding 1-6; Ezra's mission and reform 7-10.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Ezra material is limited and often overlaps the broader Ezra-Nehemiah tradition Second Temple period | Subst. Early Hebrew evidence for Ezra is limited; comparison with Greek 1 Esdras is especially important n/a | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Ezra/Esdras material in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use of Persian restoration history by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Ezra is text-critically important because 1 Esdras sometimes preserves material parallel to canonical Ezra with differences in order and wording.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Ezra as true post-exilic history under God's providence, with Greek parallels used to illuminate, not unsettle, the canonical book.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Ezra and Nehemiah}
\markboth{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH}{}
\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 1}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now in the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he issued a proclamation through all his kingdom, and that in writing, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus said Cyrus king of the Persians, The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has given me a charge to build him a house in Jerusalem that is in Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who [is] there among you of all his people? for his God shall be with him, and he shall go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and let him build the house of the God of Israel: he [is] the God that is in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [let] every [Jew] that is left [go] from every place where he sojourns, and the men of his place shall help him with silver, and gold, and goods, and cattle, together with the voluntary offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then the chiefs of the families of Juda and Benjamin arose, and the priests, and the Levites, all whose spirit the Lord stirred up to go up to build the house of the Lord that [is] in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all that were round about strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with cattle, and with presents, besides the voluntary offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And king Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of the Lord, which Nabuchodonosor had brought from Jerusalem, and put in the house of his god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Cyrus king of the Persians brought them out by the hand of Mithradates the treasurer, and he numbered them to Sasabasar, the chief man of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And this [is] their number: thirty gold basins, and a thousand silver basins, nine and twenty changes, thirty golden goblets, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and four hundred [and] ten double silver [vessels], and a thousand other vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All the gold and silver vessels were five thousand four hundred, [even] all that went up with Sasabasar from the [place of] transportation, from Babylon to Jerusalem.\par

He was born about 600 years before Christ, and died at the age of 70, after a reign of 30 years. He was mentioned by name, and his conquests foretold, by the prophet Isaiah, about a century before his birth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} We therefore declare to the king, that, if that city be built, and its walls be set up, you shall not have peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then the king sent to Reum the chancellor, and Sampsa the scribe, and the rest of their fellow-servants who lived in Samaria, and the rest beyond the river, [saying, ]Peace; and he says, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The tribute-gatherer whom you⌃ sent to us, has been called before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And a decree has been made by me, and we have examined, and found that city of old time exalts itself against kings, and that rebellions and desertions take place within it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And there were powerful kings in Jerusalem, and they ruled over all the [country] beyond the river, and abundant revenues and tribute were given to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now therefore make a decree to stop the work of those men, and that city shall no more be built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} [See] that you⌃ be careful of the decree, [not] to be remiss concerning this matter, lest at any time destruction should abound to the harm of kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Then the tribute-gatherer of king Arthasastha read [the letter] before Reum the chancellor, and Sampsa the scribe, and his fellow-servants: and they went in haste to Jerusalem and through Juda, and caused them to cease with horses and an [armed] force. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then ceased the work of the house of God in Jerusalem, and it was at a stand until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.\par

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 5}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Aggaeus the prophet, and Zacharias the [son] of Addo, prophesied a prophesy to the Jews in Juda and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, [even] to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then rose up Zorobabel the [son] of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec, and began to build the house of God that was in Jerusalem: and with them [were] the prophets of God assisting them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} At the same time came there upon them Thanthanai, the governor on this side the river, and Satharbuzanai, and their fellow-servants, and spoke thus to them, Who has ordained a decree for you to build this house, and to [provide] this preparation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then they spoke thus to them, What are the names of the men that build this city? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the eyes of God were upon the captivity of Juda, and they did not cause them to cease till the decree was brought to Darius; and then was sent by the tribute-gatherer concerning this {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the copy of a letter, which Thanthanai, the governor of the part on this side the river, and Satharbuzanai, and their fellow-servants the Apharsachaeans who were on this side of the river, sent to king Darius. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They sent an account to him, and thus it was written in it: All peace to king Darius. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be it known to the king, that we went into the land of Judea, to the house of the great God; and it is building with choice stones, and they are laying timbers in the walls, and that work is prospering, and goes on favorably in their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then we asked those elders, and thus we said to them, Who gave you the order to build this house, and to [provide] this preparation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And we asked them their names, [in order] to declare [them] to you, so as to write to you the names of their leading men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they answered us thus, saying, We [are] the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we [are] building the house which had been built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it, and established it for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But after that our fathers provoked the God of heaven, he gave them into the hands of Nabuchodonosor the Chaldean, king of Babylon, and he destroyed this house, and carried the people captive to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And in the first year of king Cyrus, Cyrus the king made a decree that this house of God should be built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nabuchodonosor brought out from the house that was in Jerusalem, and carried them into the temple of the king, them did king Cyrus bring out from the temple of the king, and gave them to Sabanasar the treasurer, who was over the treasurer; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and said to him, Take all the vessels, and go, put them in the house that is in Jerusalem in their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then that Sabanazar came, and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem: and from that time even until now it has been building, and has not been finished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And now, if it [seem] good to the king, lest search be made in the treasure-house of the king at Babylon, that you may know [if it be] that a decree was made by king Cyrus to build that house of God that was in Jerusalem, and let the king send to us when he has learned concerning this [matter].\par

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 6}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Darius the king made a decree, and caused a search to be made in the record-offices, where the treasure is stored in Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there was found in the city, in the palace, a volume, and this was the record written in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} In the first year of king Cyrus, Cyrus the king made a decree concerning the holy house of God that was in Jerusalem, [saying, ]Let the house be built, and the place where they sacrifice the sacrifices. (Also he appointed its elevation, in height sixty cubits; its breadth [was] of sixty cubits.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And [let there be] three strong layers of stone, and one layer of timber; and the expense shall be paid out of the house of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the silver and the gold vessels of the house of God, which Nabuchodonosor carried off from the house that was in Jerusalem, and carried to Babylon, let them even be given, and be carried to the temple that is in Jerusalem, and put in the place where they were set in the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now, you⌃ rulers beyond the river, Satharbuzanai, and their fellow-servants the Apharsachaeans, who [are] on the other side of the river, give [these things], keeping far from that place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now let alone the work of the house of God: let the rulers of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Also a decree has been made by me, if haply you⌃ may do somewhat in concert with the elders of the Jews for the building of that house of God: to wit, out of the king's property, [even] the tributes beyond the river, let there be money to defray the expenses carefully granted to those men, so that they be not hindered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And whatever need [there may be], you⌃ shall give both the young of bulls and rams, and lambs for whole burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, oil:—let it be given them according to the word of the priests that are in Jerusalem, day by day whatever they shall ask; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} that they may offer sweet savours to the God of heaven, and that they may pray for the life of the king and his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And a decree has been made by me, that every man who shall alter this word, timber shall be pulled down from his house, and let him be lifted up and slain upon it, and his house shall be confiscated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And may the God whose name dwells there, overthrow every king and people who shall stretch out his hand to alter or destroy the house of God which is in Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree; let it be diligently [attended to]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then Thanthanai the governor on this side beyond the river, Satharbuzanai, and his fellow-servants, according to that which king Darius sent, so they did diligently. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the elders of the Jews and the Levites built, at the prophecy of Aggaeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo: and they built up, and finished [it], by the decree of the God of Israel, and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Arthasastha, kings of the Persians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they finished this house by the third day of the month Adar, which is the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the children of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of the house of God with gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they offered for the dedication of the house of God one hundred calves, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, twelve kids of the goats for a sin-offering for all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their separate orders, for the services of God in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the priests and Levites were purified, all were clean to a man, and they killed the passover for all the children of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the children of Israel ate the passover, [even] they that were of the captivity, and every one who separated himself to them from the uncleanness of the nations of the land, to seek the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with gladness, because the Lord made them glad, and he turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} and search, ; rolls Chal, books;, ; laid up Chal, made to descend \textsuperscript{2} at Achmetha or, at Ecbatana, or, in a coffer, ΰηξϊΰ, probably from the Persian Mx, kham, "a house for a summer residence, " with a prefix, ΰ, aleph, and the Chaldee termination )t, tha, most likely denotes Ecbatana, as the Vulgate and Josephus read, the summer residence of the Persian monarchs. It was situated in a mountainous region at the foot of mount Orontes, or Jasonius, according to Ammianus, on the southern confines of Media and Persia, and according to Pliny, 750 miles from Seleucia the Great, 20 miles from the Caspian passes, 450 miles from Susa, and the same from Gaze Atropatene, and in lat. 37 degrees 45 min., long. 88 degrees, according to Ptolemy. The building of the city is ascribed to Semiramis by Diodorus, but to Deioces by Eusebius (in Chron. ), and Herodotus, who states that it was surrounded by seven walls, strong and ample, built in circles one within another, rising each above each by the height of their respective battlements; each being distinguished by a different colour, the first white, the second black, the third purple, the fourth blue, the fifth orange, the sixth plated with silver, and the seventh with gold. The largest of these was nearly the extent of Athens, i.e., 200 furlongs, according to Dion Chrysostom; but Diodorus Siculus states the circumference of Ecbatana to be 250 furlongs. Within the inner circle stood the king's palace and the royal treasury, so much celebrated for its splendour and riches by Polybius. It is highly probable, as D'Anville and Major Rennel suppose, that the present Hamadan, whose ruins attest its former splendour, occupies the site of Ecbatana. It is situated in Al Gebal, at the foot of the lofty mountain Alwend, about 80 leagues from Ispahan, and also from Bagdad. \textsuperscript{3} the first year; the place; the height \textsuperscript{5} the golden; which Nebuchadnezzar; brought Chal, go \textsuperscript{6} Tatnai your companions Chal, their societies, be ye far \textsuperscript{8} I make a decree Chal, by me a decree is made the king's, ; hindered Chal, made to cease \textsuperscript{9} young bullocks, ; lambs; Num. 28:1-29:40 wheat; salt; let it be given \textsuperscript{10} sweet savours Chal, rest; pray \textsuperscript{11} whosoever timber, hanged Chal, destroyed his house \textsuperscript{12} caused; destroy, ; I Darius, speed \textsuperscript{14} And the elders, through; Zech. 2:1-4:14, finished it according; commandment Chal, decree Cyrus, Artaxerxes This was Artaxerxes, the third son and successor of Xerxes, surnamed Μακροχειρ, or Longimanus, or in Persian, Ardsheer deeraz dest, "Ardsheer the long-handed; " so called, according to the Greeks, from the extra-ordinary length of his hands, but according to the Easterners, from the extent of his dominions. He ascended the Persian throne, am 3540, bc 464, and reigned forty-one years. \subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 7}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now after these things, in the reign of Arthasastha king of the Persians, came up Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias, the son of Chelcias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} the son of Selum, the son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the son of Samarias, the son of Esria, the son of Mareoth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} the son of Zaraia, the son of Ozias, the son of Bokki, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} the son of Abisue, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the first priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} This Esdras went up out of Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel gave: and the king gave him [leave], for the hand of the Lord his God was upon him in all things which he sought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And [some] of the children of Israel went up, and [some] of the priests, and of the Levites, and the singers, and the doorkeepers, and the Nathinim, to Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Arthasastha the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, this [was] the seventh year of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For in the first [day] of the first month he began the going up from Babylon, and in the first day of the fifth month, they came to Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For Esdras had determined in his heart to seek the law, and to do and teach the ordinances and judgments in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And this [is] the copy of the order which Arthasastha gave to Esdras the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the commandments of the Lord, and of his ordinances to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Arthasastha, king of kings, to Esdras, the scribe of the law of the Lord God of heaven, Let the order and the answer be accomplished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A decree is made by me, that every one who is willing in my kingdom of the people of Israel, and of the priests and Levites, to go to Jerusalem, [be permitted] to go with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [One] has been sent from the king and the seven councillors, to visit Judea and Jerusalem, according to the law of their God that is in your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And for the house of the Lord [there have been sent] silver and gold, which the king and the councillors have freely given to the God of Israel, who dwells in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And all the silver and gold, whatever you shall find in all the land of Babylon, with the free will offering of the people, and the priests that offer freely for the house of God which is in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And as for every one that arrives [there], speedily order him by this letter [to bring] calves, rams, lambs, and their meat-offerings, and their drink-offerings; and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And whatever it shall seem good to you and to your brethren to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do as it is pleasing to your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And deliver the vessels that are given you for the service of the house of God, before God in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And as to the rest of the need of the house of your God, you shall give from the king's treasure-houses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and from me, whatever it shall seem [good] to you to give. I king Arthasastha have made a decree for all the treasuries that are in the [country] beyond the river, that whatever Esdras the priest and scribe of the God of heaven may ask you, it shall be done speedily, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} to [the amount of] one hundred talents of silver, and one hundred measures of wheat, and one hundred baths of wine, and one hundred baths of oil, and salt without reckoning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Let whatever is in the decree of the God of heaven, be done: take heed lest any one make an attack on the house of the God of heaven, lest at any time there shall be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Also this has been declared to you, with respect to all the priests, and Levites, the singers, porters, Nathinim and ministers of the house of God, let no tribute be [paid] to you; you shall not have power to oppress them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you, Esdras, as the wisdom of God [is] in your hand, appoint scribes and judges, that they may judge for all the people beyond the river, all that know the law of the Lord your God; and you⌃ shall make it known to him that knows not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And whoever shall not do the law of God, and the law of the king readily, judgment shall be taken upon him, whether for death or for chastisement, or for a fine of his property, or casting into prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Blessed [be] the Lord God of our fathers, who has put it thus into the heart of the king, to glorify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and has given me favor in the eyes of the king, and of his councillors, and all the rulers of the king, the exalted ones. And I was strengthened according to the good hand of God upon me, and I gathered chief men of Israel to go up with me.\par

\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these [are] the heads of their families, the leaders that went up with me in the reign of Arthasastha the king of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Of the sons of Phinees; Gerson: of the sons of Ithamar; Daniel: of the sons of David; Attus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Of the sons of Sachania, and the sons of Phoros; Zacharias: and with him a company [of] one hundred and fifty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Of the sons of Phaath-Moab; Eliana the son of Saraia, and with him two hundred that were males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And of the sons of Zathoes; Sechenias the son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And of the sons of Adin; Obeth the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And of the sons of Elam; Isaeas the son of Athelia, and with him seventy males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And of the sons of Saphatia; Zabadias the son of Michael, and with him eighty males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And of the sons of Joab; Abadia the son of Jeiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And of the sons of Baani; Selimuth the son of Josephia, and with him one hundred and sixty males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And of the sons of Babi; Zacharias the son of Babi, and with him twenty-eight males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And of the sons of Asgad; Joanan the son of Accatan, and with him one hundred and ten males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And of the sons of Adonicam [were the] last, and these [were] their names, Eliphalat, Jeel, and Samaea, and with them sixty males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And of the sons of Baguae, Uthai, and Zabud, and with him seventy males. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I gathered them to the river that comes to Evi, and we encamped there three days: and I reviewed the people and the priests, and found none of the sons of Levi there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And I sent men of understanding to Eleazar, to Ariel, to Semeias, and to Alonam, and to Jarib, and to Elnatham, and to Nathan, and to Zacharias, and to Mesollam, and to Joarim, and to Elnathan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I forwarded them to the rulers with the money of the place, and I put words in their mouth to speak to their brethren the Athinim with the money of the place, that they should bring us singers for the house of our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they came to us, as the good hand of our God was upon us, even a man of understanding of the sons of Mooli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and at the commencement came his sons and his brethren, eighteen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Asebia, and Isaia of the sons of Merari, his brethren and his sons, twenty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And of the Nathinim; whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites [there were] two hundred and twenty Nathinim; all were gathered by [their] names. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And I proclaimed there a fast, at the river Aue, that [we] should humble ourselves before our God, to seek of him a straight way for us, and for our children, and for all our property. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For I was ashamed to ask of the king a guard and horsemen to save us from the enemy in the way: for we had spoken to the king, saying, The hand of our God [is] upon all that seek him, for good; but his power and his wrath [are] upon all that forsake him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So we fasted, and asked of our God concerning this; and he listened to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I gave charge to twelve of the chiefs of the priests, to Saraia, to Asabia, and ten of their brethren with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I weighed to them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of the first fruits of the house of our God, which the king, and his councillors, and his princes, and all Israel that were found, had dedicated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I even weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and one hundred silver vessels, and one hundred talents of gold; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and twenty golden bowls, [weighing] about a thousand drachmas, and superior vessels of fine shining brass, [precious] as gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And I said to them, You⌃ [are] holy to the Lord; and the vessels [are] holy; and the silver and the gold are free will offerings to the Lord God of our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Be watchful and keep them, until you⌃ weigh [them] before the chief priests and the Levites, and the chiefs of families in Jerusalem, at the chambers of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So the priests and the Levites took the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to bring to Jerusalem into the house of our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And we departed from the river of Aue on the twelfth day of the first month, to come to Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and delivered us from the hand of the enemy and adversary in the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And it came to pass on the fourth day that we weighed the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, in the house of our God, into the hand of Merimoth the son of Uria the priest; and with him [was] Eleazar the son of Phinees, and with them Jozabad the son of Jesus, and Noadia the son of Banaia, the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} All things [were reckoned] by number and weight, and the whole weight was written [down]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} At that time the children of the banishment that came from the captivity offered whole burnt offerings to the God of Israel, twelve calves for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve goats for a sin-offering; all whole burnt offerings to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And they gave the king's mandate to the king's lieutenants, and the governors beyond the river: and they honored the people and the house of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the chief; genealogy; them that went up \textsuperscript{3} Pharosh This variation is attributable to the translators; the original being uniformly Parosh.;, Parosh \textsuperscript{12} Azgad; the son of Hakkatan or, the youngest son \textsuperscript{14} Bigvai; Zabbud or, Zaccur, as some read \textsuperscript{15} the river that runneth Ahava is supposed to be the river Adiava, which, with the Diava, is said by Ammianus to have given name to Adiabene, a province of Assyria, through which they flowed into the Tigris. These rivers were also called respectively, Anzabas and Zabas, the Caprus and Lycus of Ptolemy; the former of which he places, at its source, in long. 79 degrees, lat. 39+ degrees, and at its junction with the Tigris, in long. 79+ degrees, lat. 36 degrees 6 minutes; and the latter, at its source, in long 78 degrees, lat. 39 degrees; and where it falls into the Tigris, in long. 79 degrees, lat. 36+ degrees. They are now called the Great and Little Zab, or the Zabein, i.e., the two Zabs, which, says Ibn Haukal, "are considerable streams, each about half as large as the Dejleh (or Tigris). They rise among the mountains of Azerbaijan. Of these, the larger is that which runs towards Haditheh. These streams form part of the Tigris, and water the district of Semerah."; Ahava, abode Heb. pitched and found \textsuperscript{16} Shemaiah, Nathan Zechariah chief men of understanding \textsuperscript{17} Casiphia is supposed to denote the Caspian mountains, between Media and Hyrcania, near the Caspian Sea. It is evident, from a comparison of with, that Casiphia could not be far from Ahava. I told them Heb. I put words in their mouth; the Nethinims, ministers \textsuperscript{18} by the good hand; a man of understanding; Mahli; Sherebiah \textsuperscript{21} I proclaimed; afflict ourselves, ; to seek, ;, ; for our little ones \textsuperscript{22} I was ashamed; The hand, ; his power and his wrath \textsuperscript{23} we fasted; besought, and he was entreated \textsuperscript{27} fine copper Heb. yellow, or shining brass, The Syriac renders, nechosho korinthyo tovo, "good Corinthian brass; " so called from the brass found after the burning of Corinth by Lucius Mummius, which was, as is generally supposed, brass, copper, silver, and gold, melted together. Sir J. Chardin, however, in a manuscript note, cited by Harmer, mentioned a factitious metal used in the East, and highly esteemed there, which might probably be of an origin as ancient as Ezra. He says, "I have heard some Dutch gentlemen speak of a metal in the island of Sumatra, and among the Macassars, much more esteemed than gold, which royal personages alone are privileged to wear. It is a mixture, if I remember right, of gold and steel, or copper and steel." He afterwards added, "calmbac is the name of this metal, which is composed of gold and copper." precious Heb. desirable \textsuperscript{28} Ye are holy; the vessels \textsuperscript{29} Watch ye; until ye weigh them before \textsuperscript{30} the house of our God \textsuperscript{31} the river of Ahava, the hand, ; and he delivered Ezra and his company had now entered upon a journey of several hundred miles through the desert, which they were nearly four months in completing, encumbered with families and possessions, and carrying large treasures with them, which would invite the attempts of the Arabian hordes, and others, that infested that neighbourhood; yet, having declared to the king, "that the hand of God was upon all them for good that seek him, and that his power and wrath were against all them that forsook him, " ( ), he determined to travel without a guard, except that of the Almighty, being ashamed to ask any other, after his former avowed confidence in Him! Having, therefore, humbled themselves before the Lord, and besought his guidance and protection, he was intreated by them, their enemies were restrained or disabled, and they arrived unmolested at Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{33} weighed; Meremoth Uriah, Urijah Jozabad Binnui \textsuperscript{35} offered burnt Lev. 1:1-7:38; twelve bullocks \textsuperscript{36} the king's commissions lieutenants, they furthered\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 9}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when these things were finished, the princes drew near to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands in their abominations, [even] the Chananite, the Ethite, the Pherezite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, and the Moserite and the Amorite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and their sons; and the holy seed has passed among the nations of the lands, and the hand of the rulers [has been] first in this transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when I heard this thing, I tore my garments, and trembled, and plucked [some] of the hairs of my head and of my beard, and sat down mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then there assembled to me all that followed the word of the God of Israel, on account of the transgression of the captivity; and I remained mourning until the evening sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And at the evening sacrifice I rose up from my humiliation; and when I had torn my garments, then I trembled, and I bow myself on my knees, and spread out my hands to the Lord God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and I said, O Lord, I am ashamed and confounded, O my God, to lift up my face to you: for our transgressions have abounded over our head, and our trespasses have increased even to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} From the days of our fathers we have been in a great trespass until this day: and because of our iniquities we, and our kings, and our children, have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the Gentiles by the sword, and by captivity, and by spoil, and with shame of our face, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now our God has dealt mercifully with us, so as to leave us to escape, and to give us an establishment in the place of his sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes, and to give a little quickening in our servitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For we are slaves, yet in our servitude the Lord our God has not deserted us; and he has extended favor to us in the sight of the kings of the Persians, to give us a quickening, that they should raise up the house of our God, and restore the desolate places of it, and to give us a fence in Juda and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} What shall we say, our God, after this? for we have forsaken your commandments, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} which you have given us by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying, The land, into which you⌃ go to inherit it, is a land subject to disturbance by the removal of the people of the nations for their abominations, wherewith they have filled it from one end to the other by their uncleanness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And now give not your daughters to their sons, and take not of their daughters for your sons, neither shall you⌃ seek their peace or their good for ever: that you⌃ may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and transmit it as an inheritance to your children for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And after all that is come upon us because of our evil deeds, and our great trespass, [it is clear] that there is none such as our God, for you have lightly visited our iniquities, and given us deliverance; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} whereas we have repeatedly broken your commandments, and intermarried with the people of the lands: be not very angry with us to [our] utter destruction, so that there should be no remnant or escaping one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} O Lord God of Israel, you [are] righteous; for we remain [yet] escaped, as at this day: behold, we [are] before you in our trespasses: for we can’t stand before you on this account.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the princes; have not separated; doing according; of the Canaanites; Ammonites;, Moabites \textsuperscript{2} taken of their; the holy seed; mingled; the hand \textsuperscript{5} heaviness or, affliction I fell; spread \textsuperscript{6} I am ashamed;, ; our iniquities; trespass or, guiltiness grown up \textsuperscript{7} Since the days; for our iniquities;, ; into the hand, ; to confusion as it is this day \textsuperscript{8} little space Heb. moment grace hath; a remnant; a nail or a pin, i.e. a constant and sure abode; in his holy place; lighten; reviving \textsuperscript{9} we were bondmen yet our God; in the sight, to set up; repair Heb. set up a wall Or rather, a hedge or fence, gader, such as were made for sheep-folds. \textsuperscript{11} by thy servants Heb. by the hand of thy servants The land; the filthiness; one end to another Heb. mouth to mouth, *marg. \textsuperscript{12} give not; nor seek their peace; that ye may; and eat and leave it \textsuperscript{13} after all; hast punished etc. Heb. hast withheld beneath our iniquities less; hast given us \textsuperscript{14} we again; join in; wouldest not thou; no remnant \textsuperscript{15} thou art righteous; for we remain in our trespasses; we cannot\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 10}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} So when Esdras [had] prayed, and when he [had] confessed, weeping and praying before the house of God, a very great assembly of Israel came together to him, men and women and youths; for the people wept, and wept aloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Sechenias the son of Jeel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Esdras, We have broken covenant with our God, and have taken strange wives of the nations of the land: yet now there is patience [of hope] to Israel concerning this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now then let us make a covenant with our God, to put away all the wives, and their offspring, as you shall advise: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} arise, and alarm them with the commands of our God; and let [it] be done according to the law. Rise up, for the matter [is] upon you; and we [are] with you: be strong and do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then Esdras arose, and caused the rulers, the priests, and Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they would do according to this word: and they swore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esdras rose up from before the house of God, and went to the treasury of Joanan the son of Elisub; he even went there: he ate no bread, and drank no water; for he mourned over the unfaithfulness [of them] of the captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they made proclamation throughout Juda and Jerusalem to all the children of the captivity, that they should assemble at Jerusalem, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Every one who shall not arrive within three days, as [is] the counsel of the rulers and the elders, all his substance shall be forfeited, and he shall be separated from the congregation of the captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So all the men of Juda and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days. This [was] the ninth month: on the twentieth day of the month all the people sat down in the street of the house of the Lord, because of their alarm concerning the word, and because of the storm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Esdras the priest arose, and said to them, You⌃ have broken covenant, and have taken strange wives, to add to the trespass of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now therefore give praise to the Lord God of our fathers, and do that which is pleasing in his sight: and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land, and from the strange wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then all the congregation answered and said, This your word [is] powerful upon us to do it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But the people [is] numerous, and the season [is] stormy, and there is no power to stand without, and the work is more than enough for one day or for two; for we have greatly sinned in this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let now our rulers stand, and for all those in our cities who have taken strange wives, let them come at appointed times, and with them elders from every several city, and judges, to turn away the fierce wrath of our God from us concerning this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Only Jonathan the son of Asael, and Jazias the son of Thecoe [were] with me concerning this; and Mesollam, and Sabbathai the Levite helped them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the children of the captivity did thus: and Esdras the priest, and heads of families according to [their] house were separated, and all by their names, for they returned in the first day of the tenth month to search out the matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they made an end with all the men who had taken strange wives by the first day of the first month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there were found [some] of the sons of the priests who had taken strange wives: of the sons of Jesus the son of Josedec, and his brethren; Maasia, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gadalia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they pledged themselves to put away their wives, and [offered] a ram of the flock for a trespass-offering because of their trespass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And of the sons of Emmer; Anani, and Zabdia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And of the sons of Eram; Masael, and Elia, and Samaia, and Jeel, and Ozia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And of the sons of Phasur; Elionai, Maasia, and Ismael, and Nathanael, and Jozabad, and Elasa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And of the Levites; Jozabad, and Samu, and Colia (he [is] Colitas,) and Phetheia, and Judas, and Eliezer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And of the singers; Elisab: and of the porters; Solmen, and Telmen, and Oduth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Also of Israel: of the sons of Phoros; Ramia, and Azia, and Melchia, and Meamin, and Eleazar, and Asabia, and Banaia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And of the sons of Helam; Matthania, and Zacharia, and Jaiel, and Abdia, and Jarimoth, and Elia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And of the sons of Zathua; Elionai, Elisub, Matthanai, and Armoth, and Zabad, and Oziza. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And of the sons of Babei; Joanan, Anania, and Zabu, and Thali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And of the sons of Banui; Mosollam, Maluch, Adaias, Jasub, and Saluia, and Remoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And of the sons of Phaath Moab; Edne, and Chalel, and Banaia, Maasia, Matthania, Beseleel, and Banui, and Manasse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And of the sons of Eram; Eliezer, Jesia, Melchia, Samaias, Semeon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Benjamin, Baluch, Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And of the sons of Asem; Metthania, Matthatha, Zadab, Eliphalet, Jerami, Manasse, Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And of the sons of Bani; Moodia, Amram, Uel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Banaia, Badaia, Chelkia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Uvania, Marimoth, Eliasiph, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Matthania, Matthanai: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} and [so] did the children of Banui, and the children of Semei, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and Selemia, and Nathan, and Adaia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Machadnabu, Sesei, Sariu, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Ezriel, and Selemia, and Samaria, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} and Sellum, Amaria, Joseph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Of the sons of Nabu; Jael, Matthanias, Zabad, Zebennas, Jadai, and Joel, and Banaia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} All these had taken strange wives, and had begotten sons of them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} when Ezra; when he had; weeping; before the house; a very great; very sore Heb. a great weeping \textsuperscript{2} Shechaniah; Elam; We have trespassed Shechaniah here speaks in the name of the people, not acknowledging himself culpable; for he is not in the following list., Compare; yet now there is hope \textsuperscript{3} let us make Nichrath berith, "let us cut a covenant:"; put away Heb. bring forth according to the counsel of those that; at the commandment; let it; Shechaniah's counsel, which he was then so clear in, will not hold now. Such marriages, it is certain, are contrary to the will of God, and ought not to be made; but they are not null. Our rule under the gospel is Quod fieri non debuit, factum valet, "That which ought not to have been done must, when done, abide." See note on \textsuperscript{4} Arise; for this matter By the decree of Artaxerxes, Ezra was authorised to do every thing that the law of God required.; we also will; be of good \textsuperscript{6} the chamber Johanan, he did eat; he mourned \textsuperscript{8} And that whosoever; forfeited Heb. devoted; himself separated \textsuperscript{9} the ninth month That is, some time in December, which is the coldest and most rainy time of the year in Palestine. Dr. Russel, in his account of the weather at Aleppo, which very much resembles that in Judea, says, that the natives reckon the severity of the winter, which they call marbania, to last but forty days, beginning from the 12th of December, and ending the 20th of January, and that this computation comes in fact very near the truth, and that the air during this time is excessively piercing, even to those that are just come from a cold climate.; trembling; great rain Heb. showers \textsuperscript{10} taken Heb. caused to dwell, or, brought back to increase \textsuperscript{11} make confession; do his; separate; and from the \textsuperscript{12} As thou hast said They all resolved to do what Ezra had commanded; and they did put away their wives, even those by whom they had children ( ), each of whom doubtless received a portion according to the circumstances of her husband, and was not turned away desolate. Humanity must have dictated this, and no law of God is contrary to humanity. so must we do \textsuperscript{13} the people; we are many that have transgressed in this thing or, we have greatly offended in this thing \textsuperscript{14} our rulers; the fierce; for this matter be turned from us or, be turned from us, till this matter be dispatched. \textsuperscript{15} were employed Heb. stood Meshullam, Shabbethai \textsuperscript{17} am 3548, bc 456 the first day The cases brought before the council were either so many, or so complicated, that, though they separated themselves from other employments, yet they were three whole months in examining into their affairs, and making the necessary separations required by the law. \textsuperscript{18} the sons; Jeshua, ; Joshua Maaseiah \textsuperscript{19} gave their hands They bound themselves in the most solemn manner to do as the rest of the delinquents had done, and make and acknowledgment to God of their iniquity, by offering each a ram for a trespass offering.; *marg.; a ram \textsuperscript{25} Moreover of Israel That is, as Calmet observes, simple Israelites; thus distinguished from the priests, Levites, and singers, mentioned in, . sons of Parosh \textsuperscript{31} Harim; Malchiah This variation only exists in the translation, the original being uniformly Malchijah, or rather, Malkeeyah., Malchijah \textsuperscript{40} Machnadebai or, Mabnadebai, according to some copies \textsuperscript{44} strange wives, and some of them This observation was probably intended to shew that only a few of them had children, and also how rigorously the law was put in execution. According to a passage in Justin Martyr's Dialogue with Trypho, a Jew, Ezra offered a paschal lamb on this occasion, and addressed the people thus: "And Ezra said to the people, This pass-over is our Saviour and our Refuge; and if ye will be persuaded of it, and let it enter into your hearts, that we are to humble to Him in a sign, and afterwards shall believe in Him, this place shall not be destroyed forever, saith the Lord of hosts; but, if ye will not believe in Him, nor hearken to his preaching, ye shall be a laughing-stock to the Gentiles." This was probably a marginal note added by some early Christian.\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 1}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The words of Neemias the son of Chelcia. And it came to pass in the month Chaseleu, of the twentieth year, that I was in Susan the palace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Anani, one of my brethren, came, he and [some] men of Juda; and I asked them concerning those that had escaped, who had been left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they said to me, The remnant, [even] those that are left of the captivity, [are] there in the land, in great distress and reproach: and the walls of Jerusalem [are] thrown down, and its gates are burnt with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass, when I heard these words, [that] I sat down and wept, and mourned for [several] days, and continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I said, Nay, I pray you, O Lord God of heaven, the mighty, the great and terrible, keeping your covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to those that keep his commandments: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} let now your ear be attentive, and your eyes open, that you may hear the prayer of your servant, which I pray before you at this time, this day [both] day and night, for the children of Israel your servants, and make confession for the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against you: both I and the house of my father have sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} We have altogether broken [covenant] with you, and we have not kept the commandments, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which you did command your servant Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remember, I pray you, the word wherewith you did charge your servant Moses, saying, If you⌃ break covenant [with me], I will disperse you among the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But if you⌃ turn again to me, and keep my commandments, and do them; if you⌃ should be scattered under the utmost [bound] of heaven, thence will I gather them, and I will bring them into the place which I have chosen to cause my name to dwell there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now they [are] your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed with your great power, and with your strong hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [Turn] not [away], I pray you, O Lord, but let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants, who desire to fear your name: and prosper, I pray you, your servant this day, and cause him to find mercy in the sight of this man. Now I was the king's cupbearer.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Hanani I asked, that had escaped \textsuperscript{3} the province; in great; , reproach; , the wall \textsuperscript{4} I sat down; the God \textsuperscript{6} thine ear; day and night; confess; both I \textsuperscript{7} dealt; corruptly; the commandments;, ; which thou \textsuperscript{9} if ye turn; yet will I; will bring; the place \textsuperscript{10} Now these; whom; thy strong \textsuperscript{11} Let now; who desire; grant; For I was The office of cup-bearer was one of great trust, honour, and emolument, in the Persian court. To be in such a place of trust he must have been in the king's confidence; for no eastern potentate would have a cup-bearer to whom he could not trust his life, poison being often administered in that way. It was an office much desired, because it gave access to the king in those seasons of hilarity when men are most disposed to grant favours.\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 2}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the month Nisan of the twentieth year of king Arthasastha, that the wine was before me: and I took the wine, and gave [it] to the king: and there was not another before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king said to me, Why is your countenance sad, and do you not control yourself? and now this is nothing but sorrow of heart. Then I was very much alarmed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and I said to the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be said, forasmuch as the city, even the home of the sepulchres of my fathers, has been laid waste, and her gates have been devoured with fire? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king said to me, For what do you ask thus? So I prayed to the God of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I said to the king, If [it seem] good to the king, and if your servant shall have found favor in your sight, [I ask] that [you] would send him into Juda, to the city of the sepulchres of my fathers; then will I rebuild it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the king, and his concubine that sat next to him, said to me, For how long will your journey be, and when will you return? and [the proposal] was pleasing before the king, and he sent me away, and I appointed him a time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I said to the king, If [it seem] good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the river, so as to forward me till I come to Juda; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the garden which belongs to the king, that he may give me timber to cover the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for the house into which I shall enter. And the king gave to me, according as the good hand of God [was upon me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I came to the governors beyond the river, and I gave them the king's letters. (Now the king had sent with me captains of the army and horsemen.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Sanaballat the Aronite heard [it], and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and it was grievous to them that a man was come to seek good for the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I rose up by night, I and a few men with me; and I told no man what God put into my heart to do with Israel; and there was no beast with me, except the beast which I rode upon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I went forth by the gate of the valley by night, and to the mouth of the well of fig trees, and to the dung-gate: and I mourned over the wall of Jerusalem which they were destroying, and her gates were devoured with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I passed on to the fountain gate, and to the king's pool; and there was no room for the beast to pass under me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I went up by the wall of the brook by night, and mourned over the wall, and passed through the gate of the valley, and returned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the sentinels knew not why I went, nor what I was doing; and until that time I told [it] not to the Jews, or to the priests, or to the nobles, or to the captains, or to the rest [of the men] who wrought the works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then I said to them, You⌃ see this evil, in which we are, how Jerusalem is desolate, and her gates have been set on fire: come, and let us build throughout the wall of Jerusalem, and we shall be no longer a reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I told them of the hand of God which was good upon me, also about the words of the king which he spoke to me: and I said, Let us arise and build. And their hands were strengthened for the good [work]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Sanaballat the Aronite, and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and Gesam the Arabian, heard [it], and they laughed us to scorn, and came to us, and said, What [is] this thing that you⌃ are doing? are you⌃ revolting against the king? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And I answered them, and said to them, The God of heaven, he shall prosper us, and we his servants are pure, and we will build: but you⌃ have no part, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Nisan the twentieth; I took up \textsuperscript{2} Why is thy sorrow Then I Probably the king spoke as if he had some suspicion that Nehemiah harboured some bad design, and that his face indicated some conceived treachery, or remorse; and, indeed, the words rendered sad, and sorrow of heart, might be rendered evil, and wickedness of heart. \textsuperscript{3} Let the king Far from wishing ill to my master, I wish him to live forever.;, the city; the place \textsuperscript{4} For what; So I prayed \textsuperscript{5} If it please;, and if thy \textsuperscript{6} the queen Heb. the wife, It was probably Esther who was present at this time, and who seconded Nehemiah's request. So it pleased;, I set him a time It is probable that this time was no more than six months, or a year; after which he either returned, or had his leave of absence lengthened, as we find he was twelve years governor of the Jews. \textsuperscript{7} let letters; that they may \textsuperscript{8} the wall, the house, the king \textsuperscript{9} to the governors Now the \textsuperscript{10} Sanballat, Horonite; the servant; the Ammonite it grieved; , there was come \textsuperscript{12} I arose; neither; my God This pious and noble-minded man attributes every thing to God. If he purposed any good, it was because God put it into his heart; if he did or received any good, it was because the good hand of his God was upon him; if he expected any good, it was because he earnestly prayed God to remember him for good. \textsuperscript{13} the gate; the dung port This was the gate on the eastern side of the city, through which the filth was carried to the brook Kidron and valley of Hinnom., the walls \textsuperscript{14} the gate of the fountain The gate leading either to the fountain of Siloam, on the east of the city, or to that of Gihon, on the west.; the king's pool Probably the aqueduct made by Hezekiah to bring the waters of Gihon to the city of David. \textsuperscript{15} the brook The brook Kidron; the gate The gate leading to the valley of Jehoshaphat, east of the city, through which the brook Kidron flows. It was by this gate he went out; so that he went round the whole of the city, and entered by the same gate. \textsuperscript{17} Ye see, come; a reproach \textsuperscript{18} the hand So they strengthened \textsuperscript{19} Sanballat, Geshem, Gashmu they; will ye rebel \textsuperscript{20} The God;, ; ye have no; memorial; When Nehemiah had prayed for the relief of his countrymen, and perhaps in David's words, he did not sit still and say, "Let God now do his own work, for I have no more to do; " but set himself to do what he could towards it; and here we find that the people were of one heart with Nehemiah. Our prayers must be seconded with our serious endeavours, or else we mock God. Nearly four months had passed, namely, from Chisleu to Nisan (November to March), before Nehemiah made his application to the king for leave to go to Jerusalem; either because the winter was not a proper time for such a journey, and he would not make a motion till he could pursue it, or because it was so long before his month of waiting upon the king came, and there was no coming into his presence until called for, . We are not thus limited to certain moments in our addresses to the King of kings, but have liberty of access to him at all times; to the throne of grace we never come unseasonably.\par}
