\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 3}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Eliasub the high priest, and his brethren the priests, rose up, and built the sheep-gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even to the tower of the hundred they sanctified [it], to the tower of Anameel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And [they builded] by the side of the men of Jericho, and by the side of the sons of Zacchur, the son of Amari. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the sons of Asana built the fish-gate; they roofed it, and covered in its doors, and bolts, and bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And next to them [the order] reached to Ramoth the son of Uria, the son of Accos, and next to them Mosollam son of Barachias the son of Mazebel took [his] place: and next to them Sadoc the son of Baana took [his] place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And next to them the Thecoim took [their] place; but the Adorim applied not their neck to their service. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Joida the son of Phasec, and Mesulam son of Basodia, repaired the old gate; they covered it in, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And next to them repaired Maltias the Gabaonite, and Evaron the Meronothite, the men of Gabaon and Maspha, to the throne of the governor on this side the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And next to him Oziel the son of Arachias of the smiths, carried on the repairs: and next to them Ananias the son of one of the apothecaries repaired, and they finished Jerusalem to the broad wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And next to them repaired Raphaea the son of Sur, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And next to them repaired Jedaia the son of Eromaph, and [that] in front of his house: and next to him repaired Attuth son of Asabania. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And next [to him] repaired Melchias son of Heram, and Asub son of Phaat Moab, even to the tower of the furnaces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And next to him repaired Sallum the son of Alloes, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem, he and his daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Anun and the inhabitants of Zano repaired the gate of the valley: they built it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the dung-gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Melchia the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district round about Beth-accharim, repaired the dung-gate, he and his sons; and they covered it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But Solomon the son of Choleze repaired the gate of the fountain, the ruler of part of Maspha; he built it, and covered it, and set up its doors and its bars, and the wall of the pool of the skins by the meadow of the king, and as far as the steps that lead down from the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} After him repaired Neemias son of Azabuch, ruler of half the district round about Bethsur, as far as the garden of David's sepulchre, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} After him repaired the Levites, [even] Raum the son of Bani: next to him repaired Asabia, ruler of half the district round about Keila, in his district. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And after him repaired his brethren, Benei son of Enadad, ruler of half the district round about Keila. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And next to him repaired Azur the son of Joshua, ruler of Masphai, another portion of the tower of ascent, where it meets the corner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} After him repaired Baruch the son of Zabu, a second portion, from the corner as far as the door of the house of Eliasub the high priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} After him repaired Meramoth the son of Uria the son of Accos, a second part from the door of the house of Eliasub, to the end of the house of Eliasub. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And after him repaired the priests, the men of Ecchechar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And after him repaired Benjamin and Asub over against their house: and after him repaired Azarias son of Maasias the son of Ananias, [the parts] near to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} After him repaired Bani the son of Adad, another portion from the house of Azaria as far as the corner and to the turning, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} of Phalach the son of Uzai, opposite the corner, and [where is] also the tower that projects from the king's house, even the upper one of the prison-house: and after him [repaired] Phadaea the son of Phoros. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the Nathinim lived in Ophal, as far as the garden of the water-gate eastward, and [there is] the projecting tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And after them the Thecoim repaired, another portion opposite the great projecting tower, even as far as the wall of Ophla. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The priests repaired above the horse-gate, [every] man over against his own house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And after him Sadduc the son of Emmer repaired opposite his own house: and after him repaired Samaea son of Sechenia, guard of the east-gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} After him repaired Anania son of Selemia, and Anom, the sixth son of Seleph, another portion: after him Mesulam the son of Barachia repaired over against his treasury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} After him repaired {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And between [that and] the sheep-gate the smiths and chapmen repaired.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Eliashib, the sheep gate This gate is supposed to have immediately communicated with the temple, and to have been called the sheep gate, because the sheep intended for sacrifice passed through it. But, after all which learned men have written on this subject, which is but of little interest, we scarcely know anything about these gates. What they were, why called by these names, or in what part of the wall they were situated, beyond what may be learned from the parallel passages.; sanctified it; *title, the tower \textsuperscript{2} next unto him Heb. at his hand the men; Zaccur \textsuperscript{3} the fish gate; the beams, the doors \textsuperscript{5} the Tekoites; their nobles; put not \textsuperscript{7} the Gibeonite; Mizpah; the throne That is, probably, the palace of the Persian governor, west of the Euphrates; the term throne being used to signify any royal abode. For Sir J. Chardin, describing a splendid tent erected by the king of Persia, says "that there was an inscription wrought upon the cornice of the anti-chamber, which gave it the appellation of the throne of the second Solomon." Sitting upon a throne has, however, sometimes been granted to governors. \textsuperscript{8} the goldsmiths; of the apothecaries; fortified or, left the broad wall \textsuperscript{11} Harim Pahathmoab; other piece Heb. second measure the tower \textsuperscript{12} the ruler, he and his daughters \textsuperscript{13} the valley gate Zanoah There were two towns of the name of Zanoah in the tribe of Judah. See the parallel passages. \textsuperscript{14} the dung gate, the ruler, Bethhaccerem Beth-haccerem was a town of Judah, situated on a mountain, between Jerusalem and Tekoa, according to Jerome on . Dr. Pococke conjectures that the Mountain of the Franks, called also the Mount of Bethulia, from a village of that name near it, west-north-west of Tekoa, is the ancient Beth-haccerem; the position of which seems to agree with the citadel of Herodium, built by Herod, on a moderate-sized hill, sixty furlongs from Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{15} the gate; the ruler, Mizpah;, Mizpeh, Siloah was situated under the eastern wall of Jerusalem, between that city and the brook Kedron, and is described by Chateaubriand as lying at the foot of Mount Zion. Dr. Richardson represents the pool of Siloam as occurring higher up the valley of Jehoshaphat, towards the north, than the well of Nehemiah, a little beyond the village of Siloa, and nearly opposite the tombs of Jehoshaphat and Zechariah., Shiloah; Siloam the stairs \textsuperscript{16} the ruler, Bethzur; the sepulchres; the pool; the house \textsuperscript{20} Zabbai or, Zaccai earnestly; Eliashib \textsuperscript{22} the men of the plain \textsuperscript{24} Binnui another piece That which had been left by Azariah, after he had repaired the wall by his own house. It is probable that some of the principal people were either obliged, or voluntarily offered, to repair those parts of the wall which were opposite, or adjacent, to their own houses. The names of those who repaired the walls are commemorated, because it was an undertaking of piety, virtue, and courage, to restore the holy city., the turning \textsuperscript{25} the king's, by the court;, Pedaiah Parosh \textsuperscript{26} Nethinims; dwelt etc. or, which dwelt in Ophel, repaired unto Ophel or, the tower.; the water The water gate is supposed to have been that by which the Nethinim brought in water for the use of the temple. \textsuperscript{29} the son; Shechaniah the east gate \textsuperscript{31} the goldsmith's, going up of the corner or, corner-chamber \textsuperscript{32} the sheep gate Thus the whole city was surrounded with a wall; for Eliashib began at the sheep gate.; the goldsmiths The word tzeraphim may denote smiths, or refiners, or persons that worked in metals of any kind; but it is generally understood of those who worked in gold. From the remotest period of the history of the Jews, they had artists in all the elegant and ornamental trades; and it appears that goldsmiths, apothecaries, and merchants were formed into companies in the time of Nehemiah.\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 4}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, that it was grievous to him, and he was very angry, and railed against the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said before his brethren (that [is] the army of the Samaritans) [Is it true] that these Jews are building their city? do they indeed offer sacrifices? will they prevail? and will they this day restore the stones, after they have been burnt and made a heap of rubbish? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Tobias the Ammanite came near to him, and said to them, Do they sacrifice or eat in their place? shall not a fox go up and pull down their wall of stones? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Hear, O our God, for we have become a scorn; and return you their reproach upon their head, and make them a scorn in a land of captivity, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and do not cover [their] iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But it came to pass, when Sanaballat and Tobia, and the Arabians, and the Ammanites, heard that the building of the walls of Jerusalem was advancing, [and] that the breaches began to be stopped, that it appeared very grievous to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And all of them assembled together, to come to fight against Jerusalem, and to destroy it utterly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So we prayed to our God and set watchmen against them day and night, because of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Juda said, The strength of the enemies is broken, yet [there is] much rubbish, and we shall not be able to build the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they that afflicted us said, They shall not know, and they shall not see, until we come into the midst of them, and kill them, and cause the work to cease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it came to pass, when the Jews who lived near them came, that they said to us, They are coming up against us from every quarter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So I set [men] in the lowest part of the place behind the wall in the lurking-places, I even set the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I looked, and arose, and said to the nobles, and to the captains, and to the rest of the people, Be not afraid of them: remember our great and terrible God, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it was made known to us, and God had frustrated their counsel, that we all returned to the wall, [every] man to his work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass from that day [that] half of them that had been driven forth, wrought the work, and half of them kept guard; and [there were] spears, and shields, and bows, and breastplates, and rulers behind the whole house of Juda, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} even of them that were building the wall:—and those who carried the burdens [were] under arms: [each] with one hand wrought his work, and with the other held his dart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the builders [wrought] each man having his sword girded upon his loins, and so they built: and the trumpeter with his trumpet next to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And I said to the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, The work [is] great and abundant, and we are dispersed upon the wall, each at a great distance from his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In whatever place you⌃ shall hear the sound of the cornet, there gather yourselves together to us; and our God shall fight for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So we [continued] laboring at the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appeared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And at that time I said to the people, Lodge you⌃ every man with his servant in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be a watch-time to you, and the day a work-time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I was [there], and the watchmen behind me, and there was not a man of us that put off his garments.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the army feeble; fortify themselves Heb. leave to themselves sacrifice, revive \textsuperscript{4} Hear despised Heb. despite turn \textsuperscript{5} cover not, ; their sin; before the builders \textsuperscript{7} Sanballat, the Ammonites; Ashdodites; heard, were made up Heb. ascended then \textsuperscript{8} all; hinder it Heb. make an error to it \textsuperscript{12} ten times; From all places etc. or, That from all places ye must return to us ye shall return Houbigant, Michaelis, and Dathe contend, that instead of tashoovoo, "ye shall return, " we should read chashevoo, "they designed." \textsuperscript{13} Therefore; in the lower places Heb. from the lower parts of the place, etc. their swords. \textsuperscript{14} Be ye not afraid; remember, ; great; fight \textsuperscript{16} my servants; and the other half This is no unusual thing in Palestine, even at the present day; people sowing their seed are often attended by armed men, to prevent the Arabs from robbing them of it. habergeons Habergeon, from the Teutonic hals, the neck, and bergen, to cover, defend, may be considered as signifying a breast-plate, though the Franco-Gallic hautbergon signifies a coat of mail; the original shiryon, we have already seen, denotes a corslet. \textsuperscript{17} bare burdens every one That is, he had his arms at hand; and was as fully prepared to fight as to work. The builders could not possibly have made any progress, if they had literally held a weapon in one of their hands; but the expression is evidently figurative, implying that every man was a much a soldier as a builder. with one \textsuperscript{18} by his side Heb. on his loins he that sounded \textsuperscript{23} So neither I; saving that etc. or, every one went with his weapon for water; The original of this obscure clause is ish shilcho hammayim, which is rendered by Montanus, vir missile suum aquas, "a man his dart to the waters, " of which it is difficult to make sense. It is wholly omitted by the LXX; and one of De Rossi's manuscripts reads, meshallachah al hammayim, "in order to send them to the water."\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 5}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the cry of the people and their wives [was] great against their brethren the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And some said, We [are] numerous with our sons and our daughters; so we will take corn, and eat, and live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And some said, [As to] our fields and vineyards and houses, let us pledge [them], and we will take corn, and eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And some said, We have borrowed money for the king's tributes:—our fields, and our vineyards, and houses [are pledged]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And now our flesh [is] as the flesh of our brethren, our children [are] as their children: yet, behold, we are reducing our sons and our daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are enslaved: and there is no power of our hands, for our fields and our vineyards [belong] to the nobles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I was much grieved as I heard their cry and these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended against the nobles, and the princes, and I said to them, Should every man demand of his brother what you⌃ demand? And I appointed against them a great assembly, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and I said to them, We of our free-will have redeemed our brethren the Jews that were sold to the Gentiles; and do you⌃ sell your brethren? and shall they be delivered to us? And they were silent, and found no answer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I said, The thing which you⌃ do [is] not good; you⌃ will not so walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the Gentiles our enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Both my brethren, and my acquaintances, and I, have lent them money and corn: let us now leave off this exaction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Restore to them, I pray, as at this day, their fields, and their vineyards, and their olive yards, and their houses, and bring forth to them corn and wine and oil of the money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they said, We will restore, and we will not exact of them; we will do thus as you say. Then I called the priests, and bound them by oath to do according to this word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I shook out my garment, and said, So may God shake out every man who shall not keep to this word, from his house, and from his labors, he shall be even thus shaken out, as an outcast and empty. And all the congregation said, Amen, and they praised the Lord: and the people did this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} From the day that he charged me to be their ruler in the land of Juda, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years, I and my brethren ate not [provision] extorted from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But as for the former acts of extortion wherein [those who were] before me oppressed them, they even took of them their last money, forty didrachmas for bread and wine; and the [very] outcasts of them exercised authority over the people: but I did not so, because of the fear of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Also in the work of the wall I treated them not with rigor, I bought not land: and all that were gathered together [came] there to the work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Jews, to [the number of] one hundred and fifty men, besides those coming to us from the nations round about, [were] at my table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And there came [to me] for one day one calf, and I had six choice sheep and a goat; and every ten days wine in abundance of all sorts: yet with these I required not the bread of extortion, because the bondage was heavy upon this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Remember me, O God, for good, [in] all that I have done to this people.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a great cry; their brethren \textsuperscript{2} our sons; we take up corn \textsuperscript{7} I consulted with myself Heb. my heart consulted in me, I rebuked; Ye exact usury; I set a great assembly \textsuperscript{8} We after; redeemed sell your; shall they; held \textsuperscript{9} It is not;, walk; reproach \textsuperscript{10} I likewise; I pray you, ; leave \textsuperscript{11} Restore; their lands the hundredth This was probably the rate of interest which they obliged their poor debtors to pay each month, which would amount to about 12 percent. Another author states that this is the lowest rate of interest in Syria. The usual rate is 20; and it is sometimes as high as 30 percent. \textsuperscript{12} We will restore; I called \textsuperscript{13} I shook my lap So "when the Roman ambassadors entered the senate of Carthage, they had their toga gathered up in their bosom, and said, We carry here peace and war; you may have which you will. The senate answered, You may give which you please. They then shook their toga, and said, We bring you war." - Livy.; So God; emptied Heb. empty, or void Amen; praised the people \textsuperscript{14} from the twentieth, I and my; the bread \textsuperscript{15} even their; so did; because \textsuperscript{16} I continued; neither bought; all my \textsuperscript{17} Moreover He kept open house, and entertained all comers; besides having 150; Jews, who had their food constantly at his table, and at his expense. at my table; an hundred \textsuperscript{18} Now that one ox This was food sufficient for more than two hundred men. Bp. Pococke says that the bey of Tunis had daily twelve sheep, with fish and fowls, soups, oranges, eggs, onions, boiled rice, etc., etc. His nobles dined with him; after they had done, the servants sat down; and when they had finished, the poor took what was left. Here the bey's twelve sheep are equal to Nehemiah's one ox and six choice sheep; and probably the mode of living between the two was nearly alike. It is still the practice in the East to calculate the expenses of the table, not by the money paid, but by the provisions consumed by the guests. required because the bondage\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 6}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat, and Tobias, and Gesam the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies, heard that I had built the wall, and [that] there was no opening left therein; ([but] hitherto I had not set up the doors on the gates;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that Sanaballat and Gesam sent to me, saying, Come and let us meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono. But they [were] plotting to do me mischief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So I sent messengers to them, saying, I am doing a great work, and I shall not be able to come down, lest the work should cease: as soon as I shall have finished it, I will come down to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they sent to me [again] to this effect; and I sent them [word] accordingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then Sanaballat sent his servant to me with an open letter in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And in it was written, It has been reported among the Gentiles that you and the Jews are planning to revolt: therefore you are building the wall, and you will be a king to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And moreover you have appointed prophets to yourself, that you might dwell in Jerusalem as a king over Juda: and now these words will be reported to the king. Now then, come, let us take counsel together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I sent to him, saying, It has not happened according to these words, [even] as you say, for you frame them falsely out of your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For all were trying to alarm us, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from this work, and it shall not be done. Now therefore I have strengthened my hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I came into the house of Semei the son of Dalaia the Son of Metabeel, and he was shut up; and he said, Let us assemble together in the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut the doors of it; for they are coming by night to kill you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I said, Who is the man that shall enter into the house, that he may live? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I observed, and, behold, God had not sent him, for the prophecy was a fable [devised] against me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and Tobias and Sanaballat had hired against me a multitude, that I might be frightened, and do this, and sin, and become to them an ill name, that they might reproach me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Remember, O God, Tobias and Sanaballat, according to these their deeds, and the prophetess Noadia, and the rest of the prophets who tried to alarm me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the [month] Elul, in fifty-two days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass, when all our enemies heard [of it], that all the nations round about us feared, and great alarm fell upon them, and they knew that it was of our God that this work should be finished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And in those days letters came to Tobias from many nobles of Juda, and those of Tobias came to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For many in Juda were bound to him by oath, because he was son-in-law of Sechenias the son of Herae; and Jonan his son had taken the daughter of Mesulam the son of Barachia to wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they reported his words to me, and carried out my words to him: and Tobias sent letters to terrify me.\par

the original being uniformly Paseah., Paseah \textsuperscript{52} Meunim The first of these variations is attributable to the translation, the original being uniformly, ξςεπιν, Meunim; and the latter arises from the mutation of, ε, wav, and, ι, yood, and insertion of, ωΡ, sheen, though in the parallel passage the Kethiv is πτιριν, Nephisim; and here the Keri and many manuscripts have πτιωΡριν, Nephishesim ., Mehunim, Nephusim \textsuperscript{54} Bazlith Instead of Bazlith, many manuscripts and the LXX have Bazluth, as in the parallel place., Bazluth \textsuperscript{55} Tamah Here there is no variation in the original; it being uniformly Tamah., Thamah \textsuperscript{57} Solomon's Perida Three manuscripts have Peruda, instead of Perida, as in Ezra., Peruda \textsuperscript{58} Jaala The variation of ιςμδ, Jaalah, and ιςμΰ, Jaala, merely arises from the mutation of δ, hay, into ΰ, aleph, according to the Chaldee dialect., Jaalah \textsuperscript{59} Amon Instead of Amon, two of De Rossi's manuscripts have Amin, and the LXX have Ημιμ, Emim; which nearly approaches the Ami of Ezra., Ami \textsuperscript{61} Telharesha The first of these variations only exists in the translation; the original being uniformly ϊμ ηψωΡΰ, Tel̇harshà the latter simply arises from the insertion of a ε, wav; being written ΰγο, Addan, in the parallel passage, and ΰγεο, Addon, here., Tel-harsa, Addan seed or, pedigree \textsuperscript{64} These sought those that were; but it was as polluted \textsuperscript{65} the Tirshatha or, the governor, ; that they should, till there \textsuperscript{69} Here Jerome adds, in the Vulgate, Hucusque refertur quid in commentario scriptum fuerit; exin Nehemie historia texitur̀ "Thus far do the words extend which were written in the register; what follows belongs to the history of Nehemiah." This addition is not found in the Hebrew, or any ancient version. It is also wanting in the Paris and Complutensian Polyglotts; but is found in the Editio Prima of the Vulgate. What follows, however, seems to relate to a distinct oblation from that recorded in Ezra; and was probably made after the people were registered by Nehemiah, who was the Tirshatha, or governor, at this time, as Zerubbabel had been at the first return of the Jews from captivity. Blessed be God that our faith and hope are not built upon the niceties of names and numbers, genealogy and chronology, but on the great things of the law and gospel. Whatever is given to the work of God and his cause will surely be remembered by him ( ). \textsuperscript{70} some Heb. part, the chief; The Tirshatha, drams Darkemonim, or darics; a Persian gold coin, worth about 1£. 5s. basins \textsuperscript{71} chief; pound Manim, manehs or minas, As a weight, the maneh was equal to 100 shekels; but as a coin, equal to 60 shekels, or about 9£. \textsuperscript{73} all Israel It was for the purpose of ascertaining the different families, and consequently the different cities, villages, etc., which belonged to them, according to the ancient division of the land, that the public registers were examined. when the seventh\par}

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 8}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the seventh month arrived, and the children of Israel [were settled] in their cities; and all the people were gathered as one man to the broad place before the water-gate, and they told Esdras the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord commanded Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} So Esdras the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and every one who had understanding [was present] to listen, on the first day of the seventh month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he read in it from the time of sunrise to the middle of the day, before the men and the women; and they understood [it], and the ears of all the people [were attentive] to the book of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Esdras the scribe stood on a wooden stage, and there stood next to him Mattathias, and Samaeas, and Ananias, and Urias, and Chelcia, and Massia, on his right hand; and on his left Phadaeas, and Misael, and Melchias, and Asom, and Asabadma, and Zacharias, and Mesollam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Esdras opened the book before all the people, for he was above the people; and it came to pass when he had opened it, [that] all the people stood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esdras blessed the Lord, the great God: and all the people answered, and said, Amen, lifting up their hands: and they bowed down and worshipped the Lord with their face to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jesus and Banaias and Sarabias instructed the people in the law, and the people [stood] in their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they read in the book of the law of God, and Esdras taught, and instructed them distinctly in the knowledge of the Lord, and the people understood [the law] in the reading. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Neemias, and Esdras the priest and scribe, and the Levites, and they that instructed the people, spoke and said to all the people, It is a holy day to the Lord our God; do not mourn, nor weep. For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And [the governor] said to them, Go, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to them that have nothing; for the day is holy to our Lord: and faint not, for the Lord is our strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Levites caused all the people to be silent, saying, Be silent, for [it is] a holy day, and despond not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So all the people departed to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, for they understood the words which he made known to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And on the second day the heads of families assembled with all the people, [also] the priests and Levites, to Esdras the scribe, to attend to all the words of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they found written in the law which the Lord commanded Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths, in the feast in the seventh month: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and that they should sound with trumpets in all their cities, and in Jerusalem. And Esdras said, Go forth to the mountain, and bring branches of olive, and branches of cypress trees, and branches of myrtle, and branches of palm trees, and branches of [every] thick tree, to make booths, according to that which was written. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the people went forth, and brought [them], and made booths for themselves, each one upon his roof, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the streets of the city, and as far as the gate of Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And all the congregation who had returned from the captivity, made booths, and lived in booths: for the children of Israel [had] not done so from the days of Jesus the son of Naue until that day: and there was great joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And [Esdras] read in the book of the law of God daily, from the first day even to the last day: and they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.\par

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 9}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel assembled with fasting, and in sackcloths, and with ashes on their head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the children of Israel separated themselves from every stranger, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they stood in their place, and read in the book of the law of the Lord their god: and they confessed [their sins] to the Lord, and worshipped the Lord their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [And] there stood upon the stairs, of the Levites, Jesus, and the sons of Cadmiel, Sechenia the son of Sarabia, sons of Choneni; and they cried with a loud voice to the Lord their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Levites, Jesus and Cadmiel, said, Rise up, bless the Lord our God forever and ever: and let them bless your glorious name, and exalt it with all blessing and praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esdras said, You are the only true Lord; you made the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, and all their array, the earth, and all things that are in it, the seas, and all things in them; and you quicken all things, and the hosts of heaven worship you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You are the Lord God, you did choose Abram, and brought him out of the land of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name of Abraam: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and you found his heart faithful before you, and did make a covenant with him to give to him and to his seed the land of the Chananites, and the Chettites, and Amorites, and Pherezites, and Jebusites, and Gergesites; and you have confirmed your words, for you [are] righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and you heard their cry at the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you showed signs and wonders in Egypt, on Pharao and all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for you know that they behaved insolently against them: and you made yourself a name, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you did cleave the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry land; and you did cast into the deep them that were about to pursue them, as a stone in the mighty water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you guided them by day by a pillar of cloud, and by night by a pillar of fire, to enlighten for them the way wherein they should walk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Also you came down upon mount Sina, and you spoke to them out of heaven, and gave them right judgments, and laws of truth, ordinances, and good commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you did make known to them your holy sabbath; you did enjoin upon them commandments, and ordinances, and a law, by the hand of your servant Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you gave them bread from heaven for their food, and you brought them forth water from a rock for their thirst; and you bade them go in to inherit the land over which you stretched out your hand to give [it] them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But they and our fathers behaved proudly, and hardened their neck, and did not listen to your commandments, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and refused to listen, and remembered not your wonders which you wrought with them; and they hardened their neck, and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt: but you, O God, [are] merciful and compassionate, longsuffering, and abundant in mercy, and you did not forsake them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And still farther they even made to themselves a molten calf, and said, These [are] the gods that brought us up out of Egypt: and they wrought great provocations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Yet you in your great compassions did not forsake them in the wilderness: you did not turn away from them the pillar of the cloud by day, to guide them in the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to enlighten for them the way wherein they should walk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And you gave your good Spirit to instruct them, and you did not withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water in their thirst. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you did sustain them forty years in the wilderness; you did not allow anything to fail them: their garments did not wax old, and their feet were not bruised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Moreover, you gave them kingdoms, and did divide nations to them: and they inherited the land of Seon king of Esebon, and the land of Og king of Basan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you did multiply their children as the stars of heaven, and brought them into the land of which you spoke to their fathers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they inherited it: and you did destroy from before them the dwellers in the land of the Chananites, and you gave into their hands them and their kings, and the nations of the land, to do to them as it pleased them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they took lofty cities, and inherited houses full of all good things, wells dug, vineyards, and olive yards, and every fruit tree in abundance: so they ate, and were filled, and grew fat, and rioted in your great goodness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But they turned, and revolted from you, and cast your law behind their backs; and they killed your prophets, who testified against them to turn them back to you, and they wrought great provocations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then you gave them into the hand of them that afflicted them, and they did afflict them: and they cried to you in the time of their affliction, and you did hear them from your heaven, and in your great compassions gave them deliverers, and did save them from the hand of them that afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But when they rested, they did evil again before you: so you left them in the hands of their enemies, and they ruled over them: and they cried again to you, and you heard [them] from heaven, and did deliver them in your great compassions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you did testify against them, to bring them back to your law: but they listened not, but sinned against your commandments and your judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them; and they turned their back, and hardened their neck, and heard not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Yet you did bear long with them many years, and did testify to them by your Spirit by the hand of your prophets: but they listened not; so you gave them into the hand of the nations of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But you in your many mercies did not appoint them to destruction, and did not forsake them; for you are strong, and merciful, and pitiful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And now, O our God, the powerful, the great, the mighty, and the terrible, keeping your covenant and your mercy, let not all the trouble seem little in your sight which has come upon us, and our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, and upon all your people, from the days of the kings of Assur even to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But you [are] righteous in all the things that come upon us; for you have wrought faithfully, but we have greatly sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our fathers, have not performed your law, and have not given heed to your commandments, and [have not kept] your testimonies which you did testify to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they did not serve you in your kingdom, and in your great goodness which you gave to them, and in the large and fat land which you did furnish before them, and they turned not from their evil devices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Behold, we are servants this day, and [as for] the land which you gave to our fathers to eat the fruit of it and the good things of it, behold, we are servants upon it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} and its produce [is] abundant for the kings whom you did appoint over us because of our sins; and they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, as it pleases them, and we are in great affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And in regard to all these circumstances we make a covenant, and write [it], and our princes, our Levites, [and] our priests, set their seal to [it].\par

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 10}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And over them that sealed were Neemias the Artasastha, son of Achalia, and Zedekias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} the son of Araea, and Azaria, and Jeremia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Phasur, Amaria, Melchia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Attus, Sebani, Maluch, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Iram, Meramoth, Abdia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Daniel, Gannathon, Baruch, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Mesulam, Abia, Miamin, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Maazia, Belgai, Samaia; these [were] priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Levites; Jesus the son of Azania, Banaiu of the sons of Enadad, Cadmiel {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and his brethren, Sabania, Oduia, Calitan, Phelia, Anan, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Micha, Roob, Asebias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Zacchor, Sarabia, Sebania, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Odum, the sons of Banuae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The heads of the people; Phoros, Phaath Moab, Elam, Zathuia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} the sons of Bani, Asgad, Bebai, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Adania, Bagoi, Hedin {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Ater, Ezekia, Azur, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Oduia, Esam, Besi, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Ariph, Anathoth, Nobai, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Megaphes, Mesullam, Ezir, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Mesozebel, Saduc, Jeddua, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Phaltia, Anan, Anaea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Osee, Anania, Asub, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Aloes, Phalai, Sobec, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Reum, Essabana, Maasia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and Aia, Aenan, Enam, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Maluch, Eram, Baana. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the porters, the singers, the Nathinim, and every one who drew off from the nations of the land to the law of God, their wives, their sons, their daughters, every one who had knowledge and understanding, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} were urgent with their brethren, and bound them under a curse, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses, the servant of God; to keep and to do all the commandments of the Lord, and his judgments, and his ordinances; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} and that we will not, [they said, ]give our daughters to the people of the land, nor will we take their daughters to our sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And [as for] the people of the land who bring wares and all [manner of] merchandise to sell on the sabbath-day, we [will] not buy of them on the sabbath or on the holy day: and we will leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And we will impose ordinances upon ourselves, to levy on ourselves the third part of a didrachm yearly for the service of the house of our God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} the show bread, and the continual meat-offering, and for the continual whole burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moon, for the feast, and for the holy things, and the sin-offerings, to make atonement for Israel, and for the works of the house of our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And we cast lots for the office of wood-bearing, [we] the priests, and the Levites, and the people, to bring [wood] into the house of our God, according to the house of our families, at certain set times, year by year, to burn on the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} and to bring the first fruits of our land, and the first fruits of the fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} the firstborn of our sons, and of our cattle, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, for the priests that minister in the house of our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the first fruits of our corn, and the fruit of every tree, of wine, and of oil, will we bring to the priests to the treasury of the house of God; \subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 11}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the chiefs of the people lived in Jerusalem: and the rest of the people cast lots, to bring one of [every] ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the [other] cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the people blessed all the men that volunteered to dwell in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now these [are] the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem, and in the cities of Juda; [every] man lived in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nathinim, and the children of the servants of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there lived in Jerusalem [some] of the children of Juda, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Juda; Athaia son of Azia, the son of Zacharia, the son of Samaria, the son of Saphatia, the son of Maleleel, and [some] of the sons of Phares; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and Maasia son of Baruch, son of Chalaza, son of Ozia, son of Adaia, son of Joarib, son of Zacharias, son of Seloni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} All the sons of Phares who lived in Jerusalem [were] four hundred and sixty-eight men of might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And these [were] the children of Benjamin; Selo son of Mesulam, son of Joad, son of Phadaia, son of Coleia, son of Maasias, son of Ethiel, son of Jesia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And after him Gebe, Seli, nine hundred and twenty-eight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Joel son of Zechri [was] overseer over them: and Juda son of Asana was second in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Of the priests: both Jadia son of Joarib, and Jachin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Saraia, son of Elchia, son of Mesulam, son of Sadduc, son of Marioth, son of Aetoth, was over the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And their brethren doing the work of the house were eight hundred and twenty-two: and Adaia son of Jeroam, son of Phalalia, son of Amasi, son of Zacharia, son of Phassur, son of Melchia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and his brethren, chiefs of families, two hundred and forty-two: and Amasia son of Esdriel, son of Mesarimith, son of Emmer, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and his brethren, mighty men of war, one hundred and twenty-eight: and [their] overseer [was] Badiel son of [one of the] great men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And of the Levites; {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the rulers; cast lots Jerusalem certainly had many inhabitants at this time, but not sufficient to preserve the city, which was now encompassed with a wall, the building of which was going on fast. Nehemiah, therefore, obliged one-tenth of the country people to come and dwell in it, that the population might be sufficient for the defence of the city. Some volunteered their services, which was at that time considered a sacrifice to patriotism; as Jerusalem then afforded very few advantages, and was a place of considerable danger. Hence "the people blessed them that willingly offered themselves."; one of ten the holy \textsuperscript{3} Now There is a good deal of difference between this enumeration and that in Chronicles; as this comprehends not only those who came first with Zerubbabel, but also those who came with Ezra and Nehemiah. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the sons of Levi, heads of families, [were] written in the book of the chronicles, even to the days of Joanan son of Elisue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the heads of the Levites [were] Asabia, and Sarabia, and Jesu: and the sons of Cadmiel, and their brethren over against them, were to sing hymns of praise, according to the commandment of David the man of God, course by course. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} When I gathered the porters, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [it was] in the days of Joakim son of Jesus, son of Josedec, and in the days of Neemia: and Esdras the priest [was] scribe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep a feast of dedication and gladness with thanksgiving, and they sounded cymbals with songs, and [had] lutes and harps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the sons of the singers were assembled both from the neighbourhood round about to Jerusalem, and from the villages, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and from the country: for the singers built themselves villages by Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, and the porters, and the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they brought up the princes of Juda on the wall, and they appointed two great [companies] for {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} of Ephraim, and to the fish-gate, and by the tower of Anameel, and as far as the sheep-gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the singers were heard, and were numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And in that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced; for God had made them very joyful: and their wives and their children rejoiced: and the joy in Jerusalem was heard from afar off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And in that day they appointed men over the treasuries, for the treasures, the first fruits, and the tithes, and [for] the chiefs of the cities who were assembled among them, [to furnish] portions for the priests and Levites: for [there was] joy in Juda over the priests and over the Levites that waited. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And they kept the charges of their God, and the charges of the purification, and [ordered] the singers and the porters, according to the commandments of David and his son Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} For in the days of David Asaph was originally first of the singers, and [they sang] hymns and praise to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And all Israel in the days of Zorobabel, and in the days of Neemias, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, a daily rate: and consecrated them to the Levites: and the Levites consecrated them to the sons of Aaron.\par

\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 13}
\markright{EZRA AND NEHEMIAH 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In that day they read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people; and it was found written in it, that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the congregation of God for ever; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} because they met not the children of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them: but our God turned the curse into a blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it came to pass, when they heard the law, that they were separated, [even] every alien in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And before this time Eliasib the priest lived in the treasury of the house of our God, connected with Tobias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and he made himself a great treasury, and there they were formerly in the habit of bestowing the offerings, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil, the ordered portion of the Levites, and singers, and porters; and the first fruits of the priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But in all this [time] I was not in Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after a certain time I made my request of the king; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the mischief which Eliasib had done in the case of Tobias, in making for him a treasury in the court of the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it appeared very evil to me: so I cast forth all the furniture of the house of Tobias from the treasury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I gave orders, and they purified the treasuries: and I restored there the vessels of the house of God, [and] the offerings, and the frankincense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I understood that the portion of the Levites had not been given: and they had fled every one to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I strove with the commanders, and said, Therefore has the house of God been abandoned? and I assembled them, and set them in their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all Juda brought a tithe of the wheat and the wine and the oil into the treasuries, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} to the charge of Selemia the priest, and Sadoc the scribe, and Phadaea of the Levites: and next to them [was] Anan the son of Zacchur, son of Matthanias; for they were accounted faithful: [it was] their office to distribute to their brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my kindness be forgotten which I have wrought in [regard to] the house of the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In those days I saw in Juda [men] treading wine presses on the sabbath, and carrying sheaves, and loading asses with both wine, and grapes, and figs, and every [kind of] burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath-day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and I testified in the day of their sale. Also their lived in it [men] bringing fish, and selling every [kind of] merchandise to the children of Juda and in Jerusalem on the sabbath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I strove with the free children of Juda, and said to them, What [is] this evil thing which you⌃ do, and profane the sabbath-day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Did not your fathers thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us and upon this city all these evils? and do you⌃ bring additional wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And it came to pass, when the gates were set up in Jerusalem, before the sabbath, that I spoke, and they shut the gates; and I gave orders that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and I set [some] of my servants at the gates, that none should bring [in] burdens on the sabbath-day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So all [the merchants] lodged, and carried on traffic without Jerusalem once or twice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then I testified against them, and said to them, Why do you⌃ lodge in front of the wall? if you⌃ do so again, I will stretch out my hand upon you. From that time they came not on the sabbath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and I told the Levites who were purifying themselves, and came and kept the gates, that they should sanctify the sabbath-day. Remember me, O God, for these things, and spare me according to the abundance of your mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, [and] of Moab: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and their children spoke half in the language of Ashdod, and did not know how to speak in the Jewish language. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I strove with them and cursed them; and I struck some of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, [saying, ]You⌃ shall not give your daughters to their sons, and you⌃ shall not take of their daughters to your sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Did not Solomon king of Israel sin thus? though there was no king like him among many nations, and he was beloved of God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet strange women turned him aside. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So we will not listen to you to do all this evil, to break covenant with our God, —to marry strange wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and Elisub the high priest, [one] of the sons of Joada, [being] son-in-law of Sanaballat the Uranite, I chased him away from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Remember them, O God, for their [false] connection with the priesthood, and [the breaking] the covenant of the priesthood, and [for defiling] the Levites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So I purged them from all foreign connection, and established courses for the priests and the Levites, [every] man according to his work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the offering of the wood-bearers [was] at certain set times, and in the [times of the] first fruits. Remember me, O our God, for good.\par

\section*{Esther Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Mordecai or a near-contemporary Jewish witness (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book itself points to court knowledge and written records; Jewish tradition often linked it with Mordecai or a witness close to the events.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Though God's name is not explicit in the Hebrew form, the canonical narrative is received as true providential history preserving the covenant people.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Persian period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} likely 5th century BC or soon after\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology places Esther in the reign of Ahasuerus/Xerxes I within the Persian dispersion.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The Greek Esther tradition is much fuller than the MT, adding prayers, letters, and explicit references to God; this edition's OT base uses the Greek Esther tradition in the LXX stream.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Jewish preservation in Persia during the reign of Ahasuerus, between return waves to Judah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To show God's providential preservation of His covenant people under foreign rule and the origin of Purim.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} providence; preservation; reversal; covenant people in exile; Purim\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Royal court crisis 1-4; Esther's intervention 5-7; Deliverance and Purim 8-10. 4Q Proto-Esther? evidence is debated and no certain Qumran Esther manuscript is widely accepted | Subst. uncertain No certain Hebrew Qumran Esther witness is securely established | Heb. n/a Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Esther with additions\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Retelling of Esther traditions (Josephus)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1st century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Esther is a major MT/LXX divergence point because the Greek tradition contains substantial additions absent from the MT; this study edition should note those differences clearly.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Esther (Greek)}
\markboth{ESTHER (GREEK)}{}
\subsection*{Esther (Greek) 1}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great king, on the first [day] of Nisan, Mardochaeus the [son] of Jarius, the [son] of Semeias, the [son] of Cisaus, of the tribe of Benjamine, a Jew dwelling in the city Susa, a great man, serving in the king's palace, saw a vision. Now he was of the captivity which Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried captive from Jerusalem, with Jachonias the king of Judea. And this was his dream: Behold, voices and a noise, thunders and earthquake, tumult upon the earth. And, behold, two great serpents came forth, both ready for conflict, and there came from them a great voice, and by their voice every nation was prepared for battle, even to fight against the nation of the just. And, behold, a day of darkness and blackness, tribulation and anguish, affection and tumult upon the earth. And all the righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own afflictions; and they prepared to die, and cried to God: and from their cry there came as it were a great river from a little fountain, [even] much water. And light and the sun arose, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the honorable. And Mardochaeus who had seen this vision and what God desired to do, having awoke, kept it in his heart, and desired by all means to interpret it, even till night. And Mardochaeus rested quiet in the palace with Gabatha and Tharrha the king's two chamberlains, eunuchs who guarded the palace. And he heard their reasoning and searched out their plans, and learned that they were preparing to lay hands on king Artaxerxes: and he informed the king concerning them. And the king examined the two chamberlains, and they confessed, and were executed. And the king wrote these things for a memorial: also Mardochaeus wrote concerning these matters. And the king commanded Mardochaeus to attend in the palace, and gave gifts for this service. And Aman the son of Amadathes the Bugean was honorable in the sight of the king, and he endeavored to hurt Mardochaeus and his people, because of the two chamberlains of the king.] And it came to pass after these things in the days of Artaxerxes, —(this Artaxerxes ruled over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India)— {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} in those days, when king Artaxerxes was on the throne in the city of Susa, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} in the third year of his reign, he made a feast to his friends, and the other nations, and to the nobles of the Persians and Medes, and the chief of the satraps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And after this, after he had shown to them the wealth of his kingdom, and the abundant glory of his wealth during one hundred and eighty days, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} when, [I say], the days of the marriage feast were completed, the king made a banquet to the nations who were present in the city six days, in the court of the king's house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} [which was] adorned with [hangings] of fine linen and flax on cords of fine linen and purple, fastened to golden and silver studs, on pillars of Parian marble and stone: [there were] golden and silver couches on a pavement of emerald stone, and of pearl, and of Parian stone, and open-worked coverings variously flowered, [having] roses worked round about; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} gold and silver cups, and a small cup of carbuncle set out of the value of thirty thousand talents, abundant and sweet wine, which the king himself drank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And this banquet was not according to the appointed law; but so the king would have it: and he charged the stewards to perform his will and that of the company. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Also Astin the queen made a banquet for the women in the palace where king Artaxerxes [lived]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now on the seventh day the king, being merry, told Aman, and Bazan, and Tharrha, and Barazi, and Zatholtha, and Abataza, and Tharaba, the seven chamberlains, servants of king Artaxerxes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} to bring in the queen to him, to enthrone her, and crown her with the diadem, and to show her to the princes, and her beauty to the nations: for she was beautiful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But queen Astin listened not to him to come with the chamberlains: so the king was grieved and angered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to his friends, Thus have Astin spoken: pronounce therefore upon this [case] law and judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So Arkesaeus, and Sarsathaeus, and Malisear, the princes of the Persians and Medes, who were near the king, who sat chief [in rank] by the king, drew near to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and reported to him according to the laws how it was proper to do to queen Astin, because she had not done the things commanded of the king by the chamberlains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Muchaeus said to the king and to the princes, Queen Astin has not wronged the king only, but also all the king's rulers and princes: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} for he has told them the words of the queen, and how she disobeyed the king. As then, [said he], she refused [to obey] king Artaxerxes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} so this day shall the other ladies of the chiefs of the Persians and Medes, having heard what she said to the king, dare in the same way to dishonor their husbands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} If then it seem good to the king, let him make a royal decree, and let it be written according to the laws of the Medes and Persians, and let him not alter [it]: and let not the queen come in to him any more; and let the king give her royalty to a woman better than she. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And let the law of the king which he shall have made, be widely proclaimed, in his kingdom: and so shall all the women give honor to their husbands, from the poor even to the rich. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did as Muchaeus had said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and sent into all his kingdom through the several provinces, according to their language, in order that men might be feared in their own houses.\par

What to do \textsuperscript{16} Vashti This reasoning was inconsequent and false. She disobeyed only in one particular; and this, to serve a purpose, Memucan draws into a general consequence, and the rest came into the conclusion, being either too intoxicated to be able to discern right from wrong, or too intent on reducing women to a state of vassalage, to neglect the present favourable opportunity. done wrong \textsuperscript{18} the ladies Saroth, the princesses, but the meaning is well expressed by our term ladies. \textsuperscript{19} it please the king Heb. it be good with the king, from him Heb. from before him it be not altered Heb. it pass not away; Let it be inserted among the permanent laws, and be made a part of the constitution of the empire.
