\subsection*{Esther (Greek) 2}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after this the king's anger was pacified, and he no more mentioned Astin, bearing in mind what she had said, and how he had condemned her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then the servants of the king said, Let there be sought for the king chaste [and] beautiful young virgins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And let the king appoint local governors in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them select fair [and] chaste young damsels [and bring them] to the city Susa, into the women's apartment, and let them be consigned to the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women; and let things for purification and other attendance be given [to them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And let the woman who shall please the king be queen instead of Astin. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now there was a Jew in the city Susa, and his name was Mardochaeus, the [son] of Jairus, [the son] of Semeias, [the son] of Cisaeus, of the tribe of Benjamin; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} who had been brought a prisoner from Jerusalem, which Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried into captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he had a foster child, daughter of Aminadab his father's brother, and her name [was] Esther; and when her parents were dead, he brought her up for a wife for himself: and the damsel was beautiful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And because the king's ordinance was published, many damsels were gathered to the city Susa under the hand of Gai; and Esther was brought to Gai the keeper of the women. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the damsel pleased him, and she found favor in his sight; and he hasted to give her the things for purification, and her portion, and the seven maidens appointed her out of the palace: and he treated her and her maidens well in the women's apartment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But Esther did not reveal her family nor her kindred: for Mardochaeus had charged her not to tell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But Mardochaeus used to walk every day by the women's court, to see what would become of Esther. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now this was the time for a virgin to go into the king, when she should have fulfilled twelve months; for so are the days of purification fulfilled, six months while they are anointing themselves with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and women's purifications. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And then [the damsel] goes in to the king; and [the officer] to whoever he shall give the command, will bring her to come in with him from the women's apartment to the king's chamber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} She enters in the evening, and in the morning she departs to the second women's apartment, where Gai the king's chamberlain [is] keeper of the women: and she goes not in to the king again, unless she should be called by name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when the time. was fulfilled for Esther the daughter of Aminadab the brother of Mardochaeus' father to go in to the king, she neglected nothing which the chamberlain, the women's keeper, commanded; for Esther found grace in the sight of all that looked upon her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So Esther went in to king Artaxerxes in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king loved Esther, and she found favor beyond all the [other] virgins: and he put on her the queen's crown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the king made a banquet for all his friends and great men for seven days, and he highly celebrated the marriage of Esther; and he made a release to those who were under his dominion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But Mardochaeus served in the palace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now Esther had not revealed her kindred; for so Mardochaeus commanded her, to fear God, and perform his commandments, as when she was with him: and Esther changed not her manner of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And two chamberlains of the king, the chiefs of the body-guard, were grieved, because Mardochaeus was promoted; \noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after this king Artaxerxes highly honored Aman [son] of Amadathes, the Bugaean, and exalted him, and set his seat above all his friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all in the palace did him obeisance, for so the king had given orders to do: but Mardochaeus did not do him obeisance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they in the king's palace said to Mardochaeus, Mardochaeus, why do you transgress the commands of the king? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [Thus] they spoke daily to him, but he listened not to them; so they represented to Aman that Mardochaeus resisted the commands of the king: and Mardochaeus had shown to them that he was a Jew. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when Aman understood that Mardochaeus did not obeisance to him, he was greatly enraged, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and took counsel to destroy utterly all the Jews who were under the rule of Artaxerxes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, and cast lots daily and monthly, to kill in one day the race of Mardochaeus: and the lot fell on the fourteenth [day] of the month which is Adar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he spoke to king Artaxerxes, saying, There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws differ from [those of] all the [other] nations; and they disobey the laws of the king; and it is not expedient for the king to let them alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If it seem good to the king, let him make a decree to destroy them: and I will remit into the king's treasury ten thousand talents of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king took off his ring, and gave it into the hands of Aman, to seal the decrees against the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the king said to Aman, Keep the silver, and treat the nation as you will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So the king's recorders were called in the first month, on the thirteenth [day], and they wrote as Aman commanded to the captains and governors in every province, from India even to Ethiopia, to one hundred and twenty-seven provinces; and to the rulers of the nations according to their [several] languages, in the name of king Artaxerxes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And [the message] was sent by posts throughout the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to destroy utterly the race of the Jews on the first day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their goods. [And the following is the copy of the letter; The great king Artaxerxes writes thus to the rulers and inferior governors of one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India even to Ethiopia, who hold authority under [him]. Ruling over many nations and having obtained dominion over the whole world, I was minded (not elated by the confidence of power, but ever conducting [myself] with great moderation and gentleness) to make the lives of [my] subjects continually tranquil, desiring both to maintain the kingdom quiet and orderly to [its] utmost limits, and to restore the peace desired by all men. But when I had enquired of my counselors how this should be brought to pass. Aman, who excels in soundness of judgment among us, and has been manifestly well inclined without wavering and with unshaken fidelity, and had obtained the second post in the kingdom, informed us that a certain ill-disposed people is mixed up with all the tribes throughout the world, opposed in their law to every [other] nation, and continually neglecting the commands of the king, so that the united government blamelessly administered by us is not quietly established. Having then conceived that this nation [alone of all others] is continually set in opposition to every man, introducing as a change a foreign code of laws, and injuriously plotting to accomplish the worst of evils against our interests, and against the happy establishment of the monarchy; we signified to you in the letter written by Aman, who is set over [the public] affairs and is our second governor, to destroy them all utterly with their wives and children by the swords of the enemies, without pitying or sparing any, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar, of the present year; that the people aforetime and now ill-disposed [to us] having been violently consigned to death in one day, may hereafter secure to us continually a well constituted and quiet [state of affairs.] ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the copies of the letters were published in every province; and an order was given to all the nations to be ready against that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the business was hastened, and [that] at Susa: and the king and Aman began to drink; but the city was troubled.\par

Ten thousand talents of silver, counted by the Babylonish talent, amount to 2, 119, 000£.; but reckoned by the Jewish talent, they amount to double that sum. In those days, silver and gold were more plentiful than at present; and we have many instances of individuals possessing almost incredible riches. Herodotus relates, that when Xerxes went into Greece, Pythius the Lydian had 2, 000 talents of silver, and 4, 000, 000 of gold darics, which unitedly amount to nearly 5, 500, 000£. Plutarch tells us, that after Crassus had dedicated the tenth of all he had to Hercules, he entertained the Roman people at 10, 000 tables, and distributed to every citizen as much corn as was sufficient for three months; and, after all these expenses, he had 7, 100; Roman talents left, which amount to more than 1, 500, 000£. Lentulus the augur is said to have possessed no less than 3, 333, 333£. 6s. 8d. Apicius was worth more than 916, 671£ 13s. 4d.; and, after having spent in his kitchen 833, 333£ 6s. 8d. he considered the remainder too little for his support, and poisoned himself! ten thousand \textsuperscript{12} Then were scribes or, secretaries according, in the name;, sealed \textsuperscript{13} by posts; both young, in one day; the spoil \textsuperscript{15} hastened, sat down; the city\par}

\subsection*{Esther (Greek) 4}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Mardochaeus having perceived what was done, tore his garments, and put on sackcloth, and sprinkled dust upon himself; and having rushed forth through the open street of the city, he cried with a loud voice, A nation that has done no wrong is going to be destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he came to the king's gate, and stood; for it was not lawful for him to enter into the palace, wearing sackcloth and ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And in every province where the letters were published, [there was] crying and lamentation and great mourning on the part of the Jews: they spread for themselves sackcloth and ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the queen's maids and chamberlains went in and told her: and when she had heard what was done, she was disturbed; and she sent to clothe Mardochaeus, and take away his sackcloth; but he consented not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So Esther called for her chamberlain Achrathaeus, who waited upon her; and she sent to learn the truth from Mardochaeus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Mardochaeus showed him what was done, and the promise which Aman had made the king of ten thousand talents [to be paid] into the treasury, that he might destroy the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he gave him the copy [of the writing] that was published in Susa concerning their destruction, to show to Esther; and told him to charge her to go in and entreat the king, and to beg him for the people, remembering, [said he], the days of your low estate, how you were nursed by my hand: because Aman who holds the next place to the king has spoken against us for death. Do you call upon the Lord, and speak to the king concerning us, to deliver us from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So Achrathaeus went in and told her all these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Esther said to Achrathaeus, Go to Mardochaeus, and say, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All the nations of the empire know, that whoever, man or woman, shall go in to the king into the inner court uncalled, that person can’t live: only to whoever the king shall stretch out [his] golden sceptre, he shall live: and I have not been called to go into the king, for these thirty days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Achrathaeus reported to Mardochaeus all the words of Esther. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then Mardochaeus said to Achrathaeus, Go, and say to her, Esther, say not to yourself that you alone will escape in the kingdom, more than all the [other] Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if you shall refuse to listen on this occasion, help and protection will be to the Jews from another quarter; but you and your father's house will perish: and who knows, if you have been made queen for this [very] occasion? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Esther sent the [man] that came to her to Mardochaeus, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Go and assemble the Jews that are in Susa, and fast you⌃ for me, and eat not and drink not for three days, night and day: and I also and my maidens will fast; and then I will go in to the king contrary to the law, even if I must die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So Mardochaeus went and did all that Esther commanded him. [And he implored the Lord, making mention of all the works of the Lord; and he said, Lord God, king ruling over all, for all things are in your power, and there is no one that shall oppose you, in your purpose to save Israel. - For you have made the heaven and the earth and every wonderful thing in the [world] under heaven. And you are Lord of all, and there is no one who shall resist you Lord. You know all things: you know, Lord, that it is not in insolence, nor haughtiness, nor love of glory, that I have done this, to refuse obeisance to the haughty Aman. For I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the safety of Israel. But I have done this, that I might not set the glory of man above the glory of God: and I will not worship any one except you, my Lord, and I will not do these things in haughtiness. And now, O Lord God, the King, the God of Abraam, spare your people, for [our enemies] are looking upon us to [our] destruction, and they have desired to destroy your ancient inheritance. Do not overlook your peculiar people, whom you have redeemed for yourself out of the land of Egypt. Listen to my prayer, and be propitious to your inheritance, and turn our mourning into gladness, that we may live and sing praise to your name, O Lord; and do not utterly destroy the mouth of them that praise you, O Lord. And all Israel cried with [all] their might, for death [was] before their eyes. And queen Esther betook herself for refuge to the Lord, being taken [as it were] in the agony of death. And having taken off her glorious apparel, she put on garments of distress and mourning; and instead of grand perfumes she filled her head with ashes and dung, and she greatly brought down her body, and she filled every place of her glad adorning with the [torn] curls of her hair. And she implored the Lord God of Israel, and said, O my Lord, you alone are our king: help me [who am] destitute, and have no helper but you, for my danger [is] near at hand. I have heard from my birth, in the tribe of my kindred that you, Lord, took Israel out of all the nations, and our fathers out of all their kindred for a perpetual inheritance, and have wrought for them all that you have said. And now we have sinned before you, and you have delivered us into the hands of our enemies, because we honored their gods: you are righteous, O Lord. But now they have not been contented with the bitterness of our slavery, but have laid their hands on the hands of their idols, [in order] to abolish the decree of your mouth, and utterly to destroy your inheritances, and to stop the mouth of them that praise you, and to extinguish the glory of your house and your altar, and to open the mouth of the Gentiles to [speak] the praises of vanities, and [in order] that a mortal king should be admired for ever. O Lord, do not resign your sceptre to them that are not, and let them not laugh at our fall, but turn their counsel against themselves, and make an example of him who has begun [to injure] us. Remember [us], O Lord, manifest yourself in the time of our affliction, and encourage me, O King of gods, and ruler of all dominion. Put harmonious speech into my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hate him that fights against us, to the utter destruction of him that consent with him. But deliver us by your hand, and help me [who am] destitute, and have none but the, O Lord. You know all things, and know that I hate the glory of transgressors, and that I abhor the couch of the uncircumcised, and of every stranger. You know my necessity, for I abhor the symbol of my proud station, which is upon my head in the days of my splendor: I abhor it as a menstruous cloth, and I wear it not in the days of my tranquility. And your handmaid has not eaten [at] the table of Aman, and I have not honored the banquet of the king, neither have I drunk wine of libations. Neither has your handmaid rejoiced since the day of my promotion until now, except in you, O Lord God of Abraam. O god, who has power over all, listen to the voice of the desperate, and deliver us from the hand of them that devise mischief; and deliver me from my fear.]\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} all that rent; with ashes; and cried Mordecai gave every demonstration of the most poignant grief. Nor did he hide this from the city; and the Greek says that he uttered these words aloud: Αιρεται εθνος μηδεν ηδικηκος, "A people is going to be destroyed who have done no evil." \textsuperscript{3} in every province, great mourning It cannot reasonably be doubted, that the mournings, fastings, and weepings of the Jews were attended by constant prayers and supplications; though all mention of them, and of the glorious God whom they worshipped, seems to have been studiously avoided.;, weeping, many lay in sackcloth and ashes Heb. sackcloth and ashes were laid under many \textsuperscript{4} chamberlains Heb. eunuchs; *marg.; but he received it not \textsuperscript{5} appointed to attend upon her Heb. set before her, to know \textsuperscript{8} the copy to charge; to make supplication; request \textsuperscript{11} shall come Herodotus informs us, that ever since the reign of Deioces, king of Media, for the security of the king's person, it was enacted that no one should be admitted into his presence; but that if any one had business with him, he should transact it through the medium of his ministers. the inner court one law the king shall, the golden sceptre That the kings of Persia carried a golden sceptre, we have the following proof in Xenophon: Οτι ου τοδε το χρυσουν σκηπτρον το μην βασιλειαν διασωζον εστιν, αλλ οι πιστοι φιλοι σκηπτρον βασιλευσιν αληθεστατον και ασφαλεστατον . "It is not (said Cyrus to his son Cambyses) the golden sceptre that saves the kingdom; but faithful friends are the truest and best sceptre of the kingdom." but I \textsuperscript{14} then shall; enlargement Heb. respiration; but thou; whether; for such a time; The fact related in this verse was unquestionably the reason why Esther was raised to regal honours, by the overruling providence of God. She was therefore bound in gratitude to do this service for God, else she would not have answered the end of her elevation, and she need not fear the miscarriage of the enterprise, for if God designed her for it, he would surely bear her through and give success. It appeared by the event that Mordecai spoke prophetically, when he modestly conjectured that Esther came to the kingdom that she might be the instrument of the Jews' deliverance. Mordecai thoroughly believed that it was a cause which one way or other would certainly be carried, and which, therefore, she might safely venture upon. Instruments might fail, but God's covenant cannot. There is a wise design in all the providences of God, which is unknown to us till it is accomplished; but it will prove in the issue that all is intended for and centre in the good of those who trust in Him. \textsuperscript{16} present Heb. found fast; eat nor drink; I also; if I perish If I lose my life in the attempt to save my people, I shall lose it cheerfully. I see it is my duty to make the attempt; and, come what will, I am resolved to do it.\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass on the third day, when she had ceased praying, that she put off her mean dress, and put on her glorious apparel. And being splendidly arrayed, [and] having called upon God the Overseer and Preserver of all things, she took her two maids, and she leaned upon one, as a delicate female, and the other followed bearing her train. And she [was] blooming in the perfection of her beauty; and her face [was] cheerful, and [it were] benevolent, but her heart [was] straitened for fear. And having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king: and he was sitting upon his royal throne, and he had put on all his glorious apparel, [covered] all over with gold and precious stones, and was very terrible. And having raised his face resplendent with glory, he looked with intense anger: and the queen fell, and changed her color as she fainted; and she bowed herself upon the head of the maid that went before [her]. But God changed the spirit of the king to gentleness, and in intense feeling he sprang from off his throne, and took her into his arms, until she recovered: and he comforted her with peaceful words, and said to her, What is [the matter], Esther? I [am] your brother; be of good cheer, you shall not die, for our command is openly declared [to you], Draw near. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And having raised the golden sceptre he laid it upon her neck, and embraced her, and said, Speak to me. And she said to him, I saw you, [my] lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled for fear of your glory; for you, [my] lord, are to be wondered at, and your face [is] full of grace. And while she was speaking, she fainted and fell. Then the king was troubled, and all his servants comforted her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king said, What will you, Esther? and what is your request? Olearius, describing an entertainment at the Persian court, says, "The floor of the hall was covered with cotton cloth, which was covered with all sorts of fruits and sweetmeats in basons of gold. With them was served up excellent Shiraz wine. After an hour's time, the sweetmeats were removed, to make way for the more substantial part of the entertainment, such as rice, boiled and roast mutton, etc. When the company had been at table an hour and a half, warm water was brought, in a ewer of gold, for washing; and grace being said, they began to retire without speaking a word, according to the custom of the country." \textsuperscript{8} perform Heb. do let the king Esther probably wished another interview, that she might ingratiate herself more fully into the king's favour, and thus secure the success of her design. \subsection*{Esther (Greek) 8}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in that day king Artaxerxes gave to Esther all that belonged to Aman the slanderer: and Mardochaeus was called by the king; for Esther had shown that he was related to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king took the ring which he had taken away from Aman, and gave it to Mardochaeus: and Esther appointed Mardochaeus over all that had been Aman's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And she spoke yet again to the king, and fell at his feet, and implored [him] to do away the mischief of Aman, and all that he had done against the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then the king stretched out to Esther the golden sceptre: and Esther arose to stand near the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Esther said, If it seem good to you, and I have found favor [in your sight], let an order be sent that the letters sent by Aman may be reversed, that were written for the destruction of the Jews, who are in your kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For how shall I be able to look upon the affliction of my people, and how shall I be able to survive the destruction of my kindred? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the king said to Esther, If I have given and freely granted you all that was Aman's, and hanged him on a gallows, because he laid his hands upon the Jews, what do you yet further seek? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Write you⌃ also in my name, as it seems good to you, and seal [it] with my ring: for whatever [orders] are written at the command of the king, and sealed with my ring, it is not lawful to gainsay them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisan, on the three and twentieth day of the same year; and [orders] were written to the Jews, whatever [the king had] commanded to the local governors and chiefs of the satraps, from India even to Ethiopia, one hundred and twenty-seven satraps, according to the several provinces, according to their dialects. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they were written by order of the king, and sealed with his ring, and they sent the letters by the posts: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} wherein he charged them to use their [own] laws in every city, and to help each other, and to treat their adversaries, and those who attacked them, as they pleased, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} on one day in all the kingdom of Artaxerxes, on the thirteenth [day] of the twelfth month, which is Adar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom, and let all the Jews be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies. And the following is the copy of the letter of the orders. [The great king Artaxerxes sends greetings to the rulers of provinces [in] one hundred and twenty-seven satrapies, from India to Ethiopia, even to those who are faithful to our interests. Many who have been frequently honored by the most abundant kindness of their benefactors have conceived ambitious designs, and not only endeavor to hurt our subjects, but moreover, not being able to bear prosperity, they also endeavor to plot against their own benefactors. And they not only would utterly abolish gratitude from among men, but also, elated by the boastings of men who are strangers to all that is good, they supposed that they shall escape the sin-hating vengeance of the ever-seeing God. And oftentimes [evil] exhortation has made partakers of the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and has involved in irremediable calamities, many of those who had been appointed to offices of authority, who had been entrusted with the management of their friends' affairs; while [men], by the false sophistry of an evil disposition, have deceived the simple candour of the ruling powers. And it is possible to see [this], not so much from more ancient traditionary accounts, as it is immediately in your power [to see it] by examining what things have been wickedly perpetrated by the baseness of men unworthily holding power. And [it is right] to take heed with regard to the future, that we may maintain the government in undisturbed peace for all men, adopting [needful] changes, and ever judging those cases which come under our notice, with truly equitable decision. For whereas Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadathes, in reality an alien from the blood of the Persians, and differing widely from our mild course of government, having been hospitable entertained by us, obtained so large a share of our universal kindness, as to be called our father, and to continue the person next to the royal throne, reverenced of all; [he however], overcome by the pride [of his station], endeavored to deprive us of our dominion, and our life: having by various and subtle artifices demanded for destruction both Mardochaeus our deliverer and perpetual benefactor, and Esther the blameless consort of [our] kingdom, with their whole nation. For by these methods he thought, having surprised us in a defenceless state, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who have been consigned to destruction by the most abominable of men, are not malefactors, but living according to the justest laws, and being the sons of the living God, the most high and mighty, who maintains the kingdom. to us as well as to our forefathers, in the most excellent order. You⌃ will therefore do well in refusing to obey the letter sent by Aman the son of Amadathes, because he that has done these things, has been hanged with his whole family at the gates of Susa, Almighty God having swiftly returned to him a worthy recompence, [We enjoin you] then, having openly published a copy of this letter in every place, to give the Jews permission to use their own lawful customs, and to strengthen them, that on the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, on the self-same day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them in a time of affliction. For in the place of the destruction of the chosen race, Almighty God has granted them this [time of] gladness. Do you⌃ therefore also, among your [notable] feasts, keep a distinct day with all festivity, that both now and hereafter it may be a day of deliverance to us and who are well disposed toward the Persians, but to those that plotted against us a memorial of destruction. And every city and province collectively, which shall not do accordingly, shall be consumed with vengeance by spear and fire: it shall be made not only inaccessible to men, but most hateful to wild beasts and birds for ever.] And let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom and let all the Jews be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So the horsemen went forth with haste to perform the king's commands; and the ordinance was also published in Susa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Mardochaeus went forth robed in the royal apparel, and wearing a golden crown, and a diadem of fine purple linen: and the people in Susa saw [it] and rejoiced. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the Jews had light and gladness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} in every city and province wherever the ordinance was published: wherever the proclamation took place, the Jews had joy and gladness, feasting and mirth: and many of the Gentiles were circumcised, and became Jews, for fear of the Jews.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} give the house; came before \textsuperscript{3} fell; besought him with tears Heb. she wept and besought him; mischief \textsuperscript{5} if I; I be pleasing, letters Heb. device, which he wrote or, who wrote \textsuperscript{6} For how; endure to see Heb. be able that I may see the evil \textsuperscript{7} Behold; him they have hanged \textsuperscript{8} in the king's name; may no man reverse No, not the king himself; and this was the reason that the king was forced not to reverse, but to give a contradictory decree; that if the Jews, pursuant to the first decree, were assaulted, they might legitimately, by virtue of the second, defend themselves, slay their enemies, and even take the spoil. \textsuperscript{9} the king's and to the lieutenants, ; India The Hebrew word Hoddo, in Syriac, Hendoo, and in Arabic, Hind, is rendered India by all the versions. India, or Hindostan, is a large country of the south of Asia, extending from north to south about 2, 400 miles, and from east to west 1, 800, between 8 degrees and 35 degrees n lat. and 68 degrees and 92 degrees e long.; being bounded on the west by the Indus, east by the Birman empire and Thibet, north by the Indian Caucasus, and south by the Indian Ocean. It is probable, however, that all the country east of the Indus was anciently called India. and according \textsuperscript{10} in the king; by posts; mules Rechesh, in Syriac, rechesha, probably denotes a swift horse. camels Achashteranim, from the Persian akhash, large, and aster, a mule, probably, as Bochart supposes, denotes a large mule. young dromedaries Beney harammachim, "the sons of mares, " as the word ramakat denotes in Arabic; probably an expletive of the preceeding word. \textsuperscript{11} to gather to destroy, ; and to take the spoil \textsuperscript{12} one day; upon the thirteenth \textsuperscript{13} published Heb. revealed avenge themselves \textsuperscript{15} royal apparel, ; blue or, violet, and with a great crown Mordecai was now made the chief minister, or vizier, instead of Haman; and was accordingly invested with the "royal apparel, " in conformity to the custom of the East. So we are informed, in the History of the Revolt of Ali Bey, that on the election of a new sheikh bellet, or chief of the country, in Egypt, the pasha who approves of him invests him with a robe of valuable fur. Perhaps the crown was one of the insignia of the office of vizier. Concerning the blue, fine linen, and purple; see note on, and see note on . the city Haman was too proud to be popular. Few lamented his fall. \textsuperscript{16} Jews; had light That is, prosperity and hope. \subsection*{Esther (Greek) 9}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth day of the month which is Adar, the letters written by the king arrived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In that day the adversaries of the Jews perished: for no one resisted, through fear of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the chiefs of the satraps, and the princes and the royal scribes, honored the Jews; for the fear of Mardochaeus lay upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the order of the king was in force, that he should be celebrated in all the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And in the city Susa the Jews killed five hundred men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} both Pharsannes, and Delphon and Phasga, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and Pharadatha, and Barea, and Sarbaca, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and Marmasima, and Ruphaeus, and Arsaeus, and Zabuthaeus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} the ten sons of Aman the son of Amadathes the Bugaean, the enemy of the Jews, and they plundered [their property] on the same day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and the number of them that perished in Susa was rendered to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the king said to Esther, The Jews have slain five hundred men in the city Susa; and how, think you, have they used them in the rest of the country? What then do you yet ask, that it may be [done] for you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Esther said to the king, let it be granted to the Jews so to treat them tomorrow as to hand the ten sons of Aman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he permitted it to be so done; and he gave up to the Jews of the city the bodies of the sons of Aman to hang. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Jews assembled in Susa on the fourteenth [day] of Adar, and killed three hundred men, but plundered no property. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom assembled, and helped one another, and obtained rest from their enemies: for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth [day] of Adar, but took no spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Jews in the city Susa assembled also on the fourteenth [day] and rested; and they kept also the fifteenth with joy and gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} On this account then [it is that] the Jews dispersed in every foreign land keep the fourteenth of Adar [as] a holy day with joy, sending portions each to his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Mardochaeus wrote these things in a book, and sent them to the Jews, as many as were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes, both them that were near and them that were afar off, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} to establish these [as] joyful days, and to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} for on these days the Jews obtained rest from their enemies; and [as to] the month, which was Adar, in which a change was made for them, from mourning to joy, and from sorrow to a good day, to spend the whole of it [in] good days of feasting and gladness, sending portions to their friends, and to the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the Jews consented [to this] accordingly as Mardochaeus wrote to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [showing] how Aman the son of Amadathes the Macedonian fought against them, how he made a decree and cast lots to destroy them utterly; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} also how he went in to the king, telling [him] to hang Mardochaeus: but all the calamities he tried to bring upon the Jews came upon himself, and he was hanged, and his children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore these days were called Phrurae, because of the lots; (for in their language they are called Phrurae;) because of the words of this letter, and [because of] all they suffered on this account, and all that happened to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And [Mardochaeus] established it, and the Jews took upon themselves, and upon their seed, and upon those that were joined to them [to observe it], neither would they on any account behave differently: but these days [were to be] a memorial kept in every generation, and city, and family, and province. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And these days of the Phrurae, [said they, ]shall be kept for ever, and their memorial shall not fail in any generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And queen Esther, the daughter of Aminadab, and Mardochaeus the Jew, wrote all that they had done, and the confirmation of the letter of Phrurae. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And Mardochaeus and Esther the queen appointed [a fast] for themselves privately, even at that time also having formed their plan against their own health. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Esther established it by a command for ever, and it was written for a memorial.\par

They stood for their lives; and gave full proof that they sought their own personal safety, and not the property of their enemies. Though the decree in their favour gave them authority to take the property of all their adversaries. \textsuperscript{13} If it please the king Esther had probably been informed by Mordecai, that there were still many enemies of the Jews who sought their destruction, who had escaped the preceding day; and therefore begged that the second day might be added to the former permission; and that the sons of Haman, who had already been slain, might be suspended on gibbets, as a terror to those who sought the destruction of the Jews. according unto let Haman's ten sons be hanged Heb. let men hang Haman's ten sons \textsuperscript{15} gathered themselves, ; but on the prey \textsuperscript{17} of the same Heb. in it \textsuperscript{19} gladness; sending portions The eastern princes and people not only invite their friends to feasts, but it is their custom to send a portion of the banquet to those that cannot well attend, especially their relations, and those in a state of mourning. Thus, when the Grand Emir found that it incommoded M. D'Arvieux to eat with him, he desired him to take his own time for eating, and sent him from his kitchen what he liked best. \textsuperscript{20} Mordecai That is, as the words imply, the history contained in this book; and not merely the letters afterwards mentioned, as some understand it. wrote these; in all the provinces \textsuperscript{22} the days; from sorrow; sending portions \textsuperscript{24} the enemy, Pur The word pur seems to be derived either from the Persian bahr and bar, a part, portion, lot, or pari, anything which happens fortuitously or fortunately; whence the annual festival in commemoration of the wonderful deliverance of the Jews from their enemies was called Purim, or in Arabic and Persian, Fuhr, or Lots; which has been observed by them, in all places of their dispersion, from that day to the present time, without any interruption. consume Heb. crush \textsuperscript{25} when Esther came Heb. when she came, return \textsuperscript{26} they called; Pur that is, Lot letter \textsuperscript{27} and upon their seed; all such; fail Heb. pass \textsuperscript{28} remembered; fail Heb. pass the memorial; perish from their seed Heb. be ended from their seed \textsuperscript{29} the daughter of Abihail authority Heb. strength confirm \textsuperscript{31} themselves Heb. their souls and for their seed the fastings\par}

\subsection*{Esther (Greek) 10}
\markright{ESTHER (GREEK) 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the king levied [a tax] upon [his] kingdom both by land and sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And [as for] his strength and valour, and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, behold, they are written in the book of the Persians and Medes, for a memorial. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Mardochaeus was viceroy to king Artaxerxes, and was a great man in the kingdom, and honored by the Jews, and passed his life beloved of all his nation. [And Mardocheus said, These things have been done of God. For I remember the dream which I had concerning these matters: for not one particular of them has failed. [There was] the little fountain which became a river, and there was light, and the sun and much water. The river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen. And the two serpents are I and Aman. And the nations are those [nations] that combined to destroy the name of the Jews. But [as for] my nation, this is Israel, [even] they that cried to God and were delivered: for the Lord delivered his people. And the Lord rescued us out of all these calamities; and God wrought such signs and great wonders as have not been done among the nations. Therefore did he ordain two lots. One for the people of God, and one for all the other [nations]. And these two lots came for an appointed season, and for a day of judgment, before God, and for all the nations. And God remembered his people, and vindicated his inheritance. And they shall observe these days in the month Adar, on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth [day] of the month, with an assembly, and joy and gladness before God, throughout the generations for ever among his people Israel. In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemeus and Cleopatra, Dositheus, who said he was a priest and Levite, and Ptolemeus his son, brought this epistle of Phurim, which they said was the same, and that Lysimachus the son of Ptolemeus, that was in Jerusalem, had interpreted.]\par

Persia Proper, now Fars, was but a small province, being bounded on the north by Media, west by Susiana, south by the Persian Gulf, and east by Caramania, extending from 27 degrees to 33 degrees n lat. and 50 degrees to 55 degrees e long. But the Persian empire in its ancient state extended from the Hellespont to the Indus, above 2, 800 miles, and from Pontus to the shores of Arabia, above 2, 000 miles; comprehending a multitude of various nations. \textsuperscript{3} next unto king; accepted; seeking\par}

\section*{Job Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Job or an early inspired patriarchal-era recorder (conservative options vary)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Conservative scholarship differs on the exact human writer, but commonly treats the book as preserving very early patriarchal wisdom history under inspiration.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} James 5:11 treats Job as a real historical exemplar of endurance.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} patriarchal-era setting; composition date debated\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT places Job in wisdom literature without explicit historical anchoring, but many conservative readers place the events in the patriarchal period.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX of Job is notably shorter than the MT and can reflect a different Greek Vorlage or abridgment history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} A wisdom dialogue set in the land of Uz around the suffering of a righteous man under God's sovereignty.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To vindicate God's wisdom and sovereignty in suffering and to expose the limits of merely human explanations.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} suffering; sovereignty; wisdom; righteousness; endurance; divine speeches\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Prologue 1-2; Dialogues 3-31; Elihu 32-37; The LORD's answer 38-42; Epilogue 42.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Job and 11Q Targum Job witness early circulation of the book Hasmonean period | Subst. Qumran Job fragments preserve early Hebrew evidence, though the Greek Job tradition is especially significant Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Job 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Job used as historical example by James (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Job is a major MT/LXX comparison point because the Greek text is materially shorter than the MT; the difference should be noted regularly in apparatus work.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Job as truthful wisdom history with originally inerrant wording, even where witness traditions differ substantially in extent or phrasing.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\markboth{JOB}{}
\subsection*{Job 1}
\markright{JOB 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There was a certain man in the land of Ausis, whose name [was] Job; and that man was true, blameless, righteous, [and] godly, abstaining from everything evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he had seven sons and three daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his cattle consisted of seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred she-asses in the pastures, and a very great household, and he had a great husbandry on the earth; and that man was [most] noble of the [men] of the east. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his sons visiting one another prepared a banquet every day, taking with them also their three sisters to eat and drink with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when the days of the banquet were completed, Job sent and purified them, having risen up in the morning, and offered sacrifices for them, according to their number, and one calf for a sin-offering for their souls: for Job said, Lest perhaps my sons have thought evil in their minds against God. Thus, then Job did continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass on a day, that behold, the angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord said to the devil, Whence are you come? And the devil answered the Lord, and said, I am come from compassing the earth, and walking up and down in the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord said to him, Have you diligently considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a man blameless, true, godly, abstaining from everything evil? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then the devil answered, and said before the Lord, Does Job worship the Lord for nothing? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Have you not made a hedge about him, and about his household, and all his possessions round about? and have you not blessed the works of his hands, and multiplied his cattle upon the land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But put forth your hand, and touch all that he has: verily he will bless you to [your] face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then the Lord said to the devil, Behold, I give into your hand all that he has, but touch not himself. So the devil went out from the presence of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass on a certain day, that Job's sons and his daughters were drinking wine in the house of their elder brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And, behold, there came a messenger to Job, and said to him, The yokes of oxen were plowing, and the she-asses were feeding near them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the spoilers came and took them for a prey, and killed the servants with the sword; and I having escaped alone am come to tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} While he was yet speaking, there came another messenger, and said to Job, Fire has fallen from heaven, and burnt up the sheep, and devoured the shepherds like wise; and I having escaped alone am come to tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} While he was yet speaking, there came another messenger, and said to Job, The horsemen formed three companies against us, and surrounded the camels, and took them for a prey, and killed the servants with the sword; and I only escaped, and am come to tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} While he is yet speaking, another messenger comes, saying to Job, While your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking with their elder brother, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} suddenly a great wind came on from the desert, and caught the four corners of the house, and the house fell upon your children, and they are dead; and I have escaped alone, and am come to tell you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So Job arose, and tore his garments, and shaved the hair of his head, and fell on the earth, and worshipped, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and said, I myself came forth naked from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there; the Lord gave, the Lord has taken away: as it seemed good to the Lord, so has it come to pass; blessed be the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} In all these events that befell him Job sinned not at all before the Lord, and did not impute folly to God.\par

\subsection*{Job 2}
\markright{JOB 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass on a certain day, that the angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came among them to stand before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord, said to the devil, Whence come you? Then the devil said before the Lord, I am come from going through the world, and walking about the whole earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord said to the devil, Have you then observed my servant Job, that there is none of [men] upon the earth like him, a harmless, true, blameless, godly man, abstaining from all evil? and he yet cleaves to innocence, whereas you have told [me] to destroy his substance without cause? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the devil answered and said to the Lord, Skin for skin, all that a man has will he give as a ransom for his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Nay, but put forth your hand, and touch his bones and his flesh: verily he will bless you to [your] face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord said to the devil, Behold, I deliver him up to you; only save his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So the devil went out from the Lord, and struck Job with sore boils from [his] feet to [his] head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he took a potsherd to scrape away the discharge, and sat upon a dung-heap outside the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when much time had passed, his wife said to him, How long will you hold out, saying, Behold, I wait yet a little while, expecting the hope of my deliverance? for, behold, your memorial is abolished from the earth, [even your] sons and daughters, the pangs and pains of my womb which I bore in vain with sorrows; and you yourself sit down to spend the nights in the open air among the corruption of worms, and I am a wanderer and a servant from place to place and house to house, waiting for the setting of the sun, that I may rest from my labors and my pangs which now beset me: but say some word against the Lord, and die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But he looked on her, and said to her, You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things of the hand of the Lord, shall we not endure evil things? In all these things that happened to him, Job sinned not at all with his lips before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now his three friends having heard of all the evil that was come upon him, came to him each from his own country: Eliphaz the king of the Thaemans, Baldad sovereign of the Saucheans, Sophar king of he Minaeans: and they came to him with one accord, to comfort and to visit him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when they saw him from a distance they did not know him; and they cried with a loud voice, and wept, and tore every one his garment, and sprinkled dust upon [their heads], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and they sat down beside him seven days and seven nights, and no one of them spoke; for they saw that his affliction was dreadful and very great.\par

\subsection*{Job 3}
\markright{JOB 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let the day perish in which I was born, and that night in which they said, Behold a boy! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let that night be darkness, and let not the Lord regard it from above, neither let light come upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But let darkness and the shadow of death seize it; let blackness come upon it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} let that day and night be cursed, let darkness carry them away; let it not come into the days of the year, neither let it be numbered with the days of the months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But let that night be pain, and let not mirth come upon it, nor joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But let him that curses that day curse it, [even] he that is ready to attack the great whale. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let the stars of that night be darkened; let it remain [dark], and not come into light; and let it not see the morning star arise: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} because it shut not up the gates of my mother's womb, for [so] it would have removed sorrow from my eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For why died I not in the belly? and [why] did I not come forth from the womb and die immediately? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and why did the knees support me? and why did I suck the breasts? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now I should have lain down and been quiet, I should have slept and been at rest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} with kings [and] councillors of the earth, who gloried in [their] swords; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} or with rulers, whose gold was abundant, who filled their houses with silver: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} or [I should have been] as an untimely birth proceeding from his mother's womb, or as infants who never saw light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} There the ungodly have burnt out the fury of rage; there the wearied in body rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the men of old time have together ceased to hear the exactor's voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The small and great are there, and the servant that feared his lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For why is light given to those who are in bitterness, and life to those souls which are in griefs? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} who desire death, and obtain it not, digging [for it] as [for] treasures; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and would be very joyful if they should gain it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Death [is] rest to [such] a man, for God has hedged him in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For my groaning comes before my food, and I weep being beset with terror. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For the terror of which I meditated has come upon me, and that which I had feared has befallen me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I was not at peace, nor quiet, nor had I rest; yet wrath came upon me.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} After, opened; cursed, ; his day That is, the day of his birth. \textsuperscript{3} Let the day That is, as we say, "Let it be blotted out of the calendar." \textsuperscript{5} the shadow, ;, ; stain it or, challenge it let a cloud; let the blackness or, let them terrify it, as those who have a bitter day \textsuperscript{6} let it not be joined unto the days or, let it not rejoice among the days \textsuperscript{8} who are ready; their mourning or, a leviathan \textsuperscript{9} look for light; the dawning of the day Heb. the eye-lids of the morning \textsuperscript{11} died I; when I came \textsuperscript{13} then had I been at rest \textsuperscript{14} kings; which built Who erect splendid mausoleums, funeral monuments, etc. to keep their names from perishing, while their bodies are turned to corruption. \textsuperscript{15} who filled their houses That is, "the covetous, whom nothing can satisfy, " as the poet Saady has observed, "but the dust that fills his mouth, when laid in the grave." \textsuperscript{17} the wicked; the weary Heb. the wearied in strength at rest \textsuperscript{19} The small; and the servant \textsuperscript{24} my sighing; I eat Heb. my meat my roarings \textsuperscript{25} the thing etc. Heb. \subsection*{Job 4}
\markright{JOB 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Eliphaz the Thaemanite answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Have you been often spoken to in distress? but who shall endure the force of your words? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For whereas you have instructed many, and have strengthened the hands of the weak one, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and have supported the failing with words, and have imparted courage to feeble knees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Yet now [that] pain has come upon you, and touched you, you are troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Is not your fear [founded] in folly, your hope also, and the mischief of your way? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember then who has perished, being pure? or when were the true-hearted utterly destroyed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Accordingly as I have seen men plowing barren places, and they that sow them will reap sorrows for themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They shall perish by the command of the Lord, and shall be utterly consumed by the breath of his wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The strength of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the exulting cry of serpents are quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The old lion has perished for lack of food, and the lions' whelps have forsaken one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But if there had been any truth in your words, none of these evils would have befallen you. Shall not my ear receive excellent [revelations] from him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But [as when] terror falls upon men, with dread and a sound in the night, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} horror and trembling seized me, and caused all my bones greatly to shake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And a spirit came before my face; and my hair and flesh quivered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I arose and perceived it not: I looked, and there, was no form before my eyes: but I only heard a breath and a voice, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} What, shall a mortal be pure before the Lord? or a man be blameless in regard to his works? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Whereas he trust not in his servants, and perceives perverseness in his angels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But [as for] them that dwell in houses of clay, of whom we also are formed of the same clay, he smites them like a moth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And from the morning to evening they no longer exist: they have perished, because they can’t help themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For he blows upon them, and they are withered: they have perished for lack of wisdom.\par

\subsection*{Job 5}
\markright{JOB 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But call, if any one will listen to you, or if you shall see any of the holy angels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For wrath destroys the foolish one, and envy slays him that has gone astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I have seen foolish ones taking root: but suddenly their habitation was devoured. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let their children be far from safety, and let them be crushed at the doors of vile men, and let there be no deliverer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For what they have collected, the just shall eat; but they shall not be delivered out of calamities: let their strength be utterly exhausted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For labor can’t by any means come out of the earth, nor shall trouble spring out of the mountains: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} yet man is born to labor, and [even so] the vulture's young seek the high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Nevertheless I will beseech the Lord, and will call upon the Lord, the sovereign of all; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} who does great things and untraceable, glorious things also, and marvelous, of which there is no number: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} who gives rain upon the earth, sending water on the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} who exalts the lowly, and raises up them that are lost: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} frustrating the counsels of the crafty, and their hands shall not perform the truth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} who takes the wise in their wisdom, and subverts the counsel of the crafty {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} In the day darkness shall come upon them, and let them grope in the noon-day even as in the night: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and let them perish in war, and let the weak escape from the hand of the mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And let the weak have hope, but the mouth of the unjust be stopped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But blessed [is] the man whom the Lord has reproved; and reject not you the chastening of the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} for he causes [a man] to be in pain, and restores [him] again: he smites, and his hands heal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Six time he shall deliver you out of distresses: and in the seventh harm shall not touch you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In famine he shall deliver you from death: and in war he shall free you from the power of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He shall hide you from the scourge of the tongue: and you shall not be afraid of coming evils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You shall laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless: and you shall not be afraid of wild beasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the wild beasts of the field shall be at peace with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then shall you know that your house shall be at peace, and the provision for your tabernacle shall not fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall know that your seed [shall be] abundant; and your children shall be like the herbage of the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And you shall come to the grave like ripe corn reaped in its season, or as a heap of the corn-flour collected in proper time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Behold, we have thus sought out these matters; these are what we have heard: but do you reflect with yourself, if you have done anything [wrong].\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} and to which; the saints; turn or, look \textsuperscript{2} wrath; the foolish, ; envy or, indignation; one \textsuperscript{4} children, ;, they are crushed; neither \textsuperscript{5} harvest; the thorns; the robber, ; swalloweth \textsuperscript{6} affliction or, iniquity trouble; spring out \textsuperscript{7} man; trouble or, labour, sparks fly upward Heb. sons of the burning coal lift up to fly \textsuperscript{9} doeth, ; unsearchable Heb. there is no search, marvellous without number Heb. till there be no number \textsuperscript{12} disappointeth; their hands; their enterprise or, anything \textsuperscript{14} meet with or, run into darkness \textsuperscript{20} famine; redeem; in war; the power Heb. hands \textsuperscript{21} be hid, ; from the scourge or, when the tongue scourgeth neither \textsuperscript{24} thou shalt know, ; thy tabernacle etc. or, peace is thy tabernacle, thou shalt visit; sin or, err \textsuperscript{25} thy seed; , great or, much. as the grass \textsuperscript{26} in a full age; cometh Heb. ascendeth \textsuperscript{27} we have searched, ; for thy good Heb. for thyself\par}

\subsection*{Job 6}
\markright{JOB 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Oh that one would indeed weigh the wrath that is upon me, and take up my griefs in a balance together! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And verily they would be heavier than the sand by the seashore: but, as it seems, my words are vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the arrows of the Lord are in my body, whose violence drinks up my blood: whenever I am going to speak, they pierce me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} What then? will the wild ass bray for nothing, if he is not seeking food? or again, will the ox low at the manger, when he has a fodder? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Shall bread be eaten without salt? or again, is there taste in empty words? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For my wrath can’t cease; for I perceive my food as the smell of a lion [to be] loathsome. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For oh that he would grant [my desire], and my petition might come, and the Lord would grant my hope! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let the Lord begin and wound me, but let him not utterly destroy me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let the grave be my city, upon the walls of which I have leaped: I will not shrink from it; for I have not denied the holy words of my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For what is my strength, that I continue? what is my time, that my soul endures? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Or have I not trusted in him? but help is [far] from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Mercy has rejected me; and the visitation of the Lord has disregarded me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} My nearest relations have not regarded me; they have passed me by like a failing brook, or like a wave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They who used to reverence me, now have come against me like snow or congealed ice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} When it has melted at the approach of heat, it is not known what it was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Thus I also have been deserted of all; and I am ruined, and become an outcast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Behold the ways of the Thaemanites, you⌃ that mark the paths of the Sabaeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} They too that trust in cities and riches shall come to shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But you⌃ also have come to me without pity; so that beholding my wound you⌃ are afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} What? have I made any demand of you? or do I ask for strength from you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} to deliver me from enemies, or to rescue me from the hand of the mighty ones? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Teach you⌃ me, and I will be silent: if in anything I have erred, tell me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But as it seems, the words of a true man are vain, because I do not ask strength of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Neither will your reproof cause me to cease my words, for neither will I endure the sound of your speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Even because you⌃ attack the fatherless, and insult your friend. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But now, having looked upon your countenances, I will not lie. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Sit down now, and let there not be unrighteousness; and unite again with the just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For there is no injustice in my tongue; and does not my throat meditate understanding?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} thoroughly, laid Heb. lifted up \textsuperscript{3} heavier; my words are swallowed up that is, I want words to express my grief \textsuperscript{4} the arrows;, ; drinketh up; the terrors \textsuperscript{5} when he hath grass Heb. at grass, loweth \textsuperscript{8} the thing that I long for Heb. my expectation \textsuperscript{9} that it would, ; that he would \textsuperscript{10} Then, I would let him not; have not concealed;, ; the Holy One \textsuperscript{13} Is not my; and is wisdom \textsuperscript{14} To him, ; is afflicted Heb. melteth he forsaketh \textsuperscript{15} My brethren;, ; as the stream \textsuperscript{17} vanish Heb. are cut off when it is hot they are consumed Heb. in the heat thereof they are extinguished. \textsuperscript{21} ye are nothing or, ye are like to them, Heb. to it, ; nothing Heb. not ye see \textsuperscript{24} Teach me, ; I will; cause me \textsuperscript{26} reprove, ; one that, as wind \textsuperscript{27} overwhelm Heb. cause to fall upon the fatherless, ; ye dig \textsuperscript{28} evident unto you Heb. before your face if I lie \textsuperscript{29} Return; my righteousness in it that is, in this matter \textsuperscript{30} iniquity, cannot, ; taste Heb. palate\par}
