\subsection*{Job 7}
\markright{JOB 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Is not the life of man upon earth a state of trial? and his existence as that of a hireling by the day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Or as a servant that fears his master, and one who has grasped a shadow? or as a hireling waiting for his pay? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So have I also endured months of vanity, and nights of pain have been appointed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Whenever I lie down, I say, When [will it be] day? and whenever I rise up, again [I say] when [will it be] evening? and I am full of pains from evening to morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And my body is covered with loathsome worms; and I waste away, scraping off clods of dust from my eruption. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And my life is lighter than a word, and has perished in vain hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember then that my life is breath, and my eye shall not yet again see good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The eye of him that sees me shall not see me [again]: your eyes are upon me, and I am no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} [I am] as a cloud that is cleared away from the sky: for if a man go down to the grave, he shall not come up again: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and he shall surely not return to his own house, neither shall his place know him any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Then neither will I refrain my mouth: I will speak being in distress; being in anguish I will disclose the bitterness of my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Am I a sea, or a serpent, that you have set a watch over me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I said that my bed should comfort me, and I would privately counsel with myself on my couch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You scare me with dreams, and do terrify me with visions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You will separate life from my spirit; and yet [keep] my bones from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For I shall not live for ever, that I should patiently endure: depart from me, for my life [is] vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For what is man, that you have magnified him? or that you give heed to him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Will you visit him till the morning, and judge him till [the time of] rest? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} How long do you not let me alone, nor let me go, until I shall swallow down my spittle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} If I have sinned, what shall I be able to do, O you that understand the mind of men? why have you made me as your accuser, and [why] am I a burden to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Why have you not forgotten my iniquity, and purged my sin? but now I shall depart to the earth; and in the morning I am no more.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Is there; an appointed time or, a warfare, like the days \textsuperscript{2} earnestly desireth Heb. gapeth after, the shadow as an hireling \textsuperscript{4} When, ;, night etc. Heb. evening be measured tossings \textsuperscript{7} remember; , ; my life; no more see Heb. not return to see, that is, to enjoy \textsuperscript{8} The eye; thine eyes; I am not that is, I can live no longer \textsuperscript{11} I will not, ; the anguish; the bitterness \textsuperscript{12} I a sea; a whale \textsuperscript{16} I loathe it, ; let me alone; my days \textsuperscript{17} What is man; magnify; set thine \textsuperscript{20} I have sinned, ; O thou preserver; why hast, ; I am \textsuperscript{21} why dost; take away; sleep, ; in the morning but I shall not be\par}

\subsection*{Job 8}
\markright{JOB 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Baldad the Sauchite answered, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How long will you speak these things, [how long shall] the breath of your mouth [be] abundant in words? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Will the Lord be unjust when he judges; or will he that has made all things pervert justice? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If your sons have sinned before him, he has cast them away because of their transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But be you early in prayer to the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If you are pure and true, he will listen to your supplication, and will restore to you the habitation of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Though then your beginning should be small, yet your end should be unspeakably great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For ask of the former generation, and search diligently among the race of [our] fathers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} (for we are of yesterday, and know nothing; for our life upon the earth is a shadow:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} shall not these teach you, and report [to you], and bring out words from [their] heart? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Does the rush flourish without water, or shall the flag grow up without moisture? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When it is yet on the root, and [though] it has not been cut down, does not any herb wither before it has received moisture? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Thus then shall be the end of all that forget the Lord: for the hope of the ungodly shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For his house shall be without inhabitants, and his tent shall prove a spider's web. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If he should prop up his house, it shall not stand: and when he has taken hold of it, it shall not remain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For it is moist under the sun, and his branch shall come forth out of his dung-heap. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He lies down upon a gathering of stones, and shall live in the mist of flints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} If [God] should destroy [him], his place shall deny him. Have you not seen such things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} that such is the overthrow of the ungodly? and out of the earth another shall grow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the Lord will by no means reject the harmless man; but he will not receive any gift of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But he will fill with laughter the mouth of the sincere, and their lips with thanksgiving. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But their adversaries shall clothe themselves with shame; and the habitation of the ungodly shall perish.\par

Used for impiety and moral pollution. \textsuperscript{17} Gk. vocab: rhiza (ῥίζα) = root. Common English renderings: root. Literal root and figurative source are both possible.\par}

\subsection*{Job 9}
\markright{JOB 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I know of a truth that it is so: for how shall a mortal man be just before the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For if he would enter into judgment with him, [God] would not listen to him, so that he should answer to one of his charges of a thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For he is wise in mind, and mighty, and great: who has hardened himself against him and endured? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who wears out the mountains, and [men] know it not: who overturns them in anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who shakes the [earth] under heaven from its foundations, and its pillars totter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Who commands the sun, and it rises not; and he seals up the stars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Who alone has stretched out the heavens, and walks on the sea as on firm ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who makes Pleias, and Hesperus, and Arcturus, and the chambers of the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who does great and unsearchable things; glorious also and excellent things, innumerable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If ever he should go beyond me, I shall not see him: if he should pass by me, neither thus have I known [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If he would take away, who shall turn him back? or who shall say to him, What have you done? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For [if] he has turned away [his] anger, the whales under heaven have stooped under him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Oh then that he would listen to me, or judge my cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For though I be righteous, he will not listen to me: I will entreat his judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if I should call and he should not listen, I can’t believe that he has listened to my voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let him not crush me with a dark storm: but he has made by bruises many without cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For he suffers me not to take breath, but he has filled me with bitterness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For indeed he is strong in power: who then shall resist his judgment? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For though I should seem righteous, my mouth will be profane: and though I should seem blameless, I shall be proved perverse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For even if I have sinned, I know it not [in] my soul: but my life is taken away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore I said, Wrath slays the great and mighty man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the worthless die, but the righteous are laughed to scorn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For they are delivered into the hands of the unrighteous [man]: he covers the faces of the judges [of the earth]: but if it be not he, who is it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But my life is swifter than a post: [my days] have fled away, and they knew it not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Or again, is there a trace of [their] path [left] by ships? or is there one of the flying eagle as it seeks [its] prey? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And if I should say, I will forget to speak, I will bow down my face and groan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} I quake in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me alone [as] innocent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But since I am ungodly, why have I not died? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For if I should wash myself with snow, and purge myself with pure hands, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} you had thoroughly plunged me in filth, and my garment had abhorred me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For you are not man like me, with whom I could contend, that we might come together to judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Would that [he] our mediator were [present], and a reprover, and one who should hear [the cause] between both. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Let him remove [his] rod from me, and let not his fear terrify me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} so shall I not be afraid, but I will speak: for I am not thus conscious [of guilt].\par

\subsection*{Job 10}
\markright{JOB 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Weary in my soul, I will pour my words with groans upon him: I will speak being straitened in the bitterness of my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I will say to the Lord, Do not teach me to be impious; and therefore have you thus judged me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Is it good before you if I be unrighteous? for you have disowned the work of your hands, and attended to the counsel of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Or do you see as a mortal sees? or will you look as a man sees? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Or is your life human, or your years [the years] of a man, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} that you have enquired into my iniquity, and searched out my sins? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For you know that I have not committed iniquity: but who is he that can deliver out of your hands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Your hands have formed me and made me; afterwards you did change [your mind], and strike me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Remember that you have made me [as] clay, and you do turn me again to earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Have you not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you did clothe me with skin and flesh, and frame me with bones and sinews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you did bestow upon me life and mercy, and your oversight has preserved my spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Having these things in yourself, I know that you can do all things; for nothing is impossible with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if I should sin, you watch me; and you have not cleared me from iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Or if I should be ungodly, woe is me: and if I should be righteous, I can’t lift myself up, for I am full of dishonor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For I am hunted like a lion for slaughter; for again you have changed and are terribly destroying me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} renewing against me my torture: and you have dealt with me in great anger, and you have brought trials upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Why then did you bring me out of the womb? and why did I not die, and no eye see me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and I become as if I had not been? for why was I not carried from the womb to the grave? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Is not the time of my life short? suffer me to rest a little, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} before I go whence I shall not return, to a land of darkness and gloominess; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} to a land of perpetual darkness, where there is no light, neither [can any one] see the life of mortals.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} My soul, ; is weary of my life or, cut off while I live I will leave, I will speak \textsuperscript{3} Is it good, ; despise the work Heb. the labour, ; shine upon \textsuperscript{7} Thou knowest Heb. It is upon thy knowledge, ;, ; and there \textsuperscript{8} hands; have made me Heb. took pains about me yet thou \textsuperscript{9} Remember;, thou hast; into dust again \textsuperscript{15} If I be wicked, ; righteous, ; I am full, see \textsuperscript{17} witnesses that is, plagues; changes I am as if attacked by successive troops; if one company be wearied, another succeeds to the attack.; war \textsuperscript{21} I go whence; the land; the shadow \textsuperscript{22} the shadow of death Where death projects his shadow, intercepting the light of life. \subsection*{Job 11}
\markright{JOB 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Sophar the Minaean answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He that speaks much, should also hear on the other side: or does the fluent speaker think himself to be righteous? blessed [is] the short lived offspring of woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Be not a speaker of many words; for is there none to answer you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For say not, I am pure in my works, and blameless before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But oh that the Lord would speak to you, and open his lips to you! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then shall he declare to you the power of wisdom; for it shall be double of that which is with you: and then shall you know, that a just recompence of your sins has come to you from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Will you find out the traces of the Lord? or have you come to the end [of that] which the Almighty has made? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Heaven [is] high; and what will you do? and there are deeper things than those in hell; what do you know? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Or longer than the measure of the earth, or the breadth of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if he should overthrow all things, who will say to him, What have you done? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For he knows the works of transgressors; and when he sees wickedness, he will not overlook [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But man vainly buoys himself up with words; and a mortal born of woman [is] like an ass in the desert. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For if you have made your heart pure, and lift up [your] hands towards him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} if there is any iniquity in your hands, put it far from you, and let not unrighteousness lodge in your habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For thus shall your countenance shine again, as pure water; and you shall dive yourself of uncleanness, and shall not fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And you shall forget trouble, as a wave that has passed by; and you shall not be scared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And your prayer [shall be] as the morning star, and life shall arise to you [as] from the noonday. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And you shall be confident, because you have hope; and peace shall dawn to you from out of anxiety and care. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For you shall be at ease, and there shall be no one to fight against you; and many shall charge, and make supplication to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But safety shall fail them; for their hope is destruction, and the eyes of the ungodly shall waste away.\par

\subsection*{Job 12}
\markright{JOB 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} So then you⌃ [alone] are men, and wisdom shall die with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [But] I also have a heart as well as you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For a righteous and blameless man has become a subject for mockery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For it had been ordained that he should fall under others at the appointed time, and that his houses should be spoiled by transgressors: let not however any one trust that, being evil, he shall be [held] guiltless, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} even as many as provoke the Lord, as if there were indeed to be no inquisition [made] of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But ask now the beasts, if they may speak to you; and the birds of the air, if they may declare to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Tell the earth, if it may speak to you: and the fishes of the sea shall explain to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who then has not known in all these things, that the hand of the Lord has made them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Whereas the life of all living things is in his hand, and the breath of every man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the ear tries words, and the palate tastes meats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} In length of time is wisdom, and in long life knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} With him are wisdom and power, with him counsel and understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} If he should cast down, who will build up? if he should shut up against man, who shall open? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If he should withhold the water, he will dry the earth: and if he should let it loose, he overthrows and destroys it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} With him are strength and power: he has knowledge and understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He leads counselors away captive, and maddens the judges of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He seats kings upon thrones, and girds their loins with a girdle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He sends away priests into captivity, and overthrows the mighty ones of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He changes the lips of the trusty, and he knows the understanding of the elders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He pours dishonor upon princes, and heals the lowly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Revealing deep things out of darkness: and he has brought into light the shadow of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Causing the nations to wander, and destroying them: overthrowing the nations, and leading them [away]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Perplexing the minds of the princes of the earth: and he causes them to wander in a way, they have not known, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let them grope [in] darkness, and [let there be] no light, and let them wander as a drunken man.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} But I have; understanding Heb. an heart I am not inferior to you Heb. I fall not lower than you. who knoweth not such things as these. Heb. with whom are not such as these. \textsuperscript{4} one mocked, ; calleth; the just \textsuperscript{5} ready; a lamp; of him \textsuperscript{10} whose hand; soul or, life the breath; mankind Heb. flesh of man \textsuperscript{11} Doth; *marg.; mouth Heb. palate \textsuperscript{13} him that is, God, wisdom, ; counsel \textsuperscript{14} he breaketh; he shutteth;, *marg.; *marg. up Heb. upon \textsuperscript{20} the speech of the trusty Heb. the lip of the faithful, taketh \textsuperscript{21} poureth; weakeneth the strength of the mighty or, looseth the girdle of the strong \textsuperscript{23} increaseth;, ; straiteneth them again Heb. leadeth in \textsuperscript{24} He taketh; and causeth, in a wilderness Bethohoo, "in chaos, " i.e., in a state of utter confusion; it is the same word which is employed in, to describe the chaotic state of the earth at the creation. \textsuperscript{25} grope; maketh; stagger Heb. wander\par}

\subsection*{Job 13}
\markright{JOB 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold, my eye has seen these things, and my ear has heard [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I know all that you⌃ too know; and I have not less understanding than you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Nevertheless I will speak to the Lord, and I will reason before him, if he will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But you⌃ are all bad physicians, and healers of diseases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But would that you⌃ were silent, and it would be wisdom to you in the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But hear you⌃ the reasoning of my mouth, and attend to the judgment of my lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Do you⌃ not speak before the Lord, and utter deceit before him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Or will you⌃ draw back? nay do, you⌃ yourselves be judges. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For [it were] well if he would thoroughly search you: for though doing all things [in your power] you⌃ should attach yourselves to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} he will not reprove you at all the less: but if moreover you⌃ should secretly respect persons, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} shall not his whirlpool sweep you round, and terror from him fall upon you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And your glorying shall prove in the end to you like ashes, and your body [like a body] of clay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Be silent, that I may speak, and cease from [my] anger, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} while I may take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Though the Mighty One should lay hand upon me, forasmuch as he has begun, verily I will speak, and plead before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And this shall turn to me for salvation; for fraud shall have no entrance before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Hear, hear you⌃ my words, for I will declare in your hearing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold, I am near my judgment: I know that I shall appear evidently just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For who is he that shall plead with me, that I should now be silent, and expire? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But grant me two things: then I will not hide myself from your face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Withhold [your] hand from me: and let not your fear terrify me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then shall you call, and I will listen to you: or you shall speak, and I will give you an answer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} How many are my sins and my transgressions? teach me what they are. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore hide you yourself from me, and deem me your enemy? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Will you be startled [at me], as [at] a leaf shaken by the wind? or will you set yourself against me as against grass borne upon the breeze? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} for you have written evil things against me, and you have compassed me with the sins of my youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And you have placed my foot in the stocks; and you have watched all my works, and have penetrated my heels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} [I am as] that which waxes old like a bottle, or like a moth-eaten garment.\par

\subsection*{Job 14}
\markright{JOB 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For a mortal born of a woman [is] short lived, and full of wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Or he falls like a flower that has bloomed; and he departs like a shadow, and can’t continue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Have you not taken account even of him, and caused him to enter into judgment before you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For who shall be pure from uncleanness? not even one; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} if even his life should be [but] one day upon the earth: and his months are numbered by him: you have appointed [him] for a time, and he shall by no means exceed [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Depart from him, that he may be quiet, and take pleasure in his life, [though] as a hireling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For there is hope for a tree, even if it should be cut down, [that] it shall blossom again, and its branch shall not fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For though its root should grow old in the earth, and its stem die in the rock; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} it will blossom from the scent of water, and will produce a crop, as one newly planted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But a man that has died is utterly gone; and when a mortal has fallen, he is no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the sea wastes in [length of] time, and a river fails and is dried up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And man that has lain down [in death] shall certainly not rise again till the heaven be dissolved, and they shall not awake from their sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For oh that you had kept me in the grave, and had hidden me until your wrath should cease, and you should set me a time in which you would remember me! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if a man should die, shall he live [again], having accomplished the days of his life? I will wait till I exist again? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then shall you call, and I will listen to you: but do not you reject the work of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But you have numbered my devices: and not one of my sins shall escape you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And you have sealed up my transgressions in a bag, and marked if I have been guilty of any transgression unawares. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And verily a mountain falling will utterly be destroyed, and a rock shall be worn out of its place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The waters wear the stones, and waters falling headlong [overflow] a heap of the earth: and you destroy the hope of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You drive him to an end, and he is gone: you set your face against him, and send him away; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and though his children be multiplied, he knows [it] not; and if they be few, he is not aware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But his flesh is in pain, and his soul mourns.\par

\subsection*{Job 15}
\markright{JOB 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Eliphaz the Thaemanite answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Will a wise man give for answer a [mere] breath of wisdom? and does he fill up the pain of his belly, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} reasoning with improper sayings, and with words wherein is no profit? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Have not you moreover cast off fear, and accomplished such words before the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} You are guilty by the words of your mouth, neither have you discerned the words of the mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let your own mouth, and not me, reprove you: and your lips shall testify against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} What! are you the first man that was born? or were you established before the hills? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Or have you heard the ordinance of the Lord? or has God used you as [his] counsellor? and has wisdom come [only] to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For what know you, that, we know not? or what understand you, which we do not also? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Truly among us [are] both the old and very aged man, more advanced in days than your father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You have been scourged for [but] few of your sins: you have spoken haughtily [and] extravagantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} What has your heart dared? or what have your eyes [aimed at], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} that you have vented [your] rage before the Lord, and delivered such words from [your] mouth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For who, being a mortal, [is such] that he shall be blameless? or, [who that is] born of a woman, that he should be just? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Forasmuch as he trusts not his saints; and the heaven is not pure before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Alas then, abominable and unclean is man, drinking unrighteousness as a draught. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But I will tell you, listen to me; I will tell you now what I have seen; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} things wise men say, and their fathers have not hidden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} To them alone the earth was given, and no stranger came upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} All the life of the ungodly [is spent] in care, and the years granted to the oppressor are numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And his terror is in his ears: just when he seems to be at peace, his overthrow will come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Let him not trust that he shall return from darkness, for he has been already made over to the power of the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he has been appointed to be food for vultures; and he knows within himself that he is doomed to be a carcass: and a dark day shall carry him away as with a whirlwind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Distress also and anguish shall come upon him: he shall fall as a captain in the first rank. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For he has lifted his hands against the Lord, and he has hardened his neck against the Almighty Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he has run against him with insolence, on the thickness of the back of his shield. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For he has covered his face with his fat, and made layers of fat upon his thighs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And let him lodge in desolate cities, and enter into houses without inhabitant: and what they have prepared, others shall carry away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Neither shall he at all grow rich, nor shall his substance remain: he shall not cast a shadow upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Neither shall he in any wise escape the darkness: let the wind blast his blossom, and let his flower fall off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Let him not think that he shall endure; for his end shall be vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} His harvest shall perish before the time, and his branch shall not flourish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And let him be gathered as the unripe grape before the time, and let him fall as the blossom of the olive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} For death is the witness of an ungodly man, and fire shall burn the houses of them that receive gifts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he shall conceive sorrows, and his end shall be vanity, and his belly shall bear deceit.\par

\subsection*{Job 16}
\markright{JOB 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I have heard many such things: poor comforters are you⌃ all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} What! is there any reason in vain words? or what will hinder you from answering? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I also will speak as you⌃ [do]: if indeed your soul were in my [soul's] stead, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} then would I insult you with words, and I would shake my head at you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And would there were strength in my mouth, and I would not spare the movement of my lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For if I should speak, I shall not feel the pain of my wound: and if I should be silent, how shall I be wounded the less? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But now he has made me weary, and a worn-out fool; and you have laid hold of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} My falsehood has become a testimony, and has risen up against me: it has confronted me to my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In his anger he has cast me down; he has gnashed his teeth upon me: the weapons of his robbers have fallen upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He has attacked me with the keen glances of his eyes; with his sharp [spear] he has struck me [down] upon my knees; and they have run upon me with one accord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the Lord has delivered me into the hands of unrighteous men, and thrown me upon the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When I was at peace he distracted me: he took me by the hair of the head, and plucked it out: he set me up as a mark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} They surrounded me with spears, aiming at my reins: without sparing [me] they poured out my gall upon the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} They overthrew me with fall upon fall: they ran upon me in [their] might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and my strength has been spent on the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} My belly has been parched with wailing, and darkness is on my eyelids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yet there was no injustice in my hands, and my prayer is pure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Earth, cover not over the blood of my flesh, and let my cry have no place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Let my supplication come to the Lord, and let my eye weep before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Oh that a man might plead before the Lord, even [as] the son of man with his neighbor! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But my years are numbered and [their end] come, and I shall go by the way by which I shall not return.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Gk. vocab: paraklēsis (παράκλησις) = comfort; exhortation. Common English renderings: consolation; exhortation. Can denote comfort, encouragement, or exhortation.\par}

\subsection*{Job 17}
\markright{JOB 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I perish, carried away by the wind, and I seek for burial, and obtain [it] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Weary I entreat; and what have I done? and strangers have stolen my goods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who is this? let him join hands with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For you have hid their heart from wisdom; therefore you shall not exalt them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He shall promise mischief to [his] companions: but [their] eyes have failed for [their] children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But you have made me a byword among the nations, and I am become a scorn to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For my eyes are dimmed through pain; I have been grievously beset by all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Wonder has seized true men upon this; and let the just rise up against the transgressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But let the faithful hold on his own way, and let him that is pure of hands take courage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Howbeit, do you⌃ all strengthen [yourselves] and come now, for I do not find truth in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} My days have passed in groaning, and my heart-strings are broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I have turned the night into day: the light is short because of darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For if I remain, Hades is my habitation: and my bed has been made in darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I have called upon death to be my father, and corruption [to be] my mother and sister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Where then is yet my hope? or [where] shall I see my good? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Will they go down with me to Hades, or shall we go down together to the tomb?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} breath is corrupt or, spirit is spent, my days; the graves \textsuperscript{2} mockers, ; continue Heb. lodge, *marg. provocation \textsuperscript{6} a byword; aforetime or, before them as a tabret \textsuperscript{7} Mine eye; members or, thoughts, shadow \textsuperscript{9} hold on; clean; be stronger and stronger Heb. add strength \textsuperscript{10} do ye return; for I \textsuperscript{11} My days; purposes; thoughts Heb. possessions \textsuperscript{13} If I wait; the grave, I have made \textsuperscript{14} said Heb. cried, or, called corruption; to the worm \textsuperscript{16} the bars of the pit; rest\par}

\subsection*{Job 18}
\markright{JOB 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Baldad the Sauchite answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How long will you continue? forbear, that we also may speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For therefore have we been silent before you like brutes? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Anger has possessed you: for what if you should die; would [the earth] under heaven be desolate? or shall the mountains be overthrown from their foundations? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the light of the ungodly shall be quenched, and their flame shall not go up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} His light [shall be] darkness in [his] habitation, and his lamp shall be put out with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Let the meanest of men spoil his goods, and let his counsel deceive [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} His foot also has been caught in a snare, [and] let it be entangled in a net. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And let snares come upon him: he shall strengthen those that thirst for his destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} His snare is hid in the earth, and that which shall take him is by the path. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let pains destroy him round about, and let many [enemies] come about him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [vex him] with distressing hunger: and a signal destruction has been prepared for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let the soles of his feet be devoured: and death shall consume his beauty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And let health be utterly banished from his tabernacle, and let distress seize upon him with a charge from the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} It shall dwell in his tabernacle in his night: his excellency shall be sown with brimstone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} His roots shall be dried up from beneath, and his crop shall fall away from above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let his memorial perish out of the earth, and his name shall be publicly cast out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Let [one] drive him from light into darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He shall not be known among his people, nor his house preserved on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But strangers shall dwell in his possessions: the last groaned for him, and wonder seized the first. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} These are the houses of the unrighteous, and this is the place of them that know not the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Job 19}
\markright{JOB 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How long will you⌃ vex my soul, and destroy me with words? only know that the Lord has dealt with me thus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You⌃ speak against me; you⌃ do not feel for me, but bear hard upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Yes verily, I have erred in truth, (but the error abides with myself) in having spoken words which it was not right [to speak]; and my words err, and are unreasonable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But alas! for you⌃ magnify yourselves against me, and insult me with reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Know then that it is the Lord that has troubled [me], and has raised his bulwark against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold, I laugh at reproach; I will not speak: [or] I will cry out, but [there is] nowhere judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I am fenced round about, and can by no means escape: he has set darkness before my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he has stripped me of my glory, and has taken the crown from my head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He has torn me around about, and I am gone: and he has cut off my hope like a tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he has dreadfully handled me in anger, and has counted me for an enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} His troops also came upon me with one accord, liars in wait compassed my ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} My brethren have stood aloof from me; they have recognized strangers [rather] than me: and my friends have become pitiless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} My nearest of kin have not acknowledged me, and they that knew my name, have forgotten me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [As for] my household, and my maidservants, I was a stranger before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I called my servant, and he listened not; and my mouth entreated [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I implored my wife, and earnestly entreated the sons of my concubines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But they rejected me for ever; whenever I rise up, they speak against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They that saw me abhorred me: the very persons whom I had loved, rose up against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} My flesh is corrupt under my skin, and my bones are held in [my] teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Pity me, pity me, O friends; for it is the hand of the Lord that has touched me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore do you⌃ persecute me as also the Lord [does], and are not satisfied with my flesh? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For oh that my words were written, and that they were recorded in a book forever, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} with an iron pen and lead, or graven in the rocks! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For I know that he is eternal who is about to deliver me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [and] to raise up upon the earth my skin that endures these [sufferings]: for these things have been accomplished to me of the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} which I am conscious of in myself, which my eye has seen, and not another, but all have been fulfilled to me in [my] bosom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if you⌃ shall also say, What shall we say before him, and [so] find the root of the matter in him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Do you⌃ also beware of deceit: for wrath will come upon transgressors; and then shall they know where their substance is.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{25} Name of God: Goel (גֹּאֵל) — Redeemer; Kinsman-Redeemer Common English renderings: redeemer. Proclaims God as the one who vindicates, rescues, and stands for His own. Heb. vocab: go’el (גֹּאֵל) = redeemer; avenger; kinsman-redeemer. Common English renderings: redeemer. Noun for one who acts to recover, avenge, or restore kin.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} How long; vex; break me \textsuperscript{3} ten times; ye reproached, make yourselves strange to me or, harden yourselves against me \textsuperscript{7} I cry, ; wrong or, violence no judgment \textsuperscript{10} destroyed; I am gone; mine hope \textsuperscript{18} Yea; young children or, the wicked \textsuperscript{19} my inward friends Heb. the men of my secret, they whom \textsuperscript{20} bone;, ; and to or, as and I am \textsuperscript{23} Oh Heb. Who will give, etc my words; oh that they were Rather, "Oh that they were described yuchakoo in a book, with an iron stile and lead! Were graven on a rock for ever!" Pliny observes, "At first men wrote on palm leaves, and afterwards on the bark or rind of other trees. In process of time, public monuments were written on rolls of lead ( plumbeis voluminibus ); and those of a private nature on linen books, or tables covered with wax." \textsuperscript{26} And though etc. Or, After I shall awake, though this body be destroyed, yet out of my flesh shall I see God. in my flesh \textsuperscript{27} I shall; another Heb. a stranger, though my reins, etc. or, my reins within me are consumed with earnest desire for that day.; within me Heb. in my bosom \textsuperscript{28} Why; seeing etc. or, and what root of matter is found in me, the root. in me Instead of bee, "in me, " bo, "in him, " is the reading of more than 100 manuscripts. \textsuperscript{29} ye afraid; that ye may\par}

\subsection*{Job 20}
\markright{JOB 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Sophar the Minaean answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I did not suppose that you would answer thus: neither do you⌃ understand more than I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I will hear my shameful reproach; and the spirit of my understanding answers me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Have you [not] known these things of old, from the time that man was set upon the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the mirth of the ungodly is a signal downfall, and the joy of transgressors is destruction: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} although his gifts should go up to heaven, and his sacrifice reach the clouds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For when he shall seem to be now established, then he shall utterly perish: and they that knew him shall say, Where is he? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Like a dream that has fled away, he shall not be found; and he has fled like a vision of the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The eye has looked upon him, but shall not [see him] again; and his place shall no longer perceive him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let [his] inferiors destroy his children, and let his hands kindle the fire of sorrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} His bones have been filled with [vigour of] his youth, and it shall lie down with him in the dust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Though evil be sweet in his mouth, [though] he will hide it under his tongue; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} though he will not spare it, and will not leave it, but will keep it in the midst of his throat: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} yet he shall not at all be able to help himself; the gall of an asp is in his belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [His] wealth unjustly collected shall be vomited up; a messenger [of wrath] shall drag him out of his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And let him suck the poison of serpents, and let the serpent's tongue kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let him not see the milk of the pastures, nor the supplies of honey and butter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He has laboured unprofitably and in vain, [for] wealth of which he shall not taste: [it is] as a lean thing, unfit for food, which he can’t swallow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For he has broken down the houses of many mighty men: and he has plundered an habitation, though he built [it] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} There is no security to his possessions; he shall not be saved by his desire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} There is nothing remaining of his provisions; therefore his goods shall not flourish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But when he shall seem to be just satisfied, he shall be straitened; and all distress shall come upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} If by any means he would fill his belly, let [God] send upon him the fury of wrath; let him bring a torrent of pains upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he shall by no means escape from the power of the sword; let the brazen bow wound him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And let the arrow pierce through his body; and let the stars be against his dwelling-place: let terrors come upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And let all darkness wait for him: a fire that burns not out shall consume him; and let a stranger plague his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And let the heaven reveal his iniquities, and the earth rise up against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Let destruction bring his house to an end; let a day of wrath come upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of his goods [appointed him] by the all-seeing [God].\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} my thoughts, ; and for; I make haste Heb. my haste is in me \textsuperscript{5} the triumphing, ; short Heb. from near the joy \textsuperscript{6} his excellency; clouds Heb. cloud \textsuperscript{10} His children etc. or, The poor shall oppress his children, seek his hands \textsuperscript{13} spare it; within his mouth Heb. in the midst of his palate \textsuperscript{17} shall not see; the rivers; floods or, streaming brooks of honey \textsuperscript{18} shall he restore, swallow; his substance Heb. the substance of his exchange and he shall \textsuperscript{19} Because, ; , oppressed Heb. crushed; he hath violently \textsuperscript{21} none of his meat be left or, be none left for his meat \textsuperscript{22} the fulness; every hand, ; wicked or, troublesome \textsuperscript{23} he is about; rain it \textsuperscript{24} flee from; the bow strike him \textsuperscript{26} darkness; a fire; it shall go \textsuperscript{29} the portion, ; appointed unto him by God Heb. of his decree from God\par}

\subsection*{Job 21}
\markright{JOB 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear you⌃, hear you⌃ my words, that I may not have this consolation from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Raise me, and I will speak; then you⌃ shall not laugh me to scorn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} What! is my reproof of man? and why should I not be angry? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Look upon me, and wonder, laying your hand upon your cheek. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For even when I remember, I am alarmed, and pains seize my flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore do the ungodly live, and grow old even in wealth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Their seed is according to [their] desire, and their children are in [their] sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Their houses are prosperous, neither [have they] any where [cause for] fear, neither is there a scourge from the Lord upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Their cow does not cast her calf, and their [beast] with young is safe, and does not miscarry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they remain as an unfailing flock, and their children play before [them], taking up the lute and harp; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and they rejoice at the voice of a song. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they spend their days in wealth, and fall asleep in the rest of the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Yet [such a man] says to the Lord, Depart from me; I desire not to know your ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} What is the Mighty One, that we should serve him? and what profit is there that we should approach him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For their good things were in [their] hands, but he regards not the works of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Nevertheless, the lamp of the ungodly also shall be put out, and destruction shall come upon them, and pangs of vengeance shall seize them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall be as chaff before the wind, or as dust which the storm has taken up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Let his substance fail [to supply] his children: [God] shall recompense him, and he shall know it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Let his eyes see his own destruction, and let him not be saved by the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For his desire is in his house with him, and the number of his months has been suddenly cut off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? and does not he judge murders? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} One shall die in his perfect strength, and wholly at ease and prosperous; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and his inwards are full of fat, and his marrow is diffused [throughout him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And another dies in bitterness of soul, not eating any good thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But they lie down in the earth together, and corruption covers them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So I know you, that you⌃ presumptuously attack me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} so that you⌃ will say, Where is the house of the prince? and where is the covering of the tabernacles of the ungodly? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Ask those that go by the way, and do not disown their tokens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For the wicked hastens to the day of destruction: they shall be led away for the day of his vengeance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Who will tell him his way to his face, whereas he has done [it]? who shall recompense him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he has been led away to the tombs, and he has watched over the heaps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The stones of the valley have been sweet to him, and every man shall depart after him, and [there are] innumerable [ones] before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} How then do you⌃ comfort me in vain? whereas I have no rest from your molestation.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} that I may, mock on \textsuperscript{4} is my complaint;, *title; if it were; troubled Heb. shortened, *marg. \textsuperscript{5} Mark me Heb. Look unto me be astonished, lay your \textsuperscript{9} safe from fear Heb. peace from fear, ; the rod \textsuperscript{15} What is; and what; if we \textsuperscript{17} oft; candle or, lamp distributeth \textsuperscript{18} as stubble; , ; carrieth Heb. stealeth \textsuperscript{19} layeth; iniquity that is, the punishment of his iniquity; for his; he rewardeth; he shall \textsuperscript{23} in his full strength Heb. in his very perfection, or, the strength of his perfection \textsuperscript{24} His breasts or, His milk pails; moistened \textsuperscript{25} in the bitterness, ; *marg.; never \textsuperscript{28} Where; dwelling places Heb. tent of the tabernacles \textsuperscript{30} the wicked; day; wrath Heb. wraths \textsuperscript{32} he be; grave Heb. graves remain in the tomb Heb. watch in the heap \textsuperscript{34} comfort seeing, falsehood Heb. transgression\par}

\subsection*{Job 22}
\markright{JOB 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Eliphaz the Thaemanite answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Is it not the Lord that teaches understanding and knowledge? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For what matters it to the Lord, if you were blameless in [your] works? or is it profitable that you should perfect your way? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Will you maintain and plead your own cause? and will he enter into judgment with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Is not your wickedness abundant, and your sins innumerable? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you have taken security of your brethren for nothing, and have taken away the clothing of the naked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Neither have you given water to the thirsty to drink, but have taken away the morsel of the hungry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you have accepted the persons of some; and you have established those [that were already settled] on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But you have sent widows away empty, and has afflicted orphans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore snares have compassed you, and disastrous war has troubled you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The light has proved darkness to you, and water has covered you on your lying down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Does not he that dwells in the high places observe? and has he not brought down the proud? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you have said, What does the Mighty One know? does he judge in the dark? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A cloud is his hiding-place, and he shall not be seen; and he passes through the circle of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Will you [not] mark the old way, which righteous men have trodden? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} who were seized before their time: their foundations [are as] an overflowing stream. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Who say, What will the Lord do to us? or what will the Almighty bring upon us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel for the wicked is far from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The righteous have seen [it], and laughed, and the blameless one has derided [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Verily their substance has been utterly destroyed, and the fire shall devour what is left of their [property]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Be firm, I pray you, if you can endure; then your fruit shall prosper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And receive a declaration from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And if you shall turn and humble yourself before the Lord, you have [thus] removed unrighteousness far from your habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You shall lay up for yourself [treasure] in a heap on the rock; and Sophir [shall be] as the rock of the torrent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So the Almighty shall be your helper from enemies, and he shall bring you forth pure as silver that has been tried by fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then shall you have boldness before the Lord, looking up cheerfully to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he shall hear you when you pray to him, and he shall grant you [power] to pay your vows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he shall establish to you again a habitation of righteousness and there shall be light upon your paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Because you have humbled yourself; and you shall say, [Man] has behaved proudly, but he shall save him that is of lowly eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} He shall deliver the innocent, and do you save yourself by your pure hands.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Gk. vocab: kerdos (κέρδος) = gain; profit. Common English renderings: gain. A term for gain or advantage.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a man; as he that etc. or, if he may be profitable, doth his good success depend thereon \textsuperscript{4} reprove, ; for fear will he enter \textsuperscript{6} For thou; stripped etc. Heb. stripped the clothes of the naked \textsuperscript{8} But as; mighty man Heb. man of arm honourable Heb. eminent, or, accepted for countenance. \textsuperscript{12} not God; height Heb. head the stars \textsuperscript{13} How or, What doth God know \textsuperscript{16} cut down; whose foundation was overflown with a flood Heb. a flood was poured upon their foundation \textsuperscript{17} Depart; and what; for them or, to them \textsuperscript{20} our substance or, our estate, ; the remnant or, their excellency the fire \textsuperscript{21} Acquaint; him that is, God be at peace \textsuperscript{23} return; built up; thou shalt; put \textsuperscript{24} lay up;, as dust or, on the dust Ophir \textsuperscript{25} the Almighty; defence or, gold; plenty of silver Heb. silver of strength \textsuperscript{29} men;, he shall; the humble person Heb. him that hath low eyes \textsuperscript{30} He shall deliver the island of the innocent or, The innocent shall deliver the island; pureness\par}

\subsection*{Job 23}
\markright{JOB 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Yes, I know that pleading is out of my reach; and his hand has been made heavy upon my groaning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who would then know that I might find him, and come to an end [of the matter]? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I would plead my own cause, and he would fill my mouth with arguments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I would know the remedies which he would speak to me, and I would perceive what he would tell me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Though he should come on me in [his] great strength, then he would not threaten me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} for truth and reproof are from him; and he would bring forth my judgment to an end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For if I shall go first, and exist no longer, still what do I know [concerning] the latter end? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} When he wrought on the left hand, then I observed [it] not: his right hand shall encompass me but I shall not see [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he knows already my way; and he has tried me as gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will go forth according to his commandments, for I have kept his ways; and I shall not turn aside from his commandments, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} neither shall I transgress; but I have hid his words in my bosom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if too he has thus judged, who is he that has contradicted, for he has both willed [a thing] and done it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore am I troubled at him; and when I was reproved, I thought of him. Therefore let me take good heed before him: I will consider, and be afraid of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But the Lord has softened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For I knew not that darkness would come upon me, and thick darkness has covered [me] before my face.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} my complaint; stroke Heb. hand heavier \textsuperscript{3} Oh that, ; where; that I might \textsuperscript{10} he knoweth; the way that I take Heb. the way that is with me he hath; I shall \textsuperscript{12} Neither; I have esteemed Heb. hid, or, laid up;, ; necessary food or, appointed portion \textsuperscript{17} cut off; the darkness from\par}
