\subsection*{Job 24}
\markright{JOB 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But why have the seasons been hidden from the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} while the ungodly have passed over the bound, carrying off the flock with the shepherd? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} They have led away, the ass of the fatherless, and taken the widow's ox for a pledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They have turned aside the weak from the right way: and the meek of the earth have hidden themselves together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they have departed like asses in the field, having gone forth on my account according to their own order: his bread is sweet to [his] little ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They have reaped a field that was not their own before the time: the poor have laboured in the vineyards of the ungodly without pay and without food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They have caused many naked to sleep without clothes, and they have taken away the covering of their body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They are wet with the drops of the mountains: they have embraced the rock, because they had no shelter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They have snatched the fatherless from the breast, and have afflicted the outcast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they have wrongfully caused [others] to sleep without clothing, and taken away the morsel of the hungry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They have unrighteously laid wait in narrow places, and have not known the righteous way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Who have cast forth [the] poor from the city and their own houses, and the soul of the children has groaned aloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Why then has he not visited these? forasmuch as they were upon the earth, and took no notice, and they knew not the way of righteousness, neither have they walked in their [appointed] paths? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But having known their works, he delivered them into darkness: and in the night one will be as a thief: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and the eye of the adulterer has watched [for] the darkness, saying, Eye shall not perceive me, and he puts a covering on his face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} In darkness he digs through houses: by day they conceal themselves securely: they know not the light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the morning is to them all [as] the shadow of death, for [each] will be conscious of the terror of the shadow of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He is swift on the face of the water: let his portion be cursed on the earth; and let their plants be laid bare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [Let them be] withered upon the earth; for they have plundered the sheaves of the fatherless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Then is his sin brought to remembrance, and he vanishes like a vapor of dew: but let what he has done be recompensed to him, and let every unrighteous one be crushed like rotten wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For he has not treated the barren woman well, and has had no pity on a feeble woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And in wrath he has overthrown the helpless: therefore when he has arisen, [a man] will not feel secure of his own life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} When he has fallen sick, let him not hope to recover: but let him perish by disease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For his exaltation has hurt many; but he has withered as mallows in the heat, or as an ear of corn falling off of itself from the stalk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But if not, who is he that says I speak falsely, and will make my words of no account?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} seeing; they that know; not see \textsuperscript{2} landmarks; violently, feed thereof or, feed them \textsuperscript{5} wild asses; rising; the wilderness \textsuperscript{6} They reap; corn Heb. mingled corn, or, dredge they gather etc. Heb. the wicked gather the vintage. \textsuperscript{7} the naked, ; no covering; *marg. \textsuperscript{13} rebel; they know; nor abide \textsuperscript{15} eye; No eye; disguiseth his face Heb. setteth his face in secret, Or, "putteth a covering on his face; " probably the hood of the burnoose, or cloak, which the Arabs sometimes throw over their other garments. \textsuperscript{16} In the dark; they know \textsuperscript{19} Drought consume Heb. violently take so doth \textsuperscript{20} the worm, he shall be; wickedness \textsuperscript{22} draweth; no man is sure of life or, he trusteth not his own life \textsuperscript{23} it be given; whereon; yet his eyes \textsuperscript{24} are exalted;, ; gone Heb. not, *marg. taken out Heb. closed up cut off\par}

\subsection*{Job 25}
\markright{JOB 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Baldad the Sauchite answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} What beginning or fear is his—even he that makes all things in the highest? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For let none think that there is a respite for robbers: and upon whom will there not come a snare from him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For how shall a mortal be just before the Lord? or who that is born of a woman shall purify himself? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If he gives an order to the moon, then it shines not; and the stars are not pure before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But alas! man is corruption, and the son of man a worm.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{6} How much less etc. The original is degradingly expressive: "How much less enosh, miserable man, who is a worm; and the son of Adam, who is toleah, a maggot."\par}

\subsection*{Job 26}
\markright{JOB 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Job answered and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To whom do you attach yourself, or whom are you going to assist? is it not he that [has] much strength, and [he] who has a strong arm? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} To whom have you given counsel? is it not to him who has all wisdom? whom will you follow? is it not one who has the greatest power? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To whom have you uttered words? and whose breath is it that has come forth from you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Shall giants be born from under the water and the inhabitants thereof? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Hell is naked before him, and destruction has no covering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He stretches out the north wind upon nothing, and he upon nothing hangs the earth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} binding water in his clouds, and the cloud is not torn under it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He keeps back the face of his throne, stretching out his cloud upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He has encompassed the face of the water by an appointed ordinance, until the end of light and darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The pillars of heaven are prostrate and astonished at his rebuke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He has calmed the sea with [his] might, and by [his] wisdom the whale has been overthrown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the barriers of heaven fear him, and by a command he has slain the apostate dragon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Behold, these are parts of his way; and we will listen to him at the least intimation of his word: but the strength of his thunder who knows, when he shall employ [it]?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} How hast thou Bildad had produced no argument to refute Job's doctrine; and therefore Job ironically admires the assistance which Bildad had given to his friends in their extremity, and the instruction he had afforded him in his perplexity.; helped \textsuperscript{5} Dead things Or, "The giants rephaim are in anguish under the waters and their inhabitants; " probably in allusion to the destruction of the earth by the deluge.; and or, with \textsuperscript{8} bindeth up, ; thick clouds; and the cloud \textsuperscript{10} compassed; until; day and night come to an end Heb. end of light with darkness \textsuperscript{12} divideth;, ; he smiteth; the proud Heb. pride \textsuperscript{13} his spirit; the crooked serpent\par}

\subsection*{Job 27}
\markright{JOB 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Job further continued and said in his parable, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [As] God lives, who has thus judge me; and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} verily, while my breath is yet in [me], and the breath of God which remains to me is in my nostrils, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} my lips shall not speak evil words, neither shall my soul meditate unrighteous thoughts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Far be it from me that I should justify you till I die; for I will not let go my innocence, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} but keeping fast to [my] righteousness I will by no means let it go: for I am not conscious to myself of having done any thing amiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Nay rather, but let my enemies be as the overthrow of the ungodly, and they that rise up against me, as the destruction of transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For what is the hope of the ungodly, that he holds to it? will he indeed trust in the Lord [and] be saved? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Will God hear his prayer? or, when distress has come upon him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} has he any confidence before him? or will [God] hear him as he calls upon him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Yet now I will tell you what is in the hand of the Lord: I will not lie concerning the things which are with the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Behold, you⌃ all know that you⌃ are adding vanity to vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of oppressors shall come upon them from the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if their children be many, they shall be for slaughter: and if they grow up, they shall beg. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they that survive of him shall utterly perish, and no one shall pity their widows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Even if he should gather silver as earth, and prepare gold as clay; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} All these things shall the righteous gain, and the true-hearted shall possess his wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And his house is gone like moths, and like a spider's web. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The rich man shall lie down, and shall not continue: he has opened his eyes, and he is not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Pains have come upon him as water, and darkness has carried him away by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And a burning wind shall catch him, and he shall depart, and it shall utterly drive him out of his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [God] shall cast [trouble] upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He shall cause [men] to clap their hands against them, and shall hiss him out of his place.\par

\subsection*{Job 28}
\markright{JOB 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For there is a place for the silver, whence it comes, and a place for the gold, whence it is refined. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For iron comes out of the earth, and brass is hewn out like stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He has set a bound to darkness, and he searches out every limit: a stone [is] darkness, and the shadow of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} There is a cutting off the torrent by reason of dust: so they that forget the right way are weakened; they are removed from [among] men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [As for] the earth, out of it shall come bread: under it has been turned up as it were fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Her stones are the place of the sapphire: and [her] dust [supplies] man with gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [There is] a path, the fowl has not known it, neither has the eye of the vulture seen it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} neither have the sons of the proud trodden it, a lion has not passed upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He has stretched forth his hand on the sharp [rock], and turned up mountains by the roots: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and he has interrupted the whirlpools of rivers, and my eye has seen every precious thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he has laid bare the depths of rivers, and has brought his power to light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But whence has wisdom been discovered? and what is the place of knowledge? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A mortal has not known its way, neither indeed has it been revealed among men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The depth said, It is not in me: and the sea said, It is not with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} One shall not give fine gold instead of it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Neither shall it be compared with gold of Sophir, with the precious onyx and sapphire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Gold and crystal shall not be equalled to it, neither shall vessels of gold be its exchange. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Coral and fine pearl shall not be mentioned: but do you esteem wisdom above the most precious things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equalled to it; it shall not be compared with pure gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whence then is wisdom found? and of what kind is the place of understanding? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} It has escaped the notice of every man, and has been hidden from the birds of the sky. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Destruction and Death said, We have heard the report of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} God has well ordered the way of it, and he knows the place of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For he surveys the whole [earth] under heaven, knowing the things in the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} all that he has made; the weight of the winds, the measures of the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} When he made [them], thus he saw and numbered them, and made a way for the pealing of the thunder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then he saw it, and declared it: he prepared it [and] traced it out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And he said to man, Behold, godliness is wisdom: and to abstain from evil is understanding.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} vein or, mine the silver, ; where they fine it \textsuperscript{6} sapphires; dust of gold or, gold ore \textsuperscript{9} rock or, flint he overturneth \textsuperscript{11} bindeth; overflowing Heb. weeping and the thing \textsuperscript{15} It cannot be gotten for gold Heb. Fine gold shall not be given for it \textsuperscript{18} coral or, Ramoth, pearls;, rubies \textsuperscript{21} hid; from the fowls air or, heaven \textsuperscript{25} To make the weight etc. God has given an atmosphere to the earth, which, possessing a certain degree of gravity perfectly suited to the necessities of all animals, vegetables, and fluids, should be the cause, in His hands, of preserving animal and vegetable life; for by it the blood circulates in the veins of animals, and the juices in the tubes of vegetables. Without this atmospheric pressure there could be no respiration; and the elasticity of the particles of air in animal and vegetable bodies, would rupture the vessels in which they are contained, and destroy both kinds of life.; he weigheth He has exactly proportioned the aqueous surface of the earth to the terrene parts, for the purpose of evaporation, etc. \textsuperscript{27} declare it or, number it he prepared it \textsuperscript{28} unto man; fear; to depart\par}

\subsection*{Job 29}
\markright{JOB 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Job continued and said in his parable, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Oh that I were as in months past, wherein God preserved me! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} As when his lamp shone over my head; when by his light I walked through darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [As] when I steadfastly pursued my ways, when God took care of my house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When I was very fruitful, and my children were about me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} when my ways were moistened with butter, and the mountains flowed for me with milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} When I went forth early in the city, and the seat was placed for me in the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and all the old men stood up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the great men ceased speaking, and laid their finger on their mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they that heard [me] blessed me, and their tongue clave to their throat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the ear heard, and blessed me; and the eye saw me, and turned aside. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For I saved the poor out of the hand of the oppressor, and helped the fatherless who had no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let the blessing of the perishing one come upon me; yes, the mouth of the widow has blessed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Also I put on righteousness, and clothed myself with judgment like a mantle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I was the eye of the blind, and the foot of the lame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I was the father of the helpless; and I searched out the cause which I knew not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I broke the jaw teeth of the unrighteous; I plucked the spoil out of the midst of their teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I said, My age shall continue as the stem of a palm tree; I shall live a long while. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [My] root was spread out by the water, and the dew would lodge on my crop. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} My glory was fresh in me, and by bow prospered in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [Men] heard me, and gave heed, and they were silent at my counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} At my word they spoke not again, and they were very gland whenever I spoke to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} As the thirsty earth expecting the rain, so they [waited for] my speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Were I to laugh on them, they would not believe [it]; and the light of my face has not failed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I chose out their way, and sat chief, and lived as a king in the midst of warriors, as one comforting mourners.\par

\subsection*{Job 30}
\markright{JOB 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But now the youngest have laughed me to scorn, now they reprove me in [their] turn, whose fathers I set at nothing; whom I did not deem worthy [to be with] my shepherd dogs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Yes, why had I the strength of their hands? for them the full term [of life] was lost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [One is] childless in lack and famine, [such as] they that fled but lately the distress and misery of drought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who compass the salt places on the sounding [shore], who had salt [herbs] for their food, and were dishonorable and of no repute, in lack of every good thing; who also ate roots of trees by reason of great hunger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thieves have risen up against me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} whose houses were the caves of the rocks, who lived under the wild shrubs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They will cry out among the rustling [bushes]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} [They are] sons of fools and vile men, [whose] name and glory [are] quenched from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But now I am their music, and they have me for a byword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they stood aloof and abhorred me, and spared not to spit in my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For he has opened his quiver and afflicted me: they also have cast off the restraint of my presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They have risen up against [me] on the right hand of [their] offspring; they have stretched out their foot, and directed against me the ways of their destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} My paths are ruined; for they have stripped off my raiment: he has shot at me with his weapons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he has pleaded against me as he will: I am overwhelmed with pains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} My pains return upon [me]; my hope is gone like the wind, and my safety as a cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Even now my life shall be poured forth upon me; and days of anguish seize me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And by night my bones are confounded; and my sinews are relaxed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} With great force [my disease] has taken hold of my garment: it has compassed me as the collar of my coat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you have counted me as clay; my portion in dust and ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And I have cried to you, but you hear me not: but they stood still, and observed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They attacked me also without mercy: you have scourged me with a strong hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you have put me to grief, and have cast me away from safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For I know that death will destroy me: for the earth is the house [appointed] for every mortal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Oh then that I might lay hands upon myself, or at least ask another, and he should do this for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Yet I wept over every helpless man; I groaned when I saw a man in distress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But I, when I waited for good things, behold, days of evils came the more upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} My belly boiled, and would not cease: the days of poverty prevented me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} I went mourning without restraint: and I have stood and cried out in the assembly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} I am become a brother of monsters, and a companion of ostriches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And my skin has been greatly blackened, and my bones are burned with heat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} My harp also has been turned into mourning, and my song into my weeping.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} they that are; younger than I Heb. of fewer days than I whose \textsuperscript{3} solitary or, dark as the night, fleeing into; in former time Heb. yesternight \textsuperscript{4} mallows The Hebrew malluach, in Arabic, malluch, and in Syriac mallucho, is probably the Lalima or Lalimos of the Greeks, and halimus of the Romans, which Dioscorides describes as a kind of bramble, without thorns, the leaves of which are boiled and eaten. juniper roots The Hebrew rothem, in Arabic, ratim, and in Spanish, retama, most probably signifies the genista or broom, which is very abundant in the deserts of Arabia. for their meat \textsuperscript{7} brayed; the nettles Charul probably denotes some kind of briar or bramble, so Vulgate renders it by spina or sentis, ( . ). Celsius and Scheuchzer are inclined to think it the paliurus, a shrub growing sometimes to a considerable height in desert places. "One of the inconveniences of the vegetable thickets of Egypt is, " says Denon, "that it is difficult to remain in them, as nine tenths of the trees and plants are armed with inexorable thorns, which suffer only an unquiet enjoyment of the shadow which is so constantly desirable." \textsuperscript{8} children; fools, base men Heb. men of no name viler \textsuperscript{10} abhor me; flee far; spare not to spit in my face Heb. withhold not spittle from my face \textsuperscript{15} Terrors, ; soul Heb. principal one as a cloud \textsuperscript{16} my soul; have taken hold \textsuperscript{17} My bones; in the night season \textsuperscript{21} become cruel Heb. turned to be cruel, ; thy strong hand Heb. the strength of thy hand \textsuperscript{22} liftest me; to ride, substance or, wisdom \textsuperscript{24} grave Heb. heap they cry \textsuperscript{25} Did not I; in trouble Heb. hard of day was \textsuperscript{29} a brother; owls or, ostriches, Benoth yaanah, in Arabic, bintu naamatin, not owls, but ostriches, so called from their doleful and hideous noises. "I have often, " says Dr. Shaw, "heard them groan as if they were in the greatest agonies."\par}

\subsection*{Job 31}
\markright{JOB 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I made a covenant with my eyes, and I will not think upon a virgin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Now what portion has God given from above? and is there an inheritance [given] of the Mighty One from the highest? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Alas! destruction to the unrighteous, and rejection to them that do iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Will he not see my way, and number all my steps? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But if I had gone with scorners, and if too my foot has hasted to deceit: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} (for I am weighed in a just balance, and the Lord knows my innocence:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} if my foot has turned aside out of the way, or if my heart has followed my eye, and if too I have touched gifts with my hands; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} then let me sow, and let others eat; and let me be uprooted on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If my heart has gone forth after another man's wife, and if I laid wait at her doors; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} then let my wife also please another, and let my children be brought low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the rage of anger is not to be controlled, [in the case] of defiling [another] man's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For it is a fire burning on every side, and whoever it attacks, it utterly destroys. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if too I despised the judgment of my servant or [my] handmaid, when they pleaded with me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} what then shall I do if the Lord should try me? and if also he should at all visit me, can I make an answer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Were not they too formed as I also was formed in the womb? yes, we were formed in the same womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But the helpless missed not whatever need they had, and I did not cause the eye of the widow to fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if too I ate my morsel alone, and did not impart [of it] to the orphan; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} (for I nourished [them] as a father from my youth and guided [them] from my mother's womb.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if too I overlooked the naked as he was perishing, and did not clothe him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and if the poor did not bless me, and their shoulders were [not] warmed with the fleece of my lambs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} if I lifted my hand against an orphan, trusting that my strength was far superior [to his]: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} let them my shoulder start from the blade-bone, and my arm be crushed off from the elbow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the fear of the Lord constrained me, and I can’t bear up by reason of his burden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} If I made gold my treasure, and if too I trusted the precious stone; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and if too I rejoiced when my wealth was abundant, and if too I laid my hand on innumerable [treasures]: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} (do we not see the shining sun eclipsed, and the moon waning? for they have not [power to continue]:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and if my heart was secretly deceived, and if I have laid my hand upon my mouth and kissed it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} let this also then be reckoned to me as the greatest iniquity: for I [should] have lied against the Lord Most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And if too I was glad at the fall of my enemies, and my heart said, Aha! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} let then my ear hear my curse, and let me be a byword among my people in my affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And if too my handmaids have often said, Oh that we might be satisfied with his flesh; (whereas I was very kind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} for the stranger did not lodge without, and my door was opened to every one that came:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} or if too having sinned unintentionally, I hid my sin; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} (for I did not stand in awe of a great multitude, so as not to declare boldly before them:) and if too I permitted a poor man to go out of my door with an empty bosom: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} (Oh that I had a hearer,) and if I had not feared the hand of the Lord; and [as to] the written charge which I had against any one, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} I would place [it] as a chaplet on my shoulders, and read it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And if I did not read it and return it, having taken nothing from the debtor: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} If at any time the land groaned against me, and if its furrows mourned together; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and if I ate its strength alone without price, and if I too grieved the heart of the owner of the soil, by taking [anything] from [him]: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} then let the nettle come up to me instead of wheat, and a bramble instead of barley. And Job ceased speaking.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{6} Let me be weighed in an even balance Heb. \subsection*{Job 32}
\markright{JOB 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And his three friends also ceased any longer to answer Job: for Job was righteous before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then Elius the son of Barachiel, the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, of the country of Ausis, was angered: and he was very angry with Job, because he justified himself before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he was also very angry with [his] three friends, because they were not able to return answers to Job, yet set him down for an ungodly man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But Elius had forborne to give an answer to Job, because they were older than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Elius saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men; and he was angered in his wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Elius the Buzite the son of Barachiel answered and said, I am younger in age, and you⌃ are elder, therefore I kept silence, fearing to declare to you my own knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I said, It is not time that speaks, though in many years [men] know wisdom: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} but there is a spirit in mortals; and the inspiration of the Almighty is that which teaches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The long-lived are not wise [as such]; neither do the aged know judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore I said, Hear me, and I will tell you what I know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Listen to my words; for I will speak in your hearing, until you⌃ shall have tried [the matter] with words: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and I shall understand as far as you; and, behold, there was no one of you that answered Job his words in argument, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} lest you⌃ should say, We have found that we have added wisdom to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you⌃ have commissioned a man to speak such words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} They were afraid, they answered no longer; they gave up their speaking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I waited, (for I had not spoken,) because they stood still, they answered not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Elius continued, and said, I will again speak, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} for I am full of words, for the spirit of my belly destroys me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And my belly is as a skin of sweet wine, bound up [and] ready to burst; or as a brazier's laboring bellows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I will speak, that I may open my lips and relieve myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For truly I will not be awed because of man, nor indeed will I be confounded before a mortal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For I know not how to respect persons: and if otherwise, even the moths would eat me.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} to answer Heb. from answering righteous \textsuperscript{2} kindled; Buzite because, ; himself Heb. his soul \textsuperscript{4} waited till Job had spoken Heb. expected Job in words; elder Heb. elder for days \textsuperscript{6} I am; young Heb. few of days ye are durst not Heb. feared \textsuperscript{11} I waited for, reasons Heb. understandings, Instead of tevoonotheychem, nine manuscripts read techoonotheychem, "your arguments; " but the sense is nearly the same. whilst Ad tachkeroon millin, "whilst ye were searching for words; " a fine irony, which they must have felt.; what to say Heb. words \textsuperscript{12} unto you Weadeychem is rendered "and your testimonies, " by the Syriac, Arabic, and LXX, and one of De Rossi's manuscripts (874) is so pointed as to require this reading. behold \textsuperscript{15} amazed;, left off speaking Heb. removed speeches from themselves \textsuperscript{18} matter Heb. words the spirit; within me Heb. of my belly \textsuperscript{19} hath no vent Heb. is not opened new \textsuperscript{20} I will speak, be refreshed Heb. breathe I will open \textsuperscript{22} I know not That is, I cannot\par}

\subsection*{Job 33}
\markright{JOB 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Howbeit hear, Job, my words, and listen to my speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For behold, I have opened my mouth, and my tongue has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} My heart [shall be found] pure by [my] words; and the understanding of my lips shall meditate purity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The Divine Spirit is that which formed me, and the breath of the Almighty that which teaches me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If you can, give me an answer: wait therefore; stand against me, and I [will stand] against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You are formed out of the clay as also I: we have been formed out of the same [substance]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} My fear shall not terrify you, neither shall my hand be heavy upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But you have said in my ears, (I have heard the voice of your words;) because you say, I am pure, not having sinned; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} I am blameless, for I have not transgressed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Yet he has revealed a charge against me, and he has reckoned me as an adversary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he has put my foot in the stocks, and has watched all my ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For how say you, I am righteous, yet he has not listened to me? for he that is above mortals is eternal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But you say, Why has he not heard every word of my cause? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For when the Lord speaks once, or a second time, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [sending] a dream, or in the meditation of the night; (as when a dreadful alarm happens to fall upon men, in slumberings on the bed:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} then opens he the understanding of men: he scares them with such fearful visions: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} to turn a man from unrighteousness, and he delivers his body from a fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He spares also his soul from death, and [suffers] him not to fall in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And again, he chastens him with sickness on his bed, and the multitude of his bones is benumbed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he shall not be able to take any food, though his soul shall desire meat; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} until his flesh shall be consumed, and he shall show his bones bare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} His soul also draws near to death, and his life is in Hades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Though there should be a thousand messengers of death, not one of them shall wound him: if he should purpose in his heart to turn to the Lord, and declare to man his fault, and show his folly; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} he will support him, that he should not perish, and will restore his body as [fresh] plaster upon a wall; and he will fill his bones with morrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he will make his flesh tender as that of a babe, and he will restore him among men in [his] full strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he shall pray to the Lord, and his prayer shall be accepted of him; he shall enter with a cheerful countenance, with a full expression [of praise]: for he will render to men [their] due. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Even then a man shall blame himself, saying, What kind of things have I done? and he has not punished me according to the full amount of my sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Deliver my soul, that it may not go to destruction, and my life shall see the light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Behold, all these things, the Mighty One works in a threefold manner with a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he has delivered my soul from death, that my life may praise him in the light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Listen, Job, and hear me: be silent, and I will speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} If you have words, answer me: speak, for I desire you to be justified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} If not, do you hear me: be silent, and I will teach you.\par

\subsection*{Job 34}
\markright{JOB 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elius continued, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear me, you⌃ wise men; listen, you⌃ that have knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the ear tries words, and the mouth tastes meat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let us choose judgment to ourselves: let us know amount ourselves what is right. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For Job has said, I am righteous: the Lord has removed my judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he has erred in my judgment: my wound is severe without unrighteousness [of mine]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} What man is as Job, drinking scorning like water? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} [saying], I have not sinned, nor committed ungodliness, nor had fellowship with workers of iniquity, to go with the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For you should not say, There shall be no visitation of a man, whereas [there is] a visitation on him from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore hear me, you⌃ that are wise in heart: far be it from me to sin before the Lord, and to pervert righteousness before the almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Yes, he renders to a man accordingly as each of them does, and in a man's path he will find him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And think you that the Lord will do wrong, or will the Almighty who made the earth wrest judgment? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And who is he that made [the whole world] under heaven, and all things therein? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if he would confine, and restrain his spirit with himself; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} all flesh would die together, and every mortal would return to the earth, whence also he was formed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Take heed lest he rebuke [you]: hear this, listen to the voice of words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold then the one that hates iniquities, and that destroys the wicked, who is for ever just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} [He is] ungodly that says to a king, You are a transgressor, [that says] to princes, O most ungodly one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [Such a one] as would not reverence the face of an honorable man, neither knows how to give honor to the great, so as that their persons should be respected. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But it shall turn out vanity to them, to cry and beseech a man; for they dealt unlawfully, the poor being turned aside [from their right]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For he surveys the works of men, and nothing of what they do has escaped him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Neither shall there be a place for the workers of iniquity to hide themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For he will not lay upon a man more [than right]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For the Lord looks down upon all men, who comprehends unsearchable things, glorious also and excellent things without number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Who discovers their works, and will bring night about [upon them], and they shall be brought low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he quite destroys the ungodly, for they are seen before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Because they turned aside from the law of God, and did not regard his ordinances, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} so as to bring before him the cry of the needy; for he will hear the cry of the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he will give quiet, and who will condemn? and he will hide his face, and who shall see him? whether [it be done] against a nation, or against a man also: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} causing a hypocrite to be king, because of the waywardness of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For [there is] one that says to the Mighty One, I have received [blessings]; I will not take a pledge: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} I will see apart from myself: do you show me if I have done unrighteousness; I will not do [so] any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Will he take vengeance for it on you, whereas you will put [it] far [from you]? for you shall choose, and not I; and what you know, speak you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Because the wise in heart shall say this, and a wise man listens to my word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} But Job has not spoken with understanding, his words are not [uttered] with knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Howbeit do you learn, Job: no longer make answer as the foolish: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} that we add not to our sins: for iniquity will be reckoned against us, if [we] speak many words before the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Job 35}
\markright{JOB 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elius resumed and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} What is this that you think to be according to right? who are you that you have said, I am righteous before the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I will answer you, and your three friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Look up to the sky and see; and consider the clouds, how high [they are] above you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If you have sinned, what will you do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and if too you have transgressed much, what can you perform? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And suppose you are righteous, what will you give him? or what shall he receive of your hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Your ungodliness [may affect] a man who is like to you; or your righteousness a son of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They that are oppressed of a multitude will be ready to cry out; they will call for help because of the arm of many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But none said, Where is God that made me, who appoints the night-watches; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} who makes me to differ from the four-footed beasts of the earth, and from the birds of the sky? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There they shall cry, and none shall listen, even because of the insolence of wicked men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the Lord desires not to look on error, for he is the Almighty One. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} He beholds them that perform lawless deeds, and he will save me: and do you plead before him, if you can praise him, as it is [possible] even now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For he is not [now] regarding his wrath, nor has he noticed severely any trespass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Yet Job vainly opens his mouth, in ignorance he multiplies words.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} what advantage, ; If I be cleansed from my sin or, by it more than by my sin \textsuperscript{4} answer thee Heb. return to thee words thy \textsuperscript{15} because; he that is, God visited; he that is, Job in great\par}

\subsection*{Job 36}
\markright{JOB 36}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Elius further continued, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Wait for me yet a little while, that I may teach you: for there is yet speech in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Having fetched my knowledge from afar, and according to my works, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I will speak just things truly, and you shall not unjustly receive unjust words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But know that the Lord will not cast off an innocent man: being mighty in strength of wisdom, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} he will not by any means save alive the ungodly: and he will grant the judgment of the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He will not turn away his eyes from the righteous, but [they shall be] with kings on the throne: and he will establish them in triumph, and they shall be exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But they that are bound in fetters shall be holden in cords of poverty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he shall recount to them their works, and their transgressions, for such will act with violence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But he will listen to the righteous: and he has said that they shall turn from unrighteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If they should hear and serve [him], they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But he preserves not the ungodly; because they are not willing to know the Lord, and because when reproved they were disobedient. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the hypocrites in heart will array wrath [against themselves]; they will not cry, because he has bound them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore let their soul die in youth, and their life be wounded by messengers [of death]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Because they afflicted the weak and helpless: and he will vindicate the judgment of the meek. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he has also enticed you out of the mouth of the enemy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [there is] a deep gulf [and] a rushing stream beneath it, and your table came down full of fatness. Judgment shall not fail from the righteous; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} but there shall be wrath upon the ungodly, by reason of the ungodliness of the bribes which they received for iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Let not [your] mind willingly turn you aside from the petition of the feeble that are in distress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And draw not forth all the mighty [men] by night, so that the people should go up instead of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But take heed lest you do that which is wrong: for of this you have made choice because of poverty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Behold, the Mighty One shall prevail by his strength: for who is powerful as he is? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And who is he that examines his works? or who can say, he has wrought injustice? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Remember that his works are great [beyond] those which men have attempted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Every man has seen in himself, how many mortals are wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Behold, the Mighty One is great, and we shall not know [him]: the number of his years is even infinite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the drops of rain are numbered by him, and shall be poured out in rain to form a cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The ancient [heavens] shall flow, and the clouds overshadow innumerable mortals: he has fixed a time to cattle, and they know the order of rest. [Yet] by all these things your understanding is not astonished, neither is your mind disturbed in [your] body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And though one should understand the outspreadings of the clouds, [or] the measure of his tabernacle; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} behold he will stretch his bow against him, and he covers the bottom of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For by them he will judge the nations: he will give food to him that has strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} He has hidden the light in [his] hands, and given charge concerning it to the interposing [cloud]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The Lord will declare concerning this [to] his friend: [but there is] a portion also for unrighteousness.\par

\subsection*{Job 37}
\markright{JOB 37}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} At this also my heart is troubled, and moved out of its place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear you a report by the anger of the Lord's wrath, and a discourse shall come out of his mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} His dominion is under the whole heaven, and his light is at the extremities of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} After him shall be a cry with a [loud] voice; he shall thunder with the voice of his excellency, yet he shall not cause men to pass away, for one shall hear his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The Mighty One shall thunder wonderfully with his voice: for he has done great things which we knew not; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} commanding the snow, Be you upon the earth, and the stormy rain, and the storm of the showers of his might. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He seals up the hand of every man, that every man may know his own weakness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the wild beasts come in under the covert, and rest in [their] lair. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Troubles come on out of the secret chambers, and cold from the mountain-tops. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And from the breath of the Mighty One he will send frost; and he guides the water in whatever way he pleases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And [if] a cloud obscures [what is] precious [to him], his light will disperse the cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he will carry round the encircling [clouds] by his governance, to [perform] their works: whatever he shall command them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} this has been appointed by him on the earth, whether for correction, [or] for his land, or if he shall find him [an object] for mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Listen to this, O Job: stand still, and be admonished of the power of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} We know that god has disposed his works, having made light out of darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he knows the divisions of the clouds, and the signal overthrows of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But your robe is warm, and there is quiet upon the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Will you establish with him [foundations] for the ancient [heavens? they are] strong as a molten mirror. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore teach me, what shall we say to him? and let us cease from saying much. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Have I a book or a scribe my me, that I may stand and put man to silence? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But the light is not visible to all: it shines afar off in the heavens, as that which is from him in the clouds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} From the [north] come the clouds shining like gold: in these great are the glory and honor of the Almighty; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and we do not find another his equal in strength: [as for] him that judges justly, do you not think that he listens? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore men shall fear him; and the wise also in heart shall fear him.\par

\subsection*{Job 38}
\markright{JOB 38}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after Elius had ceased from speaking, the Lord spoke to Job through the whirlwind and clouds, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who is this that hides counsel from me, and confines words in [his] heart, and thinks to conceal [them] from me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Gird your loins like a man; and I will ask you, and do you answer me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Where were you when I founded the earth? tell me now, if you have knowledge, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} who set the measures of it, if you know? or who stretched a line upon it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} On what are its rings fastened? and who is he that laid the corner-stone upon it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I shut up the sea with gates, when it rushed out, coming forth out its mother's womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I made a cloud its clothing, and swathed it in mist. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I set bounds to it, surrounding it with bars and gates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I said to it, Hitherto shall you come, but you shall not go beyond, but your waves shall be confined within you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Or did I order the morning light in your time; and [did] the morning star [then first] see his appointed place; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} to lay hold of the extremities of the earth, to cast out the ungodly out of it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Or did you take clay of the ground, and form a living creature, and set it with the power of speech upon the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And have you removed light from the ungodly, and crushed the arm of the proud? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Or have you gone to the source of the sea, and walked in the tracks of the deep? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And do the gates of death open to you for fear; and did the porters of hell quake when they saw you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And have you been instructed in the breadth of the [whole earth] under heaven? tell me now, what is the extent of it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And in what kind of a land does the light dwell? and of what kind is the place of darkness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} If you could bring me to their [utmost] boundaries, and if also you know their paths; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I know then that you were born at that time, and the number of your years is great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But have you gone to the treasures of snow? and have you seen the treasures of hail? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And is there a store [of them], for you against the time of [your] enemies, for the day of wars and battle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And whence proceeds the frost? or [whence] is the south wind dispersed over the [whole world] under heaven? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And who prepared a course for the violent rain, and a way for the thunders; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} to rain upon the land where [there is] no man, the wilderness, where there is not a man in it; so as to feed the untrodden and uninhabited [land], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and cause it to send forth a crop of green herbs? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Who is the rain's father? and who has generated the drops of dew? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And out of whose womb comes the ice? and who has produced the frost in the sky, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} which descends like flowing water? who has terrified the face of the ungodly? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And do you understand the band of Pleias, and have you opened the barrier of Orion? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Or will you reveal Mazuroth in his season, and the evening star with his rays? Will you guide them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And know you the changes of heaven, or the events which take place together under heaven? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And will you call a cloud with your voice, and will it obey you with a violent shower of much rain? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And will you send lightnings, and they shall go? and shall they say to you, What is [your pleasure]? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And who has given to women skill in weaving, or knowledge of embroidery? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And who is he that numbers the clouds in wisdom, and has bowed the heaven [down] to the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} For it is spread out as dusty earth, and I have cemented it as one hewn stone to another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And will you hunt a prey for the lions? and satisfy the desires of the serpents? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For they fear in their lairs, and lying in wait couch in the woods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And who has prepared food for the raven? for its young ones wander and cry to the Lord, in search of food.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} Gird; for, answer thou me Heb. make me know \textsuperscript{4} Where, I; hast Heb. knowest \textsuperscript{6} Whereupon; foundations Heb. sockets, fastened Heb. made to sink, or \textsuperscript{7} the morning, the sons; shouted \textsuperscript{10} brake up for it my decreed place or, established my decree upon it \textsuperscript{11} Hitherto Thus far shall thy flux and reflux extend. The tides are marvellously limited and regulated, not only by the lunar and solar attraction, but by the quantum of time required to remove any part of the earth's surface, by its rotation round its axis, from under the immediate attractive influence of the sun and moon. Hence the attraction of the sun and moon, and the gravitation of the sea to its own centre, which prevent too great a flux on the one hand, and too great reflux on the other, are some of those bars and doors by which its proud waves are stayed, and prevented from coming farther.; but; thy proud waves Heb. the pride of thy waves \textsuperscript{13} take, ends Heb. wings, *marg. the wicked \textsuperscript{20} it to or, it at the bound \textsuperscript{26} To cause It is well known that rain falls copiously in thunder storms. The flash is first seen, the clap is next heard, and last the rain descends; though in fact they all take place at the same time. The lightning traverses all space in no perceivable succession of time. Sound is propagated at the rate of 1, 142 feet in a second. Rain travels still more slowly, and will be seen sooner or later according to the weight of the drops, and the distance of the cloud. Now as water is composed of two elastic airs or gases, called oxygen and hydrogen, in the proportion of 88+ of the former and 11, 3/4 of the latter in 100 parts, the electric spark, or matter of lightning, passing through the atmosphere, ignites and decomposes those gases, which explode; and the water falls down in the form of rain. This explosion, as well as the rushing in of the circumambient air to restore the equilibrium, will account for the clap and peal; and thus by the lightning of thunder God causes it to rain on the earth. on the wilderness \textsuperscript{30} the face frozen Heb. taken \textsuperscript{31} Pleiades or, the seven stars, Heb. Cimah, *marg. Orion or, Cesil \textsuperscript{32} Mazzaroth or, the twelve signs, Probably the same as mazzaloth . guide Arcturus Heb. guide them \textsuperscript{35} Canst; Here we are Heb. Behold us; *marg. \textsuperscript{36} Who hath put; who hath given \textsuperscript{37} number; or who, stay Heb. cause to lie down \textsuperscript{38} groweth into hardness or, is turned into mire, Heb. is poured\par}
