\subsection*{Psalm 67 (MT 68)}
\markright{PSALM 67 (MT 68)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (68) For the end, a Psalm of a Song by David. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; and let them that hate him flee from before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} As smoke vanishes, let them vanish: as wax melts before the fire, so let the sinners perish from before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But let the righteous rejoice; let them exult before God: let them be delighted with joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Sing to God, sing praises to his name: make a way for him that rides upon the west (the Lord is his name) and exult before him. They shall be troubled before the face of him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [who is] the father of the orphans, and judge of the widows: [such is] God in his holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} God settles the solitary in a house; leading forth prisoners mightily, also them that act provokingly, [even] them that dwell in tombs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} O God, when you went forth before your people, when you went through the wilderness; Pause: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} the earth quaked, yes, the heavens dropped [water] at the presence of the God of Sina, at the presence of the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} O God, you will grant to your inheritance a gracious rain; for it was weary, but you did refresh it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Your creatures dwell in it: you have in your goodness prepared for the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The Lord God will give a word to them that preach [it] in a great company. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The king of the forces of the beloved, of the beloved, [will] even [grant them] for the beauty of the house to divide the spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Even if you⌃ should lie among the lots, [you⌃ shall have] the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her breast with yellow gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} When the heavenly One scatters kings upon it, they shall be made snow-white in Selmon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The mountain of God is a rich mountain; a swelling mountain, a rich mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore do you⌃ conceive [evil], you⌃ swelling mountains? [this is] the mountain which God has delighted to dwell in; yes, the Lord will dwell [in it] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The chariots of God are ten thousand fold, thousands of rejoicing ones: the Lord is among them, in Sina, in the holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} You are gone up on high, you have led captivity captive, you have received gifts for man, yes, for [they were] rebellious, that you might dwell among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Blessed be the Lord God, blessed be the Lord daily; and the God of our salvation shall prosper us. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Our God is the God of salvation; and to the Lord belong the issues from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But God shall crust the heads of his enemies; the hairy crown of them that go on in their trespasses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The Lord said, I will bring again from Basan, I will bring [my people] again through the depths of the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} That your foot may be dipped in blood, [and] the tongue of your dogs [be stained] with that of [your] enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Your goings, O God, have been seen; the goings of my God, the king, in the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The princes went first, next before the players on instruments, in the midst of damsels playing on timbrels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Praise God in the congregations, the Lord from the fountains of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} There is Benjamin the younger [one] in ecstasy, the princes of Juda their rulers, the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} O God, command you your strength: strengthen, O God, this which you have wrought in us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Because of your temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed: let the crowd of bulls with the heifers of the nations [be rebuked], so that they who have been proved with silver may not be shut out: scatter you the nations that wish for wars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Ambassadors shall arrive out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall hasten [to stretch out] her hand readily to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Sing to God, you⌃ kingdoms of the earth; sing psalms to the Lord. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Sing to God that rides on the heaven of heaven, eastward: behold, he will utter a mighty sound with his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Give you⌃ glory to God: his excellency is over Israel, and his power is in the clouds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} God is wonderful in his holy [places], the God of Israel: he will give power and strength to his people: blessed be God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} God; bless us; cause, ; upon us Heb. with us \textsuperscript{4} O let; for thou, ; govern Heb. lead\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 68 (MT 69)}
\markright{PSALM 68 (MT 69)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (69) For the end, [a Psalm] of David, for alternate [strains]. Save me, O God; for the waters have come in to my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I am stuck fast in deep mire, and there is no standing: I am come in to the depths of the sea, and a storm has overwhelmed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I am weary [of] crying, my throat has become hoarse; my eyes have failed by my waiting on my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: my enemies that persecute me unrighteously are strengthened: then I restored that which I took not away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O God, you know my foolishness; and my transgressions are not hidden from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let not them that wait on you, O Lord of hosts, be ashamed on my account: let not them that seek you, be ashamed on my account, O God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For I have suffered reproach for your sake; shame has covered my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I became strange to my brethren, and a stranger to my mother's children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For the zeal of your house has eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached you are fallen upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I bowed down my soul with fasting, and that was made my reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I put on sackcloth for my covering; and I became a proverb to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They that sit in the gate talked against me, and they that drank wine sang against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But I [will cry] to you, O Lord, in my prayer; O God, it is a propitious time: in the multitude of your mercy hear me, in the truth of your salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Save me from the mire, that I stick not [in it]: let me be delivered from them that hate me, and from the deep waters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Let not the waterflood drown me, nor let the deep swallow me up; neither let the well shut its mouth upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Hear me, O Lord; for your mercy is good: according to the multitude of your compassions look upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And turn not away your face from your servant; for I am afflicted: hear me speedily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Draw near to my soul and redeem it: deliver me because of my enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For you know my reproach, and my shame, and my confusion; all that afflict me are before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} My soul has waited for reproach and misery; and I waited for one to grieve with me, but there was none; and for one to comfort me, but I found none. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They gave [me] also gall for my food, and made me drink vinegar for my thirst. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Let their table before them be for a snare, and for a recompense, and for a stumbling block. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Let their eyes be darkened that they should not see; and bow down their back continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Pour out your wrath upon them, and let the fury of your anger take hold on them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let their habitation be made desolate; and let there be no inhabitant in their tents: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Because they persecuted him whom you have struck; and they have added to the grief of my wounds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Add iniquity to their iniquity; and let them not come into your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} I am poor and sorrowful; but the salvation of your countenance has helped me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} I will praise the name of my God with a song, I will magnify him with praise; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and [this] shall please God more than a young calf having horns and hoofs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Let the poor see and rejoice; seek the Lord diligently, and you⌃ shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} For the Lord hears the poor, and does not set at nothing his fettered ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Let the heavens and the earth raise him, the sea, and all things moving in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For God will save Sion, and the cities of Judea shall be built; and [men] shall dwell there, and inherit it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the seed of his servants shall possess it, and they that love his name shall dwell therein.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 69 (MT 70)}
\markright{PSALM 69 (MT 70)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (70) For the end, by David for a remembrance, that the Lord may save me. Draw near, O God, to my help. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek my soul: let them be turned backward and put to shame, that wish me evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let them that say to me, Aha, aha, be turned back and put to shame immediately. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let all that seek you exult and be glad in you: and let those that love your salvation say continually, Let God be magnified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But I am poor and needy; O God, help me: you are my helper and deliverer, O Lord, delay not.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm It is uncertain when this Psalm was composed; though it is probable that it was written by David during the rebellion of Absalom. It is an exceedingly fine composition; it evidently refers to the advent, passion, and resurrection of our Lord, to the vocation of the Gentiles, and the reprobation of Jews. See the marginal references. the waters \textsuperscript{2} I sink; deep mire Heb. the mire of depth deep waters Heb. depth of waters; the floods \textsuperscript{3} I am, ; my throat; mine; I wait \textsuperscript{4} hate; more than being, then I \textsuperscript{5} and my sins Heb. and my guiltiness, hid\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 70 (MT 71)}
\markright{PSALM 70 (MT 71)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (71) By David, [a Psalm sung by] the sons of Jonadab, and the first that were taken captive. O Lord, I have hoped in you: let me never be put to shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me: incline your ear to me, and save me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Be to me a protecting God, and a strong hold to save me: for you are my fortress and my refuge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the transgressor and unjust man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For you are my support, O Lord; O Lord, [you are] my hope from my youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} On you have I been stayed from the womb: from the belly of my mother you are my protector: of you is my praise continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I am become as it were a wonder to many: but you are [my] strong helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may hymn your glory, [and] your majesty all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Cast me not off at the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength fails. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For my enemies have spoken against me; and they that lay wait for my soul have taken counsel together, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} saying, God has forsaken him: persecute you⌃ and take him; for there is none to deliver [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O God, go not far from me, O my God, draw near to my help. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let those that plot against my soul be ashamed and utterly fail: let those that seek my hurt be clothed with shame and dishonor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But I will hope continually, and will praise you more and more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} My mouth shall declare your righteousness openly, [and] your salvation all the day; for I am not acquainted with the affairs [of men]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I will go on in the might of the Lord: O Lord, I will make mention of your righteousness only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} O God, you have taught me from my youth, and until now will I declare your wonders; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} even until I am old and advanced in years. O God, forsake me not; until I shall have declared your arm to all the generation that is to come: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} even your power and your righteousness, O God, up to the highest [heavens, even] the mighty works which you have done: O God, who is like to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} What afflictions many and sore have you showed me! yet you did turn and quicken me, and brought me again from the depths of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You did multiply your righteousness, and did turn and comfort me, and brought me again out of the depths of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} I will also therefore give thanks to you, O God, [because of] your truth, on an instrument of psalmody: I will sing psalms to you on the harp, O Holy One of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} My lips shall rejoice when I sing to you; and my soul, which you have redeemed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Moreover also my tongue shall dwell all the day upon your righteousness; when they shall be ashamed and confounded that seek my hurt.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} to bring *title O God, to help me Heb. to my help \textsuperscript{2} Let, ; my soul Rather, "my life, " naphshee; for the word has frequently this meaning. be turned \textsuperscript{3} back; aha Heach! Heach! a note of extreme contempt; marking insult and triumph at the same time. \textsuperscript{5} I am, make O Lord\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 38:1; Ps 40:13-17; Ps 69:18; Ps 71:12; Ps 143:7 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 6:10; Ps 35:4; Ps 35:26; Ps 71:13; Ps 109:29; Isa 41:11; Isa 28:13; John 18:6 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 40:15; Acts 1:18; Ps 35:21; Ps 35:25; Prov 24:17-18; Ezek 25:3; Ezek 26:2; Ezek 36:2 \textsuperscript{4} Ps 5:11; Ps 35:27; Ps 40:16; Ps 97:12; Isa 61:10; Isa 65:13-14; Lam 3:25; John 16:20 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 40:17; Ps 69:29; Ps 109:22; Ps 141:1; Ps 13:1-2; Heb 10:37; Rev 22:20\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 71 (MT 72)}
\markright{PSALM 71 (MT 72)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (72) For Solomon. O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [that he may] judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let the mountains and the hills raise peace to your people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} he shall judge the poor of the people in righteousness, and save the children of the needy; and shall bring low the false accuser. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shall continue as long as the sun, and before the moon for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He shall come down as rain upon a fleece; and as drops falling upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In his days shall righteousness spring up; and abundance of peace till the moon be removed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Ethiopians shall fall down before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The kings of Tharsis, and the isles, shall bring presents: the kings of the Arabians and Saba shall offer gifts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all kings shall worship him; all the Gentiles shall serve him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For he has delivered the poor from the oppressor; and the needy who had no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall deliver the souls of the needy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} He shall redeem their souls from usury and injustice: and their name [shall be] precious before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he shall live, and there shall be given him of the gold of Arabia: and [men] shall pray for him continually; [and] all the day shall they praise him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} There shall be an establishment on the earth on the tops of the mountains: the fruit thereof shall be exalted above Libanus, and they of the city shall flourish as grass of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let his name be blessed for ever: his name shall endure longer than the sun: and all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And blessed is his glorious name for ever, even for ever and ever: and all the earth shall be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The hymns of David the son of Jessae are ended.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} my strong habitation Heb. to me for a rock of habitation, ; thou hast, ; my rock \textsuperscript{6} By thee; thou art; my praise \textsuperscript{7} as a wonder Kemopaton, "as a prodigy, " my low estate: - my slaying the lion and bear, - conquering the Philistine, - escaping the fury of Saul, - being raised to the throne of Israel, - enduring such uncommon trials and afflictions, - and experiencing such wonderful deliverances. These all mark me out as the subject of "wonder unto many; but Thou art my strong Refuge."; thou art \textsuperscript{9} Cast; old age This determines the period when this Psalm was composed; for it was in David's old age that the rebellion of Absalom took place. when \textsuperscript{10} and they; lay wait for Heb. watch or observe; take \textsuperscript{13} Let them be etc. "They shall be confounded, " etc.. These are prophetic denunciations., ; covered \textsuperscript{15} My mouth, all the day, I know \textsuperscript{16} I will go; I will make, thy righteousness \textsuperscript{18} Now; when I am old and greyheaded Heb. until old age and grey hairs until I, ; strength Heb. arm \textsuperscript{19} Thy righteousness, ; who hast; who is like God is alone - who can resemble Him? He is that eternal, illimitable, unimpartible, unchangeable, incomprehensible, uncompounded, ineffable Being, whose essence is hidden from all created intelligences, and whose counsels cannot be fathomed by any creature.\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 72 (MT 73)}
\markright{PSALM 72 (MT 73)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (73) A Psalm for Asaph. How good is God to Israel, to the upright in heart! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But my feet were almost overthrown; my goings very nearly slipped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I was jealous of the transgressors, beholding the tranquility of sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For there is no sign of reluctance in their death: and [they have] firmness under their affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They are not in the troubles of [other] men; and they shall not be scourged with [other] men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore pride has possessed them; they have clothed themselves with their injustice and ungodliness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Their injustice shall go forth as out of fatness: they have fulfilled their intention. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They have taken counsel and spoken in wickedness: they have uttered unrighteousness loftily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They have set their mouth against heaven, and their tongue has gone through upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore shall my people return hither: and full days shall be found with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they said, How does God know? and is there knowledge in the Most High? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Behold, these [are] the sinners, and they that prosper always: they have possessed wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I said, Verily in vain have I justified my heart, and washed my hands in innocency. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For I was plagued all the day, and my reproof [was] every morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If I said, I will speak thus; behold, I [should] have broken covenant with the generation of your children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And I undertook to understand this, [but] it is too hard for me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} until I go into the sanctuary of God; [and so] understand the latter end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Surely you have appointed [judgments] to them because of their crafty dealings: you have cast them down when they were lifted up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} How have they become desolate! suddenly they have failed: they have perished because of their iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As the dream of one awakening, O Lord, in your city you will despise their image. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For my heart has rejoiced, and my reins have been gladdened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But I [was] vile and knew not: I became brutish before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Yet I am continually with you: you have holden my right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You have guided me by your counsel, and you have taken me to yourself with glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For what have I in heaven [but you]? and what have I desired upon the earth beside you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} My heart and my flesh have failed: [but] God [is the strength] of my heart, and God is my portion for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For, behold, they that remove themselves far from you shall perish: you have destroyed every one that goes a whoring from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But it is good for me to cleave close to God, to put my trust in the Lord; that I may proclaim all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} for or, of, *title Give; the king's \textsuperscript{4} He shall judge; break; the oppressor \textsuperscript{7} In his days;, ;, ; abundance; so long as the moon endureth Heb. till there be no moon \textsuperscript{9} They that; his enemies, ; lick \textsuperscript{15} And he; to him; shall be given Heb. one shall give prayer; daily \textsuperscript{16} There; upon the fruit; of the city \textsuperscript{17} His name; shall endure Heb. shall be his name etc. Heb. shall be as a son to continue his father's name forever; men; all nations \textsuperscript{20} The prayers This was probably the last Psalm he ever wrote; and with it ends the second book of the Psalter.\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 73 (MT 74)}
\markright{PSALM 73 (MT 74)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (74) [A Psalm] of instruction for Asaph. Therefore have you rejected [us], O God, for ever? [therefore] is your wrath kindled against the sheep of your pasture? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Remember your congregation which you have purchased from the beginning; you did ransom the rod of your inheritance; this mount Sion wherein you have lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Lift up your hands against their pride continually; [because of] all that the enemy has done wickedly in your holy places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they that hate you have boasted in the midst of your feast; they have set up their standards for signs, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} ignorantly as it were in the entrance above; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} they cut down its doors at once with axes as in a wood of trees; they have broken it down with hatchet and stone cutter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They have burnt your sanctuary with fire to the ground; they have profaned the habitation of your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They have said in their heart, [even] all their kindred together, Come, let us abolish the feasts of the Lord from the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} We have not seen our signs; there is no longer a prophet; and [God] will not know us any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach? shall the enemy provoke your name forever? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore turn you away your hand, and your right hand from the midst of your bosom for ever? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But God is our King of old; he has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You did establish the sea, in your might, you did break to pieces the heads of the dragons in the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You did break to pieces the heads of the dragon; you did give him [for] meat to the Ethiopian nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You did cleave fountains and torrents; you dried up mighty rivers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The day is yours, and the night is yours; you have prepared the sun and the moon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You have made all the borders of the earth; you have made summer and spring. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Remember this your creation: an enemy has reproached the Lord, and a foolish people has provoked your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Deliver not to the wild beasts a soul that gives praise to you: forget not for ever the souls of your poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Look upon your covenant: for the dark [places] of the earth are filled with the habitations of iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} let not the afflicted and shamed one be rejected: the poor and needy shall praise your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Arise, O God, plead your cause: remember your reproaches that come from the foolish one all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Forget not the voice of your suppliants: let the pride of them that hate you continually ascend before you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Truly or, Yet, God; to such;, of a clean heart Heb. clean of heart \textsuperscript{5} They are; in trouble as other Heb. in the trouble of other like Heb. with. \textsuperscript{6} Therefore; as a chain; violence *marg.; covereth \textsuperscript{7} eyes; have etc. Heb. pass the thoughts of the heart \textsuperscript{8} corrupt; speak wickedly, ; speak loftily \textsuperscript{14} For all;, ; chastened Heb. my chastisement was \textsuperscript{16} When, ; too painful for me Heb. labour in mine eyes \textsuperscript{22} So; ignorant Heb. I knew not as a; before thee Heb. with thee\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 74 (MT 75)}
\markright{PSALM 74 (MT 75)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (75) For the end, Destroy not, a Psalm of a Song for Asaph. We will give thanks to you, O God, we will give thanks, and call upon your name: I will declare all your wonderful works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} When I shall take a set time, I will judge righteously. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The earth is dissolved, and all that dwell in it: I have strengthened its pillars. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I said to the transgressors, Do not transgress; and to the sinners, Lift not up the horn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Lift not up your horn on high; speak not unrighteousness against God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For [good comes] neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For God is the judge; he puts down one, and raises up another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For [there is] a cup in the hand of the Lord, full of unmingled wine; and he has turned [it] from side to side, but its dregs have not been wholly poured out; all the sinners of the earth shall drink [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But I will exult for ever: I will sing praises to the God of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I will break all the horns of sinners; but the horns of the righteous one shall be exalted.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} O God, ; smoke; the sheep \textsuperscript{2} purchased; rod or, tribe thine, ; redeemed; this mount \textsuperscript{7} cast fire into thy sanctuary Heb. sent thy sanctuary into the fire; defiled; dwelling \textsuperscript{8} said; destroy Heb. break all the synagogues\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 75 (MT 76)}
\markright{PSALM 75 (MT 76)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (76) For the end, among the Hymns, a Psalm for Asaph; a Song for the Assyrian. God is known in Judea: his name is great in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And his place has been in peace, and his dwelling-place in Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} There he broke the power of the bows, the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You do wonderfully shine forth from the everlasting mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} All the simple ones in heart were troubled; all the men of wealth have slept their sleep, and have found nothing in their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, the riders on horses slumbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You are terrible; and who shall withstand you, because of your anger? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You did cause judgment to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} when God arose to judgment, to save all the meek in heart. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the inward thought of man shall give thanks to you: and the memorial of his inward thought shall keep a feast to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Vow, and pay [your vows] to the Lord our God; all that are round about him shall bring gifts, [even] to him that is terrible, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and that takes away the spirits of princes; to him that is terrible among the kings of the earth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm Some consider this Psalm to have been written by David on his accession to the throne over all Israel; others refer it to the time of the captivity, considering it as a continuation of the subject in the preceding; but Bp. Patrick and others are of opinion that it was composed by Asaph to commemorate the overthrow of Sennacherib's army, . of Asaph or, for Asaph for that; wondrous \textsuperscript{2} When;, receive the congregation or, take a set time \textsuperscript{8} For in; it is full Alluding to the medicated wine or potion of stupifying drugs given to criminals to drink previous to their execution.; but the dregs \textsuperscript{10} All the horns; but the horns\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 76 (MT 77)}
\markright{PSALM 76 (MT 77)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (77) For the end, for Idithun, a Psalm of Asaph. I cried to the Lord with my voice, yes, my voice [was addressed] to God; and he gave heed to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In the day of my affliction I earnestly sought the Lord; [even] with my hands by night before him, and I was not deceived; my soul refused to be comforted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I remembered God, and rejoiced; I poured out my complaint, and my soul fainted. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} All my enemies set a watch [against me]: I was troubled, and spoke not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I considered the days of old, and remembered ancient years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I meditated; I communed with my heart by night, and diligently searched my spirit, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will he be well pleased no more? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Will he cut off his mercy for ever, even for ever and ever? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Will God forget to pity? or will he shut up his compassions in his wrath? Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I said, Now I have begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I remembered the works of the Lord; for I will remember your wonders from the beginning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I will meditate on all your works, and will consider your doings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} O God, your way is in the sanctuary; who is a great God as our God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You are the God that do wonders; you have made known your power among the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You have with your arm redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you, and feared; and the depths were troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [There was] an abundant sound of waters: the clouds uttered a voice; for your arrows went abroad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The voice of your thunder was abroad, and around your lightnings appeared to the world; the earth trembled a quaked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters, and your footsteps can’t be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} You did guide your people as sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm This Psalm is entitled in the Septuagint, which is followed by the Vulgate and Appollinarius, Ωδη προς τον Ασσυριον, "An ode against the Assyrian; " and it is considered by many of the best commentators to have been composed by Asaph after the defeat of Sennacherib. of Asaph or, for Asaph In Judah; his \textsuperscript{11} Vow; let all; unto him Heb. to fear\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 77 (MT 78)}
\markright{PSALM 77 (MT 78)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (78) [A Psalm] of instruction for Asaph. Give heed, O my people, to my law: incline your ear to the words of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I will open my mouth in parables: I will utter dark sayings [which have been] from the beginning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} All which we have heard and known, and our fathers have declared to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They were not hid from their children to a second generations; [the fathers] declaring the praises of the Lord, and his mighty acts, and his wonders which he wrought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he raised up a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, to make it known to their children: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} that another generation might know, even the sons which should be born; and they should arise and declare them to their children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} That they might set their hope on God, and not forget the works of God, but diligently seek his commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} That they should not be as their fathers, a perverse and provoking generation; a generation which set not its heart aright, and its spirit was not steadfast with God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The children of Ephraim, bending and shooting [with] the bow, turned [back] in the day of battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} They kept not the covenant of God, and would not walk in his law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they forgot his benefits, and his miracles which he [had] showed them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} the miracles which he wrought before their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Tanes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He clave the sea, and led them through: he made the waters to stand as [in] a bottle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he guided them with a cloud by day, and all the night with a light of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} he clave a rock in the wilderness, and made them drink as in a great deep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he brought water out of the rock, and caused waters to flow down as rivers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they sinned yet more against him; they provoked the Most High in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they tempted God in their hearts, in asking meat for [the desire of] their souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They spoke also against God, and said, Will God be able to prepare a table in the wilderness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Forasmuch as he struck the rock, and the waters flowed, and the torrents ran abundantly; will he be able also to give bread, or prepare a table for his people? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Therefore the Lord heard, and was provoked: and fire was kindled in Jacob, and wrath went up against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in his salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Yet he commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and rained upon them manna to eat, and gave them the bread of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Man ate angels' bread; he sent them provision to the full. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He removed the south wind from heaven; and by his might he brought in the southwest wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he rained upon them flesh like dust, and feathered birds like the sand of the seas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they fell into the midst of their camp, round about their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So they ate, and were completely filled; and he gave them their desire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} They were not disappointed of their desire: [but] when their food was yet in their mouth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} then the indignation of God rose up against them, and killed the fattest of them, and overthrew the choice men of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} In the midst of all this they sinned yet more, and believed not his miracles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And their days were consumed in vanity, and their years with anxiety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} When he killed them, they sought him: and they returned and called betimes upon God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And they remembered that God was their helper, and the most high God was their redeemer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Yet they loved him [only] with their mouth, and lied to him with their tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} For their heart [was] not right with him, neither were they steadfast in his covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} But he is compassionate, and will forgive their sins, and will not destroy [them]: yes, he will frequently turn away his wrath, and will not kindle all his anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he remembered that they are flesh; a wind that passes away, and returns not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} How often did they provoke him in the wilderness, [and] anger him in a dry land! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Yes, they turned back, and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} They remembered not his hand, the day in which he delivered them from the hand of the oppressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} How he had wrought his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Tanes: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} and had changed their rivers into blood; and their streams, that they should not drink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} He sent against them the dog-fly, and it devoured them; and the frog, and it spoiled them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And he gave their fruit to the canker worm, and their labors to the locust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} He killed their vines with hail, and their sycamores with frost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And he gave up their cattle to hail, and their substance to the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} He sent out against them the fury of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and affliction, a message by evil angels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} He made a way for his wrath; he spared not their souls from death, but consigned their cattle to death; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} and struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt; the first fruits of their labors in the tents of Cham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And he removed his people like sheep; he led them as a flock in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And he guided them with hope, and they feared not: but the sea covered their enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And he brought them in to the mountain of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand had purchased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And he cast out the nations from before them, and made them to inherit by a line of inheritance, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Yet they tempted and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And they turned back, and broke covenant, even as also their fathers: they became like a crooked bow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} And they provoked him with their high places, and moved him to jealousy with their graven images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} God heard and lightly regarded [them], and greatly despised Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} And he rejected the tabernacle of Selom, his tent where he lived among men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And he gave their strength into captivity, and their beauty into the enemy's hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And he gave his people to the sword; and disdained his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} Fire devoured their young men; and their virgins mourned not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} Their priests fell by the sword; and their widows shall not be wept for. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} So the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, [and] as a mighty man who has been heated with wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} And he struck his enemies in the hinder parts: he brought on them a perpetual reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} but chose the tribe of Juda, the mount Sion which he loved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{69}} And he built his sanctuary as [the place] of unicorns; he founded it for ever on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{70}} He chose David also his servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{71}} He took him from following the ewes great with young, to be the shepherd of Jacob his servant, and Israel his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{72}} So he tended them in the innocency of his heart; and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm This Psalm is allowed by the best judges to have been written during the Babylonian captivity. of Asaph or, for Asaph, *title I cried, gave \textsuperscript{2} In the, ; my; sore Heb. hand my soul \textsuperscript{3} I remembered, ; I complained; spirit \textsuperscript{8} Is his; doth; for evermore Heb. to generation and generation \textsuperscript{10} This is etc. Or, as Dr. Waterland renders, "This my affliction is a change of the right hand of the Most High, " i.e., it proceeds from a change of God's conduct towards me. De Dieu renders, Precari, hoc meum est; mutare dextram Altissimì "To pray, this is my business. To change the right hand of the Most High." I can do nothing else than pray: God is the Ruler of events. Mr. N. M. Berlin translates, Dolere meum hoc est: mutare est dextre Altissimi . "To grieve is my portion. To change (my condition) belongs to the right hand of the Most High.", ; the years \textsuperscript{17} poured out like water, Heb. were poured forth with water, thine\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 78 (MT 79)}
\markright{PSALM 78 (MT 79)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (79) A Psalm for Asaph. O God, the heathen are come into your inheritance; they have polluted your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a storehouse of fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} They have given the dead bodies of your servants [to be] food for the birds of the sky, the flesh of your holy ones for the wild beasts of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} They have shed their blood as water, round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} We are become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to them [that are] round about us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} How long, O Lord? will you be angry for ever? shall your jealousy burn like fire? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Pour out your wrath upon the heathen that have not known you, and upon the kingdoms which have not called upon your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For they have devoured Jacob, and laid his place waste. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remember not our old transgressions; let your tender mercies speedily prevent us; for we are greatly impoverished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Help us, O God our Saviour; for the glory of your name, O Lord, deliver us; and be merciful to our sins, for your name's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Lest haply they should say among the heathen, Where is their God? and let the avenging of your servant's blood that has been shed be known among the heathen before our eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let the groaning of the prisoners come in before you; according to the greatness of your arm preserve the sons of the slain ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Repay to our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their reproach, with which they have reproached you, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For we are your people and the sheep of your pasture; we will give you thanks for ever; we will declare your praise throughout all generations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} For he, ; testimony The word testimony is used for the ark, and for the law, written on tables of stone, put within the ark, and covered with the mercy seat. This testified the Lord's gracious presence with his people, and seemed to point out to them both the way of access and acceptance, and the standard or rule of their duty., that they \textsuperscript{8} as their;, ; set not Heb. prepared not;, whose \textsuperscript{9} The children Some think this refers to a defeat of the Ephraimites mentioned in; but it probably refers to the conduct and defeat of the ten tribes of which Ephraim was the head. Nothing is recorded in the history of Israel concerning the cowardice of the Ephraimites, as distinct from that of the other tribes. Some therefore think, "that the children of Ephraim" is put by a figure of speech for the nation in general.; carrying Heb. throwing forth turned \textsuperscript{12} Marvellous, ; Exod. 7:1-12:51; Zoan, the ancient capital of the Pharaohs, where Moses wrought so many miracles, is rendered by the Chaldee, Tanium, LXX Τανις, Vulgate, Tanis, and Coptic, Tane, from the Coptic, ten, plain, flat, level; being situated in the low ground of the Delta, on one of the eastern branches of the Nile, bearing its own name, near a large lake, now called the lake of Menzala, 44 miles west of Pelusium, and 169 miles east of Alexandria, according to the Antonine Itinerary, and three miles from the Mediterranean, according to the Geograph. Nubiens. Clim. 3, par. 3. There are ruins still remaining to mark the site of Zoan, or Tanis, called San by the Arabs; comprising broken obelisks, capitals of the Corinthian order, a granite monument, etc.\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 79 (MT 80)}
\markright{PSALM 79 (MT 80)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (80) For the end, for alternate [strains], a testimony for Asaph, a Psalm concerning the Assyrian. Attend, O Shepherd of Israel, who guide Joseph like a flock; you who sit upon the cherubs, manifest yourself; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasse, stir up your power, and come to deliver us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Turn us, O God, and cause your face to shine; and we shall be delivered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O Lord God of hosts, how long are you angry with the prayer of your servant? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} You will feed us with bread of tears; and will cause us to drink tears by measure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You have made us a strife to our neighbors; and our enemies have mocked at us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Turn us, O Lord God of hosts, and cause your face to shine; and we shall be saved. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You have transplanted a vine out of Egypt: you have cast out the heathen, and planted it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You made a way before it, and did cause its roots to strike, and the land was filled [with it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Its shadow covered the mountains, and its shoots [equalled] the goodly cedars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} It sent forth its branches to the sea, and its shoots to the river. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore have you broken down its hedge, while all that pass by the way pluck it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The boar out of the wood has laid it waste, and the wild beast has devoured it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} O God of hosts, turn, we pray you: look on [us] from heaven, and behold and visit this vine; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and restore that which your right hand has planted: and look on the son of man whom you did strengthen for yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [It is] burnt with fire and dug up: they shall perish at the rebuke of your presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, and upon the son of man whom you did strengthen for yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So will we not depart from you: you shall quicken us, and we will call upon your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Turn us, O Lord God of hosts, and make your face to shine; and we shall be saved.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} of Asaph or, for Asaph, *title, marg: the heathen; into; holy; have laid \textsuperscript{3} Their; , and there etc. Either there was no friend or relation left to bury them, or none was allowed to perform this last sad office. The despotism of eastern princes often proceeds to such a degree of extravagance as to fill the mind with astonishment and horror. In Morocco, no person dares to bury the body of a malefactor without an order from the emperor; and Windus, speaking of a man who was to have been sawn in two, informs us, that "his body must have remained to be eaten by the dogs, if the emperor had not pardoned him." \textsuperscript{6} Pour; upon, ;, 46:1-51:64 not known; not called \textsuperscript{8} remember; former iniquities or, the iniquities of them that were before us; let thy, we are \textsuperscript{9} for the; purge; for thy \textsuperscript{10} Wherefore, ; let him, ; by the; revenging Heb. vengeance \textsuperscript{11} sighing, ; according; thy power Heb. thine arm, preserve thou those that are appointed to die Heb. reserve the children of death, *marg. \textsuperscript{12} render; wherewith See note on, and see note on . \textsuperscript{13} thy people, we will, ; all generations Heb. generation and generation\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 80 (MT 81)}
\markright{PSALM 80 (MT 81)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (81) For the end, a Psalm for Asaph, concerning the wine presses. Rejoice you⌃ in God our helper; shout aloud to the God of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Take a psalm, and produce the timbrel, the pleasant lute with the harp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Blow the trumpet at the new moon, in the glorious day of your feast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For [this] is an ordinance for Israel, and a statute of the God of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He made it [to be] a testimony in Joseph, when he came forth out of the land of Egypt: he heard a language which he understood not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He removed his back from burdens: his hands slaved in making the baskets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You did call upon me in trouble, and I delivered you; I heard you in the secret place of the storm: I proved you at the water of Strife. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, O Israel; and I will testify to you: if you will listen to me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} there shall be no new god in you; neither shall you worship a strange god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For I am the Lord your God, that brought you out of the land of Egypt: open your mouth wide, and I will fill it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But my people listened not to my voice; and Israel gave no heed to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So I let them go after the ways of their own hearts: they will go on in their own ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} If my people had listened to me, if Israel had walked in my ways, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I should have put down their enemies very quickly, and should have laid my hand upon those that afflicted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The Lord's enemies [should have] lied to him: but their time shall be for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he fed them with the fat of wheat; and satisfied them with honey out of the rock.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm This Psalm is generally supposed to have been written during the Babylonian captivity; but some think it refers to the desolations made by Sennacherib. of Asaph or, for Asaph Give ear, O Shepherd; leadest; dwellest; shine \textsuperscript{2} Before These three tribes, in the wilderness, marched immediately after the ark and cherubim, by Divine appointment, to which this appears to be an allusion., stir up, ; come and save us Heb. come for salvation to us \textsuperscript{4} how long; be angry Heb. smoke \textsuperscript{8} a vine; thou hast cast; This most elegant allegory, which is every where well supported, is frequently employed by sacred writers. See the parallel passages. \textsuperscript{9} preparedst; to take; and it \textsuperscript{10} goodly cedars Heb. cedars of God \textsuperscript{13} The boar This wild boar, chazir, is the parent stock of our domestic hog. He is much smaller, but stronger, and more undaunted, colour, an iron grey inclining to black; snout, longer than that of the common breed. Ears comparatively short; tusks, very formidable; and habits, fierce and savage. He is particularly destructive to corn-fields and vineyards. 2Kings 18:1-19:37, 24:1-25:30 \textsuperscript{15} vineyard; the branch Or, "the Son, " ben, or as 18 manuscripts, LXX, Vulgate, Syriac, Arabic, and Ethiopic read, ben adam, "Son of man; " which the Targumist renders makla mesheecha, "the King Messiah."\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 81 (MT 82)}
\markright{PSALM 81 (MT 82)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (82) A Psalm for Asaph. God stands in the assembly of gods; and in the midst [of them] will judge gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How long will you⌃ judge unrighteously, and accept the persons of sinners? Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Judge the orphan and poor: do justice to the low and needy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Rescue the needy, and deliver the poor out of the hand of the sinner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They know not, nor understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth shall be shaken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I have said, You⌃ are gods; and all [of you] children of the Most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But you⌃ die as men, and fall as one of the princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Arise, O God, judge the earth: for you shall inherit all nations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Psalm Some suppose this Psalm to have been composed to be sung at the feast of Trumpets, before the time of David; and others think it was written at the removal of the ark to Mount Zion; but the most probable opinion is, that it was sung at the dedication of the second temple. of Asaph or, for Asaph Sing; our strength, ; make, the God \textsuperscript{5} in Joseph; for a; through or, against, where \textsuperscript{6} I removed; were delivered Heb. passed away from the pots Or rather, as dood also signifies (see; the basket, so LXX, and Symmachus, κοφινοϚ, and Vulgate and Jerome, cophino; and Diodati, le sue mani si non dipartite dalle corbe, "his hands were removed from the baskets, " i.e., says he in a note, de portar la terra da far mattoni, "from carrying earth to make bricks, " . \textsuperscript{7} calledst;, secret, proved; Meribah or, strife\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 82 (MT 83)}
\markright{PSALM 82 (MT 83)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (83) A Song of a Psalm for Asaph. O God, who shall be compared to you? be not silent, neither be still, O God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For behold, your enemies have made a noise; and they that hate you have lifted up the head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Against your people they have craftily imagined a device, and have taken counsel against your saints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They have said, Come, and let us utterly destroy them out of the nation; and let the name of Israel be remembered no more at all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For they have taken counsel together with one consent: they have made a confederacy against you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} even the tents of the Idumeans, and the Ismaelites; Moab, and the Agarenes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalec; the Philistines also, with them that dwell at Tyre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Yes, Assur too is come with them: they have become a help to the children of Lot. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Do you to them as to Madiam, and to Sisera; as to Jabin at the brook of Kison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} They were utterly destroyed at Aendor: they became as dung for the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Make their princes as Oreb and Zeb, and Zebee and Salmana; [even] all their princes: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} who said, let us take to ourselves the altar of God as an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} O my God, make them as a wheel; as stubble before the face of the wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As fire which shall burn up a wood, as the flame may consume the mountains; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} so shall you persecute them with your tempest, and trouble them in your anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Fill their faces with dishonor; so shall they seek your name, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let them be ashamed and troubled for evermore; yes, let them be confounded and destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And let them know that your name is Lord; that you alone are Most High over all the earth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} of Asaph or, for Asaph God etc. Or, "God standeth in the assembly of God, ail, he judgeth among the judges." Elohim̀ God is among His own people; and presides especially in those courts of justice which Himself has established.; the gods \textsuperscript{5} They That is, the judges know not. know not; walk; all the etc. All the civil institutions of the land totter.; out of course Heb. moved \textsuperscript{7} But; like men Or, "like Adam, " keadam . and fall etc. Or, "as fall as one of them, O ye princes."\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 83 (MT 84)}
\markright{PSALM 83 (MT 84)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (84) For the end, a Psalm for the sons of Core, concerning the wine presses. How amiable are your tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} My soul longs, and faints for the courts of the Lord: my heart and my flesh have exulted in the living god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Yes, the sparrow has found himself a home, and the turtle-dove a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, [even] your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King, and my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Blessed are they that dwell in your house: they will praise you evermore. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Blessed is the man whose help is of you, O Lord; in his heart he has purposed to go up {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the valley of weeping, to the place which he has appointed, for [there] the law-giver will grant blessings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They shall go from strength to strength: the God of gods shall be seen in Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: listen, O God of Jacob. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Behold, O God our defender, and look upon the face of your anointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For one day in your courts is better than thousands. I would rather be an abject in the house of God, than dwell in the tents of sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the Lord loves mercy and truth: God will give grace and glory: the Lord will not withhold good things from them that walk in innocence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusts in you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} of Asaph or, for Asaph Keep, be not \textsuperscript{5} For; consent Heb. heart they are \textsuperscript{6} The tabernacles Tents are mentioned because it was the custom of these people, particularly the Ishmaelites, to live a migratory or wandering life; encamping sometimes in one place, and sometimes in another, as they found convenience for themselves and cattle; a custom retained by their descendants to the present day. Edom, Hagarenes;, Hagarites \textsuperscript{8} Assur is the same in the original as Asshur, or Assyria., Asshur, holpen Heb. been an arm to, the children \textsuperscript{9} as unto; as to Sisera of Kison The variations of Kison and Kishon only exists in the translation; the original being uniformly Kishon.\par}
