\subsection*{Psalm 105 (MT 106)}
\markright{PSALM 105 (MT 106)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (106) Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who shall tell the mighty acts of the Lord? [who] shall cause all his praises to be heard? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Blessed are they that keep judgment, and do righteousness at all times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Remember us, O Lord, with the favor [you have] to your people: visit us with your salvation; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} that we may behold the good of your elect, that we may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that we may glory with your inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} We have sinned with our fathers, we have transgressed, we have done unrighteously. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Our fathers in Egypt understood not your wonders, and remembered not the multitude of your mercy; but provoked [him] as they went up by the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Yet he saved them for his name's sake, that he might cause his mighty power to be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up: so he led them through the deep as through the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he saved them out of the hand of them that hated [them], and redeemed them out of the hand of the enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The water covered those that oppressed them: there was not one of them left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then they believed his words, and celebrated his praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} They made haste, they forgot his works; they waited not for his counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the dry [land]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he gave them their request, and sent fullness into their souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They provoked Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the holy one of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and closed upon the congregation of Abiron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And a fire was kindled in their congregation, and a flame burnt up the sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they made a calf in Choreb, and worshipped the graven image, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and they changed their glory into the similitude of a calf that feeds on grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They forgot God that saved them, who had wrought great deeds in Egypt; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} wondrous [works] in the land of Cham, and terrible things at the Red Sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So he said that he would have destroyed them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn [him] away from the fierceness of his anger, so that he should not destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Moreover they set at nothing the desirable land, and believed not his word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they murmured in their tents: they listened not to the voice of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} So he lifted up his hand against them, to cast them down in the wilderness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} and to cast down their seed among the nations, and to scatter them in the countries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} They were joined also to Beelphegor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead. And they provoked him with their devices; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} and destruction, was multiplied among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Then Phinees stood up, and made atonement: and the plague ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it was counted to him for righteousness, to all generations for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} They provoked him also at the water of Strife, and Moses was hurt for their sakes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} for they provoked his spirit, and he spoke [unadvisedly] with his lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} They destroyed not the nations which the Lord told them [to destroy]; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} but were mingled with the heathen, and learned their works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And they served their graven images; and it became an offense to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to devils, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} and shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Chanaan; and the land was defiled with blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} and was polluted with their works; and they went a whoring with their own devices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So the Lord was very angry with his people, and he abhorred his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And he delivered them into the hands of [their] enemies; and they that hated them ruled over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Ands their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought down under their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Many a time he delivered them; but they provoked him by their counsel, and they were brought low by their iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} You⌃ the Lord looked upon their affliction, when he heard their petition. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And he remembered his covenant, and repented according to the multitude of his mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And he caused them to be pitied in the sight of all who carried them captive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen, that we may give thanks to your holy name, that we may glory in your praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting and to everlasting; and all the people shall say, Amen, Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2962, bc 1042 (Title), It appears from, where the former part of this Psalm, as far as the, is found with little variation, that David composed it at the removal of the ark to Mount Zion, and he himself probably enlarged it afterwards with the glorious detail of God's merciful dealings with Abraham and his posterity till their settlement in the land of Promise. The Hallelujah, which terminates the preceding Psalm, is made the title of this by the Septuagint, Vulgate, Arabic, and Ethiopic; and the Syriac considers it a paraphrase on the words, "Fear not, Jacob, to go down into Egypt; " "and teaches us spiritually not to fear when we are obliged to contend with devils; for God is our shield, and will fight for us." Give;, call; make known \textsuperscript{4} Seek; his strength; seek his face \textsuperscript{8} He hath remembered, ; a thousand \textsuperscript{11} Unto thee, lot Heb. cord \textsuperscript{18} Whose; he was laid in iron Heb. his soul came into iron \textsuperscript{27} They; Exod. 7:1-11:10; his signs Heb. words of his signs wonders \textsuperscript{32} them hail for rain Heb. their rain hail \textsuperscript{37} brought; and there Considering the immense number of men, women, children, and cattle, it must certainly have appeared extraordinary, that there was none among them weak or feeble, none unable to perform the journey. The order was that "not a hoof should be left behind; " and He who commanded gave strength to obey. \textsuperscript{43} And he; with joy, ; gladness Heb. singing \textsuperscript{44} gave, ; inherited; the labour That is, "the produce of their labour; " the cities and houses they had built, the vineyards they had planted, etc. \textsuperscript{45} That, ; Praise ye the Lord Heb. Hallelujah, *marg.\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 106 (MT 107)}
\markright{PSALM 106 (MT 107)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (107) Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let them say [so] who have been redeemed by the Lord, whom he has redeemed from the hand of the enemy; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and gathered them out of the countries, from the east, and west, and north, and south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They wandered in the wilderness in a dry land; they found no way to a city of habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he delivered them out of their distresses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he guided them into a straight path, that they might go to a city of habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let them acknowledge to the Lord his mercies, and his wonderful works to the children of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For he satisfies the empty soul, and fills the hungry [soul] with good things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [even] them that sit in darkness and the shadow of death, fettered in poverty and iron; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} because they rebelled against the words of God, and provoked the counsel of the Most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So their heart was brought low with troubles; they were weak, and there was no helper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he saved them out of their distresses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke their bonds asunder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Let them acknowledge to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For he broke to pieces the brazen gates, and crushed the iron bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He helped them out of the way of their iniquity; for they were brought low because of their iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Their soul abhorred all meat; and they drew near to the gates of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he saved them out of their distresses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them out of their destructions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Let them acknowledge to the Lord his mercies, and his wonderful works to the children of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And let them offer to him the sacrifice of praise, and proclaim this works with exultation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} They that go down to the sea in ships, doing business in many waters; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} these [men] have seen the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He speaks, and the stormy wind arises, and its waves are lifted up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} They go up to the heavens, and go down to the depths; their soul melts because of troubles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} They are troubled, they stagger as a drunkard, and all their wisdom is swallowed up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Then they cry to the Lord in their affliction, and he brings them out of their distresses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he commands the storm, and it is calmed into a gentle breeze, and its waves are still. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And they are glad, because they are quiet; and he guides them to their desire haven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Let them acknowledge to the Lord his mercies, and his wonderful works to the children of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Let them exalt him in the congregation of the people, and praise him in the seat of the elders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} He turns rivers into a desert, and streams of water into a dry land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} a fruitful land into saltness, for the wickedness of them that dwell in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} He turns a wilderness into pools of water, and a dry land into streams of water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And there he causes the hungry to dwell, and they establish for themselves cities of habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And they sow fields, and plant vineyards, and they yield fruit of increase. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he blesses them, and they multiply exceedingly, and he diminishes not the number of their cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Again they become few, and are brought low, by the pressure of evils and pain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Contempt is poured upon their princes, and he causes them to wander in a desert and trackless land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} But he helps the poor out of poverty, and makes [him] families as a flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} The upright shall see and rejoice; and all iniquity shall stop her mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Who is wise, and will observe these things, and understand the mercies of the Lord?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} (Title), As part of the preceding Psalm is found in, so the first and two last verses of this are found in the same place; and it is highly probable this was composed upon the same occasion as the former, to which it seems to be a continuation; for as that celebrates the mercies of God to Israel, so this confesses and deplores the rebellions of Israel against Jehovah. Praise ye the Lord Heb. Hallelujah, O give, ; for he \textsuperscript{3} Blessed, ; keep; doeth; at all times \textsuperscript{9} He rebuked In the descriptions of the Psalmist, everything has life. The sea is an animated being, behaves itself proudly, is rebuked, and retires in confusion., ; so he \textsuperscript{13} They soon forgat Heb. They made haste, they forgat, Three days afterwards, at the waters of Marah.;, waited \textsuperscript{14} But; lusted exceedingly Heb. lusted a lust tempted \textsuperscript{15} he gave; but sent They despised the manna, calling it light or innutritive food. God gave them flesh as they desired, but no blessing accompanied it; and, in consequence, they did not fatten, but grew lean upon it; and many, surfeited by excess, died of disease. Instead of razon, "leanness, " however, Bp. Lowth supposes we should read zeraon, "nausea or loathing, " which appears to be supported by several ancient versions, and by, where this portion of the history of the Israelites is recorded, and where the word zara is used, and rendered, "it be loathsome." \textsuperscript{20} Thus; their glory That is, their God, who ought to have been the peculiar object of their glory. into \textsuperscript{22} Wondrous The plagues he inflicted on the Egyptians. Egypt is called the land of Ham, or rather, Cham, because it was peopled by Mizraim the son of Ham, and grandson of Noah. Plutarch informs us, that the Egyptians called their country Χημια, Chemia; and the Copts give it the name of Chemi, Χημι, to the present day., terrible \textsuperscript{23} he said;, ; his chosen; stood \textsuperscript{24} they despised; the pleasant land Heb. a land of desire, ; they believed \textsuperscript{27} overthrow Heb. make them fall to scatter \textsuperscript{28} joined, ; of the dead The word maithim signifies dead men; for the idols of the heathen were generally men - warriors, kings, or lawgivers - who had been deified after their death; though many of them had been execrated during their life. \textsuperscript{37} they sacrificed However unnatural and horrid human sacrifices may appear, it is certain, that they did not only exist, but almost universally prevailed in the heathen world, especially among the Canaanites and Phoenicians.; , devils \textsuperscript{40} the wrath; insomuch; his own \textsuperscript{43} Many; with their, brought low or, impoverished, or weakened\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 107 (MT 108)}
\markright{PSALM 107 (MT 108)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (108) Song of a Psalm by David. O God, my heart is ready, my heart is ready; I will sing and sing psalms with my glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Awake, lute and harp; I will awake early. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I will give thanks to you, O Lord, among the people; I will sing praise to you among the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For your mercy is great above the heavens, and your truth [reaches] to the clouds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Be you exalted, O God, above the heavens; and your glory above all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} That your beloved [ones] may be delivered, save with your right hand, and hear me. God has spoken in his sanctuary; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I will be exalted, and will divide Sicima, and will measure out the valley of tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Galaad is mine; and Manasses is mine; and Ephraim is the help of my head; Judas is my king; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Moab is the caldron of my hope; over Idumea will I cast my sandal; the Philistines are made subject to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who will bring me into the fortified city? or who will guide me to Idumea? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Will not you, O God, who have rejected us? and will not you, O God, go forth with our hosts? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Give us help from tribulation: for vain is the help of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Through God we shall do valiantly; and he will bring to nothing our enemies.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3468, bc 536 (Title), The author of this Psalm is unknown; but it was evidently written to commemorate the return of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity; and it may easily be perceived that it must have been sung in alternate parts, having a double burden, or two intercalary verses often recurring. Bp. Lowth considers it as written "after the method of the ancient pastorals, where, be the subject of their verse what it will, each swain endeavours to excel the other; and one may perceive their thoughts and expressions gradually to rise upon each other." "No doubt, " he adds, "the composition of this Psalm is admirable throughout; and the descriptive part of it adds at least its share of beauty to the whole; but what is most to be admired is its conciseness, and withal the expressiveness of the diction, which strikes the imagination with illimitable elegance. The weary and bewildered traveller - the miserable captive in the dungeon - the sick and dying man - the seaman foundering in a storm - are described in so affecting a manner, that they far exceed anything of the kind, though never so much laboured." Give, ;, good; for his mercy \textsuperscript{4} wandered; they found This is the first similitude; in which the Israelites in captivity are compared to travellers in a dreary, uninhabited, and barren desert, spent with hunger and thirst, as well as by the fatigues of the journey. \textsuperscript{8} Oh that men, ; praise, ; his wonderful \textsuperscript{10} Such Here begins the second comparison; in which the state of the captives in Babylon is illustrated by that of prisoners in a dreary dungeon. as sit; bound\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 108 (MT 109)}
\markright{PSALM 108 (MT 109)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (109) For the end, a Psalm of David. For the end, a Psalm of David. O God, pass not over my praise in silence; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the crafty [man] have been opened against me: they have spoken against me with a crafty tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they have compassed me with words of hatred; and fought against me without a cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Instead of loving me, they falsely accused me: but I continued to pray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Set you a sinner against him; and let the devil stand at his right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} When he is judged, let him go forth condemned: and let his prayer become sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let his days be few: and let another take his office of overseer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let his children be orphans, and his wife a widow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let his children wander without a dwelling-place, and beg: let them be cast out of their habitations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let [his] creditor exact all that belongs to him: and let strangers spoil his labors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let him have no helper; neither let there be any one to have compassion on his fatherless children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let his children be [given up] to utter destruction: in one generation let his name be blotted out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before the Lord; and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Let them be before the Lord continually; and let their memorial be blotted out from the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Because he remembered not to show mercy, but persecuted the needy and poor man, and [that] to kill him that was pricked in the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He loved cursing also, and it shall come upon him; and he took not pleasure in blessing, so it shall be removed far from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yes, he put on cursing as a garment, and it is come as water into his bowels, and as oil into his bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Let it be to him as a garment which he puts on, and as a girdle with which he girds himself continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This is the dealing of the Lord with those who falsely accuse me, and of them that speak evil against my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But you, O Lord, Lord, deal [mercifully] with me, for your name's sake: for your mercy is good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Deliver me, for I am poor and needy; and my heart is troubled within me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} I am removed as a shadow in its going down: I am tossed up and down like locusts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} My knees are weakened through fasting, and my flesh is changed by reason of [the lack of] oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I became also a reproach to them: [when] they saw me they shook their heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Help me, O Lord my God; and save me according to your mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And let them know that this is your hand; and [that] you, Lord, have wrought it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Let them curse, but you shall bless: let them that rise up against me be ashamed, but let your servant rejoice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Let those that falsely accuse me be clothed with shame, and let them cover themselves with their shame as with a mantle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} I will give thanks to the Lord abundantly with my mouth; and in the midst of many I will praise him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For he stood on the right hand of the poor, to save [me] from them that persecute my soul.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 109 (MT 110)}
\markright{PSALM 109 (MT 110)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (110) A Psalm of David. The Lord said to my Lord, Sit you on my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The Lord shall send out a rod of power for you out of Sion: rule you in the midst of your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} With you is dominion in the day of your power, in the splendors of your saints: I have begotten you from the womb before the morning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The Lord swore, and will not repent, You are a priest for ever, after the order of Melchisedec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The Lord at your right hand has dashed in pieces kings in the day of his wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He shall judge among the nations, he shall fill up [the number of] corpses, he shall crush the heads of many on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He shall drink of the brook in the way; therefore shall he lift up the head.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2942, bc 1062 (Title), It is generally supposed that this Psalm was composed by David, when persecuted by Saul, who was rendered more implacable by the base and malicious calumnies of Doeg and others; though some are of opinion, that it was written when David fled from Absalom, and that Ahithophel, rather than Doeg, is the typical person against whom it is principally directed. Hold, ; O God \textsuperscript{2} the mouth, ; of the deceitful Heb. of deceit are opened Heb. have opened themselves with \textsuperscript{6} Set thou Dr. Sykes, Michaelis, and others, contend that these imprecations are those of David's enemies against himself; and they would render, "Set, say they, a wicked, " etc, but this is rendered highly improbable by the being applied by St. Peter to the traitor Judas, of whom David was certainly not a type. (See .) Bp. Horsley and others, however, render the verbs in the future tense, the first verb alone being in the imperative; justly considering the Psalmist as merely uttering prophetic denunciations of God's displeasure against sinners. and let; Satan or, an adversary \textsuperscript{7} be condemned Heb. go out guilty, or wicked; and let\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 110 (MT 111)}
\markright{PSALM 110 (MT 111)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (111) Alleluia. I will give you thanks, O Lord, with my whole heart, in the council of the upright, and [in] the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The works of the Lord are great, sought out according to all his will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} His work is [worthy of] thanksgiving and honor: and his righteousness endures for ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He has caused his wonderful works to be remembered: the Lord is merciful and compassionate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He has given food to them that fear him: he will remember his covenant for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He has declared to his people the power of his works, to give them the inheritance of the heathen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The works of his hands are truth and judgment: all his commandments are sure: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} established for ever and ever, done in truth and uprightness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He sent redemption to his people: he commanded his covenant for ever: holy and fearful is his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and all that act accordingly have a good understanding; his praise endures for ever and ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2962, bc 1042 (Title), This Psalm was probably composed by David after Nathan's prophetic address; and, from the grandeur of the subject and the sublimity of the expressions, it is evident that it can only refer, as the ancient Jews fully acknowledged, to the royal dignity, priesthood, victories, and triumphs of the MESSIAH. The Lord; Sit; until \textsuperscript{3} Thy; day, ; beauties; from the womb etc. or, more than the womb of the morning, thou shalt have, etc. thou hast. \textsuperscript{5} at thy; strike, ;, in the day \textsuperscript{6} judge;, ; fill, ; wound; many or, great\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 111 (MT 112)}
\markright{PSALM 111 (MT 112)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (112) Alleluia. Blessed is the man that fears the Lord: he will delight greatly in his commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} His seed shall be mighty in the earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Glory and riches shall be in his house; and his righteousness endures for evermore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To the upright light has sprung up in darkness: he is pitiful, and merciful, and righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The good man is he that pities and lends: he will direct his affairs with judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For he shall not be moved for ever; the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He shall not be afraid of [any] evil report: his heart is ready to trust in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} His heart is established, he shall not fear, till he shall see [his desire] upon his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He has dispersed abroad; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures for evermore: his horn shall be exalted with honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The sinner shall see and be angry, he shall gnash his teeth, and consume away: the desire of the sinner shall perish.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3468, bc 536 Praise ye the Lord Heb. Hallelujah, ; As this is an alphabetical Psalm, every member of each verse beginning consecutively with a letter of the Hebrew alphabet, Hallelujah, which begins with the fifth, must be considered as the title. I will, assembly \textsuperscript{5} hath given; meat Heb. prey he will \textsuperscript{8} They; stand fast Heb. are established are done \textsuperscript{10} fear; a good understanding or, good success; do his commandments Heb. do them; his praise\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 112 (MT 113)}
\markright{PSALM 112 (MT 113)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (113) Alleluia. Praise the Lord, you⌃ servants [of his], praise, the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let the name of the Lord be blessed, from this present time and for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} From the rising of the sun to his setting, the name of the Lord is to be praised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The Lord is high above all the nations; his glory is above the heavens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who is as the Lord our God? who dwells in the high places, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and [yet] looks upon the low things in heaven, and on the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} who lifts up the poor from the earth, and raises up the needy from the dunghill; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} to set him with princes, [even] with the princes of his people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} who settles the barren [woman] in a house, [as] a mother rejoicing over children.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Praise ye the Lord Heb. Hallelujah, ; This is another of the alphabetical Psalms, being formed exactly as the preceding in the division of its verses; and, like it, was probably composed for the use of the Jews, after their return from captivity. Blessed, ; delighteth \textsuperscript{4} there ariseth; he is gracious; , ; righteous \textsuperscript{5} good; showeth; he will, ; discretion Heb. judgment\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 113 (MT 114-115)}
\markright{PSALM 113 (MT 114-115)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (114) Alleluia. At the going forth of Israel from Egypt, of the house of Jacob from a barbarous people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Judea became his sanctuary, [and] Israel his dominion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The sea saw and fled: Jordan was turned back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} What [ailed] you, O sea, that you fled? and you Jordan, that you were turned back? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} [You⌃] mountains, that you⌃ skipped like rams, and [you⌃] hills, like lambs? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The earth trembled at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} who turned the rock into pools of water, and the flint into fountains of water.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} (Title), This and the following five Psalms form what is called by the Hebrews the great Hallel, or praise; which was sung on their most solemn festivals, and particularly after the celebration of the Passover. (See . .) This and the following were probably composed after the return from the captivity. Praise ye the Lord Heb. Hallelujah, O \textsuperscript{5} like; dwelleth Heb. exalteth himself to dwell \textsuperscript{6} humbleth; in heaven Bp. Lowth observes that the two members of this line are to be referred severally to the two preceding lines; as if it were, "Who is exalted to dwell in the heavens; and who humbleth himself to inspect the things on earth." in the earth\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Matt 26:30; Mark 14:26; Ps 112:1; Ps 33:1-2; Ps 103:20-21; Ps 134:1; Ps 135:1-3; Ps 135:20; Ps 145:10; Eph 5:19-20; Rev 19:5 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 41:13; Ps 106:48; 1Chr 16:36; 1Chr 29:10-13; Dan 2:20; Eph 3:21; Rev 5:13 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 72:11; Ps 72:17-19; Ps 86:9; Isa 24:16; Isa 42:10-12; Isa 49:13; Isa 59:19; Hab 2:14; Mal 1:11; Rom 15:9-10; Rev 11:15 \textsuperscript{4} Ps 97:9; Ps 99:2; Isa 40:15; Isa 40:17; Isa 40:22; Ps 8:1; Ps 57:10-11; 1Kgs 8:27; Isa 66:1 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 89:6; Ps 89:8; Exod 15:11; Deut 33:26; Isa 40:18; Isa 40:25; Isa 16:5; Jer 10:6 \textsuperscript{6} Ps 11:4; Job 4:18; Job 15:15; Isa 6:2; Ps 138:6; Isa 57:15; Isa 66:2 \textsuperscript{7} Ps 75:6-7; Ps 107:41; Job 5:11; Job 5:15-16; Ezek 17:24; Ezek 21:26-27; Luke 1:52-53; Jas 2:5; Ps 22:15; Isa 26:19; Dan 12:2-3; Acts 2:31-33; Eph 1:20-21; 1Pet 3:21-22; 1Sam 2:7-8; 1Sam 24:14; 2Sam 7:8-9; Job 2:8; Job 36:6-7 \textsuperscript{8} Ps 45:16; Ps 68:13; Gen 41:41; Phil 2:8-11; Rev 5:9-10\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 114 (MT 116:1-9)}
\markright{PSALM 114 (MT 116:1-9)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (115) Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} lest at any time the nations should say, Where is their God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But our God has done in heaven and on earth, whatever he has pleased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They have a mouth, but they can’t speak; they have eyes, but they can’t see: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} they have ears, but they can’t hear; they have noses, but they can’t smell; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} they have hands, but they can’t handle; they have feet, but they can’t walk: they can’t speak through their throat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let those that make them become like to them, and all who trust in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The house of Israel trusts in the Lord: he is their helper and defender. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The house of Aaron trusts in the Lord: he is their helper and defender. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They that fear the Lord trust in the Lord: he is their helper and defender. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The Lord has remembered us, and blessed us: he has blessed the house of Israel, he has blessed the house of Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He has blessed them that fear the Lord, both small and great. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord add [blessings] to you and to your children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Blessed are you⌃ of the Lord, who made the heaven and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The heaven of heavens [belongs] to the Lord: but he has given the earth to the sons of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The dead shall not praise you, O Lord, nor any that go down to Hades. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But we, the living, will bless the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} (Title), This short, and apparently imperfect Psalm, for elegance and sublimity, yields to few in the whole book. The composition of it is inexpressibly beautiful, and in the highest style of poetry. Israel, ; a people\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 115 (MT 116:10-19)}
\markright{PSALM 115 (MT 116:10-19)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (116) Alleluia. I am well pleased, because the Lord will listen to the voice of my supplication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Because he has inclined his ear to me, therefore will I call upon him while I live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The pangs of death compassed me; the dangers of hell found me: I found affliction and sorrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then I called on the name of the Lord: O Lord, deliver my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The Lord is merciful and righteous; yes, our God has pity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The Lord preserves the simple: I was brought low, and he delivered me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Return to your rest, O my soul; for the Lord has dealt bountifully with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For he has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} I shall be well-pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living. (115) Alleluia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I believed, therefore I have spoken: but I was greatly afflicted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I said in my amazement, Every man is a liar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} What shall I render to the Lord for all the things wherein he has rewarded me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I will pay my vows to the Lord, in the presence of all his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} O Lord, I am your servant; I am your servant, and the son of your handmaid: you have burst my bonds asunder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I will offer to you the sacrifice of praise, and will call upon the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I will pay my vows to the Lord, in the presence of all his people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} in the courts of the Lord's house, in the midst of you, Jerusalem.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 116 (MT 117)}
\markright{PSALM 116 (MT 117)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (117) Alleluia. Praise the Lord, all you⌃ nations: praise him, all you⌃ peoples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For his mercy has been abundant toward us: and the truth of the Lord endures for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3468, bc 536 (Title), From several instances of the Chaldee dialect being used in this Psalm, it appears to have been written after the Babylonian captivity. love; because \textsuperscript{2} therefore, ; as long as I live Heb. in my days\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 18:1-6; Ps 119:132; Mark 12:33; John 21:17; 1John 4:19; 1John 5:2-3; Ps 18:6; Ps 31:22-23; Ps 34:3-4; Ps 40:1; Ps 66:19-20; Ps 69:33; Gen 35:2; 1Sam 1:26; John 16:24 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 55:16-17; Ps 86:6-7; Ps 88:1; Ps 145:18-19; Job 27:10; Luke 18:1; Phil 4:6; Col 4:2\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 117 (MT 118)}
\markright{PSALM 117 (MT 118)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (118) Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord; for [he is] good: for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let now the house of Israel say, that [he is] good: for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let now the house of Aaron say, that [he is] good: for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let now all that fear the Lord say, that [he is] good: for his mercy [endures] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I called on the Lord out of affliction: and he listened to me, [so as to bring me] into a wide place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The Lord is my helper; and I will not fear what man shall do to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord is my helper; and I shall see [my desire] upon my enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} [It is] better to trust in the Lord than to trust in man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} [It is] better to hope in the Lord, than to hope in princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All nations compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They completely compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They compassed me about as bees [do] a honeycomb, and they burst into flame as fire among thorns: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I was thrust, and sorely shaken, that I might fall: but the Lord helped me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord is my strength and my song, and is become my salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The voice of exultation and salvation is in the tabernacles of the righteous: the right hand of the Lord has wrought mightily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The right hand of the Lord has exalted me: the right hand of the Lord has wrought powerfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I shall not die, but live, and recount the works of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The Lord has chastened me sore: but he has not given me up to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and give praise to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter by it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I will give thanks to you; because you have heard me, and are become my salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} This has been done of the Lord; and it is wonderful in our eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} O Lord, save now: O Lord, send now prosperity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord: we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} God is the Lord, and he has shined upon us: celebrate the feast with thick [branches, binding the victims] even to the horns of the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} You are my God, and I will give you thanks: you are my God, and I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you, for you have heard me, and are become my salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy [endures] for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} (Title), This Psalm, the shortest in the whole collection, is written as a part of the preceding in thirty-two manuscripts. It celebrates the deliverance from the Babylonian captivity, the grand type of the redemption of the world by the Messiah. O praise, ; praise him\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 66:1; Ps 66:4; Ps 67:3; Ps 86:9; Isa 24:15-16; Isa 42:10-12; Rom 15:11; Rev 15:4; Ps 148:11-14; Ps 150:6; Rev 5:9; Rev 7:9-10 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 85:10; Ps 89:1; Ps 100:4-5; Isa 25:1; Mic 7:20; Luke 1:54-55; John 14:6; Rom 15:8-9; 1John 5:6\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 118 (MT 119)}
\markright{PSALM 118 (MT 119)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (119) Alleluia. Blessed are the blameless in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Blessed are they that search out his testimonies: they will diligently seek him with the whole heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For they that work iniquity have not walked in his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You have commanded [us] diligently to keep your precepts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O that my ways were directed to keep your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then shall I not be ashamed, when I have respect to all your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I will give you thanks with uprightness of heart, when I have learned the judgments of your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I will keep your ordinances: O forsake me not greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Wherewith shall a young man direct his way? by keeping your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} With my whole heart have I diligently sought you: cast me not away from your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I have hidden your oracles in my heart, that I might not sin against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Blessed are you, O Lord: teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} With my lips have I declared all the judgments of your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I have delighted in the way of your testimonies, [as much] as in all riches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I will meditate on your commandments, and consider your ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I will meditate on your ordinances: I will not forget your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Render a recompense to your servant: [so] shall I live, and keep your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Unveil you my eyes, and I shall perceive wondrous things of your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I am a stranger in the earth: hide not your commandments from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} My soul has longed exceedingly for your judgments at all times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You have rebuked the proud: cursed are they that turn aside from your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Remove from me reproach and contempt; for I have sought out your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For princes sat and spoke against me: but your servant was meditating on your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For your testimonies are my meditation, and your ordinances are my counselors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} My soul has cleaved to the ground; quicken you me according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I declared my ways, and you did hear me: teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Instruct me in the way of your ordinances; and I will meditate on your wondrous works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} My soul has slumbered for sorrow; strengthen you me with your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Remove from me the way of iniquity; and be merciful to me by your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} I have chosen the way of truth; and have not forgotten your judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} I have cleaved to your testimonies, O Lord; put me not to shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} I ran the way of your commandments, when you did enlarge my heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Teach me, O Lord, the way of your ordinances, and I will seek it out continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Instruct me, and I will search out your law, and will keep it with my whole heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Guide me in the path of your commandments; for I have delighted in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Incline my heart to your testimonies, and not to covetousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Turn away my eyes that I may not behold vanity: quicken you me in your way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Confirm your oracle to your servant, that he may fear you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Take away my reproach which I have feared: for your judgments are good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Behold, I have desired your commandments: quicken me in your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And let your mercy come upon me, O Lord; [even] your salvation, according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And [so] I shall render an answer to them that reproach me: for I have trusted in your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; for I have hoped in your judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} So shall I keep your law continually, for ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} I walked also at large: for I sought out your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And I spoke of your testimonies before kings, and was not ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And I lifted up my hands to your commandments which I loved; and I meditated in your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Remember your words to your servant, wherein you have made me hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} This has comforted me in my affliction: for your oracle has quickened me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} The proud have transgressed exceedingly; but I swerved not from your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} I remembered your judgments of old, O Lord; and was comforted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} Despair took hold upon me, because of the sinners who forsake your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Your ordinances were my songs in the place of my sojourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} I remembered your name, O Lord, in the night, and kept your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} This I had, because I diligently sought your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} You are my portion, O Lord: I said that I would keep your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} I implored your favor with my whole heart: have mercy upon me according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} I thought on your ways, and turned my feet to your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} I prepared myself, (and was not terrified,) to keep your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} The snares of sinners entangled me: but I forgot not your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} At midnight I arose, to give thanks to you for the judgments of your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} I am a companion of all them that fear you, and of them that keep your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} O Lord, the earth is full of your mercy: teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} You have wrought kindly with your servant, o Lord, according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} Teach me kindness, and instruction, and knowledge: for I have believed your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} Before I was afflicted, I transgressed; therefore have I kept your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} Good are you, O Lord; therefore in your goodness teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{69}} The injustice of the proud has been multiplied against me: but I will search out your commandments with all my heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{70}} Their heart has been curdled like milk; but I have meditated on your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{71}} [It is] good for me that you have afflicted me; that I might learn your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{72}} The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{73}} Your hands have made me, and fashioned me: instruct me, that I may learn your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{74}} They that fear you will see me and rejoice: for I have hoped in your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{75}} I know, O Lord, that your judgments are righteousness, and [that] you in truthfulness have afflicted me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{76}} Let, I pray you, your mercy be to comfort me, according to your word to your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{77}} Let your compassions come to me, that I may live: for your law is my meditation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{78}} Let the proud be ashamed; for they transgressed against me unjustly: but I will meditate in your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{79}} Let those that fear you, and those that know your testimonies, turn to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{80}} Let my heart be blameless in your ordinances, that I may not be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{81}} My soul faints for your salvation: I have hoped in your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{82}} My eyes failed [in waiting] for your word, saying, When will you comfort me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{83}} For I am become as a bottle in the frost: [yet] I have not forgotten your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{84}} How many are the days of your servant? when will you execute judgment for me on them that persecute me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{85}} Transgressors told me [idle tales]; but not according to your law, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{86}} All your commandments are truth; they persecuted me unjustly; help you me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{87}} They nearly made an end of me in the earth; but I forsook not your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{88}} Quicken me according to your mercy; so shall I keep the testimonies of your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{89}} Your word, O Lord, abides in heaven for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{90}} Your truth [endures] to all generations; you have founded the earth, and it abides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{91}} The day continues by your arrangement; for all things are your servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{92}} Were it not that your law is my meditation, then I should have perished in my affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{93}} I will never forget your ordinances; for with them you have quickened me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{94}} I am your, save me; for I have sought out your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{95}} Sinners laid wait for me to destroy me; [but] I understood your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{96}} have seen an end of all perfection; [but] your commandment is very broad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{97}} How I have loved your law, O Lord! it is my meditation all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{98}} You have made me wiser than my enemies [in] your commandment; for it is mine for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{99}} I have more understanding than all my teachers; for your testimonies are my medication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{100}} I understand more that the aged; because I have sought out your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{101}} I have kept back my feet from every evil way, that I might keep your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{102}} I have not declined from your judgments; for you have instructed me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{103}} How sweet are your oracles to my throat! more so than honey to my mouth! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{104}} I gain understanding by your commandments: therefore I have hated every way of unrighteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{105}} Your law is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{106}} I have sworn and determined to keep the judgments of your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{107}} I have been very greatly afflicted, O Lord: quicken me, according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{108}} Accept, I pray you, O Lord, the free will offerings of my mouth, and teach me your judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{109}} My soul is continually in your hands; and I have not forgotten your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{110}} Sinners spread a snare for me; but I erred not from your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{111}} I have inherited your testimonies for ever; for they are the joy of my heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{112}} I have inclined my heart to perform your ordinances for ever, in return [for your mercies]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{113}} I have hated transgressors; but I have loved your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{114}} You are my helper and my supporter; I have hoped in your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{115}} Depart from me, you⌃ evil-doers; for I will search out the commandments of my God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{116}} Uphold me according to your word, and quicken me; and make me not ashamed of my expectation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{117}} Help me, and I shall be saved; and I will meditate in your ordinances continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{118}} You have brought to nothing all that depart from your ordinances; for their inward thought is unrighteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{119}} I have reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore have I loved your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{120}} Penetrate my flesh with your fear; for I am afraid of your judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{121}} I have done judgment and justice; deliver me not up to them that injure me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{122}} Receive your servant for good: let not the proud accuse me falsely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{123}} My eyes have failed for your salvation, and for the word of your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{124}} Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{125}} I am your servant; instruct me, and I shall know your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{126}} [It is] time for the Lord to work: they have utterly broken your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{127}} Therefore have I loved your commandments more than gold, or the topaz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{128}} Therefore I directed myself [according] to all your commandments: I have hated every unjust way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{129}} Your testimonies are wonderful: therefore my soul has sought them out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{130}} The manifestation of your words will enlighten, and instruct the simple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{131}} I opened my mouth, and drew breath: for I earnestly longed after your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{132}} Look upon me and have mercy upon me, after the manner of them that love your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{133}} Order my steps according to your word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{134}} Deliver me from the false accusation of men: so will I keep your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{135}} Cause your face to shine upon your servant: and teach me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{136}} My eyes have been bathed in streams of water, because I kept not your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{137}} Righteous are you, O Lord, and upright are your judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{138}} You have commanded righteousness and perfect truth, [as] your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{139}} Your zeal has quite wasted me: because my enemies have forgotten your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{140}} Your word [has been] very fully tried; and your servant loves it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{141}} I am young and despised: [yet] I have not forgotten your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{142}} Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and your law is truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{143}} Afflictions and distresses found me: [but] your commandments [were] my meditation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{144}} Your testimonies [are] an everlasting righteousness: instruct me, and I shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{145}} I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will search out your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{146}} I cried to you; save me, and I will keep your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{147}} I arose before the dawn, and cried: I hoped in your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{148}} My eyes prevented the dawn, that I might meditate on your oracles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{149}} Hear my voice, O Lord, according to your mercy; quicken me according to your judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{150}} They have drawn near who persecuted me unlawfully; and they are far removed from your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{151}} You are near, O Lord; and all your ways are truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{152}} I have known of old concerning your testimonies, that you have founded them for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{153}} Look upon my affliction, and rescue me; for I have not forgotten your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{154}} Plead my cause, and ransom me: quicken me because of your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{155}} Salvation is far from sinners: for they have not searched out your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{156}} Your mercies, O Lord, are many: quicken me according to your judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{157}} Many are they that persecute me and oppress me: [but] I have not declined from your testimonies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{158}} I saw men acting foolishly, and I pined away; for they kept not your oracles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{159}} Behold, I have loved your commandments, O Lord: quicken me in your mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{160}} The beginning of your words is truth; and all the judgments of your righteousness [endure] for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{161}} Princes persecuted me without a cause, but my heart feared because of your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{162}} I will exult because of your oracles, as one that finds much spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{163}} I hate and abhor unrighteousness; but I love your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{164}} Seven times in a day have I praised you because of the judgments of your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{165}} Great peace have they that love your law: and there is no stumbling block to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{166}} I waited for your salvation, O Lord, and have loved your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{167}} My soul has kept your testimonies, and loved them exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{168}} I have kept your commandments and your testimonies; for all my ways are before you, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{169}} Let my supplication come near before you, o Lord; instruct me according to your oracle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{170}} Let my petition come in before you, O Lord; deliver me according to your oracle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{171}} Let my lips utter a hymn, when you shall have taught me your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{172}} Let my tongue utter your oracles; for all your commandments are righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{173}} Let your hand be [prompt] to save me; for I have chosen your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{174}} I have longed after your salvation, O Lord; and your law is my meditation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{175}} My soul shall live, and shall praise you; and your judgments shall help me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{176}} I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant; for I have not forgotten your commandments.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 2962, bc 1042 (Title), This Psalm was probably composed by David after Nathan's prophetic address; and sung by alternate choirs at some public festival. It largely partakes of David's spirit, and everywhere shews the hand of a master; the style is grand and sublime; the subject noble and majestic. \textsuperscript{5} called, ; in distress Heb. out of distress, set me \textsuperscript{6} The Lord, ; on my side Heb. for me \textsuperscript{10} All nations, ; destroy them Heb. cut them off \textsuperscript{12} like bees quenched; in the name, ; , destroy them Heb. cut them down \textsuperscript{20} This gate Dr. Kennicott supposes that this verse was sung by the priest, the by the king, the by a chorus of people, the by the king, the by the priest, the by the king, and the grand chorus of the whole assembly. \textsuperscript{23} the Lord's doing Heb. from the Lord, ; it is \textsuperscript{27} God, showed; bind; the horns\par}
