\subsection*{Psalm 119 (MT 120)}
\markright{PSALM 119 (MT 120)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (120) A Song of Degrees. In my affliction I cried to the Lord, and he listened to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Deliver my soul, O Lord, from unjust lips, and from a deceitful tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} What should be given to you, and what should be added to you, for [your] crafty tongue? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Sharpened weapons of the mighty, with coals of the desert. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged; I have tabernacled among the tents of Kedar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} My soul has long been a sojourner; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I was peaceful among them that hated peace; when I spoke to them, they warred against me without a cause.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3560, bc 444 (Title), This Psalm, which was probably composed by Ezra, is another of the alphabetical Psalms. It consists of twenty-two parts, answering to the number of the Hebrew letters; every part being divided into eight verses, and each verse beginning with that letter which forms the title of the part; that is, the first part of eight verses with ΰ, the second with α, etc. It is an elegant, important, and useful composition; the chief subjects of which are the excellence of God's laws, and the happiness of those who observe them. Blessed, ; undefiled or, perfect, or sincere; walk \textsuperscript{7} I will, ; when, ; thy righteous judgments Heb. judgments of thy righteousness\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 1:1-3; Ps 32:1-2; Ps 112:1; Ps 128:1; Matt 5:3-12; Luke 11:28; John 13:17; Jas 1:25; Rev 22:14; 2Kgs 20:3; 2Chr 31:20-21; Job 1:1; Job 1:8; John 1:47; Acts 24:16; 2Cor 1:12; Titus 2:11-12; Ezek 11:20; Hos 14:9; Luke 1:6; 1Thess 4:1-2 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 119:22; Ps 119:146; Ps 25:10; Ps 105:45; Deut 6:17; 1Kgs 2:3; Prov 23:26; Ezek 36:27; John 14:23; 1John 3:20; Ps 119:10; Deut 4:29; 2Chr 31:21; Jer 29:13 \textsuperscript{3} 1John 3:9; 1John 5:18 \textsuperscript{4} Deut 4:1; Deut 4:9; Deut 5:29-33; Deut 6:17; Deut 11:13; Deut 11:22; Deut 12:32; Deut 28:1-14; Deut 30:16; Josh 1:7; Jer 7:23; Matt 28:20; John 14:15; John 14:21; Phil 4:8-9; 1John 5:3 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 119:32; Ps 119:36; Ps 119:44-45; Ps 119:131; Ps 119:159; Ps 119:173; Ps 51:10; Jer 31:33; Rom 7:22-24; 2Thess 3:5; Heb 13:21 \textsuperscript{6} Ps 119:31; Ps 119:80; Job 22:26; Dan 12:2-3; 1John 2:28; 1John 3:20-21; Ps 119:128; John 15:14; Jas 2:10 \textsuperscript{7} Ps 119:171; Ps 9:1; Ps 86:12-13; 1Chr 29:13-17; Ps 119:12; Ps 119:18-19; Ps 119:27; Ps 119:33-34; Ps 119:64; Ps 119:73; Ps 119:124; Ps 25:4-5; Ps 25:8-10; Ps 143:10; Isa 48:17; John 6:45; Ps 119:138\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 120 (MT 121)}
\markright{PSALM 120 (MT 121)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (121) A Song of Degrees. I lifted up my eyes to the mountains, whence my help shall come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} My help [shall come] from the Lord, who made the heaven and the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let not your foot be moved; and let not your keeper slumber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Behold, he that keeps Israel shall not slumber nor sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The Lord shall keep you: the Lord is your shelter upon your right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The sun shall not burn you by day, neither the moon by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} May the Lord preserve you from all evil: the Lord shall keep your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Lord shall keep your coming in, and your going out, from henceforth and even for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} What shall etc. or, What shall the deceitful tongue give unto thee, or, What shall it profit thee; done Heb. added \textsuperscript{4} Sharp etc. or, It is as the sharp arrows of the mighty man, with coals of juniper.;, ; arrows \textsuperscript{5} Woe, ; Mesech; Meshech. the tents \textsuperscript{7} for peace or, a man of peace, ; when\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 121 (MT 122)}
\markright{PSALM 121 (MT 122)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (122) A Song of Degrees. I was glad when they said to me, Let us go into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Our feet stood in your courts, O Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Jerusalem is built as a city whose fellowship is complete. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For there are set thrones for judgment, [even] thrones for the house of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Pray now for the peace of Jerusalem: and [let there be] prosperity to them that love you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Let peace, I pray, be within your host, and prosperity in your palaces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the sake of my brethren and my neighbors, I have indeed spoken peace concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Because of the house of the Lord our God, I have diligently sought your good.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I will etc. or, Shall I lift up my eyes to the hills, whence should my help come? lift up \textsuperscript{8} thy going out; from this time\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 122 (MT 123)}
\markright{PSALM 122 (MT 123)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (123) A Song of Degrees. To you who dwell in heaven have I lifted up my eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, as the eyes of servants [are directed] to the hands of their masters, [and] as the eyes of a maidservant to the hands of her mistress; so our eyes [are directed] to the Lord our God, until he have mercy upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Have pity upon us, O Lord, have pity upon us: for we are exceedingly filled with contempt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [Yes], our soul has been exceedingly filled [with it]: [let] the reproach [be] to them that are at ease, and contempt to the proud.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} was glad, Let us go \textsuperscript{4} Whither;, the testimony, to give\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 42:4; Ps 55:14; Ps 63:1-3; Ps 84:1-2; Ps 84:10; Ps 119:111; Isa 2:3; Jer 31:6; Jer 50:4-5; Mic 4:2; Zech 8:21-23 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 84:7; Ps 87:1-3; Ps 100:4; Exod 20:24; 2Chr 6:6 \textsuperscript{3} 2Sam 5:9; Eph 2:20-21; Eph 4:4-7; Rev 21:10-27 \textsuperscript{4} Ps 78:68; Ps 132:13; Exod 23:17; Exod 34:23-24; Deut 12:5; Deut 12:11; Deut 16:16; Exod 16:34; Exod 26:33-34; Exod 32:15; Ps 66:13-16; Ps 107:1-3; Ps 116:17-19; Ps 118:19\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 123 (MT 124)}
\markright{PSALM 123 (MT 124)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (124) A Song of Degrees. If it had not been that the Lord was among us, let Israel now say; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} if it had not been that the Lord was among us, when men rose up against us; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} verily they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} verily the water would have drowned us, our soul would have gone under the torrent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Yes, our soul would have gone under the overwhelming water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us for a prey to their teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Our soul has been delivered as a sparrow from the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are delivered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} as the eyes, so our eyes \textsuperscript{3} Have mercy, ; for we are\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 25:15; Ps 121:1; Ps 141:8; Luke 18:13; Ps 2:4; Ps 11:4; Ps 113:5-6; Ps 115:3; Isa 57:15; Isa 66:1; Matt 6:9 \textsuperscript{2} Josh 9:23; Josh 9:27; Josh 10:6; Ps 40:1-3; Ps 119:82; Ps 119:123-125; Ps 130:5-6; Gen 32:26; Gen 49:18; Lam 3:25-26; Luke 18:1 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 56:1-2; Ps 57:1; Ps 69:13-16; Luke 18:11-13; Ps 44:13-16; Ps 89:50-51; Neh 4:2-4; Isa 53:3; Luke 16:14; Luke 23:35 \textsuperscript{4} Ps 73:5-9; Ps 119:51; Job 12:5; Job 16:4; Jer 48:11; Jer 48:27; Jer 48:29; Acts 17:21; Acts 17:32; Acts 26:24; 1Cor 4:13\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 124 (MT 125)}
\markright{PSALM 124 (MT 125)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (125) A Song of Degrees. They that trust in the Lord [shall be] as mount Sion: he that dwells in Jerusalem shall never be moved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The mountains are round about her, and [so] the Lord is round about his people, from henceforth and even for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the Lord will not allow the rod of sinners to be upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous should stretch forth their hands to iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Do good, O Lord, to them [that are] good, and to them [that are] upright in heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But them that turn aside to crooked ways the Lord will lead away with the workers of iniquity: [but] peace [shall be] upon Israel.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 125 (MT 126)}
\markright{PSALM 125 (MT 126)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (126) A Song of Degrees. When the Lord turned the captivity of Sion, we became as comforted ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then was our mouth filled with joy, and our tongue with exultation: then would they say among the Gentiles, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord has done great things among them. The Lord has done great things for us, we became joyful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Turn, O Lord, our captivity, as the streams in the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They went on and wept as they cast their seeds; but they shall surely come with exultation, bringing their sheaves [with them].\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} that trust, ; be as mount;, ; but abideth \textsuperscript{2} As the mountains the Lord \textsuperscript{3} the rod; the wicked Heb. wickedness \textsuperscript{5} As for such; crooked; with the workers, peace\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 126 (MT 127)}
\markright{PSALM 126 (MT 127)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (127) A Song of Degrees. Except the Lord build the house, they that build labor in vain: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman watches in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} It is vain for you to rise early: you⌃ rise up after resting, you⌃ that eat the bread of grief; while he gives sleep to his beloved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, the inheritance of the Lord, children, the reward of the fruit of the womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} As arrows in the hand of a mighty man; so are the children of those who were outcasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Blessed is the man who shall satisfy his desire with them: they shall not be ashamed when they shall speak to their enemies in the gates.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} turned again etc. Heb. returned the returning of Zion, ; we were like \textsuperscript{2} Then was, ; then said; done great things for them Heb. magnified to do with them \textsuperscript{4} Turn again; as the streams \textsuperscript{5} that sow; joy or, singing\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 53:6; Ps 85:1; Ezra 1:1-11; Job 42:10; Jer 31:8-10; Hos 6:11; Joel 3:1; Job 9:16; Mark 16:11; Luke 24:11; Luke 24:41; Acts 12:9; Acts 12:14-16 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 14:7; Ps 53:6; Ps 106:47-48; Ezra 3:11; Job 8:21; Isa 35:10; Isa 49:9-13; Jer 31:12-13; Jer 33:11; Rev 11:15-17; Num 23:23; Josh 2:9-11; Josh 9:9-10; Neh 6:16; Zech 8:22-23; Rom 11:15 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 18:50; Ps 31:19; Ps 66:5-6; Ps 68:7-8; Ps 68:22; Ezra 7:27-28; Isa 11:11-16; Isa 12:4-6; Isa 51:9-11; Isa 52:9-10; Isa 66:14; Luke 1:46; Luke 1:49; Eph 1:18-22; Rev 12:10; Rev 19:1-7 \textsuperscript{4} Ps 126:1; Ps 85:4; Hos 1:11; Josh 3:16; Isa 41:18 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 137:1; Isa 12:1-3; Jer 31:9-13; Joel 2:17; Joel 2:23; Matt 5:4; John 16:20-22; 2Cor 7:8-11\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 127 (MT 128)}
\markright{PSALM 127 (MT 128)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (128) A Song of Degrees. Blessed are all they that fear the Lord; who walk in his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You shall eat the labors of your hands: blessed are you, and it shall be well with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine on the sides of your house: your children as young olive-plants round about your table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that fears the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} May the Lord bless you out of Sion; and may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And may you see your children's children. Peace be upon Israel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} for Solomon or, of Solomon, *title The Lord; build, ; they labour; that build it Heb. that are builders of it in it except; the watchman \textsuperscript{2} vain;, rise up the bread; for so he \textsuperscript{5} Happy; his quiver full of them Heb. filled his quiver with them, they shall.; speak or, subdue, or, destroy\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 128 (MT 129)}
\markright{PSALM 128 (MT 129)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A Song of Degrees. Many a time have they warred against me from my youth, let Israel now say: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Many a time have they warred against me from my youth: and yet they prevailed not against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The sinners wrought upon my back: they prolonged their iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The righteous Lord has cut asunder the necks of sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Let all that hate Sion be put to shame and turned back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let them be as the grass of the housetops, which withers before it is plucked up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Wherewith the reaper fills not his hand, nor he that makes up the sheaves, his bosom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Neither do they that go by say, The blessing of the Lord be upon you: we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} thou shalt eat;, ; and it shall \textsuperscript{3} a fruitful vine; olive plants; round about \textsuperscript{5} bless thee, ; thou shalt see\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 103:1; Ps 103:13; Ps 103:17; Ps 112:1; Ps 115:13; Ps 147:11; Luke 1:50; Ps 1:1-3; Ps 81:13; Ps 119:1; Luke 1:6; Acts 9:31; 1Thess 4:1 \textsuperscript{2} Gen 3:19; Deut 28:4; Deut 28:11; Deut 28:39; Deut 28:51; Judg 6:3-6; Eccl 5:18-19; Isa 62:8; Isa 65:13; Isa 65:21-23; Eccl 8:12; Isa 3:10; Jer 22:15; 1Cor 15:58; Eph 6:3 \textsuperscript{3} Gen 49:22; Prov 5:15-18; Ezek 19:10; Ps 52:8; Ps 144:12; Jer 11:16; Hos 14:6-7; Rom 11:24; Ps 127:5 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 20:2; Ps 118:26; Ps 134:3; Isa 2:3; Eph 1:3; Ps 122:6; Isa 33:20 \textsuperscript{6} Gen 50:23; Job 42:16; Ps 125:5; Isa 66:12; Gal 1:16\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 129 (MT 130)}
\markright{PSALM 129 (MT 130)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (130) A Song of Degrees. Out of the depths have I cried to you, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} O Lord, listen to my voice; let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For with you is forgiveness: for your name's sake {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} have I waited for you, O Lord, my soul has waited for your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} My soul has hoped in the Lord; from the morning watch till night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Let Israel hope in the Lord: for with the Lord is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Many or, Much. have they, ; from; may\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Exod 1:12-14; Exod 1:22; Exod 5:7-19; Judg 2:15; Judg 10:8-12; 1Sam 13:19; Lam 1:3; Jer 2:2; Ezek 23:3; Hos 2:15; Hos 11:1; Ps 124:1 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 34:19; Ps 118:13; Ps 125:1; Job 5:19; Matt 16:18; Rom 8:35-39; John 16:33; Rev 12:8-9 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 141:7; Isa 51:23 \textsuperscript{4} Ezra 9:15; Neh 9:33; Lam 1:18; Lam 3:22; Dan 9:7; Ps 124:6-7; Ps 140:5-11 \textsuperscript{5} Ps 83:4-11; Ps 122:6; Esth 6:13; Esth 9:5; Isa 10:12; Isa 37:22; Isa 37:28-29; Isa 37:35; Zech 1:14-17; Zech 12:3; Zech 12:6; 1Cor 16:22 \textsuperscript{6} Ps 37:2; Ps 92:7; Jer 17:5-6; Matt 13:6 \textsuperscript{7} Ps 126:6; Isa 17:10-11; Hos 8:7; Gal 6:8 \textsuperscript{8} Ps 118:26; Ruth 2:4\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 130 (MT 131)}
\markright{PSALM 130 (MT 131)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (131) A Song of Degrees. O Lord, my heart is not exalted, neither have my eyes been [haughtily] raised: neither have I exercised myself in great [matters], nor in things too wonderful for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [I shall have sinned] if I have not been humble, but have exulted my soul: according to [the relation of] a weaned child to his mother, so will you recompense my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let Israel hope in the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{X: }}\textsuperscript{1} Ps 18:4-6; Ps 18:16; Ps 25:16-18; Ps 40:2; Ps 42:7; Ps 69:1-2; Ps 69:14-15; Ps 71:20; Ps 88:6-7; Ps 116:3-4; Lam 3:53-55; Jonah 2:2-4; Heb 5:7 \textsuperscript{2} Ps 5:1-2; Ps 17:1; Ps 55:1-2; Ps 61:1-2; 2Chr 6:40; Neh 1:6; Neh 1:11; Isa 37:17; Dan 9:17-19 \textsuperscript{3} Ps 143:2; Job 9:2-3; Job 9:20; Job 10:14; Job 15:14; Isa 53:6; John 8:7-9; Rom 3:20-24\par}
\subsection*{Psalm 131 (MT 132)}
\markright{PSALM 131 (MT 132)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (132) A Song of Degrees. Lord, remember David, and all his meekness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} how he swore to the Lord, [and] vowed to the God of Jacob, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I will not go into the tabernacle of my house; I will not go up to the couch of my bed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I will not give sleep to my eyes, nor slumber to my eyelids, nor rest to my temples, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} until I find a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Behold, we heard of it in Ephratha; we found it in the fields of the wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Let us enter into his tabernacles: let us worship at the place where his feet stood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Arise, O Lord, into your rest; you, and the ark of your holiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Your priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness; and your saints shall exult. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the sake of your servant David turn not away the face of your anointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The Lord swore [in] truth to David, and he will not annul it, [saying], Of the fruit of your body will I set [a king] upon your throne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If your children will keep my covenant, and these my testimonies which I shall teach them, their children also shall sit upon your throne for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the Lord has elected Sion, he has chosen her for a habitation for himself, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have chosen it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I will surely bless her provision: I will satisfy her poor with bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I will clothe her priests with salvation; and her saints shall greatly exult. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} There will I cause to spring up a horn to David: I have prepared a lamp for my anointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} His enemies will I clothe with a shame; but upon himself shall my holiness flourish.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 136 (MT 137)}
\markright{PSALM 136 (MT 137)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (137) For David, [a Psalm] of Jeremias. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat; and wept when we remembered Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} We hung our harps on the willows in the midst of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For there they that had taken us captive asked of us the words of a song; and they that had carried us away [asked] a hymn, [saying], Sing us [one] of the songs of Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} How should we sing the Lord's song in a strange land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget [its skill]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} May my tongue cleave to my throat, if I do not remember you; if I do not prefer Jerusalem as the chief of my joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase [it], rase [it], even to its foundations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Wretched daughter of Babylon! blessed [shall he be] who shall reward you as you have rewarded us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Blessed [shall he be] who shall seize and dash your infants against the rock.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} (Title), This Psalm is little else than a repetition of the preceding, with the addition of the burden, "for his mercy endureth for ever, " at the end of each verse; and it was doubtless composed on the same occasion. It seems evidently to have been a responsive song; the first part of the verse being probably sung by the Levites, and the burden by the people. Give thanks, ; for his mercy \textsuperscript{5} In the contrivance of the celestial bodies - in their specific gravities, relations, connections, influences on each other, revolutions, etc.; and in the wonderful adaptation of the atmosphere for the purposes of refracting the light, forming rain, dew, snow, etc., are exhibited the most astonishing displays of the Divine wisdom. \textsuperscript{8} The sun; to rule Heb. for the rulings \textsuperscript{9} The moon and stars The sun is the monarch of day, the state of light; the moon of the night, the state of darkness. The rays of the sun falling on the atmosphere, are refracted and diffused over the whole of the hemisphere of the earth immediately under his orb; while those rays of that vast luminary which, because of the earth's smallness in comparison with the sun, are diffused on all sides beyond the earth, falling on the opaque disc of the moon, are reflected back on the lower hemisphere, or the part of the earth opposite the sun. But the reflected light being 50, 000 times less in intensity than that of the sun, there is a sufficient distinction between day and night, though each is ruled and determined by one of these two great lights.\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 137 (MT 138)}
\markright{PSALM 137 (MT 138)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (138) A Psalm for David, of Aggaeus and Zacharias. I will give you thanks, O Lord, with my whole heart; and I will sing psalms to you before the angels; for you have heard all the words of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I will worship toward your holy temple, and give thanks to your name, on account of your mercy and your truth; for you have magnified your holy name above every thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} In whatever day I shall call upon you, hear me speedily; you shall abundantly provide me with your power in my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Let all the kings of the earth, o Lord, give thanks to you; for they have heard all the words of your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And let them sing in the ways of the Lord; for great is the glory of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the Lord is high, and [yet] regards the lowly; and he knows high things from afar off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Though I should walk in the midst of affliction, you will quicken me; you have stretched forth your hands against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand has saved me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} O Lord, you shall recompense [them] on my behalf: your mercy, O Lord, [endures] for ever: overlook not the works of your hands.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am cir, 3463, bc cir, 541 (Title), The author of this beautiful and affecting elegy is unknown, but the occasion is evident; and it was most probably composed during, or near the close of, the captivity. the rivers; there sat, ; we wept \textsuperscript{2} we hanged Willows were so plentiful at Babylon, on the banks of the Euphrates, that Isaiah calls it "the brook or river of willows." \textsuperscript{3} For there; a song Heb. the words of a song wasted us Heb. laid us on heaps; the songs of Zion \textsuperscript{4} How shall; strange land Heb. land of a stranger \textsuperscript{5} I forget, ; let my right \textsuperscript{6} let my tongue; if I prefer; my chief joy Heb. the head of my joy \textsuperscript{7} Remember; the children; Raze it Heb. make bare \textsuperscript{8} daughter; who art, ; 50:1-51:64;, destroyed Heb. wasted happy;, rewardeth etc. Heb. recompenseth unto thee thy deed which thou didst unto us\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 138 (MT 139)}
\markright{PSALM 138 (MT 139)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (139) For the end, a Psalm of David. O Lord, you have proved me, and known me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} You know my down-sitting and my up-rising: you understand my thoughts long before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You have traced my path and my bed, and have foreseen all my ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For there is no unrighteous word in my tongue: behold, O Lord, you have known all things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} the last and the first: you have fashioned me, and laid your hand upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The knowledge of you is too wonderful for me; it is very difficult, I can’t [attain] to it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Whither shall I go from your Spirit? and whither shall I flee from your presence? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If I should go up to heaven, you are there: if I should go down to hell, you are present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If I should spread my wings [to fly] straight forward, and sojourn at the extremity of the sea, [it would be vain], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} for even there your hand would guide me, and your right hand would hold me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When I said, Surely the darkness will cover me; even the night [was] light in my luxury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For darkness will not be darkness with you; but night will be light as day: as its darkness, so shall its light [be to you]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For you, O Lord, have possessed my reins; you have helped me from my mother's womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I will give you thanks; for you are fearfully wondrous; wondrous are your works; and my soul knows [it] well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} My bones, which you made in secret were not hidden from you, nor my substance, in the lowest parts of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Your eyes saw my unwrought [substance], and all [men] shall be written in your book; they shall be formed by day, though [there should for a time] be no one among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But your friends, O God, have been greatly honored by me; their rule has been greatly strengthened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I will number them, and they shall be multiplied beyond the sand; I awake, and am still with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Oh that you would kill the wicked, O God; depart from me, you⌃ men of blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For you will say concerning [their] thought, [that] they shall take your cities in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hate you? and wasted away because of your enemies? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} I have hated them with perfect hatred; they were counted my enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Prove me, O God, and know my heart; examine me, and know my paths; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} and see if [there is any] way of iniquity in me, and lead me in an everlasting way.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 139 (MT 140)}
\markright{PSALM 139 (MT 140)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (140) For the end, a Psalm of David. Rescue me, O Lord, from the evil man; deliver me from the unjust man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who have devised injustice in their hearts; all the day they prepared war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} They have sharpened their tongue as [the tongue] of a serpent; the poison of asps is under their lips. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner; rescue me from unjust men; who have purposed to overthrow my goings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The proud have hid a snare for me, and have stretched out ropes [for] snares for my feet; they set a stumbling block for me near the path. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I said to the Lord, You are my God; listen, O Lord, to the voice of my supplication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} O Lord God, the strength of my salvation; you have screened my head in the day of battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Deliver me not, O Lord, to the sinner, according to my desire: they have devised [mischief] against me; forsake me not, lest they should be exalted. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} [As for] the head of them that compass me, the mischief of their lips shall cover them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Coals of fire shall fall upon them on the earth; and you shall cast them down in afflictions: they shall not bear up [under them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A talkative man shall not prosper on the earth: evils shall hunt the unrighteous man to destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the poor, and the right of the needy ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Surely the righteous shall give thanks to your name: the upright shall dwell in your presence.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} compassest or, winnowest, ; my path;, and art acquainted \textsuperscript{4} there is not;, ; thou knowest \textsuperscript{9} If I take Light has been proved, by many experiments, to travel at the astonishing rate of 194, 188 miles in one second of time; and comes from the sun to the earth, a distance of 95, 513, 794 miles in 8 minutes and nearly 12 seconds! But, could I even fly upon the wings or rays of the morning light, which diffuses itself with such velocity over the globe from east to west, instead of being beyond Thy reach, or by this sudden transition be able to escape Thy notice, Thy arm could still at pleasure prevent or arrest my progress, and I should still be encircled with the immensity of Thy essence. The sentiment in this noble passage is remarkably striking and the description truly sublime. the wings; dwell \textsuperscript{12} the darkness; hideth not Heb. darkeneth not the darkness etc. Heb. as is the darkness, so is the light\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 140 (MT 141)}
\markright{PSALM 140 (MT 141)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (141) A Psalm of David. O Lord, I have cried to you; hear me: attend to the voice of my supplication, when I cry to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let my prayer be set forth before you as incense; the lifting up of my hands [as] an evening sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Set a watch, O Lord, on my mouth, and a strong door about by lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Incline not my heart to evil things, to employ pretexts for sins, with those who work iniquity. Let me not unite with their choice ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The righteous shall chasten me with mercy, and reprove me: but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head: for yet shall my prayer also be in their pleasures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Their mighty ones have been swallowed up near the rock: they shall hear my words, for they are sweet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} As a lump of earth is crushed upon the ground, our bones have been scattered by the [mouth of] the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For my eyes are to you, O Lord God: I have hoped in you; take not away my life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Keep me from the snare which they have set for me, and from the stumbling blocks of them that work iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Sinners shall fall by their own net: I am alone until I shall escape.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 141 (MT 142)}
\markright{PSALM 141 (MT 142)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (142) [A Psalm] of instruction for David, when he was in the cave, —a Prayer. I cried to the Lord with my voice; with my voice I made supplication to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I will pour out before him my supplication: I will declare before him my affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} When my spirit was fainting within me, then you knew my paths; in the very way wherein I was walking, they hid a snare for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I looked on [my] right hand, and behold, for there was none that noticed me; refuge failed me; and there was none that cared for my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I cried to you, O Lord, and said, You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Attend to my supplication, for I am brought very low; deliver me from them that persecute me; for they are stronger than I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name, O Lord; the righteous shall wait for me, until you recompense me.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Let my prayer David, who was now driven from Judea, and far from the sanctuary, here prays that the devotion of his heart, and the elevation of his hands, might be accepted; that the one might ascend to heaven fragrant and well pleasing as the cloud of incense, and the other, in conjunction with it, be prevalent as the minchah, or evening oblation. set forth Heb. directed, as incense; the lifting, ; the evening \textsuperscript{4} Incline not; to practice; and let me \textsuperscript{5} the righteous; , ; smite etc. or, smite me kindly and reprove me; let not their precious oil break my head, etc for yet my \textsuperscript{6} When their judges; they shall hear; for they\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 142 (MT 143)}
\markright{PSALM 142 (MT 143)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (143) A Psalm of David, when his son pursued him. O Lord, attend to my prayer: listen to my supplication in your truth; hear me in your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And enter not into judgment with your servant, for in your sight shall no [man] living be justified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the enemy has persecuted my soul; he has brought my life down to the ground; he has made me to dwell in a dark [place], as those that have been long dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore my spirit was grieved in me; my heart was troubled within me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I remembered the days of old; and I meditated on all your doings: [yes], I meditated on the works of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I spread forth my hands to you; my soul [thirsts] for you, as a dry land. Pause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Hear me speedily, O Lord; my spirit has failed; turn not away your face from me, else I shall be like to them that go down to the pit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Cause me to hear your mercy in the morning; for I have hoped in you; make known to me, O Lord, the way wherein I should walk; for I have lifted up my soul to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord; for I have fled to you for refuge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Teach me to do your will; for you are my God; your good Spirit shall guide me in the straight [way]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} You shall quicken me, O Lord, for your name's sake; in your righteousness you shall bring my soul out of affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And in your mercy you will destroy my enemies, and will destroy all those that afflict my soul; for I am your servant.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A Prayer David was twice in great peril in caves. On one occasion, in the cave of Adullam, when he fled from Achish king of Gath; and on another, in the cave of Engedi, where he had taken refuge from the pursuit of Saul. It is not certain to which of these events this Psalm refers; though probably to the former. when he was; with my voice \textsuperscript{2} poured out, *title; I showed \textsuperscript{3} my spirit, ; then thou, ; In the way \textsuperscript{4} I looked etc. or, Look on the right hand and see but there was, ; refuge, failed me, no man cared for my soul Heb. perished from me; no man sought after my soul \textsuperscript{5} Thou art, ; my portion, ; in the land \textsuperscript{6} for I am, for they \textsuperscript{7} my soul *title:, ; the righteous, thou shalt\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 143 (MT 144)}
\markright{PSALM 143 (MT 144)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (144) [A Psalm] of David concerning Goliad. Blessed [be] the Lord my God, who instructs my hands for battle, [and] my fingers for war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} My mercy, and my refuge; my helper, and my deliverer; my protector, in whom I have trusted; who subdues my people under me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Lord, what is man, that you are made known to him? or the son of man, that you take account of him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Man is like to vanity: his days pass as a shadow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O Lord, bow your heavens, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Send lightning, and you shall scatter them: send forth your arrows, and you shall discomfit them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Send forth your hand from on high; rescue me, and deliver me out of great waters, out of the hand of strange children; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} O God, I will sing a new song to you: I will play to you on a lute of ten strings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [Even] to him who gives salvation to kings: who redeems his servant David from the hurtful sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Deliver me, and rescue me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} whose children are as plants, strengthened in their youth: their daughters are beautiful, sumptuously adorned after the similitude of a temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Their garners are full, and bursting with one kind of store after another; their sheep are prolific, multiplying in their streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Their oxen are fat: there is no falling down of a hedge, nor going out, nor cry in their folds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Men bless the people to whom this lot belongs, [but] blessed is the people whose God is the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 144 (MT 145)}
\markright{PSALM 144 (MT 145)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (145) David's [Psalm of] praise. I will exalt you, my God, my king; and I will bless your name for ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Every day will I bless you, and I will praise your name for ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord is great, and greatly to be praised; and there is no end to his greatness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Generation after generation shall praise your works, and tell of your power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall speak of the glorious majesty of your holiness, and recount your wonders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they shall speak of the power of your terrible [acts]; and recount your greatness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They shall utter the memory of the abundance of your goodness, and shall exult in your righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Lord is compassionate, and merciful; long suffering, and abundant in mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Lord is good to those that wait [on him]; and his compassions are over all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Let all your works, O Lord, give thanks to you; and let your saints bless you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom, and talk of your dominion; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} to make known to the sons of men your power, and the glorious majesty of your kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion [endures] through all generations. The Lord is faithful in his words, and holy in all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord supports all that are falling, and sets up all that are broken down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The eyes of all wait upon you; and you give [them] their food in due season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You open your hands, and fill every living thing with pleasure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The Lord is near to all that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He will perform the desire of them that fear him: and he will hear their supplication, and save them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The Lord preserves all that love him: but all sinners he will utterly destroy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 145 (MT 146)}
\markright{PSALM 145 (MT 146)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (146) Alleluia, [a Psalm] of Aggaeus and Zacharias. My soul, praise the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} While I live will I praise the Lord: I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Trust not in princes, nor in the children of men, in whom there is no safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} His breath shall go forth, and he shall return to his earth; in that day all his thoughts shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} who made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all things in them: who keeps truth for ever: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} who executes judgment for the wronged: who gives food to the hungry. The Lord looses the fettered ones: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} the Lord gives wisdom to the blind: The Lord sets up the broken down: the Lord loves the righteous: the Lord preserves the strangers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} he will relieve the orphan and widow: but will utterly remove the way of sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The Lord shall reign for ever, [even] your God, O Sion, to all generations.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 146 (MT 147:1-11)}
\markright{PSALM 146 (MT 147:1-11)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} (147) Alleluia, [a Psalm] of Aggaeus and Zacharias. Praise you⌃ the Lord: for psalmody is a good thing; let praise be sweetly sung to our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The Lord builds up Jerusalem; and he will gather together the dispersed of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He numbers the multitudes of stars; and calls them all by names. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Great is our Lord, and great is his strength; and his understanding is infinite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The Lord lifts up the meek; but brings sinners down to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Begin [the song] with thanksgiving to the Lord; sing praises on the harp to our God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} who covers the heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who causes grass to spring up on the mountains, [[and green herb for the service of men;]] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and gives cattle their food, and to the young ravens that call upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He will not take pleasure in the strength of a horse; neither is he well-pleased with the legs of a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The Lord takes pleasure in them that fear him, and in all that hope in his mercy.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3489, bc 515 Praise ye the Lord Heb. \subsection*{Psalm 147 (MT 147:12-20)}
\markright{PSALM 147 (MT 147:12-20)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alleluia, a Psalm of Aggaeus and Zacharias. Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He makes your borders peaceful, and fills you with the flour of wheat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He sends his oracle to the earth: his word will run swiftly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He gives snow like wool: he scatters the mist like ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Casting [forth] his ice like morsels: who shall stand before his cold? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He shall send out his word, and melt them: he shall blow [with] his wind, and the waters shall flow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He sends his word to Jacob, his ordinances and judgments to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He has not done so to any [other] nation; and he has not shown them his judgments.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} for it is good, and praise \textsuperscript{5} Great, ; his understanding is infinite Heb. of his understanding there is no number\par}

\subsection*{Psalm 148}
\markright{PSALM 148}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alleluia, [a Psalm] of Aggaeus and Zacharias. Praise you⌃ the Lord from the heavens: praise him in the highest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Praise you⌃ him, all his angels: praise you⌃ him, all his hosts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you⌃ stars and light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Praise him, you⌃ heavens of heavens, and the water that is above the heavens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He has established them for ever, even for ever and ever: he has made an ordinance, and it shall not pass away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Praise the Lord from the earth, you⌃ serpents, and all deeps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy wind; the things that perform his word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Mountains, and all hills; fruitful trees, and all cedars: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} wild beasts, and all cattle; reptiles, and winged birds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} kings of the earth, and all peoples; princes, and all judges of the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} young men and virgins, old men with youths: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} let them praise the name of the Lord: for his name only is exalted; his praise is above the earth and heaven, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and he shall exalt the horn of his people, [there is] a hymn for all his saints, [even] of the children of Israel, a people who draw near to him.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 149}
\markright{PSALM 149}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alleluia. Sing to the Lord a new song: his praise is in the assembly of the saints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let Israel rejoice in him that made him; and let the children of Sion exult in their king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let them praise his name in the dance: let them sings praises to him with timbrel and lute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the Lord takes pleasure in his people; and will exalt the meek with salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The saints shall rejoice in glory; and shall exult on their beds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The high praises of God shall be in their throat, and two-edged swords in their hands; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} to execute vengeance on the nations, [and] punishments among the peoples; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} to bind their kings with fetters, and their nobles with manacles of iron; to execute on them the judgment written: this honor have all his saints.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Praise ye the Lord Heb. \subsection*{Psalm 150}
\markright{PSALM 150}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alleluia. Praise God in his holy places: praise him in the firmament of his power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Praise him on [account of] his mighty acts: praise him according to his abundant greatness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Praise him with the sound of a trumpet: praise him with lute and harp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Praise him with timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and the organ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Praise him with melodious cymbals: praise him with loud cymbals. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let every thing that has breath praise the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Psalm 151 (MT no MT equivalent)}
\markright{PSALM 151 (MT NO MT EQUIVALENT)}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This Psalm is a genuine one of David, though supernumerary, composed when he fought in single combat with Goliad. I was small among my brethren, and youngest in my father's house: I tended my father's sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} My hands formed a musical instrument, and my fingers tuned a lute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And who shall tell my Lord? the Lord himself, he himself hears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He sent forth his angel, and took me from my father's sheep, and he anointed me with the oil of his anointing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} My brothers were handsome and tall; but the Lord did not take pleasure in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I went forth to meet the Philistine; and he cursed me by his idols. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But I drew his own sword, and beheaded him, and removed reproach from the children of Israel.\par
\newpage
\section*{Proverbs Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Solomon chiefly\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} with Agur and Lemuel sections and later inspired compilation\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The book itself names Solomon as principal source and includes later collected materials plus named sayings of Agur and Lemuel.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 1 Kings 4:32 testifies to Solomon's proverbial activity; the canonical book itself supplies the remaining internal attributions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} mainly 10th century BC with later collected sections\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT Proverbs presents the standard Hebrew order of sayings and collections.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The LXX of Proverbs differs notably in order and some wording from the MT, making it a significant comparison point.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Wisdom instruction for covenant life under the fear of the LORD.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To impart practical, moral, and covenantal wisdom ordered under the fear of the LORD.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} wisdom; fear of the LORD; righteousness; speech; family; kingship; discipline\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Prologue 1-9; Solomonic sayings 10-24; Additional collections 25-29; Agur 30; Lemuel 31. Qumran Proverbs fragments survive in limited form | Subst. Second Temple period Early Hebrew evidence is limited compared with Psalms or Samuel, so the MT and ancient versions carry special weight | Heb. n/a Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Proverbs\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Use of proverbial material in later Jewish wisdom tradition (Ben Sira and others)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2nd century BC and later\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Proverbs is one of the books where the Greek tradition can differ markedly in order and arrangement from the MT.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Proverbs}
\markboth{PROVERBS}{}
\subsection*{Proverbs 1}
\markright{PROVERBS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The Proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} to know wisdom and instruction, and to perceive words of understanding; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} to receive also hard saying, and to understand true justice, and [how] to direct judgment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} that he might give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man discernment and understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For by the hearing of these a wise man will be wiser, and man of understanding will gain direction; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and will understand a parable, and a dark speech; the saying of the wise also, and riddles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; and [there is] good understanding to all that practise it: and piety toward God is the beginning of discernment; but the ungodly will set at nothing wisdom and instruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Hear, [my] son, the instruction of your father, and reject not the rules of your mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For you shall receive for your head a crown of graces, and a chain of gold round your neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [My] son, let not ungodly men lead you astray, neither consent you [to them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If they should exhort you, saying, Come with us, partake in blood, and let us unjustly hide the just man in the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and let us swallow him alive, as Hades [would], and remove the memorial of him from the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} let us seize on his valuable property, and let us fill our houses with spoils: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} but do you cast in your lot with us, and let us all provide a common purse, and let us have one pouch: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} go not in the way with them, but turn aside your foot from their paths: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [For their feet run to do evil, and are swift to shed blood. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} for nets are not without cause spread for birds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For they that are concerned in murder store up evils for themselves; and the overthrow of transgressors is evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} These are the ways of all that perform lawless deeds; for by ungodliness they destroy their own life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Wisdom sings aloud in passages, and in the broad places speaks boldly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she makes proclamation on the top of the walls, and sits by the gates of princes; and at the gates of the city boldly says, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So long as the simple cleave to justice, they shall not be ashamed: but the foolish being lovers of haughtiness, having become ungodly have hated knowledge, and are become subject to reproofs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Behold, I will bring forth to you the utterance of my breath, and I will instruct you in my speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Since I called, and you⌃ did not listen; and I spoke at length, and you⌃ gave no heed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} but you⌃ set at nothing my counsels, and disregarded my reproofs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} therefore I also will laugh at your destruction; and I will rejoice against [you] when ruin comes upon you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} yes when dismay suddenly comes upon you, and [your] overthrow shall arrive like a tempest; and when tribulation and distress shall come upon you, or when ruin shall come upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For it shall be that when you⌃ call upon me, I will not listen to you: wicked men shall seek me, but shall not find [me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the word of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} neither would they attend to my counsels, but derided my reproofs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Therefore shall they eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own ungodliness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For because they wronged the simple, they shall be slain; and an inquisition shall ruin the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But he that hearkens to me shall dwell in confidence, and shall rest securely from all evil.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 2}
\markright{PROVERBS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, if you will receive the utterance of my commandment, and hide it with you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} your ear shall listen to wisdom; you shall also apply your heart to understanding, and shall apply it to the instruction of your son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For if you shall call to wisdom, and utter your voice for understanding; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and if you shall seek it as silver, and search diligently for it as for treasures; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} then shall you understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the Lord gives wisdom; and from his presence [come] knowledge and understanding, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and he treasures up salvation for them that walk uprightly: he will protect their way; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} that he may guard the righteous ways: and he will preserve the way of them that fear him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then shall you understand righteousness, and judgment; and shall direct all your course aright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For if wisdom shall come into your understanding, and discernment shall seem pleasing to your soul, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} good counsel shall guard you, and holy understanding shall keep you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} to deliver you from the evil way, and from the man that speaks nothing faithfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Alas [for those] who forsake right paths, to walk in ways of darkness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} who rejoice in evils, and delight in wicked perverseness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} whose paths are crooked, and their courses winding; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} to remove you far from the straight way, and to estrange you from a righteous purpose. [My] son, let not evil counsel overtake you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [of her] who has forsaken the instruction of her youth, and forgotten the covenant of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For she has fixed her house near death, and [guided] her wheels near Hades with the giants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} None that go by her shall return, neither shall they take hold of right paths, for they are not apprehended of the years of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For had they gone in good paths, they would have found the paths of righteousness easy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For the upright shall dwell in the earth, and the holy shall be left behind in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The paths of the ungodly shall perish out of the earth, and transgressors shall be driven away from it.\par

Common English renderings: knowledge. Often denotes fuller or more exact knowledge. \textsuperscript{10} Gk. vocab: nous (νοῦς) = mind; understanding. Common English renderings: mind.
