\subsection*{Proverbs 3}
\markright{PROVERBS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, forget not my laws; but let your heart keep my words: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} for length of existence, and years of life, and peace, shall they add to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let not mercy and truth forsake you; but bind them about your neck: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} so shall you find favor: and do you provide things honest in the sight of the Lord, and of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Trust in God with all your heart; and be not exalted in your own wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In all your ways acquaint yourself with her, that she may rightly direct your paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Be not wise in your own conceit; but fear God, and depart from all evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then shall there be health to your body, and good keeping to your bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Honor the Lord with your just labors, and give him the first of your fruits of righteousness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} that your storehouses may be completely filled with corn, and that your presses may burst forth with wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [My] son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; nor faint when you are rebuked of him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} for whom the Lord loves, he rebukes, and scourges every son whom he receives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who knows prudence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For it is better to traffic for her, than for treasures of gold and silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And she is more valuable than precious stones: no evil thing shall resist her: she is well known to all that approach her, and no precious thing is equal to her in value. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For length of existence and years of life are in her right hand; and in her left hand are wealth and glory: out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and she carries law and mercy upon her tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are peaceful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} She is a tree of life to all that lay hold upon her; and she is [a] secure [help] to all that stay themselves on her, as on the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} God by wisdom founded the earth, and by prudence he prepared the heavens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} By understanding were the depths broken up, and the clouds dropped water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [My] son, let [them] not pass from [you], but keep my counsel and understanding: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} that your soul may live, and that there may be grace round your neck; and it shall be health to your flesh, and safety to your bones: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} that you may go confidently in peace in all your ways, and that your foot may not stumble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For if you rest, you shall be undismayed; and if you sleep, you shall slumber sweetly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you shall not be afraid of alarm coming upon you, neither of approaching attacks of ungodly men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For the Lord shall be over all your ways, and shall establish your foot that you be not moved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Forbear not to do good to the poor, whenever your hand may have [power] to help [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Say not, Come back another time, to-morrow I will give; while you are able to do [him] good: for you know not what the next day will bring forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Devise not evil against your friend, living near you and trusting in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Be not ready to quarrel with a man without a cause, lest he do you some harm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Procure not the reproaches of bad men, neither do you covet their ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For every transgressor is unclean before the Lord; neither does he sit among the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly; but the habitations of the just are blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} The wise shall inherit glory; but the ungodly have exalted [their own] dishonor.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{8} Heb. vocab: marpe (מַרְפֵּא) = healing; remedy. Common English renderings: health; healing. Noun for healing or cure.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} length, ; long life Heb. years of life, and peace \textsuperscript{4} shalt; good understanding or, good success, *marg. \textsuperscript{8} shall; health Heb. medicine thy marrow Heb. watering, or moistening \textsuperscript{13} is the; getteth Heb. draweth out \textsuperscript{27} Withhold; them to whom it is due Heb. the owners thereof in the \textsuperscript{29} Devise not evil or, Practise no evil \textsuperscript{31} Envy, ; the oppressor Heb. a man of violence, choose \textsuperscript{35} wise; but; shall be the promotion of fools Heb. exalteth the fools\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 4}
\markright{PROVERBS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Hear, you⌃ children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I give you a good gift; forsake you⌃ not my law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I also was a son obedient to [my] father, and loved in the sight of [my] mother: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} who spoke and instructed me, [saying], Let our speech be fixed in your heart, keep [our] commandments, forget them not: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and do not neglect the speech of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And forsake it not, and it shall cleave to you: love it, and it shall keep you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Secure it, and it shall exalt you: honor it, that it may embrace you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} that it may give to your head a crown of graces, and may cover you with a crown of delight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Hear, [my] son, and receive my words; and the years of your life shall be increased, that the resources of your life may be many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For I teach you the ways of wisdom; and I cause you to go in right paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For when you go, your steps shall not be straitened; and when you run, you shall not be distressed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Take hold of my instruction; let it not go, —but keep it for yourself for your life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Go not in the ways of the ungodly, neither covet the ways of transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In whatever place they shall pitch their camp, go not there; but turn from them, and pass away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For they can’t sleep, unless they have done evil: their sleep is taken away, and they rest not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For these live upon the bread of ungodliness, and are drunken with wine of transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go on and shine, until the day be fully come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they know not how they stumble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [My] son, attend to my speech; and apply your ear to my words: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} that your fountains may not fail you; keep them in [your] heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For they are life to those that find them, and health to all [their] flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Keep your heart with the utmost care; for out of these are the issues of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Remove from you a froward mouth, and put far away from you unjust lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let your eyes look right on, and let your eyelids assent [to] just [things]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Make straight paths for your feet, and order your ways aright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Turn not aside to the right hand nor to the left, but turn away your foot from an evil way: [for God knows the ways on the right hand, but those on the left are crooked:] and he will make your ways straight, and will guide your steps in peace.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{9} give; a crown etc. or, she shall compass thee with a crown of glory \textsuperscript{22} life, health Heb. medicine, *marg. \textsuperscript{23} Keep, ; with all diligence Heb. above all keeping, ; for \textsuperscript{24} Put; a etc. Heb. frowardness of mouth, and perverseness of lips \textsuperscript{26} Ponder; let all thy ways be established or, all thy ways shall be ordered aright\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 5}
\markright{PROVERBS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, attend to my wisdom, and apply your ear to my words; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that you may keep good understanding, and the discretion of my lips gives you a charge. Give no heed to a worthless woman; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} for honey drops from the lips of a harlot, who for a season pleases your palate: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} but afterwards you will find her more bitter than gall, and sharper than a two-edged sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For the feet of folly lead those who deal with her down to the grave with death; and her steps are not established. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For she goes not upon the paths of life; but her ways are slippery, and not easily known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now then, [my] son, hear me, and make not my words of none effect. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remove your way far from her; draw not near to the doors of her house: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} lest you give away your life to others, and your substance to the merciless: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your labors come into the houses of strangers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you repent at last, when the flesh of your body is consumed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and you shall say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart avoided reproofs! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I heard not the voice of him that instructed me, and taught me, neither did I apply my ear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Drink waters out of your own vessels, and out of your own springing wells. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Let not waters out of your fountain be spilled by you, but let your waters go into your streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let them be only your own, and let no stranger partake with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Let your fountain of water be [truly] your own; and rejoice with the wife of your youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Let [your] loving hart and your graceful colt company with you, and let her be considered your own, and be with you at all times; for ravished with her love you shall be greatly increased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Be not intimate with a strange woman, neither fold yourself in the arms of a woman not your own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For the ways of a man are before the eyes of God, and he looks on all his paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Iniquities ensnare a man, and every one is bound in the chains of his own sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Such a man dies with the uninstructed; and he is cast forth from the abundance of his own substance, and has perished through folly.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the lips, ; mouth Heb. palate smoother \textsuperscript{19} as the, satisfy thee Heb. water thee, be thou ravished always with her love Heb. err thou always in her love \textsuperscript{22} His, ; holden sins Heb. sin\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 6}
\markright{PROVERBS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, if you become surety for your friend, you shall deliver your hand to an enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For a man's own lips become a strong snare to him, and he is caught with the lips of his own mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [My] son, do what I command you, and deliver yourself; for on your friend's account you are come into the power of evil [men]: faint not, but stir up even your friend for whom you are become surety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Give not sleep to your eyes, nor slumber with your eyelids; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} that you may deliver yourself as a doe out of the toils, and as a bird out of a snare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Go to the ant, O sluggard; and see, and emulate his ways, and become wiser than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For whereas he has no husbandry, nor any one to compel him, and is under no master, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} he prepares food for himself in the summer, and lays by abundant store in harvest. Or go to the bee, and learn how diligent she is, and how earnestly she is engaged in her work; whose labors kings and private men use for health, and she is desired and respected by all: though weak in body, she is advanced by honouring wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} How long will you lie, O sluggard? and when will you awake out of sleep? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You sleep a little, and you rest a little, and you slumber a short [time], and you fold your arms over your breast a little. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Then poverty comes upon you as an evil traveller, and lack as a swift courier: but if you be diligent, your harvest shall arrive as a fountain, and poverty shall flee away as a bad courier. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A foolish man and a transgressor goes in ways that are not good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the same winks with the eye, and makes a sign with his foot, and teaches with the beckonings of his fingers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [His] perverse heart devises evils: at all times such a one causes troubles to a city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore his destruction shall come suddenly; overthrow and irretrievable ruin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For he rejoices in all things which God hates, and he is ruined by reason of impurity of soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The eye of the haughty, a tongue unjust, hands shedding the blood of the just; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do evil, —[are hateful to God]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} An unjust witness kindles falsehoods, and brings on quarrels between brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [My] son, keep the laws of your father, and reject not the ordinances of your mother: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} but bind them upon your soul continually, and hang them as a chain about your neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Whenever you walk, lead this along and let it be with you; that it may talk with you when you wake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the commandment of the law is a lamp and a light; a way of life; reproof also and correction: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} to keep you continually from a married woman, and from the calumny of a strange tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let not the desire of beauty overcome you, neither be you caught by your eyes, neither be captivated with her eyelids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For the value of a harlot is as much as of one loaf; and a woman hunts for the precious souls of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Shall any one bind fire in his bosom, and not burn his garments? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} or will any one walk on coals of fire, and not burn his feet? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So is he that goes in to a married woman; he shall not be held guiltless, neither any one that touches her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} It is not to be wondered at if one should be taken stealing, for he steals that when hungry he may satisfy his soul: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} but if he should be taken, he shall repay sevenfold, and shall deliver himself by giving all his goods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But the adulterer through lack of sense procures destruction to his soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} He endures both pain and disgrace, and his reproach shall never be wiped off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} For the soul of her husband is full of jealousy: he will not spare in the day of vengeance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} He will not forego [his] enmity for any ransom: neither will he be reconciled for many gifts.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 7}
\markright{PROVERBS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, keep my words, and hide with you my commandments. [My] son, honor the Lord, and you shall be strong; and fear none but him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} keep my commandments, and you shall live; and [keep] my words as the pupils of [your] eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And bind them on your fingers, and write [them] on the table of your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Say that wisdom is your sister, and gain prudence as an acquaintance for yourself; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} that she may keep you from the strange and wicked woman, if she should assail you with flattering words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For she looks from a window out of her house into the streets, at one whom she may see of the senseless ones, a young man void of understanding, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} passing by the corner in the passages near her house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and speaking, in the dark of the evening, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} when there happens [to be] the stillness of night and of darkness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and the woman meets him having the appearance of a harlot, that causes the hearts of young men to flutter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And she is fickle, and debauched, and her feet abide not at home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For at one time she wanders without, and at [another] time she lies in wait in the streets, at every corner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I have a peace-offering; today I pay my vows: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} therefore I came forth to meet you, desiring your face; [and] I have found you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I have spread my bed with sheets, and I have covered it with double tapestry from Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Come, and let us enjoy love until the morning; come, and let us embrace in love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For my husband is not at home, but is gone on a long journey, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} having taken in his hand a bundle of money: after many days he will return to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So with much converse she prevailed on him to go astray, and with the snares of her lips forced him from [the right path]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he followed her, being gently led on, and [that] as an ox is led to the slaughter, and as a dog to bonds, or as a hart shot in the liver with an arrow: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} and he hastens as a bird into a snare, not knowing that he is running for [his] life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Now then, [my] son, listen to me, and attend to the words of my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let not your heart turn aside to her ways : {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} for she has wounded and cast down many, and those whom she has slain are innumerable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Her house is the way of hell, leading down to the chambers of death.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Keep; as the As the pupil of the eye, the hole or the opening of the uveous coat, or iris, through which the rays of light pass, and falling upon the retina, there depict every object in its natural colour, as upon a piece of white paper. Now the pupil of the eye being essentially necessary to sight, and easily injured, it is not only, in common with the other parts, deeply entrenched in the skull, ramparted with the forehead and cheek bones, defended by the eyebrows, eyelids, and eyelashes, and placed so as to be best protected by the hands, but, by a wonderful mechanism, is contracted or dilated by the muscular power of the iris, without which an excess of light would cause instant blindness. \textsuperscript{6} at the; casement Eshnav, rather a lattice, so called from the Arabic shanaba, " to be cool, " because of its use in keeping the apartments cool. \textsuperscript{7} the simple, ; the youths Heb. the sons void \textsuperscript{9} the twilight; evening Heb. evening of the day, *marg. \textsuperscript{13} she; with an impudent face said Heb. she strengthened her face and said \textsuperscript{14} I have peace offerings with me Heb. Peace-offerings are upon me, ; this \textsuperscript{20} with him Heb. in his hand the day appointed or, the new moon \textsuperscript{22} straightway Heb. suddenly as an as a Dr. Grey, making a slight alteration in the text, renders, "as a dog to the chain, and as a deer, till a dart strike through his liver; " and Dr. Hunt, "Or as a hart boundeth into the toils, till a dart strike through his liver." The LXX, Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic, concur in this interpretation. The circumstance of the dart, as applied to the deer, is beautiful and proper, which otherwise we are at a loss to dispose of; and this creature, of all others, was the most proper to be noticed on this occasion; for the usual representation which the Egyptians made of a man overthrown by flattery and fair speeches was the picture of a heart captivated and ensnared by the sound of music. the correction \textsuperscript{23} a dart as a bird; knoweth\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 8}
\markright{PROVERBS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You shall proclaim wisdom, that understanding may be obedient to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For she is on lofty eminences, and stands in the midst of the ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For she sits by the gates of princes, and sings in the entrances, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You, O men, I exhort; and utter my voice to the sons of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O you⌃ simple, understand subtlety, and you⌃ that are untaught, imbibe knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Listen to me; for I will speak solemn [truths]; and will produce right [sayings] from my lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For my throat shall meditate truth; and false lips are an abomination before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing in them wrong or perverse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They are all evident to those that understand, and right to those that find knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Receive instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than tried gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For wisdom is better than precious stones; and no valuable substance is of equal worth with it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I wisdom have lived [with] counsel and knowledge, and I have called upon understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, and insolence, and pride, and the ways of wicked men; and I hate the perverse ways of bad men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Counsel and safety are mine; prudence is mine, and strength is mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} By me kings reign, and princes decree justice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} By me nobles become great, and monarchs by me rule over the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I love those that love me; and they that seek me shall find [me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Wealth and glory belong to me; yes, abundant possessions and righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [It is] better to have my fruit than [to have] gold and precious stones; and my produce is better than choice silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I walk in ways of righteousness, and [am] conversant with the paths of judgment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} that I may divide substance to them that love me, and may fill their treasures with good things. If I declare to you the things that daily happen, I will remember [also] to recount the things of old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The Lord made me the beginning of his ways for his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He established me before time [was] in the beginning, before he made the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} even before he made the depths; before the fountains of water came forth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} before the mountains were settled, and before all hills, he begets me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The Lord made countries and uninhabited [tracks], and the highest inhabited parts of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} When he prepared the heaven, I was present with him; and when he prepared his throne upon the winds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} and when he strengthened the clouds above; and when he secured the fountains of the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} decree. and when he strengthened the foundations of the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} I was by him, suiting [myself to him], I was that wherein he took delight; and daily I rejoiced in his presence continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For he rejoiced when he had completed the world, and rejoiced among the children of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Now then, [my] son, hear me: blessed is the man who shall listen to me, and the mortal who shall keep my ways; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} [Hear wisdom and be wise, and] [be not strangers to it. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my entrances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For my outgoings are the outgoings of life, and [in them] is prepared favor from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But they that sin against me act wickedly against their own souls: and they that hate me love death.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 9}
\markright{PROVERBS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wisdom has built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} She has killed her beasts; she has mingled her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} She has sent forth her servants, calling with a loud proclamation to the feast, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Whoso is foolish, let him turn aside to me: and to them that lack understanding she says, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I have mingled for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Leave folly, that you⌃ may reign for ever; and seek wisdom, and improve understanding by knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He that reproves evil [men] shall get dishonor to himself; and he that rebukes an ungodly [man] shall disgrace himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Rebuke not evil [men], lest they should hate you: rebuke a wise [man], and he will love you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Give an opportunity to a wise [man], and he will be wiser: instruct a just man, and he will receive more [instruction]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the counsel of saints is understanding: for to know the law is [the character] of a sound mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For in this way you shall live long, and years of your life shall be added to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Son, if you be wise for yourself, you shall also be wise for your neighbors; and if you should prove wicked, you alone will bear the evil. He that stays himself upon falsehoods, attempts to rule the winds, and the same will pursue birds in their fight: for he has forsaken the ways of his own vineyard, and he has caused the axles of his own husbandry to go astray; and he goes through a dry desert, and a [land] appointed to drought, and he gathers barrenness with his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A foolish and bold woman, who knows not modesty, comes to lack a morsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} She sits at the doors of her house, on a seat openly in the streets, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} calling to passers by, and to those that are going right on their ways; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [saying], Whoso is most senseless of you, let him turn aside to me; and I exhort those that lack prudence, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Take and enjoy secret bread, and the sweet water of theft. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But he knows that mighty men die by her, and he falls in with a snare of hell. But hasten away, delay not in the place, neither fix your eye upon her: for thus shall you go through strange water; but do you abstain from strange water, and drink not of a strange fountain, that you may live long, and years of life may be added to you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Wisdom The infinite and eternal Wisdom of God, which has so framed the universe as to exhibit a scene of grandeur and stability, and made ample provision for the innumerable beings by which it is inhabited. builded; pillars \textsuperscript{2} killed; beasts Heb. killing, mingled \textsuperscript{17} Stolen; eaten in secret Heb. of secrecies\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 10}
\markright{PROVERBS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A wise son makes [his] father glad: but a foolish son is a grief to his mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Treasures shall not profit the lawless: but righteousness shall deliver from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord will not famish a righteous soul: but he will overthrow the life of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Poverty brings a man low: but the hands of the vigorous make rich. A son who is instructed shall be wise, and shall use the fool for a servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A wise son is saved from heat: but a lawless son is blighted of the winds in harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but untimely grief shall cover the mouth of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The memory of the just is praised; but the name of the ungodly [man] is extinguished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A wise man in heart will receive commandments; but he that is unguarded in his lips shall be overthrown in his perverseness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that walks simply, walks confidently; but he that perverts his ways shall be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He that winks with his eyes deceitfully, procures griefs for men; but he that reproves boldly is a peacemaker. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [There is] a fountain of life in the hand of a righteous man; but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Hatred stirs up strife; but affection covers all that do not love strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He that brings forth wisdom from his lips smites the fool with a rod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The wise will hide discretion; but the mouth of the hasty draws near to ruin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The wealth of rich men is a strong city; but poverty is the ruin of the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The works of the righteous produce life; but the fruits of the ungodly [produce] sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Instruction keeps the right ways of life; but instruction unchastened goes astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Righteous lips cover enmity; but they that utter railings are most foolish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} By a multitude of words you shall not escape sin; but if you refrain your lips you will be prudent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The tongue of the just is tried silver; but the heart of the ungodly shall fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The lips of the righteous know sublime [truths]: but the foolish die in lack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; it enriches [him], and grief of heart shall not be added to [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A fool does mischief in sport; but wisdom brings forth prudence for a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The ungodly is engulfed in destruction; but the desire of the righteous is acceptable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} When the storm passes by, the ungodly vanishes away; but the righteous turns aside and escapes for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} As a sour grape is hurtful to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so iniquity hurts those that practise it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The fear of the Lord adds [length] of days: but the years of the ungodly shall be shortened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Joy rests long with the righteous: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} The fear of the Lord is a strong hold of the saints: but ruin [comes] to them that work wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The righteous shall never fail: but the ungodly shall not dwell in the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom: but the tongue of the unjust shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} The lips of just men drop grace: but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} will;, ; but, ; the substance of the wicked or, the wicked for their wickedness \textsuperscript{4} becometh, ; with a slack hand That is, slothfully and negligently. but \textsuperscript{8} wise, ; but, prating fool Heb. a fool of lips, fall or, be beaten \textsuperscript{10} that; but, fall or, be beaten \textsuperscript{13} the lips, ; a rod, ; understanding Heb. heart, *marg. \textsuperscript{17} the way, ; he that, ; erreth or, causeth to err \textsuperscript{21} feed; fools, ; wisdom Heb. heart \textsuperscript{26} vinegar, as smoke As the acidity of vinegar causes the unpleasantness and pain to the teeth, and by softening and dissolving the alkali of the bone, impairs their texture, and renders them incapable of mastication; and as smoke, by irritating the tender vessels, causes the eyes to smart, and prevents distinct vision; so a sluggish messenger is a continual vexation and loss to those by whom he is employed. so \textsuperscript{27} fear, ;, prolongeth Heb. addeth the years \textsuperscript{32} know; but, frowardness Heb. Frowardnesses\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 11}
\markright{PROVERBS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} False balances are an abomination before the Lord: but a just weight is acceptable to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Wherever pride enters, there will be also disgrace: but the mouth of the lowly meditates wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} When a just man dies he leaves regret: but the destruction of the ungodly is speedy, and causes joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [Possessions will not profit in a day of wrath, but righteousness will deliver from death. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Righteousness traces out blameless paths: but ungodliness encounters unjust dealing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The righteousness of upright men delivers them: but transgressors are caught in their own destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} At the death of a just man his hope does not perish: but the boast of the ungodly perishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A righteous man escapes from a snare, and the ungodly man is delivered up in his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In the mouth of ungodly men is a snare to citizens: but the understanding of righteous men is prosperous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the prosperity of righteous men a city prospers: but by the mouth of ungodly men it is overthrown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [At the blessing of the upright a city shall be exalted. ] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A man void of understanding sneers at [his fellow] citizens: but a sensible man is quiet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A double-tongued man discloses the [secret] counsels of an assembly: but he that is faithful in spirit conceals matters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} They that have no guidance fall like leaves: but in much counsel there is safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} A bad man does harm wherever he meets a just man: and he hates the sound of safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A gracious wife brings glory to her husband: but a woman hating righteousness is a theme of dishonor. The slothful come to lack: but the diligent support themselves with wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A merciful man does good to his own soul: but the merciless destroys his own body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} An ungodly man performs unrighteous works: but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A righteous son is born for life: but the persecution of the ungodly [ends] in death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord: but all they that are blameless in their ways are acceptable to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He that unjustly strikes hands shall not be unpunished: but he that sows righteousness he shall receive a faithful reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} As an ornament in a swine's snout, so is beauty to an ill-minded woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All the desire of the righteous is good: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} There are [some] who scatter their own, and make it more: and there are [some] also who gather, [yet] have less. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Every sincere soul is blessed: but a passionate man is not graceful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} May he that hoards corn leave it to the nation: but blessing be on the head of him that gives [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He that devises good [counsels] seeks good favor: but [as for] him that seeks after evil, [evil] shall overtake him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He that trusts in wealth shall fall; but he that helps righteous men shall rise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} He that deals not graciously with his own house shall inherit the wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Out of the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life; but the souls of transgressors are cut off before their time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} A false balance is Heb. \subsection*{Proverbs 12}
\markright{PROVERBS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that loves instruction loves sense, but he that hates reproofs is a fool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He that has found favor with the Lord [is made] better; but a transgressor shall be passed over in silence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A man shall not prosper by wickedness; but the roots of the righteous shall not be taken up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a bad woman destroys her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The thoughts of the righteous [are true] judgments; but ungodly men devise deceits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The words of ungodly men are crafty; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} When the ungodly is overthrown, he vanishes away; but the houses of the just remain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The mouth of an understanding [man] is praised by a man; but he that is dull of heart is had in derision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Better is a man in dishonor serving himself, than one honouring himself and lacking bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A righteous man has pity for the lives of his cattle; but the bowels of the ungodly are unmerciful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He that tills his own land shall be satisfied with bread; but they that pursue vanities are void of understanding. He that enjoys himself in banquets of wine, shall leave dishonor in his own strong holds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The desires of the ungodly are evil; but the roots of the godly are firmly set. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the sin of [his] lips a sinner falls into snare; but a righteous man escapes from them. He whose looks are gentle shall be pitied, but he that contends in the gates will afflict souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The soul of a man shall be filled with good from the fruits of his mouth; and the recompence of his lips shall be given to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The ways of fools are right in their own eyes; but a wise man hearkens to counsels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A fool declares his wrath the same day; but a prudent man hides his own disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A righteous man declares the open truth; but an unjust witness is deceitful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Some wound as they speak, [like] swords; but the tongues of the wise heal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} True lips establish testimony; but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [There is] deceit in the heart of him that imagines evil; but they that love peace shall rejoice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} No injustice will please a just man; but the ungodly will be filled with mischief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Lying lips are a abomination to the Lord; but he that deals faithfully is accepted with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} An understanding man is a throne of wisdom; but the heart of fools shall meet with curses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The hand of chosen men shall easily obtain rule; but the deceitful shall be for a prey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A terrible word troubles the heart of a righteous man; but a good message rejoices him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} A just arbitrator shall be his own friend; but mischief shall pursue sinners; and the way of ungodly men shall lead them astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A deceitful man shall catch no game; but a blameless man is a precious possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} In the ways of righteousness is life; but the ways of those that remember injuries [lead] to death.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} shall not be established;, the root \textsuperscript{8} commended; he, ; of a perverse heart Heb. perverse of heart \textsuperscript{9} He that is etc. Or, rather, as in the old translation "He that is despised, and is his own servant, is better than he that boasteth himself and wanteth bread; " with which the versions generally agree. That is, it is better to be in lowness and obscurity, and to support oneself by manual labour, than to want the necessaries of life, through a foolish vanity, or the pride of birth, which refuses to labour. despised \textsuperscript{10} righteous; but; tender mercies or, bowels \textsuperscript{12} desireth; net or, fortress, the root \textsuperscript{13} wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips Heb. snare of the wicked is in the transgression of lips, ; but \textsuperscript{16} fool's; presently Heb. in that day but \textsuperscript{24} hand, ; but, slothful or, deceitful \textsuperscript{26} righteous; excellent or, abundant but\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 13}
\markright{PROVERBS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A wise son is obedient to his father: but a disobedient son will be destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A good [man] shall eat of the fruits of righteousness: but the lives of transgressors shall perish before their time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He that keeps his own mouth keeps his own life: but he that is hasty with his lips shall bring terror upon himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Every slothful man desires, but the hands of the active are diligent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A righteous man hates an unjust word: but an ungodly man is ashamed, and will have no confidence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} There are [some] who, having nothing, enrich themselves: and there are [some] who bring themselves down in [the midst of] much wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A man's own wealth is the ransom of his life: but the poor endures not threatening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The righteous always have light: but the light of the ungodly is quenched. Crafty souls go astray in sins: but just men pity, and are merciful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A bad man does evil with insolence: but they that are judges of themselves are wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Wealth gotten hastily with iniquity is diminished: but he that gathers for himself with godliness shall be increased. The righteous is merciful, and lends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Better is he that begins to help heartily, than he that promises and leads [another] to hope: for a good desire is a tree of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He that slights a matter shall be slighted of it: but he that fears the commandment has health [of soul]. To a crafty son there shall be nothing good: but a wise servant shall have prosperous doings, and his way shall be directed aright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The law of the wise is fountain of life: but the man void of understanding shall die by a snare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Sound discretion gives favor, and to know the law is the part of a sound understanding: but the ways of scorners tend to destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Every prudent man acts with knowledge: but the fool displays his own mischief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A rash king shall fall into mischief: but a wise messenger shall deliver him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Instruction removes poverty and disgrace: but he that attends to reproofs shall be honored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The desires of the godly gladden the soul, but the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} If you walk with wise men you shall be wise: but he that walks with fools shall be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Evil shall pursue sinners; but good shall overtake the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A good man shall inherit children's children; and the wealth of ungodly men is laid up for the just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The righteous shall spend many years in wealth: but the unrighteous shall perish suddenly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that spares the rod hates his son: but he that loves, carefully chastens [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A just [man] eats and satisfies his soul: but the souls of the ungodly are in lack.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{7} is that maketh himself rich; that maketh himself poor \textsuperscript{11} Wealth, ;, ; he, ; by labour Heb. with the hand \textsuperscript{13} despiseth; he; rewarded Heb. in peace \textsuperscript{16} prudent, ; a fool, ; layeth Heb. spreadeth \textsuperscript{17} wicked; but; a faithful ambassador Heb. an ambassador of faithfulness \textsuperscript{19} The desire; it is depart \textsuperscript{20} that; but, ; destroyed Heb. broken\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 14}
\markright{PROVERBS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wise women build houses: but a foolish one digs [hers] down with her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He that walks uprightly fears the Lord; but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Out of the mouth of fools [comes] a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Where no oxen are, the cribs are clean; but where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is apparent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A faithful witness does not lie; but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You shall seek wisdom with bad men, and shall not find it; but discretion is easily available with the prudent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All things are adverse to a foolish man; but wise lips are the weapons of discretion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The wisdom of the prudent will understand their ways; but the folly of fools leads astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The houses of transgressors will need purification; but the houses of the just are acceptable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [If] a man's mind is intelligent, his soul is sorrowful; and when he rejoices, he has no fellowship with pride. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The houses of ungodly men shall be utterly destroyed; but the tabernacles of them that walk uprightly shall stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depths of hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Grief mingles not with mirth; and joy in the end comes to grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A stout-hearted [man] shall be filled with his own ways; and a good man with his own thoughts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The simple believes every word: but the prudent man betakes himself to afterthought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A wise man fears, and departs from evil; but the fool trusts in himself, and joins himself with the transgressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A passionate man acts inconsiderately; but a sensible man bears up under many things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Fools shall have mischief for their portion; but the prudent shall take fast hold of understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Evil men shall fall before the good; and the ungodly shall attend at the gates of the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He that dishonors the needy sins: but he that has pity on the poor is most blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} They that go astray devise evils: but the good devise mercy and truth. The framers of evil do not understand mercy and truth: but compassion and faithfulness are with the framers of good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} With every one [who is] careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in lack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A prudent man is the crown of the wise: but the occupation of fools is evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evil: but a deceitful [man] kindles falsehoods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and he leaves his children a support. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causes [men] to turn aside from the snare of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} In a populous nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of people is the ruin of a prince. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A meek-spirited man is a healer of the heart: but a sensitive heart is a corruption of the bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} He that oppresses the needy provokes his Maker: but he that honors him has pity upon the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} The ungodly shall be driven away in his wickedness: but he who is secure in his own holiness is just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} There is wisdom in the good heart of a man: but in the heart of fools it is not discerned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Righteousness exalts a nation: but sins diminish tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} An understanding servant is acceptable to a king; and by his good behavior he removes disgrace.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{24} Gk. vocab: mōria (μωρία) = foolishness. Common English renderings: foolishness. Used for folly or foolishness.\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 15}
\markright{PROVERBS 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Anger slays even wise men; yet a submissive answer turns away wrath: but a grievous word stirs up anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The tongue of the wise knows what is good: but the mouth of the foolish tells out evil things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good in every place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The wholesome tongue is a tree of life, and he that keeps it shall be filled with understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A fool scorns his father's instruction; but he that keeps his commandments is more prudent. In abounding righteousness is great strength: but the ungodly shall utterly perish from the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In the houses of the righteous is much strength: but the fruits of the ungodly shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The lips of the wise are bound by discretion: but the hearts of the foolish are not safe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord; but the prayers of them that walk honestly are acceptable with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The ways of an ungodly [man] are an abomination to the Lord; but he loves those that follow after righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The instruction of the simple is known by them that pass by; but they that hate reproofs die disgracefully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Hell and destruction are manifest to the Lord; how shall not also be the hearts of men? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} An uninstructed person will not love those that reprove him; neither will he associate with the wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When the heart rejoices the countenance is cheerful; but when it is in sorrow, [the countenance] is sad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} An upright heart seeks discretion; but the mouth of the uninstructed will experience evils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The eyes of the wicked are always looking for evil things; but the good are always quiet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without the fear [of the Lord]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Better is an entertainment of herbs with friendliness and kindness, than a feast of calves, with enmity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A passionate man stirs up strife; but [he that is] slow to anger appeases even a rising one. A man slow to anger will extinguish quarrels; but an ungodly man rather stirs [them] up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The ways of sluggards are strewn with thorns; but those of the diligent are made smooth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A wise son gladdens [his] father; but a foolish son sneers at his mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The ways of a foolish man are void of sense; but a wise man proceeds on his way aright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} They that honor not councils put off deliberation; but counsel abides in the hearts of counselors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A bad man will by no means attend to counsel; neither will he say anything seasonable, or good for the common [weal]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The thoughts of the wise are ways of life, that he may turn aside and escape from hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The Lord pulls down the houses of scorners; but he establishes the border of the widow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} An unrighteous thought is abomination to the Lord; but the sayings of the pure are held in honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A receiver of bribes destroys himself; but he that hates the receiving of bribes is safe. [By alms and by faithful dealings] [sins are purged away;] but by the fear of the Lord every one departs from evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The hearts of the righteous meditate faithfulness; but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things. The ways of righteous men are acceptable with the Lord; and through them even enemies become friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} God is far from the ungodly; but he hearkens to the prayers of the righteous. Better are small receipts with righteousness, than abundant fruits with unrighteousness. Let the heart of a man think justly, that his steps may be rightly ordered of God. The eye that sees rightly rejoices the heart; and a good report fattens the bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} He that rejects instruction hates himself; but he that mind reproofs loves his soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom; and the highest honor will correspond therewith.\par

The healing of the, ; a tree; a breach \textsuperscript{6} the house, ; in the revenues \textsuperscript{10} Correction or, Instruction grievous, ; and he \textsuperscript{19} way of the slothful, ; the way of the righteous;, ; made plain Heb. raised up as a causey \textsuperscript{21} joy, destitute of wisdom Heb. void of heart, *marg. a man \textsuperscript{23} joy, ; in due season Heb. in his season; how \textsuperscript{26} thoughts; but; pleasant words Heb. words of pleasantness \textsuperscript{32} refuseth, ; instruction or, correction; heareth or, obeyeth; getteth understanding Heb. possesseth an heart, *marg.\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 16}
\markright{PROVERBS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} All the works of the humble [man] are manifest with God; but the ungodly shall perish in an evil day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Every one that is proud in heart is unclean before God, and he that unjustly strikes hands with hand shall not be held guiltless. The beginning of a good way is to do justly; and it is more acceptable with God than to offer sacrifices. He that seeks the Lord shall find knowledge with righteousness: and they that rightly seek him shall find peace. All of the works of the Lord [are done] with righteousness; and the ungodly [man] is kept for the evil day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [There is] an oracle upon the lips of a king; and his mouth shall not err in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The poise of the balance is righteousness with the Lord; and his works are righteous measures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} An evil-doer is an abomination to a king; for the throne of rule is established by righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Righteous lips are acceptable to a king; and he loves right words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The anger of a king is a messenger of death; but a wise man will pacify him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The son of a king is in the light of life; and they that are in favor with him are as a cloud of latter rain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The brood of wisdom is more to be chosen than gold, and the brood of prudence more to be chosen than silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The paths of life turn aside from evil; and the ways of righteousness are length of life. He that receives instruction shall be in prosperity; and he that regards reproofs shall be made wise. He that keeps his ways, preserves his own soul; and he that loves his life will spare his mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Pride goes before destruction, and folly before a fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Better is a meek-spirited [man] with lowliness, than one who divides spoils with the proud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [He who is] skillful in business finds good: but he that trusts in God is most blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [Men] call the wise and understanding evil: but they that are pleasing in speech shall hear more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessors; but the instruction of fools is evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The heart of the wise will discern the [things which proceed] from his own mouth; and on his lips he will wear knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Good words are honeycombs, and the sweetness thereof is a healing of the soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} There are ways that seem to be right to a man, but the end of them looks to the depth of hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} A man who labors, labors for himself, and drives from [him] his own ruin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But the perverse bears destruction upon his own mouth: a foolish man digs up evil for himself, and treasures fire on his own lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} A perverse man spreads mischief, and will kindle a torch of deceit with mischiefs; and he separates friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} A transgressor tries [to ensnare] friends, and leads them in ways [that are] not good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the man that fixes his eyes devises perverse things, and marks out with his lips all evil: he is a furnace of wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Old age is a crown of honor, but it is found in the ways of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} A man slow to anger is better than a strong [man]; and he that governs [his] temper better than he that takes a city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} All [evils] come upon the ungodly into [their] bosoms; but all righteous things [come] of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} that; though unpunished Heb. held innocent \textsuperscript{10} A divine sentence Heb. Divination; transgresseth \textsuperscript{23} heart; teacheth Heb. maketh wise \textsuperscript{26} He Heb. The soul of him laboureth; craveth it of him Heb. boweth unto him \textsuperscript{27} An ungodly man Heb. a man of Belial; diggeth; in \textsuperscript{28} froward, ; soweth Heb. sendeth forth a whisperer\par}
