\subsection*{Proverbs 17}
\markright{PROVERBS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace, than a house [full] of many good things and unjust sacrifices, with strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A wise servant shall have rule over foolish masters, and shall divide portions among brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} As silver and gold are tried in a furnace, so are choice hearts with the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A bad man hearkens to the tongue of transgressors: but a righteous man attends not to false lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He that laughs at the poor provokes him that made him; and he that rejoices at the destruction of another shall not be held guiltless: but he that has compassion shall find mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Children's children are the crown of old men; and their fathers are the glory of children. The faithful has the whole world full of wealth; but the faithless not even a farthing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Faithful lips will not suit a fool; nor lying lips a just man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Instruction is to them that use it a gracious reward; and wherever it may turn, it shall prosper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that conceals injuries seeks love; but he that hates to hide [them] separates friends and kindred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A threat breaks down the heart of a wise man; but a fool, though scourged, understands not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Every bad man stirs up strifes: but the Lord will send out against him an unmerciful messenger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Care may befall a man of understanding; but fools will meditate evils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not be removed from his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Rightful rule gives power to words; but sedition and strife precede poverty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He that pronounces the unjust just, and the just unjust, is unclean and abominable with God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Why has the fool wealth? for a senseless man will not be able to purchase wisdom. He that exalts his own house seeks ruin; and he that turns aside from instruction shall fall into mischief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Have you a friend for every time, and let brethren be useful in distress; for on this account are they born. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A foolish man applauds and rejoices over himself, [as he] also that becomes surety would make himself responsible for his own friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A lover of sin rejoices in strifes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the hard-hearted man comes not in for good. A man of a changeful tongue will fall into mischiefs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and the heart of a fool is grief to its possessor. A father rejoices not over an uninstructed son; but a wise son gladdens his mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A glad heart promotes health; but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The ways of a man who unjustly receives gifts in [his] bosom do not prosper; and an ungodly man perverts the ways of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The countenance of a wise man is sensible; but the eyes of a fool [go] to the ends of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A foolish son [is a cause of] anger to his father, and grief to her that bore him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [It is] not right to punish a righteous man, nor [is it] holy to plot against righteous princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He that forbears to utter a hard word is discreet, and a patient man is wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Wisdom shall be imputed to a fool who asks after wisdom: and he who holds his peace shall seem to be sensible.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} a dry; an house sacrifices or, good cheer with \textsuperscript{5} mocketh; and; unpunished Heb. held innocent, *marg. \textsuperscript{7} Excellent speech Heb. A lip of excellency; much; lying lips Heb. a lip of lying \textsuperscript{8} gift;, ; precious stone Heb. stone of grace whithersoever \textsuperscript{9} that covereth; seeketh or, procureth but \textsuperscript{10} or, A reproof aweth more a wise man, than to strike a fool an hundred times. \textsuperscript{20} He that hath a froward heart Heb. The froward of heart, ; and he \textsuperscript{22} merry, ; like a medicine Heb. to a medicine a broken \textsuperscript{27} spareth; an excellent spirit or, a cool spirit\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 18}
\markright{PROVERBS 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A man who wishes to separate from friends seeks excuses; but at all times he will be liable to reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A senseless man feels no need of wisdom, for he is rather led by folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} When an ungodly man comes into a depth of evils, he despises [them]; but dishonor and reproach come upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A word in the heart of a man is a deep water, and a river and fountain of life spring forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [It is] not good to accept the person of the ungodly, nor [is it] holy to pervert justice in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The lips of a fool bring [him] into troubles, and his bold mouth calls for death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} A fool's mouth is ruin to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Fear casts down the slothful; and the souls of the effeminate shall hunger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A man who helps not himself by his labor is brother of him that ruins himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The name of the Lord is of great strength; and the righteous running to it are exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The wealth of a rich man is a strong city; and its glory casts a broad shadow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Before ruin a man's heart is exalted, and before honor it is humble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whoso answers a word before he hears [a cause], it is folly and reproach to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A wise servant calms a man's anger; but who can endure a faint-hearted man? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The heart of the sensible [man] purchases discretion; and the ears of the wise seek understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A man's gift enlarges him, and seats him among princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A righteous man accuses himself at the beginning of his speech, but when he has entered upon the attack, the adversary is reproved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A silent [man] quells strifes, and determines between great powers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A brother helped by a brother is as a strong and high city; and is [as] strong as a [well]-founded palace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A man fills his belly with the fruits of his mouth; and he shall be satisfied with the fruits of his lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Life and death are in the power of the tongue; and they that rule it shall eat the fruits thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He that has found a good wife has found favours, and has received gladness from God. [He that puts away a good wife, puts away a] [good thing, and he that keeps an adulteress is foolish and ungodly.]\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Through etc. or, He that separateth himself seeketh, according to his desire and intermeddleth in every business.; seeketh; intermeddleth \textsuperscript{8} words, ; talebearer or, whisperer as wounds or, like as when men are wounded innermost parts Heb. chambers \textsuperscript{9} that is slothful, ; is brother \textsuperscript{10} name; a strong;, ; the righteous; safe Heb. set aloft \textsuperscript{13} that; answereth a matter Heb. returneth a word\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 19}
\markright{PROVERBS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The folly of a man spoils his ways: and he blames God in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Wealth acquires many friends; but the poor is deserted even of the friend he has. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that accuses unjustly shall not escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Many court the favor of kings; but every bad man becomes a reproach to [another] man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Every one who hates [his] poor brother shall also be far from friendship. Good understanding will draw near to them that know it, and a sensible man will find it. He that does much harm perfects mischief; and he that used provoking words shall not escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that procures wisdom loves himself; and he that keeps wisdom shall find good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A false witness shall not be unpunished; and whoever shall kindle mischief shall perish by it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Delight does not suit a fool, nor [is it seemly] if a servant should begin to rule with haughtiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A merciful man is longsuffering; and his triumph overtakes transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The threatening of a king is like the roaring of a lion; but as dew on the grass, so is his favor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A foolish son is a disgrace to his father: vows [paid out] of the hire of a harlot are not pure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Fathers divide house and substance to [their] children: but a wife is suited to a man by the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Cowardice possesses the effeminate [man]; and the soul of the sluggard shall hunger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} He that keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; but he that despises his ways shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He that has pity on the poor lends to the Lord; and he will recompense to him according to his gift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Chasten your son, for so he shall be hopeful; and be not exalted in your soul to haughtiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A malicious man shall be severely punished, and if he commit injury, he shall also lose his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Hear, son, the instruction of your father, that you may be wise at your latter end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [There are] many thoughts in a man's heart; but the counsel of the Lord abides for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Mercy is a fruit to a man: and a poor man is better than a rich liar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The fear of the Lord is life to a man: and he shall lodge without fear in places where knowledge is not seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that unjustly hides his hands in his bosom, will not even [bring] them up to his mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} When a pestilent character is scourged, a simple man is made wiser: and if you reprove a wise man, he will understand discretion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He that dishonors his father, and drives away his mother, shall be disgraced and shall be exposed to reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A son who ceases to attend to the instruction of a father will cherish evil designs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He that becomes surety for a foolish child will despise the ordinance: and the mouth of ungodly men shall drink down judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Scourges are preparing for the intemperate, and punishments likewise for fools.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 20}
\markright{PROVERBS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wine is an intemperate thing, and strong drink full of violence: but every fool is entangled with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The threat of a king differs not from the rage of a lion; and he that provokes him sins against his own soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [It is] a glory to a man to turn aside from railing; but every fool is entangled with such matters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A sluggard when reproached is not ashamed: so also he who borrows corn in harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; but a prudent man will draw it out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A man is valuable, and a merciful man precious: but [it is] hard to find a faithful man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He that walks blameless in justice, shall leave his children blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Whenever a righteous king sits on the throne, no evil thing can stand before his presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who will boast that he has a pure heart? or who will boldly say that he is pure from sins? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A large and small weight, and various measures, are even both of them unclean before the Lord; and [so is] he that makes them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A youth [when in company] with a godly man, will be restrained in his devices, and [then] his way will be straight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The ear hears, and the eye sees: even both of them are the Lord's work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Love not to speak ill, lest you be cut off: open your eyes, and be filled with bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The lamp of him that reviles father or mother shall be put out, and his eyeballs shall see darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} A portion hastily gotten at first shall not be blessed in the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Say not, I will avenge myself on my enemy; but wait on the Lord, that he may help you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A double weight is an abomination to the Lord; and a deceitful balance is not good in his sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A man's goings are directed of the Lord: how then can a mortal understand his ways? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} It is a snare to a man hastily to consecrate some of his own property: for [in that case] repentance comes after vowing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} A wise king utterly crushes the ungodly, and will bring a wheel upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The spirit of man is a light of the Lord, who searches the inmost parts of the belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Mercy and truth are a guard to a king, and will surround his throne with righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Wisdom is an ornament to young men; and grey [hairs] are the glory of old men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Bruises and contusions befall bad men; and plagues [shall come] in the inward parts of [their] belly.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} sluggard, cold or, winter therefore \textsuperscript{6} proclaim;, ; goodness or, bounty but \textsuperscript{10} Divers weights, and divers measures Heb. a stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah, both, ; abomination \textsuperscript{20} curseth; his; lamp or, candle \textsuperscript{23} weights; a false balance Heb. balances of deceit \textsuperscript{27} spirit; candle or, lamp, searching \textsuperscript{30} cleanseth away evil Heb. is a purging medicine against evil stripes\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 21}
\markright{PROVERBS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} As a rush of water, so is the king's heart in God's hand: he turns it wherever he may desire to point out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Every man seems to himself righteous; but the Lord directs the hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} To do justly and to speak truth, are more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A high-minded man is stout-hearted in [his] pride; and the lamp of the wicked is sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He that gathers treasures with a lying tongue pursues vanity [on] to the snares of death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Destruction shall lodge with the ungodly; for they refuse to do justly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} To the froward God sends froward ways; for his works are pure and right. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} [It is] better to dwell in a corner on the house-top, than in plastered [rooms] with unrighteousness, and in an open house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The soul of the ungodly shall not be pitied by any man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When an intemperate man is punished the simple becomes wiser: and a wise man understanding will receive knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly: and despises the ungodly for their wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He that stops his ears from hearing the poor, himself also shall cry, and there shall be none to hear [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A secret gift calms anger: but he that forbears to give stirs up strong wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [It is] the joy of the righteous to do judgment: but a holy [man] is abominable with evil-doers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A man that wanders out of the way of righteousness, shall rest in the congregation of giants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A poor man loves mirth, loving wine and oil in abundance; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and a transgressor is the abomination of a righteous man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [It is] better to dwell in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and talkative and passionate woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A desirable treasure will rest on the mouth of the wise; but foolish men will swallow it up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A wise man assaults strong cities, and demolishes the fortress in which the ungodly trusted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He that keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from trouble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A bold and self-willed and insolent [man] is called a pest: and he that remembers injuries is a transgressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Desires kill the sluggard; for his hands do not choose to do anything. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} An ungodly man entertains evil desires all the day: but the righteous is unsparingly merciful and compassionate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The sacrifices of the ungodly are abomination to the Lord, for they offer them wickedly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} A false witness shall perish; but an obedient man will speak cautiously. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} An ungodly man impudently withstands with his face; but the upright man himself understands his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel against the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} A horse is prepared for the day of battle; but help is of the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{4} An high look Heb. Haughtiness of eyes, ; and the; plowing of the wicked or, light of the wicked \textsuperscript{7} robbery, ; destroy them Heb. saw them, or, dwell with them, because \textsuperscript{9} better, brawling woman in a wide house Heb. woman of contentions in a house of society \textsuperscript{10} soul; findeth no favour Heb. is not favoured \textsuperscript{11} the scorner; when the wise \textsuperscript{19} better; wilderness Heb. land of the desert \textsuperscript{24} haughty, ; proud wrath Heb. the wrath of pride \textsuperscript{27} sacrifice; with a wicked mind Heb. in wickedness \textsuperscript{28} false witness Heb. witness of lies, ; the man \textsuperscript{29} hardeneth;, he directeth or, he considereth \textsuperscript{31} horse, ; but, safety or, victory, *marg.\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 22}
\markright{PROVERBS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A fair name is better than much wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The rich and the poor meet together; but the Lord made them both. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} An intelligent man seeing a bad man severely punished is himself instructed, but fools pass by and are punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The fear of the Lord is the offspring of wisdom, and wealth, and glory, and life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thistles and snares are in perverse ways; but he that keeps his soul will refrain from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The rich will rule over the poor, and servants will lend to their own masters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that sows wickedness shall reap troubles; and shall fully receive the punishment of his deeds. God loves a cheerful and liberal man; but [a man] shall fully prove the folly of his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that has pity on the poor shall himself be maintained; for he has given of his own bread to the poor. He that gives liberally secures victory an honor; but he takes away the life of them that posses [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Cast out a pestilent person from the council, and strife shall go out with him; for when he sits in the council he dishonors all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The Lord loves holy hearts, and all blameless persons are acceptable with him: a king rules with his lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But the eyes of the Lord preserve discretion; but the transgressor despises [wise] words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The sluggard makes excuses, and says, [There is] a lion in the ways, and murderers in the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The mouth of a transgressor is a deep pit; and he that is hated of the Lord shall fall into it. Evil ways are before a man, and he does not like to turn away from them; but it is needful to turn aside from a perverse and bad way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Folly is attached to the heart of a child, but the rod and instruction are [then] far from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} He that oppresses the poor, increases his own substance, yet gives to the rich so as to make it less. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Incline your ear to the words of wise men: hear also my word, and apply your heart, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} that you may know that they are good: and if you lay them to heart, they shall also gladden you on your lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} That your hope may be in the Lord, and he may make your way known to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And do you too repeatedly record them for yourself on the table of your heart, for counsel and knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I therefore teach you truth, and knowledge good to hear; that you may answer words of truth to them that question you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Do no violence to the poor, for he is needy: neither dishonor the helpless [man] in the gates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the Lord will plead his cause, and you shall deliver your soul in safety. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Be not companion to a furious man; neither lodge with a passionate man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} lest you learn of his ways, and get snares to your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Become not surety from respect of a man's person. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For if those have not whence to give compensation, they will take the bed [that is] under you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Remove not the old landmarks, which your fathers placed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} It is fit that an observant man and [one] diligent in his business should attend on kings, and not attend on slothful men.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} name; loving favour rather than or, favour is better than, etc. \textsuperscript{4} By etc. Heb. The reward of humility, etc. \textsuperscript{7} rich, ;, ;, the borrower; lender Heb. man that lendeth \textsuperscript{8} that; the rod of his anger shall fail or, with the rod of his anger he shall be consumed \textsuperscript{9} He that hath a bountiful eye Heb. Good of eye \textsuperscript{11} that; for the grace of his lips or, and hath grace in his lips; the king \textsuperscript{12} eyes; he; words or, matters \textsuperscript{13} The slothful That is, the slothful man uses any pretext, however improbable, to indulge his love of ease and indolence. \textsuperscript{14} mouth, ; a deep pit That is, it is like a deep pit, or pitfall, in which animals are often taken alive. abhorred \textsuperscript{16} that oppresseth, ; he that giveth \textsuperscript{18} it is, ;, ; within thee Heb. within thy belly; fitted \textsuperscript{19} thy; even to thee or, trust thou also \textsuperscript{21} I; answer them that send unto thee or, those that send thee \textsuperscript{22} Rob; oppress; in the gate That is, in the court of justice, which, as we have already seen, was held at the gates of cities in the East. \textsuperscript{29} a man; he shall stand That is, he shall have the honour of serving kings; as the phrase denotes. mean men Heb. obscure men\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 23}
\markright{PROVERBS 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} If you sit to sup at the table of a prince, consider attentively the things set before you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and apply your hand, knowing that it behoves you to prepare such [meats]: but if you are very insatiable, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} desire not his provisions; for these belong to a false life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If you are poor, measure not yourself with a rich man; but refrain yourself in your wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If you should fix your eye upon him, he will disappear; for wings like an eagle's are prepared for him, and he returns to the house of his master. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Sup not with an envious man, neither desire you his meats: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} so he eats and drinks as if any one should swallow a hair, and do not bring him in to yourself, nor eat your morsel with him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} for he will vomit it up, and spoil your fair words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Say nothing in the ears of a fool, lest at any time he sneer at your wise words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Remove not the ancient landmarks; and enter not upon the possession of the fatherless: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} for the Lord is their redeemer; he is mighty, and will plead their cause with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Apply your heart to instruction, and prepare your ears for words of discretion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Refrain not from chastening a child; for if you beat him with the rod, he shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For you shall beat him with the rod, and shall deliver his soul from death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Son, if your heart be wise, you shall also gladden my heart; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and your lips shall converse with my lips, if they be right. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let not your heart envy sinners: but be you in the fear of the Lord all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For if you should keep these things, you shall have posterity; and your hope shall not be removed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Hear, [my] son, and be wise, and rightly direct the thoughts of your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Be not a wine-bibber, neither continue long at feasts, and purchases of flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} for every drunkard and whoremonger shall be poor; and every sluggard shall clothe himself with tatters and ragged garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Listen, [my] son, to your father which begot you, and despise not [your mother] because she is grown old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A righteous father brings up [his children] well; and his soul rejoices over a wise son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Let your father and your mother rejoice over you, and let her that bore you be glad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [My] son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For a strange house is a vessel full of holes; and a strange well is narrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For such a one shall perish suddenly; and every transgressor shall be cut off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Who [has] woe? who trouble? who [has] quarrels? and who vexations and disputes? who [has] bruises without a cause? whose eyes are livid? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Are not those of them that stay long at wine? [are] not [those] of them that haunt [the places] where banquets are? Be not drunk with wine; but converse with just men, and converse [with them] openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For if you should set your eyes on bowls and cups, you shall afterwards go more naked than a pestle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But at last [such a one] stretches himself out as one struck by a serpent, and venom is diffused through him as by a horned serpent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Whenever your eyes shall behold a strange woman, then your mouth shall speak perverse things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And you shall lie as in the midst of the sea, and as a pilot in a great storm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And you shall say, They struck me, and I was not pained; and they mocked me, and I knew it not: when will it be morning, that I may go and seek those with whom I may go in company?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} thou; set thine eyes upon Heb. cause thine eyes to fly upon, etc. "He expresses it in such a way, " says Abp. Tillotson, "as if a rich man sat brooding over an estate till it was fledged, and gotten itself wings to fly away." that which; riches \textsuperscript{10} Remove; landmark or, bound fatherless \textsuperscript{15} My son, ; if, ; even mine or, even I will rejoice \textsuperscript{18} surely; end or, reward; thine \textsuperscript{19} and guide, in the way That is "in the right way." \textsuperscript{20} not, ; flesh Heb. their flesh \textsuperscript{28} as for a prey or, as a robber, ; increaseth \textsuperscript{30} tarry; mixed That is, not wine diluted and lowered with water, but made stronger and more inebriating, by the addition of more powerful ingredients, as honey, spices, myrrh, defrutum, opiates, etc. \textsuperscript{32} At; biteth; an adder or, a cockatrice \textsuperscript{35} stricken; I felt it not Heb. I knew it not, I will\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 24}
\markright{PROVERBS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [My] son, envy not bad men, nor desire to be with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For their heart meditates falsehoods, and their lips speak mischiefs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A house is built by wisdom, and is set up by understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} By discretion the chambers are filled with all precious and excellent wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A wise man is better than a strong man; and a man who has prudence than a large estate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} War is carried on with generalship, and aid is supplied to the heart of a counsellor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Wisdom and good understanding are in the gates of the wise: the wise turn not aside from the mouth of the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} but deliberate in council. Death befalls uninstructed [men]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The fools also dies in sins; and uncleanness [attaches] to a pestilent man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He shall be defiled in the evil day, and in the day of affliction, until he be utterly consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Deliver them that are led away to death, and redeem them that are appointed to be slain; spare not [your help]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But if you should say, I know not this man; know that the Lord knows the hearts of all; and he that formed breath for all, he knows all things, who renders to every man according to his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [My] son, eat honey, for the honeycomb is good, that your throat may be sweetened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Thus shall you perceive wisdom in your soul: for if you find it, your end shall be good, and hope shall not fail you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Bring not an ungodly man into the dwelling of the righteous: neither be deceived by the feeding of the belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For a righteous man will fall seven times, and rise [again]: but the ungodly shall be without strength in troubles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} If your enemy should fall, rejoice not over him, neither be elated at his overthrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the Lord will see [it], and it will not please him, and he will turn away his wrath from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Rejoice not in evil-doers, neither be envious of sinners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the evil man shall have no posterity: and the light of the wicked shall be put out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} [My] son, fear God and the king; and do not disobey either of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For they will suddenly punish the ungodly, and who can know the vengeance [inflicted] by both? [A son that keeps the commandment shall escape destruction; for [such an one] has fully received it. Let no falsehood be spoken by the king from the tongue; yes, let no falsehood proceed from his tongue. The king's tongue is a sword, and not one of flesh; and whoever shall be given up to [it] shall be destroyed: for if his wrath should be provoked, he destroys men with cords, and devours men's bones, and burns them up as a flame, so that they are not [even] fit to be eaten by the young eagles. [My] son, reverence my words, and receive them, and repent.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And this thing I say to you that are wise [for you] to learn: It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that says of the ungodly, He is righteous, shall be cursed by peoples, and hateful among the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But they that reprove [him] shall appear more excellent, and blessing shall come upon them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and [men] will kiss lips that answer well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Prepare your works for [your] going forth, and prepare yourself for the field; and come after me, and you shall rebuild your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Be not a false witness against your [fellow] citizen, neither exaggerate with your lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Say not, As he has treated me, so will I treat him, and I will avenge myself on him for that wherein he has injured me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A foolish man is like a farm, and a senseless man is like a vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} If you let him alone, he will altogether remain barren and covered with weeds; and he becomes destitute, and his stone walls are broken down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Afterwards I reflected, I looked that I might receive instruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} [The sluggard says, ]I slumber a little, and I sleep a little, and for a little while I fold my arms across [my] breast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But if you do this, your poverty will come speedily; and your lack like a swift courier.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} A wise, ; strong Heb. in strength increaseth strength Heb. strengtheneth might. \textsuperscript{12} doth not he that; that keepeth; and shall \textsuperscript{13} eat; to thy taste Heb. upon thy palate \textsuperscript{18} displease him Heb. be evil in his eyes and he \textsuperscript{19} Fret or, Keep not company with the wicked.; neither \textsuperscript{21} fear; meddle; given to change Heb. changers \textsuperscript{25} them; , ; a good blessing Heb. a blessing of good \textsuperscript{26} shall, ; giveth a right answer Heb. answereth right words \textsuperscript{32} considered it Heb. set my heart; I looked \textsuperscript{34} thy poverty, armed man Heb. a man of shield\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 25}
\markright{PROVERBS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} These are the miscellaneous instructions of Solomon, which the friends of Ezekias king of Judea copied out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The glory of God conceals a matter: but the glory of a king honors business. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Heaven is high, and earth is deep, and a king's heart is unsearchable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Beat the drossy silver, and it shall be made entirely pure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Slay the ungodly from before the king, and his throne shall prosper in righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Be not boastful in the presence of the king, and remain not in the places of princes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} for [it is] better for you that it should be said, Come up to me, than that [one] should humble you in the presence of the prince; speak of that which your eyes have seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Get not suddenly into a quarrel, lest you repent at last. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Whenever your friend shall reproach you, retreat backward, despise [him] not; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} lest your friend continue to reproach you, so your quarrel and enmity shall not depart, but shall be to you like death. Favour and friendship set [a man] free, which do you keep for yourself, lest you be made liable to reproach; but take heed to your ways peaceably. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [As] a golden apple in a necklace of sardius, so [is it] to speak a [wise] word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} In an ear-ring of gold a precious sardius is also set; [so is] a wise word to an obedient ear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} As a fall of snow in the time of harvest is good against heat, so a faithful messenger [refreshes] those that send him; for he helps the souls of his employers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As winds and clouds and rains are most evident [objects], so is he that boasts of a false gift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In longsuffering is prosperity to kings, and a soft tongue breaks the bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Having found honey, eat [only] what is enough, lest haply you be filled, and vomit it up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Enter sparingly into your friend's house, lest he be satiated with your company, and hate you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} [As] a club, and a dagger, and a pointed arrow, so also is a man who bears false witness against his friend. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The way of the wicked and the foot of the transgressor shall perish in an evil day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As vinegar is bad for a sore, so trouble befalling the body afflicts the heart. As a moth in a garment, and a worm in wood, so the grief of a man hurts the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If your enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} for so doing you shall heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward you [with] good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The north wind raises clouds; so an impudent face provokes the tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [It is] better to dwell on a corner of the roof, than with a railing woman in an open house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} As cold water is agreeable to a thirsting soul, so is a good message from a land far off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} As if one should stop a well, and corrupt a spring of water, so [is it] unseemly for a righteous man to fall before an ungodly man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} [It is] not good to eat much honey; but it is right to honor venerable sayings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} As a city whose walls are broken down, and which is unfortified, so is a man who does anything without counsel.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{15} Gk. vocab: makrothymia (μακροθυμία) = longsuffering; patience. Common English renderings: longsuffering. Literally long-tempered, especially toward persons.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} heaven; is unsearchable Heb. there is no searching \textsuperscript{6} Put not forth thyself Heb. Set not out thy glory, in the presence \textsuperscript{7} that it; Come Be humble; affect not high things; keep thyself quiet; and thou shalt live at ease, in safety, and in peace. than \textsuperscript{9} with a secret to another or, the secret of another \textsuperscript{11} word; fitly spoken Heb. spoken upon his wheels is like Rather "is like golden apples ( tappuchim, in Arabic, tuffach ), in baskets ( maskeeyoth, in Arabic, shakeekat ), of silver." A word spoken with propriety, opportunely, and suitably to the occasion, is as much in its place, and as conspicuously beautiful, as the golden fruit which appears through the apertures of an exquisitely wrought silver basket. \textsuperscript{14} boasteth; of a false gift Heb. in a gift of falsehood \textsuperscript{15} long; the bone Rather, "a bone; " that is, soft and conciliating language will often accomplish the most difficult things. \textsuperscript{17} Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's or, Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbour's; weary Heb. full \textsuperscript{22} For Not to consume, but to melt him into kindness; a metaphor taken from smelting metalic ores. the Lord \textsuperscript{23} north driveth etc. or, bringeth forth rain; so doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance, Monconys says, that when travelling on the second of January, 1648, from Tripoli in Syria, between Lebanon and the sea, it rained without ceasing, while the north wind blew directly in his face. so\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 26}
\markright{PROVERBS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} As dew in harvest, and as rain in summer, so honor is not [seemly] for a fool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} As birds and sparrows fly, so a curse shall not come upon any one without a cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} As a whip for a horse, and a goad for an ass, so [is] a rod for a simple nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Yet answer a fool according to his folly, lest he seem wise in his own conceit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He that sends a message by a foolish messenger procures for himself a reproach from his own ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [As well] take away the motion of the legs, as transgression from the mouth of fools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that binds up a stone in a sling, is like one that gives glory to a fool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Thorns grow in the hand of a drunkard, and servitude in the hand of fools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All the flesh of fools endures much hardship; for their fury is brought to nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} As when a dog goes to his own vomit, and becomes abominable, so is fool who returns in his wickedness to his own sin. [There is a shame that brings sin: and there is a shame [that is] glory and grace.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I have seen a man who seemed to himself to be wise; but a fool had more hope than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A sluggard when sent on a journey says, [There is] a lion in the ways, and [there are] murderers in the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As a door turns on the hinge, so does a sluggard on his bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} A sluggard having hid his hand in his bosom, will not be able to bring it up to his mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A sluggard seems to himself wiser than one who most satisfactorily brings back a message. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} As he that lays hold of a dog's tail, so is he that makes himself the champion of another's cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} As those who need correction put forth [fair] words to men, and he that first falls in with the proposal will be overthrown; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} so are all that lay wait for their own friends, and when they are revealed, say, I did it in jest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} With much wood fire increases; but where there is not a double-minded man, strife ceases. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} A hearth for coals, and wood for fire; and railing man for the tumult of strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The words of cunning knaves are soft; but they strike [even] to the inmost parts of the bowels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Silver dishonestly given is to be considered as a potsherd: smooth lips cover a grievous heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A weeping enemy promises all things with his lips, but in his heart he contrives deceit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Though [your] enemy entreat you with a loud voice, consent not: for there are seven abominations in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He that hides enmity frames deceit: but being easily discerned, exposes his own sins in the public assemblies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He that digs a pit for his neighbor shall fall into it: and he that rolls a stone, rolls it upon himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} A lying tongue hates the truth; and an unguarded mouth causes tumults.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} According to our notions, we should rather say, a bridle for the horse, and a whip for the ass; but it should be considered, that the Eastern asses are not only much more beautiful, but better goers that ours; and being active and well broken, they need only a bridle to guide them; whereas their horses being scarce, and often caught wild, and badly broken, are much less manageable, and need the correction of the whip. \textsuperscript{5} a fool;, ; lest; conceit Heb. eyes \textsuperscript{7} not equal Heb. lifted up so \textsuperscript{8} bindeth a stone in a sling Heb. putteth a precious stone in a heap of stones, This probably refers, as Coverdale understands it, to the custom of throwing a stone to the heap under which a criminal was buried. So the Vulgate, Sicut qui mittit lapidem in acervum Mercurii; ita qui tribuit insipienti honorem, "As he who throws a stone to Mercury's heap, so is he who gives honour to a fool." Mercury was a heathen god of highways; and stones were erected in different parts to guide the traveller: hence those lines of Dr. Young, "Death stands like Mercuries in every way; And kindly points us to our journey's end." so \textsuperscript{10} The great etc. or, A great man grieveth all; and he hireth the fool, he hireth also the transgressors. both \textsuperscript{11} a dog; returneth to his folly Heb. iterateth his folly \textsuperscript{15} slothful it grieveth him or, he is weary \textsuperscript{17} passeth, ; meddleth or, is enraged \textsuperscript{18} firebrands Heb. flames, or sparks arrows \textsuperscript{20} Where no wood is Heb. Without wood so, ; talebearer or, whisperer ceaseth Heb. is silent \textsuperscript{22} words; innermost parts Heb. chambers \textsuperscript{23} That is, ardent professions of friendship from a wicked heart, however smooth, shining, and splendid they may appear, are like a vile vessel covered over with base metal. \textsuperscript{24} dissembleth or, is known deceit \textsuperscript{25} speaketh fair Heb. maketh his voice gracious, ; believe; seven \textsuperscript{26} Whose hatred is covered by deceit or, Hatred is covered in secret \textsuperscript{28} lying He that injures another hates him in proportion to the injury; Proprium humani ingenii est, odisse quem leseris, says Tacitlus, and strange to say, in proportion to the innocence of the injured., a flattering\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 27}
\markright{PROVERBS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Boast not of to-morrow; for you know not what the next day shall bring forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let your neighbor, and not your own mouth, praise you; a stranger, and not your own lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A stone is heavy, and sand cumbersome; but a fool's wrath is heavier than both. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Wrath is merciless, and anger sharp: but envy can bear nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Open reproofs are better than secret love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The wounds of a friend are more to be trusted than the spontaneous kisses of an enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} A full soul scorns honeycombs; but to a hungry soul even bitter things appear sweet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} As when a bird flies down from its own nest, so a man is brought into bondage whenever he estranges himself from his own place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The heart delights in ointments and wines and perfumes: but the soul is broken by calamities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Your own friend, and your father's friend, forsake not; and when you are in distress go not into your brother's house: better is a friend [that is] near than a brother living far off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Son, be wise, that your heart may rejoice; and remove you from yourself reproachful words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A wise man, when evils are approaching, hides himself; but fools pass on, and will be punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Take away the man's garment, (for a scorner has passed by) whoever lays waste another's goods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whosoever shall bless a friend in the morning with a loud voice, shall seem to differ nothing from one who curses [him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} On a stormy day drops [of rain] drive a man out of his house; so also does a railing woman [drive a man] out of his own house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The north wind is sharp, but it is called by name propitious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Iron sharpens iron; and a man sharpens his friend's countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He that plants a fig tree shall eat the fruits of it: so he that waits on his own master shall be honored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} As faces are not like [other] faces, so neither are the thoughts of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Hell and destruction are not filled; so also are the eyes of men insatiable. [He that fixes his eye is an abomination to the Lord; and the uninstructed do not restrain their tongue.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Fire is the trial for silver and gold; and a man is tried by the mouth of them that praise him. The heart of the transgressor seeks after mischiefs; but an upright heart seeks knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Though you scourge a fool, disgracing him in the midst of the council, you will [still] in no wise remove his folly from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Do you thoroughly know the number of your flock, and pay attention to your herds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For a man [has] not strength and power for ever; neither does he transmit it from generation to generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Take care of the herbage in the field, and you shall cut grass, and gather the mountain hay; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} that you may have [wool of] sheep for clothing: pay attention to the land, that you may have lambs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} [My] son, you have from me words very useful for your life, and for the life of your servants.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Boast; to morrow Heb. to morrow day thou \textsuperscript{4} cruel, and anger is outrageous Heb. cruelty, and anger an overflowing, but; *marg.; envy or, jealousy \textsuperscript{6} the wounds; the kisses; deceitful or, earnest, or, frequent \textsuperscript{7} full, loatheth Heb. treadeth under foot to \textsuperscript{9} Ointment; so, ; by hearty counsel Heb. from the counsel of the soul \textsuperscript{20} Hell; never Heb. not so \textsuperscript{23} diligent; look well Heb. set thy heart, *marg. \textsuperscript{24} For; riches Heb. strength, doth; every generation Heb. generation and generation \textsuperscript{25} hay Rather, herbage, as chatzir uniformly denotes.\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 28}
\markright{PROVERBS 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The ungodly [man] flees when no one pursues: but the righteous is confident as a lion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} By reason of the sins of ungodly men quarrels arise; but a wise man will quell them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A bold man oppresses the poor by ungodly deeds. As an impetuous and profitable rain, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} so they that forsake the law praise ungodliness; but they that love the law fortify themselves with a wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Evil men will not understand judgment: but they that seek the Lord will understand everything. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A poor man walking in truth is better than a rich liar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} A wise son keeps the law: but he that keeps up debauchery dishonors his father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that increases his wealth by usuries and [unjust] gains, gathers it for him that pities the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even he has made his prayer abominable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He that causes upright men to err in an evil way, himself shall fall into destruction: transgressor also shall pass by prosperity, but shall not enter into it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A rich man is wise in his own conceit; but an intelligent poor man will condemn him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} By reason of the help of righteous men great glory arises: but in the places of the ungodly men are caught. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He that covers his own ungodliness shall not prosper: but he that blames [himself] shall be loved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Blessed is the man who religiously fears always: but the hard of heart shall fall into mischiefs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf [is he], who, being poor, rules over a poor nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A king in need of revenues is a great oppressor: but he that hates injustice shall live a long time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He that becomes surety for a man charged with murder shall be an exile, and not in safety. Chasten your son, and he shall love you, and give honor to your soul: he shall not obey a sinful nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He that walks justly is assisted: but he that walks in crooked ways shall be entangled [therein]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He that tills his own land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that follows idleness shall have plenty of poverty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A man worthy of credit shall be much blessed: but the wicked shall not be unpunished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He that reverences not the persons of the just is not good: such a one will sell a man for a morsel of bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} An envious man makes haste to be rich, and knows not that the merciful man will have the mastery over him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He that reproves a man's ways shall have more favor than he that flatters with the tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that casts off father or mother, and thinks he sins not; the same is partaker with an ungodly man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} An unbelieving man judges rashly: but he that trusts in the Lord will act carefully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He that trusts to a bold heart, such an one is a fool: but he that walks in wisdom shall be safe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He that gives to the poor shall not be in lack: but he that turns away his eye [from him] shall be in great distress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} In the places of ungodly [men] the righteous mourn: but in their destruction the righteous shall be multiplied.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} the transgression, ; but; by a man etc. by men of understanding and wisdom shall they likewise be prolonged \textsuperscript{3} poor man which leaveth no food Heb. without food \textsuperscript{7} keepeth, but, ; is a companion of riotous men or, feedeth gluttons \textsuperscript{8} that by; unjust gain Heb. by increase;, pity \textsuperscript{11} rich; his own conceit Heb. his eyes; the poor \textsuperscript{12} righteous, ; but; hidden Heb. sought for \textsuperscript{15} a roaring; a ranging; so \textsuperscript{20} faithful; but, ; innocent or, unpunished, *marg. \textsuperscript{21} respect; for Erasmus observes that this expression probably originated from the circumstance of holding out a piece of bread to a dog, in order to soothe him. \textsuperscript{22} that hasteth etc. Heb. that hath an evil eye hasteth to be rich; an evil; and \textsuperscript{24} robbeth; the same, a destroyer Heb. a man destroying \textsuperscript{25} that is, he that putteth; made \textsuperscript{28} the wicked, hide they perish\par}

\subsection*{Proverbs 29}
\markright{PROVERBS 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A reprover is better than a stiff-necked man: for when the latter is suddenly set on fire, there shall be no remedy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} When the righteous are praised, the people will rejoice: but when the ungodly rule, men mourn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} When a man loves wisdom, his father rejoices: but he that keeps harlots will waste wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A righteous king establishes a country: but a transgressor destroys [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He that prepares a net in the way of his own friend, entangles his own feet in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A great snare [is spread] for a sinner: but the righteous shall be in joy and gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} A righteous man knows how to judge for the poor: but the ungodly understands not knowledge; and the poor man has not an understanding mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Lawless men burn down a city: but wise men turn away wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A wise man shall judge nations: but a worthless man being angry laughs and fears not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Bloody men hate a holy [person], but the upright will seek his soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A fool utters all his mind: but the wise reserves his in part. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When a king hearkens to unjust language, all his subjects are transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When the creditor and debtor meet together, the Lord oversees them both. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} When a king judges the poor in truth, his throne shall be established for a testimony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Stripes and reproofs give wisdom: but an erring child disgraces his parents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} When the ungodly abound, sins abound: but when they fall, the righteous are warned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Chasten your son, and he shall give you rest; and he shall give honor to your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} There shall be no interpreter to a sinful nation: but he that observes the law is blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A stubborn servant will not be reproved by words: for even if he understands, still he will not obey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} If you see a man hasty in [his] words, know that the fool has hope rather than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} He that lives wantonly from a child, shall be a servant, and in the end shall grieve over himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A furious man stirs up strife, and a passionate man digs up sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Pride brings a man low, but the Lord upholds the humble-minded with honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that shares with a thief, hates his own soul: and if any having heard an oath uttered tell not of it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} [they] fearing and reverencing men [unreasonably] have been overthrown, but he that trusts in the Lord shall rejoice. Ungodliness causes a man to stumble: but he that trusts in his master shall be safe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Many wait on the favor of rulers; but justice comes to a man from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A righteous man is an abomination to an unrighteous man, and the direct way is an abomination to the sinner.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} He, that being often reproved Heb. a man of reproofs;, ; hardeneth; shall \textsuperscript{2} the righteous, ; in authority or, increased when the wicked \textsuperscript{4} king, ; he that receiveth gifts Heb. a man of oblations \textsuperscript{8} Scornful; bring a city into a snare or, set a city on fire, wise \textsuperscript{10} The bloodthirsty Heb. Men of bloods; but \textsuperscript{13} the deceitful man or, the usurer; meet; Lord \textsuperscript{18} there; perish or, is made naked, but \textsuperscript{20} Seest; words or, matters, more \textsuperscript{25} fear, ; whoso, ; safe Heb. set on high \textsuperscript{26} seek; ruler's favour Heb. face of a ruler\par}
