\subsection*{Proverbs 30}
\markright{PROVERBS 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} These things says the man to them that trust in God; and I cease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I am the most simple of all men, and there is not in me the wisdom of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} God has taught me wisdom, and I know the knowledge of the holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who has gone up to heaven, and come down? who has gathered the winds in his bosom? who has wrapped up the waters in a garment? who has dominion of all the ends of the earth? what is his name? or what is the name of his children? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For all the words of God are tried in the fire, and he defends those that reverence him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Add not to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be made a liar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Two things I ask of you; take not favor from me before I die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remove far from me vanity and falsehood: and give me not wealth [or] poverty; but appoint me what is needful and sufficient: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} lest I be filled and become false, and say, Who sees me? or be poor and steal, and swear [vainly] by the name of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Deliver not a servant into the hands of his master, lest he curse you, and you be utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A wicked generation curse their father, and do not bless their mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A wicked generation judge themselves to be just, but do not cleanse their way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A wicked generation have lofty eyes, and exalt themselves with their eyelids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A wicked generation have swords [for] teeth and jaw teeth [as] knives, so as to destroy and devour the lowly from the earth, and the poor of them from among men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The horse-leech had three dearly beloved daughters: and these three did not satisfy her; and the fourth was not contented so as to say, Enough. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The grave, and the love of a woman, and the earth not filled with water; water also and fire will not say, It is enough. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The eye that laughs to scorn a father, and dishonors the old age of a mother, let the ravens of the valleys pick it out, and let the young eagles devour it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Moreover there are three things impossible for me to comprehend, and the fourth I know not: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} the track of a flying eagle; and the ways of a serpent on a rock; and the paths of a ship passing through the sea; and the ways of a man in youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Such is the way of an adulterous woman, who having washed herself from what she has done, says she has done nothing amiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} By three things the earth is troubled, and the fourth it can’t bear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} if a servant reign; or a fool be filled with food; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} or if a maidservant should cast out her own mistress; and if a hateful woman should marry a good man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And [there are] four very little things upon the earth, but these are wiser than the wise: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} the ants which are weak, and [yet] prepare [their] food in summer; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} the rabbits also [are] a feeble race, who make their houses in the rocks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The locusts have no king, and [yet] march orderly at one command. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the eft, which supports itself by [its] hands, and is easily taken, dwells in the fortresses of kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And there are three things which go well, and a fourth which passes along finely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A lion's whelp, stronger than [all other] beasts, which turns not away, nor fears [any] beast; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} and a cock walking in boldly among the hens, and the goat leading the herd; and a king publicly speaking before a nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} If you abandon yourself to mirth, and stretch forth your hand in a quarrel, you shall be disgraced. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Milk out milk, and there shall be butter, and if you wing [one's] nostrils there shall come out blood: so if you extort words, there will come forth quarrels and strifes.\par

Hurt not with thy tongue;, ; lest \textsuperscript{11} a generation; that curseth; doth \textsuperscript{15} The horseleach; Give; There, ;, It is enough Heb. \subsection*{Proverbs 31}
\markright{PROVERBS 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My words have been spoken by God—the oracular answer of a king, whom his mother instructed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} What will you keep, my son, what? the words of God. My firstborn son, I speak to you: what? son of my womb? what? son of my vows? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Give not your wealth to women, nor your mind and living to remorse. Do all things with counsel: drink wine with counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Princes are prone to anger: let them then not drink wine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} lest they drink, and forget wisdom, and be not able to judge the poor rightly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Give strong drink to those that are in sorrow, and the wine to drink to those in pain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} that they may forget their poverty, and may not remember their troubles any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge all fairly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Open your mouth and judge justly, and plead the cause of the poor and weak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who shall find a virtuous woman? for such a one is more valuable than precious stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The heart of her husband trusts in her: such a one shall stand in no need of fine spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For she employs all her living for her husband's good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Gathering wool and flax, she makes it serviceable with her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} She is like a ship trading from a distance: so she procures her livelihood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And she rises by night, and gives food to her household, and [appointed] tasks to her maidens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} She views a farm, and buys it: and with the fruit of her hands she plants a possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} She strongly girds her loins, and strengthens her arms for work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And she finds by experience that working is good; and her candle goes not out all night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} She reaches forth her arms to needful [works], and applies her hands to the spindle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And she opens her hands to the needy, and reaches out fruit to the poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Her husband is not anxious about those at home when he tarries anywhere abroad: for all her household are clothed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} She makes for her husband clothes of double texture, and garments for herself of fine linen and scarlet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And her husband becomes a distinguished [person] in the gates, when he sits in council with the old inhabitants of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} She makes fine linens, and sells girdles to the Chananites: she opens her mouth heedfully and with propriety, and controls her tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} She puts on strength and honor; and rejoices in the last days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But she opens her mouth wisely, and according to law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The ways of her household are careful, and she eats not the bread of idleness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And [her] kindness to them sets up her children for them, and they grow rich, and her husband praises her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Many daughters have obtained wealth, many have wrought valiantly; but you have exceeded, you have surpassed all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Charms are false, and woman's beauty is vain: for it is a wise woman that is blessed, and let her praise the fear the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Give her of the fruit of her lips; and let her husband be praised in the gates.\par

\section*{Ecclesiastes Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Solomon (Qoheleth) in conservative evangelical reading\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The speaker identifies himself as son of David, king in Jerusalem; conservative interpretation receives this as Solomonic.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The canonical self-presentation is the principal basis; conservative readers do not treat the Solomonic voice as literary fiction.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 10th century BC in Solomon's later life\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT Ecclesiastes presents Qoheleth's reflections in the standard Hebrew form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX of Ecclesiastes is often quite literal but still participates in the broader Greek textual history of the book.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} A wisdom reflection on life under the sun, mortality, vanity, and the fear of God.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To expose the vanity of life apart from God and to drive the reader to fear God and keep His commandments.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} vanity; mortality; joy; wisdom; judgment; fear of God\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Prologue 1:1-11; Qoheleth's investigations 1:12-12:7; Epilogue 12:8-14.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Ecclesiastes fragments survive, including 4Q109 1st century BC | Subst. Qumran fragments provide early Hebrew support for the book's text Late Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Ecclesiastes 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use in later Jewish and Christian wisdom reflection by Multiple (later Second Temple and early Christian periods)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Ecclesiastes is comparatively stable textually, though interpretation and voice remain more debated than the text itself.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Ecclesiastes as Solomonic wisdom and reads its realism as fully compatible with inspiration and inerrancy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\markboth{ECCLESIASTES}{}
\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 1}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Vanity of vanities, said the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} What advantage [is there] to a man in all his labor that he takes under the sun? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A generation goes, and a generation comes: but the earth stands for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sun arises, and the sun goes down and draws toward its place; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} arising there it proceeds southward, and goes round toward the north. The wind goes round and round, and the wind returns to its circuits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All the rivers run into the sea; and yet the sea is not filled: to the place whence the rivers come, there they return again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} All things are full of labor; a man will not be able to speak [of them]: neither shall the eye be satisfied with seeing, neither shall the ear be filled with hearing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} What is that which has been? the very thing which shall be: and what is that which has been done? the very thing which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [Who is he] that shall speak and say, Behold, this is new? it has already been in the ages that have passed before us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} There is no memorial to the first things; neither to the things that have been last shall their memorial be with them that shall at the last [time]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I applied my heart to seek out and examine by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven, for God has given to the sons of men an evil trouble to be troubled therewith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I saw all the works that were done under the sun; and, behold, all were vanity and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} That which is crooked can’t be made straight: and deficiency can’t be numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I spoke in my heart, saying, Behold, I am increased, and have acquired wisdom beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem: also I applied my heart to know wisdom and knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And my heart knew much—wisdom, and knowledge, parables and understanding: I perceived that this also is waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For in the abundance of wisdom is abundance of knowledge; and he that increases knowledge will increase sorrow.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{2} Gk. vocab: mataiotēs (ματαιότης) = vanity; futility. Common English renderings: vanity. A major wisdom term for futility or emptiness.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{6} The wind This verse should be connected with the preceding, and rendered, "The sun also riseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose; going toward the south, and turning about unto the north. The wind whirleth about continually, " etc. Alluding, in the former part, to the apparent daily motion of the sun from east to west, and to his annual course through the signs of the zodiac. \textsuperscript{7} the rivers run; return again Heb. return to go \textsuperscript{13} I gave, ;, ; this sore, ; to be exercised or, to afflict them \textsuperscript{16} communed; Lo;, ;, great experience of Heb. seen much\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 2}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I said in my heart, Come now, I will prove you with mirth, and behold you good: and, behold, this is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I said to laughter, Madness: and to mirth, Why do you this: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I examined whether my heart would excite my flesh as [with] wine, (though my heart guided [me] in wisdom,) and [I desired] to lay hold of mirth, until I should see of what kind is the good to the sons of men, which they should do under the sun all the days of their life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I enlarged my work; I built me houses; I planted me vineyards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I made me gardens and orchards, and planted in them every kind of fruit tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I made me pools of water, to water from them the timber-bearing wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I got servants and maidens, and servants were born to me in the house: also I had abundant possession of flocks and herds, beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Moreover I collected for myself both silver and gold also, and the peculiar treasures of kings and provinces: I procured me singing men and singing women, and delights of the sons of men, a butler and female cupbearers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So I became great, and advanced beyond all that were before in Jerusalem: also my wisdom was established to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And whatever my eyes desired, I withheld not from them, I withheld not my heart from all my mirth: for my heart rejoiced in all my labor; and this was my portion of all my labor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I looked on all my works which my hands had wrought, and on my labor which I laboured to perform: and behold, all was vanity and waywardness of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then I looked on to see wisdom, and madness, and folly: for who is the man who will follow after counsel, in all things where in he employs it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I saw that wisdom excels folly, as much as light excels darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I perceived, even I, that one event shall happen to them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I said in my heart, As the event of the fool is, so shall it be to me, even to me: and to what purpose have I gained wisdom? I said moreover in my heart, This is also vanity, because the fool speaks of his abundance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For there is no remembrance of the wise man with the fool for ever; forasmuch as now [in] the coming days all things are forgotten: and how shall the wise man die with the fool? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So I hated life; because the work that was wrought under the sun was evil before me: for all is vanity and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And I hated the whole of my labor which I took under the sun; because I must leave it to the man who will come after me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And who knows whether he will be a wise [man] or a fool? and whether he will have power over all my labor in which I laboured, and wherein I grew wise under the sun? this is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} so I went about to dismiss from my heart all my labor wherein I had laboured under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For there is [such] a man that his labor is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in fortitude; [yet] this man shall give his portion to one who has not laboured therein. This is also vanity and great evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For it happens to a man in all his labor, and in the purpose of his heart wherein he labors under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For all his days [are days] of sorrows, and vexation of spirit is his; in the night also his heart rests not. This is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A man has nothing [really] good to eat, and to drink, and to show his soul [as] good in his trouble. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For who shall eat, or who shall drink, without him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For [God] has given to the man who is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but he has given to the sinner trouble, to add and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God; for this is also vanity and waywardness of spirit.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} said, ;, ; Go to; I will \textsuperscript{2} I said Solomon is not speaking here of sober enjoyment of the things of the world, but of intemperate pleasure, whose two attendants, laughter and mirth, are introduced by a beautiful prosopopoeia, as two persons, whom he treats with the utmost contempt. It is \textsuperscript{3} sought; give myself unto wine Heb. draw my flesh with wine yet; and to lay; till, all Heb. the number of \textsuperscript{4} made; I builded;, ; I planted \textsuperscript{7} servants; and had servants born in my house Heb. sons of my house also \textsuperscript{8} silver, ; men singers; musical instruments etc. Heb. musical instrument and instruments, ; The difficult words shiddah weshiddoth are variously rendered. The LXX have οινοχοον και οινοχοας, "male and female cup-bearers, " with which the Syriac and Arabic and Parkhurst agree; Aquila, κυλικον και κυλικια, "a cup and smaller cups; " Jerome, scyphos et urceolos, Vulgate urceos ), "goblets and pots; " Targum, "warm and cold baths; " others, as M. Desvoeux, "male and female captives; " others, "cooks and confectioners; " others, "a species of musical compositions, " derived from Sido, a celebrated Phoenician woman, to whom Sanchoniatho attributes the invention of music; but others, with more probability, "wives and concubines; " and siddoth may be in this sense synonymous with the Arabic seedat, domina, conjux from sada, in Conj. V. conjugium inivit . Of the former, Solomon had three hundred, and of the latter, seven hundred; and if they are not mentioned here they are not mentioned at all, which is wholly unaccountable. \textsuperscript{12} I turned, even that which hath already been done, or, in those things which have been already done \textsuperscript{13} I saw; that wisdom excelleth folly Heb. that there is an excellency in wisdom more than in folly, etc light \textsuperscript{15} even to me Heb. to me even to me and why, ; Then I \textsuperscript{18} I hated, taken Heb. laboured I should \textsuperscript{22} hath man, ; and of the \textsuperscript{24} nothing, ; make his soul enjoy good or, delight his senses that it \textsuperscript{26} in his sight Heb. before him; wisdom; to the sinner\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 3}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} To all things there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A time of birth, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what has been planted; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to pull down, and a time to build up; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to lament, and a time to dance; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} a time to throw stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to abstain from embracing; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to be silent, and a time to speak; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} What advantage [has] he that works in those things wherein he labors? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I have seen all the trouble, which God has given to the sons of men to be troubled with. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All the things which he has made are beautiful in his time: he has also set the whole world in their heart, that man might not find out the work which God has wrought from the beginning even to the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I know that there is no good in them, except [for a man] to rejoice, and to do good in his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Also [in the case of] every man who shall eat and drink, and see good in all his labor, [this] is a gift of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I know that whatever things God has done, they shall be for ever: it is impossible to add to it, and it is impossible to take away from it: and God has done [it], that [men] may fear before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} That which has been is now; and whatever things [are appointed] to be have already been; and God will seek out that which is past. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, there was the ungodly one; and the place of righteousness, there was the godly one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the ungodly: for there is a time there for every action and for every work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I said in my heart, concerning the speech of the sons of man, God will judge them, and that to show that they are beasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Also to them is the event of the sons of man, and the event of the brute; one event befalls them: as is the death of the one, so also the death of the other; and there is one breath to all: and what has the man more than the brute? nothing; for all is vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} All [go] to one place; all were formed of the dust, and all will return to dust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And who has seen the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward? and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I saw that there was no good, but that wherein a man shall rejoice in his works, for it is his portion, for who shall bring him to see any thing of that which shall be after him?\par

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 4}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} So I returned, and saw all the oppressions that were done under the sun: and behold the tear of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of them that oppressed them was power; but they had no comforter: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and I praised all the dead that had already died more than the living, as many as are alive until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Better also than both these is he who has not yet been, who has not seen all the evil work that is done under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I saw all labor, and all the diligent work, that this is a man's envy from his neighbor. This is also vanity and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Better is a handful of rest than two handfuls of trouble and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So I returned, and saw vanity under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} There is one [alone], and there is not a second; yes, he has neither son nor brother: yet there is no end to all his labor; neither is his eye satisfied with wealth; and for whom do I labor, and deprive my soul of good? this is also vanity, and an evil trouble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Two [are] better than one, [seeing] they have a good reward for their labor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls, and there is not a second to lift him up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Also if two should lie together, they also get heat: but how shall one be warmed [alone?] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if one should prevail against [him], the two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord shall not be quickly broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king, who knows not how to take heed any longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For he shall come forth out of the house of the prisoners to reign, because [he] also that was in his kingdom has become poor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I saw all the living who were walking under the sun, with the second youth who shall stand up in each one's place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them: and the last shall not rejoice in him: for this also is vanity and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Keep your foot, whenever you go to the house of God; and [when you are] near to hear, let your sacrifice [be] better than the gift of fools: for they know not that they are doing evil.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I returned; and considered, ;, ; , ; the tears, ; they had; side Heb. hand \textsuperscript{4} every etc. Heb. all the rightness of work, that this is the envy of man from his neighbour, ; This is \textsuperscript{5} fool, eateth That is, with envy (see ), though too idle to follow his neighbour's example. \textsuperscript{8} one; he hath no is his; For; it is \textsuperscript{12} And if This is well illustrated by the fable of the dying father, who, to shew his sons the advantages of union, gave them a bundle of twigs, which could not be broken when bound together, but were easily snapped asunder one by one. and a \textsuperscript{13} is a poor;, will no more be Heb. knoweth not to be \textsuperscript{14} For out This is probably an allusion to some fact with which we are unacquainted. History furnishes many instances of mean persons raised to sovereign authority, and of kings being reduced to the meanest offices, and to a morsel. Agrippa mounted the throne of Israel after having been long in prison; and similar instances are not wanting in modern times.; also \textsuperscript{16} no end;, they also; this\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 5}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Be not hasty with your mouth, and let not your heart be swift to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven above, and you upon earth: therefore let your words be few. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For through the multitude of trial a dream comes; and a fool's voice is with a multitude of words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Whenever you shall vow a vow to God, defer not to pay it; for [he has] no pleasure in fools: pay you therefore whatever you shall have vowed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [It is] better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Suffer not your mouth to lead your flesh to sin; and say not in the presence of God, It was an error: lest God be angry at your voice, and destroy the works of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For [there is evil] in a multitude of dreams and vanities and many words: but fear you God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} If you should see the oppression of the poor, and the wresting of judgment and of justice in the land, wonder not at the matter: for [there is] a high one to watch over him that is high, and high ones over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Also the abundance of the earth is for every one: the king [is dependent on] the tilled field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver: and who has loved gain, in the abundance thereof? this is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the multitude of good they are increased that eat it: and what virtue has the owner, but the right of beholding [it] with his eyes? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The sleep of a servant is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but to one who is satiated with wealth, there is none that suffers him to sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There is an infirmity which I have seen under the sun, [namely], wealth kept for its owner to his hurt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And that wealth shall perish in an evil trouble: and [the man] begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As he came forth naked from his mother's womb, he shall return back as he came, and he shall receive nothing for his labor, that it should go [with him] in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And this is also an evil infirmity: for as he came, so also shall he return: and what is his gain, for which he vainly labors? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Yes, all his days are in darkness, and in mourning, and much sorrow, and infirmity, and wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold, I have seen good, that it is a fine thing [for a man] to eat and to drink, and to see good in all his labor in which he may labor under the sun, [all] the number of the days of his life which God has given to him: for it is his portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yes, and [as for] every man to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to receive his portion, and to rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For he shall not much remember the days of his life; for God troubles him in the mirth of his heart.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} not rash, ; thing or, word for; let thy \textsuperscript{6} thy mouth; before Or, "before the messenger, " hammalach, the priest whose business it was to take cognizance of vows and offerings.; it was, destroy \textsuperscript{8} thou seest; marvel; matter Heb. will, or purpose, ; for;, regardeth; , ;, ; higher than they \textsuperscript{10} He that The more he gets, the more he would get; for Crescit amor nummi, quantum ipsa pecunia crescit, "The love of money increases, in proportion as money itself increases."; this \textsuperscript{18} it is good and comely Heb. there is a good which is comely, etc., ; the days Heb. the number of the days it is his\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 6}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is abundant with man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} a man to whom God shall give wealth, and substance, and honor, and he wants nothing for his soul of all things that he shall desire, yet God shall not give him power to eat of it, for a stranger shall devour it: this is vanity, and an evil infirmity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If a man beget one hundred [children], and live many years, yes, however abundant the days of his years shall be, yet [if] his soul shall not be satisfied with good, and also he have no burial; I said, An untimely birth is better than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For he came in vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered in darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known rest: there is [no more rest] to this one than another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Though he has lived to the return of a thousand years, yet he has seen no good: do not all go to one place? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All the labor of a man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite shall not be satisfied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For [what] advantage has the wise man over the fool, since [even] the poor knows how to walk in the direction of life? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The sight of the eyes is better than that which wanders in soul: this is also vanity, and waywardness of spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If anything has been, its name has already been called: and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is stronger than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For there are many things which increase vanity.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} a man; so; yet A man may possess much earthly goods, and yet have neither the heart nor power to enjoy them. Possession and fruition are not necessarily joined together; and this is also among the vanities of life, and was and still is a very "common evil among men." It belongs to God as much to give the power to enjoy, as it does to give earthly blessings. but; vanity \textsuperscript{3} a man; so; and also; that an \textsuperscript{7} the labour; appetite Heb. soul \textsuperscript{8} what hath the wise, the poor \textsuperscript{9} Better, wandering of the desire Heb. walking of the soul; this\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 7}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} What advantage has a man? for who knows [what is] good for a man in his life, [during] the number of the life of the days of his vanity? and he has spent them as a shadow; for who shall tell a man what shall be after him under the sun? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A good name is better than good oil; and the day of death than the day of birth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [It is] better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the banquet house: since this is the end of every man; and the living man will apply good [warning] to his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart will be made better. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} [It is] better to hear a reproof of a wise man, than for a man to hear the song of fools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} As the sound of thorns under a caldron, so is the laughter of fools: this is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} for oppression makes a wise man mad, and destroys his noble heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The end of a matter is better than the beginning thereof: the patient is better than the high-minded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry: for anger will rest in the bosom of fools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Say not, What has happened, that the former days were better than these? for you do not enquire in wisdom concerning this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and [there is] an advantage [by it] to them that see the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For wisdom in its shadow is as the shadow of silver: and the excellence of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to him that has it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Behold the works of God: for who shall be able to straighten him whom God has made crooked? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In the day of prosperity live joyfully, and consider in the day of adversity: consider, [I say], God also has caused the one to agree with the other for [this] reason, that man should find nothing after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I have seen all things in the days of my vanity: there is a just man perishing in his justice, and there is an ungodly man remaining in his wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Be not very just; neither be very wise: lest you be confounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Be not very wicked; and be not stubborn: lest you should die before your time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} It is well for you to hold fast by this; also by this defile not your hand: for to them that fear God all things shall come forth [well]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Wisdom will help the wise man more than ten mighty men which are in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For there is not a righteous man in the earth, who will do good, and not sin {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Also take no heed to all the words which ungodly men shall speak; lest you hear your servant cursing you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For many times he shall trespass against you, and repeatedly shall he afflict your heart; for thus also have you cursed others. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} All these things have I proved in wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} [That which is] far beyond what was, and a great depth, who shall find it out? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I and my heart went round about to know, and to examine, and to seek wisdom, and the account [of things], and to know the folly and trouble and madness of the ungodly man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And I find her [to be], and I will pronounce [to be] more bitter than death the woman which is a snare, and her heart nets, [who has] a band in her hands: [he that is] good in the sight of God shall be delivered from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Behold, this have I found, said the Preacher, [seeking] by one at a time to find out the account, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} which my soul sought after, but I found not: for I have found one man of a thousand; but a woman in all these I have not found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But, behold, this have I found, that God made man upright; but they have sought out many devices.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} Sorrow or, Anger is better, ; by \textsuperscript{6} as; crackling Heb. sound the laughter \textsuperscript{10} What; wisely Heb. out of wisdom \textsuperscript{11} good with an inheritance or, as good as an inheritance, yea, better too.; them \textsuperscript{12} wisdom;, ; a defence Heb. a shadow; the excellency \textsuperscript{14} the day; but; set Heb. made \textsuperscript{15} have I, ; there is a just, ; there is a wicked \textsuperscript{16} Be not This verse is probably the language of an ungodly man; to which Solomon answers, as in the following verse, "Do not multiply wickedness; do not add direct opposition to godliness, to the rest of your crimes. Why should you provoke God to destroy you before your time?";, ; neither; destroy thyself Heb. be desolate \textsuperscript{17} not; why; before thy time Heb. not in thy time \textsuperscript{21} take no heed Heb. give not thine heart, unto \textsuperscript{25} I applied mine heart Heb. I and my heart compassed, the reason *marg., ; know \textsuperscript{26} I find;, whoso pleaseth God Heb. he that is good before God \textsuperscript{27} saith, counting one by one, to find out the account or, weighing one thing after another, to find out the reason \textsuperscript{28} yet; one; but Solomon, instead of seeking one rational, virtuous woman, had collected an immense multitude, of various countries and religions, for magnificence and indulgence; among whom, as might have been expected, he had not found one who was thoroughly faithful, upright, and pious. He here uses the language of a penitent, warning others of the errors into which he had been led; and not that of a wasphish satirist, lashing indiscriminately one half of the human species. \textsuperscript{29} God, they The descendants of Adam have sought out an immense number of inventions, in order to find happiness in the world, without God, which have only proved so many variations of impiety and iniquity.\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 8}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Who knows the wise? and who knows the interpretation of a saying? A man's wisdom will lighten his countenance; but a man of shameless countenance will be hated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Observe the commandment of the king, and [that] because of the word of the oath of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Be not hasty; you shall go forth out of his presence: stand not in an evil matter; for he will do whatever he shall please, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} even as a king having power: and who will say to him, What do you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He that keeps the commandment shall not know an evil thing: and the heart of the wise knows the time of judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For to every thing there is time and judgment; for the knowledge of a man is great to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For there is no one that knows what is going to be: for who shall tell him how it shall be? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit; and there is no power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in the day of the battle; neither shall ungodliness save her votary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So I saw all this, and I applied my heart to every work that has been done under the sun; all the things wherein man has power over man to afflict him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And then I saw the ungodly carried into the tombs, and [that] out of the holy place: and they departed, and were praised in the city, because they had done thus: this also is vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Because there is no contradiction made on the part of those who do evil quickly, therefore the heart of the children of men is fully determined in them to do evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He that has sinned has done evil from that time, and long from beforehand: nevertheless I know, that it is well with them that fear God, that they may fear before him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} but it shall not be well with the ungodly, and he shall not prolong his days, [which are] as a shadow; forasmuch as he fears not before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are righteous persons to whom it happens according to the doing of the ungodly; and there are ungodly men, to whom it happens according to the doing of the just: I said, This is also vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then I praised mirth, because there is no good for a man under the sun, but to eat, and drink, and be merry: and this shall attend him in his labor all the days of his life, which God has given him under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whereupon I set my heart to know wisdom, and to perceive the trouble that was wrought upon the earth: for there is that neither by day nor night sees sleep with his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I saw all the works of God, that a man shall not be able to discover the work which is wrought under the sun; whatever things a man shall endeavor to seek, however a man may labor to seek it, yet he shall not find it; yes, how much soever a wise man may speak of knowing it, he shall not be able to find it: for I applied all this to my heart, and my heart has seen all this.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Heb. vocab: pitgam (פִּתְגָם) = edict; decree; word. Common English renderings: decree; sentence. Loanword used especially in later biblical books.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} as the; who knoweth, ; a man's; and the; boldness Heb. strength \textsuperscript{5} keepeth; feel Heb. know a wise \textsuperscript{7} he knoweth, ; when or, how \textsuperscript{8} is no; power; discharge or, casting off weapons; neither \textsuperscript{10} so; the place; they were \textsuperscript{12} a sinner; surely;, ; fear before \textsuperscript{13} it shall, ; neither; as a \textsuperscript{14} a vanity, there be just \textsuperscript{15} Then I Some consider this as the cavil of an infidel objector, equivalent to the Epicurean maxim, Ede, bibe, lude; post mortem nulla voluptas, "Eat, drink, and play; there is no pleasure after death." But it may be regarded as a recommendation of a moderate use of worldly things, with a cheerful and contented mind; which may justly be considered as the greatest advantage which can be made of all below the sun, and amidst all changes, such a frame of mind, if the result of right principles, may and ought to be preserved; and it will be the recompence and solace of all our labours and toils. \textsuperscript{16} When I Solomon here records the result of his perplexing inquiries into the affairs of men, and the purposes, providence, and works of God. And when he examined with great attention and diligence into the works of God, he found he could neither comprehend nor explain them; and was persuaded, that no application or capacity would enable a man to fathom the depth of the Divine dispensations in this lower world. How vain, then, are all cavils against Divine providence; when we can neither understand, nor comprehend it!, there is that\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 9}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [I saw] that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: yes, there is no man that knows either love or hatred, [though] all are before their face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Vanity is in all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good, and to the bad; both to the pure, and to the impure; both to him that sacrifices, and to him that sacrifice not: as is the good, so is the sinner: as is the swearer, even so is he that fears an oath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} There is this evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes, the heart of the sons of men is filled with evil, and madness is in their heart during their life, and after that [they go] to the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} for who is he that has fellowship with all the living? there is hope [of him]: for a living dog is better than a dead lion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For the living will know that they shall die: but the dead know nothing, and there is no longer any reward to them; for their memory is lost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, have now perished; yes, there is no portion for them any more for ever in all that is done under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Go, eat your bread with mirth, and drink your wine with a joyful heart; for now God has favourably accepted your works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let your garments be always white; and let not oil be lacking on your head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And see life with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which are given you under the sun: for that is your portion in your life, and in your labor wherein you labor under the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Whatsoever your hand shall find to do, do with all your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Hades wither you go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor yet bread to the wise, nor yet wealth to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of knowledge; for time and chance will happen to them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For surely man also knows not his time: as fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as birds that are caught in a snare; even thus the sons of men are snared at an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This I also saw [to be] wisdom under the sun, and it is great before me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [suppose there were] a little city, and few men in it; and there should come against it a great king, and surround it, and build great mounds against it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and should find in it a poor wise man, and he should save the city through his wisdom: yet no man would remember that poor man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And I said Wisdom is better than power: yet the wisdom of the poor man is set at nothing, and his words not listened to. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The words of the wise are heard in quiet more than the cry of them that rule in folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Wisdom is better than weapons of war: and one sinner will destroy much good.\par

See, or Enjoy life with the wife, ; all the days of the life; for \textsuperscript{11} returned, ; that the race; but \textsuperscript{12} man; as the fishes; the sons\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 10}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Pestilent flies will corrupt a preparation of sweet ointment: [and] a little wisdom is more precious than great glory of folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Yes, and whenever a fool walks by the way, his heart will fail him, and all that he thinks of is folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If the spirit of the ruler rise up against you, leave not your place; for soothing will put an end to great offenses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, wherein an error has proceeded from the ruler. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The fool has been set in very high places, while rich men would sit in a low one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and him that breaks down a hedge a serpent shall bite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He that removes stones shall be troubled thereby; he that cleaves wood shall be endangered thereby. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If the axe-head should fall off, then the man troubles his countenance, and he must put forth more strength: and [in that case] skill is of no advantage to a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If a serpent bite when there is no [charmer's] whisper, then there is no advantage to the charmer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The words of a wise mouth are gracious: but the lips of a fool will swallow him up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly: and the end of his talk mischievous madness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A fool moreover multiplies words: man knows not what has been, nor what will be: who shall tell him what will come after him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The labor of fools will afflict them, [as that of one] who knows not to go to the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Woe to you, O city, whose king is young, and your princes eat in the morning! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Blessed are you, O land, whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes shall eat seasonably, for strength, and shall not be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} By slothful neglect a building will be brought low: and by idleness of the hands the house will fall to pieces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Men prepare bread for laughter, and wine and oil that the living should rejoice: but to money all things will humbly yield obedience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Even in your conscience, curse not the king; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry your voice, and that which has wings shall report your speech.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{20} Gk. vocab: syneidēsis (συνείδησις) = conscience. Common English renderings: conscience. A moral-awareness term important especially in Paul.\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 11}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Send forth your bread upon the face of the water: for you shall find it after many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for you know not what evil there shall be upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If the clouds be filled with rain, they pour [it] out upon the earth: and if a tree fall southward, or if it fall northward, in the place where the tree shall fall, there it shall be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He that observes the wind sows not; and he that looks at the clouds will not reap. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Among whom none knows what is the way of the wind: as the bones [are hid] in the womb of a pregnant [woman], so you shall not know the works of God, [even] all things whatever he shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening let not your hand be slack: for you know not what sort shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether both shall be good alike. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Moreover the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For even if a man should live many years, [and] rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Rejoice, O young man, in your youth; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart blameless, but not in the sight of your eyes: yet know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh: for youth and folly are vanity.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Cast That is, says Bp. Lowth, "Sow thy seed or corn on the face of the waters; " in plain terms, sow without any hope of a harvest. Do good even to them on whom your benefactions seem thrown away. Dr. Jebb has well illustrated it by the following passages: "Vain are the favours done to vicious men; Not vainer 'tis to sow the foaming deep. The deep no pleasant harvest shall afford, Nor will the wicked ever make return. "To befriend the wicked is like sowing in the sea. These, indeed, invert this precept; Nor is it extraordinary that they should. "The one, frail human power alone produced, The other, God." thy bread; waters Heb. face of the waters, for \textsuperscript{3} the clouds; if the tree \textsuperscript{5} thou knowest not what nor even;, 39:1-41:34 \textsuperscript{6} sow; thou knowest; prosper Heb. be right \textsuperscript{8} if a man, rejoice, yet;, ; All that \textsuperscript{9} Rejoice; in thy youth; walk; in the sight; know \textsuperscript{10} remove; sorrow or, anger, and put; for\par}

\subsection*{Ecclesiastes 12}
\markright{ECCLESIASTES 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of evil come, and the years overtake [you] in which you shall say, I have no pleasure in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} While the sun and light are not darkened, nor the moon and the stars; nor the clouds return after the rain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} in the day wherein the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the mighty men shall become bent, and the grinding [women] cease because they have become few, and the [women] looking out at the windows be dark; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} and they shall shut the doors in the marketplace, because of the weakness of the voice of her that grinds [at the mill]; and he shall rise up at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be brought low; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and they shall look up, and fears [shall be] in the way, and the almond tree shall blossom, and the locust shall increase, and the caper shall be scattered: because man has gone to his eternal home, and the mourners have gone about the market: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} before the silver cord be [let go], or the choice gold be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel run down to the cistern; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [before] the dust also return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return to God who gave it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Vanity of vanities, said the Preacher; all is vanity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And because the Preacher was wise above [others, so it was] that he taught man excellent knowledge, and the ear will trace out the parables. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The Preacher sought diligently to find out acceptable words, and a correct writing, [even] words of truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails firmly fastened, which have been given from one shepherd by agreement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And moreover, my son, guard yourself by means of them: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Hear the end of the matter, the sun: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For God will bring every work into judgment, with everything that has been overlooked, whether [it be] good, or whether [it be] evil.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} the almond, ; because; the mourners \textsuperscript{9} moreover, because the Preacher was wise or, the more wise the Preacher was, etc he still, he gave \textsuperscript{10} Preacher, acceptable words Heb. words of delight, ; written \textsuperscript{12} by these; study or, reading weariness \textsuperscript{13} Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter or, The end of the matter, even all that hath been heard is Fear; , ; for\par}

\section*{Song of Solomon Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Solomon\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The superscription identifies the Song with Solomon; conservative reading receives this straightforwardly.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The book's own superscription supplies the primary attribution.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 10th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT Song of Songs preserves the Hebrew love poetry collection in its canonical form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same basic collection, though poetic nuance can shift in translation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} A poetic song celebrating covenantal love, beauty, longing, and marital delight.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To honor covenant love and marriage while also fitting within the wider canonical pattern of the Lord's delight in His people.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} love; marriage; beauty; delight; covenant affection; desire rightly ordered\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Opening desire 1-2; courtship and longing 3-5; mutual praise 6-8.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Song of Songs fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Qumran fragments provide early Hebrew witness to the Song Hasmonean-Herodian periods | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve the Song in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use in later Jewish interpretation by Rabbinic and later Jewish tradition (later Second Temple and after)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} The Song is less about major textual divergence than poetic translation nuance between Hebrew and Greek.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives the Song as inspired Solomonic poetry honoring God-ordained love and marriage, without denying its place in the larger redemptive canon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Song of Songs 1}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The Song of songs, which is Solomon's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for your breasts are better than wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the smell of your ointments is better than all spices: your name is ointment poured forth; therefore do the young maidens love you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They have drawn you: we will run after you, for the smell of your ointments: the king has brought me into closet: let us rejoice and be glad in you; we will love your breasts more than wine: righteousness loves you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I am black, but beautiful, you⌃ daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Look not upon me, because I am dark, because the sun has looked unfavourably upon me: my mother's sons strove with me; they made me keeper in the vineyards; I have not kept my own vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Tell me, [you] whom my soul loves, where you tend your flock, where you cause [them] to rest at noon, lest I become as one that is veiled by the flocks of your companions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If you know not yourself, you fair one among women, go you forth by the footsteps of the flocks, and feed your kids by the shepherd's tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} I have likened you, my companion, to my horses in the chariots of Pharao. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} How are your cheeks beautiful as [those] of a dove, your neck as chains! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} We will make you figures of gold with studs of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So long as the king was at table, my spikenard gave forth its smell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} My kinsman is to me a bundle of myrrh; he shall lie between my breasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} My kinsman is to me a cluster of camphor in the vineyards of Engaddi. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Behold, you are fair, my companion; behold, you are fair; your eyes are doves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Behold, you are fair, my kinsman, yes, beautiful, overshadowing our bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The beams of our house are cedars, our ceilings are of cypress.\par

\subsection*{Song of Songs 2}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I am a flower of the plain, a lily of the valleys. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} As a lily among thorns, so is my companion among the daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} As the apple among the trees of the wood, so is my kinsman among the sons. I desired his shadow, and sat down, and his fruit was sweet in my throat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Bring me into the wine house; set love before me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Strengthen me with perfumes, stay me with apples: for I [am] wounded with love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} His left [hand shall be] under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I have charged you, you⌃ daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the virtues of the field, that you⌃ do not rouse or wake [my] love, until he please. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The voice of my kinsman! behold, he comes leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} My kinsman is like a roe or a young hart on the mountains of Baethel: behold, he is behind our wall, looking through the windows, peeping through the lattices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} My kinsman answers, and says to me, Rise up, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For, behold, the winter is past, the rain is gone, it has departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The flowers are seen in the land; the time of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtle-dove has been heard in our land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The fig tree has put forth its young figs, the vines put forth the tender grape, they yield a smell: arise, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove; yes, come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [You are] my dove, in the shelter of the rock, near the wall: show me your face, and cause me to hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is beautiful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Take us the little foxes that spoil the vines: for our vines put forth tender grapes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} My kinsman is mine, and I am his: he feeds [his flock] among the lilies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Until the day dawn, and the shadows depart, turn, my kinsman, be you like to a roe or young hart on the mountains of the ravines.\par
