\subsection*{Song of Songs 3}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but found him not; I called him, but he listened not to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I will rise now, and go about in the city, in the marketplaces, and in the streets, and I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The watchmen who go their rounds in the city found me. [I said], Have you⌃ seen him whom my soul loves? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} [It was] as a little [while] after I parted from them, that I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and did not let him go, until I brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I have charged you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the virtues of the field, that you⌃ rouse not nor awake [my] love, until he please. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who is this that comes up from the wilderness as pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the perfumer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold Solomon's bed; sixty mighty men of the mighty ones of Israel are round about it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They all hold a sword, being expert in war: every man [has] his sword upon his thigh because of fear by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} King Solomon made himself a litter of woods of Lebanon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He made the pillars of it silver, the bottom of it gold, the covering of it scarlet, in the midst of it a pavement of love, for the daughters of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Go forth, you⌃ daughters of Sion, and behold king Solomon, with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him, in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} will rise; the streets, ; I sought \textsuperscript{4} but; I held; I had \textsuperscript{6} this; like Probably the clouds of incense arising from the palanquin, which seemed like pillars of smoke.; perfumed \textsuperscript{9} a chariot or, a bed, Appiryon, rendered by Montanus, sponsarum ithalamum, "a nuptial bed; " but probably it denotes a kind of palanquin, perhaps synonymous with the Arabic farfar, a species of vehicle for women. \textsuperscript{11} Go; O ye; behold; his mother; in the day of his; in the day of the\par}

\subsection*{Song of Songs 4}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold, you are fair, my companion; behold, you are fair; your eyes are doves, beside your veil: your hair is as flocks of goats, that have appeared from Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Your teeth are as flocks of shorn [sheep], that have gone up from the washing; all of them bearing twins, and there is not a barren one among them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Your lips are as a thread of scarlet, and your speech is comely: like the rind of a pomegranate is your cheek without your veil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Your neck is as the tower of David, that was built for an armory: a thousand shields hang upon it, [and] all darts of mighty men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Your two breasts are as two twin fawns, that feed among the lilies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Until the day dawn, and the shadows depart, I will betake me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You are all fair, my companion, and there is no spot in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Come from Libanus, [my] bride, come from Libanus: you shall come and pass from the top of Faith, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} My sister, [my] spouse, you have ravished my heart; you have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} How beautiful are your breasts, my sister, my spouse! how much more beautiful are your breasts than wine, and the smell of your garments than all spices! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Your lips drop honeycomb, my spouse: honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your garments is as the smell of Libanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} My sister, [my] spouse is a garden enclosed; a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Your shoots are a garden of pomegranates, with the fruit of choice berries; camphor, with spikenard: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon; with all woods of Libanus, myrrh, aloes, with all chief spices: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} a fountain of a garden, and a well of water springing and gurgling from Libanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Awake, O north wind; and come, O south; and blow through my garden, and let my spices flow out.\par

\subsection*{Song of Songs 5}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Let my kinsman come down into his garden, and eat the fruit of his choice berries. I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spices; I have eaten my bread with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; yes, brethren, drink abundantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I sleep, but my heart is awake: the voice of my kinsman knocks at the door, [saying], Open, open to me, my companion, my sister, my dove, my perfect one: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} My kinsman put forth his hand by the hole [of the door], and my belly moved for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I rose up to open to my kinsman; my hands dropped myrrh, my fingers choice myrrh, on the handles of the lock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I opened to my kinsman; my kinsman was gone: my soul failed at his speech: I sought him, but found him not; I called him, but he answered me not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The watchman that go their rounds in the city found me, they struck me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I have charged you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the virtues of the field: if you⌃ should find my kinsman, what are you⌃ to say to him? That I am wounded with love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} What is your kinsman [more] than [another] kinsman, O you beautiful among women? what is your kinsman [more] than [another] kinsman, that you have so charged us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} My kinsman is white and ruddy, chosen out from myriads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} His head is [as] very fine gold, his locks are flowing, black as a raven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} His eyes are as doves, by the pools of waters, washed with milk, sitting by the pools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} His cheeks are as bowls of spices pouring forth perfumes: his lips are lilies, dropping choice myrrh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} His hands are as turned gold set with beryl: his belly is an ivory tablet on a sapphire stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} His legs are marble pillars set on golden sockets: his form is as Libanus, choice as the cedars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} His throat is most sweet, and altogether desirable. This is my kinsman, and this is my companion, O daughters of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Whither is your kinsman gone, you beautiful among women? whither has your kinsman turned aside? [tell us], and we will seek him with you.\par

\subsection*{Song of Songs 6}
\markright{SONG OF SONGS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My kinsman is gone down to his garden, to the beds of spice, to feed [his flock] in the gardens, and to gather lilies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I am my kinsman's, and my kinsman is mine, who feeds among the lilies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You are fair, my companion, as Pleasure, beautiful as Jerusalem, terrible as [armies] set in array. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Turn away your eyes from before me, for they have ravished me: your hair is as flocks of goats which have appeared from Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Your teeth are as flocks of shorn [sheep], that have gone up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and there is none barren among them: your lips are as a thread of scarlet, and your speech is comely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Your cheek is like the rind of a pomegranate, [being seen] without your veil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and maidens without number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} My dove, my perfect one is one; she is the [only] one of her mother; she is the choice of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and the queens will pronounce her blessed, yes, and the concubines, and they will praise her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who is this that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, choice as the sun, terrible as [armies] set in array? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I went down to the garden of nuts, to look at the fruits of the valley, to see if the vine flowered, [if] the pomegranates blossomed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} There I will give you my breasts: my soul knew [it] not: it made me as the chariots of Aminadab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Return, return, O Sunamite; return, return, and we will look at you. \section*{Isaiah Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Isaiah son of Amoz\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book repeatedly names Isaiah son of Amoz, and conservative scholarship receives the whole canonical book as Isaianic prophecy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} John 12:38-41 cites both Isaiah 53 and Isaiah 6 as Isaiah; Matthew 13:14; Acts 28:25; Romans 10:16,20 all treat Isaiah as the prophet speaking these words.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 8th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} ca. 740-680 BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT chronology places Isaiah in the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The LXX preserves the same prophetic horizon, though Isaiah is one of the major books where Greek renderings can significantly shape later quotation and interpretation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Judah in the Assyrian crisis, with prophecy reaching far beyond to exile, restoration, and Messiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To announce the Holy One's judgment on sin and His salvation through the coming Servant-King.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} holiness; judgment; remnant; Messiah; servant; Zion; new creation\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Oracles of judgment and hope 1-39; Comfort and redemption 40-55; Restoration and consummation 56-66. 1Q Isaiah a, the Great Isaiah Scroll | Subst. 2nd century BC 1Q Isaiah a is an almost complete early Hebrew witness; 1Q Isaiah b and others also survive | Heb. 2nd-1st centuries BC Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Isaiah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Extensive use in later Jewish literature and the NT (Multiple)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2nd century BC onward\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Isaiah is a premier book for MT/LXX and NT quotation study because both traditions are richly attested and frequently cited.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Esaias}
\markboth{ESAIAS}{}
\subsection*{Esaias 1}
\markright{ESAIAS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The vision which Esaias the son of Amos saw, which he saw against Juda, and against Jerusalem, in the reign of Ozias, and Joatham, and Achaz, and Ezekias, who reigned over Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear, O heaven, and listen, O earth: for the Lord has spoken, [saying], I have begotten and reared up children, but they have rebelled against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The ox knows his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel does not know me, and the people has not regarded me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Ah sinful nation, a people full of sins, an evil seed, lawless children: you⌃ have forsaken the Lord, and provoked the Holy One of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Why should you⌃ be struck [any] more, transgressing more and more? the whole head is pained, and the whole heart sad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} From the feet to the head, there is no soundness in them; neither wound, nor bruise, nor festering ulcer [are healed]: it is not possible to apply a plaister, nor oil, nor bandages. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is made desolate, overthrown by strange nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The daughter of Sion shall be deserted as a tent in a vineyard, and as a storehouse of fruits in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And if the Lord of Sabaoth had not left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been made like Gomorrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Hear the word of the Lord, you⌃ rulers of Sodoma; attend to the law of God, you people of Gomorrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Of what [value] to me is the abundance of your sacrifices? says the Lord: I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams; and I delight not in the fat of lambs, and the blood of bulls and goats: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} neither shall you⌃ come [with these] to appear before me; for who has required these things at your hands? You⌃ shall no more tread my court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Though you⌃ bring fine flour, [it is] vain; incense is an abomination to me; I can’t bear your new moons, and your sabbaths, and the great day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [your] fasting, and rest from work, your new moons also, and your feasts my soul hates: you⌃ have become loathsome to me; I will no more pardon your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} When you⌃ stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes from you: and though you⌃ make many supplications, I will not listen to you; for your hands are full of blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Wash you, be clean; remove your iniquities from your souls before my eyes; cease from your iniquities; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} learn to do well; diligently seek judgment, deliver him that is suffering wrong, plead for the orphan, and obtain justice for the widow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And come, let us reason together, says the Lord: and though your sins be as purple, I will make them white as snow; and though they be as scarlet, I will make [them] white as wool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if you⌃ be willing, and listen to me, you⌃ shall eat the good of the land: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} but if you⌃ be not willing, nor listen to me, a sword shall devour you: for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} How has the faithful city Sion, [once] full of judgment, become a harlot! wherein righteousness lodged, but now murderers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Your silver is worthless, your wine merchants mix the wine with water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Your princes are rebellious, companions of thieves, loving bribes, seeking after rewards; not pleading for orphans, and not heeding the cause of widows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord of hosts, Woe to the mighty [men] of Israel; for my wrath shall not cease against my adversaries, and I will execute judgment on my enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I will bring my hand upon you, and purge you completely, and I will destroy the rebellious, and will take away from you all transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And I will establish your judges as before, and your counselors as at the beginning: and afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful mother-city of Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For her captives shall be saved with judgment, and with mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the transgressors and the sinners shall be crushed together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be utterly consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For they shall be ashamed of their idols, which they delighted in, and they are made ashamed of the gardens which they coveted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For they shall be as a turpentine tree that has cast its leaves, and as a garden that has no water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And their strength shall be as a thread of tow, and their works as sparks, and the transgressors and the sinners shall be burnt up together, and there shall be none to quench [them].\par

\subsection*{Esaias 2}
\markright{ESAIAS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The word which came to Esaias the son of Amos concerning Judea, and concerning Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be glorious, and the house of God [shall be] on the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall come to it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And many nations shall go and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will tell us his way, and we will walk in it: for out of Sion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord out of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles: and nation shall not take up sword against nation, neither shall they learn to war any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And now, O house of Jacob, come, [and] let us walk in the light of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For he has forsaken his people the house of Israel, because their land is filled as at the beginning with divinations, as the [land] of the Philistines, and many strange children were born to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For their land is filled with silver and gold, and there was no number of their treasures; their land also is filled with horses, and there was no number of chariots. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the land is filled with abominations, [even] the works of their hands; and they have worshipped [the works] which their fingers made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the mean man bowed down, and the great man was humbled: and I will not pardon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now therefore enter you⌃ into the rocks, and hide yourselves in the earth, for fear of the Lord, and by reason of the glory of his might, when he shall arise to strike terribly the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the eyes of the Lord are high, but man is low; and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and haughty, and upon every one that is high and towering, and they shall be brought down; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and upon every cedar of Libanus, of them that are high and towering, and upon every oak of Basan, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and upon every high tower, and upon every high wall, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and upon every ship of the sea, and upon every display of fine ships. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And every man shall be brought low, and the pride of men shall fall: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall hide all [idols] made with hands, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} having carried [them] into the caves, and into the clefts of the rocks, and into the caverns of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and by reason of the glory of his might, when he shall arise to strike terribly the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For in that day a man shall cast forth his silver and gold abominations, which they made [in order] to worship vanities and bats; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} to enter into the caverns of the solid rock, and into the clefts of the rocks, for fear of the Lord, and by reason of the glory of his might, when he shall arise to strike terribly the earth.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 3}
\markright{ESAIAS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold now, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, will take away from Jerusalem and from Judea the mighty man and mighty woman, the strength of bread, and the strength of water, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} the great and mighty man, the warrior and the judge, and the prophet, and the counsellor, and the elder, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the captain of fifty also, and the honorable counsellor, and the wise artificer, and the intelligent hearer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will make youths their princes, and mockers shall have dominion over them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the people shall fall, man upon man, and [every] man upon his neighbor: the child shall insult the elder man, and the base the honorable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For a man shall lay hold of his brother, as one of his father's household, saying, You have raiment, be you our ruler, and let my meat be under you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he shall answer in that day, and say, I will not be your ruler; for I have no bread in my house, nor raiment: I will not be the ruler of this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judea has fallen, and their tongues [have spoken] with iniquity, disobedient [as they are] towards the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore now their glory has been brought low, and the shame of their countenance has withstood them, and they have proclaimed their sin as Sodom, and made it manifest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Woe to their soul, for they have devised an evil counsel against themselves, saying against themselves, Let us bind the just, for he is burdensome to us: therefore shall they eat the fruits of their works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Woe to the transgressor! evils shall happen to him according to the works of his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O my people, your exactors strip you, and extortioners rule over you: O my people, they that pronounce you blessed lead you astray, and pervert the path of your feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But now the Lord will stand up for judgment, and will enter into judgment with his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The Lord himself shall enter into judgment with the elders of the people, and with their rulers: but why have you⌃ set my vineyard on fire, and [why is] the spoil of the poor in your houses? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Why do you⌃ wrong my people, and shame the face of the poor? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus says the Lord, Because the daughters of Sion are haughty, and have walked with an outstretched neck, and with winking of the eyes, and motion of the feet, at the same time drawing their garments in trains, and at the same time sporting with their feet: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} therefore the Lord will humble the chief daughters of Sion, and the Lord will expose their form in that day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and the Lord will take away the glory of their raiment, the curls and the fringes, and the crescents, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the chains, and the ornaments of their faces, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and the array of glorious ornaments, and the armlets, and the bracelets, and the wreathed work, and the finger-rings, and the ornaments for the right hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and the ear-rings, and the garments with scarlet borders, and the garments with purple grounds, and the shawls to be worn in the house, and the Spartan transparent dresses, and those made of fine linen, and the purple [ones], and the scarlet [ones], and the fine linen, interwoven with gold and purple, and the light coverings for couches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And there shall be instead of a sweet smell, dust; and instead of a girdle, you shall gird yourself with a rope; and instead of a golden ornament for the head, you shall have baldness on account of your works; and instead of a tunic with a scarlet ground, you shall gird yourself with sackcloth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And your most beautiful son whom you love shall fall by the sword; and your mighty men shall fall by the sword, and shall be brought low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the stores of your ornaments shall mourn, and you shall be left alone, and shall be levelled with the ground.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} behold the Lord, the stay \textsuperscript{3} captain; the honourable man Heb. a man eminent in countenance, eloquent orator or, skilful of speech \textsuperscript{7} swear Heb. lift up the hand; healer Heb. binder up; neither bread Princes and great men in the East, as Sir J. Chardin testifies, are obliged to have a great stock of clothes in readiness for presents on all occasions; and a great quantity of provisions for the table is equally necessary (see . ). Hence the person desired to undertake the government, alleges as an excuse that he is not able to support the dignity of his station. \textsuperscript{9} The show; and they declare, ; Woe \textsuperscript{10} Say ye; they shall eat \textsuperscript{11} Woe, ; for the reward; given him Heb. done to him \textsuperscript{12} children; lead thee or, which call thee blessed; destroy Heb. swallow up \textsuperscript{14} enter; the ancients ye have eaten or, ye have burnt \textsuperscript{16} the daughters; are haughty; wanton eyes Heb. deceiving with their eyes, Or, as messakkaroth ainayim is rendered in the Targum, "painting their eyes with stibium": for sakar is probably the same as the Chaldee sekar or that import. mincing or, tripping nicely and making The Eastern ladies wear on their ankles large rings to which smaller ones are attached, which make a tinkling sound as they move nimbly. \textsuperscript{17} smite; discover Heb. made naked \textsuperscript{18} tinkling ornaments cauls or, networks, Shevisim probably the rich embroidered kerchiefs used to bind on their caps on the head, described by Lady M. W. Montague, Let. 32. round tires *marg. \textsuperscript{19} chains or, sweet-balls, Neteephoth earrings or drops; in Arabic, netafaṫ the bracelets, ; mufflers or, spangled ornaments \textsuperscript{20} tablets Heb. houses of the soul, Probably perfume boxes, as rendered by Bp. Lowth. the earrings Lechashim probably amulets. \textsuperscript{22} The changeable suits Machalatzoth probably loose robes, used according to the weather. \textsuperscript{24} instead; baldness; a girding;, ; burning\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 4}
\markright{ESAIAS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own raiment: only let your name be called upon us, [and] take away our reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And in that day God shall shine gloriously in counsel on the earth, to exalt and glorify the remnant of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it shall be, [that] the remnant left in Sion, and the remnant left in Jerusalem, [even] all that are appointed to life in Jerusalem, shall be called holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the Lord shall wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Sion, and shall purge out the blood from the midst of them, with the spirit of judgment, and the spirit of burning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shall come, and it shall be with regard to every place of mount Sion, yes, all the region round about it shall a cloud overshadow by day, and [there shall be] as it were the smoke and light of fire burning by night: and upon all the glory shall be a defence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it shall be for a shadow from the heat, and as a shelter and a hiding place from inclemency [of weather] and from rain.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And in, ; seven, We will eat let us be called by thy name Heb. let thy name be called upon us to take away or, take thou away reproach \textsuperscript{2} the branch; beautiful and glorious Heb. beauty and glory; the fruit, ; them that are escaped Heb. the escaping \textsuperscript{3} shall be, ; written; , ; among the living or, to life \textsuperscript{4} washed away;, ; have purged; by the spirit \textsuperscript{5} upon every; a cloud, ; upon or, above all the glory, ; a defence Heb. a covering\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 5}
\markright{ESAIAS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now I will sing to [my] beloved a song of my beloved concerning my vineyard. [My] beloved had a vineyard on a high hill in a fertile place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I made a hedge round it, and dug a trench, and planted a choice vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and dug a place for the wine-vat in it: and I waited [for it] to bring forth grapes, and it brought forth thorns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And now, you⌃ dwellers in Jerusalem, and [every] man of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} What shall I do any more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it? Whereas I expected [it] to bring forth grapes, but it has brought forth thorns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it shall be for a spoil; and I will pull down its walls, and it shall be [left] to be trodden down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will forsake my vineyard; and it shall not be pruned, nor dug, and thorns shall come up upon it as on barren land; and I will command the clouds to rain no rain upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Juda [his] beloved plant: I expected [it] to bring forth judgment, and it brought forth iniquity; and not righteousness, but a cry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Woe [to them] that join house to house, and add field to field, that they may take away something of their neighbor's: will you⌃ dwell alone upon the land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For these things have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts: for though many houses should be built, many and fair houses shall be desolate, and there shall be no inhabitants in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For where ten yoke of oxen plow [the land] shall yield one , and he that sows six homers shall produce three measures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Woe [to them] that rise up in the morning, and follow strong drink; who wait [at it till] evening: for the wine shall inflame them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For they drink wine with harp, and lute, and drums, and pipes: but they regard not the works of the Lord, and consider not the works of his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore my people have been taken captive, because they know not the Lord: and there has been a multitude of dead [bodies], because of hunger and of thirst for water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore hell has enlarged its desire and opened its mouth without ceasing: and her glorious and great, and her rich and her pestilent men shall go down [into it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the mean man shall be brought low, and the great man shall be disgraced, and the lofty eyes shall be brought low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy God shall be glorified in righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they that were spoiled shall be fed as bulls, and lambs shall feed on the waste places of them that are taken away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Woe [to them] that draw sins to them as with a long rope, and iniquities as with a thong of the heifer's yoke: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} who say, Let him speedily hasten what he will do, that we may see [it]: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, that we may know [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Woe [to them] that call evil good, and good evil; who make darkness light, and light darkness; who make bitter sweet, and sweet bitter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Woe [to them] that are wise in their own conceit, and knowing in their own sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Woe to the strong [ones] of you that drink wine, and the mighty [ones] that mingle strong drink: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} who justify the ungodly for rewards, and take away the righteousness of the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore as stubble shall be burnt by a coal of fire, and shall be consumed by a violent flame, their root shall be as chaff, and their flower shall go up as dust: for they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts, and insulted the word of the Holy One of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore the Lord of hosts was greatly angered against his people, and he reached forth his hand upon them, and struck them: and the mountains were troubled, and their carcasses were as dung in the midst of the way: yet for all this his anger has not been turned away, but his hand is yet raised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore shall he lift up a signal to the nations that are afar, and shall hiss for them from the end of the earth; and, behold, they are coming very quickly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} They shall not hunger nor be weary, neither shall they slumber nor sleep; neither shall they loose their girdles from their loins, neither shall their shoe-latchets be broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Whose arrows are sharp, and their bows bent; their horses' hoofs are counted as solid rock: their chariot-wheels are as a storm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} They rage as lions, and draw near as a lion's whelps: and he shall seize, and roar as a wild beast, and he shall cast [them] forth, and there shall be none to deliver them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he shall roar on account of them in that day, as the sound of the swelling sea; and they shall look to the land, and, behold, [there shall be] thick darkness in their perplexity.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Now; wellbeloved, touching; a very fruitful hill Heb. the horn of the son of oil \textsuperscript{2} fenced it or, made a wall about it; planted the choicest vine Sorek in Arabic, sharik certainly denotes an excellent vine; but some with Bp. Lowth, retain it as a proper name. \subsection*{Esaias 6}
\markright{ESAIAS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the year in which king Ozias died, [that] I saw the Lord sitting on a high and exalted throne, and the house was full of his glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And seraphs stood round about him: each one had six wings: and with two they covered [their] face, and with two they covered [their] feet, and with two they flew. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And one cried to the other, and they said, Holy, holy, holy [is the] Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the lintel shook at the voice they uttered, and the house was filled with smoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I said, Woe is me, for I am pricked to the heart; for being a man, and having unclean lips, I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips; and I have seen with my eyes the King, the Lord of hosts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there was sent to me one of the seraphs, and he had in his hand a coal, which he had taken off the altar with the tongs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and he touched my mouth, and said, Behold, this has touched your lips, and will take away your iniquities, and will purge off your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said, behold, I am [here], send me. And he said, Go, and say to this people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You⌃ shall hear indeed, but you⌃ shall not understand; and you⌃ shall see indeed, but you⌃ shall not perceive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the heart of this people has become gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I said, How long, O Lord? And he said, Until cities be deserted by reason of their not being inhabited, and the houses by reason of there being no men, and the land shall be left desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And after this God shall remove the men far off, and they that are left upon the land shall be multiplied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And yet there shall be a tenth upon it, and again it shall be for a spoil, as a turpentine tree, and as an acorn when it falls out of its husk.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3245, bc 759 the year, Azariah, I saw also; sitting; , ; high; his train or, the skirts thereof filled \textsuperscript{2} stood; seraphims; wings;, ; covered his face; his feet; did fly \textsuperscript{3} one cried unto another Heb. this cried to this; Holy; the whole earth etc. Heb. his glory is the fulness of the whole earth \textsuperscript{4} posts; door Heb. thresholds the house \textsuperscript{5} said I; undone Heb. cut off a man, ; I dwell; mine eyes \textsuperscript{6} flew; having etc. Heb. and in his hand a live coal; which \textsuperscript{7} he laid it upon Heb. caused it to touch; thine iniquity \textsuperscript{8} I heard; Whom; us, Then; Here am I Heb. Behold me \textsuperscript{9} Go; Hear ye; indeed or, without ceasing, Heb. in hearing indeed Heb. in seeing. \textsuperscript{10} the heart;, ; fat; ears heavy; lest; convert \textsuperscript{11} Lord, Until the, utterly desolate Heb. desolate with desolation \textsuperscript{13} But yet, ; and it shall return etc. or, when it is returned, and hath been broused teil tree The teil-tree is the linden or lime-tree, a species very common in Palestine; the leaf of which resembles that of the laurel, and its flower that of the olive. But the original ailah which our translators render the oak (but here distinguished from allon the oak), and Bp. Lowth the ilex in, probably denotes, as Celsius contends, the terebintḣ It is an evergreen of moderate size, but having the top and branches large in proportion to the trunk; leaves, like those of the olive, but green intermixed with red and purple; flowers, like those of the vine, growing in bunches, and purple; fruit, of a ruddy purple, the size of a juniper berry, hanging in clusters, very juicy, and containing a single seed of the size of a grape stone; wood, hard and fibrous, from which a resin distils; with an excresence scattered among the leaves, of the size of a chestnut, of a purple colour, variegated with green and white. substance or, stock, or stem, so the holy\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 7}
\markright{ESAIAS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the days of Achaz [the son] of Joatham, the son of Ozias, king of Juda, there came up Rasim king of Aram, and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, against Jerusalem to war against it, but they could not take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And a message was brought to the house of David, saying, Aram has conspired with Ephraim. And his soul was amazed, and the soul of his people, as in a wood a tree is moved by the wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord said to Esaias, Go forth to meet Achaz, you, and your son Jasub who is left, to the pool of the upper way of the fuller's field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall say to him, Take care to be quiet, and fear not, neither let your soul be disheartened because of these two smoking firebrands: for when my fierce anger is over, I will heal again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And [as for] the son of Aram, and the son of Romelias, forasmuch as they have devised an evil counsel, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} We will go up against Judea, and having conferred with them we will turn them away to our side, and we will make the son of Tabeel king of it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} thus says the Lord of hosts, This counsel shall not abide, nor come to pass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus, Rasim; and yet within sixty and five years the kingdom of Ephraim shall cease from [being] a people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the head of Ephraim is Somoron, and the head of Somoron the son of Romelias: but if you⌃ believe not, neither will you⌃ at all understand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord again spoke to Achaz, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Ask for yourself a sign of the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Achaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said, Hear you⌃ now, O house of David; is it a little thing for you to contend with men? and how do you⌃ contend against the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb, and shall bring forth a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Butter and honey shall he eat, before he knows either to prefer evil [or] choose the good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For before the child shall know good or evil, he refuses evil, to choose the good; and the land shall be forsaken which you are afraid of because of the two kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But God shall bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days which have never come, from the day that Ephraim took away from Juda the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall hiss for the flies, which [insect] shall rule over a part of the river of Egypt, and for the bee which is in the land of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they all shall enter into the clefts of the land, and into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves, and into every ravine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In that day the Lord shall shave with the hired razor of the king of Assyria beyond the river the head, and the hairs of the feet, and will remove the beard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] a man shall rear a heifer, and two sheep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And it shall come to pass from their drinking an abundance of milk, [that] every one that is left on the land shall eat butter and honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [for] every place where there shall be a thousand vines at a thousand shekels, they shall become barren land and thorns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} [Men] shall enter there with arrow and bow; for all the land shall be [barren] ground and thorns. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And every mountain shall be certainly plowed: there shall no fear come there: for there shall be from [among] the [barren] ground and thorns that whereon cattle shall feed and oxen shall tread.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the days; Rezin; but could \textsuperscript{2} the house, ; is confederate with Heb. resteth on, ; And his heart \textsuperscript{3} Go forth; Shearjashub that is, The remnant shall return, ; the end; highway or, causeway \textsuperscript{4} Take heed; fear not, ; neither be fainthearted Heb. let not they heart be tender; the two tails \textsuperscript{6} vex or, waken, lit, disgust \textsuperscript{8} For the head Dr. Jubb transposes the former part of, and renders, "Though the head of Syria be Damascus; and the head of Damascus Retzin; and the head of Ephraim be Samaria; and the head of Samaria Remaliah's son; yet within threescore and five years Ephraim shall be broken, that he be no more a people." This renders the passage perfectly clear; and the prophecy received its full accomplishment when Esarhaddon carried away the remains of the ten tribes. within; that it be not a people Heb. from a people \textsuperscript{9} the head; If ye etc. or, ye not believe, it is because ye are not stable \textsuperscript{10} Moreover etc. Heb. and the Lord added to speak, ; *marg. \textsuperscript{11} a sign, ; ask it either in the depth or, make thy petition deep \textsuperscript{12} I will not ask; neither tempt \textsuperscript{13} O house; Is it a small;, to weary; will ye \textsuperscript{14} Behold; shall call or, thou, O virgin shall call, ; Immanuel \textsuperscript{15} Butter Connecting this verse with the preceding and following, we may render with Dr. Jubb and Lowth, "Behold the virgin ( haalmah as the word uniformly signifies; ) shall conceive and bear a son, and thou shalt call his name Immanuel; butter and honey shall he eat when he shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good. \subsection*{Esaias 8}
\markright{ESAIAS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord said to me, Take to yourself a volume of a great new [book], and write in it with a man's pen concerning the making a rapid plunder of spoils; for it is near at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And make me witnesses [of] faithful men, Urias, and Zacharias the son of Barachias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I went in to the prophetess; and she conceived, and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, Call his name, Spoil quickly, plunder speedily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For before the child shall know [how] to call [his] father or [his] mother, [one] shall take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord spoke to me yet again, [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Because this people chooses not the water of Siloam that goes softly, but wills to have Rassin, and the son of Romelias [to be] king over you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} therefore, behold, the Lord brings up upon you the water of the river, strong and abundant, [even] the king of the Assyrians, and his glory: and he shall come up over every valley of yours, and shall walk over every wall of yours: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and he shall take away from Juda [every] man who shall be able to lift up his head, [and every one] able to accomplish anything; and his camp shall fill the breadth of your land, [O] God with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Know, you⌃ Gentiles, and be conquered; listen you⌃, even to the extremity of the earth: be conquered, after you⌃ strengthened yourselves; for even if you⌃ should again strengthen yourselves, you⌃ shall again be conquered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And whatever counsel you⌃ shall take, the Lord shall bring it to nothing; and whatever word you⌃ shall speak, it shall not stand among you: for God is with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus says the Lord, With a strong hand they revolt from the course of the way of this people, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let them not say, [It is] hard, for whatever this people says, is hard: but fear not you⌃ their fear, neither be dismayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Sanctify you⌃ the Lord himself; and he shall be your fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if you shall trust in him, he shall be to you for a sanctuary; and you⌃ shall not come against [him] as against a stumbling-stone, neither as against the falling of a rock: but the houses of Jacob are in a snare, and the dwellers in Jerusalem in a pit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore many among them shall be weak, and fall, and be crushed; and they shall draw near, and men shall be taken securely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then shall those who seal themselves that they may not learn the law be made manifest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And [one] shall say, I will wait for God, who has turned away his face from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold I and the children which God has given me: and they shall be [for] signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells in mount Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if they should say to you, Seek those who have in them a divining spirit, and them that speak out of the earth, them that speak vain words, who speak out of their belly: shall not a nation diligently seek to their God? why do they seek to the dead concerning the living? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For he has given the law for a help, that they should not speak according to this word, concerning which there are no gifts to give for it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And famine shall come sorely upon you, and it shall come to pass, [that] when you⌃ shall be hungry, you⌃ shall be grieved, and you⌃ shall speak ill of the prince and your fathers' ordinances: and they shall look up to heaven above, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} and they shall look on the earth below, and behold severe distress, and darkness, affliction, and anguish, and darkness so that [one can’t] see; and he that is in anguish shall not be distressed only for a time.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 9}
\markright{ESAIAS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Drink this first. Act quickly, O land of Zabulon, land of Nephthalim, and the rest [inhabiting] the sea-coast, and [the land] beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} O people walking in darkness, behold a great light: you⌃ that dwell in the region [and] shadow of death, a light shall shine upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The multitude of the people which you have brought down in your joy, they shall even rejoice before you as they that rejoice in harvest, and as they that divide the spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Because the yoke that was laid upon them has been taken away, and the rod that was on their neck: for he has broken the rod of the exactors, as in the day of Madiam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For they shall compensate for every garment that has been acquired by deceit, and [all] raiment with restitution; and they shall be willing, [even] if they were burnt with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us, whose government is upon his shoulder: and his name is called the Messenger of great counsel: for I will bring peace upon the princes, and health to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} His government shall be great, and of his peace there is no end: [it shall be] upon the throne of David, and [upon] his kingdom, to establish it, and to support [it] with judgment and with righteousness, from henceforth and forever. The seal of the Lord of hosts shall perform this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Lord has sent death upon Jacob, and it has come upon Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And all the people of Ephraim, and they that lived in Samaria shall know, who say in their pride and lofty heart, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The bricks are fallen down, but come, let us hew stones, and cut down sycamores and cedars, and let us build for ourselves a tower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God shall dash down them that rise up against him on mount Sion, and shall scatter his enemies; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [even] Syria from the rising of the sun, and the Greeks from the setting of the sun, who devour Israel with open mouth. For all this [his] anger is not turned away, but still [his] hand is exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But the people turned not until they were struck, and they sought not the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So the Lord took away from Israel the head and tail, great and small, in one day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} the old man, and them that respect persons, this is the head; and the prophet teaching unlawful things, he is the tail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they that pronounce this people blessed shall mislead them; and they mislead them that they may devour them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore the Lord shall not take pleasure in their young men, neither shall he have pity on their orphans or on their widows: for they are all transgressors and wicked, and every mouth speaks unjustly. For all this [his] anger is not turned away, but [his] hand is yet exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And iniquity shall burn as fire, and shall be devoured by fire as dry grass: and it shall burn in the thickets of the wood, and shall devour all that is round about the hills. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The whole earth is set on fire because of the fierce anger of the Lord, and the people shall be as men burnt by fire: no man shall pity his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But [one] shall turn aside to the right hand, for he shall be hungry; and shall eat on the left, and a man shall by no means be satisfied with eating the flesh of his own arm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For Manasses shall eat [the flesh] of Ephraim, and Ephraim [the flesh] of Manasses; for they shall besiege Juda together. For all this [his] anger is not turned away, but [his] hand is yet exalted.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 10}
\markright{ESAIAS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to them that write wickedness; for when they write they do write wickedness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} perverting the cause of the poor, violently wresting the judgment of the needy ones of my people, that the widow may be a prey to them, and the orphan a spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And what will they do in the day of visitation? for affliction shall come to you from afar: and to whom will you⌃ flee for help? and where will you⌃ leave your glory, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} that you⌃ may not fall into captivity? For all this [his] wrath is not turned away, but [his] hand is yet exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Woe to the Assyrians; the rod of my wrath, and anger are in their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I will send my wrath against a sinful nation, and I will charge my people to take plunder and spoil, and to trample the cities, and to make them dust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But he meant not thus, neither did he devise thus in his soul: but his mind shall change, and [that] to destroy nations not a few. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if they should say to him, You alone are ruler; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} then shall he say, Have I not taken the country above Babylon and Chalanes, where the tower was built? and have I [not] taken Arabia, and Damascus, and Samaria? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As I have taken them, I will also take all the kingdoms: howl, you⌃ idols in Jerusalem, and in Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For as I did to Samaria and her idols, so will I do also to Jerusalem and her idols. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall come to pass, when the Lord shall have finished doing all things on Mount Sion and Jerusalem, [that] I will visit upon the proud heart, [even] upon the ruler of the Assyrians, and upon the boastful haughtiness of his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For he said, I will act in strength, and in the wisdom of [my] understanding I will remove the boundaries of nations, and will spoil their strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will shake the inhabited cities: and I will take with my hand all the world as a nest: and I will even take them as eggs that have been left; and there is none that shall escape me, or contradict me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Shall the axe glorify itself without him that hews with it? or shall the saw lift up itself without him that uses it, as if one should lift a rod or staff? but it shall not be so; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} but the Lord of hosts shall send dishonor upon your honor, and burning fire shall be kindled upon your glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and he shall sanctify him with burning fire, and it shall devour the wood as grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} In that day the mountains shall be consumed, and the hills, and the forests, and [fire] shall devour [both] soul and body: and he that flees shall be as one fleeing from burning flame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they that are left of them shall be a [small] number, and a child shall write them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it shall come to pass in that day [that] the remnant of Israel shall no more join themselves with, and the saved of Jacob shall no more trust in, them that injured them; but they shall trust in the Holy God of Israel, in truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the remnant of Jacob shall [trust] on the mighty God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And though the people of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them shall be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because the Lord will make a short work in all the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, Be not afraid, my people who dwell in Sion, of the Assyrians, because he shall strike you with a rod: for I am bringing a stroke upon you, that [you] may see the way of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For yet a little while, and the indignation shall cease: but my wrath shall be against their council. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And God will stir up [enemies] against them, according to the stroke of Madiam in the place of affliction: and his wrath shall be by the way of the sea, [even] to the way that leads to Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] his yoke shall be taken away from your shoulder, and his fear from you, and the yoke shall be destroyed from off your shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For he shall arrive at the city of Angai, and shall pass on to Maggedo, and shall lay up his stores in Machmas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he shall pass by the valley, and shall arrive at Angai: fear shall seize upon Rama, the city of Saul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The daughter of Gallim shall flee; Laisa shall hear; one shall hear in Anathoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Madebena also is amazed, and the inhabitants of Gibbir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Exhort you⌃ [them] today to remain in the way: exhort you⌃ [beckoning] with the hand the mountain, the daughter of Sion, even you⌃ hills that are in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, will mightily confound the glorious ones; and the haughty in pride shall be crushed, and the lofty shall be brought low: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} and the lofty ones shall fall by the sword, and the Libanus shall fall with his lofty ones.\par

Aiath, or Ai, was situated a little east of Bethel about twelve miles north of Jerusalem; Michmash about three miles nearer, where there was a narrow pass between two sharp hills; Geba and Ramah about three miles more to the south; Gibeah a mile and a half more southward; Anathoth within three miles of Jerusalem; to the westward of which, towards Lydda, was Nob, from which place Sennacherib might have a prospect of Zion, and near which, it would appear, his army was destroyed. \subsection*{Esaias 11}
\markright{ESAIAS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a blossom shall come up from [his] root: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} and the Spirit of God shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and godliness shall fill him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} the spirit of the fear of God. He shall not judge according to appearance, nor reprove according to report: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} but he shall judge the cause of the lowly, and shall reprove the lowly of the earth: and he shall strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he destroy the ungodly one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shall have his loins girded with righteousness, and his sides clothed with truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the wolf shall feed with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the young calf and bull and lion shall feed together; and a little child shall lead them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the ox and bear shall feed together; and their young shall be together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And an infant shall put his hand on the holes of asps, and on the nest of young asps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they shall not hurt, nor shall they at all be able to destroy any one on my holy mountain: for the whole [world] is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as much water covers the seas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall arise to rule over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust, and his rest shall be glorious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it shall be in that day, [that] the Lord shall again show his hand, to be zealous for the remnant that is left of the people, which shall be left by the Assyrians, and [that] from Egypt, and from the country of Babylon, and from Ethiopia, and from the Elamites, and from the rising of the sun, and out of Arabia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he shall lift up a standard for the nations, and he shall gather the lost ones of Israel, and he shall gather the dispersed of Juda from the four corners of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Juda shall perish: Ephraim shall not envy Juda, and Juda shall not afflict Ephraim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they shall fly in the ships of the Philistines: they shall at the same time spoil the sea, and them [that come] from the east, and Idumea: and they shall lay their hands on Moab first; but the children of Ammon shall first obey [them.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord shall make desolate the sea of Egypt; and he shall lay his hand on the river with a strong wind, and he shall strike the seven channels, so that men shall pass through it dry-shod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And there shall be a passage for my people that is left in Egypt: and it shall be to Israel as the day when he came forth out of the land of Egypt.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 12}
\markright{ESAIAS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And in that day you shall say, I [will] bless you, O Lord; for you were angry with me, but you have turned aside your wrath, and have pitied me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, my God is my Saviour; I will trust in him, and not be afraid: for the Lord is my glory and my praise, and is become my salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Draw you⌃ therefore water with joy out of the wells of salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in that day you shall say, sing to the Lord, call aloud upon his name, proclaim his glorious [deeds] among the Gentiles; make mention that his name is exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Sing praise to the name of the Lord; for he has done great [things]: declare this in all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Exalt and rejoice, you⌃ that dwell in Sion: for the Holy One of Israel is exalted in the midst of her.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} And in that, ; O Lord, ;, ; though \textsuperscript{4} in that day;, call upon his name or, proclaim his name, ; declare;, ; his name \textsuperscript{6} Cry out, ; thou, ; inhabitant Heb. inhabitress great\par}
