\subsection*{Esaias 13}
\markright{ESAIAS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE VISION WHICH ESAIAS SON OF AMOS SAW AGAINST BABYLON. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Lift up a standard on the mountain of the plain, exalt the voice to them, beckon with the hand, open [the gates], you⌃ rulers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I give command, and I bring them: giants are coming to fulfil my wrath, rejoicing at the same time and insulting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A voice of many nations on the mountains, [even] like [to that] of many nations; a voice of kings and nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts has given command to a warlike nation, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} to come from a land afar off, from the utmost foundation of heaven; the Lord and his warriors [are coming] to destroy all the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Howl you⌃, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction from God shall arrive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore every hand shall become powerless, and every soul of man shall be dismayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The elders shall be troubled, and pangs shall seize them, as of a woman in travail: and they shall mourn one to another, and shall be amazed, and shall change their countenance as a flame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For behold! the day of the Lord is coming which can’t be escaped, [a day] of wrath and anger, to make the world desolate, and to destroy sinners out of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the stars of heaven, and Orion, and all the host of heaven, shall not give their light; and it shall be dark at sunrise, and the moon shall not give her light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will command evils for the whole world, and [will visit] their sins on the ungodly: and I will destroy the pride of transgressors, and will bring low the pride of the haughty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they that are left shall be more precious than gold tried in the fire; and a man shall be more precious than the stone that is in Suphir. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the heaven shall be enraged, and the earth shall be shaken from her foundation, because of the fierce anger of the Lord of hosts, in the day in which his wrath shall come on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they that are left shall be as a fleeing fawn, and as a stray sheep, and there shall be none to gather [them]: so that a man shall turn back to his people, and a man shall flee to his own land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For whoever shall be taken shall be overcome; and they that are gathered together shall fall by the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they shall dash their children before their eyes; and they shall spoil their houses, and shall take their wives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold, I will stir up against you the Medes, who do not regard silver, neither have they need of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} They shall break the bows of the young men; and they shall have no mercy on your children; nor shall their eyes spare your children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, shall be as [when] God overthrew Sodoma, and Gomorrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} It shall never be inhabited, neither shall any enter into it for many generations: neither shall the Arabians pass through it; nor shall shepherds at all rest in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But wild beasts shall rest there; and the houses shall be filled with howling; and monsters shall rest there, and devils shall dance there, and satyrs shall dwell there; and hedgehogs shall make their nests in their houses. It will come soon, and will not wait.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3292, bc 712 burden, ; of Babylon, ; 50:1-51:23; Dan. 5:28-6:28; Rev. 17:1-18:24 which Isaiah \textsuperscript{2} Lift ye up, ; upon the high shake, go into \textsuperscript{3} commanded, ; mighty ones; them that \textsuperscript{4} noise;, ; like as Heb. the likeness of; the Lord \textsuperscript{5} from a far;, ; and the weapons \textsuperscript{6} Howl ye, ; for the day; as a \textsuperscript{7} shall all, ; be faint or, fall down every \textsuperscript{8} pangs; be amazed one at another Heb. wonder every man at his neighbour flames Heb. faces of the flames \textsuperscript{11} I will punish; and I will cause \textsuperscript{13} I will; the earth; in the wrath \textsuperscript{17} I will, ; shall not regard \textsuperscript{19} Babylon, whose destruction and utter ruin are here predicted, was situated in the midst of a large plain, having a very deep and fruitful soil, on the Euphrates, about 252 miles south-east of Palmyra, and the same distance north-west of Susa and the Persian gulf, in lat. 32 degrees 30 minutes n and long. 44 degrees 20 minutes e. According to Herodotus, it formed a perfect square, each side of which was 120 stadia, and consequently its circumference 480 stadia, or sixty miles; inclosed by a wall 200 cubits high, and fifty wide, on the top of which were small watch towers of one story high, leaving a space between them, through which a chariot and four might pass and turn. On each side were twenty-five gates of solid brass; from each of which proceeded a street, 150 feet broad, making in all fifty streets; which, crossing each other at right angles, intersected the city into 676 squares, extending four stadia and a half on each side, along which stood the houses, all built three or four stories high, and highly decorated towards the street; the interior of these squares being employed as gardens, pleasure grounds, etc. Its principal ornaments were the temple of Belus, having a tower of eight stories, upon a base of a quarter of a mile square; a most magnificent palace; and the famous hanging gardens, or artificial mountains raised upon arches, and planted with large and beautiful trees. Cyrus took it by diverting the waters of the Euphrates, which ran through the midst, and entering by the channel; and the river being never restored to its proper course, overflowed the whole country, and made it a morass. Darius Hystaspes afterwards depopulated the place, lowered the walls, and demolished the gates; Xerxes destroyed the temples; the building of Seleucia nearly exhausted it of its inhabitants; a king of the Parthians carried a number of them into slavery, and destroyed the most beautiful parts; so that modern travellers describe it as a mass of shapeless ruins, the habitation of wild beasts.; when God overthrew Heb. the overthrowing of \textsuperscript{21} But; wild beasts Heb. Ziim doleful creatures Heb. Ochim, owls. or, ostriches. Heb. daughters of the owl.\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 14}
\markright{ESAIAS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and they shall rest on their land: and the stranger shall be added to them, yes, shall be added to the house of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Gentiles shall take them, and bring them into their place: and they shall inherit them, and they shall be multiplied upon the land for servants and handmaidens: and they that took them captives shall become captives [to them]; and they that had lordship over them shall be under [their] rule. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] the Lord shall give you rest from your sorrow and vexation, [and from] your hard servitude wherein you did serve them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall take up this lamentation against the king of Babylon, How has the extortioner ceased, and the taskmaster ceased! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The Lord has broken the yoke of sinners, the yoke of princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Having struck a nation in wrath, with an incurable plague, striking a nation with a wrathful plague, which spared [them] not, he rested in quiet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All the earth cries aloud with joy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} the trees also of Libanus rejoice against you, and the cedar of Libanus, [saying], From the time that you have been laid low, no one has come up to cut us down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Hell from beneath is provoked to meet you: all the great ones that have ruled over the earth have risen up together against you, they that have raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All shall answer and say to you, You also have been taken, even as we; and you are numbered among us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Your glory has come down to Hades, and your great mirth: under you they shall spread corruption, and the worm shall be your covering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} How has Lucifer, that rose in the morning, fallen from heaven! He that sent [orders] to all the nations is crushed to the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But you said in your heart, I will go up to heaven, I will set my throne above the stars of heaven: I will sit on a lofty mount, on the lofty mountains toward the north: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I will go up above the clouds: I will be like the Most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But now you shall go down to hell, even to the foundations of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They that see you shall wonder at you, and say, This is the man that troubled the earth, that made kings to shake; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} that made the whole world desolate, and destroyed its cities; he loosed not those who were in captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} All the kings of the nations lie in honor, [every] man in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But you shall be cast forth on the mountains, as a loathed carcass, with many dead who have been pierced with swords, going down to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As a garment defiled with blood shall not be pure, so neither shall you be pure; because you have destroyed my land, and have slain my people: you shall not endure for ever, —[you] an evil seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Prepare your children to be slain for the sins of their father; that they arise not, and inherit the earth, nor fill the earth with wars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts, and I will destroy their name, and remnant, and seed: thus says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I will make the region of Babylon desert, so that hedgehogs shall dwell [there], and it shall come to nothing: and I will make it a pit of clay for destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Thus says the Lord of hosts, As I have said, so it shall be: and as I have purposed, so [the matter] shall remain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} [even] to destroy the Assyrians upon my land, and upon my mountains: and they shall be for trampling; and their yoke shall be taken away from them, and their glory shall be taken away from their shoulders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} This is the purpose which the Lord has purposed upon the whole earth: and this the hand that is uplifted against all the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For what the Holy God has purposed, who shall frustrate? and who shall turn back his uplifted hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} In the year in which king Achaz died this word came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Rejoice not, all you⌃ Philistines, because the yoke of him that struck you is broken: for out of the seed of the serpent shall come forth the young asps, and their young shall come forth flying serpents, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the poor shall be fed by him, and poor men shall rest in peace: but he shall destroy your seed with hunger, and shall destroy your remnant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Howl, you⌃ gates of cities; let the cities be troubled and cry, [even] all the Philistines: for smoke is coming from the north, and there is no [possibility] of living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And what shall the kings of the nations answer? That the Lord has founded Sion, and by him the poor of the people shall be saved.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 15}
\markright{ESAIAS 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE WORD AGAINST THE LAND OF MOAB. By night the land of Moab shall be destroyed; for by night the wall of the land of Moab shall be destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Grieve for yourselves; for even Debon, where your altar is, shall be destroyed: there shall you⌃ go up to weep, over Nabau of the land of Moab: howl you⌃: baldness shall be on every head, [and] all arms [shall be] wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Gird yourselves with sackcloth in her streets: and lament upon her roofs, and in her streets, and in her ways; howl all of you with weeping. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For Esebon and Eleale have cried: their voice was heard to Jassa: therefore the loins of the region of Moab cry aloud; her soul shall know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The heart of the region of Moab cries within her to Segor; for it is [as] a heifer of three years old: and on the ascent of Luith they shall go up to you weeping by the way of Aroniim: she cries, Destruction, and trembling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The water of Nemerim shall be desolate, and the grass thereof shall fail: for there shall be no green grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Shall [Moab] even thus be delivered? for I [will] bring the Arabians upon the valley, and they shall take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the cry has reached the border of the region of Moab, [even] of Agalim; and her howling [has gone] as far as the well of Aelim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the water of Dimon shall be filled with blood: for I will bring Arabians upon Dimon, and I will take away the seed of Moab, and Ariel, and the remnant of Adama.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} burden This and the following chapter form one entire prophecy; which was most probably delivered, as Bp. Lowth supposes, soon after the foregoing ( ), in the first year of Hezekiah, and accomplished in his fourth year when Shalmaneser invaded Israel., Moab; in the; Ar; brought to silence or, cut off Kir, Kir-hareseth, Kir-haresh, Kir-haraseth, Kir-heres \textsuperscript{2} is gone; Moab, ; Nebo; Medeba; all \textsuperscript{3} their streets; on the; weeping abundantly Heb. descending into weeping; or, coming down with weeping \textsuperscript{5} My heart;, ; his fugitives etc. or, to the borders thereof, even as an heifer Zoar, three; the mounting, with, destruction Heb. breaking \textsuperscript{6} Nimrim, Nimrah, Beth-nimrah, Beth-nimrah desolate Heb. desolations the grass \textsuperscript{7} the abundance, ; to the brook of the willows or, valley of the Arabians \textsuperscript{8} the cry; Eglaim, En-eglaim, Eglaim is called Agallim by Eusebius, who places it eight miles south from Ar or Areopolis. \textsuperscript{9} Dimon Some have Dibon; and Jerome says that the same town was called both Dibon and Dimon. more Heb. additions, ; lions; him Bp. \subsection*{Esaias 16}
\markright{ESAIAS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I will send as it were reptiles on the land: is [not] the mount of the daughter of Sion a desolate rock? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For you shall be as a young bird taken away from a bird that has flown: [even] you shall be [so], daughter of Moab: and then do you, O Arnon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} take farther counsel, and continually make you a shelter from grief: they flee in darkness at mid-day; they are amazed; be not you led captive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The fugitives of Moab shall sojourn with you; they shall be to you a shelter from the face of the pursuer: for your alliance has been taken away, and the oppressing ruler has perished from off the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And a throne shall be established with mercy; and one shall sit upon it with truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and earnestly seeking judgments, and hasting righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud. I have cut off his pride: your prophecy shall not be thus, [no] not thus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Moab shall howl; for all shall howl in the land of Moab: but you shall care for them that dwell in Seth, and you shall not be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The plains of Esebon shall mourn, the vine of Sebama: swallowing up the nations, trample you⌃ her vines, even to Jazer: you⌃ shall not come together; wander you⌃ in the desert: they that were sent are deserted, for they have gone over to the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore will I weep as with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sebama; Esebon and Eleale have cast down your trees; for I will trample on your harvest and on your vintages, and all [your plants] shall fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And gladness and rejoicing shall be taken away from the vineyards; and they shall not at all tread wine into the vats; for [the vintage] has ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore my belly shall sound as a harp for Moab, and you have repaired my inward parts as a wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall be to your shame, (for Moab is wearied at the altars,) that he shall go in to the idols thereof to pray, but they shall not be at all able to deliver him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This is the word which the Lord spoke against Moab, when he spoke. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And now I say, in three years, of the years of an hireling, the glory of Moab shall be dishonored [with] all his great wealth; and he shall be left few in number, and not honored.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 17}
\markright{ESAIAS 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE WORD AGAINST DAMASCUS. Behold, Damascus shall be taken away from among cities, and shall become a ruin; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} abandoned for ever, to [be] a fold and resting-place for flocks, and there shall be none to go after them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And she shall no longer be a strong place for Ephraim to flee to, and there shall no longer be a kingdom in Damascus, or a remnant of Syrians; for you are no better than the children of Israel, [even] than their glory; thus says the Lord of hosts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} There shall be in that day a failure of the glory of Jacob, and the riches of his glory shall be shaken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And it shall be as if one should gather standing corn, and reap the grain of the ears; and it shall be as if one should gather ears in a rich valley; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and [as if] there should be left stubble therein, or [as it were] the berries of an olive tree, two or three on the topmost bough, or [as if] four or five should be left on their branches; thus says the Lord, the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In that day a man shall trust in him that made him, and his eyes shall have respect to the Holy One of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they shall not at all trust in their altars, nor in the works of their hands, which their fingers made; and they shall not look to the trees, nor to their abominations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In that day your cities shall be deserted, as the Amorites and the Evaeans deserted [theirs], because of the children of Israel; and they shall be desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Because you have forsaken God your Saviour, and have not been mindful of the Lord your helper; therefore shall you plant a false plant, and a false seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In the day wherein you shall plant you shall be deceived; but if you sow in the morning, [the seed] shall spring up for a crop in the day wherein you shall obtain an inheritance, and as a man's father, you shall obtain an inheritance for your sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Woe [to] the multitude of many nations, as the swelling sea, so shall you⌃ be confounded; and the force of many nations shall sound like water; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} many nations like much water, as when much water rushes violently: and they shall drive him away, and pursue him afar, as the dust of chaff when men winnow before the wind, and as a storm whirling the dust of the wheel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Toward evening, and there shall be grief; before the morning, and he shall not be. This is the portion of them that spoiled you, and the inheritance to them that robbed you of your inheritance.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 18}
\markright{ESAIAS 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to you, you⌃ wings of the land of ships, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He sends messengers by the sea, and paper letters on the water: for swift messengers shall go to a lofty nation, and to a strange and harsh people. Who is beyond it? a nation not looked for, and trodden down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now all the rivers of the land shall be inhabited as an inhabited country; their land shall be as when a signal is raised from a mountain; it shall be audible as the sound of a trumpet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For thus said the Lord to me, There shall be security in my city, as the light of noonday heat, and it shall be as a cloud of dew in the day of harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Before the reaping time, when the flower has been completely formed, and the unripe grape has put forth its flower and blossomed, then shall he take away the little clusters with pruning-hooks, and shall take away the small branches, and cut them off; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he shall leave [them] together to the birds of the sky, and to the wild beasts of the earth: and the fowls of the sky shall be gathered upon them, and all the beasts of the land shall come upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In that time shall presents be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people afflicted and peeled, and from a people great from henceforth and for ever; a nation hoping and [yet] trodden down, which is in a part of a river of his land, to the place where is the name of the Lord of hosts, the mount Sion.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am cir, 3290, bc cir, 714 Woe Bp. Lowth renders, after Bochart, "Ho! to the land of the winged cymbal; " which he thinks is a periphrasis for the Egyptian sistrum; and consequently, that Egypt, "which borders on the rivers of Cush, " is the country to which the prophecy is addressed. If we translate "shadowing with wings, " it may allude to the multitude of its vessels, whose sails may be represented under the notion of wings. the land, shadowing;, ; which \textsuperscript{2} sendeth; vessels It is well known that the Egyptians commonly used on the Nile a light sort of ships or boats made of the papyrus. See note on . to a nation scattered and peeled or, outspread and polished, Or, as Bp. Lowth renders, "stretched out in length and smoothed." Egypt, which is situated between 24 degrees and 32 degrees n lat. and 30 degrees and 33 degrees e long., being bounded on the south by Ethiopia, on the north by the Mediterranean, on the east by the mountains of Arabia, and on the west by those of Lybia, is one long vale, 750 miles in length (through the middle of which runs the Nile), in breadth from one to two or three day's journey, and even at the widest part of the Delta, from Pelusium to Alexandria, not above 250 miles broad. to a people;, Heb Meted out and trodden down or, that meteth out and treadeth down, Heb. of line, line, and treading under foot, This is an allusion to the frequent necessity of having recourse to mensuration in Egypt, in order to determine their boundaries, after the inundation of the Nile had smoothed their land and effaced their landmarks; and to their method of throwing seed upon the mud, when the waters had subsided, and treading it in by turning their cattle into the fields. have spoiled or, despise \textsuperscript{4} I will; consider in my dwelling place or, regard my set dwelling, ; like a clear; upon herbs or, after rain \textsuperscript{7} shall the, ; scattered and peeled or, outspread and polished, to the\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 19}
\markright{ESAIAS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE VISION OF EGYPT. Behold, the Lord sits on a swift cloud, and shall come to Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and their heart shall faint within them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Egyptians shall be stirred up against the Egyptians: and a man shall fight against his brother, and a man against his neighbor, city against city, and law against law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the spirit of the Egyptians shall be troubled within them; and I will frustrate their counsel: and they shall enquire of their gods and their images, and them that speak out of the earth, and them that have in them a divining spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I will deliver Egypt into the hands of men, of cruel lords; and cruel kings shall rule over them: thus says the Lord of hosts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Egyptians shall drink the water that is by the sea, but the river shall fail, and be dried up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the streams shall fail, and the canals of the river; and every reservoir of water shall be dried up, in every marsh also of reed and papyrus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And all the green herbage round about the river, and everything sown by the side of the river, shall be blasted with the wind and dried up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the fishermen shall groan, and all that cast a hook into the river shall groan; they also that cast nets, and the anglers shall mourn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And shame shall come upon them that work fine flax, and them that make fine linen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they that work at them shall be in pain, and all that make beer shall be grieved, and be pained in their souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the princes of Tanis shall be fools: [as for] the king's wise counselors, their counsel shall be turned into folly: how will you⌃ say to the king, we are sons of wise men, sons of ancient kings? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Where are now your wise men? and let them declare to you, and say, What has the Lord of hosts purposed upon Egypt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The princes of Tanis have failed, and the princes of Memphis are lifted up [with pride], and they shall cause Egypt to wander by tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the Lord has prepared for them a spirit of error, and they have caused Egypt to err in all their works, as one staggers who is drunken and vomits also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And there shall be no work to the Egyptians, which shall make head or tail, or beginning or end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But in that day the Egyptians shall be as women, in fear and in trembling because of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shall bring upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the land of the Jews shall be for a terror to the Egyptians: whoever shall name it to them, they shall fear, because of the counsel which the Lord of hosts has purposed concerning it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} In that day there shall be five cities in Egypt speaking the language of Chanaan, and swearing by the name of the Lord of hosts; one city shall be called the city of Asedec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians, and a pillar to the Lord by its border. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it shall be for a sign to the Lord for ever in the land of Egypt: for they shall presently cry to the Lord by reason of them that afflict them, and he shall send them a man who shall save them; he shall judge and save them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the Lord shall be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day; and they shall offer sacrifices, and shall vow vows to the Lord, and pay [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord shall strike the Egyptians with a stroke, and shall completely heal them: and they shall return to the Lord, and he shall hear them, and thoroughly heal them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} In that day there shall be a way from Egypt to the Assyrians, and the Assyrians shall enter into Egypt, and the Egyptians shall go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians shall serve the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} In that day shall Israel be third with the Egyptians and the Assyrians, blessed in the land which the Lord of hosts has blessed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} saying, Blessed be my people that is in Egypt, and that is among the Assyrians, and Israel my inheritance.\par

Nebuchadnezzar, who first conquered and ravaged Egypt, bc 573, and the following year; and then, not only his successors, but Cambyses (who invaded Egypt, bc 526), the son of Cyrus, and the whole succession of Persian kings till the time of Alexander, who were in general hard masters, and grievously oppressed the country. \textsuperscript{7} every; be no more Heb. shall not be \textsuperscript{9} work; net works, or, white works \textsuperscript{10} purposes Heb. foundations make; for fish or, of living things \textsuperscript{11} the princes, ; Zoan; brutish; I am \textsuperscript{12} where are thy; let them \textsuperscript{13} princes of Zoan; Noph, ; stay or, governors, Heb. corners; *marg. \textsuperscript{14} hath mingled, ; perverse spirit Heb. spirit of perverseness as a \textsuperscript{18} that day, ; shall five; speak language Heb. lip, and swear; destruction Heb. Heres, or, the sun, Instead of heres "destruction, " which is also the reading of Aquila, Theodotion, and the Syriac, fifteen manuscripts and seven editions have cheres "the sun; " agreeable to Symmachus, the Arabic, and Vulgate; while the Chaldee takes in both readings; and the LXX reads πολις ασεδεκ, "the city of righteousness, " a name apparently contrived by the party of Onias, to give credit to his temple. As, however, heres in Arabic signifies a lion, Conrad Ikenius is of opinion that the place here mentioned is not Heliopolis, as is commonly supposed, but Leontopolis in the Heliopolitan nome, as it is termed in the letter of Onias to Ptolemy. The whole passage, from this verse to the end, contains a general intimation of the propagation of the knowledge of the true God in Egypt and Syria, under the successors of Alexander, and the early reception of the gospel in the same countries. \textsuperscript{20} for a;, they shall, ; he shall send \textsuperscript{21} Lord shall, ; and shall; shall vow \textsuperscript{22} he shall smite; they shall \textsuperscript{25} the Lord; Blessed; and Israel\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 20}
\markright{ESAIAS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the year when Tanathan came to Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians, and warred against Azotus, and took it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} then the Lord spoke to Esaias the son of Amos, saying, Go and take the sackcloth off your loins, and loose your sandals from off your feet, and do thus, going naked and barefoot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord said, As my servant Esaias has walked naked and barefoot three years, there shall be three years for signs and wonders to the Egyptians and Ethiopians; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} for thus shall the king of the Assyrians lead the captivity of Egypt and the Ethiopians, young men and old, naked and barefoot, having the shame of Egypt exposed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Egyptians being defeated shall be ashamed of the Ethiopians, in whom they had trusted; for they were their glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they that dwell in this island shall say in that day, Behold, we trusted to flee to them for help, who could not save themselves from the king of the Assyrians: and how shall we be saved?\par

\subsection*{Esaias 21}
\markright{ESAIAS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE VISION OF THE DESERT. As though a whirlwind should pass through the desert, coming from a desert, [even] from such a land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [so] a fearful and a grievous vision was declared to me: he that is treacherous deals treacherously, the transgressor transgresses. The Elamites are upon me, and the ambassadors of the Persians come against me: now will I groan and comfort myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore are my loins filled with feebleness, and pangs have seized me as a travailing woman: I dealt wrongfully that I might not hear; I hasted that I might not see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} My heart wanders, and transgression overwhelms me; my soul is occupied with fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Prepare the table, eat, drink: arise, you⌃ princes, and prepare [your] shields. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For thus said the Lord to me, Go and station a watchman for yourself, and declare whatever you shall see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I saw two mounted horsemen, and a rider on an ass, and a rider on a camel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Listen with great attention, and call you Urias to the watch-tower: the Lord has spoken. I stood continually during the day, and I stood in the camp all night: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and, behold, he comes riding in a chariot and pair: and he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all her images and her idols have been crushed to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Hear, you⌃ that are left, and you⌃ that are in pain, hear what things I have heard of the Lord of hosts [which] the God of Israel has declared to us. THE VISION OF IDUMEA. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Call to me out of Seir; guard you⌃ the bulwarks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I watch in the morning and the night: if you would enquire, enquire, and dwell by me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You may lodge in the forest in the evening, or in the way of Daedan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You⌃ that dwell in the country of Thaeman, bring water to meet him that is thirsty; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} meet the fugitives with bread, because of the multitude of the slain, and because of the multitude of them that lose their way, and because of the multitude of swords, and because of the multitude of bent bows, and because of the multitude of them that have fallen in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For thus said the Lord to me, Yet a year, as the year of an hireling, [and] the glory of the sons of Kedar shall fail: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and the remnant of the strong bows of the sons of Kedar shall be small: for the Lord God of Israel has spoken [it].\par

\subsection*{Esaias 22}
\markright{ESAIAS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE WORD OF THE VALLEY OF SION. What has happened to you, that now you⌃ are all gone up to the housetops which help you not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The city is filled with shouting [men]: your slain are not slain with swords, nor are your dead those who have died in battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} All your princes have fled, and [your] captives are tightly bound, and the mighty [men] in you have fled far away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore I said, Let me alone, I will weep bitterly; labor not to comfort me for the breach of the daughter of my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For [it is] a day of trouble, and of destruction, and of treading down, and [there is] perplexity [sent] from the Lord of hosts: they wander in the valley of Sion; they wander from the least to the greatest on the mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Elamites took [their] quivers, and [there were] men mounted on horses, and [there was] a gathering for battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it shall be [that] your choice valleys shall be filled with chariots, and horsemen shall block up your gates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they shall uncover the gates of Juda, and they shall look in that day on the choice houses of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they shall uncover the secret places of the houses of the citadel of David: and they saw that they were many, and that one [had] turned the water of the old pool into the city; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and that they [had] pulled down the houses of Jerusalem, to fortify the wall of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you⌃ procured to yourselves water between the two walls within the ancient pool: but you⌃ looked not to him that made it from the beginning, and regarded not him that created it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord, the Lord of hosts, called in that day for weeping, and lamentation, and baldness, and for girding with sackcloth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} but they engaged in joy and gladness, slaying calves, and killing sheep, so as to eat flesh, and drink wine; saying, Let us eat and drink; for to-morrow we die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And these things are revealed in the ears of the Lord of hosts: for this sin shall not be forgiven you, until you⌃ die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Thus says the Lord of hosts, Go into the chamber, to Somnas the treasurer, and say to him, Why are you here? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and what have you to do here, that you have here hewn yourself a sepulchre, and made yourself a sepulchre on high, and have graven for yourself a dwelling in the rock? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold now, the Lord of hosts casts forth and will utterly destroy [such] a man, and will take away your robe and your glorious crown, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} and will cast you into a great and unmeasured land, and there you shall die: and he will bring your fair chariot to shame, and the house of your prince to be trodden down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall be removed from your stewardship, and from your place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Chelcias: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and I will put on him your robe, and I will grant him your crown with power, and I will give your stewardship into his hands: and he shall be as a father to them that dwell in Jerusalem, and to them that dwell in Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will give him the glory of David; and he shall rule, and there shall be none to speak against him: and I will give him the key of the house of David [upon] his shoulder; and he shall open, and there shall be none to shut; and he shall shut, and there shall be none to open. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I will make him a ruler in a sure place, and he shall be for a glorious throne of his father's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And every one that is glorious in the house of his father shall trust in him, from the least to the greatest; and they shall depend upon him in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Thus says the Lord of hosts, The man that is fastened in the sure place shall be removed and be taken away, and shall fall; and the glory that is upon him shall be utterly destroyed: for the Lord has spoken it.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am cir, 3292, bc cir, 712 the valley Jerusalem being situated in the midst of surrounding hills, and the seat of Divine revelation, is here termed "the valley of vision." This prophecy foretells the invasion of Jerusalem by the Assyrians under Sennacherib; and probably also, by the Chaldeans under Nebuchadnezzar.; of vision; What; that thou The eastern houses are built with a court within, into which chiefly the windows open; those that open to the street being so obstructed with lattice work, that no one can see through them. Whenever, therefore, anything is to be seen or heard in the streets, any public spectacle, or any alarm, everyone immediately goes up to the house-top to satisfy his curiosity. Hence all the people running to the top of their houses, gives a lively image of a sudden general alarm. \textsuperscript{3} thy rulers; by the archers Heb. of the bow \textsuperscript{4} Look; Weep bitterly Heb. be bitter in weeping; labour \textsuperscript{5} a day; treading, perplexity; breaking; crying \textsuperscript{6} Elam; Kir; uncovered Heb. made naked \textsuperscript{7} thy choicest valleys Heb. the choice of thy valleys full, ; at or, toward \textsuperscript{16} What hast; hewed There are some monuments still remaining in Persia, of great antiquity, says Bp. Lowth, called Naksi Rustam, which give a clear idea of Shebna's pompous design for his sepulchre. They consist of several sepulchres, each of them hewn in a high rock near the top. The front of the rock to the valley below is adorned with carved work in relief, being the outside of the sepulchre. Some of these sepulchres are about thirty feet in the perpendicular from the valley, which is itself raised perhaps about half as much by the accumulation of the earth since they were made.; as he or, O he \textsuperscript{17} will carry etc. or, who covered thee with an excellent covering, and clothed thee gorgeously, shall surely violently turn, etc. a mighty captivity Heb. the captivity of a man cover \textsuperscript{18} surely; a large country Heb. a land large of spaces \textsuperscript{22} And the key As the robe and the baldric, mentioned in the preceding verse, were the ensigns of power and authority; so likewise was the key the mark of office, either sacred or civil. \subsection*{Esaias 23}
\markright{ESAIAS 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE WORD CONCERNING TYRE. Howl, you⌃ ships of Carthage; for she has perished, and [men] no longer arrive from the land of the Citians: she is led captive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To whom are the dwellers in the island become like, the merchants of Phoenice, passing over the sea {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} in great waters, a generation of merchants? as when the harvest is gathered in, [so are] these traders with the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Be ashamed, O Sidon: the sea has said, yes, the strength of the sea has said, I have not travailed, nor brought forth, nor have I brought up young men, nor reared virgins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Moreover when it shall be heard in Egypt, sorrow shall seize them for Tyre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Depart you⌃ to Carthage; howl, you⌃ that dwell in this island. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Was not this your pride from the beginning, before she was given up? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Who has devised this counsel against Tyre? Is she inferior? or has she no strength? her merchants were the glorious princes of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Lord of hosts has purposed to bring down all the pride of the glorious ones, and to disgrace every glorious thing on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Till your land; for ships no more come out of Carthage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And your hand prevails no more by sea, which troubled kings: the Lord of hosts has given a command concerning Chanaan, to destroy the strength thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And [men] shall say, You⌃ shall no longer at all continue to insult and injure the daughter of Sidon: and if you depart to the Citians, neither there shall you have rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And [if you depart] to the land of the Chaldeans, this also is laid waste by the Assyrians, for her wall is fallen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Howl, you⌃ ships of Carthage: for your strong hold is destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] Tyre shall be left seventy years, as the time of a king, as the time of a man: and it shall come to pass after seventy years, [that] Tyre shall be as the song of a harlot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Take a harp, go about, O city, you harlot that have been forgotten; play well on the harp, sing many [songs], that you may be remembered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it shall come to pass after the seventy years, [that] God will visit Tyre, and she shall be again restored to her primitive state, and she shall be a mart for all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And her trade and her gain shall be holiness to the Lord: it shall not be gathered for them, but for those that dwell before the Lord, [even] all her trade, to eat and drink and be filled, and for a covenant [and] a memorial before the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3289, bc 715 burden Tyre, whose destruction by Nebuchadnezzar is here foretold, was a city of Phoenicia, on the shore of the Mediterranean, twenty-four miles south of Sidon, and thirty-two north of Accho or Ptolemais, according to the Antonine and Jerusalem Itineraries, about latitude 33 degrees 18 minutes north, longitude 35 degrees 10 minutes east. There were two cities of this name; one on the continent called Pale Tyrus, or Old Tyre, according to Strabo, thirty stadia south of the other, which was situated on an island, not above 700 paces from the main land, says Pliny. Old Tyre was taken by Nebuchadnezzar, after a siege of thirteen years, bc 573, which he so utterly destroyed, that it never afterwards rose higher than a village. But previous to this, the inhabitants had removed their effects to the island which afterwards became so famous by the name of Tyre, though now consisting only of about 800 dwellings., ; Ezek. 26:1-28:25; Howl; ye ships; for it is; the land \textsuperscript{2} still Heb. silent, ; the isle, the merchants \textsuperscript{3} Sihor; the harvest; she is \textsuperscript{7} your whose her own; afar off Heb. from afar off \textsuperscript{8} Who hath; the crowning, merchants \textsuperscript{9} Lord, ; to stain Heb. to pollute, ; bring \textsuperscript{10} O daughter no more; strength Heb. girdle \textsuperscript{11} stretched; the Lord; against the merchant city or, concerning a merchantman; the merchant city Heb. \subsection*{Esaias 24}
\markright{ESAIAS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold, the Lord is about to lay waste the world, and will make it desolate, and will lay bare the surface of it, and scatter them that dwell therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the people shall be as the priest, and the servant as the lord, and the maid as the mistress; the buyer shall be as the seller, the lender as the borrower, and the debtor as his creditor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The earth shall be completely laid waste, and the earth shall be utterly spoiled: for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The earth mourns, and the world is ruined, the lofty ones of the earth are mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she has sinned by reason of her inhabitants; because they have transgressed the law, and changed the ordinances, [even] the everlasting covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore a curse shall consume the earth, because the inhabitants thereof have sinned: therefore the dwellers in the earth shall be poor, and few men shall be left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The wine shall mourn, the vine shall mourn, all the merry-hearted shall sigh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The mirth of timbrels has ceased, the sound of the harp has ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They are ashamed, they have not drunk wine; strong drink has become bitter to them that drink [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All the city has become desolate: one shall shut his house so that none shall enter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} There is a howling for the wine everywhere; all the mirth of the land has ceased, all the mirth of the land has departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And cities shall be left desolate, and houses being left shall fall to ruin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} All this shall be in the land in the midst of the nations, as if one should strip an olive tree, so shall they strip them; but when the vintage is done, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} these shall cry aloud; and they that are left on the land shall rejoice together in the glory of the Lord: the water of the sea shall be troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore shall the glory of the Lord be in the isles of the sea; the name of the Lord shall be glorious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} O Lord God of Israel, from the ends of the earth we have heard wonderful things, [and there is] hope to the godly: but they shall say, Woe to the despisers, that despise the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Fear, and a pit, and a snare, are upon you that dwell on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And it shall come to pass, [that] he that flees from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that comes up out of the pit shall be caught by the snare: for windows have been opened in heaven, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} the earth shall be utterly confounded, and the earth shall be completely perplexed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} It reels as a drunkard and one oppressed with wine, and the earth shall be shaken as a storehouse of fruits; for iniquity has prevailed upon it, and it shall fall, and shall not be able to rise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And God shall bring [his] hand upon the host of heaven, and upon the kings of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they shall gather the multitude thereof into prisons, and they shall shut them into a strong hold: after many generations they shall be visited. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the brick shall decay, and the wall shall fall; for the Lord shall reign from out of Sion, and out of Jerusalem, and shall be glorified before [his] elders.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 25}
\markright{ESAIAS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O Lord God, I will glorify you, I will sing to your name; for you have done wonderful things, [even] an ancient [and] faithful counsel. So be it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For you have made cities a heap, [even] cities [made] strong that their foundations should not fall: the city of ungodly men shall not be built for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore shall the poor people bless you, and cities of injured men shall bless you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For you have been a helper to every lowly city, and a shelter to them that were disheartened by reason of poverty: you shall deliver them from wicked men: [you have been] a shelter of them that thirst, and a refreshing air to injured men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} [We were] as faint-hearted men thirsting in Sion, by reason of ungodly men to whom you did deliver us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord of hosts shall make [a feast] for all the nations: on this mount they shall drink gladness, they shall drink wine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} they shall anoint themselves with ointment in this mountain. Impart you all these things to the nations; for this is [God's] counsel upon all the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Death has prevailed and swallowed [men] up; but again the Lord God has taken away every tear from every face. He has taken away the reproach of [his] people from all the earth: for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And in that day they shall say, behold our God in whom we have trusted, and he shall save us: this [is] the Lord; we have waited for him, and we have exulted, and will rejoice in our salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} God will give rest on this mountain, and the country of Moab shall be trodden down, as they tread the floor with wagons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he shall spread forth his hands, even as he also brings down [man] to destroy [him]: and he shall bring low his pride [in regard to the thing] on which he has laid his hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he shall bring down the height of the refuge of the wall, and it shall come down even to the ground.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} thou art; , ; thou hast, ; thy counsels \textsuperscript{4} thou hast, ; , ; a refuge, when \textsuperscript{5} shalt bring, ; Rev. 16:1-19:21, as the heat; branch \textsuperscript{6} in this; make; all people; of wines \textsuperscript{7} he will; , destroy Heb. swallow up cast Heb. covered \textsuperscript{9} it shall; Lo, ;, ; we will \textsuperscript{10} in this, ; Moab, 15:1-16:14; trodden down or, threshed; even, ; for the dunghill or, in Madmenah \textsuperscript{11} he shall spread, ; he shall bring \textsuperscript{12} the fortress; to the dust\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 26}
\markright{ESAIAS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In that day they shall sing this song in the land of Judea; Behold a strong city; and he shall make salvation [its] wall and bulwark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Open you⌃ the gates, let the nation enter that keeps righteousness, and keeps truth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} supporting truth, and keeping peace: for on you, O Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} they have trusted with confidence for ever, the great, the eternal God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} who have humbled and brought down them that dwell on high, you shall cast down strong cities, and bring them to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the feet of the meek and lowly shall trample them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The way of the godly is made straight: the way of the godly is also prepared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the way of the Lord is judgment: we have hoped in your name, and on the remembrance [of you], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} which our soul longs for: my spirit seeks you very early in the morning, O God, for your commandments are a light on the earth: learn righteousness, you⌃ that dwell upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the ungodly one is put down: no one who will not learn righteousness on the earth, shall be able to do the truth: let the ungodly be taken away, that he see not the glory of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} O Lord, your arm is exalted, yet they knew it not: but when they know they shall be ashamed: jealousy shall seize upon an untaught nation, and now fire shall devour the adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O Lord our God, give us peace: for you have rendered to us all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} O Lord our God, take possession of us: O Lord, we know not [any] other beside you: we name your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But the dead shall not see life, neither shall physicians by any means raise [them] up: therefore you have brought [wrath] upon [them], and slain [them], and have taken away every male of them. Bring more evils upon them, O Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} bring more evils on the glorious ones of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Lord, in affliction I remembered you; your chastening was to us with small affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And as a woman in travail draws near to be delivered, [and] cries out in her pain; so have we been to your beloved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} We have conceived, O Lord, because of your fear, and have been in pain, and have brought forth the breath of your salvation, which we have wrought upon the earth: we shall not fall, but all that dwell upon the land shall fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The dead shall rise, and they that are in the tombs shall be raised, and they that are in the earth shall rejoice: for the dew from you is healing to them: but the land of the ungodly shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Go, my people, enter into your closets, shut your door, hide yourself for a little season, until the anger of the Lord have passed away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For, behold, the Lord is bringing wrath from [his] holy place upon the dwellers on the earth: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall not cover her slain.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 27}
\markright{ESAIAS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In that day God shall bring [his] holy and great and strong sword upon the dragon, even the serpent that flees, upon the dragon, the crooked serpent: he shall destroy the dragon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In that day [there shall be] a fair vineyard, [and] a desire to commence [a song] concerning it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I am a strong city, a city in a siege: in vain shall I water it; for it shall be taken by night, and by day the wall shall fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} There is no woman that has not taken hold of it; who will set me to watch stubble in the field? because of this enemy I have set her aside; therefore on this account the Lord has done all that he appointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I am burnt up; they that dwell in her shall cry, Let us make peace with him, let us make peace, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} they that are coming are the children of Jacob. Israel shall bud and blossom, and the world shall be filled with his fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Shall he himself be thus struck, even as he struck? and as he killed, shall he be thus slain? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Fighting and reproaching he will dismiss them; did you not meditate with a harsh spirit, to kill them with a wrathful spirit? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be taken away; and this is his blessing, when I shall have taken away his sin; when they shall have broken to pieces all the stones of the altars as fine dust, and their trees shall not remain, and their idols shall be cut off, as a thicket afar off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The flock that lived [there] shall be left, as a deserted flock; and [the ground] shall be for a long time for pasture, and there shall flocks lie down to rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And after a time there shall be in it no green thing because of [the grass] being parched. Come hither, you⌃ women that come from a sight; for it is a people of no understanding; therefore he that made them shall have no pity upon them, and he that formed them shall have no mercy [upon them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And it shall come to pass in that day [that] God shall fence [men] off from the channel of the river as far as Rhinocorura; but do you⌃ gather one by one the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it shall come to pass in that day [that] they shall blow the great trumpet, and the lost ones in the land of the Assyrians shall come, and the lost ones in Egypt, and shall worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 28}
\markright{ESAIAS 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to the crown of pride, the hirelings of Ephraim, the flower that has fallen from the glory of the top of the fertile mountain, they that are drunken without wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, the anger of the Lord is strong and severe, as descending hail where there is no shelter, violently descending; as a great body of water sweeping away the soil, he shall make rest for the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The crown of pride, the hirelings of Ephraim, shall be beaten down with the hands and with the feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the fading flower of the glorious hope on the top of the high mountain shall be as the early fig; he that sees it, before he takes it into his hand, will desire to swallow it down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} In that day the Lord of hosts shall be the crown of hope, the woven [crown] of glory, to the remnant of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They shall be left in the spirit of judgment for judgment, and for the strength of them that hinder slaying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For these have trespassed through wine; they have erred through strong drink: the priest and the prophet are mad through strong drink, they are swallowed up by reason of wine, they have staggered through drunkenness; they have erred: this is [their] vision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A curse shall devour this counsel, for this [is their] counsel for the sake of covetousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} To whom have we reported evils? and to whom have we reported a message? [even to those] that are weaned from the milk, who are drawn from the breast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Expect you affliction on affliction, hope upon hope: yet a little, [and] yet a little, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} by reason of the contemptuous [words] of the lips, by means of another language: for they shall speak to this people, saying to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} This is the rest to him that is hungry, and this is the calamity: but they would not hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore the oracle of God shall be to them affliction on affliction, hope on hope, yet a little, [and] yet a little, that they may go and fall backward; and they shall be crushed and shall be in danger, and shall be taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore hear you⌃ the word of the Lord, you⌃ afflicted men, and you⌃ princes of this people that is in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Because you⌃ have said, We have made a covenant with Hades, and agreements with death; if the rushing storm should pass, it shall not come upon us: we have made falsehood our hope, and by falsehood shall we be protected: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore thus says the Lord, [even] the Lord, Behold, I lay for the foundations of Sion a costly stone, a choice, a corner-stone, a precious [stone], for its foundations; and he that believes [on him] shall by no means be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And I will cause judgment [to be] for hope, and my compassion shall be for [just] measures, and you⌃ that trust vainly in falsehood [shall fall]: for the storm shall by no means pass by you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} except it also take away your covenant of death, and your trust in Hades shall by no means stand: if the rushing storm should come upon you, you⌃ shall be beaten down by it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Whenever it shall pass by, it shall take you; morning by morning it shall pass by in the day, and in the night there shall be an evil hope. Learn to hear, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} you⌃ that are distressed; we can’t fight, but we are ourselves too weak for you to be gathered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The Lord shall rise up as a mountain of ungodly [men], and shall be in the valley of Gabaon; he shall perform his works with wrath, [even] a work of bitterness, and his wrath shall deal strangely, and his destruction shall be strange. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore do not you⌃ rejoice, neither let your bands be made strong; for I have heard of works finished and cut short by the Lord of hosts, which he will execute upon all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Listen, and hear my voice; attend, and hear my words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Will the plowman plow all the day? or will he prepare the seed beforehand, before he tills the ground? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Does he not, when he has levelled the surface thereof, then sow the small black poppy, or cumin, and afterward sow wheat, and barley, and millet, and bread-corn in your borders? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} So you shall be chastened by the judgment of your God, and shall rejoice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For the black poppy is not cleansed with harsh treatment, nor will a wagon-wheel pass over the cumin; but the black poppy is threshed with a rod, and the cumin shall be eaten with bread; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} for I will not be angry with you for ever, neither shall the voice of my anger crush you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And these signs came forth from the Lord of hosts. Take counsel, exalt vain comfort.\par
