\subsection*{Esaias 29}
\markright{ESAIAS 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alas for the city of Ariel, which David besieged. Gather you⌃ fruits year by year; eat you⌃, for you⌃ shall eat with Moab. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I will grievously afflict Ariel: and her strength and her wealth shall be mine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I will compass you about like David, and will raise a mound about you, and set up towers round you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And your words shall be brought down to the earth, and your words shall sink down to the earth, and your voice shall be as they that speak out of the earth, and your voice shall be lowered to the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the wealth of the ungodly shall be as dust from a wheel, and the multitude of them that oppress you as flying chaff, and it shall be suddenly as a moment, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} from the Lord of Hosts: for there shall be a visitation with thunder, and earthquake, and a loud noise, a rushing tempest, and devouring flame of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the wealth of all the nations together, as many as have fought against Ariel, and all they that war against Jerusalem, and all who are gathered against her, and they that distress her, shall be as one that dreams in sleep by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And as men drink and eat in sleep, and when they have arisen, the dream is vain: and as a thirsty man dreams as if he drank, and having arisen is still thirsty, and his soul has desired in vain: so shall be the wealth of all the nations, as many as have fought against the mount Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Faint you⌃, and be amazed, and be overpowered, not with strong drink nor with wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the Lord has made you to drink a spirit of deep sleep; and he shall close their eyes, and [the eyes] of their prophets and of their rulers, who see secret things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all these things shall be to you as the words of this sealed book, which if they shall give to a learned man, saying, Read this, he shall then say, I can’t read [it], for it is sealed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And this book shall be given into the hands of a man that is unlearned, and [one] shall say to him, Read this; and he shall say, I am not learned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord has said, This people draw near to me with their mouth, and they honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me: but in vain do they worship me, teaching the commandments and doctrines of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore behold I will proceed to remove this people, and I will remove them: and I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will hide the understanding of the prudent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Woe to them that deepen their counsel, and not by the Lord. Woe to them that take secret counsel, and whose works are in darkness, and they say, Who has seen us? and who shall know us, or what we do? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Shall you⌃ not be counted as clay of the potter? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, You did not form me? or the work to the maker, You have not made me wisely? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} [Is it] not yet a little while, and Libanus shall be changed as the mountains of Chermel, and Chermel shall be reckoned as a forest? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and they that are in darkness, and they that are in mist: the eyes of the blind shall see, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the poor shall rejoice with joy because of the Lord, and they that had no hope among men shall be filled with joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The lawless man has come to nothing, and the proud man has perished, and they that transgress mischievously have been utterly destroyed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and they that cause men to sin by a word: and men shall make all that reprove in the gates an offense, because they have unjustly turned aside the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, whom he set apart from Abraam, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall he now change countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But when their children shall have seen my works, they shall sanctify my name for my sake, and they sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they that erred in spirit shall know understanding, and the murmurers shall learn obedience, and the stammering tongues shall learn to speak peace.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3292, bc 712 woe etc. or, O Ariel, that is, the lion of God; the city or, of the city, add; kill Heb. cut off the heads \textsuperscript{2} I will, ; and it shall Or, as Bp. Lowth renders, "and it shall be unto me as the hearth of the great altar; " that is, it shall be the seat of the fire of God, which shall issue from thence to consume his enemies. The hearth of the altar is expressly called ariel by Ezekiel; which is put, in the former part of the verse, for Jerusalem, the city in which the altar was. The subject of this and the four following chapters, says Bp. Lowth, is the invasion of Sennacherib; the great distress of the Jews while it continued; their sudden and unexpected deliverance by God's immediate and miraculous interposition on their behalf; the subsequent prosperous state of the kingdom under Hezekiah; interspersed with severe reproofs and threats of punishment for their hypocrisy, stupidity, infidelity, their want of trust in God, and their vain reliance on the assistance of Egypt; and with promises of better times, both immediately to succeed, and to be expected in the future age. \textsuperscript{4} thou shalt, ; whisper Heb. peep, or chirp \textsuperscript{5} the multitude, as chaff; at an \textsuperscript{7} the multitude; that distress as a dream \textsuperscript{9} and wonder; cry ye out, and cry or, take your pleasure and riot; they are \textsuperscript{10} the Lord; hath closed; rulers Heb. heads; the seers \textsuperscript{11} book or, letter that is sealed I cannot \textsuperscript{14} I will; proceed Heb. add for the wisdom \textsuperscript{15} seek, ; and their works; Who seeth \textsuperscript{16} your turning; as the potter's; or shall \textsuperscript{17} yet a very; Lebanon, ; the fruitful \textsuperscript{19} meek; increase Heb. add the poor, ; rejoice \textsuperscript{20} the terrible, ; the scorner;, and all \textsuperscript{21} make; and lay, ; and turn \textsuperscript{23} the work, ; sanctify; fear the God \textsuperscript{24} also; come to understanding Heb. know understanding\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 30}
\markright{ESAIAS 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to the apostate children, says the Lord: you⌃ have framed counsel, not by me, and covenants not by my Spirit, to add sins to sins: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [even] they that proceed to go down into Egypt, but they have not enquired of me, that they might be helped by Pharao, and protected by the Egyptians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the protection of Pharaoh shall be to you a disgrace, and [there shall be] a reproach to them that trust in Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For there are princes in Tanes, evil messengers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} In vain shall they labor [in seeking] to a people, which shall not profit them for help, but [shall be] for a shame and reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} THE VISION OF THE QUADRUPEDS IN THE DESERT. In affliction and distress, [where are] the lion and lion's whelp, thence [come] also asps, and the young of flying asps, [there shall they be] who bore their wealth on asses and camels to a nation which shall not profit them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Egyptians shall help you utterly in vain: tell them, This your consolation is vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now then sit down and write these words on a tablet, and in a book; for these things shall be for [many long] days, and even for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For the people is disobedient, false children, who would not hear the law of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} who say to the prophets, Report not to us; and to them that see visions, Speak [them] not to us, but speak and report to us another error; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and turn us aside from this way; remove from us this path, and remove from us the oracle of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel, Because you⌃ have refused to obey these words, and have trusted in falsehood; and because you have murmured, and been confident in this respect: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} therefore shall this sin be to you as a wall suddenly falling when a strong city has been taken, of which the fall is very near at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the fall thereof shall be as the breaking of an earthen vessel, [as] small fragments of a pitcher, so that you should not find among them a sherd, with which you might take up fire, and with which you should draw a little water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Thus says the Lord, the Holy Lord of Israel; When you shall turn and mourn, then you shall be saved; and you shall know where you were, when you did trust in vanities: [then] your strength became vain, yet you⌃ would not listen: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} but you⌃ said, We will flee upon horses; therefore shall you⌃ flee: and, We will be aided by swift riders; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A thousand shall flee because of the voice of one, and many shall flee on account of the voice of five; until you⌃ be left as a signal-post upon a mountain, and as one bearing an ensign upon a hill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord will again wait, that he may pity you, and will therefore be exalted that he may have mercy upon you: because the Lord your God is a judge: blessed are they that stay themselves upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the holy people shall dwell in Sion: and [whereas] Jerusalem has wept bitterly, [saying], Pity me; he shall pity you: when he perceived the voice of your cry, he listened to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And [though] the Lord shall give you the bread of affliction and scant water, yet they that cause you to err shall no more at all draw near to you; for your eyes shall see those that cause you to err, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} and your ears shall hear the words of them that went after you to lead you astray, who say, This [is] the way, let us walk in it, whether to the right or to the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And you shall pollute the plated idols, and you shall grind to powder the gilt ones, and shall scatter them as the water of a removed [woman], and you shall thrust them forth as dung. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Then shall there be rain to the seed of your land; and the bread of the fruit of your land shall be plenteous and rich: and your cattle shall feed in that day in a fertile and spacious place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Your bulls and your oxen that till the ground, shall eat chaff mixed with winnowed barley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there shall be upon every lofty mountain and upon every high hill, water running in that day, when many shall perish, and when the towers shall fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold in the day when the Lord shall heal the breach of his people, and shall heal the pain of your wound. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a [long] time, burning wrath: the word of his lips is with glory, a word full of anger, and the anger of his wrath shall devour as fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And his breath, as rushing water in a valley, shall reach as far as the neck, and be divided, to confound the nations for [their] vain error: error also shall pursue them, and overtake them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Must you⌃ always rejoice, and go into my holy places continually, as they that keep a feast? and must you⌃ go with a pipe, as those that rejoice, into the mountain of the Lord, to the God of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the Lord shall make his glorious voice to be heard, and the wrath of his arm, to make a display with wrath and anger and devouring flame: he shall lighten terribly, and [his wrath shall be] as water and violent hail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For by the voice of the Lord the Assyrians shall be overcome, [even] by the stroke wherewith he shall strike them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And it shall happen to him from every side, [that] they from whom their hope of assistance was, in which he trusted, themselves shall war against him in turn with drums and with harp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} For you shall be required before [your] time: has it been prepared for you also to reign? nay, God has [prepared for you] a deep trench, wood piled, fire and much wood: the wrath of the Lord [shall be] as a trench kindled with sulphur.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 31}
\markright{ESAIAS 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, who trust in horses and chariots, for they are many; and in horses, [which are] a great multitude; and have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel, and have not sought the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Therefore he has wisely brought evils upon them, and his word shall not be frustrated; and he shall rise up against the houses of wicked men, and against their vain hope, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [even] an Egyptian, a man, and not God; the flesh of horses, and there is no help [in them]: but the Lord shall bring his hand upon them, and the helpers shall fail, and all shall perish together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For thus said the Lord to me, As a lion would roar, or a lion's whelp over prey which he has taken, and cry over it, until the mountains are filled with his voice, and [the animals] are awe-struck and tremble at the fierceness of his wrath: so the Lord of hosts shall descend to fight upon the mount Sion, [even] upon her mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} As birds flying, so shall the Lord of hosts defend; he shall defend Jerusalem, and he shall rescue, and save and deliver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Turn, you⌃ children of Israel, who devise a deep and sinful counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For in that day men shall renounce their silver idols and [their] golden idols, which their hands made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Assyrian shall fall: not the sword of a great man, nor the sword of a mean man shall devour him; neither shall he flee from the face of the sword: but the young men shall be overthrown: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} for they shall be compassed with rocks as with a trench, and shall be worsted; and he that flees shall be taken. Thus says the Lord, Blessed is he that has a seed in Sion, and household friends in Jerusalem.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} to them, ; stay on horses;, the look, ; neither \textsuperscript{2} he also; will bring; will not; call back Heb. remove arise; against the help \textsuperscript{3} the Egyptians; their horses stretch; both \textsuperscript{4} Like as; noise or, multitude so shall \textsuperscript{5} birds; defending passing Or rather, as Bp. Lowth renders, "leaping forward, " pasoacḣ As the mother bird spreads her wings to cover her young, throws herself before them, and opposes the rapacious bird that assaults them; so shall Jehovah protect, as with a shield, Jerusalem from the enemy, protecting and delivering, springing forward and rescuing her. \textsuperscript{7} in that; his idols of gold Heb. the idols of his gold for a sin \textsuperscript{8} shall the, ; he shall flee from the sword or, for fear of the sword discomfited or, tributary. Heb. for melting, or tribute. \textsuperscript{9} he shall pass over to his strong hold for fear Heb. his rock shall pass away for fear. or, his strength. the ensign., whose fire\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 32}
\markright{ESAIAS 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For, behold, a righteous king shall reign, and princes shall govern with judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And a man shall hide his words, and be hidden, as from rushing water, and shall appear in Sion as a rushing river, glorious in a thirsty land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they shall no more trust in men, but they shall incline their ears to hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the heart of the weak ones shall attend to hear, and the stammering tongues shall soon learn to speak peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they shall no more at all tell a fool to rule, and your servants shall no more at all say, Be silent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the fool shall speak foolish words, and his heart shall meditate vanities, and to perform lawless deeds and to speak error against the Lord, to scatter hungry souls, and he will cause the thirsty souls to be empty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the counsel of the wicked will devise iniquity, to destroy the poor with unjust words, and ruin the cause of the poor in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the godly have devised wise [measures], and this counsel shall stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Rise up, you⌃ rich women, and hear my voice; you⌃ confident daughters, listen to my words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Remember for a full year in pain, yet with hope: the vintage has been cut off; it has ceased, it shall by no means come again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Be amazed, be pained, you⌃ confident ones: strip you, bare yourselves, gird your loins; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and beat your breasts, because of the pleasant field, and the fruit of the vine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [As for] the land of my people, the thorn and grass shall come upon [it], and joy shall be removed from every house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} [As for] the rich city, the houses are deserted; they shall abandon the wealth of the city, [and] the pleasant houses: and the villages shall be caves for ever, the joy of wild asses, shepherds' pastures; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} until the Spirit shall come upon you from on high, and Chermel shall be desert, and Chermel shall be counted for a forest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then judgment shall abide in the wilderness, and righteousness shall dwell in Carmel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the works of righteousness shall be peace; and righteousness shall ensure rest, and [the righteous] shall be confident for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And his people shall inhabit a city of peace, and dwell in [it] in confidence, and they shall rest with wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if the hail should come down, it shall not come upon you; and they that dwell in the forests shall be in confidence, as those in the plain country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Blessed are they that sow by every water, where the ox and ass tread.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 33}
\markright{ESAIAS 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Woe to them that afflict you; but no one makes you miserable: and he that deals perfidiously with you does not deal perfidiously: they that deal perfidiously shall be taken and given up, and as a moth on a garment, so shall they be spoiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Lord, have mercy upon us; for we have trusted in you: the seed of the rebellious is gone to destruction, but our deliverance was in a time of affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} By reason of the terrible sound the nations were dismayed for fear of you, and the heathen were scattered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And now shall the spoils of your small and great be gathered: as if one should gather locusts, so shall they mock you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The God who dwells on high is holy: Sion is filled with judgment and righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They shall be delivered up to the law: our salvation is our treasure: there are wisdom and knowledge and piety toward the Lord; these are the treasures of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold now, these shall be terrified with fear of you: those whom you⌃ feared shall cry out because of you: messengers shall be sent, bitterly weeping, entreating for peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the ways of these shall be made desolate: the terror of the nations has been made to cease, and the covenant with these is taken away, and you⌃ shall by no means deem them men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The land mourns; Libanus is ashamed: Saron is become marshes; Galilee shall be laid bare, and Chermel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now will I arise, says the Lord, now will I be glorified; now will I be exalted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now shall you⌃ see, now shall you⌃ perceive; the strength of your breath, shall be vain; fire shall devour you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the nations shall be burnt up; as a thorn in the field cast out and burnt up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} They that are afar off shall hear what I have done; they that draw near shall know my strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The sinners in Sion have departed; trembling shall seize the ungodly. Who will tell you that a fire is kindled? Who will tell you of the eternal place? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He that walks in righteousness, speaking rightly, hating transgression and iniquity, and shaking his hands from gifts, stopping his ears that he should not hear the judgment of blood, shutting his eyes that he should not see injustice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} he shall dwell in a high cave of a strong rock: bread shall be given him, and his water shall be sure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} You⌃ shall see a king with glory: your eyes shall behold a land from afar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Your soul shall meditate terror. Where are the scribes? where are the counselors, where is he that numbers them that are growing up, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [even] the small and great people? with whom he took not counsel, neither did he understand [a people] of deep speech, so that a despised people should not hear, and there is no understanding to him that hears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Behold the city of Sion, our refuge: your eyes shall behold Jerusalem, a rich city, tabernacles which shall not be shaken, neither shall the pins of her tabernacle be moved for ever, neither shall her cords be at all broken: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} for the name of the Lord is great to you: you⌃ shall have a place, [even] rivers and wide and spacious channels: you shall not go this way, neither a vessel with oars go [thereby]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For my God is great: the Lord our judge shall not pass me by: the Lord is our prince, the Lord is our king; the Lord, he shall save us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Your cords are broken, for they had no strength: your meat has given way, it shall not spread the sails, it shall not bear a signal, until it be given up for plunder; therefore shall many lame men take spoil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the people dwelling among them shall by no means say, I am in pain: for their sin shall be forgiven them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} thee that, ; when thou shalt cease \textsuperscript{2} be gracious, ;, ; be thou; our salvation \textsuperscript{5} The Lord, ;, ;, ; he dwelleth; he hath \textsuperscript{6} wisdom; , ; strength, salvation Heb. salvations fear \textsuperscript{7} valiant ones or, messengers the ambassadors \textsuperscript{8} highways; he hath broken he hath despised; he regardeth \textsuperscript{9} earth, ; Lebanon; hewn down or, withered away Sharon; Bashan \textsuperscript{10} Now will I rise, ; now will I be exalted; will I lift \textsuperscript{13} Hear, ; ye that are near \textsuperscript{14} sinners, ; the hypocrites; Who among us shall dwell with the, ; everlasting \textsuperscript{15} that walketh;, ; righteously Heb. in righteousnesses uprightly Heb. in uprightnesses despiseth; oppressions or, deceits shaketh; stoppeth; blood Heb. bloods shutteth \textsuperscript{16} shall dwell;, ; high Heb. heights, or high places his place; bread \textsuperscript{17} eyes; that is very far off Heb. of far distances \textsuperscript{18} heart; Where is the scribe receiver Heb. weigher;, where is he \textsuperscript{19} shalt not; deeper; stammering or, ridiculous \textsuperscript{20} Look the city; thine eyes, not one \textsuperscript{21} the glorious; a place broad rivers and streams Heb. broad of spaces, or hands \textsuperscript{22} the Lord is our judge; lawgiver Heb. statute-maker; the Lord is our king, ; he will \textsuperscript{23} Thy tacklings are loosed or, they have forsaken thy tacklings;, then; the lame \textsuperscript{24} the inhabitant; shall be forgiven\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 34}
\markright{ESAIAS 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Draw near, you⌃ nations; and listen, you⌃ princes; let the earth hear, and they that are in it; the world, and the people that are therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the wrath of the Lord is upon all nations, and [his] anger upon the number of them, to destroy them, and give them up to slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And their slain shall be cast forth, and their corpses; and their [ill] savor shall come up, and the mountains shall be made wet with their blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And all the powers of the heavens shall melt, and the sky shall be rolled up like a scroll: and all the stars shall fall like leaves from a vine, and as leaves fall from a fig tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} My sword has been made drunk in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and with judgment upon the people doomed to destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is glutted with fat, with the blood of goats and lambs, and with the fat of goats and rams: for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosor, and a great slaughter in Idumea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the mighty ones shall fall with them, and the rams and the bulls; and the land shall be soaked with blood, and shall be filled with their fat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For it is the day of judgment of the Lord, and the year of the recompence of Sion in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And her valleys shall be turned into pitch, and her land into sulphur; and her land shall be as pitch burning night and day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and it shall never be quenched, and her smoke shall go up: it shall be made desolate throughout her generations, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and for a long time birds and hedgehogs, and ibises and ravens shall dwell in it: and the measuring line of desolation shall be cast over it, and satyrs shall dwell in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Her princes shall be no more; for her kings and her great men shall be destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And thorns shall spring up in their cities, and in her strong holds: and they shall be habitations of monsters, and a court of ostriches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And devils shall meet with satyrs, and they shall cry one to the other: there shall satyrs rest, having found for themselves [a place of] rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} There has the hedgehog made its nest, and the earth has safely preserved its young: there have the deer met, and seen one another's faces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They passed by in [full] number, and not one of them perished: they sought not one another; for the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he shall cast lots for them, and his hand has portioned out [their] pasture, [saying], You⌃ shall inherit [the land] for ever: they shall rest on it [through] all generations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Come This and the following chapter, as Bp. Lowth observes, form one distinct prophecy; an entire, regular, and beautiful poem, consisting of two parts; the first containing a denunciation of Divine vengeance against the enemies of the people or church of God; the second describing the flourishing state of that church consequent upon those judgments. The event foretold is represented as of the highest importance, and of universal concern; all nations are called upon to attend to the declaration of it; and the wrath of God is denounced against all the nations who had provoked to anger the Defender of the cause of Zion. By a figure frequently occurring in the prophetical writings, the cities and people mentioned here, who were remarkably distinguished as the enemies of the people of God, are put for those enemies in general., ; let the; all that is therein Heb. the fulness thereof \textsuperscript{2} the indignation; Amos 1:1-2:16; , and his \textsuperscript{5} my sword; upon Idumea; the people \textsuperscript{6} filled; the fat the Lord hath \textsuperscript{7} unicorns or, rhinoceroses, ; the bullocks;, soaked or, drunken \textsuperscript{10} shall not; the smoke, from \textsuperscript{13} thorns; an habitation;, ; owls or, ostriches, Heb. daughters of the owl \textsuperscript{14} The wild beasts of the desert Heb. \subsection*{Esaias 35}
\markright{ESAIAS 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Be glad, you thirsty desert: let the wilderness exult, and flower as the lily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the desert places of Jordan shall blossom and rejoice; the glory of Libanus has been given to it, and the honor of Carmel; and my people shall see the glory of the Lord, and the majesty of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Be strong, you⌃ relaxed hands and palsied knees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Comfort one another, you⌃ faint-hearted; be strong, fear not; behold, our God renders judgment, and he will render [it]; he will come and save us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the stammerers shall speak plainly; for water has burst forth in the desert, and a channel [of water] in a thirsty land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the dry land shall become pools, and a fountain of water shall [be poured] into the thirsty land; there shall there be a joy of birds, ready habitations and marshes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} There shall be there a pure way, and it shall be called a holy way; and there shall not pass by there any unclean person, neither shall there be there an unclean way; but the dispersed shall walk on it, and they shall not go astray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there shall be no lion there, neither shall any evil beast go up upon it, nor at all be found there; but the redeemed and gathered on the Lord's behalf, shall walk in it, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and shall return, and come to Sion with joy, and everlasting joy [shall be] over their head; for on their head [shall be] praise and exultation, and joy shall take possession of them: sorrow and pain, and groaning have fled away.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 36}
\markright{ESAIAS 36}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of the reign of Ezekias, [that] Sennacherim, king of the Assyrians, came up against the strong cities of Judea, and took them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabsaces out of Laches to Jerusalem to king Ezekias with a large force: and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the way of the fuller's field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And there went forth to him Heliakim the steward, the [son] of Chelcias, and Somnas the scribe, and Joach the [son] of Asaph, the recorder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Rabsaces said to them, Say to Ezekias, Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians, Why are you secure? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Is war carried on with counsel and [mere] words of the lips? and now on whom do you trust, that you rebel against me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Behold, you trust on this bruised staff of reed, on Egypt: [as soon] as a man leans upon it, it shall go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharao king of Egypt and all that trust in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But if you⌃ say, We trust in the Lord our God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} yet now make an agreement with my lord the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you⌃ shall be able to set riders upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And how can you⌃ [then] turn to the face of the satraps? They that trust on the Egyptians for horse and rider, are [our] servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now, Have we come up against this land to fight against it without the Lord? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Then Eliakim and Somnas and Joach said to him, Speak to your servants in the Syrian tongue; for we understand [it]: and speak not to us in the Jewish tongue: and therefore speak you in the ears of the men on the wall? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Rabsaces said to them, Has my lord sent me to your lord or to you, to speak these words? [has he] not [sent] me to the men that sit on the wall, that they may eat dung, and drink [their] water together with you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Rabsaces stood and cried with a loud voice in the Jewish language, and said, Hear you⌃ the words of the great king, the king of the Assyrians: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} thus says the king, Let not Ezekias deceive you with words: he will not be able to deliver you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And let not Ezekias say to you, That God will deliver you, and this city will not at all be delivered into the hand of the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Listen not to Ezekias: thus says the king of the Assyrians, If you⌃ wish to be blessed, come out to me: and you⌃ shall eat every one [of] his vine and his fig-trees, and you⌃ shall drink water out of your own cisterns: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} until I come and take you to a land, like your own land, a land of corn and wine, and bread, and vineyards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Let not Ezekias deceive you, saying, God will deliver you. Have the gods of the nations delivered each one his own land out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Where is the god of Emath, and Arphath? and where is the god of Eppharuaim? have they been able to deliver Samaria out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Which is the god of all these nations, that has delivered his land out of my hand, that God should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they were silent, and none answered him a word; because the king had commanded that none should answer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Heliakim the [son] of Chelcias, the steward, and Somnas the military scribe, and Joach the [son] of Asaph, the recorder, came in to Ezekias, having their garments torn, and they reported to him the words of Rabsaces.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} am 3294, bc 710 sent; the conduit \textsuperscript{3} Eliakim Shebna, scribe or, secretary \textsuperscript{4} Thus saith; Assyria proper, now Kourdistan, was bounded by Armenia on the north, Media and Persia on the east, Babylonia on the south, and the Tigris, which divides it from Mesopotamia, on the west, between 33 degrees and 38 degrees n lat. and 42 degrees and 46 degrees e long. But the Assyrian empire, the bounds of which were different at different times, in its most flourishing state, according to the descriptions of the Greek and Roman writers, comprehended all the countries and nations between the Mediterranean on the west, and the Indus on the east, and between the deserts of Scythia on the north, and the Indian ocean on the south. Hiller considers the name as denoting Sephar of the Parvaim, i.e., Mount Sephar adjacent to the regions of Arabia called Parvaim. But it is more probable, as Wells and others suppose, that Sepharvaim is the Σιπφαρα, Sipphara, of Ptolemy, the Σιππαρηνων πολις, the city of the Sippareni, mentioned by Abydenus, and probably the Hipparenum of Pliny, a city of Mesopotamia, situated upon the Euphrates, near where it is divided into two arms, by one of which, it is probable, it was divided into two parts. and have \textsuperscript{22} Eliakim, with their; The history of the invasion of Sennacherib, observes Bp. Lowth, and the miraculous destruction of his army, which makes the subject of so many of Isaiah's prophecies, is very properly inserted here, as affording the best light to many parts of these prophecies; and as almost necessary to introduce the prophecy in the, being the answer of God to Hezekiah's prayer, which could not be properly understood without it. Sennacherib succeeded his father Shalmaneser on the throne of Assyria, am 3290, bc 714, and reigned only about eight years.\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 37}
\markright{ESAIAS 37}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, when king Ezekias heard [it, that] he tore his clothes, and put on sackcloth, and went up to the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he sent Heliakim the steward, and Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests clothed with sackcloth, to Esaias the son of Amos, the prophet. And they said to him, Thus says Ezekias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} To-day is a day of affliction, and reproach, and rebuke, and anger: for the pangs are come upon the travailing [woman], but she has not strength to bring forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} May the Lord your God hear the words of Rabsaces, which the king of the Assyrians has sent, to reproach the living God, even to reproach with the words which the Lord your God has heard: therefore you shall pray to your Lord for these that are left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So the servants of king Ezekias came to Esaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Esaias said to them, Thus shall you⌃ say to your master, Thus says the Lord, Be not you afraid at the words which you have heard, wherewith the ambassadors of the king of the Assyrians have reproached me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Behold, I [will] send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a report, and return to his own country, and he shall fall by the sword in his own land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So Rabsaces returned, and found the king of the Assyrians besieging Lobna: for he had heard that he had departed from Lachis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Tharaca king of the Ethiopians went forth to attack him. And when he heard it, he turned aside, and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Thus shall you⌃ say to Ezekias king of Judea, Let not your God, in whom you trust, deceive you, saying, Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Have you not heard what the kings of the Assyrians have done, how they have destroyed the whole earth? and shall you be delivered? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Have the gods of the nations which my fathers destroyed delivered them, both Gozan, and Charrhan, and Rapheth, which are in the land of Theemath? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Where are the kings of Emath? and where [is the king of] Arphath? and where [is the king] of the city of Eppharuaim, [and of] Anagugana? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Ezekias received the letter from the messengers, and read it, and went up to the house of the Lord, and opened it before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Ezekias prayed to the Lord, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who sit upon the cherubs, you alone are the God of every kingdom of the world: you have made heaven and earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Incline your ear, O Lord, listen, O Lord; open your eyes, O Lord, look, O Lord: and behold the words of Sennacherim, which he has sent to reproach the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For of a truth, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the whole world, and the countries thereof, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and have cast their idols into the fire: for, they were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone; and they have cast them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But now, O Lord our God, deliver us from his hands, that every kingdom of the earth may know that you are God alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Esaias the son of Amos was sent to Ezekias, and said to him, Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, I have heard your prayer to me concerning Sennacherim king of the Assyrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} This is the word which God has spoken concerning him; The virgin daughter of Sion has despised you, and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Whom have you reproached and provoked? and against whom have you lifted up your voice? and have you not lifted up your eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For you have reproached the Lord by messengers; for you have said, With the multitude of chariots have I ascended to the height of mountains, and to the sides of Libanus; and I have cropped the height of his cedars and the beauty of his cypresses; and I entered into the height of the forest region: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and I have made a bridge, and dried up the waters, and every pool of water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Have you not heard of these things which I did of old? I appointed [them] from ancient times; but now have I manifested [my purpose] of desolating nations in [their] strong holds, and them that dwell in strong cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} I weakened [their] hands, and they withered; and they became as dry grass on the housetops, and as grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But now I know your rest, and your going out, and your coming in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And your wrath wherewith you have been enraged, and your rancour has come up to me; therefore I will put a hook in your nose, and a bit in your lips, and will turn you back by the way by which you came. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And this shall be a sign to you, Eat this year what you have sown; and the second year that which is left: and the third year sow, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they that are left in Judea shall take root downward, and bear fruit upward: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} for out of Jerusalem there shall be a remnant, and the saved ones out of mount Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall perform this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians, He shall not enter into this city, nor cast a weapon against it, nor bring a shield against it, nor make a rampart round it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But by the way by which he came, by it shall he return, and shall not enter into this city: thus says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} I will protect this city to save it for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the angel of the Lord went forth, and killed out of the camp of the Assyrians one hundred and eighty-five thousand: and they arose in the morning and found all [these] bodies dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Sennacherim king of the Assyrians turned and departed, and lived in Nineve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And while he was worshipping Nasarach his country's god in the house, Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with swords; and they escaped into Armenia: and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} it came he rent; and went \textsuperscript{3} his day, ; blasphemy or, provocation, for the \textsuperscript{4} It may; to reproach, ; and will; lift up, ; for the, ; left Heb. found \textsuperscript{7} I will, ; send a blast upon him or, put a spirit into him I will cause \textsuperscript{9} he heard Ethiopia Cush, which is generally rendered Ethiopia, is applied in Scripture to at least three distinct and different countries. 1. The country watered by the Gihon or Araxes ( ), also called Cuth, . 2. A country of Arabia Petrea, bordering upon Egypt, which extended from the northern extremity of the Red sea along its eastern shore. (Compare with and ). 3. Ethiopia Proper, an extensive country of Africa, comprehending Nubia and Abyssinia; being bounded on the north by Egypt, on the east by the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, and on the south and west by various nations of Africa, and extending from about 6 degrees to 24 degrees n lat. and 25 degrees to 45 degrees e long. It is probable that it was this latter Cush, or Ethiopia, of which Tirhakah was king; he being in league with his kinsman Sevechus, son of So, or Sabacon, king of Egypt, against Sennacherib, the king of Assyria. \textsuperscript{12} the gods, Gozan, Haran, the Carrhe of the Greeks and Romans, is situated in the north-west part of Mesopotamia, between the Euphrates and the river Chebar; about 110 miles west of Nisibis, 90 east of Bir, 100 south of Diarbekir, and 170 north of Palmyra., ; Eden It is probable that this Eden is the country near Diarbekir, on the Tigris, called Madon, according to Asseman.; Telassar is probably the same as Ellasar, as the Jerusalem Targum reads; for both of which the Syriac has Dolassar; and perhaps, as Doederlein supposes, the same as Sharra, a city of Mesopotamia, half a mile from the Euphrates., Thelasar \textsuperscript{13} Hamath; Hena is probably the same as Anah, a city of Mesopotamia, situated on an island in the Euphrates. Ararat; Esarhaddon Esar-haddon, called Asar-addinus in the Canon of Ptolemy, was the third son of Sennacherib; and having reigned twenty-nine years over the Assyrians, he took advantage of the anarchy and confusion which followed the death of Mesessimordacus, and seized upon Babylon; which he added to his former empire, and reigned over both for thirteen years; when he was succeeded by his son Saosduchinus, am 3336, bc 668.\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 38}
\markright{ESAIAS 38}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass at that time, [that] Ezekias was sick even to death. And Esaias the prophet the son of Amos came to him, and said to him, Thus says the Lord, Give orders concerning your house: for you shall die, and not live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ezekias turned his face to the wall, and prayed to the Lord, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Remember, O Lord, how I have walked before you in truth, with a true heart, and have done that which was pleasing in your sight. And Ezekias wept bitterly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the word of the Lord came to Esaias, saying, Go, and say to Ezekias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father, I have heard your prayer, and seen your tears: behold, I [will] add to your time fifteen years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians: and I will defend this city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And this [shall be] a sign to you from the Lord, that God will do this thing; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} behold, I will turn back the shadow of the degrees [of the dial] by which ten degrees on the house of your father the sun has gone down—I will turn back the sun the ten degrees; so the sun went back the ten degrees by which the shadow had gone down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} THE PRAYER OF EZEKIAS KING OF JUDEA, WHEN HE HAD BEEN SICK, AND WAS RECOVERED FROM HIS SICKNESS. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I said in the end of my days, I shall go to the gates of the grave: I shall part with the remainder of my years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I said, I shall no more at all see the salvation of God in the land of the living: I shall no more at all see the salvation of Israel on the earth: I shall no more at all see man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [My life] has failed from among my kindred: I have parted with the remainder of my life: it has gone forth and departed from me, as one that having pitched a tent takes it down [again]: my breath was with me as a weaver's web, when she that weaves draws near to cut off [the] thread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} In that day I was given up as to a lion until the morning: so has he broken all my bones: for I was so given up from day [even] to night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As a swallow, so will I cry, and as a dove, so do I mourn: for my eyes have failed with looking to the height of heaven to the Lord, who has delivered me, and removed the sorrow of my soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [Yes], O Lord, for it was told you concerning this; and you have revived my breath; and I am comforted, and live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For you have chosen my soul, that it should not perish: and you have cast all [my] sins behind me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For they that are in the grave shall not praise you, neither shall the dead bless you, neither shall they that are in Hades hope for your mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The living shall bless you, as I also [do]: for from this day shall I beget children, who shall declare your righteousness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} O God of my salvation; and I will not cease blessing you with the lute all the days of my life before the house of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now Esaias had said to Ezekias; Take a cake of figs, and mash them, and apply them as a plaster, and you shall be well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And Ezekias said, This is a sign to Ezekias, that I shall go up to the house of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3291, bc 718 was Hezekiah; And Isaiah, Set thine house in order Heb. Give charge concerning thy house; for thou \textsuperscript{2} turned Hezekiah's couch was probably placed in a corner, which is the place of honour in the East; in which, turning on either side, he must turn his face to the wall; by which he would withdraw himself from those attending him in his apartment. \textsuperscript{3} Remember, ; I have, ; a perfect; wept; sore Heb. with great weeping \textsuperscript{5} and say; God;, ; I have heard; I have seen, ; I will \textsuperscript{8} I will bring; the sun dial Heb. the degrees by, or, with the sun, Or, as the Hebrew might be rendered, "the steps of Ahaz." The researches of curious travellers in Hindostan, observes Bp. Stock, have lately discovered in that country, three observatories of similar form, the most remarkable of which is to be seen within four miles of Delhi, the ancient capital of the Mogul empire. A rectangled triangle, whose hypotenuse is a staircase (apparently parallel to the axis of the earth), bisects a zone, or coping of a wall, which wall connects the two terminating towers at right and left. The coping itself is of a circular form, and accurately graduated, to mark, by the gnomon above, the sun's progress before and after noon. \textsuperscript{9} writing; *title, ; he had; We have here Hezekiah's thanksgiving song, which he penned by Divine direction, after his recovery. He might have used some of the Psalms of David his father, as he had appointed the Levites to praise the Lord with the words of David, but the occasion here was extraordinary. His heart being full of devout affections, he would not confine himself to the compositions he had, though of Divine inspiration, but offered up his praises in his own words. The Lord put a new song into his mouth. He put his thanksgiving into writing, that he might review it himself afterwards, for the reviving of the good impressions made upon him by the providential interference, and that it might be recommended to others also for their use upon the like occasion. \textsuperscript{12} is removed;, as a, have cut, ; he will cut; with pining sickness or, from the thrum \textsuperscript{14} a crane; I did mourn; mine eyes, ; I am, undertake for me or, ease me \textsuperscript{17} for peace I had great bitterness or, on my peace came great bitterness, ; in love to my soul delivered it from the pit Heb. loved my soul from the pit, ; thou hast cast\par}

\subsection*{Esaias 39}
\markright{ESAIAS 39}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} At that time Marodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, the king of Babylonia, sent letters and ambassadors and gifts to Ezekias: for he had heard that he had been sick [even] to death, and was recovered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ezekias was glad of their coming, and he showed them the house of [his] spices, and of silver, and gold, and myrrh, and incense, and ointment, and all the houses of his treasures, and all that he had in his stores: and there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, which Ezekias did not show. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Esaias the prophet came to king Ezekias, and said to him, What say these men? and whence came they to you? and Ezekias said, They are come to me from a land afar off, from Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Esaias said, What have they seen in your house? and Ezekias said, They have seen everything in my house; and there is nothing in my house which they have not seen: yes, also the [possessions] in my treasuries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Esaias said to him, Hear the word of the Lord of hosts: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Behold, the days come, when they shall take all the [things that are] in your house, and all that your fathers have gathered until this day, shall go to Babylon; and they shall not leave anything at all: and God has said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} that they shall take also of your children whom you shall beget; and they shall make them eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Ezekias said to Esaias, Good is the word of the Lord, which he has spoken: let there, I pray, be peace and righteousness in my days.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 40}
\markright{ESAIAS 40}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Comfort you⌃, comfort you⌃ my people, says God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speak, you⌃ priests, to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her, for her humiliation is accomplished, her sin is put away: for she has received of the Lord's hand double [the amount of] her sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare you⌃ the way of the Lord, make straight the paths of our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low: and all the crooked [ways] shall become straight, and the rough [places] plains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the glory of the Lord shall appear, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God: for the Lord has spoken [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The voice of one saying, Cry; and I said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The grass withers, and the flower fades: but the word of our God abides for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} O you that bring glad tidings to Zion, go up on the high mountain; lift up your voice with strength, you that bring glad tidings to Jerusalem; lift it up, fear not; say to the cities of Juda, Behold your God! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Behold the Lord! The Lord is coming with strength, and [his] arm is with power: behold, his reward is with him, and [his] work before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He shall tend his flock as a shepherd, and he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and shall soothe them that are with young. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Who has measured the water in his hand, and the heaven with a span, and all the earth in a handful? Who has weighed the mountains in scales, and the forests in a balance? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Who has known the mind of the Lord? and who has been his counsellor, to instruct him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Or with whom has he taken counsel, and he has instructed him? or who has taught him judgment, or who has taught him the way of understanding; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} since all the nations are counted as a drop from a bucket, and as the turning of a balance, [and] shall be counted as spittle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Libanus is not enough to burn, nor all beasts enough for a whole burnt offering: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and all the nations are as nothing, and counted as nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} To whom have you⌃ compared the Lord? and with what likeness have you⌃ compared him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Has not the artificer made an image, or the goldsmith having melted gold, gilt it over, [and] made it a similitude? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the artificer chooses out a wood that will not rot, and will wisely enquire how he shall set up his image, and [that so] that it should not be moved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Will you⌃ not know? will you⌃ not hear? has it not been told you of old? Have you⌃ not known the foundations of the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} [It is] he that comprehends the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants in it are as grasshoppers; he that set up the heaven as a chamber, and stretched [it] out as a tent to dwell in: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} he that appoints princes to rule as nothing, and has made the earth as nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For they shall not plant, neither shall they sow, neither shall their root be fixed in the ground: he has blown upon them, and they are withered, and a storm shall carry them away like sticks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Now then to whom have you⌃ compared me, that I may be exalted? says the Holy One. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Lift up your eyes on high, and see, who has displayed all these things? [even] he that brings forth his host by number: he shall call them all by name by [means of his] great glory, and by the power of his might: nothing has escaped you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For say not you, O Jacob, and why have you spoken, Israel, [saying], My way is hid from God, and my God has taken away [my] judgement, and has departed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And now, have you not known? have you not heard? the eternal God, the God that formed the ends of the earth, shall not hunger, nor be weary, and there is no searching of his understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} He gives strength to the hungry, and sorrow to them that are not suffering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For the young [men] shall hunger, and the youths shall be weary, and the choice [men] shall be powerless: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} but they that wait on God shall renew [their] strength; they shall put forth new feathers like eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not hunger.\par

\subsection*{Esaias 41}
\markright{ESAIAS 41}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Hold a feast to me, you⌃ islands: for the princes shall renew [their] strength: let them draw near and speak together: then let them declare judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who raised up righteousness from the east, [and] called it to his feet, so that it should go? shall appoint [it] an adversary of Gentiles, and shall dismay kings, and bury their swords in the earth, and cast forth their bows and arrows as sticks? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he shall pursue them; the way of his feet shall proceed in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who has wrought and done these things? he has called it who called it from the generations of old; I God, the first and to [all] futurity, I AM. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The nations saw, and feared; the ends of the earth drew near, and came together, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} every one judging for his neighbor and [that] to assist his brother: and one will say, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The artificer has become strong, and the coppersmith that smites with the hammer, [and] forges also: sometimes he will say, It is a piece well joined: they have fastened them with nails; they will fix them, and they shall not be moved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But you, Israel, are my servant Jacob, and he whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraam, whom I have loved: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and from the high places of it I have called you, and said to you, You are my servant; I have chosen you, and I have not forsaken you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Fear not; for I am with you: wander not; for I am your God, who have strengthened you; and I have helped you, and have established you with my just right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, all your adversaries shall be ashamed and confounded; for they shall be as if they were not: and all your opponents shall perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You shall seek them, and you shall not find the men who shall insolently rage against you: for they shall be as if they were not, and they that war against you shall not be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For I am your God, who holds your right hand, who says to you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Fear not, Jacob, [and you] Israel few in number; I have helped you, says your God, he that redeems you, O Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Behold, I have made you as new saw-shaped threshing wheels of a wagon; and you shall thresh the mountains, and beat the hills to powder, and make [them] as chaff: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} and you shall winnow [them], and the wind shall carry them away, and a tempest shall scatter them: but you shall rejoice in the holy ones of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the poor and the needy shall exult; for [when] they shall seek water, and there shall be none, [and] their tongue is parched with thirst, I the Lord God, I the God of Israel will hear, and will not forsake them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} but I will open rivers on the mountains, and fountains in the midst of plains: I will make the desert pools of water, and a thirsty land watercourses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I will plant in the dry land the cedar and box, the myrtle and cypress, and white poplar: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} that they may see, and know, and perceive, and understand together, that the hand of the Lord has wrought these [works], and the Holy One of Israel has displayed [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Your judgment draws near, says the Lord God; your counsels have drawn near, says the King of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Let them draw near, and declare to you what things shall come to pass; or tell [us] what things were of old, and we will apply [our] understanding, and we shall know what are the last and the future things: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} tell us, declare you⌃ to us the things that are coming on at the last [time], and we shall know that you⌃ are gods: do good, and do evil, and we shall wonder, and see at the same time {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} whence you⌃ are, and whence is your works: they have chosen you an abomination out of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But I have raised up him that [comes] from the north, and him that [comes] from the rising of the sun: they shall be called by my name: let the princes come, and as potter's clay, and as a potter treading clay, so shall you⌃ be trodden down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For who will declare the things from the beginning, that we may know also the former things, and we will say that they are true? there is no one that speaks beforehand, nor anyone that hears your words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} I will give dominion to Sion, and will comfort Jerusalem by the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For from among the nations, behold, [there was] no one; and of their idols there was none to declare [anything]: and if I should ask them, Whence are you⌃? they could not answer me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For [these] are your makers, [as you⌃ think], and they that cause you to err in vain.\par
