\subsection*{Jeremias 43}
\markright{JEREMIAS 43}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} IN THE FOURTH YEAR OF JOAKIM son of Josias king of Juda, the word of the Lord came to me, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Take you a roll of a book, and write upon it all the words which I spoke to you against Jerusalem, and against Juda, and against all the nations, from the day when I spoke to you, from the days of Josias king of Juda, even to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Perhaps the house of Juda will hear all the evils which I purpose to do to them; that they may turn from their evil way; and [so] I will be merciful to their iniquities and their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So Jeremias called Baruch the son of Nerias: and he wrote from the mouth of Jeremias all the words of the Lord, which he had spoken to him, on a roll of a book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jeremias commanded Baruch, saying, I am in prison; I can’t enter into the house of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} so you shall read in this roll in the ears of the people in the house of the Lord, on the fast day; and in the ears of all Juda that come out of their cities, you shall read to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Peradventure their supplication will come before the Lord, and they will turn from their evil way: for great is the wrath and the anger of the Lord, which he has pronounced against this people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Baruch did according to all that Jeremias commanded him—reading in the book the words of the Lord in the Lord's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it came to pass in the eighth year of king Joakim, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem, and the house of Juda, proclaimed a fast before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Baruch read in the book the words of Jeremias in the house of the Lord, in the house of Gamarias son of Saphan the scribe, in the upper court, in the entrance of the new gate of the house of the Lord, and in the ears of all the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Michaeas the son of Gamarias the son of Saphan heard all the words of the Lord, out of the book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he went down to the king's house, into the house of the scribe: and, behold, there were sitting there all the princes, Elisama the scribe, and Dalaeas the son of Selemias, and Jonathan the son of Acchobor, and Gamarias the son of Saphan, and Sedekias the son of Ananias, and all the princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Michaeas reported to them all the words which he had heard Baruch reading in the ears of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the princes sent to Baruch son of Nerias Judin the son of Nathanias, the son of Selemias, the son of Chusi, saying, Take in your hand the roll in which you read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch took the roll, and went down to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they said to him, Read [it] again in our ears. And Baruch read [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it came to pass, when they [had] heard all the words, [that] they took counsel each with his neighbor, and said, Let us by all means tell the king all these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they asked Baruch, saying, Where did you write all these words? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Baruch said, Jeremias told me from his [own] mouth all these words, and I wrote them in a book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they said to Baruch, Go, and hide, you and Jeremias; let no man know where you⌃ [are]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they went in to the king into the court, and gave the roll [to one] to keep in the house of Elisama; and they told the king all these words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the king sent Judin to fetch the roll: and he took it out of the house of Elisama: and Judin read in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes who stood round the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Now the king was sitting in the winter house: and [there was] a fire on the hearth before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass when Judin had read three or four leaves, he cut them off with a penknife, and cast [them] into the fire that was on the hearth, until the whole roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king and his servants that heard all these words sought not [the Lord], and tore not their garments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But Elnathan and Godolias suggested to the king that he should burn the roll. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king commanded Jeremeel the king's son, and Saraeas the son of Esriel, to take Baruch and Jeremias: but they were hidden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremias, after the king had burnt the roll, [even] all the words which Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremias, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Again take you another roll, and write all the words that were on the roll, which king Joakim has burnt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And you shall say, Thus says the Lord; You have burnt this roll, saying, Why have you written therein, saying, The king of Babylon shall certainly come in, and destroy this land, and man and cattle shall fail from off it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Joakim king of Juda; He shall not have [a man] to sit on the throne of David: and his carcass shall be cast forth in the heat by day, and in the frost by night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And I will visit him, and his family, and his servants: and I will bring upon him, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the land of Juda, all the evils which I spoke of to them; and they listened not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And Baruch took another roll, and wrote upon it from the mouth of Jeremias all the words of the book which Joakim had burnt: and there were yet more words added to it like the former.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} had made, all the words \textsuperscript{2} Azariah, Jezaniah Johanan, all the;, ; Thou speakest They had no other colour for their rebellion than flatly to deny that God had spoken what the prophet had declared, the constant method of hypocrites and infidels, who pretend that they are not satisfied of the truth of Divine revelation, when the true cause of their unbelief is, that the commands of God contradict their lusts and appetites. \textsuperscript{7} So Tahpanhes, Tahapanhes, ; Hanes, Tehaphnehes \textsuperscript{10} I will send, ; my servant, ; his royal \textsuperscript{11} he shall smite; 30:1-32:32 such as are for death \textsuperscript{13} images Heb. statues, or standing images Bethshemesh or, the house of the sun. *marg. and the\par}

\subsection*{Jeremias 44}
\markright{JEREMIAS 44}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Sedekias the son of Josias reigned instead of Joakim, whom Nabuchodonosor appointed to reign over Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he and his servants and the people of the land listened not to the words of the Lord, which he spoke by Jeremias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And king Sedekias sent Joachal son of Selemias and Sophonias the priest son of Maasaeas to Jeremias, saying, Pray now for us to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now Jeremias came and went through the midst of the city: for they [had] not put him into the house of the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the host of Pharao was come forth out of Egypt; and the Chaldeans heard the report of them, and they went up from Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the word of the Lord came to Jeremias, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Thus said the Lord; Thus shall you say to the king of Juda who sent to you, to seek me; Behold, the army of Pharao which is come forth to help you: they shall return to the land of Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and the Chaldeans themselves shall turn again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For thus says the Lord; Suppose not in your hearts, saying, The Chaldeans will certainly depart from us: for they shall not depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And though you⌃ should strike the whole host of the Chaldeans that fight against you, and there should be left a few wounded [men], these should rise up each in his place, and burn this city with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, when the host of the Chaldeans had gone up from Jerusalem for fear of the host of Pharao, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that Jeremias went forth from Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to buy thence [a property] in the midst of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he was in the gate of Benjamin, and [there was] there a man with whom he lodged, Saruia the son of Selemias, the son of Ananias; and he caught Jeremias, saying, You are fleeing to the Chaldeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said, [It is] false; I do not flee to the Chaldeans. But he listened not to him; and Saruia caught Jeremias, and brought him to the princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the princes were very angry with Jeremias, and struck him, and sent him into the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made this a prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So Jeremias came into the dungeon, and into the cells, and he remained there many days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then Sedekias sent, and called him; and the king asked him secretly, saying, Is there a word from the Lord? and he said, There is: you shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jeremias said to the king, Wherein have I wronged you, or your servants, or this people, that you put me in prison? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And where are your prophets who prophesied to you saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against this land? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now therefore, my lord the king, let my supplication come before your face: and why do you send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe? and let me not on any account die there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then the king commanded, and they cast him into the prison, and gave him a loaf a day out of the place where they bake, until the bread failed out of the city. So Jeremias continued in the court of the prison.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Cir, am 3433, bc 571 The word Dahler supposes this discourse to have been delivered in the seventeenth or eighteenth year after the taking of Jerusalem. concerning, Migdol; *Heb: Tahpanhes rendered Ταφνη and Ταφναι by the LXX, is no doubt the Δαφναι of Herodotus, a royal city of Lower Egypt, situated, according to the Itinerary of Antoninus, sixteen miles south from Pelusium, from which it was called Daphne Pelusice. Forster says that there is now a place situated in the vicinity of Pelusium called Safnas, which may be a vestige of the ancient name. It appears to have been the very first town in Egypt, in the road from Palestine, that afforded tolerable accommodation for the fugitives. It was at this place that, according to Jerome and several of the ancients, tradition says the faithful Jeremiah was stoned to death by these rebellious wretches, for whose welfare he had watched, prayed, and suffered every kind of indignity and hardship.; Tehaphnehes Noph, ; Pathros, Pathrusim \textsuperscript{7} against, *marg.;, ; to cut, ; child; Judah Heb. the midst of Judah to leave \textsuperscript{8} ye provoke; that ye might cut; a curse \textsuperscript{9} ye forgotten; wickedness Heb. wickedness, or punishments, etc the wickedness of your \textsuperscript{10} are not; , ; humbled Heb. contrite; neither \textsuperscript{12} I will take, from the and they shall be \textsuperscript{14} So It is evident from verse 28, that some Jews were to escape the general destruction in Egypt, and to return into their own country, though but a few; and the same thing is implied in the latter clause of this verse. But the former part excludes from the number of those who should escape every individual of those who are properly termed "the remnant of Judah; " those who had willingly and rebelliously "set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to dwell there, " on a presumption that they knew better than God how to consult their own restoration. The few, then, who were destined to escape, were to be such as had come into the land of Egypt with Johanan by compulsion, or had previously fled thither, or in some other less offensive manner, and chanced to be there when the storm burst upon them. which are shall escape; which they, have a desire Heb. lift up there soul for none \textsuperscript{17} whatsoever; queen of heaven or, frame of heaven. As the Sun was worshipped, not only under the name of baal shamayim "Lord of heaven, " but also by that of Molech or King; it is likely also that the Moon was adored as melecheth hashshamayim "the Queen of heaven." So the Orphic hymn addressed to the Moon begins Κλυθι θεα ΒΑΣΙΛΕΙΑ, "Hear, goddess Queen." And Homer, in his Hymn to the Moon, addresses her, Χαιρε, ανασσα, θεα "All hail, Queen, goddess." In Epiphanius, we find some women of Arabia, towards the end of the fourth century, had set up another queen of heaven, the Virgin Mary, too well known since under that name and character, whom they likewise worshipped as a goddess, by holding stated assemblies every year to her honour, and by offering a cake of bread in her name; whence these heretics were called Collyridians, from the Greek κολλυρις, a cake.; as we; our fathers; in the cities, then; victuals Heb. bread \textsuperscript{19} we burned, without, ; men or, husbands\par}

\subsection*{Jeremias 45}
\markright{JEREMIAS 45}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Saphanias the son of Nathan, and Godolias the son of Paschor, and Joachal the son of Semelias, heard the words which Jeremias spoke to the people, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus says the Lord; He that remains in this city shall die by the sword, and by the famine: but he that goes out to the Chaldeans shall live; and his soul shall be given him for a found treasure, and he shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For thus says the Lord; This city shall certainly be delivered into the hands of the host of the king of Babylon, and they shall take it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they said to the king, Let that man, we pray you, be slain, for he weakens the hands of the fighting men that are left in the city, and the hands of all the people, speaking to them according to these words: for this man does not prophesy peace to this people, but evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then the king said, Behold, he is in your hands. For the king could not resist them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they cast him into the dungeon of Melchias the king's son, which was in the court of the prison; and they let him down into the pit: and there was no water in the pit, but mire: and he was in the mire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Abdemelech the Ethiopian heard, (now he was in the king's household,) that they [had] put Jeremias into the dungeon; and the king was in the gate of Benjamin: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and he went forth to him, and spoke to the king and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You have done evil in what you have done to kill this man with hunger: for there is no more bread in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king commanded Abdemelech, saying, Take with you hence thirty men, and bring him up out of the dungeon, that he die not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So Abdemelech took the men and went into the underground [part of the] king's house, and took thence old rags and old ropes, and threw them to Jeremias into the dungeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said, Put these under the ropes. And Jeremias did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they drew him with the ropes, and lifted him out of the dungeon: and Jeremias remained in the court of the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then the king sent, and called him to himself into the house of Aselisel, which was in the house of the Lord: and the king said to him, I will ask you a question, and I pray you hide nothing from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jeremias said to the king, If I tell you, will you not certainly put me to death? and if I give you counsel, you will not at all listen to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the king swore to him, saying, [As] the Lord lives who gave us this soul, I will not kill you, neither will I give you into the hands of these men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And Jeremias said to him, Thus says the Lord; If you will indeed go forth to the captains of the king of Babylon, your soul shall live, and this city shall certainly not be burnt with fire; and you shall live, and your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But if you will not go forth this city shall be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall by no means escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the king said to Jeremias, I consider the Jews that have gone over to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hands, and they mock me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jeremias said, They shall in no wise deliver you up. Hear the word of the Lord which I speak to you; and it shall be better for you, and your soul shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But if you will not go forth, this is the word which the Lord has shown me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And, behold, all the women that are left in the house of the king of Juda were brought forth to the princes of the king of Babylon; and they said, The men who were at peace with you have deceived you, and will prevail against you; and they shall cause your foot to slide and fail, they have turned back from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they shall bring forth your wives and your children to the Chaldeans: and you shall by no means escape, for you shall be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city shall be burnt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then the king said to him, Let no man know [any] of these words, and certainly you shall not die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if the princes shall hear that I have spoken to you, and they come to you, and say to you, Tell us, what said the king to you? hide [it] not from us, and we will in no wise kill you, and what said the king to you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then you shall say to them, I brought my supplication before the presence of the king, that he would not send me back into the house of Jonathan, that I should die there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And all the princes came to Jeremias, and asked him: and he told them according to all these words, which the king had commanded him. And they were silent, because the word of the Lord was not heard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Jeremias remained in the court of the prison, until the time when Jerusalem was taken.\par

\subsection*{Jeremias 46}
\markright{JEREMIAS 46}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the ninth month of Sedekias king of Juda, [that] Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and they besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And in the eleventh year of Sedekiass, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken [up]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all the leaders of the king of Babylon went in, and sat in the middle gate, Marganasar, and Samagoth, and Nabusachar, and Nabusaris, Nagargas, Naserrabamath, and the rest of the leaders of the king of Babylon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and they sent, and took Jeremias out of the court of the prison, and gave him [in charge] to Godolias the son of Achicam, the son of Saphan: and they brought him out, and he sat in the midst of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the word of the Lord came to Jeremias in the court of the prison, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Go and say to Abdemelech the Ethiopian, Thus said the Lord God of Israel; Behold, I [will] bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But I will save you in that day, and I will by no means deliver you into the hands of the men before whom you are afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For I will surely save you, and you shall by no means fall by the sword; and you shall find your life, because you did trust in me, says the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} The word This is a general title to the prophecies contained in this and the following chapters, concerning different nations which had less or more connexion with the Jews, either as enemies, neighbours, or allies. They were not delivered at the same time. To some the date is annexed; in others it is left uncertain. against \textsuperscript{2} Against Egypt, ; Ezek. 29:1-32:32 Pharaohnecho, Pharaoh-nechoh, Necho Carchemish in the \textsuperscript{3} This is a poetical and ironical call to the Egyptians to muster their forces; and implies that all their courage and efforts would be vain. \textsuperscript{16} made many to fall Heb. multiplied the faller one they said\par}

\subsection*{Jeremias 47}
\markright{JEREMIAS 47}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The word that came from the Lord to Jeremias, after that Nabuzardan the captain of the guard had let him go out of Rama, when he had taken him in manacles in the midst of the captivity of Juda, [even] those who were carried to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the chief captain of the guard took him, and said to him, The Lord your God has pronounced all these evils upon this place: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and the Lord has done it; because you⌃ sinned against him, and listened not to his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Behold, I have loosed you from the manacles that were upon your hands. If it seem good to you to go with me to Babylon, then will I set my eyes upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But if not, depart; return to Godolias the son of Achicam, the son of Saphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed governor in the land of Juda, and dwell with him in the midst of the people in the land of Juda: to whatever places it seems good in your eyes to go, do you even go. And the captain of the guard made him presents, and let him go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he came to Godolias to Massepha, and lived in the midst of his people that was left in the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And all the leaders of the host that was in the country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Godolias [governor] in the land, and they committed to him the men and their wives, whom [Nabuchodonosor had] not removed to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And there came to Godolias to Massepha Ismael the son of Nathanias, and Joanan son of Caree, and Saraeas the son of Thanaemeth, and the sons of Jophe the Netophathite, and Ezonias son of the Mochathite, they and their men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Godolias swore to them and to their men, saying, Be not afraid before the children of the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be better for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And, behold, I dwell in your presence at Massepha, to stand before the Chaldeans who shall come against you: and do you⌃ gather grapes, and fruits, and oil, and put [them] into your vessels, and dwell in the cities which you⌃ have obtained possession of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the children of Ammon, and those [that were] in Idumea, and those [that were] in all [the rest of] the country, heard that the king of Babylon [had] granted a remnant to Juda, and that he had appointed over them Godolias the son of Achicam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they came to Godolias into the land of Juda, to Massepha, and gathered grapes, and very much summer fruit, and oil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Joanan the son of Caree, and all the leaders of the host, who were in the fields, came to Godolias to Massepha, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and said to him, Do you indeed know that king Beleissa son of Ammon has sent Ismael to you to kill you? But Godolias believed them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Joanan said to Godolias secretly in Massepha, I will go now and strike Ismael, and let no man know [it]; lest he kill you, and all the Jews that are gathered to you be dispersed, and the remnant of Juda perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But Godolias said to Joanan, Do not the thing, for you speak lies concerning Ismael.\par

\subsection*{Jeremias 48}
\markright{JEREMIAS 48}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now it came to pass in the seventh month that Ismael the son of Nathanias the son of Eleasa of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, to Godolias to Massepha: and they ate bread there together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Ismael rose up, and the ten men that were with him, and struck Godolias, whom the king of Babylon had appointed [governor] over the land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and all the Jews that were with him in Massepha, and all the Chaldeans that were found there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass on the second day after he had struck Godolias, and no man knew [of it], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} that there came men from Sychem, and from Salem, and from Samaria, [even] eighty men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes torn, and beating their breasts, and [they had] manna and frankincense in their hands, to bring [them] into the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Ismael went out to meet them; [and] they went on and wept: and he said to them, Come in to Godolias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass, when they had entered into the midst of the city, [that] he killed them [and cast them] into a pit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But ten men were found there, and they said to Ismael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, wheat and barley, honey and oil. So he passed by, and killed them not in the midst of their brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now the pit into which Ismael cast all whom he struck, is the great pit, which king Asa had made for fear of Baasa king of Israel: [even] this Ismael filled with slain men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Ismael brought back all the people that were left in Massepha, and the king's daughter, whom the captain of the guard had committed in charge to Godolias the son of Achicam: and he went away beyond the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Joanan the son of Caree, and all the leaders of the host that were with him, heard of all the evil deeds which Ismael had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they brought all their army, and went to fight against him, and found him near much water in Gabaon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And it came to pass, when all the people that was with Ismael saw Joanan, and the leaders of the host that was with him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} that they returned to Joanan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But Ismael escaped with eight men and went to the children of Ammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Joanan, and all the leaders of the host that were with him, took all the remnant of the people, whom he [had] brought back from Ismael, mighty men in war, and the women, and the other [property], and the eunuchs, whom they [had] brought back from Gabaon: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} and they departed, and lived in Gaberoch-amaa, that is by Bethleem, to go into Egypt, for fear of the Chaldeans: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} for they were afraid of them, because Ismael had struck Godolias, whom the king of Babylon made [governor] in the land.\par

\subsection*{Jeremias 49}
\markright{JEREMIAS 49}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then came all the leaders of the host, and Joanan, and Azarias the son of Maasaeas, and all the people great and small, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} to Jeremias the prophet, and said to him, Let now our supplication come before your face, and pray you to the Lord your God for this remnant; for we are left few out of many, as your eyes see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And let the Lord your God declare to us the way wherein we should walk, and the thing which we should do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jeremias said to them, I have heard [you]; behold, I will pray for you to the Lord our God, according to your words; and it shall come to pass, [that] whatever word the Lord God shall answer, I will declare [it] to you; I will not hide anything from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they said to Jeremias, Let the Lord be between us for a just and faithful witness, if we do not according to every word which the Lord shall send to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And whether [it be] good, or whether [it be] evil, we will listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send you; that it may be well with us, because we shall listen to the voice of the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it came to pass after ten days, [that] the word of the Lord came to Jeremias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he called Joanan, and the leaders of the host, and all the people from the least even to the greatest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and he said to them, Thus says the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If you⌃ will indeed dwell in this land, I will build you, and will not pull [you] down, but will plant you, and in no wise pluck you up: for I have ceased from the calamities which I brought upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you⌃ are afraid; be not afraid of him, says the Lord: for I am with you, to deliver you, and save you out of their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I will grant you mercy, and pity you, and will restore you to your land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But if you⌃ say, We will not dwell in this land, that we may not listen to the voice of the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} for we will go into the land of Egypt, and we shall see no war, and shall not hear the sound of a trumpet, and we shall not hunger for bread; and there we will dwell: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} then hear the word of the Lord; thus says the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} If you⌃ set your face toward Egypt, and go in there to dwell; then it shall be, [that] the sword which you⌃ fear shall find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine to which you⌃ have regard, shall overtake you, [coming] after you in Egypt; and there you⌃ shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And all the men, and all the strangers who have set their face toward the land of Egypt to dwell there, shall be consumed by the sword, and by the famine: and there shall not one of them escape from the evils which I bring upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For thus says the Lord; As my wrath has dropped upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so shall my wrath drop upon you, when you⌃ have entered into Egypt: and you⌃ shall be a desolation, and under the power of others, and a curse and a reproach: and you⌃ shall no more see this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} [These are the words] which the Lord has spoken concerning you the remnant of Juda; Enter you⌃ not into Egypt: and now know you⌃ for a certainty, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} that you⌃ have wrought wickedness in your hearts, when you⌃ sent me, saying, Pray you for us to the Lord; and according to all that the Lord shall speak to you we will do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And you⌃ have not listened to the voice of the Lord, with which he sent me to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Now therefore you⌃ shall perish by sword and by famine, in the place which you⌃ desire to go into to dwell there.\par

\subsection*{Jeremias 50}
\markright{JEREMIAS 50}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, when Jeremias ceased speaking to the people all the words of the Lord, [for] which the Lord had sent him to them, [even] all these words, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that Azarias son of Maasaeas spoke, and Joanan, the son of Caree, and all the men who had spoken to Jeremias, saying, [It is] false: the Lord has not sent you to us, saying, Enter not into Egypt to dwell there: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} but Baruch the son of Nerias sets you against us, that you may deliver us into the hands of the Chaldeans, to kill us, and that we should be carried away captives to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So Joanan, and all the leaders of the host, and all the people, refused to listen to the voice of the Lord, to dwell in the land of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Joanan, and all the leaders of the host, took all the remnant of Juda, who had returned to dwell in the land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the mighty men, and the women, and the children that were left, and the daughters of the king, and the souls which Nabuzardan had left with Godolias the son of Achicam and Jeremias the prophet, and Baruch the son of Nerias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they came into Egypt: for they listened not to the voice of the Lord: and they entered into Taphnas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the word of the Lord came to Jeremias in Taphnas, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Take you great stones, and hide them in the entrance, at the gate of the house of Pharao in Taphnas, in the sight of the men of Juda: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and you shall say, Thus has the Lord said; Behold, I [will] send, and will bring Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and he shall place his throne upon these stones which you have hidden, and he shall lift up weapons against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he shall enter in, and strike the land of Egypt, [delivering] some for death to death; and some for captivity to captivity; and some for the sword to the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he shall kindle a fire in the houses of their gods, and shall burn them, and shall carry them away captives: and shall search the land of Egypt, as a shepherd searches his garment; and he shall go forth in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he shall break to pieces the pillars of Heliopolis that are in On, and shall burn their houses with fire.\par

\subsection*{Jeremias 51}
\markright{JEREMIAS 51}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} THE WORD THAT CAME TO JEREMIAS for all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt, and for those settled in Magdolo and in Taphnas, and in the land of Pathura, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus has the Lord God of Israel said; You⌃ have seen all the evils which I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon the cities of Juda; and, behold, they are desolate without inhabitants, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} because of their wickedness, which they have wrought to provoke me, [by] going to burn incense to other gods, whom you⌃ knew not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} yet I sent to you my servants the prophets early in the morning, and I sent, saying, Do not you⌃ this abominable thing which I hate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But they listened not to me, and inclined not their ear to turn from their wickedness, so as not to burn incense to strange gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So my anger and my wrath dropped [upon them], and was kindled in the gates of Juda, and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they became a desolation and a waste, as at this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And now thus has the Lord Almighty said, Therefore do you⌃ commit [these] great evils against your souls? to cut off man and woman of you, infant and suckling from the midst of Juda, to the end that not one of you should be left; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} by provoking me with the works of your hands, to burn incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, into which you⌃ entered to dwell there, that you⌃ might be cut off, and that you⌃ might become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Have you⌃ forgotten the sins of your fathers, and the sins of the kings of Juda, and the sins of your princes, and the sins of your wives, which they wrought in the land of Juda, and in the streets of Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And have not ceased even to this day, and they have not kept to my ordinances, which I set before their fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore thus says the Lord; Behold I do set my face against [you] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} to destroy all the remnant that are in Egypt; and they shall fall by the sword, and by famine, and shall be consumed small and great: and they shall be for reproach, and for destruction, and for a curse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I will visit them that dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have visited Jerusalem, with sword and with famine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and there shall not one be preserved of the remnant of Juda that sojourn in the land of Egypt, to return to the land of Juda, to which they hope in their hearts to return: they shall not return, but only they that escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then all the men that knew that their wives burned incense, and all the women, a great multitude, and all the people that lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathura, answered Jeremias, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} [As for] the word which you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For we will surely perform every word that shall proceed out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour drink-offerings to her, as we and our fathers have done, and our kings and princes, in the cities of Juda, and in the streets of Jerusalem: and [so] we were filled with bread, and were well, and saw no evils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, we have all been brought low, and have been consumed by sword and by famine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And whereas we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured drink-offerings to her, did we make cakes to her, and pour drink-offerings to her, without our husbands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Then Jeremias answered all the people, the mighty men, and the women, and all the people that returned him [these] words for answer, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Did not the Lord remember the incense which you⌃ burned in the cities of Juda, and in the streets of Jerusalem, you⌃, and your fathers, and your kings, and your princes, and the people of the land? and came it not into his heart? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the Lord could no longer bear [you], because of the wickedness of your doings, and because of your abominations which you⌃ wrought; and so your land became a desolation and a waste, and a curse, as at this day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} because of your burning incense, and [because] of the things wherein you⌃ sinned against the Lord: and you⌃ have not listened to the voice of the Lord, and have not walked in his ordinances, and in his law, and in his testimonies; and so these evils have come upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Jeremias said to the people, and to the women, Hear you⌃ the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Thus has the Lord God of Israel said; You⌃ women have spoken with your mouth, and you⌃ fulfilled [it] with your hands, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour drink-offerings to her: full well did you⌃ keep to your vows, and you⌃ have indeed performed [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore hear you⌃ the word of the Lord, all Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, my name shall no longer be in the mouth of every Jew to say, The Lord lives, in all the land of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For I have watched over them, to hurt them, and not to do them good: and all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt shall perish by sword and by famine, until they are utterly consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they that escape the sword shall return to the land of Juda few in number, and the remnant of Juda, who have continued in the land [of] Egypt to dwell there, shall know whose word shall stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And this [shall be] a sign to you, that I will visit you for evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Thus said the Lord; Behold, I [will] give Uaphres king of Egypt into the hands of his enemy, and into the hands of one that seeks his life; as I gave Sedekias king of Juda into the hands of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, his enemy, and who sought his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} THE WORD WHICH JEREMIAS THE PROPHET spoke to Baruch son of Nerias, when he wrote these words in the book from the mouth of Jeremias, in the fourth year of Joakim the son of Josias king of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Thus has the Lord said to you, O Baruch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Whereas you have said, Alas! alas! for the Lord has laid a grievous trouble upon me; I lay down in groaning, I found no rest; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} say you to him, Thus says the Lord; Behold, I pull down those whom I have built up, and I pluck up those whom I have planted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And will you seek great things for yourself? seek [them] not: for, behold, I bring evil upon all flesh, says the Lord: but I will give [to you] your life for a spoil in every place whither you shall go.\par

Cyrus had conquered Armenia, defeated Croesus king of Lydia (bc 548), and subdued several nations from the Egean sea to the Euphrates, before he marched against Babylon; and Xenophon also informs us that there were not only Armenians, but both Phrygians and Cappadocians in the army of Cyrus. Ashchenaz, Ashkenaz, cause, ; After Cyrus had been the instrument in the hands of God of taking Babylon, he marched against Tomyris, queen of the Massagete, a Scythian nation, and was totally defeated (bc 530). The victorious queen, who had lost her son in a previous battle, was so incensed against Cyrus, that she cut off his head, and threw it into a vessel filled with human blood, exclaiming, "Sattia te sanguine, quem sitisti." \textsuperscript{30} The mighty Accordingly, the Babylonians, after the loss of a battle or two, never recovered their courage to the face the enemy in the field, they retired within their walls; and the first time that Cyrus came with his army before the place he could not provoke them to venture forth, though he challenged the king to fight a duel with him; and the last time he came he consulted with his officers respecting the best mode of carrying on the siege "since, " said he, "they do not come out to fight.", ; her bars *marg. \textsuperscript{33} is like; it is time to thresh her or, in the time that he thresheth her the time \textsuperscript{34} the king, ; he hath made; swallowed \textsuperscript{35} The violence Heb. \subsection*{Jeremias 52}
\markright{JEREMIAS 52}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} It was the twenty-first year of Sedekias, when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Amitaal, the daughter of Jeremias, of Lobena. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the ninth month, on the tenth day of the month, [that] Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and they made a rampart round it, and built a wall round about it with large stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So the city was besieged, until the eleventh year of king Sedekias, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} on the ninth day of the month, and [then] the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the city was broken up, and all the men of war went out by night by the way of the gate, between the wall and the outworks, which were by the king's garden; and the Chaldeans were by the city round about; and they went by the way [leading] to the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the host of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook him in the [country] beyond Jericho; and all his servants were dispersed from [about] him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they took the king, and brought him to the king of Babylon to Deblatha, and he judged him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the king of Babylon killed the sons of Sedekias before his eyes; and he killed all the princes of Juda in Deblatha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he put out the eyes of Sedekias, and bound him in fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon, and put him into the grinding-house, until the day when he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nabuzardan the captain of the guard, who waited on the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} and he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house; and all the houses of the city, and every great house he burnt with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the host of the Chaldeans that was with the captain of the guard pulled down all the wall of Jerusalem round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But the captain of the guard left the remnant of the people to be vinedressers and husbandmen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the Chaldeans broke in pieces the brazen pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the Lord, and they took the brass thereof, and carried it away to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Also the rim, and the bowls, and the flesh hooks, and all the brazen vessels, wherewith they ministered; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} and the basins, and the snuffers, and the oil-funnels, and the candlesticks, and the censers, and the cups, the golden, of gold, and the silver, of silver, the captain of the guard took away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the two pillars, and the one sea, and the twelve brazen oxen under the sea, which [things] king Solomon made for the house of the Lord; the brass of which [articles] was without weight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And as for the pillars, the height of one pillar was thirty-five cubits; and a line of twelve cubits compassed it round; and the thickness of it [all] round was four fingers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [there was] a brazen chapiter upon them, and the length was five cubits, [even] the height of one chapiter; and [there were] on the chapiter round about network and pomegranates, all of brass: and correspondingly the second pillar [had] eight pomegranates to a cubit for the twelve cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the pomegranates were ninety-six on a side; and all the pomegranates on the network round about were one hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the captain of the guard took the chief priest, and the second priest, and those that kept the way; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} and one eunuch, who was over the men of war, and seven men of renown, who were in the king's presence that were found in the city; and the scribe of the forces, who did the part of a scribe to the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were found in the midst of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And Nabuzardan the captain of the king's guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Deblatha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the king of Babylon struck them in Deblatha, in the land of Aemath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year after that Joakim king of Juda had been carried away captive, in the twelfth month, on the four and twentieth [day] of the month, [that] Ulaemadachar king of Babylon, in the year in which he began to reign, raised the head of Joakim king of Juda, and shaved him, and brought him out of the house where he was kept, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} and spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the kings that were with him in Babylon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} and changed his prison garments: and he ate bread continually before him all the days that he lived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And his appointed portion was given him continually by the king of Babylon from day to day, until the day when he died.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} am 3406-3416, bc 598-588 one; began to reign Heb. reigned Libnah \textsuperscript{4} am 3414, bc 590 the ninth year; in the tenth month pitched \textsuperscript{6} am 3416, bc 588 the fourth; the famine \textsuperscript{7} the city; all the men \textsuperscript{11} put out the eyes of Zedekiah Heb. blinded Zedekiah; chains or, fetters prison Heb. house of the wards \textsuperscript{12} fifth; the tenth It appears from the parallel passage of Kings, that Nebuzar-adan came from Riblah to Jerusalem on the seventh of the fifth month; but it seems that he did not set fire to the temple and city till the tenth day, being probably occupied on the intervening days in taking the vessels out of the house of the Lord, and collecting together all the riches that could be found. In memory of this calamity, the Jews devote two fasts to this day; the seventeenth of the fourth month, which falls in June, for the destruction of Jerusalem, and the ninth of the fifth month, which falls in July, for the destruction of the temple; both of which are mentioned by Zechariah as kept from this event till his time, a period of seventy years, under the names of the fast of the fourth month, and fast of the fifth month. the nineteenth; captain of the guard or, chief marshal, Heb. chief of the executioners, or slaughtermen, and so, ; *marg. served Heb. stood before \textsuperscript{18} caldrons; the shovels or, instruments to remove the ashes; the snuffers; bowls or, basons, ; the spoons \textsuperscript{19} fire pans, or, censers; and the candlesticks \textsuperscript{20} two the brass Heb. their brass without \textsuperscript{24} the captain; Seraiah; Zephaniah, ; door Heb. threshold; *marg. \textsuperscript{25} an eunuch were near the king's person Heb. saw the face of the king; principal scribe of the host or, scribe of the captain of the host \textsuperscript{31} am 3442, bc 562 it came in the twelfth Nearly answering to our 25th of April, am 3442. king of Babylon lifted up This phrase is founded on the observation that those in sorrow hold down their heads; and, when comforted, or the cause of their sorrow removed, they lift up their heads. \textsuperscript{32} kindly unto him Heb. good things with him, set Gave him a more respectable seat than any of the captive princes. \textsuperscript{33} changed Presented him with a caftan, or robe, as a mark of favour, as is still the practice in the East.; he did \textsuperscript{34} there was; every day a portion Heb. the matter of the day in his day\par}

\section*{Lamentations Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Jeremiah (traditional conservative view)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Jewish and Christian tradition long associated Lamentations with Jeremiah in response to Jerusalem's fall.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The NT does not explicitly name the writer, but the traditional Jeremianic setting remains the standard conservative reading.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} shortly after 586 BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places the poems in the aftermath of Jerusalem's destruction by Babylon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same exilic lament setting and explicitly frames the poems with a Jeremianic superscription in some traditions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Poetic lament over Jerusalem's destruction, suffering, sin, and hope in God's mercies.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To give faithful lament language for covenant catastrophe while sustaining hope in God's compassion.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} lament; judgment; grief; confession; hope; mercy\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Poems 1-4 over the fall; prayer for restoration 5.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Lamentations fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Qumran fragments provide early Hebrew witness Hasmonean-Herodian periods | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Lamentations 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use in later Jewish lament tradition by Multiple (Second Temple and later)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Lamentations is relatively stable textually, though the Greek superscription and poetic choices deserve notice.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives the traditional Jeremianic connection as strong and fitting the historical situation immediately after Jerusalem's fall.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Lamentations}
\markboth{LAMENTATIONS}{}
\subsection*{Lamentations 1}
\markright{LAMENTATIONS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, after Israel was taken captive, and Jerusalem made desolate, [that] Jeremias sat weeping, and lamented [with] this lamentation over Jerusalem, and said, ALEPH. How does the city that was filled with people sit solitary! she is become as a widow: she that was magnified among the nations, [and] princess among the provinces, has become tributary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} BETH. She weeps sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks; and there is none of all her lovers to comfort her: all that were her friends have dealt deceitfully with her, they are become her enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} GIMEL. Judea is gone into captivity by reason of her affliction, and by reason of the abundance of her servitude: she dwells among the nations, she has not found rest: all her pursuers have overtaken her between her oppressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} DALETH. The ways of Sion mourn, because there are none that come to the feast: all her gates are ruined: her priests groan, her virgins are led captive, and she is in bitterness in herself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} HE. Her oppressors are become the head, and her enemies have prospered; for the Lord has afflicted her because of the multitude of her sins: her young children are gone into captivity before the face of the oppressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} VAU. And all her beauty has been taken away from the daughter of Sion: her princes were as rams finding no pasture, and are gone [away] in weakness before the face of the pursuer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} ZAIN. Jerusalem remembered the days of her affliction, and her rejection; [she thought on] all her desirable things which were from the days of old, when her people fell into the hands of the oppressor, and there was none to help her: when her enemies saw [it] they laughed at her habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} HETH. Jerusalem has sinned a [great] sin; therefore has she come into tribulation, all that used to honor her have afflicted her, for they have seen her shame: yes, she herself groaned, and turned backward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} TETH. Her uncleanness is before her feet; she remembered not her last end; she has lowered her boasting [tone], there is none to comfort her. Behold, O Lord, my affliction: for the enemy has magnified himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} JOD. The oppressor has stretched out his hand on all her desirable things: for she has seen the Gentiles entering into her sanctuary, [concerning] whom you did command that they should not enter into your congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} CHAPH. All her people groan, seeking bread: they have given their desirable things for meat, to restore their soul: behold, Lord, and look; for she is become dishonored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} LAMED. All you⌃ that pass by the way, turn, and see if there is sorrow like to my sorrow, which has happened [to me]. The Lord who spoke by me has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} MEM. He has sent fire from his lofty habitation, he has brought it into my bones: he has spread a net for my feet, he has turned me back: he has made me desolate [and] mourning all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} NUN. He has watched over my sins, they are twined about my hands, they have come up on my neck: my strength has failed; for the Lord has laid pains on my hands, I shall not be able to stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} SAMECH. The Lord has cut off all my strong men from the midst of me: he has summoned against me a time for crushing my choice men: the Lord has trodden a wine-press for the virgin daughter of Juda: for these things I weep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} AIN. My eye has poured out water, because he that should comfort me, that should restore my soul, has been removed far from me: my sons have been destroyed, because the enemy has prevailed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} PHE. Sion has spread out her hand, [and] there is none to comfort her: the Lord has commanded [concerning] Jacob, his oppressors are round about him: Jerusalem has become among them as a removed woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} TSADE. The Lord is righteous; for I have provoked his mouth: hear, I pray you, all people, and behold my grief: my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} KOPH. I called my lovers, but they deceived me: my priests and my elders failed in the city; for they sought meat that they might restore their souls, and found [it] not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} RHECHS. Behold, O Lord; for I am afflicted: my belly is troubled, and my heart is turned within me; for I have been grievously rebellious: abroad the sword has bereaved me, even as death at home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} CHSEN. Hear, I pray you, for I groan: there is none to comfort me: all my enemies have heard [of] my afflictions, and rejoice because you have done [it]: you have brought on the day, you have called the time: they are become like to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} THAU. Let all their wickedness come before your face; and strip them, as they have made a gleaning for all my sins: for my groans are many, and my heart is grieved.\par

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} How doth The LXX have the following words as an introduction: "And it came to pass after Israel had been carried captive, and Jerusalem was become desolate, that Jeremiah sat weeping, and lamented with this lamentation over Jerusalem, and said."; sit;, ; full; as a; great; how is \textsuperscript{2} weepeth, ; , among; none, ; all her friends \textsuperscript{3} gone, ;, because of great servitude Heb. for the greatness of servitude she; all \textsuperscript{4} ways; all her gates;, her priests \textsuperscript{6} from; all; , her princes; , harts \textsuperscript{7} remembered; all her, ; pleasant or, desirable, the adversaries \textsuperscript{8} hath; removed Heb. become a removing, or wandering, ; *marg. all; they; she sigheth \textsuperscript{9} filthiness; she remembereth; came; she had, ; behold, ; for \textsuperscript{10} spread;, pleasant or, desirable, seen; whom \textsuperscript{11} seek, ; relieve the soul Heb. make the soul to come again, see \textsuperscript{12} Is it nothing or, It is nothing pass by Heb. pass by the way if The church in distress here magnifies her affliction; and yet no more than there was cause for her groaning was not heavier than her strokes. She appeals to all spectators - see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow. This might truly be said of the griefs which were suffered in Jerusalem of old; but Christians are apt to apply these words too sensibly and sensitively to themselves, when they are in trouble, and sometimes more than there is reasonable cause to warrant. All men feel most from their own burden, and cannot be persuaded to reconcile themselves to it; how often do thy cry out in the words we are illustrating! whereas, if their troubles were to be thrown into a common stock with those of others, and then an equal dividend made, share and share alike, rather than approve such an arrangement, each would be ready to say, "Pray give me my own again." - Henry. \textsuperscript{13} above; he hath spread; he hath turned, ; desolate \textsuperscript{15} trodden, ; *marg.; crush; *marg. the virgin etc. or, the winepress of the virgin, etc. as in \textsuperscript{16} I weep, ;, ; relieve Heb. bring back, my children \textsuperscript{18} Lord; for I; commandment Heb. mouth, hear; my virgins \textsuperscript{20} Behold; my bowels; for; abroad \textsuperscript{21} have heard that, they are; , ; thou wilt Isa. 13:1-14:32; 46:1-51:64; Ezek. 25:1-32:32; the day; called or, proclaimed they shall\par}

\subsection*{Lamentations 2}
\markright{LAMENTATIONS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} ALEPH. How has the Lord darkened in his wrath the daughter of Sion! he has cast down the glory of Israel from heaven to earth, and has not remembered his footstool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} BETH. In the day of his wrath the Lord has overwhelmed [her] as in the sea, [and] not spared: he has brought down in his fury all the beautiful things of Jacob; he has brought down to the ground the strongholds of the daughter of Juda; he has profaned her kings and her princes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} GIMEL. He has broken in his fierce anger all the horn of Israel: he has turned back his right hand from the face of the enemy, and has kindled a flame in Jacob as a fire, and it has devoured all things round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} DALETH. He has bent his bow as an opposing enemy: he has strengthened his right hand as an adversary, and has destroyed all the desirable things of my eyes in the tabernacle of the daughter of Sion: he has poured forth his anger as fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} HE. The Lord is become as an enemy: he has overwhelmed Israel as in the sea, he has overwhelmed her palaces: he has destroyed her strongholds, and has multiplied the afflicted and humbled ones to the daughter of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} VAU. And he has scattered his tabernacle as a vine, he has marred his feast: the Lord has forgotten the feast and the sabbath which he appointed in Sion, and in the fury of his wrath has vexed the king, and priest, and prince. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} ZAIN. The Lord has rejected his altar, he has cast off his sanctuary, he has broken by the hand of the enemy the wall of her palaces; they have uttered their voice in the house of the Lord as on a feast day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} HETH. And he has turned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Sion: he has stretched out the measuring line, he has not turned back his hand from afflicting [her]: therefore the bulwark mourned, and the wall was weakened with it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} TETH. Her gates are sunk into the ground: he has destroyed and broken to pieces her bars, [and] her king and her prince among the Gentiles: there is no law, nay, her prophets have seen no vision from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} JOD. The elders of the daughter of Sion have sat upon the ground, they have kept silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloths: they have brought down to the ground the chief virgins in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} CHAPH. My eyes have failed with tears, my heart is troubled, my glory is cast down to the ground, for the destruction of the daughter of my people; while the infant and suckling swoon in the streets of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} LAMED. They said to their mothers, Where is corn and wine? while they fainted like wounded men in the streets of the city, while their souls were poured out into their mother's bosom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} MEM. What shall I testify to you, or what shall I compare to you, O daughter of Jerusalem? who shall save and comfort you, O virgin daughter of Sion? for the cup of your destruction is enlarged: who shall heal you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} NUN. Your prophets have seen for you vanities and folly: and they have not revealed your iniquity, to turn back your captivity; but they have seen for you vain burdens, and worthless visions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} SAMECH. All that go by the way have clapped their hands at you; they have hissed and shaken their head at the daughter of Jerusalem. Is this the city, they say, the crown of joy of all the earth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} AIN. All your enemies have opened their mouth against you: they have hissed and gnashed their teeth, and said, We have swallowed her up: moreover this is the day which we looked for; we have found it, we have seen it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} PHE. The Lord has done that which he purposed; he has accomplished his word, [even] the things which he commanded from the ancient days: he has thrown down, and has not spared: and he has caused the enemy to rejoice over you, he has exalted the horn of him that afflicted you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} TSADE. Their heart cried to the Lord, You⌃ walls of Sion, pour down tears like torrents day and night: give yourself no rest; let not the apple of your eyes cease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} KOPH. Arise, rejoice in the night at the beginning of your watch: pour out your heart as water before the face of the Lord; lift up your hands to him for the life of your infants, who faint for hunger at the top of all the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} RHECHS. Behold, O Lord, and see for whom you have gathered thus. Shall the women eat the fruit of their womb? the cook has made a gathering: shall the infants sucking at the breasts be slain? will you kill the priest and prophet in the sanctuary of the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} CHSEN. The child and old man have lain down in the street: my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity: you have slain [them] with the sword and with famine; in the day of your wrath you have mangled [them], you have not spared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} THAU. He has called my sojourners round about to a solemn day, and there was not in the day of the wrath of the Lord any one that escaped or was left; whereas I have strengthened and multiplied all my enemies.\par
