\subsection*{Lamentations 3}
\markright{LAMENTATIONS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} ALEPH. I am the man that sees poverty, through the rod of his wrath upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He has taken me, and led me away into darkness, and not [into] light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Nay, against me has he turned his hand all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He has made old my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} BETH. He has built against me, and compassed my head, and brought travail [upon me]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He has set me in dark places, as them that have long been dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He has builded against me, and I can’t come forth: he has made my brazen [chain] heavy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} GIMEL. Yes, [though] I cry and shout, he shuts out my prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} DALETH. He has built up my ways, he has hedged my paths; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} he has troubled me, [as] a she-bear lying in wait: he is to me [as] a lion in secret places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He pursued [me] after I departed, and brought me to a stand: he has utterly ruined me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} HE. He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He has caused the arrows of his quiver to enter into my reins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I became a laughing stock to all my people; and their song all the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} VAU. He has filled me with bitterness, he has drenched me with gall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he has dashed out my teeth with gravel, he has fed me with ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He has also removed my soul from peace: I forgot prosperity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore my success has perished, and my hope from the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} ZAIN. I remembered by reason of my poverty, and because of persecution my bitterness and gall shall be remembered; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} and my soul shall meditate with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} This will I lay up in my heart, therefore I will endure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} HETH. [It is] the mercies of the Lord, that he has not failed me, because his compassions are not exhausted. Pity [us], O Lord, early [every] month: for we are not brought to an end, because his compassions are not exhausted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} [They are] new every morning: great is your faithfulness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The Lord is my portion, says my soul; therefore will I wait for him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} TETH. The Lord is good to them that wait for him: the soul which shall seek him {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} [is] good, and shall wait for, and quietly expect salvation of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} TETH. [It is] good for a man when he bears a yoke in his youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He will sit alone, and be silent, because he has borne [it] upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} JOD. He will give [his] cheek to him that smites him: he will be filled full with reproaches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For the Lord will not reject for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} CHAPH. For he that has brought down will pity, and [that] according to the abundance of his mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} He has not answered [in anger] from his heart, though he has brought low the children of a man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} LAMED. To bring down under his feet all the prisoners of the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} to turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the Most High, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} to condemn a man [unjustly] in his judgment, the Lord has not given commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Who has thus spoken, and it has come to pass? the Lord has not commanded it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Out of the mouth of the Most High there shall not come forth evil and good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} MEM. Why should a living man complain, a man concerning his sin? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} NUN. Our way has been searched out and examined, and we will turn to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Let us lift up our hearts with [our] hand to the lofty One in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} We have sinned, we have transgressed; and you have not pardoned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} SAMECH. You have visited [us] in wrath, and driven us away: you have slain, you have not pitied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} You have veiled yourself with a cloud because of prayer, that I might be blind, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} and be cast off. AIN. You have set us [alone] in the midst of the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} All our enemies have opened their mouth against us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Fear and wrath are come upon us, suspense and destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} My eye shall pour down torrents of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} PHE. My eye is drowned [with tears], and I will not be silent, so that there shall be no rest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} until the Lord look down, and behold from heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} My eye shall prey upon my soul, because of all the daughters of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} TSADE. The fowlers chased me as a sparrow, all my enemies destroyed my life in a pit without cause, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} and laid a stone upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Water flowed over my head: I said, I am cut off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} KOPH. I called upon your name, O Lord, out of the lowest dungeon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} You heard my voice: close not your ears to my supplication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} You drew near to my help: in the day wherein I called upon you you said to me, Fear not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} RECHS. O Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul; you have redeemed my life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} You have seen, O Lord, my troubles: you have judged my cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} You have seen all their vengeance, [you have looked] on all their devices against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} CHSEN. You have heard their reproach [and] all their devices against me; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} the lips of them that rose up against me, and their plots against me all the day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} their sitting down and their rising up: look you upon their eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} You will render them a recompense, O Lord, according to the works of their hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} THAU. You will give them [as] a covering, the grief of my heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} You will persecute them in anger, and will consume them from under the heaven, O Lord.\par

\subsection*{Lamentations 4}
\markright{LAMENTATIONS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} ALEPH. How will the gold be tarnished, [and] the fine silver changed! the sacred stones have been poured forth at the top of all the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} BETH. The precious sons of Zion, who were equalled in value with gold, how are they counted as earthen vessels, the works of the hands of the potter! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} GIMEL. Nay, serpents have drawn out the breasts, they give suck to their young, the daughters of my people are incurably cruel, as an ostrich in a desert. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} DALETH. The tongue of the sucking child cleaves to the roof of its mouth for thirst: the little children ask for bread, [and] there is none to break [it] to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} HE. They that feed on dainties are desolate in the streets: they that used to be nursed in scarlet have clothed themselves with dung. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} VAU. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people has been increased beyond the iniquities of Sodoma, [the city] that was overthrown very suddenly, and none laboured against her [with their] hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} ZAIN. Her Nazarites were made purer than snow, they were whiter than milk, they were purified [as] with fire, their polishing was superior to sapphire stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} HETH. Their countenance is become blacker than smoke; they are not known in the streets: their skin has cleaved to their bones; they are withered, they are become as a stick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} TETH. The slain with the sword were better than they that were slain with hunger: they have departed, pierced through from [lack of] the fruits of the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} JOD. The hands of tender-hearted women have sodden their own children: they became meat for them in the destruction of the daughter of my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} CHAPH. The Lord has accomplished his wrath; he has poured out fierce anger, and has kindled a fire in Sion, and it has devoured her foundations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} LAMED. The kings of the earth, [even] all that dwell in the world, believed not that an enemy and oppressor would enter through the gates of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} MEM. For the sins of her prophets, [and] iniquities of her priests, who shed righteous blood in the midst of her, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} NUN. her watchmen staggered in the streets, they were defiled with blood in their weakness, they touched their raiment [with it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} SAMECH. Depart you⌃ from the unclean ones: call you⌃ them: depart, depart, touch [them] not: for they are on fire, yes, they stagger: say you⌃ among the nations, They shall no more sojourn [there]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} AIN. The presence of the Lord [was] their portion; [but] he will not again look upon them: they regarded not the person of the priests, they pitied not the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} PHE. While we yet lived our eyes failed, while we looked in vain for our help. TSADE. We looked to a nation that could not save. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} We have hunted [for] our little ones, that they should not walk in our streets. KOPH. Our time has drawn near, our days are fulfilled, our time is come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky, they flew on the mountains, in the wilderness they laid wait for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} RECHS. The breath of our nostrils, [our] anointed Lord, was taken in their destructive snares, of whom we said, In his shadow we shall live among the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} CHSEN. Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Idumea, that dwell in the land: yet the cup of the Lord shall pass through to you: you shall be drunken, and pour forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} THAU. O daughter of Sion, your iniquity has come to an end; he shall no more carry you captive: he has visited your iniquities, O daughter of Edom; he has revealed your sins.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} How is the gold; the stones \textsuperscript{3} sea monsters or, sea calves the daughter; like \textsuperscript{6} punishment of the iniquity of the daughter or, iniquity of the daughter, etc.; the punishment \textsuperscript{7} Nazarites; purer; their polishing Gizrathom rendered by Dr. Blayney, "their veining, " from gazar to divide, intersect, as the blue veins do the surface of the body. This is approved by Dr. A. Clarke, who remarks, "Milk will most certainly well apply to the whiteness of the skin; the beautiful ruby to the ruddiness of the flesh; and the sapphire, in its clear, transcendent purple, to the veins in a fine complexion." \textsuperscript{8} visage; blacker than a coal Heb. darker than blackness. Or, as Dr. Blayney renders, "duskier than the dawn; " shachar signifying "the dawn of the day, when it is neither light nor dark, but between both, at which time objects are not easily distinguished." they; their skin \textsuperscript{9} for; pine away Heb. flow out \textsuperscript{14} have wandered; they have polluted; so that men could not touch or, in that they could not but touch \textsuperscript{16} anger or, face hath; he will; they respected \textsuperscript{17} our eyes; for a For the Egyptians, who were their pretended allies; but who were neither able nor willing to help them. \textsuperscript{18} hunt; our end is near \textsuperscript{19} persecutors; the eagles The eagle, whose wings are of an extraordinary length, darts with amazing rapidity through the voids of heaven. they pursued \textsuperscript{20} breath; the anointed, ; was taken \textsuperscript{21} be glad;, ; the land; the cup; and shalt \textsuperscript{22} The punishment of thine iniquity or, Thine iniquity, *marg.; he will no; he will visit; discover thy sins or, carry thee captive for thy sins\par}

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Remember, O Lord, what has happened to us: behold, and look on our reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Our inheritance has been turned away to aliens, our houses to strangers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} we are become orphans, we have no father, our mothers are as widows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} We have drunk our water for money; our wood is sold to us [for a burden] on our neck: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} we have been persecuted, we have laboured, we have had no rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Egypt gave the hand [to us], Assur to their own satisfaction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Our fathers sinned, [and] are not: we have borne their iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Servants have ruled over us: there is none to ransom [us] out of their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} We shall bring in our bread with [danger of] our lives, because of the sword of the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Our skin is blackened like an oven; \section*{Ezekiel Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Ezekiel the priest-prophet\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book repeatedly names Ezekiel and is anchored in his exilic visionary ministry.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The NT echoes Ezekiel extensively and receives his prophecies as authoritative Scripture, though without naming authorship in the same way as Isaiah or Jeremiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} ca. 593-571 BC in the Babylonian exile\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology anchors Ezekiel's visions by dated notices in exile.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same exilic framework and is an important witness for some difficult passages.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Exilic prophetic ministry among the deportees in Babylon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To announce judgment on Jerusalem and the nations, then restoration, new heart, new temple, and renewed land.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} glory of God; judgment; exile; new heart; shepherd; restoration; temple\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Judgment visions 1-24; Oracles against nations 25-32; Restoration and temple vision 33-48.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Ezekiel fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Qumran Ezekiel manuscripts provide early Hebrew witness to parts of the book Hasmonean-Herodian periods | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Ezekiel 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use in later Jewish apocalyptic and Christian interpretation by Multiple (Second Temple and early Christian periods)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Ezekiel's symbolic language, measurements, and temple vision make versional comparison useful, though not as radically divergent as Jeremiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Ezekiel as the named priest-prophet of the book and treats the dated vision notices as historically grounded prophetic testimony.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Ezekiel}
\markboth{EZEKIEL}{}
\subsection*{Ezekiel 1}
\markright{EZEKIEL 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now it came to pass in the thirties year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, that I was in the midst of the captivity by the river of Chobar; and the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} On the fifth day of the month; this was the fifth year of the captivity of king Joakim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the word of the Lord came to Jezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river of Chobar; and the hand of the Lord was upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I looked, and, behold, a sweeping wind came from the north, and a great cloud on it, and [there was] brightness round about it, and gleaming fire, and in the midst of it as it were the appearance of amber in the midst of the fire, and brightness in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in the midst as it were the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; the likeness of a man was upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And each one [had] four faces, and each one [had] four wings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And their legs were straight; and their feet were winged, and [there were] sparks, like gleaming brass, and their wings were light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the hand of a man was under their wings on their four sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the faces of them four turned not when they went; they went everyone straight forward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right of the four; and the face of a calf on the left of the four; and the face of an eagle to the four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the four had their wings spread out above; each one [had] two joined to one another, and two covered their bodies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And each one went straight forward: wherever the spirit was going they went, and turned not back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And in the midst of the living creatures [there was] an appearance as of burning coals of fire, as an appearance of lamps turning among the living creatures; and the brightness of fire, and out of the fire came forth lightning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I looked, and, behold, the four [had each] one wheel on the ground near the living creatures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the appearance of the wheels was as the appearance of beryl: and the four had one likeness: and their work was as it were a wheel in a wheel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They went on their four sides: they turned not as they went; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} neither did their backs [turn]: and they were high: and I saw them, and the backs of them four were full of eyes round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures lifted themselves off the earth, the wheels were lifted off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Wherever the cloud happened to be, there was the spirit ready to go: the wheels went and were lifted up with them; because the spirit of life was in the wheels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} When those went, [the wheels] went; and when those stood, [the wheels] stood; and when those lifted themselves off the earth, they were lifted off with them: for the spirit of life was in the wheels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the likeness over the heads of the living creatures was as a firmament, as the appearance of crystal, spread out over their wings above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And their wings were spread out under the firmament, reaching one to the other; two [wings] to each, covering their bodies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I heard the sound of their wings when they went, as the sound of much water: and when they stood, their wings were let down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And behold! a voice from above the firmament {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} that was over their head, [there was] as the appearance of a sapphire stone, [and] the likeness of a throne upon it: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as an appearance of a man above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And I saw as it were the resemblance of amber from the appearance of the loins and upwards, and from the appearance of the loins and under I saw an appearance of fire, and the brightness thereof round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} As the appearance of the bow when it is in the cloud in days of rain, so was the form of brightness round about.\par

Jehezkel and the \textsuperscript{4} a whirlwind;, ; a great; , ; infolding itself Heb. catching itself colour \textsuperscript{6} And every one had four faces These living creatures were probably hieroglyphical representations of the holy angels, the attendants on "the King of Glory, " and the ministers of his providence. They were four, apparently to denote that they were employed in the four corners of the world; and they had the likeness of a man, to signify that they were intelligent and rational creatures., ; every one had four wings \textsuperscript{7} straight feet Heb. a straight foot like the sole, the colour \textsuperscript{10} for the; the face of a man; the face of a lion; the face of an ox, Cherub; the face of an eagle \textsuperscript{11} and their, stretched upward or, divided above and two \textsuperscript{18} they were so; rings or, stakes full \textsuperscript{20} the spirit; for the; of the living creature or, of life \textsuperscript{21} When those went, of the living creature or, of life \textsuperscript{22} the likeness; , crystal The Hebrew kerach which generally denotes ice, doubtless here signifies crystal ( κρυσταλλος, from κρυος, cold, ice, and στελλομαι, to concrete), as it is rendered by the LXX and Vulgate. It is a very large class of silicious minerals, hard, pellucid, naturally colourless, of regularly angular figures, and of simple plates; not flexible, nor elastic, but giving fire with steel; not fermenting by acid menstrua, but calcinable in a strong fire. There are three orders of pure crystal. The first is perfect columnar crystals, with double pyramids, of eighteen planes, in an hexangular pyramid at each end; the second is that of perfect crystals, without a column, of twelve or sixteen planes, in two hexangular pyramids; and the third is that of imperfect crystals, with single pyramids, of ten or twelve planes, in an hexangular or pentangular column. Terrible crystal seems to denote that which was well cut and polished, vividly refracting the rays of light. \textsuperscript{24} like; as the voice;, as the noise \textsuperscript{26} And above Abp. \subsection*{Ezekiel 2}
\markright{EZEKIEL 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And I saw and fell upon my face, and heard the voice of one speaking: and he said to me, Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Spirit came upon me, and took me up, and raised me, and set me on my feet: and I heard him speaking to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said to me, Son of Man, I send you forth to the house of Israel, them that provoke me; who have provoked me, they and their fathers to this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Whether then indeed they shall hear or fear, (for it is a provoking house,) yet they shall know that you are a prophet in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you, son of man, fear them not, nor be dismayed at their face; (for they will madden and will rise up against you round about, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions): be not afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their countenance, for it is a provoking house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you shall speak my words to them, whether they will hear or fear: for it is a provoking house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you, son of man, hear him that speaks to you; be not you provoking, as the provoking house: open your mouth, and eat what I give you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I looked, and behold, a hand stretched out to me, and in it a volume of a book. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he unrolled it before me: and in it the front and the back were written [upon]: and there was written [in it] Lamentation, and mournful song, and woe.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} I send; , ; a rebellious nation Heb. rebellious nations, rebelled \textsuperscript{4} they; impudent Heb. hard of face, Thus \textsuperscript{6} be not; briers or, rebels; scorpions; though they \textsuperscript{7} thou;, ; whether most rebellious Heb. rebellion \textsuperscript{9} an hand;, a roll All ancient books were written so as to be rolled up. Hence volumen a volume, from volvo I roll. \textsuperscript{10} spread; was written within Contrary to the state of rolls in general, which are written on the inside only. lamentations\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 3}
\markright{EZEKIEL 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he said to me, Son of Man, eat this volume, and go and speak to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} So he opened my mouth, and caused me to eat the volume. And he said to me, Son of man, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} your mouth shall eat, and your belly shall be filled with this volume that is given to you. So I ate it; and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he said to me, Son of man, go your way, and go in to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For you are not sent to a people of hard speech, [but] to the house of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} neither to many nations of other speech and other tongues, nor of harsh language, whose words you would not understand: although if I [had] sent you to such, they would have listened to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you; for they will not listen to me: for all the house of Israel are stubborn and hard-hearted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And, behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your power against their power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall be continually stronger than a rock: be not afraid of them, neither be dismayed at their faces, because it is a provoking house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said to me, Son of man, receive into your heart all the words that I have spoken to you, and hear [them] with your ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And go your way, go in to the captivity, to the children of your people, and you shall speak to them, and say to them, Thus says the Lord; whether they will hear, [or] whether they will forbear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then the Spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the voice [as] of a great earthquake, [saying], Blessed [be] the glory of the Lord from his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I perceived the sound of the wings of the living creatures clapping one to the other, and the sound of the wheels was near them, and the sound of the earthquake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Spirit lifted me, and took me up, and I went in the impulse of my spirit; and the hand of the Lord was mighty upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then I passed through the air and came into the captivity, and went round [to] them that lived by the river of Chobar who were there; and I sat there seven days, conversant in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And after the seven days the word of the Lord came to me, saying, Son of man, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel; and you shall hear a word of my mouth, and shall threaten them from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} When I say to the wicked, You shall surely die; and you have not warned him, to give warning to the wicked, to turn from his ways, that he should live; that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But if you warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, and from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, and you shall deliver your soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits a trespass, and I shall bring punishment before him, he shall die, because you did not warn him: he shall even die in his sins, because his righteousness shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But if you warn the righteous not to sin, and he sin not, the righteous shall surely live, because you have warned him; and you shall deliver your own soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the hand of the Lord came upon me; and he said to me, Arise, and go forth into the plain, and there shall you be spoken to. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And I arose, and went forth to the plain: and, behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, according to the vision, and according to the glory of the Lord, which I saw by the river of Chobar: and I fell on my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then the Spirit came upon me, and set me on my feet, and spoke to me, and said to me, Go in, and shut yourself up in the midst of your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And you, son of man, behold, bonds are prepared for you, and they shall bind you with them, and you shall not come forth of the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Also I will bind your tongue, and you shall be dumb, and shall not be to them a reprover: because it is a provoking house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord, He that hears, let him hear; and he that is disobedient, let him be disobedient: because it is a provoking house.\par

\subsection*{Ezekiel 4}
\markright{EZEKIEL 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And you, son of man, take you a brick, and you shall set it before your face, and shall portray on it the city, [even] Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you shall besiege it, and build works against it, and throw up a mound round about it, and pitch camps against it, and set up engines round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And take you to yourself an iron pan, and you shall set it [for] an iron wall between you and the city: and you shall set your face against it, and it shall be in a siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall lie upon your left side, and lay the iniquities of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of the hundred and fifty days [during] which you shall lie upon it: and you shall bear their iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For I have appointed you their iniquities for a number of days, for one hundred and ninety days: so you shall bear the iniquities of the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall accomplish this, and [then] shall lie on your right side, and shall bear the iniquities of the house of Juda forty days: I have appointed you a day for a year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So you shall set your face to the siege of Jerusalem, and shall strengthen your arm, and shall prophesy against it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And, behold, I have prepared bonds for you, land you may not turn from your one side to the other, until the days of your siege shall be accomplished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Take you also to you wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and bread-corn; and you shall cast them into one earthen vessel, and shall make them into loaves for yourself; and you shall eat them one hundred and ninety days, according to the number of the days [during] which you sleep on your side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you shall eat your food by weight, twenty shekels a day: from time to time shall you eat them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall drink water by measure, even from time to time you shall drink the sixth part of a hin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall eat them [as] a barley cake: you shall bake them before their eyes in man's dung. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you shall say, Thus says the Lord God of Israel; Thus shall the children of Israel eat unclean things among the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then I said, Not so, Lord God of Israel: surely my soul has not been defiled with uncleanness; nor have I eaten, that which died of itself or was torn of beasts from my birth until now; neither has any corrupt flesh entered into my mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to me, Behold, I have given you dung of oxen instead of man's dung, and you shall prepare your loaves upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he said to me, Son of man, behold, I break the support of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight and in lack; and shall drink water by measure, and in a state of ruin: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} that they may lack bread and water; and a man and his brother shall be brought to ruin, and they shall pine away in their iniquities.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} take; , ; a tile μαπδ, levainah generally denotes a brick, and Palladius informs us that the bricks in common use among the ancients were "two feet long, one foot broad, and four inches thick; " and on such a surface the whole siege might be easily pourtrayed. Perhaps, however, it may here denote a flat tile, like a Roman brick, which were commonly used for tablets, as we learn from Pliny, Hist. "Beginning from . Ending ." \textsuperscript{6} forty days This represented the forty years during which gross idolatry prevailed in Judah, from the reformation of Josiah, bc 624, to the same final desolation of the land. Some think that the period of 390 days also predicts the duration of the siege of the Babylonians ( ), deducting from it five months and twenty-nine days, when the besiegers went to meet the Egyptians (; ); and that forty days may have been employed in desolating the temple and city. "Beginning from, . Ending ." each day for a year Heb. a day for a year, a day for a year \textsuperscript{8} I will from one side to another Heb. from thy side to thy side \textsuperscript{9} wheat, millet Dochan in Arabic, dokhn the holcus dochna of Forskal, is a kind of millet, of considerable use as a food; the cultivation of which is described by Browne. fitches or, spelt, Kussemim is doubtless ζεα, or spelt, as Aquila and Symmachus render here; and so LXX and Theodotion, ολυρα . In times of scarcity it is customary to mix several kinds of coarser grains with the finer, to make it last the longer. three \textsuperscript{14} Ah; my soul have I; abominable \textsuperscript{15} cow's dung Dried cow-dung is a common fuel in the East, as it is in many parts of England, to the present day; but the prophet was ordered to prepare his bread with human ordure, to shew the extreme degree of wretchedness to which the besieged should be exposed, as they would be obliged literally to use it, from not being able to leave the city to collect other fuel. \textsuperscript{16} I will; eat The prophet was allowed each day only twenty shekels weight, or about ten ounces, of the coarse food he had prepared, and the sixth part of a hin, scarcely a pint and a half, of water; all of which was intended to shew that they should be obliged to eat the meanest and coarsest food, and that by weight, and their water by measure.\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 5}
\markright{EZEKIEL 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And you, son of man, take you a sword sharper than a barber's razor; you shall procure it for yourself, and shall bring it upon your head, and upon your beard: and you shall take a pair of scales, and shall separate the hair. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A fourth part you shall burn in the fire in the midst of the city, at the fulfillment of the days of the siege: and you shall take a fourth part, and burn it up in the midst of it: and a fourth part you shall cut with a sword round about it: and a fourth part you shall scatter to the wind; and I will draw out a sword after them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And you shall take thence a few in number, and shall wrap them in the fold of your garment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you shall take of these again, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them up with fire: from thence shall come forth fire; and you shall say to the whole house of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thus says the Lord; This is Jerusalem: I have set her and the countries round about her in the midst of the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall declare my ordinances to the lawless one from out of the nations; and my statutes [to the sinful one] of the countries round about her: because they have rejected my ordinances, and have not walked in my statutes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore thus says the Lord, Because your occasion [for sin has been taken] from the nations round about you, and you⌃ have not walked in my statutes, nor kept my ordinances, nay, you⌃ have not even done according to the ordinances of the nations round about you; therefore thus says the Lord; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Behold, I am against you, and I will execute judgment in the midst of you in the sight of the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will do in you things which I have not done, and the like of which I will not do again, for all your abominations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore the fathers shall eat [their] children in the midst of you, and children shall eat [their] fathers; and I will execute judgments in you, and I will scatter all that are left of you to every wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore, [as] I live, says the Lord; surely, because you have defiled my holy things with all your abominations, I also will reject you; my eye shall not spare, and I will have no mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} A fourth part of you shall be cut off by pestilence, and a fourth part of you shall be consumed in the midst of you with famine: and [as for another] fourth part of you, I will scatter them to every wind; and a fourth part of you shall fall by sword round about you, and I will draw out a sword after them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And my wrath and my anger shall be accomplished upon them: and you shall know that I the Lord have spoken in my jealousy, when I have accomplished my anger upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will make you desolate, and your daughters round about you, in the sight of every one that passes through. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you shall be mourned over and miserable among the nations round about you, when I have executed judgments in you in the vengeance of my wrath. I the Lord have spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when I have sent against them shafts of famine, then they shall be consumed, and I will break the strength of your bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So I will send forth against you famine and evil beasts, and I will take vengeance upon you; and pestilence and blood shall pass through upon you; and I will bring a sword upon you round about. I the Lord have spoken.\par

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Son of man, set your face against the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them; and I will cast down your slain [men] before your idols. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I will scatter your bones round about your altars, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} and in all your habitations: the cities shall be made desolate, and the high places utterly laid waste; that your altars may be destroyed, and your idols be broken to pieces, and your consecrated plats be abolished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And slain [men] shall fall in the midst of you, and you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} When there are [some] of you escaping from the sword among the Gentiles, and when you⌃ are scattered in the countries; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} then they of you that escape among the nations whither they were carried captive shall remember me; (I have sworn [an oath] against their heart that goes a-whoring from me, and their eyes that go a-whoring after their practices;) and they shall mourn over themselves for all their abominations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they shall know that I the Lord have spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus says the Lord; Clap with [your] hand, and stamp with [your] foot and say, Aha, aha! for all the abominations of the house of Israel: they shall fall by the sword, and by pestilence, and by famine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He that is near shall fall by the sword; and he that is far off shall die by the pestilence; and he that is in the siege shall be consumed with famine: and I will accomplish my anger upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain are in the midst of your idols round about your altars, on every high hill, and under [every] shady tree, where they offered a sweet savor to all their idols. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will stretch out my hand against them, and I will make the land desolate and ruined from the wilderness of Deblatha, in all their habitations: [and] you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Ezekiel 7}
\markright{EZEKIEL 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying, Also, you, son of man, say, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus says the Lord; An end is come to the land of Israel, the end is come on the four corners of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The end is come on you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} the inhabitant of the land: the time is come, the day has drawn near, not with tumult, nor with pangs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now I will pour out my anger upon you near at hand, and I will accomplish my wrath on you: and I will judge you for your ways, and recompense upon you all your abominations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} My eye shall not spare, nor will I have any mercy: for I will recompense your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in the midst of you; and you shall know that I am the Lord that strike [you]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now the end [is come] to you, and I will send [judgment] upon you: and I will take vengeance on your ways, and will recompense all your abominations upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} My eye shall not spare, nor will I have any mercy: for I will recompense your way upon you, and your abominations shall be in the midst of you; and you shall know that I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For thus says the Lord; Behold, the end is come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Behold, the day of the Lord! although the rod has blossomed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} pride has sprung up, and will break the staff of the wicked one, and [that] not with tumult, nor with haste. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The time is come, behold the day: let not the buyer rejoice, and let not the seller mourn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the buyer shall never again return to the seller, neither shall a man cleave with the eye [of hope] to his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Sound you⌃ the trumpet, and pass sentence on all together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} [There shall be] war with the sword without, and famine and pestilence within: he that is in the field shall die by the sword; and famine and pestilence shall destroy them that are in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But they that escape of them shall be delivered, and shall be upon the mountains: and I will kill all [the rest], every one for his iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} All hands shall be completely weakened, and all thighs shall be defiled with moisture. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall gird themselves with sackcloth, and amazement shall cover them; and shame shall be upon them, [even] upon every face, and baldness upon every head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Their silver shall be cast forth in the streets, and their gold shall be despised: their souls shall not be satisfied, and their bellies shall not be filled: for it was the punishment of their iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} [As for] their choice ornaments, they employed them for pride, and they made of them images of their abominations: therefore have I made them uncleanness to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And I will deliver them into the hands of strangers to make them a prey, and to the pests of the earth for a spoil; and they shall profane them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I will turn away my face from them, and they shall defile my charge, and shall go in to them unguardedly, and profane them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they shall work uncleanness: because the land is full of strange nations, and the city is full of iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And I will turn back the boasting of their strength; and their holy things shall be defiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And [though] propitiation shall come, and [one] shall seek peace, yet there shall be none. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} There shall be woe upon woe, and there shall be message upon message; and a vision shall be sought from a prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The prince shall clothe himself with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be made feeble: I will do to them according to their ways, and according to their judgments will I punish them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} unto, ; An end Two or three manuscripts read ketz ba, ba hakketz "the end cometh, come is the end; " which is supported by all the ancient versions. \textsuperscript{3} and I, will judge, ; recompense Heb. give \textsuperscript{6} An end This is similar to the; but there is a paronomasia, or play upon words, here, deserving of notice: ketz ba, ba hakketz, haikeetz ailayich "the end cometh, come is the end. \subsection*{Ezekiel 8}
\markright{EZEKIEL 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth [day] of the month, I was sitting in the house, and the elders of Juda were sitting before me: and the hand of the Lord came upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I looked, and, behold, the likeness of a man: from his loins and downwards [there was] fire, and from his loins upwards [there was] as the appearance of amber. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he stretched forth the likeness of a hand, and took me by the crown of my head; and the Spirit lifted me up between the earth and sky, and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the porch of the gate that looks to the north, where was the pillar of the Purchaser. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And, behold, the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, according to the vision which I saw in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to me, Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north. So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and, behold, [I looked] from the north toward the eastern gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he said to me, Son of man, have you seen what these do? They commit great abominations here so that I should keep away from my sanctuary: and you shall see yet greater iniquities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he brought me to the porch of the court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he said to me, Son of man, dig: so I dug, and behold a door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to me, Go in, and behold the iniquities which they practise here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So I went in and looked; and saw vain abominations, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed upon them round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, and Jechonias the son of Saphan stood in their presence in the midst of them, and each one held his censer in his hand; and the smoke of the incense went up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he said to me, You have seen, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel do, each one of them in their secret chamber: because they have said, The Lord see not; The Lord has forsaken the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to me, You shall see yet greater iniquities which these do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he brought me in to the porch of the house of the Lord that looks to the north; and, behold [there were] women sitting there lamenting for Thammuz. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he said to me, Son of man, you have seen; but you shall yet see [evil] practices greater then these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord, and at the entrance of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty men, with their back parts toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces [turned] the opposite way; and these were worshipping the sun. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he said to me, Son of man, you have seen this. [Is it] a little thing to the house of Juda to practise the iniquities which they have practised here? for they have filled the land with iniquity: and, behold, these are as scorners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore will I deal with them in wrath: my eye shall not spare, nor will I have any mercy.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} in the sixth year, and the, ; that the \textsuperscript{2} I beheld; amber Amber is a hard, inflammable, bituminous substance, of a beautiful yellow colour, very transparent, and susceptible of an exquisite polish. When rubbed it is highly endowed with electricity; a name which the moderns have formed from its Greek name ηλεκτρον . But, as amber becomes dim as soon as it feels the fire, and is speedily consumed, it is probable that the original chashmal which Bochart derives from the Chaldee nechash copper, and melala gold, was a mixed metal, similar to that which the Greeks called ηλεκτρον, electrum, as the LXX and Vulgate render, from its resemblance to amber in colour. \textsuperscript{3} he put;, the spirit, ; to the door; the image; provoketh \textsuperscript{6} seest; even, ; that I; greater \textsuperscript{10} and behold These images portrayed on the wall were no doubt the objects of Egyptian idolatry, the ox, ape, crocodile, ibis, beetle, etc., as we find those idols were painted on the walls of the tombs of kings and nobles. every \textsuperscript{12} hast, ancients, ; in the; The Lord seeth \textsuperscript{16} the inner, at the door; about with their; their faces; and they It seems that the Jews had incorporated every species of idolatry into their worship, Egyptian, Phoenician, and Persian; for this evidently was the Magian worship of the sun. \textsuperscript{17} Is it a light etc. or, Is there anything lighter than to commit, etc for, ; they put So the Vulgate has, applicant ramum ad nares suas "they apply the branch to their nose; " which Jerome explains by "a branch of the palm tree with which they adored the idols; " and it seems plainly to allude to the Magian fire-worshippers, who, Strabo tells us, held a little bunch of twigs in their hand, when praying before the fire. \textsuperscript{18} will I also, ; and though\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 9}
\markright{EZEKIEL 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying, The judgment of the city has drawn near; and each had the weapons of destruction in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And, behold, six men came from the way of the high gate that looks toward the north, and each one's axe was in his hand; and there was one man in the midst of them clothed with a long robe down to the feet, and a sapphire girdle was on his loins: and they came in and stood near the brazen altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the glory of the God of Israel, that was upon them, went up from the cherubs to the porch of the house. And he called the man that was clothed with the long robe, who had the girdle on his loins; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And said to him, Go through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that groan and that grieve for all the iniquities that are done in the midst of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he said to the first in my hearing, Go after him into the city, and strike: and let not your eyes spare, and have no mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Slay utterly old man and youth, and virgin, and infants, and women: but go you⌃ not near any on whom is the mark: begin at my sanctuary. So they began with the elder men who were within in the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he said to them, Defile the house, and go out and fill the ways with dead bodies, and strike. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass as they were striking, that I fell upon my face, and cried out, and said, Alas, O Lord! will you destroy the remnant of Israel, in pouring out your wrath upon Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then said he to me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Juda is become very exceedingly great: for the land is filled with many nations, and the city is filled with iniquity and uncleanness: because they have said, The Lord has forsaken the earth, The Lord looks not upon [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore my eye shall not spare, neither will I have any mercy: I have recompensed their ways upon their heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And, behold, the man clothed with the long robe, and girded with the girdle about his loins, answered and said, I have done as you did command me.\par

\subsection*{Ezekiel 10}
\markright{EZEKIEL 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then I looked, and, behold, over the firmament that was above the head of the cherubs [there was] a likeness of a throne over them, as a sapphire stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said to the man clothed with the [long] robe, Go in between the wheels that are under the cherubs, and fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubs, and scatter [them] over the city. And he went in my sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the cherubs stood on the right hand of the house, as the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then the glory of the Lord departed from the cherubs to the porch of the house; and the cloud filled the house, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sound of the cherubs' wings was heard as far as the outer court, as the voice of the Almighty God speaking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass, when he gave a charge to the man clothed with the sacred robe, saying, Take fire from between the wheels from between the cherubs, that he went in, and stood near the wheels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he stretched forth his hand into the midst of the fire that was between the cherubs, and took [thereof], and put [it] into the hands of the man clothed with the sacred robe: and he took [it], and went out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I saw the cherubs [having] the likeness of men's hands under their wings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I saw, and behold, four wheels stood by the cherubs, one wheel by each cherub: and the appearance of the wheels was as the appearance of a carbuncle stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And [as for] their appearance, [there was] one likeness to the four, as if there should be a wheel in the midst of a wheel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When they went, they went on their four sides; they turned not when they went, for whichever way the first head looked, they went; and they turned not as they went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about the four wheels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these wheels were called Gelgel in my hearing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the cherubs were the same living creature which I saw by the river of Chobar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when the cherubs went, the wheels went, and they were close to them: and when the cherubs lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, their wheels turned not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} When they stood, [the wheels] stood; and when they mounted up, [the wheels] mounted up with them: because the spirit of life was in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then the glory of the Lord departed from the house, and went up on the cherubs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the cherubs lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight: when they went forth, the wheels were also beside them, and they stood at the entrance of the front gate of the house of the Lord; and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This is the living creature which I saw under the God of Israel by the river of Chobar; and I knew that they were cherubs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Each one [had] four faces, and each one [had] eight wings; and under their wings was the likeness of men's hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And [as for] the likeness of their faces, these are the [same] faces which I saw under the glory of the God of Israel by the river of Chobar: and they went each straight forward.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I looked; in the; above; as the \textsuperscript{2} unto, Go, thine hand Heb. the hollow of thine hand coals; scatter \textsuperscript{4} the glory, ; went up Heb. was lifted up and the house \textsuperscript{5} the sound outer; the voice \textsuperscript{7} stretched forth Heb. sent forth unto the, and went \textsuperscript{9} behold as the; a beryl Tarshish is generally rendered by the LXX and the Vulgate the chrysolite, so called by the ancients (from χρυσος ( χρψσος ), gold, and λιθος, a stone), because of its fine gold yellow colour. It is now called by the moderns the topaz; is a very beautiful and valuable gem in its pure and perfect state, though very rarely found so; and the finer pieces of it are in hardness second only to the diamond. The Vulgate, however, in, renders, quasi visio maris "as the appearance of the seas, " i.e., azure; and Dr. Geddes (on ) says, that, with Abarbanel, he believes the beryl to be intended. It is a pellucid gem, called by our lapidaries, aqua marina of a sea or bluish green colour, found in the East Indies and about the gold mines of Peru. The genuine beryl never receives any other mixture of colour; and in its perfect state approaches the hardness of garnet. \textsuperscript{13} it was cried etc. or, they were called in my hearing, Wheel, or Galgal. \textsuperscript{17} for, of the living creature or, of life \textsuperscript{19} the cherubims, of the east, and the glory \textsuperscript{20} the living, the river and I\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 11}
\markright{EZEKIEL 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover the Spirit took me up, and brought me to the front gate of the house of the Lord, that looks eastward: and behold at the entrance of the gate were about five and twenty men; and I saw in the midst of them Jechonias the son of Ezer, and Phaltias the son of Banaeas, the leaders of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to me, Son of man, these are the men that devise vanities, and take evil counsel in this city: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} who say, Have not the houses been newly built? This is the caldron, and we are the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, son of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Spirit of the Lord fell upon me, and said to me, say; Thus says the Lord; Thus have you⌃ said, O house of Israel: and I know the devices of your spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You⌃ have multiplied your dead in this city, and you⌃ have filled your ways with slain men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore thus says the Lord; Your dead whom you⌃ have struck in the midst of it, these are the flesh, and this[city] is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You⌃ fear the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will bring you forth out of the midst of it, and will deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You⌃ shall fall by the sword; I will judge you on the mountains of Israel; and you⌃ shall know that I am the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it came to pass, while I was prophesying, that Phaltias the son of Banaeas died. And I fell upon my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, Alas, alas, O Lord! will you utterly destroy the remnant of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Son of man, your brethren, and the men of your captivity, and all the house of Israel are come to the full, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said, Keep you⌃ far away from the Lord: the land is given to us for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore say you, Thus says the Lord; I will cast them off among the nations, and will disperse them into every land, yet will I be to them for a little sanctuary in the countries which they shall enter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore say you, Thus says the Lord; I will also take them from the heathen, and gather them out of the lands wherein I have scattered them, and will give them the land of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall enter in there, and shall remove all the abominations of it, and all its iniquities from it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And I will give them another heart, and will put a new spirit within them; and will extract the heart of stone from their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} that they may walk in my commandments, and keep my ordinances, and do them: and they shall be to me a people, and I will be to them a God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And as for the heart [set upon] their abominations and their iniquities, as their heart went [after them], I have recompensed their ways on their heads, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then the cherubs lifted up their wings, and the wheels beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city, and stood on the mountain which was in front of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Spirit took me up, and brought me to the land of the Chaldeans, to the captivity, in a vision by the Spirit of God: and I went up after the vision which I saw. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And I spoke to the captivity all the words of the Lord which he had showed me.\par
