\subsection*{Ezekiel 41}
\markright{EZEKIEL 41}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he brought me into the temple, the porch of which he measured, six cubits the breadth on one side, and six cubits the breadth of the porch on the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the breadth of the gateway was ten cubits, and the side-pieces of the gateway were five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and he measured the length of it, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he went into the inner court, and measured the post of the door, two cubits; and the door, six cubits; and the side-pieces of the door, seven cubits on one side, and seven cubits on the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he measured the length of the doors, forty cubits; and the breadth, twenty cubits, in front of the temple: and he said, This is the holy of holies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits: and the breadth of [each] side, four cubits round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the sides were twice ninety, side against side; and [there was] a space in the wall of the house at the sides round about, that they should be for them that take hold of them to see, that they should not at all touch the walls of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the breadth of the upper side [was made] according to the projection out of the wall, against the upper one round about the house, that it might be enlarged above, and that [men] might go up to the upper chambers from those below, and from the ground-sills to the third story. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And as for the height of the house round about, [each] space between the sides was equal to a reed of six cubits; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} and the breadth of the wall of each side without was five cubits; and the spaces that were left between the sides of the house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and between the chambers, were a width of twenty cubits, the circumference of the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the doors of the chambers were toward the space left by the one door that looked northward, and [there was] one door southward; and the breadth of the remaining open space [was] five cubits in extent round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the partition [wall] in front of the remaining space, toward the west, was seventy cubits in breadth; the breadth of the partition wall was five cubits round about, and the length of it ninety cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he measured in front of the house a length of one hundred cubits, and the remaining spaces and the partitions; and the walls thereof were in length one hundred cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the breadth in front of the house, and the remaining [spaces] before [it were] one hundred cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he measured the length of the partition in front of the space left by the back parts of that house; and the [spaces] left on this side and on that side were in length one hundred cubits: and the temple and the corners and the outer porch were ceiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the windows were latticed, [giving] light round about to the three [stories], so as to look through: and the house and the parts adjoining were planked round about, and [so was] the floor, and from the floor up to the windows, and the window [shutters] folded back in three parts for one to look through. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And almost all the way to the inner, and close to the outer [side], and upon all the wall round about within and without, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} were carved cherubs and palm-trees between the cherubs, [and each] cherub [had] two faces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The face of a man was toward one palm tree on this side and on that side, and the face of a lion toward another palm tree on this side and on that side: the house was carved all round. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} From the floor to the ceiling were cherubs and palm-trees carved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the holy place and the temple opened on four sides; in front of the holy places the appearance was as the look of {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} a wooden altar, the height of it three cubits, and the length two cubits, and the breadth two cubits; and it had horns, and the base of it and the sides of it were of wood: and he said to me, This is the table, which is before the face of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the temple [had] two doors, and the sanctuary [had] two doors, with two turning leaves [apiece]; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} two leaves to the one, and two leaves to the other door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And [there was] carved work upon them, and cherubs on the doors of the temple, and palm-trees according to the carving of the sanctuary; and [there were] stout planks in front of the porch without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And [there were] secret windows; and he measured from side to side, to the roofing of the porch; and the sides of the house were closely planked.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} he brought, to the temple; the posts These were probably a sort of door-case on each side of the entrance; and the tabernacle perhaps was a kind of covering to the door, of the same dimensions. \textsuperscript{2} the door or, the entrance, This was the door out of the porch into the sanctuary, which seems to have been wider than that from the court to the porch.; the length \textsuperscript{3} two cubits This was the thickness of the partition wall between the sanctuary ( ) and holy of holies ( ); the breadth of the wall on each side of the gate being seven cubits, and the entrance into the holy place six cubits in width. \textsuperscript{6} one over another Heb. side chamber over side chamber, thirty in order. or, three and thirty times, or feet. We find by Josephus, that around Solomon's temple were chambers three stories high, each story consisting of thirty chambers; which are supposed to have been on the north, south, and east sides of the temple. and they, have hold Heb. be holden, but That is, the beams or supporters, of the chambers were not let into the main wall of the temple; but rested on projections of the outer wall, which became a cubit narrower at every story, leaving a ledge of one cubit, to support the beams. \textsuperscript{7} there was Heb. it was, made broader, and went round; an enlarging In the same proportion in which the thickness of the wall decreased, the chambers increased, so that the middle story was one cubit larger, and the upper story two cubits larger, than the lower rooms; and a winding staircase, which widened in the same manner as the rooms, ascended from the bottom to the top. \textsuperscript{9} was five that which This appears to have been a walk, or gallery of communication between the chambers, five cubits broad, into which the doors opened. \textsuperscript{10} the chambers As the word rendered chambers is different from that used before, it is supposed there was another row of buildings, parallel with the side chambers, with a passage of twenty cubits between. \textsuperscript{12} separate, ; the wall This appears to have been a building erected at the west end of the temple. \textsuperscript{13} he measured seem to intimate, that all the buildings of the temple occupied an area of 100 square cubits. \textsuperscript{15} galleries or, several walks, or walks with pillars; with the \textsuperscript{16} narrow, ; ceiled with wood Heb. ceiling of wood; from the ground up to the windows or, the ground unto the windows covered Probably either by jutting out of the main wall of the temple; or by lattice work, or curtains, or by both. \textsuperscript{17} To that That is, the windows were placed above the height of the door, at the east end of the temple, and thus continued, at the same height, and at measured distances, along both sides of the holy place, to the wall of the inner sanctuary, in which there were no windows. measure Heb. measures \textsuperscript{18} with cherubims; palm trees; and every \textsuperscript{22} altar This must signify the altar of incense; which, both in the tabernacle and Solomon's temple, was covered with plates of gold. It is very remarkable, that in this temple described by Ezekiel, there is not the least mention of gold or silver, though there was such a profusion of these metals in the former; which may probably imply, that a glory of a more spiritual nature was intended under these emblems.; This is; before\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 42}
\markright{EZEKIEL 42}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he brought me into the inner court eastward, opposite the northern gate: and he brought me in, and behold five chambers near the vacant space, and near the northern partition, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} one hundred cubits in length toward the north, and in breadth fifty, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} ornamented accordingly as the gates of the inner court, and arranged accordingly as the peristyles of the outer court, [with] triple porticos fronting one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in front of the chambers was a walk ten cubits in breadth, the length [reaching] to one hundred cubits; and their doors were northward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the upper walks were in like manner: for the peristyle projected from it, [even] from the range of columns below, and [there was] a space between; so [were there] a peristyle and a space between, and so [were there] two porticos. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For they were triple, and they had not pillars like the pillars of the outer ones: therefore they projected from the lower ones and the middle ones from the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And [there was] light without, corresponding to the chambers of the outer court looking toward the front of the northern chambers; the length [of them was] fifty cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the length of the chambers looking toward the inner court was fifty cubits, and these are the ones that front the others; the whole was one hundred cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And [there were] doors of these chambers for an outlet toward the east, so that one should go through them out of the outer court, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} by the opening of the walk at the corner; and the south parts were toward the south, toward the remaining space, and toward the partition, and [so were] the chambers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the walk was in front of them, according to the measures of the chambers toward the north, both according to the length of them, and according to the breadth of them, and according to all their openings, an according to all their turnings, and according to their lights, and according to their doors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [So were the measures] of the chambers toward the south, and according to the doors at the entrance of the walk, as it were the distance of a reed for light, and eastward as one went in by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said to me, The chambers toward the north, and the chambers toward the south, in front of the void spaces, these are the chambers of the sanctuary, wherein the priests the sons of Sadduc, who draw near to the Lord, shall eat the most holy things: and there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meat-offering, and the sin-offerings, and the trespass-offerings; because the place is holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} None shall go in there except the priests, [and] they shall not go forth of the holy place into the outer court, that they that draw near [to me] may be continually holy, and may not touch their garments in which they minister, [with defilement], for they are holy; and they shall put on other garments whenever they come in contact with the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So the measurement of the house within was accomplished: and he brought me forth by the way of the gate that looks eastward, and measured the plan of the house round about in order. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he stood behind the gate looking eastward, and measured five hundred [cubits] with the measuring reed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he turned to the north and measured in front of the north [side] five hundred cubits with the measuring reed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he turned to the west, and measured in front of the west side, five hundred [cubits] with the measuring reed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he turned to the south, and measured in front of the south side, five hundred [cubits] by the measuring reed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The [four sides he measured] by the same reed, and he marked out the house and the circumference of the parts round about, [a space] of five hundred [cubits] eastward, and a breadth of five hundred cubits, to make a division between the sanctuary and the outer wall, that [belonged to] the design of the house.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} he brought, the utter court; chamber This seems to denote a row of chambers in three stories; which appear to have been situated in the inner court (here called the outer court in reference to the temple, ), just before the separate place, at the entrance from the north. \textsuperscript{2} Before Perhaps this means, that the north door was 100 cubits from the entrance into the court; and that the door-way, or portico, was 50 cubits in length; or, that it faced one of the cloisters, the length of which was 100 cubits, and its breadth 50, which was the proportion of all the cloisters. \textsuperscript{3} Over One side of these buildings looked upon the void space about the temple of twenty cubits, and the other toward the pavement belonging to the outer court. the twenty the pavement; gallery against \textsuperscript{4} before These seems to have been two rows of these chambers, and a walk between of ten cubits in width; with an entrance into it from the chambers, of one cubit in width. a walk a way \textsuperscript{5} were higher than these or, did eat of these, than the lower, and than the middlemost of the building or, and the building consisted of the lower and the middlemost. \textsuperscript{8} before Passing from the north to the south side of the temple ( ), the prophet was shewn that the space of ground, which was before the temple on the east, measured 100 cubits. \textsuperscript{9} from under or, from the place of, the entry or, he that brought me as one goeth or, as he came \textsuperscript{10} the thickness Rather, "the breadth of the wall, " that is, the breadth of ground which it enclosed. over against These south chambers were exactly like those on the north. \textsuperscript{13} they be holy;, ; approach; the most holy \textsuperscript{14} they not go; and shall put \textsuperscript{16} side Heb. wind the measuring reed Estimating the reed at 10+ feet, 500 reeds will be nearly equal to a mile; so that from this statement we find the temple, with its outbuildings, was built on a square, nearly an English mile on each side, and four miles in circumference. This not only far exceeds the size of Solomon's temple, or that after the captivity, which was only 500 cubits, or a furlong, on each side, and exactly half a mile in circuit; but is nearly equal to the whole extent of Jerusalem itself, which, when greatest, was but 33 furlongs in circumference, somewhat less than 4+ miles. This seems clearly to intimate, that the vision cannot be explained of any temple that has hitherto been built, or indeed of any literal temple, but figuratively and mystically of the spiritual temple, the church under the gospel, and its spiritual glory. \textsuperscript{20} it had; five hundred; a separation\par}

\markright{EZEKIEL 43}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover he brought me to the gate looking eastward, and led me forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came by the eastern way; and [there was] a voice of an army, as the sound of many redoubling [their shouts], and the earth shone like light from the glory round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the vision which I saw was like the vision which I saw when I went in to anoint the city: and the vision of the chariot which I saw was like the vision which I saw at the river Chobar; and I fell upon my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the glory of the Lord came into the house, by the way of the gate looking eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Spirit took me up, and brought me into the inner court; and, behold, the house of the Lord was full of glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I stood, and behold [there was] a voice out of the house of one speaking to me, and a man stood near me, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and he said to me, Son of man, you have seen the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, in which my name shall dwell in the midst of the house of Israel for ever; and the house of Israel shall no more profane my holy name, they and their princes, by their fornication, or by the murders of [their] princes in the midst of them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} when they set my door-way by their door-way, and my thresholds near to their thresholds: and they made my wall as it were joining myself and them, and they profaned my holy name with their iniquities which they wrought: and I destroyed them in my wrath and with slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now let them put away from me their fornication, and the murders of their princes, and I will dwell in the midst of them forever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, that they may cease from their sins; and [show] its aspect and the arrangement of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they shall bear their punishment for all the things that they have done: and you shall describe the house, and its entrances, and the plan thereof, and all its ordinances, and you shall make known to them all the regulations of it, and describe [them] before them: and they shall keep all my commandments, and all my ordinances, and do them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you shall show the plan of the house on the top of the mountain: all its limits round about [shall be] most holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these are the measures of the altar by the cubit of a cubit and a span, the cavity [shall be] a cubit deep, and a cubit shall be the breadth, and the border on the rim of it round about shall be a span: and this [shall be] the height of the altar {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} from the bottom at the commencement of the hollow part to this great mercy-seat, from beneath was two cubits, and the breadth was a cubit; and from the little mercy-seat to the great mercy-seat, four cubits, and the breadth was a cubit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the altar [shall be] four cubits; and from the altar and above the horns a cubit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the altar [shall be] of the length of twelve cubits, by twelve cubits [in breadth], square upon its four sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the mercy-seat [shall be] fourteen cubits in length, by fourteen cubits in breadth on its four sides; and [there shall be] a border to it carried round about it of half a cubit; and the rim of it [shall be] a cubit round about; and the steps thereof looking eastward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he said to me, Son of man, thus says the Lord God of Israel; These are the ordinances of the altar in the day of its being made, to offer upon it whole burnt offerings, and to pour blood upon it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And you shall appoint to the priests the Levites of the seed of Sadduc, that draw near to me, says the Lord God, to minister to me, a calf of the herd for a sin-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they shall take of its blood, and shall put [it] on the four horns of the altar, and upon the four corners of the propitiatory, and upon the base round about, and they shall make atonement for it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they shall take the calf of the sin-offering, and it shall be consumed by fire in the separate place of the house, outside the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And on the second day they shall take two kids of the goats without blemish for a sin-offering; and they shall make atonement for the altar, as they made atonement with the calf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And after they have finished the atonement, they shall bring an unblemished calf of the herd, and an unblemished ram of the flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you⌃ shall offer [them] before the Lord, and the priests shall sprinkle salt upon them, and shall offer them up [as] whole burnt offerings to the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Seven days shall you offer a kid daily for a sin-offering, and a calf of the herd, and a ram out of the flock: they shall sacrifice them unblemished for seven days: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and they shall make atonement for the altar, and shall purge it; and they shall consecrate themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And it shall come to pass from the eighth day and onward, [that] the priests shall offer your whole burnt offerings on the altar, and your peace-offerings; and I will accept you, says the Lord.\par

\subsection*{Ezekiel 44}
\markright{EZEKIEL 44}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then he brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary that looks eastward; and it was shut. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord said to me, This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it; for the Lord God of Israel shall enter by it, and it shall be shut. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the prince, he shall sit in it, to eat bread before the Lord; he shall go in by the way of the porch of the gate, and shall go forth by the way of the same. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he brought me in by the way of the gate that looks northward, in front of the house: and I looked, and, behold, the house was full of the glory of the Lord: and I fell upon my face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord said to me, Son of man, attend with your heart, and see with [your] eyes, and hear with your ears all that I say to you, according to all the ordinances of the house of the Lord, and all the regulations thereof; and you shall attend well to the entrance of the house, according to all its outlets, in all the holy things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you shall say to the provoking house, [even] to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord God; Let it suffice you [to have committed] all your iniquities, O house of Israel! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} that you⌃ have brought in aliens, uncircumcised in heart, and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, and to profane it, when you⌃ offered bread, flesh, and blood; and you⌃ transgressed my covenant by all your iniquities; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} and you⌃ appointed [others] to keep the charges in my sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore thus says the Lord God; No alien, uncircumcised in heart or uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of all the children of strangers that are in the midst of the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But as for the Levites who departed far from me when Israel went astray from me after their imaginations, they shall even bear their iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} yet they shall minister in my sanctuary, [being] porters at the gates of the house, and serving the house: they shall kill the victims and the whole burnt offerings for the people, and they shall stand before the people to minister to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became to the house of Israel a punishment of iniquity; therefore have I lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they shall not draw near to me to minister to me in the priests' office, nor to approach the holy things of the children of Israel, nor [to approach] my holy of holies: but they shall bear their reproach for the error wherein they erred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} They shall bring them to keep the charges of the house, for all the service of it, and for all that they shall do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The priests the Levites, the sons of Sadduc, who kept the charges of my sanctuary when the house of Israel went astray from me, these shall draw near to me to minister to me, and shall stand before my face, to offer sacrifice to me, the fat and the blood, says the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} These shall enter into my sanctuary, and these shall approach my table, to minister to me, and they shall keep my charges. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it shall come to pass when they enter the gates of the inner court, [that] they shall put on linen robes; and they shall not put on woollen garments when they minister at the gate of the inner court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they shall have linen mitres upon their heads, and shall have linen drawers upon their loins; and they shall not tightly gird themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall put off their robes, in which they minister; and they shall lay them up in the chambers of the sanctuary, and shall put on other robes, and they shall not sanctify the people with their robes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they shall not shave their heads, nor shall they pluck off their hair; they shall carefully cover their heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And no priest shall drink any wine, when they go into the inner court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Neither shall they take to themselves to wife a widow, or one that is put away, but a virgin of the seed of Israel: but if there should happen to be a priest's widow, they shall take [her]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they shall teach my people [to distinguish] between holy and profane, and they shall make known to them [the difference] between unclean and clean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And these shall attend at a judgment of blood to decide it: they shall rightly observe my ordinances, and judge my judgments, and keep my statutes and my commandments in all my feasts; and they shall hallow my sabbaths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And they shall not go in to the dead body of a man to defile themselves: only [a priest] may defile himself for a father, or for a mother, or for a son, or for a daughter, or for a brother, or for his sister, who has not been married. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And after he has been cleansed, let him number to himself seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And on whatever day they shall enter into the inner court to minister in the holy place, they shall bring a propitiation, says the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it shall be to them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance: and no possession shall be given them among the children of Israel; for I am their possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And these shall eat the meat-offerings, and the sin-offerings, and the trespass-offerings; and every special offering in Israel shall be theirs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} [And] the first fruits of all things, and the firstborn of all [animals] and all offerings, of all your first fruits there shall be [a share] for the priests; and you⌃ shall give your earliest produce to the priest, to bring your blessings upon your houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the priests shall eat no bird or beast that dies of itself, or is taken of wild beasts.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the outward So called in opposition to the temple itself, which was the inner sanctuary., ; looketh \textsuperscript{3} for; the prince It is probable that the prince mentioned here and elsewhere, does not mean the Messiah, but the ruler of the Jewish nation for the time being. For it is not only directed where he should sit in the temple, and eat his portion of the sacrifices, and when and how he should go out; but it is also ordered ( ), that at the passover he shall offer a bullock, a sin offering for himself and the people; and to guard him against any temptation of oppressing the people, he had a provision of land allotted to him ( ), out of which he is to give an inheritance for his sons ( ). These appear plainly to be political rules for common princes, and for a succession of them; but as no such rules were observed under the second temple, the fulfilment of it must still be future.; to eat; he shall enter \textsuperscript{4} the way, the glory, ; and I fell \textsuperscript{5} mark well Heb. set thine heart; *marg.; *marg. concerning; and mark well the entering \textsuperscript{6} thou shalt say, let it suffice \textsuperscript{7} ye have brought, ; strangers Heb. children of a stranger, uncircumcised in heart The introduction of uncircumcised persons to eat of the peace offerings and oblations, would have been a gross violation of the Mosaic law; but, as there was no law to exclude "the uncircumcised of heart, " who were circumcised and ritually clean, this seems to point out a new and different constitution.; when, ; the fat, broken \textsuperscript{8} ye have not; charge or, ward, or ordinance, and so \textsuperscript{11} they shall be As few, if any, of those who, before the captivity, had been guilty in these respects, lived to witness the restoration of the temple service; and as it does not appear that their descendants were thus degraded for the idolatry of their ancestors; it is probable that a thorough reformation of the whole church, or the prevalence of pure religion among the converted Jews, is here predicted. having charge; shall slay, and they \textsuperscript{12} they ministered; caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity Heb. were for a stumbling-block of iniquity unto, etc. therefore, ; and they shall \textsuperscript{15} the sons, ; , when they shall stand; the fat; the blood \textsuperscript{16} They shall enter to my table To place the shew-bread there. \subsection*{Ezekiel 45}
\markright{EZEKIEL 45}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when you⌃ measure the land for inheritance, you⌃ shall set apart first fruits to the Lord, a holy space of the land, in length twenty and five thousand [reeds], and in breadth twenty thousand; it shall be holy in all the borders thereof round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And there shall be a sanctuary out of this, five hundred [reeds in length] by five hundred in breadth, a square round about; and [there shall be] a vacant space [beyond] this of fifty cubits round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And out of this measurement shall you measure the length five and twenty thousand, and the breadth twenty thousand: and in it shall be the holy of holies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Of the land shall be [a portion] for the priests that minister in the holy place, and it shall be for them that draw near to minister to the Lord: and it shall be to them a place for houses set apart for their sacred office; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} the length [shall be] twenty-five thousand, and the breadth twenty thousand: and the Levites that attend the house, they shall have cities to dwell in for a possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you⌃ shall appoint [for] the possession of the city five thousand in breadth, and in length twenty-five thousand: after the manner of the first fruits of the holy portion, they shall be for all the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the prince [shall have a portion] out of this, and out of this [there shall be a portion] for the first fruits of the sanctuary, [and] for the possession of the city, in front of the first fruits of the sanctuary, and in front of the possession of the city westward, and from the western parts eastward: and the length [shall be] equal to one of the parts of the western borders, and the length [shall be] to the eastern borders of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he shall have it for a possession in Israel: and the princes of Israel shall no more oppress my people; but the house of Israel shall inherit the land according to their tribes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Thus says the Lord God; Let it suffice you, you⌃ princes of Israel: remove injustice and misery, execute judgment and justice; take away oppression from my people, says the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You⌃ shall have a just balance, and a just measure, and a just choenix for measure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And in like manner there shall be one choenix as a measure of capacity; the tenth of the homer [shall be] the choenix, and the tenth of the homer shall be in fair proportion to the homer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the weights [shall be] twenty oboli, your pound shall be five shekels, fifteen shekels and fifty shekels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these are the first fruits which you⌃ shall offer; a sixth part of a homer of wheat, and the sixth part of it [shall consist] of an ephah of a core of barley. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And [you⌃ shall give as] the appointed measure of oil one bath of oil out of ten baths; for ten baths are a homer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And one sheep from the flock out of ten, as an oblation from all the tribes of Israel, for sacrifices, and for whole burnt offerings, and for peace-offerings, to make atonement for you, says the Lord God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And all the people shall give these first fruits to the prince of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And through the prince shall be [offered] the whole burnt offerings and the meat-offerings, and the drink-offerings in the feasts, and at the new moons, and on the sabbaths; and in all the feasts of the house of Israel: he shall offer the sin-offerings, and the meat-offering, and the whole burnt offerings, and the peace-offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Thus says the Lord God; In the first month, on the first [day] of the month, you⌃ shall take a calf without blemish out of the herd, to make atonement for the holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the priest shall take of the blood of the atonement, and put it on the thresholds of the house, and upon the four corners of the temple, and upon the altar, and upon the thresholds of the gate of the inner court. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And thus shall you do in the seventh month; on the first [day] of the month you shall take a rate from each one; and you⌃ shall make atonement for the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And in the first [month], on the fourteenth [day] of the month, you⌃ shall have the feast of the passover; seven days shall you⌃ eat unleavened bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the prince shall offer in that day a calf for a sin-offering for himself, and the house, and for all the people of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And for the seven days of the feast he shall offer as whole burnt offerings to the Lord seven calves and seven rams without blemish daily for the seven days; and a kid of the goats daily for a sin-offering, and a meat-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And you shall prepare a cake for the calf, and cakes for the ram, and a hin of oil for the cake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And in the seventh month, on the fifteenth [day] of the month, you shall sacrifice in the feast in the same way seven days, as [they sacrificed] the sin-offerings, and the whole burnt offerings, and the free will offering, and the oil.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} shall divide by lot Heb. cause the land to fall by lot, ; ye shall offer; an holy portion Heb. holiness, the length That our translators rightly added the word reeds, is evident from the length and breadth of the sanctuary being exactly the same as before (compare with ). Estimating the reed at 3+ yards, this holy oblation would constitute a square of nearly fifty miles on every side. From the north side a portion of nearly twenty miles in width, and nearly fifty in length, was appointed for the priests; and in the midst of this portion, the area of the sanctuary, about a mile square, to be enclosed by a wall ( ). Next to this, on the south, was the Levites' portion, of the same dimensions as that of the priests' ( ); and south of this was the portion for the city, of the same length as those of the priests and Levites, but only half the width ( ). These three formed the square of 25, 000 reeds, or nearly fifty miles; and that set apart for the prince, the breadth of which is not mentioned, extended in length from north to south, along the east and west sides of the square. As Canaan would not admit of so large a portion for the sanctuary, etc., this was no doubt intended to intimate the large extent of the church in the glorious times predicted. \textsuperscript{2} five hundred in length suburbs or, void places \textsuperscript{5} the five, the ministers for a possession \textsuperscript{8} and my princes In the predicted period, not only shall the ministers and worshippers of God be liberally provided for, but the princes will be both able and willing to defray the expenses of government, without oppressing their subjects, and will rule over them with equity and clemency, as the vicegerents of God; while the people will submit to them conscientiously, and live in peace, prosperity, and holiness. These things seem to be represented in language taken from the customs of the times in which the prophet wrote. Tithes are not mentioned in part of the vision, which shows that the ritual Mosaic law will not be in force., ; according \textsuperscript{9} Let it; remove; execute take away; exactions Heb. expulsions \textsuperscript{11} ephah The ephah was a dry measure, and the bath a liquid measure, containing about seven gallons, four pints, or three pecks, three pints; and the homer about seventy-five gallons, five pints. \textsuperscript{12} the shekel; twenty shekels That is, 20+25+15=60; for the maneh as a weight was equal to sixty shekels, though as a coin it was only equal to fifty, weighing about 2 lb. 6 oz.; and reckoning the shekel at 2s 6d being in value 6£ 5s. \textsuperscript{15} lamb or, kid out of the fat; peace offerings or, thank offerings, to make \textsuperscript{16} the people shall give this Heb. shall be for or, with \textsuperscript{17} the prince's The prince is never mentioned in the ritual appointments of Moses, but here he is required to provide the oblations; and the variations in the Mosaic law, in the number of the several sacrifices, and the proportion of the meat offering to each, being ten times as much as the law prescribed, with several other circumstances, seem more like enacting a new law, than enforcing that of Moses. These variations may intimate a change in the external constitution of the church; and it is probable that they are to be understood emblematically.; , ; in the feasts; Num. 28:1-29:40; he shall prepare; peace offerings or, thank offerings \textsuperscript{18} In the first month This seems to enjoin, not a mere dedication, but an annual purification of the sanctuary; of which there is nothing said in the Mosaic law.; without blemish; and cleanse \textsuperscript{19} and upon the four corners \textsuperscript{20} every one; that is simple Who wants understanding to conduct himself properly. so shall \textsuperscript{23} seven days a burnt, seven bullocks \textsuperscript{25} In the seventh The prince shall do at the feast of tabernacles the same thing he was desired to do on the passover.\par}

\subsection*{Ezekiel 46}
\markright{EZEKIEL 46}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Thus says the Lord God; The gate that is in the inner court, that looks eastward, shall be shut the six working days; [but] let it be opened on the sabbath-day, and it shall be opened on the day of the new moon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of the inner gate, and shall stand at the entrance of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his whole burnt offerings and his peace-offerings, and he shall worship at the entrance of the gate: then shall he come forth; but the gate shall not be shut till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate, both on the sabbaths and at the new moons, before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the prince shall offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord on the sabbath-day, six lambs without blemish, and a ram without blemish; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} and a free will offering, a meat-offering for the ram, and a meat-offering for the lambs, the gift of his hand, and a hin of oil for the meat-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And on the day of the new moon a calf without blemish, and six lambs, and there shall be a ram without blemish; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and a meat-offering for the ram, and there shall be a meat-offering for the calf as a free will offering, and for the lambs, according as his hand can furnish, and [there shall be] a hin of oil for the cake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when the prince goes in, he shall go in by the way of the porch of the gate, and he shall go forth by the way of the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And whenever the people of the land shall go in before the Lord at the feasts, he that goes in by the way of the north gate to worship shall go forth by the way of the south gate; and he that goes in by the way of the south gate shall go forth by the way of the north gate: he shall not return by the gate by which he entered, but he shall go forth opposite it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the prince shall enter with them in the midst of them when they go in; and when they go forth, he shall go forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And in the feasts and in the general assemblies the free will oblation shall be a meat-offering for the calf, and a meat-offering for the ram, and for the lambs, as his hand can furnish, and a hin of oil for the meat-offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And if the prince should prepare [as] a thanksgiving a whole burnt-peace-offering to the Lord, and should open for himself the gate looking eastward, and offer his whole burnt offering, and his peace-offerings, as he does on the sabbath-day; then shall he go out, and shall shut the doors after he has gone out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he shall prepare daily as a whole burnt offering to the Lord a lamb of a year old without blemish: in the morning shall he prepare it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he shall prepare a free will offering for it in the morning, the sixth part of a measure [of flour], and a third part of a hin of oil to mix [therewith] the fine flour, [as] a free will offering to the Lord, a perpetual ordinance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You⌃ shall prepare the lamb, and the free will offering, and the oil in the morning, [for] a perpetual whole burnt sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus says the Lord God; If the prince shall give a gift to one of his sons out of his inheritance, this shall be to his sons a possession [as] an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But if he give a gift to one of his servants, then it shall belong to him until the year of release; and [then] he shall restore [it] to the prince: but of the inheritance of his sons [the possession] shall continue to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the prince shall by no means take of the inheritance of the people, to oppress them: he shall give an inheritance to his sons out of his [own] possession: that my people be not scattered, every one from his possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he brought me into the entrance of the [place] behind the gate, into the chamber of the sanctuary belonging to the priests, that looks toward the north: and, behold, there was a place set apart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said to me, This is the place where the priests shall boil the trespass-offerings and the sin-offerings, and there shall they bake the meat-offering always; so as not to carry [them] out into the outer court, to sanctify the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he brought me into the outer court, and led me round upon the four sides of the court; and, behold, there was a court on [each of] the sides of the court, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} on [every] side a court, [even] a court for all the four [sides], and [each] little court belonging to the court was in length forty cubits, and [in] breadth thirty cubits, [there was] one measure to the four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And [there were] chambers in them round about, round about the four, and cooking-places formed under the chambers round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he said to me, These are the cooks' houses, where they that serve the house shall boil the sacrifices of the people.\par

In the latter history of the Jewish church, the law of Moses only was followed, except in the corruption of following the traditions of the fathers. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the door, waters issued Solomon's temple and the second temple were doubtless well supplied with water, probably conveyed there by means of pipes; but these waters flowed from the temple, not as a common sewer, but as a fertilizing river. A fountain producing abundance of water was not in the temple, and could not be there on the top of such a hill; and consequently these waters, as well as those spoken of by Joel and Zechariah, must be understood figuratively and typically. These waters doubtless were an emblem of the "gospel preached with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven; " and their gradual rise beautifully represents it progress, from small beginnings to an immensely large increase; and the latter part of the representation may relate to the times when it shall fill the earth, and produce the most extensive and important effects on the state of making in every nation.; from under the threshold \textsuperscript{3} the man; waters were to the ankles Heb. waters of the ancles \textsuperscript{4} the waters were to the knees \textsuperscript{5} waters to swim in Heb. waters of swimming \textsuperscript{7} bank Heb. lip; *marg. many \textsuperscript{8} and go down, ; desert or, plain, ; the sea This was the Dead sea, or sea of Sodom, east of Jerusalem, in which it is said no living creature is found; or, at least, from its extreme saltness, it does not abound with fish like other seas. The ten tribes, as well as Judah and Benjamin, were to be admitted to a full share in this inheritance, which seems to imply, that the future restoration to the promised land is predicted; while the admission of strangers who sojourned in the land to a share in the inheritance, as if native Israelites, plainly intimates the calling of the Gentiles into the church, and their joint inheritance of its privileges, and of the heavenly felicity. {\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the names; From; a portion Heb. one portion Dan \textsuperscript{4} by the border In this division of the Holy Land, a portion is laid out for each of the twelve tribes directly across the country, from east to west; and deducting the square of 25, 000 reeds, or nearly fifty miles on each side, between Judah and Benjamin, for the priests, Levites, city, and temple, with the inheritance of the prince to the east and west (See note on ), from 280 miles, the length of the country from north to south, there will remain for each tribe a portion of less than twenty miles in width, and 150 in length. This division of the land entirely differs from that which was made in the days of Joshua, in which the tribes were not only differently placed, but confused and inter-mixed; while here distinct lots are assigned to each of the twelve tribes, in a regular mathematical form. Literally such a division never took place. It seems to denote the equality of privileges which subsists among all the tribes of Believers, of whatever nation, and whatever their previous character may have been. Manasseh \textsuperscript{10} for the priests; and the sanctuary \textsuperscript{11} It shall be for the priests that are sanctified or, The sanctified portion shall be for the priests the sons, charge or, ward, or ordinance, ; as the Levites \textsuperscript{13} five and twenty thousand in \textsuperscript{15} a profane, for the city The holy oblation of 25, 000 square reeds, or near fifty square miles, was divided into three parts from north to south (see note on ); a portion on the north of 10, 000 reeds in width, and 25, 000 in length, for the priests, in the midst of which was the sanctuary or temple, surrounded by a wall 500 reeds square (; see note on ); next to this another portion of the same dimensions for the Levites ( ); and on the south another portion of the same length, but only 5, 000 reeds in breadth, for the city ( ). The city was situated in the midst of this portion, being 4, 500 reeds, or about nine miles square ( ), having a suburb of 250 reeds, or about half a mile, on each side ( ), leaving 10, 000 reeds or nearly ten miles, on the east side, and the same on the west side, for the profit of those who serve the city out of all the tribes ( ). On the east and west sides of this square of 25, 000 reeds, is the portion of the prince; each of which, estimating the breadth of the land at 150 miles, would form a square of fifty miles. Thus the whole plan of the division of the country, laying out of the city, temple, and all its appendages, is perfectly regular and uniform; and would therefore convey to the minds of the Jews the most complete idea they were capable of conceiving of the most perfect church, commonwealth, city, temple, and conveniences, on the largest and grandest scale for the Divine worship; and it doubtless ultimately points out the land of Immanuel, the city of the New Jerusalem, and his temple, the Christian church, the house of the living God. \textsuperscript{23} Benjamin; a portion Heb. one portion \textsuperscript{28} from Tamar; strife in Kadesh Heb. Meribah-kadesh, ; the river; the great sea \textsuperscript{30} the goings; four It is certainly most obvious to interpret these measures, not of cubits, but of the measuring reed which the prophet's conductor had in his hand; according to which, the city would be about thirty-six miles in circumference, and nine miles on each side of the square; which was nearly nine times larger than the greatest extent to which Jerusalem ever attained (See note on, and see note on .) The large dimensions of the city and land were perhaps intended to intimate the extensive and glorious propagation of the gospel in the times predicted; and the land was not called Canaan, nor the city Jerusalem, probably because they were figurative of spiritual blessings to the church and to Israel. \textsuperscript{35} and the name; The Lord Heb. \section*{Daniel Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Daniel\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book names Daniel and conservative scholarship receives both court tales and visions as Danielic, with later copying but not late pseudonymous authorship.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Jesus explicitly refers to Daniel as the prophet in Matthew 24:15.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 6th century BC in the Babylonian and Persian periods\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Daniel in the exile from Babylon through Persian rule; the Hebrew-Aramaic form is part of the canonical witness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The Greek tradition preserves Daniel in Old Greek and Theodotionic forms; this edition's LXX stream especially requires careful note of Greek Daniel material and its relation to the MT/Aramaic form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Court history and apocalyptic visions in exile, showing God's rule over empires and the coming kingdom.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To reveal God's sovereignty over world kingdoms and His final triumph through the Son of Man's everlasting dominion.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} sovereignty; exile; kingdom; resurrection; antichrist pattern; Son of Man; deliverance\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Court narratives 1-6; Visions 7-12; Greek Daniel additions in the wider tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. 4Q Daniel manuscripts 2nd-1st centuries BC | Subst. Qumran Daniel manuscripts provide early Hebrew-Aramaic witness close to the Maccabean era and argue strongly for the book's early acceptance 2nd-1st centuries BC | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Daniel traditions, though Theodotion became dominant in much Christian use 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Use in later Jewish apocalyptic and explicit citation by Jesus by Jesus and later Jewish literature (1st century AD and earlier)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Daniel is central for comparing Hebrew-Aramaic text, Old Greek, Theodotion, and the Greek additions such as Susanna and Bel and the Dragon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Daniel as the prophet named by Christ and therefore rejects late pseudonymous theories as incompatible with Christ's testimony.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Daniel 1}
\markright{DANIEL 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the third year of the reign of Joakim king of Juda, came Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon to Jerusalem, and besieged it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the Lord gave into his hand Joakim king of Juda, and part of the vessels of the house of God: and he brought them into the land of Sennaar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasure-house of his god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king told Asphanez his chief eunuch, to bring in some of the captive children of Israel, and of the seed of the kingdom, and of the princes; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} young men in whom was no blemish, and beautiful in appearance, and skilled in all wisdom, and possessing knowledge, and acquainted with prudence, and who had ability to stand in the house before the king, and the king gave commandment to teach them the learning and language of the Chaldeans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the king appointed them a daily portion from the king's table, and from the wine which he drank; and [gave orders] to nourish them three years, and [that] afterwards they should stand before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now these were among them of the children of Juda, Daniel, and Ananias, and Azarias, and Misael. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the chief of the eunuchs gave them names: to Daniel, Baltasar; and to Ananias, Sedrach; and to Misael, Misach; and to Azarias, Abdenago. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Daniel purposed in his heart, that he would not defile himself with the king's table, nor with the wine of his drink: and he entreated the chief of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now God [had] brought Daniel into favor and compassion with the chief of the eunuchs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your meat and your drink, lest he see your countenances gloomy in comparison of the young men your equals; also shall you⌃ endanger my head to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Ananias, Misael, [and] Azarias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Prove now your servants ten days; and let them give us pulse, and let us eat, and let us drink water: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And let our countenances be seen by you, and the countenances of the children that eat [at] the king's table; and deal with your servants according as you shall see. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he listened to them, and proved them ten days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And at the end of the ten days their countenances appeared fairer and stouter in flesh, than the children that fed at the king's table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So Amelsad took away their supper and the wine of their drink, and gave them pulse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And [as for] these four children, God gave them understanding and prudence in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And at the end of the days, [after] which the king had given orders to bring them in, then the chief of the eunuchs brought them in before Nabuchodonosor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the king spoke with them; and there were not found out of them all any like Daniel, and Ananias and Misael, and Azarias: and they stood before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And in every matter of wisdom and knowledge wherein the king questioned them, he found them ten times wiser than all the enchanters and sorcerers that were in all his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And Daniel continued till the first year of king Cyrus.\par

\subsection*{Daniel 2}
\markright{DANIEL 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the second year of [his] reign Nabuchodonosor dreamed a dream, and his spirit was amazed, and his sleep departed from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the king gave orders to call the enchanters, and the magicians, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to declare to the king his dreams. And they came and stood before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the king said to them, I have dreamed, and my spirit was troubled to know the dream. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, [saying], O king, live for ever: do you tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The king answered the Chaldeans, The thing has departed from me: if you⌃ do not make known to me the dream and the interpretation, you⌃ shall be destroyed, and your houses shall be spoiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But if you⌃ make known to me the dream, and the interpretation thereof, you⌃ shall receive of me gifts and presents and much honor: only tell me the dream, and the interpretation thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They answered the second time, and said, Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare the interpretation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the king answered and said, I verily know that you⌃ are trying to gain time, because you⌃ see that the thing has gone from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If then you⌃ do not tell me the dream, I know that you⌃ have concerted to utter before me a false and corrupt tale, until the time shall have past: tell me my dream, and I shall know that you⌃ will also declare to me the interpretation thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is no man upon the earth, who shall be able to make known the king's matter: forasmuch as no great king or ruler asks such a question of an enchanter, magician, or Chaldean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the question which the king asks is difficult, and there is no one else who shall answer it before the king, but the gods, whose dwelling is not with any flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then the king in rage and anger commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} So the decree went forth, and they began to kill the wise men; and they sought Daniel and his fellows to kill [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then Daniel answered [with] counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the royal guard, who was gone forth to kill the wise men of Babylon; [saying], {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Chief magistrate of the king, therefore has the preemptory command proceeded from the king? So Arioch made known the matter to Daniel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Daniel entreated the king to give him time, and that he might [thus] declare to the king the interpretation of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So Daniel went into his house, and made known the matter to Ananias, and Misael, and Azarias, his friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they sought mercies from the God of heaven concerning this mystery; that Daniel and his friends might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night; and Daniel blessed the God of heaven, and said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} May the name of God be blessed from everlasting and to everlasting: for wisdom and understanding are his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he changes times and seasons: he appoints kings, and removes [them], giving wisdom to the wise, and prudence to them that have understanding: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} he reveals deep and secret [matters]; knowing what is in darkness, and the light is with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} I give thanks to you, and praise [you], O God of my fathers, for you have given me wisdom and power, and has made known to me the things which we asked of you; and you have made known to me the king's vision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Daniel came to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him; Destroy not the wise men of Babylon, but bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Then Arioch in haste brought in Daniel before the king, and said to him, I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judea, who will declare the interpretation to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Baltasar, Canst you declare to me the dream which I saw, and the interpretation thereof? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Daniel answered before the king, and said, The mystery which the king asks [the explanation of] is not [in the power] of the wise men, magicians, enchanters, [or] soothsayers to declare to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, and he has made known to king Nabuchodonosor what things must come to pass in the last days. Your dream, and the visions of your head upon your bed, are as follows, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} O king: your thoughts upon your bed arose [as to] what must come to pass hereafter: and he that reveals mysteries has made known to you what must come to pass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Moreover, this mystery has not been revealed to me by reason of wisdom which is in me beyond all [others] living, but for the sake of making known the interpretation to the king, that you might know the thoughts of your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} You, O king, saw, and behold an image: that image was great, and the appearance of it excellent, standing before your face; and the form of it was terrible. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} [It was] an image, the head of which was of fine gold, its hands and breast and arms of silver, [its] belly and thighs of brass, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} its legs of iron, its feet, part of iron and part of earthenware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} You saw until a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands, and it struck the image upon its feet of iron and earthenware, and utterly reduced them to powder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Then once for all the earthenware, the iron, the brass, the silver, the gold, were ground to powder, and became as chaff from the summer threshing floor; and the violence of the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them: and the stone which had struck the image became a great mountain, and filled all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} You, O king, are a king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a powerful and strong and honorable kingdom, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} in every place where the children of men dwell: and he has given into your hand the wild beasts of the field, and the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and he has made you lord of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} You are the head of gold. And after you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you, an a third kingdom which is the brass, which shall have dominion over all the earth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} and a fourth kingdom, which shall be strong as iron: as iron beats to powder and subdues all things, so shall it beat to powder and subdue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And whereas you saw the feet and the toes, part of earthenware and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; yet there shall be in it of the strength of iron, as you saw the iron mixed with earthenware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And [whereas] the toes of the feet were part of iron and part of earthenware, part of the kingdom shall be strong, and [part] of it shall be broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Whereas you saw the iron mixed with earthenware, they shall be mingled with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave together, as the iron does not mix itself with earthenware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And in the days of those kings the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed: and his kingdom shall not be left to another people, [but] it shall beat to pieces and grind to powder all [other] kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Whereas you saw that a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands, and it beat to pieces the earthenware, the iron, the brass, the silver, the gold; the great God has made known to the king what must happen hereafter: and the dream is true, and the interpretation thereof sure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Then king Nabuchodonosor fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel, and gave orders to offer to him gifts and incense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And the king answered and said to Daniel, Of a truth your God is a God of gods, and Lord of kings, who reveals mysteries; for you have been able to reveal this mystery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And the king promoted Daniel, and gave him great and abundant gifts, and set him over the whole province of Babylon, and [made him] chief satrap over all the wise men of Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And Daniel asked of the king, and he appointed Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, over the affairs of the province of Babylon: but Daniel was in the king's palace.\par
