\subsection*{Amos 7}
\markright{AMOS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Thus has the Lord God showed me; and, behold, a swarm of locusts coming from the east; and, behold, one caterpillar, king Gog. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it came to pass when he had finished devouring the grass of the land, that I said, Lord God, be merciful; who shall raise up Jacob? for he is small in number. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Repent, O Lord, for this. And this shall not be, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Thus has the Lord showed me; and, behold, the Lord called for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep, and devoured the Lord's portion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then I said, O Lord, cease, I pray you: who shall raise up Jacob? for he is small in number. Repent, O Lord, for this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} This also shall not be, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Thus the Lord showed me; and behold, he stood upon a wall of adamant, and in his hand [was] an adamant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the Lord said to me, What see you, Amos? And I said, An adamant. And the Lord said to me, Behold, I appoint an adamant in the midst of my people Israel: I will not pass by them any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the joyful altars shall be abolished, and the sacrifices of Israel shall be set aside; and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then Amasias the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of the house of Israel: the land will be utterly unable to bear all his words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For thus says Amos, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from his land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Amasias said to Amos, Go, seer, remove you into the land of Juda, and live there, and you shall prophesy there: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} but you shall no longer prophesy at Bethel: for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is the royal house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Amos answered, and said to Amasias, I was not a prophet, nor the son of a prophet; but I was a herdman, and a gatherer of sycamore fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, Go, and prophesy to my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now hear the word of the Lord: You say, Prophesy not to Israel, and raise not a tumult against the house of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore thus says the Lord; Your wife shall be a harlot in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be measured with the line; and you shall die in an unclean land; and Israel shall be led captive out of his land. Thus has the Lord God showed me.\par

\subsection*{Amos 8}
\markright{AMOS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And behold a fowler's basket. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he said, What see you, Amos? And I said, A fowler's basket. And the Lord said to me, The end is come upon my people Israel; I will not pass by them any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the ceilings of the temple shall howl in that day, says the Lord God: [there shall be] many a fallen one in every place; I will bring silence upon [them]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Hear now this, you⌃ that oppress the poor in the morning, and drive the needy ones by tyranny from the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} saying, When will the month pass away, and we shall sell, and the sabbath, and we shall open the treasure, to make the measure small, and to enlarge the weight, and make the balance unfair? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for shoes; and we will trade in every kind of fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord swears against the pride of Jacob, None of your works shall ever be forgotten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And shall not the land be troubled for these things, and shall not every one who dwells in it mourn? whereas destruction shall come up as a river, and shall descend as the river of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord God, [that] the sun shall go down at noon, and the light shall be darkened on the earth by day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} and I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring up sackcloth on all loins, and baldness on every head; and I will make them as the mourning of a beloved [friend], and those with them as a day of grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, the days come, says the Lord, that I will send forth a famine on the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the waters shall be troubled from sea to sea, and from the north to the east shall [men] run hither and there, seeking the word of the Lord, and they shall not find [it]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} In that day shall the fair virgins and the young men faint for thirst; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} they who swear by the propitiation of Samaria, and who say, Your god, O Dan, lives; and, Your god, O Bersabee, lives; and they shall fall, and shall no more rise again.\par

\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I saw the Lord standing on the altar: and he said, Strike the mercy-seat, and the porch shall be shaken: and cut through into the heads of all; and I will kill the remnant of them with the sword: no one of them fleeing shall escape, and no one of them, striving to save himself shall be delivered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Though they hid themselves in hell, thence shall my hand drag them forth; and though they go up to heaven, thence will I bring them down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, thence will I search [them] out and take them; and if they should go down from my presence into the depths of the sea, there will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if they should go into captivity before the face of their enemies, there will I command the sword, and it shall kill them: and I will set my eyes against them for evil, and not for good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord, the Lord God Almighty, [is he] that takes hold of the land, and causes it to shake, and all that inhabit it shall mourn; and its destruction shall go up as a river, and shall descend as the river of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} [It is he] that builds his ascent up to the sky, and establishes his promise on the earth; who calls the water of the sea, and pours it out on the face of the earth; the Lord Almighty is his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Are not you⌃ to me as the sons of the Ethiopians, O children of Israel? says the Lord. Did I not bring Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Cappadocia, and the Syrians out of the deep? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of sinners, and I will cut it off from the face of the earth; only I will not utterly cut off the house of Jacob, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For I [will] give commandment, and sift the house of Israel among all the Gentiles, as [corn] is sifted in a sieve, and [yet] a fragment shall not in any wise fall upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say, Calamities shall certainly not draw near, nor come upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and will rebuild the ruins of it, and will set up the parts thereof that have been broken down, and will build it up as in the ancient days: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} that the remnant of men, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, may earnestly seek [me], says the Lord who does all these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Behold, the days come, says the Lord, when the harvest shall overtake the vintage, and the grapes shall ripen at seed time; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall be planted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will turn the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall rebuild the ruined cities, and shall inhabit [them]; and they shall plant vineyards, and shall drink the wine from them; and they shall form gardens, and eat the fruit of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I will plant them on their land, and they shall no more be plucked up from the land which I have given them, says the Lord God Almighty.\par

\section*{Obadiah Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Obadiah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book names Obadiah; the exact historical setting is debated, but conservative scholarship receives the named prophet as genuine.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the writer, but the prophecy stands in the canonical witness against Edom and for Zion.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} date debated\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} often 9th or 6th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} MT preserves the short oracle against Edom and promise of Zion's kingdom.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} The LXX preserves the same message with ordinary versional differences.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Oracle against Edom for violence against Jacob and promise of Zion's triumph.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} To announce the LORD's judgment on proud Edom and vindication of His covenant people.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} judgment on Edom; pride; Zion; kingdom of the LORD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Edom's downfall 1-14; Day of the LORD and Zion's triumph 15-21. Qumran Obadiah fragments survive | Subst. Second Temple period Early Hebrew witness is fragmentary | Heb. Second Temple period Leningrad Codex | Gk. AD 1008 Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Obadiah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} 4th-5th century AD by Use in later Jewish interpretation (Multiple)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Second Temple and later\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Obadiah's brevity makes each textual variant proportionally weighty in interpretation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Obadiah}
\markboth{OBADIAH}{}
\subsection*{Obadiah 1}
\markright{OBADIAH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The vision of Obdias. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea; I have heard a report from the Lord, and he has sent forth a message to the nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Arise you⌃, and let us rise up against her to war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, I have made you small among the Gentiles: you are greatly dishonored. The pride of your heart has elated you, dwelling [as you do] in the holes of the rocks, [as one that] exalts his habitation, saying in his heart, Who will bring me down to the ground? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} If you should mount up as the eagle, and if you should make your nest among the stars, thence will I bring you down, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? would they not have stolen [just] enough for themselves? and if grape gatherers went in to you, would they not leave a gleaning? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} How has Esau been searched out, and [how] have his hidden things been detected? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} They sent you to your coasts: all the men of your covenant have withstood you; your allies have prevailed against you, they have set snares under you: they have no understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise men out of Idumea, and understanding out of the mount of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And your warriors from Thaeman shall be dismayed, to the end that man may be cut off from the mount of Esau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Because of the slaughter and the sin [committed against] your brother Jacob, shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} From the day that you stood in opposition [to him], in the days when foreigners were taking captive his forces, and strangers entered into his gates, and cast lots on Jerusalem, you also was as one of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And you should not have looked on the day of your brother in the day of strangers; nor should you have rejoiced against the children of Juda in the day of their destruction; neither should you have boasted in the day of [their] affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither should you have gone into the gates of the people in the day of their troubles; nor yet should you have looked upon their gathering in the day of their destruction, nor should you have attacked their host in the day of their perishing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Neither should you have stood at the opening of their passages, to destroy utterly those of them that were escaping; neither should you have shut up his fugitives in the day of affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For the day of the Lord is near upon all the Gentiles: as you have done, so shall it be [done] to you: your recompense shall be returned on your [own] head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For as you have drunk upon my holy mountain, [so] shall all the nations drink wine; they shall drink, and go down, and be as if they were not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But on mount Sion there shall be deliverance, and there shall be a sanctuary; and the house of Jacob shall take for an inheritance those that took them for an inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the house of Jacob shall be fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau [shall be] for stubble; and [Israel] shall flame forth against them, and shall devour them, and there shall not be a corn-field [left] to the house of Esau; because the Lord has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they [that dwell] in the south shall inherit the mount of Esau, and they in the plain the Philistines: and they shall inherit the mount of Ephraim, and the plain of Samaria, and Benjamin, and the land of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And this [shall be] the domain of the captivity of the children of Israel, the land of the Chananites as far as Sarepta; and the captives of Jerusalem [shall inherit] as far as Ephratha; they shall inherit the cities of the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they that escape shall come up from mount Sion, to take vengeance on the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord's.\par

\section*{Jonah Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Jonah son of Amittai\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book's prophetic identity matches 2 Kings 14:25, and conservative scholarship receives Jonah as historical.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Jesus explicitly treats Jonah and the fish as historical in Matthew 12:39-41.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 8th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Jonah in the era of Jeroboam II and Assyrian significance.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same narrative with some wording differences but the same historical claim.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Narrative of a prophet sent to Nineveh who fled, was chastened, and preached repentance.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To show the LORD's sovereign mercy to sinners, including Gentiles, and to expose the narrowness of the prophet's heart.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} mercy; repentance; Gentiles; prophet; sovereignty; sign of Jonah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Flight and storm 1; Fish and prayer 2; Nineveh's repentance 3; Jonah's complaint and God's lesson 4.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Jonah fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Early Hebrew witness is fragmentary Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Jonah 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Explicit appeal by Jesus by Jesus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Jonah's historicity is reinforced by Christ's own use of Jonah as a sign; textual differences are secondary to that anchor.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Jonah as historical prophetic narrative because Christ did.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Jonah}
\markboth{JONAH}{}
\subsection*{Jonah 1}
\markright{JONAH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now the word of the Lord came to Jonas the son of Amathi, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Rise, and go to Nineve, the great city, and preach in it; for the cry of its wickedness is come up to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But Jonas rose up to flee to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord. And he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tharsis: and he paid his fare, and went up into it, to sail with them to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord raised up a wind on the sea; and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship was in danger of being broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the sailors were alarmed, and cried every one to his god, and cast out the wares that were in the ship into the sea, that it might be lightened of them. But Jonas was gone down into the hold of the ship, and was asleep, and snored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the shipmaster came to him, and said to him, Why snore you? arise, and call upon your God, that God may save us, and we perish not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And each man said to his neighbor, Come, let us cast lots, and find out for whose sake this mischief is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And they said to him, Tell us what is your occupation, and whence come you, and of what country and what people are you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said to them, I am a servant of the Lord; and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea, and the dry [land]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then the men feared exceedingly, and said to him, What is this [that] you have done? for the men knew that he was fleeing from the face of the Lord, because he had told them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they said to him, What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us? for the sea rose, and lifted its wave exceedingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Jonas said to them, Take me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm to you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the men tried hard to return to the land, and were not able: for the sea rose and grew more and more tempestuous against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they cried to the Lord, and said, Forbid it, Lord: let us not perish for the sake of this man's life, and bring not righteous blood upon us: for you, Lord, have done as you would. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So they took Jonas, and cast him out into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the men feared the Lord very greatly, and offered a sacrifice to the Lord, and vowed vows.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} to flee; from; Joppa; Tarshish As Jonah embarked at Joppa, a seaport on the Mediterranean, it was probably either Tarsus in Cilicia, or rather Tartessus in Spain, to which he intended to flee. When we reflect how such a message would be received in the streets of London at this day, we shall not wonder at the prophet's reluctance to announce the destruction of the proud and idolatrous Nineveh. \textsuperscript{4} the Lord, ; sent out Heb. cast forth like Heb. thought \textsuperscript{5} cried, ; and cast; the sides and was \textsuperscript{7} every; and let; for, ; and the \textsuperscript{9} I am; and I, ; the Lord or, Jehovah the God, ; which \textsuperscript{10} were exceedingly afraid Heb. afraid, with great fear, Why; he fled \textsuperscript{11} What; calm unto us Heb. silent from us. wrought, and was tempestuous. or, grew more and more tempestuous. \subsection*{Jonah 2}
\markright{JONAH 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now the Lord had commanded a great whale to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Jonas prayed to the Lord his God out of the belly of the whale, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and said, I cried in my affliction to the Lord my God, and he listened to me, [even] to my cry out of the belly of hell: you heard my voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You did cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and the floods compassed me: all your billows and your waves have passed upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I said, I am cast out of your presence: shall I indeed look again toward your holy temple? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Water was poured around me to the soul: the lowest deep compassed me, my head went down {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} to the clefts of the mountains; I went down into the earth, whose bars are the everlasting barriers: yet, O Lord my God, let my ruined life be restored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} When my soul was failing me, I remembered the Lord; and may my prayer come to you into your holy temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They that observe vanities and lies have forsaken their own mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of praise and thanksgiving: all that I have vowed I will pay to you, the Lord of [my] salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the whale was commanded by the Lord, and it cast up Jonas on the dry [land].\par

\subsection*{Jonah 3}
\markright{JONAH 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the word of the Lord came to Jonas the second time, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Rise, go to Nineve, the great city, and preach in it according to the former preaching which I spoke to you of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jonas arose, and went to Nineve, as the Lord had spoken. Now Nineve was an exceeding great city, of about three days' journey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jonas began to enter into the city about a day's journey, and he proclaimed, and said, Yet three days, and Nineve shall be overthrown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the men of Nineve believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloths, from the greatest of them to the least of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the word reached the king of Nineve, and he arose from off his throne, and took off his raiment from him, and put on sackcloth, and sat on ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And proclamation was made, and it was commanded in Nineve by the king an by his great men, saying, Let not men, or cattle, or oxen, or sheep, taste [any thing], nor feed, nor drink water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So men and cattle were clothed with sackcloths, and cried earnestly to God; and they turned every one from their evil way, and from the iniquity that was in their hands, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who knows if God will repent, and turn from his fierce anger, and [so] we shall not perish? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil ways; and God repented of the evil which he had said he would do to them; and he did [it] not.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, was situated on the eastern bank of the river Tigris, opposite the present Mosul, about 280 miles north of Babylon, 400 ne of Damascus, in latitude 36 degrees 20 minutes n longitude 73 degrees 10 minutes e. It was not only a very ancient ( ), but also a very great city. Strabo says that it was much larger than Babylon, the circuit of which he estimates at 385 furlongs; and, according to Diodorus Siculus, it was an oblong parallelogram, extending 150 furlongs in length, 90 in breadth, and 480 in circumference, i.e., about 20 miles long, 12 broad, and 60 in compass. This agrees with the account given here of its being "an exceeding great city of three days' journey, " i.e., in circuit; for 20 miles a day was the common computation for a pedestrian. It was surrounded by large walls 100 feet high, so broad that three chariots could drive abreast on them, and defended by 1, 500 towers 200 feet in height. \subsection*{Jonah 4}
\markright{JONAH 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Jonas was very deeply grieved, and he was confounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he prayed to the Lord, and said, O Lord, were not these my words when I was yet in my land? therefore I made haste to flee to Tharsis; because I knew that you are merciful and compassionate, longsuffering, and abundant in kindness, and repent of evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And now, Lord God, take my life from me; for [it is] better for me to die than to live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord said to Jonas, Are you very much grieved? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Jonas went out from the city, and sat over against the city; and he made for himself there a booth, and he sat under it, until he should perceive what would become of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Lord God commanded a gourd, and it came up over the head of Jonas, to be a shadow over his head, to shade him from his calamities: and Jonas rejoiced with great joy for the gourd. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And God commanded a worm the next morning, and it struck the gourd, and it withered away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass at the rising of the sun, that God commanded a burning east wind; and the sun struck on the head of Jonas, and he fainted, and despaired of his life, and said, [It is] better for me to die than to live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And God said to Jonas, Are you very much grieved for the gourd? And he said, I am very much grieved, even to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the Lord said, You had pity on the gourd, for which you have not suffered, neither did you rear it; which came up before night, and perished before [another] night: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and shall not I spare Nineve, the great city, in which dwell more than twelve myriads of human beings, who do not know their right hand or their left hand; and [also] much cattle?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} he prayed; I fled; thou art;, ; and of \textsuperscript{4} Doest thou well to be angry or, Art thou greatly angry \textsuperscript{6} the Lord; gourd or, palmcrist, Heb. \section*{Micah Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Micah\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book names Micah of Moresheth and is received as his prophecy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Matthew 2:5-6 cites Micah 5; Jeremiah 26:18 cites Micah 3:12 by name.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 8th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Micah alongside Isaiah in Judah during the Assyrian crisis.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same setting and provides an important witness for NT quotation points.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Judah-focused prophecy of judgment and restoration in the 8th century BC.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To confront sin in leaders and people while announcing Bethlehem's ruler and the LORD's final restoration.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} judgment; remnant; Bethlehem ruler; justice; mercy; restoration\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Judgment cycles 1-3; Hope and ruler from Bethlehem 4-5; Covenant lawsuit and final hope 6-7.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Micah fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Early Hebrew witness is fragmentary Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Micah 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Named citation in Jeremiah and NT use in Matthew by Jeremiah and Matthew (7th century BC and 1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Micah matters for messianic quotation study, especially Micah 5 in Matthew 2.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Micah as the named prophet and reads Micah 6:8 and 5:2 in the full canonical-messianic frame.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Micah}
\markboth{MICAH}{}
\subsection*{Micah 1}
\markright{MICAH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And the word of the Lord came to Michaeas the son of Morasthi, in the days of Joatham, and Achaz, and Ezekias, kings of Juda, concerning what he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear [these] words, you⌃ people; and let the earth give heed, and all that are in it: and the Lord God shall be among you for a testimony, the Lord out of his holy habitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For, behold, the Lord comes forth out of his place, and will come down, and will go upon the high places of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the mountains shall be shaken under him, and the valleys shall melt like wax before the fire, and as water rushing down a declivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} All these [calamities are] for the transgression of Jacob, and for the sin of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? [is it] not Samaria? and what is the sin of the house of Juda? [is it] not Jerusalem? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore I will make Samaria [as] a store-house of the fruits of the field, and [as] a planting of a vineyard: and I will utterly demolish her stones, and I will expose her foundations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they shall cut in pieces all the graven images, and all that she has hired they shall burn with fire, and I will utterly destroy all her idols: because she has gathered of the hires of fornication, and of the hires of fornication has she amassed [wealth]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Therefore shall she lament and wail, she shall go barefooted, and [being] naked she shall make lamentation as [that] of serpents, and mourning as of the daughters of sirens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For her plague has become grievous; for it has come even to Juda; and has reached to the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} You⌃ that are in Geth, exalt not yourselves, and you⌃ Enakim, do not rebuild from [the ruins of] the house in derision: sprinkle dust [in the place of] your laughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The inhabitant of Sennaar, fairly inhabiting her cities, came not forth to mourn for the house next to her: she shall receive of you the stroke of grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Who has begun [to act] for good to her that dwells in sorrow? for calamities have come down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [even] a sound of chariots and horsemen: the inhabitants of Lachis, she is the leader of sin to the daughter of Sion: for in you were found the transgressions of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Therefore shall he cause men to be sent forth as far as the inheritance of Geth, [even] vain houses; they are become vanity to the kings of Israel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} until they bring the heirs, O inhabitant of Lachis: the inheritance shall reach to Odollam, [even] the glory of the daughter of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Shave your hair, and make yourself bald for your delicate children; increase your widowhood as an eagle; for [your people] are gone into captivity from you.\par

\subsection*{Micah 2}
\markright{MICAH 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} They meditated troubles, and wrought wickedness on their beds, and they put it in execution with the daylight; for they have not lifted up their hands to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they desired fields, and plundered orphans, and oppressed families, and spoiled a man and his house, even a man and his inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore thus says the Lord; Behold, I devise evils against this family, out of which you⌃ shall not lift up your necks, neither shall you⌃ walk upright speedily: for the time is evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In that day shall a parable be taken up against you, and a plaintive lamentation shall be uttered, saying, We are thoroughly miserable: the portion of my people has been measured out with a line, and there was none to hinder him so as to turn him back; your fields have been divided. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Therefore you shall have no one to cast a line for the lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Weep not with tears in the assembly of the Lord, neither let [any] weep for these things; for he shall not remove the reproaches, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} who says, The house of Jacob has provoked the Spirit of the Lord; are not these his practices? Are not the Lord's words right with him? and have they not proceeded correctly? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Even beforetime my people withstood [him] as an enemy against his peace; they have stripped off his skin to remove hope [in] the conflict of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The leaders of my people shall be cast forth from their luxurious houses; they are rejected because of their evil practices; draw you⌃ near to the everlasting mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Arise you, and depart; for this is not your rest because of uncleanness: you⌃ have been utterly destroyed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} you⌃ have fled, no one pursuing [you: your] spirit has framed falsehood, it has dropped on you for wine and strong drink. But it shall come to pass, [that] out of the dropping of this people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Jacob shall be completely gathered with all [his people:] I will surely receive the remnant of Israel; I will cause them to return together, as sheep in trouble, as a flock in the midst of their fold: they shall rush forth from among men through the breach made before them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} they have broken through, and passed the gate, and gone out by it: and their king has gone out before them, and the Lord shall lead them.\par

\subsection*{Micah 3}
\markright{MICAH 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he shall say, Hear now these words, you⌃ heads of the house of Jacob, and you⌃ remnant of the house of Israel; is it not for you to know judgment? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} [who] hate good, and seek evil; [who] tear their skins off them, and their flesh off their bones: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} even as they devoured the flesh of my people, and stripped their skins off them, and broke their bones, and divided [them] as flesh for the caldron, and as meat for the pot, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} thus they shall cry to the Lord, but he shall not listen to them; and he shall turn away his face from them at that time, because they have done wickedly in their practices against themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets that lead my people astray, that bit with their teeth, and proclaim peace to them; and [when] nothing was put into their mouth, they raised up war against them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} therefore there shall be night to you instead of a vision, and there shall be to you darkness instead of prophecy; and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall be dark upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the seers of night-visions shall be ashamed, and the prophets shall be laughed to scorn: and all the people shall speak against them, because there shall be none to listen to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Surely I will strengthen myself with the Spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of power, to declare to Jacob his transgressions, and to Israel his sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Hear now these words, you⌃ chiefs of the house of Jacob, and the remnant of the house of Israel, who hate judgment, and pervert all righteousness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} who build up Sion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The heads thereof have judged for gifts, and the priests thereof have answered for hire, and her prophets have divined for silver: and [yet] they have rested on the Lord, saying, Is not the Lord among us? no evil shall come upon us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore on your account Sion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a storehouse of fruits, and the mountain of the house as a grove of the forest.\par

\subsection*{Micah 4}
\markright{MICAH 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And at the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, established on the tops of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and the peoples shall hasten to it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And many nations shall go, and say, Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and they shall show us his way, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Sion shall go forth a law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he shall judge among many peoples, and shall rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles; and nation shall no more lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn to war any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And every one shall rest under his vine, and every one under his fig tree; and there shall be none to alarm [them]: for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these [words]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For all [other] nations shall walk everyone in his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In that day, says the Lord, I will gather her that is bruised, and will receive her that is cast out, and those whom I rejected. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I will make her that was bruised a remnant, and her that was rejected a mighty nation: and the Lord shall reign over them in mount Sion from henceforth, even for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you, dark tower of the flock, daughter of Sion, on you the dominion shall come and enter in, [even] the first kingdom from Babylon to the daughter of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now, why have you known calamities? was there not a king to you? or has your counsel perished that pangs as of a woman in travail have seized upon you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Be in pain, and strengthen yourself, and draw near, O daughter of Sion, as a woman in travail: for now you shall go forth out of the city, and shall lodge in the plain, and shall reach even to Babylon: thence shall the Lord your God deliver you, and thence shall he redeem you out of the hand of your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now have many nations gathered against you, saying, We will rejoice, and our eyes shall look upon Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But they know not the thought of the Lord, and have not understood his counsel: for he has gathered them as sheaves of the floor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Arise, and thresh them, O daughter of Sion: for I will make your horns iron, and I will make your hoofs brass: and you shall utterly destroy many nations, and shall consecrate their abundance to the Lord, and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.\par

\subsection*{Micah 5}
\markright{MICAH 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now shall the daughter [of Sion] be completely hedged in: he has laid siege against us: they shall strike the tribes of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And you, Bethleem, house of Ephratha, are few in number to be [reckoned] among the thousands of Juda; [yet] out of you shall one come forth to me, to be a ruler of Israel; and his goings forth were from the beginning, [even] from eternity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore shall he appoint them [to wait] till the time of her that travails: she shall bring forth, and [then] the remnant of their brethren shall return to the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the Lord shall stand, and see, and feed his flock with power, and they shall dwell in the glory of the name of the Lord their God: for now shall they be magnified to the ends of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And she shall have peace when Assur shall come into your land, and when he shall come up upon your country; and there shall be raised up against him seven shepherds, and eight attacks of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they shall tend the Assyrian with a sword, and the land of Nebrod with her trench: and he shall deliver [you] from the Assyrian, when he shall come upon your land, and when he shall invade your coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many peoples, as dew falling from the Lord, and as lambs on the grass; that none may assemble nor resist among the sons of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many nations, as a lion in the forest among cattle, and as a [lion's] whelp among the flocks of sheep, even as when he goes through, and selects, and carries off [his prey], and there is none to deliver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Your hand shall be lifted up against them that afflict you, and all your enemies shall be utterly destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, [that] I will utterly destroy the horses out of the midst of you, and destroy your chariots; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} and I will utterly destroy the cities of your land, and demolish all your strongholds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} and I will utterly destroy your sorceries out of your hands; and there shall be no soothsayers in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And I will utterly destroy your graven images, and your statues out of the midst of you; and you shall never any more worship the works of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I will cut off the groves out of the midst of you, and I will abolish your cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} and I will execute vengeance on the heathen in anger and wrath, because they listened not.\par

\subsection*{Micah 6}
\markright{MICAH 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Hear now a word: the Lord God has said; Arise, plead with the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear you⌃, O mountains, the controversy of the Lord, and [you⌃] valleys [even] the foundations of the earth: for the Lord [has] a controversy with his people, and will plead with Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} O my people, what have I done to you? or wherein have I grieved you? or wherein have I troubled you? answer me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For I brought tee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, and sent before you Moses, and Aaron, and Mariam. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O my people, remember now, what counsel Balac king of Moab took against you, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, from the reeds to Galgal; that the righteousness of the Lord might be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Wherewithal shall I reach the Lord, [and] lay hold of my God most high? shall I reach him by whole burnt offerings, by calves of a year old? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Will the Lord accept thousands of rams, or ten thousands of fat goats? should I give my firstborn for ungodliness, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Has it [not] been told you, O man, what [is] good? or what does the Lord require of you, but to do justice, and love mercy, and be ready to walk with the Lord your God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The Lord's voice shall be proclaimed in the city, and he shall save those that fear his name: hear, O tribe; and who shall order the city? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [Is there] not fire, and the house of the wicked heaping up wicked treasures, and [that] with the pride of unrighteousness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Shall the wicked be justified by the balanced, or deceitful weights in the bag, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} whereby they have accumulated their ungodly wealth, and they that dwell in the city have uttered falsehoods, and their tongue has been exalted in their mouth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore will I begin to strike you; I will destroy you in your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You shall eat, and shall not be satisfied; and there shall be darkness upon you; and he shall depart from [you], and you shall not escape; and all that shall escape shall be delivered over to the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} You shall sow, but you shall not reap; you shall press the olive, but you shall not anoint yourself with oil; and [shall make] wine, but you⌃ shall drink no wine: and the ordinances of my people shall be utterly abolished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For you have kept the statues of Zambri, and [done] all the works of the house of Achaab; and you⌃ have walked in their ways, that I might deliver you to utter destruction, and those that inhabit the city to hissing: and you⌃ shall bear the reproach of nations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} ye; Arise The manner of raising attention, says Abp. Newcome, in, by calling a man to urge his plea in the face of all nature, and on the inanimate creation to hear the expostulation of Jehovah with his people, is truly awakening and magnificent. The words of Jehovah follow in; and God's mercies having been set before the people, one of them is introduced in a beautiful manner, asking what his duty is towards so gracious a God, . The answer follows in the words of the prophet, . contend; before or, with; let \textsuperscript{3} O my;, what, wherein testify \textsuperscript{4} I brought, ;, ; and redeemed, ; Moses \textsuperscript{5} remember, ; Balak Num. 22:1-25:18; Balaam; Shittim, ;, know *marg. \textsuperscript{6} Wherewith; bow; the high;, ; with; of a year old Heb. sons of a year \textsuperscript{7} pleased; rivers shall;, ; body Heb. belly \textsuperscript{8} O man; what is; and what to do; love, ; walk humbly Heb. humble thyself to walk \textsuperscript{9} Lord's;, ; and; the man of wisdom shall see thy name or, thy name shall see that which is wisdom; hear \textsuperscript{10} Are etc. or, Is there yet unto every man an house of the wicked, etc the treasures; and; scant measure Heb. measure of leanness \textsuperscript{11} count them pure or, be pure the wicked the bag \textsuperscript{16} the statutes of Omri are kept or, he doth much keep the, etc.; the works, ; ye walk; that; desolation or, astonishment therefore\par}

\subsection*{Micah 7}
\markright{MICAH 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Alas for me! for I am become as one gathering straw in harvest, and as [one gathering] grape-gleanings in the vintage, when there is no cluster for me to eat the first-ripe fruit: alas my soul! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the godly is perished from the earth; and there is none among men that orders [his way] aright: they all quarrel even to blood: they grievously afflict every one his neighbor: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} they prepare their hands for mischief, the prince asks [a reward], and the judge speaks flattering words; it is the desire of their soul: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} therefore I will take away their goods as a devouring moth, and as one who acts by a [rigid] rule in a day of visitation. Woe, woe, your times of vengeance are come; now shall be their lamentations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Trust not in friends, and confide not in guides: beware of your wife, so as not to commit anything to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the son dishonors his father, the daughter will rise up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law: those in his house [shall be] all a man's enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But I will look to the Lord; I will wait upon God my Saviour: my God will listen to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Rejoice not against me, my enemy; for I have fallen [yet] shall arise; for though I should sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he make good my cause: he also shall maintain my right, and shall bring me out to the light, [and] I shall behold his righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And she that is my enemy shall see it, and shall clothe herself with shame, who says, Where [is] the Lord your God? my eyes shall look upon her: now shall she be for trampling as mire in the ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} [It is] the day of making of brick; that day shall be your utter destruction, and that day shall utterly abolish your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And your cities shall be levelled, and parted among the Assyrians; and your strong cities shall be parted from Tyre to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the land shall be utterly desolate together with them that inhabit it, because of the fruit of their doings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Tend your people with your rod, the sheep of your inheritance, those that inhabit by themselves the thicket in the midst of Carmel: they shall feed in the land of Basan, and in the land of Galaad, as in the days of old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And according to the days of your departure out of Egypt shall you⌃ see marvelous [things]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The nations shall see and be ashamed; and at all their might they shall lay their hands upon their mouth, their ears shall be deafened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They shall lick the dust as serpents crawling on the earth, they shall be confounded in their holes; they shall be amazed at the Lord our God, and will be afraid of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Who is a God like you, cancelling iniquities, and passing over the sins of the remnant of his inheritance? and he has not kept his anger for a testimony, for he delights in mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He will return and have mercy upon us; he will sink our iniquities, and they shall be cast into the depth of the sea, [even] all our sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He shall give blessings truly to Jacob, and mercy to Abraam, as you swore to our fathers, according to the former days.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} woe;, when they have gathered the summer fruits Heb. the gatherings of summer as, desired \textsuperscript{2} good or, godly, or, merciful is perished; they all; hunt \textsuperscript{3} do; the prince; the great his mischievous desire Heb. the mischief of his soul wrap \textsuperscript{4} is a; the day; thy; now \textsuperscript{7} I will look, ; wait;, ; my God \textsuperscript{8} Rejoice;, ; when I fall; when I sit; the Lord \textsuperscript{10} Then etc. or, And thou wilt see her that is mine enemy, and cover her with shame she that; Nahum 2:1-3:19; shame; Where, ; mine; now; trodden down Heb. for a treading down \textsuperscript{12} also, ; and from or, even to, This verse may be rendered, "In that day they (people) shall come to thee from Assyria and the fenced cities; and from the fortress (probably Pelusium at the entrance of Egypt), even to the river (Euphrates), " etc. The expressions employed in this prophecy appear to be too strong for the events which transpired after the Babylonian captivity; and seem to refer to the future restoration of Israel, after their land has lain desolate for ages. \textsuperscript{13} Not withstanding the land shall be, or, After that the land hath been; for \textsuperscript{14} Feed or, Rule, *marg., ; *marg. which; in the midst, ; as \textsuperscript{17} lick; move; worms or, creeping things they shall be \textsuperscript{18} a God; , ;, that; , ; passeth; the remnant, ; he retaineth, ; he delighteth\par}

\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Nahum\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book names Nahum the Elkoshite and is received as his prophecy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the writer, but Nahum's oracle against Nineveh stands in the prophetic canon as genuine revelation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 7th century BC before Nineveh's fall in 612 BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Nahum in the late Assyrian period after Thebes and before Nineveh's fall.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same Assyrian setting with normal versional variation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Oracle announcing Nineveh's downfall and comfort for Judah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To proclaim the LORD's justice against oppressive empire and comfort for His people.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} judgment; justice; Nineveh; comfort; divine vengeance\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} The LORD's majesty 1; Nineveh's siege and fall 2-3.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Nahum pesher and fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. The Nahum pesher provides important early reception evidence alongside Hebrew fragments Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Nahum 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Qumran Nahum Pesher by Community at Qumran (1st century BC)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Nahum is notable not only for text but also for early interpretive reception in the pesher tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Nahum as a true historical oracle of judgment and comfort, not merely anti-Assyrian rhetoric.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{Nahum 1}
\markright{NAHUM 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The burden of Nineve: the book of the vision of Naum the Elkesite. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} God is jealous, and the Lord avenges; the Lord avenges with wrath; the Lord takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he cuts off his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The Lord is longsuffering, and his power is great, and the Lord will not hold any guiltless: his way is in destruction and in the whirlwind, and the clouds are the dust of his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He threatens the sea, and dries it up, and exhausts all the rivers: the land of Basan, and Carmel are brought low, and the flourishing [trees] of Libanus have come to nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The mountains quake at him, and the hills are shaken, and the earth recoils at his presence, [even] the world, and all that dwell in it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who shall stand before his anger? and who shall withstand in the anger of his wrath? his wrath brings to nothing kingdoms, and the rocks are burst asunder by him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The Lord is good to them that wait on him in the day of affliction; and he knows them that reverence him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end: darkness shall pursue those that rise up against [him] and his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} What do you⌃ devise against the Lord? he will make a complete end: he will not take vengeance by affliction twice at the same time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For [the enemy] shall be laid bare even to the foundation, and shall be devoured as twisted yew, and as stubble fully dry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Out of you shall proceed a device against the Lord, counselling evil things hostile [to him]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Thus says the Lord who rules over many waters, Even thus shall they be sent away, and the report of you shall not be heard any more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And now will I break his rod from off you, and will burst [your] bonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the Lord shall give a command concerning you; there shall no more of your name be scattered: I will utterly destroy the graven [images] out of the house of your god, and the molten [images]: I will make your grave; for [they are] swift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that brings glad tidings, and publishes peace! \subsection*{Nahum 2}
\markright{NAHUM 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} It is all over with him, he has been removed, [one] who has been delivered from affliction has come up panting into your presence, watch the way, strengthen [your] loins, be very valiant in [your] strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the Lord has turned aside the pride of Jacob, as the pride of Israel: for they have utterly rejected them, and have destroyed their branches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [They have destroyed] the arms of their power from among men, their mighty men sporting with fire: the reins of their chariots [shall be destroyed] in the day of his preparation, and the horsemen shall be thrown into confusion {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} in the ways, and the chariots shall clash together, and shall be entangled in each other in the broad ways: their appearance is as lamps of fire, and as gleaming lightnings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And their mighty men shall bethink themselves and flee by day; and they shall be weak as they go; and they shall hasten to her walls, and shall prepare their defences. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The gates of the cities have been opened, and the palaces have fallen into ruin, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and the foundation has been exposed; and she has gone up, and her maidservants were led [away] as doves moaning in their hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And [as for] Nineve, her waters [shall be] as a pool of water: and they fled, and staid not, and there was none to look back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They plundered the silver, they plundered the gold, and there was no end of their adorning; they were loaded [with it] upon all their pleasant vessels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} [There is] thrusting forth, and shaking, and tumult, and heart-breaking, and loosing of knees, and pangs on all loins; \markright{NAHUM 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O city of blood, wholly false, full of unrighteousness; the prey shall not be handled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The noise of whips, and the noise of the rumbling of wheels, and of the pursuing horse, and of the bounding chariot, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and of the mounting rider, and of the glittering sword, and of the gleaming arms, and of a multitude of slain, and of heavy falling: and there was no end to her nations, but they shall be weak in their bodies {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} because of the abundance of fornication: [she is] a fair harlot, and well-favoured, skilled in sorcery, that sells the nations by her fornication, and peoples by her sorceries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Behold, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty, and I will uncover your skirts in your presence, and I will show the nations your shame, and the kingdoms your disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will cast abominable filth upon you according to your unclean ways, and will make you a public example. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And it shall be [that] every one that sees you shall go down from you, and shall say, Wretched Nineve! who shall lament for her? whence shall I seek comfort for her? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Prepare you a portion, tune the chord, prepare a portion for Ammon: she that dwells among the rivers, water is round about her, whose dominion is the sea, and whose walls are water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Ethiopia is her strength, and Egypt; and there was no limit of the flight [of her enemies]; and the Libyans became her helpers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Yet she shall go as a prisoner into captivity, and they shall dash her infants against the ground at the top of all her ways: and they shall cast lots upon all her glorious [possessions], and all her nobles shall be bound in chains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And you shall be drunken, and shall be overlooked; and you shall seek for yourself strength because of [your] enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} All your strongholds are as fig-trees having watchers: if they be shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Behold, your people within you are as women: the gates of your land shall surely be opened to your enemies: the fire shall devour your bars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Draw you water for a siege, and well secure your strongholds: enter into the clay, and be you trodden in the chaff, make [the fortifications] stronger than brick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} There the fire shall devour you; the sword shall utterly destroy you, it shall devour you as the locust, and you shall be pressed down as a palmerworm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} You have multiplied your merchandise beyond the stars of heaven: the palmerworm has attacked [it], and has flown away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Your mixed [multitude] has suddenly departed as the grasshopper, as the locust perched on a hedge in a frosty day; your wound has rankled: all that hear the report of you shall clap their hands against you; for upon whom has not your wickedness passed continually?\par

\section*{Habakkuk Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Habakkuk\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book names Habakkuk and is received as his prophetic dialogue and prayer.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11, and Hebrews 10:38 quote Habakkuk 2:4.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} late 7th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Habakkuk on the eve of Babylonian judgment.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same setting and is crucial at Habakkuk 2:4 and other quotation points.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Dialogue of a prophet wrestling with violence, Babylon, and the righteous life of faith.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To answer the problem of unchecked evil by revealing God's sovereign justice and calling the righteous to live by faith.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} faith; judgment; Babylon; theodicy; waiting; worship\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Dialogue 1-2; Prayer and hymn 3.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Habakkuk Pesher and fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. The Habakkuk Pesher is a major early witness to reception, alongside Hebrew fragments Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Habakkuk 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Explicit NT quotation and Qumran pesher by Paul and the Qumran community (1st century AD and earlier)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Habakkuk is major for NT theology because Habakkuk 2:4 is cited repeatedly, and MT/LXX wording affects doctrinal emphasis.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Habakkuk as the named prophet and sees the faith text as central to biblical theology without detaching it from its historical context.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Habakkuk}
\markboth{HABAKKUK}{}
\subsection*{Habakkuk 1}
\markright{HABAKKUK 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The burden which the prophet Ambacum saw. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and you will not listen? [how long] shall I cry out to you being injured, and you will not save? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore have you shown me troubles and griefs to look upon, misery and ungodliness? judgment is before me, and the judge receives a reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore the law is frustrated, and judgment proceeds not effectually, for the ungodly [man] prevails over the just; therefore perverse judgment will proceed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Behold, you⌃ despisers, and look, and wonder marvelously, and vanish: for I work a work in your days, which you⌃ will in no wise believe, though a man declare [it to you]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore, behold, I stir up the Chaldeans, the bitter and hasty nation, that walks upon the breadth of the earth, to inherit tabernacles not his own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He is terrible and famous; his judgment shall proceed of himself, and his dignity shall come out of himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And his horses shall bound [more swiftly] than leopards, and [they are] fiercer than the wolves of Arabia: and his horsemen shall ride forth, and shall rush from far; and they shall fly as an eagle hasting to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Destruction shall come upon ungodly men, resisting with their adverse front, and he shall gather the captivity as the sand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he shall be at his ease with kings, and princes are his toys, and he shall mock at every strong-hold, and shall cast a mound, and take possession of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Then shall he change his spirit, and he shall pass through, and make an atonement, [saying], This strength [belongs] to my god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} [Are] not you from the beginning, O Lord God, my Holy One? and surely we shall not die. O Lord, you have established it for judgment, and he has formed me to chasten [with] his correction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [His] eye is too pure to behold evil [doings], and to look upon grievous afflictions: therefore do you look upon despisers? will you be silent when the ungodly swallows up the just? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And will you make men as the fishes of the sea, and as the reptiles which have no guide? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He has brought up destruction with a hook, and drawn one with a casting net, and caught another in his drags: therefore shall his heart rejoice and be glad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore will he sacrifice to his drag, and burn incense to his casting-net, because by them he has made his portion fat, and his meats choice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore will he cast his net, and will not spare to kill the nations continually.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: Habakkuk (Chavaqquq) — Embrace Embraced God in faith despite coming judgment.\par}
