\subsection*{Zacharias 11}
\markright{ZACHARIAS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Open your doors, O Libanus, and let the fire devour your cedars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Let the pine howl, because the cedar has fallen; for the mighty men have been greatly afflicted: howl, you⌃ oaks of the land of Basan; for the thickly planted forest has been torn down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} [There is] a voice of the shepherds mourning; for their greatness is brought low: a voice of roaring lions; for the pride of Jordan is brought down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Thus says the Lord Almighty, Feed the sheep of the slaughter; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} which their possessors have slain, and have not repented: and they that sold them said, Blessed be the Lord; for we have become rich: and their shepherds have suffered no sorrow for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore I will no longer have mercy upon the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord: but, behold, I will deliver up the men every one into the hand of his neighbor, and into the hand of his king; and they shall destroy the land, and I will not rescue out of their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I will tend the flock of slaughter in the land of Chanaan: and I will take for myself two rods; the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Line; and I will tend the flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I will cut off three shepherds in one month; and my soul shall grieve over them, for their souls cried out against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I said, I will not tend you: that which dies, let it die; and that which falls off, let it fall off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I will take my beautiful staff, and cast it away, that I may break my covenant which I made with all the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And it shall be broken in that day; and the Chananites, the sheep that are kept for me, shall know that it is the word of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I will say to them, If it be good in your eyes, give [me] my price, or refuse it. And they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the Lord said to me, Drop them into the furnace, and I will see if it is good [metal], as I was proved for their sakes. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them into the furnace in the house of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And I cast away [my] second rod, [even] Line, that I might break the possession between Juda and Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the Lord said to me, Take yet to you shepherd's implements belonging to an unskillful shepherd. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For, behold, I [will] raise up a shepherd against the land: he shall not visit that which is perishing, and he shall not seek that which is scattered, and he shall not heal that which is bruised, nor guide that which is whole: but he shall devour the flesh of the choice [ones], and shall dislocate the joints [of their necks]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Alas for the vain shepherds that have forsaken the sheep! the sword [shall be] upon the arms of such a one, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be completely withered, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.\par

\subsection*{Zacharias 12}
\markright{ZACHARIAS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The burden of the word of the Lord for Israel; says the Lord, that stretches out the sky, and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, I [will] make Jerusalem as trembling door-posts to all the nations round about, and in Judea there shall be a siege against Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it shall come to pass in that day [that] I will make Jerusalem a trodden stone to all the nations: every one that tramples on it shall utterly mock at [it], and all the nations of the earth shall be gathered together against it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will strike every horse with amazement, and his rider with madness: but I will open my eyes upon the house of Juda, and I will strike all the horses of the nations with blindness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the captains of thousands of Juda shall say in their hearts, We shall find for ourselves the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the Lord Almighty their God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In that day I will make the captains of thousands of Juda as a firebrand among wood, and as a torch of fire in stubble; and they shall devour on the right hand and on the left all the nations round about: and Jerusalem shall dwell again by herself, [even] in Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And the Lord shall save the tabernacles of Juda as at the beginning, that the boast of the house of David, and the pride of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, may not magnify themselves against Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] the Lord shall defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the weak one among them in that day shall be as David, and the house of David as the house of God, as the angel of the Lord before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and compassion: and they shall look upon me, because they have mocked [me], and they shall make lamentation for him, as for a beloved [friend], and they shall grieve intensely, as for a firstborn [son]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In that day the lamentation in Jerusalem shall be very great, as the mourning for the pomegranate grove cut down in the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the land shall lament in separate families, the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} the family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of Symeon by itself, and their wives by themselves; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} all the families that are left, each family by itself, and their wives by themselves.\par

\subsection*{Zacharias 13}
\markright{ZACHARIAS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In that day every place shall be opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for removal and for separation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord of hosts, [that] I will utterly destroy the names of the idols from off the land, and there shall be no longer [any] remembrance of them: and I will cut off the false prophets and the evil spirit from the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And it shall come to pass, if a man will yet prophesy, that his father and his mother which gave birth to him shall say to him, You shall not live; for you have spoken lies in the name of the Lord: and his father and his mother who gave him birth shall bind him as he is prophesying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision when he prophesies; and they shall clothe themselves with a garment of hair, because they have lied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And [one] shall say, I am not a prophet, for I am a tiller of the ground, for a man brought me up [thus] from my youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And I will say to him, What are these wounds between your hands? and he shall say, [Those] with which I was wounded in my beloved house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Awake, O sword, against my shepherds, and against the man [who is] my citizen, says the Lord Almighty: strike the shepherds, and draw out the sheep: and I will bring my hand upon the little ones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it shall come to pass, [that] in all the land, says the Lord, two parts thereof shall be cut off and perish; but the third shall be left therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I will bring the third [part] through the fire, and I will try them as silver is tried, and I will prove them as gold is proved: they shall call upon my name, and I will hear them, and say, This is my people: and they shall say, The Lord [is] my God.\par

\subsection*{Zacharias 14}
\markright{ZACHARIAS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold, the days of the Lord come, and your spoils shall be divided in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I will gather all the Gentiles to Jerusalem to war, and the city shall be taken, and the houses plundered, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, but the rest of my people shall not be utterly cut off from the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the Lord shall go forth, and fight with those Gentiles as when he fought in the day of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his feet shall stand in that day on the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave asunder, half of it toward the east and the west, a very great division; and half the mountain shall lean to the north, and half of it to the south. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the valley of my mountains shall be closed up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined on to Jasod, and shall be blocked up as it was blocked up in the days of the earthquake, in the days of Ozias king of Juda; and the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it shall come to pass in that day that there shall be no light, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} and there shall be for one day cold and frost, and that day [shall be] known to the Lord, and [it shall] not [be] day nor night: but towards evening it shall be light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And in that day living water shall come forth out of Jerusalem; half of it toward the former sea, and half of it toward the latter sea: and so shall it be in summer and spring. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name one, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} compassing all the earth, and the wilderness from Gabe to Remmon south of Jerusalem. And Rama shall remain in its place. From the gate of Benjamin to the place of the first gate, to the gate of the corners, and to the tower of Anameel, as far as the king's wine presses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} they shall dwell in the city; and there shall be no more any curse, and Jerusalem shall dwell securely. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And this shall be the overthrow with which the Lord will strike all the nations, as many as have fought against Jerusalem; their flesh shall consume away while they are standing upon their feet, and their eyes shall melt out of their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And there shall be in that day a great panic from the Lord upon them; and they shall lay hold every man of the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall be clasped with the hand of his neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Juda also shall fight in Jerusalem; and [God] shall gather the strength of all the nations round about, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And this shall be the overthrow of the horses, and mules, and camels, and asses, and all the beasts that are in those camps, according to this overthrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And it shall come to pass, [that] whoever shall be left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem, shall even come up every year to worship the king, the Lord Almighty, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it shall come to pass, [that] whoever of all the families of the earth shall not come up to Jerusalem to worship the king, the Lord Almighty, even these shall be added to the others. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if the family of Egypt shall not go up, nor come; then upon them shall be the overthrow with which the Lord shall strike all the nations, whichever of them shall not come up to keep the feast of tabernacles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} This shall be the sin of Egypt, and the sin of all the nations, whoever shall not come up to keep the feast of tabernacles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} In that day there shall be upon the bridle of every horse Holiness to the Lord Almighty; and the caldrons in the house of the Lord shall be as bowls before the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And every pot in Jerusalem and in Juda shall be holy to the Lord Almighty: and all that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and shall seethe [meat] in them: and in that day there shall be no more the Chananite in the house of the Lord Almighty.\par

no more; *marg.; , in the; The predictions contained in this chapter seem to relate to events which gradually extend from the death of Christ to the glorious days of the millennium - the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans, whose armies were composed of many nations, which was "the day of the Lord, " in which he came "to destroy those who would not that he should reign over them, " ( ); the subversion of the Roman empire, after being the executioners of the Divine vengeance on the Jews, by God's stirring up the barbarous nations to invade them ( ); the effusion of Divine knowledge from Jerusalem, by the promulgation of the Gospel ( ); the rebuilding and replenishing of Jerusalem ( ); the destruction of the nations who shall fight against her ( ); the conversion of the remnant of those nations to the Lord ( ); and the peace and purity of the universal church in the latter days ( ).\par}

\section*{Malachi Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Malachi\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book identifies its burden through Malachi, understood conservatively as the prophet's name or title borne by the human messenger.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No direct NT attribution names the writer, but Malachi's prophecy of the forerunner is foundational in the Gospels.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} 5th century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT chronology places Malachi in the late post-exilic period after temple restoration but before the intertestamental silence.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The LXX preserves the same post-exilic setting and the same key promises about the forerunner and day of the LORD.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Post-exilic rebuke of priestly corruption, covenant unfaithfulness, and spiritual weariness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To call God's people to covenant faithfulness and announce the coming messenger before the day of the LORD.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} covenant faithfulness; priesthood; tithes; divorce; forerunner; day of the LORD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Disputations 1-3; Closing warning and Elijah promise 4.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Qumran Malachi fragments survive Second Temple period | Subst. Early Hebrew witness is fragmentary Second Temple period | Heb. Leningrad Codex AD 1008 | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Malachi 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Interpreted in the Gospels as fulfilled in John the Baptist by Jesus and Gospel writers (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Malachi is vital for intertestamental framing because its forerunner promise is directly tied to John the Baptist in the NT.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Malachi as the closing prophetic voice of the OT canon, genuinely predicting the messenger fulfilled in John the Baptist.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Malachi}
\markboth{MALACHI}{}
\subsection*{Malachi 1}
\markright{MALACHI 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of his messenger. Lay [it], I pray you, to heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I have loved you, says the Lord. And you⌃ said, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? says the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} and hated Esau and laid waste his borders, and made his heritage as dwellings of the wilderness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Because one will say, Idumea has been overthrown, but let us return and rebuild the desolate places; thus says the Lord Almighty, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall be called The borders of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord has set himself for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And your eyes shall see, and you⌃ shall say, The Lord has been magnified upon the borders of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A son honors [his] father, and a servant his master: if then I am a father, where is my honor? and if I am a master, where is my fear? says the Lord Almighty. You⌃ the priests are they that despise my name: yet you⌃ said, Wherein have we despised your name? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In that you⌃ bring to my altar polluted bread; and you⌃ said, Wherein have you⌃ polluted it? In that you⌃ say, The table of the Lord is polluted, and that which was set thereon you⌃ have despised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For if you⌃ bring a blind [victim] for sacrifices, [is it] not evil? and if you⌃ bring the lame or the sick, [is it] not evil? offer it now to your ruler, [and see] if he will receive you, if he will accept your person, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now entreat the face of your God, and make supplication to him. These things have been done by your hands; shall I accept you? says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Because even among you the doors shall be shut, and [one] will not kindle [the fire of] my altar for nothing, I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice at your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For from the rising of the sun even to the going down [thereof] my name has been glorified among the Gentiles; and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering: for my name is great among the Gentiles, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But you⌃ profane it, in that you⌃ say, The table of the Lord is polluted, and his meats set thereon are despised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And you⌃ said, These [services] are troublesome: therefore I have utterly rejected them with scorn, says the Lord Almighty: and you⌃ brought in torn victims, and lame, and sick: if then you⌃ should bring an offering, shall I accept them at your hands? says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And cursed [is the man] who had the power, and possessed a male in his flock, and whose vow is upon him, and who sacrifices a corrupt thing to the Lord: for I am a great King, says the Lord Almighty, and my name is glorious among the nations.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: Malachi (Malaki) — My messenger The last Old Testament messenger before John the Baptist.\par}

\subsection*{Malachi 2}
\markright{MALACHI 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And now, O priests, this commandment is to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If you⌃ will not listen, and if you⌃ will not lay [it] to heart, to give glory to my name, says the Lord Almighty, then I will send forth the curse upon you, and I will bring a curse upon your blessing: yes, I will curse it, and I will scatter your blessing, and it shall not exist among you, because you⌃ lay not this to heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, I turn my back upon you, and I will scatter dung upon your faces, the dung of your feasts, and I will carry you away at the same time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And you⌃ shall know that I have sent this commandment to you, that my covenant might be with the sons of Levi, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} My covenant of life and peace was with him, and I gave [it] him that he might reverently fear me, and that he might be awe-struck at my name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked before me directing [his way] in peace, and he turned many from unrighteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But you⌃ have turned aside from the way, and caused many to fail in [following] the law: you⌃ have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And I have made you despised and cast out among all the people, because you⌃ have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Have you⌃ not all one father? Did not one God create you? why have you⌃ forsaken every man his brother, to profane the covenant of your fathers? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Juda has been forsaken, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Juda has profaned the holy things of the Lord, which he delighted in, and has gone after other gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The Lord will utterly destroy the man that does these things, until he be even cast down from out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and from among them that offer sacrifice to the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And these things which I hated, you⌃ did: you⌃ covered with tears the altar of the Lord, and with weeping and groaning because of troubles: [is it] meet [for me] to have respect to your sacrifice, or to receive [anything] from your hands [as] welcome? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Yet you⌃ said, Therefore? Because the Lord has borne witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have forsaken, and [yet] she was your partner, and the wife of your covenant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And did he not do well? and [there was] the residue of his spirit. But you⌃ said, What does God seek but a seed? But take you⌃ heed to your spirit, and forsake not the wife of your youth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But if you should hate [your wife] and put her away, says the Lord God of Israel, then ungodliness shall cover your thoughts, says the Lord Almighty: therefore take you⌃ heed to your spirit, and forsake [them] not, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} you⌃ that have provoked God with your words. But you⌃ said, Wherein have we provoked him? In that you⌃ say, Every one that does evil is a pleasing [object] in the sight of the Lord, and he takes pleasure in such; and where is the God of justice?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} ye will not hear; , ; if ye will not lay, to give; and I; I have cursed By sending them unfruitful seasons \textsuperscript{3} I will corrupt or reprove spread Heb. scatter; one shall take you away with it or, it shall take you away to it \textsuperscript{6} law; he walked, ; and did \textsuperscript{8} ye are; ye have caused; stumble at or, fall in ye have corrupted \textsuperscript{9} made; before; but;, ; have been partial in or, lifted up the face against, Heb. accepted faces. *marg. \textsuperscript{11} and an; profaned; , loved or, ought to love and hath \textsuperscript{12} cut; the master and the scholar or, him that waketh, and him that answereth; out; and him \textsuperscript{14} Wherefore; the Lord; the wife; thy companion; *marg. \textsuperscript{15} did; residue or, excellency the spirit; That he, ; godly seed Heb. seed of God; take; treacherously or, unfaithfully \textsuperscript{16} the Lord; that he hateth putting away or, if he hate her, put her away, Heb. to put away covereth\par}

\subsection*{Malachi 3}
\markright{MALACHI 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Behold, I send forth my messenger, and he shall survey the way before me: and the Lord, whom you⌃ seek, shall suddenly come into his temple, even the angel of the covenant, whom you⌃ take pleasure in: behold, he is coming, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And who will abide the day of his coming? or who will withstand at his appearing? for he is coming in as the fire of a furnace and as the herb of fullers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He shall sit to melt and purify as it were silver, and as it were gold: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver, and they shall offer to the Lord an offering in righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the sacrifice of Juda and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the Lord, according to the former days, and according to the former years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And I will draw near to you in judgment; and I will be a sift witness against the witches, and against the adulteresses, and against them that swear falsely by my name, and against them that keep back the hireling's wages, and them that oppress the widow, and afflict orphans, and that wrest the judgment of the stranger, and fear not me, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For I am the Lord your God, and I am not changed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} but you⌃, the sons of Jacob, have not refrained from the iniquities of your fathers: you⌃ have perverted my statutes, and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord Almighty. But you⌃ said, Wherein shall we return? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Will a man insult God? for you⌃ insult me. But you⌃ say, Wherein have we insulted you? In that the tithes and first fruits are with you [still]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And you⌃ do surely look off from me, and you⌃ insult me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The year is completed, and you⌃ have brought all the produce into the storehouses; but there shall be the plunder thereof in its house: return now on this behalf, says the Lord Almighty, [see] if I will not open to you the torrents of heaven, and pour out my blessing upon you, until you⌃ are satisfied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I will appoint food for you, and I will not destroy the fruit of your land; and your vine in the field shall not fail, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all nations shall call you blessed: for you⌃ shall be a desirable land, says the Lord Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} You⌃ have spoken grievous words against me, says the Lord. Yet you⌃ said, Wherein have we spoken against you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} You⌃ said, He that serves God labors in vain: and what have we gained in that we have kept his ordinances, and in that we have walked as suppliants before the face of the Lord Almighty? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And now we pronounce strangers blessed; and all they who act unlawfully are built up; and they have resisted God, and [yet] have been delivered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus spoke they that feared the Lord, every one to his neighbor: and the Lord gave heed, and listened, and he wrote a book of remembrance before him for them that feared the Lord and reverenced his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they shall be mine, says the Lord Almighty, in the day which I appoint for a peculiar possession; and I will make choice of them, as a man makes choice of his son that serves him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then shall you⌃ return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between him that serves God, and him that serves [him] not.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I will; and he; and; , ; even; he shall come \textsuperscript{2} who may abide;, ;, ;, ; for; like fullers' \textsuperscript{4} the offering; as, ;, ; former or, ancient \textsuperscript{5} I will come; a swift; the sorcerers, ; against those; oppress or, defraud, fear \textsuperscript{6} I am, ; I change not; therefore \textsuperscript{7} from the, ; , ; Return unto me; Wherein \textsuperscript{10} all; the storehouse;, and prove; open; pour you out Heb. empty out, that there \textsuperscript{11} rebuke; destroy Heb. corrupt neither \textsuperscript{14} It is, ; ordinance Heb. observation and that; mournfully Heb. in black \textsuperscript{15} we call; yea; set Heb. built, they that tempt \textsuperscript{16} that feared; spake; , ; and the; a book; that thought \textsuperscript{17} they shall; jewels or, special treasure; and I; son\par}

\section*{Matthew Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Matthew the apostle and former tax collector\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Early church testimony, especially Papias and Irenaeus, associates this Gospel with Matthew.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The canonical title and unanimous early church witness support Matthean authorship; apostolic status fits the book's Jewish and instructional character.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} before AD 70 in common conservative dating\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} MT timeline not applicable; historically set in the earthly ministry of Christ before the fall of Jerusalem.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} LXX timeline not applicable; the Gospel quotes the OT often in forms reflecting both Hebrew and Greek textual streams.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Gospel account presenting Jesus as the promised Messiah and King in fulfillment of Scripture.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To present Jesus as the Messiah, teacher, son of David, and fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} Messiah; kingdom; fulfillment; discipleship; judgment; church\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Narrative and infancy 1-4; ministry and discourses 5-25; passion and resurrection 26-28.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 104 late 2nd century AD | Subst. Papyrus 64/67 and other early Matthew witnesses preserve larger sections late 2nd to early 3rd century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus preserve complete Greek Matthew 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Tradition on Matthew's composition by Papias (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Matthew's quotations are crucial for MT/LXX comparison because he often cites OT texts in forms close to Hebrew, Greek, or a mixed testimony tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Matthew as the apostolic Gospel and treats its fulfillment formulas as inspired interpretation of the OT.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Matthew}
\markboth{MATTHEW}{}
\subsection*{Matthew 1}
\markright{MATTHEW 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Abraham brings forth Isaac; and Isaac brings forth Jacob; and Jacob brings forth Judas and his brethren; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Judas brings forth Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares brings forth Esrom; and Esrom brings forth Aram; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Aram brings forth Aminadab; and Aminadab brings forth Naasson; and Naasson brings forth Salmon; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Salmon brings forth Booz of Rachab; and Booz brings forth Obed of Ruth; and Obed brings forth Jesse; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And Jesse brings forth David the king; and David the king brings forth Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Solomon brings forth Roboam; and Roboam brings forth Abia; and Abia brings forth Asa; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And Asa brings forth Josaphat; and Josaphat brings forth Joram; and Joram brings forth Ozias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And Ozias brings forth Joatham; and Joatham brings forth Achaz; and Achaz brings forth Ezekias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Ezekias brings forth Manasses; and Manasses brings forth Amon; and Amon brings forth Josias; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Josias brings forth Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias brings forth Salathiel; and Salathiel brings forth Zorobabel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Zorobabel brings forth Abiud; and Abiud brings forth Eliakim; and Eliakim brings forth Azor; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Azor brings forth Sadoc; and Sadoc brings forth Achim; and Achim brings forth Eliud; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Eliud brings forth Eleazar; and Eleazar brings forth Matthan; and Matthan brings forth Jacob; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jacob brings forth Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now the birth of Jesus Christ was likewise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privately. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, you son of David, fear not to take unto you Mary your wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And she shall bring forth a son, and you shall call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And had sexual contact with her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Name meaning: Mary (Miryam) — Bitter; beloved; exalted one Mother of Jesus; experienced bitterness yet exaltation. Name meaning: Joseph (NT) (Yosef) — He adds God added protection and provision for the holy family. \textsuperscript{20} Name of God: Kyrios (κύριος) — Lord Common English renderings: Lord. In the New Testament this title is used both for the Lord God and, in a full divine sense, for Jesus. \textsuperscript{21} Name meaning: Jesus (Yeshua) — Yahweh saves He will save His people from their sins. \textsuperscript{23} Name of God: Theos (θεός) — God Common English renderings: God. The standard Greek New Testament word for God, corresponding broadly to Hebrew Elohim. \textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: prōtotokos (πρωτότοκος) = firstborn. Common English renderings: firstborn. A major Christological term with legal, familial, and rank-related force.\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 2}
\markright{MATTHEW 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And you Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, are not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of you shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then Herod, when he had privately called the wise men, enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go and search diligently for the young child; and when all of you have found him, bring me word again, that I may come and worship him also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense and myrrh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding angry, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child's life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he arose, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 3}
\markright{MATTHEW 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And saying, Repent all of you: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Isaiah, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare all of you the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who has warned you to flee from the wrath to come? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which brings not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and with fire: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then comes Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of you, and come you to me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becomes us to fulfill all righteousness. Then he suffered him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up immediately out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: John (Yochanan) — Yahweh is gracious Forerunner of Jesus; proclaimed God’s grace. Name meaning: John the Baptist (Yochanan) — Yahweh is gracious Prepared the way with grace. \textsuperscript{2} Gk. vocab: metanoeō (μετανοέω) = to repent; change one’s mind. Common English renderings: repent. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament. \textsuperscript{8} Gk. vocab: metanoia (μετάνοια) = repentance; change of mind. Common English renderings: repentance. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 4}
\markright{MATTHEW 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then was Jesus led up of the spirit (o. pneuma) into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when the tempter came to him, he said, If you be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word (o. rhema) that proceeds out of the mouth of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then the devil takes him up into the holy city, and sets him on a pinnacle of the temple, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And says unto him, If you be the Son of God, cast yourself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning you: and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest at any time you dash your foot against a stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Jesus said unto him, It is written again, You shall not tempt the Lord your God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And says unto him, All these things will I give you, if you will fall down and worship me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then says Jesus unto him, Get you behind, Satan: for it is written, You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Then the devil left him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now when Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he says unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they immediately left their nets, and followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatic, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judaea, and from beyond Jordan.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{18} Name meaning: Peter (Kepha; Petros) — Rock; stone The rock-like apostle. Name meaning: Andrew (Andreas) — Manly; courageous Courageous fisherman turned fisher of men. \textsuperscript{21} Name meaning: James (Yaaqov) — Supplanter One of the sons of thunder; later a pillar of the Church. \textsuperscript{23} Gk. vocab: therapeia (θεραπεία) = service; healing. Common English renderings: healing. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} was; of the spirit;, ; to \textsuperscript{4} It is; Man; but;, ; , but That is, as Dr. Campbell renders, "by every thing which God is pleased to appoint; " for ρημα, which generally signifies a word, is, by a Hebraism, here taken for a thing, like davar in Hebrew. NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 8:3 man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God shall man live.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 8:3 man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.” \textsuperscript{6} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Psalms 90:11,12 For he shall give his angels charge concerning thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up on their hands, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Psalms 91:11,12 For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.” \textsuperscript{7} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 6:16 Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 6:16 Ye shall not tempt the LORD your God,” \textsuperscript{10} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 6:13 Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve, and thou shalt cleave to him, and by his name though shalt swear. Deuteronomy 10:20 Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shall cleave to him, and shalt swear by his name.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 6:13, 10:20 Thou shalt fear the LORD thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name.” \textsuperscript{12} when; cast or, delivered up \textsuperscript{13} leaving Capernaum;, Zabulon, Zebulun Nephthalim, Naphtali \textsuperscript{15} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. O people walking in darkness, behold a great light: ye that dwell in the region and shadow of death, a light shall shine upon you.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 9:1,2 ...he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” \textsuperscript{16} which sat in darkness; shadow \textsuperscript{18} walking; sea; Chinnereth, lake of Gennesaret, sea of Tiberias two; for \textsuperscript{23} Jesus; teaching; , the gospel; healing \textsuperscript{24} his fame, ; Syria; all sick, ; possessed, ; lunatic those that\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 5}
\markright{MATTHEW 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Blessed are the poor in spirit: (o. pneuma) for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Blessed are all of you, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil (o. rhema) against you falsely, for my sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} All of you are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} All of you are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it gives light unto all that are in the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, all of you shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} All of you have heard that it was said of them of old time, You shall not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, You fool, shall be in danger of hell fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has ought against you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Leave there your gift before the altar, and go your way; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Agree with yours adversary quickly, while you are in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Verily I say unto you, You shall by no means come out thence, till you have paid the uttermost farthing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} All of you have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not commit adultery: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And if your right eye offend you, pluck it out, and cast it from you: for it is profitable for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And if your right hand offend you, cut it off, and cast it from you: for it is profitable for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause (o. logos) of fornication, causes her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced commits adultery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Again, all of you have heard that it has been said by them of old time, You shall not renounce swearing yourself, but shall perform unto the Lord yours oaths: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Neither shall you swear by your head, because you can not make one hair white or black. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} But let your communication (o. logos) be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these comes of evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} All of you have heard that it has been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But I say unto you, That all of you resist not evil: but whosoever shall strike you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And if any man will sue you at the law, and take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And whosoever shall compel you to go a mile, go with him two. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Give to him that asks you, and from him that would borrow of you turn not you away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} All of you have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate yours enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} That all of you may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he makes his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} For if all of you love them which love you, what reward have all of you? do not even the publicans the same? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And if all of you salute your brethren only, what do all of you more than others? do not even the publicans so? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Be all of you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{16} Name of God: Pater (πατήρ) — Father Common English renderings: Father. A dominant New Testament divine address, especially in the teaching of Jesus. \textsuperscript{18} Gk. vocab: keraia (κεραία) = small stroke; little horn. Common English renderings: tittle. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

Whosoever; Raca that is, vain fellow; the council The Sanhedrin, συνεδριον, composed of 72 elders, who alone punished by stoning.; fool, ; hell \textsuperscript{29} if; offend thee or, do cause thee to offend pluck; for\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 6}
\markright{MATTHEW 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Take heed that all of you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise all of you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Therefore when you do yours alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But when you do alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand does: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That yours alms may be in secret: and your Father which sees in secret himself shall reward you openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But you, when you pray, enter into your closet, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father which is in secret; and your Father which sees in secret shall reward you openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But when all of you pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be not all of you therefore like unto them: for your Father knows what things all of you have need of, before all of you ask him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} After this manner therefore pray all of you: Our Father which are in heaven, Hallowed be your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Your kingdom come, Your will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Give us this day our daily bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if all of you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if all of you forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Moreover when all of you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But you, when you fast, anoint yours head, and wash your face; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} That you appear not unto men to fast, but unto your Father which is in secret: and your Father, which sees in secret, shall reward you openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust does corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The light of the body is the eye: if therefore yours eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But if yours eye be evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you be darkness, how great is that darkness! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. All of you cannot serve God and mammon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what all of you shall eat, or what all of you shall drink; nor yet for your body, what all of you shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body than raiment? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are all of you not much better than they? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And why take all of you thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O all of you of little faith? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knows that all of you have need of all these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But seek all of you first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Take therefore no thought for the next day: for the next day shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.\par
