\subsection*{Matthew 7}
\markright{MATTHEW 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Judge not, that all of you be not judged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For with what judgment all of you judge, all of you shall be judged: and with what measure all of you mete, it shall be measured to you again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And why behold you the splinter that is in your brother's eye, but consider not the beam that is in yours own eye? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Or how will you say to your brother, Let me pull out the splinter out of yours eye; and, behold, a beam is in yours own eye? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} You hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of yours own eye; and then shall you see clearly to cast out the splinter out of your brother's eye. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast all of you your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and return and rend you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and all of you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For every one that asks receives; and he that seeks finds; and to him that knocks it shall be opened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If all of you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore all things whatsoever all of you would that men should do to you, do all of you even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Enter all of you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leads unto life, and few there be that find it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} All of you shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Even so every good tree brings forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree brings forth evil fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Every tree that brings not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Wherefore by their fruits all of you shall know them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Not every one that says unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that does the will of my Father which is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name? and in your name have cast out devils? and in your name done many wonderful works? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, all of you that work iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore whosoever hears these sayings (o. logos) of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And every one that hears these sayings (o. logos) of mine, and does them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, (o. logos) the people were astonished at his doctrine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Gk. vocab: margaritēs (μαργαρίτης) = pearl. Common English renderings: pearl. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{14} because or, How narrow; and few\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 8}
\markright{MATTHEW 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if you will, you can make me clean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be you clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jesus says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And saying, Lord, my servant lies at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And Jesus says unto him, I will come and heal him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof: but speak the word (o. logos) only, and my servant shall be healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go your way; and as you have believed, so be it done unto you. And his servant was healed in the very same hour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when Jesus was come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother laid, and sick of a fever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits (o. pneuma) with his word, (o. logos) and healed all that were sick: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow you anywhere you go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Jesus says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man has not where to lay his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he says unto them, Why are all of you fearful, O all of you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Jesus, you Son of God? are you come here to torment us before the time? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} So the devils besought him, saying, If you cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} behold; a leper; , ; worshipped, ; if \textsuperscript{5} entered, ; a centurion This was a Roman military title; and therefore this officer may be concluded to have been a Gentile. (See fuller particulars under .) \textsuperscript{11} That;, ; shall sit Ανακλιθηαονται ( κλινο ), shall recline, i.e., at table; referring to the recumbent posture used by the easterners at their meals., ; in \textsuperscript{13} Go; and as, ; And his \textsuperscript{16} the even; they brought; and he;, ; and healed \textsuperscript{17} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 53:4 He bears our sins, and is pained for us: yet we accounted him to be in trouble, and in suffering, and in affliction.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 53:4 Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows” \textsuperscript{28} when; Gergesenes Some are of opinion that Gergasa was the country of the ancient Girgashites; but it is more probable the Gergesenes was introduced by Origen upon mere conjecture; as before him most copies seem to have read Gadarenes, agreeable to the Parallel Passages and the ancient Syriac version. Gadara, says Josephus, was the metropolis of Peraea, or the region beyond Jordan; and he also observes that it was sixty furlongs, or about eight miles from Tiberias. It is therefore rightly placed opposite Tiberias, at the southeast end of the lake. Pliny says it was called Hippodion, was one of the cities of Decapolis, and had the river Hieromax, or Jarmouk, flowing before it. It was of heathen jurisdiction; whence perhaps it was destroyed by the Jews; but was rebuilt by Pompey, and joined to the province of Syria. Augustus afterwards gave it to Herod, on whose death it was again annexed to Syria. It is now called Om Keis; its ruins are in a very mutilated state, and when visited by Burckhardt it had not a single inhabitant. The remains of the sepulchral caverns in which the demoniacs abode are still to be seen.; coming; so\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 9}
\markright{MATTHEW 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; your sins be forgiven you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think all of you evil in your hearts? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For whether is easier, to say, Your sins be forgiven you; or to say, Arise, and walk? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But that all of you may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto yours house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he arose, and departed to his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he says unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at food in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eats your Master with publicans and sinners? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But go all of you and learn what that means, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples fast not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bride-chamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} No man puts a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up takes from the garment, and the rent is made worse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} While he spoke these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay your hand upon her, and she shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when Jesus came into the ruler's house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You son of David, have mercy on us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus says unto them, Believe all of you that I am able to do this? They said unto him, Yea, Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And their eyes were opened; and Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But they, when they were departed, spread abroad his fame in all that country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} As they went out, behold, they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a devil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spoke: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every disease among the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is abundant, but the labourers are few; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Pray all of you therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Name meaning: Matthew (Mattityahu) — Gift of Yahweh Tax collector given the gift of apostleship and authorship.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} they brought; seeing; Son; be; thy sins Rather, "thy sins are forgiven thee; " the words being an affirmation, not a prayer or wish. The word be, however, was used by our translators in the indicative plural for are. As the palsy is frequently produced by intemperance, it is probable, from our Lord's gracious declaration, that it was the case in the present instance. \textsuperscript{13} go, ; I will; to call; but NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Hosea 6:7 For I will have mercy rather than sacrifice” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice” \textsuperscript{16} new cloth or, raw, or unwrought cloth for \textsuperscript{18} behold; ruler, ; worshipped, ; My daughter; come \textsuperscript{20} behold; an issue touched; hem \textsuperscript{26} the fame hereof or, this fame \textsuperscript{36} when; fainted etc. or, were tired and lay down as\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 10}
\markright{MATTHEW 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, (o. pneuma) to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter all of you not: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And as all of you go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely all of you have received, freely give. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Nor pouch for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And into whatsoever city or town all of you shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till all of you go thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when all of you come into an house, salute it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, (o. logos) when all of you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be all of you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all of you shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what all of you shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what all of you shall speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For it is not all of you that speak, but the Spirit (o. pneuma) of your Father which speaks in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And all of you shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But when they persecute you in this city, flee all of you into another: for verily I say unto you, All of you shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} What I tell you in darkness, that speak all of you in light: and what all of you hear in the ear, that preach all of you upon the housetops. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Fear all of you not therefore, all of you are of more value than many sparrows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And a man's foes shall be they of his own household. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} He that loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} He that receives a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward; and he that receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man's reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 11}
\markright{MATTHEW 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And said unto him, Are you he that should come, or do we look for another? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and show John again those things which all of you do hear and see: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went all of you out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But what went all of you out in order to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But what went all of you out in order to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before your face, which shall prepare your way before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there has not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if all of you will receive it, this is Elijah, which was in order to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He that has ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But unto which shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And saying, We have piped unto you, and all of you have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and all of you have not lamented. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He has a devil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a wine indulger, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Then began he to reproach the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Woe unto you, Chorazin! woe unto you, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And you, Capernaum, which are exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in you, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in your sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and all of you shall find rest unto your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 12}
\markright{MATTHEW 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungered, and began to pluck the ears of corn and to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, your disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But he said unto them, Have all of you not read what David did, when he was an hungered, and they that were with him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the showbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Or have all of you not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But if all of you had known what this means, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, all of you would not have condemned the guiltless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then says he to the man, Stretch forth yours hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And charged them that they should not make him known: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit (o. pneuma) upon him, and he shall show judgment to the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And in his name shall the Gentiles trust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spoke and saw. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow does not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if I cast out devils by the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God, then the kingdom of God has come unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Or else how can one enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathers not with me scatters abroad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) shall not be forgiven unto men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And whosoever speaks a word (o. logos) against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} O generation of vipers, how can all of you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} A good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth evil things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But I say unto you, That every idle word (o. rhema) that men shall speak, they shall give account (o. logos) thereof in the day of judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} For by your words (o. logos) you shall be justified, and by your words (o. logos) you shall be condemned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} When the unclean spirit (o. pneuma) is gone out of a man, he walks through dry places, seeking rest, and finds none. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Then he says, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he has come, he finds it empty, swept, and garnished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Then goes he, and takes with himself seven other spirits (o. pneuma) more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then one said unto him, Behold, your mother and your brethren stand without, desiring to speak with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{7} if; I will That is, I desire, or require mercy, or acts of humanity, rather than sacrifice.; condemned \textsuperscript{11} what This was an argumentum ad homineṁ The Jews held that such things were lawful on the sabbath day, and our Saviour very properly appealed to their canons in vindication of his intention to heal the distressed man., and if \textsuperscript{14} went; , held a council or, took counsel \textsuperscript{18} Behold This prophecy is expressly referred to the Messiah by the Targumist, who renders, "Behold my servant the Messiah, " etc., ha avdi mesheecha; and it was amply fulfilled in the gentle, lowly, condescending and beneficent nature of Christ's miracles and personal ministry, his perseverance in the midst of opposition, without engaging in contentious disputation, and his kind and tender dealing with weak and tempted believers. my servant, ; whom I; my beloved; *marg. I will; and he NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 42:1-4 Jacob is my servant, I will help him: Israel is my chosen, my soul has accepted him; I have put my Spirit upon him; he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles. He shall not cry, nor lift up his voice, nor shall his voice be heard without. A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench; but he shall bring forth judgment to truth. He shall shine out, and shall not be discouraged, until he have set judgment on the earth: and in his name shall the Gentiles trust.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 42:1-4 Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles. He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street. A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth. He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.” \textsuperscript{24} when; Beelzebub Gr. Beelzebul, and so \textsuperscript{31} All; *etc:; blasphemy Blasphemy, βλασφημια, either from βλαπειν, την φημην, to hurt, or blast the reputation, or from βαλλειν, ταις φημαις, to smite with words, or reports, when applied to men denotes injurious speaking, or calumny, and when used in reference to God signifies speaking impiously of his nature, attributes, and works. but \textsuperscript{32} whosoever; but; it shall not \textsuperscript{33} make the good tree; and his fruit good \textsuperscript{36} every; idle word Ρημα, αργος, i.e., ἀεργον - (work, act, deed) from α, privative, and εργον, work, a word that produces no good effect, and is not calculated to produce any. "Discourse, " says Dr. Doddridge, "tending to innocent mirth, to exhilarate the spirits, is not idle discourse; as the time spent in necessary recreation is not idle time." \textsuperscript{40} as so, ; in the heart \textsuperscript{41} men rise; this, because behold \textsuperscript{43} when Had there been no reality in demoniacal possessions, as some have supposed, our Lord would scarcely have appealed to a case of this kind here, to point out the real state of the Jewish people, and their approaching desolation. Had this been only a vulgar error, of the nonsense of which the learned scribes and wise Pharisees must have been convinced, the case, not being in point, because not true, must have been treated with contempt by the very people for whose conviction it was designed. the unclean; he; dry; seeking \textsuperscript{45} seven; more and the; Even And so it was; for they became worse and worse, as if totally abandoned to diabolical influence, till the besom of destruction swept them away. \textsuperscript{50} do; , ; the same, ; and sister, ; and mother\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 13}
\markright{MATTHEW 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship, and sat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he spoke many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who has ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speak you unto them in parables? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For whosoever has, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever has not, from him shall be taken away even that he has. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which says, By hearing all of you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing all of you shall see, and shall not perceive: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which all of you see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which all of you hear, and have not heard them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Hear all of you therefore the parable of the sower. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} When any one hears the word (o. logos) of the kingdom, and understands it not, then comes the wicked one, and catches away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that hears the word, (o. logos) and soon with joy receives it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Yet has he not root in himself, but endures for a while: for when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, (o. logos) by and by he is offended. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He also that received seed among the thorns is he that hears the word; (o. logos) and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, (o. logos) and he becomes unfruitful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But he that received seed into the good ground is he that hears the word, (o. logos) and understands it; which also bears fruit, and brings forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, did not you sow good seed in your field? from whence then has it tares? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He said unto them, An enemy has done this. The servants said unto him, Will you then that we go and gather them up? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But he said, Nay; lest while all of you gather up the tares, all of you root up also the wheat with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather all of you together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Another parable spoke he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} All these things spoke Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spoke he not unto them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} He answered and said unto them, He that sows the good seed is the Son of man; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who has ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Jesus says unto them, Have all of you understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which brings forth out of his treasure things new and old. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence has this man this wisdom, and these mighty works? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then has this man all these things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: mystērion (μυστήριον) = mystery; secret. Common English renderings: mystery. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament. \textsuperscript{22} Gk. vocab: apatē (ἀπάτη) = deceit. Common English renderings: deceit. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} great; so; a ship Το πλοιον, "the ship" or boat; which Mr. Wakefield supposes was a particular vessel kept on the lake for the use of Christ and his disciples. \textsuperscript{3} in, ; , ; *marg. parables A parable, παραβολη, from παρα, near, and βαλλω, I cast, or put, has been justly defined to be a comparison or similitude, in which one thing is compared with another, especially spiritual things with natural, by which means those spiritual things are better understood, and make a deeper impression on a honest and attentive mind. In a parable, a resemblance in the principal incidents is all that is required; smaller matters being considered as a sort of drapery. Maimonides, in Moreh Nevochim, gives an excellent rule on this head: "Fix it as a principle to attach yourself to the grand object of the parable, without attempting to make a particular application of all the circumstances and terms which it comprehends." a sower \textsuperscript{14} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 6:9,10 Ye shall hear indeed, but ye shall not understand; and ye shall see indeed, but ye shall not perceive. For the heart of this people has become gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 6:9,10 And he said, God, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” \textsuperscript{15} heart ears; their eyes; and should be; and I \textsuperscript{19} the word; and understandeth, ;, ; the wicked; , This \textsuperscript{22} seed; the care; , ; the deceitfulness; choke \textsuperscript{23} that received; good; beareth, ; some an \textsuperscript{30} both, ; to the; and bind burn; but \textsuperscript{32} the least; *Gr:; so that \textsuperscript{33} Another like; measures Gr. "A measure containing about a peck and a half, wanting a little more than a pint." till \textsuperscript{35} it, I will open I will utter; from NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Psalms 77:2 I will open my mouth in parables: I will utter dark sayings which have been from the beginning.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Psalms 78:2 I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old” \textsuperscript{38} field; the good; the children of the wicked \textsuperscript{41} The son; and they; things that offend or, scandals and them \textsuperscript{54} when; he taught; they were \textsuperscript{55} is not this; the carpenter's; and his\par}

\subsection*{Matthew 14}
\markright{MATTHEW 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For John said unto him, It is not lawful for you to have her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But when Herod's birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist's head in a charger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath's sake, and them which sat with him at food, he commanded it to be given her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When Jesus heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But Jesus said unto them, They need not depart; give all of you them to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He said, Bring them here to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And immediately Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But immediately Jesus spoke unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be you, bid me come unto you on the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O you of little faith, wherefore did you doubt? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Truthfully you are the Son of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{3} Name meaning: Herodias (Herodias) — Heroic Manipulative figure who sought John’s head.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Herod This was Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, and tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, which produced a revenue of 200 talents a year. He married the daughter of Aretas, king of Arabia, whom he divorced in order to marry Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, who was still living. Aretas, to revenge the affront which Herod had offered his daughter, declared war against him, and vanquished him after an obstinate engagement. This defeat, Josephus assures us, the Jews considered as a punishment for the death of John the Baptist. Having gone to Rome to solicit the title of king, he was accused by Agrippa of carrying on a correspondence with Artabanus king of Parthia, against the Romans, and was banished by the emperor Caius to Lyons, and thence to Spain, where he and Herodias died in exile.;, ; Tetrarch \textsuperscript{2} This; do show forth themselves in him or, are wrought by him \textsuperscript{3} Herod; Herodias' This infamous woman was the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice, and granddaughter of Herod the Great. his Philip's Herod Philip, son of Herod the Great and Mariamne. \textsuperscript{6} birthday; the daughter danced before them Gr. in the midst \textsuperscript{9} the king; sorry; the oath's \textsuperscript{10} and beheaded, ; the prison Josephus informs us that John the Baptist was imprisoned and beheaded by Herod in the strong castle of Machaerus, which he describes as situated about 60 stadia east of Jordan, not far from where the river discharges itself into the Dead Sea. \textsuperscript{19} he commanded; looking; he blessed \textsuperscript{25} the fourth watch The Jews at this time divided the night into four watches; the first was from six o'clock in the evening till nine, the second from nine to twelve, the third from twelve till three, and the fourth from three till six; so that it probably began to be daylight before our Lord came to his disciples.; walking This suspension of the laws of gravitation was a proper manifestation of omnipotence. \textsuperscript{30} when; boisterous or, strong Lord \textsuperscript{31} stretched; and caught; O thou \textsuperscript{34} when the land of Gennesaret was a fertile district, in which were situated the cities of Tiberias and Capernaum, extending along the western shore of the lake to which it gave name, about 30 stadia, or nearly four miles, in length, and twenty stadia, or two miles and a half, in breadth, according to Josephus.\par}
