\subsection*{Mark 2}
\markright{MARK 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And immediately many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word (o. logos) unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, your sins be forgiven you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But there was certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Why does this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit (o. pneuma) that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason all of you these things in your hearts? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Your sins be forgiven you; or to say, Arise, and take up your bed, and walk? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But that all of you may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, (he says to the sick of the palsy,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I say unto you, Arise, and take up your bed, and go your way into yours house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at food in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eats and drinks with publicans and sinners? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} When Jesus heard it, he says unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples fast not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} No man also sews a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up takes away from the old, and the rent is made worse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And no man puts new wine into old bottles: else the new wine does burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be ruined: but new wine must be put into new bottles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he said unto them, Have all of you never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungered, he, and they that were with him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the showbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{5} saw; he said; Son The Jews believed that not only death but all disease was the consequence of sin. "There is no death without sin, nor any chastisement without iniquity; " and that "no diseased person could be healed of his disease till his sins were blotted out." Our Lord, therefore, as usual, appeals to their received opinions, and asserts his high dignity, by first forgiving the sins, and then healing the body of the paralytic.; sins \textsuperscript{14} he saw; Alphaeus; receipt of custom or, place where the custom was received Follow me \textsuperscript{17} They that are whole;, ; I came \textsuperscript{20} the bridegroom; be taken;, ; and \textsuperscript{21} seweth; new or, raw, or, unwrought \textsuperscript{26} Abiathar It appears from the passage referred to here, that Ahimelech was then high priest at Nob; and from other passages, that Abiathar was his son. Various conjectures have been formed in order to solve this difficulty; and some, instead of untying, have cut the knot, by pronouncing it an interpolation. The most probable opinion seems to be, that both father and son had two names, the father being also called Abiathar; and this appears almost certain from; where Ahimelech seems evidently termed Abiathar, while Abiathar is called Ahimelech or Abimelech. (Compare .), ;, ;, which is not lawful\par}

\subsection*{Mark 3}
\markright{MARK 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he says unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he says unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he says unto the man, Stretch forth yours hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the Pharisees went forth, and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he spoke to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should crowd upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him in order to touch him, as many as had plagues. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And unclean spirits, (o. pneuma) when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, You are the Son of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he strictly charged them that they should not make him known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he goes up into a mountain, and calls unto him whom he would: and they came unto him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Simon he surnamed Peter; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the multitude comes together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He has Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casts he out devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but has an end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith whatsoever they shall blaspheme: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) has never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Because they said, He has an unclean spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, your mother and your brethren without seek for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} he saith; Stand forth or, Arise, stand forth in the midst \textsuperscript{5} with anger With anger at their desperate malice and wickedness, and with commiseration for the calamities which they would thereby bring on themselves.; grieved; hardness or, blindness, ; Stretch \textsuperscript{8} Idumaea; Edom beyond; Tyre; Ezek. 26:1-28:26 \textsuperscript{10} he had, pressed or, rushed, touched, ; as many \textsuperscript{18} Andrew, ; Philip, Bartholomew; Matthew; Levi, Thomas, ; James; Alphaeus Thaddaeus; Judas the brother of James, Simon; Simon Zelotes Canaanite Κανανιτης, so called, not from being a native of Canaan, Χανααν, which would have been Χαναναος, but from the Hebrew Kana, to be zealous, whence he is called in Greek Ζηλωτης, Zelotes, or the Zealot, from ζηλοω, to be zealous. \textsuperscript{19} Judas, ;, ; into an house or, home \textsuperscript{21} when Some render, "And they who were with him (in the house, ), hearing (the noise) went out to restrain ( αυτον, i.e., οχλον, the multitude), for they said, It (the mob) is mad." This, however, is contrary to all the versions; and appears an unnatural construction. friends or, kinsmen; He is\par}

\subsection*{Mark 4}
\markright{MARK 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said unto them, He that has ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he said unto them, Know all of you not this parable? and how then will all of you know all parables? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The sower sows the word. (o. logos) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And these are they by the way side, where the word (o. logos) is sown; but when they have heard, Satan comes immediately, and takes away the word (o. logos) that was sown in their hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, (o. logos) immediately receive it with gladness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution arises for the word's sake, (o. logos) immediately they are offended. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, (o. logos) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, (o. logos) and it becomes unfruitful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, (o. logos) and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} If any man have ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he said unto them, Take heed what all of you hear: with what measure all of you mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For he that has, to him shall be given: and he that has not, from him shall be taken even that which he has. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knows not how. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For the earth brings forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he said, Unto which shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But when it is sown, it grows up, and becomes greater than all herbs, and shoots out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And with many such parables spoke he the word (o. logos) unto them, as they were able to hear it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But without a parable spoke he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the same day, when the even was come, he says unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, care you not that we perish? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And he said unto them, Why are all of you so fearful? how is it that all of you have no faith? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{11} Unto you, ; them; all these \textsuperscript{12} That seeing Rather, as ινα frequently denotes, "So that seeing they see, and do not perceive, and hearing they hear, and do not understand, " etc. The expression appears to be proverbial; and relates to those who might see what they now overlook through inattention and folly. See the parallel texts.; be converted \textsuperscript{19} the cares, ; the deceitfulness; and the lusts; unfruitful \textsuperscript{21} Is a; bushel "The word in the original signifieth a less measure, as, marg." \textsuperscript{29} brought forth or, ripe; he putteth \textsuperscript{31} like; mustard seed Mustard, σιναπι, is a well-known plant of the tetradynamia siliquosa class, distinguished by its yellow cruciform flowers, with expanding calyx, and its pods smooth, square, and close to the stem. Its seed was probably the smallest known to the Jews; and though its ordinary height does not exceed four feet, yet a species grows to the height of from three to five cubits, with a tapering, ligneous stalk, and spreading branches. is less than \textsuperscript{38} in the; and they; carest \textsuperscript{39} he arose, ;, ; rebuked; the wind\par}

\subsection*{Mark 5}
\markright{MARK 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit, (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But when he saw Jesus far off, he ran and worshipped him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the most high God? I adjure you by God, that you torment me not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For he said unto him, Come out of the man, you unclean spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he asked him, What is your name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits (o. pneuma) went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Nevertheless Jesus suffered him not, but says unto him, Go home to your friends, and tell them how great things the Lord has done for you, and has had compassion on you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And, behold, there comes one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lies at the point of death: I pray you, come and lay your hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing improved, but rather grew worse, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And his disciples said unto him, You see the multitude thronging you, and says you, Who touched me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And he said unto her, Daughter, your faith has made you whole; go in peace, and be whole of your plague. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} While he yet spoke, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain which said, Your daughter is dead: why trouble you the Master any further? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} As soon as Jesus heard the word (o. logos) that was spoken, he says unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And he comes to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and sees the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And when he was come in, he says unto them, Why make all of you this disturbance, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleeps. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he takes the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and enters in where the damsel was lying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto you, arise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And immediately the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And he charged them strictly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{22} Name meaning: Jairus (Yair) — He enlightens His daughter was raised.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} out; a man Matthew gives a brief account of two demoniacs who were dispossessed on this occasion; but Mark and Luke omit the mention of one (who was perhaps not so remarkable). That these wretched men were not merely mad, as some suppose, but really possessed of evil spirits, appears clearly from the language employed, as well as from the narrative itself. Matthew expressly affirms that they were "possessed with devils, " or demoniacs, δαιμονιζομενοι; Mark says he had "an unclean spirit, " i.e., a fallen spirit; and Luke asserts, that he "had devils (or demons) a long time, " and was called Legion, "because many devils were entered into him." With supernatural strength the demons burst asunder the chains and fetters with which he was bound; they address Christ as the "Son of the most high God; " they beseech him to suffer them to enter into the swine; and when he had given them leave, they "went out and entered into the swine, " etc. with \textsuperscript{7} What; Son; I adjure; that \textsuperscript{25} a certain; an issue, twelve \textsuperscript{26} had suffered No person will wonder at this account when he considers the therapeutics of the Jewish physicians, in reference to diseases of this kind (for an account of which, see Drs. Lightfoot and Clarke). She was, therefore, a fit patient for the Great Physician.;, nothing \textsuperscript{35} there came thy daughter, why;, the Master \textsuperscript{40} they; when; he taketh He took just so many as prudence required, and as were sufficient to prove the reality of the cure; to have permitted the presence of more, might have savoured of ostentation. \textsuperscript{41} took; Talitha cumi θμιϊΰ χεξι, which is pure Syriac, the same as in the Syriac version, the proper translation of which is given by the evangelist. Damsel \textsuperscript{43} he charged, ;, ; and commanded This was to shew that she had not only returned to life, but was also restored to perfect health; and to intimate, that though raised to life by extraordinary power, she must be continued in existence, as before, by the use of ordinary means. The advice of a heathen, on another subject, is quite applicable: Nec Deus intersit, nisi dignus vindice nodus incideriṫ "When the miraculous power of God is necessary, let it be resorted to; when not necessary, let the ordinary means be used." To act otherwise would be to tempt God. Given\par}

\subsection*{Mark 6}
\markright{MARK 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence has this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits; (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no pouch, no bread, no money in their purse: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he said unto them, In what place whatsoever all of you enter into an house, there abide till all of you depart from that place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when all of you depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they went out, and preached that men should repent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Others said, That it is Elijah. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he has risen from the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife: for he had married her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever you will, and I will give it you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he swore unto her, Whatsoever you shall ask of me, I will give it you, unto the half of my kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And she came in immediately with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that you give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath's sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he said unto them, Come all of you yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they departed into a desert place by ship privately. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran on foot thither out of all cities, and advanced before them, and came together unto him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} He answered and said unto them, Give all of you them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} He says unto them, How many loaves have all of you? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And they did all eat, and were filled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And immediately he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he comes unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and says unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} And when they were come out of the ship, immediately they knew him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And anywhere he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.\par

{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} this; carpenter; James; Juda; Simon; offended \textsuperscript{7} the twelve;, two and; power \textsuperscript{8} take; save Matthew says that they were to take "neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves; " but this precept plainly means, "Go just as you are; take no other coat, shoes, or staff than what you already have." money "The word signifieth a piece of brass money in value something less than a farthing., but here it is taken in general for money." \textsuperscript{9} be shod sandals The sandal consisted only of a sole, fastened about the foot and ankle with straps. \textsuperscript{11} whosoever; It shall; and Gr. or in the day \textsuperscript{15} it is Elias, ; Elijah, ; a prophet \textsuperscript{19} Herodias; a quarrel or, an inward grudge \textsuperscript{20} feared; observed him or, kept him, or saved him and heard \textsuperscript{27} the king an executioner or, one of his guard, Σπεκουλατωρ, in Latin, speculator, from speculor, to look about, spy, properly denotes a sentinel; and as these sentinels kept guard at the palaces of kings, and the residences of Roman governors, so they were employed in other offices besides guarding, and usually performed that of executioners. As, however, we learn from Josephus, that Herod was at this very time engaged in war with Aretas, king of Arabia, in consequence of Herod's having divorced his daughter in order to marry Herodias, his brother Philip's wife; and as this event occurred at an entertainment given at the castle of Machaerus, while his army was on its march against his father-in-law; we are furnished with an additional reason why a speculator, or sentinel, should have been employed as an executioner; and are thus enabled to discover such a latent and undesigned coincidence as clearly evinces the truth of the evangelical narrative. \textsuperscript{37} give; Shall; pennyworth "The Roman penny is sevenpence halfpenny; as, marg." \textsuperscript{40} by hundreds It is generally supposed that they were so arranged as to be a hundred in rank, or depth, and fifty in front, or file; which would make the number just five thousand, and will reconcile this account with Luke's, who only speaks of their sitting down by fifties. \textsuperscript{45} straightway; unto Bethsaida or, over against Bethsaida, Bethsaida, according to Josephus, was situated on the sea of Gennesaret, in the lower Gaulonitis (consequently on the east of the lake, as Pliny states), and at the beginning of the mountainous country; and it was raised from a village to the honour of a city by Philip, and called Julias in honour of the emperor's daughter. Some learned men, however, are of opinion that the Bethsaida mentioned in the gospels was a different place; and that it was situated on the western shore of the sea of Tiberias, in Galilee, near Chorazin and Capernaum, with which it is associated (, . ); and Bishop Pococke mentions the ruins of a town or large village in the plain of Huttin, about two miles west of the lake, still bearing the name of Baitsida, which he thinks occupies its site. \textsuperscript{48} he saw; the fourth; he cometh; would \textsuperscript{56} they laid touch; the border; him or, it\par}

\subsection*{Mark 7}
\markright{MARK 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashed, hands, they found fault. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands often, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brazen vessels, and of tables. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not your disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He answered and said unto them, Well has Isaiah prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Nevertheless in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For laying aside the commandment of God, all of you hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things all of you do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said unto them, Full well all of you reject the commandment of God, that all of you may keep your own tradition. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For Moses said, Honour your father and your mother; and, Whoso curses father or mother, let him die the death: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But all of you say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever you might be profited by me; he shall be free. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And all of you suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Making the word (o. logos) of God of no effect through your tradition, which all of you have delivered: and many such like things do all of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} If any man have ears to hear, let him hear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he says unto them, Are all of you so without understanding also? Do all of you not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without enters into the man, it cannot defile him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Because it enters not into his heart, but into the belly, and goes out into the draught, purging all meats? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said, That which comes out of the man, that defiles the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All these evil things come from within, and defile the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, (o. pneuma) heard of him, and came and fell at his feet: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it unto the dogs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he said unto her, For this saying (o. logos) go your way; the devil is gone out of your daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an barrier in his speech; and they plead to him to put his hand upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and says unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He has done all things well: he makes both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} defiled or, common, they found \textsuperscript{3} oft or, diligently, Gr. With the fist, Up to the elbow, Theophylact. Πυγμη, the fist; which Dr. Lightfoot illustrates by a tradition from the Talmudical tracts, that when they washed their hands, they washed the fist up to the joint of the arm, ςγ τψχ . The Jews laid great stress on these washings, or baptisms, βαπτισμους, considering eating with unwashen hands no ordinary crime, and feigning that an evil spirit, called Shibta, has a right to sit on the food of him who thus eats, and render it hurtful. the tradition \textsuperscript{4} except; pots "Gr. Sextarius; about a pint and a half." tables or, beds \textsuperscript{11} It is Corban Rather, "Let it be a corban " a formula common among the Jews on such occasions; by which the Pharisees released a child from supporting his parents; and even deemed it sacrilege if he afterwards gave anything for their use. \textsuperscript{15} There Though it is very true, says Dr. Doddridge, that a man may bring guilt upon himself by eating to excess, and a Jew, by eating what was forbidden by the Mosaic law; yet still the pollution would arise from the wickedness of the heart, and be just proportionable to it, which is all our Lord asserts. nothing;, ; but \textsuperscript{22} covetousness, wickedness Gr. covetousnesses, wickednesses an evil, ; pride; foolishness \textsuperscript{26} Greek or, Gentile; a Syrophenician \textsuperscript{33} he took; put This was clearly a symbolical action; for these remedies evidently could not, by their natural efficacy, avail to produce so wonderful an effect. As the ears of the deaf appear closed, he applies his fingers to intimate that he would open them; and as the tongue of the dumb seems to be tied, or to cleave to the palate, he touches it, to intimate he would give loose and free motion to it. He accommodated himself to the weakness of those who might not indeed doubt his power, but fancy some external sign was requisite to healing. It was also thus made manifest, that this salutiferous power came from Himself, and that He who by one word, εφφαθα, had healed the man, must be Divine. \textsuperscript{34} looking; he sighed; Ephphatha, Be opened \textsuperscript{37} were, ;, He hath; he maketh\par}

\subsection*{Mark 8}
\markright{MARK 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and says unto them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he asked them, How many loaves have all of you? And they said, Seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken food that was left seven baskets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And immediately he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he sighed deeply in his spirit, (o. pneuma) and says, Why does this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when Jesus knew it, he says unto them, Why reason all of you, because all of you have no bread? perceive all of you not yet, neither understand? have all of you your heart yet hardened? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Having eyes, see all of you not? and having ears, hear all of you not? and do all of you not remember? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took all of you up? They say unto him, Twelve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took all of you up? And they said, Seven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said unto them, How is it that all of you do not understand? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he comes to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And they answered, John the Baptist; but some say, Elijah; and others, One of the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he says unto them, But whom say all of you that I am? And Peter answers and says unto him, You are the Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And he charged them that they should tell no man of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And he spoke that saying (o. logos) openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get you behind me, Satan: for you savour not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's, the same shall save it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words (o. logos) in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{8} and were This was another incontestable miracle - four thousand men, besides women and children ( ), fed with seven loaves (or rather cakes) and a few small fishes! Here there must have been a manifest creation of substance - for, they all ate, and were filled.; , ; they took \textsuperscript{10} straightway Dalmanutha is supposed to have been a town east of the sea of Gennesaret, in the district of Magdala, and not far from the city of that name. \textsuperscript{15} he charged; Take; the leaven of the; of Herod \textsuperscript{22} Bethsaida; they bring, to touch \textsuperscript{31} he began; , rejected; , and after \textsuperscript{33} turned; he rebuked; Get; savourest; *Gr: \textsuperscript{38} ashamed; , ; adulterous; the Son;, ;, when\par}

\subsection*{Mark 9}
\markright{MARK 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And after six days Jesus takes with him Peter, and James, and John, and leads them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no launderer on earth can white them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there appeared unto them Elijah with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For he knows not what to say; for they were sore afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they kept that saying (o. logos) with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elijah must first come? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And he answered and told them, Elijah verily comes first, and restores all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But I say unto you, That Elijah is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And immediately all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And he asked the scribes, What question all of you with them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto you my son, which has a dumb spirit; (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And where ever he takes him, he tears him: and he foams, and gnashes with his teeth, and pins away: and I spoke to your disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He answers him, and says, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, immediately the spirit (o. pneuma) tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And frequently it has cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if you can do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Jesus said unto him, If you can believe, all things are possible to him that believes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And immediately the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help you mine unbelief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, (o. pneuma) saying unto him, You dumb and deaf spirit, (o. pneuma) I charge you, come out of him, and enter no more into him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But they understood not that saying, (o. rhema) and were afraid to ask him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house he asked them, What was it that all of you disputed among yourselves by the way? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who should be the greatest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And he sat down, and called the twelve, and says unto them, If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receives me: and whosoever shall receive me, receives not me, but him that sent me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in your name, and he follows not us: and we forbad him, because he follows not us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For he that is not against us is on our part. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because all of you belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And if your hand offend you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter into life physically disabled, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And if your foot offend you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And if yours eye offend you, pluck it out: it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltiness, wherewith will all of you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} after; Peter; an high; transfigured \textsuperscript{4} appeared;, ; Elias Moses was the founder of the Jewish polity, and Elias the most zealous reformer and prophet of the Jewish church; and their presence implied that the ministry of Christ was attested by the law and the prophets., Elijah Moses \textsuperscript{16} What; with them or, among yourselves \textsuperscript{18} teareth him or, dasheth him; he foameth As these symptoms accord very much with those of epileptic persons, some have ventured to assert that it was no real possession; but the evangelist expressly affirms that he had a "dumb spirit" which tare him, that our Lord charged him to "come out of him, " etc.; gnasheth; and they \textsuperscript{25} he rebuked; thou If this had been only a natural disease, as some have contended, could our Lord with any propriety have thus addressed it? If the demoniacal possession had been false, or merely a vulgar error, would our Lord, the Revealer of truth, have thus established falsehood, sanctioned error, or encouraged deception, by teaching men to ascribe effects to the malice and power of evil spirits, which they had no agency in producing? Impossible! Such conduct is utterly unworthy the sacred character of the Redeemer.; I charge \textsuperscript{43} if; offend thee or, cause thee to offend, and so, maimed \textsuperscript{44} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 66:24 And they shall go forth, and see the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched; and they shall be a spectacle to all flesh.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 66:24 And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” \textsuperscript{47} thine; offend thee or, cause thee to offend, *marg. \textsuperscript{50} is good; Have salt; have peace\par}
