\subsection*{Acts 19}
\markright{ACTS 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He said unto them, Have all of you received the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) since all of you believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he said unto them, Unto what then were all of you baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) came on them; and they spoke with tongues, and prophesied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And all the men were about twelve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And he went into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spoke evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word (o. logos) of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits (o. pneuma) went out of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits (o. pneuma) the name of the LORD Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the evil spirit (o. pneuma) answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are all of you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the man in whom the evil spirit (o. pneuma) was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And many that believed came, and confessed, and showed their deeds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So mightily grew the word (o. logos) of God and prevailed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, (o. pneuma) when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the same time there arose no small stir about that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, all of you know that by this craft we have our wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Moreover all of you see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nothing; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused: and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And when the public clerk had appeased the people, he said, All of you men of Ephesus, what man is there that knows not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, all of you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} For all of you have brought here these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter (o. logos) against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them sue one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But if all of you enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account (o. logos) of this concourse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{22} Name meaning: Erastus (Erastos) — Beloved Beloved city treasurer who served Paul. \textsuperscript{29} Name meaning: Gaius (Gaius) — Rejoice; happy Hospitable host who brought joy to the Church. Name meaning: Aristarchus (Aristarchos) — Best ruler Loyal companion and fellow prisoner. \textsuperscript{33} Name meaning: Alexander (Alexandros) — Defender of men The coppersmith who strongly opposed Paul.\par}

\subsection*{Acts 20}
\markright{ACTS 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed in order to go into Macedonia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, (o. logos) he came into Greece, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} These going before tarried for us at Troas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the next day; and continued his speech (o. logos) until midnight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third upper room, and was taken up dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And we went on board ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go on foot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And we sailed thence, and came the next day opposite to Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And when they were come to him, he said unto them, All of you know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Serving the LORD with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have showed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit (o. pneuma) unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Save that the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) witnesses in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But none of these things (o. logos) move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And now, behold, I know that all of you all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) has made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he has purchased with his own blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word (o. logos) of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Yea, all of you yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} I have showed you all things, how that so labouring all of you ought to support the weak, and to remember the words (o. logos) of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Sorrowing most of all for the words (o. logos) which he spoke, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.\par

\subsection*{Acts 21}
\markright{ACTS 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it came to pass, that after we were got from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unload her burden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, (o. pneuma) that he should not go up to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus says the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owns this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then Paul answered, What mean all of you to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they are informed of you, that you teach all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} What is it therefore? the multitude must essentially come together: for they will hear that you are come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Do therefore this that we say to you: We have four men which have a vow on them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Them take, and purify yourself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning you, are nothing; but that you yourself also walk orderly, and keep the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} As concerning the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teaches all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and has polluted this holy place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto you? Who said, Can you speak Greek? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Are not you that Egyptian, which before these days made an uproar, and led out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I plead to you, suffer me to speak unto the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spoke unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,\par

Rhodes. Rhodes is a celebrated island in the same sea, southward of Caria, from which it is distant about twenty miles, next to Cyprus and Lesbos in extent, being 120 miles in circumference. It was remarkable for the clearness of the air, and its pleasant and healthy climate, and chiefly for its Colossus of brass, seventy cubits high, with each finger as large as an ordinary man, standing astride over the mouth of the harbour, so that ships in full sail passed between its legs. \textsuperscript{5} and they, with; we kneeled \textsuperscript{8} we that, Caesarea, Philip, the evangelist \textsuperscript{11} he took; Thus, ; So shall, ; and shall \textsuperscript{16} of the, Cyprus, an old \textsuperscript{20} they glorified;, ; how, ; thousands *Gr. and they \textsuperscript{24} and purify; that they;, ; but \textsuperscript{27} the Jews stirred, ; and laid \textsuperscript{38} that "This Egyptian rose ad 55." \textsuperscript{39} I am, Cilicia, a citizen, suffer \textsuperscript{40} on; and beckoned, a great Hebrew\par}

\subsection*{Acts 22}
\markright{ACTS 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Men, brethren, and fathers, hear all of you my defence which I make now unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} (And when they heard that he spoke in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he says,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as all of you all are this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} As also the high priest does bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, in order to be punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And I said, What shall I do, LORD? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told you of all things which are appointed for you to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive your sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen you, that you should know his will, and see that Just One, and should hear the voice of his mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For you shall be his witness unto all men of what you have seen and heard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And now why tarry you? arise, and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get you quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive your testimony concerning me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send you far behind unto the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they gave him audience unto this word, (o. logos) and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do: for this man is a Roman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then immediately they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} On the next day, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} Jew; in Tarsus, a city, ; at;, Gamaliel taught; was \textsuperscript{5} also, and all; the brethren \textsuperscript{6} that It is evident that the apostle considered his extraordinary conversion as a most complete demonstration of the truth of Christianity; and when all the particulars of his education, his previous religious principles, his zeal, his enmity against Christians, and his prospects of secular honours and preferments by persecuting them, are compared with the subsequent part of his life, and the sudden transition from a furious persecutor to a zealous preacher of the gospel, in which he laboured and suffered to the end of his life, and for which he died a martyr, it must convince every candid and impartial person that no rational account can be given of this change, except what he himself assigns; and consequently, if that be true, that Christianity is Divine. that, Damascus; about \textsuperscript{14} The God, ; hath; and see, ; that; hear \textsuperscript{24} The chief As the chief captain did not understand Hebrew, he was ignorant of the charge against Paul, and also of the defence which the apostle had made; but as he saw that they grew more and more outrageous, he supposed that Paul must have given them the highest provocation, and therefore, according to the barbarous and irrational practice which has existed in all countries, he determined to put him to the torture, in order to make him confess his crime., that he should \textsuperscript{25} the centurion, ; Is it By the Roman law, no magistrate was allowed to punish a Roman citizen capitally, or by inflicting stripes, or even binding him; and the single expression, I am a Roman citizen, arrested their severest decrees, and obtained, if not an escape, at least a delay of his punishment. \textsuperscript{28} But It is extremely probable that the inhabitants of Tarsus, born in that city, had the same rights and privileges as Roman citizens, in consequence of a grant or charter from Julius Cesar, from whom it was called Juliopolis. But if this were not the case, St. Paul's father, or some of his ancestors, might have been rewarded with the freedom of the city of Rome, for his fidelity and bravery in some military service, as Josephus says several of the Jews were; or his father might have obtained it by purchase, as in the instance of the chief captain. \textsuperscript{29} examined him or, tortured him; the chief\par}

\subsection*{Acts 23}
\markright{ACTS 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to strike him on the mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Then said Paul unto him, God shall strike you, you whitewashed wall: for sit you to judge me after the law, and command me to be smitten contrary to the law? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they that stood by said, Revile you God's high priest? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then said Paul, I know not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: (o. pneuma) but the Pharisees confess both. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit (o. pneuma) or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must you bear witness also at Rome. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Now therefore all of you with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you tomorrow, as though all of you would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, before even he comes near, are ready to kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he has a certain thing to tell him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto you, who has something to say unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring down Paul tomorrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But do not you yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See you tell no man that you have showed these things to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And he wrote a letter after this manner: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sends greeting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent immediately to you, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} On the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} I will hear you, said he, when yours accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{24} Name meaning: Felix (Felix) — Happy; fortunate Trembled before the truth yet never found true happiness.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} God did smite him in a remarkable manner; for about five years after this, after his house had been reduced to ashes, in a tumult raised by his own son, he was besieged and taken in the royal palace; where having attempted in vain to hide himself, he was dragged out and slain. thou whited for; smitten \textsuperscript{5} I wist Soon after the holding of the first council at Jerusalem, Ananias, son of Nebedenus, was deprived of the high priest's office, for certain acts of violence, and sent to Rome, whence he was afterwards released, and returned to Jerusalem. Between the death of Jonathan, who succeeded him and was murdered by Felix, and the high priesthood of Ismael, who was invested with that office by Agrippa, an interval elapsed in which this dignity was vacant. This was the precise time when Paul was apprehended; and the Sanhedrin being destitute of a president, Ananias undertook to discharge the office. It is probable that Paul was ignorant of this circumstance. Thou NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Exodus 22:28 Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor speak ill of the ruler of thy people.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Exodus 22:28 Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.” \textsuperscript{6} Paul I am; of the hope \textsuperscript{11} the Lord, ; Be; for, ; must \textsuperscript{12} certain, ; bound; under a curse or, with an oath of execration; *Gr:; that Such execrable vows as these were not unusual among the Jews, who, from their perverted traditions, challenged to themselves a right of punishing without any legal process, those whom they considered transgressors of the law; and in some cases, as in the case of one who had forsaken the law of Moses, they thought they were justified in killing them. They therefore made no scruple of acquainting the chief priests and elders with their conspiracy against the life of Paul, and applying for their connivance and support; who, being chiefly of the sect of the Sadducees, and the apostle's bitterest enemies, were so far from blaming them for it, that they gladly aided and abetted them in this mode of dispatching him, and on its failure they soon afterwards determined upon making a similar attempt ( ). If these were, in their bad way, conscientious men, they were under no necessity of perishing for hunger, when the providence of God had hindered them from accomplishing their vow; for their vows of abstinence from eating and drinking were as easy to loose as to bind, any of their wise men or Rabbis having power to absolve them, as Dr. Lightfoot has shown from the Talmud. \textsuperscript{21} do not for, ; an oath \textsuperscript{23} two centurions at About nine o'clock in the evening, for the greater secrecy, and to elude the cunning, active malice of the Jews. \textsuperscript{30} it was and gave, Farewell\par}

\subsection*{Acts 24}
\markright{ACTS 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by your providence, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Notwithstanding, that I be not wearisome anymore unto you, I pray you that you would hear us of your clemency a few words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who also has gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Commanding his accusers to come unto you: by examining of whom yourself may take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that you have been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Because that you may understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem in order to worship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But this I confess unto you, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void to offence toward God, and toward men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Who ought to have been here before you, and object, if they had ought against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And as he reasoned of righteousness, wilful restrain, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: enkrateia (ἐγκράτεια) = self-control. Common English renderings: temperance. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament. \textsuperscript{27} Name meaning: Festus (Festus) — Festive; joyful Roman governor who heard Paul’s defense.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} Seeing Felix, bad as he was, had certainly rendered some services to Judaea. He had entirely subdued a very formidable banditti which had infested the country, and sent their captain, Eliezar, to Rome; had suppressed the sedition raised by the Egyptian impostor ( ); and had quelled a very afflictive disturbance which took place between the Syrians and Jews of Cesarea. But, though Tertullus might truly say, "by thee we enjoy great quietness, " yet it is evident that he was guilty of the grossest flattery, as we have seen both from his own historians and Josephus, that he was both a bad man and a bad governor. \textsuperscript{5} we have, ; and a mover; , ; the sect *Gr:, ; *Gr. \subsection*{Acts 25}
\markright{ACTS 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as you very well know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shall you go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore, when they were come here, without any delay on the next day I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And on the next day, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, all of you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not likewise to signify the crimes laid against him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{13} Name meaning: Agrippa (Agrippas) — Wild horse Heard the gospel but remained untamed. Name meaning: Bernice (Bernike) — Bringer of victory Present at Paul’s trial.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} into the province By the province, Judea is meant; for after the death of Herod Agrippa, Claudius thought it imprudent to trust the government in the hands of his son Agrippa, who was then but seventeen years of age; and therefore, Cuspius Fadus was sent to be procurator. And when afterwards Claudius had given to Agrippa the tetrarchy of Philip, he nevertheless kept the province of Judea in his own hands, and governed it by procurators sent from Rome. he \textsuperscript{6} more than ten days or, as some copies read no more than eight or ten days sitting \textsuperscript{10} I stand Every procurator represented the emperor in the province over which he presided; and as the seat of government was at Cesarea, St. Paul was before the tribunal where, as a Roman citizen, he ought to be judged., as thou \textsuperscript{11} if I; no man; I appeal An appeal to the emperor was the right of a Roman citizen, and was highly respected. The Julian law condemned those magistrates, and others, as violaters of the public peace, who had put to death, tortured, scourged, imprisoned, or condemned any Roman citizen who had appealed to Cesar. This law was so sacred and imperative, that, in the persecution under Trajan, Pliny would not attempt to put to death Roman citizens, who were proved to have turned Christians, but determined to send them to Rome, probably because they had appealed. \textsuperscript{16} It is not and have \textsuperscript{20} doubted of such manner of questions or, was doubtful how to enquire hereof, etc I asked \textsuperscript{21} had; hearing or, judgment Augustus; I commanded \textsuperscript{24} King Agrippa King Agrippa was the son of Herod Agrippa; who upon the death of his uncle Herod, king of Chalcis, ad 28, succeeded to his dominions, by the favour of the emperor Claudius. Four years afterwards, Claudius removed him from that kingdom to a larger one; giving him the tetrarchy of Philip, that of Lysanias, and the province which Varus governed. Nero afterwards added Julias in Peraea, Tarichaea, and Tiberias. Claudius gave him the power of appointing the high priest among the Jews; and instances of his exercising this power may be seen in Josephus. He was strongly attached to the Romans, and did every thing in his power to prevent the Jews from rebelling; and when he could not prevail, he united his troops to those of Titus, and assisted at the siege of Jerusalem. After the ruin of his country, he retired with his sister Berenice to Rome where he died, aged 70, about ad 90. about, that he \textsuperscript{25} committed, ; and that Augustus The honourable title of Σεβαστος, or Augustus, that is venerable or august, which was first conferred by the senate on Octavius Caesar, was afterwards assumed by succeeding Roman emperors.\par}

\subsection*{Acts 26}
\markright{ACTS 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Agrippa said unto Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you concerning all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I plead to you to hear me patiently. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God, unto our fathers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I punished them often in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? it is hard for you to kick against the pricks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But rise, and stand upon your feet: for I have appeared unto you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But showed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should show light unto the people, and to the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And as he thus spoke for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are out of your mind; much learning does make you mad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words (o. rhema) of truth and soberness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} King Agrippa, believe you the prophets? I know that you believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost you persuade me to be a Christian. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Paul said, I would to God, that not only you, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: sōphrosynē (σωφροσύνη) = soundness of mind; sobriety. Common English renderings: soberness. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

\subsection*{Acts 27}
\markright{ACTS 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously pleaded Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come opposite to Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, opposite to Salmone; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh unto which was the city of Lasea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Which when they had taken up, they used support cables, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksand, strake sail, and so were driven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the third day we cast out with our own hands the cordage of the ship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, all of you should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Saying, Fear not, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God has given you all them that sail with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Nevertheless we must be cast upon a certain island. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the sailors deemed that they drew near to some country; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And as the sailors were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the bow, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, all of you cannot be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that all of you have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Wherefore I pray you to take some food: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the front part stuck fast, and remained immoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.\par

Salmone, now Salamina, was a city and cape on the east of the island of Crete. \textsuperscript{8} The fair havens The Fair Havens, still known by the same name, was a port on the south-eastern part of Crete, near Lasea, of which nothing now remains. \textsuperscript{9} the fast "The fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month." \textsuperscript{10} I perceive, ; damage or, injury \textsuperscript{12} the haven; Phenice, was a sea-port on the western side of Crete; probably defended from the fury of the winds by a high and winding shore, forming a semicircle, and perhaps by some small island in front; leaving two openings, one towards the south-west, and the other towards the north-west. Crete \textsuperscript{14} not; arose or beat a tempestuous; Euroclydon Probably, as Dr. Shaw supposes, one of those tempestuous winds called levanters, which blow in all directions, from ne round by e to se \textsuperscript{16} Clauda, called Cauda and Gaudos by Mela and Pliny, and Claudos by Ptolemy, and now Gozo, according to Dr. Shaw, is a small island, situated at the south-western extremity of the island of Crete. \textsuperscript{27} the fourteenth Adria strictly speaking, was the name of the Adriatic gulf, now the Gulf of Venice, an arm of the Mediterranean, about 400 miles long and 140 broad, stretching along the eastern shores of Italy on one side, and Dalmatia, Sclavonia, and Macedonia on the other. But the term Adria was extended far beyond the limits of this gulf, and appears to have been given to an indeterminate extent of sea, as we say, generally, the Levant. It is observable, that the sacred historian does not say "in the Adriatic gulf, " but "in Adria, " (that is, the Adriatic sea, πελαγος being understood); which, says Hesychius, was the same as the Ionian sea; and Strabo says that the Ionian gulf "is a part of that now called the Adriatic." But not only the Ionian, but even the Sicilian sea, and part of that which washes Crete, were called the Adriatic. Thus the scholiast on Dionysius Periegetis says, "they call this Sicilian sea Adria." And Ptolemy says that Sicily was bounded on the east by the Adriatic, υπο, Αδριοι, and that Crete was bounded on the west by the Adriatic sea, υπο, του, Αδριατικον πελαγος . the shipmen \textsuperscript{38} they lightened; The wheat The Romans imported corn from Egypt, by way of Alexandria, to which this ship belonged; for a curious account of which see Bryant's treatise on the Euroclydon. \textsuperscript{40} taken up etc. or, cut the anchors, they left them in the sea, etc. the rudder bands Or, "the bands of the rudders; " for large vessels in ancient times had two or more rudders, which were fastened to the ship by means of bands, or chains, by which they were hoisted out of the water when incapable of being used. These bands being loosed, the rudders would fall into their proper places, and serve to steer the vessel into the creek, which they had in view, and hoisted. \textsuperscript{44} that; land Melita, now Malta, the island on which Paul and his companions were cast, is situate in the Mediterranean sea, about fifty miles from the coast of Sicily, towards Africa; and is one immense rock of soft white free-stone, twenty miles long, twelve in its greatest breadth, and sixty in circumference. Some, however, with the learned Jacob Bryant, are of opinion that this island was Melita in the Adriatic gulf, near Illyricum; but it may be sufficient to observe, that the course of the Alexandrian ship, first to Syracuse and then to Rhegium, proves that it was the present Malta, as the proper course from the Illyrian Melita would have been first to Rhegium, before it reached Syracuse, to which indeed it need not have gone at all.\par}
