\subsection*{Acts 28}
\markright{ACTS 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the natives people showed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Nevertheless they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a dysentery: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning you, neither any of the brethren that came showed or spoke any harm of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But we desire to hear of you what you think: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, (o. rhema) Well spoke the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) by Isaiah the prophet unto our fathers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing all of you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing all of you shall see, and not perceive: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.\par

\section*{Romans Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and the church has always received Romans as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The book explicitly names Paul and coheres with Acts and the Pauline corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 56-57 from Corinth\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Paul's fullest doctrinal letter, written to the believers in Rome before his visit there.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To set forth the righteousness of God in the gospel and unify Jew and Gentile believers in Christ.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} righteousness; justification; union with Christ; Israel; sanctification; gospel\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Guilt and justification 1-5; sanctification 6-8; Israel and God's plan 9-11; practical exhortation 12-16.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 46 ca. AD 200 | Subst. Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial Romans witness ca. AD 200 | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek Romans 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in 1 Clement by Clement of Rome (late 1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Romans is textually well attested and theologically central, with some variation in closing doxology placement.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Romans as Paul's Spirit-inspired magisterial exposition of the gospel.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Romans}
\markboth{ROMANS}{}
\subsection*{Romans 1}
\markright{ROMANS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} (Which he had promised before by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit (o. pneuma) of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Among whom are all of you also the called of Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit (o. pneuma) in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end all of you may be established; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let until now,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believes; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God has showed it unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, ill will; whisperers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Without understanding, covenant-breakers, without natural affection, refusing to reconcile, unmerciful: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: charisma (χάρισμα) = gift of grace. Common English renderings: gift. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

\subsection*{Romans 2}
\markright{ROMANS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, whosoever you are that judge: for wherein you judge another, you condemn yourself; for you that judge do the same things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And think you this, O man, that judge them which do such things, and do the same, that you shall escape the judgment of God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Or despise you the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But after your hardness and refusing to repent heart treasure up unto yourself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who will render to every man according to his deeds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that does evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For there is no respect of persons with God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Which show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Behold, you are called a Jew, and rest in the law, and make your boast of God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And know his will, and approve the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} You therefore which teach another, teach you not yourself? you that preach a man should not steal, do you steal? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} You that says a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? you that abhor idols, do you commit sacrilege? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} You that make your boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonour you God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For circumcision verily profits, if you keep the law: but if you be a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfill the law, judge you, who by the letter and circumcision do transgress the law? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, (o. pneuma) and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: prosōpolēmpsia (προσωπολημψία) = partiality; favoritism. Common English renderings: respect of persons. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

\subsection*{Romans 3}
\markright{ROMANS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} What advantage then has the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That you might be justified in your sayings, (o. logos) and might overcome when you are judged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who takes vengeance? (I speak as a man) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For if the truth of God has more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} There is none that understands, there is none that seeks after God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} They are all gone out of the way, they are together become useless; there is none that does good, no, not one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Their throat is an open tomb; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Their feet are swift to shed blood: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Destruction and misery are in their ways: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the way of peace have they not known: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} There is no fear of God before their eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now we know that what things whatsoever the law says, it says to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whom God has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believes in Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.\par

\subsection*{Romans 4}
\markright{ROMANS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, has found? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For if Abraham were justified by works, he has whereof to glory; but not before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For what says the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now to him that works is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But to him that works not, but believes on him that justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Even as David also describes the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputes righteousness without works, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Comes this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of no effect: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Because the law works wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} (As it is written, I have made you a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who replenishes life to the dead, and calls those things which be not as though they were. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall your seed be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{25} Gk. vocab: dikaiōsis (δικαίωσις) = justification; acquittal. Common English renderings: justification. A judicial term closely related to justification in Pauline theology.\par}

\subsection*{Romans 5}
\markright{ROMANS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation works patience; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And patience, experience; and experience, hope: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And hope makes not ashamed; because the love (o. agape) of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) which is given unto us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet possibly for a good man some would even dare to die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But God commends his love (o. agape) toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the embodiment of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, has abounded unto many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} That as sin has reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: katallagē (καταλλαγή) = reconciliation. Common English renderings: reconciliation. A major Pauline salvation term for restored relation with God. \textsuperscript{16} Gk. vocab: katakrima (κατάκριμα) = condemnation. Common English renderings: condemnation. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} By whom, ; wherein, ; and rejoice, ; the glory \textsuperscript{6} For; without; in due time or, according to the time; Christ; ungodly \textsuperscript{10} when; reconciled *marg.; we shall \textsuperscript{11} but we;, ; by whom; atonement or, reconciliation \textsuperscript{12} as by; and death; for that or, in whom all \textsuperscript{14} death;, ; even; who is the figure Or "type (pattern, or resemblance, τυπον ), of him who was to come, " i.e., THE MESSIAH. \subsection*{Romans 6}
\markright{ROMANS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Know all of you not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For he that is dead is freed from sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dies no more; death has no more dominion over him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he lives, he lives unto God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Likewise reckon all of you also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that all of you should obey it in the lusts thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither yield all of you your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For sin shall not have dominion over you: for all of you are not under the law, but under grace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Know all of you not, that to whom all of you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants all of you are to whom all of you obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But God be thanked, that all of you were the servants of sin, but all of you have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Being then made free from sin, all of you became the servants of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as all of you have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For when all of you were the servants of sin, all of you were free from righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} What fruit had all of you then in those things whereof all of you are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, all of you have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.\par

\subsection*{Romans 7}
\markright{ROMANS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Know all of you not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law has dominion over a man as long as he lives? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the woman which has an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he lives; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So then if, while her husband lives, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Wherefore, my brethren, all of you also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that all of you should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, (o. pneuma) and not in the oldness of the letter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, You shall not covet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwells in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwells no good thing: in order to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwells in me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For I delight in the law of God after the inward man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: sarkikos (σαρκικός) = fleshly; carnal. Common English renderings: carnal; fleshly. In Paul this often contrasts life shaped by the flesh with life shaped by the Spirit.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Know brethren, them that; the law, a man Or, person, either man or woman; ανθρωπος and homo having this extent of signification. \textsuperscript{2} the woman Rather, a woman. The apostle here illustrates the position laid down in the preceding verse by a familiar instance. \textsuperscript{4} ye also, ; the body; that ye; that we \textsuperscript{5} in the flesh; motions Gr. passions, *Gr. which, ; did work; members, ; bring \textsuperscript{6} But;, that being dead or, being dead to that, serve \textsuperscript{7} What, is the law, ; I had; lust or, concupiscence; Thou shalt \textsuperscript{8} sin, wrought For without etc. Rather, "For without a law sin is dead." Where there is no law, there is no transgression; for sin is the transgression of the law. The very essence of sin consists in the violation of some positive law. \textsuperscript{9} For I;, ; without; but; sin, and I died, *marg. \textsuperscript{14} the law; but; carnal; sold \textsuperscript{15} For that; allow or, know; what;, ; what I hate \textsuperscript{17} it is no more; sin \textsuperscript{18} that in me; in my, ; for to will \textsuperscript{24} wretched;, ; who;, ; the body of this or, this body of\par}

\subsection*{Romans 8}
\markright{ROMANS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For the law of the Spirit (o. pneuma) of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit (o. pneuma) the things of the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In order to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually (o. pneuma) minded is life and peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But all of you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) if so be that the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit (o. pneuma) of Christ, he is none of his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit (o. pneuma) is life because of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But if the Spirit (o. pneuma) of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also retore life in your mortal bodies by his Spirit (o. pneuma) that dwells in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For if all of you live after the flesh, all of you shall die: but if all of you through the Spirit (o. pneuma) do mortify the deeds of the body, all of you shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For as many as are led by the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God, they are the sons of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For all of you have not received the spirit (o. pneuma) of bondage again to fear; but all of you have received the Spirit (o. pneuma) of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The Spirit (o. pneuma) itself bears witness with our spirit, (o. pneuma) that we are the children of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the earn expectation of the creature waits for the manifestation of the sons of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who has subjected the same in hope, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For we know that the whole creation groans and labors in pain together until now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first-fruits of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to know, the redemption of our body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man sees, why does he yet hope for? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Likewise the Spirit (o. pneuma) also helps our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit (o. pneuma) itself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And he that searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) because he makes intercession for the saints according to the will of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Who is he that condemns? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that has risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Who shall separate us from the love (o. agape) of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} As it is written, For your sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love (o. agape) of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{6} Gk. vocab: phronēma (φρόνημα) = mindset; way of thinking. Common English renderings: mind. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament. \textsuperscript{15} Gk. vocab: huiothesia (υἱοθεσία) = adoption as a son. Common English renderings: adoption. A distinctly Pauline term for filial adoption and inheritance.\par}

\subsection*{Romans 9}
\markright{ROMANS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who are Israelites; to whom pertains the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Not as though the word (o. logos) of God has taken no effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall your seed be called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For this is the word (o. logos) of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calls;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For he says to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So then it is not of him that wills, nor of him that runs, but of God that shows mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the scripture says unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised you up, that I might show my power in you, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore has he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You will say then unto me, Why does he yet find fault? For who has resisted his will? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} On the contrary; O man, who are you that reply against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why have you made me thus? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Has not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had before prepared unto glory, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Even us, whom he has called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} As he says also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, All of you are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Isaiah also cries concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For he will finish the work, (o. logos) and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work (o. logos) will the Lord make upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And as Isaiah said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumbling stone; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumbling stone and rock of offence: and whosoever believes on him shall not be ashamed.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{11} Gk. vocab: eklogē (ἐκλογή) = choice; election. Common English renderings: election. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} I could were; , accursed or, separated my kinsmen \textsuperscript{4} are Israelites; the adoption; and the glory; covenants or, testaments, ; the giving; the service; promises \textsuperscript{5} are the fathers; of whom; who is; blessed; Amen \textsuperscript{6} as though; they are not \textsuperscript{7} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Genesis 21:12 But God said to Abraam, Let it not be hard before thee concerning the child, and concerning the bondwoman; in all things whatsoever Sarrha shall say to thee, hear her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Genesis 21:12 And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy bondwoman; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.” \textsuperscript{9} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Genesis 18:10 And he said, I will return and come to thee according to this period seasonably, and Sarrha thy wife shall have a son; and Sarrha heard at the door of the tent, being behind him. Genesis 18:14 Shall anything be impossible with the Lord? At this time I will return to thee seasonably, and Sarrha shall have a son.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Genesis 18:10 And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard [it] in the tent door, which [was] behind him. Genesis 18:14 Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.” \textsuperscript{10} not only; but when, Rebekah \textsuperscript{11} the children; that the;, ; according; not of works; but of \textsuperscript{12} The elder or, The greater; younger or, lesser NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Genesis 25:23 And the Lord said to her, There are two nations in thy womb, and two peoples shall be separated from thy belly, and one people shall excel the other, and the elder shall serve the younger.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Genesis 25:23 And the LORD said unto her, Two nations [are] in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and [the one] people shall be stronger than [the other] people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” \textsuperscript{13} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Malachi 1:2,3 I have loved you, saith the Lord. And ye said, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, and hated Esau, and laid waste his borders, and made his heritage as dwellings of the wilderness?” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Malachi 1:2,3 I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? [Was] not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” \textsuperscript{15} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Exodus 33:19 And God said, I will pass by before thee with my glory, and I will call by my name, the Lord, before thee; and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have pity on whom I will have pity.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Exodus 33:19 And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.” \textsuperscript{17} For;, Even I raised; that, ; that my NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Exodus 9:16 And for this purpose hast thou been preserved, that I might display in thee my strength, and that my name might be published in all the earth.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Exodus 9:16 And in very deed for this [cause] have I raised thee up, for to shew [in] thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.” \textsuperscript{20} O man; who art, ; repliest or, answerest again; or, disputes with God; Shall NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 29:16 Shall ye not be counted as clay of the potter? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Thou didst not form me? or the work to the maker, Thou hast not made me wisely? Isaiah 45:9 What excellent thing have I prepared as clay of the potter? Will the ploughman plough the earth all day? shall the clay say to the potter, What art thou doing that thou dost not work, nor hast hands? shall the thing formed answer him that formed it?” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 29:16 Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding? Isaiah 45:9 Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! [Let] the potsherd [strive] with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?” \textsuperscript{22} willing, ; endured; the vessels The Apostle, by employing the appellation of the vessels of wrath, carries on the similitude of the potter, by which he had illustrated the sovereignty of God.; fitted or, made up \textsuperscript{24} whom; not of the Jews \textsuperscript{25} in Osee, Hosea I will call; beloved NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Hosea 2:23 And I will sow her to me on the earth; and will love her that was not loved, and will say to that which was not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art the Lord my God. Hosea 1:10 Yet the number of the children of Israel was as the sand of the sea, which shall not be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said to them, Ye are not my people, even they shall be called the sons of the living God.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Hosea 2:23 And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to [them which were] not my people, Thou [art] my people; and they shall say, [Thou art] my God. Hosea 1:10 Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, [that] in the place where it was said unto them, Ye [are] not my people, [there] it shall be said unto them, [Ye are] the sons of the living God.” \textsuperscript{27} Esaias, Isaiah though a remnant NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 10:22,23 And though the people of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them shall be saved. He will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because the Lord will make a short work in all the world.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 10:22,23 For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, [yet] a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness. For the Lord GOD of hosts shall make a consumption, even determined, in the midst of all the land.” \textsuperscript{28} work or, account and cut; in righteousness \textsuperscript{29} Except; Sabaoth we had been; Sodoma Gomorrah NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 1:9 And if the Lord of Sabaoth had not left us a seed, we should have been as Sodoma, and we should have been made like to Gomorrha.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 1:9 Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, [and] we should have been like unto Gomorrah.” \textsuperscript{30} shall, the Gentiles, ; followed; even the righteousness \textsuperscript{33} Behold; and whosoever; ashamed or, confounded NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 8:14 And if thou shalt trust in him, he shall be to thee for a sanctuary; and ye shall not come against him as against a stumbling-stone, neither as against the falling of a rock: but the houses of Jacob are in a snare, and the dwellers in Jerusalem in a pit. Isaiah 28:16 therefore thus saith the Lord, even the Lord, Behold I lay for the foundations of Sion a costly stone, a choice, a corner-stone, a precious stone, for its foundations; and he that believes on him shall by no means be ashamed.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 8:14 And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Isaiah 28:16 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner [stone], a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.”\par}

\subsection*{Romans 10}
\markright{ROMANS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For Moses describes the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which does those things shall live by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But the righteousness which is of faith speaks likewise, Say not in yours heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But what says it? The word (o. rhema) is nigh you, even in your mouth, and in your heart: that is, the word (o. rhema) of faith, which we preach; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} That if you shall confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe in yours heart that God has raised him from the dead, you shall be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For with the heart man believes unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the scripture says, Whosoever believes on him shall not be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed our report? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word (o. rhema) of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words (o. rhema) unto the ends of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses says, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But Isaiah is very bold, and says, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But to Israel he says, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.\par
