\subsection*{1 Corinthians 7}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now concerning the things whereof all of you wrote unto me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The wife has not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband has not power of his own body, but the wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Defraud all of you not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that all of you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man has his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But to the rest speak I, not the Lord: If any brother has a wife that believes not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not put her away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the woman which has an husband that believes not, and if he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God has called us to peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For what know you, O wife, whether you shall save your husband? or how know you, O man, whether you shall save your wife? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But as God has distributed to every man, as the Lord has called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Is any man called being circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised. Is any called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Are you called being a servant? care not for it: but if you may be made free, use it rather. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For he that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lord's freeman: likewise also he that is called, being free, is Christ's servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All of you are bought with a price; be not all of you the servants of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Brethren, let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: yet I give my judgment, as one that has obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I suppose therefore that this is good for the present distress, I say, that it is good for a man so to be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Are you bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed. Are you loosed from a wife? seek not a wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But and if you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she has not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But this I say, brethren, the time is short: it remains, that both they that have wives be as though they had none; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And they that weep, as though they wept not; and they that rejoice, as though they rejoiced not; and they that buy, as though they possessed not; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passes away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried cares for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But he that is married cares for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: (o. pneuma) but she that is married cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And this I speak for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that all of you may attend upon the Lord without distraction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But if any man think that he behaves himself indecent toward his virgin, if she pass the flower of her age, and need so require, let him do what he will, he sins not: let them marry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Nevertheless he that stands steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, but has power over his own will, and has so decreed in his heart that he will keep his virgin, does well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} So then he that gives her in marriage does well; but he that gives her not in marriage does better. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} But she is happier if she so abide, after my judgment: and I think also that I have the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{7} I would St. Paul evidently gave this advice in reference to the necessities of the church, or what he calls ( ) the present distress; for it would be perfectly absurd to imagine that an inspired apostle would in the general, discountenance marriage, since it was of the greatest importance to the existence and happiness of future generations, and expressly agreeable to a Divine institution.; But \textsuperscript{15} A brother; but; to peace Gr. in peace \textsuperscript{16} O wife; how Gr. what \textsuperscript{17} as God; as the, so ordain \textsuperscript{21} being; a servant Rather, a slave, δουλος, the property of another, and bought with his money. In these verses the apostle shows that Christianity makes no change in our civil connections. care, *marg. \textsuperscript{22} is the; freeman Gr. made free is Christ's \textsuperscript{25} concerning, ; virgins The word παρθενος, as well as the Latin virgo "a virgin, " though it generally signifies a maid, frequently denotes unmarried persons of both sexes; in which sense it is evidently used here by the apostle. have, ; obtained \textsuperscript{31} use;, ; , ; for; the fashion Το, σχημα, the form or appearance. Grotius remarks that the apostle's expression is borrowed from the theatre, where το, σχημα, της σκηνης, παραγει means that the scene changes, and presents an appearance entirely new. \textsuperscript{32} I would; He that belong to the Lord Gr. of the Lord, as \textsuperscript{35} not This is an allusion to the Retiarius among the Romans, who carried a small casting net, rete which he endeavoured to throw over his adversary's head., ; comely; and that \textsuperscript{36} his virgin Some interpret this of a man's continuing in a state of celibacy, and render παρθενος, not a virgin, but virginity; but such a construction of the original appears without example. It appears most obvious to explain it of a parent, or guardian, who had the charge of a virgin; and Kypke has shown that την παρθενον αυτου is an elegant phrase for his virgin daughter. the flower and need, he sinneth \textsuperscript{38} then doeth well; doeth better \textsuperscript{40} she, I think Rather, "I judge (or consider) also that I have the Spirit of God; " for δοκειν is frequently used to express not what is doubtful, but what is true and certain.\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 8}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now as concerning things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love (o. agape) edifies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And if any man think that he knows any thing, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But if any man love God, the same is known of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Nevertheless there is not in every man that knowledge: for some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But food commends us not to God: for neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But take heed lest by any means this liberty of your's become a stumbling block to them that are weak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For if any man see you which have knowledge sit to eat in the idol's temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And through your knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But when all of you sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, all of you sin against Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Wherefore, if food make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world stands, lest I make my brother to offend.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} touching, ;, ;, we are, ; Knowledge, ;, but \textsuperscript{6} one God; , ; of whom; and we, in him or, for him, and one; and we by \textsuperscript{7} there with Rather, as Dr. Doddridge renders, "with consciousness of (some religious regard to) the idol, " as συνειδησις, and formerly conscience, also imports. \textsuperscript{8} meat; are we the better or, have we the more are we the worse or, have we the less. \textsuperscript{9} take, ; liberty or, power a stumblingblock; weak \textsuperscript{10} which hast sit; shall not; emboldened Gr. edified\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 9}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Am I not an apostle? am I not free? have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? are not all of you my work in the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are all of you in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Mine answer to them that do examine me is this, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Have we not power to eat and to drink? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Or I only and Barnabas, have not we power to forbear working? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Who goes a warfare any time at his own charges? who plants a vineyard, and eats not of the fruit thereof? or who feeds a flock, and eats not of the milk of the flock? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Say I these things as a man? or says not the law the same also? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For it is written in the law of Moses, You shall not suppress the mouth of the ox that treads out the corn. Does God take care for oxen? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Or says he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that plows should plow in hope; and that he that threshes in hope should be partaker of his hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If others be partakers of this power over you, are not we rather? Nevertheless we have not used this power; but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Do all of you not know that they which minister about holy things live of the things of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Even so has the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for it were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For though I be free from all men, yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} To them that are without law, as without law, (being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ,) that I might gain them that are without law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak: I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And this I do for the gospel's sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Know all of you not that they which run in a race run all, but one receives the prize? So run, that all of you may obtain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And every man that strives for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beats the air: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I not an, ;, ; am I not free; have;, are \textsuperscript{5} to lead; a sister; wife or, woman the brethren; Cephas \textsuperscript{7} goeth; planteth; or; eateth not of the milk \textsuperscript{9} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 25:4 Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treads out the corn.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 25:4 Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out [the corn].” \textsuperscript{12} others are not, Nevertheless; but, hinder \textsuperscript{17} if I, ; have; against; dispensation \textsuperscript{19} I be; I made; that \textsuperscript{22} To the weak; I am that I might by \textsuperscript{24} they run in; so run \textsuperscript{27} I keep, ; and lest; a castaway\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 10}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover, brethren, I would not that all of you should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And did all eat the same spiritual food; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Neither be all of you idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Neither murmur all of you, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore let him that thinks he stands take heed lest he fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} There has no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that all of you are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that all of you may be able to bear it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I speak as to wise men; judge all of you what I say. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Behold Israel after the flesh: are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} What say I then? that the idol is any thing, or that which is offered in sacrifice to idols is any thing? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But I say, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that all of you should have fellowship with devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} All of you cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: all of you cannot be partakers of the Lord's table, and of the table of devils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than he? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For the earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and all of you be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that showed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Conscience, I say, not yours own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Whether therefore all of you eat, or drink, or whatsoever all of you do, do all to the glory of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the church of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Even as I please all men in all things, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{14} Gk. vocab: eidōlolatria (εἰδωλολατρία) = idolatry. Common English renderings: idolatry. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} I would; our; were, ; and all \textsuperscript{4} did; followed them or, went with them, that Rock \textsuperscript{6} these; examples Gr. figures; lust \textsuperscript{7} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Exodus 32:6 And having risen early on the morrow, he offered whole burnt-offerings, and offered a peace-offering; and the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Exodus 32:6 And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” \textsuperscript{11} ensamples or, types they; upon \textsuperscript{13} hath; common or, moderate but; who; make \textsuperscript{16} cup; the communion of the blood, ; The bread \textsuperscript{26} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Psalms 23:1 The earth is the Lord's and the fulness thereof; the world, and all that dwell in it. Deuteronomy 10:14 Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord thy God, the earth and all things that are in it.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Psalms 24:1 The earth [is] the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein. Deuteronomy 10:14 Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens [is] the LORD'S thy God, the earth [also], with all that therein [is].” \textsuperscript{30} grace or, thanksgiving for which \textsuperscript{31} Whether The apostle concludes the subject by giving them a general rule, sufficient to regulate every man's conscience and practice - that whether they eat, or drink, or whatsoever they do, to do it all with an habitual aim to the glory of God; by considering his precepts, and the propriety, expediency, appearance, and tendency of their actions. ye eat \textsuperscript{32} none; Gentiles or, Greeks the church\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 11}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Be all of you followers of me, even as I also am of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Now I praise you, brethren, that all of you remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonours his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But every woman that prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonours her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For the man is not of the woman: but the woman of the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Does not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that all of you come together not for the better, but for the worse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For first of all, when all of you come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} When all of you come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord's supper. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For in eating every one takes before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} What? have all of you not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise all of you the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do all of you, as often as all of you drink it, in remembrance of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For as often as all of you eat this bread, and drink this cup, all of you do show the Lord's death till he comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For he that eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord's body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Wherefore, my brethren, when all of you come together to eat, tarry one for another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that all of you come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} I praise; that, keep; ordinances or, traditions \textsuperscript{3} the head of every, ;, and the head of the; and the head of Christ \textsuperscript{10} power That is, a covering in sign that she is under the power of her husband. Εξουσια, appears here to be used for the sign or token of being under power or authority, that is, a veil, as Theophylact (Ecumenius, and Photius) explain; and so one manuscript of the Vulgate, the Sixtine edition, and some copies of the Itala, have velamen ., because \textsuperscript{18} I hear, divisions or, schisms \textsuperscript{19} there; heresies or, sects, ; *Gr. which; *Gr: \textsuperscript{20} this is not to eat or, ye cannot eat \textsuperscript{22} have or; that have not or, that are poor \textsuperscript{23} I have; the same, took \textsuperscript{24} eat; this, in remembrance or, for a remembrance \textsuperscript{26} ye do show or, shew ye till \textsuperscript{29} damnation or, judgment, Κριμα, judgment, or punishment, not damnation, for it was inflicted upon the disorderly and profane for their amendment.; *Gr:, *marg. not \textsuperscript{34} if any condemnation or, judgment will I; when\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 12}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} All of you know that all of you were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as all of you were led. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God calls Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which works all in all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the manifestation of the Spirit (o. pneuma) is given to every man to profit likewise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In order to one is given by the Spirit (o. pneuma) the word (o. logos) of wisdom; to another the word (o. logos) of knowledge by the same Spirit; (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} To another faith by the same Spirit; (o. pneuma) to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit; (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; (o. pneuma) to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But all these works that one and the very same Spirit, (o. pneuma) dividing to every man severally as he will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For as the body is one, and has many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For by one Spirit (o. pneuma) are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the body is not one member, but many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But now has God set the members every one of them in the body, as it has pleased him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if they were all one member, where were the body? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But now are they many members, yet but one body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of you: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our indecent parts have more abundant loveliness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For our comely parts have no need: but God has tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} That there should be no division in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Now all of you are the body of Christ, and members in particular. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And God has set some in the church, first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? are all workers of miracles? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet show I unto you a more excellent way.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} no man; accursed or, anathema; no man \textsuperscript{10} the working; prophecy, ; , ; discerning; divers, ;, to another the \textsuperscript{13} by; whether we be Jews; Gentiles Gr. \subsection*{1 Corinthians 13}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not love, (o. agape) I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not love, (o. agape) I am nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not love, (o. agape) it profits me nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Love (o. agape) suffers long, and is kind; love (o. agape) envies not; love (o. agape) vaunts not itself, is not puffed up, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Does not behave itself unseemly, seeks not her own, is not easily provoked, thinks no evil; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Rejoices not in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Love (o. agape) never fails: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part shall be done away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And now abides faith, hope, love, (o. agape) these three; but the greatest of these is love. (o. agape)\par

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 14}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Follow after love, (o. agape) and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that all of you may prophesy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For he that speaks in an unknown tongue speaks not unto men, but unto God: for no man understands him; nevertheless in the spirit (o. pneuma) he speaks mysteries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But he that prophesies speaks unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He that speaks in an unknown tongue edifies himself; but he that prophesies edifies the church. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I would that all of you all spoke with tongues but rather that all of you prophesied: for greater is he that prophesies than he that speaks with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So likewise all of you, except all of you utter by the tongue words (o. logos) easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for all of you shall speak into the air. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaks a barbarian, and he that speaks shall be a barbarian unto me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Even so all of you, forasmuch as all of you are zealous of spiritual (o. pneuma) gifts, seek that all of you may excel to the edifying of the church. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Wherefore let him that speaks in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit (o. pneuma) prays, but my understanding is unfruitful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, (o. pneuma) and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, (o. pneuma) and I will sing with the understanding also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Else when you shall bless with the spirit, (o. pneuma) how shall he that occupies the room of the unlearned say Amen at your giving of thanks, seeing he understands not what you says? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For you verily give thanks well, but the other is not edified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than all of you all: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Yet in the church I had rather speak five words (o. logos) with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words (o. logos) in an unknown tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Brethren, be not children in understanding: nevertheless in malice be all of you children, but in understanding be men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, says the LORD. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serves not for them that believe not, but for them which believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that all of you are mad? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believes not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you truthfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} How is it then, brethren? when all of you come together, every one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} If any thing be revealed to another that sits by, let the first hold his peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For all of you may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And the spirits (o. pneuma) of the prophets are subject to the prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience as also says the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} What? came the word (o. logos) of God out from you? or came it unto you only? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Let all things be done decently and in order.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} he that, ; understandeth Gr. heareth, howbeit \textsuperscript{6} what shall I, ; revelation; knowledge, ; prophesying, doctrine \textsuperscript{7} things except; sounds or, tunes \textsuperscript{12} forasmuch, ; spiritual gifts Gr. spirits, seek \textsuperscript{14} my spirit, but That is, "not productive of any benefit to others." \textsuperscript{15} What; I will pray with the spirit; and I will sing \textsuperscript{20} not; malice; but men Gr. perfect, or, of a ripe age \textsuperscript{21} the law The passage quoted is taken from the prophet Isaiah; but the term torah, Law, was used by the Jews to express the whole Scriptures, law, prophets, and hagiographia; and they used it to distinguish these Sacred Writings from the words of the scribes. It is not taken from the LXX, from which it varies as much as any words can differ from others where the general meaning is similar. It accords much more with the Hebrew; and may be considered as a translation from it; "only what is said of God in the third person, in the Hebrew, is here expressed in the first person, with the addition of λεγει, Κυριος, " saith the Lord. - Dr. Randolph.; With NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 28:11,12 by reason of the contemptuous words of the lips, by means of another language: for they shall speak to this people, saying to them, This is the rest to him that is hungry, and this is the calamity: but they would not hear.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 28:11,12 For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. To whom he said, This [is] the rest [wherewith] ye may cause the weary to rest; and this [is] the refreshing: yet they would not hear.” \textsuperscript{22} for a; not to but for \textsuperscript{29} the prophets; the other Rather, the others, οι αλλοι . \textsuperscript{31} all may learn, ; all may be \textsuperscript{33} confusion Gr. tumult, or unquietness but; in\par}

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 15}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also all of you have received, and wherein all of you stand; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} By which also all of you are saved, if all of you keep in memory what (o. logos) I preached unto you, unless all of you have believed in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so all of you believed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; all of you are yet in your sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the first-fruits of them that slept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But every man in his own order: Christ the first-fruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Then comes the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For he must reign, till he has put all enemies under his feet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For he has put all things under his feet. But when he says all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our LORD, I die daily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantages it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; in order to morrow we die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} You fool, that which you sow is not quickened, except it die: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And that which you sow, you sow not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} But God gives it a body as it has pleased him, and to every seed his own body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differs from another star in glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a life-giving spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Nevertheless that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} The first man is of the earth, earthy; the second man is the Lord from heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither does corruption inherit incorruption. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Behold, I show you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying (o. logos) that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} O death, where is your sting? O grave, where is your victory? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} But thanks be to God, which gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Therefore, my beloved brethren, be all of you steadfast, immoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as all of you know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.\par

\subsection*{1 Corinthians 16}
\markright{1 CORINTHIANS 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do all of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God has prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when I come, whomsoever all of you shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that all of you may bring me on my journey anywhere I go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he works the work of the Lord, as I also do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} As concerning our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Watch all of you, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let all your things be done with love. (o. agape) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I plead to (all of you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first-fruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} That all of you submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helps with us, and labours. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For they have refreshed my spirit (o. pneuma) and your's: therefore acknowledge all of you them that are such. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} All the brethren greet you. Greet all of you one another with an holy kiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} My love (o. agape) be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{17} Name meaning: Fortunatus (Fortunatus) — Fortunate Corinthian who refreshed Paul. Name meaning: Achaicus (Achaicus) — From Achaia Helped Paul.\par}

\section*{2 Corinthians Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and the church has always received 2 Corinthians as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The personal, travel, and conflict material fits Paul in Acts and the wider Pauline corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 55-56 from Macedonia\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Paul's deeply personal defense of his ministry and appeal to the Corinthians.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To reconcile with the church, defend apostolic ministry, and display Christ's strength in weakness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} apostolic ministry; weakness; comfort; generosity; reconciliation\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Ministry and comfort 1-7; collection 8-9; defense against opponents 10-13.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 46 ca. AD 200 | Subst. Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial 2 Corinthians witness ca. AD 200 | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek 2 Corinthians 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in early Christian correspondence by Polycarp or Clement (late 1st to early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Corinthians' unity is debated by some, but conservative scholarship receives the canonical letter as Pauline and coherent.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 2 Corinthians as authentic apostolic self-disclosure under inspiration.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{2 Corinthians}
\markboth{2 CORINTHIANS}{}
\subsection*{2 Corinthians 1}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who comforts us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also abounds by Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And our hope of you is steadfast, knowing, that as all of you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall all of you be also of the consolation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raises the dead: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All of you also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly toward you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For we write no other things unto you, than what all of you read or acknowledge; and I trust all of you shall acknowledge even to the end; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As also all of you have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as all of you also are our's in the day of the Lord Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that all of you might have a second benefit; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} When I therefore was thus minded, did I use levity? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But as God is true, our word (o. logos) toward you was not yea and nay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now he which establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, is God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Who has also sealed us, and given the earn of the Spirit (o. pneuma) in our hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith all of you stand.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{22} Gk. vocab: arrabōn (ἀρραβών) = pledge; earnest; down payment. Common English renderings: earnest. Used by Paul for the Spirit as the pledge of what is to come.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Paul; Timothy; the church; all; Achaia \textsuperscript{3} Blessed; the Father of our; the Father of mercies; the God \textsuperscript{6} whether; it is effectual or, wrought \textsuperscript{9} sentence or, answer that, ; in God \textsuperscript{12} our rejoicing, ; simplicity; godly; not, ; we have That is, "We have conducted ourselves; " for αναστρεφω in Greek, and conversatio in Latin, are used to denote the whole of a man's conduct, the tenor and practice of his life. \textsuperscript{14} in part; that; *Gr. your That is "the cause and object of your rejoicing." even; *Gr:; in the \textsuperscript{15} in, that; benefit or, grace \textsuperscript{19} the Son;, ; , ; even, Silas was not \textsuperscript{20} all, ; , ; Amen *Heb: *Gr: unto\par}

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 2}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For if I make you sorry, who is he then that makes me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that all of you should be grieved, but that all of you might know the love (o. agape) which I have more abundantly unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But if any have caused grief, he has not grieved me, but in part: that I may not burden you all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So that contrariwise all of you ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Wherefore I plead to you that all of you would confirm your love (o. agape) toward him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In order to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether all of you be obedient in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} To whom all of you forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I had no rest in my spirit, (o. pneuma) because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now thanks be unto God, which always causes us to triumph in Christ, and makes manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For we are not as many, which corrupt the word (o. logos) of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{13} Name meaning: Titus (Titus) — Honorable; defender Defended the faith and organized churches.\par}
