\subsection*{2 Corinthians 3}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} All of you are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Forasmuch as all of you are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit (o. pneuma) of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And such trust have we through Christ toward God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who also has made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: (o. pneuma) for the letter kills, but the spirit (o. pneuma) gives life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But if the ministration of death, written and engraved in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not steadfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} How shall not the ministration of the spirit (o. pneuma) be rather glorious? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more does the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remains is glorious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not steadfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But their minds were blinded: for until this day remains the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now the Lord is that Spirit: (o. pneuma) and where the Spirit (o. pneuma) of the Lord is, there is liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit (o. pneuma) of the LORD.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} the epistle;, ministered the living; not, but \textsuperscript{6} hath; the new; , *marg. not, for; but the; giveth life or, quickeneth \textsuperscript{7} the ministration; written;, ;, ; was;, ; that; which \textsuperscript{9} the ministration of condemnation; the ministration of righteousness; , ; exceed \textsuperscript{12} we use; plainness or, boldness \textsuperscript{13} which could not to the \textsuperscript{18} with as in; the glory; *Gr. are; from, by the Spirit of the Lord or, of the Lord the Spirit\par}

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 4}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word (o. logos) of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, has shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For we which live are always delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So then death works in us, but life in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} We having the same spirit (o. pneuma) of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, works for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{4} Name of God: Eikon tou Theou (εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ) — Image of God Common English renderings: image of God. Applied to Christ as the perfect visible revelation of the invisible God.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} seeing, ; as; we faint not; *marg. \textsuperscript{2} renounced dishonesty or, shame, ; not, ; by \textsuperscript{4} the god;, ; *Gr: blinded; lest, ; the image, ; shine \textsuperscript{6} who; hath Gr. is he who hath shined; the light; in the \textsuperscript{8} troubled, yet; not in despair or, not altogether without help, or means \textsuperscript{13} the same; I believed we also NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. \subsection*{2 Corinthians 5}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now he that has wrought us for the very same thing is God, who also has given unto us the earn of the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} (For we walk by faith, not by sight:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he has done, whether it be good or bad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that all of you may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the love (o. agape) of Christ constrains us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And all things are of God, who has reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and has given to us the ministry of reconciliation; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} To know, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and has committed unto us the word (o. logos) of reconciliation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did plead to you by us: we pray you in Christ's position, be all of you reconciled to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For he has made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.\par

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 6}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} We then, as workers together with him, plead to you also that all of you receive not the grace of God in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} (For he says, I have heard you in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I helped you: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) by love (o. agape) sincere, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} By the word (o. logos) of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} O all of you Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} All of you are not straitened in us, but all of you are straitened in your own bowels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be all of you also enlarged. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Be all of you not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion has light with darkness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And what concord has Christ with Belial? or what part has he that believes with an infidel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? for all of you are the temple of the living God; as God has said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Wherefore come out from among them, and be all of you separate, says the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And will be a Father unto you, and all of you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Jeremiah 37:22 Jeremiah 38:1 Jeremiah 39:38 Zechariah 8:8 and I will bring them in, and cause them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be to me a people, and I will be to them a God, in truth and in righteousness. Ezekiel 36:28 Ezekiel 37:23 Ezekiel 37:27 And my tabernacle shall be among them; and I will be to them a God, and they shall be my people.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Exodus 29:45 And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God. Ezekiel 37:27 My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” \textsuperscript{17} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Jeremiah 23:3 Jeremiah 38:9 They went forth with weeping, and I will bring them back with consolation, causing them to lodge by the channels of waters in a straight way, and they shall not err in it: for I am become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my first-born.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 52:11 Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean [thing]; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD. Jeremiah 31:9 They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim [is] my firstborn.”\par}

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 7}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, (o. pneuma) perfecting holiness in the fear of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I speak not this to condemn you: for I have said before, that all of you are in our hearts to die and live with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Nevertheless God, that comforts those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earn desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle has made you sorry, though it were but for a season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now I rejoice, not that all of you were made sorry, but that all of you sorrowed to repentance: for all of you were made sorry after a godly manner, that all of you might receive damage by us in nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For godly sorrow works repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world works death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For behold this very same thing, that all of you sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things all of you have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly more rejoice did we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit (o. pneuma) was refreshed by you all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spoke all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And his inward affection is more abundant toward you, whilst he remembers the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling all of you received him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.\par

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 8}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover, brethren, we do you to know of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} In order to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Praying us with much entreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Insomuch that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore, as all of you abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, (o. logos) and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love (o. agape) to us, see that all of you abound in this grace also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love. (o. agape) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For all of you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that all of you through his poverty might be rich. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now therefore perform the doing of it; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which all of you have. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man has, and not according to that he has not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For I mean not that other men be eased, and all of you burdened: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their lack, that their abundance also may be a supply for your lack: that there may be equality: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} As it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But thanks be to God, which put the same earn care into the heart of Titus for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Whether any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellow-helper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Wherefore show all of you to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, (o. agape) and of our boasting on your behalf.\par

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 9}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For as concerning the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal has provoked very many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Yet have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain in this behalf; that, as I said, all of you may be ready: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Lest lest by any means if they of Macedonia come with me, and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, all of you) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof all of you had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But this I say, He which sows sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which sows bountifully shall reap also bountifully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Every man according as he purposes in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loves a cheerful giver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that all of you, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} (As it is written, He has dispersed abroad; he has given to the poor: his righteousness remains for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now he that ministers seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causes through us thanksgiving to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the administration of this service not only supplies the lack of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} While by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution unto them, and unto all men; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And by their prayer for you, which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{7} Gk. vocab: hilaros (ἱλαρός) = cheerful; willing. Common English renderings: cheerful. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par}

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 10}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now I Paul myself plead to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But I plead to you, that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And being alert to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Do all of you look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord has given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech (o. logos) contemptible. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let such an one think this, that, such as we are in word (o. logos) by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But we will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God has distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men's labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But he that glories, let him glory in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For not he that commends himself is approved, but whom the Lord commends.\par

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 11}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Would to God all of you could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent misled Eve through his subtlety, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For if he that comes preaches another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if all of you receive another spirit, (o. pneuma) which all of you have not received, or another gospel, which all of you have not accepted, all of you might well bear with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For I suppose I was not a thing behind the very chiefest apostles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But though I be rude in speech, (o. logos) yet not in knowledge; but we have been thoroughly made manifest among you in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Have I committed an offence in abasing myself that all of you might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Wherefore? because I love you not? God knows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For all of you suffer fools gladly, seeing all of you yourselves are wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For all of you suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take of you, if a man exalt himself, if a man strike you on the face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Nevertheless whatever that anyone is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths often. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Three times was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} In journeys often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Beside those things that are without, that which comes upon me daily, the care of all the churches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} If I must essentially glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knows that I lie not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Would; bear with me a; in, ;, bear with me or, ye do bear with me \textsuperscript{2} jealous; I have; I may; a chaste \textsuperscript{3} I fear; as; so, ; the simplicity \textsuperscript{4} preacheth; receive; another gospel with him or, with me \textsuperscript{9} wanted; I was; the brethren; burdensome \textsuperscript{10} the truth, ; no man shall stop me of this boasting Gr. this boasting shall not be stopped in me, ; the regions \textsuperscript{12} what; that I may; them; they glory \textsuperscript{15} no; his; , the ministers, whose \textsuperscript{16} say Let, receive me or, suffer me \textsuperscript{20} if a man bring;, take; a man smite \textsuperscript{21} as though, whereinsoever; I speak \textsuperscript{23} ministers; I am, in labours; in stripes; in prisons, ; in deaths \textsuperscript{26} journeyings, 13:1-14:28, 16:1-18:1; in perils by mine, ; in perils by the;, ; in perils in the city \textsuperscript{27} weariness; in watchings in hunger; fastings; nakedness \textsuperscript{29} is weak, ; and I burn \textsuperscript{32} Damascus; Aretas This Aretas was an Arabian king, and the father-in-law of Herod Antipas, upon whom he made war in consequence of his having divorced his daughter. Herod applied to Tiberius for help, who sent Vitellius to reduce Aretas, and to bring him alive or dead to Rome. By some means or other Vitellius delayed his operations, and in the mean time Tiberius died; and it is probable that Aretas, who was thus snatched from ruin, availed himself of the favourable state of things, and seized on Damascus, which had belonged to his ancestors.\par}

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 12}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} It is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knows;) such an one caught up to the third heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knows;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, (o. rhema) which it is not lawful for a man to utter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Of such an one will I glory: yet of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but now I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he sees me to be, or that he hears of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For this thing I besought the Lord three times, that it might depart from me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for you: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I am become a fool in glorying; all of you have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For what is it wherein all of you were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not your's but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? (o. pneuma) walked we not in the same steps? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Again, think all of you that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as all of you would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall mourn for many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.\par

\subsection*{2 Corinthians 13}
\markright{2 CORINTHIANS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word (o. rhema) be established. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which in time past have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Since all of you seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which toward you is not weak, but is mighty in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Examine yourselves, whether all of you be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know all of you not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except all of you be reprobates? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But I trust that all of you shall know that we are not reprobates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now I pray to God that all of you do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that all of you should do that which is honest, though we be as reprobates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For we are glad, when we are weak, and all of you are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord has given me to edification, and not to destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love (o. agape) and peace shall be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Greet one another with an holy kiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} All the saints salute you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love (o. agape) of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) be with you all. Amen.\par

\section*{Galatians Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and the church has always received Galatians as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Paul's autobiographical defense and doctrinal argument fit the apostolic controversy reflected in Acts.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 48-49 or 54-55 depending on destination theory\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Polemic letter against justification by works of the law and for freedom in Christ.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To defend the true gospel of justification by faith and the Spirit's transforming work.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} justification; law and gospel; promise; Spirit; liberty\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Apostolic defense 1-2; doctrinal argument 3-4; practical freedom 5-6.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 46 ca. AD 200 | Subst. Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial Galatians witness ca. AD 200 | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek Galatians 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in Polycarp and later fathers by Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Galatians is important for text-critical and doctrinal comparison because of its central soteriological language.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Galatians as authentic Pauline controversy literature defending the once-for-all apostolic gospel.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Galatians}
\markboth{GALATIANS}{}
\subsection*{Galatians 1}
\markright{GALATIANS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I marvel that all of you are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} As we said before, so say I now again, if any man preach any other gospel unto you than that all of you have received, let him be accursed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For all of you have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preaches the faith which once he destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they glorified God in me.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} an; not, neither, but, ; and;, raised \textsuperscript{6} marvel; so, ; that called; the grace; unto \textsuperscript{10} do I now; persuade; *Gr: do I seek; for if; the servant \textsuperscript{14} profited, equals Gr. equals in years being, ; traditions \textsuperscript{18} I went up or, I returned \textsuperscript{19} James; James the son of Alphaeus; the Lord's\par}

\subsection*{Galatians 2}
\markright{GALATIANS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And that because of false brethren unexpectedly brought in, who came in privately to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it makes no matter to me: God accepts no man's person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compell you the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ lives in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.\par

\subsection*{Galatians 3}
\markright{GALATIANS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you, that all of you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ has been evidently set forth, crucified among you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} This only would I learn of you, Received all of you the Spirit (o. pneuma) by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Are all of you so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) are all of you now made perfect by the flesh? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Have all of you suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He therefore that ministers to you the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and works miracles among you, does he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Know all of you therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In you shall all nations be blessed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continues not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the law is not of faith: but, The man that does them shall live in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangs on a tree: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit (o. pneuma) through faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a man's covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man nullifies, or adds thereto. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He says not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to your seed, which is Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot nullify, that it should make the promise of no effect. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Wherefore then serves the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But the scripture has concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But after that faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For all of you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for all of you are all one in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And if all of you be Christ's, then are all of you Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{19} Gk. vocab: mesitēs (μεσίτης) = mediator; go-between. Common English renderings: mediator. A covenantal and redemptive term, especially important in Hebrews.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Foolish; *marg. who, ; , ye; Jesus Christ \textsuperscript{4} ye; so many or, so great \textsuperscript{5} that; worketh, ; , by the works \textsuperscript{8} the scripture; foreseeing God, preached In \textsuperscript{10} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 27:26 Cursed is every man that continues not in all the words of this law to do them: and all the people shall say, So be it.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 27:26 Cursed [be] he that confirmeth not [all] the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” \textsuperscript{13} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 21:23 his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but ye shall by all means bury it in that day; for every one that is hanged on a tree is cursed of God; and ye shall by no means defile the land which the Lord thy God gives thee for an inheritance.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 21:23 His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged [is] accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the LORD thy God giveth thee [for] an inheritance.” \textsuperscript{15} I speak; it be covenant or, testament \textsuperscript{17} this; the covenant, ; which; cannot; that it; none \textsuperscript{19} then, It was added; , ; till, by; in, ; The Apostle, having just before been speaking of the promise made to Abraham, and representing that as the rule of our justification, and not the law, lest they should think he derogated too much from the law, and thereby rendered it useless - he thence takes occasion to discourse of the design and tendency of it, and to acquaint us for what purposes it was given. \textsuperscript{21} the law; God forbid; for; righteousness \textsuperscript{23} faith came, ; under, ; the faith\par}

\subsection*{Galatians 4}
\markright{GALATIANS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differs nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But when the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And because all of you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit (o. pneuma) of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Wherefore you are no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Nevertheless then, when all of you knew not God, all of you did service unto them which by nature are no gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But now, after that all of you have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn all of you again to the weak and beggarly elements, unto which all of you desire again to be in bondage? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All of you observe days, and months, and times, and years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Brethren, I plead to you, be as I am; for I am as all of you are: all of you have not injured me at all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} All of you know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And my temptation which was in my flesh all of you despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Where is then the blessedness all of you spoke of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, all of you would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that all of you might affect them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Tell me, all of you that desire to be under the law, do all of you not hear the law? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which genders to bondage, which is Agar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For it is written, Rejoice, you barren that bear not; break forth and cry, you that travail not: for the desolate has many more children than she which has an husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, (o. pneuma) even so it is now. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Nevertheless what says the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} when, in, ; elements or, rudiments \textsuperscript{4} the fulness; God;, ; made; of a; , made under \textsuperscript{9} ye have; are known; how; again or, back, elements or, rudiments \textsuperscript{14} ye; an angel; as Christ \textsuperscript{15} Where is or, What was the blessedness, ;, I bear; if \textsuperscript{17} zealously; exclude you or, exclude us \textsuperscript{20} to be; stand in doubt of you or, am perplexed for you \textsuperscript{21} ye that, ;, do; the law \textsuperscript{24} an allegory; *Gr: for; the two;, covenants or, testament Sinai Gr. Sina which; Agar, Hagar \textsuperscript{25} is Sinai; Arabia; answereth to or, is in the same rank with her \textsuperscript{27} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 54:1 Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not break forth and cry, thou that dost not travail: for more are the children of the desolate than of her that has a husband: for the Lord has said,” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 54:1 Sing, O barren, thou [that] didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou [that] didst not travail with child: for more [are] the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD.” \textsuperscript{29} he that after the Spirit; even \textsuperscript{30} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Genesis 21:10 then she said to Abraam, Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son Isaac.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Genesis 21:10 Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bondwoman and her son: for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, [even] with Isaac.”\par}

\subsection*{Galatians 5}
\markright{GALATIANS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if all of you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; all of you are fallen from grace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For we through the Spirit (o. pneuma) wait for the hope of righteousness by faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision avails any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which works by love. (o. agape) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All of you did run well; who did hinder you that all of you should not obey the truth? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} This persuasion comes not of him that calls you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A little leaven leavens the whole lump. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I have confidence in you through the Lord, that all of you will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubles you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I would they were even cut off which trouble you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For, brethren, all of you have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love (o. agape) serve one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For all the law is fulfilled in one word, (o. logos) even in this; You shall love your neighbour as yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if all of you bite and devour one another, take heed that all of you be not consumed one of another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and all of you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and the Spirit (o. pneuma) against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that all of you cannot do the things that all of you would. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But if all of you be led of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) all of you are not under the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, worldy jealousies, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But the fruit of the Spirit (o. pneuma) is love, (o. agape) joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Meekness, wilful restrain: against such there is no law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} If we live in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) let us also walk in the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{7} run; hinder you or, drive you back, obey \textsuperscript{16} I say; Walk; and; ye shall not fulfil or, fulfil not \textsuperscript{17} the flesh, ; , ; and these;, so \textsuperscript{21} drunkenness; revellings that they; inherit \textsuperscript{22} the fruit; love; goodness faith \textsuperscript{24} they; crucified, ; affections or, passions\par}
