\subsection*{Colossians 4}
\markright{COLOSSIANS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that all of you also have a Master in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Likewise praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of (o. logos) utterance, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let your (o. logos) speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that all of you may know how all of you ought to answer every man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Aristarchus my fellow-prisoner salutes you, and Marcus, sister's (concerning whom all of you received commandments: if he comes unto you, receive him;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Jesus, which is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only are my fellow workers unto the kingdom of God, which have been a comfort unto me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, salutes you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that all of you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For I bear him record, that he has a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Salute the brethren which are in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that all of you likewise read the epistle from Laodicea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you fulfill it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{9} Name meaning: Onesimus (Onesimos) — Useful; profitable The runaway slave who became useful. \textsuperscript{14} Name meaning: Demas (Demas) — Popular Loved this present world and forsook Paul. Name meaning: Luke (Loukas) — Light-giving; from Lucania Beloved physician who brought gospel light. \textsuperscript{15} Name meaning: Nymphas (Nymphas) — Bridegroom Hosted a house church.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} praying; that; a door The term door is used metaphorically for an entrance to any business, or occasion or opportunity of doing any thing; and consequently "a door of utterance" is an opportunity of preaching the gospel successfully. See the parallel texts. the mystery; for \textsuperscript{7} my Tychicus; a beloved; a faithful \textsuperscript{10} Aristarchus, ; saluteth and Marcus, ; receive \textsuperscript{12} Epaphras; a servant; always; labouring or, striving, that; see note on, ; *Gr:; *Gr:; complete or, filled \textsuperscript{13} I bear; Laodicea and Hierapolis were both cities of Phrygia in Asia Minor, between which, and equidistant from each, was situated Colosse. Laodicea was seated near the Lycus, about 63 miles east of Ephesus; and became one of the largest and richest towns in Phrygia, vying in power with the maritime cities. It is now called Eski-hissar, the old castle; and besides the whole surface within the city's wall being strewed with pedestals and fragments, the ruins of an amphitheatre, a magnificent odeum, and other public buildings, attest its former splendour and magnificence. But, when visited by Dr. Chandler, all was silence and solitude; and a fox, first discovered by his ears peeping over a brow, was the only inhabitant of Laodicea. Hierapolis, now Pambouk-Kaiesi, was situated, according to the Itinerary, six miles n of Laodicea; and its ruins are now about a mile and a half in circumference. \textsuperscript{17} Archippus Take; the ministry; fulfil\par}

\section*{1 Thessalonians Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and the church has always received 1 Thessalonians as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} It fits the Acts 17-18 setting and early apostolic mission period.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 50-51 from Corinth\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} One of Paul's earliest letters, written to a young persecuted church.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To encourage steadfastness, holiness, brotherly love, and hope in Christ's return.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} sanctification; hope; second coming; persecution; work\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Thanksgiving and defense 1-3; holy living and the Lord's coming 4-5.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 46 ca. AD 200 | Subst. Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial 1 Thessalonians witness ca. AD 200 | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek 1 Thessalonians 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely early echoes in Ignatius and Polycarp by Ignatius and Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1 Thessalonians is early and textually strong, with eschatological passages especially important for apparatus work.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 1 Thessalonians as among Paul's earliest surviving apostolic letters.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 1}
\markright{1 THESSALONIANS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} We give thanks to God always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, (o. agape) and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For our gospel came not unto you in word (o. logos) only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and in much assurance; as all of you know what manner of men we were among you for your sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all of you became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word (o. logos) in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So that all of you were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For from you sounded out the word (o. logos) of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For they themselves show of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how all of you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 2}
\markright{1 THESSALONIANS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully pleaded, as all of you know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which tries our hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For neither at any time used we flattering words, (o. logos) as all of you know, nor a coat of covetousness; God is witness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherishes her children: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you, not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because all of you were dear unto us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For all of you remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} All of you are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} As all of you know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father does his children, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That all of you would walk worthy of God, who has called you unto his kingdom and glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when all of you received the word (o. logos) of God which all of you heard of us, all of you received it not as the word (o. logos) of men, but as it is in truth, the word (o. logos) of God, which effectually works also in you that believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For all of you, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for all of you also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins always: for the wrath has come upon them to the uttermost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavoured the more abundantly to see your face with great desire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even all of you in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For all of you are our glory and joy.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 3}
\markright{1 THESSALONIANS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wherefore when we could no longer forbear, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And sent Timotheus, our brother, and minister of God, and our fellow labourer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} That no man should be moved by these afflictions: for yourselves know that we are appointed thereunto. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For verily, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass, and all of you know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For this cause, when I could no longer forbear, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But now when Timotheus came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and love, (o. agape) and that all of you have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also to see you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore, brethren, we were comforted over you in all our affliction and distress by your faith: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For now we live, if all of you stand fast in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For what thanks can we render to God again for you, for all the joy wherewith we joy for your sakes before our God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Night and day praying exceedingly that we might see your face, and might perfect that which is lacking in your faith? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love (o. agape) one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} To the end he may establish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 4}
\markright{1 THESSALONIANS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Furthermore then we plead to you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as all of you have received of us how all of you ought to walk and to please God, so all of you would abound more and more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For all of you know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that all of you should abstain from fornication: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Not in the lust of concupiscence, even as the Gentiles which know not God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For God has not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He therefore that despises, despises not man, but God, who has also given unto us his holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But as concerning brotherly love all of you need not that I write unto you: for all of you yourselves are taught of God to love one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And indeed all of you do it toward all the brethren which are in all Macedonia: but we plead to you, brethren, that all of you increase more and more; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And that all of you study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That all of you may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that all of you may have lack of nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that all of you sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For this we say unto you by the word (o. logos) of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Wherefore comfort one another with these words. (o. logos)\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 5}
\markright{1 THESSALONIANS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But of the times and the seasons, brethren, all of you have no need that I write unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so comes as a thief in the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction comes upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But all of you, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} All of you are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; (o. agape) and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also all of you do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And we plead to you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And to esteem them very highly in love (o. agape) for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Rejoice evermore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Pray without ceasing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Quench not the Spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Despise not prophesyings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Abstain from all appearance of evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit (o. pneuma) and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Faithful is he that calls you, who also will do it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Brethren, pray for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.\par

\section*{2 Thessalonians Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and conservative scholarship receives 2 Thessalonians as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Its close relationship to 1 Thessalonians and its apostolic tone support authenticity.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 51-52 from Corinth\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Follow-up letter correcting confusion about the day of the Lord and urging steadfastness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To steady the church amid persecution and clarify events connected with the Lord's return.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} day of the Lord; lawlessness; perseverance; discipline\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Persecution and justice 1; man of lawlessness 2; exhortation and discipline 3.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 30 and Papyrus 46 witness 2 Thessalonians 3rd century AD and ca. AD 200 | Subst. Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial 2 Thessalonians witness ca. AD 200 | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek 2 Thessalonians 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in early fathers by Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Thessalonians is central in eschatological discussion and textually well attested.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 2 Thessalonians as Pauline clarification, not pseudonymous imitation.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{2 Thessalonians}
\markboth{2 THESSALONIANS}{}
\subsection*{2 Thessalonians 1}
\markright{2 THESSALONIANS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Grace unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} We are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because that your faith grows exceedingly, and the love (o. agape) of every one of you all toward each other abounds; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that all of you endure: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that all of you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which all of you also suffer: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfill all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and all of you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{3} are; , as is; your; groweth The word, υπεραυξανω, from υπερ, intensive, and αυξανω, to grow, increase, signifies, as Dr. Clarke remarks, to grow luxuriantly, as a good and healthy tree in a good soil; and, if a fruit tree, bearing an abundance of fruit to compensate the labour of the husbandman. Faith is one of the seeds of the kingdom. This the Apostle had sowed and watered, and God gave an abundant increase. Their faith was multiplied, and their love abounded, and this was not the case with some distinguished characters only; it was the case with every one of them. For this the apostle felt himself bound to give continual thanks to God on their behalf, as it was "meet" and right. \textsuperscript{4} glory, ; your patience;, ; your persecutions \textsuperscript{7} who; , when, ; his mighty angels Gr. the angels of his power \textsuperscript{8} flaming; , taking or, yielding vengeance, ; that know; and that \textsuperscript{9} be; , from the presence; the glory; *Gr: \textsuperscript{10} to be glorified; , ; , ; to be admired our; in that \textsuperscript{11} we pray; our God; would; count or, vouchsafe calling; fulfil; the good; the work \textsuperscript{12} the name; and ye; the grace\par}

\subsection*{2 Thessalonians 2}
\markright{2 THESSALONIANS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now we plead to you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That all of you be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, (o. pneuma) nor by word, (o. logos) nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Remember all of you not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now all of you know what withholds that he might be revealed in his time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the mystery of iniquity does already work: only he who now lets will let, until he be taken out of the way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit (o. pneuma) of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love (o. agape) of the truth, that they might be saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But we are bound to give thanks always to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God has from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit (o. pneuma) and belief of the truth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Unto which he called you by our gospel, to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore, brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which all of you have been taught, whether by word, (o. logos) or our epistle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which has loved us, and has given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Comfort your hearts, and establish you in every good word (o. logos) and work.\par

\subsection*{2 Thessalonians 3}
\markright{2 THESSALONIANS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word (o. logos) of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified, even as it is with you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But the Lord is faithful, who shall establish you, and keep you from evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that all of you both do and will do the things which we command you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And the Lord direct your hearts into the love (o. agape) of God, and into the patient waiting for Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you withdraw yourselves from every brother that walks disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For yourselves know how all of you ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Neither did we eat any man's bread for nothing; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an example unto you to follow us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But all of you, brethren, be not weary in well doing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And if any man obey not our word (o. logos) by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.\par

\section*{1 Timothy Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and conservative scholarship receives the Pastoral Epistles as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The letter's personal address, church-order concerns, and later travel setting fit traditional Pauline chronology.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} mid-60s AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Pastoral instruction to Timothy for ordering doctrine and life in the Ephesian sphere.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To guard sound doctrine, shape church leadership, and call believers to godliness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} church order; sound doctrine; eldership; godliness; warning against error\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Charge and doctrine 1; worship and leadership 2-3; warning and exhortation 4-6.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 133 is an early fragment; later majuscules preserve the full book 3rd century AD | Subst. No papyrus as substantial as P46 survives for 1 Timothy; major uncials are primary full witnesses n/a | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve complete Greek 1 Timothy 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in Polycarp by Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} The Pastorals have different witness patterns from the major Pauline collection, but remain textually secure in the broad sense.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 1 Timothy as authentic Pauline pastoral instruction.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{1 Timothy}
\markboth{1 TIMOTHY}{}
\subsection*{1 Timothy 1}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} As I besought you to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that you might charge some that they teach no other doctrine, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now the end of the commandment is love (o. agape) out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith sincere: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} From which some having miss the mark have turned aside unto vain arguments; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for men-stealers (p. slave traders, kidnappers), for liars, for promise breakers, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and prone to cause hurt: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love (o. agape) which is in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} This is a faithful saying, (o. logos) and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Nevertheless for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might show forth all longsuffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} This charge I commit unto you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on you, that you by them might war a good warfare; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{20} Name meaning: Hymenaeus (Hymenaios) — Of Hymen False teacher who shipwrecked faith.\par}

\subsection*{1 Timothy 2}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Unto which I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with reverence and sobriety; not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But (which becomes women professing godliness) with good works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For Adam was first formed, then Eve. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and love (o. agape) and holiness with sobriety.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} exhort or, desire; first supplications; and; all men \textsuperscript{2} kings; for all; authority or, eminent place that; all godliness \textsuperscript{5} one God; and;, the man \textsuperscript{6} gave; to be testified or, a testimony; in \textsuperscript{7} I am a preacher, ; I speak; a teacher;, ; in faith; verity \textsuperscript{8} I will; *Gr: pray; lifting; without;, ; and \textsuperscript{9} that with shamefacedness; not; broided or, plaited \textsuperscript{15} she; in childbearing in faith sobriety\par}

\subsection*{1 Timothy 3}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This is a true saying, (o. logos) If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desires a good work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, able to teach; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Not given to wine, not an attacker, not greedy of filthy illegal gain; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} One that rules well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Likewise must the deacons be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy illegal gain; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} These things write I unto you, hoping to come unto you shortly: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But if I tarry long, that you may know how you ought to behave yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} is a; the office; bishop; *Gr. desireth \textsuperscript{2} bishop blameless; the husband; vigilant; of good behaviour or, modest given; apt \textsuperscript{3} Not given to wine or, Not ready to quarrel, and offer wrong, as one in wine;, ; no; not greedy; filthy; patient; a brawler; *marg. not covetous \textsuperscript{6} novice or, one newly come to the faith; lest; the condemnation \textsuperscript{7} a good; them; lest; the snare \textsuperscript{8} the deacons; be doubletongued, ; not given \textsuperscript{11} their; be not, ; *Gr: sober; *Gr: faithful \textsuperscript{13} they; used or, ministered; degree *Gr. great \textsuperscript{15} know; the house; the church the living; the pillar; ground or, stay the truth \textsuperscript{16} without the mystery; God; manifest Gr. manifested, justified; seen; preached; believed; received\par}

\subsection*{1 Timothy 4}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now the Spirit (o. pneuma) speaks expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, (o. pneuma) and doctrines of devils; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God has created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For it is sanctified by the word (o. logos) of God and prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If you put the brethren in remembrance of these things, you shall be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in the words (o. logos) of faith and of good doctrine, unto which you have attained. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise yourself rather unto godliness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For bodily exercise profits little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} This is a faithful saying (o. logos) and worthy of all acceptation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} These things command and teach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let no man despise your youth; but be you an example of the believers, in word, (o. logos) in conversation, in love, (o. agape) in spirit, (o. pneuma) in faith, in purity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Neglect not the gift that is in you, which was given you by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Meditate upon these things; give yourself wholly to them; that your profiting may appear to all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Take heed unto yourself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this you shall both save yourself, and them that hear you.\par

\subsection*{1 Timothy 5}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Rebuke not an elder, but implore him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Honour widows that are widows indeed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to show piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusts in God, and continues in supplications and prayers night and day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But she that lives in pleasure is dead while she lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And likewise they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but gossiping also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For some are already turned aside after Satan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} If any man or woman that believes have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word (o. logos) and doctrine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the scripture says, You shall not suppress the ox that treads out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} I charge you before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that you observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep yourself pure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for your stomach's sake and yours often infirmities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Rebuke; an elder;, ; entreat; as brethren \textsuperscript{4} nephews *marg.; learn; piety or, kindness; to requite, ; good \textsuperscript{5} a widow; and desolate, ; trusteth; continueth \textsuperscript{6} she; in pleasure or, delicately, ; dead \textsuperscript{8} and specially; house or, kindred, he hath; and is \textsuperscript{9} a widow taken or, chosen under; having \textsuperscript{10} reported; good, ; if she have brought, if she have lodged; washed, ; if she have relieved; if she have diligently; , *Gr. \textsuperscript{11} the younger, to wax; they will \textsuperscript{13} to be; wandering; busybodies; speaking \textsuperscript{14} I will the younger; guide; *Gr. give; to speak reproachfully Gr. for their railing \textsuperscript{17} the elders rule; , be; double; labour; word \textsuperscript{18} the scripture, ; Thou; The labourer \textsuperscript{19} receive; before or, under two \textsuperscript{21} charge; the elect; that; without preferring or, without prejudice; partiality\par}

\subsection*{1 Timothy 6}
\markright{1 TIMOTHY 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, (o. logos) even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof comes envy, strife, railings, evil questionings, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw yourself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But godliness with contentment is great gain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And having food and raiment let us be therewith content. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But you, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, (o. agape) patience, meekness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, unto which you are also called, and have professed a good profession before many witnesses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I give you charge in the sight of God, who replenishes life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That you keep this commandment without spot, blameless, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Which in his times he shall show, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Who only has immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man has seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not high-minded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who gives us richly all things to enjoy; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} O Timothy, keep that which is committed to your trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{15} Name of God: Basileus basileon kai Kyrios kyrion (βασιλεὺς βασιλέων καὶ κύριος κυρίων) — King of kings and Lord of lords Common English renderings: King of kings, and Lord of lords. An ultimate title of sovereignty used of God and also gloriously applied to Christ.\par}

\section*{2 Timothy Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and conservative scholarship receives it as Paul's final surviving letter.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Its personal tone, martyrdom horizon, and coworker references suit Paul's last imprisonment.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 66-67 from Rome\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Final apostolic charge to Timothy in view of suffering and death.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To summon Timothy to faithful ministry, endurance, and preservation of the apostolic deposit.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} endurance; Scripture; ministry; apostasy; martyrdom\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Guard the deposit 1; endure as a soldier 2; perilous times 3; final charge 4.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 61 and other small witnesses survive; full text rests mainly in uncials 3rd-4th century AD | Subst. Major uncials preserve the earliest substantial 2 Timothy text 4th century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve complete Greek 2 Timothy 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in Polycarp and later fathers by Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Timothy contains key statements on Scripture and ministry and is well preserved in the main textual tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 2 Timothy as Paul's final inspired testament to the church.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{2 Timothy}
\markboth{2 TIMOTHY}{}
\subsection*{2 Timothy 1}
\markright{2 TIMOTHY 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of you in my prayers night and day; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Greatly desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When I call to remembrance the sincere faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in you also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Wherefore I put you in remembrance that you stir up the gift of God, which is in you by the putting on of my hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For God has not given us the spirit (o. pneuma) of fear; but of power, and of love, (o. agape) and of a sound mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be not you therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be you partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who has saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who has abolished death, and has brought life and immortality to light through the gospel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Unto which I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Hold fast the form of sound words, (o. logos) which you have heard of me, in faith and love (o. agape) which is in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That good thing which was committed unto you keep by the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) which dwells in us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} This you know, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day: and in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, you know very well.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{15} Name meaning: Phygelus (Phygelos) — Fugitive Deserted Paul in Asia. Name meaning: Hermogenes (Hermogenes) — Born of Hermes Also deserted Paul. \textsuperscript{16} Name meaning: Onesiphorus (Onesiphoros) — Bringing profit Refreshing and profitable servant.\par}

\subsection*{2 Timothy 2}
\markright{2 TIMOTHY 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And the things that you have heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit you to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} You therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} No man that wars entangles himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who has chosen him to be a soldier. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The farmer that labours must be first partaker of the fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Consider what I say; and the Lord give you understanding in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word (o. logos) of God is not bound. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore I endure all things for the elect's sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} It is a faithful saying: (o. logos) For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} If we believe not, yet he abides faithful: he cannot deny himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Study to show yourself approved unto God, a workman that needs not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word (o. logos) of truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And their word (o. logos) will eat as does a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Nevertheless the foundation of God stands sure, having this seal, The Lord knows them that are his. And, Let every one that names the name of Christ depart from iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, love, (o. agape) peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, able to teach, patient, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God possibly will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.\par

\subsection*{2 Timothy 3}
\markright{2 TIMOTHY 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This know also, that in the last days dangerous times shall come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Traitors, rebellious, high-minded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as their's also was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But you have fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, (o. agape) patience, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But continue you in the things which you have learned and have been assured of, knowing of whom you have learned them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And that from a child you have known the holy scriptures, which are able to make you wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} lovers; covetous; boasters, ; proud; blasphemers; , disobedient \textsuperscript{3} natural; trucebreakers; *Gr. false accusers or, make-bates; All in Gr incontinent; fierce;, despisers \textsuperscript{4} Traitors; highminded; lovers of God \textsuperscript{6} of this; laden; led; divers \textsuperscript{8} as, resist; , men; reprobate or, of no judgment \textsuperscript{10} thou hast fully known or, thou hast been a diligent follower of; *Gr. my; manner; purpose; faith \textsuperscript{16} All;, ; and is, ; for doctrine for reproof; *Gr. for instruction \textsuperscript{17} the man; thoroughly furnished or, perfected\par}
