\subsection*{2 Timothy 4}
\markright{2 TIMOTHY 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I charge you therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Preach the word; (o. logos) be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But watch you in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of your ministry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Do your diligence to come shortly unto me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For Demas has forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you: for he is profitable to me for the ministry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The coat that I left at Troas with Carpus, when you come, bring with you, and the books, but especially the parchments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Of whom be you ware also; for he has greatly withstood our words. (o. logos) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Do your diligence to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. (o. pneuma) Grace be with you. Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{10} Name meaning: Crescens (Crescens) — Growing Faithful coworker who went to Galatia. \textsuperscript{21} Name meaning: Pudens (Pudens) — Modest; shamefaced Roman Christian who greeted Paul. Name meaning: Linus (Linos) — Flaxen; net Early Christian leader. Name meaning: Claudia (Claudia) — Lame Woman who greeted Paul. Name meaning: Eubulus (Euboulos) — Good counselor Faithful in Rome.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} charge; who, ; at; his kingdom \textsuperscript{2} Preach; be; *marg.; in;, reprove; exhort all \textsuperscript{3} the time; they will; sound but; , ; having; *Gr: \textsuperscript{5} watch; endure, an; make full proof of or, fulfil \textsuperscript{7} have thought, I have finished; I have kept \textsuperscript{8} there; a crown; , the righteous; at that; that love \textsuperscript{10} Demas; hath; having, ; Thessalonica, Galatia; Titus \textsuperscript{15} be; withstood words or, preachings \textsuperscript{16} answer; *Gr. no; I pray \textsuperscript{17} the Lord; strengthened; by; and I \textsuperscript{18} deliver; and will; to whom \textsuperscript{20} Erastus; Trophimus, Miletum, Miletus sick\par}

\section*{Titus Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and conservative scholarship receives Titus as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Its personal directions and pastoral instruction fit the same post-Acts missionary horizon as 1 Timothy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} mid-60s AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Pastoral letter for church order and godly living in Crete.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To establish qualified leadership, oppose false teachers, and adorn the doctrine of God with good works.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} leadership; good works; sound doctrine; grace; order\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Leadership and rebuke 1; fitting conduct 2; grace and good works 3.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 32 preserves a small early Titus witness 3rd century AD | Subst. Major uncials preserve the earliest substantial Titus text 4th century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve complete Greek Titus 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed in early fathers by Clement of Alexandria or later fathers (late 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Titus is textually stable overall and closely linked to the Pastoral corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Titus as authentic Pauline pastoral direction.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Titus}
\markboth{TITUS}{}
\subsection*{Titus 1}
\markright{TITUS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But has in due times manifested his word (o. logos) through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For this cause left I you in Crete, that you should set in order the things that are lacking, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not self-willed, not soon angry, not given to wine, not an attacker, not given to filthy illegal gain; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Holding fast the faithful word (o. logos) as he has been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy illegal gain's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are always liars, evil beasts, sluggards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.\par

\subsection*{Titus 2}
\markright{TITUS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But speak you the things which become sound doctrine: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in love, (o. agape) in patience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becomes holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word (o. logos) of God be not blasphemed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} In all things showing yourself a pattern of good works: in doctrine showing incorruptness, gravity, sincerity, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Sound speech, (o. logos) that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Not embezzling, but showing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself an exclusive people, zealous of good works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise you.\par

\subsection*{Titus 3}
\markright{TITUS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, showing all meekness unto all men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Spirit; (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} This is a faithful saying, (o. logos) and these things I will that you affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are useless and vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} A man that is an heretic after the first and second admonition reject; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sins, being condemned of himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When I shall send Artemas unto you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be lacking unto them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And let our's also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} All that are with me salute you. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{12} Name meaning: Artemas (Artemas) — Gift of Artemis Faithful coworker Paul sent to Crete. \textsuperscript{13} Name meaning: Zenas (Zenas) — Living Lawyer who traveled with Apollos.\par}

\section*{Philemon Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Paul the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Paul, and the church has always received Philemon as Pauline.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Its close ties to Colossians and concrete personal details strongly support authenticity.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} AD 60-62 during Roman imprisonment\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Brief personal prison letter appealing for Onesimus's reception.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To embody gospel reconciliation and brotherhood in Christ in a concrete case.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} reconciliation; brotherhood; grace; appeal; slavery and freedom in Christ\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Opening and thanksgiving 1-7; appeal for Onesimus 8-25.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 87 preserves a small early Philemon witness 3rd century AD | Subst. Major uncials preserve the earliest substantial Philemon text 4th century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus preserve complete Greek Philemon 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely known in early Pauline reception by Marcion or later fathers (2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Philemon is short and comparatively stable textually, but historically valuable for the Pauline network.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives Philemon as authentic Pauline personal correspondence under inspiration.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Philemon}
\markboth{PHILEMON}{}
\subsection*{Philemon 1}
\markright{PHILEMON 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellow labourer, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I thank my God, making mention of you always in my prayers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Hearing of your love (o. agape) and faith, which you have toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} That the communication of your faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For we have great joy and consolation in your love, (o. agape) because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by you, brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to admonish you that which is convenient, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Yet for love's (o. agape) sake I rather plead to you, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I plead to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Which in time past was to you useless, but now profitable to you and to me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Whom I have sent again: you therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whom I would have retained with me, that in your position he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But without your mind would I do nothing; that your benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that you should receive him for ever; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto you, both in the flesh, and in the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} If you count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} If he has wronged you, or owes you ought, put that on mine account; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: although it be I do not say to you how you owe unto me even yours own self besides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Yea, brother, let me have joy of you in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Having confidence in your obedience I wrote unto you, knowing that you will also do more than I say. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But likewise prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} There salute you Epaphras, my fellow-prisoner in Christ Jesus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellow labourers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. (o. pneuma) Amen.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{T: }}\textsuperscript{1} Name meaning: Philemon (Philemon) — Affectionate Showed affectionate forgiveness to Onesimus. \textsuperscript{2} Name meaning: Archippus (Archippos) — Master of the horse Called to fulfill his ministry. Name meaning: Apphia (Apphia) — Productive; increasing Hostess connected with a growing house church.\par}
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} ad 64, am 4068 a prisoner; Timothy; Philemon Th e apostle in this epistle indulges in some fine paronomasais on the proper names. Thus Philemon, Φιλημον, affectionate, or beloved, is "our dearly beloved; " Apphia ( Απφια, from απφα ), the affectionate address of a brother or sister, according to Suidas), is "the beloved sister, " as several manuscripts, Vulgate, and others correctly read; Archippus ( Αρχιππος, the ruler of the horse, for the managing of which heros were anciently famous), is "our fellow- soldier; " and Onesimus ( Ονησιμος, useful or profitable), once unprofitable, is now profitable., and fellow labourer \textsuperscript{2} Archippus our fellowsoldier; the church \textsuperscript{6} the communication; the acknowledging; , in you \textsuperscript{13} in thy stead; the bonds \textsuperscript{22} prepare for I trust; through \textsuperscript{24} Marcus, ; Aristarchus, Demas; Lucas my fellowlabourers\par}

\section*{Hebrews Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Unknown human writer; conservative options often include Paul\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} Luke\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Barnabas\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} or Apollos\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} The church received Hebrews as canonical and apostolic in doctrine, though the human penman remains uncertain.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} 2 Peter 3:15 may possibly allude to Pauline teaching received alongside Hebrews, but the book itself is anonymous.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} before AD 70 in common conservative dating\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Sustained sermon-letter exalting Christ's superiority and warning against apostasy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. To show the finality of Christ's priesthood and covenant and to call believers to persevering faith. superiority of Christ; priesthood; covenant; perseverance; faith | Subst. Christ superior 1-10; persevering faith and exhortation 11-13. Papyrus 46 | Heb. ca. AD 200 Papyrus 46 is the earliest substantial Hebrews witness | Gk. ca. AD 200 No complete Hebrew original survives\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} n/a by Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus preserve complete Greek Hebrews (4th century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Clearly used by Clement of Rome\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Clement of Rome\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Hebrews}
\markboth{HEBREWS}{}
\subsection*{Hebrews 1}
\markright{HEBREWS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} God, who at several times and in divers manners spoke in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Has in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he has appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word (o. rhema) of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Being made so much better than the angels, as he has by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For unto which of the angels said he at any time, You are my Son, this day have I begotten you? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And again, when he brings in the First-Born into the world, he says, And let all the angels of God worship him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And of the angels he says, Who makes his angels spirits, (o. pneuma) and his ministers a flame of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But unto the Son he says, Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of your kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You have loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And, You, Lord, in the beginning have laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of yours hands: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They shall perish; but you remain; and they all shall wax old as does a garment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And as a vesture shall you fold them up, and they shall be changed: but you are the same, and your years shall not fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make yours enemies your footstool? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Are they not all ministering spirits, (o. pneuma) sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 2}
\markright{HEBREWS 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore we ought to give the more earn heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For if the word (o. logos) spoken by angels was steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) according to his own will? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For unto the angels has he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that you are mindful of him? or the son of man that you visit him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honour, and did set him over the works of your hands: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You have put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For both he that santifies and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Saying, I will declare your name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God has given me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Wherefore in all things it was essential for him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help them that are tempted.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 3}
\markright{HEBREWS 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who has built the house has more honour than the house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For every house is built by some man; but he that built all things is God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But Christ as a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Wherefore (as the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) says, To day if all of you will hear his voice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do always go astray in their heart; and they have not known my ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So I swore in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast unto the end; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} While it is said, To day if all of you will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For some, when they had heard, did provoke: nevertheless not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And to whom swore he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 4}
\markright{HEBREWS 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word (o. logos) preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For he spoke in a certain place of the seventh day likewise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Seeing therefore it remains that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Again, he limits a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if all of you will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} There remains therefore a rest to the people of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he that is entered into his rest, he also has ceased from his own works, as God did from his. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the word (o. logos) of God is active, and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, (o. pneuma) and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do. (o. logos) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 5}
\markright{HEBREWS 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And no man takes this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, You are my Son, to day have I begotten you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} As he says also in another place, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Of whom we have (o. logos) many things to say, (o. logos) and hard to be uttered, seeing all of you are dull of hearing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For when for the time all of you ought to be teachers, all of you have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong food. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For every one that uses milk is unskillful in the word (o. logos) of righteousness: for he is a babe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But strong food belongs to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 6}
\markright{HEBREWS 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine (o. logos) of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And this will we do, if God permit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And have tasted the good word (o. rhema) of God, and the powers of the world to come, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the earth which drinks in the rain that comes often upon it, and brings forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receives blessing from God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But that which bears thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, (o. agape) which all of you have showed toward his name, in that all of you have ministered to the saints, and do minister. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And we desire that every one of you do show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} That all of you be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he swore by himself, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Saying, Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Wherein God, willing more abundantly to show unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and which enters into that within the veil; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Where the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 7}
\markright{HEBREWS 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abides a priest continually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receives them, of whom it is witnessed that he lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And as I may so say, Levi also, who receives tithes, paid tithes in Abraham. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For he of whom these things are spoken pertains to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it is yet far more evident: for that after the embodiment of Melchisedec there arises another priest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For he testifies, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord swore and will not repent, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} By so much was Jesus made a guarantor of a better testament. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But this man, because he continues ever, has an unchangeable priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever lives to make intercession for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Who needs not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For the law makes men high priests which have infirmity; but the word (o. logos) of the oath, which was since the law, makes the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 8}
\markright{HEBREWS 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, says he, that you make all things according to the pattern showed to you in the mount. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But now has he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For finding fault with them, he says, Behold, the days come, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, says the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} In that he says, A new covenant, he has made the first old. Now that which decays and waxs old is ready to vanish away.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 9}
\markright{HEBREWS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the showbread; which is called the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercy seat; of which we cannot now speak particularly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while the first tabernacle was yet standing: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, santifies to the purifying of the flesh: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit (o. pneuma) offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God has commanded with authority unto you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place every year with blood of others; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world has he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.\par

\subsection*{Hebrews 10}
\markright{HEBREWS 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Wherefore when he comes into the world, he says, Sacrifice and offering you would not, but a body have you prepared me: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you have had no pleasure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do your will, O God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin you would not, neither had pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then said he, Lo, I come to do your will, O God. He takes away the first, that he may establish the second. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And every priest stands daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For by one offering he has perfected for ever them that are sanctified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Whereof the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} By a new and living way, which he has consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And having an high priest over the house of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And let us consider one another to provoke unto love (o. agape) and to good works: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as all of you see the day approaching. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For if we sin willfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Of how much greater punishment, suppose all of you, shall he be thought worthy, who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and has done despite unto the Spirit (o. pneuma) of grace? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For we know him that has said, Vengeance belongs unto me, I will recompense, says the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after all of you were illuminated, all of you endured a great fight of afflictions; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Partly, whilst all of you were made a gazing-stock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst all of you became companions of them that were so used. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} For all of you had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that all of you have in heaven a better and an enduring substance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Cast not away therefore your confidence, which has great recompence of reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For all of you have need of patience, that, after all of you have done the will of God, all of you might receive the promise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{2} would they not have or, they would have once; conscience Our translators use the word conscience here, as elsewhere, for consciousness. \textsuperscript{4} not, ; take There were essential defects in these sacrifices. 1st - They were not of the same nature with those who sinned. 2nd - They were not of sufficient value to make satisfaction for the affronts done to the justice and government of God. 3rd - The beasts offered up under the law could not consent to put themselves in the sinner's room and place. The atoning sacrifice must be one capable of consenting, and must voluntarily substitute himself in the sinner's stead: Christ did so. \textsuperscript{5} when; *Gr. Sacrifice; but, ; hast thou prepared me or, thou hast fitted me NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Psalms 39:6-8 Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; but a body hast thou prepared me: whole-burn-offering and sacrifice for sin thou didst not require. Then I said, Behold, I come: in the volume of the book it is written concerning me, I desired to do thy will, O my God, and thy law in the midst of mine heart.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Psalms 40:6-8 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book [it is] written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law [is] within my heart.” \textsuperscript{17} And Some copies have, Then he said, And their, etc. \textsuperscript{19} Having; boldness or, liberty to enter \textsuperscript{20} a new, consecrated or, new made through; his \textsuperscript{22} draw; a true;, ;, ; in full; sprinkled, ; an evil; our bodies \textsuperscript{25} forsaking;, ; but; *marg. as ye \textsuperscript{29} how, trodden; *marg.; the blood, wherewith; and hath; the Spirit \textsuperscript{30} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Deuteronomy 32:36 For the Lord shall judge his people, and shall be comforted over his servants; for he saw that they were utterly weakened, and failed in the hostile invasion, and were become feeble:” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Deuteronomy 32:36 For the LORD shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants, when he seeth that [their] power is gone, and [there is] none shut up, or left.” \textsuperscript{34} in my; and took; in yourselves that ye have or, that ye have in yourselves, or, for yourselves. \textsuperscript{36} ye have; after; ye might\par}
