\subsection*{Hebrews 11}
\markright{HEBREWS 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For by it the elders obtained a good report. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word (o. rhema) of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that comes to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing where he went. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he looked for a city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them far off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he has prepared for them a city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall your seed be called: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} faith, ; is the, substance or, ground, or, confidence, ; *Gr. hoped, the evidence \textsuperscript{4} faith, ; a more; he obtained; and by; yet speaketh or, is yet spoken of \textsuperscript{5} Enoch; translated; and was; this testimony that he NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Genesis 5:24 And Enoch was well-pleasing to God, and was not found, because God translated him.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Genesis 5:24 And Enoch walked with God: and he [was] not; for God took him.” \textsuperscript{6} without, ;, ; he that; must a rewarder; , ; diligently \textsuperscript{7} Noah, ; Noe, warned; things moved with fear or, being wary, *Gr. prepared, ; he condemned; righteousness \textsuperscript{9} he sojourned, ; dwelling, the heirs \textsuperscript{12} and him as the stars, ; as the sand \textsuperscript{13} all died, in faith Gr. according to faith not but; and were; *Gr. confessed \textsuperscript{16} they desire, God is to be; for \textsuperscript{17} faith; when; received offered only \textsuperscript{22} faith; made mention of or, remembered \textsuperscript{23} faith; a proper child That is, a fine, beautiful, or fair child, as our translators render αστειος in; which was in their time the sense of proper, from the French propre . and they;, ; the king's \textsuperscript{25} Choosing; the people; the pleasures \textsuperscript{26} the reproach; of Christ or, for Christ greater; for he had \textsuperscript{27} he forsook, not fearing, endured, ; seeing \textsuperscript{31} the harlot; believed not or, were disobedient; she had \textsuperscript{32} what shall, the time Gedeon Judg. 6:1-8:35, Gideon, Jerubbaal Barak Judg. 4:1-5:31 Samson Judg. 13:1-16:31 Jephthae Judg. 11:1-12:7, Jephthah David, 17:1-18:30; Samuel, 3:1-12:25; the prophets \textsuperscript{33} through Josh. 6:1-13:33;, wrought, obtained; stopped \textsuperscript{34} Quenched; escaped; out of, ; turned \textsuperscript{35} Women; tortured, not accepting that they \textsuperscript{37} stoned; were slain;, ; in sheepskins; being destitute \textsuperscript{40} provided or, foreseen better, they without; made; The apostle in the early part of the chapter having given us a general account of the grace of faith, proceeds to set before us some illustrious examples of it in Old Testament times. The leading instance and example of faith recorded, is that of righteous Abel. One of the first saints and the first martyr for religion - one who lived by faith and died for it, and therefore a fit pattern for the Hebrews to imitate. It is observable that the Holy Spirit has not thought fit to say anything here of the faith of our first parents; and yet the church of God has generally, by a pious charity, taken it for granted that God gave them repentance and faith in the promised seed; that he instructed them in the mystery of sacrificing, that they instructed their children in it, and that they found mercy with God, after they had ruined themselves and all their posterity. But God has left the matter still under some doubt, as a warning to all who have great talents given to them, and a great trust reposed in them, that they do not prove unfaithful, since God would not enrol our first parents among the number of believers in this blessed calendar. - Henry.\par}

\subsection*{Hebrews 12}
\markright{HEBREWS 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which does so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest all of you be wearied and faint in your minds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} All of you have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And all of you have forgotten the exhortation which speaks unto you as unto children, My son, despise not you the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are rebuked of him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For whom the Lord loves he chastens, and scourges every son whom he receives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} If all of you endure chastening, God deals with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chastens not? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But if all of you be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are all of you bastards, and not sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, (o. pneuma) and live? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now no chastening for the present seems to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of food sold his birthright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For all of you know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For all of you are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; (o. rhema) which voice they that heard implored that the word (o. logos) should not be spoken to them any more: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But all of you are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits (o. pneuma) of just men made perfect, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaks better things that that of Abel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} See that all of you refuse not him that speaks. For if they escaped not who refused him that spoke on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaks from heaven: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he has promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And this word, Yet once more, signifies the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For our God is a consuming fire.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} seeing a cloud; witnesses; let us lay;, ; and the sin; and let us; with patience \textsuperscript{2} Looking; the author or, the beginner; *Gr:, finisher, *Gr:; for; endured;, ; despising; and is \textsuperscript{5} ye have forgotten; the exhortation; despise; nor faint NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. \subsection*{Hebrews 13}
\markright{HEBREWS 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Let brotherly love continue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unexpectedly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as all of you have: for he has said, I will never leave you, nor forsake you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word (o. logos) of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, (o. logos) that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is useless for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But I plead to you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is well-pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And I plead to you, brethren, suffer the word (o. logos) of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Know all of you that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he comes shortly, I will see you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Grace be with you all. Amen.\par

\section*{James Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} James the brother of the Lord\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The letter names James, and conservative scholarship receives it as written by James the Lord's brother, leader of the Jerusalem church.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} Acts 15 and Galatians 1-2 establish James's authority and profile consistent with the epistle.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} mid-40s to early 60s AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Practical wisdom epistle addressing scattered believers under trial.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To call believers to steadfastness, whole-hearted obedience, bridled speech, and living faith.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} trials; wisdom; faith and works; speech; worldliness; prayer\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Trials and wisdom 1; impartiality and living faith 2; speech and wisdom 3; worldliness and humility 4; endurance and prayer 5.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 20 and Papyrus 23 preserve early James fragments 3rd century AD | Subst. Major uncials preserve the earliest substantial James text 4th century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus preserve complete Greek James 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely early allusions in 1 Clement and Shepherd of Hermas; clear later attestation by Origen or earlier echoes (2nd-3rd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} James is comparatively late in explicit patristic attestation but textually secure in the received Greek tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives James as the epistle of the Lord's brother and not as a later pseudonymous moral tract.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{James}
\markboth{JAMES}{}
\subsection*{James 1}
\markright{JAMES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} My brethren, count it all joy when all of you fall into divers temptations; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Knowing this, that the trying of your faith works patience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But let patience have her perfect work, that all of you may be perfect and entire, lacking nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that gives to all men liberally, and reproaches not; and it shall be given him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavers is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A double minded man is unstable in all his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withers the grass, and the flower thereof falls, and the grace of the fashion of it perishes: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Blessed is the man that endures temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to them that love him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempts he any man: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then when lust has conceived, it brings forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, brings forth death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Do not go astray, my beloved brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Of his own will brings forth he us with the word (o. logos) of truth, that we should be a kind of first-fruits of his creatures. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the wrath of man works not the righteousness of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and abundance of evil, and receive with meekness the implanted word, (o. logos) which is able to save your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But be all of you doers of the word, (o. logos) and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For if any be a hearer of the word, (o. logos) and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For he beholds himself, and goes his way, and immediately forgets what manner of man he was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But whoso looks into the perfect law of liberty, and continues therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridles not his tongue, but deceives his own heart, this man's religion is vain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.\par

\subsection*{James 2}
\markright{JAMES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And all of you have respect to him that wears the cheerful clothing, and say unto him, Sit you here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand you there, or sit here under my footstool: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Are all of you not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Hearken, my beloved brethren, Has not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he has promised to them that love him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But all of you have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which all of you are called? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If all of you fulfill the royal law according to the scripture, You shall love your neighbour as yourself, all of you do well: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But if all of you have respect to persons, all of you commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if you commit no adultery, yet if you kill, you are become a transgressor of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So speak all of you, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For he shall have judgment without mercy, that has showed no mercy; and mercy rejoices against judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} What does it profit, my brethren, though a man say he has faith, and have not works? can faith save him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be all of you warmed and filled; notwithstanding all of you give them not those things which are necessary to the body; what does it profit? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Even so faith, if it has not works, is dead, being alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yea, a man may say, You have faith, and I have works: show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} You believe that there is one God; you do well: the devils also believe, and tremble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But will you know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} See you how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} All of you see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For as the body without the spirit (o. pneuma) is dead, so faith without works is dead also.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} the faith; the Lord; with \textsuperscript{2} assembly Gr. synagogue gold; goodly; in vile \textsuperscript{3} ye in a good place or well, or, seemly to the \textsuperscript{5} Hearken; Hath not; rich; , heirs; the or, that which \textsuperscript{8} the royal; Thou; ye do \textsuperscript{10} For While the Jews taught that "he who transgresses all the precepts of the law has broken the yoke, dissolved the covenant, and exposed the law to contempt; and so has he done who has only broken one precept; " they also taught, "that he who observed any principal command was equal to him who kept the whole law, " and gave for an example the forsaking of idolatry. To correct this false doctrine was the object James had in view. whosoever \textsuperscript{11} he said that, or, that law, which said Do not commit; Now \textsuperscript{13} he; , ; and; rejoiceth or, glorieth \textsuperscript{17} so, ; alone Gr. by itself \textsuperscript{18} Thou; without thy works Some copies read, by thy works. and I will \textsuperscript{22} Seest thou or, Thou seest faith; faith made \textsuperscript{23} the scripture; Abraham; the Friend; *marg. \textsuperscript{25} was; the harlot justified, when \textsuperscript{26} as; spirit or, breath so\par}

\subsection*{James 3}
\markright{JAMES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, (o. logos) the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, anywhere the governor decides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasts great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindles! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and has been tamed of mankind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the embodiment of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Does a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Who is a wise man and imbued with knowledge among you? let him show out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But if all of you have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} This wisdom descends not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be implored, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.\par

\subsection*{James 4}
\markright{JAMES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not behind, even of your lusts that war in your members? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} All of you lust, and have not: all of you kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: all of you fight and war, yet all of you have not, because all of you ask not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} All of you ask, and receive not, because all of you ask amiss, that all of you may consume it upon your lusts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} All of you adulterers and adulteresses, know all of you not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Do all of you think that the scripture says in vain, The spirit (o. pneuma) that dwells in us lusts to envy? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, God resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, all of you sinners; and purify your hearts, all of you double minded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaks evil of his brother, and judges his brother, speaks evil of the law, and judges the law: but if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who are you that judge another? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Go to now, all of you that say, To day or tomorrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whereas all of you know not what shall be on the next day. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For that all of you ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But now all of you rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore to him that knows to do good, and does it not, to him it is sin.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} whence fightings or, brawlings come they; lusts or, pleasures, in \textsuperscript{2} lust; kill or, envy because \textsuperscript{3} and; ye may, lusts or, pleasures \textsuperscript{4} adulterers; the friendship, ; enmity; whosoever is the \textsuperscript{5} the scripture, ; The spirit, ; to envy or, enviously \textsuperscript{6} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. \subsection*{James 5}
\markright{JAMES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Go to now, all of you rich men, weep and wail for your miseries that shall come upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth-eaten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. All of you have heaped treasure together for the last days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, cries: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} All of you have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; all of you have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} All of you have condemned and killed the just; and he does not resist you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, and has long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be all of you also patient; establish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draws nigh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest all of you be condemned: behold, the judge stands before the door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Behold, we count them happy which endure. All of you have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest all of you fall into condemnation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that all of you may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Brethren, if any of you do go astray from the truth, and one convert him; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Let him know, that he which converts the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.\par

\section*{1 Peter Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Peter the apostle\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The opening identifies Peter, and the church has always received 1 Peter as Petrine.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} The letter's self-identification and pastoral authority fit Peter speaking through Silvanus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} early 60s AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Circular letter to suffering believers in Asia Minor.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To strengthen believers under suffering with living hope, holy conduct, and Christ's example.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} suffering; holiness; hope; exile; Christ's example\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Living hope and holiness 1-2; suffering and witness 3-4; shepherding and humility 5.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Papyrus 72 contains 1 Peter 3rd-4th century AD | Subst. Papyrus 72 is the earliest substantial 1 Peter witness 3rd-4th century AD | Heb. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Gk. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus preserve complete Greek 1 Peter 4th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Likely echoed by Polycarp by Polycarp (early 2nd century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1 Peter is well attested and often discussed for its relation to the LXX in OT quotations.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} This edition receives 1 Peter as apostolic Petrine instruction to suffering exiles.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{1 Peter}
\markboth{1 PETER}{}
\subsection*{1 Peter 1}
\markright{1 PETER 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy has begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fades not away, reserved in heaven for you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Wherein all of you greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, all of you are in heaviness through manifold temptations: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perishes, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Whom having not seen, all of you love; in whom, though now all of you see him not, yet believing, all of you rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit (o. pneuma) of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister the things, which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But as he which has called you is holy, so be all of you holy in all manner of conversation; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Because it is written, Be all of you holy; for I am holy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And if all of you call on the Father, who without respect of persons judges according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Forasmuch as all of you know that all of you were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Who by him do believe in God, that raised him up from the dead, and gave him glory; that your faith and hope might be in God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Seeing all of you have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit (o. pneuma) unto sincere love of the brethren, see that all of you love one another with a pure heart fervently: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word (o. logos) of God, which lives and abides for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower thereof falls away: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But the word (o. rhema) of the Lord endures for ever. And this is the word (o. rhema) which by the gospel is preached unto you.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Peter; the; scattered; Pontus, Galatia; Cappadocia Asia, ; Bithynia \textsuperscript{2} Elect; , ; the foreknowledge;, sanctification; unto;, ; sprinkling, Grace; be *marg. \textsuperscript{3} Blessed; which; abundant Gr. much. hath; , unto, ; by \textsuperscript{4} an; incorruptible, undefiled fadeth; reserved; for you or, for us \textsuperscript{5} kept;, ; , ; through; unto; ready; in \textsuperscript{6} ye greatly; for; if; ye are; manifold \textsuperscript{7} the trial; precious; that; tried; might; at \textsuperscript{8} having; ye love; , ; believing; , unspeakable; full \textsuperscript{11} the Spirit; the sufferings, ; the glory \textsuperscript{12} it;, ; that not, ; that have; with;, ; sent; which things \textsuperscript{13} gird; be sober; hope; to the end Gr. perfectly the grace \textsuperscript{16} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 40:6-8 The voice of one saying, Cry; and I said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower fades: but the word of our God abides for ever.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 40:6-8 The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh [is] grass, and all the goodliness thereof [is] as the flower of the field: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people [is] grass. The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.”\par}

\subsection*{1 Peter 2}
\markright{1 PETER 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, all evil speaking, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that all of you may grow thereby: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If so be all of you have tasted that the Lord is gracious. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} All of you also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believes on him shall not be confounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, (o. logos) being disobedient: unto which also they were appointed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But all of you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, an exclusive people; that all of you should show forth the praises of him who has called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Dearly beloved, I plead to you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Or unto governors, as unto them that are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For so is the will of God, that with well doing all of you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} As free, and not using your liberty for a coat of maliciousness, but as the servants of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the perverse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For this deserves giving of thanks, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For what glory is it, if, when all of you be buffeted for your faults, all of you shall take it patiently? but if, when all of you do well, and suffer for it, all of you take it patiently, this is acceptable with God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For even hereunto were all of you called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that all of you should follow his steps: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judges righteously: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes all of you were healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For all of you were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} Wherefore laying; malice; guile; hypocrisies;, ; envies;, ; , all evil \textsuperscript{4} To; a living, ; stone; disallowed; chosen; precious \textsuperscript{5} also; are built or, be ye built an holy;, spiritual, ; acceptable \textsuperscript{7} you; precious or, an honour; which be; *marg.; *marg. the stone; the head \textsuperscript{9} a chosen; a royal;, an holy; peculiar or, purchased, ; show; praises or, virtues who \textsuperscript{11} I beseech; as; abstain; war \textsuperscript{12} your conversation; honest; among; that, ; , whereas or, wherein they may; glorify; the day \textsuperscript{15} so; with; the ignorance; foolish \textsuperscript{16} free; and using Gr. having a cloak; but \textsuperscript{17} Honour or, Esteem; Love; Fear, ; Honour \textsuperscript{19} this; thankworthy or, thank; *Gr. for conscience; suffering \textsuperscript{20} For; buffeted; when this; acceptable or, thank \textsuperscript{21} even; because, ; for us Some read, for you. leaving \textsuperscript{22} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 53:9 And I will give the wicked for his burial, and the rich for his death; for he practised no iniquity, nor craft with his mouth.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 53:9 And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither [was any] deceit in his mouth.” \textsuperscript{23} when he was; threatened; but; himself or, his cause judgeth \textsuperscript{24} his own self; on or, to the tree; being;, *marg., *Gr:; live; by; healed NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. \subsection*{1 Peter 3}
\markright{1 PETER 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Likewise, all of you wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, (o. logos) they also may without the word (o. logos) be won by the conversation of the wives; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with (o. rhema) fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of braiding the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, (o. pneuma) which is in the sight of God of great price. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters all of you are, as long as all of you do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Likewise, all of you husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Finally, be all of you all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that all of you are thereunto called, that all of you should inherit a blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let him shun evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and pursue it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And who is he that will harm you, if all of you be followers of that which is good? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But and if all of you suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are all of you: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asks you a reason (o. logos) of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For it is better, if the will of God be so, that all of you suffer for well doing, than for evil doing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For Christ also has once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} By which also he went and preached unto the spirits (o. pneuma) in prison; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The like figure unto which even baptism does also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.\par
{\notefont\fontsize{6.8}{7.5}\selectfont\noindent{\color{tnaccent}\textit{N: }}\textsuperscript{1} ye; *Gr:; obey; they; won \textsuperscript{4} the hidden; which is not a meek;, ; quiet; which is in \textsuperscript{6} as Sara daughters Gr. children; and \textsuperscript{8} be; having; love as brethren or, loving to the brethren, ; pitiful; courteous \textsuperscript{10} he love;, ; see, ; refrain, speak NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Psalms 33:12-16 What man is there that desires life, loving to see good days? Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile. Turn away from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil, to destroy their memorial from the earth. The righteous cried, and the Lord hearkened to them.” Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Psalms 34:12-16 What man [is he that] desireth life, [and] loveth [many] days, that he may see good? Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile. Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the LORD [are] upon the righteous, and his ears [are open] unto their cry. The face of the LORD [is] against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.” \textsuperscript{12} the eyes; his ears; but, ; against Gr. upon \textsuperscript{14} NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. \subsection*{1 Peter 4}
\markright{1 PETER 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Forasmuch then as Christ has suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind: for he that has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} That he no longer should live the rest of his time in the flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For the time past of our life may suffice us to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when we walked in lasciviousness, lusts, excess of wine, revellings, banquetings, and abominable idolatries: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Wherein they think it strange that all of you run not with them to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who shall give account (o. logos) to him that is ready to judge the quick and the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit. (o. pneuma) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But the end of all things is at hand: be all of you therefore sober, and watch unto prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And above all things have fervent love (o. agape) among yourselves: for love (o. agape) shall cover the multitude of sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Use hospitality one to another without grudging. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As every man has received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God gives: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But rejoice, inasmuch as all of you are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, all of you may be glad also with exceeding joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} If all of you be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are all of you; for the spirit (o. pneuma) of glory and of God rests upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men's matters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the time has come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.\par

\subsection*{1 Peter 5}
\markright{1 PETER 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The elders which are among you I exhort, who am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy illegal gain, but of a ready mind; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, all of you shall receive a crown of glory that fades not away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Likewise, all of you younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resists the proud, and gives grace to the humble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Casting all your care upon him; for he cares for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walks about, seeking whom he may devour: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Whom resist steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But the God of all grace, who has called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that all of you have suffered a while, make you perfect, establish, strengthen, settle you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein all of you stand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, salutes you; and so does Marcus my son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Greet all of you one another with a kiss of love. (o. agape) Peace be with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen.\par
