{\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Or like as when an arrow is shot at a mark, it parts the air, which immediately comes together again, so that a man can’t know where it went through: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to show; but were consumed in our own wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passes away as the remembrance of a guest that waits but a day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord's hand: for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armor, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} His severe wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then shall the right aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Yes, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 6}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Hear therefore, O you⌃ kings, and understand; learn, you⌃ that be judges of the ends of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Give ear, you⌃ that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you⌃ have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For he which is Lord over all shall fear no man's person, neither shall he stand in awe of any man's greatness: for he has made the small and great, and careth for all alike. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} To you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that you⌃ may learn wisdom, and not fall away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For they that keep holiness holily shall be judged holy: and they that have learned such things shall find what to answer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and you⌃ shall be instructed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Wisdom is glorious, and never fades away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} She prevents them that desire her, in making herself first known to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whoso seeks her early shall have no great travail: for he shall find her sitting at his doors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} To think therefore upon her is perfection of wisdom: and whoso watches for her shall quickly be without care. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, shows herself favourably to them in the ways, and meets them in every thought. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And incorruption makes us near to God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Therefore the desire of wisdom brings to a kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres, O you⌃ kings of the people, honor wisdom, that you⌃ may reign for evermore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Neither will I go with consuming envy; for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the upholding of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Receive therefore instruction through my words, and it shall do you good.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 7}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And in my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And when I was born, I drew in the common air, and fell upon the earth, which is of like nature, and the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and that with cares. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Neither compared I to her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that comes from her never goes out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goes before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} God has granted me to speak as I would, and to conceive as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leads to wisdom, and directs the wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For in his hand are both we and our words; all wisdom also, and knowledge of workmanship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For he has given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The circuits of years, and the positions of stars: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds, and the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtle, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good quick, which can’t be letted, ready to do good, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtle, spirits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passes and goes through all things by reason of her pureness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she makes all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she makes them friends of God, and prophets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For God loves none but him that dwells with wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For after this comes night: but vice shall not prevail against wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 8}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} [Wisdom] reaches from one end to another mightily: and sweetly does she order all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} I loved her, and sought her out from my youth, I desired to make her my spouse, and I was a lover of her beauty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} In that she is conversant with God, she magnifies her nobility: yes, the Lord of all things himself loved her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For she is privy to the mysteries of the knowledge of God, and a lover of his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If riches be a possession to be desired in this life; what is richer than wisdom, that works all things? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And if prudence work; who of all that are is a more cunning workman than she? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And if a man love righteousness her labors are virtues: for she teaches temperance and prudence, justice and fortitude: which are such things, as men can have nothing more profitable in their life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If a man desire much experience, she knows things of old, and conjectures aright what is to come: she knows the subtilties of speeches, and can expound dark sentences: she foresees signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and times. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellor of good things, and a comfort in cares and grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honor with the elders, though I be young. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When I hold my tongue, they shall bide my leisure, and when I speak, they shall give good ear to me: if I talk much, they shall lay their hands upon their mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Moreover by the means of her I shall obtain immortality, and leave behind me an everlasting memorial to them that come after me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I shall set the people in order, and the nations shall be subject to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Horrible tyrants shall be afraid, when they do but hear of me; I shall be found good among the multitude, and valiant in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} After I am come into my house, I will repose myself with her: for her conversation has no bitterness; and to live with her has no sorrow, but mirth and joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now when I considered these things in myself, and pondered them in my heart, how that to be allied to wisdom is immortality; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And great pleasure it is to have her friendship; and in the works of her hands are infinite riches; and in the exercise of conference with her, prudence; and in talking with her, a good report; I went about seeking how to take her to me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For I was a witty child, and had a good spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Yes rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Nevertheless, when I perceived that I could not otherwise obtain her, except God gave her me; and that was a point of wisdom also to know whose gift she was; I prayed to the Lord, and implored him, and with my whole heart I said,\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 9}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who have made all things with your word, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And ordained man through your wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which you have made, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And order the world according to equity and righteousness, and execute judgment with an upright heart: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Give me wisdom, that sits by your throne; and reject me not from among your children: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For I your servant and son of your handmaid am a feeble person, and of a short time, and too young for the understanding of judgment and laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if your wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a judge of your sons and daughters: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein you dwell, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And wisdom was with you: which knows your works, and was present when you made the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the throne of your glory, that being present she may labor with me, that I may know what is pleasing to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For she knows and understands all things, and she shall lead me soberly in my doings, and preserve me in her power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my father's seat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For what man is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can think what the will of the Lord is? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For the corruptible body presses down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weighs down the mind that muses upon many things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth, and with labor do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven who has searched out? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And your counsel who has known, except you give wisdom, and send your Holy Spirit from above? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you, and were saved through wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 10}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} She preserved the first formed father of the world, that was created alone, and brought him out of his fall, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And gave him power to rule all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserved him blameless to God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion toward his son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smokes is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For regarding not wisdom, they got not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good; but also left behind them to the world a memorial of their foolishness: so that in the things wherein they offended they could not so much as be hid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Rut wisdom delivered from pain those that attended upon her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} When the righteous fled from his brother's wrath she guided him in right paths, showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things, made him rich in his travels, and multiplied the fruit of his labors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In the covetousness of such as oppressed him she stood by him, and made him rich. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} She defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait, and in a sore conflict she gave him the victory; that he might know that goodness is stronger than all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When the righteous was sold, she forsook him not, but delivered him from sin: she went down with him into the pit, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she showed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} She delivered the righteous people and blameless seed from the nation that oppressed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} She entered into the soul of the servant of the Lord, and withstood dreadful kings in wonders and signs; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Rendered to the righteous a reward of their labors, guided them in a marvelous way, and was to them for a cover by day, and a light of stars in the night season; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Brought them through the Red sea, and led them through much water: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottom of the deep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, and praised your holy name, O Lord, and magnified with one accord your hand, that fought for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of them that can’t speak eloquent.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 11}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} She prospered their works in the hand of the holy prophet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} They went through the wilderness that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in places where there lay no way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} They stood against their enemies, and were avenged of their adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} When they were thirsty, they called upon you, and water was given them out of the flinty rock, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their need were benefited. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For instead of a fountain of a perpetual running river troubled with foul blood, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For a manifest reproof of that commandment, whereby the infants were slain, you gave to them abundance of water by a means which they hoped not for: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Declaring by that thirst then how you had punished their adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For when they were tried albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the ungodly were judged in wrath and tormented, thirsting in another manner than the just. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For these you did admonish and try, as a father: but the other, as a severe king, you did condemn and punish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Whether they were absent or present, they were vexed alike. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For a double grief came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they had some feeling of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For whom they respected with scorn, when he was long before thrown out at the casting forth of the infants, him in the end, when they saw what came to pass, they admired. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But for the foolish devices of their wickedness, wherewith being deceived they worshipped serpents void of reason, and vile beasts, you did send a multitude of unreasonable beasts upon them for vengeance; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} That they might know, that wherewithal a man sins, by the same also shall he be punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For your Almighty hand, that made the world of matter without form, wanted not means to send among them a multitude of bears or fierce lions, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Or unknown wild beasts, full of rage, newly created, breathing out either a fiery vapor, or filthy scents of scattered smoke, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their eyes: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Whereof not only the harm might dispatch them at once, but also the terrible sight utterly destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Yes, and without these might they have fallen down with one blast, being persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad through the breath of your power: but you have ordered all things in measure and number and weight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For you can show your great strength at all times when you will; and who may withstand the power of your arm? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For the whole world before you is as a little grain of the balance, yes, as a drop of the morning dew that falls down upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But you have mercy upon all; for you can do all things, and wink at the sins of men, because they should amend. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For you love all the things that are, and abhor nothing which you have made: for never would you have made any thing, if you had hated it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And how could any thing have endured, if it had not been your will? or been preserved, if not called by you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But you spare all: for they are your, O Lord, you lover of souls.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 12}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For your incorruptible Spirit is in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Therefore chasten you them by little and little that offend, and warn them by putting them in remembrance wherein they have offended, that leaving their wickedness they may believe on you, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For it was your will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of your holy land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Whom you hated for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And also those merciless murderers of children, and devourers of man's flesh, and the feasts of blood, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} With their priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} That the land, which you esteemed above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God's children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Nevertheless even those you spared as men, and did send wasps, forerunners of your host, to destroy them by little and little. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Not that you were unable to bring the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at once with cruel beasts, or with one rough word: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gave them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither did you for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment? or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish, whom you made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be revenged for the unrighteous men? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For neither is there any God but you that careth for all, to whom you might show that your judgment is not unright. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Neither shall king or tyrant be able to set his face against you for any whom you have punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Forsomuch then as you are righteous yourself, you order all things righteously: thinking it not agreeable with your power to condemn him that has not deserved to be punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For your power is the beginning of righteousness, and because you are the Lord of all, it makes you to be gracious to all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For when men will not believe that you are of a full power, you show your strength, and among them that know it you make their boldness manifest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But you, mastering your power, judge with equity, and order us with great favor: for you may use power when you will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful, and have made your children to be of a good hope that you give repentance for sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For if you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death, with such deliberation, giving them time and place, whereby they might be delivered from their malice: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} With how great circumspection did you judge your own sons, to whose fathers you have sworn, and made covenants of good promises? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore, whereas you do chasten us, you scourge our enemies a thousand times more, to the intent that, when we judge, we should carefully think of your goodness, and when we ourselves are judged, we should look for mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Therefore, whereas men have lived dissolutely and unrighteously, you have tormented them with their own abominations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For they went astray very far in the ways of error, and held them for gods, which even among the beasts of their enemies were despised, being deceived, as children of no understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore to them, as to children without the use of reason, you did send a judgment to mock them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But they that would not be reformed by that correction, wherein he dallied with them, shall feel a judgment worthy of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For, look, for what things they grudged, when they were punished, that is, for them whom they thought to be gods; [now] being punished in them, when they saw it, they acknowledged him to be the true God, whom before they denied to know: and therefore came extreme damnation upon them.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 13}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty has created them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But if they were astonished at their power and virtue, let them understand by them, how much mightier he is that made them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For by the greatness and beauty of the creatures proportionably the maker of them is seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But yet for this they are the less to be blamed: for they perhaps err, seeking God, and desirous to find him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For being conversant in his works they search him diligently, and believe their sight: because the things are beautiful that are seen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who call them gods, which are the works of men's hands, gold and silver, to show are in, and resemblances of beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the work of an ancient hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now a carpenter that fells timber, after he has sawn down a tree meet for the purpose, and taken off all the bark skilfully round about, and has wrought it handsomely, and made a vessel thereof fit for the service of man's life; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And after spending the refuse of his work to dress his meat, has filled himself; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And taking the very refuse among those which served to no use, being a crooked piece of wood, and full of knots, has carved it diligently, when he had nothing else to do, and formed it by the skill of his understanding, and fashioned it to the image of a man; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint colouring it red, and covering every spot therein; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And when he had made a convenient room for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast with iron: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For he provided for it that it might not fall, knowing that it was unable to help itself; for it is an image, and has need of help: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then makes he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For health he calls upon that which is weak: for life prays to that which is dead; for aid humbly implores that which has least means to help: and for a good journey he asks of that which can’t set a foot forward: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And for gaining and getting, and for good success of his hands, asks ability to do of him, that is most unable to do any thing.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 14}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Again, one preparing himself to sail, and about to pass through the raging waves, calls upon a piece of wood more rotten than the vessel that carries him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For verily desire of gain devised that, and the workman built it by his skill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But your providence, O Father, governs it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Shewing that you can save from all danger: yes, though a man went to sea without are. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Nevertheless you would not that the works of your wisdom should be idle, and therefore do men commit their lives to a small piece of wood, and passing the rough sea in a weak vessel are saved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For in the old time also, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world governed by your hand escaped in a weak vessel, and left to all ages a seed of generation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For blessed is the wood whereby righteousness comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For the ungodly and his ungodliness are both alike hateful to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For that which is made shall be punished together with him that made it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore even upon the idols of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of God they are become an abomination, and stumbling blocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he has made an image of his child soon taken away, now honored him as a god, which was then a dead man, and delivered to those that were under him ceremonies and sacrifices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Thus in process of time an ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Whom men could not honor in presence, because they lived far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they honored, to the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Also the singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For he, perhaps willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god, which a little before was but honored. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And this was an occasion to deceive the world: for men, serving either calamity or tyranny, did ascribe to stones and stocks the incommunicable name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God; but whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For while they killed their children in sacrifices, or used secret ceremonies, or made revellings of strange rites; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} They kept neither lives nor marriages any longer undefiled: but either one killed another traitorously, or grieved him by adultery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So that there reigned in all men without exception blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, unfaithfulness, tumults, perjury, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Disquieting of good men, forgetfulness of good turns, defiling of souls, changing of kind, disorder in marriages, adultery, and shameless uncleanness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For either they are mad when they be merry, or prophesy lies, or live unjustly, or else lightly forswear themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For insomuch as their trust is in idols, which have no life; though they swear falsely, yet they look not to be hurt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Howbeit for both causes shall they be justly punished: both because they thought not well of God, giving heed to idols, and also unjustly swore in deceit, despising holiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} For it is not the power of them by whom they swear: but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punishes always the offense of the ungodly.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 15}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But you, O God, are gracious and true, longsuffering, and in mercy ordering all things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For if we sin, we are your, knowing your power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted your. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For to know you is perfect righteousness: yes, to know your power is the root of immortality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For neither did the mischievous invention of men deceive us, nor an image spotted with various colors, the painter's fruitless labor; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The sight whereof entices fools to lust after it, and so they desire the form of a dead image, that has no breath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are lovers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust upon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashions every vessel with much labor for our service: yes, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And employing his labors lewdly, he makes a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returns to the same, out when his life which was lent him shall be demanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labor, nor that his life is short: but strives to excel goldsmiths and silversmiths, and endeavors to do like the workers in brass, and counts it his glory to make counterfeit things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile than earth, and his life of less value than clay: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Forasmuch as he knew not his Maker, and him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed in a living spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But they counted our life a pastime, and our time here a market for gain: for, say they, we must be getting every way, though it be by evil means. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For this man, that of earthly matter makes brittle vessels and graven images, knows himself to offend above all others. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And all the enemies of your people, that hold them in subjection, are most foolish, and are more miserable than very babes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them: but no man can make a god like to himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For being mortal, he works a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himself is better than the things which he worships: whereas he lived once, but they never. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Yes, they worshipped those beasts also that are most hateful: for being compared together, some are worse than others. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Neither are they beautiful, so much as to be desired in respect of beasts: but they went without the praise of God and his blessing.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 16}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore by the like were they punished worthily, and by the multitude of beasts tormented. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Instead of which punishment, dealing graciously with your own people, you prepared for them meat of a strange taste, even quails to stir up their appetite: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} To the end that they, desiring food, might for the ugly sight of the beasts sent among them lothe even that, which they must needs desire; but these, suffering penury for a short space, might be made partakers of a strange taste. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For it was requisite, that upon them exercising tyranny should come penury, which they could not avoid: but to these it should only be showed how their enemies were tormented. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, your wrath endured not for ever: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by you, that are the Saviour of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And in this you made your enemies confess, that it is you who deliver from all evil: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For them the bitings of grasshoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But your sons not the very teeth of venomous dragons overcame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For they were pricked, that they should remember your words; and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulness, they might be continually mindful of your goodness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but your word, O Lord, which heals all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For you have power of life and death: you lead to the gates of hell, and bring up again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A man indeed kills through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But it is not possible to escape your hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For the ungodly, that denied to know you, were scourged by the strength of your arm: with strange rains, hails, and showers, were they persecuted, that they could not avoid, and through fire were they consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water, that quenches all things: for the world fights for the righteous. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For sometime the flame was mitigated, that it might not burn up the beasts that were sent against the ungodly; but themselves might see and perceive that they were persecuted with the judgment of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And at another time it burns even in the midst of water above the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an unjust land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Instead whereof you fed your own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labor, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man's liking. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But snow and ice endured the fire, and melted not, that they might know that fire burning in the hail, and sparkling in the rain, did destroy the fruits of the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But this again did even forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For the creature that serves you, who are the Maker increases his strength against the unrighteous for their punishment, and abates his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore even then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to your grace, that nourishes all things, according to the desire of them that had need: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} That your children, O Lord, whom you love, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For that which was not destroyed of the fire, being warmed with a little sunbeam, soon melted away: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} That it might be known, that we must prevent the sun to give you thanks, and at the dayspring pray to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For the hope of the unthankful shall melt away as the winter's hoar frost, and shall run away as unprofitable water.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 17}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 17}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} For great are your judgments, and can’t be expressed: therefore unnurtured souls have erred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the holy nation; they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bonds of a long night, lay [there] exiled from the eternal providence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For while they supposed to lie hid in their secret sins, they were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, being horribly astonished, and troubled with [strange] apparitions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For neither might the corner that held them keep them from fear: but noises [as of waters] falling down sounded about them, and sad visions appeared to them with heavy countenances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the stars endure to lighten that horrible night. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Only there appeared to them a fire kindled of itself, very dreadful: for being much terrified, they thought the things which they saw to be worse than the sight they saw not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} As for the illusions of are magick, they were put down, and their vaunting in wisdom was reproved with disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For they, that promised to drive away terrors and troubles from a sick soul, were sick themselves of fear, worthy to be laughed at. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For though no terrible thing did fear them; yet being scared with beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} They died for fear, denying that they saw the air, which could of no side be avoided. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasts grievous things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the help which reason offers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the expectation from within, being less, counts the ignorance more than the cause which brings the torment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But they sleeping the same sleep that night, which was indeed intolerable, and which came upon them out of the bottoms of inevitable hell, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Were partly vexed with monstrous apparitions, and partly fainted, their heart failing them: for a sudden fear, and not looked for, came upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So then whoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For whether he were husbandman, or shepherd, or a labourer in the field, he was overtaken, and endured that necessity, which could not be avoided: for they were all bound with one chain of darkness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Whether it were a whistling wind, or a melodious noise of birds among the spreading branches, or a pleasing fall of water running violently, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Or a terrible sound of stones cast down, or a running that could not be seen of skipping beasts, or a roaring voice of most savage wild beasts, or a rebounding echo from the hollow mountains; these things made them to swoon for fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the whole world shined with clear light, and none were hindered in their labor: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Over them only was spread an heavy night, an image of that darkness which should afterward receive them: but yet were they to themselves more grievous than the darkness.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 18}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 18}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Nevertheless your saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing, and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But for that they did not hurt them now, of whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, and implored them pardon for that they had been enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Instead whereof you gave them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honorably. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For they were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept your sons shut up, by whom the uncorrupt light of the law was to be given to the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when they had determined to kill the babes of the saints, one child being cast forth, and saved, to reprove them, you took away the multitude of their children, and destroyed them altogether in a mighty water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Of that night were our fathers certified before, that assuredly knowing to what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So of your people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For wherewith you did punish our adversaries, by the same you did glorify us, whom you had called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy law, that the saints should be like partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But on the other side there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, showed the cause of his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Yes, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wilderness: but the wrath endured not long. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his proper ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and your Majesty upon the diadem of his head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} To these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 19}
\markright{WISDOM OF SOLOMON 19}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy to the end: for he knew before what they would do; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} How that having given them leave to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For while they were yet mourning and making lamentation at the graves of the dead, they added another foolish device, and pursued them as fugitives, whom they had entreated to be gone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them to this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfil the punishment which was lacking to their torments: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And that your people might pass a wonderful way: but they might find a strange death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Where through all the people went that were defended with your hand, seeing your marvelous strange wonders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambs, praising you, O Lord, who had delivered them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For they were yet mindful of the things that were done while they sojourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, and how the river cast up a multitude of frogs instead of fishes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But afterwards they saw a new generation of fowls, when, being led with their appetite, they asked delicate meats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For quails came up to them from the sea for their contentment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And punishments came upon the sinners not without former signs by the force of thunders: for they suffered justly according to their own wickedness, insomuch as they used a more hard and hateful behavior toward strangers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For the Sodomites did not receive those, whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserved of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And not only so, but perhaps some respect shall be had of those, because they used strangers not friendly: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But these very grievously afflicted them, whom they had received with feastings, and were already made partakers of the same laws with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore even with blindness were these stricken, as those were at the doors of the righteous man: when, being compassed about with horrible great darkness, every one sought the passage of his own doors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, like as in a lute notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds; which may well be perceived by the sight of the things that have been done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For earthly things were turned into watery, and the things, that before swam in the water, now went upon the ground. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of the corruptible living things, though they walked therein; neither melted they the icy kind of heavenly meat that was of nature apt to melt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For in all things, O Lord, you did magnify your people, and glorify them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.\par
\newpage
\section*{Sirach Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Jesus son of Sirach; translated by his grandson\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The prologue identifies the translator and points back to Jesus ben Sirach as the original author.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the writer; the work is included here as part of the Brenton/Apocrypha corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} early 2nd century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Hebrew witnesses exist in part, though the book circulated widely in Greek through the translator's version.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The Greek translation by the grandson is the principal full form used in the LXX tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Extended wisdom instruction combining practical, moral, and covenantal teaching with praise of Israel's fathers.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To teach wisdom, fear of the Lord, and faithful covenant life in a changing Hellenistic world.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} wisdom; fear of the Lord; ethics; praise of fathers; law\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Instruction and ethics 1-43; praise of the fathers 44-50; closing prayer and colophon 51.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. Hebrew Sirach fragments from Cairo Geniza and other finds; Greek translator's prologue 2nd century BC onward | Subst. Hebrew fragments are substantial but partial; Greek remains the principal full witness Second Temple and medieval periods | Heb. No complete ancient Hebrew witness survives n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Sirach 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Known and used by early Jewish and Christian writers by Early Christian fathers (2nd-4th centuries AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Sirach is important because partial Hebrew survives, allowing comparison with the Greek translation in many places.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as Brenton Apocrypha material, with its partial Hebrew evidence noted but its non-Hebrew-canonical status maintained.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Sirach}
\markboth{SIRACH}{}
\subsection*{Sirach 1}
\markright{SIRACH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} All wisdom [comes] from the Lord, and is with him for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The word of God most high is the fountain of wisdom; and her ways are everlasting commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? or who has known her wise counsels? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} [To whom has the knowledge of wisdom been made manifest? and who has understood her great experience?] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} There is one wise and greatly to be feared, the Lord sitting upon his throne. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He created her, and saw her, and numbered her, and poured her out upon all his works. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} She is with all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her to them that love him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The fear of the Lord is honor, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The fear of the Lord makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whoso fears the Lord, it shall go well with him at the last, and he shall find favor in the day of his death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} She has built an everlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} To fear the Lord is fulness of wisdom, and fills men with her fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} She fills all their house with things desirable, and the garners with her increase. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish; both which are the gifts of God: and it enlarges their rejoicing that love him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Wisdom rains down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalts them to honor that hold her fast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and the branches thereof are long life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The fear of the Lord drives away sins: and where it is present, it turns away wrath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A furious man can’t be justified; for the sway of his fury shall be his destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A patient man will tear for a time, and afterward joy shall spring up to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He will hide his words for a time, and the lips of many shall declare his wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godliness is an abomination to a sinner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Distrust not the fear of the Lord when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Exalt not yourself, lest you fall, and bring dishonor upon your soul, and so God discover your secrets, and cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you came not in truth to the fear of the Lord, but your heart is full of deceit.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 2}
\markright{SIRACH 2}
