and be bold, it will not burst you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A fool travails with a word, as a woman in labor of a child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} As an arrow that sticks in a man's thigh, so is a word within a fool's belly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} There is one that slips in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that has not offended with his tongue? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Admonish your neighbor before you threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted [of him,] and wisdom obtains his love. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleases you; though afterward he do it, he angers him that nourishes him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool lacking in wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that has small understanding, and fears God, is better than one that has much wisdom, and transgresses the law of the most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turns aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wise man that justifies in judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} There is a wicked man that hangs down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not known, he will do you a mischief before you be aware. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And if for lack of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he finds opportunity he will do evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meet him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} A man's attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, show what he is.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 20}
\markright{SIRACH 20}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There is a reproof that is not comely: again, some man holds his tongue, and he is wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesses his fault shall be preserved from hurt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} How good is it, when you are reproved, to show repentance! for so shall you escape wilful sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; so is he that executes judgment with violence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} There is one that keeps silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becomes hateful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Some man holds his tongue, because he has not to answer: and some keeps silence, knowing his time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that uses many words shall be abhorred; and he that takes to himself authority therein shall be hated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} There is a sinner that has good success in evil things; and there is a gain that turns to loss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} There is a gift that shall not profit you; and there is a gift whose recompence is double. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifts up his head from a low estate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There is that buys much for a little, and repays it sevenfold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} A wise man by his words makes him beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The gift of a fool shall do you no good when you have it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looks to receive many things for one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He gives little, and upbraids much; he opens his mouth like a crier; to day he lends, and to morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of God and man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The fool says, I have no friends, I have no thank for all my good deeds, and they that eat my bread speak evil of me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} How often, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorn! for he knows not aright what it is to have; and it is all one to him as if he had it not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} An unseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the unwise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A wise sentence shall be rejected when it comes out of a fool's mouth; for he will not speak it in due season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} There is that is hindered from sinning through lack: and when he takes rest, he shall not be troubled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} There is that destroys his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthrows himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} There is that for bashfulness promises to his friend, and makes him his enemy for nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A wise man shall promote himself to honor with his words: and he that has understanding will please great men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He that tils his land shall increase his heap: and he that pleases great men shall get pardon for iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he can’t reprove. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Better is he that hides his folly than a man that hides his wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Necessary patience in seeking the Lord is better than he that leads his life without a guide.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 21}
\markright{SIRACH 21}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if you come too near it, it will bite you: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof can’t be healed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A prayer out of a poor man's mouth reaches to the ears of God, and his judgment comes speedily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He that hates to be reproved is in the way of sinners: but he that fears the Lord will repent from his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} An eloquent man is known far and near; but a man of understanding knows when he slips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that builds his house with other men's money is like one that gathers himself stones for the tomb of his burial. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He that keeps the law of the Lord gets the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} He that is not wise will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplies bitterness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel is like a pure fountain of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} If a skillful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding hears it, it displeases him, and he casts it behind his back. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as talk without sense. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Doctrine to fools is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} A fool lifts up his voice with laughter; but a wise man does scarce smile a little. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Learning is to a wise man as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A foolish man's foot is soon in his [neighbor's] house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A fool will peep in at the door into the house: but he that is well nurtured will stand without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} It is the rudeness of a man to listen at the door: but a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not to them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} When the ungodly curses Satan, he curses his own soul. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} A whisperer defiles his own soul, and is hated wherever he dwells.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 22}
\markright{SIRACH 22}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up will shake his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} An evil-nurtured man is the dishonor of his father that became the father of him: and a [foolish] daughter is born to his loss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that lives dishonestly is her father's heaviness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} She that is bold dishonors both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A tale out of season [is as] musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisdom are never out of time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Whoso teaches a fool is as one that glues a potsherd together, and as he that wakes one from a sound sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} He that tells a tale to a fool speaks to one in a slumber: when he has told his tale, he will say, What is the matter? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If children live honestly, and have wherewithal, they shall cover the baseness of their parents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} But children, being haughty, through disdain and lack of nurture do stain the nobility of their kindred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Weep for the dead, for he has lost the light: and weep for the fool, for he lacks understanding: make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the fool is worse than death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Seven days do men mourn for him that is dead; but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Talk not much with a fool, and go not to him that has no understanding: beware of him, lest you have trouble, and you shall never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and you shall find rest, and never be disquieted with madness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} What is heavier than lead? and what is the name thereof, but a fool? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} As timber girded and bound together in a building can’t be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is established by advised counsel shall fear at no time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A heart settled upon a thought of understanding is as a fair plaistering on the wall of a gallery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool can’t stand against any fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He that pricks the eye will make tears to fall: and he that pricks the heart makes it to show her knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whoso casts a stone at the birds frays them away: and he that upbraids his friend breaks friendship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Though you drew a sword at your friend, yet despair not: for there may be a returning [to favor.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} If you have opened your mouth against your friend, fear not; for there may be a reconciliation: except for upbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for for these things every friend will depart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Be faithful to your neighbor in his poverty, that you may rejoice in his prosperity: abide stedfast to him in the time of his trouble, that you may be heir with him in his heritage: for a mean estate is not always to be contemned: nor the rich that is foolish to be had in admiration. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} As the vapor and smoke of a furnace goes before the fire; so reviling before blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I will not be ashamed to defend a friend; neither will I hide myself from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And if any evil happen to me by him, every one that hears it will beware of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?\par
\subsection*{Sirach 23}
\markright{SIRACH 23}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart? that they spare me not for my ignorances, and it pass not by my sins: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Lest my ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me, whose hope is far from your mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O Lord, Father and God of my life, give me not a proud look, but turn away from your servants always a haughty mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and you shall hold him up that is desirous always to serve you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me your servant into an impudent mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Hear, O you⌃ children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keeps it shall never be taken in his lips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The sinner shall be left in his foolishness: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use yourself to the naming of the Holy One. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a blue mark: so he that swears and names God continually shall not be faultless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} A man that uses much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offense: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There is a word that is clothed about with death: God grant that it be not found in the heritage of Jacob; for all such things shall be far from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Use not your mouth to intemperate swearing, for therein is the word of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Remember your father and your mother, when you sit among great men. Be not forgetful before them, and so you by your custom become a fool, and wish that you had not been born, and curse they day of your nativity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words will never be reformed all the days of his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has kindled a fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who sees me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body sees me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knows not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He knew all things ere ever they were created; so also after they were perfected he looked upon them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspects not he shall be taken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaves her husband, and brings in an heir by another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For first, she has disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she has trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she has played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And they that remain shall know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter than to take heed to the commandments of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} It is great glory to follow the Lord, and to be received of him is long life.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 24}
\markright{SIRACH 24}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} I lived in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the holy tabernacle I served before him; and so was I established in Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Likewise in the beloved city he gave me rest, and in Jerusalem was my power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And I took root in an honorable people, even in the portion of the Lord's inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aspalathus, and I yielded a pleasant odour like the best myrrh, as galbanum, and onyx, and sweet storax, and as the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} As the turpentine tree I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honor and grace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} As the vine brought I forth pleasant savor, and my flowers are the fruit of honor and riches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} I am the mother of fair love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope: I therefore, being eternal, am given to all my children which are named of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Come to me, all you⌃ that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For my memorial is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than the honeycomb. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He that obeys me shall never be confounded, and they that work by me shall not do amiss. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high God, even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Faint not to be strong in the Lord; that he may confirm you, cleave to him: for the Lord Almighty is God alone, and beside him there is no other Saviour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He fills all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He makes the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He makes the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, behold, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Behold that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 25}
\markright{SIRACH 25}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbors, a man and a wife that agree together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Three sorts of men my soul hates, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doats. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} If you have gathered nothing in your youth, how can you find any thing in your age? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} There be nine things which I have judged in my heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that has joy of his children; and he that lives to see the fall of his enemy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Well is him that has found prudence, and he that speaks in the ears of them that will hear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} O how great is he that finds wisdom! yet is there none above him that fears the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But the love of the Lord passes all things for illumination: he that holds it, whereto shall he be likened? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleaving to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} [Give me] any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any revenge, but the revenge of enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} There is no head above the head of a serpent; and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The wickedness of a woman changes her face, and darkens her countenance like sackcloth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Her husband shall sit among his neighbors; and when he hears it shall sigh bitterly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall upon her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} A woman, if she maintain her husband, is full of anger, impudence, and much reproach. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A wicked woman abates the courage, makes an heavy countenance and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distress makes weak hands and feeble knees. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Give the water no passage; neither a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} If she go not as you would have her, cut her off from your flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 26}
\markright{SIRACH 26}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A virtuous woman rejoices her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Whether a man be rich or poor, if he have a good heart toward the Lord, he shall at all times rejoice with a cheerful countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} There be three things that my heart fears; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicates with all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that has hold of her is as though he held a scorpion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} A drunken woman and a gadder abroad causes great anger, and she will not cover her own shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If your daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Watch over an impudent eye: and marvel not if she trespass against you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} She will open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller when he has found a fountain, and drink of every water near her: by every hedge will she sit down, and open her quiver against every arrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The grace of a wife delights her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind can’t be valued. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} As the sun when it arises in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} As the clear light is upon the holy candlestick; so is the beauty of the face in ripe age. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of silver; so are the fair feet with a constant heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} My son, keep the flower of your age sound; and give not your strength to strangers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} When you have gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with your own seed, trusting in the goodness of your stock. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So your race which you leave shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that fears the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} A dishonest woman contemns shame: but an honest woman will reverence her husband. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A shameless woman shall be counted as a dog; but she that is shamefaced will fear the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} A woman that honors her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonors him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} A loud crying woman and a scold shall be sought out to drive away the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} There be two things that grieve my heart; and the third makes me angry: a man of war that suffers poverty; and men of understanding that are not set by; and one that returns from righteousness to sin; the Lord prepares such an one for the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} A merchant shall hardly keep himself from doing wrong; and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 27}
\markright{SIRACH 27}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Many have sinned for a small matter; and he that seeks for abundance will turn his eyes away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} As a nail sticks fast between the joinings of the stones; so does sin stick close between buying and selling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} As when one sifts with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The furnace proves the potter's vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The fruit declares if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} If you follow righteousness, you shall obtain her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The birds will resort to their like; so will truth return to them that practise in her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As the lion lies in wait for the prey; so sin for them that work iniquity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} The discourse of a godly man is always with wisdom; but a fool changes as the moon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If you be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The talk of him that swears much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The strife of the proud is blood shedding, and their revilings are grievous to the ear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whoso discovers secrets loses his credit; and shall never find friend to his mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Love your friend, and be faithful to him: but if you betray his secrets, follow no more after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For as a man has destroyed his enemy; so have you lost the love of your neighbor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} As one that lets a bird go out of his hand, so have you let your neighbor go, and shall not get him again {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Follow after him no more, for he is too far off; he is as a roe escaped out of the snare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement: but he that betrays secrets is without hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He that winks with the eyes works evil: and he that knows him will depart from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} When you are present, he will speak sweetly, and will admire your words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander your sayings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} I have hated many things, but nothing like him; for the Lord will hate him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whoso casts a stone on high casts it on his own head; and a deceitful stroke shall make wounds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Whoso digs a pit shall fall therein: and he that sets a trap shall be taken therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} He that works mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it comes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 28}
\markright{SIRACH 28}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that revenges shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins [in remembrance.] {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you pray. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from the Lord? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} He shows no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will entreat for pardon of his sins? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Remember your end, and let enmity cease; [remember] corruption and death, and abide in the commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbor: [remember] the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins: for a furious man will kindle strife, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A sinful man disquiets friends, and makes debate among them that be at peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} As the matter of the fire is, so it burns: and as a man's strength is, so is his wrath; and according to his riches his anger rises; and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} An hasty contention kindles a fire: and an hasty fighting sheds blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If you blow the spark, it shall burn: if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Curse the whisperer and double-tongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} A backbiting tongue has disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities has it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} A backbiting tongue has cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whoso hearkens to it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Well is he that is defended through the venom thereof; who has not drawn the yoke thereof, nor has been bound in her bands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For the yoke thereof is a yoke of iron, and the bands thereof are bands of brass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The death thereof is an evil death, the grave were better than it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} It shall not have rule over them that fear God, neither shall they be burned with the flame thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Such as forsake the Lord shall fall into it; and it shall burn in them, and not be quenched; it shall be sent upon them as a lion, and devour them as a leopard. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Look that you hedge your possession about with thorns, and bind up your silver and gold, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And weigh your words in a balance, and make a door and bar for your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Beware you slide not by it, lest you fall before him that lies in wait.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 29}
\markright{SIRACH 29}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that is merciful will lend to his neighbor; and he that strengthens his hand keeps the commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Lend to your neighbor in time of his need, and pay you your neighbor again in due season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Keep your word, and deal faithfully with him, and you shall always find the thing that is necessary for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Many, when a thing was lent them, reckoned it to be found, and put them to trouble that helped them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Till he has received, he will kiss a man's hand; and for his neighbor's money he will speak submissly: but when he should repay, he will prolong the time, and return words of grief, and complain of the time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If he prevail, he shall hardly receive the half, and he will count as if he had found it: if not, he has deprived him of his money, and he has gotten him an enemy without cause: he pays him with cursings and railings; and for honor he will pay him disgrace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Many therefore have refused to lend for other men's ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Yet have you patience with a man in poor estate, and delay not to show him mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Help the poor for the commandment's sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and let it not rust under a stone to be lost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} It shall fight for you against your enemies better than a mighty shield and strong spear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} An honest man is surety for his neighbor: but he that is impudent will forsake him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Forget not the friendship of your surety, for he has given his life for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} A sinner will overthrow the good estate of his surety: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And he that is of an unthankful mind will leave him [in danger] that delivered him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Suretiship has undone many of good estate, and shaken them as a wave of the sea: mighty men has it driven from their houses, so that they wandered among strange nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A wicked man transgressing the commandments of the Lord shall fall into suretiship: and he that undertakes and follows other men's business for gain shall fall into suits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Help your neighbor according to your power, and beware that you yourself fall not into the same. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man's house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Be it little or much, hold you contented, that you hear not the reproach of your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where you are a stranger, you dare not open your mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} You shall entertain, and feast, and have no thanks: moreover you shall hear bitter words: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Come, you stranger, and furnish a table, and feed me of that you have ready. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Give place, you stranger, to an honorable man; my brother comes to be lodged, and I have need of my house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} These things are grievous to a man of understanding; the upbraiding of houseroom, and reproaching of the lender.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 30}
\markright{SIRACH 30}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that loves his son causes him often to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He that chastises his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} He that teaches his son grieves the enemy: and before his friends he shall rejoice of him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he has left one behind him that is like himself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He that makes too much of his son shall bind up his wounds; and his bowels will be troubled at every cry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} An horse not broken becomes headstrong: and a child left to himself will be wilful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Cocker your child, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he will bring you to heaviness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow with him, and lest you gnash your teeth in the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient to you, and so bring sorrow to your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Chastise your son, and hold him to labor, lest his lewd behavior be an offense to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Better is the poor, being sound and strong of constitution, than a rich man that is afflicted in his body. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Delicates poured upon a mouth shut up are as messes of meat set upon a grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} What good does the offering to an idol? for neither can it eat nor smell: so is he that is persecuted of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} He sees with his eyes and groanes, as an eunuch that embraces a virgin and sighs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Give not over your mind to heaviness, and afflict not yourself in your own counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongs his days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Love your own soul, and comfort your heart, remove sorrow far from you: for sorrow has killed many, and there is no profit therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Envy and wrath shorten the life, and carefulness brings age before the time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} A cheerful and good heart will have a care of his meat and diet.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 31}
\markright{SIRACH 31}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Watching for riches consumes the flesh, and the care thereof drives away sleep. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Watching care will not let a man slumber, as a sore disease breaks sleep, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The rich has great labor in gathering riches together; and when he rests, he is filled with his delicates. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The poor labores in his poor estate; and when he leaves off, he is still needy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that follows corruption shall have enough thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} It is a stumbling block to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken therewith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Who is he? and we will call him blessed: for wonderful things has he done among his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Who has been tried thereby, and found perfect? then let him glory. Who might offend, and has not offended? or done evil, and has not done it? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} His goods shall be established, and the congregation shall declare his alms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weeps upon every occasion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Stretch not your hand wherever it looks, and thrust it not with him into the dish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Judge not your neighbor by yourself: and be discreet in every point. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Eat as it becomes a man, those things which are set before you; and devour note, lest you be hated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Leave off first for manners' sake; and be not unsatiable, lest you offend. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} When you sit among many, reach not your hand out first of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} A very little is sufficient for a man well nurtured, and he fetches not his wind short upon his bed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Sound sleep comes of moderate eating: he rises early, and his wits are with him: but the pain of watching, and choler, and pangs of the belly, are with an unsatiable man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And if you have been forced to eat, arise, go forth, vomit, and you shall have rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} My son, hear me, and despise me not, and at the last you shall find as I told you: in all your works be quick, so shall there no sickness come to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Whoso is liberal of his meat, men shall speak well of him; and the report of his good housekeeping will be believed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But against him that is a niggard of his meat the whole city shall murmur; and the testimonies of his niggardness shall not be doubted of. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Show not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The furnace proves the edge by dipping: so does wine the hearts of the proud by drunkenness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Wine measurably drunk and in season brings gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But wine drunken with excess makes bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminishes strength, and makes wounds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Rebuke not your neighbor at the wine, and despise him not in his mirth: give him no despiteful words, and press not upon him with urging him [to drink.]\par
\subsection*{Sirach 32}
\markright{SIRACH 32}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} If you be made the master [of a feast,] lift not yourself up, but be among them as one of the rest; take diligent care for them, and so sit down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when you have done all your office, take your place, that you may be merry with them, and receive a crown for your well ordering of the feast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Speak, you that are the elder, for it becomes you, but with sound judgment; and hinder not musick. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Pour not out words where there is a musician, and show not forth wisdom out of time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A concert of musick in a banquet of wine is as a signet of carbuncle set in gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} As a signet of an emerald set in a work of gold, so is the melody of musick with pleasant wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Speak, young man, if there be need of you: and yet scarcely when you are twice asked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Let your speech be short, comprehending much in few words; be as one that knows and yet holds his tongue. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} If you be among great men, make not yourself equal with them; and when ancient men are in place, use not many words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Before the thunder goes lightning; and before a shamefaced man shall go favor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Rise up betimes, and be not the last; but get you home without delay. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} There take your pastime, and do what you will: but sin not by proud speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And for these things bless him that made you, and has replenished you with his good things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whoso fears the Lord will receive his discipline; and they that seek him early shall find favor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He that seeks the law shall be filled therewith: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} A sinful man will not be reproved, but finds an excuse according to his will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} A man of counsel will be considerate; but a strange and proud man is not daunted with fear, even when of himself he has done without counsel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Do nothing without advice; and when you have once done, repent not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Go not in a way wherein you may fall, and stumble not among the stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Be not confident in a plain way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And beware of your own children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} In every good work trust your own soul; for this is the keeping of the commandments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He that believes in the Lord takes heed to the commandment; and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.\par
\subsection*{Sirach 33}
\markright{SIRACH 33}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There shall no evil happen to him that fears the Lord; but in temptation even again he will deliver him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} A wise man hates not the law; but he that is an hypocrite therein is as a ship in a storm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} A man of understanding trusts in the law; and the law is faithful to him, as an oracle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard: and bind up instruction, and then make answer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axle tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} A stallion horse is as a mocking friend, he neighs under every one that sits upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Why does one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Some of them has he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them has he made ordinary days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In much knowledge the Lord has divided them, and made their ways diverse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Some of them has he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself: but some of them has he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} As the clay is in the potter's hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as likes him best. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I awaked up last of all, as one that gathers after the grape gatherers: by the blessing of the Lord I profited, and filled my winepress like a gatherer of grapes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Hear me, O you⌃ great men of the people, and listen with your ears, you⌃ rulers of the congregation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Give not your son and wife, your brother and friend, power over you while you live, and give not your goods to another: lest it repent you, and you entreat for the same again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As long as you live and have breath in you, give not yourself over to any. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} For better it is that your children should seek to you, than that you should stand to their courtesy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} In all your works keep to yourself the preeminence; leave not a stain in your honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} At the time when you shall end your days, and finish your life, distribute your inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} If you set your servant to labor, you shall find rest: but if you let him go idle, he shall seek liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} A yoke and a collar do bow the neck: so are tortures and torments for an evil servant. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Send him to labor, that he be not idle; for idleness teaches much evil. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} If you have a servant, let him be to you as yourself, because you have bought him with a price. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} If you have a servant, entreat him as a brother: for you have need of him, as of your own soul: if you entreat him evil, and he run from you, which way will you go to seek him?\par
\subsection*{Sirach 34}
\markright{SIRACH 34}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Whoso regards dreams is like him that catches at a shadow, and follows after the wind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Of an unclean thing what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false what truth can come? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain: and the heart fancies, as a woman's heart in travail. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} If they be not sent from the most High in your visitation, set not your heart upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} A man that has travelled knows many things; and he that has much experience will declare wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He that has no experience knows little: but he that has travelled is full of prudence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The spirit of those that fear the Lord shall live; for their hope is in him that saves them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whoso fears the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Blessed is the soul of him that fears the Lord: to whom does he look? and who is his strength? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, a preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} He raises up the soul, and lightens the eyes: he gives health, life, and blessing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} He that sacrifices of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor does as one that kills the son before his father's eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The bread of the needy is their life: he that defrauds him thereof is a man of blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} He that takes away his neighbor's living slays him; and he that defrauds the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} When one builds, and another pulls down, what profit have they then but labor? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} When one prays, and another curses, whose voice will the Lord hear? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He that washes himself after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what avails his washing? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} So is it with a man that fasts for his sins, and goes again, and does the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?\par
\subsection*{Sirach 35}
\markright{SIRACH 35}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} He that keeps the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} He that requites a good turn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrifices praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You shall not appear empty before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For all these things [are to be done] because of the commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The offering of the righteous makes the altar fat, and the sweet savor thereof is before the most High. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable. and the memorial thereof shall never be forgotten. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Give the Lord his honor with a good eye, and diminish not the first fruits of your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} In all your gifts show a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Give to the most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For the Lord recompenses, and will give you seven times as much. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Do not think to corrupt with gifts;
