and so my prayer was heard: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For you saved me from destruction, and delivered me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise you, and bless they name, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Even from the flower till the grape was ripe has my heart delighted in her: my foot went the right way, from my youth up sought I after her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} I bowed down my ear a little, and received her, and got much learning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} I profited therein, therefore will I ascribe glory to him that gives me wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For I purposed to do after her, and earnestly I followed that which is good; so shall I not be confounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} My soul has wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact: I stretched forth my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I directed my soul to her, and I found her in pureness: I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The Lord has given me a tongue for my reward, and I will praise him therewith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Draw near to me, you⌃ unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Therefore are you⌃ slow, and what say you⌃ to these things, seeing your souls are very thirsty? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} I opened my mouth, and said, Buy her for yourselves without money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labor, and have gotten to me much rest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Get learning with a great sum of money, and get much gold by her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.\par
\newpage
\section*{Baruch Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Attributed to Baruch in the book's frame; exact composition history debated\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The work presents itself in Baruch's name, but the final literary history is complex.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; this edition includes Baruch as part of the Brenton/Apocrypha corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} exilic frame; likely later composition history\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} No secure full Hebrew original survives for the whole book.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The Greek tradition is the principal full witness.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Exilic-style confession, wisdom, and consolation material linked to Jeremiah's circle.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To call the exiles to confession, wisdom, and hope in God's mercy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} confession; wisdom; exile; consolation; Jerusalem\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Confession and prayer 1-3; wisdom poem 3-4; consolation 4-5.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No early full Hebrew witness survives n/a | Subst. Greek tradition is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Greek Baruch 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used in later Christian tradition by Church fathers (2nd-4th centuries AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Baruch is transmitted in Greek with important ties to Jeremiah material and to the Letter of Jeremiah in some traditions.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as part of the Brenton Apocrypha and clearly separated from the Hebrew canon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Baruch}
\markboth{BARUCH}{}
\subsection*{Baruch 1}
\markright{BARUCH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And these are the words of the book, which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maasias, the son of Sedecias, the son of Asadias, the son of Chelcias, wrote in Babylon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} In the fifth year, and in the seventh day of the month, what time as the Chaldeans took Jerusalem, and burnt it with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And Baruch did read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias the son of Joachim king of Juda, and in the ears of all the people that came to hear the book, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And in the hearing of the nobles, and of the king's sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and of all the people, from the lowest to the highest, even of all them that lived at Babylon by the river Sud. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Whereupon they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} They made also a collection of money according to every man's power: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they sent it to Jerusalem to Joachim the high priest, the son of Chelcias, son of Salom, and to the priests, and to all the people which were found with him at Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} At the same time when he received the vessels of the house of the Lord, that were carried out of the temple, to return them into the land of Juda, the tenth day of the month Sivan, namely, silver vessels, which Sedecias the son of Josias king of Jada had made, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} After that Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away Jechonias, and the princes, and the captives, and the mighty men, and the people of the land, from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And they said, Behold, we have sent you money to buy you burnt offerings, and sin offerings, and incense, and prepare you⌃ manna, and offer upon the altar of the Lord our God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Balthasar his son, that their days may be upon earth as the days of heaven: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And the Lord will give us strength, and lighten our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Balthasar his son, and we shall serve them many days, and find favor in their sight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Pray for us also to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God; and to this day the fury of the Lord and his wrath is not turned from us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And you⌃ shall read this book which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the Lord, upon the feasts and solemn days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And you⌃ shall say, To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us the confusion of faces, as it is come to pass this day, to them of Juda, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And to our kings, and to our princes, and to our priests, and to our prophets, and to our fathers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For we have sinned before the Lord, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And disobeyed him, and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments that he gave us openly: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Since the day that the Lord brought our forefathers out of the land of Egypt, to this present day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we have been negligent in not hearing his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Therefore the evils cleaved to us, and the curse, which the Lord appointed by Moses his servant at the time that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land that flows with milk and honey, like as it is to see this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Nevertheless we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, according to all the words of the prophets, whom he sent to us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But every man followed the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our God.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 2}
\markright{BARUCH 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Therefore the Lord has made good his word, which he pronounced against us, and against our judges that judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Juda, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the law of Moses; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Moreover he has delivered them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be as a reproach and desolation among all the people round about, where the Lord has scattered them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and have not been obedient to his voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} To the Lord our God appertains righteousness: but to us and to our fathers open shame, as appears this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For all these plagues are come upon us, which the Lord has pronounced against us {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Yet have we not prayed before the Lord, that we might turn every one from the imaginations of his wicked heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore the Lord watched over us for evil, and the Lord has brought it upon us: for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he has commanded us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Yet we have not listened to his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he has set before us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now, O Lord God of Israel, that have brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and high arm, and with signs, and with wonders, and with great power, and have gotten yourself a name, as appears this day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} O Lord our God, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all your ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let your wrath turn from us: for we are but a few left among the heathen, where you have scattered us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliver us for your own sake, and give us favor in the sight of them which have led us away: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} That all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by your name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} O Lord, look down from your holy house, and consider us: bow down your ear, O Lord, to hear us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Open your eyes, and behold; for the dead that are in the graves, whose souls are taken from their bodies, will give to the Lord neither praise nor righteousness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But the soul that is greatly vexed, which goes stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will give you praise and righteousness, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore we do not make our humble supplication before you, O Lord our God, for the righteousness of our fathers, and of our kings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For you have sent out your wrath and indignation upon us, as you have spoken by your servants the prophets, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Thus says the Lord, Bow down your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon: so shall you⌃ remain in the land that I gave to your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But if you⌃ will not hear the voice of the Lord, to serve the king of Babylon, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} I will cause to cease out of the cites of Judah, and from without Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: and the whole land shall be desolate of inhabitants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But we would not listen to your voice, to serve the king of Babylon: therefore have you made good the words that you spoke by your servants the prophets, namely, that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers, should be taken out of their place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And, behold, they are cast out to the heat of the day, and to the frost of the night, and they died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And the house which is called by your name have you laid waste, as it is to be seen this day, for the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Juda. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} O Lord our God, you have dealt with us after all your goodness, and according to all that great mercy of yours, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} As you spoke by your servant Moses in the day when you did command him to write the law before the children of Israel, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} If you⌃ will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiff-necked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 3}
\markright{BARUCH 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish the troubled spirit, cries to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for you are merciful: and have pity upon us, because we have sinned before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For you endure for ever, and we perish utterly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O Lord Almighty, you God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before you, and not listened to the voice of you their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Remember not the iniquities of our forefathers: but think upon your power and your name now at this time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For you are the Lord our God, and you, O Lord, will we praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And for this cause you have put your fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon your name, and praise you in our captivity: for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our forefathers, that sinned before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where you have scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Hear, Israel, the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} How is it Israel, that you are in your enemies' land, that you have become old in a strange country, that you are defiled with the dead, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} That you are counted with them that go down into the grave? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For if you had walked in the way of God, you should have dwelled in peace for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that you may know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Who has found out her place? or who has come into her treasures? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Where are the princes of the heathen become, and such as ruled the beasts upon the earth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} They that had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and they that hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and made no end of their getting? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For they that wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are unsearchable, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their steads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Young men have seen light, and lived upon the earth: but the way of knowledge have they not known, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Nor understood the paths thereof, nor laid hold of it: their children were far off from that way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} It has not been heard of in Chanaan, neither has it been seen in Theman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The Agarenes that seek wisdom upon earth, the merchants of Meran and of Theman, the authors of fables, and searchers out of understanding; none of these have known the way of wisdom, or remember her paths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} O Israel, how great is the house of God! and how large is the place of his possession! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Great, and has none end; high, and unmeasurable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge to them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} No man knows her way, nor thinks of her path. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But he that knows all things knows her, and has found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore has filled it with four-footed beasts: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} He that sends forth light, and it goes, calls it again, and it obeys him with fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calls them, they say, Here we be; and so with cheerfulness they showed light to him that made them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Afterward did he show himself upon earth, and conversed with men.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 4}
\markright{BARUCH 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Turn you, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that you may be illuminated. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Give not your honor to another, nor the things that are profitable to you to a strange nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You⌃ were sold to the nations, not for [your] destruction: but because you⌃ moved God to wrath, you⌃ were delivered to the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For you⌃ provoked him that made you by sacrificing to devils, and not to God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} You⌃ have forgotten the everlasting God, that brought you up; and you⌃ have grieved Jerusalem, that nursed you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For when she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, she said, Listen, O you⌃ that dwell about Sion: God has brought upon me great mourning; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} With joy did I nourish them; but sent them away with weeping and mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Let no man rejoice over me, a widow, and forsaken of many, who for the sins of my children am left desolate; because they departed from the law of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} They knew not his statutes, nor walked in the ways of his commandments, nor trod in the paths of discipline in his righteousness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember you⌃ the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting has brought upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} For he has brought a nation upon them from far, a shameless nation, and of a strange language, who neither reverenced old man, nor pitied child. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} These have carried away the dear beloved children of the widow, and left her that was alone desolate without daughters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But what can I help you? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For he that brought these plagues upon you will deliver you from the hands of your enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} I have put off the clothing of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my prayer: I will cry to the Everlasting in my days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Be of good cheer, O my children, cry to the Lord, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you; and joy is come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come to you from the Everlasting our Saviour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Like as now the neighbors of Sion have seen your captivity: so shall they see shortly your salvation from our God which shall come upon you with great glory, and brightness of the Everlasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for your enemy has persecuted you; but shortly you shall see his destruction, and shall tread upon his neck. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flock caught of the enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry to God: for you⌃ shall be remembered of him that brought these things upon you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For he that has brought these plagues upon you shall bring you everlasting joy with your salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave you that name will comfort you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Miserable are they that afflicted you, and rejoiced at your fall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Miserable are the cities which your children served: miserable is she that received your sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} For as she rejoiced at your ruin, and was glad of your fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Behold, your sons come, whom you sent away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 5}
\markright{BARUCH 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Put off, O Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and affliction, and put on the comeliness of the glory that comes from God for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Cast about you a double garment of the righteousness which comes from God; and set a diadem on your head of the glory of the Everlasting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For God will show your brightness to every country under heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For your name shall be called of God for ever The peace of righteousness, and The glory of God's worship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For they departed from you on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but God brings them to you exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For God has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Moreover even the woods and every sweet smelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.\par
\newpage
\section*{Letter of Jeremiah Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Attributed to Jeremiah in literary frame; exact human authorship uncertain\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The superscription links it with Jeremiah, but the work's precise literary history is debated.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; it is included here as part of the Brenton Apocrypha corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Hellenistic period or earlier tradition\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek is the principal full witness, though some Semitic background has been proposed.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Polemic letter against idolatry framed as warning to exiles.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To expose the folly of idols and strengthen covenant faithfulness in exile.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} idolatry critique; exile; polemic; fidelity\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Single sustained anti-idolatry discourse.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No secure full Hebrew witness survives n/a | Subst. Greek tradition is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve the Greek Letter of Jeremiah 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used in later Christian tradition by Church fathers (2nd-4th centuries AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Often transmitted with Baruch; textual handling depends on the Greek tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as apocryphal material attached to the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Epistle of Jeremy}
\markboth{EPISTLE OF JEREMY}{}
\subsection*{Epistle of Jeremy 1}
\markright{EPISTLE OF JEREMY 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} A copy of an epistle, which Jeremy sent to them which were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to certify them, as it was commanded him of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Because of the sins which you⌃ have committed before God, you⌃ shall be led away captives into Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So when you⌃ be come to Babylon, you⌃ shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now shall you⌃ see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Beware therefore that you⌃ in no wise be like to strangers, neither be you⌃ and of them, when you⌃ see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But say you⌃ in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} For my angel is with you, and I myself caring for your souls. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} As for their tongue, it is polished by the workman, and they themselves are gilded and laid over with silver; yet are they but false, and can’t speak. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And taking gold, as it were for a virgin that loves to go gay, they make crowns for the heads of their gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Sometimes also the priests convey from their gods gold and silver, and bestow it upon themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Yes, they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, [being] gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Yet can’t these gods save themselves from rust and moth, though they be covered with purple raiment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And he that can’t put to death one that offends him holds a scepter, as though he were a judge of the country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He has also in his right hand a dagger and an axe: but can’t deliver himself from war and thieves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For like as a vessel that a man uses is nothing worth when it is broken; even so it is with their gods: when they be set up in the temple, their eyes be full of dust through the feet of them that come in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And as the doors are made sure on every side upon him that offends the king, as being committed to suffer death: even so the priests make fast their temples with doors, with locks, and bars, lest their gods be spoiled with robbers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} They light them candles, yes, more than for themselves, whereof they can’t see one. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} They are as one of the beams of the temple, yet they say their hearts are gnawed upon by things creeping out of the earth; and when they eat them and their clothes, they feel it not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Their faces are blacked through the smoke that comes out of the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Upon their bodies and heads sit bats, swallows, and birds, and the cats also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} By this you⌃ may know that they are no gods: therefore fear them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Notwithstanding the gold that is about them to make them beautiful, except they wipe off the rust, they will not shine: for neither when they were molten did they feel it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The things wherein there is no breath are bought for a most high price. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} They are borne upon shoulders, having no feet whereby they declare to men that they be nothing worth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} They also that serve them are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they can’t rise up again of themselves: neither, if one set them upright, can they move of themselves: neither, if they be bowed down, can they make themselves straight: but they set gifts before them as to dead men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} As for the things that are sacrificed to them, their priests sell and abuse; in like manner their wives lay up part thereof in salt; but to the poor and impotent they give nothing of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Menstruous women and women in childbed eat their sacrifices: by these things you⌃ may know that they are no gods: fear them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} For how can they be called gods? because women set meat before the gods of silver, gold, and wood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the priests sit in their temples, having their clothes torn, and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing upon their heads. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} They roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} The priests also take off their garments, and clothe their wives and children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Whether it be evil that one does to them, or good, they are not able to recompense it: they can neither set up a king, nor put him down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money: though a man make a vow to them, and keep it not, they will not require it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} They can save no man from death, neither deliver the weak from the mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} They can’t restore a blind man to his sight, nor help any man in his distress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} They can show no mercy to the widow, nor do good to the fatherless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Their gods of wood, and which are overlaid with gold and silver, are like the stones that be hewn out of the mountain: they that worship them shall be confounded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} How should a man then think and say that they are gods, when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Who if they shall see one dumb that can’t speak, they bring him, and entreat Bel that he may speak, as though he were able to understand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Yet they can’t understand this themselves, and leave them: for they have no knowledge. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} The women also with cords about them, sitting in the ways, burn bran for perfume: but if any of them, drawn by some that passes by, lie with him, she reproaches her fellow, that she was not thought as worthy as herself, nor her cord broken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Whatsoever is done among them is false: how may it then be thought or said that they are gods? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} They are made of carpenters and goldsmiths: they can be nothing else than the workmen will have them to be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And they themselves that made them can never continue long; how should then the things that are made of them be gods? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} For they left lies and reproaches to them that come after. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} For when there comes any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselves, where they may be hidden with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} How then can’t men perceive that they be no gods, which can neither save themselves from war, nor from plague? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} For seeing they be but of wood, and overlaid with silver and gold, it shall be known hereafter that they are false: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} And it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men's hands, and that there is no work of God in them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Who then may not know that they are no gods? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} For neither can they set up a king in the land, nor give rain to men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Neither can they judge their own cause, nor redress a wrong, being unable: for they are as crows between heaven and earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Whereupon when fire falls upon the house of gods of wood, or laid over with gold or silver, their priests will flee away, and escape; but they themselves shall be burned asunder like beams. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Moreover they can’t withstand any king or enemies: how can it then be thought or said that they be gods? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} Neither are those gods of wood, and laid over with silver or gold, able to escape either from thieves or robbers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Whose gold, and silver, and garments wherewith they are clothed, they that are strong take, and go away withal: neither are they able to help themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Therefore it is better to be a king that shows his power, or else a profitable vessel in an house, which the owner shall have use of, than such false gods; or to be a door in an house, to keep such things therein, than such false gods. or a pillar of wood in a palace, than such false gods. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} For sun, moon, and stars, being bright and sent to do their offices, are obedient. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} In like manner the lightning when it breaks forth is easy to be seen; and after the same manner the wind blows in every country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And when God commands the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are bidden. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} And the fire sent from above to consume hills and woods does as it is commanded: but these are like to them neither in show nor power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} Therefore it is neither to be supposed nor said that they are gods, seeing, they are able neither to judge causes, nor to do good to men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} For they can neither curse nor bless kings: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} Neither can they show signs in the heavens among the heathen, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} The beasts are better than they: for they can get under a cover and help themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{69}} It is then by no means manifest to us that they are gods: therefore fear them not. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{70}} For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keeps nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{71}} And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold, are like to a white thorn in an orchard, that every bird sits upon; as also to a dead body, that is east into the dark. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{72}} And you⌃ shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rots upon them: and they themselves afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{73}} Better therefore is the just man that has none idols: for he shall be far from reproach.\par

\section*{Susanna Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Attached to Greek Daniel tradition\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The story survives in the Greek Daniel tradition rather than the Hebrew canon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies a human writer; included here as a Greek Daniel addition in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Hellenistic period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek tradition is primary; this is one of the additions to Daniel preserved in the LXX stream.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Court tale of Susanna's vindication through Daniel's wisdom.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To vindicate chastity, expose corrupt judges, and honor God's justice.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} justice; chastity; wisdom; vindication\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Single narrative of accusation, trial, and vindication.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No early Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek Daniel traditions are the primary witnesses Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Susanna in Greek Daniel tradition 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used in Christian tradition with Daniel by Church fathers (2nd-4th centuries AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} Susanna belongs to the Greek Daniel textual tradition and must be handled alongside Old Greek/Theodotionic Daniel evidence.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as Greek Daniel material in the Brenton corpus, not as part of the Hebrew Daniel canon.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Susanna}
\markboth{SUSANNA}{}
\subsection*{Susanna 1}
\markright{SUSANNA 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} There lived a man in Babylon, called Joacim: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, a very fair woman, and one that feared the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Her parents also were righteous, and taught their daughter according to the law of Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Now Joacim was a great rich man, and had a fair garden joining to his house: and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honorable than all others. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spoke of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} These kept much at Joacim's house: and all that had any suits in law came to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband's garden to walk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look to heaven, nor remember just judgments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet dared not one show another his grief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when they might find her alone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And there was no body there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and watched her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden doors, that I may wash me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they did as she bade them, and shut the garden doors, and went out themselves at privy doors to fetch the things that she had commanded them: but they saw not the elders, because they were hid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran to her, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with you; therefore consent to us, and lie with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If you will not, we will bear witness against you, that a young man was with you: and therefore you did send away your maids from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death to me: and if I do it not I can’t escape your hands. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Then ran the one, and opened the garden door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done to her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And it came to pass the next day, when the people were assembled to her husband Joacim, the two elders came also full of mischievous imagination against Susanna to put her to death; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And said before the people, Send for Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, Joacim's wife. And so they sent. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So she came with her father and mother, her children, and all her kindred. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beauteous to behold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And these wicked men commanded to uncover her face, (for she was covered) that they might be filled with her beauty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Therefore her friends and all that saw her wept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Then a young man, who there was hid, came to her, and lay with her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Then the assembly believed them as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice, and said, O everlasting God, that know the secrets, and know all things before they be: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} You know that they have borne false witness against me, and, behold, I must die; whereas I never did such things as these men have maliciously invented against me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And the Lord heard her voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that you have spoken? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} So he standing in the midst of them said, Are you⌃ such fools, you⌃ sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth you⌃ have condemned a daughter of Israel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Therefore all the people turned again in haste, and the elders said to him, Come, sit down among us, and show it us, seeing God has given you the honor of an elder. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Then said Daniel to them, Put these two aside one far from another, and I will examine them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said to him, O you that have become old in wickedness, now your sins which you have committed aforetime are come to light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} For you have pronounced false judgment and have condemned the innocent and have let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord says, The innocent and righteous shall you not kill. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Now then, if you have seen her, tell me, Under what tree saw you them companying together? Who answered, Under a mastick tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And Daniel said, Very well; you have lied against your own head; for even now the angel of God has received the sentence of God to cut you in two. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said to him, O you seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty has deceived you, and lust has perverted your heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} Thus have you⌃ dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Now therefore tell me, Under what tree did you take them companying together? Who answered, Under an holm tree. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Then said Daniel to him, Well; you have also lied against your own head: for the angel of God waits with the sword to cut you in two, that he may destroy you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saves them that trust in him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} And according to the law of Moses they did to them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbor: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} Therefore Chelcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joacim her husband, and all the kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} From that day forth was Daniel had in great reputation in the sight of the people.\par
\newpage

\vspace{0.18em}

\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No early Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek Daniel traditions are the primary witnesses Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve Bel and the Dragon in Greek Daniel tradition 4th-5th century AD\par

\section*{Bel and the Dragon}
\markboth{BEL AND THE DRAGON}{}
\subsection*{Bel and the Dragon 1}
\markright{BEL AND THE DRAGON 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And king Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia received his kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And Daniel conversed with the king, and was honored above all his friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now the Babylonians had an idol, called Bel, and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And the king worshipped it and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God. And the king said to him, Why do not you worship Bel? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who has created the heaven and the earth, and has sovereignty over all flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Then said the king to him, Thinkest you not that Bel is a living God? see you not how much he eats and drinks every day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, and did never eat or drink any thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So the king was angry, and called for his priests, and said to them, If you⌃ tell me not who this is that devours these expenses, you⌃ shall die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} But if you⌃ can certify me that Bel devours them, then Daniel shall die: for he has spoken blasphemy against Bel. And Daniel said to the king, Let it be according to your word. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now the priests of Bel were threescore and ten, beside their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So Bel's priests said, Behold, we go out: but you, O king, set on the meat, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast and seal it with your own signet; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And to morrow when you come in, if you find not that Bel has eaten up all, we will suffer death: or else Daniel, that speaks falsely against us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a privy entrance, whereby they entered in continually, and consumed those things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So when they were gone forth, the king set meats before Bel. Now Daniel had commanded his servants to bring ashes, and those they strewed throughout all the temple in the presence of the king alone: then they went out, and shut the door, and sealed it with the king's signet, and so departed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Now in the night came the priests with their wives and children, as they were wont to do, and did eat and drink up all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} In the morning betime the king arose, and Daniel with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And the king said, Daniel, are the seals whole? And he said, Yes, O king, they be whole. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked upon the table, and cried with a loud voice, Great are you, O Bel, and with you is no deceit at all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then laughed Daniel, and held the king that he should not go in, and said, Behold now the pavement, and mark well whose footsteps are these. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the king said, I see the footsteps of men, women, and children. And then the king was angry, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And took the priests with their wives and children, who showed him the privy doors, where they came in, and consumed such things as were upon the table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore the king killed them, and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, who destroyed him and his temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And in that same place there was a great dragon, which they of Babylon worshipped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the king said to Daniel, Will you also say that this is of brass? behold, he lives, he eats and drinks; you can not say that he is no living god: therefore worship him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Then said Daniel to the king, I will worship the Lord my God: for he is the living God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But give me leave, O king, and I shall kill this dragon without sword or staff. The king said, I give you leave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he put in the dragon's mouth, and so the dragon burst in sunder: and Daniel said, Behold, these are the gods you⌃ worship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he has destroyed Bel, he has slain the dragon, and put the priests to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So they came to the king, and said, Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy you and your house. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Now when the king saw that they pressed him sore, being constrained, he delivered Daniel to them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Who cast him into the lions' den: where he was six days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And in the den there were seven lions, and they had given them every day two carcasses, and two sheep: which then were not given to them, to the intent they might devour Daniel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Now there was in Jewry a prophet, called Habbacuc, who had made pottage, and had broken bread in a bowl, and was going into the field, for to bring it to the reapers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But the angel of the Lord said to Habbacuc, Go, carry the dinner that you have into Babylon to Daniel, who is in the lions' den. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And Habbacuc said, Lord, I never saw Babylon; neither do I know where the den is. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then the angel of the Lord took him by the crown, and bare him by the hair of his head, and through the vehemency of his spirit set him in Babylon over the den. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And Habbacuc cried, saying, O Daniel, Daniel, take the dinner which God has sent you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And Daniel said, You have remembered me, O God: neither have you forsaken them that seek you and love you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} So Daniel arose, and did eat: and the angel of the Lord set Habbacuc in his own place again immediately. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Upon the seventh day the king went to bewail Daniel: and when he came to the den, he looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Then cried the king with a loud voice, saying, Great are you Lord God of Daniel, and there is none other beside you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And he drew him out, and cast those that were the cause of his destruction into the den: and they were devoured in a moment before his face.\par
\newpage
\section*{1 Maccabees Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Anonymous Jewish historian\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The author is anonymous but writes close to the events in a sober historiographic style.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; included here as historical Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} late 2nd century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} A Hebrew original is widely believed though not fully preserved; the complete book survives in Greek.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} The Greek tradition is the principal full witness for the surviving text.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Historical narrative of the Maccabean revolt and Hasmonean rise.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To recount Jewish resistance, temple restoration, and political deliverance from Seleucid oppression.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} revolt; temple; covenant zeal; martyrdom; deliverance; Hasmoneans\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Antiochus and revolt 1-2; Judas Maccabeus 3-9; Jonathan 9-12; Simon 13-16.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek text is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. No complete Hebrew witness survives n/a | Gk. Codex Alexandrinus preserves 1 Maccabees in Greek 5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used by Josephus by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1 Maccabees is historically valuable and comparatively straightforward textually within the Greek tradition.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included as historical Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus, not as Hebrew-canonical Scripture.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{1 Maccabees}
\markboth{1 MACCABEES}{}
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 1}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And it happened, after that Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettiim, had struck Darius king of the Persians and Medes, that he reigned in his stead, the first over Greece, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And made many wars, and won many strong holds, and killed the kings of the earth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And went through to the ends of the earth, and took spoils of many nations, insomuch that the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And he gathered a mighty strong host and ruled over countries, and nations, and kings, who became tributaries to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And after these things he fell sick, and perceived that he should die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore he called his servants, such as were honorable, and had been brought up with him from his youth, and parted his kingdom among them, while he was yet alive. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So Alexander reigned twelve years, and then died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And his servants bare rule every one in his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And after his death they all put crowns upon themselves; so did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And there came out of them a wicked root Antiochus [surnamed] Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had been an hostage at Rome, and he reigned in the hundred and thirty and seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So this device pleased them well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Whereupon they built a place of exercise at Jerusalem according to the customs of the heathen: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And made themselves uncircumcised, and forsook the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathen, and were sold to do mischief. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now when the kingdom was established before Antiochus, he thought to reign over Egypt that he might have the dominion of two realms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Therefore he entered into Egypt with a great multitude, with chariots, and elephants, and horsemen, and a great navy, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And made war against Ptolemee king of Egypt: but Ptolemee was afraid of him, and fled; and many were wounded to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Thus they got the strong cities in the land of Egypt and he took the spoils thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And after that Antiochus had struck Egypt, he returned again in the hundred forty and third year, and went up against Israel and Jerusalem with a great multitude, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And entered proudly into the sanctuary, and took away the golden altar, and the candlestick of light, and all the vessels thereof, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the table of the show bread, and the pouring vessels, and the vials. and the censers of gold, and the veil, and the crown, and the golden ornaments that were before the temple, all which he pulled off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} He took also the silver and the gold, and the precious vessels: also he took the hidden treasures which he found. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And when he had taken all away, he went into his own land, having made a great massacre, and spoken very proudly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore there was a great mourning in Israel, in every place where they were; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} So that the princes and elders mourned, the virgins and young men were made feeble, and the beauty of women was changed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Every bridegroom took up lamentation, and she that sat in the marriage chamber was in heaviness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The land also was moved for the inhabitants thereof, and all the house of Jacob was covered with confusion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And after two years fully expired the king sent his chief collector of tribute to the cities of Juda, who came to Jerusalem with a great multitude, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And spoke peaceful words to them, but all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and struck it very sore, and destroyed much people of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And when he had taken the spoils of the city, he set it on
