fire, and pulled down the houses and walls thereof on every side. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} But the women and children took they captive, and possessed the cattle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then builded they the city of David with a great and strong wall, and with mighty towers, and made it a strong hold for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And they put therein a sinful nation, wicked men, and fortified themselves therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} They stored it also with armor and food, and when they had gathered together the spoils of Jerusalem, they laid them up there, and so they became a sore snare: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For it was a place to lie in wait against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Thus they shed innocent blood on every side of the sanctuary, and defiled it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Insomuch that the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them: whereupon the city was made an habitation of strangers, and became strange to those that were born in her; and her own children left her. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness, her feasts were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach her honor into contempt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} As had been her glory, so was her dishonor increased, and her excellency was turned into mourning. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Yes, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed to idols, and profaned the sabbath. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} For the king had sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And pollute the sanctuary and holy people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine's flesh, and unclean beasts: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And whoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} In the selfsame manner wrote he to his whole kingdom, and appointed overseers over all the people, commanding the cities of Juda to sacrifice, city by city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Then many of the people were gathered to them, to wit every one that forsook the law; and so they committed evils in the land; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And drove the Israelites into secret places, even wherever they could flee for succour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Now the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and fifth year, they set up the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and builded idol altars throughout the cities of Juda on every side; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And burnt incense at the doors of their houses, and in the streets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And when they had torn in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} And whoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed to the law, the king's commandment was, that they should put him to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Thus did they by their authority to the Israelites every month, to as many as were found in the cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Now the five and twentieth day of the month they did sacrifice upon the idol altar, which was upon the altar of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And they hanged the infants about their necks, and rifled their houses, and killed them that had circumcised them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} Howbeit many in Israel were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} Therefore the rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} And there was very great wrath upon Israel.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 2}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and lived in Modin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Simon; called Thassi: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Judas, who was called Maccabeus: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And when he saw the blasphemies that were committed in Juda and Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He said, Woe is me! therefore was I born to see this misery of my people, and of the holy city, and to dwell there, when it was delivered into the hand of the enemy, and the sanctuary into the hand of strangers? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Her temple is become as a man without glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Her glorious vessels are carried away into captivity, her infants are slain in the streets, her young men with the sword of the enemy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} What nation has not had a part in her kingdom and gotten of her spoils? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} All her ornaments are taken away; of a free woman she is become a bondslave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And, behold, our sanctuary, even our beauty and our glory, is laid waste, and the Gentiles have profaned it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} To what end therefore shall we live any longer? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then Mattathias and his sons tore their clothes, and put on sackcloth, and mourned very sore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In the mean while the king's officers, such as compelled the people to revolt, came into the city Modin, to make them sacrifice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when many of Israel came to them, Mattathias also and his sons came together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then answered the king's officers, and said to Mattathias on this wise, You are a ruler, and an honorable and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and brethren: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now therefore come you first, and fulfil the king's commandment, like as all the heathen have done, yes, and the men of Juda also, and such as remain at Jerusalem: so shall you and your house be in the number of the king's friends, and you and your children shall be honored with silver and gold, and many rewards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Then Mattathias answered and spoke with a loud voice, Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} We will not listen to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now when he had left speaking these words, there came one of the Jews in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king's commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Which thing when Mattathias saw, he was inflamed with zeal, and his reins trembled, neither could he forbear to show his anger according to judgment: therefore he ran, and killed him upon the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Also the king's commissioner, who compelled men to sacrifice, he killed at that time, and the altar he pulled down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God like as Phinees did to Zambri the son of Salom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintains the covenant, let him follow me. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that ever they had in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then many that sought after justice and judgment went down into the wilderness, to dwell there: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Both they, and their children, and their wives; and their cattle; because afflictions increased sore upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Now when it was told the king's servants, and the host that was at Jerusalem, in the city of David, that certain men, who had broken the king's commandment, were gone down into the secret places in the wilderness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} They pursued after them a great number, and having overtaken them, they camped against them, and made war against them on the sabbath day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And they said to them, Let that which you⌃ have done hitherto suffice; come forth, and do according to the commandment of the king, and you⌃ shall live. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But they said, We will not come forth, neither will we do the king's commandment, to profane the sabbath day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} So then they gave them the battle with all speed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Howbeit they answered them not, neither cast they a stone at them, nor stopped the places where they lay hid; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} But said, Let us die all in our innocency: heaven and earth will testify for us, that you⌃ put us to death wrongfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} So they rose up against them in battle on the sabbath, and they killed them, with their wives and children and their cattle, to the number of a thousand people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Now when Mattathias and his friends understood hereof, they mourned for them right sore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And one of them said to another, If we all do as our brethren have done, and fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whosoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Then came there to him a company of Assideans who were mighty men of Israel, even all such as were voluntarily devoted to the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Also all they that fled for persecution joined themselves to them, and were a stay to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} So they joined their forces, and struck sinful men in their anger, and wicked men in their wrath: but the rest fled to the heathen for succour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Then Mattathias and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And what children soever they found within the coast of Israel uncircumcised, those they circumcised valiantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} They pursued also after the proud men, and the work prospered in their hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} So they recovered the law out of the hand of the Gentiles, and out of the hand of kings, neither suffered they the sinner to triumph. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Now when the time drew near that Mattathias should die, he said to his sons, Now has pride and rebuke gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Now therefore, my sons, be you⌃ zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time; so shall you⌃ receive great honor and an everlasting name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was imputed to him for righteousness? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment and was made lord of Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Phinees our father in being zealous and fervent obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Jesus for fulfilling the word was made a judge in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Caleb for bearing witness before the congregation received the heritage of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} David for being merciful possessed the throne of an everlasting kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, by believing were saved out of the flame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} Daniel for his innocency was delivered from the mouth of lions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And thus consider you⌃ throughout all ages, that none that put their trust in him shall be overcome. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} Fear not then the words of a sinful man: for his glory shall be dung and worms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} To day he shall be lifted up and to morrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his dust, and his thought is come to nothing. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} Therefore, you⌃ my sons, be valiant and show yourselves men in the behalf of the law; for by it shall you⌃ obtain glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} And behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel, give ear to him always: he shall be a father to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} As for Judas Maccabeus, he has been mighty and strong, even from his youth up: let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} Take also to you all those that observe the law, and avenge you⌃ the wrong of your people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} Recompense fully the heathen, and take heed to the commandments of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{69}} So he blessed them, and was gathered to his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{70}} And he died in the hundred forty and sixth year, and his sons buried him in the sepulchres of his fathers at Modin, and all Israel made great lamentation for him.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 3}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then his son Judas, called Maccabeus, rose up in his stead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And all his brethren helped him, and so did all they that held with his father, and they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} So he got his people great honor, and put on a breastplate as a giant, and girded his warlike harness about him, and he made battles, protecting the host with his sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion's whelp roaring for his prey. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For He pursued the wicked, and sought them out, and burnt up those that vexed his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore the wicked shrunk for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled, because salvation prospered in his hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} He grieved also many kings, and made Jacob glad with his acts, and his memorial is blessed for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Moreover he went through the cities of Juda, destroying the ungodly out of them, and turning away wrath from Israel: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So that he was renowned to the utmost part of the earth, and he received to him such as were ready to perish. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together, and a great host out of Samaria, to fight against Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Which thing when Judas perceived, he went forth to meet him, and so he struck him, and killed him: many also fell down slain, but the rest fled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore Judas took their spoils, and Apollonius' sword also, and therewith he fought all his life long. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now when Seron, a prince of the army of Syria, heard say that Judas had gathered to him a multitude and company of the faithful to go out with him to war; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} He said, I will get me a name and honor in the kingdom; for I will go fight with Judas and them that are with him, who despise the king's commandment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So he made him ready to go up, and there went with him a mighty host of the ungodly to help him, and to be avenged of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when he came near to the going up of Bethhoron, Judas went forth to meet him with a small company: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Who, when they saw the host coming to meet them, said to Judas, How shall we be able, being so few, to fight against so great a multitude and so strong, seeing we are ready to faint with fasting all this day? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} To whom Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For the victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; but strength comes from heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} They come against us in much pride and iniquity to destroy us, and our wives and children, and to spoil us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But we fight for our lives and our laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore the Lord himself will overthrow them before our face: and as for you, be you⌃ not afraid of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now as soon as he had left off speaking, he leapt suddenly upon them, and so Seron and his host was overthrown before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And they pursued them from the going down of Bethhoron to the plain, where were slain about eight hundred men of them; and the residue fled into the land of the Philistines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Then began the fear of Judas and his brethren, and an exceeding great dread, to fall upon the nations round about them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Insomuch as his fame came to the king, and all nations talked of the battles of Judas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Now when king Antiochus heard these things, he was full of indignation: therefore he sent and gathered together all the forces of his realm, even a very strong army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} He opened also his treasure, and gave his soldiers pay for a year, commanding them to be ready whenever he should need them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Nevertheless, when he saw that the money of his treasures failed and that the tributes in the country were small, because of the dissension and plague, which he had brought upon the land in taking away the laws which had been of old time; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} He feared that he should not be able to bear the charges any longer, nor to have such gifts to give so liberally as he did before: for he had abounded above the kings that were before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Therefore, being greatly perplexed in his mind, he determined to go into Persia, there to take the tributes of the countries, and to gather much money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} So he left Lysias, a nobleman, and one of the blood royal, to oversee the affairs of the king from the river Euphrates to the borders of Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And to bring up his son Antiochus, until he came again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Moreover he delivered to him the half of his forces, and the elephants, and gave him charge of all things that he would have done, as also concerning them that lived in Juda and Jerusalem: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} To wit, that he should send an army against them, to destroy and root out the strength of Israel, and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to take away their memorial from that place; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And that he should place strangers in all their quarters, and divide their land by lot. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} So the king took the half of the forces that remained, and departed from Antioch, his royal city, the hundred forty and seventh year; and having passed the river Euphrates, he went through the high countries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Then Lysias chose Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the king's friends: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And with them he sent forty thousand footmen, and seven thousand horsemen, to go into the land of Juda, and to destroy it, as the king commanded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So they went forth with all their power, and came and pitched by Emmaus in the plain country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves: a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Now when Judas and his brethren saw that miseries were multiplied, and that the forces did encamp themselves in their borders: for they knew how the king had given commandment to destroy the people, and utterly abolish them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Then was the congregation gathered together, that they might be ready for battle, and that they might pray, and ask mercy and compassion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Now Jerusalem lay void as a wilderness, there was none of her children that went in or out: the sanctuary also was trodden down, and aliens kept the strong hold; the heathen had their habitation in that place; and joy was taken from Jacob, and the pipe with the harp ceased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Therefore the Israelites assembled themselves together, and came to Maspha, over against Jerusalem; for in Maspha was the place where they prayed aforetime in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then they fasted that day, and put on sackcloth, and cast ashes upon their heads, and tore their clothes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} They brought also the priests' garments, and the first fruits, and the tithes: and the Nazarites they stirred up, who had accomplished their days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Then cried they with a loud voice toward heaven, saying, What shall we do with these, and whither shall we carry them away? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} For your sanctuary is trodden down and profaned, and your priests are in heaviness, and brought low. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} And behold, the heathen are assembled together against us to destroy us: what things they imagine against us, you know. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} How shall we be able to stand against them, except you, O God, be our help? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Then sounded they with trumpets, and cried with a loud voice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} And after this Judas ordained captains over the people, even captains over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} But as for such as were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, those he commanded that they should return, every man to his own house, according to the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} So the camp removed, and pitched upon the south side of Emmaus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} And Judas said, arm yourselves, and be valiant men, and see that you⌃ be in readiness against the morning, that you⌃ may fight with these nations, that are assembled together against us to destroy us and our sanctuary: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} For it is better for us to die in battle, than to behold the calamities of our people and our sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} Nevertheless, as the will of God is in heaven, so let him do.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 4}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then took Gorgias five thousand footmen, and a thousand of the best horsemen, and removed out of the camp by night; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} To the end he might rush in upon the camp of the Jews, and strike them suddenly. And the men of the fortress were his guides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now when Judas heard thereof he himself removed, and the valiant men with him, that he might strike the king's army which was at Emmaus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} While as yet the forces were dispersed from the camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} In the mean season came Gorgias by night into the camp of Judas: and when he found no man there, he sought them in the mountains: for said he, These fellows flee from us {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But as soon as it was day, Judas showed himself in the plain with three thousand men, who nevertheless had neither armor nor swords to their minds. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And they saw the camp of the heathen, that it was strong and well harnessed, and compassed round about with horsemen; and these were expert of war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then said Judas to the men that were with him, Fear you⌃ not their multitude, neither be you⌃ afraid of their assault. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Remember how our fathers were delivered in the Red sea, when Pharaoh pursued them with an army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now therefore let us cry to heaven, if perhaps the Lord will have mercy upon us, and remember the covenant of our fathers, and destroy this host before our face this day: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} That so all the heathen may know that there is one who delivers and saves Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then the strangers lifted up their eyes, and saw them coming over against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore they went out of the camp to battle; but they that were with Judas sounded their trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So they joined battle, and the heathen being discomfited fled into the plain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Howbeit all the hindmost of them were slain with the sword: for they pursued them to Gazera, and to the plains of Idumea, and Azotus, and Jamnia, so that there were slain of them upon a three thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} This done, Judas returned again with his host from pursuing them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And said to the people, Be not greedy of the spoil inasmuch as there is a battle before us, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And Gorgias and his host are here by us in the mountain: but stand you⌃ now against our enemies, and overcome them, and after this you⌃ may boldly take the spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} As Judas was yet speaking these words, there appeared a part of them looking out of the mountain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Who when they perceived that the Jews had put their host to flight and were burning the tents; for the smoke that was seen declared what was done: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} When therefore they perceived these things, they were sore afraid, and seeing also the host of Judas in the plain ready to fight, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} They fled every one into the land of strangers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Then Judas returned to spoil the tents, where they got much gold, and silver, and blue silk, and purple of the sea, and great riches. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} After this they went home, and sung a song of thanksgiving, and praised the Lord in heaven: because it is good, because his mercy endures forever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Thus Israel had a great deliverance that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Now all the strangers that had escaped came and told Lysias what had happened: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Who, when he heard thereof, was confounded and discouraged, because neither such things as he would were done to Israel, nor such things as the king commanded him were come to pass. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} The next year therefore following Lysias gathered together threescore thousand choice men of foot, and five thousand horsemen, that he might subdue them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} So they came into Idumea, and pitched their tents at Bethsura, and Judas met them with ten thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed are you, O Saviour of Israel, who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gave the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armor bearer; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Shut up this army in the hand of your people Israel, and let them be confounded in their power and horsemen: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Make them to be of no courage, and cause the boldness of their strength to fall away, and let them quake at their destruction: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Cast them down with the sword of them that love you, and let all those that know your name praise you with thanksgiving. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} So they joined battle; and there were slain of the host of Lysias about five thousand men, even before them were they slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Now when Lysias saw his army put to flight, and the manliness of Judas' soldiers, and how they were ready either to live or die valiantly, he went into Antiochia, and gathered together a company of strangers, and having made his army greater than it was, he purposed to come again into Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then said Judas and his brethren, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Upon this all the host assembled themselves together, and went up into mount Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And when they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned up, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest, or in one of the mountains, yes, and the priests' chambers pulled down; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} They tore their clothes, and made great lamentation, and cast ashes upon their heads, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And fell down flat to the ground upon their faces, and blew an alarm with the trumpets, and cried toward heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Then Judas appointed certain men to fight against those that were in the fortress, until he had cleansed the sanctuary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} So he chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And when as they consulted what to do with the altar of burnt offerings, which was profaned; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} They thought it best to pull it down, lest it should be a reproach to them, because the heathen had defiled it: therefore they pulled it down, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to show what should be done with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} And made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} They made also new holy vessels, and into the temple they brought the candlestick, and the altar of burnt offerings, and of incense, and the table. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And upon the altar they burned incense, and the lamps that were upon the candlestick they lighted, that they might give light in the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Furthermore they set the loaves upon the table, and spread out the veils, and finished all the works which they had begun to make. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Now on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and eighth year, they rose up betimes in the morning, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Then all the people fell upon their faces, worshipping and praising the God of heaven, who had given them good success. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} And so they kept the dedication of the altar eight days and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliverance and praise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} They decked also the forefront of the temple with crowns of gold, and with shields; and the gates and the chambers they renewed, and hanged doors upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Thus was there very great gladness among the people, for that the reproach of the heathen was put away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Moreover Judas and his brethren with the whole congregation of Israel ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} At that time also they builded up the mount Sion with high walls and strong towers round about, lest the Gentiles should come and tread it down as they had done before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} And they set there a garrison to keep it, and fortified Bethsura to preserve it; that the people might have a defence against Idumea.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 5}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now when the nations round about heard that the altar was built and the sanctuary renewed as before, it displeased them very much. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Therefore they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that was among them, and thereupon they began to kill and destroy the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea at Arabattine, because they besieged Gael: and he gave them a great overthrow, and abated their courage, and took their spoils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Also he remembered the injury of the children of Bean, who had been a snare and an offense to the people, in that they lay in wait for them in the ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He shut them up therefore in the towers, and encamped against them, and destroyed them utterly, and burned the towers of that place with fire, and all that were therein. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Afterward he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found a mighty power, and much people, with Timotheus their captain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So he fought many battles with them, till at length they were discomfited before him; and he struck them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And when he had taken Jazar, with the towns belonging thereto, he returned into Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then the heathen that were at Galaad assembled themselves together against the Israelites that were in their quarters, to destroy them; but they fled to the fortress of Dathema. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And sent letters to Judas and his brethren, The heathen that are round about us are assembled together against us to destroy us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And they are preparing to come and take the fortress whereunto we are fled, Timotheus being captain of their host. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Come now therefore, and deliver us from their hands, for many of us are slain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Yes, all our brethren that were in the places of Tobie are put to death: their wives and their children also they have carried away captives, and borne away their stuff; and they have destroyed there about a thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} While these letters were yet reading, behold, there came other messengers from Galilee with their clothes torn, who reported on this wise, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And said, They of Ptolemais, and of Tyrus, and Sidon, and all Galilee of the Gentiles, are assembled together against us to consume us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now when Judas and the people heard these words, there assembled a great congregation together, to consult what they should do for their brethren, that were in trouble, and assaulted of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then said Judas to Simon his brother, Choose you out men, and go and deliver your brethren that are in Galilee, for I and Jonathan my brother will go into the country of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} So he left Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias, captains of the people, with the remnant of the host in Judea to keep it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} To whom he gave commandment, saying, Take you⌃ the charge of this people, and see that you⌃ make not war against the heathen until the time that we come again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now to Simon were given three thousand men to go into Galilee, and to Judas eight thousand men for the country of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then went Simon into Galilee, where he fought many battles with the heathen, so that the heathen were discomfited by him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he pursued them to the gate of Ptolemais; and there were slain of the heathen about three thousand men, whose spoils he took. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And those that were in Galilee, and in Arbattis, with their wives and their children, and all that they had, took he away with him, and brought them into Judea with great joy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Judas Maccabeus also and his brother Jonathan went over Jordan, and travelled three days' journey in the wilderness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Where they met with the Nabathites, who came to them in a peaceful manner, and told them every thing that had happened to their brethren in the land of Galaad: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And how that many of them were shut up in Bosora, and Bosor, and Alema, Casphor, Maked, and Carnaim; all these cities are strong and great: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And that they were shut up in the rest of the cities of the country of Galaad, and that against to morrow they had appointed to bring their host against the forts, and to take them, and to destroy them all in one day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Hereupon Judas and his host turned suddenly by the way of the wilderness to Bosora; and when he had won the city, he killed all the males with the edge of the sword, and took all their spoils, and burned the city with fire, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} From whence he removed by night, and went till he came to the fortress. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And betimes in the morning they looked up, and, behold, there was an innumerable people bearing ladders and other engines of war, to take the fortress: for they assaulted them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} When Judas therefore saw that the battle was begun, and that the cry of the city went up to heaven, with trumpets, and a great sound, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} He said to his host, Fight this day for your brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} So he went forth behind them in three companies, who sounded their trumpets, and cried with prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Then the host of Timotheus, knowing that it was Maccabeus, fled from him: therefore he struck them with a great slaughter; so that there were killed of them that day about eight thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} This done, Judas turned aside to Maspha; and after he had assaulted it he took and killed all the males therein, and received the spoils thereof and burnt it with fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} From thence went he, and took Casphon, Maged, Bosor, and the other cities of the country of Galaad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} After these things gathered Timotheus another host and encamped against Raphon beyond the brook. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} So Judas sent men to espy the host, who brought him word, saying, All the heathen that be round about us are assembled to them, even a very great host. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} He has also hired the Arabians to help them and they have pitched their tents beyond the brook, ready to come and fight against you. Upon this Judas went to meet them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Then Timotheus said to the captains of his host, When Judas and his host come near the brook, if he pass over first to us, we shall not be able to withstand him; for he will mightily prevail against us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} But if he be afraid, and camp beyond the river, we shall go over to him, and prevail against him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Now when Judas came near the brook, he caused the scribes of the people to remain by the brook: to whom he gave commandment, saying, Suffer no man to remain in the camp, but let all come to the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} So he went first over to them, and all the people after him: then all the heathen, being discomfited before him, cast away their weapons, and fled to the temple that was at Carnaim. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} But they took the city, and burned the temple with all that were therein. Thus was Carnaim subdued, neither could they stand any longer before Judas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Then Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the country of Galaad, from the least to the greatest, even their wives, and their children, and their stuff, a very great host, to the end they might come into the land of Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Now when they came to Ephron, (this was a great city in the way as they should go, very well fortified) they could not turn from it, either on the right hand or the left, but must needs pass through the midst of it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then they of the city shut them out, and stopped up the gates with stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Whereupon Judas sent to them in peaceful manner, saying, Let us pass through your land to go into our own country, and none shall do you any hurt; we will only pass through on foot: howbeit they would not open to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Therefore Judas commanded a proclamation to be made throughout the host, that every man should pitch his tent in the place where he was. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} So the soldiers pitched, and assaulted the city all that day and all that night, till at the length the city was delivered into his hands: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Who then killed all the males with the edge of the sword, and rased the city, and took the spoils thereof, and passed through the city over them that were slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} After this they went over Jordan into the great plain before Bethsan. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} And Judas gathered together those that came behind, and exhorted the people all the way through, till they came into the land of Judea. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} So they went up to mount Sion with joy and gladness, where they offered burnt offerings, because not one of them were slain until they had returned in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Now what time as Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Galaad, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias, captains of the garrisons, heard of the valiant acts and warlike deeds which they had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} Therefore they said, Let us also get us a name, and go fight against the heathen that are round about us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} So when they had given charge to the garrison that was with them, they went toward Jamnia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} Then came Gorgias and his men out of the city to fight against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} And so it was, that Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, and pursued to the borders of Judea: and there were slain that day of the people of Israel about two thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} Thus was there a great overthrow among the children of Israel, because they were not obedient to Judas and his brethren, but thought to do some valiant act. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} Moreover these men came not of the seed of those, by whose hand deliverance was given to Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} Howbeit the man Judas and his brethren were greatly renowned in the sight of all Israel, and of all the heathen, wherever their name was heard of; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} Insomuch as the people assembled to them with joyful acclamations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} Afterward went Judas forth with his brethren, and fought against the children of Esau in the land toward the south, where he struck Hebron, and the towns thereof, and pulled down the fortress of it, and burned the towers thereof round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} From thence he removed to go into the land of the Philistines, and passed through Samaria. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} At that time certain priests, desirous to show their valour, were slain in battle, for that they went out to fight unadvisedly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{68}} So Judas turned to Azotus in the land of the Philistines, and when he had pulled down their altars, and burned their carved images with fire, and spoiled their cities, he returned into the land of Judea.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 6}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} About that time king Antiochus travelling through the high countries heard say, that Elymais in the country of Persia was a city greatly renowned for riches, silver, and gold; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And that there was in it a very rich temple, wherein were coverings of gold, and breastplates, and shields, which Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian king, who reigned first among the Grecians, had left there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore he came and sought to take the city, and to spoil it; but he was not able, because they of the city, having had warning thereof, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Rose up against him in battle: so he fled, and departed thence with great heaviness, and returned to Babylon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Moreover there came one who brought him tidings into Persia, that the armies, which went against the land of Judea, were put to flight: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And that Lysias, who went forth first with a great power was driven away of the Jews; and that they were made strong by the armor, and power, and store of spoils, which they had gotten of the armies, whom they had destroyed: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Also that they had pulled down the abomination, which he had set up upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had compassed about the sanctuary with high walls, as before, and his city Bethsura. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Now when the king heard these words, he was astonished and sore moved: whereupon he laid him down upon his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not befallen him as he looked for. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And there he continued many days: for his grief was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Therefore he called for all his friends, and said to them, The sleep is gone from my eyes, and my heart fails for very care. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And I thought with myself, Into what tribulation am I come, and how great a flood of misery is it, wherein now I am! for I was bountiful and beloved in my power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} But now I remember the evils that I did at Jerusalem, and that I took all the vessels of gold and silver that were therein, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judea without a cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I perceive therefore that for this cause these troubles are come upon me, and, behold, I perish through great grief in a strange land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then called he for Philip, one of his friends, who he made ruler over all his realm, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And gave him the crown, and his robe, and his signet, to the end he should bring up his son Antiochus, and nourish him up for the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So king Antiochus died there in the hundred forty and ninth year. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now when Lysias knew that the king was dead, he set up Antiochus his son, whom he had brought up being young, to reign in his stead, and his name he called Eupator. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} About this time they that were in the tower shut up the Israelites round about the sanctuary, and sought always their hurt, and the strengthening of the heathen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore Judas, purposing to destroy them, called all the people together to besiege them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So they came together, and besieged them in the hundred and fifties year, and he made mounts for shot against them, and other engines. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Howbeit certain of them that were besieged got forth, to whom some ungodly men of Israel joined themselves: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And they went to the king, and said, How long will it be ere you execute judgment, and avenge our brethren? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} We have been willing to serve your father, and to do as he would have us, and to obey his commandments; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For which cause they of our nation besiege the tower, and are alienated from us: moreover as many of us as they could light on they killed, and spoiled our inheritance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Neither have they stretched out their hand against us only, but also against their borders. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And, behold, this day are they besieging the tower at Jerusalem, to take it: the sanctuary also and Bethsura have they fortified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Therefore if you do not prevent them quickly, they will do the greater things than these, neither shall you be able to rule them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Now when the king heard this, he was angry, and gathered together all his friends, and the captains of his army, and those that had charge of the horse. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} There came also to him from other kingdoms, and from isles of the sea, bands of hired soldiers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} So that the number of his army was one hundred thousand footmen, and twenty thousand horsemen, and two and thirty elephants exercised in battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} These went through Idumea, and pitched against Bethsura, which they assaulted many days, making engines of war; but they of Bethsura came out, and burned them with fire, and fought valiantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Upon this Judas removed from the tower, and pitched in Bathzacharias, over against the king's camp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then the king rising very early marched fiercely with his host toward Bathzacharias, where his armies made them ready to battle, and sounded the trumpets. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And to the end they might provoke the elephants to fight, they showed them the blood of grapes and mulberries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Moreover they divided the beasts among the armies, and for every elephant they appointed a thousand men, armed with coats of mail, and with helmets of brass on their heads; and beside this, for every beast were ordained five hundred horsemen of the best. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} These were ready at every occasion: wherever the beast was, and wherever the beast went, they went also, neither departed they from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And upon the beasts were there strong towers of wood, which covered every one of them, and were girded fast to them with devices: there were also upon every one two and thirty strong men, that fought upon them, beside the Indian that ruled him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} As for the remnant of the horsemen, they set them on this side and that side at the two parts of the host giving them signs what to do, and being harnessed all over amidst the ranks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold and brass, the mountains glistered therewith, and shined like lamps of fire. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So part of the king's army being spread upon the high mountains, and part on the valleys below, they marched on safely and in order. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Therefore all that heard the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the company, and the rattling of the harness, were moved: for the army was very great and mighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Then Judas and his host drew near, and entered into battle, and there were slain of the king's army six hundred men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Eleazar also, surnamed Savaran, perceiving that one of the beasts, armed with royal harness, was higher than all the rest, and supposing that the king was upon him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Put himself in jeopardy, to the end he might deliver his people, and get him a perpetual name: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Therefore he ran upon him courageously through the midst of the battle, slaying on the right hand and on the left, so that they were divided from him on both sides. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Which done, he crept under the elephant, and thrust him under, and killed him: whereupon the elephant fell down upon him, and there he died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Howbeit the rest of the Jews seeing the strength of the king, and the violence of his forces, turned away from them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Then the king's army went up to Jerusalem to meet them, and the king pitched his tents against Judea, and against mount Sion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} But with them that were in Bethsura he made peace: for they came out of the city, because they had no food there to endure the siege, it being a year of rest to the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} So the king took Bethsura, and set a garrison there to keep it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} As for the sanctuary, he besieged it many days: and set there artillery with engines and instruments to cast fire and stones, and pieces to cast darts and slings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} Whereupon they also made engines against their engines, and held them battle a long season. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} Yet at the last, their vessels being without food, (for that it was the seventh year, and they in Judea that were delivered from the Gentiles, had eaten up the residue of the store;) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} There were but a few left in the sanctuary, because the famine did so prevail against them, that they were fain to disperse themselves, every man to his own place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} At that time Lysias heard say, that Philip, whom Antiochus the king, while he lived, had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus, that he might be king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} Was returned out of Persia and Media, and the king's host also that went with him, and that he sought to take to him the ruling of the affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} Therefore he went in all haste, and said to the king and the captains of the host and the company, We decay daily, and our food are but small, and the place we lay siege to is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom lie upon us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} Now therefore let us be friends with these men, and make peace with them, and with all their nation; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} And covenant with them, that they shall live after their laws, as they did before: for they are therefore displeased, and have done all these things, because we abolished their laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} So the king and the princes were content: therefore he sent to them to make peace; and they accepted thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} Also the king and the princes made an oath to them: whereupon they went out of the strong hold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} Then the king entered into mount Sion; but when he saw the strength of the place, he broke his oath that he had made, and gave commandment to pull down the wall round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} Afterward departed he in all haste, and returned to Antiochia, where he found Philip to be master of the city: so he fought against him, and took the city by force.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 7}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the hundred and one and fifties year Demetrius the son of Seleucus departed from Rome, and came up with a few men to a city of the sea coast, and reigned there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And as he entered into the palace of his ancestors, so it was, that his forces had taken Antiochus and Lysias, to bring them to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Therefore, when he knew it, he said, Let me not see their faces. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So his host killed them. Now when Demetrius was set upon the throne of his kingdom, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} There came to him all the wicked and ungodly men of Israel, having Alcimus, who was desirous to be high priest, for their captain: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they accused the people to the king, saying, Judas and his brethren have slain all your friends, and driven us out of our own land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now therefore send some man whom you trust, and let him go and see what havock he has made among us, and in the king's land, and let him punish them with all them that aid them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then the king chose Bacchides, a friend of the king, who ruled beyond the flood, and was a great man in the kingdom, and faithful to the king, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And him he sent with that wicked Alcimus, whom he made high priest, and commanded that he should take vengeance of the children of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So they departed, and came with a great power into the land of Judea, where they sent messengers to Judas and his brethren with peaceful words deceitfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But they gave no heed to their words; for they saw that they were come with a great power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then did there assemble to Alcimus and Bacchides a company of scribes, to require justice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now the Assideans were the first among the children of Israel that sought peace of them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For said they, One that is a priest of the seed of Aaron is come with this army, and he will do us no wrong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} So he spoke to them, peaceably, and swore to them, saying, we will procure the harm neither of you nor your friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whereupon they believed him: howbeit he took of them threescore men, and killed them in one day, according to the words which he wrote, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The flesh of your saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore the fear and dread of them fell upon all the people, who said, There is neither truth nor righteousness in them; for they have broken the covenant and oath that they made. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} After this, removed Bacchides from Jerusalem, and pitched his tents in Bezeth, where he sent and took many of the men that had forsaken him, and certain of the people also, and when he had slain them, he cast them into the great pit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Then committed he the country to Alcimus, and left with him a power to aid him: so Bacchides went to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But Alcimus contended for the high priesthood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And to him resorted all such as troubled the people, who, after they had gotten the land of Juda into their power, did much hurt in Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now when Judas saw all the mischief that Alcimus and his company had done among the Israelites, even above the heathen, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He went out into all the coasts of Judea round about, and took vengeance of them that had revolted from him, so that they dared no more go forth into the country. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} On the other side, when Alcimus saw that Judas and his company had gotten the upper hand, and knew that he was not able to abide their force, he went again to the king, and said all the worst of them that he could. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then the king sent Nicanor, one of his honorable princes, a man that bare deadly hate to Israel, with commandment to destroy the people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great force; and sent to Judas and his brethren deceitfully with friendly words, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, that I may see you in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} He came therefore to Judas, and they saluted one another peaceably. Howbeit the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by violence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Which thing after it was known to Judas, to wit, that he came to him with deceit, he was sore afraid of him, and would see his face no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Nicanor also, when he saw that his counsel was revealed, went out to fight against Judas beside Capharsalama: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Where there were slain of Nicanor's side about five thousand men, and the rest fled into the city of David. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} After this went Nicanor up to mount Sion, and there came out of the sanctuary certain of the priests and certain of the elders of the people, to salute him peaceably, and to show him the burnt sacrifice that was offered for the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But he mocked them, and laughed at them, and abused them shamefully, and spoke proudly, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And swore in his wrath, saying, Unless Judas and his host be now delivered into my hands, if ever I come again in safety, I will burn up this house: and with that he went out in a great rage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then the priests entered in, and stood before the altar and the temple, weeping, and saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} You, O Lord, did choose this house to be called by your name, and to be a house of prayer and petition for your people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Be avenged of this man and his host, and let them fall by the sword: remember their blasphemies, and suffer them not to continue any longer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} So Nicanor went out of Jerusalem, and pitched his tents in Bethhoron, where an host out of Syria met him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} But Judas pitched in Adasa with three thousand men, and there he prayed, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} O Lord, when they that were sent from the king of the Assyrians blasphemed, your angel went out, and struck one hundred fourscore and five thousand of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Even so destroy you this host before us this day, that the rest may know that he has spoken blasphemously against your sanctuary, and judge you him according to his wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} So the thirteenth day of the month Adar the
