\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now in the hundred threescore and twelfth year king Demetrius gathered his forces together, and went into Media to get him help to fight against Tryphon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But when Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius was entered within his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Who went and struck the host of Demetrius, and took him, and brought him to Arsaces, by whom he was put in ward. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} As for the land of Judea, that was quiet all the days of Simon; for he sought the good of his nation in such wise, as that evermore his authority and honor pleased them well. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And as he was honorable in all his acts, so in this, that he took Joppa for an haven, and made an entrance to the isles of the sea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And enlarged the bounds of his nation, and recovered the country, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And gathered together a great number of captives, and had the dominion of Gazera, and Bethsura, and the tower, out of the which he took all uncleanness, neither was there any that resisted him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then did they till their ground in peace, and the earth gave her increase, and the trees of the field their fruit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} The ancient men sat all in the streets, communing together of good things, and the young men put on glorious and warlike apparel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} He provided food for the cities, and set in them all manner of munition, so that his honorable name was renowned to the end of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Neither was there any left in the land to fight against them: yes, the kings themselves were overthrown in those days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Moreover he strengthened all those of his people that were brought low: the law he searched out; and every contemner of the law and wicked person he took away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He beautified the sanctuary, and multiplied vessels of the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now when it was heard at Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Jonathan was dead, they were very sorry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But as soon as they heard that his brother Simon was made high priest in his stead, and ruled the country, and the cities therein: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} They wrote to him in tables of brass, to renew the friendship and league which they had made with Judas and Jonathan his brethren: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Which writings were read before the congregation at Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And this is the copy of the letters that the Lacedemonians sent; The rulers of the Lacedemonians, with the city, to Simon the high priest, and the elders, and priests, and residue of the people of the Jews, our brethren, send greeting: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} The ambassadors that were sent to our people certified us of your glory and honor: therefore we were glad of their coming, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And did register the things that they spoke in the council of the people in this manner; Numenius son of Antiochus, and Antipater son of Jason, the Jews' ambassadors, came to us to renew the friendship they had with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And it pleased the people to entertain the men honorably, and to put the copy of their ambassage in publick records, to the end the people of the Lacedemonians might have a memorial thereof: furthermore we have written a copy thereof to Simon the high priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great shield of gold of a thousand pound weight to confirm the league with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Whereof when the people heard, they said, What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For he and his brethren and the house of his father have established Israel, and chased away in fight their enemies from them, and confirmed their liberty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So then they wrote it in tables of brass, which they set upon pillars in mount Sion: and this is the copy of the writing; The eighteenth day of the month Elul, in the hundred threescore and twelfth year, being the third year of Simon the high priest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} At Saramel in the great congregation of the priests, and people, and rulers of the nation, and elders of the country, were these things notified to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Forasmuch as oftentimes there have been wars in the country, wherein for the maintenance of their sanctuary, and the law, Simon the son of Mattathias, of the posterity of Jarib, together with his brethren, put themselves in jeopardy, and resisting the enemies of their nation did their nation great honor: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} (For after that Jonathan, having gathered his nation together, and been their high priest, was added to his people, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Their enemies prepared to invade their country, that they might destroy it, and lay hands on the sanctuary: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} At which time Simon rose up, and fought for his nation, and spent much of his own substance, and armed the valiant men of his nation and gave them wages, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And fortified the cities of Judea, together with Bethsura, that lies upon the borders of Judea, where the armor of the enemies had been before; but he set a garrison of Jews there: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Moreover he fortified Joppa, which lies upon the sea, and Gazera, that borders upon Azotus, where the enemies had lived before: but he placed Jews there, and furnished them with all things convenient for the reparation thereof.) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} The people therefore sang the acts of Simon, and to what glory he thought to bring his nation, made him their governor and chief priest, because he had done all these things, and for the justice and faith which he kept to his nation, and for that he sought by all means to exalt his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For in his time things prospered in his hands, so that the heathen were taken out of their country, and they also that were in the city of David in Jerusalem, who had made themselves a tower, out of which they issued, and polluted all about the sanctuary, and did much hurt in the holy place: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} But he placed Jews therein. and fortified it for the safety of the country and the city, and raised up the walls of Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} King Demetrius also confirmed him in the high priesthood according to those things, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And made him one of his friends, and honored him with great honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For he had heard say, that the Romans had called the Jews their friends and confederates and brethren; and that they had entertained the ambassadors of Simon honorably; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Also that the Jews and priests were well pleased that Simon should be their governor and high priest for ever, until there should arise a faithful prophet; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Moreover that he should be their captain, and should take charge of the sanctuary, to set them over their works, and over the country, and over the armor, and over the fortresses, that, I say, he should take charge of the sanctuary; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Beside this, that he should be obeyed of every man, and that all the writings in the country should be made in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple, and wear gold: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Also that it should be lawful for none of the people or priests to break any of these things, or to gainsay his words, or to gather an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or wear a buckle of gold; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And whoever should do otherwise, or break any of these things, he should be punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Thus it liked all the people to deal with Simon, and to do as has been said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Then Simon accepted hereof, and was well pleased to be high priest, and captain and governor of the Jews and priests, and to defend them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} So they commanded that this writing should be put in tables of brass, and that they should be set up within the compass of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Also that the copies thereof should be laid up in the treasury, to the end that Simon and his sons might have them.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 15}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Moreover Antiochus son of Demetrius the king sent letters from the isles of the sea to Simon the priest and prince of the Jews, and to all the people; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The contents whereof were these: King Antiochus to Simon the high priest and prince of his nation, and to the people of the Jews, greeting: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Forasmuch as certain pestilent men have usurped the kingdom of our fathers, and my purpose is to challenge it again, that I may restore it to the old estate, and to that end have gathered a multitude of foreign soldiers together, and prepared ships of war; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} My meaning also being to go through the country, that I may be avenged of them that have destroyed it, and made many cities in the kingdom desolate: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now therefore I confirm to you all the oblations which the kings before me granted you, and whatever gifts besides they granted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} I give you leave also to coin money for your country with your own stamp. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And as concerning Jerusalem and the sanctuary, let them be free; and all the armor that you have made, and fortresses that you have built, and keep in your hands, let them remain to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And if anything be, or shall be, owing to the king, let it be forgiven you from this time forth for evermore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Furthermore, when we have obtained our kingdom, we will honor you, and your nation, and your temple, with great honor, so that your honor shall be known throughout the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the hundred threescore and fourteenth year went Antiochus into the land of his fathers: at which time all the forces came together to him, so that few were left with Tryphon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore being pursued by king Antiochus, he fled to Dora, which lies by the sea side: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For he saw that troubles came upon him all at once, and that his forces had forsaken him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Then camped Antiochus against Dora, having with him one hundred and twenty thousand men of war, and eight thousand horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And when he had compassed the city round about, and joined ships close to the town on the sea side, he vexed the city by land and by sea, neither suffered he any to go out or in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} In the mean season came Numenius and his company from Rome, having letters to the kings and countries; wherein were written these things: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Lucius, consul of the Romans to king Ptolemee, greeting: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} The Jews' ambassadors, our friends and confederates, came to us to renew the old friendship and league, being sent from Simon the high priest, and from the people of the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And they brought a shield of gold of a thousand pound. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} We thought it good therefore to write to the kings and countries, that they should do them no harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or countries, nor yet aid their enemies against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} It seemed also good to us to receive the shield of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} If therefore there be any pestilent fellows, that have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Simon the high priest, that he may punish them according to their own law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The same things wrote he likewise to Demetrius the king, and Attalus, to Ariarathes, and Arsaces, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And to all the countries and to Sampsames, and the Lacedemonians, and to Delus, and Myndus, and Sicyon, and Caria, and Samos, and Pamphylia, and Lycia, and Halicarnassus, and Rhodus, and Aradus, and Cos, and Side, and Aradus, and Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the copy hereof they wrote to Simon the high priest. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So Antiochus the king camped against Dora the second day, assaulting it continually, and making engines, by which means he shut up Tryphon, that he could neither go out nor in. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} At that time Simon sent him two thousand chosen men to aid him; silver also, and gold, and much armor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Nevertheless he would not receive them, but brake all the covenants which he had made with him before, and became strange to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Furthermore he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to commune with him, and say, You⌃ withhold Joppa and Gazera; with the tower that is in Jerusalem, which are cities of my realm. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} The borders thereof you⌃ have wasted, and done great hurt in the land, and got the dominion of many places within my kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Now therefore deliver the cities which you⌃ have taken, and the tributes of the places, whereof you⌃ have gotten dominion without the borders of Judea: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Or else give me for them five hundred talents of silver; and for the harm that you⌃ have done, and the tributes of the cities, other five hundred talents: if not, we will come and fight against you {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} So Athenobius the king's friend came to Jerusalem: and when he saw the glory of Simon, and the cupboard of gold and silver plate, and his great attendance, he was astonished, and told him the king's message. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Then answered Simon, and said to him, We have neither taken other men's land, nor holden that which appertains to others, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies had wrongfully in possession a certain time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Therefore we, having opportunity, hold the inheritance of our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And whereas you demand Joppa and Gazera, albeit they did great harm to the people in our country, yet will we give you one hundred talents for them. Hereunto Athenobius answered him not a word; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But returned in a rage to the king, and made report to him of these speeches, and of the glory of Simon, and of all that he had seen: whereupon the king was exceeding angry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} In the mean time fled Tryphon by ship to Orthosias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Then the king made Cendebeus captain of the sea coast, and gave him an host of footmen and horsemen, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And commanded him to remove his host toward Judea; also he commanded him to build up Cedron, and to fortify the gates, and to war against the people; but as for the king himself, he pursued Tryphon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So Cendebeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people and to invade Judea, and to take the people prisoners, and kill them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And when he had built up Cedron, he set horsemen there, and an host of footmen, to the end that issuing out they might make outroads upon the ways of Judea, as the king had commanded him.\par
\subsection*{1 Maccabees 16}
\markright{1 MACCABEES 16}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then came up John from Gazera, and told Simon his father what Cendebeus had done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Therefore Simon called his two oldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I, and my brethren, and my father's house, have ever from my youth to this day fought against the enemies of Israel; and things have prospered so well in our hands, that we have delivered Israel oftentimes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But now I am old, and you⌃, by God's mercy, are of a sufficient age: be you⌃ instead of me and my brother, and go and fight for our nation, and the help from heaven be with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} So he chose out of the country twenty thousand men of war with horsemen, who went out against Cendebeus, and rested that night at Modin. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when as they rose in the morning, and went into the plain, behold, a mighty great host both of footmen and horsemen came against them: howbeit there was a water brook between them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So he and his people pitched over against them: and when he saw that the people were afraid to go over the water brook, he went first over himself, and then the men seeing him passed through after him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} That done, he divided his men, and set the horsemen in the midst of the footmen: for the enemies' horsemen were very many. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then sounded they with the holy trumpets: whereupon Cendebeus and his host were put to flight, so that many of them were slain, and the remnant got them to the strong hold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} At that time was Judas John's brother wounded; but John still followed after them, until he came to Cedron, which Cendebeus had built. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So they fled even to the towers in the fields of Azotus; therefore he burned it with fire: so that there were slain of them about two thousand men. Afterward he returned into the land of Judea in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Moreover in the plain of Jericho was Ptolemeus the son of Abubus made captain, and he had abundance of silver and gold: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For he was the high priest's son in law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Therefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to get the country to himself, and thereupon consulted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to destroy them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Now Simon was visiting the cities that were in the country, and taking care for the good ordering of them; at which time he came down himself to Jericho with his sons, Mattathias and Judas, in the hundred threescore and seventeenth year, in the eleventh month, called Sabat: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Where the son of Abubus receiving them deceitfully into a little hold, called Docus, which he had built, made them a great banquet: howbeit he had hid men there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So when Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and killed him, and his two sons, and certain of his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} In which doing he committed a great treachery, and recompensed evil for good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then Ptolemee wrote these things, and sent to the king, that he should send him an host to aid him, and he would deliver him the country and cities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} He sent others also to Gazera to kill John: and to the tribunes he sent letters to come to him, that he might give them silver, and gold, and rewards. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And others he sent to take Jerusalem, and the mountain of the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now one had run before to Gazera and told John that his father and brethren were slain, and, quoth he, Ptolemee has sent to kill you also. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Hereof when he heard, he was sore astonished: so he laid hands on them that were come to destroy him, and killed them; for he knew that they sought to make him away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} As concerning the rest of the acts of John, and his wars, and worthy deeds which he did, and the building of the walls which he made, and his doings, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Behold, these are written in the chronicles of his priesthood, from the time he was made high priest after his father.\par
\newpage
\section*{2 Maccabees Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Epitomist of Jason of Cyrene\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book identifies itself as an epitome of a larger work by Jason of Cyrene.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; included here as historical Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} late 2nd century BC\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek is the primary surviving form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Theological historical narrative focused on selected episodes from the Maccabean crisis, temple, martyrdom, and divine justice.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To interpret the Maccabean crisis theologically, emphasizing prayer, martyrdom, resurrection hope, and God's vindication.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} martyrdom; temple; resurrection hope; divine judgment; intercession\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Preface 1-2; Heliodorus to Nicanor narratives 3-15.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek text is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Alexandrinus preserves 2 Maccabees in Greek 5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used by later Jewish and Christian writers by Josephus and church fathers (1st-4th centuries AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 2 Maccabees is openly selective and theological rather than a full parallel chronicle to 1 Maccabees.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included as Greek historical-religious Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{2 Maccabees}
\markboth{2 MACCABEES}{}
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 1}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} The brethren, the Jews that be at Jerusalem and in the land of Judea, wish to the brethren, the Jews that are throughout Egypt health and peace: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} God be gracious to you, and remember his covenant that he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his faithful servants; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And open your hearts in his law and commandments, and send you peace, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And now we be here praying for you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} What time as Demetrius reigned, in the hundred threescore and ninth year, we the Jews wrote to you in the extremity of trouble that came upon us in those years, from the time that Jason and his company revolted from the holy land and kingdom, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And burned the porch, and shed innocent blood: then we prayed to the Lord, and were heard; we offered also sacrifices and fine flour, and lighted the lamps, and set forth the loaves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now see that you⌃ keep the feast of tabernacles in the month Casleu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} In the hundred fourscore and eighth year, the people that were at Jerusalem and in Judea, and the council, and Judas, sent greeting and health to Aristobulus, king Ptolemeus' master, who was of the stock of the anointed priests, and to the Jews that were in Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Insomuch as God has delivered us from great perils, we thank him highly, as having been in battle against a king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For he cast them out that fought within the holy city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For when the leader was come into Persia, and the army with him that seemed invincible, they were slain in the temple of Nanea by the deceit of Nanea's priests. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For Antiochus, as though he would marry her, came into the place, and his friends that were with him, to receive money in name of a dowry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Which when the priests of Nanea had set forth, and he was entered with a small company into the compass of the temple, they shut the temple as soon as Antiochus was come in: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And opening a privy door of the roof, they threw stones like thunderbolts, and struck down the captain, hewed them in pieces, struck off their heads and cast them to those that were without. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Blessed be our God in all things, who has delivered up the ungodly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore whereas we are now purposed to keep the purification of the temple upon the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, we thought it necessary to certify you thereof, that you⌃ also might keep it, as the feast of the tabernacles, and of the fire, which was given us when Neemias offered sacrifice, after that he had builded the temple and the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} For when our fathers were led into Persia, the priests that were then devout took the fire of the altar privily, and hid it in an hollow place of a pit without water, where they kept it sure, so that the place was unknown to all men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now after many years, when it pleased God, Neemias, being sent from the king of Persia, did send of the posterity of those priests that had hid it to the fire: but when they told us they found no fire, but thick water; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then commanded he them to draw it up, and to bring it; and when the sacrifices were laid on, Neemias commanded the priests to sprinkle the wood and the things laid thereupon with the water. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} When this was done, and the time came that the sun shone, which before was hid in the cloud, there was a great fire kindled, so that every man marveled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And the priests made a prayer while the sacrifice was consuming, I say, both the priests, and all the rest, Jonathan beginning, and the rest answering thereto, as Neemias did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And the prayer was after this manner; O Lord, Lord God, Creator of all things, who are fearful and strong, and righteous, and merciful, and the only and gracious King, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The only giver of all things, the only just, almighty, and everlasting, you that deliver Israel from all trouble, and did choose the fathers, and sanctify them: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Receive the sacrifice for your whole people Israel, and preserve your own portion, and sanctify it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Gather those together that are scattered from us, deliver them that serve among the heathen, look upon them that are despised and abhorred, and let the heathen know that you are our God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Punish them that oppress us, and with pride do us wrong. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Plant your people again in your holy place, as Moses has spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And the priests sung psalms of thanksgiving. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Now when the sacrifice was consumed, Neemias commanded the water that was left to be poured on the great stones. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} When this was done, there was kindled a flame: but it was consumed by the light that shined from the altar. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} So when this matter was known, it was told the king of Persia, that in the place, where the priests that were led away had hid the fire, there appeared water, and that Neemias had purified the sacrifices therewith. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Then the king, inclosing the place, made it holy, after he had tried the matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And the king took many gifts, and bestowed thereof on those whom he would gratify. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And Neemias called this thing Naphthar, which is as much as to say, a cleansing: but many men call it Nephi.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 2}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} It is also found in the records, that Jeremy the prophet commanded them that were carried away to take of the fire, as it has been signified: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And how that the prophet, having given them the law, charged them not to forget the commandments of the Lord, and that they should not err in their minds, when they see images of silver and gold, with their ornaments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And with other such speeches exhorted he them, that the law should not depart from their hearts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} It was also contained in the same writing, that the prophet, being warned of God, commanded the tabernacle and the ark to go with him, as he went forth into the mountain, where Moses climbed up, and saw the heritage of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when Jeremy came there, he found an hollow cave, wherein he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And some of those that followed him came to mark the way, but they could not find it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Which when Jeremy perceived, he blamed them, saying, As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that God gather his people again together, and receive them to mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Then shall the Lord show them these things, and the glory of the Lord shall appear, and the cloud also, as it was showed under Moses, and as when Solomon desired that the place might be honorably sanctified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} It was also declared, that he being wise offered the sacrifice of dedication, and of the finishing of the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And as when Moses prayed to the Lord, the fire came down from heaven, and consumed the sacrifices: even so prayed Solomon also, and the fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt offerings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And Moses said, Because the sin offering was not to be eaten, it was consumed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So Solomon kept those eight days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} The same things also were reported in the writings and commentaries of Neemias; and how he founding a library gathered together the acts of the kings, and the prophets, and of David, and the epistles of the kings concerning the holy gifts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} In like manner also Judas gathered together all those things that were lost by reason of the war we had, and they remain with us, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore if you⌃ have need thereof, send some to fetch them to you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Whereas we then are about to celebrate the purification, we have written to you, and you⌃ shall do well, if you⌃ keep the same days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} We hope also, that the God, that delivered all his people, and gave them all an heritage, and the kingdom, and the priesthood, and the sanctuary, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} As he promised in the law, will shortly have mercy upon us, and gather us together out of every land under heaven into the holy place: for he has delivered us out of great troubles, and has purified the place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Now as concerning Judas Maccabeus, and his brethren, and the purification of the great temple, and the dedication of the altar, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes, and Eupator his son, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And the manifest signs that came from heaven to those that behaved themselves manfully to their honor for Judaism: so that, being but a few, they overcame the whole country, and chased barbarous multitudes, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And recovered again the temple renowned all the world over, and freed the city, and upheld the laws which were going down, the Lord being gracious to them with all favor: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} All these things, I say, being declared by Jason of Cyrene in five books, we will assay to abridge in one volume. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For considering the infinite number, and the difficulty which they find that desire to look into the narrations of the story, for the variety of the matter, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} We have been careful, that they that will read may have delight, and that they that are desirous to commit to memory might have ease, and that all into whose hands it comes might have profit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore to us, that have taken upon us this painful labor of abridging, it was not easy, but a matter of sweat and watching; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Even as it is no ease to him that prepares a banquet, and seeks the benefit of others: yet for the pleasuring of many we will undertake gladly this great pains; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Leaving to the author the exact handling of every particular, and laboring to follow the rules of an abridgement. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For as the master builder of a new house must care for the whole building; but he that undertakes to set it out, and paint it, must seek out fit things for the adorning thereof: even so I think it is with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} To stand upon every point, and go over things at large, and to be curious in particulars, belongs to the first author of the story: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But to use brevity, and avoid much laboring of the work, is to be granted to him that will make an abridgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Here then will we begin the story: only adding thus much to that which has been said, that it is a foolish thing to make a long prologue, and to be short in the story itself.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 3}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now when the holy city was inhabited with all peace, and the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} It came to pass that even the kings themselves did honor the place, and magnify the temple with their best gifts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Insomuch that Seleucus of Asia of his own revenues bare all the costs belonging to the service of the sacrifices. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But one Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the son of Thraseas, who then was governor of Celosyria and Phenice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king's hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had showed him of the money whereof he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So forthwith Heliodorus took his journey; under a color of visiting the cities of Celosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king's purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when he was come to Jerusalem, and had been courteously received of the high priest of the city, he told him what intelligence was given of the money, and declared therefore he came, and asked if these things were so indeed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then the high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: the sum whereof in all was four hundred talents of silver, and two hundred of gold: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And that it was altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done to them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place, and to the majesty and inviolable sanctity of the temple, honored over all the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But Heliodorus, because of the king's commandment given him, said, That in any wise it must be brought into the king's treasury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So at the day which he appointed he entered in to order this matter: therefore there was no small agony throughout the whole city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests' vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to he kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then whoso had looked the high priest in the face, it would have wounded his heart: for his countenance and the changing of his color declared the inward agony of his mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For the man was so compassed with fear and horror of the body, that it was manifest to them that looked upon him, what sorrow he had now in his heart. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Others ran flocking out of their houses to the general supplication, because the place was like to come into contempt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And the women, girded with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And all, holding their hands toward heaven, made supplication. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Then it would have pitied a man to see the falling down of the multitude of all sorts, and the fear of the high priest being in such an agony. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} They then called upon the Almighty Lord to keep the things committed of trust safe and sure for those that had committed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Nevertheless Heliodorus executed that which was decreed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, the Lord of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of God, and fainted, and were sore afraid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness: but they that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Thus him, that lately came with a great train and with all his guard into the said treasury, they carried out, being unable to help himself with his weapons: and manifestly they acknowledged the power of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} For he by the hand of God was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But they praised the Lord, that had miraculously honored his own place: for the temple; which a little before was full of fear and trouble, when the Almighty Lord appeared, was filled with joy and gladness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then straightways certain of Heliodorus' friends prayed Onias, that he would call upon the most High to grant him his life, who lay ready to give up the ghost. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} So the high priest, suspecting lest the king should misconceive that some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the health of the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake the Lord has granted you life: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And seeing that you have been scourged from heaven, declare to all men the mighty power of God. And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} So Heliodorus, after he had offered sacrifice to the Lord, and made great vows to him that had saved his life, and saluted Onias, returned with his host to the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Then testified he to all men the works of the great God, which he had seen with his eyes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And when the king Heliodorus, who might be a fit man to be sent yet once again to Jerusalem, he said, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} If you have any enemy or traitor, send him there, and you shall receive him well scourged, if he escape with his life: for in that place, no doubt; there is an especial power of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} For he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defends it; and he beats and destroys them that come to hurt it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} And the things concerning Heliodorus, and the keeping of the treasury, fell out on this sort.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 4}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} This Simon now, of whom we spoke before, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Onias seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius, as being the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, did rage, and increase Simon's malice, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} He went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereto. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Promising to the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Beside this, he promised to assign one hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And the royal privileges granted of special favor to the Jews by the means of John the father of Eupolemus, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, he took away; and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For he built gladly a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Not setting by the honors of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly, and to whom they desired to be like in all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God: but the time following shall declare these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now when the game that was used every faith year was kept at Tyrus, the king being present, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} This ungracious Jason sent special messengers from Jerusalem, who were Antiochians, to carry three hundred drachmas of silver to the sacrifice of Hercules, which even the bearers thereof thought fit not to bestow upon the sacrifice, because it was not convenient, but to be reserved for other charges. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} This money then, in regard of the sender, was appointed to Hercules' sacrifice; but because of the bearers thereof, it was employed to the making of gallies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now when Apollonius the son of Menestheus was sent into Egypt for the coronation of king Ptolemeus Philometor, Antiochus, understanding him not to be well affected to his affairs, provided for his own safety: whereupon he came to Joppa, and from thence to Jerusalem: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Where he was honorably received of Jason, and of the city, and was brought in with torch alight, and with great shoutings: and so afterward went with his host to Phenice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon's brother, to bear the money to the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So he came with the king's mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So Menelaus got the principality: but as for the money that he had promised to the king, he took no good order for it, albeit Sostratis the ruler of the castle required it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} For to him appertained the gathering of the customs. Therefore they were both called before the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Now Menelaus left his brother Lysimachus in his stead in the priesthood; and Sostratus left Crates, who was governor of the Cyprians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} While those things were in doing, they of Tarsus and Mallos made insurrection, because they were given to the king's concubine, called Antiochus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then came the king in all haste to appease matters, leaving Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lies by Antiochia. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} Therefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed, him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded thereto, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For the which cause not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And when the king was come again from the places about Cilicia, the Jews that were in the city, and certain of the Greeks that abhorred the fact also, complained because Onias was slain without cause. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Therefore Antiochus was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behavior of him that was dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And being kindled with anger, forthwith he took away Andronicus his purple, and tore off his clothes, and leading him through the whole city to that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there killed he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Now when many sacrileges had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the fruit thereof was spread abroad, the multitude gathered themselves together against Lysimachus, many vessels of gold being already carried away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Whereupon the common people rising, and being filled with rage, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men, and began first to offer violence; one Auranus being the leader, a man far gone in years, and no less in folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} They then seeing the attempt of Lysimachus, some of them caught stones, some clubs, others taking handfuls of dust, that was next at hand, cast them all together upon Lysimachus, and those that set upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Thus many of them they wounded, and some they struck to the ground, and all of them they forced to flee: but as for the churchrobber himself, him they killed beside the treasury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} Of these matters therefore there was an accusation laid against Menelaus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Now when the king came to Tyrus, three men that were sent from the senate pleaded the cause before him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} But Menelaus, being now convicted, promised Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes to give him much money, if he would pacify the king toward him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} Whereupon Ptolemee taking the king aside into a certain gallery, as it were to take the air, brought him to be of another mind: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} Insomuch that he discharged Menelaus from the accusations, who notwithstanding was cause of all the mischief: and those poor men, who, if they had told their cause, yes, before the Scythians, should have been judged innocent, them he condemned to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Thus they that followed the matter for the city, and for the people, and for the holy vessels, did soon suffer unjust punishment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Therefore even they of Tyrus, moved with hatred of that wicked deed, caused them to be honorably buried. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} And so through the covetousness of them that were of power Menelaus remained still in authority, increasing in malice, and being a great traitor to the citizens.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 5}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} About the same time Antiochus prepared his second voyage into Egypt: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And then it happened, that through all the city, for the space almost of forty days, there were seen horsemen running in the air, in cloth of gold, and armed with lances, like a band of soldiers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And troops of horsemen in array, encountering and running one against another, with shaking of shields, and multitude of pikes, and drawing of swords, and casting of darts, and glittering of golden ornaments, and harness of all sorts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Therefore every man prayed that that apparition might turn to good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now when there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men, and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and they that were upon the walls being put back, and the city at length taken, Menelaus fled into the castle: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} But Jason killed his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now when this that was done came to the king's ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And commanded his men of war not to spare such as they met, and to kill such as went up upon the houses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Thus there was killing of young and old, making away of men, women, and children, slaying of virgins and infants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And taking the holy vessels with polluted hands, and with profane hands pulling down the things that were dedicated by other kings to the augmentation and glory and honor of the place, he gave them away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And so haughty was Antiochus in mind, that he considered not that the Lord was angry for a while for the sins of them that lived in the city, and therefore his eye was not upon the place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For had they not been formerly wrapped in many sins, this man, as soon as he had come, had forthwith been scourged, and put back from his presumption, as Heliodorus was, whom Seleucus the king sent to view the treasury. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Nevertheless God did not choose the people for the place's sake, but the place for the people's sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And therefore the place itself, that was partaker with them of the adversity that happened to the nation, did afterward communicate in the benefits sent from the Lord: and as it was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty, so again, the great Lord being reconciled, it was set up with all glory. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} So when Antiochus had carried out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he departed in all haste to Antiochia, weening in his pride to make the land navigable, and the sea passable by foot: such was the haughtiness of his mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And he left governors to vex the nation: at Jerusalem, Philip, for his country a Phrygian, and for manners more barbarous than he that set him there; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And at Garizim, Andronicus; and besides, Menelaus, who worse than all the rest bare an heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to kill all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Jews keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And so he killed all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons killed great multitudes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But Judas Maccabeus with nine others, or thereabout, withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, with his company, who fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 6}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that lived in the place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbids. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And in the day of the king's birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices; and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbor cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes handing at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And others, that had run together into caves near by, to keep the sabbath day secretly, being discovered by Philip, were all burnt together, because they made a conscience to help themselves for the honor of the most sacred day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now I beseech those that read this book, that they be not discouraged for these calamities, but that they judge those punishments not to be for destruction, but for a chastening of our nation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For it is a token of his great goodness, when wicked doers are not suffered any long time, but forthwith punished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} For not as with other nations, whom the Lord patiently forbears to punish, till they be come to the fulness of their sins, so deals he with us, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Lest that, being come to the height of sin, afterwards he should take vengeance of us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And therefore he never withdraws his mercy from us: and though he punish with adversity, yet does he never forsake his people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But let this that we at spoken be for a warning to us. And now will we come to the declaring of the matter in a few words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine's flesh. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But they that had the charge of that wicked feast, for the old acquaintance they had with the man, taking him aside, implored him to bring flesh of his own provision, such as was lawful for him to use, and make as if he did eat of the flesh taken from the sacrifice commanded by the king; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} That in so doing he might be delivered from death, and for the old friendship with them find favor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But he began to consider discreetly, and as became his age, and the excellency of his ancient years, and the honor of his gray head, whereon was come, and his most honest education from a child, or rather the holy law made and given by God: therefore he answered accordingly, and willed them straightways to send him to the grave. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} For it becomes not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And so they through my hypocrisy, and desire to live a little time and a moment longer, should be deceived by me, and I get a stain to my old age, and make it abominable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Therefore now, manfully changing this life, I will show myself such an one as my age requires, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honorable and holy laws. And when he had said these words, immediately he went to the torment: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} They that led him changing the good will they bare him a little before into hatred, because the foresaid speeches proceeded, as they thought, from a desperate mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But when he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest to the Lord, that has the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only to young men, but to all his nation.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 7}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 7}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} It came to pass also, that seven brethren with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine's flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But one of them that spoke first said thus, What would you ask or learn of us? we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Then the king, being in a rage, commanded pans and caldrons to be made hot: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Which forthwith being heated, he commanded to cut out the tongue of him that spoke first, and to cut off the utmost parts of his body, the rest of his brethren and his mother looking on. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now when he was thus maimed in all his members, he commanded him being yet alive to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the pan: and as the vapor of the pan was for a good space dispersed, they exhorted one another with the mother to die manfully, saying thus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The Lord God looks upon us, and in truth has comfort in us, as Moses in his song, which witnessed to their faces, declared, saying, And he shall be comforted in his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So when the first was dead after this number, they brought the second to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, Will you eat, before you be punished throughout every member of your body? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But he answered in his own language, and said, No. Therefore he also received the next torment in order, as the former did. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury take us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marveled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Now when this man was dead also, they tormented and mangled the
