fourth in like manner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for you, you shall have no resurrection to life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Afterward they brought the fifth also, and mangled him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then looked he to the king, and said, You have power over men, you are corruptible, you do what you will; yet think not that our nation is forsaken of God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} But abide a while, and behold his great power, how he will torment you and your seed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} After him also they brought the sixth, who being ready to die said, Be not deceived without cause: for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our God: therefore marvelous things are done to us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} But think not you, that take in hand to strive against God, that you shall escape unpunished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But the mother was marvelous above all, and worthy of honorable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Yes, she exhorted every one of them in her own language, filled with courageous spirits; and stirring up her womanish thoughts with a manly stomach, she said to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} I can’t tell how you⌃ came into my womb: for I neither gave you breath nor life, neither was it I that formed the members of every one of you; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you⌃ now regard not your own selves for his laws' sake. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Now Antiochus, thinking himself despised, and suspecting it to be a reproachful speech, while the youngest was yet alive, did not only exhort him by words, but also assured him with oaths, that he would make him both a rich and a happy man, if he would turn from the laws of his fathers; and that also he would take him for his friend, and trust him with affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But when the young man would in no case listen to him, the king called his mother, and exhorted her that she would counsel the young man to save his life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And when he had exhorted her with many words, she promised him that she would counsel her son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spoke in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare you nine months in my womb, and gave you such three years, and nourished you, and brought you up to this age, and endured the troubles of education. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} I beseech you, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, and consider that God made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Fear not this tormentor, but, being worthy of your brethren, take your death that I may receive you again in mercy with your brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} While she was yet speaking these words, the young man said, Whom wait you⌃ for? I will not obey the king's commandment: but I will obey the commandment of the law that was given to our fathers by Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And you, that have been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews, shall not escape the hands of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} For we suffer because of our sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And though the living Lord be angry with us a little while for our chastening and correction, yet shall he be at one again with his servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} But you, O godless man, and of all other most wicked, be not lifted up without a cause, nor puffed up with uncertain hopes, lifting up your hand against the servants of God: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} For you have not yet escaped the judgment of Almighty God, who sees all things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} For our brethren, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under God's covenant of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of God, shall receive just punishment for your pride. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} But I, as my brethren, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching God that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is God; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And that in me and my brethren the wrath of the Almighty, which is justly brought upon our nation, may cease. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} Then the king, being in a rage, handed him worse than all the rest, and took it grievously that he was mocked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So this man died undefiled, and put his whole trust in the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Last of all after the sons the mother died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Let this be enough now to have spoken concerning the idolatrous feasts, and the extreme tortures.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 8}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 8}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Judas Maccabeus, and they that were with him, went privily into the towns, and called their kinsfolks together, and took to them all such as continued in the Jews' religion, and assembled about six thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And they called upon the Lord, that he would look upon the people that was trodden down of all; and also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And that he would have compassion upon the city, sore defaced, and ready to be made even with the ground; and hear the blood that cried to him, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And remember the wicked slaughter of harmless infants, and the blasphemies committed against his name; and that he would show his hatred against the wicked. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now when Maccabeus had his company about him, he could not be withstood by the heathen: for the wrath of the Lord was turned into mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Therefore he came at unawares, and burnt up towns and cities, and got into his hands the most commodious places, and overcame and put to flight no small number of his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But specially took he advantage of the night for such privy attempts, insomuch that the fruit of his holiness was spread every where. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} So when Philip saw that this man increased by little and little, and that things prospered with him still more and more, he wrote to Ptolemeus, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, to yield more aid to the king's affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then forthwith choosing Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of his special friends, he sent him with no fewer than twenty thousand of all nations under him, to root out the whole generation of the Jews; and with him he joined also Gorgias a captain, who in matters of war had great experience. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} So Nicanor undertook to make so much money of the captive Jews, as should defray the tribute of two thousand talents, which the king was to pay to the Romans. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Therefore immediately he sent to the cities upon the sea coast, proclaiming a sale of the captive Jews, and promising that they should have fourscore and ten bodies for one talent, not expecting the vengeance that was to follow upon him from the Almighty God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Now when word was brought to Judas of Nicanor's coming, and he had imparted to those that were with him that the army was at hand, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} They that were fearful, and distrusted the justice of God, fled, and conveyed themselves away. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Others sold all that they had left, and withal implored the Lord to deliver them, sold by the wicked Nicanor before they met together: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And if not for their own sakes, yet for the covenants he had made with their fathers, and for his holy and glorious name's sake, by which they were called. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So Maccabeus called his men together to the number of six thousand, and exhorted them not to be stricken with terror of the enemy, nor to fear the great multitude of the heathen, who came wrongly against them; but to fight manfully, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And to set before their eyes the injury that they had unjustly done to the holy place, and the cruel handling of the city, whereof they made a mockery, and also the taking away of the government of their forefathers: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For they, said he, trust in their weapons and boldness; but our confidence is in the Almighty who at a beck can cast down both them that come against us, and also all the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Moreover, he recounted to them what helps their forefathers had found, and how they were delivered, when under Sennacherib one hundred fourscore and five thousand perished. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And he told them of the battle that they had in Babylon with the Galatians, how they came but eight thousand in all to the business, with four thousand Macedonians, and that the Macedonians being perplexed, the eight thousand destroyed one hundred and twenty thousand because of the help that they had from heaven, and so received a great booty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Thus when he had made them bold with these words, and ready to die for the law and the country, he divided his army into four parts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And joined with himself his own brethren, leaders of each band, to wit Simon, and Joseph, and Jonathan, giving each one fifteen hundred men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Also he appointed Eleazar to read the holy book: and when he had given them this watchword, The help of God; himself leading the first band, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And by the help of the Almighty they killed above nine thousand of their enemies, and wounded and maimed the most part of Nicanor's host, and so put all to flight; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} And took their money that came to buy them, and pursued them far: but lacking time they returned: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For it was the day before the sabbath, and therefore they would no longer pursue them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So when they had gathered their armor together, and spoiled their enemies, they occupied themselves about the sabbath, yielding exceeding praise and thanks to the Lord, who had preserved them to that day, which was the beginning of mercy distilling upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And after the sabbath, when they had given part of the spoils to the maimed, and the widows, and orphans, the residue they divided among themselves and their servants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} When this was done, and they had made a common supplication, they implored the merciful Lord to be reconciled with his servants for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Moreover of those that were with Timotheus and Bacchides, who fought against them, they killed above twenty thousand, and very easily got high and strong holds, and divided among themselves many spoils more, and made the maimed, orphans, widows, yes, and the aged also, equal in spoils with themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And when they had gathered their armor together, they laid them up all carefully in convenient places, and the remnant of the spoils they brought to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} They killed also Philarches, that wicked person, who was with Timotheus, and had annoyed the Jews many ways. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Furthermore at such time as they kept the feast for the victory in their country they burnt Callisthenes, that had set fire upon the holy gates, who had fled into a little house; and so he received a reward meet for his wickedness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} As for that most ungracious Nicanor, who had brought a thousand merchants to buy the Jews, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} He was through the help of the Lord brought down by them, of whom he made least account; and putting off his glorious apparel, and discharging his company, he came like a fugitive servant through the midland to Antioch having very great dishonor, for that his host was destroyed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Thus he, that took upon him to make good to the Romans their tribute by means of captives in Jerusalem, told abroad, that the Jews had God to fight for them, and therefore they could not be hurt, because they followed the laws that he gave them.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 9}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} About that time came Antiochus with dishonor out of the country of Persia {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} For he had entered the city called Persepolis, and went about to rob the temple, and to hold the city; whereupon the multitude running to defend themselves with their weapons put them to flight; and so it happened, that Antiochus being put to flight of the inhabitants returned with shame. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now when he came to Ecbatane, news was brought him what had happened to Nicanor and Timotheus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Then swelling with anger. he thought to avenge upon the Jews the disgrace done to him by those that made him flee. Therefore commanded he his chariotman to drive without ceasing, and to dispatch the journey, the judgment of God now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} But the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And that most justly: for he had tormented other men's bowels with many and strange torments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews, and commanding to haste the journey: but it came to pass that he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And thus he that a little before thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, showing forth to all the manifest power of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and while he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And the man, that thought a little before he could reach to the stars of heaven, no man could endure to carry for his intolerable stink. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Here therefore, being plagued, he began to leave off his great pride, and to come to the knowledge of himself by the scourge of God, his pain increasing every moment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when he himself could not abide his own smell, he said these words, It is meet to be subject to God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This wicked person vowed also to the Lord, who now no more would have mercy upon him, saying thus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} That the holy city (to the which he was going in haste to lay it even with the ground, and to make it a common burying place,) he would set at liberty: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And as touching the Jews, whom he had judged not worthy so much as to be buried, but to be cast out with their children to be devoured of the fowls and wild beasts, he would make them all equals to the citizens of Athens: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And the holy temple, which before he had spoiled, he would garnish with goodly gifts, and restore all the holy vessels with many more, and out of his own revenue defray the charges belonging to the sacrifices: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Yes, and that also he would become a Jew himself, and go through all the world that was inhabited, and declare the power of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But for all this his pains would not cease: for the just judgment of God was come upon him: therefore despairing of his health, he wrote to the Jews the letter underwritten, containing the form of a supplication, after this manner: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Antiochus, king and governor, to the good Jews his citizens wishes much joy, health, and prosperity: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} If you⌃ and your children fare well, and your affairs be to your contentment, I give very great thanks to God, having my hope in heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} As for me, I was weak, or else I would have remembered kindly your honor and good will returning out of Persia, and being taken with a grievous disease, I thought it necessary to care for the common safety of all: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Not distrusting my health, but having great hope to escape this sickness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} But considering that even my father, at what time he led an army into the high countries. appointed a successor, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} To the end that, if any thing fell out contrary to expectation, or if any tidings were brought that were grievous, they of the land, knowing to whom the state was left, might not be troubled: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Again, considering how that the princes that are borderers and neighbors to my kingdom wait for opportunities, and expect what shall be the event. I have appointed my son Antiochus king, whom I often committed and commended to many of you, when I went up into the high provinces; to whom I have written as follows: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Therefore I pray and request you to remember the benefits that I have done to you generally, and in special, and that every man will be still faithful to me and my son. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} For I am persuaded that he understanding my mind will favourably and graciously yield to your desires. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Thus the murderer and blasphemer having suffered most grievously, as he entreated other men, so died he a miserable death in a strange country in the mountains. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And Philip, that was brought up with him, carried away his body, who also fearing the son of Antiochus went into Egypt to Ptolemeus Philometor.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 10}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 10}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now Maccabeus and his company, the Lord guiding them, recovered the temple and the city: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and show bread. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} When that was done, they fell flat down, and implored the Lord that they might come no more into such troubles; but if they sinned any more against him, that he himself would chasten them with mercy, and that they might not be delivered to the blasphemous and barbarous nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now upon the same day that the strangers profaned the temple, on the very same day it was cleansed again, even the five and twentieth day of the same month, which is Casleu. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And they kept the eight days with gladness, as in the feast of the tabernacles, remembering that not long before they had held the feast of the tabernacles, when as they wandered in the mountains and dens like beasts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} They ordained also by a common statute and decree, That every year those days should be kept of the whole nation of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And this was the end of Antiochus, called Epiphanes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now will we declare the acts of Antiochus Eupator, who was the son of this wicked man, gathering briefly the calamities of the wars. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} So when he was come to the crown, he set one Lysias over the affairs of his realm, and appointed him his chief governor of Celosyria and Phenice. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} For Ptolemeus, that was called Macron, choosing rather to do justice to the Jews for the wrong that had been done to them, endeavoured to continue peace with them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Whereupon being accused of the king's friends before Eupator, and called traitor at every word because he had left Cyprus, that Philometor had committed to him, and departed to Antiochus Epiphanes, and seeing that he was in no honorable place, he was so discouraged, that he poisoned himself and died. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But when Gorgias was governor of the holds, he hired soldiers, and nourished war continually with the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And therewithal the Idumeans, having gotten into their hands the most commodious holds, kept the Jews occupied, and receiving those that were banished from Jerusalem, they went about to nourish war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Then they that were with Maccabeus made supplication, and implored God that he would be their helper; and so they ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And assaulting them strongly, they won the holds, and kept off all that fought upon the wall, and killed all that fell into their hands, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And because certain, who were no less than nine thousand, were fled together into two very strong castles, having all manner of things convenient to sustain the siege, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Maccabeus left Simon and Joseph, and Zaccheus also, and them that were with him, who were enough to besiege them, and departed himself to those places which more needed his help. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachmas, and let some of them escape. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But when it was told Maccabeus what was done, he called the governors of the people together, and accused those men, that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} So he killed those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And having good success with his weapons in all things he took in hand, he killed in the two holds more than twenty thousand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Now Timotheus, whom the Jews had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But when he drew near, they that were with Maccabeus turned themselves to pray to God, and sprinkled earth upon their heads, and girded their loins with sackcloth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And fell down at the foot of the altar, and implored him to be merciful to them, and to be an enemy to their enemies, and an adversary to their adversaries, as the law declares. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So after the prayer they took their weapons, and went on further from the city: and when they drew near to their enemies, they kept by themselves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Now the sun being newly risen, they joined both together; the one part having together with their virtue their refuge also to the Lord for a pledge of their success and victory: the other side making their rage leader of their battle {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But when the battle waxed strong, there appeared to the enemies from heaven five comely men upon horses, with bridles of gold, and two of them led the Jews, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And took Maccabeus between them, and covered him on every side weapons, and kept him safe, but shot arrows and lightnings against the enemies: so that being confounded with blindness, and full of trouble, they were killed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And there were slain of footmen twenty thousand and five hundred, and six hundred horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} As for Timotheus himself, he fled into a very strong hold, called Gazara, where Chereas was governor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} But they that were with Maccabeus laid siege against the fortress courageously four days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And they that were within, trusting to the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus' company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Others likewise ascending after them, while they were busied with them that were within, burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive; and others broke open the gates, and, having received in the rest of the army, took the city, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And killed Timotheus, that was hid in a certain pit, and Chereas his brother, with Apollophanes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} When this was done, they praised the Lord with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Israel, and given them the victory.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 11}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 11}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Not long after the, Lysias the king's protector and cousin, who also managed the affairs, took sore displeasure for the things that were done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And when he had gathered about fourscore thousand with all the horsemen, he came against the Jews, thinking to make the city an habitation of the Gentiles, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And to make a gain of the temple, as of the other chapels of the heathen, and to set the high priesthood to sale every year: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Not at all considering the power of God but puffed up with his ten thousands of footmen, and his thousands of horsemen, and his fourscore elephants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} So he came to Judea, and drew near to Bethsura, which was a strong town, but distant from Jerusalem about five furlongs, and he laid sore siege to it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Now when they that were with Maccabeus heard that he besieged the holds, they and all the people with lamentation and tears implored the Lord that he would send a good angel to deliver Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Then Maccabeus himself first of all took weapons, exhorting the other that they would jeopard themselves together with him to help their brethren: so they went forth together with a willing mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And as they were at Jerusalem, there appeared before them on horseback one in white clothing, shaking his armor of gold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Then they praised the merciful God all together, and took heart, insomuch that they were ready not only to fight with men, but with most cruel beasts, and to pierce through walls of iron. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Thus they marched forward in their armor, having an helper from heaven: for the Lord was merciful to them {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And giving a charge upon their enemies like lions, they killed eleven thousand footmen, and sixteen hundred horsemen, and put all the other to flight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Many of them also being wounded escaped naked; and Lysias himself fled away shamefully, and so escaped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Who, as he was a man of understanding, casting with himself what loss he had had, and considering that the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty God helped them, he sent to them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} And persuaded them to agree to all reasonable conditions, and promised that he would persuade the king that he must needs be a friend to them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Then Maccabeus consented to all that Lysias desired, being careful of the common good; and whatever Maccabeus wrote to Lysias concerning the Jews, the king granted it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} For there were letters written to the Jews from Lysias to this effect: Lysias to the people of the Jews sends greeting: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} John and Absalon, who were sent from you, delivered me the petition subscribed, and made request for the performance of the contents thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Therefore what things soever were meet to be reported to the king, I have declared them, and he has granted as much as might be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And if then you⌃ will keep yourselves loyal to the state, hereafter also will I endeavor to be a means of your good. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} But of the particulars I have given order both to these and the other that came from me, to commune with you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Fare you⌃ well. The hundred and eight and fortieth year, the four and twentieth day of the month Dioscorinthius. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Now the king's letter contained these words: King Antiochus to his brother Lysias sends greeting: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Since our father is translated to the gods, our will is, that they that are in our realm live quietly, that every one may attend upon his own affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} We understand also that the Jews would not consent to our father, for to be brought to the custom of the Gentiles, but had rather keep their own manner of living: for the which cause they require of us, that we should suffer them to live after their own laws. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Therefore our mind is, that this nation shall be in rest, and we have determined to restore them their temple, that they may live according to the customs of their forefathers. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} You shall do well therefore to send to them, and grant them peace, that when they are certified of our mind, they may be of good comfort, and ever go cheerfully about their own affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And the letter of the king to the nation of the Jews was after this manner: King Antiochus sends greeting to the council, and the rest of the Jews: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} If you⌃ fare well, we have our desire; we are also in good health. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Menelaus declared to us, that your desire was to return home, and to follow your own business: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Therefore they that will depart shall have safe conduct till the thirties day of Xanthicus with security. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And the Jews shall use their own kind of meats and laws, as before; and none of them any manner of ways shall be molested for things ignorantly done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} I have sent also Menelaus, that he may comfort you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Fare you⌃ well. In the hundred forty and eighth year, and the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The Romans also sent to them a letter containing these words: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manlius, ambassadors of the Romans, send greeting to the people of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} Whatsoever Lysias the king's cousin has granted, therewith we also are well pleased. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} But touching such things as he judged to be referred to the king, after you⌃ have advised thereof, send one forthwith, that we may declare as it is convenient for you: for we are now going to Antioch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Therefore send some with speed, that we may know what is your mind. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Farewell. This hundred and eight and fortieth year, the fifteenth day of the month Xanthicus.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 12}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 12}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} When these covenants were made, Lysias went to the king, and the Jews were about their husbandry. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} But of the governors of several places, Timotheus, and Apollonius the son of Genneus, also Hieronymus, and Demophon, and beside them Nicanor the governor of Cyprus, would not suffer them to be quiet and live in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The men of Joppa also did such an ungodly deed: they prayed the Jews that lived among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When Judas heard of this cruelty done to his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And calling upon God the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brethren, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled there he killed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And when the town was shut up, he went backward, as if he would return to root out all them of the city of Joppa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} But when he heard that the Jamnites were minded to do in like manner to the Jews that lived among them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He came upon the Jamnites also by night, and set fire on the haven and the navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Now when they were gone from thence nine furlongs in their journey toward Timotheus, no fewer than five thousand men on foot and five hundred horsemen of the Arabians set upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Whereupon there was a very sore battle; but Judas' side by the help of God got the victory; so that the Nomades of Arabia, being overcome, implored Judas for peace, promising both to give him cattle, and to pleasure him otherwise. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then Judas, thinking indeed that they would be profitable in many things, granted them peace: whereupon they shook hands, and so they departed to their tents. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} He went also about to make a bridge to a certain strong city, which was fenced about with walls, and inhabited by people of various countries; and the name of it was Caspis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} But they that were within it put such trust in the strength of the walls and provision of food, that they behaved themselves rudely toward them that were with Judas, railing and blaspheming, and uttering such words as were not to be spoken. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Therefore Judas with his company, calling upon the great Lord of the world, who without rams or engines of war did cast down Jericho in the time of Joshua, gave a fierce assault against the walls, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And took the city by the will of God, and made unspeakable slaughters, insomuch that a lake two furlongs broad near adjoining thereto, being filled full, was seen running with blood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Then departed they from thence seven hundred and fifty furlongs, and came to Characa to the Jews that are called Tubieni. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} But as for Timotheus, they found him not in the places: for before he had dispatched any thing, he departed from thence, having left a very strong garrison in a certain hold. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Howbeit Dositheus and Sosipater, who were of Maccabeus' captains, went forth, and killed those that Timotheus had left in the fortress, above ten thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And Maccabeus ranged his army by bands, and set them over the bands, and went against Timotheus, who had about him one hundred and twenty thousand men of foot, and two thousand and five hundred horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now when Timotheus had knowledge of Judas' coming, he sent the women and children and the other baggage to a fortress called Carnion: for the town was hard to besiege, and uneasy to come to, by reason of the straitness of all the places. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} But when Judas his first band came in sight, the enemies, being struck with fear and terror through the appearing of him who sees all things, fled amain, one running into this way, another that way, so as that they were often hurt of their own men, and wounded with the points of their own swords. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he killed about thirty thousand men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Moreover Timotheus himself fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he implored with much craft to let him go with his life, because he had many of the Jews' parents, and the brethren of some of them, who, if they put him to death, should not be regarded. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} So when he had assured them with many words that he would restore them without hurt, according to the agreement, they let him go for the saving of their brethren. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Then Maccabeus marched forth to Carnion, and to the temple of Atargatis, and there he killed five and twenty thousand persons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} And after he had put to flight and destroyed them, Judas removed the host toward Ephron, a strong city, wherein Lysias abode, and a great multitude of various nations, and the strong young men kept the walls, and defended them mightily: wherein also was great provision of engines and darts. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But when Judas and his company had called upon Almighty God, who with his power breaks the strength of his enemies, they won the city, and killed twenty and five thousand of them that were within, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} From thence they departed to Scythopolis, which lies six hundred furlongs from Jerusalem, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} But when the Jews that lived there had testified that the Scythopolitans dealt lovingly with them, and entreated them kindly in the time of their adversity; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} They gave them thanks, desiring them to be friendly still to them: and so they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks approaching. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And after the feast, called Pentecost, they went forth against Gorgias the governor of Idumea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Who came out with three thousand men of foot and four hundred horsemen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And it happened that in their fighting together a few of the Jews were slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} At which time Dositheus, one of Bacenor's company, who was on horseback, and a strong man, was still upon Gorgias, and taking hold of his coat drew him by force; and when he would have taken that cursed man alive, a horseman of Thracia coming upon him struck off his shoulder, so that Gorgias fled to Marisa. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Now when they that were with Gorgias had fought long, and were weary, Judas called upon the Lord, that he would show himself to be their helper and leader of the battle. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And with that he began in his own language, and sung psalms with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon Gorgias' men, he put them to flight. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers' graves. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause therefore they were slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} All men therefore praising the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Betook themselves to prayer, and implored him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachmas of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And also in that he perceived that there was great favor laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 13}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 13}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} In the hundred forty and ninth year it was told Judas, that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a great power into Judea, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, one hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} But the King of kings moved Antiochus' mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him to Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And whoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Jews, than had been done in his father's time. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon the Lord night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} So when they had all done this together, and implored the merciful Lord with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king's host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even to death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of God; with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king's tent by night, and killed in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And at last they filled the camp with fear and tumult, and departed with good success. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} This was done in the break of the day, because the protection of the Lord did help him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Now when the king had taken a taste of the manliness of the Jews, he went about to take the holds by policy, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And marched toward Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Jews: but he was put to flight, failed, and lost of his men: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} For Judas had conveyed to them that were in it such things as were necessary. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} But Rhodocus, who was in the Jews' host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The king treated with them in Bethsura the second time, gave his hand, took their's, departed, fought with Judas, was overcome; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, entreated the Jews, submitted himself, and swore to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honored the temple, and dealt kindly with the place, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And accepted well of Maccabeus, made him principal governor from Ptolemais to the Gerrhenians; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Came to Ptolemais: the people there were grieved for the covenants; for they stormed, because they would make their covenants void: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king's coming and departing.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 14}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 14}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} After three years was Judas informed, that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having entered by the haven of Tripolis with a great power and navy, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Had taken the country, and killed Antiochus, and Lysias his protector. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fifties year, presenting to him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprise, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Jews stood affected, and what they intended, he answered thereto: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Those of the Jews that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore I, being deprived of my ancestors' honor, I mean the high priesthood, am now come here: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of my own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforesaid. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Therefore, O king, seeing know all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that you readily show to all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} For as long as Judas lives, it is not possible that the state should be quiet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king's friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Commanding him to kill Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then the heathen, that had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Jews to be their welfare. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Now when the Jews heard of Nicanor's coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helps his portion with manifestation of his presence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So at the commandment of the captain they removed straightways from thence, and came near to them at the town of Dessau. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Now Simon, Judas' brother, had joined battle with Nicanor, but was somewhat discomfited through the sudden silence of his enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the manliness of them that were with Judas, and the courageousness that they had to fight for their country, dared not try the matter by the sword. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Therefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotus, and Mattathias, to make peace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} So when they had taken long advisement thereupon, and the captain had made the multitude acquainted therewith, and it appeared that they were all of one mind, they consented to the covenants, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And appointed a day to meet in together by themselves: and when the day came, and stools were set for either of them, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Judas placed armed men ready in convenient places, lest some treachery should be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made a peaceful conference. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Now Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no hurt, but sent away the people that came flocking to him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he love the man from his heart {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He prayed him also to take a wife, and to beget children: so he married, was quiet, and took part of this life. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was between them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king's successor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} When this came to Nicanor's hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish to him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behavior came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas' policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And when they swore that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If you⌃ will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple to Bacchus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} After these words he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and implored him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} You, O Lord of all things, who have need of nothing, was pleased that the temple of your habitation should be among us: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Therefore now, O holy Lord of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Now was there accused to Nicanor one Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen, and a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} So Nicanor, willing to declare the hate that he bare to the Jews, sent above five hundred men of war to take him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} For he thought by taking him to do the Jews much hurt. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} Now when the multitude would have taken the tower, and violently broken into the outer door, and bade that fire should be brought to burn it, he being ready to be taken on every side fell upon his sword; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} Choosing rather to die manfully, than to come into the hands of the wicked, to be abused otherwise than beseemed his noble birth: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} But missing his stroke through haste, the multitude also rushing within the doors, he ran boldly up to the wall, and cast himself down manfully among the thickest of them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} But they quickly giving back, and a space being made, he fell down into the midst of the void place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Nevertheless, while there was yet breath within him, being inflamed with anger, he rose up; and though his blood gushed out like spouts of water, and his wounds were grievous, yet he ran through the midst of the throng; and standing upon a steep rock, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} When as his blood was now quite gone, he plucked out his bowels, and taking them in both his hands, he cast them upon the throng, and calling upon the Lord of life and spirit to restore him those again, he thus died.\par
\subsection*{2 Maccabees 15}
\markright{2 MACCABEES 15}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} But Nicanor, hearing that Judas and his company were in the strong places about Samaria, resolved without any danger to set upon them on the sabbath day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Nevertheless the Jews that were compelled to go with him said, O destroy not so cruelly and barbarously, but give honor to that day, which he, that sees all things, has honored with holiness above all other days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Then the most ungracious wretch demanded, if there were a Mighty one in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And when they said, There is in heaven a living Lord, and mighty, who commanded the seventh day to be kept: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} Then said the other, And I also am mighty upon earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king's business. Yet he obtained not to have his wicked will done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} So Nicanor in exceeding pride and haughtiness determined to set up a publick monument of his victory over Judas and them that were with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} But Maccabeus had ever sure confidence that the Lord would help him: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Therefore he exhorted his people not to fear the coming of the heathen against them, but to remember the help which in former times they had received from heaven, and now to expect the victory and aid, which should come to them from the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won before, he made them more cheerful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, showing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Thus he armed every one of them, not so much with defence of shields and spears, as with comfortable and good words: and beside that, he told them a dream worthy to be believed, as if it had been so indeed, which did not a little rejoice them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And this was his vision: That Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken also, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue, holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} This done, in like manner there appeared a man with gray hairs, and exceeding glorious, who was of a wonderful and excellent majesty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then Onias answered, saying, This is a lover of the brethren, who prays much for the people, and for the holy city, to wit, Jeremias the prophet of God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Whereupon Jeremias holding forth his right hand gave to Judas a sword of gold, and in giving it spoke thus, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which you shall wound the adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas, which were very good, and able to stir them up to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men, they determined not to pitch camp, but courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict, because the city and the sanctuary and the temple were in danger. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} For the care that they took for their wives, and their children, their brethren, and folks, was in least account with them: but the greatest and principal fear was for the holy temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Also they that were in the city took not the least care, being troubled for the conflict abroad. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And now, when as all looked what should be the trial, and the enemies were already come near, and the army was set in array, and the beasts conveniently placed, and the horsemen set in wings, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Maccabeus seeing the coming of the multitude, and the various preparations of armor, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretched out his hands toward heaven, and called upon the Lord that works wonders, knowing that victory comes not by arms, but even as it seems good to him, he gives it to such as are worthy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Therefore in his prayer he said after this manner; O Lord, you did send your angel in the time of Ezekias king of Judea, and did kill in the host of Sennacherib one hundred fourscore and five thousand: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Therefore now also, O Lord of heaven, send a good angel before us for a fear and dread to them; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And through the might of your arm let those be stricken with terror, that come against your holy people to blaspheme. And he ended thus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Then Nicanor and they that were with him came forward with trumpets and songs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} But Judas and his company encountered the enemies with invocation and prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} So that fighting with their hands, and praying to God with their hearts, they killed no less than thirty and five thousand men: for through the appearance of God they were greatly cheered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Now when the battle was done, returning again with joy, they knew that Nicanor lay dead in his harness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Then they made a great shout and a noise, praising the Almighty in their own language. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} And Judas, who was ever the chief defender of the citizens both in body and mind, and who continued his love toward his countrymen all his life, commanded to strike off Nicanor's head, and his hand with his shoulder, and bring them to Jerusalem. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} So when he was there, and called them of his nation together, and set the priests before the altar, he sent for them that were of the tower, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And showed them vile Nicanor's head, and the hand of that blasphemer, which with proud brags he had stretched out against the holy temple of the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And when he had cut out the tongue of that ungodly Nicanor, he commanded that they should give it by pieces to the fowls, and hang up the reward of his madness before the temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} So every man praised toward the heaven the glorious Lord, saying, Blessed be he that has kept his own place undefiled. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} He hanged also Nicanor's head upon the tower, an evident and manifest sign to all of the help of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} And they ordained all with a common decree in no case to let that day pass without solemnity, but to celebrate the thirties day of the twelfth month, which in the Syrian tongue is called Adar, the day before Mardocheus' day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} Thus went it with Nicanor: and from that time forth the Hebrews had the city in their power. And here will I make an end. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And if I have done well, and as is fitting the story, it is that which I desired: but if slenderly and meanly, it is that which I could attain to. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} For as it is hurtful to drink wine or water alone; and as wine mingled with water is pleasant, and delights the taste: even so speech finely framed delights the ears of them that read the story. And here shall be an end.\par
\newpage
\section*{1 Esdras Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Anonymous compiler of Greek Ezra material\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The book is an anonymous Greek retelling/arrangement of material parallel to Chronicles-Ezra-Nehemiah plus the Three Guards episode.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; included here as Greek Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Hellenistic period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek is the principal textual tradition; it overlaps heavily with canonical Ezra material.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Retelling of restoration history with an added court tale about the strongest thing.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To present restoration themes and divine favor in a Greek retelling of Ezra-related history.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} restoration; temple; return; wisdom; royal favor\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Historical retelling 1-9 with Three Guards episode embedded.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek text is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Vaticanus and Alexandrinus preserve 1 Esdras in Greek 4th-5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used by Josephus in places by Josephus (1st century AD)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 1 Esdras is text-critically important because it parallels canonical Ezra material and can preserve alternate Greek forms.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as Greek Apocrypha and useful for comparison with Ezra-Nehemiah.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{1 Esdras}
\markboth{1 ESDRAS}{}
\subsection*{1 Esdras 1}
\markright{1 ESDRAS 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem to his Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Having set the priests according to their daily courses, being arrayed in long garments, in the temple of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And he spoke to the Levites, the holy ministers of Israel, that they should hallow themselves to the Lord, to set the holy ark of the Lord in the house that king Solomon the son of David had built: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And said, You⌃ shall no more bear the ark upon your shoulders: now therefore serve the Lord your God, and minister to his people Israel, and prepare you after your families and kindred, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} According as David the king of Israel prescribed, and according to the magnificence of Solomon his son: and standing in the temple according to the several dignity of the families of you the Levites, who minister in the presence of your brethren the children of Israel, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Offer the passover in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brethren, and keep the passover according to the commandment of the Lord, which was given to Moses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And to the people that was
