gave by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{83}} That the land, which you⌃ enter into to possess as an heritage, is a land polluted with the pollutions of the strangers of the land, and they have filled it with their uncleanness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{84}} Therefore now shall you⌃ not join your daughters to their sons, neither shall you⌃ take their daughters to your sons. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{85}} Moreover you⌃ shall never seek to have peace with them, that you⌃ may be strong, and eat the good things of the land, and that you⌃ may leave the inheritance of the land to your children for evermore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{86}} And all that is befallen is done to us for our wicked works and great sins; for you, O Lord, did make our sins light, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{87}} And did give to us such a root: but we have turned back again to transgress your law, and to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the nations of the land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{88}} Mightest not you be angry with us to destroy us, till you had left us neither root, seed, nor name? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{89}} O Lord of Israel, you are true: for we are left a root this day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{90}} Behold, now are we before you in our iniquities, for we can’t stand any longer by reason of these things before you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{91}} And as Esdras in his prayer made his confession, weeping, and lying flat upon the ground before the temple, there gathered to him from Jerusalem a very great multitude of men and women and children: for there was great weeping among the multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{92}} Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out, and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land, and now is all Israel aloft. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{93}} Let us make an oath to the Lord, that we will put away all our wives, which we have taken of the heathen, with their children, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{94}} Like as you have decreed, and as many as do obey the law of the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{95}} Arise and put in execution: for to you does this matter appertain, and we will be with you: do valiantly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{96}} So Esdras arose, and took an oath of the chief of the priests and Levites of all Israel to do after these things; and so they swore.\par
\subsection*{1 Esdras 9}
\markright{1 ESDRAS 9}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Esdras rising from the court of the temple went to the chamber of Joanan the son of Eliasib, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And remained there, and did eat no meat nor drink water, mourning for the great iniquities of the multitude. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} And there was a proclamation in all Jewry and Jerusalem to all them that were of the captivity, that they should be gathered together at Jerusalem: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} And that whoever met not there within two or three days according as the elders that bare rule appointed, their cattle should be seized to the use of the temple, and himself cast out from them that were of the captivity. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} And in three days were all they of the tribe of Judah and Benjamin gathered together at Jerusalem the twentieth day of the ninth month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} And all the multitude sat trembling in the broad court of the temple because of the present foul weather. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} So Esdras arose up, and said to them, You⌃ have transgressed the law in marrying strange wives, thereby to increase the sins of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And now by confessing give glory to the Lord God of our fathers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And do his will, and separate yourselves from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then cried the whole multitude, and said with a loud voice, Like as you have spoken, so will we do. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} But forasmuch as the people are many, and it is foul weather, so that we can’t stand without, and this is not a work of a day or two, seeing our sin in these things is spread far: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Therefore let the rulers of the multitude stay, and let all them of our habitations that have strange wives come at the time appointed, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And with them the rulers and judges of every place, till we turn away the wrath of the Lord from us for this matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Then Jonathan the son of Azael and Ezechias the son of Theocanus accordingly took this matter upon them: and Mosollam and Levis and Sabbatheus helped them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} And they that were of the captivity did according to all these things. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And Esdras the priest chose to him the principal men of their families, all by name: and in the first day of the tenth month they sat together to examine the matter. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} So their cause that held strange wives was brought to an end in the first day of the first month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} And of the priests that were come together, and had strange wives, there were found: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Of the sons of Jesus the son of Josedec, and his brethren; Matthelas and Eleazar, and Joribus and Joadanus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And they gave their hands to put away their wives and to offer rams to make reconcilement for their errors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And of the sons of Emmer; Ananias, and Zabdeus, and Eanes, and Sameius, and Hiereel, and Azarias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And of the sons of Phaisur; Elionas, Massias Israel, and Nathanael, and Ocidelus and Talsas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} And of the Levites; Jozabad, and Semis, and Colius, who was called Calitas, and Patheus, and Judas, and Jonas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Of the holy singers; Eleazurus, Bacchurus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Of the porters; Sallumus, and Tolbanes. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Of them of Israel, of the sons of Phoros; Hiermas, and Eddias, and Melchias, and Maelus, and Eleazar, and Asibias, and Baanias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Of the sons of Ela; Matthanias, Zacharias, and Hierielus, and Hieremoth, and Aedias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} And of the sons of Zamoth; Eliadas, Elisimus, Othonias, Jarimoth, and Sabatus, and Sardeus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Of the sons of Babai; Johannes, and Ananias and Josabad, and Amatheis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Of the sons of Mani; Olamus, Mamuchus, Jedeus, Jasubus, Jasael, and Hieremoth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} And of the sons of Addi; Naathus, and Moosias, Lacunus, and Naidus, and Mathanias, and Sesthel, Balnuus, and Manasseas. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} And of the sons of Annas; Elionas and Aseas, and Melchias, and Sabbeus, and Simon Chosameus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} And of the sons of Asom; Altaneus, and Matthias, and Baanaia, Eliphalet, and Manasses, and Semei. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} And of the sons of Maani; Jeremias, Momdis, Omaerus, Juel, Mabdai, and Pelias, and Anos, Carabasion, and Enasibus, and Mamnitanaimus, Eliasis, Bannus, Eliali, Samis, Selemias, Nathanias: and of the sons of Ozora; Sesis, Esril, Azaelus, Samatus, Zambis, Josephus. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} And of the sons of Ethma; Mazitias, Zabadaias, Edes, Juel, Banaias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} All these had taken strange wives, and they put them away with their children. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And the priests and Levites, and they that were of Israel, lived in Jerusalem, and in the country, in the first day of the seventh month: so the children of Israel were in their habitations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} And the whole multitude came together with one accord into the broad place of the holy porch toward the east: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} And they spoke to Esdras the priest and reader, that he would bring the law of Moses, that was given of the Lord God of Israel. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} So Esdras the chief priest brought the law to the whole multitude from man to woman, and to all the priests, to hear law in the first day of the seventh month. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} And he read in the broad court before the holy porch from morning to midday, before both men and women; and the multitude gave heed to the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} And Esdras the priest and reader of the law stood up upon a pulpit of wood, which was made for that purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} And there stood up by him Mattathias, Sammus, Ananias, Azarias, Urias, Ezecias, Balasamus, upon the right hand: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} And upon his left hand stood Phaldaius, Misael, Melchias, Lothasubus, and Nabarias. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} Then took Esdras the book of the law before the multitude: for he sat honorably in the first place in the sight of them all. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} And when he opened the law, they stood all straight up. So Esdras blessed the Lord God most High, the God of hosts, Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} And all the people answered, Amen; and lifting up their hands they fell to the ground, and worshipped the Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} Also Jesus, Anus, Sarabias, Adinus, Jacubus, Sabateas, Auteas, Maianeas, and Calitas, Azarias, and Joazabdus, and Ananias, Biatas, the Levites, taught the law of the Lord, making them withal to understand it. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} Then spoke Attharates to Esdras the chief priest. and reader, and to the Levites that taught the multitude, even to all, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} This day is holy to the Lord; (for they all wept when they heard the law:) {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} Go then, and eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send part to them that have nothing; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} For this day is holy to the Lord: and be not sorrowful; for the Lord will bring you to honor. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} So the Levites published all things to the people, saying, This day is holy to the Lord; be not sorrowful. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} Then they went their way, every one to eat and drink, and make merry, and to give part to them that had nothing, and to make great cheer; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} Because they understood the words wherein they were instructed, and for the which they had been assembled.\par

\section*{Prayer of Manasseh Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Anonymous liturgical writer; framed in Manasseh's voice\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The prayer is transmitted as Manasseh's penitential prayer, though its literary history is uncertain.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; included here as liturgical Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Hellenistic or later\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek is the principal widely transmitted form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Short penitential prayer framed by 2 Chronicles 33's notice about Manasseh's prayer.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To model repentance, confession, and appeal to divine mercy.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} repentance; mercy; confession; humility\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Single penitential prayer.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No complete Hebrew original survives n/a | Subst. Greek text is the principal substantial witness late antiquity | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Greek and later liturgical traditions preserve the prayer late antique and medieval periods\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used in Christian liturgical and devotional tradition by Church tradition (late antique and medieval)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} The prayer is brief and textually simple compared with larger apocryphal books.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as devotional Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{Prayer of Manasseh}
\markboth{PRAYER OF MANASSEH}{}
\subsection*{Prayer of Manasseh 1}
\markright{PRAYER OF MANASSEH 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then Azarias stood up, and prayed on this manner; and opening his mouth in the midst of the fire said,\par
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} O LORD Almighty, the God of our fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and of their righteous seed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} Blessed are you, O Lord God of our fathers: your name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} that have made the heaven and the earth with all their adornment; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} For you are righteous in all the things that you have done to us: yes, true are all your works, your ways are right, and all your judgments truth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} that have bound the sea with the word of your commandment; that have closed the abyss and sealed it with your fearful and glorious name; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} In all the things that you have brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, you have executed true judgment: for according to truth and judgment did you bring all these things upon us because of our sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} whom all things revere and tremble before the face of your power, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} because the magnificence of your glory is unendurable and irresistible the wrath of your threatening against sinners: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} In all things have we trespassed, and not obeyed your commandments, nor kept them, neither done as you have commanded us, that it might go well with us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} the mercy of your promise is both immeasurable and inscrutable; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Therefore all that you have brought upon us, and every thing that you have done to us, you have done in true judgment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} for you are the Lord most high, compassionate, longsuffering, and most merciful, repenting of the evils of men. You, Lord, according to the abundance of your goodness, have proclaimed repentance and forgiveness to those that have sinned against you, and in the multitude of your kindnesses you have decreed for sinners repentance to salvation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} And you did deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful forsakers of God, and to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Surely you, O Lord, the God of the just, have not appointed repentance for the just, for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob who have not sinned against you; but you have appointed repentance for me a sinner: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now we can’t open our mouths, we are become a shame and reproach to your servants; and to them that worship you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} for I have sinned above the number of the sand of the sea. My transgressions are multiplied, O Lord, they are multiplied, and I am not worthy to look at or see the height of heaven, for the multitude of my iniquities, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Yet deliver us not up wholly, for your name's sake, neither disannul you your covenant: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} being bowed down by many iron bonds, so that I can’t uplift my head, and there is no release for me, because I have provoked your anger, and have done evil before you, not doing your will, nor keeping your commandments, but setting up abominations and multiplying offenses. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And cause not your mercy to depart from us, for your beloved Abraham's sake, for your servant Isaac's sake, and for your holy Israel's sake; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And now I bend the knee of my heart, beseeching your goodness: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} To whom you have spoken and promised, that you would multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that lies upon the seashore. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my transgressions: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} For we, O Lord, are become less than any nation, and be kept under this day in all the world because of our sins. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} but I pray and beseech you, release me, Lord, release me, and destroy me not with my transgressions; keep not evils for me in anger for ever, nor condemn me to the lowest parts of the earth: because you are God, the God of the repenting; and in me you will show all your benevolence, for that me unworthy you will save, according to your great mercy: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Neither is there at this time prince, or prophet, or leader, or burnt offering, or sacrifice, or oblation, or incense, or place to sacrifice before you, and to find mercy. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} and I will praise you continually all the days of my life: for all the hosts of the heavens sings to you, and your is the glory for ever and ever. Amen. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Nevertheless in a contrite heart and an humble spirit let us be accepted. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Like as in the burnt offerings of rams and bullocks, and like as in ten thousands of fat lambs: so let our sacrifice be in your sight this day, and grant that we may wholly go after you: for they shall not be confounded that put their trust in you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} And now we follow you with all our heart, we fear you, and seek your face. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Put us not to shame: but deal with us after your lovingkindness, and according to the multitude of your mercies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Deliver us also according to your marvelous works, and give glory to your name, O Lord: and let all them that do your servants hurt be ashamed; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And let them be confounded in all their power and might, and let their strength be broken; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} And let them know that you are God, the only God, and glorious over the whole world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} And the king's servants, that put them in, ceased not to make the oven hot with rosin, pitch, tow, and small wood; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} So that the flame streamed forth above the furnace forty and nine cubits. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} And it passed through, and burned those Chaldeans it found about the furnace. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} But the angel of the Lord came down into the oven together with Azarias and his fellows, and struck the flame of the fire out of the oven; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} And made the midst of the furnace as it had been a moist whistling wind, so that the fire touched them not at all, neither hurt nor troubled them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Then the three, as out of one mouth, praised, glorified, and blessed, God in the furnace, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Blessed are you, O Lord God of our fathers: and to be praised and exalted above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} And blessed is your glorious and holy name: and to be praised and exalted above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory: and to be praised and glorified above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Blessed are you that behold the depths, and sit upon the cherubims: and to be praised and exalted above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Blessed are you on the glorious throne of your kingdom: and to be praised and glorified above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven: and above all to be praised and glorified for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} O all you⌃ works of the Lord, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} O you⌃ heavens, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} O you⌃ angels of the Lord, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} O all you⌃ waters that be above the heaven, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} O all you⌃ powers of the Lord, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} O you⌃ sun and moon, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} O you⌃ stars of heaven, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} O every shower and dew, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} O all you⌃ winds, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} O you⌃ fire and heat, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} O you⌃ winter and summer, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} O you⌃ dews and storms of snow, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} O you⌃ nights and days, bless you⌃ the Lord: bless and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} O you⌃ light and darkness, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} O you⌃ ice and cold, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} O you⌃ frost and snow, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} O you⌃ lightnings and clouds, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} O let the earth bless the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{52}} O you⌃ mountains and little hills, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{53}} O all you⌃ things that grow in the earth, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{54}} O you⌃ mountains, bless you⌃ the Lord: Praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{55}} O you⌃ seas and rivers, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{56}} O you⌃ whales, and all that move in the waters, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{57}} O all you⌃ fowls of the air, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{58}} O all you⌃ beasts and cattle, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{59}} O you⌃ children of men, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{60}} O Israel, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{61}} O you⌃ priests of the Lord, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{62}} O you⌃ servants of the Lord, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{63}} O you⌃ spirits and souls of the righteous, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{64}} O you⌃ holy and humble men of heart, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{65}} O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless you⌃ the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever: for he has delivered us from hell, and saved us from the hand of death, and delivered us out of the midst of the furnace and burning flame: even out of the midst of the fire has he delivered us. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{66}} O give thanks to the Lord, because he is gracious: for his mercy endures for ever. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{67}} O all you⌃ that worship the Lord, bless the God of gods, praise him, and give him thanks: for his mercy endures for ever.\par

\section*{3 Maccabees Introduction}
{\notefont\fontsize{8.7}{10.2}\selectfont
\noindent\textbf{Author and Attribution.} Anonymous Hellenistic Jewish author\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Authorship Basis.} The author is anonymous and writes in Greek about persecution under Ptolemaic rule.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Jesus / NT Attribution.} No NT attribution identifies the human writer; included here as Greek Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Composition Date.} Hellenistic period\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{MT Timeline.} Not applicable\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{LXX Timeline.} Greek is the original and principal form.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Historical Setting.} Diaspora narrative of threatened persecution and divine deliverance in Egypt.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Purpose.} To encourage Jews under pressure by recounting God's deliverance from royal oppression.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Key Themes.} diaspora; persecution; deliverance; prayer; reversal\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Outline.} Royal threat 1-4; divine deliverance 5-7.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest Witnesses.} Frag. No Hebrew original is known n/a | Subst. Greek text is the principal substantial witness Hellenistic and later | Heb. n/a n/a | Gk. Codex Alexandrinus preserves 3 Maccabees in Greek 5th century AD\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Earliest External Attestation.} Used in later Eastern Christian tradition by Later church tradition (late antique and medieval)\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Textual Notes.} 3 Maccabees is Greek Jewish literature distinct from the Hasmonean history of 1-2 Maccabees.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
\noindent\textbf{Conservative Notes.} Included here as Greek Apocrypha in the Brenton corpus.\par
\vspace{0.18em}
}

\section*{3 Maccabees}
\markboth{3 MACCABEES}{}
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 1}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 1}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now Philopater, on learning from those who came back that Antiochus had made himself master of the places which belonged to himself, sent orders to all his footmen and horsemen, took with him his sister Arsinoe, and marched out as far as the parts of Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces encamped. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} And one Theodotus, intending to carry out his design, took with him the bravest of the armed men who had been before committed to his trust by Ptolemy, and got through at night to the tent of Ptolemy, to kill him on his own responsibility, and so to end the war. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} But Dositheus, called the son of Drimulus, by birth a Jew, afterward a renegade from the laws and observances of his country, conveyed Ptolemy away, and made an obscure person lie down in his stead in the tent. It befell this man to receive the fate which was meant for the other. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} A fierce battle then took place; and the men of Antiochus prevailing, Arsinoe continually went up and down the ranks, and with dishevelled hair, with tears and entreaties, begged the soldiers to fight manfully for themselves, their children, and wives; and promised that if they proved conquerors, she would give them two minas of gold apiece. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} It thus fell out that their enemies were defeated in hand-to-hand encounter, and that many of them were taken prisoners. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Having vanquished this attempt, the king then decided to proceed to the neighbouring cities, and encourage them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} By doing this, and by making donations to their temples, he inspired his subjects with confidence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The Jews sent some of their council and of their elders to him. The greetings, guest-gifts, and congratulations of the past, bestowed by them, filled him with the greater eagerness to visit their city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Having arrived at Jerusalem, sacrificed, and offered thank-offerings to the Greatest God, and done whatever else was suitable to the sanctity of the place, and entered the inner court, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} he was so struck with the magnificence of the place, and so wondered at the orderly arrangements of the temple, that he considered entering the sanctuary itself. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying Be it that they were deprived of this honor, I ought not to be. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} And he put the question, Why, when he entered all the temples, none of the priests who were present forbad him? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} He was thoroughly answered by some one, That he did wrong to boast of this. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Well; since I have done this, said he, be the cause what it may, shall I not enter with or without your consent? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} And when the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest God to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} then those who had been left behind in the city were scared, and rushed forth, uncertain of the event. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Virgins, who had been shut up within their chambers, came out with their mothers, scattering dust and ashes on their heads, and filling the streets with outcries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Women, but recently separated off, left their bridal chambers, left the reserve that befitted them, and ran about the city in a disorderly manner. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} New-born babes were deserted by the mothers or nurses who waited upon them; some here, some there, in houses, or in fields; these now, with an ardour which could not be checked, swarmed into the Most High temple. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Various were the prayers offered up by those who assembled in this place, on account of the unholy attempt of the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Along with these there were some of the citizens who took courage, and would not submit to his obstinacy, and his intention of carrying out his purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} Calling out to arms, and to die bravely in defence of the law of their fathers, they created a great uproar in the place, and were with difficulty brought back by the aged and the elders to the station of prayer which they had occupied before. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} During this time the multitude kept on praying. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The elders who surrounded the king strove in many ways to divert his haughty mind from the design which he had formed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onwards with the view of carrying out this design. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Yet even his own officers, when they saw this, joined the Jews in an appeal to Him who has all power, to aid in the present crisis, and not wink at such overweening lawlessness. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Such was the frequency and the vehemence of the cry of the assembled crowd, that an indescribable noise ensued. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Not the men only, but the very walls and floor seemed to sound forth; all things preferring dissolution rather than to see the place defiled.\par
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 2}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 2}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Now was it that the high priest Simon bowed his knees over against the holy place, and spread out his hands in reverent form, and uttered the following supplication: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} O Lord, Lord, King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exults in his confidence and strength. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} It is you, the Creator of all, the Lord of the universe, who are a righteous Governor, and judge all who act with pride and insolence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} It was you who did destroy the former workers of unrighteousness, among whom were the giants, who trusted in their strength and hardihood, by covering them with a measureless flood. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} It was you who did make the Sodomites, those workers of exceeding iniquity, men notorious for their vices, an example to after generations, when you did cover them with fire and brimstone. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} You did make known your power when you caused the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of your people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} And you rolled the depths of the sea over him, when he made pursuit with chariots, and with a multitude of followers, and gave a safe passage to those who put their trust in you, the Lord of the whole creation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} These saw and felt the works of your hands, and praised you the Almighty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} You, O King, when you created the illimitable and measureless earth, did choose out this city: you did make this place sacred to your name, albeit you need nothing: you did glorify it with your illustrious presence, after constructing it to the glory of your great and honorable name. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} And you did promise, out of love to the people of Israel, that should we fall away from you, and become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, you would hear our prayer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Verily you are faithful and true. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} And when you did often aid our fathers when hard pressed, and in low estate, and delivered them out of gret dangers, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} see now, holy King, how through our many and great sins we are borne down, and made subject to our enemies, and are become weak and powerless. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} We being in this low condition, this bold and profane man seeks to dishonor this your holy place, consecrated out of the earth to the name of your Majesty. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Your dwelling place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} But since it seemed good to you to exhibit your glory among your people Israel, you did sanctify this place. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} Punish us not by means of the uncleanness of their men, nor chastise us by means of their profanity; lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and show forth your compassion in this hour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} Let your mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the cast down and broken hearted may praise you with their mouth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} At that time God, who sees all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable; and scourged the man greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} His friends and bodyguards, beholding the swift recompense which had suddenly overtaken him, struck with exceeding terror, and fearing that he would die, speedily removed him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} When in course of time he had come to himself, this severe check caused no repentance within him, but he departed with bitter threatenings. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} He proceeded to Egypt, grew worse in wickedness through his before mentioned companions in wine, who were lost to all goodness; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} and not satisfied with countless acts of impiety, his audacity so increased that he raised evil reports there, and many of his friends, watching his purpose attentively, joined in furthering his will. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} His purpose was to indict a public stigma upon our race; therefore he erected a pillar at the tower-porch, and caused the following inscription to be engraved upon it: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} That entrance to their own temple was to be refused to all those who would not sacrifice; that all the Jews were to be registered among the common people; that those who resisted were to be forcibly seized and put to death; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} that those who were thus registered, were to be marked on their persons by the ivy-leaf symbol of Dionysus, and to be set apart with these limited rights. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} To do away with the appearance of hating them all, he had it written underneath, that if any of them should elect to enter the community of those initiated in the rites, these should have equal rights with the Alexandrians. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Some of those who were over the city, therefore, abhorring any approach to the city of piety, unhesitatingly gave in to the king, and expected to derive some great honor from a future connection with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} A nobler spirit, however, prompted the majority to cling to their religious observances, and by paying money that they might live unmolested, these sought to escape the registration: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} cheerfully looking forward to future aid, they abhorred their own apostates, considering them to be national foes, and debarring them from the common usages of social intercourse.\par
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 3}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 3}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Jews in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} While this was going on, an invidious rumour was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Jewish race. The purport of their charge was, that the Jews kept them away from the ordinances of the law. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} Now, while the Jews always maintained a feeling of un-swerving loyalty towards the kings, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} yet, as they worshipped God, and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} although, as they adorned their conversation with works of righteousness, they had established themselves in the good opinion of the world. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} What all the rest of mankind said, was, however, made of no account by the foreigners; {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} who said much of the exclusiveness of the Jews with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} Nor was this unexpected uproar and sudden conflux of people unobserved by the Greeks who lived in the city, concerning men who had never harmed them: yet to aid them was not in their power, since all was oppression around; but they encouraged them in their troubles, and expected a favourable turn of affairs: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} He who knows all things, will not, [said they,] disregard so great a people. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Some of the neighbors, friends, and fellow dealers of the Jews, even called them secretly to an interview, pledged them their assistance, and promised to do their very utmost for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of God, but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} King Ptolemy Philopater, to the commanders and soldiers in Egypt, and in all places, health and happiness! {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} I am right well; and so, too, are my affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} Since our Asiatic campaign, the particulars of which you⌃ know, and which by the aid of the gods, not lightly given, and by our own vigour, has been brought to a successful issue according to our expectation, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} we resolved, not with strength of spear, but with gentleness and much humanity, as it were to nurse the inhabitants of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, and to be their willing benefactors. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} So, having bestowed considerable sums of money upon the temples of the several cities, we proceeded even as far as Jerusalem; and went up to honor the temple of these wretched beings who never cease from their folly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} To outward appearance they received us willingly; but belied that appearance by their deeds. When we were eager to enter their temple, and to honor it with the most beautiful and exquisite gifts, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} they were so carried away by their old arrogance, as to forbid us the entrance; while we, out of our forbearance toward all men, refrained from exercising our power upon them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any thing reasonable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} We then, having endeavoured to make allowance for the madness of these persons, and on our victorious return treating all people in Egypt courteously, acted in a manner which was befitting. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Accordingly, bearing no ill-will against their kinsmen [at Jerusalem,] but rather remembering our connection with them, and the numerous matters with sincere heart from a remote period entrusted to them, we wished to venture a total alteration of their state, by bestowing upon them the rights of citizens of Alexandria, and to admit them to the everlasting rites of our solemnities. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} All this, however, they have taken in a very different spirit. With their innate malignity, they have spurned the fair offer; and constantly inclining to evil, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} have rejected the inestimable rights. Not only so, but by using speech, and by refraining from speech, they abhor the few among them who are heartily disposed towards us; ever deeming that their ignoble course of procedure will force us to do away with our reform. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} Having then, received certain proofs that these [Jews] bear us every sort of ill-will, we must look forward to the possibility of some sudden tumult among ourselves, when these impious men may turn traitors and barbarous enemies. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those [Jews] who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} For by the punishment of them in one body we perceive that we have found the only means of establishing our affairs for the future on a firm and satisfactory basis. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Whosoever shall shield a Jew, whether it be old man, child, or suckling, shall with his whole house be tortured to death. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Whoever shall inform against the [Jews,] besides receiving the property of the person charged, shall be presented with two thousand drachmas from the royal treasury, shall be made free, and shall be crowned. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Whatever place shall shelter a Jew, shall, when he is hunted forth, be put under the ban of fire, and be for ever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} Such was the purport of the king's letter.\par
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 4}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 4}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting; as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred, were now to show itself openly. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} The Jews suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} They were sent out unanimously by the generals in the several cities, with such stern and pitiless feeling, that the exceptional nature of the infliction moved even some of their enemies. These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at this their miserable expulsion. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} A multitude of aged hoary-haired old men, were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled; and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} Bound, and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} The planks of the deck above them barred out the light, and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} When this was done, the king, hearing that their brethren in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same (and not one whit milder) treatment. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name; not for that hard servitude of labor which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might extirpate them by his cruelties. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth, gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest God. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Jews was too great for registration, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places; so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Jews: but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} Now this was an active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Jews from heaven.\par
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 5}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 5}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Jews the most. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} The underlings appointed for the purpose went out about eventide and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} The heathen believed the Jews to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} they invoked the Almighty Lord, and ceaselessly implored with tears their merciful God and Father, Ruler of all, Lord of every power, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} to overthrow the evil purpose which was gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} Their litany so earnest went up to heaven. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious draughts of mingled wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to certify the kind thereof. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof now upon the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} By this sweet and profound influence of the Lord he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} But the Jews, having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy God, and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the overweening Gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The middle of the tenth hour had well near arrived, when the master-bidder, seeing the guests who were bidden collected, came and shook the king. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his potations, commanded the guests to sit down before him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and enquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Jews had been allowed to outlive that day. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, That they might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against tomorrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved; and then each man went to his own home. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} Nor did they employ the night in sleep, so much as in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} The Jews, breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest God, in mournful strains, again to help them speedily. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} The sun's rays were not yet shed abroad, and the king was waiting for his friends, when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying, That his desires could now be realized. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} But this was the working of that Almighty God who had made him forget all his purpose. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} Hermon, and all his friends, pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The king was filled with fierce anger at these words; for, by the Providence of God regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Your parents, or your children, were they here, to these wild beasts a large repast they should have furnished; not these innocent Jews, who me and my forefathers loyally have served. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{33}} Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in visage, and depressed in countenance. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{34}} The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their respective occupations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{35}} The Jews, having heard of these events, praised the glorious God and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{36}} Now the king arranged another banquet after the same manner, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{37}} And he summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to you about these same persons? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{38}} Once more, arm the elephants against the morrow for the extermination of the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{39}} His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{40}} O king, how long do you make trial of us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that you have ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, you change your mind, and recall your instructions. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{41}} For this cause the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city: it swarms with factions; and is continually on the point of being plundered. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{42}} The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Jews. He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{43}} He would also invade Judea, and level its towns with fire and the sword; and destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{44}} Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{45}} And the master of the elephants urged the beasts into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful instruments. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{46}} About early morning, when the city was now filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace, and called the king to the business in hand. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{47}} The king's heart teemed with impious rage; and he rushed forth with the mass, along with the elephants. With feelings unsoftened, and eyes pitiless, he longed to gaze at the hard and wretched doom of the above-mentioned [Jews]. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{48}} But the [Jews], when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force; and when they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{49}} thought that they had come to the last moment of their lives, to the end of what they had tremblingly expected. They gave way, therefore, to lamentations and moans: they kissed each other: those nearest of kin to each other hung about one another's necks: fathers about their sons, mother their daughters: other women held their infants to their breasts, which drew what seemed their last milk. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{50}} Nevertheless, when they reflected upon the succour before granted them from heaven, they prostrated themselves with one accord; removed even the sucking children from the breasts, and {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{51}} sent up an exceeding great cry entreating the Lord of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of hades.\par
\subsection*{3 Maccabees 6}
\markright{3 MACCABEES 6}
\noindent {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{1}} And Eleazar, an illustrious priest of the country, who had attained to length of days, and whose life had been adorned with virtue, caused the presbyters who were about him to cease to cry out to the holy God, and prayed thus: {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{2}} O king, mighty in power, most high, Almighty God, who regulates the whole creation with your tender mercy, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{3}} look upon the seed of Abraham, upon the children of the sanctified Jacob, your sanctified inheritance, O Father, now being wrongfully destroyed as strangers in a strange land. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{4}} You destroyed Pharaoh, with his hosts of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of your mercy upon the race of Israel, you did overwhelm him with his proud army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{5}} When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against your holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, you, O Lord, did demolish him and did show forth your might to many nations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{6}} When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, you did send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{7}} It was you who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, did bring him back against unhurt to light. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{8}} When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, you did look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{9}} And now, you who hate insolence; you who do abound in mercy; you who are the protector of all things; appear quickly to those of the race of Israel, who are insulted by abhorred, lawless gentiles. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{10}} If our life has during our exile been stained with iniquity, deliver us from the hand of the enemy, and destroy us, O Lord, by the death which you prefer. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{11}} Let not the vain-minded congratulate vain idols at the destruction of your beloved, saying, Neither did their god deliver them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{12}} You, who are All-powerful and Almighty, O Eternal One, behold! have mercy upon us who are being withdrawn from life, like traitors, by the unreasoning insolence of lawless men. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{13}} Let the heathen cower before your invincible might today, O glorious One, who have all power to save the race of Jacob. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{14}} The whole band of infants and their parents with tears beseech you. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{15}} Let it be shown to all the nations that you are with us, O Lord, and have not turned your face away from us; but as you said that you would not forget them even in the land of their enemies, so do you fulfil this saying, O Lord. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{16}} Now, at the time that Eleazar had ended his prayer, the king came along to the hippodrome, with the wild beasts, and with his tumultuous power. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{17}} When the Jews saw this, they uttered a loud cry to heaven, so that the adjacent valleys resounded, and caused an irrepressible lamentation throughout the army. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{18}} Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true God, displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down and were visible to all but the Jews. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{19}} And they stood opposite, and filled the enemies' host with confusion and cowardice; and bound them with immoveable fetters. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{20}} And a cold shudder came over the person of the king, and oblivion paralysed the vehemence of his spirit. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{21}} They turned back the animals upon the armed forces which followed them; and the animals trod them down, and destroyed them. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{22}} The king's wrath was converted into compassion; and he wept at his own machinations. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{23}} For when he heard the cry, and saw them all on the verge of destruction, with tears he angrily threatened his friends, saying, {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{24}} You⌃ have governed badly; and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty; and me your benefactor you⌃ have laboured to deprive at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devising measures injurious to the kingdom. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{25}} Who has gathered here, unreasonably removing each from his home, those who, in fidelity to us, had held the fortresses of the country? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{26}} Who has thus consigned to unmerited punishments those who in good will towards us from the beginning have in all things surpassed all nations, and who often have engaged in the most dangerous undertakings? {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{27}} Loose, loose the unjust bonds; send them to their homes in peace, and deprecate what has been done. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{28}} Release the sons of the almighty living God of heaven, who from our ancestors' times until now has granted a glorious and uninterrupted prosperity to our affairs. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{29}} These things he said; and they, released the same moment, having now escaped death, praised God their holy Saviour. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{30}} The king then departed to the city, and called his financier to him, and bade him provide a seven days' quantity of wine and other materials for feasting for the Jews. He decided that they should keep a gladsome festival of deliverance in the very place in which they expected to meet with their destruction. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{31}} Then they who were before despised and near to hades, yes, rather advanced into it, partook of the cup of salvation, instead of a grievous and lamentable death. Full of exultation, they parted out the place intended for their fall and burial into banqueting booths. {\color{tnaccent}\fontsize{6.4}{6.4}\selectfont\textsuperscript{32}} Ceasing their miserable strain of woe, they took up the subject of their fatherland, hymning in praise God their wonder-working Saviour.
