\section*{Topical Verse Reference Appendix}
\subsection*{Faith \& Trust in God}
\noindent Proverbs 3:5-6 — Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.\par
\noindent Hebrews 11:1 — Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.\par
\noindent 2 Corinthians 5:7 — For we walk by faith, not by sight.\par
\noindent Philippians 4:13 — I can do all things through him who strengthens me.\par
\newpage
\section*{Biblical Name Meanings Appendix}

\noindent Adam — “Man” / “of the red earth” (Hebrew adamah)\par
\noindent First human formed from the ground; his name is literally what he was made from.\par
\noindent Eve (Chavah) — “Living” / “life-giver” (Hebrew chayah)\par
\noindent Mother of all living; the name God (and Adam) gave her after the promise of redemption.\par
\noindent Cain — “Acquired” / “spear” (Hebrew qanah)\par
\noindent Eve said, “I have acquired a man with the help of the LORD” — but he became the first murderer.\par
\noindent Abel — “Breath” / “vanity” / “futility” (Hebrew hevel)\par
\noindent His life was short and “vanished like a breath” — the first martyr.\par
\noindent Seth — “Appointed” / “compensation” / “placed” (Hebrew shith)\par
\noindent “God has appointed another seed instead of Abel” — the chosen line continues through him.\par
\noindent Enosh — “Man” / “mortal” / “frail” (Hebrew enosh)\par
\noindent In his days “men began to call upon the name of the LORD” — highlights human weakness.\par
\noindent Kenan (Cainan) — “Possession” / “smith” or “spear” (related to Cain)\par
\noindent Continues the line; name echoes the “acquired” theme of the pre-flood world.\par
\noindent Mahalalel — “Praise of God” / “the shining one of God” (Hebrew mahalal + El)\par
\noindent His very name is a shout of praise in a darkening world.\par
\noindent Jared — “Descent” / “he shall come down” (Hebrew yarad)\par
\noindent Traditional Jewish interpretation: “he shall come down” — pointing to the descent of the sons of God or the coming judgment.\par
\noindent Enoch — “Dedicated” / “trained” / “initiated” (Hebrew chanok)\par
\noindent Walked so closely with God he was “taken” without dying — fully dedicated.\par
\noindent Methuselah — “When he dies, it shall be sent” / “man of the dart” (Hebrew muth + shelach)\par
\noindent His death coincided with the Flood — his name was a 969-year prophecy of judgment.\par
\noindent Lamech — “Powerful” / “overthrower” (or possibly “poor” / “despairing”)\par
\noindent Father of Noah; spoke of relief from the curse — but his line produced violence.\par
\noindent Noah — “Rest” / “comfort” / “relief” (Hebrew nuach)\par
\noindent “This one will bring us relief from our work and the toil of our hands” — the ark brought rest from judgment.\par
\noindent Shem — “Name” / “renown” (Hebrew shem)\par
\noindent Ancestor of the Semitic line; through him came the “Name” (the line that would bear God’s name).\par
\noindent Japheth — “Enlarged” / “may he enlarge” (Hebrew yaphath)\par
\noindent “May God enlarge Japheth” — his descendants spread across the earth.\par
\noindent Ishmael — “God hears” (Hebrew Yishmaʿel)\par
\noindent God heard Hagar’s affliction in the wilderness.\par
\noindent Esau — “Hairy” / “red” (Hebrew ʿEsav)\par
\noindent Born hairy and red; sold his birthright for red stew.\par
\noindent Jacob — “Supplanter” / “heel-grabber” (Hebrew Yaʿaqov)\par
\noindent Grabbed Esau’s heel at birth; later supplanted him and became Israel.\par
\noindent Israel — “God contends” / “strives with God” (Hebrew Yisraʾel)\par
\noindent Wrestled with God and prevailed; name of the covenant nation.\par
\noindent Reuben — “Behold a son” (Hebrew Reʾuven)\par
\noindent Leah’s first son; “Behold, a son!” — hoped it would win Jacob’s love.\par
\noindent Simeon — “Heard” (Hebrew Shimʿon)\par
\noindent “The LORD has heard that I am hated” — Leah’s second son.\par
\noindent Levi — “Joined” / “attached” (Hebrew Levi)\par
\noindent “Now my husband will be joined to me” — tribe of priests.\par
\noindent Judah — “Praise” (Hebrew Yehudah)\par
\noindent “This time I will praise the LORD” — royal tribe and ancestor of Messiah.\par
\noindent Joseph — “He adds” / “may He add” (Hebrew Yosef)\par
\noindent God added to his blessings despite betrayal; savior of his family.\par
\noindent Benjamin — “Son of the right hand” (Hebrew Binyamin)\par
\noindent Rachel’s last son; “son of my sorrow” became “son of the right hand.”\par
\noindent Moses — “Drawn out” (of water) (Hebrew Mosheh)\par
\noindent Drawn out of the Nile; drew Israel out of Egypt.\par
\noindent Aaron — “Exalted” / “mountain of strength” / “teacher” (Hebrew Aharon)\par
\noindent First high priest; exalted to lead worship.\par
\noindent Joshua (Yehoshua) — “Yahweh saves” (Hebrew Yehoshuaʿ)\par
\noindent Led Israel into the Promised Land; name points to the ultimate Savior.\par
\noindent Caleb — “Whole-hearted” / “dog” (faithful like a dog) (Hebrew Kalev)\par
\noindent Followed the LORD fully; entered the land.\par
\noindent Rahab — “Broad” / “spacious” (Hebrew Rachav)\par
\noindent God’s mercy was broad enough to save a Canaanite prostitute.\par
\noindent Ruth — “Friend” / “companion” (Hebrew Ruth)\par
\noindent Loyal friend to Naomi; became ancestor of David and Messiah.\par
\noindent Samuel — “Heard of God” / “God has heard” (Hebrew Shmuʾel)\par
\noindent God heard Hannah’s prayer; last judge and anointer of kings.\par
\noindent Saul — “Asked for” / “prayed for” (Hebrew Shaʾul)\par
\noindent The people “asked for” a king; first king of Israel.\par
\noindent David — “Beloved” (Hebrew Dawid)\par
\noindent The beloved king; “a man after God’s own heart.”\par
\noindent Solomon — “Peaceable” / “peaceful” (Hebrew Shelomoh)\par
\noindent Brought peace and built the Temple.\par
\noindent Elijah — “My God is Yahweh” (Hebrew Eliyahu)\par
\noindent Confronted Baal worship; “My God is Yahweh.”\par
\noindent Elisha — “My God is salvation” (Hebrew Elishaʿ)\par
\noindent Continued Elijah’s work; brought salvation and healing.\par
\noindent Isaiah — “Yahweh saves” (Hebrew Yeshaʿyahu)\par
\noindent Prophesied the coming Savior who would save His people.\par
\noindent Jeremiah — “Yahweh exalts” / “Yahweh throws” (Hebrew Yirmeyahu)\par
\noindent Exalted God even while weeping over Jerusalem.\par
\noindent Ezekiel — “God strengthens” (Hebrew Yehezqel)\par
\noindent Strengthened by God during exile.\par
\noindent Daniel — “God is my judge” (Hebrew Daniyyel)\par
\noindent Stood before earthly kings; God was his true Judge.\par
\noindent Hosea — “Salvation” (Hebrew Hosheaʿ)\par
\noindent His life pictured God’s faithful salvation of unfaithful Israel.\par
\noindent Jonah — “Dove” (Hebrew Yonah)\par
\noindent Symbol of peace; fled yet brought salvation to Nineveh.\par
\noindent Micah — “Who is like Yahweh?” (Hebrew Mikah)\par
\noindent Asked the rhetorical question that points to God’s uniqueness.\par
\noindent Nahum — “Comfort” (Hebrew Nachum)\par
\noindent Brought comfort by announcing the end of Nineveh’s oppression.\par
\noindent Habakkuk — “Embrace” (Hebrew Chavaqquq)\par
\noindent Embraced God in faith despite coming judgment.\par
\noindent Zephaniah — “Yahweh has hidden” / “protected” (Hebrew Tsephanyah)\par
\noindent Hidden and protected the remnant during judgment.\par
\noindent Haggai — “Festal” / “my feasts” (Hebrew Chaggay)\par
\noindent Urged the people to rebuild the Temple for God’s festivals.\par
\noindent Zechariah — “Yahweh remembers” (Hebrew Zekharyah)\par
\noindent God remembered His covenant promises.\par
\noindent Malachi — “My messenger” (Hebrew Malʾaki)\par
\noindent The last Old Testament messenger before John the Baptist.\par
\noindent Esther (Hadassah) — “Star” / “myrtle” (hidden beauty) (Hebrew Hadassah)\par
\noindent Hidden like a star; saved her people.\par
\noindent Mordecai — “Little man” or “pure myrrh” (humble servant) (Hebrew Mordokay)\par
\noindent Humble servant who refused to bow to Haman.\par
\noindent Ezra — “Help” (Hebrew ʿEzraʾ)\par
\noindent Helped restore the Law and the people after exile.\par
\noindent Nehemiah — “Yahweh comforts” (Hebrew Nechemyah)\par
\noindent Comforted and rebuilt Jerusalem’s walls.\par
\noindent Mary (Miriam) — “Bitter” / “beloved” / “exalted one” (Hebrew Miryam)\par
\noindent Mother of Jesus; experienced bitterness yet exaltation.\par
\noindent Joseph (NT) — “He adds” (same as OT Joseph)\par
\noindent God added protection and provision for the holy family.\par
\noindent John (Yochanan) — “Yahweh is gracious” (Hebrew Yochanan)\par
\noindent Forerunner of Jesus; proclaimed God’s grace.\par
\noindent Jesus (Yeshua) — “Yahweh saves” (Hebrew Yeshuaʿ)\par
\noindent The ultimate fulfillment: “He will save His people from their sins.”\par
\noindent Peter (Cephas / Petros) — “Rock” / “stone” (Aramaic/Greek)\par
\noindent The rock on which the Church would be built.\par
\noindent Andrew — “Manly” / “courageous” (Greek Andreas)\par
\noindent Courageous fisherman turned fisher of men.\par
\noindent James (Jacob) — “Supplanter” (Hebrew Yaʿaqov)\par
\noindent One of the “sons of thunder”; later a pillar of the Church.\par
\noindent Philip — “Lover of horses” (used for “lover of people”) (Greek Philippos)\par
\noindent Brought people to Jesus (e.g., the Ethiopian eunuch).\par
\noindent Bartholomew (Nathanael) — “Gift of God” (Hebrew Nethanʾel)\par
\noindent Jesus called him “an Israelite in whom is no deceit.”\par
\noindent Thomas — “Twin” / “doubter” (Aramaic Taʾoma)\par
\noindent Doubting Thomas; later declared “My Lord and my God!”\par
\noindent Matthew (Levi) — “Gift of Yahweh” (Hebrew Mattityahu)\par
\noindent Tax collector given the gift of apostleship and authorship.\par
\noindent Simon the Zealot — “He has heard” (Hebrew Shimʿon)\par
\noindent Zealous revolutionary transformed into apostle.\par
\noindent Judas (not Iscariot) — “Praise” (Hebrew Yehudah)\par
\noindent Praised God; author of the epistle of Jude.\par
\noindent Paul (Saul) — “Small” / “humble” (Latin Paulus)\par
\noindent Changed from “asked for” (Saul) to the humble apostle to the Gentiles.\par
\noindent Timothy — “Honoring God” (Greek Timotheos)\par
\noindent Honored God as Paul’s faithful son in the faith.\par
\noindent Titus — “Honorable” / “defender” (Latin Titus)\par
\noindent Defended the faith and organized churches.\par
\noindent Philemon — “Affectionate” / “kissing” (Greek Philemon)\par
\noindent Showed affectionate forgiveness to his runaway slave.\par
\noindent Barnabas — “Son of encouragement” (Aramaic Bar-Nabas)\par
\noindent Encouraged the early Church and Paul.\par
\noindent Stephen — “Crown” / “garland” (Greek Stephanos)\par
\noindent Received the martyr’s crown as the first Christian martyr.\par
\noindent Lydia — “From Lydia” (purple seller — royal color) (Greek Lydia)\par
\noindent First European convert; “dealer in purple” (royal trade).\par
\noindent Aquila — “Eagle” (Latin Aquila)\par
\noindent Strong “eagle” who with Priscilla taught Apollos.\par
\noindent Priscilla — “Ancient” / “venerable” (Latin Priscilla)\par
\noindent Venerable teacher alongside her husband.\par
\noindent Apollos — “Destroyer” or “of Apollo” (eloquent preacher) (Greek Apollos)\par
\noindent Mighty preacher whose eloquence was refined by Aquila and Priscilla.\par
\noindent Silas (Silvanus) — “Forest” / “wood” (steady like a tree) (Latin Silvanus)\par
\noindent Steady companion who endured prison with Paul.\par
\noindent Onesimus — “Useful” / “profitable” (Greek Onesimos)\par
\noindent The runaway slave who became “useful” to Paul and Philemon.\par
\noindent Phoebe — “Bright” / “radiant” (Greek Phoibe)\par
\noindent Radiant deaconess who carried Paul’s letter to Rome.\par
\noindent Gaius — “Rejoice” / “happy” (Latin Gaius)\par
\noindent Hospitable host who brought joy to the Church.\par
\noindent Erastus — “Beloved” (Greek Erastos)\par
\noindent Beloved city treasurer who served Paul.\par
\noindent Demas — “Popular” (Greek Demas)\par
\noindent Loved popularity more than Christ and forsook Paul.\par
\noindent Mark (John Mark) — “Hammer” or “polite” (Latin Marcus)\par
\noindent Initially faltered but later became useful to Paul.\par
\noindent Luke — “Light-giving” / “from Lucania” (Greek Loukas)\par
\noindent “Beloved physician” who brought gospel light.\par
\noindent Theophilus — “Lover of God” (Greek Theophilos)\par
\noindent The one Luke wrote to — “lover of God.”\par
\noindent Diotrephes — “Nurtured by Zeus” (loved preeminence) (Greek Diotrephes)\par
\noindent Loved preeminence and opposed apostolic authority.\par
\noindent Gamaliel — “God is my reward” (Hebrew Gamaliel)\par
\noindent Wise teacher who advised the Sanhedrin wisely.\par
\noindent Nicodemus — “Victory of the people” (Greek Nikodemos)\par
\noindent Came to Jesus by night seeking truth.\par
\noindent Lazarus — “God has helped” (Hebrew Elʿazar)\par
\noindent Raised from the dead; God helped him.\par
\noindent Martha — “Lady” / “mistress” (Aramaic Martha)\par
\noindent Busy homemaker who learned to sit at Jesus’ feet.\par
\noindent Mary Magdalene — “Of Magdala” (tower) (Hebrew Miryam)\par
\noindent “Tower” of strength; first witness to the resurrection.\par
\noindent Salome — “Peace” / “peaceful” (Hebrew Shalom)\par
\noindent Mother of James and John; sought peaceful places at Jesus’ right hand.\par
\noindent Barabbas — “Son of the father” (Aramaic Bar-Abba)\par
\noindent Released in place of the true Son of the Father.\par
\noindent Pilate (Pontius) — “Armed with a spear” (Latin Pilatus)\par
\noindent Roman judge who washed his hands of Jesus.\par
\noindent Herod — “Heroic” / “son of a hero” (Greek Herodes)\par
\noindent Multiple “heroic” kings who opposed God’s plan.\par
\noindent Ananias — “Yahweh has been gracious” (Hebrew Chananyah)\par
\noindent Multiple figures shown God’s grace (one healed Paul, one lied).\par
\noindent Sapphira — “Sapphire” (beautiful but deceptive) (Greek Sapphira)\par
\noindent Beautiful exterior but deceptive heart.\par
\noindent Cornelius — “Horn” (Latin Cornelius)\par
\noindent Roman centurion whose “horn” (strength) was turned to God.\par
\noindent Felix — “Happy” / “fortunate” (Latin Felix)\par
\noindent Governor who trembled but never found true happiness.\par
\noindent Festus — “Festive” / “joyful” (Latin Festus)\par
\noindent Roman governor who heard Paul’s defense joyfully.\par
\noindent Agrippa — “Wild horse” (Greek Agrippas)\par
\noindent King who heard the gospel but remained untamed.\par
\noindent Bernice — “Bringer of victory” (Greek Bernike)\par
\noindent Sister of Agrippa; present at Paul’s trial.\par
\noindent Artemas — “Gift of Artemis” or follower (Greek)\par
\noindent Faithful coworker Paul sent to Crete.\par
\noindent Tychicus — “Fortunate” / “chance” (Greek Tychikos)\par
\noindent “Lucky” messenger who carried Paul’s letters.\par
\noindent Epaphras — “Lovely” / “charming” (Greek Epaphras)\par
\noindent Lovely intercessor who prayed fervently for Colossae.\par
\noindent Archippus — “Master of the horse” (Greek Archippos)\par
\noindent Called to “fulfill your ministry” like a faithful rider.\par
\noindent Apphia — “Productive” / “increasing” (Greek Apphia)\par
\noindent Hostess whose house church grew.\par
\noindent Euodia — “Prosperous journey” / “success” (Greek Euodia)\par
\noindent Worked hard in the gospel but needed unity.\par
\noindent Syntyche — “With fate” / “fortunate together” (Greek Syntyche)\par
\noindent Called to agree in the Lord.\par
\noindent Clement — “Mild” / “merciful” (Latin Clemens)\par
\noindent Fellow worker whose name is in the Book of Life.\par
\noindent Epaphroditus — “Lovely” / “charming” (Greek)\par
\noindent Risked his life to serve Paul.\par
\noindent Onesiphorus — “Bringing profit” (Greek Onesiphoros)\par
\noindent Refreshing and profitable servant.\par
\noindent Aristarchus — “Best ruler” (Greek Aristarchos)\par
\noindent Loyal prisoner with Paul.\par
\noindent Zacchaeus — “Pure” / “innocent” (Hebrew Zakkay)\par
\noindent Tax collector made pure by Jesus.\par
\noindent Bartimaeus — “Son of Timaeus” / “honorable” (Aramaic)\par
\noindent Blind beggar healed and followed Jesus.\par
\noindent Jairus — “He enlightens” (Hebrew Yaʾir)\par
\noindent Synagogue ruler whose daughter was raised.\par
\noindent Simeon (NT) — “Heard”\par
\noindent Held baby Jesus and declared he had “seen” salvation.\par
\noindent Anna — “Grace” / “favor” (Hebrew Channah)\par
\noindent Prophetess who recognized the Messiah.\par
\noindent Elizabeth — “God is my oath” (Hebrew Elisheva)\par
\noindent Mother of John; God kept His oath.\par
\noindent Zacharias — “Yahweh remembers” (Hebrew Zekharyah)\par
\noindent Father of John; God remembered him.\par
\noindent John the Baptist — “Yahweh is gracious” (Hebrew Yochanan)\par
\noindent Prepared the way with grace.\par
\noindent Herodias — “Heroic” (feminine form)\par
\noindent Manipulative “heroine” who sought John’s head.\par
\noindent Cleopas — “Glory of the father” (Greek Kleopas)\par
\noindent Disciple on Emmaus road who saw the risen Christ.\par
\noindent Matthias — “Gift of Yahweh” (Hebrew Mattityahu)\par
\noindent Chosen by lot to replace Judas.\par
\noindent Philip (evangelist) — “Lover of horses/people” (Greek Philippos)\par
\noindent Evangelized Samaria and the Ethiopian.\par
\noindent Simon the Sorcerer — “He has heard”\par
\noindent Heard the gospel but sought power.\par
\noindent Dorcas (Tabitha) — “Gazelle” (Aramaic Tabitha)\par
\noindent Full of good works; raised to life.\par
\noindent Sergius Paulus — “Small” / “humble” (Latin)\par
\noindent Proconsul who believed after seeing God’s power.\par
\noindent Elymas (Bar-Jesus) — “Wise man” (sorcerer)\par
\noindent Opposed the gospel.\par
\noindent Jason — “Healer” (Greek Iason)\par
\noindent Hosted Paul and faced riot.\par
\noindent Dionysius — “Of Dionysus” (Greek)\par
\noindent Areopagite who believed Paul’s message.\par
\noindent Damaris — “Calf” / “gentle” (Greek)\par
\noindent Athenian woman who joined the believers.\par
\noindent Gallio — “Gentle” / “calm” (Latin)\par
\noindent Proconsul who dismissed charges against Paul.\par
\noindent Alexander the coppersmith — “Defender of men” (Greek Alexandros)\par
\noindent Opposed Paul.\par
\noindent Hymenaeus — “Of Hymen” (marriage god)\par
\noindent False teacher who shipwrecked faith.\par
\noindent Phygelus — “Fugitive” (Greek Phygelos)\par
\noindent Deserted Paul in Asia.\par
\noindent Hermogenes — “Born of Hermes”\par
\noindent Also deserted.\par
\noindent Crescens — “Growing” (Latin Crescens)\par
\noindent Faithful coworker who went to Galatia.\par
\noindent Pudens — “Modest” / “shamefaced” (Latin)\par
\noindent Roman Christian who greeted Paul.\par
\noindent Linus — “Flaxen” / “net” (Greek Linos)\par
\noindent Early Church leader.\par
\noindent Claudia — “Lame” (but faithful) (Latin Claudia)\par
\noindent Woman who greeted Paul.\par
\noindent Eubulus — “Good counselor” (Greek Euboulos)\par
\noindent Faithful in Rome.\par
\noindent Zenas — “Living” (Greek Zenas)\par
\noindent Lawyer who traveled with Apollos.\par
\noindent Jude (Judas, brother of James) — “Praise” (Hebrew Yehudah)\par
\noindent Author of the epistle of Jude.\par
\noindent Sosthenes — “Safe in strength” (Greek Sosthenes)\par
\noindent Ruler of synagogue who believed.\par
\noindent Crispus — “Curly-haired” (Latin Crispus)\par
\noindent Synagogue ruler baptized by Paul.\par
\noindent Fortunatus — “Fortunate” (Latin)\par
\noindent Corinthian who refreshed Paul.\par
\noindent Achaicus — “From Achaia” (sorrowing)\par
\noindent Helped Paul.\par
\noindent Stephanas — “Crown” (Greek Stephanas)\par
\noindent First converts in Achaia.\par
\noindent Chloe — “Green herb” / “blooming” (Greek Chloe)\par
\noindent Informed Paul of divisions.\par
\noindent Nymphas — “Bridegroom” (Greek Nymphas)\par
\noindent Hosted a house church.\par
\end{document}
